1-4-billion-year-old-mushroom-fossil-in-: In an episode about mushrooms, the podcast host Jesse Michels says that an intact fossil of a mushroom about 1.4 billion years old was found in northeastern Brazil. He tells it to suggest that mushrooms are extremely ancient, which fits the episode's playful idea that they might have come from somewhere beyond Earth.
101-year-old-recalls-a-giant-graveyard-f: A man who investigates stories of ancient giants, Tim Alberino, says a 101-year-old named Anna Tuary told him that in the 1920s or 1930s, while ground was being ploughed for a vineyard near a nuraghe, an ancient stone tower on the Italian island of Sardinia, workers suddenly began unearthing the remains of gigantic people. In a second telling, Alberino adds that vans pulled up, men got out with equipment and took the remains away while a witness hid, and that a passage in the tower was sealed. If true, it would mean a race of giants once lived there and the evidence was quietly removed.
111-and-222-synchronicities-during-the-r: In 2026 the podcast host Jesse Michels went on a trip to bring together Air Force veterans who say they were taken by aliens about fifty years earlier. Michels says he kept seeing repeating numbers along the way, like 111 and 222. One example he gives: one person landed at 1:11 just as Omar, a guest coming from a group called Yes Theory, was taking off at 1:11. He tells this as a meaningful coincidence, a sign the trip was somehow meant to be.
13-year-old-corbell-hears-knapp-s-lazar-: A filmmaker named Jeremy Corbell says that around 1990, when he was 13, he heard a Las Vegas reporter, George Knapp, on the radio interviewing a man named Bob Lazar, who claimed to have worked on alien craft at a secret Nevada site. Corbell tells this on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels as the moment his interest began, the start of a path that he says led to his later work on the subject.
15th-16th-century-explorers-accounts-of-: Talking with the writer Graham Hancock, the podcast host Jesse Michels mentions old reports from European explorers of the 1400s and 1500s who said they saw large settlements in the Amazon rainforest. Michels says these stories helped drive Hancock's research and that Hancock's work then backed them up. If true, it would mean the Amazon once held cities far bigger than people usually imagine.
17-days-of-drone-swarms-over-langley-202: This story is about Langley Air Force Base in Hampton, Virginia. A podcast host named Jesse Michels says that in 2023, for 17 days, what he calls drones swarmed over the base, and that there seemed to be no defence against them. A former Navy fighter pilot, Ryan Graves, adds that the base houses F-22 fighter jets, and that they were moved to another base for fear of losing them. Michels also passes on a claim by a man named Chris Mellon that there was a larger mother ship. People tell it because, if true, unknown craft could fly freely over a key US base, and a news anchor's clip says Air Force officials confirmed several unmanned drones flew over Langley one December, though without the 17 days.
170-odd-q-cleared-witnesses-of-ufos-at-s: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that about 170 people holding a Q clearance, the top security clearance for work on US nuclear weapons, have reported seeing UFOs around the country's most sensitive nuclear sites. He says that in some cases these objects shut the sites down. If true, it would mean something unknown can interfere with America's nuclear arsenal.
1800-case-balls-of-light-come-out-of-the: A physicist who studies UFO reports, Kevin Knuth, describes a case he dates to the year 1800, at sea. According to him, balls of light rose out of the water, hovered beside a ship, followed it, and then shot off into the clouds. He tells it to show that such sightings go back long before modern aircraft.
1890s-airship-mystery-and-nymza-per-walt: Salvatore Pais, a Navy scientist who holds patents on unusual craft, speaking on a podcast, brings up the 'airship mystery' of the 1890s, when strange flying machines were reported across the United States. He mentions a writer, Walter Bosley, friend of another writer, Joseph Farrell, and Bosley's idea of a group called NYMZA, asking who these people really were. The suggestion is that someone on the ground may have been flying those airships.
1890s-airship-sightings-as-a-culturally-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, puts forward the idea that what people see in the sky is shaped by their own era. He says that in the 1890s people reported seeing airships, machines that were at the very edge of what was possible back then. On this view, strange sightings take whatever form a culture can just barely imagine.
19-non-negotiable-demands-to-change-the-: Bryce Zabel, a television writer and producer, says that in 1996 in Los Angeles, his first episode of Dark Skies, a TV series about a hidden UFO history, came back from the network with a list of 19 non-negotiable demands for changes. He tells this on Jesse Michels's podcast and names his co-creator Brent Friedman, Steven Spielberg, and Don Ohlmeyer, an executive at the NBC network who, by his account, stepped in personally. He tells it as an example of how much attention the powerful paid to UFO stories on screen.
1904-chilean-cattle-mutilations: The podcast host Jesse Michels, passing on what a man named Chris Ramsey told him, says there was a run of cattle mutilations in Chile in 1904. These are cases where farm animals are found dead with parts strangely cut away. If true, it would mean such cases go back far earlier than most people assume.
1911-superconductor-discovery-as-a-model: A young researcher, Deep Prasad, points to 1911, when a scientist named Onnes discovered superconductivity, materials that carry electricity with no resistance at all. Prasad says the lesson was that when something seems to break the laws of physics, it is probably an effect that grows out of strange quantum behaviour underneath. He uses this to suggest that UAP, the official term for unexplained flying objects, might behave impossibly for the same kind of reason.
1918-us-expeditionary-force-into-russia: A lawyer and researcher, Dan Sheehan, says that in 1918 the United States paid for and sent a full-scale military force into Russia, citing Robert Lansing, the US Secretary of State at the time. He raises it in a conversation about President Kennedy and UFOs, as part of a longer story about hidden decisions made by those in power.
1930s-homesteader-accounts-of-cattle-mut: Brandon Fugal, the owner of Skinwalker Ranch, a property in Utah known for reports of strange events, says his team's investigation turned up old stories. According to him, accounts going back to the early settlers of the 1930s describe bizarre cattle mutilation, cows found dead with odd injuries, and other strange activity on the land. If true, it would mean the strangeness there is not new but goes back generations.
1934-plot-to-overthrow-fdr-via-general-s: A guest named Dan Sheehan says that in 1934 a group tried to recruit General Smedley Butler, a former head of the US Marine Corps, to lead a major uprising of war veterans against the government of President Franklin Roosevelt. Sheehan tells it as an early example of powerful people plotting in secret against the elected government.
1941-fbi-vetting-of-silas-newton: Podcast host Jesse Michels says that FBI files, the records of the US federal police, include a check on a man named Silas Newton. He quotes a document dated July 1st, 1941, which says Newton 'appears to be a good American citizen' and 'has no accent in his speech'. Newton is a central figure in It Came to Earth at Aztec, the work of researchers Scott and Suzanne Ramsay on a claimed saucer crash, so the file bears on how far his word can be trusted.
1942-fbi-file-laurel-canyon-address-norf: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, making a documentary about Townsend Brown, a scientist said to have worked on flying-disc technology, points to a 1942 file the FBI, the US national police agency, kept on him. Michels says the file shows Brown living on Wonderland Boulevard in Laurel Canyon, Los Angeles, and also touches on Norfolk, Virginia, and on compromising material that could be used against him. He presents it as a clue to the hidden side of Brown's life.
1944-press-reports-of-silver-spheres-ove: A researcher named Merrick says that in 1944, during the Second World War, newspapers reported strange silver spheres in the sky over Germany. He points to a Newsweek magazine piece called "The Silver Sphere Puzzle" and an Associated Press news wire story on Christmas Day 1944 about balls of silver seen over the German Reich, which would show such sightings were being reported before the modern UFO era began.
1945-state-department-document-on-nazi-l: A researcher who goes by JASON, speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast and drawing on the author Peter Levenda, describes a 1945 document from the State Department, the US government's foreign affairs office. He says it shows officials had already noticed that hundreds of new companies had been set up in Nicaragua and Argentina, which he links to Nazi money and people escaping Germany. If true, it would mean Nazi networks quietly rebuilt themselves in Latin America after the war.
1945-trinity-crash-as-the-source-of-a-la: This story is about a crash said to have happened near the Trinity site in New Mexico, a place linked to early US nuclear testing. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says a crash there in 1945 was where a "larger piece" of strange material came from. A French researcher, Jacques Vallee, tells a fuller version he credits to the writer Paola Harris, two local men named Remy Baca and Jose Padilla, and the book Trinity: The Best-Kept Secret. In his telling, the crash was near San Antonio, New Mexico, and through an opening where one panel was missing, the boys saw three human-like creatures with two eyes. Another guest, Marik von Rennenkampf, mentions it more cautiously, saying there was "possibly" a crash at the test site and that it is unclear, and credits a man named DD Johnson and Vallee. In a later episode Michels dates it to 1948 instead and counts it as one of a string of UFO crashes near nuclear sites. If true, it would mean an unknown craft, with beings aboard, came down near the birthplace of the atomic bomb.
1946-military-search-of-swedish-lakes-fo: Clas Svahn, a researcher who keeps a large collection of UFO records, tells of the 'ghost rockets', rocket-like objects reported over Sweden in 1946. He says the military searched several lakes around Sweden for them, thinking some had come down. All they found, he says, were dents in the lake bottoms, which would suggest something did hit the water.
1947-national-security-act-and-majestic-: A researcher, Dylan Borland, points to the National Security Act of 1947, the US law that created the Air Force, the CIA spy agency and the National Security Council, the president's top security body. He raises the question of how closely Majestic 12, a group some say was secretly set up to handle recovered alien craft, was tied into that council. If true, it would mean the secrecy around such craft was built into the government's security system from the start.
1949-battellewright-field-contract-on-ti: The podcast host Jesse Michels says that in 1949 a private research group, the Battelle Memorial Institute, signed a contract with Wright Field, an Air Force base in Ohio later called Wright-Patterson, to study metals made of titanium and nickel. He notes that Wright Field is where wreckage from Roswell, the 1947 New Mexico crash some say was a flying saucer, was rumored to be taken, and he ties this work to Nitinol, a so-called memory metal that springs back to its shape, developed later at a Navy lab. If true, it would hint that an everyday material came from studying crash debris.
1949-green-fireball-meeting-at-los-alamo: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says the physicist Edward Teller's name appears on a 1949 document from Los Alamos, the New Mexico nuclear weapons laboratory, about what it calls the "green fireball problem", bright green lights seen in the skies there. According to Michels, Teller is named on it alongside Lincoln LaPaz, a scientist who studied the lights. If so, it would mean top weapons scientists were taking the sightings seriously.
1950s-anti-gravity-research-went-quiet-p: This story is about research into anti-gravity, ways of making things move against gravity, that was openly pursued in America in the 1950s and then seemed to stop. A physicist named Hal Puthoff says there are two ways to read this: either nobody got anywhere, or someone did, and the work went black, meaning it was moved into secret programmes. A whistleblower, David Grusch, says there were many anti-gravity groups until the early 1960s and then they simply vanished. If the second reading is true, it would mean breakthrough technology has been kept hidden for decades.
1950s-ffrdcs-and-a-program-to-dole-out-r: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, wonders aloud whether in the 1950s the US government had a program that handed out material recovered from crashed unknown craft to research centres. He has in mind FFRDCs, which are private research labs funded by the federal government. He suggests those materials may have sped up and inspired new technology, and he points to a former Army officer, Philip Corso, and an online researcher known as UAPGerb, as sources for the idea. If true, some modern inventions would trace back to recovered craft.
1950s-flying-butane-tanks-in-air-force-o: David Grusch, a whistleblower interviewed on a podcast in 2023, says that reports from the Air Force Office of Special Investigations, the Air Force's internal investigative arm, described objects in the 1950s that looked like flying butane tanks. He compares them to the Tic Tac, a white oval object shaped like the mint that Navy pilots reported in recent years, saying the Tic Tac of today was the flying butane tank of the 1950s, which would mean the same kind of craft has been seen for decades.
1950s-gravity-research-by-bryce-dewitt-d: The podcast host Jesse Michels says that in the 1950s the physicist Bryce DeWitt, along with fellow scientists Stanley Deser and Richard Arnowitt, was studying gravity. According to Michels, DeWitt wrote about superconductors, materials that carry electricity with no resistance, and wondered if spinning them could disturb gravity. Michels raises it to suggest that serious work on controlling gravity was going on decades ago, quietly.
1950s-underground-bunker-under-secret-mo: An Australian journalist, Ross Coulthart, told podcast host Jesse Michels that he has no doubt at all that a deep underground military bunker was built in the 1950s under Secret Mountain, near Sedona, Arizona. In one telling he credits two people, Jeremiah and Alexandra Hostetler, as his sources. If true, it would mean a hidden military base, possibly linked to UFOs, has been there for decades.
1952-h-bomb-test-as-a-signal-to-the-cosm: A mathematician and podcaster, Eric Weinstein, wonders what it meant when the United States set off a hydrogen bomb in the Pacific in 1952. He says that if something or someone was out there listening, they likely heard us saying we were close to being able to come visit them. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, later repeats the idea, framing it instead as a signal that we were close to deep, root-level knowledge of physics. If true, it would offer a reason why visitors might have started watching us.
1952-mit-lincoln-lab-audio-of-dod-saucer: Eric Burles, speaking on a podcast, says that at MIT Lincoln Laboratory, a defense research lab in Massachusetts linked to the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, an old audio recording from 1952 turned up. According to him, it captures a senior official from the Department of Defense briefing the lab's scientists about flying saucers, which would mean the military was taking the subject seriously with top scientists that early.
1952-washington-d-c-sightings: This story is about a wave of UFO sightings over Washington, D.C., the US capital, in July 1952. The podcast host Jesse Michels describes it several times as an overwhelming series of sightings, with saucers seen all around the city and newspaper headlines like "saucers on the White House lawn." He says President Harry Truman called Edward J. Ruppelt, then the head of the Air Force's UFO investigations, about it, and that it sent the CIA, the main US spy agency, into a frenzy over how to handle the UFO problem. Karl Nell, a former government official, tells it on the same podcast. He says the objects were seen both by eye and on radar over two weekends, that military jets went up to intercept them, and that it led to the largest press conference since the Second World War. Michels also says he recently met one of the last living witnesses in person. If true, it would mean unknown objects flew over the nation's capital in plain view of the government.
1952-washington-dc-flyover: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, recalls a time in 1952 when unexplained objects were reported flying over Washington DC, the US capital. He says it was so big that the newspapers ran headlines about saucers on the White House lawn. If true, it would mean unknown craft once showed themselves openly over the seat of American government.
1953-kingman-crash-and-upshot-knothole: This story is about a craft said to have crashed near Kingman, Arizona, in 1953. A researcher known as UAPGerb says on Jesse Michels' podcast that, according to witness accounts, nuclear tests that year, a series called Operation Upshot-Knothole, may have interfered with the craft and brought it down. The researcher Richard Dolan, on the same show, says he has no doubt Kingman was real, crediting the investigator Raymond Fowler, but says nothing about the nuclear tests. If true, it would mean a non-human craft was recovered in the US, and that atomic bombs might have knocked it out of the sky.
1954-atomic-energy-act-moved-craft-custo: A researcher known online as UAPGerb told the podcast host Jesse Michels that he believes a recovered craft was moved in 1954. His reasoning is that the Atomic Energy Act of that year gave new powers to laboratories owned by the government but run by private companies, like Sandia, a national weapons lab, which let them house such craft. If true, it would explain how recovered objects ended up outside direct government control.
1956-montgolfier-vacuum-tests-in-paris: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in 1956 a French Air Force officer named Jean-Louis Cornillon, who also worked for the big French aircraft company Sud Aviation, arranged for the scientist Townsend Brown to test his devices in a vacuum at the Montgolfier facility in Paris. Michels cites a report on these tests. If true, it would show serious aviation interest in whether Brown's devices could move without air around them.
1957-afghanistan-ufo-event-reported-to-w: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says he found a declassified document, a once-secret government paper since released, that was sent to Wright-Patterson Air Force Base in Ohio. According to Michels, it describes a UFO event in Afghanistan in 1957. He presents it as a sign that the US military was quietly collecting UFO reports from around the world.
1957-ufos-head-toward-eisenhower-s-summe: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that a UFO researcher named Brad Sparks has carefully documented a UFO heading toward the summer home of President Dwight Eisenhower in September 1957. According to Michels, the case rests on records from NORAD, the US and Canadian air defence command, and from Project Blue Book, the US Air Force's UFO study of the 1950s and 60s, and if true it would mean an unknown object approached where the president was staying.
1960s-nasa-electrostatic-accidents-spin-: Charles Buer, who speaks from a NASA background on Jesse Michels's podcast, says that in the 1960s an accident at a spin test facility, where a solid rocket went off by mistake, trapped 11 people and caused deaths. He adds the Apollo fire, which killed astronauts, and says NASA lost around 14 people in all to accidents caused by static electricity. He tells it to show how dangerous electrostatic forces can be, in a conversation about new kinds of propulsion.
1960s-patent-for-nuclear-powered-tunneli: Steven Greer, a campaigner who pushes for the government to reveal what it knows about UFOs, says his archive holds a real 1960s patent for a nuclear-powered tunneling machine. He links it to Bechtel, a large engineering company, and to underground tunnels he says connect secret sites such as Area 51 in Nevada, other military test bases in the West, and Washington, D.C. to the Virginia mountains. If true, it would point to a hidden network of underground facilities.
1963-f8-atlas-missile-tracked-by-a-tagal: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in 1963, at Vandenberg Air Force Base in California, an Atlas missile (an American rocket) on a flight he calls F8 was followed by an unknown "tagalong" object. He says this is even written in the official report, and he tells it as one more case of strange objects shadowing American missile launches, which would mean something was watching them closely.
1964-nickel-found-in-drill-site: On a podcast episode about Skinwalker Ranch, a property in Utah known for reports of strange events, a speaker who says he was there describes how drilling on the ranch's mesa recently brought up a nickel dated 1964. He mentions a man named Chris Roberts. A coin turning up deep in a drill site is told as a puzzle about what lies under the ranch.
1970s-flanagan-samples-find-calcium-sulf: A researcher named Geoffrey Drumm says that samples taken in the 1970s by a man named Richard Flanagan, as described in engineer Christopher Dunn's book The Giza Power Plant, found calcium sulfate salt in the Queen's Chamber and Grand Gallery inside the Great Pyramid of Giza. Drumm says this salt comes from weak sulfuric acid reacting with the limestone walls, and he mentions pock marks he saw on recent tours. If he is right, the pyramid was a kind of chemical power plant rather than a tomb.
1970s-muon-scan-of-the-central-pyramid: A researcher named Jeffrey, speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast, says that in the 1970s scientists scanned the middle of the three big pyramids at Giza in Egypt using muons, tiny particles from space that pass through rock and can show hidden empty spaces. He says he has the paper, and that a scientist named Luis Alvarez was part of the work. According to Jeffrey, the team scanned the Belzoni chamber, a room inside the pyramid, and the area above it, and found nothing, which matters because people still look for hidden rooms in the pyramids.
1972-rand-very-high-speed-transit-system: A researcher known online as UAPGerb points the podcast host Jesse Michels to a 1972 study by RAND, a research organization that does work for the US government. He says it was a theoretical design for a "very high-speed transit system" that could move people across great distances in minutes. He brings it up as an example of advanced travel ideas that were already being studied decades ago.
197374-radar-station-crew-see-a-cigar-sh: A Swedish UFO researcher, Clas Svahn, says he interviewed six people who worked at a mountain radar station in the far north of Sweden. According to them, around 1973 or 1974 the crew saw a cigar-shaped object. If true, it would mean trained military staff watched something they could not explain.
1974-coyame-crash-and-cia-directed-retri: This story is about a crash said to have happened in 1974 near Coyame, in northern Mexico. A researcher who goes by UAPGerb says that, according to a document called the DEB report, the CIA, America's foreign spy agency, directed a plan to gather fast-response teams and equipment to go and recover the crashed craft. He admits there is not much supporting evidence, but calls the story disturbing if true. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, retells it from a report he says leaked in the 1990s. In his version, the object collided with something in mid-air, the whole Mexican team that reached it ended up dead, and US forces flew the object out. If true, it would mean the US secretly crossed a border to retrieve an unknown craft.
1974-film-ufos-past-present-and-future: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that by 1974 something seemed to shift, and a documentary called UFOs: Past, Present and Future was made, which he places after Blue Book, the US Air Force's UFO study of the 1950s and 60s, and the Condon Committee report, a government-funded scientific study of UFOs. In a later episode he adds that the film was produced by the TV writer Rod Serling, who he says was his father's godfather, and he calls it the leading UFO documentary of its time, a sign to him that Hollywood and officials were shaping how people saw UFOs.
1975-norad-report-of-ufos-over-malmstrom: Robert Salas, a former US Air Force officer, says there is a 1975 report from NORAD, the joint US and Canadian command that watches the skies over North America, describing UFO sightings over the missile sites of Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana, a base that held nuclear missiles. He cites it as an official record that unknown objects kept showing up over nuclear weapons.
1975-nuclear-base-incursions-cable-to-th: Marik von Rennenkampf, who writes about UFOs and government, told the podcast host Jesse Michels that people should read a 1975 cable, an official message sent to the Pentagon. He says it describes unknown objects intruding over US nuclear weapons bases that year, and he credits the researcher John Greenwald with bringing it to light. If true, it would show the military itself recording strange visits to its most sensitive sites.
1980-object-sank-in-a-northern-swedish-l: A Swedish UFO researcher, Clas Svahn, says that in 1980 an object landed and then sank in a lake called Damaya, in a national park in the far north of Sweden. He says his team has been to the lake and has radar readings showing that something is lying in the mud at the bottom. If true, a physical object from the event could still be there to recover.
1980s-physicists-wormhole-billiard-ball-: A writer on dreams and seeing the future, Eric Wargo, says that physicists in the 1980s became interested in wormholes, which are theoretical shortcuts through space and time. According to him, they worked out the maths of a billiard ball sent back through a wormhole to hit its own past self, and found the results stayed consistent without paradox. He tells it because, if true, information travelling back in time would not have to break the rules of physics.
1980s-shift-from-secrecy-to-flooding-the: Talking with a UFO historian, the podcast host Jesse Michels suggests that in the 1980s the US government changed how it dealt with UFOs. He says it moved away from simply keeping secrets and denying everything, and started to "flood the zone": filling public discussion with so much mixed information that the truth would be hard to pick out.
1980s-spinning-gyroscope-mass-loss-paper: A researcher named Dave Rossi says that after the late 1970s this kind of work went private, but some scientific papers still came out in the 1980s about spinning gyroscopes with electrical parts attached. According to Rossi, these papers, done in labs shielded from magnetism, reported that the spinning gyroscope lost some of its mass. If true, it would point to a way of weakening the pull of gravity.
1981-black-sea-exercise-sighting-cameras: The president of a Russian republic, speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast, says that in 1981, during military exercises on the Black Sea, several dozen unidentified craft flew right into the area, and people photographed them with ordinary cameras. According to the story, the cameras were then taken away and the witnesses had to sign pledges to keep it secret. If true, it would mean the Soviet military saw such craft and hid it.
1982-dream-of-2060-flying-cia-ufos-after: Rolf Mowatt-Larssen, a former senior officer of the CIA, the US foreign intelligence agency, tells a podcast host, Jesse Michels, about a dream he had in 1982. In it he was in the year 2060, in a place underground run by the CIA, travelling back and forth in UFOs through a world already wrecked by a great nuclear war in 2034. He tells it as a possible glimpse of the future, which he links to the idea of time travel.
1984-string-theory-takeover-the-only-gam: A mathematician and podcaster, Eric Weinstein, says that in 1984, after a mathematical breakthrough called the Green-Schwarz anomaly cancellation, the leading physicist Ed Witten steered the whole field of theoretical physics to bet everything on one idea, string theory. Weinstein tells it to argue that physics narrowed itself to a single path and stalled, which matters if new physics is the key to understanding unexplained craft.
1985-night-encounter-my-god-bugs: Whitley Strieber, a writer who described his experiences with strange beings in a book called Communion, says that one night in 1985 at his cabin in upstate New York he came face to face with them. He says his immediate thought was, "my god, bugs." He tells it as part of his account of contact with non-human beings.
1987-new-science-encyclopedia-diagram-of: This story is about Pioneer 10 and 11, two space probes sent toward the outer solar system. A researcher, Matt LaCroix, says that an encyclopedia from 1987, called the New Science Encyclopedia, has a diagram of what the probes found. According to him, it shows that scientists at the time thought there was an object about 50 billion miles away, which he describes as a dead companion star, and he credits Thomas Van Flandern and Robert Harrington. He comes back to it several times in the same podcast episode. At one point he dates the encyclopedia to 1983 instead and points to a label on the diagram reading equal gravitational pull. If true, it would mean a large hidden body in our solar system was once quietly noted and then forgotten.
1988-resume-to-teller-leads-to-eg-g-and-: Bob Lazar, a man who says he once worked on alien craft at a secret Nevada site called S-4, says that in 1988 in Las Vegas he decided to go back into science and sent his resume to Edward Teller, a famous physicist he had met once before, asking about a job. As the story goes, this led to work through EG&G, a defense contractor, and on to S-4. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, repeats the link in passing, calling it close to certain that Teller got Lazar the job, which would matter because it would tie Lazar to real defense work.
1988-saic-anti-gravity-study-for-edwards: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in 1988 SAIC (Science Applications International Corporation, a large defense contractor) was hired to study electric propulsion and anti-gravity, meaning ways to move a craft without ordinary engines, for Edwards Air Force Base in California. He mentions the names James Woodward and Ferris Williams in connection with it, and tells it as a sign that the military took such ideas seriously.
1990-air-force-low-voltage-vacuum-test-o: Townsend Brown was an American inventor who said that very high voltages could produce a pushing force, an idea known as the Biefeld-Brown effect. The podcast host Jesse Michels says that in 1990 the US Air Force tested this effect in a vacuum, but used only 19,000 volts, while Brown had worked with millions of volts. Michels tells it to argue that the test was too weak to settle whether Brown was right.
1990s-drilling-near-the-sphinx-overseen-: A researcher of ancient Egypt, Luke Caverns, says that in the 1990s there was drilling near the Sphinx, the great carved lion-bodied statue at Giza, to check whether a hidden chamber lay there. He says the work was overseen by the Egyptian archaeologist Zahi Hawass. He raises it because a chamber there could change what we think we know about the site.
1990s-magazine-expose-on-assets-moved-fr: An online UFO researcher who goes by UAPGerb, talking with podcast host Jesse Michels, remembers a big magazine story from the 1990s, which he thinks ran in Popular Science or Popular Mechanics, two American popular science magazines. He says it was an exposé on Area 51, a secret military test site in Nevada, and on how its equipment and projects might have been moved to a mysterious new site in Dugway, Utah, nicknamed 'Area 52'. If true, it would mean the most secret work had quietly moved somewhere else.
1990s-meeting-of-eg-g-head-greer-dick-d-: UAPGerb, an online UFO researcher, tells podcast host Jesse Michels about a meeting in the 1990s, passing on what a journalist named George Knapp told him. He says a meeting was set up between one of the heads of EG&G, a defense contractor, and Steven Greer, a campaigner for UFO disclosure, along with men named Dick D'Amato and Alfred O'Donnell, and that at this meeting UFOs were taken off the table as a subject. If true, it would suggest a contractor knew enough about UFOs to steer the talk away from them.
1991-azores-case: Steven Greer, a UFO researcher and campaigner for government openness, mentions to a podcast host, Jesse Michels, a 1991 case off the Azores, a group of islands in the Atlantic Ocean. He ties it to his book Disclosure: An Illustrated History but gives no more detail in the telling. He raises it as one more sighting he thinks belongs on the record.
1991-bob-lazar-video-on-gravity-wave-a-a: Eric Weinstein, a mathematician, tells podcast host Jesse Michels about a strange video from 1991 that fellow podcast host Joe Rogan pointed him to. In it, a man named Bob Lazar talks about two kinds of gravity he calls 'gravity wave A' and 'gravity wave B', and Weinstein says that at first he seemed to be talking nonsense. The story matters because, if Lazar's ideas hold up, he would have known physics he had no ordinary way to know.
1991-paper-on-technology-assisted-consci: A researcher named Steven Greer says that in 1991 he wrote a paper about using technology together with human consciousness to make contact with extraterrestrials, ideas also found in his writing titled Extraterrestrial Contact: The Evidence and Implications. He says the paper spread throughout the aerospace industry and the CIA, the US Central Intelligence Agency, and that this is part of what put him on their radar. If so, insiders were paying attention to his work from early on.
1991-radio-caller-underground-work-along: The podcast host Jesse Michels describes a call made in 1991 to a radio show in Las Vegas, Nevada. According to Michels, the caller said he had been hired through Reynolds Electronics, part of a company Michels calls EG, to run electrical lines 3,000 feet underground at a government test site. The caller also said that military staff down there worked side by side with beings that looked like aliens, which, if true, would mean the government is secretly working with non-human beings.
1992-torr-and-li-superconductor-paper: A researcher, Dave Rossi, points to a 1992 paper by two scientists at the University of Alabama in Huntsville, Douglas Torr and Ning Li, about superconductors, materials that carry electricity with no resistance. Rossi says the paper showed that a certain spinning property inside these materials lives in the gaps of the material's crystal structure, not in the paired electrons that carry the current. He tells it because, to him, it supports advanced physics ideas that could lead to new kinds of propulsion.
1994-air-force-holographic-projector-con: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in 1999 a reporter named William Arkin wrote about a 1994 US Air Force idea for a holographic projector, a device that could cast realistic images into the sky. Michels raises it because, if such a tool existed, some UFO sightings could be the military's own staged illusions.
1994-nellis-tonopah-range-video: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, talks about a 1994 video said to show unexplained objects over the Nellis and Tonopah ranges, restricted military testing grounds in Nevada. He points out that Nellis is famous and that the airspace is closed to the public. That matters because something odd filmed there would be hard to put down to ordinary air traffic.
1996-sighting-of-a-round-craft-over-the-: Dennis Asberg, a Swedish treasure hunter, says that one early summer morning in 1996, after waking unusually early for no reason he can explain, he saw a round craft over a military site outside Stockholm. He says that seen from one angle it looked like a hot dog, and he mentions UFO Sweden, a Swedish group that collects sighting reports. He tells it on Jesse Michels's podcast as his own unexplained encounter near a military base.
1997-contact-10-000-people-paid-10-milli: Steven Greer, a doctor who campaigns for the government to reveal what it knows about UFOs, says that in Washington in 1997 a contact told him that at least 10,000 people had each been paid $10 million or more to secure their cooperation with a secret effort. If true, it would mean silence about the subject had been bought on a huge scale.
1997-greer-briefing-with-admiral-wilson: An online researcher who goes by UAPGerb says that in 1997 a meeting took place in Washington, DC, between Steven Greer, a campaigner for UFO disclosure, Willard Miller, Admiral Thomas Wilson, a senior Navy officer, and Stephen Lovekin. He describes it as a briefing on the subject of UFOs. If true, it would mean a high-ranking officer was being told about secret UFO matters.
1997-unod-declaring-the-programs-illegal: Steven Greer, a campaigner who pushes for the government to reveal what it knows about UFOs, says that in 1997 he was involved in seeking a memo marked UNOD, short for "unless otherwise directed," that would declare the secret UFO programs illegal. He says he put a deadline of two or three months on it. If true, it would mean an official order was aimed at the secrecy itself.
1998-remote-viewing-of-the-world-s-futur: Lyn Buchanan, a former Army sergeant trained in remote viewing, a practice of trying to sense distant or hidden things with the mind alone, says that in 1998 he was given the task of viewing the future of the United States. He says the session turned into a view of the whole world's future, up through the year 2050, which if true would suggest the mind can see ahead in time.
1999-paper-when-disclosure-serves-secrec: Steven Greer, a campaigner who pushes for the government to reveal what it knows about UFOs, says that in 1999 he wrote a paper called "When Disclosure Serves Secrecy" and tells listeners to go look it up. He points to it to show he warned early, as the title suggests, that releasing information can itself be a way of keeping secrets.
19th-century-baron-trump-time-travel-boo: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, brings up a book called The Adventures of Baron Trump, which he says was written in the 19th century. He describes it as the story of a character named Baron Trump and his time-travelling adventures, alongside another figure he calls Dawn. Those who raise it see it as a possible hint that someone back then saw the future.
2-a-m-buzzing-and-knocks-in-florida-home: Peter Levenda, an author who writes about hidden history, says that years after an earlier strange encounter in Singapore, he was at home in Florida around 2 in the morning when he heard buzzing and knocking. He tells it alongside the experiences of Whitley Strieber, a writer known for describing visits from strange beings, as a sign that such contact can follow a person home.
20-second-ufo-sighting-the-same-day-2016: Brandon Fugal, the owner of Skinwalker Ranch, a Utah property known for reports of strange events, tells a podcast host, Jesse Michels, that one October day he and others had a dramatic UFO sighting right in front of them. He says it lasted about 20 seconds and happened on the same day as other events at the ranch. He tells it as proof that something unusual really goes on there.
200-mainstream-scientists-want-to-study-: Chris Bledsoe is a man who says he attracts UFOs. On a podcast he said that, in the 2020s, more than 200 mainstream scientists in the United States wanted to study the phenomenon, meaning the strange lights, craft and beings people report. He says a woman he calls Dr. Anna Brady-Estevez told him that number, and if it were true it would mean the subject has quietly drawn in serious science.
200-watchers-swear-an-oath-on-mount-herm: Tim Alberino, a researcher and filmmaker, retells a story from the Book of Enoch, an ancient religious text, and from Genesis 6, a chapter of the Bible. He says that in the days before the Great Flood, 200 heavenly beings called the Watchers came down on the summit of Mount Hermon, a mountain in the Middle East, and bound themselves together by an oath there. He tells it on Jesse Michels's podcast as the origin of the giants that, by his account, came after.
2003-nasa-patent-for-an-asymmetric-barre: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that NASA, the US space agency, holds a patent from around 2003 for an asymmetrical barrel-shaped capacitor, a device that stores electric charge, and he links it to the University of Alabama in Huntsville. He connects it to earlier work by people he names, including Larry Smalley and Townsend Brown. If true, it would suggest NASA has looked into electric ways of moving craft like those described in UFO reports.
2004-carrier-encounter-drop-from-81-000-: Charlie Foltz, who describes himself as a witness, retells what he was told about a 2004 encounter off the coast of California, near a US Navy aircraft carrier group. According to his account, a craft sat at about 81,000 feet, over 15 miles up, and when planes were sent toward it and it began to show on their instruments, it dropped to about 24 inches above the water in under a second. If true, it would describe a machine moving far beyond any known aircraft.
2006-raytheon-atflir-patent-and-gimbal-r: Mick West, a skeptic who analyzes UFO videos, tells podcast host Jesse Michels about a patent he believes is from 2006, filed by the defense company Raytheon for ATFLIR, a targeting camera pod carried on Navy fighter jets. He connects it to 'Gimbal', a Navy video in which an unidentified object seems to rotate, arguing the patent helps explain that rotation as something the camera itself does rather than the object.
2007-firestonewest-paper-on-the-younger-: Randall Carlson, a researcher of ancient catastrophes, tells podcast host Jesse Michels that in 2007 scientists Richard Firestone, Allan West and others, along with George Howard, put out a paper on the Younger Dryas, a sudden cold spell near the end of the last ice age. Carlson says the paper proposed exactly what he had been arguing: that a cosmic impact caused it. If true, it would mean a disaster from space reshaped the world early humans lived in.
2007-national-press-club-event-with-inte: James Fox, a documentary filmmaker who studies UFOs, says that in 2007 he and a journalist, Leslie Kean, put on an event at the National Press Club, a well-known venue for news events in Washington, D.C. According to Fox, it brought together officials and witnesses from several countries, including an Iranian air force pilot named Parviz Jafari, to speak publicly about what they had seen.
200k-funded-fifth-dimension-gravity-theo: John Brandenburg, a physicist, says an unnamed US government funder paid him about $200,000 to work on a theory of gravity involving a fifth dimension. He tells a podcast host, Jesse Michels, that when he handed in his report they thanked him, gave him his check and told him not to let the door hit him on the way out. He tells it to show how such ideas get paid for and then quietly dropped.
2011-irkutsk-mass-ufo-sighting: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in 2011 Russia's national television station, Channel One, aired a report on a mass UFO sighting in the Irkutsk region of southeastern Siberia. The report, he says, involved people named Nelly Stepanovna and Sergey Yazev, and he brings it up as a case where many people at once said they saw something unexplained.
2013-white-house-rumours-of-confirmation: A researcher named Jason Simosa tells podcast host Jesse Michels that the recent published journals of Jacques Vallée, a longtime UFO researcher, record rumors coming out of the White House early in 2013. According to Simosa, the rumors said officials were planning something called 'confirmation, not disclosure', which would mean admitting that UFOs are real without revealing everything behind them.
2016-trip-with-tyler-and-garry-nolan: Diana Pasulka, a religious studies professor who wrote a book called American Cosmic, says that in 2016 she went to see a certain technology with people whose names she had to disguise in the book, including one she called Tyler. She says one of them, a scientist named Garry Nolan, has since come forward under his own name. She tells it as a first-hand look at the hidden world of people studying UFO material.
2017-disclosure-as-a-managed-release-of-: A US congressman, Eric Burlison, says that the public release of UFO information in 2017 was a controlled move. In his view, officials were trying to separate out what they could share without giving away the country's best technology, which would mean the disclosure was carefully managed rather than complete.
2017-new-york-times-article-as-a-new-pro: Greg Bishop, a researcher and writer on UFOs, talks about a 2017 New York Times article by journalists Leslie Kean and Ralph Blumenthal that featured a former Pentagon official named Lou Elizondo. Bishop says that when he first read it, he saw it as the start of a new project that was using the UFO subject for some purpose. If he is right, the public wave of UFO news since then would be, at least partly, something someone set in motion on purpose.
2017-release-of-three-ufo-videos-to-the-: This story is about how three military videos of UFOs came to be made public in 2017 through the New York Times. The podcast host Jesse Michels says that Lou Elizondo, a Pentagon official who worked on UFO matters, tried to brief the Secretary of Defense, General Jim Mattis, about UFOs, but was blocked by officials in between. Michels says Elizondo and his friend Christopher Mellon, a former senior Pentagon intelligence official, then went off script and got the Pentagon to clear three UFO videos for release. Michels stresses that putting the videos in a trusted outlet like the New York Times is what made people take notice after decades of silence. A well-known skeptic, Michael Shermer, also brings it up on the same podcast, but frames it as the moment the government said UAPs, its newer word for UFOs, are real, which Elizondo then repeated. It is told because, if the videos show what is claimed, the US military had recorded objects it could not explain.
2017-revelations-of-osap-ufo-study-group: Talking with a Navy scientist who holds unusual patents, the podcast host Jesse Michels recalls that in 2017 it came out that the US government had groups studying UFOs. He links these groups to something he calls OSAP, which he presents as a government body behind that work, and gives no more detail. He brings it up as the moment official UFO research first became public.
2019-aiaa-scitech-presentation-slides-4-: A Navy scientist named Salvatore Pais, who holds patents on unusual propulsion ideas, says he gave a slide presentation in 2019 at AIAA SciTech, a major aerospace engineering conference. He tells listeners to look at slides 4 to 9 of that talk to understand his ideas, which he presents as pointing toward craft like those reported as UFOs.
2019-decision-with-corrado-malanga-to-sc: A scientist named Filippo Biondi says that in 2019 he and his friend Corrado Malanga decided to try to scan inside the Great Pyramid of Khufu in Giza, Egypt. In another telling he says the scan was done in 2020 using radar data from Italy's second-generation Cosmo-SkyMed satellites, and he cites a paper reporting hidden internal structures in the pyramid. If true, it would mean unknown chambers lie inside and beneath the pyramid.
2020-pan-starrs-object-turns-out-to-be-a: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in September 2020 Pan-STARRS, a telescope that scans the sky for moving objects, found another object in space that puzzled astronomers. According to his telling, it turned out to be an old rocket booster from a 1966 mission by NASA, the US space agency. He tells it as an example of how a baffling object can end up having a human origin.
2022-scans-finding-hidden-chambers-in-th: A podcast guest named Jay Anderson says that in 2022 scans were done of the Great Pyramid of Giza in Egypt. According to him, those scans found hidden chambers beneath the pyramid. If true, there would be unexplored spaces in one of the world's most studied monuments.
2023-marco-leal-interview-inconsistency-: A surgeon from Varginha, Brazil, named Italo Venturelli, speaking on a podcast about his hospital having operated on an alien, says differences in his 2023 interview with a man named Marco Leal came from not being able to tell everything back then. He says he later told a man named James Fox about an admission to the hospital's intensive care unit. He offers this to explain why his accounts have shifted over time.
2024-egyptian-japanese-radar-survey-find: The podcast host Jesse Michels says that in 2024 Egyptian and Japanese researchers scanned the ground of the western cemetery next to the Great Pyramid at Giza. According to Michels, they used ground-penetrating radar and electrical measurements that can map what lies underground without digging, and found an L-shaped structure beneath the surface. He tells it as a hint that there may be more hidden under Giza than people know.
2024-law-protecting-icig-whistleblowers-: Dylan Borland, a whistleblower who says a top government official told him aliens run everything, describes a 2024 law. He says that under it, people who bring secrets about the CIA or the Department of Energy, the agency that runs America's nuclear weapons work, to the ICIG, the internal watchdog office for US spy agencies, cannot be prosecuted for espionage. If so, it would give insiders a safe way to report hidden programmes.
2025-jfk-files-release-and-trump-s-answe: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, talks about the 2025 release of government files on the killing of President John F. Kennedy. He says that when President Donald Trump was asked directly who killed Kennedy, Trump only said they had released the files and done something historic, and Michels also mentions the commentator Bret Weinstein. To Michels, the answer suggests the full truth is still not out.
22-000-year-old-footprints-in-north-amer: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that the writer Graham Hancock, on his television series Ancient Apocalypse, shows human footprints in North America said to be about 22,000 years old. Michels raises it because, if the dating holds, people would have been on the continent far earlier than usually thought.
23-year-us-remote-viewing-program-1972: "Remote viewing" is the idea that a person can use only their mind to see places or things far away. The podcast host Jesse Michels says the US government ran a remote viewing program for 23 years, from 1972 to 1995, which in another episode he calls Stargate, run by the CIA, and links to Joseph McMoneagle, one of its viewers. Michels argues that if such a program existed for that long, secret versions of it are probably still running today.
30-missiles-lost-to-ufo-activity-1966-67: This story is about US nuclear missile bases in the 1960s. The claim is that between September 1966 and March 1967, the United States lost 30 missiles to UFO activity, meaning the weapons were put out of action while strange objects were reported nearby. Podcast host Jesse Michels tells it and credits a researcher named Bob Hastings and his book, UFOs and Nukes. Robert Salas, a former Air Force officer who was a guest on the show, tells the same figures in his own words. Salas names two Air Force bases, Minot in North Dakota and Malmstrom in Montana. The tellers raise it because, if true, something unknown was able to interfere with America's nuclear weapons.
36-people-who-say-they-flew-the-craft-uf: A UFO researcher named Grant Cameron says on Jesse Michels's podcast that he wrote a whole book, UFO Sky Pods, about 36 people who came to him, somewhat mysteriously, and each said they had flown one of the craft. If true, it would mean many ordinary people claim to have piloted these objects themselves.
3i-atlas-anomalous-composition-2025: A physicist who studies UFO reports, Kevin Knuth, talks about 3I/ATLAS, an object from outside our solar system that passed through it in 2025. He says its makeup is odd: it shows nickel without the iron that normally goes with it, a point he links to the Harvard astronomer Avi Loeb. If so, it would hint that the object is not a normal natural rock.
40-meter-metallic-object-in-the-labyrint: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says there is a metallic object about 40 meters long sitting in a vast corridor of an underground labyrinth in Egypt, and he calls it a UFO. His guest, the podcaster Joe Rogan, repeats it from a researcher named Ben van Kerkwyk and a scan report, adding that it is shaped like a Tic Tac, a white oval like the mint, while Michels later ties the labyrinth to the ancient writers Herodotus and Pliny the Elder, who described it long ago. If true, it would mean a craft has been lying hidden beneath Egypt.
40-people-told-icig-of-reverse-engineeri: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that around 40 people have reportedly gone to the Inspector General of the Intelligence Community, a watchdog office that takes complaints from spy agency staff, and said they worked in a program taking apart non-human craft to learn how they work. He argues you would have to be very strange to make that claim to such an office if it were not true. If true, it would mean a secret effort to copy alien technology.
4602nd-monthly-report-s-ufo-b-section-19: Scott Ramsay, a researcher who investigates claimed UFO crashes, describes the 4602nd, a US Air Force intelligence unit of the 1950s. He says the unit's monthly report had a section labelled UFO B, where it counted how many UFOs had been seen. If so, it would show the Air Force was tracking sightings as routine business at the time.
4602nd-squadron-history-on-reassuring-th: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, quotes the official history of the 4602nd Air Intelligence Service Squadron, a US Air Force intelligence unit of the 1950s that looked into UFO reports. According to him, the document describes the unit's job as "reassuring the public mind that no tangible evidence existed to support the fears of an invasion from outer space," which he presents as a sign the Air Force was managing public opinion as much as investigating.
4chan-whistleblower-a-decade-working-on-: A guest on Jesse Michels's podcast, Chris Ramsay, retells a post put up in early 2023 on 4chan, an anonymous online message board, by someone calling himself a whistleblower. According to Ramsay, the poster said he had spent about a decade, in the late 1990s and early 2000s, working on recovering crashed craft. If true, it would mean the US quietly runs a programme collecting crashed objects that are not ours.
4chan-whistleblower-fewer-bodies-found-i: Chris Ramsay, a guest on Jesse Michels's podcast, retells what an anonymous poster on 4chan, an online message board, wrote in early 2023 about working on crashed craft. According to Ramsay, the poster said they now find far fewer bodies inside the crashed craft than before, which would hint that whatever flies them has changed.
4chan-whistleblower-hamburger-shaped-mot: UAPGerb, an online UFO researcher, mentions to podcast host Jesse Michels a claim from an anonymous whistleblower who posted on 4chan, an anonymous online message board. According to that post, a large mothership shaped like a hamburger, which 3D prints UFOs to order, is kept somewhere in the Bahamas. UAPGerb offers it only with the caveat 'if that whistleblower is to be believed'.
4chan-whistleblower-higher-ups-think-the: Chris Ramsay, a guest on Jesse Michels's podcast, retells the claims of an anonymous self-described whistleblower who posted on 4chan, an online message board, in early 2023. According to Ramsay, the poster said the people in charge believe the visitors simply do not care about us, and treat Earth more like a zoo. If true, it would mean we are being watched, not engaged.
4chan-whistleblower-nukes-jets-and-boats: Chris Ramsay, a guest on Jesse Michels's podcast, retells what an anonymous poster on 4chan, an online message board, wrote in early 2023 about strange craft in the ocean near the Bahamas. According to Ramsay, the poster said the military had sent nuclear weapons on submarines, fighter jets and boats after these craft, and none of them came back. If true, it would mean these objects are far beyond anything our forces can handle.
4chan-whistleblower-orange-light-orbs-sc: Chris Ramsay, a guest on Jesse Michels's podcast, retells a 2023 post by an anonymous whistleblower on 4chan, an online message board. According to Ramsay, the poster said that orange lights in the sky are scanning for minerals or living things, and that if one comes up to you, you are likely to be, or already have been, taken by them.
4chan-whistleblower-underwater-mobile-co: Chris Ramsay, a guest on Jesse Michels's podcast, retells a 2023 post by an anonymous self-described whistleblower on 4chan, an online message board. According to Ramsay, the poster said his job was to monitor huge underwater machines, called mobile construction units, on the sea floor near the Bahamas and the Bermuda Triangle, which he said were building unidentified craft (UAP, the government's term for UFOs). If true, it would mean something is manufacturing these objects under our oceans.
536542-ad-darkness-and-cooling-linked-to: Randall Carlson, a researcher of ancient catastrophes, tells podcast host Jesse Michels that from 536 to 542 AD, records left by monks and others in Europe describe weeks and months when they could not see the sun. He ties this darkness and cooling to either volcanic eruptions or debris from a comet, an idea he links to the astronomer Fred Hoyle. If true, it would show how something from space could darken the whole sky within recorded history.
5412-committee-howard-hughes-and-the-s-f: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, repeats a story he has heard linking the 5412 Committee, a secret US government panel that approved covert operations in the 1950s, the billionaire Howard Hughes, and a covert team called the S-force to the killing of President John F. Kennedy. In this version, Kennedy fired Allen Dulles, head of the CIA, and an angry Dulles, together with the Wall Street bank Brown Brothers Harriman, put the S-force back to work to take Kennedy out. If true, it would mean parts of the US secret state turned on their own president.
60-minutes-whistleblower-told-to-turn-do: Eric Hazeline, described as a former director of the NSA, the US signals intelligence agency, recalls a segment on 60 Minutes, an American television news programme. He says a man who had quit his government job told the show that a woman came to him and said they had to turn down the temperature on the UFO issue, which would suggest officials were trying to quiet the subject down.
65-corrections-to-human-evolution-as-a-p: Bob Lazar says he worked around 1988 and 1989 at S-4, a secret site in the Nevada desert, where he was shown briefing papers. Speaking to a podcast host, Jesse Michels, he says that a man he calls Barry told him the papers stated that aliens had made 65 corrections to human evolution. If true, it would mean humans were shaped on purpose by visitors.
8-000-years-of-ceremonial-site-artifacts: Brandon Fugal owns Skinwalker Ranch, a property in Utah long tied to reports of strange lights and events. He says the ranch's archaeologist, Chris Roberts, has documented artifacts there going back more than 8,000 years, from what Fugal treats as a ceremonial site. If so, it would suggest people have treated the place as special for thousands of years.
9-11-as-a-diversion-from-disclosure-2001: A doctor who campaigns for the public release of UFO secrets, Steven Greer, says that the September 11, 2001 attacks on the United States came a few months after a push for disclosure, and happened as a direct consequence of it. If true, it would mean the attacks were tied to keeping these secrets hidden.
911-calls-from-the-facility-intercepted-: Jordan Jose, who says he was taken into a secret UFO-related programme as a child, tells a podcast host, Jesse Michels, about his time around 2008 to 2010 at Baker Victory Services, a children's facility in Western New York. He says that when children tried to get out or call 911, the US emergency number, from the school facility, the phone lines were being watched. If true, it would mean the place was secretly controlled by those running the programme.
98-of-classical-knowledge-lost: Jason Jorjani, a philosopher, tells podcast host Jesse Michels that we lost 98 percent of the knowledge of the ancient Greek and Roman world, a figure he says he got from the astronomer Carl Sagan. He connects it to places like the Library of Alexandria, the great ancient library in Egypt, and the Greek city of Corinth. If true, it would mean almost everything the ancients knew is gone.
a-1-40-scale-model-of-the-red-pyramid-ex: Geoffrey Drumm, a man with his own theory about what Egypt's pyramids were really for, told podcast host Jesse Michels that he and others built a model of the Red Pyramid, an ancient Egyptian pyramid, at one fortieth of its real size. He says the model blew apart completely because of the pressure that built up inside it. He tells it because, if true, it would suggest the pyramid was built to hold or produce pressure, like a machine, and was not only a tomb.
a-30-mile-perfectly-straight-edge-on-mar: A man named Joe McMoneagle says that photo negatives from mapping of Mars by the Jet Propulsion Laboratory, the NASA center that runs space probes, show a perfectly straight edge about 30 miles long. He says nature does not make an edge like that, so to him it is a sign that something built it, meaning Mars once had intelligent life.
a-bone-on-mars-in-a-jpl-negative: A man named Joe McMoneagle says that one of the Mars mapping negatives from the Jet Propulsion Laboratory, the NASA center that runs space probes, shows a bone lying on the surface of Mars. If so, it would mean Mars once had animal life.
a-chicago-teacher-s-students-talk-about-: Ky Dickens is a filmmaker behind a documentary series about nonspeaking children who are said to read minds. She says that around 2023 she met a teacher in Chicago whose students talked about something they called "the hill," which other children in her work had also described. If true, it would suggest children who had never met were sharing the same inner experience.
a-congressman-on-the-progress-of-reverse: An unnamed US congressman, asked about secret programmes said to be taking apart recovered non-human craft to copy them, says he believes such programmes exist. But he doubts they have managed to make the technology work, because if they had, he says, the US would own the skies.
a-dramatic-event-at-the-end-of-the-ice-a: A researcher of ancient history, Luke Caverns, says a dramatic event involving the North Atlantic ice cap brought the last Ice Age to a rapid end. He says it devastated North America and wiped out its giant animals, and he mentions an unnamed evolutionary biologist in support. If true, a sudden catastrophe, not slow change, would explain the end of that era.
a-female-gray-with-a-baby-gray-at-the-mo: Lyn Buchanan, a former Army sergeant trained in remote viewing, a practice of trying to sense distant places with the mind alone, says that he saw a base at Mount Zeil in Australia. There, he says, he saw a female gray, one of the small gray-skinned beings of many UFO accounts, with a baby gray, which if true would mean such beings raise families here.
a-few-dozen-uap-reports-are-real-some-kn: Eric Hazeline, presented on a podcast as a former director of the National Security Agency, America's electronic spying agency, says that out of the many thousands of reports of UAP, the government's term for unidentified objects in the sky, a few dozen are real. He says he has inside knowledge of some of them from his time in government, and ties the view to a book called The New Science of UFOs, citing a colleague named Chris Gilbert. If true, a top intelligence insider is vouching that some cases cannot be explained away.
a-founder-s-grandfather-saw-roswell-base: Podcast host Jesse Michels, talking with documentary maker James Fox, passes on a story from the unnamed founder of one of America's largest companies. The founder told him his grandfather served in the 9th Atomic Bomber Squadron at Roswell, New Mexico, in 1947, the place where a crashed object is said to have been recovered that year, and that he saw the people on the base visibly spooked. If true, it would be one more sign that something unusual happened at Roswell.
a-genetics-biologics-component-to-the-pr: Dylan Borland, a whistleblower, says there is a genetics part to the secret government programme that is said to recover and study non-human craft and bodies. He links this to David Grusch, a former intelligence officer who testified under oath to Congress about such programmes. If true, it would mean the programme handles living or once-living material, not just machines.
a-hidden-entity-picking-recruits-from-th: A man who goes by Jordan told podcast host Jesse Michels that he was taken into a secret UFO programme as a child. He says a hidden group, separate from the public one, works behind the scenes of GATE, a US school programme for gifted and talented children, to find people it has already picked out and pull them into secret programmes. If true, it would mean bright children are being quietly scouted for this work.
a-man-falls-from-a-hotel-window-on-teleg: Brent Friedman, a Hollywood screenwriter, told podcast host Jesse Michels about something he says he saw in the late 1970s on Telegraph Avenue in Berkeley, California. He says he looked up three storeys at a hotel, saw an open window with a curtain blowing, and realised someone had just jumped or fallen from it. He tells it as part of his own story about how he came to the subjects of Hollywood, the CIA and UFOs.
a-man-named-bernie-proposes-esp-as-a-sav: A documentary filmmaker, Ky Dickens, who made a film about telepathy in children, says a man named Bernie first came up with an idea about non-speaking autistic people. The idea is that ESP, meaning extrasensory perception or sensing things beyond the ordinary senses, might be one of the special savant skills some of them have. She also mentions a psychiatrist, Diane Powell, in connection with it.
a-member-of-congress-saw-a-ufo-come-out-: Lou Elizondo, a former Pentagon official who worked on UFO questions, tells podcast host Jesse Michels that when he goes to Congress, members sometimes pull him aside to share their own sightings. One told him he was fishing on a lake with his son when an object came up out of the water. If true, it would mean even lawmakers have seen these things firsthand.
a-mutual-friend-e-saw-a-rectangular-craf: Deep Prasad, a researcher who claims artificial intelligence is alien technology, speaks of a mutual friend he calls only "E." He says she is the only person he knows who has seen a rectangular craft, which he finds unusual, though he gives no time or place.
a-police-officer-s-report-of-seeing-a-de: Italo Venturelli is a surgeon in Varginha, a town in Brazil, where in 1996 people say a strange creature was captured and taken to a hospital. He says there is a report from a police officer who said he saw a dead being. If true, it would add an official witness to the claim that non-human bodies were found there.
a-reptilian-being-appears-in-barbara-lam: A guest on Jesse Michels's podcast, Dan Sheehan, retells something a woman named Barbara Lamb told him, mentioning the Harvard psychiatrist John Mack along the way. According to Sheehan, Lamb said that one afternoon she came in from her garden and found a reptile-like being standing in her house. If true, it would mean such beings can turn up in an ordinary home.
a-small-pentagon-group-dealt-with-the-ta: Charles Hall, who says he served as an Air Force weather observer on the Nellis and Indian Springs ranges in the Nevada desert in the 1960s, told podcast host Jesse Michels that he spent years around beings he calls the tall whites: tall, pale, non-human visitors living at a base there. He says only a tiny handful of people at the Pentagon, the US military's headquarters, knew about them and dealt with them, and that their base was treated like a foreign embassy. If true, it would mean the US government kept a quiet, diplomatic relationship with aliens.
a-space-kid-calls-the-nine-a-sandbox-197: A researcher named Greg tells podcast host Jesse Michels about the 1970s lab in Ossining, New York, where a group said they were in contact with 'the Nine', described as a council of alien intelligences. He passes on what one of the young people in that circle, known as the 'space kids', said: that the Nine was basically like a sandbox for us to play in. That would make the whole contact less a message from beyond and more a kind of playground.
a-traumatized-area-51-worker-saw-reptili: Jesse Michels, a podcast host, retells a story from a couple named Garrett and Nicole McNamara. According to them, they met a man who had worked at Area 51, a secret US Air Force base in the Nevada desert, or perhaps a friend of a friend, and he was deeply traumatized after seeing reptile-like beings in a basement there.
a-uap-class-attacks-with-microwave-weapo: James Valor, from a startup called Skywatcher that says it tries to call in UFOs, which officials now call UAP, short for unidentified anomalous phenomena, says that his team has run into different types of these objects in recent years. He says one type actually attacked them with microwave weapons and shut down their equipment, which if true would mean some of these objects are hostile.
a-uap-hits-the-team-with-an-energy-weapo: James Valor, from a startup called Skywatcher that says it tries to call in UFOs, which officials call UAP, for unidentified anomalous phenomena, says that during a field operation in 2025 an object struck his team with an energy weapon. According to Valor, it happened during a U-turn, before a team member could get away, which if true would mean these objects can and do fight back.
a-ufo-control-panel-inside-a-hangar: Lyn Buchanan, a former Army sergeant, says that in the late 1980s, about a year after an interview with the Defense Intelligence Agency, the military's intelligence service, he was taken through a metal hangar holding wreckage from a midair collision. There, he says, he passed a control panel he recognized at once as coming from a UFO, one he says he had seen and operated before, which if true would mean the military held pieces of such craft.
a-voice-yelling-freeze-saves-him-before-: Joe McMoneagle, a former Army soldier later known as a psychic in a government programme that tested remote viewing (trying to see distant places with the mind), told podcast host Jesse Michels about a moment at a fire base called Two Bits during the Vietnam War. He says that as he walked down the steps into a bunker he heard someone yell "freeze," stopped, looked around, and the whole bunker was vaporised by a blast. He tells it as an early sign that something beyond ordinary senses was guiding him.
a-witness-saw-the-craft-over-the-hospita: James Fox, a documentary filmmaker, has looked into events in Varginha, Brazil in 1996, when people there say a strange craft came down and a being was found. Fox says he recently met another witness who told him the craft was out over the town's hospital, which would link the craft directly to the place where the being was said to have been taken.
aaro-appointed-to-head-a-space-tiger-tea: An unnamed researcher, speaking on a podcast, says that AARO, the Pentagon's current office for investigating unexplained objects, was put in charge of a special task team, a so-called tiger team, to study such objects in space around 2024 or 2025. If so, it would mean the government is now formally looking beyond the skies to space itself.
aaro-asks-hastings-to-bring-in-nuclear-s: Robert Hastings, a researcher who gathers accounts from military veterans of UFOs at nuclear weapons sites, says that in 2023 he was contacted by Kurt McConnell, a retired investigator for the Senate committee that oversees the armed forces. According to Hastings, McConnell said that AARO, the Pentagon office set up to look into unexplained sightings, wanted him to gather some of those veterans for interviews, which would mean the government was taking their stories seriously.
aaro-briefing-ai-quantum-and-the-grusch-: A guest named Matthew Pines, speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast in 2024, says that around 2023 someone in a briefing tied to AARO, the Pentagon's office for looking into unidentified objects, summed up the big picture as "a triangle: AI, quantum, and the Grusch stuff". That means artificial intelligence, quantum technology, and the claims of David Grusch, a witness who says he testified under oath about secret programmes that hold recovered craft. If true, it would suggest that insiders see the three as linked, though when Michels repeated the remark later he said it came from a CIA man rather than from a briefing.
aaro-did-not-record-the-veterans-intervi: Robert Hastings, a researcher who gathers accounts of UFOs seen at nuclear weapons bases, says that around 2023 he brought veterans of those sites to AARO, the Pentagon's office for looking into unidentified objects. According to Hastings, the AARO staff who took the veterans' testimony did not record it, which, if true, would mean the accounts may never have been properly preserved.
aaro-director-s-true-anomalies-2024: A podcast guest named Merrick says that Jon Kosloski, the new director of AARO, the Pentagon's office for looking into unidentified objects, has said the Pentagon has what he called "true anomalies", cases that leave them stumped. If true, it would mean the government's own UFO office admits to sightings it cannot explain.
aaro-director-says-aaro-works-with-uarcs: An online researcher who goes by UAPGerb says that in 2024 the new director of AARO, the Pentagon office that looks into unexplained objects in the sky, spoke at a Senate hearing in Washington. According to him, the director, Jon Kosloski, said AARO works with both UARCs, which are university research centres tied to the military, and FFRDCs, which are private labs funded by the government. If true, it would mean outside research groups play a part in the government's UFO work.
aaro-fishes-for-the-program-name-and-the: Dylan Borland, a former Air Force intelligence specialist who has come forward with UFO claims, told podcast host Jesse Michels about his 2023 dealings with AARO, the Pentagon office now tasked with investigating unexplained objects in the sky. He says AARO wanted him to name the people he knew working on a secret programme and to give the programme's name, and that he refused. He tells it because, in his view, the office was more interested in finding the people involved than in revealing what they knew.
aaro-found-som-1-01-crash-packaging-manu: An online researcher who goes by UAPGerb says that AARO, the Pentagon office set up to look into unidentified flying objects, found a manual called SOM 1-01. Passing on what he says he heard from Tim Phillips and from Sean Kirkpatrick, who once led that office, he says the manual explains how to package and unpack debris, craft and bodies from the crash of an extraterrestrial vehicle. If true, it would mean someone wrote down procedures for handling alien crashes.
aaro-head-john-kosloski-came-from-the-ns: A podcast host named Jesse Michels says that the current head of AARO, a Pentagon office set up to look into reports of unidentified objects in the sky, is a man named John Kosloski who came from the NSA, the US National Security Agency, which intercepts and analyses communications. Michels calls him a former NSA director. He points this out because, if true, it would mean the office studying UFOs is led by someone from the world of secret signals intelligence.
aaro-hired-sancorp-2020: An online researcher who goes by UAPGerb says that AARO, the Pentagon's current office for investigating unexplained objects, hired a company called SANCorp, which he says specializes in guarding against insider threats and whistleblower leaks. He adds that a man named Tim Phillips said on a podcast that SANCorp was hired to connect the office with experts. If true, it would suggest the office was as focused on stopping leaks as on gathering facts.
aaro-historical-report-misstated-michael: An online researcher who goes by UAPGerb says that a 2024 report from AARO, the Pentagon office set up to look into unidentified flying objects, got a witness's story wrong. The report was the first volume of the office's history of the subject, and he says it misstated the testimony of a man named Michael Herrera, pointing to Herrera's own written account as proof. If true, it would mean the official review twisted what witnesses said.
aaro-leadership-change-from-kirkpatrick-: A podcast host named Jesse Michels, talking in 2024 with a guest named Ryan Graves, says that AARO, a Pentagon office set up to look into reports of unidentified objects in the sky, had just changed leaders. According to Michels, the office passed from a director named Kirkpatrick to a new head, a man named Kosloski, whose name Graves had told him. He raises it because a change at the top could change how the government handles UFO reports.
aaro-resolution-of-aguadilla-video-2013: A well-known analyst of UFO videos, Mick West, points to the Aguadilla video, heat-camera footage from 2013 of an object near the airport at Aguadilla, Puerto Rico. He says AARO, the Pentagon's current office for investigating unexplained objects, did resolve that older case. He raises it to show the office has explained famous videos.
aaro-s-latin-motto-2022: A former Pentagon official, Matthew Brown, talks about the Latin motto of AARO, the Pentagon's current office for investigating unexplained objects, set up in 2022. He says, while admitting he may have it wrong, that it translates to something like 'the universe is what our thoughts make of it.' He finds it telling, as if the office hints at a link between mind and reality.
aaro-s-mfr-marks-borland-s-triangle-sigh: Dylan Borland, a former Air Force member, says that in 2023 he gave testimony to AARO, a Pentagon office set up to look into reports of unexplained objects, and that they wrote up a memorandum for record, an official written summary of his account. He says the summary listed his sighting of a triangle-shaped craft as unclassified, but classified his other drawings of technologies of unknown origin, moving them into a special access program, a tightly restricted secret project. He takes that split as proof that the government considers what he saw real and sensitive.
