aaro-says-go-fast-is-possibly-parallax-2: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, discusses Go Fast, a 2015 Navy video filmed off Jacksonville, Florida, that seems to show a small object racing low over the ocean. He says AARO, the Pentagon office set up to investigate unexplained objects, has said the speed is possibly parallax, an illusion where the camera's own movement makes a slow object look fast. That would mean the object may not be as remarkable as it appears.
aaro-scif-briefing-showing-only-resolved: A congressman named Eric Burles says that in 2023 in Washington he attended a briefing in a SCIF, a secure room for classified information, given by AARO, the Pentagon office that looks into unexplained sightings, with officials including Sean Kirkpatrick and John Kosowski. He says it was just a slideshow of solved cases, each one explained, such as a balloon, which to him suggested lawmakers were not being shown the cases that matter.
aaro-sends-odni-a-false-mfr-2023: A man named Dylan Borland says that sometime between 2023 and 2025, AARO, the Pentagon office that looks into UFO reports, sent a false memorandum for record, a formal written note of a meeting, to the Office of the Director of National Intelligence, which oversees US spy agencies. He says that when he went to that office on September 10, 2025, a man named Jon Kosloski was listed as AARO's director. He tells it as a sign that the UFO office misled other officials.
aaro-staffing-1-600-cases-and-a-baffled-: On a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, a guest named Merrick von Renenamp talks about AARO, the Pentagon office set up to look into reports of unexplained objects in the sky and elsewhere. He says that around 2024 the office had about three or four dozen staff, and that he had just heard it had reached "full operational capability", meaning it was fully up and running, and he credits a man named Jon Kosloski for this. It matters because the size of the office suggests how seriously the government takes these reports.
aaro-told-the-wsj-the-shutdown-was-an-em: Robert Salas, a former US Air Force officer who says he saw nuclear missiles shut down during a UFO sighting in 1967, says that in 2025 AARO, the Pentagon office that now investigates UFO reports, gave Joel Schectman, a Wall Street Journal reporter, an explanation that the shutdown was some kind of EMP test, meaning a test of an electromagnetic pulse that can knock out electronics. Salas links this to Sean Kirkpatrick, a former head of that office, and disputes it, since it would explain away his account.
aaro-under-kirkpatrick-as-a-fly-trap-for: A podcast host named Jesse Michels argues that the first version of AARO, a Pentagon office set up in 2022 to look into reports of unidentified objects in the sky, was run by a director named Sean Kirkpatrick as a "fly trap" for UFO information. In his telling, the office drew in reports and witnesses so the information could be caught and held rather than shared, and it probably had ties to older secret programs. If true, it would mean the office meant to bring things into the open was doing the opposite.
aaro-undercut-by-cia-and-air-force-figur: A writer on national security, Matthew Pines, says that once US government work on unexplained sightings moved into AARO, a Pentagon office set up to look into such reports, it was compromised by people from the CIA, the US spy agency, and from the Air Force, such as Sean Kirkpatrick, who ran the office. A filmmaker and journalist, Jeremy Corbell, goes further. He says AARO worked as counterintelligence against the American public, acting like a honey trap that drew in whistleblowers and then harassed them, and he credits sources including the journalist George Knapp. If true, it would mean the office meant to find answers was built to hide them.
aaron-paul-wrote-messages-back-and-forth: Flying Lotus, a hip hop artist and music producer, says his friend Aaron Paul, an actor, traded messages with Bob Lazar around 2023. Lazar is known for saying he once worked on alien craft at a secret site in Nevada. Flying Lotus tells it as a sign of how far Paul has gone into the subject.
aatip-as-part-of-a-government-disclosure: Jake Barber, a man who says he once carried a UFO with his helicopter, says that as recently as 2015 and 2016 AATIP, a small Pentagon office that studied unexplained aerial reports, was part of a wider government effort to slowly make public what it knows about UFOs. If true, it would mean that office was not only studying sightings but helping prepare the public.
aatip-modeled-uap-using-general-relativi: Hal Puthoff, a scientist described as a CIA expert on UFOs, says that from about 2007 to 2012 he worked with AATIP, a small Pentagon office that studied unexplained aerial reports, and that the best the team could do was take Einstein's general relativity, the theory that treats space and time as a fabric that can bend, as the working theory for how these objects, called UAP or unidentified anomalous phenomena, might move. Lou Elizondo, a former Pentagon official who says he was part of that office, credits Puthoff and goes further, saying that bending space and time this way was not just a possibility but the core theory they worked from. If true, it would mean the government seriously considered that these craft travel by warping space itself.
aatip-oap-and-the-uap-task-force-as-red-: A man named Dylan Borland describes a theory that several US government UFO efforts from about 2007 to 2021 were really red teams, groups set up to test something from the outside. These were AATIP, a small Pentagon office that studied unexplained aerial reports, a related effort called OAP, and the UAP Task Force, a later military group studying unidentified objects, and he says they were testing a secret long-running "legacy program" and mentions research papers called DIRDs. If true, the public UFO offices were cover for something bigger.
aatip-study-of-260-000-cases-and-a-possi: Jason Simosa, a researcher, says that between about 2007 and 2013 a government UFO study, run through the Defense Intelligence Agency, a military spy agency, and Bigelow Aerospace, a private space company, looked at 260,000 cases with seven levels of analysis, which he calls probably the biggest study of UFO data ever. He says that Jacques Vallee, a longtime UFO researcher, hints two or three times in his private journals that one conclusion was that an existential threat to humanity may have been detected.
aatip-the-dod-s-ufo-program-and-its-22-m: Podcast host Jesse Michels has described, across several episodes, the US military's main UFO study of recent years, called AATIP, the Advanced Aerospace Threat Identification Program, a small Pentagon office that studied unexplained aerial reports. He says it had a $22 million budget, that it began around 2007 under a push from Senator Harry Reid, and that it was run through Bigelow Aerospace, a private space company, before the New York Times, with journalist Leslie Kean, revealed it in December 2017. If true, it would mean the government was quietly treating UFOs as a real subject for years.
aawsap-idea-of-baiting-ufos-with-nuclear: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Lue Elizondo, a former Pentagon official turned whistleblower, writes in his book about AAWSAP, a Pentagon-funded program that studied UFOs. According to Michels, Elizondo says the program considered luring UFOs with nuclear material, which would suggest officials believed these objects are drawn to nuclear sites.
aawsap-set-up-to-take-a-lockheed-held-uf: AAWSAP was a Pentagon-funded study of unexplained phenomena, run through the Defense Intelligence Agency with Bigelow Aerospace, a company in Las Vegas. The podcast host Jesse Michels says it was set up so that a UFO held by the aerospace company Lockheed Martin could be moved into a special access program, a tightly restricted secret program, so that outside civilian scientists could study it. If true, a private contractor has been holding a craft that was never shown to outsiders. Michels names Jim Ryder, a vice president at a Lockheed Martin space technology centre, as the man involved in the handover, and says the craft was collected in the 1950s. He says a CIA official, Glenn Gaffney, was the gatekeeper and blocked the transfer, citing an article by a writer named Chris Sharp. A physicist, Eric Davis, says Gaffney was hostile to the company releasing its collection of crash-retrieval material, kept since before a program shut down in 1989, though he doesn't name the company. Ross Coulthart ties the story to a 2017 New York Times article by Leslie Kean and Ralph Blumenthal and suggests the craft may come from a crash in Kingman in 1953.
aawsap-to-aatip-to-elizondo-to-new-york-: On Jesse Michels's podcast, a guest named Merrick says there is a direct chain that runs from AAWSAP, a Pentagon-funded study of unexplained phenomena that began around 2007, to AATIP, a small Pentagon office that studied unexplained aerial reports, then to a man named Lou Elizondo, and finally to the New York Times newspaper, which reported on it in 2017. In his telling, this chain is the path by which the government's quiet interest in UFOs reached the public.
abandoned-radar-base-found-near-alvado-1: Scott Ramsay, a researcher looking into a claimed 1940s UFO crash in New Mexico, told podcast host Jesse Michels that in 1999 he and others went searching high peaks across the area, out toward Santa Fe, for old radar bases. He says they found one on a mountain near Alvado, hiked up through about two feet of snow, and found it just as it had been left in 1957, and he connects it to the Atomic Energy Commission, the US agency that once ran nuclear work. He tells it because such radar sites could have tracked a crashing craft.
abductee-carol-s-missing-pregnancy-and-h: On a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, a guest named Dan Sheehan passes on the story of a woman named Carol, who says she was taken from her home aboard a craft by non-human beings in the 1990s. Sheehan says she had been studied by a researcher named John Mack, and that she was furious at the people who study UFOs, which are unexplained flying objects. As the story goes, she lost a pregnancy without explanation and came to believe she had a daughter who was part human and part alien. If true, it would mean that beings are making children with people.
abductee-friend-grabs-a-gray-by-the-neck: A researcher named Tim Alberino, speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast, tells of a friend of his who says she has been taken by non-human beings more than once. He says that during one of these experiences she grabbed a gray, the small grey-skinned being common in these accounts, by the neck and squeezed it before she passed out. If true, it would mean the beings are physical enough to be grabbed and fought.
abductees-tell-alberino-of-a-forced-hybr: Tim Alberino, a researcher speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast, says that people who report being taken by non-human beings have told him they are being made part of a breeding programme against their will. In his telling, the aim is to produce beings that are part human and part something else. If true, it would mean people are being used, without consent, to make a new kind of being.
abductees-whose-memories-come-back-when-: Jesse Michels, a podcast host, says that some people who believe they were taken by non-human beings get their memories back when they see the cover of Communion, a book by the writer Whitley Strieber about his own such experiences. If true, it would suggest that real but buried memories can be triggered by a single image.
abduction-and-implant-prevalence-estimat: On a Jesse Michels podcast episode about a scientist who studies what people call alien implants, small objects said to be placed in human bodies by non-human beings, a guest named Steve Coburn gives a number. He says that, according to a doctor he calls Dr. L, named as Roger Leer, about 3 percent of Americans have been taken by these beings, and some of them were given implants. If true, it would mean millions of people have been affected.
abduction-memory-returns-25-years-later-: Lyn Buchanan, a former Army sergeant who worked in a remote viewing unit, a military team trained to try to see distant places and events with the mind, says that in the late 1980s, about 25 years after he was abducted, something a woman said made the whole memory come flooding back at his home. He says the account was then checked by remote viewers in his unit, which, if true, would mean the military's own psychic spies looked into an abduction.
abduction-phenomenon-shatters-the-wester: A psychiatrist who studied people reporting alien abductions, John Mack, says the one thing the Western mind cannot accept is something from the spirit world crossing over into the physical world. He argues that this is exactly what is happening in abduction reports. That, he says, is why these experiences have such power to shatter people's beliefs.
aborymon-the-enochian-angel-in-john-dee-: Matthew Brown, a guest described on the podcast as a Pentagon whistleblower, talks about Aborymon, an angel from the "Enochian" angel lore recorded by John Dee, a scholar at Queen Elizabeth I's court in 16th century England. Brown says this angel was recently discovered in the Sigillum Dei Aemeth, a magical seal Dee used, which he brings up as part of a long history of people claiming contact with non-human beings.
abraham-dines-with-angelic-beings: Tim Alberino, a researcher speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast, points to a story in Genesis, the first book of the Bible. He says that at a place called Mamre, in the ancient land of Canaan, the patriarch Abraham met a group of angelic beings and sat down to dinner with them. He tells it as a sign that non-human beings have met with people in physical form since ancient times.
abramelin-the-hermit-of-luxor-in-the-boo: Matthew Brown, a guest described on the podcast as a Pentagon whistleblower, talks about The Book of Abramelin, an old book of magic. He describes Abramelin, the figure at its centre, as essentially a desert hermit living in Egypt around Luxor, and brings him up as part of an older tradition of contacting non-human beings.
ac-gravity-llc-wins-a-dod-contract-and-l: A podcast host named Jesse Michels tells of a researcher named Ning Li, who worked in Huntsville, Alabama, on ideas about controlling gravity. He says that after she formed a company called AC Gravity LLC with a partner named Larry Smalley, they at once won a contract from the DoD, the US Department of Defense, and then Li went quiet. Michels tells it because, if true, it would suggest the military took antigravity research seriously enough to fund it and then keep it out of sight.
acacia-as-the-tree-of-life-in-egypt-free: A podcast host named Jesse Michels, talking with a guest named Graham Hancock, describes how the acacia tree keeps showing up in sacred traditions. He says that in ancient Egypt the acacia was the Tree of Life, that the acacia leaf plays a prominent role in Freemasonry, a centuries-old fraternal society with its own secret symbols, and that the Ark of the Covenant, the sacred chest described in the Bible, was made of acacia wood. He raises it as a thread that might link these old traditions to a shared source.
account-of-a-tic-tac-type-craft-over-pen: Steven Greer is a researcher who leads the Disclosure Project, a group pushing governments to reveal what they know about UFOs. He says one of his books has a very good account of a sighting over Pennsylvania in 1967 of a craft like the Tic Tac, a white oval object shaped like the mint that later became famous. In one telling he names the book as Disclosure: An Illustrated History and does not mention the shape. If true, it would mean such objects were seen decades before they became famous.
acquaintances-say-puharich-was-mossad-19: A researcher named Greg says that several people who knew Andrija Puharich, a scientist who claimed contact with an alien council, kept quiet until late in their lives and then told him Puharich worked for Mossad, Israel's foreign intelligence service, in the 1970s. If true, it would tie Puharich's contact work to a foreign spy agency.
acquiring-william-corliss-s-sourcebook-p: A researcher named Clas Svahn tells how, after the death of an American writer named William Corliss, he got hold of Corliss's papers and brought them from the United States to Sweden. Corliss, Svahn says, wrote a series of books called the Sourcebook Project, which gathered strange and unexplained reports, so his files would matter to anyone hunting for old evidence of unexplained things.
active-military-personnel-bring-uap-vide: Eric Burlison, a member of the US Congress, says that sometime between 2023 and 2026, people on active military duty came to him in his Washington office and showed him videos of UAP, short for unidentified anomalous phenomena, the official term for UFOs. If true, it would mean serving troops are going around their chain of command to get such footage in front of lawmakers.
actuators-pulled-out-of-portals: A UFO researcher named Grant Cameron, speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast, passes on what he says he heard from people he names as Ron Pandolfi, Dan Smith and a man called John Sillison. In his telling, there are actuators, parts that make a machine move, which are pulled out of what he calls portals. If true, it would mean someone is retrieving working technology from some other place.
adam-and-eve-as-a-memory-of-genetic-mani: Joe Rogan, a well-known podcast host, tells another host, Jesse Michels, how he reads the Bible's story of the first humans, Adam and Eve. He says he assumes it is a memory of someone changing human genes. If true, it would mean humans were shaped on purpose by some other intelligence.
adamski-photos-unanalyzed-diaries-read-b: A researcher named Clas Svahn, speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast, talks about George Adamski, a man known in the 1950s for photos he said showed craft from elsewhere. Svahn says those photos have never been properly analysed, and that diaries Adamski wrote have been read by a man named Glenn Steckling. If true, both could still hold answers about what Adamski saw.
adamski-s-contact-with-a-man-from-mars-1: A philosopher named Jason Jorjani, speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast, recalls a man from the 1950s named George Adamski. Jorjani says Adamski claimed a being he met told him he came from Mars. Jorjani brings it up as one of the early contact stories in which visitors said they were from nearby planets.
adamski-s-martian-and-venusian-nordic-so: Jason Jorjani, a philosopher, describes the claims of George Adamski, a man in 1950s America who said he met human-looking beings from space. According to Jorjani, Adamski said these beings came from Mars and Venus, lived across the whole solar system, and were far more enlightened than us, which Jorjani raises when arguing that such beings may have shaped human religion.
admiral-meeting-at-a-cemetery-at-midnigh: Brent Friedman, a Hollywood screenwriter, told podcast host Jesse Michels that in 1996 a contact he calls JC set up a secret meeting with a Navy admiral near Long Beach Harbor in California. He says he was told the admiral would leave his ship with a cover story of visiting a dead friend, and that Friedman should meet him at a cemetery at midnight. He tells it as part of his account of insiders quietly passing UFO information to people in Hollywood.
admiral-richard-byrd-antarctica-stories: Richard Byrd was a US Navy admiral famous for exploring Antarctica. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, brings him up while talking about stories tied to the frozen continent. A retired Navy admiral named Tim Gallaudet repeats it second hand, crediting a woman named Becky Schott: he says someone thought Byrd had some kind of encounter while he was down there in the 1940s. People tell it because it would mean something strange was met in Antarctica long ago.
admiral-wilson-returns-to-close-out-a-pr: Eric Davis, a physicist who has done scientific work for the Pentagon, says that sometime between 1997 and 2002 in Las Vegas, a Navy admiral named Thomas Wilson told him he was back because he had to go up to close out a project. Davis says Wilson would not say Area 51, the secret military test site in the Nevada desert, but that he knew that was what Wilson meant, a story that also involves a man named John Alexander. If true, it would point to a hidden project at that base that a senior admiral was personally winding down.
advanced-lost-civilization-and-ancient-e: Joe Rogan, a well-known podcast host, says he belongs to the school of Randall Carlson and Graham Hancock, writers who argue that an advanced human civilisation existed and was lost long before recorded history. Rogan says he does not think this is humanity's first time around, and that ancient Egypt is a great testament to that.
advanced-theoretical-physics-group-study: From the 1980s onward, the story goes, a quiet circle called the Advanced Theoretical Physics group, or ATP group, met to think about how UFOs might work. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says a figure in his story joined it, and links it to the physicist Hal Puthoff, John Alexander and Eric Davis. A researcher who goes by UAPGerb says the group met at a defence contractor called BDM in McLean, Virginia, and credits Puthoff and a man named Kit Green. If true, it would mean insiders were studying UFO physics in an organised way for decades.
aec-official-tests-the-device-on-himself: A researcher named Greg Malatzi, drawing on letters from the Atomic Energy Commission, the US agency that oversaw nuclear matters, and the work of the writer Annie Jacobsen, describes a device being shown at Intelectron, a company in New York City, around 1962 and 1963. He says one official did not believe the device worked, asked to be tested, tried it on himself, and it worked.
aerial-battles-over-basel-and-nuremberg: A philosopher, Jason Jorjani, says that long ago huge UFO battles were seen in the skies over European cities such as Basel in Switzerland and Nuremberg in Germany. He says they were recorded in broadsheets, the printed news sheets of the time, and draws on a book called Wonders in the Sky by a researcher named Jacques Vallee. If true, it would mean people have been seeing strange craft for centuries.
aerial-survey-record-altered-or-missing-: A man who speaks as the owner of Skinwalker Ranch, a ranch in Utah, says that the photos taken of the property from the air are mostly missing for the years 1964 to 1969. In his words, that stretch of the aerial record has been "deleted," and he mentions people named Dr. Taylor and Eric Barter in telling it. He raises it because, if true, it would suggest that someone wanted those years of the land hidden, on a ranch where he believes something unusual lies underground.
aerial-view-shows-replanted-trees-in-lin: A researcher named Scott Ramsay studies the story of a craft said to have crashed in 1948 in Hart Canyon, near Aztec, New Mexico. He says that he later got to see an aerial view of the site, and that from above you can see trees growing in neat lines, as if they had been replanted. He tells it because, if true, someone would have reworked the land after the crash.
aerospace-companies-ask-for-pasulka-s-an: Diana Pasulka, a university scholar of religion who has studied accounts of angels, says that from about 2012 onward she received many requests, not just one, from people at aerospace companies who wanted her data. If true, it would mean companies that build aircraft and spacecraft see something useful in reports of angelic encounters.
aerospace-companies-seek-patent-rights-o: A researcher named Dan Sheehan, speaking in 2024 on the podcast of host Jesse Michels, says that around 2023 big American aerospace companies wanted patent rights, meaning legal ownership, over technology connected to UFOs. In his telling, the companies wanted a law that would let them keep that technology for themselves for a very long time, "the next thousand years", rather than have it shared with the public. If true, it would mean private firms were working to own whatever the government holds.
aerospace-company-s-government-customers: Eric Davis, who worked on AAWSAP, a Pentagon-funded study of UFOs in the late 2000s, says an aerospace company he dealt with often during that time told him it went to its government customer about the programme. He says that customer was not always the CIA, the US spy agency, but at times the Air Force, which, if true, would mean several agencies were involved.
aerospace-corp-executives-questioned-in-: A congressman named Eric Burles says that around 2023 to 2024, through his role on a congressional oversight committee, he sent a letter to Aerospace Corp, a company that does space work for the government, asking them to come answer questions. He says they sent two people from their executive team to be questioned in a SCIF, a sealed room in Washington used for discussing classified matters. According to him, the executives knew nothing, which matters because lawmakers were trying to find out whether such companies hold secrets about UFOs.
aerospace-corporations-hold-uap-knowledg: A physicist named Hal Puthoff, who has worked on government research projects, says private aerospace companies hold knowledge about UAP, the official term for unidentified flying objects. He says that knowledge is kept out of reach of FOIA, a US law that lets anyone request government records, because it counts as company property, and that the system was deliberately set up that way.
aerospace-employee-with-an-object-moving: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says he knows of a person working at one of the big aerospace companies who has had something moving inside their body for several years. He says he will not give the name to keep the person out of trouble. He tells it as a possible sign of a strange encounter that left a physical trace.
afib-after-the-hypnosis-session: Mario Woods, a former guard at a nuclear weapons site who says he was abducted by a UFO, told podcast host Jesse Michels about a hypnosis session in Georgia meant to bring back his memories of the event. He says that when the hypnotist, Robert Upson (also named as Bob Upton), finished, something was wrong with him, and he developed AFib, an irregular heartbeat. He tells it as a sign that the memories, or the experience itself, took a real physical toll.
afosi-agent-has-crew-sign-non-disclosure: Robert Salas, a former US Air Force officer, says that in March 1967, in the squadron commander's office at Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana, he was introduced to a man from the Air Force Office of Special Investigations, the Air Force's own investigative branch. Salas says the agent had the missile crew sign a non-disclosure agreement, a pledge not to talk about what had happened. If true, it would show the incident was treated as a secret from the start.
afosi-confiscates-footage-and-swears-mis: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, citing a former Air Force officer named Bob Jacobs, says that from the 1960s on, the men who guarded and ran US nuclear missiles kept seeing UFOs near nuclear sites. He says that every time, the Air Force Office of Special Investigations, the Air Force's own detective service, showed up to take any film and swear the men to secrecy. If true, it would mean the military knew about the sightings and worked to hide them.
afosi-founding-director-a-devout-catholi: On Jesse Michels's podcast, a guest named Jason Samosa says that the first director of the Air Force Office of Special Investigations, the US Air Force's own investigative agency formed around 1948, was a devout Catholic who had wanted to train as a priest and suddenly found himself working in intelligence. In his telling, that office was behind the early days of a group known as the Collins Elite, which would suggest religious belief shaped how parts of the government handled UFOs.
afosi-officer-harassing-a-ufo-whistleblo: Matthew Brown, introduced as a Pentagon whistleblower, spoke in 2026 on the show of a podcast host, Jesse Michels, about a person who spoke out about UFOs and was then harassed. Passing on what a named person told him, Brown says there was proof in that case that the harasser was an officer of AFOSI, the US Air Force office that runs criminal and counterintelligence investigations. If true, it would mean the military itself was pressuring people who talk about UFOs.
afswp-established-at-sandia-base-1947: A researcher who goes by the online name UAPGerb says on Jesse Michels's podcast that the AFSWP, the Armed Forces Special Weapons Project, a military body that handled nuclear weapons, was set up in 1947 at Sandia Base in Albuquerque, New Mexico. He raises it because that year and place sit right at the start of the modern UFO story, hinting at links between nuclear secrets and UFO secrets.
age-of-disclosure-claims-of-a-reverse-en: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, points to a documentary film called The Age of Disclosure. He says that in it, people like Jim Semivan, who was high up at the CIA, and Chris Mellon, a former senior Pentagon intelligence official, say the US has a programme for reverse engineering recovered craft, meaning taking them apart to learn how they work. If true, it would mean the government holds technology it did not build.
age-of-disclosure-documentary-us-holds-c: Podcast host Jesse Michels describes a new documentary called The Age of Disclosure. He says it features John Brennan, a former head of the CIA, and James Clapper, a former head of all US spy agencies, along with officials such as David Grusch, who once worked at the agency that handles US satellite and map intelligence. According to Michels, these people say the US holds crashed saucers in hangars, is trying to copy their technology, and has recovered alien bodies with them, and in another episode he describes it as decades of crash recoveries passed down through generations and ties it to Area 51, a secret Air Force base in Nevada.
age-of-disclosure-joint-doecia-effort: Jesse Michels, a podcast host, points to a documentary film called Age of Disclosure, in which he says very senior people, up to the level of the director of national intelligence, the top US intelligence official, say something. According to Michels, they say the secret work on these craft was a joint effort between the Department of Energy, which runs America's nuclear science, and the CIA's science and technology branch. If true, it would mean the work was hidden inside two powerful agencies, away from normal oversight.
agencies-deny-grusch-access-to-programs-: David Grusch, a former US intelligence officer who became a whistleblower, says that between about 2019 and 2022 he went to the intelligence agencies that had written certain reports and asked for access to the programs behind them. He says they refused, and that being denied is how you know a program is real, which, if true, would mean hidden UFO programs exist inside the government.
agency-men-say-they-follow-the-varginha-: James Fox, a documentary filmmaker, says that at an event, men from a government agency told him they knew exactly what he had been doing in his investigation of the Varginha case, a story from a town in Brazil where an alien is said to have been captured, and he mentions a person named Leslie in connection with it. If true, it would mean officials are quietly keeping an eye on his work.
agents-ask-buchanan-to-influence-gorbach: Lyn Buchanan, a former Army sergeant in a military psychic spying unit based at Fort Meade, an Army base in Maryland, says that around 1991 agents asked him to use his mind to influence Mikhail Gorbachev, the leader of the Soviet Union. He says that the words in the speech that ended communism were the very words he had been mentally pushing into Gorbachev, which, if true, would mean a psychic helped bring down the Soviet system.
agents-followed-gebauer-s-daughters-to-s: A podcast host named Jesse Michels tells of a man named Leo GeBauer, linked to a story about crashed craft and alien bodies from the 1940s and 1950s. Michels says that GeBauer's daughter told people named the Ramseys that government agents used to follow her and her sister to school. He tells it because, if true, it would suggest the authorities were watching GeBauer's family closely.
aggressive-helicopter-experiment-where-e: Brandon Fugal, a businessman who owns Skinwalker Ranch, a property in Utah known for reports of strange lights and events, told podcast host Jesse Michels about an experiment there around 2024 that used a helicopter. He says it was a really aggressive experiment and that everything went wrong. He tells it as evidence that something at the ranch reacts when it is pushed.
agnew-bahnson-s-diaries-space-brothers-a: Podcast host Jesse Michels tells of a man named Agnew Bahnson, whose diaries were found years later. Michels says that in them Bahnson writes that 'space brothers' told him to get in touch with Townsend Brown, an inventor who worked on controlling gravity, because he wanted to build a spaceship. In another episode Michels ties this to a 1957 conference at the Institute of Field Physics at the University of North Carolina in Chapel Hill, attended by famous physicists such as John Wheeler, Freeman Dyson, Richard Feynman and Peter Bergmann, suggesting that serious gravity research was nudged along by claimed contact.
agnew-bahnson-s-novel-the-stars-are-too-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, talks about a writer named Agnew Bahnson and his late-1950s novel The Stars Are Too High. Michels says the book is about rogue Nazi scientists who break away and work with American scientists. He raises it because, to him, the story may hint at real secret work that went on after the Second World War.
agnew-bahnson-s-plane-crash-1960: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells of a man named Agnew Bahnson, who he says died in the early 1960s in what he calls a bizarre plane crash. According to Michels, Bahnson's family still believes to this day that he was essentially killed. If so, it would mean someone wanted him gone.
aguadilla-airport-thermal-object-2013: In 2013, near the airport at Aguadilla, a tourist town in Puerto Rico, a heat-sensing camera filmed a small object moving low over the area. Mick West, a well-known skeptic who studies UFO videos, discusses the footage in a debate on Jesse Michels's podcast and points out that it was taken right over the airport. Michels describes the same video differently on a later episode. He calls it about three minutes long and says it shows a transmedium object, meaning one that moves between air and water. According to Michels, the object seems to go down into the Atlantic Ocean and then come back out. West and Michels read the same footage in opposite directions. To those who see it Michels's way, it would show a craft able to travel through both sky and sea.
aguadilla-analyzed-in-a-200-page-scu-doc: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, talks about a 2013 sighting of an unidentified object at Aguadilla, Puerto Rico. He says a group called the Scientific Coalition for UAP Studies (UAP being the newer official term for UFOs) wrote a report of about 200 pages on it, with many experts holding doctorates taking part. He raises it because, if true, a serious and detailed study of the case already exists.
aguadilla-object-as-two-wedding-lanterns: In 2013 an object was filmed from the air over Aguadilla, Puerto Rico, and it became a well-known UFO video. A skeptic named Mick West says on Jesse Michels's podcast that a man he calls the head of Brazil's UFO investigation department, Ruben Lianza, proposed that it was simply two lanterns released at a wedding, small paper lanterns lifted by a flame. West also points to AARO, the Pentagon's office for unexplained sightings, in connection with this explanation.
ai-agent-swarm-solves-navier-stokes-2026: A researcher named Deep Prasad, talking with podcast host Jesse Michels in 2026, says that a huge team of AI programs cracked the Navier-Stokes problem, a famously hard set of equations describing how fluids like water and air move. He says no single AI agent, meaning a program that works on a task by itself, could solve it, but 10,000 of them working together for 88 hours suddenly found a solution. If true, it would show that swarms of AI can reach answers no single mind or machine could.
ai-at-moscow-conference-judged-apollo-ph: A podcast host, Joe Rogan, passes on what a man named Bart Sibrel told him: that at an artificial intelligence conference in Moscow about two years earlier, attended by Russia's president Vladimir Putin, an AI judged photographs from Apollo, the American moon landings, to be fake. If true, it would cast doubt on the famous moon photos.
ai-reads-the-buga-sphere-symbols-as-the-: Ross Coulthart, a journalist, says that in 2025 he photographed the Buga Sphere, a metal ball covered in symbols that turned up in Buga, Colombia, and uploaded the picture to an artificial intelligence program. He says the AI read the symbols as meaning 'The circuit', which, if true, would suggest the markings are a real message rather than decoration.
ai-solves-the-navier-stokes-equations-in: An unnamed researcher, speaking on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels in 2026, says that an artificial intelligence solved the Navier-Stokes equations, the famous maths that describes how liquids and gases flow, in only 88 hours. The researcher points out that these equations had stumped mathematicians for hundreds of years. It is told as a sign of how strange and powerful AI has become, which the episode likens to alien technology.
air-force-academy-friend-flew-a-back-eng: Robert Salas, a former US Air Force officer, told a podcast host, Jesse Michels, in 2025 about a friend of his from the Air Force Academy, the school that trains Air Force officers. Salas says this friend told him, about ten years after they graduated, that he had flown a craft similar to a UFO. Because of this, Salas says he is convinced the US has back-engineered recovered craft, meaning studied them and built copies, and has even flown some models, which if true would mean the government holds and uses technology that humans did not invent.
air-force-academy-religious-training: An author named Peter Levenda, who writes about the history of intelligence agencies, says on Jesse Michels's podcast that a couple of years ago he was appalled to hear that the US Air Force Academy in Colorado was training its people in religious studies. He tells it as a sign that religious thinking is creeping into how the military approaches these mysteries.
air-force-and-cia-created-two-weeks-afte: Jake Barber, a man who says he flew a helicopter to recover a UFO, points out that in 1947, about two weeks after the Roswell incident, a reported crash of a flying object near Roswell, New Mexico, the National Security Act was passed. That law, he says, created the US Air Force and the CIA at the same time. To him this suggests the system of secrecy was built around the crash from the start.
air-force-captain-oliveira-at-the-nation: A podcast host named Jesse Michels, in an episode on Brazil's UFO cases, says that in 1954 an Air Force captain named Oliveira spoke at the Escola Superior de Guerra, Brazil's national war college. According to Michels, the captain told them that the UFO phenomenon is real. It matters because, if true, it would mean a military officer said so openly inside one of Brazil's top military schools decades ago.
air-force-censorship-of-pan-starrs-image: A podcast host named Jesse Michels says that Pan-STARRS, a telescope survey that scans the whole sky and found 'Oumuamua, a strange object that passed through our solar system from outside it, had its images heavily censored by the US Air Force. He places this in the 2010s. If true, it would mean the military was controlling what astronomers could see and share about objects in the sky.
air-force-cooperation-with-stargate-1997: A podcast host named Jesse Michels points to Stargate, a science fiction TV show starring Richard Dean Anderson that ran from the late 1990s, about soldiers travelling to other worlds. He says that two sitting Air Force Chiefs of Staff, the top uniformed officers of the US Air Force, Michael E. Ryan and John P. Jumper, appeared on the show as themselves. He tells it as a sign that the Air Force cooperated closely with the show, which he suggests could mean it wanted to shape how the public thinks about such ideas.
air-force-disinformation-drives-paul-ben: Starting around 1979 in Albuquerque, New Mexico, a researcher named Paul Bennewitz came to believe in aliens. According to the story, the Air Force fed that belief on purpose until it broke him. Podcast host Jesse Michels tells it on more than one episode. He says Richard Doty, an Air Force counterintelligence agent whose job was to protect military secrets, ran a psychological operation on Bennewitz. Michels says Bennewitz had seen an unusual craft at Kirtland Air Force Base, near his home, and was fed false information afterward. Michels also points to a document called Project Beta and to a writer named Greg Bishop. Peter Levenda, an author and researcher, tells it as well, places it in the 1980s, and stresses that it is known Doty did it. To the tellers it matters because it would show the military spreading false UFO stories to steer people away from what they had seen.
air-force-documents-on-hans-kohler-s-cap: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that US Air Force documents now show that a man named Hans Kohler was caught by the Americans in Germany in the 1940s. He brings it up as written proof of a story that had circulated about this man, which would tie him to what the Americans took from Germany after the war.
air-force-flies-benowitz-to-archuleta-me: A writer named Greg Bishop, on Jesse Michels's podcast, tells about Paul Benowitz, a man in New Mexico in the early 1980s who became convinced aliens were active nearby. Bishop says, drawing on men named Rick Doty and Bill Moore, that the Air Force flew Benowitz by helicopter from Kirtland, an Air Force base, to Archuleta Mesa on the Jicarilla Apache reservation, where props had been set out for him to see, and that Paul was thrilled about it. If true, it would mean the military deliberately fed him a false story.
air-force-funding-of-the-movie-stargate-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, has said on his show more than once that the US Air Force helped pay for Stargate, a 1994 film starring Kurt Russell. In one telling he notes that the film is about a portal found by a pyramid. He raises it as a sign that the military may have a hand in shaping how the public imagines such ideas.
air-force-going-public-plan-called-off-2: A witness who goes by the online name UAPGerb, speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast in 2025, says a man named Ed told him he had been part of a US Air Force plan, around 2009 to 2010, to go public about UFOs. According to UAPGerb, a two-star general, a senior officer, called the plan off. If true, it would mean the military came close to an official announcement and then pulled back.
air-force-hunts-for-scientist-x-1950: A podcast host named Jesse Michels tells of a lecture given in Denver, Colorado, in March 1950 about crashed flying saucers, which leaned on an unnamed source called Scientist X. He says that two hours after the lecture ended, Air Force investigators showed up and questioned students for clues about who Scientist X was. If true, it would mean the Air Force took the lecture's claims seriously enough to hunt for its secret source.
air-force-interrogations-demotions-and-d: A podcast host named Jesse Michels tells of two airmen, Mario and Michael, who say they were abducted by aliens in 1977 at Ellsworth Air Force Base in South Dakota. Michels says the worst part was what came afterwards: Air Force interrogators spent most of their time trying to explain the experience away, and the men faced demotions and denial. He tells it because, if true, it would show the military working to bury what its own men reported.
air-force-lieutenant-colonel-makes-marin: A former Marine named Michael Herrera says that around 2009 or 2010, at Camp Hansen, a Marine base on the Japanese island of Okinawa, an Air Force lieutenant colonel had him and other Marines sign a non-disclosure agreement, a promise of secrecy, tied to a top secret mission in Indonesia where Herrera says he saw a huge craft in the jungle. According to Herrera, the officer told him flat out that talking about it could mean prison or even execution, which, if true, shows how hard someone was working to keep the sighting quiet.
air-force-lieutenant-colonel-ran-arv-tes: A commentator who goes by the online name UAPGerb (UAP is the government's term for UFOs) told a podcast host, Jesse Michels, in 2026 that he knows of an Air Force lieutenant colonel who claims to have run a secret test program. According to UAPGerb, the program ran from about 1998 to 2008 within the 412th Test Wing, a flight-testing unit at Edwards Air Force Base in California, with links to the Nevada Test and Training Range, a large military range in Nevada. He says it tested "alien reproduction vehicles," human-built copies of alien craft, and technology based on them, which if true would mean the Air Force has been flying copied alien technology.
air-force-lunex-crewed-moon-base-plan-19: A researcher appearing on Jesse Michels's podcast says he recently learned that the US Air Force, in the late 1950s and early 1960s, had detailed plans for its own crewed mission to the Moon, a project known as Lunex, tied to Vandenberg Air Force Base in California. He raises it because it would mean the military had its own Moon ambitions separate from the public space programme.
air-force-manned-orbiting-laboratory-can: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, talks about the Manned Orbiting Laboratory, a 1960s US Air Force plan to put crews in a small station in orbit, which he says was kept secret until 2015. He points out that it was cancelled in June 1969, exactly one month before the Apollo mission, NASA's program to fly astronauts to the Moon, first landed there. He tells it because the timing hints that a hidden military space effort ran alongside the public one.
air-force-pilots-report-drones-up-to-36-: On Jesse Michels's podcast, a guest named Merrick says that US Air Force pilots have been reporting drones flying as high as 36,000 feet, with something like 30 or 40 reports over the past couple of years. If true, it would mean unknown craft are routinely showing up at airliner altitudes.
air-force-project-blue-book-1947: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that the US Air Force once set up its own UFO investigation programme, which he calls Operation Blue Book, running from the late 1940s through the 1960s. In one telling he says it was run for a time by Edward J. Ruppelt, whom he calls an Air Force general, and who he says seemed fairly open to the idea that the sightings were real. It matters because it would mean the military itself once took the question seriously.
air-force-roswell-reports-project-mogul-: Michael Shermer, a well-known skeptic and writer, describes two US Air Force reports, one from 1994 and one from 1996, about Roswell, a town in New Mexico at the center of a famous story of a crashed flying saucer. He says the first report explained the crash as Project Mogul, a secret program flying high-altitude balloons, and the later one explained reports of bodies as test dummies. Shermer adds that in these reports the Air Force said it had made up its original cover story because it did not want the Russians to learn it was launching high-altitude spy balloons. This matters because, if accurate, it would mean the Roswell mystery came from Cold War secrecy rather than aliens.
air-force-takes-over-navy-ufo-investigat: A historian of UFOs, Richard Dolan, speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast, passes on an account from a man he names as Donald Kho. In the late 1940s and 1950s, he says, Navy sailors kept having UFO encounters, meaning sightings of unexplained flying objects, and Air Force people would come aboard Navy ships, throw their weight around and take over the investigations, which made the Navy crews angry. If true, it would mean one branch of the military was taking control of the subject early on.
air-traffic-controller-watches-the-f-5-c: Jose Manuel Fernandez, an air traffic controller at Congonhas airport in São Paulo, Brazil, told podcast host Jesse Michels about a night in 1986 when Brazilian F-5 fighter jets chased unknown objects in the sky. He says the object seemed to be playing hide and seek, popping up and then appearing again at a very distant point. The story matters to him because, if true, it would mean military jets chased something they could not catch.
aircraft-instruments-go-haywire-at-edge-: On a podcast episode with podcast host Jesse Michels about Skinwalker Ranch, a Utah property known for reports of strange events, a speaker from the ranch describes an invisible zone over the property that they call a bubble. They say fixed-wing aircraft flying there have recorded that something is present, because their instruments go haywire at its edge. If true, it would mean something unseen over the ranch can interfere with aircraft.
aircrew-briefing-to-congress-not-a-false: Marik von Rennenkampf, a commentator on UFO cases, spoke in 2025 on the show of a podcast host, Jesse Michels, in an episode where a UFO skeptic named Mick West was challenged to a debate. He pointed to a 2015 encounter involving a military aircrew and relayed that someone, later briefing the US Congress, said "we knew it was not a false hit," meaning the sensor reading was not a glitch. If true, it would mean the object the crew tracked was real.
akhenaten-abandons-amun-and-pharaohs-dep: A researcher named Luke Caverns, on Jesse Michels's podcast in 2025, tells how an ancient Egyptian king, Amenhotep IV, took the throne after his father died and declared he would no longer worship Amun, the god the great Karnak temple was built for. Caverns says the king shut Karnak's doors, turned only to the sun god called the Aten, renamed himself Akhenaten, and fell out with the priests. He adds that Egyptian art then changed suddenly, showing royals with long, stretched skulls, and says nobody knows where that came from or why it appeared just then, which to him hints at an unexplained outside influence.
akhenaten-tribute-at-the-hale-solar-labo: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that the astronomer George Ellery Hale built his own sun observatory, the Hale Solar Laboratory in Pasadena, California, in the 1920s. According to Michels, Hale put a tribute to Akhenaten, an ancient Egyptian king known for worshipping the sun, in the arch over the entrance. Michels raises it as a sign that old religious ideas sit quietly underneath modern American space science.
akhil-knows-what-his-mother-manisha-watc: A filmmaker named Ky Dickens made The Telepathy Tapes, a documentary series about children who are said to read minds, and on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels she passed on what a mother named Manisha told her about her son Akhil. According to Manisha, she could watch a movie on one floor of their home while Akhil played on his iPad in another room, unable to hear it, and afterwards he would tell her exactly what had happened in the film. If true, it would mean information can pass from mind to mind without the senses.
akil-knows-about-the-amputee-athlete-fil: A woman named Manisha appeared on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, in an episode about a documentary on children said to read minds, and she tells a story about a boy named Akil at home in New Jersey. According to the story's framing, she had watched a film downstairs about an athlete whose leg was amputated and who went on to the Special Olympics, and Akil knew about it without having seen it. If true, it would suggest the boy picked up what was in her mind.
akil-writes-the-next-word-before-it-is-w: A documentary filmmaker named Ky Dickens, who made a film about children said to read minds, told podcast host Jesse Michels about a test she says she watched around 2023 in New Jersey with a boy named Akil, with Manisha also present. She says that as soon as a word was crossed out and someone began even thinking about the next one, Akil would start writing that next word. al-jazeera-clip-of-invisible-figure-clim: John Blitch, a scientist who once worked for DARPA, the Pentagon's agency for advanced research, told podcast host Jesse Michels about a news clip from Iraq in 2004, possibly near the town of Tikrit, first aired by the Arabic news network Al Jazeera. According to Jorjani, Buchanan was told that American pilots were being trained to fly UFOs at a deep underground site in California, even though flying them caused a strange shift in the pilots' sense of time. If true, it would mean the US has working alien craft and people to fly them.
american-soldier-s-off-record-sighting: A surgeon named Italo Venturelli, interviewed by podcast host Jesse Michels, passes on what an American soldier told him privately. As Venturelli tells it, the soldier said he had seen something over his house but would not speak about it openly, because he feared losing his US military pension. It is told as an example of witnesses staying quiet out of fear.
ammonia-smell-and-staining-inside-the-re: A researcher named Geoffrey Drumm told podcast host Jesse Michels that in 2017 he went inside the Red Pyramid, an ancient pyramid at Dahshur in Egypt. He says the walls are covered in chemical staining and a strong smell of ammonia comes from the final chamber. He offers this as a clue that the pyramids may once have had a chemical purpose, not just a burial one.
amsterdam-secret-space-program-symposium: Peter Levenda, an author presented as a historian, says that sometime around 2007 or 2008 he gave a talk in Amsterdam at a gathering called the secret space program, linking UFOs and the assassination of President Kennedy. Speaking to podcast host Jesse Michels, he says people's assumptions about his views trace back to that presentation, and he mentions two other writers in the field, Richard Dolan and Timothy Good.
amy-reynolds-taken-and-found-at-a-petrol: A researcher named Mike Masters tells, on Jesse Michels's podcast, of a woman called Amy Reynolds. He says her friend Petra watched through a window as she was taken, and soon afterwards they got a call saying Amy had been found at a petrol station 790 kilometres away. Masters calls it one of his favourite cases, since it would suggest that whatever took her could move a person a great distance very quickly.
an-advanced-civilization-made-the-geneti: A researcher named Thierry Jamin, talking on Jesse Michels's podcast in 2025 about strange three-fingered bodies found in Peru, says these beings date back about 1,800 years to the Nazca region. He says it is likely that a civilization more advanced than ours created them by mixing genes, which, if true, would mean someone was doing genetic engineering long before us.
an-alien-pilot-teaches-buchanan-to-fly-a: Lyn Buchanan, a former US Army sergeant, tells podcast host Jesse Michels that he was once taken aboard a UFO, and in one version he says it happened from a country church house in East Texas in the mid 1960s. He says the alien pilot brought him up front, let him try the controls, and that he learned how to fly it. He adds that they landed somewhere that was not Earth, which, if true, would mean a human had flown a non-human craft to another world.
an-angel-with-a-sword-over-jerusalem-dur: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, retells a Bible story: after King David ordered a count of his people, a plague struck, and an angel stood over Jerusalem holding a drawn sword. He raises it as an ancient account of a being appearing in the sky, which he places alongside modern encounter stories.
an-anonymous-frontier-physicist-s-experi: Podcast host Jesse Michels mentions a friend he keeps anonymous, a physicist he describes as working at a very high level. Michels says this friend had an experience of his own, but in the telling gives no details of what happened, where or when. It is raised to suggest that serious scientists have such stories too.
an-insectoid-working-in-a-row-of-humans-: Lyn Buchanan, a former US Army sergeant, tells podcast host Jesse Michels that during a classified mission at a military facility he walked past a row of people working and saw among them an insect-like being, what he calls an insectoid. He says he looked away at once and kept walking, and admits it could have been a soldier in some kind of alien headgear. If it was what he thought, it would mean non-humans working alongside the military.
an-nsc-staffer-told-andreessen-and-horow: Two technology investors, Marc Andreessen and Ben Horowitz, are said to have been told by a staff member of the National Security Council, the White House body that advises the president on security, that parts of physics had been made secret. Jesse Michels, a podcast host, and the researcher Matthew Pines both repeat it, and Pines, calling it hearsay, says the staffer told them whole areas of basic physics had been classified before and that the same could not be done for artificial intelligence. Pippa Malmgren, speaking on Michels' show, links it to many technologies from the nuclear age being hidden away, and she also credits the researcher Eric Weinstein. Weinstein himself says the two were told not to invest in artificial intelligence startups because those would not be allowed to exist. They raise it because, if true, the government has a history of quietly locking away entire branches of science.
an-ultra-orthodox-community-in-israel-ha: Documentary maker Ky Dickens, whose film is about children said to read minds, tells podcast host Jesse Michels about a family named Golden living in a very strict religious Jewish community in Israel. She says that community has "its own Hill", her term for a shared place the children describe, though the telling gives no more detail. It is told to suggest the same experience shows up in very different communities.
anakah-and-tristan-s-off-world-past-live: Jeffrey Mishlove, a researcher with a doctorate who studies psychic experience, tells podcast host Jesse Michels about two people named Anakah and Tristan. He says they claim to remember past lives lived on other planets, and believe they are here on a mission to make humanity's first open contact with alien life go more smoothly.
analysing-element-115-with-barry-at-s4-1: Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked on recovered alien craft at S4, a secret site in the Nevada desert, in 1988 and 1989, tells podcast host Jesse Michels about element 115, a super-heavy material he links to the craft. He says it was not something that had been officially discovered at the time, but something he and a coworker named Barry were analysing there, which would suggest the craft used matter unknown to science.
analysis-by-merrick-s-colleagues-points-: In 2004, off Southern California, a Navy jet's infrared camera filmed an unknown object, and the clip is known as the FLIR1 video. In a debate on Jesse Michels's podcast with a skeptic named Mick West, Merrick von Renenamp says analysis by colleagues, including an unnamed California scientist, gives him fairly high confidence the object was a Tic Tac shaped craft, a white oval like the mint. If true, it would mean the video shows a real unknown craft, not a distant plane or balloon.
analysis-of-coburn-s-toe-implant-skewed-: A scientist named Steve Coburn, who studies small objects people believe aliens put inside their bodies, tells podcast host Jesse Michels about one found in someone's toe in California. He says it was removed with funding from a man named Jaime Maussan, and since nobody else was available to study it, Coburn used the lab equipment at his workplace and later wrote a paper on it. According to Coburn, the object showed unusual mixes of isotopes, meaning versions of chemical elements not found in normal ratios, and signs of tiny engineered structures, which would point to something not made on Earth.
analysis-of-heavy-element-real-deal-mate: A former US intelligence officer named David Grusch, who has spoken publicly about hidden government UFO programmes, says on Jesse Michels's podcast that he talked to people who had analysed what he calls "the real deal stuff", material said to come from non-human craft. He says it is very strange, made of heavy, rare elements such as europium and californium, which he names in one of the two times the clip is aired. If true, it would mean real samples of such material are being studied in secret.
analysis-of-san-augustine-new-mexico-cra: A guest identified as Steve, on Jesse Michels' podcast about a scientist who studies alleged alien implants, says he analyzed some of the wreckage from a UFO crash at San Augustine, New Mexico. That crash is said to have happened in 1947, though he does not say when he did the analysis. If true, it would mean physical pieces of a crashed craft exist and have been studied.
analysis-of-titanium-nanotube-sphere-lat: A guest named Steve told podcast host Jesse Michels that he analyzed a sphere recovered in Mexico and studied in the United States, which he says was later stolen. According to him, it was made of a titanium alloy with tiny carbon tubes, called carbon nanotubes, built into the metal. He thinks these let it fly using the Biefeld-Brown effect, an idea that high voltage can produce thrust, which would mean the object had a non-standard way of moving.
ancestor-rediscovers-the-seven-lost-span: A researcher named Luke Caverns tells podcast host Jesse Michels a family story about an ancestor in the early 1900s. He says this relative went searching in southern New Mexico for seven gold mines left by the Spanish centuries earlier and long since lost, and found them within a year. According to Caverns, the ancestor reopened these mines, about 450 years old, which he offers as proof that old legends about hidden places can turn out to be real.
ancestry-search-places-sherman-in-omaha-: A former Air Force sergeant, Dan Sherman, says the NSA (the National Security Agency, the US agency that intercepts communications) hired him to communicate with aliens. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says a search of ancestry.com, a family-records website, credited to someone named Richard Geldridge, showed that Sherman likely lived in Omaha, Nebraska, in 1993 and 1994, near Offutt Air Force Base, which Michels offers as support for parts of Sherman's story.
ancient-architects-on-the-giza-water-tab: A researcher named Jeffrey, on Jesse Michels's podcast in 2026, discusses a study claiming a huge energy network lies beneath the pyramids of Giza in Egypt. He says another figure in the same community, who goes by Ancient Architects, debunked that study using the water table, the level of underground water beneath the site.
ancient-as-above-so-below-symbol-on-prop: The owner of Skinwalker Ranch, a property in Utah known for reports of strange happenings, spoke to podcast host Jesse Michels in an episode about a UFO said to be under the ranch. He says there is a symbol on the property from ancient times, which he links to a Masonic sign, from the secretive fraternal order of Freemasons, meaning 'as above, so below.' He reads it as a hint that what happens in the sky is mirrored by something underground.
ancient-chess-pieces-in-mongolian-burial: A man named Kiran Ilum Xenov, introduced on Jesse Michels's podcast in 2025 as the president of a Russian republic who says he was taken by aliens in 1997, talks about ancient burial mounds in Mongolia. He says chess-like figures were found in one of them, some more than 5,000 years old, and he presents them as a gift from aliens, which would mean visitors shaped human culture long ago.
ancient-chinese-diagram-of-twin-serpent-: Peter Levenda, a writer on secret history, tells podcast host Jesse Michels that while researching his book Stairway to Heaven he found an old Chinese diagram, which he dates to about 600 years back. He says it shows two serpent gods of creation twisted around each other like a double helix, the spiral shape of DNA, which would suggest ancient people knew something of life's code.
ancient-precision-buildings-in-peru-leba: Kiran Ilum Xenov, a man introduced on Jesse Michels's podcast in 2025 as the president of a Russian republic who says aliens took him in 1997, points to ancient buildings in Peru, Lebanon and Egypt, including the pyramids. He says they were built with such precision that another civilization must have made them, which would mean someone beyond the ancient people we know was at work.
ancient-south-american-bird-models-resem: A man named Greg Rogers, introduced on Jesse Michels's podcast in 2025 as a NASA doctor who says he saw a UFO in a secret hangar, mentions small ancient models from South America that are usually called birds. He suggests they look like airplanes, which, if so, would mean people thousands of years ago knew about flying machines.
ancient-spartan-doctor-s-treatise-descri: A doctor named Greg Rogers, speaking on a podcast, says the lasting mental scars of combat, known today as PTSD (post-traumatic stress disorder), are nothing new. He says there is archaeological evidence going back to the Spartans, the warrior people of ancient Greece, and that a Spartan doctor of that time wrote a treatise describing it. If so, people were naming combat trauma thousands of years ago.
ancient-temples-dismantled-and-items-rem: A researcher known as Matt, speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast in 2024, says that certain ancient temples in the Lake Van region of eastern Turkey were taken apart and that things were removed from them. He says he has found very, very compelling evidence that this happened, though he does not name a source. If he is right, someone deliberately hid part of the region's ancient past.
ancient-terrestrial-civilization-with-ne: Eric Hazeline, introduced on Jesse Michels's podcast as a former leader at the National Security Agency, the US spy agency for communications, co-wrote a book with Chris Gilbert called The New Science of UFOs. He says one idea they explore is that an advanced civilization lived on Earth hundreds of millions of years ago, able to travel close to the speed of light, and that its traces were erased as the planet's surface slowly reshaped itself. If true, some visitors might not be alien at all, but from Earth's own deep past.
andres-gomez-emilsson-s-dmt-accounts-at-: Andrew Gallimore, a neuroscientist who studies DMT, a powerful psychedelic drug many users say sends them to a realm of other beings, tells Jesse Michels about a recent talk. He says that in 2025, at a psychedelic science conference in Denver, he spoke with Andrés Gómez Emilsson, a researcher of consciousness, who shared his own accounts of DMT experiences.
andrew-basiago-claims-he-went-back-to-th: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, describes Andrew Basiago, a man who claims he took part in secret government time travel. Michels stresses that Basiago literally says he went back to 1863 to see the Gettysburg Address, Abraham Lincoln's famous speech in Pennsylvania during the American Civil War. If it were true, it would mean the government had working time travel decades ago.
andrew-gallimore-dmt-experiments-and-ent: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, speaking with the scientist Donald Hoffman, mentions that Hoffman is working with a neuroscientist named Andrew Gallimore, who runs experiments with DMT, a powerful psychedelic drug. The story behind it is that people on DMT report meeting beings that fall into consistent types, which, if true, would hint that those beings are more than random imagination.
andrija-puharich-the-ossining-space-kids: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, drawing on Greg Malazi, Dan Sherman and a book called Mind Traveler, talks about a man named Andrija Puharich, whom he calls a father of much of MK Ultra, the CIA's secret mind control research. Michels says that between the 1950s and the 1970s Puharich came into contact with non-human intelligences, including a group called the Council of Nine, and worked with so-called space kids in Ossining, New York, who channeled their messages. If true, it would mean the intelligence world was in touch with non-human beings through human go-betweens.
andy-hall-s-article-supporting-the-chemi: A researcher named Geoffrey Drumm argues that the ancient pyramids were chemical factories powered by the Earth's own electricity. On Jesse Michels's podcast, Drumm says that a man named Andy Hall, connected with the Thunderbolts Project, a group that studies the role of electricity in nature and space, wrote a long article on his website in the 2020s praising Drumm's work and backing up his idea. Drumm tells it as support from an outside voice for his view of what the pyramids were for.
angel-hair-and-an-ablative-craft-hull: Lou Elizondo, a former Pentagon official who worked on UFO questions, talks on Jesse Michels's podcast about angel hair, the fine threads people sometimes report falling from the sky after sightings. He says that, as he wrote in his book Imminent, the outer skin of these craft may be ablative, built to burn or wear away as it is used, which could explain the threads.
angel-hierarchies-of-aquinas-line-up-wit: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says he heard two people he names, Karl Nell and Diana Pasulka, talking about how the ranks of angels described by Thomas Aquinas, a medieval Christian thinker, line up with many modern encounters with what they call non-human intelligence. If that is so, old religious accounts of angels and today's reports of strange beings might describe the same thing.
angleton-and-others-on-george-c-marshall: A researcher named Pippa Malmgren, appearing on Jesse Michels's podcast with her father Harald, a former presidential adviser, says that many of the figures she studies all seem to have worked on the team of General George C. Marshall, a senior US Army leader, in the years from 1945 into the 1950s. Among them, she says, was James Jesus Angleton, who went on to become a key figure at the CIA, the US foreign intelligence agency. If so, it would point to one shared circle of people behind the later handling of these secrets.
angleton-and-reuben-efron-s-mail-interce: A researcher, Jeremy Riss, talks about James Jesus Angleton, a senior CIA spy-catcher, and a man named Reuben Efron, who he says read intercepted mail of Lee Harvey Oswald, the man accused of killing President Kennedy, between 1959 and 1963. Riss says Efron appears in the JFK files, the government records on the assassination, and that when someone was asked whether they knew Efron and said no, that was a lie. If true, it would mean the CIA was watching Oswald closely years before the killing.
angleton-as-oss-man-in-italy-1940: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says a guest named Pippa Malmgren made it clear to him that an American intelligence man, James Jesus Angleton, was the key person in Italy in the 1940s for the OSS, the United States' wartime spy service. Michels tells it because it would put Angleton at the centre of whatever was going on in Italy at that time.
angleton-may-have-pushed-mj-12-as-counte: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, wonders aloud whether James Jesus Angleton, who he says ran counterintelligence for the programme for decades, may have pushed the MJ-12 story. MJ-12 refers to documents describing a supposed secret group of top officials handling UFO matters. Michels's idea is that the story could have been spread on purpose to mislead.
angleton-probably-leaked-the-mj12-docume: The MJ12 documents are papers that describe a secret US group said to handle the UFO question. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says, drawing on what he heard from a man named Harold Malmgren, that James Jesus Angleton, a senior figure at the CIA during the Cold War, is probably the person responsible for leaking them. If true, it would tie those papers to someone deep inside the US intelligence world.
angleton-s-father-and-the-knights-of-mal: James Jesus Angleton was a senior CIA official, and his father was Hugh Angleton. The Knights of Malta are an old Catholic order of knights. A former presidential advisor, Harald Malmgren, says the relationship between the Angletons and the Knights of Malta needs to be uncovered. He places the tie in Italy and around the Vatican in the 1930s and 40s, and links it to knowledge of UFOs because Angleton was there. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, goes further and says both father and son were Knights of Malta. In a later episode he adds that they were involved in other secret societies too. So the story comes from Malmgren, speaking from his own time in government, and from the host retelling it. If true, a secret religious order may have been part of who knew about UFOs.
angleton-signed-cia-wiretap-of-marilyn-m: Steven Greer, a researcher who leads the Disclosure Project, a group pushing governments to reveal what they know about UFOs, says his briefing document includes a CIA wiretap record of the actress Marilyn Monroe from 1962, signed by James Jesus Angleton, a senior CIA officer. Greer says it captured her threatening to hold a press conference a couple of days before, in his words, they killed her. If true, it would mean the secrets were guarded at the cost of lives.
angry-owens-gives-mishlove-a-sore-throat: Jeffrey Mishlove, a psychologist with a doctorate who studies psychic claims, tells podcast host Jesse Michels about a phone call in late 1976 with Ted Owens, a man who claimed psychic powers. Mishlove says Owens got angry with him and within minutes he felt a strange sensation in his throat, as if Owens could affect him from a distance.
animals-found-dead-at-the-varginha-zoo-a: In Varginha, Brazil, in 1996, people say a strange being was found. A witness, Ahmed Foratu, says the being came into contact with animals at the town zoo and that some of them were later found dead. The documentary filmmaker James Fox adds that a scientist, Marco Le, said on camera that the cause of death was completely unknown, something he had never seen before.
anna-paulina-luna-calls-for-aaro-defundi: A journalist named Ross Coulthart says that in 2025 a member of Congress, Anna Paulina Luna, posted online about what a hopeless cause AARO is. AARO is the Pentagon office set up to look into unexplained sightings in the sky. Coulthart says she called for its funding to be cut, a sign that some lawmakers no longer trust it.
anna-paulina-luna-on-joe-rogan-read-the-: A US congresswoman, Anna Paulina Luna, said on Joe Rogan's popular podcast in the 2020s that people wondering where unexplained flying objects come from should read the Book of Enoch, an ancient religious text. She says it tells of the fall of angels, which she describes as the start of a civilization that came before the first great flood. If her reading holds, it would tie today's sightings to very old stories of beings from above.
anna-paulina-luna-s-mk-ultra-hearing-202: A researcher named Michael Shurmer, debating on Jesse Michels's podcast in 2026, says that a person they are discussing is friends with Anna Paulina Luna, a member of the US Congress who he says seems to be an insider. He adds that just the day before, she had held a big congressional hearing on MK Ultra, a Cold War CIA programme of mind-control experiments. He mentions it as a sign of how close such insiders are to official efforts to open up secret files.
anne-finds-the-letters-link-the-visitors: A writer, Whitley Strieber, who says he has been visited by beings he calls the visitors, got many letters from readers of his book about it, Communion. He says that in the late 1980s his wife Anne, who was reading those letters, came out of her office one day and told him the visitors had something to do with what we call death. If true, it would link these beings to the dead.
annie-jacobsen-s-source-o-donnell-roswel: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, talks about the 1947 Roswell incident, a reported crash of a flying object near Roswell, New Mexico. He says a man named Alfred O'Donnell was a source for the journalist Annie Jacobsen's book Area 51, and that, as she said on Lex Fridman's podcast, the craft was a hoax built for Stalin with help from the Nazi doctor Josef Mengele. In another telling Michels names neither O'Donnell nor Stalin, and describes the bodies as aged-looking children used as crash dummies. If true, it would mean Roswell was a human trick, not an alien crash.
annie-jacobson-hunt-for-the-horten-broth: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, points to a book by the writer Annie Jacobson called Area 51, named after a secret US military base in Nevada. He says Jacobson writes that after 1945 there was a real effort to find the Horten brothers, two men in Germany whom the Americans very much wanted to track down. He tells it because, if true, it shows how keen the US was to get hold of certain German know-how after the war.
anomalous-craft-show-interest-in-white-s: Matthew Brown, a former Pentagon official who calls himself a whistleblower, tells podcast host Jesse Michels that unexplained craft have shown a particular interest in White Sands, a military test range in New Mexico, and the nearby Los Alamos National Laboratory, a major US weapons research site. He hints that he has more to say about it, the point being that whatever these craft are seem drawn to sensitive military places.
anomalous-metal-containing-51-elements-i: A man named Chris Bledsoe, whose strange experiences have drawn outside interest, says someone told him about a piece of metal made of 51 elements, said to include human DNA and plutonium. According to what he was told, humans at the time could only blend about 15 elements, even in the most classified work. If true, the metal would be far beyond anything people knew how to make.
anomalous-objects-seen-by-a-navy-acousti: A retired Navy admiral, Tim Gallaudet, passes on what a colleague told him: a sound specialist who retired as a Navy captain and had served on one of the Navy's listening ships off Japan, which track things underwater by sound. According to that man, on two occasions the ship's crew also saw strange objects they could not explain, which would suggest unknown craft are active in the ocean.
anonymous-navy-friend-says-the-abyss-sce: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says a friend in the Navy, whom he does not name, talked with him about The Abyss, a deep sea film by the director James Cameron. In the film a glowing object appears far down in the ocean, and according to Michels his friend said that scene may not be far from the truth. If so, it would mean something unknown and intelligent moves through the deep ocean, and the Navy knows it.
anonymous-navy-scientist-on-extended-ele: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says he learned about a theory called extended electrodynamics, a wider version of the standard physics of electricity and magnetism laid down by James Clerk Maxwell and Oliver Heaviside, from a senior Navy scientist who asked to stay anonymous for fear of trouble from his bosses. Michels says the interview appeared in his documentary about Townsend Brown, an inventor he calls a man who built UFOs for the CIA, and he returns to it in later episodes. He raises it because, if the theory holds, it might explain how unusual craft could move.
