bahnson-funds-brown-s-gravitator-experim: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in the 1950s a North Carolina man named Agnew Bahnson, head of a research group called the Institute of Field Physics, was paying for the work of an inventor named Thomas Townsend Brown. Michels says Brown was building "gravitator" devices meant to control gravity, worked on them at the back of Bahnson's house, and claimed positive results, and that Bahnson said strange things happened there. If true, it would mean serious private money was backing early efforts to control gravity.
bahnson-funds-bryce-dewitt-institute-at-: A researcher named Eric Weinstein, speaking on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, tells of a wealthy man named Agnew Bahnson who, in the 1950s, approached a physicist named Bryce DeWitt and asked him to found an institute at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill. In his first telling Weinstein was unsure of the man's name and said the money came from tobacco or air conditioning. In a later telling he says Bahnson and another physicist, John Wheeler, sought DeWitt out together and set him up at what was called the Institute of Field Physics. Weinstein says its purpose was anti-gravity, and he points to an old newspaper clipping. Michels repeats the story in his own words on other episodes, calling Bahnson an industrialist. He ties the institute to a 1957 conference at Chapel Hill and to famous physicists such as Richard Feynman, Peter Bergmann, Freeman Dyson and Wheeler, and he says the work there often dealt with gravitational anomalies, meaning strange behaviour of gravity. The two tell it because, if true, private money was quietly backing research into controlling gravity as early as the 1950s.
baiting-for-shootdowns-as-cover-for-psio: Matthew Brown, a man presented on a podcast as a Pentagon whistleblower, tells host Jesse Michels about a secret practice of using people as bait to lure unknown craft so they can be shot down. Brown says this bait story is really a cover for using psychic people, which he calls psionics, as breeding stock, with the aim of producing a super psychic child generations later. At another point he puts it more simply, saying only that these people are brought in as breeding stock, which would mean a hidden human breeding programme if true.
baker-victory-services-day-treatment-cen: A man named Jordan Jose says that from about 2008 to 2010, as a child, he attended a school at 650 Ridge Road in Western New York run by Baker Victory Services, a day treatment centre that has since closed after many lawsuits. He says that from the outside it served neurodivergent kids and kids with behavioural needs, but on the inside it supported research by a defense contractor into developing psychic abilities, a journey he says began with a game. If true, it would mean children were quietly being tested for psychic potential for the military.
baker-victory-services-training-to-quant: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, interviewing a guest who says they were taken into a UFO program as a child, talks about a place called Baker Victory Services from the guest's childhood. Michels says much of the work there involved teaching people to "quantum unentangle," meaning to cut hidden connections between themselves and things they were linked to. If true, it would mean children were being trained in unusual mental skills.
bald-shin-patches-and-jack-s-tumors-sent: Charlie Foltz, who tells of an alien abduction he says he lived through, speaks on Jesse Michels's podcast about his companion Jack Weiner. Foltz says that after 1976 Jack had tumors growing in the exact spots on his legs where the men had bald patches on their shins, and that tissue was sent from a Vermont teaching hospital to an Air Force pathology institute near Washington, a military lab that studies disease. He tells it as physical traces of the abduction that drew military interest.
balls-of-light-over-hanford-plutonium-si: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, has told several times about Hanford in Washington state, a site that made plutonium for the first atomic bombs. Drawing on the researcher Robert Hastings and his book on UFOs and nuclear weapons, Michels says that in 1945, months before the first atomic test and the bombings of Japan, a man named Bud Clem, whom Michels in one telling calls a pilot, described glowing balls of light hovering over the site, and that jet fighters chased them without success. In other tellings he ties the sightings to an Air Force study he calls Project Twinkle, which he says was deleted from Air Force archives, or credits a Lieutenant Commander Brown instead of Clem, and he tells it because it would suggest unknown objects were watching nuclear sites from the very start.
baltic-anomaly-history-lightning-smoke-n: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, talks about a strange object said to sit on the floor of the Baltic Sea, between Sweden and Finland. He says lightning has struck it, smoke has been seen coming out of it, and ships from NATO, the Western military alliance, circle it, which he calls very strange and which would suggest the object is more than an ordinary rock formation.
baltic-sea-anomaly-expedition: On the floor of the Baltic Sea, roughly midway between Sweden and Finland, a team of treasure-hunting divers says it found a strange object shaped like the Millennium Falcon, the round spaceship from Star Wars. Dennis Asberg, the Swedish treasure hunter who made the find, tells it first-hand. He says the object showed up on side scan sonar, a device that maps the seabed with sound, on 19 June 2011, and that his partner Peter Lindberg laughed and said "here is UFO". Michels says he went to the site himself in 2025, about 60 kilometres out to sea. The astronomer Beatriz Villarroel tells it as something she heard about: a team of divers found "something that looked like a crashed UFO or looked like an artificial structure". She places it off the Swedish coast rather than between the two countries. If it is what some suggest, a crashed craft is lying on the seabed.
baltic-sea-anomaly-not-attached-to-the-s: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, talks about a strange shape found on the floor of the Baltic Sea, the sea between Sweden and Finland, which people call the Baltic Sea anomaly. Michels says a friend of his, an explorer named Dennis Aspx, told him the object is not attached to the seafloor and gives off electromagnetic activity, the kind of energy that can disturb electronics. If true, it would suggest the object is something made or placed there, not a natural rock.
banister-pistol-whips-jack-martin-1963: Peter Levenda, an author introduced on Jesse Michels' podcast as a CIA historian, tells of two men in New Orleans in 1963, Guy Banister and Jack Martin. He says they got into a fist fight over the assassination, and in the story Banister pistol-whips Martin. Those who tell it see it as a sign that the men around Banister were caught up in talk of the killing.
bannister-effect-after-the-first-4-minut: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, describes what he calls the Bannister effect, named after a British runner, Roger Bannister, who ran a mile in under four minutes at Oxford in 1954. Michels says that within about two and a half years, ten other runners had done the same. He uses it to make the point that once one person shows something is possible, others quickly follow.
baptist-preacher-prays-over-the-bodies-1: Scott Ramsay, who tells the story of a saucer said to have come down at Hart Canyon near Aztec, New Mexico, in March 1948, relays an account from a local preacher named Solon Brown. According to Ramsay, Brown was asked to pray over the bodies found at the site, and he answered that he wasn't Catholic, he was a Baptist preacher, but he'd be glad to say a prayer over them. If true, it would mean ordinary local people saw the bodies of beings from the craft.
barber-goes-to-the-senate-intelligence-c: Jake Barber, a man who says he flew a helicopter to recover a UFO, says on Jesse Michels's podcast that he went to Congress, to the Senate committee that oversees intelligence agencies and to the official who monitors the CIA, the US spy agency, to tell everything he knew, and that they asked him for help. A journalist, Ross Coulthart, also says Barber's first-hand evidence was given to that Senate committee. If true, his account would have reached the people in government charged with checking secret programs.
barber-hints-at-the-two-aerospace-primes: A man named Jake Barber, who says he knows about secret efforts to recover crashed craft of non-human origin, was asked which big aerospace contractors are involved. He did not name them, but said that if you took two guesses you would get both right on the first try. The hint suggests, if true, that the best-known major defense firms hold that work.
barber-one-to-two-craft-a-year-recovered: An online researcher who goes by UAPGerb tells podcast host Jesse Michels what Jake Barber, a former helicopter pilot who says he helped retrieve a UFO, has said in public. According to UAPGerb, Barber says that over his own test range alone, one to two craft a year were recovered. If true, it would mean such recoveries are a routine affair.
barber-s-group-back-channeled-the-psioni: Jake Barber, who says he helped recover a UFO by helicopter, says on Jesse Michels's podcast that in 2023 in Washington his group quietly passed an explanation to Michael Herrera, a man who tells his own story of seeing a strange craft. The explanation involved "psionic asset transfer," the idea that people with mind-based abilities play a part in how these craft appear, and Barber says plainly, "That was us." If true, it would mean a group with inside knowledge was shaping what witnesses understood about their own experiences.
barber-s-symptoms-compared-with-john-bur: Jake Barber, a former helicopter pilot who says he retrieved a UFO, tells podcast host Jesse Michels he learned, through a scientist named Garry Nolan, about John Burroughs and Jim Penniston, two US airmen who reported a strange craft in Rendlesham Forest in England in 1980. Barber says Burroughs had health symptoms similar to his own and similar trouble with his records at the VA, the US agency that handles veterans' health care. If true, it would point to a shared pattern of harm from such encounters, and of paperwork going wrong afterward.
barber-s-team-brought-in-for-dod-59-agen: Jake Barber, who says he helped recover a UFO by helicopter, says on Jesse Michels's podcast that in December 2024 his team was brought in for the Department of Defense at Picatinny Arsenal, a military site in New Jersey. He says more than 59 local police agencies were working there without coordinating, alongside the FBI, the Defense Department and private partners, which would point to a large and messy response to something happening at the site.
barber-s-team-saw-the-same-octagonal-eig: Jake Barber, who says he helped recover a UFO by helicopter, says on Jesse Michels's podcast that his team saw an eight-sided craft, which he calls an "eight-gon." He says it is exactly what Michael Herrera, another man who tells of seeing a strange craft, reports having seen, which would mean two separate accounts describe the same object.
barber-sent-to-red-team-whistleblowers-a: Jake Barber, who says he helped recover a UFO by helicopter, says that in 2023 he went to a whistleblower conference at the National Press Club in Washington, hosted by Steven Greer, shortly after a law protecting whistleblowers took effect, and heard Michael Herrera tell his story there. Barber says he was sent by his employer to look for whistleblowers, essentially to test them from the other side, and the podcast host Jesse Michels later put it to Greer as Barber having come to infiltrate his camp. If true, it would mean people inside the secret world were watching who was coming forward.
barber-story-contractor-and-mercenary-re: An analyst named Matthew Pines, speaking with podcast host Jesse Michels, discusses the account of Jake Barber, a former helicopter pilot who says he helped retrieve a UFO. Pines says Barber's story implies that private contractor teams and mercenary retrieval units are competing with each other to recover these objects. He offers this as one of the stranger parts of the story that his own wider view would explain.
barry-says-the-secrecy-sucks-1987: Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked in the late 1980s at S4, a secret site in Nevada where he says alien craft were studied, tells on Jesse Michels's podcast of a moment with a colleague named Barry Castilio. Lazar says he asked, "Can you believe this is being kept secret?" and Barry answered that it sucks, which would mean even the insiders were uneasy about the secrecy.
basalt-bas-relief-carrying-hermetic-teac: A researcher known as Matt, on Jesse Michels's podcast in 2024, describes a giant basalt block in the Lake Van region of Turkey, about 3 by 3 by 4 feet. It is carved in raised figures, which is called a bas-relief. He says it carries sacred teachings that he thinks became the basis of Hermeticism, an old mystical tradition, which would put that tradition's roots in this region.
basel-group-extended-the-dmt-state-to-90: A neuroscientist, Andrew Gallimore, says a research group in Basel, a city in Switzerland, led by someone he thinks is called Matias Leaki, has extended the experience of DMT, a powerful psychedelic drug, to 90 minutes. For Gallimore this matters because a longer trip would let people spend more time in what he describes as an alien realm.
bases-on-the-far-side-of-the-moon: This is the idea that someone has built bases on the far side of the Moon, the half we never see from Earth. A researcher named John Brandenburg puts it forward on a podcast. He says that if you had bases on the Moon, you would put them on the far side, almost as if you were afraid we would see them. A second man, Chris Bledsoe, who says he has had many encounters with unexplained lights, backs up part of it from his own looking. Bledsoe says that, from moon photos he has seen, something is hidden back there. He speaks of "something" rather than bases. If either is right, someone other than us is active on the Moon and keeping out of sight.
bat-filled-structures-smell-different-fr: A researcher named Geoffrey Drumm, who explores ancient Egyptian sites, says his team has been inside Mastaba 17, a flat-topped ancient tomb, and the Tomb of the Birds at Saqqara, both full of bats. He says those places smell different from the Red Pyramid, a large pyramid nearby, which for him suggests something else explains the pyramid's smell.
battelle-analysis-of-1947-1952-sightings: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Battelle, a private research institute, put out a very deep study of UFO sightings reported in the United States between 1947 and 1952. According to Michels, about a third of the most credible sightings in that study stayed unexplained. He points to it as a sign that the best cases could not be explained away.
battelle-biologics-lab-at-fort-detrick: On a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, a researcher who goes by UAPGerb says that an organisation called Battelle runs some kind of biological materials lab at Fort Detrick, a US Army site in Maryland. He says that if any group out there is studying actual biologics, meaning living or once-living material, possibly from non-human beings, it is probably Battelle. If true, it would point to where such material might be studied in secret.
battelle-brainstorms-injectable-interfac: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, describes a 2020 programme called Brainstorms, run with the Air Force Research Lab, the US Air Force's science arm, to develop a link between brain and machine that could be injected rather than surgically implanted. He says that according to a 2020 press release from Battelle, a private research organisation, its team moved on to the second phase, and he mentions Carnegie Mellon University as also involved. He tells it to show how far secret brain technology work may have gone.
battelle-memorial-institute-linked-to-gi: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says an unnamed senior government official told of a link between the Battelle Memorial Institute, a private research organization, and school programs for gifted and talented children. Michels says the same official tied both to a secretive group, which he calls the Cabal, that runs UFO programs. If true, it would suggest the group looks for bright young people early.
battelle-studied-roswell-lightweight-met: An online researcher who goes by UAPGerb says there is research suggesting that the Battelle Memorial Institute, a private research organisation, studied very lightweight metals taken from the crash near Roswell, New Mexico, in 1947, where some say an unknown craft came down. He points to records tied to something called Project Stork, which he dates to 1947 to 1949. If true, it would mean private scientists were handed crash material to study.
battle-of-los-angeles-and-the-marshall-b: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells of the Battle of Los Angeles in 1942, during the Second World War, when he says a UFO showed up and flew down the California coast. According to Michels, George Marshall, the top general of the US Army, was briefed about it, which would mean the highest military levels knew of such objects even before the war ended.
bauval-hancock-and-schoch-on-sphinx-weat: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, points to three writers, Robert Bauval, Graham Hancock and Robert Schoch, who since the 1990s have argued unusual things about ancient Egypt. He mentions their claims about wear on the limestone of the Sphinx, the great stone statue at Giza, and the story also includes the idea that the pyramids line up with the stars of the constellation Orion as they stood around 10,500 BC. If true, it would mean these monuments are far older than usually thought.
bay-of-pigs-bombers-arrive-late-because-: Dan Sheehan, a guest on Jesse Michels' podcast, talks about the Bay of Pigs, the failed 1961 invasion of Cuba. He says the bombers meant to support the landing, linked in his telling to Anastasio Somoza and Nicaragua, arrived late because they were in a different time zone. In his account, a simple mix-up like that helped doom the operation.
bayer-letters-with-third-reich-generals-: A guest named Brigham Buhler, talking on Jesse Michels's podcast about the dark past of the drug industry, says there are letters exchanged between Bayer, a large German drug company, and generals of Nazi Germany during World War II. According to Buhler, these letters concerned medical trials carried out in the camps. If true, it would tie a major company directly to wartime human experiments.
bayer-ships-hiv-contaminated-hemophilia-: Brigham Buhler, a guest on Jesse Michels's podcast who talks about the drug industry, says that in the 1980s the drug company Bayer knowingly shipped large amounts of medicine for hemophilia, a condition where blood does not clot properly, that was infected with HIV, the virus that causes AIDS, to poorer countries. He tells it in a conversation about human experiments, as an example of how far big companies would go if true.
beach-photo-of-a-suited-being-in-baja-ca: Ammar Kandil, a guest on Jesse Michels's podcast, passes on a story from a friend of a friend: his best friend's sister's best friend. He says she was in Baja California, Mexico, taking photos on the beach at sunset, and one of the pictures showed a being in some kind of suit. If true, it would be a chance photo of a non-human visitor.
beam-over-the-canoe-taken-aboard-wand-ja: A man named Jim Weiner says that in August 1976, while canoeing on the Allagash Waterway in Maine, a craft hovered right on top of him and his companions and a beam of light came down around the canoe. He says they were taken aboard, and that a wand was jabbed into his ribs. If true, it would be a case of people being abducted by non-human beings.
bechtel-and-monsanto-possibly-handling-a: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells of a claim that Bechtel, a large engineering company, and Monsanto, a chemical and farming company, may have handled alien bodies and biological samples in secure underground sites. Michels says he was told Monsanto may have been involved in the past, most likely dealing with the biological samples. If true, it would mean private companies have been caring for nonhuman remains in secret.
beckwith-s-neutrino-light-detector-seize: A UFO activist, Steven Greer, tells podcast host Jesse Michels what an inventor named Bob Beckwith told him. According to Greer, Beckwith invented a detector that could pick up bursts of light from neutrinos, tiny particles that pass through almost everything, and was then hit with a national security order from the National Reconnaissance Office, the US agency that runs spy satellites. If true, it would mean the government is locking away inventions that touch on these secrets.
bedrock-mound-inside-the-great-pyramid-i: A researcher named Jeffrey, speaking on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, says that the Great Pyramid at Giza in Egypt was built over a natural mound of bedrock, and that this mound is much taller than people think. He offers it as his own opinion, and if true it would change how people understand the way the pyramid was built.
bedrock-shafts-along-the-causeway-as-ind: A researcher named Jeffrey, on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, talks about shafts cut into the bedrock along the causeway, a long ancient road on Egypt's Giza Plateau that leads to the pyramid of the pharaoh Khafre. In his opinion these shafts are part of the industrial infrastructure of the Giza Plateau. If true, it would mean the pyramid site was a working industrial complex and not only a set of tombs.
beehive-like-interior-of-the-craft-and-a: A man named Mario Woods says that in the 1960s in South Dakota he was on board a craft, and he describes it on Jesse Michels's podcast. He says the inside was like a beehive, with many levels and small Grays, short grey-skinned beings, everywhere going to and fro, and that he was held in a pyramid-shaped field, which would mean he was taken aboard by non-human beings.
beethoven-s-bone-conduction-1800: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that the composer Beethoven, after going deaf in Vienna in the early 1800s, used something called bone conduction, which means hearing sound through vibrations carried by the bones of the head. Michels brings it up while talking about unusual ways people take in signals and information.
befriending-john-wheeler-at-a-new-jersey: A man named Bob Maguire, who says he worked for a contractor serving US intelligence agencies, says he lived in New Jersey for a while and his wife was a nurse at a retirement community. He says that is how he came to befriend John Wheeler, a famous physicist linked to the Institute for Advanced Study in Princeton, in Wheeler's later years.
behavior-control-tests-on-holmesburg-pri: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in the 1960s and 70s tests aimed at controlling behavior were carried out on inmates at Holmesburg Prison in Philadelphia. He says this happened a full decade after MK Ultra, a secret CIA program that experimented on people's minds, had supposedly been shut down, which would mean that kind of testing went on long after it officially ended.
being-said-because-he-s-here-1977: An Air Force veteran named Mario Woods says that in November 1977, in the field of nuclear missile sites around Ellsworth Air Force Base in South Dakota, he and others had an encounter he describes as an abduction. He recalls hearing the words "because he's here", with no names spoken, as if the reason for what happened was the presence of one particular person.
being-shows-longitudinal-scalar-waves-as: A man named Dave Rossi says that in 2021, at his home, a non-human being showed him what he calls longitudinal or scalar waves, waves that push and pull along their direction of travel. He says the being showed them to him as something like slinkies, the coiled spring toys, existing all around us. If true, it would mean beings are teaching humans hidden physics.
being-taken-to-campinas-pathologist-then: A Brazilian surgeon, Italo Venturelli, relays a story about a being said to have been found in Brazil in 1996. He says it was carried to Campinas, a city in Brazil, to a famous pathologist, a doctor who examines bodies, named Badan Palhares, a friend of a Dr. Rodrigues, and was then taken to Area 51, a secret US Air Force base in Nevada. If true, it would mean Brazil handed a non-human body over to the United States.
beings-at-mount-zeil-let-pat-price-know-: A former US Army sergeant, Lyn Buchanan, tells podcast host Jesse Michels about Pat Price, a man who, like Buchanan, was said to be able to look at distant places with his mind, and his session targeting Mount Zeil in Australia. Buchanan says that when Price did it, the beings there let him know they knew he was watching, and that scared him. If true, it would mean whatever is at that mountain can sense being observed from afar.
beings-landing-in-townsend-brown-s-yard-: Townsend Brown was an American inventor of the mid twentieth century, and this story says that small beings used to land in his yard and give him information. A man named Chris Bledsoe, who says he has had his own encounters with strange beings, says he heard this from a man named Timothy Taylor. Bledsoe says that when they met in Zanesville, Taylor explained he was helping Brown's daughter finish a book about her father, and told him about Brown having visitors who came and landed. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, adds that Brown's daughter, Linda Brown, did an online question and answer session on the website Reddit. Michels says she talked there about pale beings coming down and entering the house, into the kitchen. If true, an inventor's ideas may have come from visitors who were not human.

He says the joke used to scare new guards was that Bigfoot, the legendary ape-like creature, was out there and would get them. But he says, as far as he knew, nobody talked about UFOs at all.
bill-casey-never-raised-ufos-1980: John Herrington, who served as US Secretary of Energy in President Reagan's cabinet in the 1980s, tells a podcast host, Jesse Michels, that the subject of UFOs never came up in his time there. He says that if it had been on the agenda of Bill Casey, who ran the CIA, the US foreign intelligence agency, Casey would have talked to him about it. It is told as a top official's word on whether the government's inner circle was dealing with the topic.
bill-clinton-s-tar-baby-remark-to-rockef: A researcher named Grant Cameron says that around 1995, at the Wyoming ranch of a wealthy businessman, Lawrence Rockefeller, then US President Bill Clinton talked with Rockefeller about UFOs, with Hillary Clinton also named in the story. Cameron says Clinton told Rockefeller the subject was like the tar baby, the old folk tale about a sticky doll that traps whoever touches it. If true, it would mean a sitting president saw the UFO question as something he could not touch without getting stuck.
bill-colby-s-death-before-delivering-a-z: Steven Greer, a doctor who campaigns for the government to reveal what it knows about UFOs, told this on Jesse Michels' podcast. He says that in 1996 William Colby, a former head of the CIA who Greer says had been told about these secrets, tried to get his group a "zero-point device", a machine said to draw energy from empty space. As Greer tells it, Colby died, near a river south of Washington, before the device could be handed over. If true, it would suggest that such technology exists and is being held back.
bill-gunston-article-b-2-has-electrograv: Nick Cook is a journalist who has written about secret aircraft research. He tells the podcast host Jesse Michels about an article by Bill Gunston, a British aviation writer. Cook says Gunston worked out that the B-2, an American stealth bomber, was too heavy for its engines to give the performance claimed for it. The idea is that it might be getting a hidden boost from electrogravitics, a claimed way of using electric charge to push against gravity, linked to the inventor Townsend Brown. He names the magazines Military Power and Air International. In a later episode Cook tells it again, saying simply that the B-2's numbers did not add up. Michels also repeats it, saying Gunston was sure Brown's work went into the B-2, and dating the article to 2000 in Air International.
bill-hamilton-feeds-witnesses-to-greer-s: A researcher who posts online as UAPGerb (UAP is the official term for UFOs) says on the show of podcast host Jesse Michels that in 1997 a UFO researcher named William "Bill" Hamilton III, author of a book called Cosmic Top Secret, was in contact with Steven Greer, who ran the Disclosure Project, an effort to get witnesses to speak publicly about UFOs. According to UAPGerb, Hamilton passed witnesses on to Greer, including a primary witness he names only as Brad S. If so, some of the project's witnesses would have come to it through one researcher's contacts.
bill-holden-kennedy-on-air-force-one-say: Steven Greer, who campaigns for UFO disclosure, relays a story from Bill Holden, the chief steward on Air Force One, the president's plane. According to Holden, in 1963, on a flight Greer places on the way to Berlin, President John F. Kennedy told him, "I know this is true and I know these are real, but the whole matter is out of my hands and I don't know why." Greer also tells it as Kennedy echoing what an earlier president had said; if true, it would mean even a president could not get at the secret.
bill-lear-cut-john-lear-out-of-his-will-: Bob Lazar, a man interviewed at length by the podcast host Jesse Michels, tells a personal story about his friend John Lear. Lazar says that Bill Lear cut John out of his will in the 1970s, and that John showed him the will, going through it paragraph by paragraph.
bill-lear-figuring-out-gravity-control-1: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, talks about Bill Lear, the inventor behind the Learjet, the first private jet, and father of John Lear. In one telling Michels quotes a 1956 article in Jane's Defence Weekly, a military trade publication, saying Lear was "already figuring out gravity control for the weightless craft to come." In another, Michels says Lear himself said in 1956 that he believed anti-gravity was possible because UFOs display it. Either way, Michels tells it as a sign that serious aviation figures in the 1950s took gravity control seriously.
bill-moore-admits-sowing-disinformation-: A researcher who goes by UAPGerb, speaking on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, recalls that a UFO writer named Bill Moore stood up at a conference of MUFON, a large American civilian group that investigates UFO reports, and admitted something. According to UAPGerb, Moore said he had been instructed to spread false information among UFO researchers. If true, it would mean someone was deliberately muddying the field from the inside.
bill-moore-did-work-for-the-cia-1960: A Canadian UFO researcher named Grant Cameron told podcast host Jesse Michels about Bill Moore, a UFO writer and researcher. Cameron says Moore told him that he never worked for the CIA, the US foreign intelligence agency, but that he did do some work for it. If true, it ties a well known UFO researcher to American intelligence.
bill-moore-interviewed-t-townsend-brown-: A writer and researcher named Greg Bishop told podcast host Jesse Michels that Bill Moore, a UFO writer and researcher, interviewed T. Townsend Brown, an inventor known for work on unusual electrical forces, sometime in the 1970s or 1980s. Bishop links this to a book called The Cosmic Conspiracy. It matters because it would connect Moore directly to one of the central figures in claims about secret propulsion.
bill-moore-s-spy-training-and-soviet-pos: A writer and researcher named Greg Bishop told podcast host Jesse Michels about Bill Moore, a UFO writer and researcher, in the early 1980s. According to Bishop, Moore was given a kind of spy training and was used to pass mail along and do other tasks involving Soviet spies. If true, it would mean a UFO researcher was being used in American intelligence work.
bill-moore-warns-steinman-off-mrs-wang-1: A UFO researcher, Grant Cameron, told podcast host Jesse Michels a story from the 1980s about another researcher, William Steinman, who was asking questions about crashed flying saucers. Cameron says that Steinman was talking to a woman he calls Mrs. Wang, linked to a man named Eric Henry Wang, when he got a phone call from a man named Bill Moore asking, "What are you talking to Mrs. Wang for?" Cameron tells it because, if true, someone was watching who Steinman spoke to and wanted him to stop.
bill-napier-links-the-younger-dryas-impa: A researcher of ancient catastrophes, Randall Carlson, says on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels that an astronomer named Bill Napier, at an observatory in England, first proposed that the Younger Dryas, a sudden cold snap around 12,900 years ago, was set off by a comet strike from the Taurids, a stream of space debris that Earth passes through each year. If true, a cosmic impact would have reshaped the world just as human prehistory was unfolding. Michels himself later tells it a little differently, dating it to about 9,600 BC and crediting the idea to Carlson and the writer Graham Hancock instead.
bill-ray-s-remote-viewing-of-buddha-1980: Lyn Buchanan, a former Army sergeant who worked in the military's remote viewing unit, says the unit had a colleague named Bill Ray remote view the Buddha in the 1980s. Remote viewing means trying to see faraway places, people or events using only the mind. Buchanan says it was a life-changing experience for Ray, which, if true, would suggest the mind can reach across time as well as distance.
bill-richardson-siphoning-us-nuclear-sec: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in the 1990s Bill Richardson, who was Secretary of Energy, the cabinet member in charge of the department that runs America's nuclear weapons labs such as Los Alamos in New Mexico, was close to the Clintons and was "systematically siphoning American nuclear secrets." If true, it would mean the man in charge of guarding those secrets was the one leaking them.
bill-sweetman-s-1980s-look-at-sap-compar: A physicist who has worked on government advanced-research projects, Eric Davis, says on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels that an aviation journalist named Bill Sweetman did a deep investigation in the 1980s, after Ronald Reagan became president. Davis says Sweetman looked at special access programs, highly secret government projects that only a few cleared people may know about, and how they were split into sealed compartments and sometimes duplicated one another. It matters to the story because such hidden structures are where secret UFO work could supposedly be kept.
bill-todman-jr-touched-a-living-ufo-in-a: Dan Sheehan, a guest on Jesse Michels's podcast, passes on a story from his college years about a man named Bill Todman Jr. Sheehan says Todman told him that while climbing in the Tetons, a mountain range, he walked into a meadow and found a UFO hovering just above the ground, and that he touched it and felt it was somehow alive. If true, it would mean someone had stood face to face with a living craft.
bill-uhouse-kingman-based-simulator-and-: A researcher who goes by the online name UAPGerb says that in the mid-2000s a man named Bill Uhouse told him about secret work in Nevada. According to Uhouse, sites linked to Area 51, a secret US military test base, held a simulator for flying an extraterrestrial vehicle, and it was built using a craft said to have crashed at a place called Kingman. If true, it would mean the US had been learning to fly a non-human craft.
billy-meier-s-early-photos-show-the-spor: Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked on alien craft at a secret Nevada site in the late 1980s, said this to podcast host Jesse Michels. He says the first photos taken in the 1970s by a man named Billy Meier, which show a craft like the one Lazar calls the "sport model", are completely genuine. If true, Meier's pictures and Lazar's account would back each other up.
billy-meier-s-faked-photos-including-din: A UFO researcher named Clas Svahn talks about Billy Meier, a man in Switzerland who says he photographed alien visitors and their craft. Svahn says some of Meier's photos were faked, including a picture of a dinosaur that he says was taken from a book, and he says he has that same book at home. If true, it would mean at least some of Meier's famous pictures were copied rather than taken.
billy-meier-s-past-as-a-middle-east-inte: A philosopher named Jason Jorjani says that a man named Billy Meier, a well-known figure in UFO circles, had an earlier life as a spy. Drawing on a source called Closer Encounters, Jorjani says that before the 1970s Meier worked in the field for intelligence services in places like Tehran and Turkey, picked up the name Billy in Tehran, and was a James Bond style operative. If true, it would put Meier's later UFO claims in a very different light.
billy-meier-s-pleiadians-1970: A philosopher and researcher, Jason Jorjani, mentions on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels a Swiss man named Billy Meier, who from the 1970s on said he was in contact with beings from the Pleiades, a star cluster. According to Jorjani, Meier described these Pleiadians as kindly visitors who were coming to save humanity. Jorjani brings it up as an example of alien contact stories carrying a message of rescue.
binary-dead-star-drives-the-great-year-a: This story is about an idea that our Sun has a hidden partner, a dead star that it circles with. A researcher on ancient history named Matt LaCroix tells it on a podcast with the host Jesse Michels. He says this partner is the entire reason for the Great Year, a long sky cycle of roughly 12,500 years in his telling, and for the times when human civilisations have been wiped out and had to start over. LaCroix says the American space agency, NASA, has covered this up, and he points to a 1987 book called the New Science Encyclopedia. Later in the same conversation he adds that the cycle shows up in ice drilled from Antarctica and Greenland. He also says the partner star is close again now, and that 'we're right in it right now,' though there he does not mention NASA. If true, it would mean another reset of civilisation could be coming soon.
biologics-as-soft-tissue-drones-in-consc: A helicopter pilot named Jake Barber, who says he helped recover a UFO, passes on an idea from a man he calls Dave. According to Dave, the so-called biologics, the living bodies said to be found with these craft, might not be pilots at all but soft-tissue drones, tools serving a craft that is itself conscious. If true, it would change what we think is actually flying these things.
biondi-and-malanga-s-2022-sar-claim-of-e: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in 2022 a small team led by an Italian radar specialist, Filippo Biondi, and his engineering colleague, Corrado Malanga, claimed that radar images taken from above, a method called SAR (synthetic aperture radar), showed eight hollow cylinder-shaped structures deep beneath the pyramids at Giza in Egypt. In a later episode Michels describes them as tubes about 20 meters wide under the Khafre pyramid, one of the great Giza pyramids. He calls it one of the boldest claims in archaeology in a century, since if true it would make the question of how and why the pyramids were built far stranger.
biondi-s-patents-on-the-method-a-second-: Filippo Biondi, a guest on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels about scans he says reveal a vast structure beneath the pyramids of Egypt, says the method he uses is protected by a patent. He adds that he is now submitting a second patent, which the story places in the United States in the 2020s. It matters to the story because it presents his technique as a formal, recorded invention.
bishop-carl-stanley-tips-the-fbi-about-f: An author on occult and intelligence history, Peter Levenda, says on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels that in 1963 a bishop from Kentucky named Carl Stanley went to the FBI, the US federal police. According to Levenda, Stanley told them to look at two men in New Orleans, David Ferrie and Jack Martin, saying they were involved in the assassination. If true, it would tie a little-known church figure to one of the era's darkest events.
bishop-mcintyre-at-edwards-afb-in-1954-d: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says there are real records of a churchman known as Bishop McIntyre spending time at Edwards Air Force Base in California in 1954. Michels points out that this is the same year President Dwight Eisenhower is rumoured to have made a secret deal with aliens. He adds that this comes from real records and not from MJ-12, a set of papers said to describe a secret group of officials handling UFO matters. If true, the bishop's visit would hint that a churchman was brought in around the time of that rumoured deal.
bismuth-magnesium-layers-could-shrink-te: Hal Puthoff, a physicist who has long worked on government-backed studies of unusual phenomena, says he examined a piece of layered bismuth and magnesium said to come from Roswell, the reported 1947 crash of a craft in New Mexico. He says he found it had tiny channels for guiding waves, a kind of part called a waveguide, far smaller than the waves themselves, which he calls quite an accomplishment. Podcast host Jesse Michels, relaying Puthoff, puts it as a claim that the material could shrink waveguides for terahertz frequencies, a band between radio and light; if true, it would point to deliberately engineered material beyond ordinary know-how.
bismuth-magnesium-sample-said-to-be-from: A small piece of layered metal made of magnesium and bismuth is said to come from Roswell, New Mexico, where a strange craft is reported to have crashed in 1947. Michels passes on what he was told: an army officer going through his grandfather's archives found the sample, and "written in the diary was that it was a piece from uh Roswell". The physicist Hal Puthoff tells it a little differently. He says it "was sent anonymously by someone claiming to be an army officer". In another version Michels makes the grandfather a colonel in the Roswell cleanup and says the piece sat in a safe. The sample is now with Garry Nolan, a Stanford scientist, and Michels says he saw it during a visit to Nolan's lab. Elsewhere Michels says the bismuth layers are "less than a human hair" thick, and that "nowhere could we find any evidence that anybody ever made one of these". He also links the piece to the researcher Jacques Vallée and guesses that it might allow magnetic levitation. If the story holds, it would be a physical scrap of a craft no one on Earth knows how to build.
bismuth-recurring-at-s4-1988: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that bismuth, a heavy metal, keeps coming up in UFO stories. He says there is a reason Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked on alien craft in the late 1980s at S4, a secret site in the Nevada desert, kept hearing about it there. In another episode Michels just calls it a common theme in UFO lore and does not mention S4. If true, it would suggest bismuth plays some real part in how these craft work.
bissell-mentions-the-1933-magenta-crash: The story goes that in June 1933 a disc-shaped craft came down near Magenta, a town in northern Italy. An economist and former presidential adviser, Harold Malmgren, says he heard of it from Richard Bissell, a senior CIA figure, who told him that this did not start last week and mentioned 1933 Magenta. A whistleblower, David Grusch, says it was the first recovery of such a craft in Europe and that a partly intact vehicle was found. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, repeats these accounts many times. He describes a disc about 10 to 12 meters across, a news blackout under the dictator Mussolini, and the craft later being sent to the United States, in one version through the Vatican. A former Air Force officer, Robert Salas, points to a new book by the Italian researcher Roberto Pinotti, which he says shows documents proving it, and says Mussolini put the radio inventor Guglielmo Marconi in charge of studying the craft. The tellers add different details, and Michels himself once calls it hypothetical. If true, it would mean governments were secretly holding unknown craft more than a decade before the famous Roswell case of 1947.
bissell-places-area-51-at-the-nevada-nuc: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Richard Bissell, a US intelligence official, founded Area 51, the secret Air Force test base in Nevada, in 1955. According to Michels, Bissell chose to put it at the Nevada test site, where hundreds of atomic bombs were being tested in the early 1950s. If true, it would mean the base was hidden on purpose inside one of the most closed-off areas in the country.
bissell-returns-to-the-cia-after-his-ous: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells of Richard Bissell, a senior official at the CIA, the US foreign spy agency, who was pushed out around 1961. Michels says the rumor was that Bissell left work at CIA headquarters in Langley, Virginia, on a Friday and was back on Monday, because he was too indispensable to certain secret activities. Michels raises it while asking whether a hidden program to recover crashed UFOs existed, since it would suggest such work went on out of sight.
black-ball-darting-around-the-security-t: Mario Woods, who in 1977 was a guard at a nuclear missile site called November-5 near Nisland, South Dakota, tells a podcast host, Jesse Michels, that a black ball came out of nowhere and darted around his security truck. In one telling he says it was about six times the size of a beach ball and seemed to have vents on it; in another he puts it at four to six feet across. He names a fellow guard, Michael Johnson, as part of the story, which would mean something unknown was taking an interest in America's nuclear weapons.
black-ball-of-no-light-formed-by-the-emi: Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked on alien craft in the late 1980s at S4, a secret site in the Nevada desert, told this to podcast host Jesse Michels. He says that when a part of the craft he calls the emitter was turned, it made a little black ball in the air from which no light escaped, like a tiny black hole, and he mentions a man named Barry Castilio. If true, it would mean the craft could bend light and space in ways no known machine can.
black-sites-staffed-by-refugees-who-didn: A man named Michael Herrera, speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast, passed on what he says someone told him about black sites, meaning secret government facilities. According to Herrera, these places are run by their own people, including refugees from other countries who applied under a refugee category he calls P3 and didn't make the cut, and who now work there as janitors, cooks and maintenance staff. If true, the secret sites would have a hidden workforce of their own, outside public view.
black-suvs-helicopters-and-a-30-ft-hole-: A man named Brett Lanner tells a podcast host, Jesse Michels, about going in 1999 to Hart Canyon near Aztec, New Mexico, a place where a craft is said to have crashed long ago. He says there were black SUVs and helicopters around, and that they came across a round hole about 30 feet deep and 30 feet wide. If true, it would suggest someone was still digging at the site decades later.
black-widow-night-fighters-redeployed-to: A researcher, John Brandenburg, told podcast host Jesse Michels about something he says he found while looking into Roswell, a town in New Mexico where, according to many people, something strange crashed in 1947. Brandenburg says that the military moved Black Widows, a night fighter plane from World War II, to patrol the skies around Roswell, and he points to a source called Cosmic Awakening. If true, it would suggest the military was guarding the area against something in the air.
blacked-out-blue-van-to-an-underground-t: Dan Sherman, a former sergeant who says the NSA, the US National Security Agency that handles code-breaking and eavesdropping, hired him to communicate with aliens, tells a podcast host, Jesse Michels, about his training in the early 1990s. He says he and others rode in an unmarked blue van with blacked-out windows from a facility in Maryland to an underground school, and he names a Captain White as involved. If true, it would mean the government was quietly training people to talk to non-human beings.
blacked-out-bus-ride-south-to-s-4-1988: Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked on alien craft in 1988 and 1989, says he was taken by bus from Area 51, a secret US Air Force base in Nevada, south to an even more hidden site called S-4. According to Lazar, it was a long, bumpy ride and the bus windows were blacked out, so workers could not see where they were going.
blacker-than-black-floating-sphere: A congressman, Eric Burlison, passes on what a man told him. The man served in special forces and says that while overseas during the wars he was brought into a room where a sphere, blacker than black, hovered in the air. He says it gave off a feeling of complete evil and darkness. Told this way, it hints that something not human, and not friendly, is being held or met in secret.
blacker-than-black-holes-above-the-insul: Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked on alien craft in 1988 and 1989 at S-4, a secret site in Nevada, describes holes above a part of a craft he calls the insulator ring. He says they looked blacker than black, like bottomless pits, though he knew they were solid, and he mentions a man named Barry. He tells it as one of the strange details he says he saw up close.
blackhawk-near-miss-with-low-flying-f-4-: Greg Rogers, a doctor who served as an Army flight surgeon, a doctor who flies with and looks after aircrews, tells a podcast host, Jesse Michels, about a flight in Germany near the Rhine River valley. He says he was in a Blackhawk, an Army helicopter, when an F-4 Phantom fighter jet came through flying very low. Rogers says they nearly died because of what the jet's pilot had done.
blanchard-boy-did-we-screw-up-1947: A researcher, John Brandenburg, told podcast host Jesse Michels what he says Roswell veterans passed on about Colonel Blanchard, an officer at the army airfield in Roswell, New Mexico, where something was said to have crashed in 1947. According to Brandenburg, when Blanchard was asked about the event later, all he would do was laugh and say, "Boy, did we screw up." Brandenburg tells it because it would mean the officer in charge admitted the official handling of the crash went wrong.
bledsoe-and-grusch-videos-throttled-on-y: A podcast host, Danny Jones, told fellow host Jesse Michels about two interviews from around 2023 to 2025: his own with Chris Bledsoe, a man who says he has had UFO encounters, and Michels's with David Grusch, a former intelligence official turned whistleblower. Jones says the videos seemed to be held back from viewers on YouTube, and that a contact at Google, which owns YouTube, told him neither video broke any rules or raised any internal red flags. If true, something other than the normal rules was keeping those videos from being seen.
bledsoe-drawing-cell-diagrams-for-taylor: Chris Bledsoe is a carpenter from North Carolina who says he has had strange experiences. He told a podcast host, Jesse Michels, that between about 2008 and 2011 a team linked to a man named Timothy Taylor sent him scientific papers to read at night, and his job was to draw whatever came to him, including diagrams of cells. He mentions Taylor and a scholar named Diana Pasulka in telling it, and if true it would mean researchers took his visions seriously enough to put them to work.
bledsoe-group-films-moving-dots-weeks-la: Eric Burles, speaking as a witness on Jesse Michels's podcast, describes something a man named Chris Bledsoe and his group did in the 2020s on the lawn of the US Capitol in Washington. Burles says that a few weeks after he had been there with them, the group went back without him, did exactly the same thing, and this time filmed dots moving in the sky. If true, it would suggest these sightings can be brought about on purpose.
bledsoe-memoir-names-taylor-as-a-nasa-in: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that a memoir by Chris Bledsoe, a North Carolina man he calls a "super experiencer" because of the many encounters with unexplained beings he reports, openly names a man called Timothy Taylor as an insider at NASA, the US space agency. According to Michels, Taylor befriended Bledsoe after those encounters in the 2010s. Michels raises it to back up another person's account of Taylor, since if true it would tie a space agency insider to people who report such contact.
bledsoe-prophecy-of-missiles-fired-at-ir: Chris Bledsoe, a North Carolina man who says he has had many UFO encounters, says a being he calls the Lady warned him in 2012 about missiles, and he wrote in his book, UFO of God, about a future time when Iran and Israel fire missiles at each other. He ties the timing to a sign in the sky: the blue star Regulus appearing red on the horizon at dawn, in the gaze of the Sphinx at Egypt's pyramids. Bob McGwier, an engineer who has worked with Bledsoe, retells it as a vision of missiles fired at Iran being stopped by these beings, around Easter 2026, which would mean non-human beings are stepping into human wars.
bledsoe-s-craft-bigger-inside-than-outsi: A UFO researcher, Grant Cameron, told podcast host Jesse Michels about an experience of Chris Bledsoe, a man in North Carolina who says he has had UFO encounters. Cameron says that Bledsoe describes a craft about 30 feet across on the outside, but when he looked inside, it seemed the size of a football field. If true, the craft would be bending space in a way nothing we build can.
bledsoe-told-that-rockets-fail-because-t: A YouTuber, Chris Ramsay, told podcast host Jesse Michels what he heard from Chris Bledsoe, a man who says he has had UFO encounters since around 2007: Bledsoe asked whether failed rockets carried weapons, was told yes, and said that is why they don't work, because "they" don't want them to. Bledsoe, telling it himself, credits a man named Timothy Taylor and says rather that the UFOs come up to look at every launch that has weapons on board. If true, someone not human would be keeping watch over weapons going into space.
bledsoe-tries-to-call-in-uap-on-capitol-: Eric Burles, who speaks as a witness, told podcast host Jesse Michels about going with Chris Bledsoe, a man who says he can call in UAP, the government's term for UFOs, to the lawn of the US Capitol in Washington sometime in the 2020s. Burles says Bledsoe "did his thing" while he sat quietly and waited. The story matters because, if true, it would mean such craft respond to a person's call, even at the seat of Congress.
blessed-animal-bladders-hung-on-the-fenc: Brandon Fugal owns Skinwalker Ranch, a property in Utah known for reports of strange happenings. He told a podcast host, Jesse Michels, that around 2016 he found that Native Americans had been hanging animal bladders along the ranch's fence line and blessing them, and he connects this to the security staff who worked there under an earlier owner named Bigelow. If true, it would suggest that local people treated the land as something that needed spiritual guarding.
blink-182-bandmate-had-intelligence-comm: A man named Jay Anderson, speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast, passed on something about the rock band Blink-182, whose member Tom DeLonge he cites. Anderson says that another member of the band had family members in the intelligence community, meaning the government's spy agencies. He tells it because, if true, it would tie the band to the secret world it has been linked with.
blitch-backs-randy-anderson-s-crane-stor: A scientist named John Blitch, who worked with DARPA, the Pentagon's advanced research agency, told podcast host Jesse Michels about a man named Randy Anderson and his story about Crane, a Navy weapons research base in Indiana. Blitch says that he met Anderson through David Grusch, a former intelligence official turned whistleblower, and that he believes every part of Anderson's story. If true, a serious scientist is vouching for an account of strange events at a military site.
blitch-has-been-inside-several-undergrou: John Blitch is a former military scientist who says he was once taken by an alien. On a podcast with host Jesse Michels he says he has been inside several underground military facilities, though he gives no dates or places. It matters to his story because it would mean he has seen hidden sites that few people ever get to see.
blitch-s-brief-saic-tenure-never-read-in: John Blitch, a former military scientist who says he was taken by an alien, told a podcast host, Jesse Michels, that he worked briefly in 2001 at SAIC, a large defense contractor, in Littleton, Colorado. He says he was never "read in" there, meaning he was never formally let into any secret programme, and he names a man called Art Morris in telling it. He tells it to make clear what he did and did not have access to.
blitch-vets-barber-s-four-man-team-on-hi: John Blitch, a former military scientist who says he was taken by an alien, told a podcast host, Jesse Michels, that around 2024 or 2025 he had a four-man team linked to a man named Jake Barber out on his boat. He says he was checking them, looking for places where their accounts did not match each other. If true, it would mean their stories held up under his own private questioning.
blog-post-predicting-that-within-a-decad: Deep Prasad, a young researcher interested in how UFOs might work, says he wrote a blog post called "Curiosity as a Time Capsule." In it, he says, he predicted that within about ten years, so by around 2032, people will accept that humans are not the only intelligent, even super intelligent, life on Earth.
blood-on-pillow-after-1988-camping-trip: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, is interviewing Richard Barth, a man who guarded nuclear missiles and says he was abducted by aliens. Michels recalls Barth saying that after a camping trip in 1988 he woke up with blood on his pillow. The detail is told as a possible sign that something was done to him in the night.
blown-out-of-a-special-electronics-helic: Joe McMoneagle, a former Army soldier, told a podcast host, Jesse Michels, that in late 1967 near Pleiku in Vietnam he was riding in a special electronics helicopter when it was hit in the belly by an RPG, a shoulder-fired rocket grenade. He says the blast blew the helicopter apart and threw him out. It is part of the story of his own life and what he says he survived.
blue-beings-appearing-at-joe-dispenza-s-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, passes on what Joe Dispenza, a man who runs large meditation retreats, says happens at them. According to Michels, Dispenza says that in his deep meditations blue beings show up in the room and tell him the people at the event need to "vibrate higher" so the beings can fully appear and heal them. If true, it would tie contact with other beings to the state of people's minds.
blue-book-closed-in-1969-citing-condon: Robert Salas, a former US Air Force officer, says that when the Air Force shut down Project Blue Book, its UFO study of the 1950s and 60s, in 1969, it pointed to the Condon investigation, a scientific study of UFOs led by physicist Edward Condon, as its reason. He tells it to suggest the closing was a way for the Air Force to get out of the subject.
blue-book-heads-grow-increasingly-anti-u: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that every head of Project Blue Book, the US Air Force's UFO study of the 1950s and 60s, became more and more against UFOs from 1952 until the project ended in 1969. In another episode he tells it a bit differently, saying the Air Force used Blue Book on purpose to sideline the UFO question. If true, it would mean the official study was steered away from taking the subject seriously.
blue-book-kecksburg-material-sent-to-pro: A UFO researcher, Grant Cameron, told podcast host Jesse Michels about a 1965 case at Kecksburg, a small town in Pennsylvania where an object was said to have come down. Cameron says that files from Project Blue Book, the US Air Force's UFO study of the 1950s and 60s, include one saying material was sent to something code-named Project Greengrass, which he looked up and says is Mount Weather, a government site in Virginia. If true, whatever was found was handed to a secret place far from the public study.
blue-book-landing-case-with-an-alien-foo: James Fox, a UFO investigator, says that in the files of Project Blue Book, the US Air Force's UFO study of the 1950s and 60s, now kept at the National Archives, there is a case of a craft landing. According to Fox, the first military officer on the scene drew a diagram of the alien's footprints, which would mean the military itself recorded a visitor on the ground.
blue-book-s-robert-friend-sees-the-chann: A UFO researcher, Grant Cameron, told podcast host Jesse Michels about a July 1959 meeting in Washington, described in an 11-page memo, where people tried to contact beings through channeling, meaning speaking with them through a person in a trance. Cameron says that Robert Friend, an officer from Project Blue Book, the US Air Force's UFO study of the 1950s and 60s, saw the session alongside a man named Arthur Lundahl, but a general then said another agency had the matter, hands off, and nothing more was heard. If true, another part of the government was quietly handling UFO contact while the Air Force study was told to stay out.
blue-book-special-report-14-contradicts-: A researcher speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast points to Project Blue Book Special Report 14, a 1950s statistical study made inside Blue Book, the US Air Force's UFO study of the 1950s and 60s. The guest, echoing the researcher Stanton Friedman, says that if you read the report's actual data table, something like 21 percent of almost a thousand cases were left unknown, which does not match how the report was presented to the public. If true, it would mean the official message played down what the data showed.
blue-dwarfs-drag-a-man-behind-a-curtain-: Whitley Strieber, a writer known for describing his own encounters with beings he believes are not human, told this to podcast host Jesse Michels. He says that in the 1970s, at a shop he calls the "horror store" near West 55th Street in Manhattan, between 7th Avenue and Broadway, he saw a man in a brown suit trying to get out from behind a curtain while blue dwarfs pulled him back. He mentions Anne Strieber in the story, and tells it as a sign that such beings move among us.
blue-energy-humanoid-takes-rossi-in-his-: Dave Rossi says that beings taught him advanced physics. On a podcast with host Jesse Michels he says that around 2021, at his home, he was taken in his sleep by what he calls a blue energy type humanoid. He told the same thing on a later episode, though there he gave no date or setting, and if true it would be the start of his contact with something not human.
blue-extraterrestrial-manifesting-physic: Jeffrey Mishlove, a researcher with a doctorate who studies the mind and the paranormal, passes on what a man named Robin Foy told him about séances held in Scole, England, in the 1990s. According to Mishlove, Foy said a blue extraterrestrial being would appear in the room so physically that he could touch it. If true, it would link contact with other beings to spirit séances.
blue-winged-angel-uap-over-barber-s-hous: Jake Barber, a helicopter pilot who says he once helped retrieve a UFO, told podcast host Jesse Michels that an unidentified object shows up over his house. He says his family calls it "the angel" because it looks blue and seems to have wings. He does not say when this happens.
bluegill-recovery-of-spherical-debris-in: In October 1962 the United States set off a nuclear bomb high above Johnston Atoll, a tiny island in the Pacific, in a test called Bluegill Triple Prime. Harold Malmgren, who is described as an adviser to four presidents, says the test report stated that the blast knocked down a "device", and that the Navy recovered it after it fell into the ocean. He says he was refused more information, went to Albuquerque to see for himself, and held the pieces in his hands. If true, something unknown was watching a nuclear test, and the US government kept what fell. A man named Kurt McConnell says Malmgren was told directly by a man named Richard Bissell that a UFO watching the test had been downed by accident. A researcher, Jeff Cruickshank, says the recovery shows up in the ships' deck logs, the daily records a ship keeps, and that a spherical piece of debris with unusual properties was found. A retired Navy admiral, Tim Gallaudet, says he co-wrote that deck-log study, though he calls it only a partial recovery of the object or something related to it, and Ross Coulthart cites an analysis by Douglas Dean Johnson that he says backs Malmgren up. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, retells the story across many episodes, and the tellers differ mostly on who Malmgren's source was and how much was recovered.
bluegill-triple-prime-as-a-proto-sdi-x-r: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, discusses Bluegill Triple Prime, a US project from 1962 and 1963. Citing a paper from the RAND Corporation, a government-funded research group, and someone named Malmgren, he suggests it was an early form of an X-ray shield against missiles, a forerunner of the Strategic Defense Initiative, the later US plan to defend against nuclear missiles from space. If true, it would mean that kind of defence was being tried decades earlier than people think.
bluegill-triple-prime-as-missile-defense: Podcast host Jesse Michels repeats what a man named Malmgren told him about Bluegill Triple Prime, a high-altitude nuclear test over the Pacific in 1962. According to Michels, Malmgren said the test was really a defense against Russian long-range nuclear missiles, and he points to a paper from the RAND Corporation, a US defense research group, and to the Institute for Defense Analysis. The story links it to the Strategic Defense Initiative, a later US plan to shield the country from missiles, which would make the test an early missile shield if true.
bluegill-triple-prime-led-to-excalibur-a: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says there is a direct link between a set of 1962 tests called Bluegill Triple Prime and the Strategic Defense Initiative, a space weapons plan of the 1980s under President Ronald Reagan, nicknamed Star Wars, and he ties the physicist Edward Teller in. A researcher who goes by UAPGerb argues that parts of that plan, a program on lethality and target hardening and another on particle beam weapons, were meant to use space-based microwave weapons to shoot down UFOs. If true, it would mean a huge public defence effort was partly aimed at unknown craft.
bluegill-triple-prime-object-tumbles-fro: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells of a US nuclear test called Bluegill Triple Prime, set off just before midnight around 25 October 1962 at Johnston Atoll, a small island in the Pacific. Drawing on a researcher named Jeff Cruickshank, he says that witnesses on a ship, and film shot from two aircraft called Kettle 1 and Kettle 2, show a bright, fiery object tumbling out of the blast cloud. In some tellings he adds that the footage still exists, that one cleaned-up version has a white triangle laid over the object, and that others, including Harald Malmgren, Tim Gallaudet and Navy ship logs, back it up; if true, it would mean something unknown was watching nuclear tests.
bluegill-video-sanitized-with-superimpos: Podcast host Jesse Michels relays a claim from a man named Jeff Kushank about film of Bluegill Triple Prime, a 1962 US nuclear test at Johnston Atoll, a remote island. Kushank says the film showed a UFO and was later censored by laying a white triangle over the spot where it appeared, which would mean the government hid a UFO at a nuclear test. In a later episode Michels tells it a bit differently, naming the footage Kettle 1 and saying the triangle was added in 1998, when the film was cleared for public release, by the Defense Special Weapons Agency, a Pentagon nuclear weapons agency, then led by Byron Ristvet.
bob-baker-mitre-paper-on-ning-li-s-ac-dc: A researcher, Dave Rossi, told podcast host Jesse Michels about a paper from the 2000s by a man named Bob Baker, written under MITRE, a research organisation that works for the US government, for a conference on high-frequency gravitational waves. Rossi says that the paper deals with the work of a physicist, Ning Li, on what is called AC/DC gravity, the idea of producing gravity-like effects with electricity. He raises it because, if true, it would show serious research into controlling gravity.
bob-ballard-s-search-for-atlantis: On a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, a former US Secretary of Energy named John Herrington talks about the hunt for Atlantis, the legendary lost city, which he says some now place in the Red Sea. He says a consultant named Bob Ballard, who works with a Navy school at an institute in Connecticut, is involved in that search. If it were true, a lost city of legend might finally be found under the sea.
bob-beck-at-ossining-during-the-space-ki: An unnamed researcher, speaking on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, tells of a man named Bob Beck who, the guest says, was almost certainly working for the CIA, the US spy agency. According to the guest, Beck was in Ossining, New York, in the 1970s at the very time of the so-called space kids experiments, tests involving children said to have unusual contact abilities. The guest raises it to suggest the intelligence world was quietly watching that work.
bob-beckwith-philadelphia-experiment-and: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that a man named Robert Beckwith claims he was somewhat involved in the Philadelphia Experiment, a rumored US Navy test from the 1940s. Michels adds that Beckwith later did interesting work with extremely strong magnetic fields and with teleportation, meaning moving things instantly from one place to another. If true, it would tie those rumored wartime experiments to real, ongoing research.
bob-brier-s-examination-suggests-tutankh: A researcher named Luke Caverns, speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast, talks about Tutankhamun, a young king of ancient Egypt. He says a Dr. Bob Brier examined the king's body, maybe in the 1990s, and found that the way blood had pooled at the back of the skull looked like he had been hit on the back of the head. If so, the boy king may not have died a natural death.
bob-jahn-from-boeing-plasma-physics-to-t: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Bob Jahn was a plasma physicist, a scientist who studies superheated electrically charged gas, and worked at the aircraft company Boeing. According to Michels, Jahn went on to run the PEAR lab at Princeton University, a lab that studied the paranormal. He tells it to show that a serious mainstream scientist took these questions on.
bob-jahn-s-random-event-generator-resear: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says a researcher spent some 40 years working with random event generators, machines that spit out random numbers, to try to prove that the human mind can affect matter. He links this work to Robert Jahn and the Princeton Engineering Anomalies Research lab, which studied such effects, and in another episode he points to a book about it by Herb Mertz of that lab. If true, it would mean thought alone can nudge the physical world.
bob-lazar-at-mit-possibly-placed-for-def: A researcher named Eric Weinstein, speaking on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, says his sense is that a man named Bob Lazar was placed at MIT, the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, or at research labs linked to it, to work on something defense related, possibly in the early 1990s. Lazar himself, in a later episode, says plainly that he was sent there, and he puts it before 1988 rather than in the 1990s. If so, it would mean Lazar was quietly working for the military in some way.
bob-lazar-at-s4-1989: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says there is only one Bob Lazar: a man who says that in 1989, at S4, a secret site in the Nevada desert, he worked on the craft itself. Michels tells it to show how rare it is for anyone to claim they handled a non-human craft with their own hands.
bob-lazar-briefed-on-project-looking-gla: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked on alien craft at a secret site in Nevada, was briefed on something called Project Looking Glass. Michels does not say what the project was. He tells it twice in the same episode, and one version puts it in Nevada in the late 1980s, while the other gives no time or place.
bob-lazar-on-parallel-engineering: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, talks about Bob Lazar, a man who says he once worked on alien craft at a secret site in the US. Michels says that if you talk to Lazar long enough, it turns out the work was not really copying the craft, which is called reverse engineering, but more like building similar machines alongside them, which he calls parallel engineering, an idea he also ties to Tom DeLonge, a musician behind a UFO book series called Sekret Machines. If true, it would mean the US was learning from alien technology and making its own versions.
bob-lazar-s-claim-of-reverse-engineering: This is the story of Bob Lazar, a man who said he worked on alien craft for the US government. According to Lazar, in the late 1980s he worked at a place called S4, a secret site near Area 51, the highly secret military base in the Nevada desert. He says his job was to reverse engineer, meaning take apart and figure out, the propulsion system of a craft not made by human hands. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, retells this many times, adding that Lazar went public on TV in 1989, with the help of a journalist, George Knapp, and a pilot named John Lear. Michels also repeats how Lazar says he was recruited: after strapping a jet engine onto a Honda and meeting the physicist Edward Teller by chance. The talk show host Joe Rogan stresses Lazar's descriptions of craft that bend gravity around themselves, and points to a documentary by the filmmaker Jeremy Corbell, while a neuroscientist, Andrew Gallimore, recalls being struck by Lazar on Rogan's show. If true, it would mean the government holds a working non-human craft and has studied it for decades.
bob-lazar-s-sport-model-grown-out-of-the: Salvatore Pais, a Navy scientist who holds patents on unusual craft designs, says on Jesse Michels's podcast that Bob Lazar once described a craft he calls the "sport model" as if it had been grown out of the vacuum of empty space itself. In another telling, Pais recalls Lazar's words as the craft being "3D printed" in our space and time, ties this to a secret site Lazar calls S-4 in 1989, and says it is exactly what his own equation for a single unifying force describes. If true, it would hint that such a craft was built from the fabric of space rather than ordinary materials.
bob-lazar-walks-underneath-the-craft-198: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, asks his guest, the UFO researcher Grant Cameron, about Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked on alien craft in 1989 at a secret site called S-4 in Nevada. Michels's question is what happened in Lazar's account when he walked underneath one of the craft. It matters because, if Lazar's story is true, people at S-4 were handling a real non-human vehicle.
bob-maguire-measures-his-girlfriend-s-im: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says he interviewed a man named Bob Maguire, whose girlfriend has an implant in her head. According to Michels, Maguire held an RF detector, a device that picks up radio signals, over her head and could measure the frequency coming out of it. If true, it would mean the implant is an active device sending out a signal.
bob-s-letter-from-nixon-thanking-him-for: Grant Cameron, a UFO researcher, tells of a man he calls Bob, in Los Angeles in the 1970s, who caused a stir because he had a letter from President Richard Nixon. According to Cameron, the letter said, "Thank you for your cooperation on the project we're working on," and people such as the journalist Linda Howe and a researcher named Larry Bryant were part of the story. If true, it would hint that a president personally knew about a secret project Bob was part of.
bobby-fischer-s-claim-that-russian-parap: A surgeon named Italo Venturelli, speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast, says the chess champion Bobby Fischer kept complaining that the Russians interfered with his games around 1974. According to Venturelli, Fischer said that while he played, the Russians brought in gurus, parapsychologists who study mind powers, to work on him. If true, it would mean a government used mental powers as a weapon at the chess board.
bobby-ray-inman-acknowledges-the-nationa: A retired Navy admiral, Tim Gallaudet, who was once the Navy's head oceanographer, says he heard via a researcher named Sam Gerbus that a man named Bobby Ray Inman had spoken of a National Underwater Reconnaissance Office, a body watching what happens under the sea. Gallaudet says Inman basically confirmed it was real, yet in all his years with access to secret undersea programs he had never heard of it. If true, it would mean a hidden office exists to watch the oceans.
bobby-ray-inman-refers-bob-oechsler-to-s: Around 1988 or 1989, a senior official named Bobby Ray Inman is said to have spoken with Bob Oechsler, a UFO researcher described as a NASA mission specialist, NASA being the US space agency. A researcher who goes by UAPGerb says Inman pointed Oechsler toward Sumner Shapiro, the director of naval intelligence, and a man named R. Evans Hineman. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells it differently, saying that on the call Inman hinted that the UFO subject might come out into the open someday. It is told as a sign that people high in US intelligence knew about UFO matters.
bobby-ray-inman-tape-recorded-at-the-ida: A researcher named Grant Cameron, on Jesse Michels's podcast, mentions a tape recording of a man named Bobby Ray Inman being asked questions about UFOs. Cameron says the recording was made at the Institute for Defense Analyses, a US defence research organisation. To Cameron, the tape is a key piece because of how Inman responded when those questions were put to him.
boebert-asks-about-hybrid-program-at-hea: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that during a hearing in the US Congress in the 2020s, Congresswoman Lauren Boebert asked about hybrids, meaning a programme said to mix human and alien beings. Michels says it was a really weird moment in the testimony. He tells it because it would mean the idea has reached the floor of Congress.
bondi-and-negative-mass-at-the-1957-chap: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, drawing on the researcher Eric Weinstein, tells of a 1957 physics conference in Chapel Hill, North Carolina, where the study of quantum gravity, the attempt to join gravity with the physics of tiny particles, got its start. He says an Austrian mathematician there named Hermann Bondi talked about negative mass, a strange kind of matter that would behave the opposite way to normal matter under gravity. Michels raises it because, if the idea held, it could point toward new ways of moving craft.
