bones-on-religion-humans-and-aliens-part: Dan Sherman is a former Air Force sergeant who says a US intelligence agency hired him to communicate with aliens. He told a podcast host, Jesse Michels, that in the early 1990s, at a place he calls Base 2, a being he calls Bones talked about religion and said that humans and aliens are part of the same creation. If true, it would mean the beings themselves see us as made by the same hand.
bonnybridge-ufo-hotspot-and-stepfather-s: Gary McKinnon, a computer hacker, tells Jesse Michels's podcast that his stepfather used to live in Falkirk, near the Scottish town of Bonnybridge. McKinnon says Bonnybridge is a Scottish UFO hotspot with so many sightings that it is almost a tourist attraction, with people going there to see UFOs. He tells it as part of how his family came to take sightings seriously.
book-of-enoch-cut-from-the-tanakh: A philosopher named Jason Jorjani says that an ancient text called the Book of Enoch, first found in Ethiopia, preserves a backstory to a short passage in Genesis, the first book of the Bible. He says Enoch was once part of the Tanakh, the Hebrew Bible, and was later cut out of it. If true, it would mean part of the original religious story was deliberately removed.
book-of-enoch-excluded-but-holding-truth: Dylan Borland, a former serviceman who says a top government official told him aliens run everything, told a podcast host, Jesse Michels, about the Book of Enoch, an ancient religious text left out of most Bibles. He says that, according to Catholic teaching as explained by Malachi Martin, a Catholic writer he describes as one of the first people to read the Dead Sea Scrolls, the book was left out yet still holds truth. He raises it because it would tie old scripture to his account of beings beyond us.
book-of-enoch-watchers-mating-with-human: This story comes from the Book of Enoch, an ancient religious text. It tells of beings called the Watchers who came down to Earth and had children with human women, and those children were giants. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, brings it up while talking about ancient times, quoting the line that there were giants on the earth in those days. The talk show host Joe Rogan tells it too, calling the offspring the Nephilim. Rogan reads it as a story of genetic engineering by visitors, and credits a US congresswoman, Anna Paulina Luna, with raising it. If read that way, it would mean old scriptures remember outside beings mixing with humanity.
book-of-job-as-a-deliberate-mithraic-kab: A researcher and author named Jason Jorjani argues in his book Iranian Leviathan that the Book of Job in the Bible was written on purpose as a text mixing Mithraic ideas, from the worship of the Persian god Mithra, with Kabbalistic ones, from Jewish mysticism. He says it ties back to the Magi, Persian priests in the ancient Achaemenid Persian Empire, who he says were involved in rebuilding Israel, which he calls the first Zionist project in history. If so, a famous biblical book would carry a hidden Persian design.
book-of-revelation-people-who-cannot-die: Tim Alberino, who says he took part in the capture of a giant in Afghanistan, talks on Jesse Michels's podcast about the Book of Revelation, the last book of the Christian Bible. He says that, in its account of the end times, as disaster falls on Earth there is a group of people who cannot die. He raises it as something that might connect to the beings he describes.
book-of-the-watchers-dated-to-around-300: A researcher named Tim Alberino says on Jesse Michels's podcast that the Book of the Watchers, the oldest part of an ancient Jewish text called 1 Enoch, was written at least around 300 BC. That section tells the tale of beings called the Watchers. He tells it to show how old the story is.
book-s-claim-of-alien-contact-at-bentwat: A UFO investigator and filmmaker, James Fox, talks about a book called Left at East Gate, which claims there was actual contact with aliens in 1980 at Bentwaters, an air base in England. Fox says the men who were there, including Charles Halt, Jim Penniston and John Burroughs, dispute that claim. It matters because, if true, it would be a case of face-to-face contact at a military base.
book-that-foretold-the-texas-tower-snipe: An author on occult and intelligence history, Peter Levenda, says on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels that there was a book which described the Texas Tower sniper, a 1966 shooting from a tower in Texas, before it ever happened. He tells it as a strange case of something written down seemingly foreseeing a real event.
boomerang-shaped-craft-over-tucson: A scientist named Eric Davis, asked on a podcast whether he has ever seen anything himself, says he and his wife did, in Tucson, Arizona. He says it was broad daylight and they saw a craft shaped like a boomerang flying lower than the height where planes normally circle to land. It is told as a personal sighting by someone who studies these questions for a living.
bootsie-galbraith-sees-a-ufo-called-in-b: Whitley Strieber, a writer known for describing his own encounters with beings, passes on what a woman named Bootsie Galbraith told him. He says that in the 1990s she was in Mexico with Steven Greer, a man who says he can summon UFOs, and that Greer called one in and everyone there saw it. If true, it would mean people can call these craft on purpose.
booze-fighters-take-over-hollister-steal: Dr. John Brandenburg, a scientist, tells Jesse Michels's podcast that in 1947 a motorcycle gang of World War veterans called the Booze Fighters took over the town of Hollister, California, for a day and threw a drunken party downtown. He says the name was a play on "foo fighters", the term wartime pilots used for strange lights in the sky. In his telling, the story stole the headlines that year, pulling attention away from UFO news.
borderland-society-knew-of-ufo-crashes-b: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that the Borderland Society, an occult research group active in the 1940s, knew about certain UFO crashes and sightings before the US Army or Air Force did, and that there are documents to show it. He credits a researcher named Richard Geldreich with uncovering this, and in one telling says the group learned of these crashes through remote viewing, the practice of trying to see distant places with the mind. If true, it would mean a small private circle was ahead of the military on the earliest UFO events.
borland-claims-first-hand-knowledge-of-c: A man named Dylan Borland, speaking on a podcast, says he has direct, first-hand knowledge of the recovery of crashed craft, of efforts to take their technology apart to learn how it works, and of building that technology into other things. The story's title adds that he claims to know about the craft's power source. If true, it would mean someone with inside access is describing a hidden recovery programme.
borland-goes-to-the-icig-after-grusch-te: Dylan Borland, a former serviceman who says a top government official told him aliens run everything, told a podcast host, Jesse Michels, what he did in 2023. He says that after David Grusch, a former intelligence officer, testified before Congress about hidden programmes, Borland went with his attorney to the ICIG, the internal watchdog for the US intelligence agencies. If true, it would mean he formally put his own account on the record with the government.
borland-on-stage-will-neither-confirm-no: Dylan Borland, a man who says he has inside knowledge of recovered craft, recalls being asked on stage at a live event about something called Project Rubik's Cube, which the telling does not explain. He says he would neither confirm nor deny it, and told the questioner to ask for receipts, meaning proof, for whistleblowers. It matters because it shows him declining to back, or rule out, a claim others were discussing.
borland-pulls-aaro-reports-on-baiting-cr: Dylan Borland, a man who says he worked inside the US government, says that in 2023, through access tied to the Defense Threat Reduction Agency, a Pentagon agency that deals with weapons threats, he could search government files. He says he began pulling reports and briefings from AARO, the Pentagon office set up to look into unexplained objects in the sky, about how to lure in unknown craft and bring them down. If true, it would mean the government has plans for catching such craft.
borland-s-alleged-classified-drawing-of-: Jeremy Corbell, a filmmaker who makes UFO documentaries, said on Jesse Michels' podcast in 2026 that people at the ODNI, the office that oversees all US spy agencies, told him something about a witness named Dylan Borland. According to Corbell, Borland made a drawing of something like a hieroglyph, and the drawing was kept classified. If true, it would mean a government witness had recorded writing or symbols from something not made by people.
borland-s-alleged-classified-icig-drawin: Jeremy Corbell, a filmmaker who makes UFO documentaries, said on Jesse Michels' podcast in 2026 that a witness named Dylan Borland gave secret testimony to the ICIG, the internal watchdog that takes complaints from US intelligence workers. Corbell says he was told that Borland drew the triangle-shaped craft he saw, and also drew a pyramid-shaped power source. If true, it would point to the government knowing how such a craft is powered.
borland-s-congressional-testimony-on-the: Dylan Borland, a former serviceman, read out to a podcast host, Jesse Michels, the testimony he says he gave to Congress in 2025. In it he says that in the summer of 2012, while his team was on standby for weather, he went back to his barracks at Langley, a military base in Virginia, and at about 1:30 in the morning saw a triangle about 100 feet on each side lift off from near the NASA hangar there. If true, it would mean a large unknown craft was flying from inside a US base.
bormann-alive-in-argentina-cashing-check: A researcher and writer named Jason Jorjani says that Martin Bormann, a top Nazi official and Hitler's close aide, did not die at the end of World War Two in 1945 but escaped to Buenos Aires, Argentina, in the time of the Argentine leader Juan Perón. Jorjani says that as late as the 1960s Bormann was cashing checks written in his own name through the big American bank Chase, now JP Morgan Chase. If true, it would mean a leading Nazi lived openly abroad for decades with help from the banking world.
born-next-to-the-army-s-first-nuclear-te: John Blitch, a former military scientist who says he was taken by an alien, told a podcast host, Jesse Michels, that he grew up in Idaho Falls, Idaho, in the late 1950s and early 1960s. He says he was born next to a nuclear test reactor the Army had started up there. He tells it as part of his life story, and it would place him near nuclear sites from his very first years.
bose-s-paper-published-under-einstein-s-: A doctor named Greg Rogers, who says he once saw a UFO in a secret hangar, tells a story from physics in the 1920s. He says the Indian scientist Satyendra Nath Bose could not get anyone to listen to his paper, so he sent it to Albert Einstein, the famous physicist, saying nobody was listening to him, and it was then published with Einstein's backing. Rogers tells it to show how new ideas can be ignored until a famous name vouches for them.
boskin-commission-s-1-1-cpi-overstatemen: A mathematician and commentator, Eric Weinstein, says on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels that in the 1990s in Washington the Boskin Commission, a government panel on economic statistics, committed what he calls a crime against the American people. According to Weinstein, the panel inserted by hand a 1.1 percent overstatement into the CPI, the official measure of how fast prices rise. He tells it as an example of officials quietly shaping what the public is told.
boss-tells-fox-the-government-admitted-t: James Fox, a filmmaker who makes UFO documentaries, recalls on Jesse Michels' podcast a talk with his boss about Roswell, New Mexico, where something is said to have crashed in 1947. Fox says his boss told him the US government had actually admitted it recovered something there, and Fox remembers answering, "Really?" If true, it would mean the government had owned up to picking up a crashed craft.
bostick-on-strange-effects-at-high-megav: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, quotes a scientist named Bostick as saying that strange things happen when millions of volts are put across very short distances. Michels connects this to the work of an inventor, Townsend Brown, who experimented with very high voltages. If true, it would hint that high voltage can produce effects that ordinary physics does not expect.
bought-ranch-as-skeptic-intending-to-don: The owner of Skinwalker Ranch, a property in Utah that his interview ties to UFOs, spoke to a podcast host, Jesse Michels. He says that when he bought the ranch around 2016 he did not believe the strange claims about it, and that he actually meant to give it away to the Boy Scouts of America. He mentions the names Robert Bigelow and Chris Lee as he tells it, and he tells it to show he started out a doubter, not a believer.
boyd-bushman-talks-antigravity-1990: Nick Cook, a British aviation journalist, says he sat down to interview Boyd Bushman, an engineer at the aerospace company Lockheed Martin in Fort Worth, Texas, for a documentary he was making called Ben Rich Secret, named after a former Lockheed executive. According to Cook, Bushman talked about antigravity, which would mean someone has built machines that can push against gravity itself.
bozeman-cattle-mutilation-with-ufo-repor: A scientist named Kevin Knuth says that around 1988, near Bozeman, Montana, there was a cattle mutilation, where two cows were found killed and, in his words, surgically manipulated. According to the story's title, there were also reports of UFOs in the area at the time. Tellers raise cases like this because they suggest the strange lights and the dead animals may be connected.
bracewell-probe-possibly-lurking-in-the-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, describes an idea from a scientist, Ronald Bracewell, from the 1960s: that an alien civilization might send unmanned probes to other stars instead of traveling itself. Michels says Bracewell went a step further and suggested such a probe might already be hiding somewhere in our own solar system, perhaps at the balance points near the Earth and Moon where an object can stay put. If true, an alien probe could be watching us from close by.
brad-sorensen-shown-alien-reproduction-v: The podcast host Jesse Michels passes on a story first told by Mark McCandlish, an illustrator of aircraft. According to it, in 1988 a man named Brad Sorensen was shown three bell- or acorn-shaped craft, called flux liners or alien reproduction vehicles, meaning human-built copies of alien craft, and they looked worn as if they had been flown. The story places this at Palmdale, California, though some tellers put it at an air show at Norton Air Force Base. A researcher known as UAPGerb says he believes the story, calls the craft a copycat vehicle, and adds that in 1990 Sorensen admitted it to Bill Scott, an editor at the aviation magazine Aviation Week. If true, it would mean the US had already built working copies of alien technology.
bradshaw-ranch-high-strangeness: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, citing a book called Merging Dimensions, talks about Bradshaw Ranch in Secret Canyon near Sedona, Arizona. He calls the ranch notorious and ground zero for Sedona's high strangeness, the term people use for clusters of odd, unexplained events. If true, it would make the ranch a hot spot for such happenings.
brain-implants-link-experiencers-to-the-: A man named Steve Coburn, who says he has had contact with alien beings, spoke on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels in an episode about implants said to be found in human bodies. Coburn says such an implant "turns you into a walking bug" and links the person to a shared group mind of the grays, the gray-skinned beings often described in abduction stories. He says the beings told him this themselves, which would mean the people who carry these implants are not fully in control of their own minds.
brain-shown-to-secrete-dmt-endogenously-: The writer Graham Hancock talks about DMT, a powerful chemical that causes vivid visions. He says scientists once thought the body made it only in the lungs, but research at the University of Michigan, linked to the scientist Jimo Borjigin, now shows the brain can make it on its own and has DMT receptors all over. If so, the brain carries its own vision-making chemistry.
brake-lines-cut-after-leaving-bae: Dylan Borland, a man who says he once worked in the defense world, says that after he left BAE, a large defense company, someone cut the brake lines on his car. He says the police looked into it and told him the lines were cut "100%," which he takes as a sign someone wanted to stop him.
bramley-plague-spreaders-are-the-sumeria: Jason Jorjani, a philosopher, explained on Jesse Michels' podcast an idea from the writer William Bramley's book The Gods of Eden. According to Jorjani, Bramley thinks the people who spread plagues in Europe, such as in the 1300s, belonged to the same group that ruled over humanity back in ancient Sumer, the early civilisation of what is now Iraq. If true, it would mean one hidden, non-human-linked faction has steered human history for thousands of years.
brandenburg-s-xenon-129-nuclear-signatur: A scientist named John Brandenburg has an idea that there was once a nuclear war on Mars. A philosopher, Jason Jorjani, says he spent several days with Brandenburg in New Mexico and wrote about his research in his book Closer Encounters. According to Jorjani, Brandenburg found that the mix of xenon-129, a form of the gas xenon that nuclear reactions produce, is unusual at Cydonia, a region of Mars. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells it too. He adds argon-40, another gas, and says both exist on Mars in greater amounts than natural decay would explain. Once he credits an unnamed friend who worked at the national weapons labs Lawrence Livermore and Sandia, and once he names Brandenburg. If true, it would mean Mars once held a civilisation that destroyed itself with nuclear weapons.
brandon-fugal-skinwalker-ranch-phenomeno: Researcher Grant Cameron says on Jesse Michels's podcast that Brandon Fugal, who goes to Skinwalker Ranch, a Utah property known for reports of strange events, says clearly that the phenomenon there is "reflective". By that, Cameron means it seems to mirror the people observing it. If true, what witnesses see would depend partly on who they are.
brandon-fugal-to-have-marrs-sphere-teste: Ross Coulthart, a journalist who covers UFOs, said on Jesse Michels' podcast in 2025 that he had hoped to see a strange sphere linked to the writer Jim Marrs, which was in Texas. Coulthart says he was told, with an apology, that a businessman named Brandon Fugal had agreed to fly it in his private jet to Utah to have it tested in a lab. The tests would matter because they could show whether the object was made by people or not.
branscomb-allegedly-offers-condon-his-cl: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells of Lewis Branscomb, then head of the National Bureau of Standards, a US government science agency. Michels says Branscomb allegedly offered Edward Condon, a physicist who chaired a 1960s committee studying UFOs, a deal: help bury the UFO question and get back his security clearance, meaning his permission to see secret information. If true, it would mean the government's official UFO study was steered toward a set answer.
branscomb-tells-condon-to-get-his-cleara: This story is about how the physicist Edward Condon came to lead a UFO study for the US Air Force in 1966. The podcast host Jesse Michels says that a fellow scientist, Lewis Branscomb, told Condon something like "maybe it's time you get your clearance back," meaning his permission to see secret material. Michels says the exchange comes from an interview Condon gave to the American Institute of Physics, a scientific body that records interviews with scientists. Robert Salas, a former Air Force officer, tells it too on the same podcast, citing the same interview. In his version, Branscomb told Condon that the Air Force needed someone to head up its UFO study, which was based at the University of Colorado. Michels also mentions the astronomer Donald Menzel in this context. It is told because, if the account is right, the man picked to judge UFOs was steered into the job with a nudge back into the world of secrets.
bray-s-navy-uap-disclosure-2021: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, mentions Scott Bray, a US Navy official. Michels says Bray was the person who disclosed information, around 2021 he thinks, about UAP, short for unidentified anomalous phenomena, the government's term for UFOs. It is told as a moment when the military spoke openly about the subject.
brazil-ordinance-551gc3-on-reporting-ufo: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that since 2009 Brazil has had a military rule, an ordinance numbered 551GC3, about UFOs, meaning unidentified flying objects. According to Michels, it requires any branch of the Brazilian military that sees one to hand the information to the Central Aerospace Defense Command, the body that watches over Brazil's skies. If so, it would mean Brazil's armed forces collect these reports as a matter of official duty.
brazil-s-night-of-ufos-1986-host-summary: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that one night in May 1986, 21 unidentified objects were spotted over four Brazilian states, in an event remembered as Brazil's Night of UFOs, with military bases near Brasília and Rio de Janeiro involved. He links the story to a Brazilian officer, Brigadier Octávio Júlio Moreira Lima, and to an official statement from the Brazilian Air Force. Michels tells it as one of Brazil's best-known cases, one he presents as confirmed by the country's own officials.
brazil-sightings: An author on occult and intelligence history, Peter Levenda, says on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels that witnesses of sightings in Brazil used different words to describe what they saw. He raises it to show how the language people reach for shapes the accounts we get.
break-in-at-brown-s-house-passport-taken: Matthew Brown, who calls himself a Pentagon whistleblower, told the podcast host Jesse Michels that someone broke into his home. He says the only thing taken and never recovered was his civilian passport, and that his grandfather's ashes had been moved and put out. He says the break-in is on a police record, and he tells it as a sign that someone was trying to intimidate him.
break-ins-at-the-homes-of-legacy-program: Dylan Borland, speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast, says that in 2018 there were break-ins at the homes of people he knew at BAE Systems, a large defence company. He says these were colleagues who worked on what he calls "Legacy", a secret programme. If true, it suggests that people tied to such programmes were being watched or pressured.
breakaway-civilization-behind-the-men-at: A writer named Whitley Strieber, who says he has met non-human beings, tells a podcast host that he thinks there is a breakaway civilization: a hidden group of people who have split off from the rest of society with secret knowledge and technology. The story's title ties this idea to men who came to his door. If true, it would mean someone other than ordinary government is behind some of what people experience.
breakaway-civilization-built-on-crash-re: A UFO historian named Richard Dolan says that since 1947, the secret world inside the United States that is said to hold crashed craft not made by humans has grown so cut off that it is like a separate civilization, one that has broken away from our own. He borrows the idea from the writings of the historian Arnold Toynbee. If true, it would mean a hidden part of society with its own knowledge and power now runs alongside the public one.
brent-hears-that-harrington-worked-on-ab: Brent Friedman, on Jesse Michels's podcast, says he heard through his mother that a man named Harrington had been involved in ABSCAM, a US federal sting operation into political corruption around 1980 and 1981 in Washington, DC. He tells it as part of explaining who this man was and how serious his government background was.
brent-offered-secret-agent-man-by-barry-: A Hollywood writer named Brent Friedman, speaking to a podcast host, Jesse Michels, in an episode about Hollywood, the CIA and UFOs, says that in the late 1990s in Los Angeles he was offered a job on a TV show called Secret Agent Man. He says its executive producer, the person overseeing the show, was the filmmaker Barry Sonnenfeld. He tells it as one link in his own path through spy and UFO themed entertainment.
brent-sees-a-fatal-motorcycle-crash-at-a: A Hollywood writer named Brent Friedman told a podcast host, Jesse Michels, about a memory from 1968, when he was five years old in the Berkeley Hills of California. He says he watched a woman on a motorcycle hit a patch of water with her back tire, slide, stop and get thrown, and that the crash killed her. He shares it as part of his own life story, a moment that stayed with him from early childhood.
brett-weinstein-advised-not-to-air-rober: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that sometime in the 2020s he asked another commentator, Brett Weinstein, whether he should put out an interview he had recorded with a man named Robert Malone. According to Michels, Weinstein answered that he had lost a third of his family's income and would not air it. Michels tells this to show how much putting out certain conversations can cost the person who does it.
brewster-lights-over-the-haunted-house-g: A witness named Charles says that around 1985 or 1986, in Brewster, New York, someone showed him a strange sight by a garage at a house said to be haunted. He says they looked up and saw six bright white lights hanging just above the treetops in formation, drifting slowly over the road with no sound and no windows. It is told as one of many sightings reported in that area in those years.
brian-fitzpatrick-s-cattle-mutilation-bo: A retired US Navy admiral, Tim Gallaudet, praises a book called The Operator by an author named Brian Fitzpatrick. The book is about cattle mutilations, cases where cows are found dead with parts of their bodies strangely removed, and Gallaudet calls it astonishing and the biggest reveal on the subject out there. He tells it because, if the book is right, it would explain who or what is behind these mysterious deaths.
briefing-attendees-rebuild-the-aquarius-: A physicist, Eric Davis, says that in 1977 some people sat through a secret briefing about Project Aquarius, said to be a hidden US government UFO programme. According to Davis, the men from the briefing then went to a motel near Washington and wrote down from memory everything they recalled, and he names Alonzo McDonald, a White House official, and Bill Moore, a UFO researcher, in connection with it. If true, it would mean a written record of a secret UFO briefing exists only because people rebuilt it by hand.
briefing-dia-head-general-patrick-hughes: A man named Steven Greer, who has spent years trying to brief officials about UFOs, says that in the 1990s he briefed a three-star general, Patrick Hughes. According to the story, Hughes headed the Defense Intelligence Agency, the US military's own spy agency. If true, it would mean the claims reached very senior people in military intelligence.
briefing-on-engineered-isotopic-ratios-o: David Grusch, a former US intelligence officer who became a whistleblower, says that sometime around 2019 to 2022 he was briefed on material from craft the government had recovered. He says the material had isotopic ratios, meaning the mix of different forms of the same element, that would have to be engineered to reach those levels. In another telling he says analysts told him it contained heavy elements such as europium and californium arranged in ways that make no sense, which would mean it was made by someone, not by nature or by us.
briefing-senate-intelligence-committee-i: Steven Greer, a man who says he has briefed many officials about UFOs, says he once met with senior investigators for the Senate Intelligence Committee, the group of US senators who oversee the country's spy agencies. He says that when he first started meeting them, they did not know certain secret facilities existed. If true, it would mean secret work was being hidden even from the people meant to oversee it.
briefing-the-institute-of-noetic-science: Steven Greer, a man who says he has briefed many officials about UFOs, says that years ago, probably in the 1990s, astronaut Edgar Mitchell invited him to brief the board of the Institute of Noetic Sciences, a group that studies the mind and consciousness. He tells it to show that serious, well-known figures were interested in what he had to say.
briefings-to-senate-intelligence-committ: A man named Jordan Jose, who says he was taken into a secret UFO programme as a child, told a podcast host, Jesse Michels, that between about 2023 and 2026 in Washington he shared what he knows with past members of the Senate Select Intelligence Committee, the Senate group that oversees US spy agencies. He says he also briefed several "three-letter agencies", meaning government agencies known by their initials, and gave them locations and names, and he mentions a man named David Grusch. If true, it would mean his claims have been put directly in front of officials.
brigham-s-senate-testimony-with-rfk-on-e: Brigham Buhler, a businessman who works in the medicine business and criticizes big drug companies, says that in the 2020s he spoke before the US Senate alongside Robert F. Kennedy Jr., known as RFK. He links that moment to the warning President Dwight Eisenhower gave in his farewell speech, and tells it as part of a bigger story about powerful interests hiding things from the public.
bright-light-over-catalina-identified-as: Kevin Knuth, a scientist described as a NASA whistleblower, tells of a 2021 research trip near Santa Catalina Island off California, where his team watched the sky for unexplained objects with a colleague, Matthew Shadagus. Knuth says a bright light they saw turned out to be the International Space Station, and that this was written up in a scientific paper on the mission.
bringing-tom-delonge-and-lue-elizondo-to: A man named Chris Bledsoe, who says UFOs appear around him and that NASA scientists have studied him, told a podcast host, Jesse Michels, that around 2017 he took a rock musician, Tom DeLonge, and a former Pentagon official, Lue Elizondo, to see a piece of metal in Zanesville, Ohio, though he is unsure whether it was Ohio or Pennsylvania. The story ties the metal to a crashed craft, and he also mentions the names Hal Puthoff and Timothy Taylor. If true, it would mean well-known figures in the UFO world went to examine possible crash material in person.
british-and-french-governments-release-u: James Fox, a filmmaker who makes UFO documentaries, recalls on Jesse Michels' podcast that around 2007 and 2008 the British and French governments released UFO documents that had been secret. He tells it as a sign that other governments were opening their files on sightings, which would matter for anyone hoping the US would do the same.
british-gravity-research-memo-stamped-wr: A writer and researcher named Greg Bishop says on Jesse Michels's podcast that he saw a copy of a British memo about gravity research that was stamped with the name of Wright-Patterson Air Force Base in Ohio. He says about five pages were missing, and that there is a legend that those pages describe something achieved in the middle of the last century before the text cuts off. If true, it would hint that a gravity breakthrough was hidden.
broad-haven-students-draw-silver-disc: A guest named Merrick, debating on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, cites a case from Broad Haven in the UK. He says ten students saw a silver disc, then each drew a picture of it, and the drawings were identical. He offers it as a case where separate witnesses agree too closely to dismiss.
broken-bleed-line-cuts-f-18-control-line: A Navy fighter pilot named Ryan Graves told a podcast host, Jesse Michels, about a training flight near Saudi Arabia during his first squadron. He says a bleed line, a pipe carrying very hot air from the engine through his F-18 fighter jet, broke and acted "like a plasma beam", cutting through things inside the jet, including control lines. He tells it as an example of how dangerous ordinary flying can be.
brookhaven-stony-brook-and-renaissance-a: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, wonders aloud whether Brookhaven National Laboratory, a government research lab on Long Island in New York, together with the nearby Stony Brook university and a firm called Renaissance, served as a hidden pool of money for secret science. He points out that Brookhaven was home to the Cosmotron, which he calls the largest particle accelerator in the US, a machine that smashes tiny particles together. If true, it would mean secret research was being funded quietly through these local institutions.
brookings-report-recommends-possible-wit: Maaneli Derakhshani, speaking on Jesse Michels' podcast, says that NASA asked the Brookings Institution, a research group in Washington, to write a study in 1959, which came out in 1960. According to him, this Brookings report suggested that if signs of alien life, such as objects left behind, were ever found, the news might be held back from the public. If so, it would show that keeping such finds secret was thought about from NASA's earliest days.
brother-victor-pushed-down-an-elevator-s: A writer named Peter Levenda tells of a man he knew as Brother Victor, connected to a branch of the Russian Orthodox Church based outside Russia, at its church on Park Avenue and 93rd Street in Manhattan, around 1968. Levenda says that someone pushed Brother Victor down an elevator shaft and broke his legs. He tells it as a sign of how dangerous the hidden world he was moving in could be.
brought-into-the-king-s-chamber-by-timot: A man named Jay Anderson told a podcast host, Jesse Michels, that sometime in the 2020s he was taken into the King's Chamber, a room deep inside the Great Pyramid of Giza in Egypt. He says a man named Timothy Hogan brought him in personally, and he tells it as a sign of the special access and connections he had.
brown-brothers-harriman-versailles-repar: A guest named Dan Sheehan tells podcast host Jesse Michels a story that starts with the Treaty of Versailles, the peace deal after the First World War, and the payments it forced on Germany. He says that in 1924 George Herbert Walker left Brown Brothers Harriman, a New York bank, and set up the Union Bank of New York, funded entirely by people from that bank, and he links this money to the rise of Hitler, naming Robert Lansing, the brothers John Foster and Allen Dulles, and a German named Fritz Thyssen. If true, American bankers would have helped pay for Hitler's rise.
brown-founds-nicap-hillenkoetter-on-boar: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that an inventor named Townsend Brown, after returning from the International Geophysical Year, a worldwide science effort of the 1950s, created NICAP, the National Investigations Committee on Aerial Phenomena, in Washington. In one telling Michels links Roscoe Hillenkoetter, a former head of the CIA, the US foreign spy agency, to the group, and in another he simply calls it the first civilian UFO tracking program, started in 1956. It matters because it would mean a scientist with secret government ties helped launch the first public UFO investigation group.
brown-has-met-someone-who-saw-a-ufo-in-a: Matthew Brown is a former Pentagon worker who calls himself a whistleblower. In a 2026 interview, podcast host Jesse Michels asked him whether he had ever met anyone he believes has seen a UFO, an unidentified flying object, sitting inside a hangar. Brown simply answered yes, which would suggest such craft are being stored somewhere, though he gave no names, places or dates.
brown-meets-teller-and-lemay-driven-by-s: Jesse Michels, a podcast host, tells how in the 1950s an inventor named Townsend Brown, who worked on ideas about controlling gravity, met with the physicist Edward Teller and the Air Force general Curtis LeMay. Drawing on a biography called The Man Who Mastered Gravity by Paul Schatzkin, Michels says Brown's daughter Linda remembers her father often being driven home in a black Cadillac by a man she later learned was Robert Sarbacher. Michels tells it because, if true, it would put Brown at the centre of secret work tied to the UFO question.
brown-repeats-the-vacuum-experiment-at-b: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that a researcher named Thomas Townsend Brown repeated one of his experiments run in a vacuum at the Institute of Field Physics in North Carolina, a lab backed by a man named Agnew Bahnson, in the 1950s. Michels tells it because, if true, it would show Brown's results held up in a second lab and not just his own.
brown-s-1953-winter-haven-proposal: This story is about a document from 1953 written by a scientist named T. Townsend Brown, known as the Winter Haven proposal after the town in Florida. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, describes Brown as a scientist who worked on flying craft early on, and says the proposal looks almost exactly like the way insiders describe America's secret UFO program. In other words, Brown seems to have laid out, in 1953, a plan for the kind of project people now say exists. A second speaker on the same show, named Jack, also refers to the proposal. He adds that in it Brown praised Oliver Heaviside, a scientist of the 1890s, saying Heaviside had a good theory of gravity worth listening to. Both are speaking in their own words rather than quoting a witness. If the comparison holds, it would suggest the secret program had roots in Brown's ideas from the 1950s.
brown-s-electrometers-pick-up-anomalies-: Linda Brown says on Jesse Michels's podcast that the scientist Townsend Brown built devices he called electrometers, which she says may have been picking up neutrinos, tiny particles that pass through almost everything. According to the telling, he kept them running until the end of his life on Catalina Island, California, in 1985, and they recorded oddities that followed the sidereal calendar, meaning time measured by the stars rather than the Sun. If true, it would point to some unknown influence coming from space.
brown-s-experiments-replicated-worldwide: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that the experiments of a researcher named Thomas Townsend Brown, who worked on the idea that electricity could affect gravity, have been repeated all over the world, in places as far away as Japan. If true, it would mean Brown's results are not a one-off but something others can reproduce.
brown-s-lost-1929-paper-the-minor-quantu: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells the story of Townsend Brown, an American scientist and inventor whom he presents as someone who built UFO-like craft long before others claimed to. Michels says that in 1929 Brown wrote a paper called The Minor Quantum, a paper now described as lost. He mentions it as part of Brown's early work on the ideas that Michels says led to those craft.
brown-s-navy-resignation-letter-1942: Townsend Brown was an American inventor whose life is the subject of a documentary by podcast host Jesse Michels. In it a researcher, Jan Lundquist, says that around 1942 Brown got a letter telling him to move his equipment from the University of Philadelphia to the Navy at Norfolk, Virginia, and she ties this to the papers around his resignation from the Navy. It is told because it would put Brown's unusual experiments in the Navy's hands during the war.
brown-s-paper-the-structure-of-space-wri: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Townsend Brown, an American scientist and inventor he presents as an early builder of UFO-like craft, wrote a scientific paper called The Structure of Space in the early 1940s. According to Michels, Brown wrote it while working at a company called Martin Corporation, and unlike some of Brown's other writing, this paper can still be read today. Michels points to it as a surviving record of Brown's ideas about how space itself works.
brown-s-patents-bought-by-sharper-image-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says he believes that a researcher named Thomas Townsend Brown was behind patents that were later bought by Sharper Image, a US gadget retailer, for its air purifiers that clean air using electrically charged particles. Michels tells it to show that Brown's odd-sounding work ended up in ordinary household products.
brown-s-saucer-shaped-gravitator-and-fou: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that a researcher named Townsend Brown built a device he called a gravitator, meant to tap into gravity, and that it looked exactly like a flying saucer. Michels adds that in the 1950s Brown helped form NICAP, the National Investigations Committee on Aerial Phenomena, which Michels calls the first civilian group to study UFOs. If true, it would tie early anti-gravity research directly to the start of public UFO investigation.
brown-s-task-force-captures-miethe-1945: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells a story from Germany at the end of the Second World War in 1945. He says that a team linked to Townsend Brown, an American inventor known for high-voltage experiments he tied to gravity, reportedly helped the Allied forces capture Richard Miethe, whom Michels calls a mysterious German high-voltage physicist. If true, it would place Brown near the hunt for advanced German science at the very start of this story.
brown-s-work-continues-in-black-aerospac: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says he believes that the work of a researcher named Thomas Townsend Brown, who tried to use electricity to affect gravity, still lives on inside the most secret parts of the American aerospace industry. In his words, it survives as whispers in tightly walled-off sub-projects where it keeps being explored. If true, it would mean the research never died but simply went out of public view.
brown-s-work-in-the-b-2-and-floyd-odlum-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Floyd Odlum, whom he calls the majority owner of the aircraft maker Northrop, paid for the work of Townsend Brown, an American inventor who experimented with high voltage and gravity, starting in the 1960s. According to Michels, Odlum paid Brown a monthly sum, something like two to four thousand dollars, and kept paying his family the same until he died. Michels links this to Brown's work feeding into the B-2, a later American stealth bomber, which if true would tie Brown's odd experiments to a real military aircraft.
brown-s-work-witnessed-by-top-government: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, drawing on a biography of the researcher Townsend Brown by Paul Shatskin, argues that Brown should not be brushed off as an amateur quack. Michels says Brown's work was witnessed by the highest levels of government and military, naming figures such as the physicist Edward Teller and the businessman Bill Lear. If true, it would mean Brown's work on what is said to be antigravity was taken seriously at the very top.
brown-spent-his-career-looking-for-a-nuc: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that a researcher named Townsend Brown, known for experiments aimed at controlling gravity, spent the rest of his career searching for a nuclear power source. Michels finds this telling because it suggests Brown believed his devices needed far more power than ordinary sources could give.
brown-spoke-of-biblical-ufos-and-aliens-: Jesse Michels, a podcast host who made a documentary about the American inventor Townsend Brown, says he learned something from Brown's daughter, Linda. According to her, Brown often talked about UFOs in the Bible and about aliens, at home and with his family, though not in public. If true, it would mean the inventor privately believed in visitors from elsewhere.
brown-tells-josh-reynolds-the-philadelph: The Philadelphia Experiment is a story about a secret Navy experiment in Philadelphia in 1943, later told in a book and a movie. Podcast host Jesse Michels says that the inventor Townsend Brown, who is often linked to that story, told his close friend and co-worker Josh Reynolds that the book and the movie were greatly inflated. brown-terminated-by-navy-joins-martin-ne: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells of a scientist named Thomas Townsend Brown who, he says, served in the US Navy for many years until 1942. bryce-dewitt-paper-on-superconductors-an: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in 1968 a scientist named Bryce DeWitt wrote a paper on superconductors, materials that carry electricity with no loss when very cold, and on a kind of gravitational drag linked to them. bryce-dewitt-s-institute-funds-townsend-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Bryce DeWitt, a physicist who helped found the study of quantum gravity, ran an Institute of Field Physics in North Carolina that was also paying for the high-voltage gravity experiments of Townsend Brown, an American inventor. buga-sphere-symbols-recognised-by-mario-: Jesse Michels, a podcast host, says he showed photos of the symbols on the Buga Sphere, a metal ball found in Buga, Colombia, to two men, Mario Woods and Randy Anderson. bugged-seattle-hotel-meeting-and-the-jou: Peter Levenda, a researcher and author, said this on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels. buzz-aldrin-chased-a-disc-in-a-military-: James Fox, a documentary filmmaker who investigates UFO stories, says Fay Ann Potter, the sister of the astronaut Buzz Aldrin, told him her brother once had a UFO encounter while flying a military jet, sometime in the 1950s or 1960s. cape-canaveral-as-cover-for-non-space-pr: A doctor named Greg Rogers, who says he worked with NASA, the US space agency, and saw an odd craft in a secret hangar, says that Cape Canaveral, a US Air Force launch site in Florida, made a good hiding place for projects that had nothing to do with space. According to Rogers, if you put some secret project there, officials could always say it was just part of the space programme. He tells it to explain how secret work could hide in plain sight.
cape-girardeau-crash-with-small-bodies-a: A scientist named John Blitch, who worked for DARPA, the US military's advanced research agency, and who says he was taken by an alien, tells of a crash near Cape Girardeau, Missouri, around 1941, years before the famous 1947 crash story at Roswell, New Mexico. He says there were small bodies at the site, and a priest or reverend was asked to give last rites because one of them was apparently still alive, and he says he visited the place in 2014. If true, it would mean a crash with living beings happened before any of the better-known ones.
captain-hollanda-lima-s-encounter-with-a: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells of Captain Uyrangê Hollanda Lima, a Brazilian military officer tied to Operation Prato, a Brazilian military investigation of strange sightings around the town of Colares in the state of Pará in the late 1970s. Michels says the captain himself saw an alien being in a space suit, and that the being gave him a hug. If true, it would mean an officer leading an official inquiry had close, personal contact with a non-human being.
captain-viriato-s-radar-track-at-mach-15: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells of a 1986 incident in Brazil. He says that a Captain Viriato recorded an object on radar moving at Mach 15, meaning fifteen times the speed of sound, while flying in a zigzag pattern. If true, that is far beyond what any known aircraft can do.
captain-warns-sherman-he-won-t-be-allowe: A former US Air Force sergeant named Dan Sherman says that in the early 1990s, at a secret site he calls Base 2, a captain told him he honestly did not think Sherman would be able to get out. Sherman tells it to show how hard it was to leave the secret work he says he was doing, which involved communicating with beings from elsewhere.
captured-german-nuclear-scientists-wiret: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that after World War Two in 1945, the German physicist Werner Heisenberg and the others on Germany's nuclear program were captured and held in a house in the English countryside. According to Michels, the whole house was wiretapped, and transcripts of their talks were made. He raises it in a conversation with a guest, Jason Jorjani, who claims Hitler had a secret UFO program, since the recordings might show what the German scientists really knew.
captured-german-ss-documents-at-the-nati: Peter Levenda, an author described as a historian, says that in the 2000s he went to the US National Archives in Washington to read German documents captured at the end of the Second World War. He says they were kept on microfilm and included records of the SS, the Nazi elite force run by Heinrich Himmler, from the 1930s and 40s.
captured-russian-and-chinese-weapons-sho: A man named Randy Anderson, who says he saw strange technology at a military base, says that in 2014 at Crane, a Navy weapons centre in Indiana, he and others were taken underground and told about Russian and Chinese weapon systems that had been captured. He tells it as part of his account of what is kept hidden below that base.
car-crash-outside-the-dark-skies-office-: A man named Brent, who worked on a 1990s TV show called Dark Skies, says that a car crash happened outside the show's production office in North Hollywood. According to Brent, as he was with the dying man, he felt all of the man's energy, like his soul, pass through his own body. He tells it as a deeply strange personal experience from those years.
car-fried-by-energy-weapon-en-route-to-f: A man named Steve says that while he was driving through a canyon to a doctor's office to film the doctor testing an implant, a small object he says was placed inside a person's body, still in place, someone zapped his car with some kind of energy weapon. Steve says a mechanic later told him the car's computer was fried as if hit by an electromagnetic pulse, a burst of energy that knocks out electronics. He tells it because, if true, it would mean someone was trying to stop that test from being filmed.
careful-handling-of-david-grusch-before-: David Grusch is a former US intelligence officer who in 2023 went public, and later spoke to Congress, about claims of secret government UFO programmes. Bryce Zabel, a writer talking about Hollywood and UFOs, says the journalist George Knapp and the filmmaker Jeremy Corbell were involved in helping bring Grusch forward. It is told to show that his going public was carefully prepared rather than sudden.
caretaker-tom-lewis-collapses-during-dri: Brandon Fugal, who owns a property called Skinwalker Ranch, tells a podcast host, Jesse Michels, about something he says happened around 2025 or 2026 while his team was drilling below a flat-topped hill on the ranch. He says that as a radio signal at 1.6 gigahertz showed up, the ranch caretaker, Tom Lewis, was brought to his knees. In another part of the same episode the incident is described as a heart episode, and someone called Dragon is said to have evacuated him immediately; that version does not name the caretaker or mention the signal. Both tellings come from the same interview, so in effect this is Fugal's own account told twice. He tells it because, in his view, it ties the strange signal under the ranch to real harm to people.
cargo-cult-text-written-for-delonge-to-s: Peter Levenda, an author, says that around 2014 or 2015 the rock musician Tom DeLonge, who was starting his own effort to bring UFO secrets to light, asked him to write something he could show people about what they were trying to do. Levenda says that piece, built around the idea of a cargo cult, a group that imitates a more advanced culture hoping its gifts return, became the opening pages of their book Sekret Machines: Gods.
cargo-cults-building-landing-tracks: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that on islands in French Polynesia, in the South Pacific, groups he calls cargo cults built landing strips, presumably for some alien craft they expected to come back, an idea he says comes from their own myths. A researcher and author, Peter Levenda, tells a similar story but places it more broadly on South Pacific islands in the early 20th century, where planes would land, and he does not mention alien craft. Another researcher, Jason Simosa, repeats the story as he heard it from Levenda, describing a tribe in a remote part of French Polynesia, though he admits he is not sure of the geography. It gets told as an example of how people may build rituals around visitors who arrive from the sky.
carl-jung-s-flying-saucers-1958: In 1958 the Swiss psychiatrist Carl Jung wrote a book about UFOs called Flying Saucers: A Modern Myth of Things Seen in the Skies. Michels brings it up several times himself. He describes it as reading the round saucers as mandalas, which he calls "the Sanskrit symbol of psychic completeness". The philosopher James Madden, a guest who has read the book closely, says Jung starts out treating the saucers as mass rumor, finds them harder to dismiss as the book goes on, and in the end says, as Madden puts it, "and yet they're on radar". Michels sometimes dates the book loosely to the 1950s. The book matters to them because one of the great minds of the century seemed to be moved from doubt toward taking the sightings seriously.
carl-jung-s-scarab-beetle-as-a-time-loop: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, retells a story about Carl Jung, a famous psychiatrist, and one of his patients, a very down-to-earth woman who did not believe in anything mystical. According to Michels, she told Jung she had dreamed of being given a golden scarab beetle as a gift. Michels frames this as a kind of time loop, which would mean events can reach backwards or forwards in time in ways we do not usually accept.
carl-nell-points-to-thomas-townsend-brow: Jesse Michels, a podcast host, says that Karl Nell, a former senior figure in the defence industry, told people to watch Michels' video about Thomas Townsend Brown, a researcher known for ideas about unusual ways to move a craft. In a later episode Michels adds that Nell once ran a business worth $2 billion and was chief technology officer of a company owned by Northrop, a big defence contractor. Michels tells it because such a hint from such a person suggests Brown's ideas may matter.
carl-pflock-broke-into-a-congressman-s-o: Aztec, New Mexico is the site of a claimed UFO crash said to have left alien bodies behind. Podcast host Jesse Michels passes on what a researcher of that case, Scott Ramsay, told him: that a congressman's office was broken into by Carl Pflock, another UFO researcher, and that evidence about Aztec was taken. If true, it would mean someone worked to make proof of the crash disappear.
carl-sagan-and-the-golden-disc-1970: Lue Elizondo, a former Pentagon official who has spoken publicly about UFOs, brings up the astronomer Carl Sagan when talking about contact with other worlds. Elizondo says Sagan helped put together the Golden Disc, a message from humanity sent out in the 1970s on a spacecraft that has now left our solar system.
carl-sagan-as-a-majestic-member-1960: Jason Jorjani, a philosopher, said on Jesse Michels's podcast that he is pretty convinced the astronomer and science writer Carl Sagan was a member of Majestic, a group said to be a secret panel that oversees what the government knows about UFOs. If true, it would mean one of the best known public voices of science was quietly part of the inner circle.
carl-sagan-calls-brandenburg-why-are-you: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, passes on a story about a man named John Brandenburg, who had done something that stirred up controversy about the Moon or space. Michels says that the famous astronomer Carl Sagan, of all people, phoned Brandenburg and asked him, "Why are you causing this trouble?" Michels tells it to suggest that even leading scientists were uneasy about the questions Brandenburg was raising.
carl-sagan-met-with-kit-green-and-got-in: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Carl Sagan, the well-known scientist, met often with Kit Green toward the end of his career, in the late 1990s, and became very interested in UFOs. In a later episode Michels describes Green as a CIA man, meaning someone from the US spy agency, who was into UFOs, and adds that Sagan held private meetings, possibly about UFOs, that the public never knew about. If true, it would mean a famous public skeptic was quietly taking the subject seriously.
carl-sagan-s-early-ufo-interest-and-turn: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Carl Sagan, the famous American astronomer and science writer, wrote about UFOs in his diary as a boy and often debated them with his mentor. According to Michels, Sagan somehow flipped to being strongly against the idea of UFOs, as seen in his book The Demon-Haunted World, a defense of scientific skepticism. Michels raises this turn in a discussion about UFOs and religion, as a puzzle about why a believer became a leading doubter.
carl-stanley-dies-a-month-after-his-bron: Peter Levenda, a researcher and author, said on Jesse Michels's podcast that a man named Carl Stanley was consecrated in a religious ceremony in the Bronx, New York, around 1965. Levenda says Stanley then went back to Kentucky and was dead within a month, a timing he tells as strange and worth noticing.
carlin-tunnel-proof-of-concept-scan-2024: A researcher named Jeffrey, working with a colleague named Filippo, shows a 2024 scan of a place called the Carlin Tunnel. He presents it as a test, a proof that their scanning method can see what lies underground. They tell it to back up their bigger claim that the same method has found a huge hidden structure beneath the pyramids of Egypt.
carlos-de-souza-witnesses-the-crash-and-: A documentary filmmaker, James Fox, tells of a man named Carlos de Souza near the town of Varginha in Brazil in January 1996. According to Fox, de Souza turned off the highway onto a dirt road up to a place called the Molini Farm, where he saw a craft struggling to stay in the air before it went boom and hit the ground. The podcast host Jesse Michels repeats the story, crediting Fox and describing de Souza as an ultralight pilot and geography teacher, as part of a wider claim that something not human crashed at Varginha.
carlos-eire-s-they-flew-and-the-historic: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, points to Carlos Eire, a respected religious studies professor at Yale University, and his book They Flew. Michels says the book looks at European saints said to have risen into the air, such as St. Joseph of Cupertino, Teresa of Avila and St. Francis of Assisi. He raises it because, if such accounts are true, people may have defied gravity long before modern reports of strange craft.
carlos-struggles-to-find-the-crash-site-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, describes a scene in Moment of Contact, a 2022 documentary by filmmaker James Fox about a reported crash of an unknown craft near the town of Varginha, Brazil. In it a witness named Carlos Dosoza goes back to look for the crash site, and according to Michels he cannot find it and says, "It wasn't here. In fact, the landscape has changed." Michels says this convinces him, because a liar would simply have pointed and said "here it is."
carlson-has-seen-ufos: A researcher of ancient catastrophes and lost history, Randall Carlson, says simply that he has seen UFOs himself. He mentions it in passing while talking about strange and psychic experiences, without saying when or where.
carlson-s-1995-warren-wilson-college-lec: A researcher of ancient catastrophes, Randall Carlson, says that in 1995 he gave five lectures at Warren Wilson College in North Carolina about the Younger Dryas, a sudden cold spell near the end of the last ice age, along with the mass extinctions and rapid climate change of that time. He says he proposed back then that a cosmic impact caused it, which would mean he had the idea years before it became widely discussed.
carlson-s-masonic-initiation-and-becomin: A researcher of ancient history, Randall Carlson, says he was raised as a Freemason, meaning he joined the old fraternal order known for its rituals and symbols, in March 1979. He says that by 1990 he had become master, the head, of his local lodge, which he offers as background to his interest in old esoteric knowledge.
carlson-visits-quarries-exposing-the-bla: A researcher of ancient catastrophes, Randall Carlson, says he has visited three or four quarries where you can see the "black mat" exposed, a dark layer of soil that some link to the start of the Younger Dryas, a sudden cold spell near the end of the last ice age. He tells it as seeing for himself the physical trace of what he thinks was a cosmic disaster.
caroline-yacht-1933-expedition-and-steph: A writer named Paul Schatzkin, who tells the life of the inventor Townsend Brown, describes a 1933 voyage on the Caroline, a yacht owned by a wealthy businessman, Eldridge Reeves Johnson. He says that when the yacht was docked in Nassau, in the Bahamas, William Stephenson, a British intelligence chief who used Nassau as a base, came aboard and had dinner there. If true, it would tie Brown's early work to the world of spies from the very start.
carrington-event-solar-storm-1859: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, brings up the Carrington event, a huge storm from the Sun that struck Earth in 1859. He says it knocked out electrical lines back then and that a storm like it today would take out the entire power grid. He raises it to show how exposed modern life would be to such an event.
carter-asks-cia-director-george-h-w-bush: Dan Sheehan, a guest on a podcast about American conspiracies, says that after Jimmy Carter won the presidency in 1976, and before he even went to Washington, he called the head of the CIA, the US spy agency, down to his home town of Plains, Georgia. According to Sheehan, the CIA head at the time, George H.W. Bush, was asked to brief Carter on UFOs and refused. If true, it would mean even an incoming president was kept out of the secret.
carter-praying-with-his-head-on-the-tabl: A physicist who has worked on Pentagon research, Eric Davis, passes on what a man named Alonzo McDonald told him and a lawyer, Dan Sheehan. According to Davis, McDonald said that President Jimmy Carter, after being briefed on UFOs in 1977 at the White House, put his head down on the table, as was his habit, and prayed. It is told as a sign of how heavy the news in that briefing was said to be.
carter-purge-of-senior-cia-officers-who-: Matthew Pines, a national security analyst, said on Jesse Michels's podcast that when Jimmy Carter became president in 1977 he purged almost the whole senior ranks of the CIA, the US spy agency. Pines suggests that many of those hundreds of officers were probably running parts of the "legacy program", meaning a long-running secret effort said to handle UFO material, and he asks what they went on to do after they left, since it would mean the secret slipped out of official hands.
carter-s-1976-ufo-briefing-by-cia-direct: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, relays a story from a lawyer, Dan Sheehan, about Jimmy Carter after he won the presidency in 1976. According to the story, one of the first things Carter did was send for the head of the CIA, America's foreign spy agency, to come to his hometown of Plains, Georgia, and brief him on UFOs. The man who came, it is said, was George H.W. Bush, which would mean UFOs were treated as serious business at the very top.
casino-skim-money-driven-in-cadillacs-to: A lawyer, Dan Sheehan, says that in the early 1960s money secretly skimmed off casino profits, linked to men named Carlos Marcello and Meyer Lansky, was driven in Cadillacs between Las Vegas, New Orleans, Miami and Mexico City to pay for a secret training base. Sheehan says he knows the man who sold them the Cadillacs, because he ran the big dealership there. He tells it as part of a larger story about hidden money and the killing of President John F. Kennedy.
catalina-as-a-ufo-hotspot: Santa Catalina, an island off the coast of Southern California, is said by many people to be a place where UFOs show up again and again. Jesse Michels, a podcast host, brings this up while discussing a book by Preston Dennett called Undersea UFO Base. Michels says the book covers Catalina and that many people consider the island a hotspot. A retired Navy admiral, Tim Gallaudet, tells a similar version on Michels' show, though he does not mention Dennett. He names the Catalina Channel, the water between the island and the mainland, as one of several hotspots in his broader argument that the oceans are full of UFOs. Both bring it up because, if true, unknown craft might be operating from under the sea just off a major American coastline.
catholic-archival-reports-of-aerial-phen: A researcher named Diana Pasulka, speaking on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, says she went through Catholic records, including the Vatican archives, which are the Catholic Church's central store of documents. She says she found reports of strange things seen in the sky, written by Catholics in Europe, Canada and the United States between about 1200 and 1800. If true, it would mean people were reporting such sightings centuries before the modern UFO era.
catholic-church-helps-nazis-escape-to-so: Peter Levenda, a researcher and author, said on Jesse Michels's podcast that after the Second World War ended in 1945, people in the Catholic Church decided to work with Nazis and hide them. According to Levenda, they gave them false papers and got them out to Bolivia, Argentina and similar places, which would mean powerful institutions helped wanted men disappear.
cattle-mutilations-done-by-humans: Steven Greer, a doctor and well-known UFO campaigner, said on Jesse Michels's podcast that the cattle mutilations, cases where farm animals are found dead and strangely cut, are done by people, not aliens. He says the journalist Linda Moulton Howe thinks aliens are behind them, but in his words, "we're doing that", meaning humans are staging what gets blamed on visitors.
cattle-mutilations-in-the-bigelow-era-19: Skinwalker Ranch is a ranch in Utah known for reports of strange events, and its current owner, Brandon Fugal, spoke about it on a podcast. He says that while Robert Bigelow, the businessman who owned it before him, ran the place from about 1996 to 2016, there were many cattle mutilations, cows found dead and strangely cut, and that animal autopsy reports were made at the time. It is told as part of the case that something unexplained goes on at the ranch.
cattle-mutilations-in-the-missile-field-: This story is about cattle found dead and cut up around a field of nuclear missile sites tied to Ellsworth, an Air Force base, in 1977. A former missile base guard named Mario Woods says cattle mutilations were going on in the area, and that a reporter, Linda Moulton Howe, was there looking into them. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells it from another veteran, Michael Johnson, who says cattle kept turning up dead in the weeks before a November night when the men say they were abducted, and adds that a camera was taken from them. People tell it because, if true, it ties strange events near nuclear weapons to the abductions those veterans describe.
caught-on-the-last-trip-and-banned-from-: Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked on alien craft at a secret site called S4 near Groom Lake, the Nevada base also known as Area 51, says that in 1989 he took friends out into the desert to watch test flights. He says the first time, nobody knew they were out there, but on the last trip they were caught, and he was banned from S4. For him, it marks the end of his time inside the program.
causeway-shafts-are-waterproof-and-hold-: A researcher named Filippo talks about shafts cut into the rock beneath the causeway, an ancient stone road on the Giza plateau in Egypt where the great pyramids stand. He says the shafts are waterproof: water stands outside them but cannot get in, so they hold air instead. He tells it as a sign that the shafts were deliberately built as part of a planned system, not just holes in the ground.
cave-of-poisoned-aboriginal-tribe-litter: A podcast host, Joe Rogan, passes on what his friend Adam Greenree told him about a visit to a site in Australia. According to Greenree, an entire tribe of Aboriginal Australians, the land's first people, had been given food that was deliberately poisoned, and the cave where they died is still littered with human bones.
caves-running-under-the-giza-plateau: This story is about caves under the Giza plateau, the area in Egypt where the great pyramids and the Sphinx stand. A researcher named Luke Caverns says on Jesse Michels' podcast that people digging there hit a cavern, and that through cracks in its walls there are caves running under the whole plateau. Another researcher, Geoffrey Drumm, says on the same show that it is known for sure that there are caves and tunnels under Giza, without telling how they were reached. If true, there would be a whole hidden underground world beneath the pyramids.
ce5-night-in-sedona-with-greer-s-team-an: A man named Michael Herrera told podcast host Jesse Michels about a night at a remote site off a trail near Sedona, Arizona. He says he was there with the team of Steven Greer, a man who leads group sessions meant to invite contact with visitors from elsewhere (a practice called CE5), along with the singer Demi Lovato and a woman named Paula Harris. Herrera says they sat and watched glowing balls of light and gold disc-shaped craft appear and vanish, and that someone took a blow from something nobody could see, which, if true, would mean such contact can be called up on purpose.
centcom-bottleneck-on-uap-information: A filmmaker and journalist, Jeremy Corbell, says that Central Command, the US military command that runs operations across the Middle East and Central Asia, acts as a bottleneck for information on UAP, the government's term for UFOs, before it ever reaches the public. If true, it would mean military reports of strange objects are held back at that level.
centcom-formation-of-12-metallic-orbs-sk: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, speaking with a man described as a Pentagon whistleblower, Matthew Brown, says that Central Command, the US military command responsible for a large region overseas, discussed a sighting on US government computer networks: twelve metallic orbs flying in a box-shaped formation, skimming low over the ocean. Michels links the account to a document he calls the Immaculate Constellation report, and no date or exact place is given. If true, it would mean the military had been quietly sharing reports of unknown craft among its own staff.
cern-physicists-report-beings-coming-thr: Astrid Stuckelberger, a guest on Jesse Michels's podcast, says physicists from CERN told her that beings are coming in and out through portals. CERN is the big European physics laboratory near Geneva, Switzerland, home to a huge particle collider. If it were true, it would mean scientists had opened doorways that something non-human uses, and in a later telling she adds that she knows physicists who are doing very strange experiments.
cernan-s-telepathic-message-on-apollo-17: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, relays a claim credited to a person named Takano Jouen about Eugene Cernan, an astronaut on Apollo 17, the 1972 mission to the Moon after which no one went back. According to this account, on the way to the Moon Cernan received some kind of telepathic message saying, "We don't really want you here." It is offered as the reason the Moon trips stopped.
cesar-demands-10-000-to-talk-to-rfk-jr: Dan Sheehan, a guest on Jesse Michels's podcast, says he talked about a man called Cesar with Robert F. Kennedy Jr., the American politician from the Kennedy family. According to Sheehan, Kennedy was going to meet the man to get him to talk, but the man insisted on being paid a large sum first, which Sheehan puts at about $110,000.
cesario-says-chereze-kept-linking-his-il: In 1996 in Varginha, a town in Brazil, people say a strange creature was caught, and a police officer named Marco Chereze, said to have helped catch it, later fell ill and died. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Cesario, a doctor who treated Chereze, recalls Chereze telling him again and again that his illness might come from the ET, short for extraterrestrial, that he had caught. If true, it would tie the officer's death directly to contact with a being not from Earth.
cesario-says-the-antibiotics-he-gave-che: A documentary filmmaker named James Fox has looked into a 1996 case in the Brazilian town of Varginha, where people say a strange creature was caught, and he talks about a doctor named Cesario who treated Marco Chereze, a police officer said to have handled the creature before falling ill. According to Fox, Cesario said he threw everything he had at the infection, and that the antibiotics should have saved Chereze's life but did nothing at all. If true, it would suggest the officer caught something no ordinary medicine could touch.
chaldean-and-sumerian-traditions-of-gods: Randall Carlson, a researcher of ancient catastrophes, said on Jesse Michels's podcast that there are traditions going back to the Chaldeans and Sumerians, ancient peoples of Mesopotamia, about gods who escaped a great catastrophe long ago. He tells it as a hint that old myths may remember a real disaster and beings who got away from it.
changes-inside-barber-s-program-after-th: Jake Barber, a helicopter pilot who says he flew a recovered UFO, told the podcast host Jesse Michels that he worked inside a secret programme. He says that when a 2017 New York Times article about Pentagon UFO work came out, things started getting really weird for his team, suggesting the article shook up those keeping the secrets.
chapel-hill-gravity-conference-kicks-off: Eric Weinstein, a mathematician, said in a debate on Jesse Michels's podcast that a famous conference on gravity at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill in the 1950s set off a lot of interest in anti-gravity, the idea of machines that cancel or control gravity. He points to it as the start of a burst of work in that area.
chariots-of-fire-as-angelic-vehicles: Tim Alberino, a guest on Jesse Michels's podcast, reads the Bible as describing real vehicles. He points out that its stories mention things called the chariots of God, the chariots of Israel, or the chariots of fire, and he suggests these were craft used by angels, which would mean ancient Israelites were describing flying machines.
charlemagne-and-the-tyrants-of-the-air: A philosopher, Jason Jorjani, drawing on a book called The Gods of Eden by a writer named William Bramley, tells of strange things in the skies over France in the time of Charlemagne, the great European king of around the year 800. Jorjani says the sightings were so common that hysteria broke out at the French court, and Charlemagne considered declaring war on the "tyrants of the air", which would mean people were dealing with visitors from the sky over a thousand years ago.
charles-and-drew-s-electrostatic-thrust-: A researcher named David said on Jesse Michels's podcast that two experimenters, Charles and Drew, have been testing devices that push using static electricity, in a lab with a shielded cage and a vacuum chamber. He describes their claim that you power the device up, unplug it from the wall, and the thrust keeps going on and on, which, if true, would point to a kind of propulsion that needs no ongoing power.
charles-buhler-leaves-nasa-for-propellan: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Charles Buhler, whom he calls the top scientist on static electricity at NASA, the US space agency, left NASA in the 2020s. According to Michels, Buhler started a venture to build a way of moving craft without burning fuel, based on gravity, which Buhler says comes from the work of Townsend Brown, an American inventor of the mid-1900s. If true, it would suggest Brown's long-dismissed ideas are being taken seriously by a NASA insider.
charles-buhler-leaves-nasa-to-found-exod: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Charles Buhler, whom he describes as NASA's lead scientist on electrostatics at Cape Kennedy, left the space agency to start his own company, Exodus Space. According to Michels, the company works on propellantless propulsion, a way of moving a craft without pushing out fuel, and Buhler credits the idea to an earlier researcher named Thomas Townsend Brown. If true, it would suggest that a once fringe idea about flight is being taken seriously by someone from inside NASA.
charles-burney-and-the-ivory-tower-of-ur: On a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, a researcher called Matt talks about Charles Burney, a scholar he calls the grandfather of the history of Urartu, an ancient kingdom around Lake Van in eastern Turkey. Matt brings him up as the kind of 'ivory tower' academic authority whose view of the region's deep past shaped the official story, which matters to anyone who thinks that story leaves something out.
charles-fort-we-are-property-like-britis: Jason Jorjani, a philosopher, said on Jesse Michels's podcast that the first person to think this way about UFOs was Charles Fort, a writer who collected reports of strange events, back in the 1920s. The idea Jorjani credits to Fort is that humans are property, owned by someone else the way Britain ruled India, which would mean we are being managed by beings we cannot see.
charles-hall-and-the-tall-whites-at-indi: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, brings up a man he calls Colonel Charles Hall, whose story is about tall, pale beings known as the tall whites. The story is set in the Indian Springs Valley in Nevada in the 1960s. If true, it would mean non-human beings were living near a US military area at the time.
charles-hall-flown-by-the-tall-whites-to: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, retells a story from a man named Charles Hall, who says he was stationed at the Nevada desert test grounds in the 1960s and met tall pale beings he calls the Tall Whites. classified-dod-payloads-as-evidence-of-a: A researcher appearing on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels says it is known that secret payloads for the US Department of Defense are routinely launched into space from Vandenberg Air Force Base in California. He points to this, from around the 1980s and 1990s on, as a sign that there could be a hidden military space program the public does not see.
classified-f-117-crash-near-bakersfield-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, mentions in passing that a secret F-117, the US military's stealth attack jet, crashed near Bakersfield, California, in 1986 "or something," as he puts it. He brings it up as an example of classified aircraft that the public didn't know about at the time, which matters to the wider question of what strange things in the sky might really be.
classified-lists-of-uncorrelated-targets: An astronomer named Beatriz Villarroel tells podcast host Jesse Michels that she learned that since the early 1960s there have been secret lists of 'uncorrelated targets', objects tracked in orbit around Earth that could not be matched to anything known. She ties this to space agencies and the US military's space branch. If true, it would mean unexplained objects have been quietly logged around our planet for decades.
