classified-navy-diver-unit-experimenting: Tim Gallaudet, a retired US Navy admiral, says there is a special unit of Navy divers, whose location he won't name, that has experimented with liquid breathing, where a person breathes an oxygen-rich liquid instead of air. He tells it while talking about what lies hidden in the ocean, and if true it would mean the Navy is quietly testing technology most people think of as science fiction.
classified-paper-comparing-human-and-et-: Lyn Buchanan, an Army sergeant, says that in the 1980s he worked in a remote viewing unit, a military programme that trained people to describe faraway places using only their minds. He says he was told to write a classified paper comparing the psychic abilities of humans and aliens, and that as soon as he turned it in, it disappeared, which he tells as a sign the subject was being kept secret.
classified-scif-testimony-to-congress-20: Jake Barber, a former military helicopter pilot who says he flew to recover a UFO, says that more than he can say publicly has been shared with members of Congress in a SCIF, a sealed room where secret material can be discussed. He says it was given at the top secret level, under the highest security clearance (TS/SCI), which if true would mean lawmakers have heard detailed evidence behind closed doors.
classified-signals-lab-picks-up-a-signal: Whitley Strieber, a writer who says he has met alien beings, says that in the mid-1990s a small object he calls an implant, taken from his body, was examined at the Southwest Research Institute, a research lab in San Antonio, Texas. He says the lab staff told him they detected a signal coming from it, which then turned off, but that they could tell him nothing more because the lab was classified. If true, it would suggest the object was a working device.
classified-tooth-implant-1960: A researcher named Greg Malatzi, on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, talks about a researcher and inventor named Andrija Puharich, who worked in the early 1960s at a New York City company called Intelectron. Malatzi says one of Puharich's inventions there was a tooth implant, a small device placed in a tooth, and that Puharich himself said it was classified. He tells it as part of the story of a scientist with ties to secret government work.
classified-video-meeting-smiling-officia: James Valor, a witness interviewed about Skywatcher, a startup that says it tries to summon UFOs, says that in 2025 he took part in a secret video meeting with an official. According to Valor, the official smiled and suggested that what they were discussing might not be from our planet, which he takes as a quiet hint from inside government.
claudio-valente-quits-his-job-and-vanish: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, telling a story about scientists who go missing, says that one day in 2013 a man named Claudio Valente showed up at work in Portugal, at a place called SAPO, and declared it would be his last day. According to Michels, Valente then vanished, and he tells it as part of a pattern of puzzling disappearances.
clay-shaw-phones-fred-crisman-during-the: A researcher and author named Peter Levenda, on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, says that a New Orleans man named Clay Shaw and another man named Fred Crisman seem to have known each other well. He says Shaw phoned Crisman in the late 1960s, while Jim Garrison, a New Orleans prosecutor, was investigating the Kennedy assassination. He raises it as a hint of hidden connections between people caught up in that case.
clearance-games-at-bae-2015-2018: Dylan Borland, who says he worked at BAE Systems, a large defense company, between 2015 and 2018, says people there were playing a game with security clearances, the official permission to see secret information. He tells it on Jesse Michels's podcast as part of his account of how secrets are guarded and handed out.
clementine-mission-as-photo-reconnaissan: Maaneli Derakhshani, speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast, passes on a claim from John Brandenburg, made in a book called Aliens on the Moon: The Truth Exposed. Brandenburg says that Clementine, a 1994 space mission to the Moon, was really a photo-spying mission to check whether someone was building bases on the Moon that we didn't know about, and whether those bases were growing. If true, it would mean officials suspected someone else was active on the Moon.
cliff-wong-on-faking-an-orb-with-a-drone: A guest on a podcast, Eric Hazeline, says he once asked a man named Cliff Wong, whom he calls the world's expert on drones, how someone would go about faking various kinds of sightings. Hazeline says Wong told him how it could be done, and the story is about faking an orb, a glowing ball seen in the sky, with a balloon pulled along by a drone. If true, it would show how some orb sightings could be staged.
clinic-doctor-turns-away-captured-creatu: A documentary filmmaker named James Fox tells a story from Varginha, a town in Brazil, where people say a strange creature was captured in January 1996. Relaying an account tied to a man named Marco Chereze, Fox says the creature was brought to a clinic, and the doctor there said, in effect, that he did not know what the thing was, but they should get it out of there. If true, it would mean a medical worker saw a living being nobody could identify.
clinical-examination-by-beings-1976: Charlie Foltz says that in August 1976, near Allagash in the Maine woods, he found himself aboard a craft, struggling to get up, when a face bent down to look into his eyes and beings began a clinical examination of him. He recalls a panel coming down from above his head that covered his whole torso and shone a blue light straight down onto him. He tells it on Jesse Michels's podcast as a first-hand account of being taken and examined by non-human beings.
clinton-and-obama-both-deny-anything-und: A researcher named Jason Simosa, on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, talks about Area 51, a secret US military base in the Nevada desert long tied to UFO stories. He says that two former presidents, Bill Clinton and Barack Obama, both said there is nothing underground at Area 51, and he finds it a weird thing for them to say, as if the denial itself hints at something hidden.
clinton-and-the-alh-84001-meteorite-as-s: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, points to a meteorite from Mars called ALH 84001, which he says President Bill Clinton spoke about publicly in the 1990s. Michels frames it as an early step in a slow, gradual release of evidence that life exists beyond Earth, the kind of drip-by-drip reveal some people call "disclosure".
clinton-briefed-on-ufos-by-civilian-bruc: This story is about how a US president may have been told about UFOs in the 1990s. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that a man named Ron Pandolfi, who worked at the CIA (the US government's spy agency), helped arrange for a civilian UFO researcher named Bruce Maccabee to brief President Bill Clinton. A researcher named Jason Simosa tells it differently, as Maccabee himself told it: Maccabee, a Navy physicist, got a call from Pandolfi asking him to repeat a lecture he had once given the CIA, this time for the president's science adviser rather than Clinton himself. If true, it would mean UFO research reached the White House through quiet back channels.
clinton-ends-the-superconducting-super-c: A researcher named Eric Weinstein, speaking on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, says that on October 30th, 1993, President Bill Clinton signed into law the "death blow" to the Superconducting Super Collider, a giant American particle physics machine then being built. Weinstein brings it up as a turning point when the United States stepped back from big physics, which matters to him if it shaped what science the country chose to pursue.
clinton-era-investigation-finds-40-tons-: An author and researcher named Peter Levenda, on Jesse Michels's podcast, says that an investigation under the Clinton administration in the 1990s found 40 tons of Nazi gold that had been shipped out of the Bank of Lisbon, in Portugal, by submarine, during the 1940s. He tells it as a trace of where hidden wartime wealth went, with places such as Macau, China and Indonesia in the background, which would matter if that money quietly funded things after the war.
clinton-era-pressure-on-the-dod-that-sha: Jake Barber, a former military helicopter pilot who says he flew to recover a UFO, says it is no coincidence that his own experience began in the 1990s, when Bill Clinton was president. He says the Clinton White House put pressure on the Department of Defense, including setting up a red team, a group meant to break in from the outside, to get into black programs, the secret projects hidden from normal oversight, which if true would mean a president tried to force open hidden UFO work.
clinton-era-technology-transfer-to-china: John Herrington, presented as a former US Secretary of Energy, says that in the 1990s, under President Bill Clinton, the US Commerce and Defense departments let important technology pass to China. As proof, he says every Chinese fighter jet looks like an American one, such as the F-15.
clinton-s-televised-statement-on-rock-84: In 1996 President Bill Clinton spoke on television about a rock known as 84001, a meteorite believed to have come from Mars. He said the rock speaks to us across billions of years and millions of miles of the possibility of life, which is why it is cited as an official nod to life beyond Earth.
clinton-said-he-didn-t-think-they-d-tell: A former CIA officer named Rolf Mowatt-Larssen, speaking with podcast host Jesse Michels, recalls an interview with former US President Bill Clinton. He says Clinton was asked whether the government had signs of alien life or a hidden programme, and answered, roughly, that he didn't think they would tell him even though he was the president. If true, it would suggest such secrets could be kept even from the person at the top.
clock-gear-found-inside-marble-in-brazil: A guest on Jesse Michels' podcast, Kiran Ilum Xenov, introduced as a former president of a republic within Russia, says that in Brazil, workers cutting marble slabs out of mountains have found pieces of a clock inside the stone, even a gear. If true, it would mean made objects sealed in rock far older than any known human history.
close-encounters-as-a-celebration-of-an-: A researcher named Dr. John Brandenburg says on Jesse Michels's podcast that, as he argues in his book Cosmic Awakening, the 1977 film Close Encounters of the Third Kind was the government's way of using Hollywood to celebrate an arrangement it had made with the grays, the gray-skinned aliens of many UFO stories. He brings in J. Allen Hynek, a UFO researcher, in telling it. If true, a famous film would have been a quiet public nod to a secret deal.
close-encounters-contains-a-visual-refer: A researcher named Bryce Zabel, on Jesse Michels' podcast, says that Steven Spielberg's 1977 film Close Encounters of the Third Kind, which ends at Devils Tower in Wyoming, contains a whole visual reference to Project Serpo, a claimed secret programme in which Americans are said to have travelled to another world. He says it is there whether or not you believe in Serpo, which would suggest the filmmakers knew of the story.
close-encounters-of-the-third-kind-as-in: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Steven Spielberg's 1977 alien film Close Encounters of the Third Kind, which ends at Devils Tower in Wyoming, borrowed from real UFO material. As an example, he says crates in the film carry the names of the aerospace companies TRW and Lockheed, and he links the film to the UFO researchers J. Allen Hynek and Jacques Vallee. If true, it would mean a famous movie quietly reflected what insiders knew.
close-up-witnesses-sensed-being-watched: A former US intelligence officer named David Grusch, speaking with a podcast host, Jesse Michels, says he has talked with people who had their own close-up sightings of unexplained objects. Grusch says they told him they got the same feeling of being watched. If true, it would suggest that close encounters bring a shared sense of being observed.
closed-session-testimony-on-rocky-flats: John Herrington, a former US Secretary of Energy, the cabinet member in charge of the Energy Department, says he went back several times to testify to Congress in closed, restricted sessions. He says these were about security issues at the Energy Department, especially at Rocky Flats, a government site in Colorado. He tells it on Jesse Michels's podcast as part of what he knows of secret government matters.
closing-down-the-first-base-and-transfer: Dan Sherman, a former Air Force sergeant who says the National Security Agency, a US spy agency, hired him to communicate with aliens, says that in the early 1990s he closed down the first base where his secret programme ran. He says the whole base closed, not just his part of it, and he moved on to a second base. If true, it would place a hidden alien-contact programme inside ordinary military bases.
clyde-tombaugh-and-earth-s-small-moons-g: A scientist named Steve Coburn, on the podcast of host Jesse Michels, says that the astronomer Clyde Tombaugh wrote an article in the 1950s saying Earth had some small moons orbiting about 500 miles up. Coburn connects this to the idea of large grey alien 'motherships' sitting in orbit. If true, it would mean big unknown craft have been circling Earth for a long time.
clyde-tombaugh-s-ashes-on-new-horizons-2: A Harvard scientist named Avi Loeb, on Jesse Michels's podcast, says that NASA put about 30 grams of the ashes of Clyde Tombaugh, the scientist who discovered Pluto, aboard New Horizons, the spacecraft sent to explore Pluto. Loeb calls this "the most embarrassing thing," using it to make a point about what humans choose to send into space, and what that would say to anyone who found it.
coanda-1936-lenticular-aerodyne-patent: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Henri Coanda, an aircraft engineer, filed a patent in 1936 for a "lenticular aerodyne," a lens-shaped flying machine much like a disc. Michels raises it because it would mean people were already designing saucer-like craft years before the wave of flying saucer reports began.
coast-to-coast-call-drops-at-the-lost-ti: Richard Barth, a former guard at a US nuclear missile site who says he was taken by aliens, says he was once on Coast to Coast AM, a late-night radio show about the unexplained, with host George Noory and researcher Robert Hastings, author of the book UFOs and Nukes. He says that when he was asked whether he had any "lost time," a gap in memory during the event, and he started to answer, the line suddenly went dead. He tells it as if something did not want him to say it.
coast-to-coast-callers-claiming-time-tra: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, recalls that in the 1990s people would phone in to Coast to Coast, a late-night radio talk show hosted by Art Bell, claiming to be insiders. According to Michels, some said they were doing time travel work at Area 51, a secret military base in Nevada. He tells it to show that whistleblowers coming forward about secret programs are nothing new.
coating-compound-found-in-the-bent-pyram: A researcher named Geoffrey Drumm says on Jesse Michels' podcast that a coating compound has been found inside the Bent Pyramid, an ancient pyramid at Dahshur in Egypt. He says the coating would have protected the limestone walls from a harsh, corrosive chemical reaction, which, if true, would mean chemical processes were once run inside the pyramid.
coburn-s-implant-scans-of-experiencers: Steve Coburn, a scientist who studies what he believes are alien implants in human bodies, says he has done about 400 scans on people who report contact with non-human beings. He tells it on Jesse Michels's podcast and mentions Roger Leir, another researcher of such implants. If true, it would mean physical objects of unknown origin are being found inside people.
cocoa-beach-light-that-exploded-split-in: A witness named Charles says that around 2013, at Cocoa Beach in Florida near Patrick Air Force Base, he and his partner saw a light in the sky that seemed to explode. He says it was then no longer one light but six, and that the lights followed the couple, something he tells as a sign the lights were acting with purpose.
cold-war-english-russian-playing-cards-f: Greg Rogers, a NASA doctor, says that during the Cold War there were playing cards printed in both English and Russian. He says the purpose was communication: you could show a word in English and the other person could read it in Russian, a way to talk with hostages or captives. He tells it on Jesse Michels's podcast as a detail from his own experience.
colleagues-close-the-door-and-reveal-hid: David Grusch, a former US intelligence officer, says that colleagues he had known for years came into his office, shut the door, and told him there were secret programmes his team was not being given access to. In one telling he says this happened at the NGA, a US spy agency that works with satellite and map intelligence, and that they brought him startling intelligence reports. He tells it as how he first learned of hidden UFO work, though his own dates differ, pointing either to around 2019 to 2021 or to about fourteen years before he spoke.
colleagues-grandparents-were-ufo-report-: A former US intelligence officer named David Grusch says some of his colleagues have told him that their grandparents were the people who handled UFO reports during the Manhattan Project, the secret US effort of the 1940s to build the atomic bomb. If true, it would mean UFO reports were being quietly gathered inside one of the government's most secret projects, long before most people had heard of flying saucers.
collecting-the-borderland-science-resear: A researcher named Clas Svahn, who gathers UFO papers and records, told podcast host Jesse Michels how he got the archive of a group called the Borderland Science Research Association. He says he went to Eureka, California, met a man in his garage, and together they packed the whole collection up and shipped it back to Sweden. He tells it as part of how he came to hold so much of this material, which would mean an old body of records now sits safely in one place.
collection-of-9-11-precognitive-dreams-2: A scientist named Rupert Sheldrake told podcast host Jesse Michels that when the World Trade Center was attacked in New York in 2001, he saw a chance to study dreams that seem to foresee the future. He says that within three days he had posters up in Washington Square and ads in the Village Voice, a New York weekly paper, asking whether people had dreamed of the towers, and that he now has more than 75 such dreams people sent him. If the dreams are what they seem, it would suggest people can sense events before they happen.
collins-elite-blocking-uap-research-as-d: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, has brought up several times a group he calls the Collins Elite, which he describes as a circle of evangelical Christians tied to the United States government. According to Michels, this group was one of the main things blocking research into UAPs, short for unidentified anomalous phenomena, the official modern term for UFOs. In one episode he links this to what Lue Elizondo has said. Elizondo is a former Pentagon official who ran a small office that studied unexplained aerial reports. In another episode Michels says the group looked at the phenomenon through a program called Stack Five at a place he calls Wright airfield, and decided it was all demonic. He credits this to an author, Nick Redfern, and his book Final Events. A researcher, Jason Simosa, adds that Redfern's sources say the effort was funded in 1952 through the CIA's Directorate of Plans, a branch of the US spy agency, with about twelve people working on it full time. Michels himself also calls the story a rumour at one point, and a guest named Maaneli Derakhshani says only that he has heard rumours of the group. If it were true, religious belief would have decided whether the government took the subject seriously.
collins-elite-met-aliens-and-considered-: A guest named Kurt Metzger, on Jesse Michels's podcast, describes what he read about a group called the Collins Elite in the book Final Events by writer Nick Redfern. He says the group first met aliens and then asked whether they could use them to assassinate people. If true, a secret group would have looked at aliens as a weapon.
colonel-alexander-s-precognitive-sentien: A researcher named Jason Jorjani, speaking on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, says that strange events at Skinwalker Ranch, a Utah ranch known for reports of odd happenings, led a military officer called Colonel Alexander to come up with a name for them: "precognitive sentient phenomena," meaning something aware that seems to know what people will do before they do it. Jorjani points to a work called Closer Encounters for this, and places it around the 1990s and 2000s. If true, it would mean whatever is at the ranch is not only intelligent but always a step ahead of the people watching it.
colonel-blanchard-announces-a-crashed-fl: A scientist named John Brandenburg, on the podcast of host Jesse Michels, retells what he says veterans of the Roswell base told him. According to them, in 1947 everyone was seeing UFOs, and the well-liked commander of Roswell Army Air Field, a military base in New Mexico, Colonel Blanchard, called the local newspaper and announced they had found a crashed flying saucer. If true, it would mean the military itself once openly admitted recovering an alien craft.
colonel-coleman-s-b-25-ufo-encounter-ove: A documentary filmmaker named James Fox says his research led him to an Air Force officer, Colonel William Coleman. According to Fox, Coleman had a dramatic encounter with a UFO in the 1950s while flying a B-25, a military bomber plane, over Alabama. If true, it would be a close sighting by an experienced military pilot.
colonel-hohman-sold-sdi-to-reagan-using-: A doctor and UFO disclosure campaigner named Steven Greer says a military officer, Colonel Hohman, told him about how the Strategic Defense Initiative, or SDI, the 1980s US plan for a missile shield in space, was sold to President Ronald Reagan. Greer says Hohman told him they pitched it using a threat from aliens that they knew was false, and it brought in billions of dollars for SDI. If true, it would mean fear of aliens was used on purpose to fund weapons.
colorado-2019-2020-sightings-over-missil: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in 2019 and 2020 people in Colorado reported strange objects in the sky, and that some of them were partly over nuclear missile silos, the underground launch sites for nuclear weapons. He says these sightings mirrored similar events in 1965, which, if true, would point to a long pattern of unknown things showing interest in nuclear weapons.
colossal-biosciences-to-run-ancient-dna-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in 2025 he contacted his friend Ben Lam at Colossal Biosciences, a genetics company, about mummified bodies from Peru that have three fingers on each hand. According to Michels, the plan was to run ancient DNA tests on them, with the geneticist George Church also named. The tests could help settle what these strange bodies really are.
colossal-dna-test-on-the-wolf-carcass-is: Brandon Fugal, the owner of Skinwalker Ranch, a Utah property known for reports of strange events, says DNA from a wolf carcass found there was sent to Colossal Biosciences, a genetics company. He says the results came back and most of the DNA could not be identified. If true, it would suggest something truly unknown about the animal.
columbia-tv-threatens-to-burn-your-negat: Bryce Zabel, a television writer and producer, says that around 1995, while making the first episode of his UFO drama series Dark Skies, he got a threat from the Columbia TV studio in Los Angeles. He says he was told to get his actors out of their black suits, the look of the secret agents known as Men in Black, that very day, or the studio would shut down the production and burn the film. He links this to Steven Spielberg's company Amblin and director Barry Sonnenfeld, and tells it as a memory seared into his head.
columbus-uses-a-predicted-eclipse-to-mak: A magician and YouTuber named Chris Ramsay, talking with podcast host Jesse Michels, tells a story he credits in part to the writer Arthur C. Clarke. He says Christopher Columbus, stranded on a Caribbean island he places in the Bahamas, told the local people that if they did not help his crew he would block out the sun in three days, and three days later a solar eclipse came. Ramsay tells it to show how more advanced knowledge can look like magic to those without it.
coming-out-after-retirement-daily-mail-a: Greg Rogers, a doctor who says he worked with NASA and saw a UFO inside a secret hangar, says he only went public after he retired. He says that on 4 May 2025 a journalist named Josh Boswell published an interview with him in the UK newspaper the Daily Mail, and that he also spoke with Ty Roberts of the International UFO Bureau in Oklahoma City for an interview called Total Disclosure. He tells it to explain how and why his story came out when it did.
commander-david-fravor-works-at-bae-2004: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says he believes that David Fravor, a Navy commander and fighter pilot, now works at BAE, a large defence company. Fravor is known for the 2004 Nimitz incident, when Navy pilots from the aircraft carrier USS Nimitz reported an unexplained object off San Diego. Michels mentions it as a link between a key UFO witness and the defence industry.
commander-george-hoover-on-aliens-saying: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that a US Navy officer, Commander George Hoover, talked about aliens who come down and tell people, "you don't know how powerful you are." Michels raises it as a hint that, if true, these beings see some hidden power in humans that we don't recognize in ourselves.
commercial-mining-pilot-tests-of-the-sar: A researcher named Filippo, who uses a radar scanning technique to look beneath the ground, says he ran many trial tests of it for mining companies under secrecy agreements. He says the results were more than 100% successful. He tells it on Jesse Michels's podcast to back up his claim that the technique can reveal what lies underground, such as beneath the pyramids of Egypt.
communicating-with-the-logical-alien-he-: A former Air Force sergeant named Dan Sherman, who says the National Security Agency (the US agency that handles eavesdropping and codes) hired him to talk with aliens, described this on Jesse Michels' podcast. He says that in the early 1990s, at his first overseas posting, he communicated with two beings, and the first, a very logical one, he nicknamed Spock. He tells the story, also covered in his book Above Black, because it would mean the government was in quiet contact with non-human beings.
communion-letters-held-in-the-archives-o: Thousands of letters that readers sent to the writer Whitley Strieber after his 1987 book Communion, about his own reported meetings with strange visitors, are said to be kept at Rice University in Houston, Texas. Strieber says "four or 5 thousand of them" sit there in a collection called the Archives of the Impossible, which he says was founded by the professor Jeff Kripal. To him, the letters are a record of how many ordinary people say they have had experiences like his.
communion-prompts-nearly-half-a-million-: Bryce Zabel, a guest on Jesse Michels' podcast, says that after the writer Whitley Strieber published his 1987 book Communion, nearly half a million people wrote letters to Strieber and his wife. Zabel tells it to show how many people the book seemed to reach, and how many may have felt it described something they knew.
communion-released-early-because-of-some: A writer named Whitley Strieber says that in 1987 his book Communion showed up in American bookstores earlier than he expected. Speaking to a podcast host, Jesse Michels, he says he had been given one publication date, and then all of a sudden the books were on the shelves, which he puts down to "some kind of resistance." If that were so, it would mean someone was working behind the scenes around how his story reached the public.
community-backlash-and-social-services-v: Chris Bledsoe is a North Carolina man who says he has had strange encounters. Speaking to podcast host Jesse Michels, he says that after what happened to him in 2007 he faced so much trouble from his community that he stopped speaking to half or even two-thirds of his own family, cousins included. He also says social services, the local agency that handles family welfare, came to his house and tried to have him removed from it, which shows how heavy a price he says he paid for speaking up.
compartmentalization-carried-over-from-t: An online researcher who goes by UAPGerb, talking with a podcast host, Jesse Michels, explains how he thinks the Pentagon's secret UFO work is organized. Echoing a former intelligence officer, David Grusch, he says the way secrets are split into sealed-off pieces, so each group knows only its own part, is all carried over from the Manhattan Project, the secret 1940s effort to build the atomic bomb. If true, it would mean today's UFO secrecy runs on a system built during World War Two.
complex-equations-in-vinod-s-automatic-w: A researcher named Greg Malatzi describes a notebook from the 1950s kept at the Round Table Foundation, a research group in Maine that explored psychic matters. He says that during sessions of automatic writing, where words are said to flow out without the writer's conscious control, a man known as Dr. Vinod produced many very complex equations. If true, it would suggest the messages came from a source with knowledge beyond the person writing them.
compton-belkovich-heat-anomaly-on-the-lu: A researcher appearing as a guest on Jesse Michels's podcast says that NASA's infrared imaging of the whole Moon shows one area on the far side, a spot called Compton-Belkovich, giving off 20 times the average heat of the rest of the far side. The guest raises it as a mystery about the Moon that, if it holds up, would point to something unusual going on there.
concrete-crane-slab-at-the-crash-site-19: Hart Canyon, near Aztec in New Mexico, is a place where some people say a craft crashed in 1948. Podcast host Jesse Michels visited the site, drawing on a man named Carl Flock, and says that somewhere out there in 1948 someone in a hurry mixed concrete, apparently to make a base for a crane. If that is true, it would point to a rushed recovery operation at the spot.
condon-committee-coordinated-with-air-fo: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells of the Condon Committee, a 1966 UFO study at the University of Colorado Boulder led by the physicist Edward Condon. Michels says the US Air Force paid for it but it was meant to be free of Air Force influence, and that Condon in fact worked with an Air Force colonel, Robert Hippler. He calls the result a hit job on UFO research, meaning the official verdict was steered.
condon-report-and-its-links-to-atomic-se: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, points out that physicist Edward Condon, who led the Condon Report, a late 1960s UFO study done in Colorado for the US Air Force, was close friends with Robert Oppenheimer, head of the atomic bomb lab at Los Alamos, going back to their student days in Göttingen, Germany, in the 1920s. Michels links this to the secrecy of the atomic age, naming a Los Alamos teaching document and the laws that put atomic knowledge under tight government control. If he is right, it would mean the study of UFOs was shaped by the same people and habits that kept the bomb secret.
condon-report-closes-blue-book-1968: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says the 1968 Condon report, the final report of a university UFO study, led to the closing of Project Blue Book, the US Air Force's UFO study of the 1950s and 60s, and brushed off its cases with ordinary explanations. Michels says that if you read the report itself, over 30 percent of the cases stayed unidentified, which he links to Blue Book's scientific adviser J. Allen Hynek. He tells it to show that the dismissive conclusion did not match the report's own contents.
condon-s-letters-with-colonel-robert-hip: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that letters between the physicist Edward Condon, who led a 1960s government-funded UFO study, and an Air Force colonel named Robert Hippler show that Condon was closely coordinating with the Air Force. Michels tells it as evidence that a study meant to be independent was not.
condon-worked-with-manhattan-project-fig: This story is about the physicist Edward Condon's ties to the Manhattan Project, the secret US effort in the 1940s to build the atomic bomb. David Grusch, a former intelligence officer who says the government hides crashed craft not made by humans, says on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels that Condon was involved, and he mentions Vannevar Bush, a top wartime science official. Michels fills in more. He says Condon is sometimes credited with helping Robert Oppenheimer, the bomb project's scientific leader, choose Los Alamos in New Mexico as its site. He says Condon was linked to the Los Alamos Primer, an early teaching document for the project, and helped with the McMahon Atomic Energy Act, the law that set up postwar control of nuclear matters. In a later episode Michels adds that Condon studied in Germany with the physicist Max Born and that he and Oppenheimer were very close. It is told because Condon later led an Air Force UFO study, and the link would tie that study to the world of nuclear secrecy.
condon-wrote-the-mcmahon-secrecy-languag: The podcast host Jesse Michels says the physicist Edward Condon wrote the secrecy rules in the McMahon Act, the 1946 US law that put atomic research under tight control, which later fed into the Atomic Energy Act of 1954. Michels argues that this meant Condon was, in effect, writing the rules of UFO secrecy before he went on to dismiss the whole UFO subject, which would make the official debunker the author of the cover.
conflicting-accounts-of-who-sent-puharic: A researcher named Greg tells of a disagreement over why Andrija Puharich, a scientist who studied psychic claims, went to Tel Aviv, Israel, around 1970 and 1971. One account says a foundation sent him, but Greg says that Uri Geller, an Israeli man known for claiming psychic powers, said Puharich was sent directly by the CIA, the US spy agency. If Geller is right, it would mean American intelligence was behind that work.
congress-denied-a-scif-for-grusch-s-clas: In 2023 a whistleblower named David Grusch testified before the US Congress about UFOs, and part of what he knew could only be shared in secret. That kind of briefing has to happen in a SCIF, a specially secured room for handling classified information. Grusch says the members of Congress were furious because, as he understood it, they couldn't reserve one for his classified briefing in Washington. A second account comes from an unnamed speaker who seems to be one of those members. This person tells it first-hand and goes further, saying flatly that "we were denied access" to the room. If true, it would suggest that someone inside the system was trying to keep lawmakers from hearing what Grusch had to say.
congress-of-vienna-vatican-monarchies-an: A man named Jason Samosa, on Jesse Michels's podcast, says that in 1815 the Vatican, the royal families of Europe and the Knights of Malta, an old Catholic order of knights, "colluded" in what was called the Congress of Vienna, a gathering of European powers led by the Austrian statesman Klemens von Metternich, to organise against revolution. He tells it as an early chapter in a story about a secret society, which he links to the hiding of UFO knowledge.
congress-sends-borland-to-aaro-at-the-en: Dylan Borland is a man who has spoken publicly about UFO matters. He told podcast host Jesse Michels that in 2023, members of Congress put him in touch with AARO, the Pentagon office set up to investigate unidentified flying objects, and that he went to meet them at the end of March. In his account, it shows lawmakers took what he had to say seriously enough to send him to the government's official UFO office.
congressional-and-senate-hearings-reveal: A podcast host named Jesse Michels says that in late 2024 there were hearings on Capitol Hill in Washington, first in the House of Representatives and then in the Senate, that brought to light a secret programme called Immaculate Constellation. In a later episode he leaves out the Senate and calls it simply a top-secret programme. If it is real, it would mean the government has been running a hidden effort on these questions.
congressional-attempts-to-study-ufos-blo: An author and researcher named Peter Levenda says that since the 1970s there have been attempts in the US Congress to get UFOs recognized and at least studied. He says that when lawmakers start learning about it, they fall back on talk of angels and demons and get frightened, and that the efforts have been blocked by groups who believe God does not want us to do this. If true, it would mean religious fear has kept the government from looking into UFOs.
congressional-report-on-the-1944-maison-: An author and researcher named Peter Levenda says that in June 1945, before the war in Asia had ended, the US Congress published a report about a meeting held in 1944 at the Maison Rouge, a hotel in Strasbourg, France. Levenda points to it as an official record of that meeting, which, if he is right, would show that Congress knew about it at the time.
congressional-research-service-ufo-study: Dan Sheehan is a lawyer who says he was involved in a UFO study in 1977. He tells podcast host Jesse Michels that President Jimmy Carter asked the House science and technology committee to have the Congressional Research Service, the research arm of Congress based at the Library of Congress in Washington, do a special project on everything the US government knew about UFOs. Sheehan says he served as special counsel on it and names a woman called Marcia Smith in connection with it, which would mean a president himself went looking for the government's UFO files.
congressional-safe-harbor-bill-gutted-20: This story is about a proposed US law in 2023, the UAP Disclosure Act, meant to push out government secrets about UAP, a term for unidentified anomalous phenomena, or UFOs. A UFO activist named Steven Greer says the bill would have given people who held these secrets safe harbour, meaning amnesty and protection, so they could come forward. He says Congress got close to passing it, but it was gutted by members of Congress he names as Turner and Rogers, along with former Speaker Nancy Pelosi and others. A lawyer named Danny Sheehan says the main person stopping the full bill was Mike Turner, a congressman from Ohio whose district includes Wright-Patterson Air Force Base, and he also mentions congressman Dan Crenshaw. A podcast host named Jesse Michels says simply that the bill was killed by Turner. People tell it because, if true, a few lawmakers blocked the best chance yet for insiders to reveal what the government knows.
congressional-source-puts-crash-retrieva: Merrick von Renenamp, a guest on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, says he asked someone who works in the US Congress a direct question sometime in the 2020s: how sure are you that secret programs exist to recover crashed craft not made by humans? According to von Renenamp, the source answered that their confidence was close to 100 percent. If that were true, it would mean people inside government believe such recovered craft are real.
congressman-on-progress-of-reverse-engin: An unnamed member of Congress, asked about the Wilson memo, a leaked set of notes said to describe secret programs that study recovered craft, says he believes such efforts exist but have not cracked the technology. His reasoning is that if they had, the US would own the skies.
congressman-schiff-and-the-deleted-roswe: James Fox, speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast, recalls what a US congressman named Schiff found in the 1990s about Roswell, the New Mexico town where many believe a craft not made by humans crashed in 1947. According to Fox, Schiff noted that all the archived government records about Roswell had been deleted. People tell this because missing records could suggest something was being hidden.
congressman-witnesses-odni-official-apol: Eric Berles, a member of the US Congress, says he watched a blunt meeting between David Grusch, a former intelligence officer who went public with claims of hidden UFO programmes, and someone from the ODNI, the office that oversees all US spy agencies. According to Berles, the official was in effect apologising for how Grusch had been treated over the years, which he presents as the government quietly admitting it handled Grusch badly.
consciousness-based-secret-space-program: Lyn Buchanan, a former US Army sergeant, is asked about the idea of a secret space programme run through the mind, where people bilocate, meaning they project themselves to be in another place, here other planets, without leaving their bodies. Buchanan answers simply that yes, he has done that, which if true would mean the mind can travel where spacecraft cannot.
consecrating-holy-prophet-aluyah-during-: Peter Levenda, an author who writes about secret history and the occult, says that around 1968 or 1969 in the Bronx, New York, he took part in consecrating a man known as Holy Prophet Aluyah as a bishop. He says this was during the Biafra war, Nigeria's civil war of that time, and that people from the Nigerian embassy were there, a detail he tells as a strange link between small religious groups and world politics.
construction-worker-visited-by-a-blue-be: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says one of his past guests was a construction worker who told him a blue being appeared in his bedroom and passed advanced physics ideas into his mind. Michels says this brought the man to the attention of two physicists, Eric Davis and Hal Puthoff, who are interested in such cases. If true, it would mean some beings can hand real scientific knowledge to ordinary people.
consulting-for-a-jeans-company-on-shadin: Don Hoffman, a scientist who studies how the brain builds what we see, says he once consulted for a jeans company, which he won't name, on how shading and stitching change the way the jeans look. He says the company's chief executive jumped out of his chair, went up to the screen and said their jeans made his backside look bad, a story he tells to show how much our perception is shaped by small tricks.
consumer-product-safety-commission-swat-: Bob Lazar, a man who says he once worked on recovered flying craft at a secret site in Nevada, told podcast host Jesse Michels about a raid on his business, United Nuclear, sometime in the 2000s. Lazar says the Consumer Product Safety Commission, a US government agency that polices the safety of products sold to the public, came to his home with an armed tactical team, and that his wife was woken in bed with a rifle pointed at her face. He tells it as an example of how heavily the government has come down on him.
contact-from-steven-greer-s-disclosure-p: Dan Sherman is a former Air Force sergeant who says the NSA, the US agency that intercepts communications, once had him communicate with aliens. He tells podcast host Jesse Michels that in 2025 someone from the Disclosure Project, a group run by UFO activist Steven Greer that gathers witnesses, contacted him and offered him whistleblower immunity, meaning legal protection, if he would testify. Sherman says it was not Greer himself, though he thinks the two spoke a long time ago.
contact-in-the-desert-appearances-replac: Peter Levenda, an author who writes about secret history, told podcast host Jesse Michels how he came to speak at Contact in the Desert, a conference about UFOs and contact with other beings. He says he was first invited long ago as a stand-in for someone, and later invited to replace another speaker, Jim Marrs, who was sick that year, which would place it around 2017.
contact-with-a-being-and-taken-aboard-a-: Steven Greer, a doctor who campaigns for the government to reveal what it knows about UFOs, told podcast host Jesse Michels that in October 1973, at a fire tower in the Blue Ridge Mountains near Boone, North Carolina, he met a being and was taken aboard a craft. He says the creature was about five feet tall with beautiful, deer-like eyes, and that it came over and touched him on his right shoulder. Greer describes this contact as the root of his later life's work, which would mean humans can meet such beings directly.
contents-of-the-cave-and-the-three-body-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, describes a cave in the Nazca region of Peru, said to have been found in 2015, and points to a witness he calls Leandro. According to Michels, the cave held over 200 body parts, including separate heads, limbs and other appendages, and in many cases whole intact bodies, said to be some 700 to 1,800 years old and of three different body types. If true, it would mean unknown beings were preserved in Peru centuries ago.
contesting-account-and-aaro-position-on-: A former US Senate staffer named Kurt McConnell, on Jesse Michels' podcast, talks about Robert Jacobs, a man who says he filmed a 1964 missile test from Vandenberg Air Force Base near Big Sur, California, and saw something unusual on the film. McConnell says another man with very good credentials disputes Jacobs, claiming Jacobs mixed up the date of the test, and the story is also tied to the position of AARO, the Pentagon office that now looks into unexplained aerial reports. It matters because it bears on whether Jacobs' well-known account holds up.
continuity-of-government-succession-harr: John Harrington served as US Secretary of Energy in the 1980s. He tells podcast host Jesse Michels that he was part of the continuity-of-government plan, the secret arrangement to keep the government running after a catastrophe, and that he was number 16 in the line of succession. He says he remembers it because his daughter sewed a big 16 on the back of his swimsuit, a detail he gives to show how close he was to the inner workings of power.
contractor-ms-finds-a-craft-being-disass: A researcher who goes by the online name UAPGerb tells a story he heard from a contractor he calls only "MS", who was reading electric meters at Dugway Proving Ground, a US Army testing range in the Utah desert. According to UAPGerb, MS walked into a building in a remote part of the base called Avery and saw a craft that seemed to be in the middle of being taken apart. If true, it would point to unusual craft being studied in secret on military land.
contractor-saic-likely-involved-in-psion: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that a government contractor known as SAIC was likely involved in psychotronic or psionic research, meaning research into mind powers and machines that act on the mind. He raises it while discussing the claims of a man named Randy Anderson. If true, it would mean private companies helped the government study the mind as a tool.
control-room-camera-challenge-produces-t: Skinwalker Ranch is a property in Utah long known for reports of strange happenings. Eric Bard, who works there, says that one day in the ranch's control room he said out loud that this was stupid, then added, "If you got something you want to show me, show me. If you got something you want to tell me, tell me," and the very first camera screenshot afterwards showed letters that spelled "I living." The ranch's owner, Brandon Fugal, says that when they examined the image, something had pulled letters on the screen together out of order in a split second to form those words, which would suggest something there was answering.
controlled-remote-viewing-created-by-ing: Lyn Buchanan, a former US Army sergeant, told podcast host Jesse Michels about controlled remote viewing, a method that claims to let a trained person describe faraway places or hidden things using only the mind. He says it was created by a man named Ingo Swann, used by the military for years to gather intelligence, and is now used by businesses, while its higher stages, eight through eighteen, are not taught to the public.
controller-reports-objects-descending-fr: In 2004, off the coast of San Diego, a US Navy group led by the aircraft carrier Nimitz is said to have tracked strange objects in the sky. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, reads the words of a pilot: the radar controller told them the objects had been seen for over two weeks, dropping down from above 80,000 feet. A guest named Merrick von Rennenkampf, crediting a man named Kevin Day, tells it a little differently: about ten days of tracking, with odd objects at 28,000 feet moving south at 100 knots. If true, it would mean something was moving through the sky in ways no known aircraft does, and the Navy watched it for days.
cook-interviews-ning-li-at-a-2003-confer: Nick Cook is a British journalist who has investigated claims about secret anti-gravity research. He tells podcast host Jesse Michels that in 2003 he met and interviewed Ning Li, a scientist linked to anti-gravity work, at a conference just outside Washington, D.C. His account puts him face to face with a key figure in that research.
cook-s-visit-to-the-bell-site-in-the-wal: Nick Cook, a British journalist who wrote a book called The Hunt for Zero Point, says he went with a Polish researcher named Igor Witkowski to the place where the Bell, a secret device supposedly built by Nazi Germany during the Second World War, was said to have been installed: deep in a mine at Waldenburg, in what is now southern Poland. Podcast host Jesse Michels retells the visit, saying the trip involved a boat ride underground and that Cook saw the test rig where the device stood, which would suggest the wartime project was real.
cooper-s-ufo-in-orbit-1963: A guest named Charlie Foltz, on the podcast of host Jesse Michels, passes on what he says the astronaut Gordon Cooper told him about a flight around 1963 during NASA's first crewed spaceflight programme. According to Foltz, Cooper said an object came close to him in orbit, and Foltz thinks Cooper said it was green. If true, it would mean an American astronaut met something unknown in space.
coordinated-hit-job-on-malmgren-after-je: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that after he interviewed a man named Harold Malmgren, who spoke about a secret history touching figures such as the CIA official Richard Bissell and the wealthy Paul Mellon, a coordinated attack piece was written about him. According to Michels, it included claims, also on Malmgren's Wikipedia page, that an archivist had never heard of him. Michels tells it because he sees it as an effort to discredit a source who was talking about hidden matters.
cop-manuel-sandoval-chases-a-disc-from-c: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells of a police officer named Manuel Sandoval in the small town of Cuba, New Mexico, on the night of March 24, 1948. According to Michels, a disc came wobbling low over the town, and Sandoval did what he had long said he would do: he chased it all night along Old Highway 44. The chase is part of a larger story of a craft said to have crashed into a nearby mesa, which would mean something unknown came down in New Mexico that year.
copperfield-s-great-wall-walk-through-an: On Jesse Michels' podcast, a magician named Chris Ramsay points to the stage magician David Copperfield, who in the 1980s appeared to walk through the Great Wall of China and to make the Statue of Liberty disappear. Ramsay uses it to show how easily people's eyes can be fooled, which matters for how much to trust what witnesses say they saw.
corbell-and-coulthart-find-witnesses-who: Bob Lazar is a man who has said he worked in the late 1980s at S4, a secret test site in the Nevada desert, on craft that he believed were not made by humans. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that a filmmaker, Jeremy Corbell, and a journalist, Ross Coulthart, found a number of people who confirm that Lazar was really there. If so, it would back up the core of Lazar's much-doubted story.
corbell-first-meets-bob-lazar-at-john-le: Jeremy Corbell, a filmmaker who makes documentaries about UFOs, told podcast host Jesse Michels how he first met Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked on recovered flying craft at a secret Nevada site. Corbell says it happened in the 2010s at the Las Vegas house of John Lear, a figure in UFO circles, and that the first thing Lear said to him was that Lazar was coming over.
corbell-fought-for-grusch-to-testify-in-: Jeremy Corbell, a filmmaker who makes documentaries about UFOs, told podcast host Jesse Michels that in 2023 he fought to make sure David Grusch, a former intelligence officer who said the government hides a programme of recovered non-human craft, could speak before the US Congress. Corbell says the people in charge did not want Grusch to testify, and that Grusch himself would confirm Corbell pushed for it.
corbell-presses-jacques-vallee-on-lazar-: Jeremy Corbell, a filmmaker who makes documentaries about UFOs, told podcast host Jesse Michels that he once pressed Jacques Vallée, a well-known UFO researcher, about Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked on recovered flying craft at a secret Nevada site. Corbell says this happened when the two of them were alone at his ranch, though he does not say when.
corbell-s-2018-iraq-jellyfish-ufo-video: Podcast host Jesse Michels tells how a UFO researcher named Jeremy Corbell released a video said to have been filmed in Iraq in 2018. According to Michels, it shows an object shaped like a jellyfish. The video drew attention because, if it is what Corbell says, it would show an unknown object filmed in a war zone.
corbell-s-private-source-on-the-existenc: Jeremy Corbell, a guest on Jesse Michels's podcast, talks about Bob Lazar, a man who has said he worked on alien craft at a secret site called S-4 in the Nevada desert. Corbell says that a private source of his had already told him that a facility like S-4 exists, and that this is why he believed Lazar was telling it as it is. If so, it would back up one of the best-known claims of a hidden base for studying non-human craft.
cordyceps-mind-controlling-bullet-ants: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, describes how bullet ants in the Amazon rainforest eat cordyceps, a kind of mushroom. According to him, the fungus takes over the ants' brains and movements and steers them to higher ground, where a mushroom stalk then sprouts from each ant's head. He tells it in a conversation that treats mushrooms as a kind of mind control, perhaps even alien in origin.
coricancha-andesite-stonework: Coricancha is an ancient temple site from Inca times in Cusco, Peru. Luke Caverns, a researcher of ancient sites, tells podcast host Jesse Michels that its stonework, cut from andesite, a hard volcanic rock, is the most impressive in the whole ancient world. To him, that skill raises questions about who built such sites and how.
corona-spy-satellite-program-offered-as-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, recounts that a sighting by a researcher named Jacques Vallee, an object seen from the Paris Observatory moving in an unusual orbit, was explained away by pointing to Corona, a series of highly secret spy satellites backed by the CIA, the US foreign intelligence agency, first launched in 1960. Michels grants that the Corona satellites did travel in a nearly polar orbit, passing over the poles, but he calls it a very poor explanation. If he is right, Vallee saw something in orbit that nobody has accounted for.
corporal-armando-vanishes-for-15-minutes: A researcher named Mike Masters, on Jesse Michels's podcast, tells of a soldier in Chile in the 1970s, Corporal Armando Valdés, who he says vanished in front of the six men in his platoon and came back 15 minutes later. According to Masters, five days had passed for the corporal, a story he tells because it would hint that whatever is behind these events can bend time.
correspondence-with-whitley-strieber-on-: An author named Peter Levenda says that years ago a writer named Whitley Strieber got in touch with him by email, at first about something unrelated. Levenda tells a podcast host, Jesse Michels, that their later conversations about UFOs fed into his book series Sinister Forces. The point of telling it is that it shows how ideas about the phenomenon passed between people who write about it.
corso-and-the-telepathic-steering-helmet: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, describes Philip J. Corso, a US Army officer, who claimed that in the 1950s he worked at the Pentagon, the US military headquarters, handing out material from crashed UFOs to private companies and civilian researchers. The story is linked to the idea of a helmet that let a pilot steer a craft with their thoughts, and if true it would mean some modern technology came from studying alien objects.
corso-government-panic-over-ufos-at-new-: John Brandenburg, a guest on Jesse Michels' podcast, points to The Day After Roswell, a book by Philip Corso named after Roswell, the New Mexico town where something is said to have crashed in 1947. Brandenburg says that according to Corso, the US government went into panic mode around 1947 because many unidentified objects were being seen in New Mexico, where it was testing V-2 rockets, the German-designed rockets the US took over after the war, and also near nuclear sites. If true, it would mean the government saw these objects as taking an interest in its most secret weapons work.
corso-in-post-war-italy-knight-of-malta: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Philip J. Corso, an Army colonel who later became famous for his book The Day After Roswell, served as a senior intelligence officer in Italy after the Second World War. In that book Corso claimed the Pentagon had copied technology from alien material. The story's title also links Corso to the Knights of Malta, an old Catholic order of knights, and Michels raises the Italian years as background to where Corso's connections may have come from.
corso-manuscript-trapped-being-asks-to-l: A researcher known online as UAPGerb points to a manuscript by Philip J. Corso, a US Army officer who wrote about secret knowledge of crashed craft. According to UAPGerb, Corso wrote that in the 1950s he met a trapped being who asked him to lower the radar so that they could get out. The story is told because it would suggest radar was interfering with or even trapping non-human craft.
corso-recruited-to-the-army-foreign-tech: An online UFO researcher who goes by UAPGerb tells podcast host Jesse Michels about Philip Corso, a US Army officer. UAPGerb says Corso stated that in 1960 he was recruited, with a link to a man named Arthur Trudeau, into the Army's foreign technology division at the Pentagon, and points to Corso's military records as backing. The story matters because Corso is tied to claims about the Army handling unusual technology.
corso-s-claims-of-a-covert-roswell-group: This story starts at Roswell, New Mexico, where in 1947 something is said to have crashed. A US Army officer named Philip J. Corso wrote a book called The Day After Roswell. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in the book Corso claims a secret government group was set up under Admiral Roscoe Hillenkoetter, the first director of the CIA. According to Michels, Corso ran the Army's foreign technology desk and was given material from the crash to pass out quietly to private industry, mainly Bell Labs, a famous research laboratory. Michels says Corso thought the transistor, the tiny switch behind modern electronics, was reverse engineered from what was found. An online researcher known as UAPGerb tells it too, saying Corso described technologies being seeded into US defense companies around 1959 and 1960. Some tellings name Bell Labs, others speak more broadly, and one places the material at Wright-Patterson, an Air Force base. If true, everyday technology would owe part of its origin to a crashed craft.
corso-s-co-author-gave-him-24-hours-to-e: Podcast host Jesse Michels has said several times that Philip Corso, author of the 1997 book The Day After Roswell (about a supposed crashed craft near Roswell, New Mexico), was given only 24 hours by his co-author to edit the book. Michels says this explains why there is some nonsense in it. In one telling he names the co-author as William Birnes and mentions an earlier manuscript called Dawn of a New Age, and in another, crediting someone called UAP Gerb, he says the co-author may have slipped in false material to make Corso look bad. If so, it would mean the book's weaker parts are not Corso's own.
corso-s-manuscript-dawn-of-a-new-age-vs-: A researcher who goes by the online name UAPGerb, speaking on Jesse Michels' podcast, says that Philip Corso, author of the 1997 book The Day After Roswell, also left a manuscript called Dawn of a New Age. UAPGerb sets the two side by side, suggesting that what Corso first wrote may differ from the book that was published.
corso-says-the-day-after-roswell-was-rus: James Fox tells podcast host Jesse Michels about The Day After Roswell, a 1997 book by Philip J. Corso about events at Roswell, New Mexico. Fox passes on that Corso said the book was rushed into print with a co-writer named William Burns, and he also mentions a man named Michael Hessman. If true, the rush might explain problems in the book without throwing out what Corso claimed.
cosmic-zoo-explanation-for-diverse-craft: On a podcast episode with podcast host Jesse Michels about Skinwalker Ranch, a Utah property known for reports of strange happenings, a speaker raises the idea that we are living in a cosmic zoo. The idea is offered to explain why so many different kinds of craft are reported there: it would mean Earth is being watched by many visitors.
cosmonaut-drew-an-object-that-stopped-be: Kevin Knuth, a scientist speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast, relays a story from a source he names about a Soviet space flight in orbit around Earth. Knuth says that halfway through the orbit an unknown craft stopped right beside their spacecraft, and a cosmonaut, a Soviet astronaut, later drew a picture of it. In one of his tellings he adds that the crew also took photographs, which, if they existed, would be rare evidence of something unexplained in space.
cosmonaut-fooled-crewmate-with-ice-parti: A Swedish UFO researcher named Clas Svahn, speaking with podcast host Jesse Michels, passes on a story he says a cosmonaut, a Soviet or Russian space traveller, told him. According to Svahn, the cosmonaut played a joke on a crewmate in their space capsule, passing off floating ice particles outside as a fleet of UFOs. Svahn tells it as a case of how ordinary things in space can be taken for something stranger.
cosmos-club-tied-to-a-ufo-crash: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, mentions in passing that he has heard the Cosmos Club, a club in Washington, DC, linked to a UFO crash. He credits the idea to a commentator who goes by the name Dark Journalist and gives no further details.
coulthart-detained-by-cbp-after-grusch-s: Ross Coulthart, a journalist who reported on UFO secrecy, told podcast host Jesse Michels that after he broke the story of David Grusch, a former intelligence officer who said the government hides recovered non-human craft, he was stopped and held by US Customs and Border Protection, the agency that controls who enters the country. He places this in 2023 and tells it as a sign of pressure on him over that reporting.
coulthart-republican-presidents-briefed-: Jason Simosa, a researcher appearing on Jesse Michels's podcast, passes on a recent remark by Ross Coulthart, a journalist who reports on UFOs. According to Simosa, Coulthart said there sometimes seems to be a pattern in which Republican US presidents are told about secret UFO matters while Democratic presidents are not. If true, it would mean that even presidents only get this information when the people holding it choose.
coulthart-s-changing-sources-on-the-dron: A hip hop musician called Flying Lotus, talking on podcast host Jesse Michels' show in 2025, looks back at 2024, when drones he calls "the Chinese drones" were seen flying over the United States. He says a journalist, Ross Coulthart, kept talking very confidently about what his sources were telling him, but the sources kept changing the story. Flying Lotus tells it as a reason to be careful about who to trust when people claim inside knowledge.
cousteau-s-atlantis-obsession-shared-wit: Jason Jorjani, a philosopher speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast, says that Ghislaine Maxwell was obsessed from childhood with Atlantis, the legendary lost civilization said to have sunk beneath the sea. He says this was because her father, the media businessman Robert Maxwell, was friends with the famous ocean explorer Jacques Cousteau, who supposedly admitted to the family that his interest in the ocean really came from wanting to find Atlantis. It is told to suggest that powerful people quietly took the Atlantis legend seriously.
cover-contract-through-the-bia-near-whit: Jake Barber, a former military helicopter pilot who says he helped retrieve a UFO, told podcast host Jesse Michels that his team, sometime after 2001, worked under a cover contract, meaning an official-looking job that hid the real work. He says the contract ran through the Bureau of Indian Affairs, the US agency that deals with Native American tribes, at a sovereign tribal nation near White Sands Missile Range, a military testing ground in New Mexico.
cover-up-of-retrieved-craft-and-beings-s: A former US Air Force officer named Robert Salas, on Jesse Michels's podcast, says that since about 1947 there has been a serious effort in the United States to cover up anything to do with UFOs, including, as the story goes, crashed craft and beings recovered from them. If true, it would mean the government has kept its biggest secret for most of a century.
coyame-lights-around-mountain-peaks: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that people living near Coyame, a town in the Chihuahua region of northern Mexico, often talk about coloured lights that blink on and off around the mountain peaks. He draws on a book called Mexico's Roswell by Noe Torres and Ruben Uriarte, whose title compares the area to the famous Roswell UFO story in New Mexico. He tells it as a sign that something unusual keeps appearing in that area.
craft-beam-lasers-over-nuclear-stockpile: A man named Charlie Foltz, speaking on Jesse Michels' podcast, says that in 1975 or 1976, at Loring Air Force Base, a US military base in northern Maine, unknown craft flew over the base. He says laser-like beams came out of them and were mapping the base's nuclear weapons stores, which would mean someone unknown was taking an interest in American nuclear weapons.
craft-crash-in-northern-iran: A UFO researcher and activist, Steven Greer, says on a podcast that a craft of unknown origin crashed in northern Iran, and that the United States had to try to go in and get it. He gives no date. If true, it would mean the US has secretly recovered such objects even from inside hostile countries.
craft-entering-and-leaving-the-atmospher: Matthew Brown, a man described as a Pentagon whistleblower, told podcast host Jesse Michels that craft come in and out of Earth's atmosphere. He says he knows this from material he saw while working inside government, as well as from other people's testimony, which would mean officials have records of such craft.
craft-flew-due-north-to-a-soft-landing-1: A researcher named Scott Ramsay, speaking on podcast host Jesse Michels' show, tells of an unknown craft that he says came down in Hart Canyon near the small town of Aztec, New Mexico, around 1948. Ramsay says that when you trace which direction it came from and how it moved, it was flying exactly due north before it made a soft landing. If true, it would mean the craft was under some kind of control rather than simply falling out of the sky.
craft-holed-by-gunfire-over-los-alamos-1: Scott Ramsay, a researcher who studies a reported 1948 crash of an unknown craft in New Mexico, offers a guess on podcast host Jesse Michels' show about why it came down. He says it is only his theory, but perhaps someone fired a heavy weapon, like a 50 caliber machine gun, at the craft as it flew over Los Alamos, the New Mexico town where America's nuclear weapons research was based, and the hole caused a sudden loss of air pressure inside. If true, it would explain both the crash and what happened to whoever was on board.
craft-hovered-over-new-underwood-reservo: Mario Woods is a former guard at nuclear missile sites in South Dakota who says he was abducted by a UFO. He tells podcast host Jesse Michels that in 1977 a craft hovered over the dam at New Underwood Lake Reservoir, a spot he places within a triangle formed by two missile sites code-named November 1 and November 5. If he is right, the craft was sitting right next to nuclear weapons sites.
craft-hovering-in-s4-hangars: Dan Sheehan, a lawyer speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast, passes on an account linked to Oscar Wolf, Bob Lazar and Dan Burisch, people who have spoken about S4, a secret site said to lie near the Area 51 military base in Nevada. Sheehan says that someone went all the way to S4, rode down in its big elevators into the hangars, and saw three or four craft there. If true, it would mean unusual craft are being kept underground at a US base.
craft-hull-material-as-an-electret-1987: Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked on recovered flying craft in the late 1980s at S4, a secret site in Nevada, told podcast host Jesse Michels his idea about what the craft's hull was made of. He thinks it is an electret, a material that holds a permanent electric charge, so that just as a magnet always has a magnetic field, the craft always carries an electrostatic field around it.
craft-looks-different-up-close-than-from: Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked on recovered flying craft around 1988 and 1989 at S-4, a secret site in Nevada, told podcast host Jesse Michels that the craft looks different depending on distance. He says that close up it looks like the craft, but from far away it does not look right, a point he links to the work of researchers Jean Huff and Luigi Vendetelli.
craft-s-power-system-explained-aboard-li: A man named Charlie Foltz says that around 1976, near Eagle Lake in Maine, he was taken aboard a craft that was not human, and that while there he asked how it was powered. He told a podcast host, Jesse Michels, that it was explained to him as working like a submarine with a bubble of air, and in another telling he says it works at different "atmospheres" the way a submarine works at different depths in the water. If true, it would be a first-hand glimpse of how such a craft moves.
craft-shot-down-before-crashing-1996: A surgeon named Italo Venturelli, speaking on podcast host Jesse Michels' show, says that in January 1996 people in the Brazilian town of Varginha saw a craft being shot down. According to him, someone fired on it and it was already falling when it got there, and he says a young man named Carlos de Souza will tell you so himself. If true, it would mean someone deliberately brought down an unknown craft over Brazil.
craft-vanishing-into-mountains-in-the-ui: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that unknown craft vanishing into mountains is a documented phenomenon, especially in places like the Uinta Basin, a remote region of northeastern Utah. He gives no date or specific case, but if true it would suggest these objects have hidden places inside the earth.
craft-wall-turns-translucent-and-shows-3: A man named Bob Lazar says that around 1988 and 1989 he worked on a disc-shaped craft at a secret site in the Nevada desert called S-4. Speaking to a podcast host, Jesse Michels, he says he watched one of the craft's walls turn translucent, so you could partly see through it, and show symbols that looked three-dimensional. If true, it would mean the craft was built with technology far beyond anything people are known to make.
crane-as-the-navy-s-off-world-reverse-en: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says his contacts told him something about two military sites. According to them, Wright-Patterson, an Air Force base, is the center of the Air Force's most exotic efforts to take apart and copy technology not made on Earth, and Naval Surface Warfare Center Crane, a Navy research base, is the Navy's center for the same kind of work. If true, both services would each have their own hub for studying off-world technology.
crane-brinton-s-last-lecture-on-humanity: A man named Dan Sheehan told a podcast host, Jesse Michels, that he was in the room at Harvard University for the last lecture of Crane Brinton, who he says was chairman of Harvard's department of intellectual history. Sheehan says Brinton spoke about humanity's next step in evolution. He dates it to May 1968 and says Brinton told the audience that this was why so many of the young men there refused to go and fight in the Vietnam War.
crane-symbols-match-sheehan-s-drawings-2: A man named Randy Anderson says that around 2014, at Naval Surface Warfare Center Crane, a US Navy site in Indiana, he saw symbols he links to technology that was not human. He told podcast host Jesse Michels that drawings made by another man, Dan Sheehan, are "very close" to what he saw. If true, it would mean two people separately describing the same markings.
cranial-modification-told-to-have-been-o: Mike Masters, a researcher who studies human origins, talks on Jesse Michels's podcast about cranial modification, the old practice of binding babies' heads so the skull grows long, found in many cultures including the Maya. He cites a 1995 paper by two authors named Gerszten, who he says asked one group why they did it, and were told their ancestors had been instructed to do so by the gods. Masters tells it because it could hint that the "gods" were real visitors whose heads looked different.
crash-debris-analysed-as-aluminum-and-ba: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, in a documentary about Townsend Brown, an inventor he describes as building disc-shaped craft for the CIA, says that debris from a reported crash, discussed by the researcher Michael Swords, was analysed and found to be aluminum and barium. Michels points out that barium also appeared on a chalkboard at the Bahnson lab where Brown worked, and in Brown's Winterhaven proposal, a plan for building his craft, where Brown suggests barium for a motor in his "gravitator discs." If true, it would suggest the crashed object and Brown's secret designs were connected.
crash-debris-and-government-pen-at-archu: A writer named Greg Bishop, speaking on podcast host Jesse Michels' show, passes on what a local lawman, Gabe Valdez, told him about Archuleta Mesa, a high plateau in New Mexico, in the early 1980s. Valdez said they went up there and found broken brush, signs that something had been picked up and taken away, and a pen marked "US government property." If true, it would suggest the government quietly recovered something from the site.
crash-investigations-with-usaf-cia-invol: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that when unexplained craft crash, the US Air Force and the CIA, the American spy agency, always seem to be involved in looking into them. He points to cases in Virginia and in Brazil as examples, without giving dates. If true, it would suggest a quiet, repeated pattern of US agencies handling crashes, even in other countries.
crash-retrieval-program-head-refused-to-: A scientist, Eric Davis, says he would have loved to speak with the man who ran the crash retrieval program, a secret effort said to recover crashed craft that are not of human make, during the era he was looking into. He says that man, Glenn Gaffney, refused to talk to them, and the story ties to a documentary called Age of Disclosure. If true, it would mean someone who could confirm such a program chose to stay silent.
crash-retrieval-traced-back-to-sarbacher: An online researcher who goes by UAPGerb, speaking on podcast host Jesse Michels' show, says the story of governments secretly recovering crashed unknown craft goes back a long way. He points to a scientist named Robert Sarbacher in 1950, and even earlier to Italy in 1933 under its dictator Benito Mussolini. If true, it would mean such recoveries began well before the famous American cases.
crash-site-regraded-for-soybeans-after-t: A man named Carlos de Souza, interviewed by a podcast host, Jesse Michels, in an episode about a hospital that he says operated on an alien, talks about a spot near the town of Varginha in Brazil where something is said to have crashed. He says that for 26 years nobody touched the place, not a single straw. Then, he says, after a documentary by a filmmaker named James Fox came out, around 2022 or 2023, people went there and graded the land, removing more than 30 meters of earth. He mentions telling James about it, and says James went to see shortly afterward. Carlos is the only teller, speaking twice in one interview; the story's title says the land was cleared for soybeans, though in the quotes he does not mention soybeans. He says he would like an explanation, since it would suggest someone wanted the site wiped clean once attention returned to it.
crash-sites-with-bob-wood-that-turned-ou: A man named Joe McMoneagle told podcast host Jesse Michels that he went with a man named Bob Wood to a number of crash sites in the United States. He says that every one of them turned out to be an American plane, not anything stranger. No dates or places are given.
crash-tech-moved-from-wright-patterson-t: Scott Ramsay, a researcher, speculates on podcast host Jesse Michels' show about what might happen after an unknown craft crashes. He asks listeners to imagine a crashed craft being taken to Wright Patterson, an Air Force base in Ohio, and suggests the technology could then be passed on to private companies. If true, it would mean the secrets of such craft sit outside government hands.
crashed-craft-found-with-nothing-inside: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that many people who talk about crashed unknown craft claim that when these craft come down, there is nothing inside them. If that were true, it would suggest the craft fly with no crew aboard, perhaps controlled from somewhere else.
crashed-saucer-from-the-1940s-and-a-secr: An author and researcher named Peter Levenda, on Jesse Michels's podcast, reasons that if the United States has a crashed flying saucer from the 1940s, and another country has one too, then there must be an agreement between the countries not to talk about it. He offers this as a reason the secret would hold across rival governments.
crashes-as-deliberate-seeding-gorilla-in: A witness named David Grusch, talking with podcast host Jesse Michels in 2023, passes on an idea he credits to a man he calls Luis. The idea is that some crashes of non-human craft were not accidents or failed missions at all, but maybe a kind of deliberate "seeding", objects left on purpose for people to find. If true, it would mean whoever made them wanted us to have them.
crawling-inside-the-craft-three-seat-lik: A man named Bob Lazar says that around 1988 and 1989, at a secret site in Nevada called S-4, he crawled inside one of the craft he was working on.
