He tells a podcast host, Jesse Michels, that inside there were three things that looked like seats. A filmmaker named Jeremy Corbell, retelling Lazar's story, puts it differently: that Lazar was inside an alien craft from another planet and saw other ones too, without mentioning the seats. If true, it would mean a man has stood inside a vehicle not made by humans.
critias-s-myth-of-athens-war-with-atlant: James Madden, a guest on Jesse Michels's podcast who talks about the ancient Greek philosopher Plato, retells a story from Plato's writings, the dialogues known as the Timaeus and the Republic. In it, a character named Critias tells Socrates a myth, which Madden calls "another good lie", about a great war between ancient Athens and Atlantis, a story said to have reached Greece from Egypt by way of the lawmaker Solon. Madden raises it to show how Plato used stories that carry a deeper truth.
critique-of-the-khafre-pyramid-sar-scan-: A researcher named Luke Caverns, speaking on podcast host Jesse Michels' show, criticises a 2025 claim by a team including Filippo Biondi that a type of radar imaging, called synthetic aperture radar, had revealed hidden structures inside the Khafre pyramid, the second great pyramid at Giza in Egypt. Caverns says the team took a 3D model of the known King's Chamber and the small chambers above it, copied it five times into the pyramid, and presented that as what they were detecting. In his telling, that would mean the striking images were a model rather than a direct picture.
crohn-s-disease-healed-after-the-2007-or: A man in North Carolina named Chris Bledsoe says he had an encounter in 2007 with orbs, glowing balls of light. Before that, he says, he suffered from Crohn's disease, a long-lasting and painful illness of the gut. Bledsoe says that after the encounter his Crohn's was gone and he had no more sickness. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, repeats this in conversation with him, saying Bledsoe was cured of the disease. Michels places the encounter in January 2007. So Bledsoe gives it firsthand and the host retells it back to him, and if it is true, contact with these lights healed a man's illness.
crookes-tube-jump-observed-by-brown-as-a: A journalist named Nick Cook says that in the 1920s, while a student at Caltech, a university in Pasadena, California, a young man named Townsend Brown was experimenting with a Crookes tube, a sealed glass tube that carries high voltage electricity. According to Cook, Brown noticed that when high voltage was applied, the wire carrying it jumped. Cook tells it as the starting point for Brown's later ideas about electricity producing a push, ideas some link to craft that fly without ordinary engines.
crowley-s-lam-entity: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, mentions Aleister Crowley, an occultist of the early twentieth century, as another man to whom an alien being seemed to appear. That being is known as Lam. Michels raises it briefly as one more case of a person who says he made contact with something not human.
crown-prince-hans-adam-s-armageddon-agen: A doctor and UFO campaigner named Steven Greer says that in 1994, at the Pierre Hotel in New York, he was at a meeting with Hans-Adam II, then crown prince of the small European country of Liechtenstein, alongside figures such as the wealthy backer Lawrence Rockefeller and alien-abduction researchers Budd Hopkins, John Mack and David Jacobs. Greer says the prince's aim, as he quotes it, was to make the public hate aliens so much that there could be an interplanetary war, bringing on Armageddon so that Christ would return. If true, it would mean powerful people were trying to steer public feeling about aliens toward a war for religious ends.
cruickshank-s-archival-research-into-ken: Matthew Pines, a guest on Jesse Michels's podcast, says some researchers, including Jeff Cruickshank, have done careful historical digging through the records of President John F. Kennedy from the 1960s, which have since been made public. According to Pines, they looked for links to the MJ12 documents, papers said to concern a secret group handling UFO matters. If such links held up, it would tie a US president to secret UFO work.
cryo-chambers-on-mars: A researcher and philosopher named Jason Jorjani, speaking with podcast host Jesse Michels in 2025, relays something he credits to a man named Joe McMoneagle. According to Jorjani, it was reported that there were cryo chambers, places for keeping bodies frozen, on Mars, and that people had been left there. If true, it would mean someone had been on Mars long before us.
cryptography-to-speak-with-angelic-being: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that some of the first codemakers in Europe, like Johannes Trithemius, a German monk and scholar, used secret codes in order to speak with angel-like beings, and he places this, by his telling, in the 13th century. The story is tied to John Dee, an English scholar and adviser at the royal court, and his partner Edward Kelley, who said they talked with angels. Michels raises it as a sign that contact with non-human beings may be a very old human thread.
ct-scan-of-the-implant-arranged-by-an-un: A writer named Whitley Strieber says there is an object he calls an implant in his body, and that an unnamed insider in California wants him to get a CT scan of it. A CT scan is a detailed X-ray image of the inside of the body. He tells a podcast host, Jesse Michels, about the plan, which would matter because a scan might show what the object actually is.
cumbre-vieja-eruption-and-lyn-buchanan-s: A researcher named Jason Jorjani says that when the Cumbre Vieja volcano on the island of La Palma erupted in 2021, he was in New York and in touch with a man named Lyn Buchanan, who had given him some warning about it. Jorjani says he asked Buchanan whether this was it and whether he should leave New York. If true, it would suggest Buchanan had foreseen something about the eruption.
current-astronauts-with-their-own-experi: A former Navy fighter pilot named Ryan Graves, who talks about unexplained objects he and other pilots saw, says on podcast host Jesse Michels' show that he has spoken with astronauts still serving today. He says some of them have had their own experiences with such things. If true, it would mean people at the top of spaceflight have seen something too, and simply have not said so publicly.
curse-of-king-tut-s-tomb: This is the old story of a curse on the tomb of Tutankhamun, an ancient Egyptian king. The podcast host Jesse Michels says in 2024 that a couple of people tried to x-ray it and then died mysteriously. A researcher who goes by Luke Caverns tells it in 2025 as being about the dig led by the archaeologist Howard Carter. He says almost everyone on that excavation met with tragedy, and several died from poisoning after breathing the air inside the chamber. The story is told as a sign that something in the tomb was dangerous to those who disturbed it.
curtis-lemay-chases-townsend-brown-down-: Podcast host Jesse Michels, in a 2026 episode, passes on a story he says he got from a woman named Linda Brown. She says that Curtis LeMay, an Air Force general, once chased Townsend Brown, a scientist, down a flight of stairs. No time or place is given, and the story is told as a sign of how heated things got around Brown's work.
curtis-lemay-gave-d-harold-byrd-a-civil-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Curtis LeMay, a top US Air Force general, gave a Texas businessman named D. Harold Byrd an award from the Civil Air Patrol, a volunteer civilian group that helps the Air Force, when Byrd was younger. He mentions it while discussing President Kennedy's killing and links to President Lyndon Johnson, as a sign of close ties between these powerful men.
custody-chain-manhattan-project-to-aec-t: A witness named David Grusch told podcast host Jesse Michels in 2023 that, starting in the 1940s, recovered unexplained material was held by the Manhattan Project, the US wartime programme that built the atomic bomb, then passed to the Atomic Energy Commission, the body that took over atomic matters after the war, and later on to the Department of Energy. Michels and a commentator named Matthew Pines later retold it a little differently, as the secrecy system built for atomic weapons, set up by a law called the Atomic Energy Act and run by the same people, being laid over UFO secrecy through the 1950s and 60s. If true, it would mean UFO secrets have been kept inside the nuclear secrecy system from the start.
custody-of-the-trinity-craft-passed-thro: A longtime UFO researcher named Jacques Vallee, speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast more than once, describes how a crashed craft linked to 1945 and Trinity, the site of the first atomic bomb test, would have been held. He says the Manhattan Project, the wartime effort that built the bomb, would have had custody of it first, then the Atomic Energy Commission, and then the Department of Energy, which has its own separate security clearances. If true, it would explain why the object stayed hidden in the nuclear world, outside the military's usual channels.
cybertruck-bomber-s-email-to-shoemate-ab: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that a man named Shoemate went on another podcast, hosted by Shawn Ryan, and said he had received an email from the bomber himself. The bomber was a former Green Beret, a US Army special forces soldier, who blew up a Tesla Cybertruck in Las Vegas in 2025. The story's title says the email was about Chinese drones driven by gravity-control technology over the US East Coast, and if true it would mean a rival nation had craft far ahead of anything known.
cydonia-said-to-hold-pyramids-the-remnan: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Cydonia, a region on the surface of Mars, contains several pyramids that are basically the remains of a city. In another episode he credits the idea to a writer, Richard Hoagland, and his book Dark Mission, and links it to the "Face on Mars," a formation there said to look like a human face. If true, it would mean someone once built on Mars.
cymatics-experiment-in-the-king-s-chambe: A researcher named Jay Anderson, on podcast host Jesse Michels' show, relays an experiment he credits to an author, David Elkington, and other scientists in the King's Chamber, the inner room of Egypt's Great Pyramid. He says they stretched a membrane over the stone box in the chamber, scattered Egyptian sand on it the way you do to make sound vibrations visible, and played frequencies matching the chamber's own tone. According to him, the sand formed the Eye of Horus, an ancient Egyptian symbol, which would suggest the builders designed the pyramid around sound and meaning.
d-harold-byrd-s-vought-built-flying-sauc: A lawyer and activist named Dan Sheehan, on Jesse Michels's podcast, says that an aerospace company tied to a businessman named D. Harold Byrd, Vought, built all the flying saucers for Wright-Patterson, an Air Force base in Ohio, in the 1940s and 1950s, under a man he names as Alfred C. Loading. If true, it would mean the US was building saucer-shaped craft of its own soon after the war.
daily-mail-cia-office-of-global-access-r: This story is about the Office of Global Access, said to be a unit of the CIA, the US spy agency, and reporting about it in the British newspaper the Daily Mail around 2023 and 2024. A podcast host named Jesse Michels says that, according to that reporting, this office is the main part of a programme that recovers crashed craft of unknown origin all around the world. He links it to a man named Doug Wolf, saying the office did rapid-response retrievals in the early 2000s under him. An online researcher known as UAPGerb says a journalist named Christopher Sharp broke the story, and that the office was created in 2003 inside the CIA's Directorate of Science and Technology, its branch for technical work. Michels adds on a later episode that the office is rumoured to work closely with JSOC, the command for America's elite special forces, and with NEST, the Nuclear Emergency Support Teams. If true, it would mean the CIA runs a standing worldwide operation to collect crashed non-human craft.
daily-mail-egg-shaped-ufo-from-area-51-2: This story is about an egg-shaped craft said to have been recovered and kept at Area 51, the secret military base in Nevada. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says the Daily Mail, a British newspaper, reported on it around 2023. A guest named Merrick tells it a little differently. He says a man named Eric Taber spoke about the egg-shaped craft to AARO, the Pentagon office set up to look into UFO reports. Merrick believes Taber placed it at Area 51 but gives no date. If true, it would mean the US military has a recovered unknown craft in its keeping.
daily-sensor-observations-of-spheres-off: A witness named Merrick, speaking on podcast host Jesse Michels's show in 2025, passes on what he credits to a man named Ryan Graves. According to him, around 2014 and 2015, sensors off the US East Coast were picking up round, sphere-shaped objects every day. If true, it would mean unknown objects were being tracked routinely near the American coast.
dalai-lama-meets-john-mack-about-aliens-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that the Dalai Lama, the spiritual leader of Tibetan Buddhism, met in the 1990s with John Mack, a Harvard psychiatrist, to talk about aliens. According to Michels, the Dalai Lama found that his own worldview and Mack's fit well together, which would suggest a major religious figure took such encounters seriously.
dale-new-mexico-as-a-tall-white-playgrou: A man named Charles Hall, who says he spent three years around tall, pale beings he calls the Tall Whites, told podcast host Jesse Michels that the area near Dale, New Mexico is one of their "playgrounds". If true, it would mean these beings come to that spot regularly.
dalton-fury-bin-laden-in-sights-three-ti: John Blitch, a former scientist at DARPA, the US military's advanced research agency, passes on a story from a soldier who wrote under the name Dalton Fury in a book called Kill Bin Laden. Blitch says Fury went on 60 Minutes, an American TV news programme, in disguise and told reporter Scott Pelley that in 2001 at Tora Bora in Afghanistan he had Osama bin Laden directly in view three separate times, but was not allowed to strike.
dam-flooded-the-egyptian-labyrinth-in-th: Podcast host Joe Rogan, speaking with Jesse Michels in 2025, retells a story he credits to a man named Ben Van Kerkwyk and to the ancient writers Herodotus and Pliny the Elder. They describe a vast ancient labyrinth, a maze of chambers in Egypt, and Rogan says that in the 1960s a dam was built to help farmers, and the diverted water filled the labyrinth. If true, it would mean an important ancient site now lies hidden under water.
dan-burisch-and-j-rod-at-s4-2003: A researcher who goes by UAPGerb, speaking with podcast host Jesse Michels in 2026, retells the story of a microbiologist named Dan Burisch, told around 2003 and 2004. According to the story, Burisch worked at S4, a site linked to Area 51, a secret US military base in Nevada, where he dealt with a living extraterrestrial being called J-Rod, kept several layers underground. If true, it would mean the US government has held a living alien.
dan-howe-vouches-for-dan-sherman-s-elint: A researcher who goes by UAPGerb told podcast host Jesse Michels in 2026 that he once spoke at length with a man named Dan Howe about something called Project Preserve Destiny, linked to a man named Dan Sherman. According to UAPGerb, Howe said Sherman's account of ELINT, short for electronic intelligence, meaning the gathering of intelligence from electronic signals, was exactly right. The point is that if Sherman knows that world so well, his wider story is more believable.
dan-sheehan-discredited-through-stigma-1: A researcher named Eric Weinstein, speaking on podcast host Jesse Michels's show in 2022, says that a man named Dan Sheehan was targeted in the late 1980s because of his work, with a group called the Christic Institute, on the Iran-Contra affair, a US political scandal of that decade. Weinstein thinks Sheehan was probably fed false information so that he would chase it and be discredited by the stigma. If true, it would mean feeding people bad UFO-type stories can be used to ruin them.
dan-sherman-and-nsa-project-preserve-des: A man named Dan Sherman says he was part of a secret programme at the National Security Agency, the US spy agency that listens in on communications, called Project Preserve Destiny, and he describes being taken to one of its buildings in Maryland around 1991 and 1992. Sherman says the programme grew out of contact with an alien species in 1947 and began in 1960. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, who interviewed him, retells it with extra details from Sherman's book Above Black: that Sherman was trained to receive messages as tones, and that he was genetically altered as an unborn baby after his mother was abducted while pregnant. If true, it would mean a US agency was quietly using specially altered people to talk with aliens.
dan-sherman-taken-to-an-nsa-complex-for-: Podcast host Jesse Michels relays the account of Dan Sherman, author of a book called Above Black, who says that in the 1990s he was taken to a complex run by the NSA, the US National Security Agency that handles electronic intelligence, possibly at Fort Meade in Maryland. There, according to Sherman, he was given headphones and trained using sine waves, simple pure tones. If true, it would mean a secret government program was training people for some kind of signal work tied to the unexplained.
dan-wilson-links-green-fireballs-to-radi: A researcher named Robert Hastings, who studies UFOs around nuclear bases, says on Jesse Michels's podcast that a man named Dan Wilson spent many hours tracking sightings of "green fireballs," glowing green lights seen in the sky in the late 1940s. According to Hastings, Wilson found the sightings lined up with radiation drifting across the American landscape, which would tie the lights to the nuclear age.
daniel-gockerell-triangle-sighting: Jeremy Corbell, a UFO researcher, tells podcast host Jesse Michels about a man named Daniel Gockerell, who says he saw a triangle-shaped object. Corbell calls it a small story and says he later had Gockerell on his show, Weaponized. He doesn't say when or where the sighting happened.
daniel-s-encounter-with-a-being-by-the-t: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, retells a story from the Book of Daniel in the Bible: a man named Daniel stands on the bank of the Tigris River and sees a being with a face like lightning and eyes like torches. In another episode Michels picks out the words "fear not" that were said to Daniel there before he received his prophecy. He brings it up to suggest that ancient religious visions may resemble modern encounters with non-human beings.
daniel-sheehan-as-chief-of-station-for-t: An analyst named Matthew Pines, on Jesse Michels's podcast, says half-jokingly that Daniel Sheehan, a lawyer active in pushing for UFO disclosure, was "chief of station" in Washington, DC, for the Jesuits, a Catholic religious order, meaning their head of intelligence there. Pines tells it to suggest that hidden church networks sit behind the people pushing the UFO story.
dannion-brinkley-s-holographic-life-revi: A computer scientist from MIT, Rizwan Virk, tells on podcast host Jesse Michels' show what a man named Dannion Brinkley says he went through in a near-death experience. Brinkley called it a holographic, three-dimensional replay of his whole life, seen not from his own eyes but from the eyes of the people he affected. Virk says Brinkley, who had been a soldier and killed people in the Vietnam War, felt what it was like to take a bullet from himself, which Virk offers as a hint that reality may work like a recording or simulation.
danny-jones-interview-throttled-over-a-m: A man named Chris Bledsoe, who says he attracts unexplained craft, told podcast host Jesse Michels that in 2025 an interview he gave to another podcast host, Danny Jones, was held back from reaching viewers. Bledsoe says this happened because he mentioned some technology at mission control of NASA, the US space agency. If true, it would suggest someone did not want that detail spread.
danny-s-dmt-laser-experiments-reveal-cod: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, asks a brain scientist about a man he calls his buddy Danny, who shines lasers through a pattern-making screen while on DMT, a very strong psychedelic drug. The idea behind these experiments is that people on the drug see a kind of code in the laser light, which, if true, would hint at a hidden structure behind reality.
danny-sheehan-says-he-has-coordinates-fo: A witness named Marik von Rennenkampf, speaking on podcast host Jesse Michels's show in 2025, says that a man named Danny Sheehan told him, around 2024, that he has map coordinates for an underwater UFO base. The place is linked to the waters off Baja California in Mexico, near Guadalupe Island. If true, it would mean something non-human is operating under the sea near North America.
danny-sheehan-shown-blue-book-files-and-: A man named Danny Sheehan says that in the late 1970s, under President Jimmy Carter's government, he was taken into a secure room in Washington to look over the files of Project Blue Book, the US Air Force's UFO study of the 1950s and 60s. According to Sheehan, he saw a sharp photo of a UFO crashed on a mountaintop, traced it, and copied down strange symbols that looked like hieroglyphs. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, has retold the story calling the room a SCIF, a sealed space for viewing classified material, but Sheehan himself says it was just a room downstairs in the Madison Building, and if his account is true, the government held pictures of a crashed craft.
darkness-retreat-study-testing-for-spike: A researcher named Andrew Gallimore, who studies DMT, a powerful psychedelic that the body may also make in small amounts, says that in 2025 he and a Florida group he works with, called New Nordics, were funding a study. He tells a podcast host, Jesse Michels, that the study would put people through a retreat in total darkness to test whether their own natural DMT levels spike. If it showed that, it would support the idea that the brain can open strange inner experiences on its own.
darpa-man-talking-to-a-computer-with-his: A UFO researcher named Grant Cameron, on podcast host Jesse Michels' show, passes on a story from a filmmaker, Bob Emenegger, set around 1974 at DARPA, the Pentagon's agency for advanced research. According to the story, a man there said, "I'm talking to this machine with my mind." If true, it would mean the military was working on linking minds and computers decades ago.
darpa-n3-brain-machine-interface-program: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in 2018 DARPA, the Pentagon's agency for advanced research, launched a program called N3, short for next generation non-surgical neurotechnology. He tells it as part of a story about the military working on ways to link brains and machines without surgery.
darpa-programs-with-nine-figure-budgets-: A physicist named John Brandenburg, on podcast host Jesse Michels' show, talks about a program manager at DARPA, the Pentagon's advanced research agency, named John Bletch. Brandenburg says Bletch kept running programs that sometimes had budgets of hundreds of millions of dollars. He is clear that Bletch never said so, but Brandenburg's own guess is that these programs went secret and moved to Area 51, a closely guarded military test site in Nevada.
darpa-robot-mission-to-search-tora-bora-: John Blitch, a former scientist at DARPA, the US military's advanced research agency, says that in 2001 and 2002 he was asked by name by his former boss, Jumo Brown, to join a mission in Afghanistan. He told podcast host Jesse Michels that the job was to send robots into the caves of Tora Bora, working from Bagram Airfield, to search for Osama bin Laden.
darpa-s-far-exception-and-canceled-steal: John Blitch, a former scientist at DARPA, the US military's advanced research agency, says that in the late 1990s he managed 130 million dollars of projects, half robots and half a stealth programme, under an exception to the FAR, the rules that govern how the US government buys things. He says the stealth programme was cancelled a month after it began, for no reason given. He links this to what a general named Trudeau is said to have told an Army officer, Philip Corso, to do, suggesting a pattern of hidden handling of advanced technology.
darpa-sid-program-protection-would-kill-: A researcher who goes by UAPGerb, speaking with podcast host Jesse Michels in 2026, says that a part of DARPA, the Pentagon's agency for advanced research, which he calls SID, will simply kill people it considers a threat from inside or outside. He points to a post he wrote on the subject and links it to a witness named David Grusch. If true, it would mean these secret programmes protect themselves by lethal means.
darpa-smart-dust-field-tests-1990: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that by 2001 DARPA, the Pentagon's agency for advanced research, was showing off smart dust, tiny wireless sensors, in field tests. He tells it as part of a story about secret military technology being further along than the public knew.
darpa-special-access-program-to-reverse-: John Blitch, a former scientist at DARPA, the US military's advanced research agency, says that around 2000 he ran a special access programme, meaning a tightly restricted secret project. He told podcast host Jesse Michels that it tried to copy the camouflage of cephalopods, sea animals like octopus and squid, working with scientists including Roger Hanlon.
darwin-s-dog-that-inherited-a-fear-of-bu: A biologist named Rupert Sheldrake, on podcast host Jesse Michels' show, recalls a case that Charles Darwin, the naturalist, reported in a paper in the science journal Nature. It was about a dog belonging to someone Darwin knew, which got very frightened whenever it walked past a butcher's shop. Sheldrake tells it as an example of a fear that may be inherited, which would mean memories can somehow pass down through generations.
daryl-bem-s-backward-causality-study-and: Michael Shermer, a researcher and skeptic, said on podcast host Jesse Michels's show in 2026 that the so-called replication crisis, when many psychology findings could not be repeated, began in 2010 with a study by Daryl Bem at Cornell University. Shermer says Bem's paper claimed to show backward causality, people sensing events before they happen, and others such as Ray Hyman, Richard Wiseman and Stuart Ritchie could not get the same results. He tells it to show how such claims fall apart when tested again.
dating-the-sphinx-by-its-vernal-equinox-: A researcher named Randall Carlson, talking with podcast host Jesse Michels, recalls that two writers, Robert Bauval and Graham Hancock, tried to date the Great Sphinx at Giza in Egypt by the stars. Their idea, as he tells it, was to work out when the sunrise on the spring equinox, the day each year when day and night are equal, would have lined up with where the Sphinx is looking, which he puts at about 10,500 BC. If true, it would make the Sphinx far older than it is usually thought to be.
daughter-s-question-at-the-church-of-the: A man named Rolf Mowatt-Larssen, presented as a former senior CIA officer, told podcast host Jesse Michels about his daughter's first visit to the Church of the Holy Sepulchre in Jerusalem, a church tied to the death of Jesus. He says that as she looked at what is shown as Jesus's cross, she asked him a question that stayed with him. No date is given.
dava-holloman-film-withheld-from-vallee-: On a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, a researcher named Eric Davis tells of a film from Holloman, an Air Force base, that was held by the Defense Audiovisual Agency, a military office that looked after film and video, in the 1970s. He says the agency was run by two retired generals, one of them possibly named Jerry Miller, and that the UFO researcher Jacques Vallee writes in his book Revelations that he and a fellow researcher, J. Allen Hynek, were invited to come and see the film. As the story is framed, the film was then kept from them, which would mean the military held footage it chose not to share.
dave-altman-connects-the-transient-dates: An astronomer named Beatriz Villarroel, who studies brief points of light that show up and vanish on old photographs of the sky, tells podcast host Jesse Michels about a moment with a colleague. Dave Altman, the media manager for her research project, asked her if she knew what happened on 19 July 1952, the date of a wave of UFO sightings over Washington, D.C. She tells it because it links the dates of her strange flashes to that famous wave of sightings, which would suggest the two are connected.
dave-rossi-s-fourth-orb-in-the-mh370-vid: Salvatore Pais, a Navy scientist who holds patents on unusual craft designs, says on Jesse Michels' podcast that a man named Dave Rossi spotted a fourth orb in videos said to show MH370, the Malaysia Airlines passenger plane that vanished over Southeast Asia in 2014. According to Pais, that is why Ashton Forbes, who has studied these videos closely, now speaks of four orbs rather than three. If true, it would tie the plane's disappearance to glowing objects seen around it.
david-ferrie-s-mysterious-death-1967: A researcher and author named Peter Levenda, speaking on podcast host Jesse Michels's show, tells of a man named David Ferrie in New Orleans around 1967. Levenda says Ferrie died during an investigation into the killing of President John F. Kennedy, an inquiry tied to a New Orleans prosecutor named Jim Garrison, and that he either killed himself or was killed in a way made to look like it, under mysterious circumstances. Told this way, it hints that someone may have wanted him silenced.
david-flynn-s-cydonia-book-reprinted-by-: A man named Tim Alberino told podcast host Jesse Michels about a book called Cydonia by a writer named David Flynn, named after a region of Mars. He says that before Flynn's daughter reprinted it, copies of the book were selling for two to three thousand dollars, showing how sought after it had become.
david-grusch-comes-forward-at-great-pers: A UFO investigator named James Fox, speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast, talks about David Grusch, a man who in 2023 went public with claims that the US government holds secrets about non-human craft. Fox says Grusch put his credibility on the line and lost his position to come forward, at great personal cost. For Fox, that sacrifice is a reason to take Grusch seriously.
david-grusch-testimony-and-icig-report-2: Jeremy Corbell, a filmmaker who makes UFO documentaries, spoke with the podcast host Jesse Michels in 2026 and pointed back to David Grusch, a former US intelligence officer who came forward as a whistleblower in Washington. Corbell says Grusch raised his hand and swore, "hand to God and to country," that the United States has been exploiting non-human technology for generations. He links this to a report from the ICIG, the inspector general who watches over the US spy agencies, and he also names Christopher Fox and Chuck McCullough. If it were true, the government would have been holding technology not made by people for decades.
david-grush-s-congressional-testimony-20: In 2023 a whistleblower named David Grusch gave sworn testimony before the US Congress about UFOs. In his own words, his claims rest on interviews with more than 40 witnesses over four years. A journalist, Michael Shellenberger, calls it really strong testimony. An official, Karl Nell, sums it up this way: Grusch told the House Committee on Oversight that a government program studies UFOs because they are real. A scientist, Donald Hoffman, describes the hearings more broadly. He says credible high-ranking military and other officials swore they had seen non-human biologics, meaning bodies or living material, and non-human technology, though he names none of them. If true, it would mean the US government knows of, and may hold, things not made by humans.
david-huggins-encounters-with-mantids-gr: A writer named Jason Jorjani, on podcast host Jesse Michels' show, relays the claims of a man named David Huggins, who says he had encounters with non-human beings from childhood on, in the American South and in underground places. According to Huggins, these included tall insect-like beings called mantids, small grey beings called grays, and a woman who was part human. Huggins claimed the mantids were in charge of the little grays, which would suggest these beings have a chain of command.
david-jay-brown-s-field-guide-to-dmt-ent: A neuroscientist named Andrew Gallimore, speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast, points to a book by David Jay Brown called Illustrated Field Guide to DMT Entities. DMT is a powerful psychedelic drug, and people who take it often report meeting beings. According to the story, the book catalogues them, from the "machine elves" made famous by the writer Terence McKenna to insect-like surgeons, which matters because, if those beings are real, the drug could be a doorway to other minds.
david-morales-fired-the-fatal-shot-from-: A lawyer and researcher named Dan Sheehan, on podcast host Jesse Michels's show, says he knows who fired the shot that killed President John F. Kennedy in Dealey Plaza, Dallas, in 1963. According to Sheehan, the fatal shot came from the grassy knoll, a small grassy slope beside the motorcade route, and was fired by a man named David Morales. If true, it would mean Kennedy was not killed by a lone gunman.
david-ruiz-a-three-fingered-humanoid-spe: David Ruiz, a researcher in Peru who appeared on a podcast about strange three-fingered bodies found there, says that in eight years of research he has never once called them extraterrestrial. In his words, what he is talking about is a humanoid species, perhaps a three-fingered hominid like us, which would mean an unknown relative of humans rather than visitors from space.
davis-asks-the-aps-historian-in-1984-whe: A physicist named Eric Davis says that in 1984, at a meeting of the American Physical Society, a professional body for physicists, he asked the society's historian where research into anti-gravity had gone. He says he was prompted by a scientist named Bob Forward, who had looked into anti-gravity while at Hughes Research Labs, a company lab in Malibu, California. Davis tells it because, if that research quietly vanished from view, it might mean it went secret.
davis-at-the-aerospace-corporation-in-hu: A physicist named Eric Davis says he worked for four and a half years at the Aerospace Corporation, a research company serving the US military, in Huntsville, Alabama. He says there were few physicists with doctorates there, and those few were all doing engineering work. He tells it to show how little room there was for deeper physics research in that world.
davis-briefs-senate-intelligence-and-arm: A physicist named Eric Davis says he gave secret briefings to the staff of two US Senate committees, the one that oversees spy agencies and the one that oversees the armed forces. He says he briefed the first group in 2019 and that more followed by 2022, in classified settings. If true, it would mean Congress was being told behind closed doors about what he knows of UFOs.
davis-hired-by-cia-as-winpac-branch-chie: A physicist named Eric Davis says that in late 2003 he was hired by the CIA, the American spy agency, as chief scientist of a branch in WINPAC, a CIA unit dealing with weapons intelligence. He tells a podcast host, Jesse Michels, about it as part of his career in secret government science, which would give weight to what he says about UFOs.
davis-joins-nids-bigelow-s-institute-199: A physicist named Eric Davis says that around 1995 and 1996 he joined the National Institute for Discovery Science, known as NIDS, a private research group in Las Vegas founded in 1995 by Bob Bigelow to study strange phenomena. Davis says he was its director of aerospace physics and astrophysics research, working alongside people like Colm Kelleher and John Alexander. He tells it to show he has studied UFO questions seriously for about thirty years.
davis-meets-grusch-at-the-aerospace-corp: A physicist named Eric Davis says that while working for the Aerospace Corporation, a research company serving the US military, at its campus in Colorado Springs, he was introduced by a man named Jay Stratton to David Grusch, a former intelligence officer who later spoke publicly about UFOs. Davis says he handed over his data to Grusch. If true, it would tie Davis's own knowledge directly to what Grusch went on to claim.
davis-s-papers-for-marc-millis-s-propuls: A physicist named Eric Davis, who has worked on Pentagon research, told the podcast host Jesse Michels that from the 1990s into the 2000s he wrote papers for a NASA research program on new ways to propel spacecraft, run by a man named Marc Millis. Davis says the work had nothing to do with UFOs: he was just contributing what he knew to Millis's propulsion physics program.
davis-says-puthoff-interviewed-brad-sore: On a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, a guest who goes by the name UAPGerb passes on something he says he heard from a man named Eric Davis: that Hal Puthoff, another figure in the world of UFO research, once interviewed a man named Brad Sorensen. The remark comes out half cut off, with no place or date given. It matters to listeners as a clue about who has spoken to whom inside this small circle of people.
davis-takes-sap-security-training-he-and: The physicist Eric Davis told the podcast host Jesse Michels that while he worked at the Aerospace Corporation, a defense research company, he went through security training for special access programs, a tightly restricted kind of secret US government project. He says he and David Grusch, a former intelligence officer, have talked about how secrets can be hidden in a different kind of classified category, called sensitive compartmented information, instead of in those programs, which matters to anyone trying to find where UFO secrets might be kept.
davis-told-definitively-that-we-are-moni: A researcher named Eric Davis says on Jesse Michels's podcast that someone told him, as a fact and not a guess, that humans are being watched and do not control our own space. Davis says he is completely sure of it because it was put to him as something known to be true. If that is right, something other than us would be in charge of the skies above us.
davis-uses-dia-deputization-to-get-acces: A Pentagon scientist named Eric Davis says that from around 2008 he used his security clearances and a letter from an official named Jim Lacatski, which named him a representative of the Defense Intelligence Agency, the US military's intelligence service, to get into what he calls the crash retrieval program, a secret effort to recover crashed craft. Davis says he could not see the craft or bodies, or talk to the people who work with them, but he did reach the people who run it at the programme level. He says they told him all of it was real and all of it happened, which, if true, would mean the US government holds crashed craft that are not human-made.
dc-fusion-center-foia-on-psychotronic-ef: A researcher named Dave Rossi, speaking on Jesse Michels' podcast, describes a records request made to the Washington D.C. fusion center, a hub where government agencies share security information. He says someone used FOIA, a US law that lets anyone request government records, to ask about certain political groups, and instead got back a file he recalls was titled "effects on the human body." Rossi tells it as a sign that officials have looked at devices said to affect the body and mind, sometimes called psychotronic effects.
dead-labrador-nelly-photographed-as-a-ba: A man named Chris Bledsoe, who says strange lights and craft appear around him and that NASA has studied him, told podcast host Jesse Michels about his dead Labrador, Nelly. He says that after a trip to see a rocket launch at Cape Canaveral, Florida, around 2007, he photographed her rising from her grave in North Carolina as a small ball of light, and that is how he got the picture, which appears in his book UFO of God. To him it would mean something of a living being carries on after death.
dead-man-switch-set-up-in-first-call-wit: Dylan Borland, a man who says he went on to become a whistleblower to the US Congress, tells of his very first conversation with a man named Jeremy Corbell. Borland says he told Corbell that they did not know each other but that he was about to blow the whistle, and that they set up a dead man switch in that call: an arrangement to release what he knows if something happens to him. The point of telling it is that he felt his life could be at risk for speaking out.
dead-sea-scrolls-isaiah-matches-text-a-t: A podcast host, Joe Rogan, says that one of his guests, Wes Huff, told him about the Dead Sea Scrolls, ancient manuscripts found at Qumran near the Dead Sea. According to Rogan, Huff explained that the Book of Isaiah, part of the Bible, found among the scrolls is word for word the same as a copy made a thousand years later. Rogan tells it to show how faithfully old texts could be handed down across the centuries.
dean-koontz-novel-predicting-covid-and-t: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that a science fiction writer named Dean Koontz predicted COVID, the pandemic disease of 2020, and the laboratory in Wuhan, China, that the outbreak has been linked to. Michels raises it as an example of fiction seeming to see the future, which, if true, would hint that writers can sometimes know things before they happen.
dean-radin-had-to-disparage-remote-viewi: A guest on Jesse Michels's podcast, Maaneli Derakhshani, passes on that the researcher Dean Radin was part of Project Stargate. Stargate was a remote viewing programme, an effort to use people's minds alone to describe faraway places, which he says was started by the CIA, the US spy agency. According to the story, Radin had to speak badly of remote viewing in public while he was working on it, which would mean the government hid its own interest in the subject.
death-of-bilgames-ziusudra-the-last-to-b: A researcher called Matt, on Jesse Michels' podcast, points to an obscure ancient Mesopotamian clay tablet known as The Death of Bilgames, Bilgames being another name for Gilgamesh, the legendary hero-king. He says the tablet tells how gods called the Anunna gave immortality to Ziusudra, the Noah-like figure who survived the great flood, and that he was the last man ever to receive it. Matt raises it as a hint that ancient texts remember a lost age when such gifts were given.
death-of-bill-steinman: Scott Ramsay, a man who investigates a claimed crash of a craft carrying alien bodies, says on Jesse Michels' podcast that Bill Steinman, a researcher of that same story, died near Goodyear, Arizona, in January a couple of years earlier. According to Ramsay, it was a massive heart attack, and Sheila Steinman was in the kitchen when it happened.
death-of-john-norseen-2007: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that a man named John Norseen died on September 27, 2007, while on business for a company called Concurrent Technologies. He tells it in an episode about top American scientists who have gone missing or died, placing Norseen's death among cases he thinks deserve a closer look.
debrief-at-ellsworth-with-rick-doty-pres: A man named Mario Woods, speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast in an episode about UFOs seen near nuclear bases, says he was questioned after an incident at Ellsworth, an Air Force base in South Dakota. According to Woods, sitting in on that debrief was a new agent from the Air Force's criminal and counterintelligence investigators, the Office of Special Investigations, named Rick Doty. He also mentions men named Jack Reed and Ralph East as part of the story.
debris-blocked-shafts-between-khafre-and: Filippo Biondi, a scientist who says he scanned beneath the pyramids of Giza in Egypt, tells of shafts blocked with debris between the Khafre pyramid, one of the great pyramids there, and the Sphinx. According to his team's scans, he says, they are very confident these shafts connect to underground facilities lying below Giza, which would mean a hidden built world under the famous monuments.
deceptive-fairy-gentry-in-medieval-folkl: A philosopher named Jason Jorjani, talking with podcast host Jesse Michels, describes old country folklore from Brittany in France and from Ireland about the fairy folk, sometimes called the gentry. Drawing on the work of Jacques Vallee, a researcher who compared such folklore with modern UFO stories, Jorjani says the peasants knew these beings lie all the time. The point, as he tells it, is that whatever people meet in such encounters may not be telling the truth about itself.
deciding-to-go-public-kasparov-calls-for: Kirsan Ilyumzhinov, the former president of Kalmykia, a republic within Russia, and at the time head of the World Chess Federation, says he was taken by aliens in 1997 and decided to talk about it publicly. He says that once he did, the former world chess champion Garry Kasparov at once declared that someone who had met aliens could not lead the federation and should be removed and replaced.
decision-to-stop-briefing-new-legacy-pro: Matthew Brown, described as a Pentagon whistleblower, speaks on Jesse Michels's podcast about the "legacy program", a supposed long-running secret effort tied to non-human craft. He says another man, Dylan Borland, told Michels quite directly that someone decided to stop telling new people in the programme about its history. If so, even the people inside it would not know how it began.
declassified-cia-memos-on-exotic-gravity: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that CIA memos from the 1950s, since released to the public, point to centres of unusual gravity research. The story places them at Indiana University, Purdue, Princeton and MIT. If true, it would mean the spy agency was quietly watching or backing work on controlling gravity decades ago.
declassified-upshot-knothole-report-puts: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, in an episode asking whether Henry Kissinger oversaw a secret program to recover crashed UFOs, talks about a man named Arthur Stansel. Michels says a declassified report from Operation Upshot-Knothole, a series of US nuclear bomb tests in Nevada in 1953, confirms that Stansel was on site for the testing. He raises it as proof that Stansel really was where his story places him.
decoded-messages-of-aliens-with-a-dying-: A writer and researcher named Greg Bishop, speaking on podcast host Jesse Michels' show, tells of Paul Bennewitz, a man in Albuquerque, New Mexico, who in the early 1980s believed he was decoding messages from aliens. According to Bishop, the messages said the aliens came from another planet, were here trying to set up a base, and needed Earth women. If taken at face value, it would mean aliens with a dying world had designs on Earth.
deconfliction-language-in-the-1971-treat: Pippa Malmgren, whose father Harald Malmgren was a presidential adviser, points on Jesse Michels's podcast to a 1971 agreement between the United States and the Soviet Union, which she calls the SALT treaty, a deal on limiting nuclear weapons. According to her, it contained "deconfliction" wording, meaning wording meant to stop either side from mistaking something for an attack. In the context of the conversation, she offers it as a hint that the two powers had to plan around things in the sky.
deconfliction-line-used-before-strike-on: Bob Maguire, introduced on Jesse Michels' podcast as a former CIA contractor, passes on an account of a clash in Syria. He says Russia, working through proxy militias, attacked a group of Americans there, and the US called the Russians on the deconfliction line, a direct channel between the two militaries meant to prevent accidental fighting, before striking back. He tells it to show how quietly such dangerous moments are handled behind the scenes.
deep-prasad-harassed-during-uap-science-: Deep Prasad, a researcher who has worked on the science of UAPs (unidentified anomalous phenomena, the official term for UFOs), was asked by a podcast host whether unpleasant people had messed with him during that work, as if he had hit a nerve with hidden power players inside government. Prasad answered that the host was not wrong at all, suggesting his research touched something someone wanted left alone.
deep-underground-bases-at-s4-and-dulce: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says there are deep underground military bases across the United States, and that some are rumored to house other beings. He names two: S4, said to be a site at Area 51, a secretive military base in Nevada, and one under Dulce, a town in New Mexico. He draws on men who have told such stories, including Bob Lazar, Phil Schneider, Dan Burisch and Richard Sauder.
deep-underground-bases-from-air-force-pr: An online researcher who goes by UAPGerb says on podcast host Jesse Michels' show that there is a rich history of deep underground military bases in the United States. He says they began in the 1950s and 1960s out of Project RAND, a research effort set up for the US Air Force. If true, it would mean a hidden network of military sites has been growing for decades.
deep-underground-bases-since-1948-with-n: An online researcher who goes by UAPGerb says on Jesse Michels's podcast that deep underground military bases are real. He says they have been a major focus of the US Defense Department and the Army Corps of Engineers, the army's building branch, since 1948. That was when, he says, the US brought over Nazi scientists, among them Xavier Dorsch, head of Nazi Germany's construction agency known as the Todt organization, to work in an underground laboratory run by Air Materiel Command, the Air Force's research and equipment arm.
defense-bases-deliberately-placed-at-nat: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, puts a question to a guest that he admits sounds trippy: could some American military bases have been built on purpose at natural "portals", places where something from elsewhere might come through? He has in mind sites set up from the 1950s on, like Area 51, a secret Air Force test site in the Nevada desert, the nearby Nevada Test Site where nuclear weapons were tested, and Skinwalker Ranch, a Utah property known for strange reports. If he were right, the military would have known about such places and quietly chosen to sit right on top of them.
defense-department-contacts-privately-en: Dave Rossi, a man who says advanced physics came to him from non-human sources, tells of meeting people inside the US Department of Defense between about 2021 and 2024. He says that officially they had no way to support him, but privately they encouraged him, which he takes as a sign that people inside the military took his claims seriously.
dehomag-ibm-s-german-subsidiary-ahead-in: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Dehomag, the German branch of the American computing company IBM, was far ahead in transistors, the tiny electronic switches behind modern computers, during the 1930s and 1940s. He raises it in an episode about a claimed secret Nazi UFO programme, where it would suggest Germany had advanced electronics earlier than is usually thought.
deinococcus-radiodurans-survives-three-y: A guest named Dr. Gilbert, on podcast host Jesse Michels's show, says that a very hardy bacterium called Deinococcus radiodurans has been found to survive three years in outer space. He says this comes from studies done on the International Space Station, the crewed laboratory that orbits Earth. If true, it suggests simple life could survive a journey between worlds.
delgado-remote-controls-a-bull-with-a-br: A researcher named Greg Malatzi, on Jesse Michels's podcast, describes an experiment by the scientist Jose Delgado in Spain in the 1960s. He says Delgado put an implant in a bull's head and could then control the bull by remote. He tells it as an example of how early scientists learned to steer a living brain from outside.
delonge-already-had-ten-advisers-by-nove: A researcher named Jason Simosa, speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast, talks about Tom DeLonge, a rock musician who started a public effort to reveal UFO secrets. Simosa says the writer Peter Levenda, who worked closely with DeLonge, told him that when he joined in November 2014 there were already ten advisers. That would mean DeLonge's circle of insiders formed earlier than people knew.
delonge-iraq-war-linked-to-groups-connec: Jason Samosa, speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast, recalls early interviews given by Tom DeLonge, a rock musician who started a public effort to reveal UFO secrets, before anyone knew who his advisers were. According to Samosa, DeLonge suggested that some of what the US did in the Iraq war, which began in 2003, may have been about groups there who were linked to non-human beings and were helping those beings spread. If true, a major war would have had a hidden motive.
delonge-on-2016-radio-weapon-systems-bui: Jay Anderson, a guest on Jesse Michels' podcast, recalls Tom DeLonge, a rock musician who became a leading voice for UFO disclosure, speaking on the radio in 2016. Anderson says that when DeLonge was asked about the archons, ruling spirit-beings from ancient religious writings, he excitedly answered that weapon systems had been developed "because we know they're coming back." If true, it would suggest that someone is preparing to fight a non-human force.
delonge-on-coast-to-coast-with-george-kn: A researcher named Jason Simosa, talking with podcast host Jesse Michels, says the musician Tom DeLonge was already close to talk of UFO secrets well before he became publicly involved. As proof, Simosa points out that DeLonge appeared in 2011 on Coast to Coast AM, a late-night American radio show about the paranormal, with the journalist and host George Knapp.
delonge-s-advisers-went-quiet-when-asked: Jason Samosa says on Jesse Michels's podcast that Tom DeLonge, a rock musician who started a public effort to reveal UFO secrets, said around 2016 and 2017 that there was a big genetic side to the phenomenon. According to Samosa, DeLonge said his advisers answered his other questions, but went quiet as soon as he asked about hybrids, meaning beings that are part human and part non-human. That silence is told as a hint that the subject was off limits.
delonge-s-contact-at-lockheed-skunk-work: A researcher named Jason Simosa, speaking on Jesse Michels' podcast, says that Tom DeLonge, a musician who became a UFO campaigner, made contact around 2015 with someone who worked at Skunk Works, the secretive advanced aircraft division of the defense company Lockheed Martin. Simosa says the longtime UFO researcher Jacques Vallée backs up this original version of the story. If true, it would mean DeLonge's UFO work began with a real insider at one of America's most secret aircraft shops.
delonge-s-meetings-at-the-pentagon-and-n: A researcher named Jason Simosa, on podcast host Jesse Michels's show, says that around 2015 and 2016 the musician Tom DeLonge began a run of meetings with officials. According to Simosa, DeLonge was flown to the Pentagon, the headquarters of the US Defense Department, where he met someone who then sent him on to NASA, the US space agency, and Simosa thinks a man he calls a one-star NASA general, Pete Worden, may have been there. If true, it would mean people inside government were quietly guiding DeLonge's UFO work.
delonge-s-nro-sources-on-predicting-epis: An online commentator who goes by UAPGerb says that around October 2017, Tom DeLonge, a musician turned UFO campaigner, said his high-level sources in the NRO, the National Reconnaissance Office, which is the US agency that runs spy satellites, had told him something striking. According to DeLonge, they said scientists had worked out ways to predict in advance when and where unknown craft would appear. If true, it would mean the government can anticipate these visits rather than simply react to them.
delongepodesta-disclosure-meeting-with-r: UFO researcher Grant Cameron says on Jesse Michels' podcast that in January 2016 a meeting took place in Washington, D.C., involving John Podesta, a senior political adviser, Tom DeLonge, a rock musician turned UFO disclosure campaigner, and a man named Robert Weiss. Cameron ties it to the Podesta emails, Podesta's private messages that later became public. He presents the meeting as part of a push to have the government reveal what it knows about UFOs.
delta-and-omicron-flight-configurations-: Bob Lazar, a man who says that in the late 1980s he worked on alien craft at a secret Nevada desert site called S4, told the podcast host Jesse Michels how one craft flew. Lazar says it had three amplifiers, parts that drove its movement: when all three were used for travel it was in what he calls the delta configuration, and when only one was used it was in the omicron configuration. If true, it would be a first-hand description of how a non-human vehicle works.
demand-for-more-stories-set-in-the-water: Bryce Zable, a Hollywood writer behind the 1990s UFO television show Dark Skies, says that in 1996 a man he calls the captain came to the show's offices in Los Angeles. According to Zable, the captain told him that in the second season the show needed to do more stories set in the water, which he tells as a hint that someone wanted attention turned to UFOs in the oceans.
demodulating-soviet-french-venus-balloon: Bob Maguire, a former contractor who says he worked for the Institute for Defense Analysis, a US defense research group, tells of a job from the mid-1980s. He says a Soviet and French probe headed for Halley's Comet swung past Venus and dropped two balloon probes into its atmosphere, and that he helped decode their signal for the Jet Propulsion Laboratory, NASA's space probe centre. He tells it to show the kind of high-level technical work he was trusted with.
demons-as-the-spirits-of-dead-nephilim-g: Filmmaker and researcher Tim Alberino tells Jesse Michels that, in ancient Hebrew belief, demons are the bodiless spirits of dead giants, the Nephilim of old Jewish texts. He points to the Book of Enoch, an ancient Jewish writing left out of most Bibles, and says it describes the giants' spirits leaving their bodies when they were killed and lingering in the world ever since. If true, it would explain where evil spirits come from.
dendera-light-bulb-relief: Jay Anderson, a guest on a podcast about secret elites and aliens, points to the temple at Dendera in Egypt, where he says a carving shows what looks like the classic light bulb. He offers it as a sign that ancient people may have had knowledge or technology far beyond what history credits them with.
denial-at-the-meeting-at-swedish-militar: Dennis Asberg, a Swedish treasure hunter who says he found a UFO-like object on the seafloor in 2011, tells of a later meeting at military headquarters in Stockholm. He says an officer flatly denied the military had ever been to the site, and Asberg answered that he had filmed them there himself, so he knew they had been. He tells it as proof the military was hiding its interest in the find.
dennis-kucinich-laughed-off-a-debate-sta: A researcher named Jason Simosa, talking with podcast host Jesse Michels, uses a politician named Dennis Kucinich as a warning about how risky the subject is. Simosa says Kucinich, a former Democratic candidate for president, was pretty much laughed off a debate stage once his name became linked with UFOs, and his campaign plummeted, which he places around a 2010 election. The point is that being tied to UFOs could end a political career.
dented-white-van-seen-at-the-facility-an: Dan Sherman, a former US Air Force sergeant who says the NSA (the National Security Agency, the US government's electronic spying agency) trained him to communicate with aliens, tells of the early 1990s in Maryland. He says he noticed a white van with a distinctive dent at the exit of his training facility, and later saw a van with the exact same dent near his Holiday Inn, which told him he was being followed and watched.
department-of-energy-holds-both-ufo-secr: A podcast host named Jesse Michels says that the Department of Energy, the US government agency in charge of nuclear weapons and national science labs, probably holds many secrets about UFOs and about efforts to copy their technology, because of a link he sees between UFOs and nuclear sites. He points out that the same agency also ran the Human Genome Project, the 1990s effort to map all human DNA. He raises it to suggest that one agency may sit at the meeting point of UFO secrecy and human biology.
department-of-energy-manages-ufo-secrecy: A podcast host named Jesse Michels says that he thinks, and in a sense knows, that the Department of Energy, the US government agency that runs nuclear weapons work and the national science labs, plays a large part in keeping UFOs secret. He says it also helps manage what he calls crash retrievals, meaning the recovery of crashed craft of unknown origin. If true, this would place a civilian science agency at the center of the UFO cover-up.
department-of-state-cleared-report-gover: Matthew Brown, who describes himself as a former government insider turned whistleblower, says that what he can speak about publicly is limited to a report the US Department of State cleared for release, plus conclusions drawn from it. He tells this to explain the bounds of his claims.
department-of-war-releases-ufo-files-on-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that on May 8, 2026, the Department of War, the name used here for the US military department, released hundreds of UFO documents, videos and audio recordings on President Trump's orders. If true, the government is officially showing some of what it has kept about these objects. In another episode, though, Michels talks as if the president is still only thinking about the release. A congressman, Eric Burlison, says the first batch was videos from MQ-9 Predator drones, military aircraft flown by remote control, that caught something strange, and he credits a man named Stephen Miller. A skeptic, Michael Shermer, says there have been three releases so far and that the photos and videos have big blacked-out rectangles. A retired Navy admiral, Tim Gallaudet, calls them the PURSUE files and says the work is still in progress, with no metadata, meaning the details of when and where things were recorded. He adds that the videos and reports show a lot of UAP activity, the official term for unexplained objects.
deputy-chris-porritt-s-myers-era-testimo: Brandon Fugal, the owner of Skinwalker Ranch, a Utah property famous for reports of strange events, tells Jesse Michels about a deputy sheriff named Chris Porritt. Fugal says Porritt went on record that strange things were going on at the ranch long before the Sherman family lived there, back in the 1980s when Kenneth and Edith Myers owned it. That would mean the ranch's oddities go back further than its best-known stories.
derinkuyu-underground-city-found-by-a-ma: A guest named Matt, speaking on podcast host Jesse Michels' show, tells how Derinkuyu, a huge ancient underground city in Turkey, was found. He says a man working on his home accidentally knocked down a wall and opened up a doorway into it. The story is told to show how much of the ancient past may still lie hidden right under people's feet.
descartes-as-jesuit-agent-sent-to-infilt: A philosopher named Jason Jorjani, on Jesse Michels' podcast, says that the Jesuits, a Catholic religious order, sent René Descartes, the 17th-century French philosopher, to infiltrate the Rosicrucians, a secretive mystical brotherhood of the time. Jorjani lays this out in his book Prometheus and Atlas. If true, it would mean one of the founders of modern thought began as a kind of religious spy.
description-of-the-osiris-shaft: A researcher named Jeffrey Drum describes the Osiris Shaft, an ancient underground structure on the Giza Plateau in Egypt, on podcast host Jesse Michels' show. He says it sits along the raised walkway running from the central pyramid down to the valley temple and the Sphinx, and that it is a three-level system of chambers reaching 33 meters underground. He tells it as part of a case that something important lies beneath the pyramids.
deser-and-arnowitt-graviton-essay-1954: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in 1954 two physicists, Stanley Deser and Richard Arnowitt, won the essay prize of the Gravity Research Foundation, a group that held a yearly contest for writing on gravity, with a paper about gravitons, theoretical particles thought to carry the force of gravity. He sets it beside a writer named Michael Gladish and a piece called "The G Engines Are Coming," as a sign that serious scientists of the 1950s were working on gravity in ways some connect to antigravity flight.
desert-meeting-with-the-boys-upstairs-fo: Jeffrey Mishlove, a researcher with a PhD who studies psychic claims, told the podcast host Jesse Michels about a night in the late 1970s in the desert near Joshua Tree and Twentynine Palms, California, where he went with a woman named Valerie Ransone to meet what was called "the boys upstairs." He says his mouth dropped open as four lights slowly came down from the sky. By his account, the lights turned out to be flares dropped by the Marines.
desert-trip-with-jake-barber: Michael Herrera, a former US Marine who says he saw a 300-foot UFO in the jungle of Indonesia, tells of a man named Jake Barber taking him on a trip out into the desert. Herrera does not say what happened there, only that it was what proved to him Barber was legit, suggesting he was shown something remarkable.
desmond-leslie-said-nazis-posed-as-venus: Researcher Jason Jorjani says on Jesse Michels' podcast that the daughter of Desmond Leslie, who wrote the book Flying Saucers Have Landed with George Adamski, told him her father always said it was Nazis who contacted Adamski. Adamski was a man who said that in the 1950s he met visitors from Venus. If true, it would mean those famous meetings with "Venusians" were really staged by humans.
detlev-bronk-and-alien-autopsies: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Detlev Bronk, a scientist who later ran the Rockefeller Foundation and was president of Johns Hopkins University, was in charge of so-called alien autopsies in the mid-20th century. In a later episode, citing the Majestic 12 documents, papers said to describe a secret group of twelve top officials handling UFO matters, Michels says the bodies supposedly came from crashes recovered at Aztec and maybe at Roswell. If true, it would mean one of the most respected scientists in America examined non-human bodies in secret.
detlev-bronk-named-as-an-mj12-member-194: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Detlev Bronk, then president of the Rockefeller Foundation, is named as one of the members of Majestic 12 in the MJ12 documents, papers said to describe a secret group of twelve top officials who handled UFO matters from the late 1940s. If true, it would place a leading figure of American science inside a hidden effort to manage what was known about UFOs.
detlev-bronk-rumored-to-be-on-majestic-1: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that a scientist named Detlev Bronk, whom he describes as president of the Rockefeller Foundation, was rumored to sit on Majestic 12, a supposed secret US panel of the late 1940s said to handle crashed flying saucers. Michels adds that Bronk was also rumored to have done the early autopsies on alien bodies, which, if true, would put a top American scientist at the heart of a hidden alien recovery effort.
dia-nro-witness-imaging-objects-in-space: Steven Greer, a doctor who runs the Disclosure Project, an effort to collect testimony from government and military insiders about UFOs, says one of his witnesses worked for the DIA, the Pentagon's military intelligence agency, and with the NRO, the US agency that runs spy satellites. According to Greer, this witness's job involved taking images of unknown objects out in space. If true, it would mean US intelligence has been quietly photographing these objects in orbit.
diana-pasulka-calls-chris-bledsoe-a-mode: A podcast host named Jesse Michels says that a writer and researcher on UFO belief, Diana Pasulka, has publicly called Chris Bledsoe, a North Carolina man who says he has had UFO encounters, a modern Paul Bennewitz. Bennewitz is a figure from an earlier chapter of UFO history whose story Michels discusses in the same episode, one titled around a man driven to madness by 'aliens'. The comparison suggests Bledsoe's experience may follow the same troubled pattern.
diana-pasulka-on-the-rituals-rocket-team: Chris Ramsay, a YouTuber who talks about UFOs, tells Jesse Michels to listen to Diana Pasulka, a religion scholar who studies belief in UFOs. He says she talks a lot about the ritual-like routines that rocket teams in the United States perform before a launch. He brings it up to suggest that even hard science carries a hidden religious side.
diana-pasulka-s-research-in-the-files-of: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that a friend of his, Diana Pasulka, a religious studies professor at the University of North Carolina Wilmington, has gone very deep on St. Joseph of Cupertino, a saint from seventeenth-century Italy. According to Michels, she has gone through many of the saint's files and agrees with the point he was making, which, if right, would let old church records back up his argument.
diana-pasulka-s-turn-while-writing-her-b: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, talks about Diana Pasulka, an academic at the University of North Carolina Wilmington who wrote a book about people's beliefs in UFOs. Michels says that halfway through the book she goes down the rabbit hole herself, and ends up thinking there is "something extremely real" going on. As he tells it, a scholar who set out to study the believers came to share some of their conviction.
diane-powell-meets-akil-after-his-mother: On a 2025 episode of a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, about children said to be able to read minds, a woman named Diane Powell tells how she came to meet a boy named Akil in New Jersey around 2022. She says Akil's mother contacted her after seeing her interviewed by the well-known author Deepak Chopra. It is part of her account of how she came to study children who, if the claims are true, can share thoughts without speaking.
diane-powell-s-inbox-full-of-parents-say: A filmmaker named Ky Dickens, who made a documentary called The Telepathy Tapes, told podcast host Jesse Michels about a researcher named Diane Powell. She says that around 2022 and 2023 Powell's email inbox filled up with messages from parents saying they had found their children could read their thoughts. If true, it would point to mind reading being far more common than people think.
diane-powell-s-medical-licence-revoked: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that a doctor named Diane Powell had her medical licence taken away because she studied children said to be telepathic, meaning able to read minds. He connects her to The Telepathy Tapes, a project about these children. If that is what happened, it would mean a doctor lost her right to practise for looking into this subject.
diane-powell-takes-on-john-mack-s-legacy: Podcast host Jesse Michels tells how John Mack, a psychiatrist who studied people who said they had met aliens, was tragically hit by a car and killed in London in 2004. According to Michels, when psychiatrist Diane Powell went to his memorial, people there urged her to take up Mack's legacy, and the story goes on to a house in Oregon tied to striking coincidences. It is told as how Powell came to her own work on the mind's unexplained abilities.
diary-of-merer-records-tura-limestone-be: Researcher Luke Caverns tells Jesse Michels about the Diary of Merer, an ancient Egyptian logbook kept by an official named Merer. He says it records blocks of limestone from Tura, a quarry area, being shipped up to Giza, to what Merer calls the "horizon of Khufu," the pharaoh whose name is linked to the Great Pyramid. Caverns cites it as a written record of how stone reached the pyramids.
dick-and-vallee-precognize-each-other-s-: A researcher named Eric Wargo, speaking on Jesse Michels' podcast in 2024, says the science fiction writer Philip K. Dick and the UFO researcher Jacques Vallée each seemed to foresee the other's work. According to Wargo, in 1974 and 1975 Vallée was writing his book The Invisible College while Dick was writing the first draft of what became his novel VALIS, and the two books echo each other. If true, it would suggest ideas can travel ahead in time between minds.
dick-billings-on-doctoring-the-zapruder-: Dan Sheehan, a lawyer who often speaks about government secrecy and UFOs, told the podcast host Jesse Michels in 2025 about a man named Dick Billings. Sheehan says Billings sat him down and told him the whole story of how the Zapruder film, the home movie that caught President Kennedy's assassination in 1963, was taken to Rochester, New York, and doctored there. He mentions the magazine publisher Henry Luce in the same story. If true, the best-known footage of the killing would have been altered.
dick-billings-visits-sheehan-over-the-se: A lawyer named Dan Sheehan told podcast host Jesse Michels about the 1980s, when his legal group, the Christic Institute, brought a sealed lawsuit tied to Iran-Contra, a US scandal over secret arms sales and covert funding. He says a man came to his Washington office, said only a couple of people in the world would have answered his question the way Sheehan did, and introduced himself as Dick Billings, former chief staff writer for the House committee that reinvestigated political assassinations, offering to help with the case. Sheehan tells it as how he gained an insider who could open doors to hidden government secrets.
dick-cheney-at-the-top-of-the-secrecy-py: The podcast host Jesse Michels says he introduced a journalist friend, Walter Kirn, to David Grusch, a former intelligence officer who became a UFO whistleblower. According to Kirn, when he asked Grusch who sits at the very top of the pyramid of secret information, Grusch said Dick Cheney, the former US vice president. Michels describes Cheney as the gatekeeper of all the long-running secret UFO programs, and a researcher known as UAPGerb adds that he held that role for quite a while. If true, it would put one of America's most powerful officials in charge of the biggest secret of all.
dick-harper-falsified-personnel-records-: A man named Scott Ramsay passes on what he says a man named Dick Harper told him about a crashed craft that people say was recovered near Aztec, New Mexico, around 1948. According to Ramsay, Harper said about 200 people took part in the recovery, so he kept 200 personnel records, the files that track where military staff served, so that nobody would ever really show up as having been at Aztec. If true, it would mean the recovery's paper trail was hidden on purpose.
dick-russell-s-1994-taped-interview-with: A researcher named Greg Malatzi, on Jesse Michels' podcast in 2026, talks about Andrija Puharich, a scientist the episode describes as a CIA man who claimed contact with an alien council. According to Malatzi, the writer Dick Russell met Puharich once and tape recorded an interview with him in 1994, the year before Puharich died, a death described as mysterious. The tape matters because it would be one of the last records of Puharich speaking for himself.
dick-russell-s-day-long-interview-with-s: A researcher named Greg Malatzi says that the writer Dick Russell got one of the only interviews ever given by Sidney Gottlieb, a CIA scientist, sometime in the 1990s at Gottlieb's house. Malatzi says Russell spent a whole day with him. If true, it would make Russell's interview a rare first-hand window into a man who knew a great deal about the agency's secret research.
dicom-ct-scans-show-capillaries-feeding-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, talks about small three-fingered bodies said to come from Peru, and the medical scans made of them. He says an independent researcher named Gonzalo Chavez, who helped set up a website called tridactyls.org, points to the public scan files, CT scans (3D X-ray images used in hospitals) saved in DICOM, a standard medical image format. Michels says that inside one of the bodies, a more reptile-looking type, you can see tiny blood vessels feeding eggs, which would suggest these were once living creatures.
dictators-outlawed-freemasonry: A researcher named Randall Carlson, on podcast host Jesse Michels's show, says that Hitler, Mao and Stalin all outlawed Freemasonry, the old fraternal society that meets in lodges. He tells it as a shared trait of those dictators, suggesting that the society was seen as a threat by men who wanted total control.
die-glocke-and-spinning-mercury: Jesse Michels, a podcast host, says that according to a Polish journalist named Igor Witkowski, a Nazi wartime project known as Die Glocke, German for "the Bell", involved rotating, spinning mercury. Michels places it in the context of Hans Kammler, a senior SS officer, during World War Two in Germany and Poland. If true, it would suggest the Nazis were experimenting with exotic propulsion or physics far beyond ordinary weapons.
different-pieces-of-legacy-hardware-held: A filmmaker and journalist, Jeremy Corbell, says that different pieces of so-called legacy hardware, meaning craft or material said to be recovered long ago, are kept in different places around the United States. He says it is public that a member of Congress, Representative Burlison, has been going to various sites in search of this hardware, which if true would mean lawmakers are chasing physical proof.
dimethyl-sulfide-found-on-exoplanets-as-: A guest named Chris Gilbert, on podcast host Jesse Michels's show, says that scientists have found a chemical called dimethyl sulfide on exoplanets, which are planets circling other stars, about 120 light years away or more. He tells it as a possible sign of life elsewhere, since if the finding holds, it would hint that living things exist beyond Earth.
dinner-companion-with-chameleon-like-eye: A man named Geoffrey Drumm says that on his first trip to Egypt, around 2017, he sat down to dinner with a man, at a hotel in one version, whose big bulging eyes looked like a chameleon's and seemed to move on their own, one looking off elsewhere. He says the man questioned him about the Serapeum, an ancient underground site in Egypt, and that when Drumm later tried to message him, the man had vanished as if into thin air. Drumm tells it on Jesse Michels' podcast, in an episode about his belief that a non-human being revealed the true purpose of the pyramids to him.
dinner-in-san-jose-with-a-female-crash-r: The physicist Eric Davis told the podcast host Jesse Michels that he once met a woman who, he says, had worked in a secret program in the 1970s and 1980s recovering crashed craft that were not made by humans. Davis says his source's wife drove him to the woman's home, picked her up, and the three of them went to a German restaurant in San Jose, California, for dinner. If true, it would mean he spoke face to face with someone who handled such material.
