dinosaur-extinction-by-chicxulub-impact-: This is the story of how the dinosaurs died out 66 million years ago, and of the scientists who first said why. The writer Graham Hancock says on Jesse Michels' podcast that nobody now disputes that a comet or asteroid did it, and that the proof is the Chicxulub crater, buried deep under land and sea around Mexico's Yucatan, which in another telling he places under the Gulf of Mexico. He credits the scientists Luis and Walter Alvarez, who put the idea forward in the 1980s, and says it was not accepted until the crater was found. Michels himself tells it more briefly, crediting only Luis Alvarez. They tell it as an example of an idea that was rejected at first and later proven right.
dinosaurs-and-roman-battles-on-benowitz-: A writer, Greg Bishop, passes on what a man named Gabe Valdez told him about a man named Benowitz, who lived in Albuquerque, New Mexico, in the early 1980s. Bishop says Valdez went over to Benowitz's home and saw some of what was showing on his screen, an old tube-style monitor. According to Valdez, it showed dinosaurs and what looked like old Roman battles.
dire-wolf-carcass-found-at-dry-gulch-cre: Brandon Fugal, the owner of Skinwalker Ranch, a Utah property known for reports of strange events, told podcast host Jesse Michels about a find at a spot called Dry Gulch Creek in the 2020s. He says that, on camera for the TV show The Secret of Skinwalker Ranch, his team came upon the rotting body of a large wolf-like animal, which a biologist named Ben Woodruff matched to the dire wolf, a huge wolf thought to be long extinct. If so, it would mean an animal from the distant past was somehow on the ranch.
direct-witnesses-scott-interviewed-1948: Scott Ramsay, a researcher looking into a reported 1948 crash of an unknown craft near Aztec, New Mexico, lists on podcast host Jesse Michels' show the people he says he spoke to directly about it. He names Doug Nolan, Ken Farley, a local preacher, the preacher's son, and one other man. If their accounts hold, it would mean the crash has living firsthand witnesses.
directional-scopaesthesia-paper-from-alm: A scientist, Rupert Sheldrake, studies scopaesthesia, the feeling of being stared at. He says his most recent paper on it, called Directional Scopaesthesia and its Implications for Theories of Vision, looked at almost a thousand case histories of people reacting to being looked at. He presents it as saying something about how seeing itself works, which would matter a great deal if the effect is real.
disappearance-mountain-near-ruwa-zimbabw: A researcher, Jason Jorjani, talks about places linked to people disappearing. He says one is a mountain in Zimbabwe, near the town of Ruwa, close to where a famous UFO sighting happened in the 1990s.
disappearance-of-los-alamos-employee-mel: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells of Melissa Casillas, a 53-year-old administrative assistant at Los Alamos National Laboratory, a US government research lab in New Mexico, who he says went missing in 2025 around Ranchos de Taos, New Mexico. He draws on her relatives Sierra and Mark Casillas and a GoFundMe, an online fundraising page, and he tells it as part of a wider question about why American scientists are going missing.
disappearance-of-malaysia-airlines-fligh: A podcast host named Jesse Michels retells the story of Malaysia Airlines flight MH370, a passenger plane that he says took off from Kuala Lumpur, the capital of Malaysia, on March 8th, 2014, with 239 people aboard, and then vanished. He brings it up in an episode about why top American scientists are going missing, placing it among other unexplained disappearances.
disappearance-of-monica-reza-near-mount-: A podcast host named Jesse Michels tells of Monica Reza, whom he calls 'the woman who taught us how to tame fire', and says she vanished on June 22nd, 2025, near Mount Waterman in the mountains of the Angeles National Forest outside Los Angeles. He mentions the Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department in connection with the case. He tells it in an episode about American scientists who have gone missing, suggesting her case may be part of a larger pattern.
disappearance-of-sharon-the-space-kid-ps: A researcher named Greg says that a girl named Sharon was one of the "space kids", young people said to have psychic gifts who were studied by Andrija Puharich, a researcher of psychic phenomena, in the late 1970s and early 1980s in the United States. According to Greg, Sharon simply disappeared, and the people who knew her then are convinced she was the real deal and was pulled into a secret government project, like the ones in the TV show Stranger Things or the legend of Montauk. If true, it would mean a gifted child was taken into hidden psychic research.
disc-sighting-on-a-blue-ridge-mountain-1: Steven Greer, a doctor who campaigns for governments to reveal what they know about UFOs, told the podcast host Jesse Michels that on a crystal clear October afternoon in 1973, when he had just turned 18, he looked up on a mountain in the Blue Ridge range near Boone, North Carolina, and saw a disc-shaped craft. He says it looked like the one he had seen as an eight-year-old, though he cannot say it was the same one.
disclosure-day-trailer-said-7-billion-bu: Podcast host Jesse Michels, discussing a Hollywood film called Disclosure Day about the world learning the truth about aliens, pointed to a small change. He says the trailer's line was that 7 billion people have the right to know the truth, while the film itself says 8 billion, a detail he raises, citing writer Bryce Zabel, as worth noticing in how the story was put together.
discovery-and-translation-of-the-necrono: An author named Peter Levenda says that in the 1970s, at the Warlock Shop in Brooklyn Heights, New York, linked to a man named Herman Slater, he looked at an old manuscript and said, "This looks like it says Necronomicon," the name of a legendary book of magic. He tells a podcast host, Jesse Michels, that the translation was finished on October 12, 1975. In his telling, this is how a book many thought was only legend came into print.
discovery-of-dmt-s-effects-by-stephen-sz: A neuroscientist named Andrew Gallimore, talking with podcast host Jesse Michels, tells how the effects of DMT, a powerful psychedelic drug, were discovered in 1956. He says a Hungarian physician named Stephen Szára, working in a hospital in communist Hungary, injected himself with it and then tried it on colleagues. Gallimore tells it as the start of the modern study of the drug's strange visions.
discovery-of-the-immaculate-constellatio: A man named Matthew Brown, who says he worked in a Pentagon policy office, says that around 2018 he came across a briefing on a classified computer system about something called Immaculate Constellation. As it was described to him, it was a special access programme, a tightly restricted secret project, that ran the watching and tracking of UAP, the official term for UFOs, around the world, using sensors both aimed at them on purpose and picking them up by chance. If true, it would mean the military has been quietly collecting UFO sightings worldwide.
discovery-of-the-martian-ocean-shoreline: A scientist named John Brandenburg told podcast host Jesse Michels that in the 1980s he and colleagues found signs of an ancient ocean on Mars. He says they spotted a shoreline near a region called Cydonia Mensa, which he wrote up in a 1986 conference paper. If true, it would mean Mars was once wet enough to support life.
disney-accelerator-brain-controlled-rock: Eric Haseltine, a former official at the National Security Agency, the US spy agency that intercepts communications, told the podcast host Jesse Michels about earlier work with a Disney lab that helped young companies. He says that before 2020 they invented a rock, nicknamed Rocky, that a person could move with their mind.
disney-laser-plasma-electronic-fireworks: Eric Haseltine, a former National Security Agency official who earlier worked at Walt Disney Imagineering, the company's design and technology arm, told the podcast host Jesse Michels that Disney was developing electronic fireworks. He says they focused a powerful laser on a spot in the air and put so much energy there that the air became electrically charged and glowed like ball lightning, a rare glowing ball sometimes seen in storms. It suggests how some glowing lights in the sky could be made by people.
disney-s-ward-kimball-expects-government: A writer named Bryce Zabel, speaking on podcast host Jesse Michels' show, tells a story from the 1950s about Ward Kimball, one of Walt Disney's animators. Zabel says Kimball believed Disney would make a documentary about UFOs and that the US government would hand over real footage for it. If true, it would mean the government once considered showing the public what it had.
dispute-over-debunk-of-a-uap-video-boost: A podcast host named Jesse Michels describes an argument over a video called Bluegill Triple Prime, which shows a UAP, the official term for an unidentified flying object, tumbling out of a fireball. Skeptics, including a man named Dean Johnson, explain the object as an ordinary rocket booster or instrument pod, and Michels says that Jeffrey Krookshank, an analyst he is in touch with who has studied the footage closely, believes Johnson is actually quite scared. If the object is not what the skeptics say, the video would show something unexplained.
diver-calls-it-the-most-important-dive-o: A diver named Stefan Hogeborn says that in 2012 he dived on the Baltic Sea anomaly, an odd-shaped object found on the seafloor between Sweden and Finland. He says that out of some 6,000 dives in his life, it was probably the most important, and he tells it on Jesse Michels' podcast in an episode about the treasure hunter who found it, a man named Dennis Asberg.
diver-finds-a-breathing-organic-object-o: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, passes on a story he links to a writer named Richard Dolan and a man named David Noble White Crow, a Native American who was himself a UFO witness. Michels says White Crow was stationed somewhere with another man who said he had dived down to a strange object off Hawaii in the 1960s, an object that seemed organic and breathing. The story is tied to Starfish Prime, a 1962 US nuclear test high above the Pacific, and if true it would mean something alive and unknown was lying under the sea.
diver-sucked-into-a-giant-grouper-s-mout: A man named Joe McMoneagle passes on a story he was told about a diver working at an oil platform in the Gulf of Mexico, in the 1960s or earlier. According to the story, a giant grouper, a huge fish, got curious, came up behind the diver, opened its mouth, and sucked him in backwards.
djoser-depicted-in-the-saqqara-step-pyra: Luke Caverns, a researcher, says on podcast host Jesse Michels' show that in the maze of tunnels beneath the Step Pyramid at Saqqara in Egypt, there are carvings of the early pharaoh Djoser striding forward during a festival. He contrasts this with the later pyramids, which he says have no decoration inside at all. In his telling, that difference raises the question of who built the later pyramids and why.
dmt-keeps-oxygen-deprived-neurons-alive-: A neuroscientist named Andrew Gallimore, on podcast host Jesse Michels's show, says that nerve cells starved of oxygen survive longer when DMT, a powerful psychedelic compound, is present. As the story's title frames it, this happens through the sigma-1 receptor, a protein on cells that DMT can attach to. If true, it would suggest the brain's own DMT may help protect it when oxygen runs short.
dmt-laser-diffraction-shows-the-same-sym: A man named Randy Anderson passes on something he heard by way of a man named Danny Jones about DMT, a powerful psychedelic drug. Anderson says that when a laser was shone a certain way, everyone who took it saw the same symbols, which would suggest the visions show something shared rather than something purely in each person's head.
dna-and-rna-building-blocks-found-in-met: A podcast host named Jesse Michels says that a few years ago a group of scientists from Japan and from NASA, the US space agency, confirmed something extraordinary: the basic building blocks of DNA and RNA, the molecules that carry genetic information, inside meteorites that fell in Canada, the US and Australia. He raises it because it would mean some of the ingredients of life can arrive from space.
dni-team-encounters-orbs-at-western-us-m: Eric Burles, speaking on a podcast, says that recently, around 2025 or 2026, a team working for Tulsi Gabbard, the Director of National Intelligence who oversees US spy agencies, flew by helicopter to a military base in the western US after reports of UAPs, the government's term for UFOs. According to him, what they met there were glowing orbs, which would mean top intelligence officials saw the phenomenon firsthand.
dni-tulsi-gabbard-s-platform-pledge-to-e: A podcast host named Jesse Michels says that Tulsi Gabbard, who in 2025 became the Director of National Intelligence, the official who oversees all US spy agencies, made it part of her stated platform to expose information about UAPs, the government's term for UFOs. He points to this as a sign that someone at the top of US intelligence is openly promising to reveal what is known.
dobrynin-asks-about-the-excitement-over-: Harald Malmgren, who advised US presidents, told the podcast host Jesse Michels something he says he had never spoken of before. In 1960s Washington, he says, Anatoly Dobrynin, the Soviet Union's ambassador to the United States, once asked him why everyone was so excited about unidentified flying objects, a hint that the Soviets were watching American interest in the subject.
doc-brown-in-back-to-the-future-as-a-nod: Podcast host Jesse Michels says that Doc Brown, the inventor in the 1985 film Back to the Future, was a nod to Townsend Brown, a real scientist who experimented with capacitors, devices that store electric charge, as a way to make things move. Michels points out that the film is set in 1985, the year Townsend Brown died, that the character's full name is Emmett Brown, that the film's "flux capacitor" echoes Brown's capacitor experiments, and that people called the real man "Doc Brown"; he links it to Steven Spielberg, who was behind the film, and says Brown's daughter told him directly she is sure the character is based on her father. If true, it would mean Hollywood quietly honored a little-known scientist tied to talk of anti-gravity.
doc-edgerton-eg-g-and-filming-the-manhat: A podcast host named Jesse Michels tells of Harold 'Doc' Edgerton, an engineer at MIT, a leading technical university, who he says developed a new way of using stroboscopic cameras, which take extremely fast flash photographs. According to Michels, this and other wartime technology ended up being used in the Manhattan Project, the secret US effort of the 1940s to build the atomic bomb, with links to the wartime science chief Vannevar Bush and to a company called EG&G. He tells it to trace how the people around the bomb program were connected to later secret work.
doctors-who-treated-a-soldier-questioned: A surgeon, Italo Venturelli, talks about events in 1996 in the town of Varginha, Brazil, where people say a strange creature was captured. He says some doctors treated a soldier, and that he was questioned by Brazil's federal police. If true, it would suggest the authorities moved to keep the medical side of the story quiet.
document-shows-pandolfi-supplying-gravit: A researcher, Grant Cameron, talks about a man named Ron Pandolfi and the Jasons, a group of top scientists who advise the US government. Cameron says a document about gravitational waves, tiny ripples in space itself, was found, and that it shows Pandolfi finding and supplying the experts who briefed the group. If true, it would put Pandolfi at the center of quiet high-level science work.
documentary-project-with-secret-dating-e: A man named Matt, speaking on Jesse Michels' podcast in 2024 in an episode about a supposed great event around 12,000 BC, says he is leading a very significant documentary. He says it covers ancient sites in Turkey, Peru, Bolivia and the Spanish island of Minorca, and holds evidence about their age that has not yet been made public, evidence that if true would push these sites much further back in time than usually thought.
documented-link-between-the-ufo-phenomen: An author and researcher named Peter Levenda says he has shown, through documents, a connection between the UFO phenomenon and the 1963 assassination of President John F. Kennedy. He makes the case in his book series Sinister Forces, pointing to people such as Fred Crisman, Guy Banister and E. Howard Hunt who, he says, turn up in both stories between 1947 and 1963. If true, it would tie the UFO mystery to one of the darkest events in American history.
dod-officials-advise-against-disclosure: A man named Dave Rossi, on Jesse Michels' podcast in 2025, says he has spoken with respected high-level people in the Department of Defense, the US military's headquarters, about going public with what he knows about non-human intelligence. He says their advice has always been the same: people will not see what you see, meaning the public would not accept it.
dod-pays-bob-monroe-to-train-him-in-out-: A man named Joe McMoneagle says that in the 1980s the US Department of Defense, the military's headquarters, hired Bob Monroe, the author known for the book Journeys Out of the Body, to train him. McMoneagle says Monroe was paid to teach him out-of-body experiences at the Monroe Institute in Virginia, which, if true, would mean the military took such abilities seriously. He tells it on Jesse Michels' podcast in 2025.
doe-and-battelle-institute-as-ufo-secret: A researcher named Bob Maguire, speaking with podcast host Jesse Michels, says he kept pointing people toward the Department of Energy, the US government agency that runs the country's nuclear weapons labs, and toward the Battelle Institute, a private research organisation. He says he kept asking why nobody was looking at them as places where UFO secrets might be kept, and he credits the idea in part to a woman named Linda Thompson. If he were right, the hidden story would sit somewhere other than the military, where most people look.
doe-check-finds-no-nuclear-tests-on-shut: A former US Air Force officer, Robert Salas, talks on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels about nuclear missiles that he says went dead on March 16 and March 24, 1967. Salas says that a check with the Department of Energy, the federal agency in charge of American nuclear weapons work, which he credits to a man named James Clattz, found no nuclear tests on either date at the Nevada test site. If that holds, test blasts could not be the reason the missiles shut down.
doe-genesis-project: A podcast host named Jesse Michels says that the Department of Energy, the US agency that runs the country's national science laboratories, now has something called the Genesis project. As he understands it, the project is a way to gather all the information from all the national labs and run it through artificial intelligence, which would put an enormous store of secret science in one place.
doe-hazing-ritual-fake-alien-and-roswell: A former CIA officer named Rolf Mowatt-Larssen, who also worked at the US Department of Energy, told podcast host Jesse Michels about a prank played on newly appointed officials there in the late 2000s. He says that, in a secure vault at the department's Washington headquarters, new arrivals were given a mock briefing on a special access program (a tightly restricted secret project) claiming the government really had aliens, one injured and one not, and had taken alien technology from the famous crash at Roswell, New Mexico. He tells it, in two interviews that differ slightly on the years and once citing his book A State of Mind, as an inside joke that shows how the alien story was treated within government.
doe-holds-the-nation-s-most-important-se: Rolf Mowatt-Larssen, introduced on Jesse Michels' podcast as a former chief at the CIA, the US spy agency, says that from 2005 to 2008 he worked at the Department of Energy, the US government department that oversees the country's nuclear sites. He says he learned some of the nation's most important secrets there, not at the CIA, hinting that the department does work few people imagine.
doe-intelligence-director-never-briefed-: Rolf Mowatt-Larssen, a former CIA officer who says he was director of intelligence at the Department of Energy, the US department that oversees nuclear sites, from 2005 to 2008, speaks on Jesse Michels' podcast in 2026. He says openly that in that job he was never briefed on unidentified objects, which the government calls UAP, entering nuclear sites, which would matter because such visits are often claimed by others.
doe-nest-as-the-hazmat-crash-retrieval-t: An online commentator who goes by UAPGerb talks about the account of Jonathan Weygandt, who has described a crashed craft site in Peru in 1997 where people from the "DOE", the US Department of Energy, showed up. UAPGerb says those people were very likely the Department of Energy's Nuclear Emergency Support Team, or NEST, a unit that handles nuclear and hazardous material incidents, acting as the crash recovery team, and he links this to the 1954 Atomic Energy Act, a law governing nuclear secrets. If true, it would mean an existing nuclear response team quietly doubles as the group that recovers crashed craft around the world.
doe-says-it-cannot-locate-kettle-2-foota: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in October 2023 a formal request was filed, linked to a man named Jeffrey Cruickshank, asking the government to review and release secret footage known as Kettle 2. According to Michels, the Department of Energy answered that it could not find the footage, which he raises as a sign that records are missing or kept out of reach.
doe-srt-and-nnsa-office-of-secure-transp: An online researcher who goes by UAPGerb tells podcast host Jesse Michels about two units inside the Department of Energy, the federal agency that runs America's nuclear work: a security unit he calls SRT, and the Office of Secure Transportation, which belongs to the department's nuclear weapons agency. UAPGerb says he thinks these two are very likely involved in recovering crashed UFOs or moving recovered UFO material between the government's national science labs in the continental United States. If true, it would mean the government quietly ships such material around the country.
doe-using-the-alien-motif-as-cover: A podcast host named Jesse Michels says that something is going on with high energy physics at the Department of Energy, the US agency in charge of nuclear weapons and the national labs. He thinks the agency may be throwing people off by leaning on the idea of aliens, which would mean the UFO story is partly a cover for secret physics work.
dog-whistle-draws-uaps-daily: A man named Jake Barber, who says he once helped retrieve a UFO by helicopter, now works with a startup called Skywatcher, which says it can summon UFOs. Barber says the company has something it calls the "dog whistle", and that once they switch it on, UAPs, short for unidentified anomalous phenomena, the official term for UFOs, come to them day after day. James Valor, another first-hand witness with the company, says nearly the same words. He credits the system to a person he calls Mr. K and puts the work between 2021 and 2025. If true, it would mean these objects can be called up on purpose instead of just waited for.
dogs-that-know-when-their-owners-are-com: A scientist named Rupert Sheldrake says some animals have abilities that are stronger than ours, such as sensing things before they happen. He says this was the subject of his own book, Dogs That Know When Their Owners Are Coming Home, which looks at pets that seem to know when someone is on the way home and at animals that seem to warn of earthquakes. If true, it would mean animals can pick up on things that science cannot yet explain.
doj-trial-under-military-order-number-on: A computer hacker named Gary McKinnon, who says he got into US government computers, tells of what happened while the US tried to bring him to trial, sometime between 2002 and 2008. He says the Department of Justice, the US government's main law enforcement department, told him he would be tried under Military Order Number One, a wartime presidential order, which he describes as giving him the same status as the prisoners held at the US military prison at Guantanamo Bay. If true, it would show how seriously the US government took what he had found or done.
dolan-finds-timothy-good-s-above-top-sec: A researcher and writer on UFOs, Richard Dolan, says that one day in 1994 he walked into an ordinary bookstore in Syracuse, New York. There he spotted Above Top Secret, a book by the British writer Timothy Good about governments keeping UFO information secret, which Dolan calls a classic. He tells it as the moment his own long interest in the subject began.
dolan-s-early-appearances-and-stanton-fr: Richard Dolan, an author who had just published a big book on UFOs, says that around 2001, at early events in Laughlin, Nevada and St. Louis, Missouri, he found himself alone with Stanton Friedman, a well-known UFO researcher. Dolan says Friedman was sizing him up and asked his opinion of Bob Lazar, a much-debated figure in UFO circles. He tells it on Jesse Michels' podcast in 2025.
dolan-s-uso-database-shows-em-interferen: A UFO historian named Richard Dolan tells podcast host Jesse Michels that he built a collection of reports of unidentified submerged objects, strange things seen in or coming out of the world's oceans, going back to 1825, with help from someone called Tracy. Dolan says that about one in ten of those cases involved electromagnetic interference, meaning radios, compasses or electrical systems acting up nearby. To him, that pattern suggests the objects share some real physical effect.
dolmens-tied-to-a-cult-of-giants: A filmmaker and researcher named Tim Alberino tells podcast host Jesse Michels that dolmens, ancient monuments made of huge standing stones topped by a flat slab and found in places like Sardinia and Minorca, are linked to giants. He says the link is not just that the stones are big, but that they were tied to an ancient cult of giants. If so, it would mean giants played a real part in early human religion.
don-carter-s-kirtland-interdisciplinary-: A podcast host named Jesse Michels says that in 1962 a man named Don Carter, head of advanced research at Kirtland Air Force Base in New Mexico, was bringing together groups of experts from many different fields. He says Henry Kissinger, who later became a top American diplomat, was involved with these groups. Michels tells it as a sign that serious, high-level thinking about unusual matters was going on near the nation's nuclear labs at the time.
don-paul-thanks-greer-for-those-stuck-in: Steven Greer, a doctor who campaigns for UFO disclosure, told the podcast host Jesse Michels that a man named Don Paul once picked him up in Los Angeles and dropped him off where he was staying. Greer says Paul thanked him on behalf of people stuck inside so-called legacy programs, secret projects said to hold recovered non-human technology, which would mean insiders support his push to make it public.
don-phillips-humans-have-the-fastest-com: Don Phillips, a man connected to Lockheed's Skunk Works, the aircraft maker's secret advanced design division, said on Jesse Michels's podcast that people carry a faster computer inside them than any machine humans could ever build. In his view the human mind is more powerful than any technology we can make.
donald-barr-dalton-school-and-the-novel-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Donald Barr, a former officer of the OSS, the American wartime spy agency, was headmaster of the Dalton School, a private school in New York, around the time a young Jeffrey Epstein got a job teaching there in the 1970s. Michels adds that Barr wrote a science fiction novel called Space Relations, which he describes as a story about aliens keeping humans as sex slaves, and he links William Barr and Epstein into the tale. He calls it the weirdest thread tying Epstein to UFOs.
donald-hornig-listed-as-present-at-kecks: Kevin Knuth, a physicist and former NASA researcher, says he came across a government summary of the 1965 Kecksburg incident, when an object was reported to have come down near Kecksburg, Pennsylvania. He says the document listed Donald Hornig, a senior government scientist, as being present, which would tie high-level science officials to the event.
donald-menzel-caught-destroying-plates-p: The podcast host Jesse Michels says that Donald Menzel, an astronomer at Harvard in the 1950s, was caught destroying astronomical plates, the glass photographs of the night sky that observatories keep as records. Michels says the person who caught him was Dorrit Hoffleit, a respected Harvard astronomer whom he also describes as Menzel's assistant, and that she wrote about it in her book. If true, a leading scientist would have been getting rid of records of the sky.
donald-trump-controls-resorts-internatio: A guest who goes by the name JASON tells podcast host Jesse Michels, in an episode about a secret society behind a UFO cover-up, that Donald Trump was in charge of Resorts International, a casino and resort company with ties to the Bahamas. JASON says Trump was basically the man running it for a year or so, which he places in the mid 1970s. He brings it up as one link in the wider web of people and money his story traces.
donald-trump-jr-interviews-ross-coulthar: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, mentions that Donald Trump Jr., the son of President Donald Trump, interviewed Ross Coulthart, a journalist who reports on UFOs, in 2025. Michels brings it up as a sign that talk of UFOs had reached people close to the White House.
donna-hare-ufos-airbrushed-out-of-images: Donna Hare is a woman who says that in the 1970s, while working at NASA's Johnson Space Center in Houston, she was shown a photo in a place called Building 8 and asked, "Is this a UFO?" She says the man just smiled and answered, "I can't tell you that," and podcast host Jesse Michels says she described UFOs being airbrushed out of images stored there, a story she told through the Disclosure Project, a group led by a man named Steven Greer that brought whistleblowers forward. Michels adds that this is why a man named Gary McKinnon later went looking for that building, and if it were true it would mean NASA was hiding UFOs from its own pictures.
donut-craft-his-father-showed-him: A man named Dave Rossi says his father once called him over at their old house to take a look at something in the sky. According to Rossi, it was a typical donut-shaped craft, on one of three times such things appeared; he tells it on Jesse Michels' podcast in 2025.
donut-shaped-ufos-above-rossi-s-old-hous: Dave Rossi, a guest on Jesse Michels' podcast in 2025, says that at his old house a few unidentified flying objects showed up above the home over a span of about five years. He says they were donut-shaped and that his father saw them too, which, if true, would mean the family had repeated close sightings.
doolittle-sent-to-investigate-swedish-gh: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says it is known for a fact that Dwight Eisenhower, then a top US Army general and later president, sent General James Doolittle, a famous World War II air commander, to investigate the Swedish ghost rockets. These were mysterious rocket-like objects reported in the skies over Sweden and Finland in 1946, and Michels tells it to show the US military was taking strange aerial sightings seriously even before the modern UFO era began.
door-to-door-survey-of-1-600-swedes: A Swedish researcher named Clas Svahn says that he and others once went door to door across Sweden and spoke with 1,600 people about strange things in the sky. According to Svahn, about one in ten of them said they had seen something, which, if true, would suggest such sightings are far more common than people admit.
doty-admits-befriending-benowitz-and-mis: In the early 1980s in Albuquerque, New Mexico, a man named Paul Benowitz came to believe he was picking up signals and messages from aliens. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that a man named Rick Doty later came forward and admitted he had made friends with Benowitz on purpose and fed him misleading material, saying he "was tasked to do that." Michels tells it because, if true, it would mean someone was deliberately steering a man's belief in aliens.
doty-and-lear-spread-quackery-around-the: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in the 1980s the story of Majestic 12, said to be a secret group in charge of the UFO question, was pushed out along with all sorts of quackery. He points to Richard Doty, an agent of the Air Force Office of Special Investigations, the Air Force's own investigative and counterintelligence service, and other counterintelligence people talking about alien beings, and to a man named John Lear saying there is a "soul catcher" on the Moon. Michels tells it to show how the subject may have been muddied on purpose.
doty-s-alien-crystal-that-showed-the-cru: A researcher, Grant Cameron, passes on a story told by a man named Richard Doty about his time in the military. Cameron says Doty calls it the most amazing thing he ever saw there: an alien crystal that showed the crucifixion of Jesus.
doty-s-claim-he-was-an-area-51-guard: A writer, Greg Bishop, says a man named Rick Doty told him he was once a guard at Area 51, a secret US military test site in the Nevada desert. Bishop adds that he has no idea whether that is so.
doty-s-disinformation-to-moulton-howe-an: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Bob Lazar, a man who claims he worked on alien craft at a secret site in Nevada, admits he may have been made to drink a liquid and then fed information. According to Michels, that information looked like the same material that Richard Doty, an Air Force intelligence agent, passed in 1979 in New Mexico to Linda Moulton Howe, a journalist, and Paul Bennewitz, a businessman who believed he had picked up alien signals, which, if true, would suggest Lazar's story was partly planted by the government's own false leads.
doty-s-rival-version-1964-at-white-sands: On a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, a UFO researcher named Grant Cameron describes two clashing versions of a story about a craft said to have landed at Holloman, an Air Force base in New Mexico. Cameron says a source named Bob Emenegger insisted it happened in May 1971. He says another man, Richard Doty, then told him no, it was 1964 at White Sands, a military testing area nearby, and that the visitors had got lost.
doty-shows-linda-moulton-howe-documents-: This story is about a moment in 1982 when a man named Rick Doty, a figure well known in UFO circles, contacted a UFO researcher named Linda Moulton Howe. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says Doty showed her documents, including one about something called Project Garnet. A writer and guest on the show, Greg Bishop, adds what he heard from Tom Adams, a researcher who studied mysterious deaths and mutilations of cattle. According to Adams, Howe visited him a couple of days afterward and was thrilled, "over the moon," about what she had seen. The story matters because, if the documents were real, they would have shown a researcher secret government papers about UFOs.
doubting-four-funds-including-renaissanc: Eric Weinstein, a researcher, says that in the early 2000s he did not believe the results of four investment operations: Bernie Madoff's, the firms Renaissance Technologies and D.E. Shaw, and Jeffrey Epstein's. He tells it on a podcast as an example of trusting his own doubts about how money is said to be made.
doug-alt-the-portal-is-real: A UFO researcher named Grant Cameron says on Jesse Michels's podcast that a man named Doug Alt brought up a question Cameron had asked him a couple of years earlier, about a portal. According to Cameron, Alt told him simply: "It's real." If true, it would mean someone Cameron trusted was confirming that some kind of doorway to elsewhere exists.
doug-and-bill-enter-the-craft-1948: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells of two men, Doug Noland and Bill Ferguson, who are said to have found a crashed flying saucer in Hart Canyon near Aztec, New Mexico, in March 1948. According to Doug, as Michels retells it, the two of them went inside the craft. If true, it would mean ordinary people stood inside an alien vehicle.
doug-noland-and-bill-ferguson-find-the-s: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells how in March 1948 two men, Doug Noland and Bill Ferguson, climbed to the rim of a mesa in Hart Canyon near Aztec, New Mexico. There, Michels says, they saw a flying saucer about 100 feet across. If true, it would be a crashed alien craft found by locals before anyone official arrived.
doug-sees-beings-through-the-punctured-p: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that at a crashed saucer near Aztec, New Mexico, in March 1948, a man named Doug Noland put his eye to a small hole punched through one of the craft's portholes. Through it, Michels says, Doug saw two small figures slumped over a control panel, and he stayed specific about that hole for the rest of his life. If true, it would be an eyewitness sighting of dead or injured alien crew.
doug-wolf-first-oga-director-with-nro-ca: An online researcher who goes by UAPGerb tells podcast host Jesse Michels about a man named Doug Wolf, who he says became director of a secretive government office known by the initials OGA around 2003, an office UAPGerb ties to the Pentagon's hidden UFO programme. UAPGerb says Wolf had spent 16 years at the NRO, the US agency that runs spy satellites, making him the first head of that office with such a background. If true, it would link the office's UFO work to satellite spying.
dousing-remote-viewing-target-sites-with: A YouTuber and magician named Chris Ramsay tells podcast host Jesse Michels about remote viewing, a US government programme from the 1970s to 1995 that tested whether people could describe faraway places using only their minds. Ramsay says the researchers used to douse the target sites with liquid nitrogen, an extremely cold liquefied gas, and that the viewers got more accurate results when they did. If true, it would hint that physical conditions at a site change how well the mind can reach it.
dr-brett-cohen-agrees-the-great-pyramid-: Geoffrey Drumm, who argues that the Great Pyramid of Giza in Egypt was built as a working chemical machine, says on Jesse Michels's podcast that a scientist, Dr. Brett Cohen, agrees with him on one key point. According to Drumm, Cohen also thinks the pyramid was producing sulfuric acid, though Cohen pictures a completely different mechanism and different stages of the reaction. If true, it would mean the pyramid was an industrial device rather than only a tomb.
dr-bug-we-can-t-take-your-soul: John Blitch, introduced on a podcast as a scientist who once worked for DARPA, the Pentagon's agency for advanced research projects, says he was taken by a non-human being. Blitch says that a being he calls "Dr Bug" told him, "we can't take your soul." He tells it as a glimpse of what such beings can and cannot do to a person.
dr-carvalho-s-35-colares-patients-interv: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that the UFO researcher Jacques Vallee spoke with a Dr. Carvalho in Colares, a town in Pará state in Brazil, around 1977. According to Michels, the doctor had seen 35 patients who all had the same sunburns and puncture wounds, and two women had died of a stroke. Michels cites Vallee's published journals, Forbidden Science, and tells it as part of Brazilian cases he says the country's defence minister confirmed as real.
dr-fernando-jane-saw-the-creature-s-foot: In 1996, people in the Brazilian town of Varginha told of a strange being that was reportedly captured and taken to hospitals. A witness, Jose Marcus Mora, says on Jesse Michels's podcast that a doctor named Fernando Jane told him he was at the town's regional hospital and saw the creature's foot. Mora says that was all the doctor could see, because a lot of military personnel were standing around it.
dr-g-as-a-consortium-of-anti-submarine-s: An online commentator who goes by UAPGerb talks about Behind the Flying Saucers, a 1950 book by the writer Frank Scully about a saucer said to have crashed near Aztec, New Mexico, whose main scientific source was called only "Dr. G". UAPGerb credits researchers Scott and Suzanne Ramsey with digging up a shortlist of eight or nine scientists, linked to anti-submarine work, who were likely all being represented by that one pseudonym. If true, it would mean Scully's mystery source was really a group of real government scientists.
dr-italo-venturelli-meets-live-being-in-: Italo Venturelli, a neurosurgeon at the regional hospital in the Brazilian town of Varginha, says that in January 1996 he came face to face with a living creature in the intensive care unit. He describes it as having a white face and red eyes, and says it showed no sign of suffering, while podcast host Jesse Michels, retelling it, says the meeting lasted about four minutes. If true, it would mean a living non-human being was held in a Brazilian hospital.
dr-iya-whitley-s-work-on-helping-infants: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, talks about a woman he calls Dr. Iya Whitley, a space psychologist, who he says is trying to train babies to keep their synesthesia, a blending of the senses such as seeing colours when hearing sounds. In a later episode he adds that the purpose is to help with communicating with aliens. If true, it would mean someone is preparing human minds for contact.
dr-iya-whitley-says-astronauts-see-thing: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says a woman named Dr. Iya Whitley told him that astronauts all see strange things while they are in space. If true, it would mean unexplained sightings are common among people who have left the Earth.
dr-jannini-s-lab-report-death-from-pulmo: A surgeon named Ahmed Foratu tells of events in 1996 in Varginha, a town in Brazil, where, according to him, a strange creature was taken to a hospital and later died. He says a doctor named Jannini, who ran a laboratory there, wrote a report stating that the creature died of a lung infection that spread into septicemia, an infection of the whole body. If true, it would mean doctors examined a living non-human being and left a written record of its death.
dr-marcos-vinicius-neves-operates-on-the: A documentary filmmaker named James Fox talks about events in January 1996 in Varginha, Brazil, where a strange living creature is said to have been captured and taken to the city's regional hospital. Fox says that, as he understands it from doctors including Italo Venturelli, a surgeon named Marcos Vinicius Neves operated on the being, which had swelling from a head injury, to relieve the pressure. If true, it would mean Brazilian doctors gave medical treatment to a live non-human creature.
dr-vinod-falls-into-a-trance-and-first-c: In 1952 a visitor known as Dr. Vinod came to the Round Table Foundation, a research group in Maine. A researcher, Greg Malatzi, says the story goes that on his very first night there, Vinod unexpectedly fell into a trance. According to the researchers, he then began channelling, meaning passing on messages said to come from another being, from a group called the Nine, which the podcast episode describes as an alien council. They point to tape recordings, session transcripts and the journals of Andrija Puharich, the man behind the foundation, as their sources. One telling speaks of the early channelling in 1952 in general rather than the first night. If true, it would mean humans made contact with non-human beings through a trance in the 1950s.
draft-notice-after-leaving-the-church-19: Peter Levenda, a writer on secret history, says that in the late 1960s in New York he left the church he had been part of because he no longer felt secure there. He says that as soon as he left, he got a notice from Selective Service, the US system that called young men into the military, saying he was being drafted.
draft-uk-us-extradition-treaty-written-i: Gary McKinnon, a British computer hacker who says he broke into US systems and found signs of a secret NASA space programme, faced a US effort to have him sent to America for trial. He also points to records from the General Accounting Office, a US government watchdog agency, as part of his case that the process was stacked against him.
dragon-feels-his-late-father-s-presence-: Brandon Fugal, the owner of Skinwalker Ranch, a property in Utah known for reports of strange happenings, says on Jesse Michels's podcast that a man called Bryant "Dragon" Arnold has had experiences there. According to Fugal, Arnold says he has felt the presence of his late father on the property. If true, it would add to the idea that the ranch touches on something beyond the physical.
dragon-wagon-used-to-haul-the-craft-away: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells of a craft said to have crashed in 1948 at Hart Canyon near Aztec, New Mexico, drawing on Behind the Flying Saucers, a book by the writer Frank Scully. In his telling, once a new road had been cut to the site, a heavy vehicle called a dragon wagon backed its way up to haul the craft away, a detail that, if true, would point to an organized military recovery.
dream-at-dionysiou-1800s-paris-brothel-t: A man named Ralph says that around 1991, while staying at Dionysiou, a monastery on Mount Athos in Greece, he had a vivid dream set in old Paris. In the dream he walked down the old streets and into a brothel just to see what was going on, and there he met a figure who turned out to be the Virgin Mary. He connects it to Harry Haller, the main character of the novel Steppenwolf, and tells it as a sign that dreams can reach beyond ordinary time and place.
dream-of-infiltrating-the-order-of-the-b: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, describes a dream told by Rolf Mowatt-Larssen, a former senior official at the CIA, the US spy agency. In the dream, Mowatt-Larssen infiltrates the Order of the Broken Cross, which Michels describes as an apocalyptic cult in Jerusalem. It comes up in an episode about Mowatt-Larssen saying he has experienced something like time travel.
dream-of-jesse-matching-the-nas-tweet-re: A man named Dylan Borland, speaking to the podcast host Jesse Michels, says that while asleep at his home on the US East Coast he dreamed of Michels coming to his house to get provolone cheese. Borland links the dream to a later reply to a social media post that seemed to match it, which, as he tells it, suggests the dream foretold something.
dream-of-sadat-s-assassination-as-it-hap: A former CIA officer named Rolf Mowatt-Larssen says that in 1981, while he was at Fort Bliss, an army base in Texas, he dreamed of the killing of Anwar Sadat, the president of Egypt, in Cairo, at the time it happened, and felt as if he was there. He says it was his first such dream and that he describes it in his book, A State of Mind: Faith in the CIA. If true, it would mean the mind can see distant events as they unfold.
dream-visit-from-a-great-uncle-at-the-mo: Jeffrey Mishlove, a researcher of psychic experience, says that in 1972 in Berkeley, California, his great-uncle came to him in a dream, something he calls a visitation. He says he later learned it happened at the very moment his great-uncle died, which, if true, would suggest the mind can reach across distance at death.
drew-s-privately-funded-vacuum-chambers: A man named Charles Buer says that his colleague Andrew Arjima, known as Drew, has paid for his own vacuum chamber, a sealed tank with the air pumped out that is used for testing equipment, and keeps one at his house. He mentions it on a podcast about claims of new propulsion technology, as a sign of how seriously Drew pursues his experiments on his own.
driving-past-bennewitz-s-thunder-corpora: A scientist named John Brandenburg says that in the 1980s he drove every morning to Sandia, a US government research laboratory in Albuquerque, New Mexico. He says his route took him right past the office of a man named Paul Bennewitz, whose company was called Thunder Corporation. He tells it as a small first-hand tie to a man who comes up in other UFO stories.
driving-past-epstein-s-victoria-s-secret: Bob Lazar, a man known for saying he worked on secret craft in Nevada, says that when he lived in New Mexico he used to drive past the ranch of financier Jeffrey Epstein all the time, a place he calls the 'Victoria's Secret Ranch'. He says he lived very close to it and found it really strange.
drone-flights-over-nevada-nuclear-testin: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in 2024 there were several mystery drone flights over the US nuclear testing range in Nevada, just north of Las Vegas. He tells it as part of a wider point that unknown objects seem to watch nuclear sites, which, if true, would mean someone is keeping an eye on the country's most sensitive weapons ground.
drone-only-tfr-set-up-over-picatinny-ars: Jake Barber, a helicopter pilot who says he once carried a UFO with his aircraft, says that in November 2024, about a month before Thanksgiving, a temporary flight restriction, a no-fly zone in the sky, was set up over Picatinny Arsenal, a US Army base in New Jersey. He says it applied only to drones, and he raises it as a telling detail about what was happening in the skies there.
drone-survey-shows-rust-like-lines-and-c: A treasure hunter named Dennis Asberg says that in 2025 his team sent an underwater drone down to the Baltic Sea anomaly, an oddly shaped object his team found on the seafloor between Sweden and Finland. Asberg says the footage showed strange lines, cracks and something that looked like rust, like metal. If true, it would hint that the object is made rather than natural.
drum-s-visit-to-the-giza-plateau-to-look: A researcher named Jeffrey Drum tells a podcast host, Jesse Michels, about a trip he says he made in the 2020s to the Giza Plateau in Egypt, where the great pyramids stand. He says he went to investigate the area around the Osiris Shaft, a deep shaft cut into the plateau. In the same interview he says he went right after a conference in Malta, as soon as they got back, and he credits someone named Alexa. He also says extra shafts were found near the causeway, the old raised road on the plateau. Drum is the only teller, describing it twice in one conversation, and it connects to his other claims about water from the shaft and the pyramid making sulfuric acid. He tells it because, as the episode puts it, it would point to a large energy system beneath the pyramids.
drumm-puts-his-head-in-the-magnetic-hole: Geoffrey Drumm, a man who says he has studied the true purpose of the pyramids, says that in the 2020s he visited the Oami Gaishi stone circle in Japan. There, he says, he put his head into a hole shaped exactly like a head, carved in a huge andesite stone that gives off a strong magnetic field. He tells it as a sign that ancient stones were built for a purpose beyond the obvious.
drumm-s-evaluation-of-the-biondi-team-s-: Geoffrey Drumm, a researcher who studies the pyramids, says on Jesse Michels' podcast that he has been weighing papers by a team led by Filippo Biondi about the pyramids on Egypt's Giza plateau, including a second paper on the Khafre pyramid and work shown at a conference in Malta. Drumm says that when he first looked at their original paper in 2020, he thought it was about a 50/50 chance they were right. He tells it to show how his view of the team's claims has developed since.
dsp-fast-walkers: A guest named Max, on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels about NASA and the Moon, points to what are called fast walkers: fast-moving unknown objects picked up by DSP, the US military's early-warning satellites that watch for missile launches. Max says these are probably what is being talked about, suggesting the satellites have caught unexplained things moving through space near Earth.
dsp-satellite-infrared-anomaly-during-th: A researcher on Jesse Michels' podcast in 2026 describes the 1976 Tehran incident, when, as the story goes, jets of the Shah's Iranian air force chased a UFO over the city. He says two aerospace researchers, Lee Graham and Ron Regehr, claimed to have looked at printouts from the Defense Support Program, US satellites that watch for heat from missile launches, and found something unusual in infrared at the very day and time of the chase; the filmmaker James Fox is also named. If true, a US satellite would have backed up what the pilots reported.
dtra-held-aec-records-saying-ufos-are-ex: An online UFO researcher known as UAPGerb told Jesse Michels in 2026 that a man named Dylan Borland had said on another podcast, Weaponized, that DTRA, a Pentagon agency that deals with weapons of mass destruction, held old records from the Atomic Energy Commission, the agency that once ran America's nuclear programme. According to Borland, those records concluded that UFOs are vehicles from beyond Earth. UAPGerb also suggests the records may tie to crash files from AFSWP, the military's early nuclear weapons office, and to Sandia, a nuclear weapons laboratory, which would mean the nuclear world reached that conclusion long ago.
dtra-official-collecting-documents-on-ex: An unnamed speaker says he once worked inside a secure room for classified work, called a SCIF, at the Defense Threat Reduction Agency, a US military agency that deals with weapons threats. He says the official in charge of gathering everything the agency had on extraterrestrials, "little green men" as the official put it, sat at his computer and pulled every related document from his system. If true, it would mean the government quietly collects such files.
duell-s-diary-records-meeting-the-presid: The MJ-12 documents are papers said to describe Majestic 12, a secret group of officials handling crashed saucers, including a briefing of President Eisenhower in the 1950s. Citing a researcher, Richard Dolan, he adds that the MJ-12 papers seem to know of meetings and diary entries no other source did, which would suggest they came from real insiders.
dugway-chief-scientist-reveals-a-huge-su: An online commentator who goes by UAPGerb says that the chief scientist at Dugway Proving Ground, a US Army testing range in the Utah desert, told a person known only as MS about a massive underground facility below the base, west of a mountain called Granite Peak. According to the story, its entrance is hidden inside an ordinary-looking shed. If true, it would mean a huge secret installation sits beneath one of America's most restricted military sites.
dugway-grey-beard-we-had-the-triangles-o: An online researcher who goes by UAPGerb, speaking on podcast host Jesse Michels's show, passes on something he says an old hand, a "grey beard", told him about Dugway Proving Ground, a military testing site in Utah, sometime between 2019 and 2022. According to UAPGerb, this man would casually say, "Oh, we had the triangles out again last night," which, if true, would mean triangle-shaped craft fly there often enough to be routine.
duke-researchers-brain-implants-let-para: Eric Haseltine, a former senior official at the National Security Agency, the US agency that intercepts communications, mentioned on Jesse Michels's podcast some work he had described in a talk at the Aspen Institute, a policy forum. He tells it as an example of how far the link between mind and machine has already gone.
dulce-base-shootout-in-lazar-s-briefing-: Grant Cameron, a UFO researcher, says on Jesse Michels's podcast that briefing papers Bob Lazar described seeing at S-4, a secret site he links to Area 51 in Nevada, told of a shootout in an underground base at Dulce, New Mexico. According to that account, 64 special forces soldiers were killed by the grays, gray-skinned beings, because the soldiers had brought weapons they were not allowed to carry. If true, it would mean humans and non-humans had shared a secret base, and that it ended in violence.
dulles-brothers-draft-the-versailles-war: Dan Sheehan, a researcher and lawyer, says on Jesse Michels's podcast that the brothers Allen and John Foster Dulles, then young lawyers at the New York law firm Sullivan and Cromwell, helped write the war reparations, the payments demanded from Germany, into the Treaty of Versailles that ended the First World War in 1918 and 1919. He ties this to their relatives Robert Lansing and John W. Foster, and he tells it to show how early the brothers were near the center of power.
dulles-greenlights-the-s-force-against-j: Dan Sheehan, a lawyer and activist, tells podcast host Jesse Michels that in 1963 Allen Dulles, the former head of the CIA, gave the go-ahead to a group Sheehan calls the S force, set against President John F. Kennedy. Sheehan also names Richard Bissell, another senior CIA man, in the story. If true, it would put former CIA leadership behind a move against the president, in an episode that links Kennedy to UFO secrets.
dulles-keeps-holding-court-in-his-george: Dan Sheehan, a lawyer and activist, tells podcast host Jesse Michels that Allen Dulles, the former CIA chief, never really left Washington after his time running the agency ended. Sheehan says that from 1961 to 1963 Dulles kept his whole operation going from his townhouse in Georgetown, a Washington neighbourhood, with CIA men Richard Bissell and counterintelligence chief James Jesus Angleton in his circle. If true, it would mean Dulles kept steering things from outside government during the Kennedy years.
dulles-reactivates-howard-hughes-s-s-for: Podcast host Jesse Michels repeats a story from researcher Dan Sheehan: in the 1960s President John F. Kennedy threatened to break up the CIA and fire its director, Allen Dulles. Michels says that Dulles then went to a private bank, Brown Brothers Harriman, and brought back the "S Force", a private group the businessman Howard Hughes had created, to go after Kennedy. In another telling Michels adds that the S Force started with Richard Nixon, then Vice President under Eisenhower and head of the 5412 committee, a panel that oversaw secret operations, working with Hughes on matters around Cuba.
dutch-museum-moon-rock-turned-out-to-be-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells of the Apollo goodwill tour, when American astronauts, including Neil Armstrong, the first man on the Moon, travelled abroad after the 1969 landing. He says a so-called moon rock passed through the American ambassador to a former prime minister of the Netherlands and later ended up in a Dutch museum, where, as the story goes, it turned out to be petrified wood, which Michels raises to question what the public has been shown about the Moon.
dylan-borland-nhi-involved-in-the-cover-: Podcast host Jesse Michels says he once asked a man named Dylan Borland whether a non-human intelligence, meaning some intelligent being that is not human, is itself involved in hiding the truth about UFOs. According to Michels, Borland answered yes, that he knew so for sure, which would mean the secrecy is not only a human project.
dylan-borland-s-triangle-over-langley: A man named Dylan Borland says that at Langley, near a NASA hangar, he saw a huge equilateral triangle one to two stories thick with sharp edges, a story he also told to Congress and that podcast host Jesse Michels dates to 2012. According to a researcher who goes by UAPGerb, Borland felt the air turn charged as the triangle took off above him, and filmmaker Jeremy Corbell retells it too. If true, it would mean an unknown craft hovered openly over a US government site.
dylan-borland-the-energy-system-is-the-m: An online researcher who goes by UAPGerb says on Jesse Michels's podcast that a man named Dylan Borland told him the most classified, most sensitive secret is not the craft themselves but the energy system that powers them. If true, it would mean the real prize being guarded is a new source of power.
dyson-s-cross-country-drive-with-feynman: The scientist Freeman Dyson recalled that in the late 1940s a colleague, Richard Feynman, was driving from Cleveland to Albuquerque, New Mexico. e-howard-hunt-links-jfk-s-death-to-ufo-i: Podcast host Jesse Michels has told several times how E. Howard Hunt, a former CIA operative who claimed a role in events around President Kennedy's 1963 killing, linked that killing to UFOs.
