If true, it would mean a president died partly over questions about UFOs.
e-howard-hunt-s-everglades-group-burned-: Dan Sheehan, a lawyer and activist, tells podcast host Jesse Michels about a second group hiding out in the Florida Everglades in 1963, run through E. Howard Hunt, a CIA officer. Sheehan says US marshals, under Attorney General Robert Kennedy, burned that camp out. He tells it as part of a story of CIA-linked groups clashing with the Kennedy brothers.
e-howard-hunt-s-occult-novels-attacking-: Peter Levenda, a writer on secret history, says on Jesse Michels's podcast that E. Howard Hunt, a former CIA officer who also wrote novels, published occult-themed books in the 1960s and 70s, one set on a "Witches Island". Levenda says that, read closely, they are a thinly veiled attack on the Kennedy family, painting them as Satan worshippers.
e-t-whittaker-s-1904-1905-papers-showing: Salvatore Pais, a Navy scientist who holds patents for unusual craft designs, says on Jesse Michels's podcast that a British mathematician named E.T. Whittaker wrote two key papers in 1904 and 1905. According to Pais, those papers showed that "scalar waves" are possible, meaning waves unlike ordinary radio waves. If true, it would give an old mathematical basis for exotic kinds of energy and propulsion.
eagle-lake-sphere-answers-sos-and-chases: Charlie Foltz says that in 1976, while camping on Eagle Lake in Maine's Allagash Waterway with Jim Weiner, Jack Weiner and Chuck Rak, he saw a small white circle he first took for the moon, until it started moving. As the story goes, the glowing sphere answered their SOS signal and chased their canoe, and Jim Weiner adds that he remembers nothing from the moment it was right behind them until they reached the shore of their campsite. If true, it would point to missing time and possibly an abduction.
ear-sensation-logged-on-blog-before-the-: Dan Sherman, a former Air Force sergeant who says the NSA, the US spy agency that intercepts communications, hired him to communicate with aliens, says he would feel a sensation in his ear when a message was coming. He says that around September 2003 he logged one such sensation on his blog, and connects it to a later disaster, the great Indian Ocean earthquake that struck Indonesia, with Japan also part of his account. He wrote about it in a 2006 update to his book Above Black, telling it as a sign the contact was real and could warn of things ahead.
earl-of-elgin-confirms-james-bruce-was-a: A writer on ancient mysteries, Graham Hancock, says that around 1990 he visited the Earl of Elgin, a Scottish nobleman, at his Broomhall estate in Scotland, while researching his book The Sign and the Seal. He says he asked whether a Scottish traveller named James Bruce had been a Freemason, a member of an old secretive brotherhood, and the Earl answered, "dear boy, of course he was," and named the Edinburgh lodge, or local chapter, Canongate Kilwinning Lodge No. 2, where Bruce had belonged. Hancock tells it because it supported the link he was tracing between Bruce and the Freemasons.
earlier-undisclosed-events-before-wwii-1: David Grusch, a former US intelligence officer who has gone public as a whistleblower about UFOs, told Jesse Michels's podcast that there are other events he cannot talk about that happened well before the cases he was discussing, before about 1944. If true, it would mean contact with non-human craft goes back earlier than the Second World War era.
earlier-weatherman-burned-by-tall-white-: A former Air Force weather observer named Charles Hall, who says he spent years in contact with tall, pale beings he calls the Tall Whites in the Nevada desert, tells of a weatherman who worked there before him, sometime before 1965. According to Hall, that man was at Range Four, a military range in Indian Springs Valley, when his shoulder almost touched one of the beings' suits, and he was burned. Hall says he saw the man's x-rays and pictures at the hospital at Nellis, a nearby Air Force base, which, if true, would be physical proof of the contact.
earliest-skinwalker-ufo-images-kept-with: Brandon Fugal, the owner of Skinwalker Ranch, a Utah property known for reports of strange events, says that since he took over in 2016 his team has photographed UFOs above it. He says that even for the earliest of these images he still has the metadata, the hidden data that records when and how a photo was taken, which he offers as a way to show they are genuine.
early-1960s-uap-event-filmed-at-a-milita: Eric Davis, a physicist who has advised government studies of UFOs, says on Jesse Michels's podcast that an event involving an unexplained flying object in the early 1960s was recorded on film at a US military base. He brings up George H.W. Bush, later president, in connection with it, and tells it as proof that such evidence exists.
early-christian-libraries-discovered-in-: Diana Pasulka, a professor who studies religion and UFO beliefs, said on Jesse Michels' podcast in 2024 that in the 1940s libraries of early Christian writings were found. She says they showed what shaped those early Christians, including Plato's allegory of the cave from his book The Republic, the story of prisoners who mistake shadows on a wall for reality. She brings it up as a way to think about how people make sense of strange visitors and hidden realities.
early-fbi-cia-army-documents-on-ufos-nea: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says there are thousands of government documents from roughly 1945 to 1953 that describe UFOs turning up in America's most sensitive airspace, especially around nuclear sites. He says they come from the FBI (the federal police), the CIA (the foreign spy agency), the Army and its counter-intelligence corps. He also points to a government effort of that time called Project Twinkle, and he raises all this as proof that officials took the sightings seriously from the very start.
early-shuttle-crews-borrowed-yellow-u-2-: Greg Rogers, a doctor who worked with NASA, says on Jesse Michels's podcast that the first space shuttle crews, around 1981, including astronauts Young and Crippen, did not have their own pressure suits. According to him, they had to go to Beale Air Force Base and borrow the yellow suits worn by pilots of the U-2 and SR-71, two high-altitude spy planes. He tells it as a glimpse of how closely the space programme leaned on secret military aviation.
earning-the-trust-of-the-space-kids: Greg Malatzi, a researcher and filmmaker, says it took him about two years to earn the trust of a group of people he calls the space kids before they would speak with him on camera. He tells it to explain how hard it was to get their stories for his film interviews.
earth-s-rarity-and-galactic-pyramids: Steve Coburn, a man who says he has had contact with non-human beings, says that "they" told him there are pyramids all over the galaxy. According to Coburn, these pyramids are power sources and places of healing rather than tombs, and that Earth is rare among worlds, which, if true, would reframe what pyramids on Earth were for.
eben-alexander-near-death-experience-200: David Grusch, a former US intelligence officer turned whistleblower about UFOs, told Jesse Michels in 2023 about Eben Alexander, who wrote a book called Proof of Heaven about his near-death experience in 2008. Grusch says Alexander has a very scientific way of looking at it and describes what he met as an overarching, loving energy. Grusch raises it because, if true, consciousness might carry on beyond the body.
ebner-effect-high-voltage-on-crops-1990: An engineer named Dave Rossi tells podcast host Jesse Michels about something he calls the Ebner effect, which he believes dates from the 1990s in Europe. As he describes it, it involved putting high voltage on crops and seeing what happened to them. He brings it up as an example of electricity shaping living things in ways that ordinary science has overlooked.
echo-flight-incident-1967: Echo Flight was a group of ten nuclear missiles at Malmstrom, a US Air Force base in Montana. A former Air Force officer named Robert Salas says that around March 16, 1967, the officer in charge there, Walt Feele, was told of something strange, could not believe it at first, and then all ten of his missiles shut down. The podcast host, Jesse Michels, places this eight days before a similar event Salas says he lived through himself, and links it to later cases at the same base. If true, it would mean something unknown could switch off American nuclear weapons.
echo-flight-incident-and-the-boeing-sac-: In 1967, at Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana, a group of nuclear missiles known as Echo Flight went out of action, and some people tell this as a UFO event. A former Air Force officer, Robert Salas, appeared on a show whose title says a UFO shut down ten nuclear missiles. He says that Boeing, the company that built the missiles, ran a bench test on a part called a logic coupler to work out what happened. He credits a researcher, James Klotz, as a source for this. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells it his own way. He says a report by Boeing and Strategic Air Command, the Air Force branch that ran the nuclear bombers and missiles, tried to recreate the effect. Michels says this report is why he thinks the incident really was UFO related. If the tellers are right, a company and the military tried to explain the shutdown and could not find an ordinary cause.
ed-gets-cold-feet-before-ssci-testimony-: An online UFO researcher who goes by UAPGerb tells podcast host Jesse Michels about a witness known only as Ed. He says that Steven Greer, a well-known UFO disclosure campaigner, was going to bring Ed to Washington around 2023 to testify before the Senate Select Committee on Intelligence, the Senate panel that oversees US spy agencies. According to UAPGerb, Ed got cold feet right before and backed out, so whatever he might have revealed never reached Congress.
ed-may-leads-stargate-research-in-its-fi: A writer named Eric Wargo tells podcast host Jesse Michels about Stargate, a secret US government programme that studied psychic abilities like seeing distant places with the mind. Wargo says a scientist named Ed May took over the research side of the programme from physicist Hal Puthoff and led it through its final decade, from about 1985 until it was made public and supposedly ended in 1995. The word "supposedly" hints that it may have carried on in some form.
ed-may-s-decision-augmentation-theory: A writer named Eric Wargo tells podcast host Jesse Michels about an idea from Ed May, a scientist who studied psychic abilities, called decision augmentation theory. As Wargo explains it, the researchers' own ability to sense the future, called precognition, may be what nudges them to start an experiment at just the right moment. If true, it would mean some surprising lab results come from good timing guided by a glimpse of the future.
ed-may-worked-with-prince-hans-adam: The podcast host Jesse Michels says that Ed May, a scientist tied to Stargate, a US government programme that studied psychic spying, talks about having worked with Hans-Adam, the reigning prince of Liechtenstein. Michels raises it because it would link that psychic research to a European royal.
eddington-s-eclipse-confirms-general-rel: A former NASA doctor named Greg Rogers tells podcast host Jesse Michels about 1919, when the British astronomer Arthur Eddington watched a solar eclipse and measured how light from a star bent as it passed the sun. Rogers says this confirmed Albert Einstein's theory of general relativity, the idea that gravity curves space, and he finds it striking that it took a man from Germany's wartime enemy to prove the German-born scientist right.
edgar-cayce-foundation-funded-zahi-hawas: A podcaster named Jay Anderson, speaking with Jesse Michels and comedian Kurt Metzger, says that the Edgar Cayce Foundation, a group built on the readings of a famous American psychic, paid for the work of Zahi Hawass, Egypt's best-known archaeologist and longtime head of its antiquities. He places this roughly in the 1980s into the early 1990s. If true, it would tie mainstream Egyptian archaeology to a group with mystical beliefs about ancient Egypt.
edgar-fouche-s-1998-tr-3b-testimony-proj: An online researcher who goes by UAPGerb points out on Jesse Michels's podcast that Edgar Fouche, a man who in 1998 gave testimony about the TR-3B, said to be a secret triangular aircraft, also said many projects were moved to Dugway Proving Ground, a military testing site in Utah. UAPGerb finds this a strange match with what he has heard about Dugway himself.
edgar-fouche-s-defense-advanced-research: An online researcher who goes by UAPGerb (UAP stands for unidentified anomalous phenomena, the official term for UFOs) says on Jesse Michels's podcast that a man named Edgar Fouché claimed S4, a secret site in Nevada, ran something called the Defense Advanced Research Center. UAPGerb says a document from ARPA, a Pentagon research agency, was found showing that such a centre had been proposed in the 1970s. If true, it would back up claims that a hidden research site really existed there.
edgar-fouche-the-tr3b-timeline-from-prot: An online UFO researcher known as UAPGerb told Jesse Michels in 2026 about Edgar Fouche, a man who said he worked on secret aircraft projects and spoke at a UFO conference in 1998. According to Fouche, the TR3B, a secret triangle-shaped American aircraft, was flown as prototypes from the 1970s at test sites such as the Navy's Patuxent River station and Edwards Air Force Base, and working models started flying in the 1990s. If true, some sightings of strange craft could have been secret US aircraft.
edgar-mitchell-founds-the-institute-of-n: A biologist named Rupert Sheldrake tells podcast host Jesse Michels that Edgar Mitchell, an astronaut who went to the moon, founded the Institute of Noetic Sciences in the United States, a group that studies consciousness and the mind. Sheldrake says he is himself a fellow of the institute, so he speaks of it from the inside.
edgar-mitchell-heard-about-roswell-1947: Roswell is a town in New Mexico where, in 1947, many people say a craft crashed and was taken away by the military. Edgar Mitchell was an Apollo astronaut, one of the men who went to the Moon. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that because of who he was, Mitchell heard all sorts of things about Roswell from people at every level. A guest named Maaneli Derakhshani puts it more directly: Mitchell said clearly that he believed an alien spacecraft had crashed at Roswell and the government had recovered it. If true, it would mean a respected astronaut had inside word of a recovered alien craft.
edgar-mitchell-on-the-moon-landing-image: James Fox, a documentary filmmaker, says on Jesse Michels's podcast that he once asked astronaut Edgar Mitchell, who walked on the Moon on the Apollo 14 mission in 1971, about the photographs from the landings. According to Fox, Mitchell said, "James, it wouldn't surprise me," and explained they worked with Hasselblad cameras that had no viewfinders while wearing bulky gloves, which suggests the pictures may not all be what they seem.
edgar-mitchell-s-apollo-14-esp-experimen: A Swedish UFO researcher named Clas Svahn tells podcast host Jesse Michels about astronaut Edgar Mitchell on the Apollo 14 moon mission in 1971. Svahn says Mitchell ran an experiment in ESP, short for extrasensory perception, meaning reading minds or sensing things without the usual senses, together with a Swedish man. He links this to the society Mitchell later started to study the mind, and if it worked, it would mean thoughts can reach across space.
edgar-mitchell-s-conversion-experience-o: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Edgar Mitchell, an astronaut on Apollo 14, the 1971 NASA mission to the Moon, had a conversion experience on the flight back to Earth. In one telling Michels calls it a telepathic, almost psychic experience that Mitchell spoke about openly and that changed his whole view of the world, which, if true, would mean a trained astronaut came home from the Moon convinced the mind reaches beyond the body.
edgar-mitchell-s-esp-experiment-on-apoll: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Edgar Mitchell, an astronaut on Apollo 14, the 1971 NASA mission to the Moon, ran a private ESP experiment on the way there, ESP meaning extrasensory perception, or sensing things with the mind alone. According to Michels, Mitchell tried to send mental images of a set of cards back to Earth, and he cites a 1971 New York Times interview, telling it as part of a story about NASA's interest in unusual science.
edgar-mitchell-s-last-filmed-interview-a: On a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, a man named Jeremy Corbell recalls filming what he describes as the last interview with Edgar Mitchell, a former astronaut, at Mitchell's home around 2015 or 2016. Corbell says that when they got down to brass tacks, Mitchell told him that a secret group was keeping information about UFOs (unidentified flying objects) from the public, and even told him who he had talked with. If true, it would mean a man who had flown in space believed such knowledge was being hidden on purpose.
edgar-mitchell-s-psi-experiments-on-the-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that many astronauts practised remote viewing, the idea of seeing distant places or things with the mind alone. He says Edgar Mitchell, an astronaut on the Apollo 14 moon mission in 1971, is especially known for doing mind experiments of this kind while up on the moon. If true, it would mean the space programme brushed up against the study of psychic powers.
edgar-mitchell-s-ufo-squadron-over-germa: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, passes on a story from Edgar Mitchell, whom he calls a naval astronaut. Michels says Mitchell described seeing a squadron of UFOs (unidentified flying objects) over several days during a training flight above Germany, flying in all sorts of formations, and filming them. According to Michels, as soon as Mitchell landed back in Washington a military plane landed too, the footage was taken, and nothing was heard of it again, which, if true, would mean the military quietly collected the evidence.
edgar-mitchell-said-no-astronaut-ever-sa: A Swedish UFO researcher named Clas Svahn says on Jesse Michels's podcast that the astronaut Edgar Mitchell was very firm on one point. According to Svahn, Mitchell insisted that no astronaut had ever seen a UFO in space, even though he was interested in the subject.
edgar-mitchell-speaks-out-on-ufos-1971: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, points to Edgar Mitchell, an astronaut on Apollo 14, the 1971 NASA mission to the Moon, as someone who ended up speaking out on UFOs in the years that followed. Michels offers him as an example of a credible insider who went public, which, if his claims hold, would lend weight to the subject.
edison-s-device-to-communicate-with-the-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Thomas Edison, the famous American inventor, tried near the end of his life in the 1920s to build a machine for talking with the dead. Michels tells it to show that serious inventors were drawn to the idea of reaching other realms through technology.
editor-asks-avi-loeb-to-cut-alien-paragr: A researcher named Michael Shermer, speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast, passes on something another researcher, Avi Loeb, said on a Zoom call. Loeb had written a paper in 2025 about 3I/ATLAS, an object passing through from outside our solar system, and according to Shermer the journal editor told him it was a great paper but he had to take out the final paragraph, the one raising the idea of aliens. Told this way, it shows how hard it can be to get the alien question into a science journal.
editor-s-computer-hit-by-the-same-electr: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in 2022, while his editor was putting together their video about Skinwalker Ranch, a Utah property known for strange reports, the editor's computer started acting up. Michels says the screen froze, which it never did, and went full of static, the same kind of electrical trouble that visitors to the ranch describe. If true, it would suggest the ranch's effects could follow people home, even through their footage.
edward-condon-atomic-insider-turned-ufo-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells of Edward Condon, a physicist who he says was close to the early atomic bomb work at Los Alamos, the lab where the first bomb was built, and who then lost his security clearance. Michels says Condon then suddenly reappeared in 1966 with his clearance mysteriously restored and was put on a panel that dealt a death blow to UFO research by calling it a waste of time and money. He tells it to suggest that the man chosen to dismiss UFOs was a trusted insider.
edward-teller-and-project-sundial-gigato: A Navy scientist named Salvatore Pais, talking on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, brings up Edward Teller, a physicist he describes as the man behind a famous bomb design he calls the "Teller-Ulam device." Pais says Teller was also behind something called Project Sundial, which this story describes as a plan for a bomb of enormous, gigaton size in the 1950s or 60s. He stresses that it is unclassified, which matters to him because it would show how far American weapons thinking went in those years.
edward-teller-on-the-ufo-legacy-program: A man called Max, speaking as a witness on Jesse Michels's podcast, says he vaguely remembers people suggesting that the physicist Edward Teller might have been involved in a so-called legacy program, meaning a hidden, long-running government effort said to study UFO material. Max says that if such a program exists, Teller would be one of the scientists in it, which would put a famous name at the heart of the secret.
edwin-may-s-scientific-oversight-committ: A researcher named Chris Ramsay, a guest on Jesse Michels' podcast, talks about Stargate, a US government programme from the 1970s to 1995 that tried to use "remote viewing," the idea that a person can sense faraway places with the mind alone. Ramsay says Edwin May, the programme's chief research physicist, had to put together a scientific oversight committee to check the work, and he names figures such as Daryl Bem, Schwartz and Zimbardo in connection with it. For Ramsay, this would mean the programme was held to outside scientific scrutiny.
eeg-neurofeedback-chair-sessions-targeti: Jordan Jose, who says he was taken into a secret UFO program as a child, says that around 2008 to 2010 he had sessions at Baker Victory Services in Western New York in what he calls "the chair." These were EEG neurofeedback sessions, where sensors read the brain's electrical waves, here aimed at the kinds called theta and gamma. Jose says this is where many of his traumatic memories came back to him.
eeg-shuts-down-inside-homestead-2-2020: Skinwalker Ranch is a property in Utah where people report strange events, and Homestead 2 is a building on it. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, recalls to the ranch's owner that when someone walked into Homestead 2 wearing an EEG, a device that records the brain's electrical activity, it shut down, then came back online once he walked out. Michels calls it super strange, since it would suggest something in that spot interferes with equipment.
effort-to-account-for-soviet-nukes-after: Rolf Mowatt-Larssen, a former CIA officer, says he took part in a push in Moscow between about 1991 and 1993, just after the Soviet Union fell apart. He tells podcast host Jesse Michels that the US government worked with the Russians in what he calls a heroic effort to account for every Soviet nuclear weapon. He tells it as a time when the world's loose nuclear weapons had to be tracked down and secured.
efim-liberman-s-research-on-cytoskeletal: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, speaking with the writer Eric Wargo, passes on a story about a Soviet scientist named Efim Liberman, the father of two of Michels's friends, Daniil and David Liberman. According to Michels, in roughly the 1970s and 80s Liberman was very interested in "cytoskeletal learning", the idea that learning happens inside the tiny scaffolding within each cell, the cytoskeleton, and he knew or was linked to the researchers Roger Penrose and Stuart Hameroff, who later took up related ideas. If true, it would mean the brain's thinking runs on something deeper than the connections between nerve cells.
eg-g-as-aec-doe-prime-contractor-running: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that a company called EG&G became the main contractor for the Atomic Energy Commission, the US agency that ran nuclear weapons work, starting around the 1950s at the Nevada Test Site, where the US tested nuclear bombs. He says it later played the same role for the Department of Energy, the agency that took over that work. Michels tells it to show how one private company sat at the centre of America's most secret sites.
eg-g-as-gatekeeper-of-area-51-1960: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in the early 1960s a special projects division of the company EG&G, based in Las Vegas, was trusted to run much of Area 51, a highly secret government base at Groom Lake in Nevada. According to Michels, it handled screening of staff, who got in, transport and daily operations. If true, it would make this company the gatekeeper of a place long linked to stories of hidden alien craft.
eg-g-engineer-s-account-of-an-egg-shaped: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that a senior engineer at EG&G, a US defense contractor, described to Michels's great uncle a craft shaped like an egg and about the size of an SUV, a large family car. As the story is titled, the craft could not be opened, which, if true, would mean a contractor held an unknown object it could not get inside.
eg-g-interview-switched-mid-way-to-the-s: Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked on secret craft in Nevada, says that in 1988 he went for a job interview at EG&G, a government contractor in Las Vegas. He says that partway through, the interviewers told him they actually had a different job in mind for him, which led him to a secret work site he calls S-4, the place where, if his story is true, he saw hidden technology.
egg-landing-in-a-brazilian-town-moment-o: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, describes a case from a film called Moment of Contact, made with James Fox. According to Michels, everyone in a small town in Brazil reported seeing an egg-shaped object land, and it seemed to give off something like ammonia. He adds that it even seemed to kill a doctor, which would make it a contact event with deadly results.
egg-shaped-object-descends-in-the-kilo-a: Mario Woods, an Air Force veteran, says that around 1978 he was posted in a stretch of nuclear missile sites run from Ellsworth Air Force Base in South Dakota, near a site called Kilo 10. He tells podcast host Jesse Michels that the only other strange thing he saw there was an object shaped like an egg that dropped straight down to the ground. He mentions a fellow veteran, Mark Wade, as part of the story, which he tells as one more sign of unknown craft around nuclear weapons.
egg-shaped-tall-white-craft-using-dog-bo: Charles Hall, a man who says he served at Air Force ranges in Nevada in the mid 1960s, says he spent about three years around tall, pale beings he calls the Tall Whites. He tells podcast host Jesse Michels that these beings had a base at the north end of Indian Springs Valley and flew egg-shaped craft that used a dry lakebed called Dog Bone Lake as their landing field. If true, it would mean beings from elsewhere were keeping a base on US military land.
egg-video-as-helicopter-sling-load-2025: Mick West, a well-known UFO skeptic, debates a guest named Merrick on Jesse Michels' podcast about a 2025 video of an egg-shaped object, tied to claims by a man named Jake Barber and the journalist Ross Coulthart. West says he thinks the object is probably larger than it looks and may be a load hanging beneath a helicopter while being moved. If so, the video would show ordinary cargo rather than a strange craft.
eglin-afb-diamond-formation-of-orbs-gaet: David Grusch, who speaks as a witness, says on Jesse Michels's podcast in 2023 that Matt Gaetz, a member of the US Congress, was turned away when he asked to speak with an aircrew at Eglin Air Force Base in Florida. According to Grusch, that crew had seen a diamond-shaped formation of glowing orbs. If true, it would mean even an elected lawmaker was blocked from hearing first-hand about such sightings.
egyptian-authorities-board-up-the-paw-an: A researcher named Matt LaCroix, speaking on Jesse Michels' podcast, says that in the 1990s, after people had been digging around beneath the Sphinx in Giza, Egypt, Egyptian authorities came and boarded up the front of one of its paws with literal wooden boards, blocking it off. The story as told also says misleading holes were drilled there. If true, it would suggest the authorities were hiding something under the Sphinx.
egyptian-decoration-at-the-mount-wilson-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says the lodges where astronomers stayed at Mount Wilson Observatory, a telescope site above Pasadena, California, linked to the astronomer George Ellery Hale, were reportedly decorated with Egyptian hieroglyphs and symbols. He brings it up as a sign that early modern science had ties to ancient mystical traditions.
egyptian-government-pumps-water-out-from: A researcher named Jeffrey Drum, on Jesse Michels' podcast, says the Egyptian government has installed pumps near the Khafre Valley Temple, an ancient stone temple next to the walled area around the Sphinx. According to Drum, the pumps are there to draw water out from below the Giza Plateau, the stretch of high ground where the pyramids stand. He brings it up as a sign that there is water, and maybe more, hidden under the site.
egyptian-priests-levitating-blocks-with-: Graham Hancock, a writer known for arguing that a lost ancient civilisation once existed, says on Jesse Michels' podcast that there are ancient Egyptian traditions describing priests who made large stone blocks float in the air. He says these stories have the lifting happen along with sound. If true, it would mean the builders of monuments like the Great Pyramid had a way of moving stone that we no longer know about.
egyptian-symbols-in-a-freemasonic-temple: A podcast host named Jesse Michels says he has been inside a temple of the Freemasons, an old society that meets in private lodges, in Washington DC. He describes it as full of Egyptian symbols, and he brings it up as a hint that ancient ideas still run quietly through the places where power sits.
eiffel-tower-pollution-prank-on-a-fellow: Lyn Buchanan, an Army sergeant who served in the 1980s in a military remote viewing unit, a team that tried to describe distant targets using only the mind, says he once played a prank on a fellow viewer. He says he told the man, "By the way, your target today is probably not the Eiffel Tower," planting an image in his head to spoil, or 'pollute', his session.
eight-hour-read-ons-with-15-minutes-to-s: Dylan Borland, a former intelligence worker who says he worked through the defence company BAE Systems between about 2015 and 2018, describes being briefed into secret programmes, a step insiders call a read-on. He tells podcast host Jesse Michels that his first read-ons lasted about eight hours, with a thick stack of paper covered in sticky notes, and that he was then given only about fifteen minutes to sign. He tells it to show how heavily guarded and rushed the access to these secrets was.
eight-sided-great-pyramid-and-the-templa: A man named Jay Anderson, a guest on Jesse Michels' podcast, says the flag of the Knights Templar, a medieval order of Christian knights, is really an eight-sided pyramid drawn flat. Take that flag and make it three-dimensional, he says, and you get the Great Pyramid of Giza, which he describes as having eight sides. He credits the idea to other researchers, Dark Journalist and Joseph P. Farrell, and tells it to suggest the Templars were linked to the secrets of ancient Egypt.
einstein-letter-to-fdr-leads-to-the-manh: Robert Salas, a former US Air Force officer, tells podcast host Jesse Michels that Albert Einstein and another man whose name Salas could not recall wrote to President Franklin D. Roosevelt warning that Germany might build an atomic bomb. Salas says this led to the Manhattan Project, the American wartime effort from 1939 to 1945 to build the bomb first. He gives it as background to the nuclear history behind his own story.
einstein-oppenheimer-letter-1940: A UFO researcher and historian named Richard Dolan, on Jesse Michels's podcast, mentions a letter said to be from the physicist Albert Einstein to Robert Oppenheimer, the scientist who led the US atomic bomb project, dating from around the 1940s. Dolan calls it "supposedly" from Einstein and "a very interesting document", without saying more about what it contains. He raises it as one of several papers that, if real, would suggest top American scientists of that era knew something about the phenomenon.
einstein-s-1923-paper-saying-general-rel: This story is about the ether, an old idea of an invisible substance filling all of space, which most physicists dropped in the early 1900s. A podcast host named Jesse Michels says that in 1923 Albert Einstein wrote a paper saying his theory of gravity, general relativity, actually fits with the ether. People raise it because, if true, it would mean the idea of a space-filling medium was never fully ruled out, which matters for some theories about unusual propulsion. A second teller, Salvatore Pais, a Navy scientist who holds patents on unusual craft, tells it on the same show. He also says Einstein was against the idea for a long time and yet brought it back in a paper. Pais dates that paper to 1921, not 1923. So the story comes from the host's own framing and from a scientist guest, and they disagree on the year.
einstein-s-cosmological-constant-and-cos: Avi Loeb, a Harvard astrophysicist, tells podcast host Jesse Michels about the cosmological constant, a term Albert Einstein added to his gravity equations in 1917 that works like a kind of cosmic antigravity. Loeb says Einstein liked the idea of a universe that never expanded, because then nobody has to imagine what came before the beginning.
einstein-s-deathbed-breakthrough-1955: A physicist named John Brandenburg, on Jesse Michels's podcast, passes on a saying about Albert Einstein's death in Princeton, New Jersey, in 1955. According to the saying, on his deathbed Einstein suddenly became ecstatic and started talking excitedly to his nurse in German. Brandenburg tells it as a hint that Einstein may have reached some last breakthrough that was never recorded, since the nurse could not understand him.
eisenhower-aware-of-foo-fighters-1942: A guest named Merrick, debating the skeptic Mick West on Jesse Michels' podcast, says that Dwight Eisenhower, the top Allied general in the Second World War and later president, knew about foo fighters, the odd glowing lights that wartime aircrews reported, from 1942 to 1945. If true, it would mean the highest military leaders knew of unexplained objects as far back as the war.
eisenhower-era-peads-used-to-create-waiv: A podcast host named Jack, speaking on Jesse Michels's show in an episode with a guest called Eric Davis, says that in the 1950s, under President Eisenhower, a type of secret order was put to an unusual use. These were Presidential Emergency Action Documents, orders written in advance for a president to use in a national emergency. According to Jack, they were used to set up "waived special access programs", top-secret projects excused from the usual reporting to Congress, which would mean some secret work could run with no lawmakers watching.
eisenhower-era-presidential-emergency-ac: Eric Davis, a physicist who has worked on Pentagon studies of UFOs, told Jesse Michels in 2026 that the presidential emergency action directives, secret orders for what the White House does in a crisis, were started under President Eisenhower in the 1950s. Davis says these rules are very strict and have been carried forward on many topics, and that he and Jim Semivan, a former CIA officer, know they were set up for UFOs too. If true, UFO secrecy would sit inside some of the government's most guarded orders.
eisenhower-s-1954-treaty-with-the-greys: This story claims that US President Dwight Eisenhower made a secret deal in 1954 with the greys, small grey aliens. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, describes the idea as a treaty letting the greys collect biological samples and run medical experiments on people, and in another episode calls it the Greada treaty, saying Eisenhower used a dentist visit in Palm Springs as cover and went instead to Edwards Air Force Base. A philosopher named Jason Jorjani tells it as Eisenhower meeting tall human-looking aliens called the Nordics first, then the greys, who offered a better deal. A writer billed as a CIA historian, Peter Levenda, mentions it only loosely, as 'Eisenhower or somebody' signing a contract with aliens in the 1950s. If true, it would mean the US government made a pact with aliens at the expense of its own people.
eisenhower-s-farewell-warning-about-the-: A researcher named Steven Greer, on Jesse Michels's podcast, points to the speech President Dwight Eisenhower gave in January 1961 as he left office and John F. Kennedy came in, when he told Americans to "beware of the military-industrial complex", meaning the powerful alliance of the armed forces and the companies that supply them. Greer says the secret control of UFO knowledge he describes is exactly what Eisenhower was warning about.
eisenhower-s-granddaughter-is-an-abducte: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Laura Eisenhower, a granddaughter of former US president Dwight Eisenhower, says she has been taken by aliens and is deeply involved in the subject. He mentions it in passing as a sign that the story reaches even into families close to the top of American power.
eisenhower-s-meeting-with-ets-about-stop: A researcher named Steven Greer says on Jesse Michels's podcast that he received a series of reports from the French Ministry of Defense showing that President Dwight Eisenhower really did meet extraterrestrials sometime around 1954 to 1956, with Palm Springs, California named as the place. Greer says the meeting was about stopping the spread of nuclear weapons, not the popular legend of a treaty with grey aliens, and he names Allen Dulles and Paul Melon among those connected to it. If true, it would mean a US president met beings from elsewhere and kept it quiet.
eisenhower-shown-five-spacecraft-at-edwa: This story claims that Dwight Eisenhower, US president in the 1950s, was secretly shown alien spacecraft. A man named Charles Hall, who says he spent three years with tall white aliens at Area 51, a secret US military site, passes on what he heard. According to Hall, on a day Eisenhower was said to be golfing in Palm Springs, he was taken instead to Edwards Air Force Base in California. There were no cameras and no press, Hall says, and five extraterrestrial spacecraft were sitting on the runway for the president to see. Some versions place it at Alamogordo in New Mexico instead. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells it differently: he gives the year as 1954, says the cover story was a dentist appointment, not golf, and describes it as a meeting without mentioning five craft. If true, it would mean a US president personally met with, or saw, visitors from elsewhere.
elderly-widow-sees-a-ball-of-light-at-he: Chris Bledsoe, a man who says strange lights and UFOs tend to appear around him, tells on Jesse Michels's podcast what an elderly widow told him. According to Bledsoe, she said she saw a ball of light go past her kitchen window. He tells it as one more sign that these lights show up to ordinary people near him, though no time or place is given.
eleanor-roosevelt-letter-to-oppenheimer-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in the late 1940s and 1950s rumours of UFOs at Los Alamos, the New Mexico lab where the atomic bomb was built, and at other nuclear sites spread so widely that former first lady Eleanor Roosevelt wrote about them to Robert Oppenheimer, the scientist who had led the bomb work. According to Michels, Oppenheimer wrote back telling her they were just rumours. Michels says the letter is verified and kept in the Library of Congress, and he tells the story to show how far the talk of UFOs over nuclear sites had travelled.
electrical-after-effects-of-the-encounte: Deep Prasad, a researcher who says he had an encounter with something non-human around 2019, describes strange electrical effects afterward. He tells podcast host Jesse Michels that his phone, even after he wiped it back to factory settings, would charge instantly for the first few days. electrodynamic-dust-shield-payload-teste: On a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, a man named Charles Buer says that just over a year before the recording, his team landed a payload on the Moon. He says it carried nine Electrodynamic Dust Shields, or EDS, devices built, as the name suggests, to shield equipment from lunar dust. He tells it as someone who took part, as proof that the technology was tried on the Moon's surface.
electronic-failures-near-the-baltic-sea-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that sometime in the 2020s he travelled to an odd object on the floor of the Baltic Sea, between Sweden and Finland, with a treasure hunter named Dennis Åsberg from a diving group called Ocean X. According to Michels, the weirdest things happen around the object, including electronic equipment failing. He tells it because, if true, the object would be doing something no ordinary rock should do.
element-115-used-to-amplify-gravity: A guest named Steve Coburn, on Jesse Michels's podcast, repeats a claim from a man named Bob Lazar about "element 115", a very heavy chemical element Lazar has linked to alien craft. Coburn says that, according to Lazar, the element was sometimes used to amplify gravity's effect, though Coburn adds he does not remember Lazar telling him this personally. If true, it would mean someone had learned to control gravity using this material.
elena-hardy-finds-gli3-mutation-in-the-n: A researcher named Elena Hardy, on Jesse Michels's podcast, talks about genetic data from the three-fingered mummies found near Nazca in Peru, which was posted to a public US government database of genetic sequences called the NCBI. Hardy says she found a mutation in a gene called GLI3, and that similar mutations are linked in the scientific literature to polysyndactyly, a condition of extra or joined fingers and toes. elephant-cage-hf-antennas-may-have-aided: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, discusses Dan Sherman, a former sergeant who says in his book Above Black that the NSA, the US agency that intercepts signals, hired him to communicate with aliens. Michels wonders whether huge high-frequency radio antenna arrays nicknamed elephant cages, at bases such as San Vito dei Normanni in Italy and Offutt in Nebraska in the early 1990s, and the signals they received, mattered for the messages Sherman was trying to decode, which, if so, would tie his story to real listening equipment.
eleusinian-mysteries-and-earlier-minoan-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, points to Brian Muraresku, author of a book called The Immortality Key, who writes about the Eleusinian mysteries, secret religious rituals of ancient Greece. Michels places these rituals much later than the earlier Minoan and Mycenaean cultures of the region, and he tells it as part of an idea that the rites carried forward something from a far older past.
eleusinian-mysteries-and-the-kykeon: In ancient Greece, at Eleusis, about 13 miles northwest of Athens, people took part in secret religious rites known as the Eleusinian Mysteries. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says those taking part drank the kykeon, a special drink. He passes on the idea of a writer, Brian Muraresku, that it may have been made with ergot, a grain fungus he says contains LSD. Drawing on Muraresku's book The Immortality Key, Michels says the rites were kept secret on pain of death, and that the little testimony that survives suggests people came away believing they were immortal. Elsewhere he describes the drink as a psychedelic that freed the soul so people could see beings, and he sums up the rites with the saying "if you die before you die, you won't die when you die." A neuroscientist, Andrew Gallimore, also points to Muraresku and says the ritual is where people may have discovered this ergot preparation. So the story comes mostly from the host, again and again, plus one scientist guest, both leaning on Muraresku. If true, it would mean one of the ancient world's great religious rites was built on a mind-altering drug that opened a door to other beings.
eleusinian-mysteries-as-near-death-ritua: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says the Eleusinian Mysteries, secret religious rites held in ancient Greece at a place called Eleusis, and other rituals like them were built around a near-death experience, a temporary killing of the body. He raises it because, if so, the ancients were deliberately sending people to the edge of death to glimpse something beyond it.
eleusis-dmtx-retreat-and-research-center: A neuroscientist named Andrew Gallimore says on Jesse Michels's podcast that, besides running DMTX, a programme built around DMT, a powerful psychedelic drug, he is helping build a retreat center and a research center in the Caribbean. According to the story, the site is in St Vincent and the Grenadines and dates from 2025, under the name Eleusis. It matters to him because he links the DMT experience to contact with what the episode calls an alien realm, and the center would be a place to study it.
elevator-descent-at-the-facility-1980: Randy Anderson, speaking on podcast host Jesse Michels's show, says that sometime in the 1980s he was taken into a building at a secret site in Nevada called S4. He says they went down in an elevator, and the first odd thing was that it felt like they went much deeper underground than you would expect. He tells it as a sign that the facility hid far more below ground than it showed above.
elijah-calls-down-fire-against-the-pries: Jeffrey Mishlove, a researcher of psychic phenomena, retold a Bible story on Jesse Michels' podcast in 2026. He tells it as an ancient example of the kind of power over nature he discusses.
elite-baal-cult-tied-to-the-epstein-mate: A guest named Tim Alberino, on Jesse Michels's podcast, says that some of today's ruling elite seem obsessed with Baal, an ancient Middle Eastern god. If true, it would mean powerful people secretly hold to an old religious cult.
elizabeth-rauscher-s-oni-grant-and-her-b: A researcher called Greg says on Jesse Michels's podcast that the scientist Elizabeth Rauscher, working with Andrija Puharich, got a huge grant in the late 1970s or early 1980s from the ONI, the Office of Naval Intelligence, which is the US Navy's spy agency. Rauscher has since died and left a large archive of her research at Berkeley, and Greg says he had someone go through it but they found nothing about the grant. If true, it would mean the Navy funded her work quietly, leaving no paper trail.
elizabeth-targ-dies-of-the-glioblastoma-: Jeffrey Mishlove, speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast, remembers Elizabeth Targ, the daughter of Russell Targ, as a psychiatrist doing brilliant medical research on psychic healers. As the story goes, she died in 2002 of glioblastoma, a deadly brain cancer, the very illness she had been studying with those healers, a sad and striking twist for someone testing whether healing at a distance works.
elizondo-confirms-hastings-ufos-and-nuke: A former Pentagon official named Lue Elizondo, speaking to podcast host Jesse Michels in 2024, backs the work of a researcher named Robert Hastings, whose book "UFOs and Nukes" collects reports of unidentified objects seen near US nuclear weapons and missile sites. Elizondo says Hastings is "legit" and that he couldn't talk about it while he was in government, but everything Hastings reported, "we saw." elizondo-directed-aatip-an-offshoot-of-a: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Lue Elizondo, a former Pentagon intelligence official, was the director of AATIP, the Advanced Aerospace Threat Identification Program, a small Pentagon office that studied unexplained aerial reports. Michels says AATIP was an offshoot of AAWSAP, the Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications Program, a larger government funded study of the same subject, and he tells it to establish Elizondo's standing as an insider.
elizondo-in-gray-fox-and-jsoc-s-link-to-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that according to Matthew Pines, who was set to be a future guest, Lue Elizondo, a former Pentagon official who has spoken publicly about UFOs, was once a member of the US Army Intelligence Support Activity, a secretive military intelligence unit nicknamed Gray Fox. Michels links this to JSOC, the Joint Special Operations Command that oversees America's elite special forces, which the story ties to recovering crashed UFOs. elizondo-met-edward-teller-on-an-air-flo: Lou Elizondo, a former US defense intelligence official, says that when he was about seven his father, who had friends in government, put him on an Air Florida flight from Sarasota to Miami. He says he sat with Edward Teller, the physicist behind the hydrogen bomb. He tells it as an early brush with the world of secret science he would later join.
elizondo-neither-confirms-nor-denies-bei: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, recalls a 2024 hearing of a US House committee in Washington, where Lou Elizondo, a former Pentagon official who has spoken publicly about UFOs, was asked whether he had been cleared into a secret programme said to exist under the name Immaculate Constellation. elizondo-on-60-minutes-the-government-sa: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, talks about Lou Elizondo, a former Pentagon official, appearing in 2021 on 60 Minutes, a long-running American TV news programme. elizondo-on-aliens-storing-messages-in-g: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, passes on something Lou Elizondo, a former Pentagon official who speaks publicly about UFOs, told him. elizondo-points-aaro-to-a-safe-drawer-th: A former US Senate staffer named Kirk McConnell, on Jesse Michels's podcast, tells of an episode in the 2020s involving AARO, the Pentagon office set up to investigate UFO reports, and Lou Elizondo, a former Pentagon official who speaks publicly about UFOs. elizondo-regularly-sees-green-orbs-in-hi: Podcast host Jesse Michels says that Lou Elizondo, a former defense intelligence official, regularly sees green orbs in his house. elizondo-s-book-blocked-from-a-lockheed-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in a book by Lou Elizondo, a former Pentagon official, Elizondo describes how his team went to Lockheed Martin, a large American defence company, to try to get inside a certain programme. elizondo-s-idea-that-ufos-are-prepping-t: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Lue Elizondo, a former Pentagon official who went public about UFOs in 2017 and was one of the first whistleblowers, has suggested that UFOs may be "prepping the battle space", meaning getting the ground ready before a conflict. elizondo-s-imminent-people-with-cherokee: Jason Samosa, speaking as a witness on Jesse Michels's podcast, points to Imminent, a book by Lue Elizondo, a former Pentagon official who has spoken out about UFOs. elizondo-s-toy-in-the-sandbox-analogy-fo: Lou Elizondo, a former Pentagon official who says he ran a small office studying unexplained aerial reports, uses the image of children in a sandbox to talk about a technology he suggests the US holds. elizondo-saw-jacobs-s-film-at-aatip-2010: On his podcast, Jesse Michels relays the account of a man named Robert Jacobs, who says that Lue Elizondo confirmed he had seen Jacobs's film and his account. elizondo-says-monsanto-linked-people-are: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, passes on what Lou Elizondo, a former Pentagon official who speaks publicly about UFOs, has said about people working against him. elizondo-time-is-not-a-luxury-that-we-ca: Lou Elizondo, a former US government official who speaks publicly about unexplained flying objects, appeared on a show hosted by the podcaster Jesse Michels and urged that the public conversation about them can't wait. elizondo-was-nro-liaison-while-at-ttsa-2: An online researcher who goes by UAPGerb, speaking on podcast host Jesse Michels's show, says that around 2017 Luis Elizondo, a former Pentagon official, was working at the same time with To The Stars Academy, or TTSA, a private company that set out to study UFOs, and as a liaison to the NRO, the US agency that runs spy satellites. elizondo-won-t-confirm-or-deny-immaculat: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Lue Elizondo, a former Pentagon intelligence official, told a hearing of the US Congress in September 2024 that he could neither confirm nor deny being briefed on Immaculate Constellation, a reported secret military program said to gather UFO data. elizondo-worked-with-grusch-in-a-scif: Lou Elizondo, a former defense intelligence official, says he worked alongside David Grusch, a former intelligence officer who became a whistleblower on government UFO secrets, in a SCIF, a sealed room for handling classified material. ellsworth-inner-zone-alert-saucer-beams-: At Ellsworth Air Force Base in South Dakota, which guarded nuclear missiles, guards say they met something strange near a missile site. ellsworth-radar-jet-chase-and-bismarck-l: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, retells a case from Project Blue Book, the US Air Force's UFO study of the 1950s and 60s, drawing on the account of Edward J. ellsworth-silo-abandoned-with-access-plu: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in 1978, at Ellsworth, an Air Force base in South Dakota with underground nuclear missile silos, a security team left a silo with its access plug, the heavy lid over the entrance, standing open. elon-musk-knows-ufo-secrets-but-can-t-sa: Joe Rogan, a popular podcast host, told podcaster Jesse Michels in 2025 that Elon Musk, the head of the rocket company SpaceX, surely knows secrets about UFOs but cannot talk about them. elon-musk-on-joe-rogan-denies-advanced-t: A podcast host named Jesse Michels says that in 2025 the businessman Elon Musk went on another podcast, hosted by Joe Rogan, and said he has an "all access pass" to the big aerospace and defense companies Lockheed and Northrop. elon-musk-on-legacy-programs-at-a-trump-: Matthew Pines, a researcher speaking on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, says that the tech entrepreneur Elon Musk was asked about "legacy programs" at a town hall event while he was campaigning for Donald Trump in 2024. elongated-skulls-without-a-sagittal-sutu: Jay Anderson, a guest on podcast host Jesse Michels's show, talks about the Hypogeum, an ancient underground chamber on the island of Malta. elvis-starr-s-memoir-tape-about-meeting-: A researcher who goes unnamed, speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast, says there is a tape from the 1970s on which a man named Elvis Starr dictates his memoirs. email-to-doty-about-who-wrote-serpo-2020: A researcher named Deep Prasad says that in early 2020 he emailed Richard Doty, a retired Air Force special agent long tied to UFO stories, about Project Serpo, a story that spread online about a secret exchange in which Americans were said to have travelled to an alien planet. email-to-nolan-about-a-glowing-object-th: Garry Nolan, a Stanford University scientist who studies material said to come from UFOs, told podcaster Jesse Michels in 2021 that he had just received an email from someone describing a glowing object that dropped molten metal. emails-from-people-who-saw-cigar-shaped-: A Swedish treasure hunter named Dennis Asberg, who says he found a strange object on the seafloor, tells Jesse Michels's podcast that since 2011 he has received many emails and even paper letters from people around the world. embassy-correspondence-waiting-for-the-a: A UFO researcher named Grant Cameron, on Jesse Michels's podcast, talks about papers from the personal files of Wilbert Smith, a Canadian government engineer of the 1950s, which also involve Omond Solandt, a senior Canadian defence science official. emenegger-and-linda-moulton-howe-promise: Bryce Zabel, a writer talking about Hollywood, the CIA and UFOs on Jesse Michels' podcast, describes a pattern of people being promised film and then having it taken away. emenegger-gave-a-copy-of-the-documentary: Grant Cameron, a longtime UFO researcher, relays what filmmaker Bob Emenegger told him about the mid 1970s. encyclopedia-galactica-alien-taxonomy-se: A member of the US Congress, Eric Burlison, says that someone sent him both volumes of a work called the Encyclopedia Galactica, which is said to sort and describe different kinds of aliens. energy-grid-like-structures-beneath-the-: This story is about the pyramids at Giza in Egypt. engineers-describe-xf-131-super-sentinel: An online UFO researcher who goes by UAPGerb, speaking with podcast host Jesse Michels, says that in 1992 a man named Bill McDonald met four engineers in California's Mojave Desert, two from the aircraft maker Northrop and two from Lockheed, who were tired of the secrecy around their work. enhanced-pilot-photo-shows-slanted-hanga: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that a researcher named Luigi Vendetelli showed a man named Bob Lazar a high-quality aerial photo taken by a pilot about 17 miles from Papoose Lake, a dry lake in Nevada. enoch-s-ascent-and-transformation-into-m: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, retells a story from the Book of Enoch, an ancient religious text. enochian-tale-found-in-dead-sea-scroll-m: A researcher and filmmaker named Tim Alberino says the old story told in the Book of Enoch, an ancient Jewish text about fallen angels and the giants they fathered, does not appear only in that one book. enrico-fermi-thinks-about-aliens-at-los-: Enrico Fermi was a physicist who laid the groundwork for splitting the atom and worked on the Manhattan Project, the wartime US effort to build the atomic bomb. ent-specialists-find-otolith-damage-in-h: Chris Gilbert, a researcher speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast, talks about Havana syndrome, a set of unexplained health complaints reported by US government staff. entities-based-on-the-moon-airdropping-t: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, floats an idea while talking with a guest: that some beings based on the Moon have been "airdropping tech here and there" on Earth. entity-pulls-him-out-of-his-body-and-sco: Joe McMoneagle, a guest on podcast host Jesse Michels's show, says that around 1970, while he was in Germany and sunk in depression, he was woken in the middle of the night by an entity that pulled him right out of his body. envelope-lettering-transferred-onto-deve: A scientist named Steve, who studies objects people say were implanted in their bodies by aliens, tells podcast host Jesse Michels about something a doctor he calls Dr. Builder showed him in his office. epiphany-during-jean-houston-s-mystery-s: Jeffrey Mishlove, a researcher of the mind and psychic experience, says he was once at a teacher named Jean Houston's mystery school, a series of teaching sessions, listening to a lecture on The Cipher of Genesis, a book by Carlos Suares about hidden meaning in the Bible's first book. epstein-as-the-front-for-a-project-or-sp: Eric Weinstein, a researcher and commentator speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast, floats the idea that the financier Jeffrey Epstein was a front for a special access program, meaning a tightly restricted secret government project, running from the 1990s until 2019. epstein-blackmail-file-on-senior-nationa: Steven Greer, a long-time campaigner for UFO secrets to be made public, says on Jesse Michels's podcast that a very senior person in the US national security world was mixed up with Jeffrey Epstein, the wealthy financier, sometime between the 2000s and 2025. epstein-circle-s-gravity-interest-as-an-: Jason Jorjani, a philosopher, says on Jesse Michels's podcast that the interest in gravity research shown by Jeffrey Epstein's circle in the 2000s and 2010s was really about electrogravitics, the idea that electricity can be used to cancel or bend gravity, linked to the work of an inventor named Townsend Brown. epstein-email-about-killing-pons-and-col: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that among the released emails of the financier Jeffrey Epstein is one where Epstein brags that he "killed Pons" years earlier. epstein-files-show-interest-in-people-wi: A man who calls himself a Pentagon whistleblower, Matthew Brown, told podcast host Jesse Michels that the Epstein files show something odd.
