Brown says the files prove the network was interested in people said to have "psi" abilities, meaning powers of the mind like psychic sensing, empathy or special states of consciousness, which, if true, would tie powerful people to a quiet hunt for such gifts.
epstein-prison-cell-video-metadata-edite: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Wired, a mainstream technology magazine, reported in 2025 that the metadata, the hidden technical record stored inside a file, of the video from Jeffrey Epstein's prison cell at the Metropolitan Correctional Center in New York in 2019 had been edited, likely with the video editing program Adobe Premiere. The video was supposed to point to Epstein's death being a suicide, so if the report is right, the footage may have been altered.
epstein-s-eugenics-plan-to-create-his-ow: A guest on Jesse Michels's podcast, Jay Anderson, says that Jeffrey Epstein, the wealthy financier, was obsessed with eugenics, the idea of improving humans through controlled breeding, and wanted to create his own race. Anderson passes this on from a woman named Juliet Byron, and ties it to Epstein's Zorro Ranch in New Mexico, from roughly the 1990s until 2019.
epstein-s-gravity-conference-and-submari: A philosopher and researcher named Jason Jorjani, speaking on the podcast of host Jesse Michels, says that in the 2000s the financier Jeffrey Epstein held a conference about gravity and took people, including the physicist Stephen Hawking, down in submarines in the Bahamas. According to Jorjani, who credits others such as the researcher Eric Weinstein and his own online essay, the dives were meant to study strange quantum gravity effects in the Bahamas basin, roughly the Bermuda Triangle, a stretch of ocean known for stories of lost ships and planes. If true, it would mean a wealthy private figure was quietly funding hunts for exotic physics.
epstein-s-gravity-conferences-casimir-ob: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that emails from Jeffrey Epstein, a wealthy financier, show he held meetings on gravity research from the 2000s into the 2010s. Michels says Epstein was obsessed with the Casimir effect, a tiny force in physics that appears between objects placed very close together in empty space, and that he knew about a physics theory from Eric Weinstein, a researcher and an old colleague of Michels. Michels insists "this is all in the emails", which would mean a powerful private figure was quietly following unusual physics.
epstein-s-keycard-access-to-harvard-evol: Jason Jorjani, a philosopher, says on Jesse Michels's podcast that in the 2000s Jeffrey Epstein, the wealthy financier, was involved with a biology research group at Harvard University that studied evolutionary dynamics, and even had a keycard to get into it. Jorjani names the scientists Robert Trivers and George Church in connection with the story. He tells it to show how close Epstein got to top science.
epstein-s-listening-post-at-one-brattle-: Eric Weinstein, a mathematician and podcaster, says on Jesse Michels's show that Jeffrey Epstein, the wealthy financier, kept what Weinstein calls a "listening post" at One Brattle Square, an address in Cambridge, Massachusetts, near Harvard, in the 2000s. Weinstein links it to the Harvard scientist Martin Nowak and to files about Epstein that have been released to the public. The point, as he tells it, is that Epstein placed himself where he could keep watch on leading scientists.
epstein-s-obsession-with-gravity-propuls: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that the financier Jeffrey Epstein was obsessed with secret science, especially gravity and ways of moving craft. According to Michels, Epstein flew well-known physicists such as Kip Thorne, Stephen Hawking and Murray Gell-Mann out to his private island in the US Virgin Islands, and gave the physicist Lawrence Krauss about $250,000. He tells it as a lesser-known thread that, if true, ties Epstein to hidden research into advanced propulsion.
epstein-s-zorro-ranch-near-los-alamos-ph: Podcast host Jesse Michels says that Jeffrey Epstein, the wealthy financier, told political strategist Steve Bannon in an interview near the end of his life why he set up Zorro Ranch in New Mexico. According to Michels, Epstein said he picked the spot to be near retiring physicists from Los Alamos, the US nuclear weapons laboratory. The story dates the ranch to 1993, though one of Michels's tellings gives no year. Michels uses it to argue that security at the DOE, the Department of Energy that runs the nuclear labs, is so lax that an outsider could get close to its scientists.
eric-bard-replicates-the-anomalies-with-: Brandon Fugal, the owner of Skinwalker Ranch, a property in Utah known for reports of strange happenings, tells of something from around 2020 that was shown in the first season of the TV series The Secret of Skinwalker Ranch. He says a team member named Eric Bard was later able to recreate the odd readings seen on the ranch by focusing intense electromagnetic force with a very strong magnet. If true, it would suggest powerful electromagnetic fields are behind what happens there.
eric-davis-at-closed-hearing-nhi-control: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that at a closed hearing in the US Congress in 2025, with Lou Elizondo, the researcher Avi Loeb and a man named Eric Davis present, Davis said that NHI, short for non-human intelligence, are themselves controlling disclosure. Disclosure here means the public release of what governments know about them. If true, it would mean the beings, not officials, decide what we learn and when.
eric-davis-calls-townsend-brown-a-phony-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that a man named Eric Davis got in touch with him, around 2024, and told him that Townsend Brown was "a phony." Brown is a figure whose name comes up in these stories about advanced propulsion. It matters because it would cast doubt on claims tied to Brown's work.
eric-davis-craft-defying-physics-but-no-: Eric Weinstein, a mathematician and podcaster, says that Eric Davis, a physicist who has worked on Pentagon studies of UFOs, told him: "We have things that defy the laws of physics and no physicists." Podcast host Jesse Michels repeats it twice, once saying only that there were no physicists on the program, and once telling it as Davis's answer when asked if any theoretical physicists were involved, where Davis said there were none. If true, it would mean a secret effort to study objects that break known physics had nobody trained to understand them.
eric-davis-denies-alien-reproduction-veh: Eric Davis is a scientist who has worked on US government studies of unexplained craft. Speaking to an online researcher known as UAPGerb, he denied the idea of "alien reproduction vehicles", meaning human-built aircraft copied from recovered alien craft. He says that no aircraft has drawn on anything of that kind and that no one has ever built an exact copy, which would mean the rumours of secret copied craft are wrong.
eric-davis-dia-report-on-teleportation: A Navy scientist named Salvatore Pais, talking with podcast host Jesse Michels, says he saw a report on teleportation written by a researcher named Eric W. Davis for the DIA, the Defense Intelligence Agency, which gathers military intelligence for the US. Pais brings it up because, in his view, it speaks to the importance of his own ideas about advanced physics.
eric-davis-helped-write-a-book-for-bigel: A podcast host named Jack, speaking on Jesse Michels's show, talks about AAWSAP, a Pentagon-funded study of unexplained phenomena that ran from around 2008 and was run through businessman Robert Bigelow's company. Jack says that during that programme, the physicist Eric Davis was helping write a book for Bigelow. He raises it to show how closely the people in that programme worked together.
eric-davis-lied-to-uapgerb-about-alien-r: An online researcher who goes by UAPGerb (UAP is the government's term for UFOs) says on Jesse Michels's podcast that Eric Davis, a physicist who has worked on Pentagon-linked UFO studies, lied to his face. He says Davis misled him about how well work had gone on technologies copied from recovered craft and on "alien reproduction vehicles", meaning human-built copies of alien craft. If true, it would mean insiders are hiding how far such programmes have got.
eric-davis-offers-full-testimony-for-bla: A researcher named Eric Weinstein, on Jesse Michels' podcast, says that the physicist Eric Davis, a scientist linked to Pentagon work on UFOs, went on record in the latest film by documentary maker James Fox. Weinstein says Davis stated that if he were given blanket immunity from prosecution, he would tell everything he knows, which would suggest he holds secrets he cannot legally share.
eric-davis-s-notes-from-the-advanced-phy: A UFO researcher named Grant Cameron says a physicist named Eric Davis gave him his notes from a group called the Advanced Physics Theoretical Working Group, which met in the 2000s in the United States. Cameron says the notes mattered a great deal to him, because, if they are what he describes, they would give an inside look at scientists studying advanced physics linked to the UFO question.
eric-davis-saw-classified-crash-retrieva: A scientist named Eric Davis tells a podcast host, Jesse Michels, about a case he says he knows of from secret material. In his words, it is a crash retrieval: there is a craft and there are alien bodies. If true, it would mean that non-human craft and their crews have been recovered.
eric-davis-says-the-head-of-crash-retrie: Eric Davis, a scientist who has worked on US government studies of unexplained craft, says that in the 2000s he and his colleagues tried to interview the man running a crash retrieval program, meaning a secret effort to recover crashed craft of unknown origin, linked in the telling to a man named Glenn Gaffney. According to Davis, that person refused to talk to them. If true, it would mean such a program existed and had a leader who was keeping it from even other insiders.
eric-davis-teleportation-study-for-mitre: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says a set of presentation slides has turned up, not exactly leaked but rediscovered, showing that a physicist named Eric Davis did a study on teleportation for the MITRE Corporation, a US research company that works for the government, around 2019. Michels tells it because, if true, it would mean serious defence-linked work was still being done on ideas that sound like science fiction.
eric-davis-writes-of-an-air-force-five-d: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, reads from Frontiers of Propulsion Science, a book on ideas for moving spacecraft, citing Eric Davis and, in another episode, also crediting Marc Millis. According to Michels, Davis concedes that an Air Force study proposed that, if you assume space has five dimensions, you can derive a link between electricity and gravity that explains the Biefeld-Brown effect, a claimed push produced by high-voltage electric charge. If so, it would suggest the military once took electric control of gravity seriously.
eric-haseltine-s-idea-of-a-massless-obje: Podcast host Jesse Michels says that a man named Eric Haseltine raised an idea about the 2004 encounter off San Diego, where Navy pilots from the aircraft carrier Nimitz reported a strange flying object. According to Michels, Haseltine asked: what if the object had no mass at all? He pointed to the physics rule that force equals mass times acceleration, which would mean such an object could move in ways normal aircraft cannot.
eric-hecker-raytheon-neutrino-system-und: Steven Greer, a long-time campaigner for UFO secrets to be made public, says that a man named Eric Hecker came forward and told him that around 2011 he worked for Raytheon, a large US defense company, at the South Pole. Greer says Hecker's team put in a system for detecting neutrinos, tiny particles from space, about a mile under the Antarctic ice, and he tells it as the setting for an account of something unusual found there.
eric-hecker-s-childhood-involvement-with: Eric Hecker, a guest on podcast host Jesse Michels's show, says he grew up on Long Island, New York, and as a child was caught up in what he calls nefarious activity tied to Stargate, a US government programme that tested psychic abilities. He describes his history with it as very peculiar. If true, it would mean children were drawn into secret government psychic work.
eric-henry-wang-s-name-on-dtic-engineeri: An online researcher who goes by UAPGerb says on Jesse Michels's podcast that a man named Eric Henry Wang really existed, because his name appears on old 1950s engineering papers linked to Wright-Patterson Air Force Base in Ohio. UAPGerb says the papers can be found through DTIC, the Defense Technical Information Center, a US military library of technical reports. The point is that a figure from UFO stories can be traced in real government records.
eric-henry-wang-special-projects-at-wrig: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, mentions a man named Eric Henry Wang, who he says was head of special projects at Wright-Patterson, a US Air Force base, in the years after 1945. Michels brings Wang up alongside the inventor Viktor Schauberger in a story about secret postwar research. If true, it would place Wang at the center of the military's most sensitive work in that era.
eric-lopes-and-the-second-capture-of-a-l: James Fox, a documentary filmmaker who investigates UFO cases, tells of a military police officer named Eric Lopes in the Brazilian town of Varginha in 1996, who is said to have been the driver when a second living creature was captured. In a later telling Fox dates it to January 20, 1996, about three hours after three girls reported seeing a strange creature, and says the creature ran across the road in front of Lopes and his fellow officer Marco Chereze. If true, it would mean the military caught a live, non-human being.
eric-lopes-refuses-to-talk-and-threatens: Documentary filmmaker James Fox says that while filming in Varginha, a Brazilian town tied to a story of a captured alien, his crew tried to reach a man named Eric Lopes. Fox says they were told that if they had come to talk about the ET, the extraterrestrial, Lopes would not talk, and that the crew were threatened with being shot. He tells it as a sign that people there are still afraid to speak.
eric-lopes-went-into-hiding-marco-cherez: The narrator of a documentary about the 1996 creature case in Varginha, Brazil, says the driver involved, Eric Lopes, has been in hiding. The narrator adds that the officer who handled the live being, Marco Chereze, died a couple of weeks later, a death that, if linked to the creature, would make it one of the case's most serious claims.
eric-walker-claimed-majestic-12-membersh: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Eric Walker, a man connected to Penn State university, seemed to claim he was part of Majestic 12, a rumoured secret group of officials said to handle the UFO question. Michels ties this to a conversation Walker had with a man named Henry Azadehdel, and to work by a UFO researcher named Grant Cameron, because if true it would put a real person inside that group.
eric-walker-interview-what-do-you-know-a: A UFO researcher named Grant Cameron describes a 1987 phone interview with a man named Eric Walker, which he says he has transcripts of. According to Cameron, when the caller pressed him, Walker cut him off and asked, "What do you know about ESP?", meaning extrasensory perception, the idea of sensing things beyond the normal five senses. Walker reportedly said that unless you understand how ESP works, you will never be let in by what he called "the control group", a hint that a hidden circle oversees the UFO secret and treats the mind as the key to it.
eric-walker-on-trw-board: An online UFO researcher who goes by UAPGerb says that Jacques Vallee, a well known UFO researcher, has talked about a man named Dr. Eric A. Walker sitting on the board of directors, or serving as chairman, of TRW, an American defense and aerospace company. UAPGerb offers it as an interesting link between Walker, who comes up elsewhere in UFO stories, and the defense industry.
eric-wang-s-secret-ufo-work-at-kirtland-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that a UFO researcher named Bill Steinman contacted Maria Wang, the wife of a scientist named Eric Wang. According to Michels, she told Steinman that her husband worked at Kirtland Air Force Base in New Mexico in the 1950s and 60s on secret UFO-related projects, which, if true, would mean the government had scientists quietly studying the subject.
eric-wargo-remote-viewing-as-precognitio: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, points to a writer named Eric Wargo, who argues in his book Time Loops that remote viewing, the claimed ability to see distant places with the mind, is really precognition, meaning a glimpse of the future. Michels raises it because, if true, it would change how such strange mental experiences, and time itself, should be understood.
eric-wargo-s-time-loops-theory-of-precog: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, describes a book called Time Loops by the writer Eric Wargo, which offers a theory of precognition, the idea of knowing things before they happen. Michels says the book treats the brain as a kind of hybrid of an ordinary computer and a quantum computer that can reach information from the future. If true, glimpses of the future would have a physical explanation.
eric-weinstein-joins-galileo-project-geo: In a 2022 conversation, a Harvard researcher, Avi Loeb, tells podcast host Jesse Michels that his colleague, the researcher Eric Weinstein, had recently joined the Galileo Project, a Harvard effort to look for evidence of alien technology. Loeb says the two sometimes speculate about the physics of UAP, the official term for unidentified flying objects. It matters because it shows serious scientists trying to work out how such objects could move.
eric-weinstein-s-secret-branch-of-physic: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says the researcher Eric Weinstein came to this subject because he became convinced there was a secret branch of physics in the 1950s to 1970s. According to Michels, it involved well-known physicists John Wheeler, Richard Feynman and Bryce DeWitt, who had much more contact with private aerospace companies than met the eye. If true, it would mean some advanced physics was quietly kept out of public science.
erich-von-daniken-on-templar-secrets: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says he once asked Erich von Däniken, a writer, about the Templars, a medieval order of Christian knights. According to Michels, von Däniken answered that there are secrets about them he cannot talk about. It is told as a hint that a well-known writer is holding back hidden knowledge.
eridu-found-in-the-1800s-its-ziggurat-ne: A researcher named Matt, speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast, says that in the 1800s explorers found Eridu, an ancient city in southern Iraq, dug up only its main part, and sent the clay tablets they found to the British Museum. According to Matt, they never excavated Eridu's ziggurat, a large stepped temple tower, which he suggests could still hold answers about the deep past.
esa-scientists-recognize-tyler-at-the-va: Diana Pasulka, a religious studies professor who writes about belief in UFOs, says she was at the Vatican Observatory at Castel Gandolfo in Italy sometime in the 2010s. She says that when a man she calls Tyler, a space industry figure she keeps anonymous, was introduced by his real name, the scientists there from ESA, the European Space Agency, erupted in recognition. Guy Consolmagno, a Jesuit astronomer at the observatory, is part of the story, which she tells to show that Tyler is a real and respected figure.
esalen-contact-exercise-brings-blue-plas: A man named Jordan Jose tells a podcast host, Jesse Michels, about a group session he says took place in 2024 at the Esalen Institute, a retreat center in Big Sur, California, where people tried to make contact with something beyond us. He says that blue glowing balls, which he calls plasma orbs, rose out of the ocean and came within about 50 yards of people. He mentions a man named Ross Coulthart in connection with it. Later in the same interview he describes the event again without naming the place, saying about 30 people were there, all very heart-centered, and they had incredible interactions with the orbs. Jordan is the only teller, speaking twice in one conversation. If true, it would mean a group can call such lights in just by their shared state of mind.
esgridge-s-poems-work-at-marshall-and-al: A podcast host called Jack, speaking on a Jesse Michels episode with the Navy scientist Salvatore Pais, lists earlier lines of research. He says a researcher named Richard Esgridge looked into something, which this story calls POEMS, at the Marshall Space Flight Center, a NASA site. He also mentions a man named Alzofon and his approaches based on "nucleonic spin," the spin of particles in the atom's core, which he says Alzofon worked through with the physicist Richard Feynman back in the 1930s, a hint that such unusual physics has a longer history than people think.
esoteric-and-occult-imagery-on-nro-missi: A YouTuber and UFO researcher named Chris Ramsay tells podcast host Jesse Michels that he looked closely at the mission patches made for launches by the NRO, the National Reconnaissance Office, the US agency that runs spy satellites. He says he found them really interesting, pointing to occult and esoteric imagery on them, which he takes as a hint of hidden beliefs inside the agency.
esp-tests-in-a-faraday-cage-at-the-round: Greg Malatzi, a researcher speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast, says that at the Round Table Foundation, a private research group in Rockland, Maine, in the early 1950s, a Faraday cage was built: a metal enclosure that blocks radio and electrical signals. As he understands it, someone there was one of the first to run ESP tests, meaning experiments on extrasensory perception, or sensing things without the ordinary senses, inside such a cage. The point is that any results could not be put down to ordinary radio signals.
esp-training-with-handler-meg-after-inte: A man named Jordan Jose says that as a child he was taken into a secret UFO program, and that around 2008 to 2010, at a place called Baker Victory Services in Western New York, he was trained in ESP, the claimed ability to sense things without the normal senses. He says a handler he calls Meg oversaw him, and that two months in, a team of interns was hired to work only on him and his case. If true, it would mean a hidden program was testing children for mental abilities.
essa-truck-mechanic-repaired-damaged-sus: A documentary filmmaker named James Fox says he spoke with a man said to be the truck mechanic at a Brazilian military base known as EsSA in 1996. According to Fox, the mechanic said he had to make extensive repairs to the trucks' suspensions at that time, which Fox raises because it would suggest the trucks carried something unusually heavy linked to a reported alien case that year.
estrada-cotton-joints-and-cyanoacrylate-: Flavio Estrada, a researcher in Peru who has examined small three-fingered mummy-like figures that some claim are not human, talks about them on Jesse Michels' podcast. He says the joints of the figures are made with cotton and cyanoacrylate, a strong superglue, which gives them a surprising hardness. If so, it would mean the figures were put together by people in modern times.
ether-drift-detected-on-mount-wilson: Steve Coburn, a guest on Jesse Michels' podcast, talks about the ether, an old idea that an invisible substance fills all of space. He says a scientist he calls Millikan did not detect the ether directly, but did detect Earth's motion through it with an experiment done, he believes, on Mount Wilson in California. If true, it would mean the ether really exists.
ethiopian-churches-keep-the-book-of-enoc: A researcher and filmmaker named Tim Alberino says that around the 4th century AD, the Tewahedo Orthodox Christians and the Beta Israel Jewish community in Ethiopia added the Book of Enoch, an ancient religious text left out of most Bibles, to their official scriptures. He brings it up because the book tells of fallen angels and giants, which ties into his own claims about giants.
ets-arrived-en-masse-after-the-first-ato: Steven Greer, a researcher who campaigns for the release of UFO secrets, says on Jesse Michels's podcast that after the first atomic bomb was detonated in 1945, extraterrestrials "came in on force in mass." In his telling, the bomb drew visitors to Earth in large numbers, which would mean the nuclear age is what brought humanity under alien watch.
ets-teleport-into-ce-5-circle: Steven Greer, a former doctor who leads groups trying to contact extraterrestrials, runs what he calls CE-5 sessions, short for "close encounter of the fifth kind": people sitting in a circle and meditating to invite contact. Greer says that in some of these sessions the ETs themselves have teleported right into the circle. If true, it would mean humans can bring about contact on purpose.
ets-tell-government-leaders-to-develop-s: A guest on Jesse Michels's podcast, Dave Rossi, passes on stories he credits to a man named Dan Sheehan about alien visitors meeting government leaders. According to these stories, the aliens told the leaders they had to grow spiritually before more technology or material could be shared with them.
eugenicist-elites-become-the-nordics-189: A writer named Jason Jorjani argues that the elites who backed eugenics, the idea of improving humans through controlled breeding, in the US, Britain and Germany from the 1890s to the 1930s, later turn up as the "Nordics", tall, fair, human-looking beings described in UFO reports. He names the birth control campaigner Margaret Sanger among them and draws on a book called Closer Encounters, suggesting that some alien sightings may tie back to these human groups.
european-crash-retrieval-initiative-and-: An astronomer, Beatriz Villarroel, says she leads from Sweden a European group meant to look into crash retrievals, meaning the recovery of crashed craft that might not be human-made. She says the group is working on an old unsolved case that she cannot describe, calling it super cool and super scary. If true, it would mean scientists in Europe are chasing a real crash of something unknown.
european-leader-confides-about-ufos-on-a: A former president of a Russian republic, Kiran Ilum Xenov, who says he was taken by aliens in 1997, tells podcast host Jesse Michels that sometime in the late 1990s the leader of an unnamed European country took a walk with him in a park. According to Xenov, the leader told him something very interesting about UFOs, which would mean that other heads of state know more than they say.
european-research-council-s-10-million-p: Donald Hoffman, a scientist speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast, describes "positive geometries", a new branch of mathematical physics associated with the physicist Nima Arkani-Hamed. He says the field has grown so big that the European Research Council, Europe's main public funder of science, now has a 10 million euro initiative devoted to it. He offers this as a sign that the ideas behind it are being taken seriously by mainstream science.
every-drilling-crew-suffers-equipment-fa: The owner of Skinwalker Ranch, a property in Utah known for reports of strange events, says his team has been drilling into a mesa on the land. He says every drilling expert they brought out had dramatic equipment failures. He tells it as a sign that something unusual sits under the ground there.
every-recovered-craft-gets-a-reverse-eng: On a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, a guest named Michael Herrera passes on something he says was told to him by others. According to what was relayed to him, every craft that is recovered also gets copies built from it, made by taking the original apart and studying it, in an attempt to copy that technology or that particular craft. If true, it would mean a hidden effort to rebuild machines that did not come from people.
evidence-of-humans-in-the-americas-130-0: Graham Hancock, a writer who argues that human history is much older than taught, says on Jesse Michels' podcast that there is evidence of people living in the Americas as long as 130,000 years ago. He points out that this would be about ten times older than the usual date given for when people first arrived there, which would upend the accepted story of how the continents were settled.
ewen-cameron-examines-rudolf-hess-to-see: Peter Levenda, an author and researcher speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast, says that in England in the 1940s the psychiatrist Ewen Cameron examined Rudolf Hess, a senior Nazi leader held by the British. According to Levenda, the aim was to figure out whether the prisoner was really Hess or a double, which, if true, would mean the Allies themselves doubted who they were holding.
exeter-wobbling-disc-1964: A man named Merrick, speaking in a debate with a UFO skeptic on Jesse Michels's podcast, describes a 1964 sighting in Exeter, New Hampshire. He says four people, two of them police officers, saw a large disc about 100 feet away and 100 feet up, moving with a wobbling motion. He offers it as a close-range case with credible witnesses that is hard to explain away.
exodus-details-written-by-someone-living: A researcher named Luke Caverns, speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast, talks about the Exodus, the Bible story of the Israelites leaving Egypt. He says the details in that story could only have been written by someone who was alive in Egypt at the time it describes, roughly the New Kingdom period of ancient Egypt, around 1500 to 1000 BC. If so, the story would come from someone who saw that world firsthand rather than being written much later.
exodus-thrusters-weigh-less-on-a-scale-p: A man named Charles, from a company called Exodus Propulsion, says that in the 2020s they put their thrusters on a scale, switched them on, and saw them get lighter, and that flipping them over made them heavier. He says the work is now going through peer review, meaning outside experts are checking it, and that it is part of their second patent application, the paperwork for legally protecting an invention. If true, it would be a device that pushes against gravity without burning fuel.
exoprobe-telescope-network-to-find-and-r: An astronomer, Beatriz Villarroel, describes a project she calls ExoProbe, a network of telescopes in New Mexico. She says the aim is to find an object sent by beings from another world and then pick it up and bring it down to Earth. If it worked, it would mean holding a real alien probe in human hands.
exorcist-boy-became-aerospace-engineer-a: Diana Pasulka, a guest discussing religion and UFOs on Jesse Michels' podcast, relays that the boy whose 1949 case inspired the film The Exorcist later grew up to become an aerospace engineer. According to what she was told, after his exorcism the boy urinated excessively. She tells it as an odd thread linking possession stories to the world of aerospace.
experiencers-account-of-breeding-experim: On Jesse Michels's podcast, a man named Bob McGwier passes on what he hears from experiencers, people who say they have had contact with non-human beings. He stresses that this is their story, not his: according to them, the beings are carrying out breeding experiments for reasons no one knows, and they also bring messages about the planet and its environment. If true, it would mean someone is deliberately working on humans and also trying to warn us.
experiment-current-induced-in-one-stone-: A researcher named Geoffrey Drumm, who says an alien showed him the true purpose of the pyramids, says that he and a collaborator named Ben ran an experiment on the stones. According to Drumm, when they sent electric current into one stone, it jumped as a spark into the next stone. He tells it as support for his idea that the pyramids were built to work with electricity.
expired-first-patent-and-a-new-second-pa: An inventor and researcher named Filippo, who appeared on a podcast about a claimed energy grid beneath the pyramids of Egypt, responds to a point raised by an archaeologist, Flint Dibble, in a video. Filippo says that yes, his first patent, filed with the US Patent and Trademark Office (the government office that grants patents), has now expired, and that he has a second, newer patent. He tells it to show that his work still stands on official ground despite the criticism.
explorer-1-launched-on-imbolc-1958: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, points out that Explorer 1, the first American satellite, built by the Jet Propulsion Laboratory, a NASA space lab, was launched on January 31st, 1958. He links the date to Imbolc, an old pagan festival at the start of February, as part of his idea that the space programme timed things to match ancient rituals.
extended-state-dmt-trials-yield-encounte: Graham Hancock, a writer on ancient mysteries and consciousness, says on Jesse Michels' podcast that scientists at Imperial College London and the University of California San Diego are running trials in the 2020s with DMT, a powerful psychedelic drug, keeping volunteers under its effects for extended periods rather than a few minutes. According to Hancock, the volunteers all come back reporting encounters with "sentient others," thinking beings they meet while under. He links this work to researchers Andrew Gallimore and Rick Strassman, and tells it because it would suggest such beings may be real in some sense.
extraction-shaft-under-the-queen-s-chamb: A researcher named Jeffrey, speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast, describes a theory from his own book about the Great Pyramid at Giza in Egypt. extradition-fight-and-we-want-to-see-him: A British computer hacker, Gary McKinnon, says he broke into US government systems and found signs of a secret NASA space program, and then faced a long fight against extradition, being sent to the US to stand trial, in the 2000s. extraterrestrial-being-interviewed-behin: Dan Sheehan, a guest on Jesse Michels' podcast, relays what a man named Albert Stein told him: that people were taken to Area 51, a secret US test site in Nevada, and then to S4, a site linked to it, where they went several floors down to a big room with a two-way mirror and an extraterrestrial being on the other side. eyewitness-accounts-of-nazi-nuclear-test: A researcher named Jason Jorjani, speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast, says there are eyewitness accounts of what seem to be nuclear tests by Nazi Germany in 1944 and 1945, including one near the Thuringian forest in central Germany. ezekiel-s-visitors-appear-as-wheels-cove: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, retells a vision from the Book of Ezekiel, a book of the Bible set in Babylon. f-86s-scrambled-to-chase-objects-away-fr: On Jesse Michels's podcast, a man named Mario Woods passes on what he says he heard from someone named Chris about Ellsworth Air Force Base in South Dakota around 1977. f-e-warren-missile-outage-blamed-on-a-ti: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells of a 2010 event at F.E. f-e-warren-witnesses-flagged-as-security: Robert Hastings, a researcher who collects accounts of UFOs at American nuclear bases, tells this on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, passing on what a man named John Mills told him. f-lee-bailey-on-the-cia-s-index-4-during: Dan Sheehan, a lawyer, says that in 1973 in Washington, during the case of James McCord, one of the Watergate burglars, he found out that the famous defense lawyer F. faa-supervisor-tracks-five-unknowns-near: Robert Hastings, author of a book about UFOs at nuclear weapons sites, says that as a teenager working as a janitor at Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana, home to nuclear missiles, a man at a radar desk called him over. fabio-furtado-sees-object-land-on-his-fa: James Fox, a UFO investigator and filmmaker, tells on Jesse Michels' podcast what a farmer named Fabio Furtado told him about January 1996, on a farm near the town of Varginha in Brazil. face-and-five-sided-pyramid-at-cydonia-m: A researcher named John Brandenburg, speaking with a podcast host, Jesse Michels, talks about Cydonia Mensa, a region of Mars where a hill photographed from orbit in 1976 is said to look like a human face. facebook-page-leads-to-michael-johnson-2: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in 2026 a fan of his show named Jason Miller sent him a Facebook page that had just been sitting there online. fail-safe-and-human-obsolescence-1963: James Madden, a writer on philosophy and consciousness, speaks on Jesse Michels' podcast about Fail-Safe, a film from around 1963 or 1964 that he says was based on a novel. failing-cia-polygraphs-because-he-knew-t: A former officer of the CIA, the US spy agency, named Rolf Mowatt-Larssen, says the agency became so suspicious at one point that he could no longer pass a polygraph, a lie detector test. fake-darpa-guest-exposed-by-an-email-fro: A man who runs his own interview show, Jay Anderson, says he once had on a guest who claimed to be from DARPA, the US military's advanced research agency. fake-military-ufo-letter-used-to-test-bi: On Jesse Michels's podcast, a writer named Greg Bishop retells what a UFO researcher named Bill Moore told him about the years around 1979 and 1980. fake-videos-offered-to-james-fox: A surgeon from Brazil named Italo Venturelli, speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast, talks about a man named James Fox. faked-gemini-spacewalk-photo-of-michael-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that a photo from Gemini, NASA's two-person spaceflight programme of the 1960s, said to show astronaut Michael Collins on a spacewalk, is verifiably fake. falcon-and-the-mj-12-films-from-dia-humi: Eric Davis, a physicist who has worked on Pentagon research, says on Jesse Michels' podcast that in the 1980s an officer of the Defense Intelligence Agency, the Pentagon's military spy agency, code-named Falcon, was sent to meet two UFO researchers, Jaime Shandera and Bill Moore. falcon-space-biefeld-brown-vacuum-test-r: A researcher named David, speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast, describes a vacuum chamber test by a group called Falcon Space of the Biefeld-Brown effect, a claimed push produced by high-voltage electrical devices that some link to antigravity. falsified-evidence-aimed-at-a-treason-de: A man named Dylan Borland, who has come forward claiming knowledge of secret UFO matters, says that in 2025 people in the US government faked evidence against him. families-selected-for-the-program-by-dem: A former Air Force sergeant named Dan Sherman, who says the NSA, the US government's code and signals spy agency, hired him to communicate with aliens, tells this on Jesse Michels's podcast. faraday-cage-test-at-the-monroe-institut: A man named Chris Bledsoe, who says UFOs seem drawn to him, tells of a test in 2025 at the Monroe Institute, a centre in Virginia that studies consciousness. faraday-finds-that-magnetic-fields-chang: A biologist and writer named Rupert Sheldrake, talking with a podcast host, Jesse Michels, recalls the 19th-century scientist Michael Faraday. farmington-armada-1950: In 1950, in Farmington, a town in New Mexico, people say huge numbers of silver discs flew over the sky. farouk-el-baz-the-king-of-apollo-site-se: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Farouk El-Baz, a scientist who oversaw lunar science planning for Apollo, NASA's moon landing programme of the 1960s, and helped pick where the astronauts landed, was nicknamed "the king" by the astronauts. fascist-elite-preparing-a-thousand-year-: A researcher named Jason Jorjani, speaking with a podcast host, Jesse Michels, puts forward an idea about the "thousand-year Reich," the lasting empire Nazi Germany promised itself. fast-walkers-code-word-for-ufos-in-space: Maaneli Derakhshani, a guest on Jesse Michels's podcast, says that the US Space Force, Northern Command (NORTHCOM, the military command that defends North America) and NORAD (the joint US and Canadian air and space defense command) have their own term for UFOs in space: "fast walkers." fast-walkers-exempt-from-foia-defense-su: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that "fast walkers," a term for very fast objects picked up by the Defense Support Program, a US military satellite system watching from high orbit, are still off limits under FOIA, a US law that lets anyone request government records. fast-walkers-in-the-wikileaks-email-betw: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that "fast walkers", a phrase used for unknown objects seen moving fast, which he links to things in high orbit around Earth, comes up in a leaked email. fatal-aircraft-mishap-and-four-lost-hour: A doctor named Greg Rogers, who says he later worked with NASA, describes his time as an Army captain and flight surgeon, a doctor who looks after pilots, in a unit called the Third Attack Battalion. father-k-takes-tyler-under-his-wing-in-r: A professor who studies religion, Diana Pasulka, says that around 2017 she visited the Vatican with a man she calls Tyler. father-peter-rinaldi-s-meeting-on-the-sh: Whitley Strieber, a writer, says that sometime in the 1970s in New York, a priest named Father Peter Rinaldi, a friend of Strieber's wife Anne, called her and invited them to a meeting. father-s-cylindrical-ufo-sighting: A scientist named Steve Coburn, speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast, passes on a story from his father. He says his father once saw a UFO over central California, shaped like a cylinder with a red light on the front.
father-s-generation-called-ufos-at-nucle: On Jesse Michels's podcast, a guest named Pippa Malmgren passes on what her father told her about nuclear bomb test sites in the 1950s and 1960s. father-s-racehorse-fixing-overheard-as-a: Bob Lazar, a man known for saying he worked on secret craft for the US government, says that as a small boy in the early 1970s, at the family home on Long Island, New York, he played in the living room while his father and other men decided who would win a horse race. father-s-ship-crew-sees-an-object-leave-: On Jesse Michels's podcast, a former nuclear base guard named Mario Woods passes on stories from his father, a seafaring man from Honduras who he says saw many strange things in the jungles and at sea. fathers-of-the-space-programs-thought-th: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says, passing on what a researcher named Diana Pasulka told him, that the men who started the big space programs all believed they were in contact with non-human beings: Jack Parsons, who founded the Jet Propulsion Laboratory, an American rocket lab, along with the Russian rocket pioneer Konstantin Tsiolkovsky and Germany's Wernher von Braun. fbi-agent-guy-hottel-investigates-condon: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in the early 1950s an FBI field agent in Washington named Guy Hottel was investigating Edward Condon, a physicist, and building a file on him. fbi-briefing-to-congress-and-ongoing-fbi: Ross Coulthart, a journalist who reports on UFOs, says on Jesse Michels' podcast that he was told a 2025 briefing the FBI, the US federal police, gave to members of Congress in Washington really blew people away. fbi-calls-brigham-young-its-top-recruiti: Matthew Pines, a researcher speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast, says the FBI, the US federal police and domestic intelligence agency, has talked about Brigham Young University, a Mormon university in Utah, as its top source of recruits. fbi-document-calling-brown-the-navy-s-le: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says an FBI document from the 1940s, now circulating, describes the scientist Thomas Townsend Brown, whom Michels links to gravity research, as the lead radar scientist in the entire US Navy, knowing more about radar than anyone else there. fbi-documents-tracking-puharich-s-moveme: A researcher named Greg says on Jesse Michels' podcast that, using a US law that lets anyone request government records, the only thing his team could get was a large batch of FBI files on Andrija Puharich, a scientist said to have links to the CIA and to have contacted an alien council. fbi-image-cheapening-of-jean-seberg-1970: Eric Weinstein, a mathematician, explains a tactic called "image cheapening", meaning ruining someone's reputation, while debating a scientist on Jesse Michels' podcast. fbi-memo-to-hoover-on-discs-and-balls-of: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in 1949 a memo, now public, was sent to J. fbi-records-on-karl-compton-destroyed-fo: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, reads out a reply that a records researcher named John Greenwald received in April 2014 after asking the FBI, the US federal police agency, for its files on Karl Compton, a leading American physicist. fbi-seizes-tesla-s-papers-after-his-deat: A former US Senate staff member, Kirk McConnell, speaking with a podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells what happened after the inventor Nikola Tesla died in 1943 at the New Yorker Hotel in New York. fbi-von-braun-sent-classified-documents-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that papers from the FBI, the US federal police agency, showed that the rocket engineer Wernher von Braun was once caught sending secret documents to his former Nazi colleagues working in the Soviet Union, sometime in the late 1940s or 1950s. fdr-letters-showing-awareness-of-the-phe: A UFO researcher, Richard Dolan, says he believes Franklin D. fdr-s-1937-desert-game-range-guarded-by-: Charles Hall, a man who says he spent years in the Nevada desert alongside tall white beings near Area 51, the secret US air base, tells of a wildlife refuge called the Desert Game Range. february-2026-white-sands-event-and-el-p: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, asks a guest what happened at White Sands, a military area in New Mexico, in February 2026, an event tied in the story to a closure of the airspace over El Paso, Texas. feds-ransack-chuck-clark-s-place-1990: James Fox, a UFO investigator and filmmaker, says on Jesse Michels' podcast that in the 1990s federal agents ransacked the home of Chuck Clark, a man living in the small town of Rachel, Nevada. felipe-vidal-santiago-and-the-umbrella-m: Dan Sheehan, a researcher speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast, says that at Dealey Plaza in Dallas, where President John F. felt-his-body-turn-to-stone-while-linked: A man named Jordan, who told podcast host Jesse Michels that he was taken into a secret UFO programme as a child, says he was once mentally linked to a craft when it was shot at, somewhere near directed energy weapons, meaning weapons that fire focused beams of energy. felt-the-virgin-mary-s-presence-and-guid: Rolf Mowatt-Larssen, presented on Jesse Michels's podcast as a former CIA chief (the CIA is the US foreign intelligence agency), says that in Portugal, around the late 1990s, he had an encounter with the Virgin Mary, the mother of Jesus. few-physicists-in-the-crash-retrieval-pr: A man named Charles, speaking on Jesse Michels' podcast, points back to Michels' previous interview, which he says showed how few physicists worked in the secret program said to recover crashed craft that are not of human origin. fewer-than-40-recovered-crashes-1930: Eric Davis, a physicist who has worked on Pentagon research, says the United States has recovered crashed craft that are not human-made, going back to the 1930s. feynman-and-wheeler-s-1945-paper-on-time: A biologist and writer named Rupert Sheldrake, talking with a podcast host, Jesse Michels, points to a 1945 paper by the physicists Richard Feynman and John Wheeler. feynman-s-any-questions-teaching-at-a-bu: A researcher named Eric Weinstein, on Jesse Michels' podcast, points to a story called "Any Questions?" from the memoirs of the famous physicist Richard Feynman. ffrdc-spun-off-from-trw-as-principal-con: Eric Davis, a physicist who has worked on Pentagon research, says on Jesse Michels' podcast that one government-funded research center, a nonprofit lab paid for by the federal government, began as a contractor in the 1960s after being spun off from TRW, a big American defense and aerospace company. fighter-jet-scrambled-and-possibly-fired: Lou Elizondo, who once led a small Pentagon office that studied unexplained aerial reports, talks on Jesse Michels' podcast about the glowing lights seen over Washington, D.C. in 1952. fighter-pilot-from-chile-meets-an-object: Aldo Rebello, described as Brazil's defense minister, told the podcast host Jesse Michels about several cases in Brazil's records of unexplained objects. One of them, he says, involved a pilot flying a fighter jet from Chile to Brazil in the 1980s who met an object that was measured moving at about 25,000 kilometres an hour. If true, that would be a speed far beyond any known aircraft.
fii-nocontract-marking-used-to-hide-ufo-: An online UFO researcher who goes by UAPGerb, speaking on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels in January 2026, describes a document label called "FII NOCONTRACT". He gives credit for the documents to a proposed US law on disclosing UFO records, and if he is right, it would mean UFO work is tucked away inside America's nuclear labs.
files-show-george-joannides-lied-about-r: A researcher named Jeremy Riss, on Jesse Michels's podcast in 2025, talks about a CIA officer named George Joannides. Riss says Joannides ran a psychological warfare program out of JM WAVE, the CIA's Miami station of the early 1960s that worked against Cuba. He says recently released files on President Kennedy's assassination prove Joannides later lied to Congress about that role, which would mean the CIA hid what it knew from the people investigating the killing.
filippo-and-corrado-conclude-the-structu: A researcher named Filippo, speaking with podcast host Jesse Michels about what he calls a huge energy grid beneath the pyramids of Giza in Egypt, says that he and a colleague named Corrado studied the structures they found under the ground. He says the two of them agree that whatever is down there is man-made, which, if true, would mean ancient builders made something large and hidden under the pyramids.
final-casino-meeting-with-dennis-mariani: This story comes from Bob Lazar, a man known for claims about secret work he says he did in the Nevada desert, and it is set in a Las Vegas casino in 1989. Lazar says he went to meet a man named Dennis Mariani there. He says he kept saying, "Dennis, I'm here, what do you want?" but Mariani never even looked up at him. Lazar says he walked over to his friend Gene Huff, and when the two of them turned back around, Mariani was gone. The story is also told on the same podcast episode, hosted by Jesse Michels, by a guest named Luigi, who says he heard it from Gene Huff. In Luigi's version, Mariani was a blonde, military-looking man who did not even look at Lazar while Lazar talked to him. Why anyone tells it: if true, it would suggest Lazar was being watched or handled by people he could not identify.
finding-the-tsar-s-submarine-som-and-que: Dennis Asberg, a Swedish treasure hunter who searches the Baltic Sea floor between Sweden and Finland, says that in 2015 he and his team, including Peter Lindberg, found the wreck of Som, a submarine built around 1904 for the Russian Tsar. He tells podcast host Jesse Michels that after the find he was questioned in Stockholm by what he calls the Swedish "FBI", meaning the country's security police. He tells it as part of his wider story of the Baltic, where he also says he found a strange object on the seafloor.
fire-department-captures-screaming-being: A documentary filmmaker named James Fox, on Jesse Michels's podcast in 2025, passes on what a witness told him about January 1996 in the Brazilian town of Varginha. According to that account, local firefighters caught a strange screaming creature with a net, the way they would catch a wild animal. If true, it would mean a living non-human being was captured by ordinary town workers.
fireballs-seen-over-washington-dc-in-the: A former government official named Eric Haseltine, speaking on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, mentions flying fireballs that were seen over Washington DC in the 1950s. He says these sightings seem to have some credibility, which would matter because it would mean strange objects were showing up over the US capital itself.
first-agreements-with-the-tall-whites-sp: Charles Hall says that from 1965 to 1967, while working in the desert near Indian Springs, Nevada, he met tall, pale non-human beings he calls the tall whites. He tells podcast host Jesse Michels that once he accepted they were real, he made agreements with them: they would talk among themselves in English whenever they were near him, and he would sing to announce he was coming. If true, it would mean humans and aliens were living side by side, by agreement, on a US military range.
first-allagash-sighting-sphere-of-light-: Charlie Foltz says that in 1976 he was camping with friends, among them Jim Weiner, at the Mud Pond campsite on Chamberlain Lake, along the Allagash Waterway in the woods of Maine. He tells podcast host Jesse Michels that someone from another group of campers shouted "What the hell is that over there?", and across the lake they all saw a sphere of light drifting very slowly, like a balloon, but moving into the wind. He tells it as the first strange sighting of a trip that he says later turned into an alien abduction.
first-captain-gives-economic-destabiliza: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, retells the account of Dan Sherman, a former Air Force sergeant who says the National Security Agency, the US spy agency for communications, hired him in the early 1990s to talk with aliens. According to the telling, when Sherman asked a captain he worked under at the agency's complex in Maryland why it was all kept secret, the captain said it was to avoid economic destabilization, meaning the news could shake the economy.
first-cia-director-on-the-nicap-board-19: A researcher named Dylan Borland, speaking with a podcast host, Jesse Michels, talks about NICAP, a private civilian group that investigated UFO reports in the 1950s and 60s. Borland says that Roscoe Hillenkoetter, a Navy admiral who was the first director of the CIA, the US foreign intelligence agency, sat on NICAP's board of directors. He tells it because, if true, it would mean a top intelligence figure took UFOs seriously.
first-classified-tour-on-eleuthera-baham: Joe McMoneagle, a guest of podcast host Jesse Michels, says his first secret military posting, in the 1960s, was an 18-month tour on Eleuthera, an island in the Bahamas. He says the work there was hidden behind a cover story of air-sea rescue, and he tells it as the start of a career spent inside classified government work.
first-earth-battalion-sergeant-kills-a-g: A former Army psychic spy named Lyn Buchanan, on Jesse Michels's podcast in 2026, passes on a story he credits to Jim Channon, the Army officer behind the First Earth Battalion, an unusual Army idea about soldiers using mental and spiritual powers. As Buchanan tells it, a sergeant in that group killed a goat using only his mind, felt himself dying along with the goat, and later stole a helicopter and disappeared. If true, it would mean the Army had people who could kill with thought alone.
first-exodus-patent-and-a-possible-natio: A man named Charles, from a company called Exodus Propulsion, says that some patents, the legal protections for inventions, apparently get sent through the Department of Defense. He points to the Invention Secrecy Act of 1952, a US law that lets the government keep certain inventions secret for national security, and suggests their first patent may have been held up that way. If true, it would mean the government saw their work as sensitive enough to keep secret.
first-foo-fighter-reports-november-1944: Merrick von Renenamp, speaking on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, marks an anniversary: he says the first reports of "Foo Fighters" came in November 1944. Foo Fighters was the nickname for strange lights that wartime pilots said they saw near their planes. He brings up the date because, to him, those reports are where the modern story of unexplained objects in the sky begins.
first-goetheanum-burned-as-a-rival-to-na: A researcher named Jason Jorjani, speaking with a podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells about the first Goetheanum, the headquarters building in Dornach, Switzerland, of anthroposophy, a spiritual movement founded by Rudolf Steiner, which burned down in the 1920s. Jorjani says the Nazis burned it because they thought anthroposophy could become a real rival to Nazism. If true, it would show how seriously the Nazis took competing spiritual movements.
first-hypnotic-regression-tall-being-wor: Mario Woods, a former guard at a nuclear weapons site, says that in 1977 in South Dakota he was taken aboard a craft. He tells podcast host Jesse Michels that during his first hypnotic regression, a session where a hypnotist helps someone recall buried memories, done with a man named Bob Upton, he remembered a very tall being working on him. If true, it would mean beings were abducting the people guarding America's nuclear weapons.
first-intuitive-communication-received-i: Dan Sherman, a former US Air Force sergeant, says the NSA, the US agency that intercepts and handles secret communications, hired him to talk with aliens through his mind. He tells podcast host Jesse Michels that in the early 1990s, at an overseas base, he sat in a C-van, a trailer packed with communications gear, and some time later the first message came into his head. He says that was when the ball started rolling, which, if true, would mean the government had a working mental channel to non-humans.
first-mobile-phone-ufo-photo-matched-to-: Clas Svahn, a Swedish UFO researcher who keeps a large archive of reports, says that in 2005 someone at a cottage in northern Sweden took what he calls the first mobile phone picture of a UFO in Sweden. He tells podcast host Jesse Michels that the sighting was matched to something seen on military radar at the same time, which, if true, would mean the object was physical and not a trick of the camera. In another moment of the same talk he places the object over a lake rather than at the cottage.
first-observation-of-the-force-laser-dis: Charles Buer, introduced on a podcast as a former NASA leader working on new propulsion, says that around 2010, in a lab in Florida, he first saw a force predicted by his own theory. He says it showed up in a laser test that measured tiny movements, done with a colleague named Nathan and a scientist, Dr. Sid Clemens. If true, it would be an early sign of a way to push objects without ordinary engines, something like antigravity.
first-peer-reviewed-paper-on-the-khufu-p: Filippo Biondi, a scientist who uses satellite radar to look beneath Egypt's pyramids, says he and his team published their first peer-reviewed paper, one checked by other scientists, on the Great Pyramid of Khufu in about 2021 or 2022. He says it is online for anyone to read and that it describes hidden structures inside the pyramid. A researcher named Jeffrey Drum dates that first paper to 2020 instead, and says many people do not know it exists.
first-question-at-eg-g-was-about-john-le: Bob Lazar, a man who says he once worked on secret flying craft in the Nevada desert, says that in 1988 he went for a job interview at EG&G, a defense contractor in Las Vegas. He says that when he sat down, maybe the very first question was about John Lear, a man Lazar knew. He tells it as a sign that the people hiring him already knew a lot about who he spent time with.
first-skywatcher-observation-class-1-tet: James Valor, from Skywatcher, a startup that says it can call up unexplained objects in the sky, says his first sighting came in 2021 during a US military war game, a practice battle exercise, at a site he does not name. He says they saw what they later rated a "first class" object in a four-part "tetra" formation, and he credits a person called Mr. K. If true, it would mean these objects show up near military drills and can be sorted and studied.
first-trip-to-egypt-and-inside-the-pyram: Filippo Biondi, a scientist who says he scanned beneath the pyramids of Giza in Egypt, tells podcast host Jesse Michels that in 2025, about two weeks before they spoke, he went to Egypt for the first time and went inside the pyramids. The trip ties into his claims that huge tubes and tunnels lie deep under the pyramids and the Sphinx, which, if true, would change what we know about who built them and why.
first-ufo-recorded-within-a-week-of-the-: Joe McMoneagle, a guest on a podcast, says, passing on what he was told, that the first UFO ever recorded appeared within seven days of Trinity, the first atomic bomb test, set off in New Mexico in 1945. If true, it would tie the arrival of UFOs to the start of the nuclear age.
first-videotaped-grusch-interview-at-bry: Bryce Zabel, a man who works in Hollywood, says that in 2023 the first videotaped interview with David Grusch, a former government insider who came forward about secret UFO programmes, was filmed at his house in Los Angeles, with Ross Coulthart and someone named Jared involved. He tells podcast host Jesse Michels that Grusch showed up for it in cargo shorts and a t-shirt, a small human detail from the start of a story that, if true, helped bring claims about hidden UFO programmes into public view.
first-voice-download-after-high-school-r: A man named Brent, speaking on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, says that just after he finished high school he heard a voice in his head for the first time. He says the message was "reality is subjective," and that it made no sense to him then. He tells it as the first of several such messages, which would mean something outside him was speaking to him.
fisherman-sees-an-orb-explode-off-ubatub: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, retells a case raised by Garry Nolan, a Stanford scientist who studies material said to come from unexplained objects. According to Michels, a fisherman near Ubatuba, on the coast of Brazil, saw a glowing ball explode over the sea and gathered up some of the pieces that fell. Michels calls it one of Nolan's most interesting samples, because if the story holds, it would be physical debris from something unexplained.
fitness-beats-truth-theorem-in-evolution: Don Hoffman, a scientist who studies how we perceive the world, describes a result he calls "fitness beats truth," built on evolutionary game theory, the maths of how traits win out under natural selection, a field shaped by the biologist John Maynard Smith and rooted in Darwin. He says his team found the chance is zero that any creature's senses evolved to show the world as it really is, only what helps it survive. If true, he suggests, it could mean much of reality, maybe even other intelligences, is hidden from us.
fitts-sees-hud-s-unauditable-books-on-li: Richard Dolan, a writer on Jesse Michels' podcast, relays a story from Catherine Austin Fitts, a former official at HUD, the US Department of Housing and Urban Development, from around the late 1980s and early 1990s. According to Fitts, when she asked for the department's books, staff wheeled in old library carts one after another, stacked with papers in no real order, so the accounts could not be audited. Dolan tells it to suggest that large sums of government money could not be traced.
fitts-tells-tucker-carlson-the-money-goe: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, recalls an interview that a woman named Katherine Austin Fitts gave to Tucker Carlson, a well-known television and podcast interviewer. According to Michels, Carlson asked her where all the missing money was going, and she told him to talk to Richard Dolan, the writer who was Michels' guest that day, and then answered with one word: "Space." It gets told because, if true, it would mean large sums of hidden government money are being spent on a secret space effort.
fitts-trillions-missing-from-dod-budget-: This story is about money. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says a woman named Catherine Austin Fitts talks about trillions of dollars missing from the budget of the Department of Defense, the US military, going to secret projects. A guest who goes by UAPGerb puts a figure on it, saying Fitts speaks of 17 to 21 trillion dollars hidden in secret military spending since the 1990s. If true, it would mean there is a vast hidden pot of money that could pay for programmes the public never hears about.
five-executive-orders-given-to-the-presi: Steven Greer, a man who has long argued that the truth about UFOs is being kept secret, told the podcast host Jesse Michels in 2025 that he was trying to get the US president to sign five executive orders, which are direct orders a president can issue without Congress.
