five-transients-appearing-and-vanishing-: An astronomer, Beatriz Villarroel, studies old photographic glass plates of the night sky taken at the Palomar Observatory, looking for points of light that appear and then vanish. She says one plate from July 27, 1952 shows five such objects lined up in a narrow band. If true, it could point to unexplained objects near Earth caught on film long ago.
five-uap-incidents-at-vandenberg-2003-20: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that between 2003 and 2005 there were five incidents involving UAP, the government's term for unidentified objects in the sky, at Vandenberg Air Force Base, a rocket and missile base on the California coast. He mentions it in an episode about a nuclear missile guard who says he was taken by aliens, as a sign that such bases draw these sightings.
five-years-of-psychokinesis-experiments-: A man named Joe McMoneagle, speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast, says he took part in five years of experiments at a research lab meant to prove psychokinesis, the idea that the mind can move or affect objects. According to him, the researchers could never isolate the target of the effect, so the work never gave a clean proof.
flames-shoot-from-kuromanta-during-an-ex: A pyramid researcher, Geoffrey Drumm, describes an excavation at Kuromanta, a mountain in Akita, Japan, that some call a pyramid, drawing on a book by a man named Suzuki about the dig. He says that during a thunderstorm the diggers looked up and saw flames shooting out of the top of the mountain. If true, it would suggest the mountain is something more than an ordinary hill.
fleeing-a-close-encounters-screening-in-: Mario Woods, a former guard at a US nuclear weapons site who says he was abducted, tells of going to see Close Encounters of the Third Kind, a 1977 film about people meeting aliens, at a theatre on Main Street in Rapid City, South Dakota. He says he jumped out of his seat, ran outside and sat on the curb, because the film felt like a replay of what he himself had been through. In a later telling he simply says he got up and fled the theatre.
flexner-report-reshapes-american-medicin: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in 1910 a study called the Flexner report, written by Abraham Flexner, came out with funding from the oil tycoon John D. Rockefeller and his fellow industrialist Andrew Carnegie. In his telling, the report changed how American medicine worked. He tells it in an episode about drug companies and human experiments, as part of a story about who has shaped medicine and science behind the scenes.
flight-19-and-the-lost-pby-from-banana-r: Greg Rogers, a doctor who has worked with NASA, the US space agency, talks about Flight 19, a group of Navy planes lost in 1945 in the Bermuda Triangle, a stretch of ocean off Florida known for disappearances, and a PBY, a Navy seaplane, that went missing from Banana River Naval Air Station, later Patrick Air Force Base. He says he spoke with men who were working flight operations there that day. Their accounts matter because they would be firsthand memories of one of the most famous vanishings at sea.
flight-surgeon-gum-exam-burns-and-skin-s: Mario Woods, who says he was an Air Force guard at nuclear missile sites, tells of a 1977 visit to a military doctor at Ellsworth Air Force Base in South Dakota after what he describes as an abduction. He says the doctor checked his gums and pointed out burns above his right eye and on the back of his right hand, while agents of the Air Force Office of Special Investigations, its internal investigative police, looked on. In a later telling he adds that the doctor clipped off a piece of skin and sealed it in a corked tube on a tray, which, if true, would mean the military took his encounter seriously enough to collect samples.
flight-with-jake-barber-over-a-lockheed-: Eric Burlison, a US congressman, says that around 2024 or 2025 he flew with a man named Jake Barber over a desert site near Burbank, California, belonging to Lockheed Martin, a large US defense company. He says they saw a bowl-shaped structure in the ground with a huge hangar door, clearly built underground, and that white vans came racing out as they circled. He tells it as a hint of hidden facilities that might hold secrets he is trying to uncover.
flir-gimbal-and-gofast-navy-videos-2004: A guest named Karl Nell, speaking from the official record, describes three US Navy videos known informally as FLIR (after the infrared camera that filmed it), Gimbal and GoFast, which show unidentified flying objects. He says the Pentagon has stated that these objects are neither American nor from any rival country, and that the events date from 2004 and 2015. If so, the US military has filmed craft that belong to no known nation.
flir1-object-may-be-a-balloon-2004: In 2004, off Southern California, a Navy jet's infrared camera recorded a short video of an unknown object, now known as FLIR1 (FLIR means forward-looking infrared, a heat-sensing camera). Mick West, a researcher known for skeptical analysis of UFO videos, says on Jesse Michels's podcast that the evidence suggests the object is actually a balloon. If he is right, one of the best-known Navy UFO videos would show something ordinary.
flir1-video-leaked-on-a-german-server-be: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that FLIR1, a military infrared camera video of an unexplained object, was already floating around online before 2017, posted on Reddit, a large discussion website, and even on a German server. He tells it because, if true, it would mean the footage was out in public well before it got wide attention.
flood-dated-up-to-40-000-years-ago-from-: A researcher identified only as Matt, speaking on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, talks about the great flood told of in ancient stories from Mesopotamia, the land of modern Iraq. Matt says the flood could have happened up to 40,000 years ago, based on ice cores, long columns of ice drilled from Greenland and Antarctica that record past climate, and on earlier climate events when floods could have occurred. If true, the old flood stories would reach back much further than usually thought.
florida-channel-wakes-up-with-an-unexpla: A researcher called Greg, on Jesse Michels's podcast in 2026, tells a story from the early 1970s in Florida drawn from a book called The Stargate Conspiracy. It involves a medium, a person said to channel messages from beyond, linked to Phyllis Schlemmer and the researcher Andrija Puharich, who say they were in contact with an alien council. Greg says the man woke up to find a metal filling in his tooth that he never had before, which, if true, would be physical evidence of something done to him from outside.
florida-coastline-extended-4050-miles-ea: Randall Carlson, a researcher of ancient history and catastrophes, says that about 14,000 years ago the Florida coast near Miami lay 40 to 50 miles further east than it does today. According to him, where the beach is now there would have been forest, a point he uses to show how much the Earth's surface has changed within human times.
fluttering-leaf-reports-are-ours-1950: In a documentary about a scientist named Townsend Brown, a woman named Jan Lundquist recalls that Linda Brown, who received UFO reports in the 1950s, was told to filter out the ones describing a motion like a fluttering leaf, because, he said, 'those are ours.' If true, it would mean some of the craft people reported as UFOs were secret American aircraft.
flying-craft-in-ancient-indian-texts: A UFO researcher named Steven Greer, on Jesse Michels' podcast, says that ancient Indian scriptures such as the Bhagavad Gita and the Vedas describe vimanas, flying craft. If true, it would mean people saw advanced flying machines thousands of years ago.
flying-craft-through-the-mind-for-a-brai: A man named Jordan Jose says that as a child, around 2008 to 2010, he was taken into a secret UFO programme at a place called Baker Victory Services in Western New York. He says the work involved linking a brain to a machine, because unidentified craft, which he calls UAP (the government's term for unidentified anomalous phenomena) and UFOs, are not flown with joysticks but through the mind. If true, it would mean children were used to learn how to pilot such craft.
flying-lotus-attends-the-tridactyl-unvei: A well-known hip hop musician who goes by Flying Lotus says that in the 2020s he went to a presentation near his home in the Los Angeles area about small three-fingered bodies said to be non-human, linked to a presenter named Jaime Maussan. He says the bodies themselves were not there, but the presenters showed photos and X-rays meant to show they were real.
flying-saucer-observatory-detection-over: A UFO researcher, Grant Cameron, tells of Project Magnet, a Canadian government effort in the 1950s, tied to the engineer Wilbert Smith, that set up a station near Ottawa to detect flying saucers. He says that on August 8, 1954, a week after a forewarning linked to a woman named Frances Swan, something flew over and, according to a man who was in the building, all the alarms went off. Cameron ties this to the project being shut down, which, if true, would mean it was ended just after it caught something.
fmri-study-of-brilliant-moves-in-the-gam: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, describes a study in which a person's brain was hooked up to an fMRI, a scanner that shows which parts of the brain are active, while they played Go, an ancient strategy board game. He brings it up in an episode about children said to read minds, as a way of asking where brilliant, intuitive moves come from.
foggy-night-encounter-with-a-scout-craft: Charles Hall, who says he lived near tall white beings in the Nevada desert, tells of a cold, snowy, foggy night in the fall sometime in the 1960s in Indian Springs Valley, Nevada. He says he nearly died in the fog and met a small "scout craft" flown by a young woman of those beings and some of her friends, with larger craft he calls the deep spacecraft and the teenage craft nearby.
foia-releases-of-thousands-of-ufo-pages-: A UFO researcher, Richard Dolan, says that in the late 1970s and early 1980s, requests under the Freedom of Information Act, a US law that lets anyone request government records, suddenly freed thousands of pages about UFOs. He says they included records of military jets failing to intercept objects, memos from the CIA, America's spy agency, and investigations by the FBI, its federal police. To him this shows the government took the subject seriously while saying little in public.
foia-request-for-usaf-campinas-flight-re: UFO researcher James Fox says his team used the Freedom of Information Act, a US law that lets anyone request government records, to ask the US Air Force for flight records linked to events in 1996 around Campinas, a city in Brazil. He says they filed it around 2022, and that the answer came back not from the Air Force but from the CIA, the US spy agency, which he takes as a sign the matter interested the intelligence world.
followed-by-a-12-year-old-tall-white-gir: Charles Hall, who says he served at Nellis Air Force Base in Nevada in the 1960s, tells of beings he calls the tall whites, very tall, pale non-human people he says lived near the base's test ranges. He says that in 1965, as he walked back to his barracks, a tall white girl he describes as about 12 years old followed him, which, if true, would mean these beings had families living alongside the military.
followed-during-his-clearance-and-told-g: Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked on secret craft in Nevada, says that in 1989 in Las Vegas, while the government was checking him for a security clearance, the approval needed to handle secrets, someone was always parked outside his house. He says he got scared and told his friend Gene Huff. He tells it as part of how he came to feel watched, and why he later went public.
followers-of-horus-secret-societies-pres: A writer on lost ancient civilisations, Graham Hancock, drawing on his book Talisman written with Robert Bauval, says the Followers of Horus in ancient Egypt, named for the falcon-headed god, were secret societies. He says they were trusted to keep knowledge from what the Egyptians called the First Time, a distant early age, and pass it down the generations. If true, it would mean wisdom from a forgotten older civilisation survived through hidden groups.
following-david-grusch-from-his-testimon: Jesse Michels, a podcast host, says that in 2023 he followed David Grusch, a former intelligence official who testified to Congress about UFOs, from his testimony on Capitol Hill in Washington back home to Colorado. Michels says they had a great time, and with someone named Omar he made a short documentary about it. He tells it as his close look at a key moment when these claims reached the US government.
following-the-second-van-to-noise-cancel: Dan Sherman, a former Air Force sergeant who says the National Security Agency, the US spy agency for communications, trained him to communicate with aliens, tells of an episode in 1991 near an agency training site in Linthicum, Maryland. He says he followed a second van and watched it go to a company called Noise Cancellation Technologies, suggesting a link between his secret programme and a private firm.
foo-fighters-and-swedish-ghost-rockets-1: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells of the "foo fighters," the nickname for glowing balls that pilots reported during the Second World War, from about 1942 to 1945. He says Allied and German-side fighter pilots alike saw what looked like ball lightning that moved as if it were being controlled, and the story is grouped with the "ghost rockets" reported over Sweden just after the war. Michels places them differently in different episodes, once over Europe in general, once over Germany, and once specifically in Bavaria in southern Germany, and he tells it as an early sign that something was flying around that no side understood.
foo-fighters-drawn-to-wwii-atomic-and-mi: During World War II, around 1944 and 1945 over southern Germany, aircrews reported strange glowing objects they called foo fighters. Lou Elizondo, a well-known voice on UFOs, says on Jesse Michels's podcast that today's unidentified objects (which officials call UAP, unidentified anomalous phenomena) seem interested in nuclear and military capabilities. He suggests the foo fighters appeared because of what was going on at the height of the war, which would mean these objects have been watching human weapons for a long time.
footage-of-the-varginha-alien-transport-: Documentary filmmaker James Fox, on Jesse Michels's podcast in 2024, talks about the 1996 events in Varginha, Brazil, where people say a living creature was captured. Fox relays what sources, a man named Marco and an unnamed military man, told him: that there is footage of the creature being moved from a military base into town, to a hospital, and back again. If that footage exists, it would show the military handling a non-human being.
football-field-sized-vehicles-moving-thr: The podcast host Joe Rogan, speaking with host Jesse Michels, repeats a claim he credits to the US politician Marco Rubio in a documentary called The Age of Disclosure. According to Rogan, there are vehicles as big as a football field moving through the ocean at 500 knots, close to 600 miles an hour, which would be far beyond any known submarine.
force-fields-bending-light-seen-in-the-n: Charles Hall, a man who says he spent years among tall white beings in Nevada, points to the Navy "Tic Tac" video, footage taken by Navy fighter pilots in 2004 of a white oval object shaped like the mint. He says the craft are wrapped in force fields that interact with light, and that you can see this bending of light in that video. If he is right, the video would show the same technology he says he saw up close.
ford-chooses-nazi-trucks-over-uk-engines: A speaker known as JASON says on Jesse Michels's podcast that, around World War II, the car company Ford was asked to build engines for Britain and refused. According to JASON, Ford said it was prioritizing trucks for Nazi Germany, a claim he uses to show powerful companies working with both sides.
ford-s-new-nsa-intelligence-system-1974: Harold Malmgren, a former advisor to US presidents, says that in 1974 at the White House, President Gerald Ford and his aide Bill Seidman asked him to set up a new intelligence system with the NSA, the US agency that gathers secret electronic intelligence. He tells it to show how close he was to sensitive government work, which would make his other claims about handling UFO material more weighty.
foreign-intelligence-attempts-to-penetra: Matthew Brown, presented on a podcast as a Pentagon whistleblower, says there have been times when it felt like foreign spy services were trying to break into his network of contacts to get information out of it. foreign-men-offer-luiza-cash-in-dollars-: Documentary filmmaker James Fox, on Jesse Michels's podcast in 2025, passes on what a woman named Luiza told him about the 1996 creature sightings in Varginha, Brazil. forensic-pathologists-with-physical-evid: This story is about Varginha, a town in Brazil where, in 1996, people say a strange creature was captured. If true, it would mean there is medical paperwork linking a death to contact with a non-human creature.
formation-of-skywatcher-technologies-202: Jake Barber, a man who says he once carried a UFO with his helicopter for a secret government program, says that after leaving that program he and others formed a company called Skywatcher Technologies. A member of the team, Matthew Pines, says its aim is to use private money and the skills they gained inside the program to gather enough evidence to convince more people that the phenomenon is real. Another member, James Valor, puts it differently: he says the company was created through UAP, the official term for unexplained objects in the sky. If true, people from inside a hidden government effort are now trying to show the public what they saw. So the story comes from the founders themselves, each describing the company in his own words on the same podcast.
former-captain-introduces-new-ppd-contac: Dan Sherman, a former Air Force sergeant who says he was secretly trained to receive messages from aliens in his head, says that in the early 1990s he was working his regular job at a large shared military post he calls Base 2. He says the captain who used to oversee him, whom he calls Captain White, simply showed up at his workplace to introduce him to a new contact for the programme.
former-darpa-man-s-hopeful-monsters-hybr: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says he met a former worker at DARPA, the US military's agency for advanced research, who described a project he once proposed that was never approved, which is why he felt free to talk about it. Michels says it was a hybrid proposal based on the work of a scientist named Richard Goldschmidt and his idea of 'hopeful monsters', sudden big leaps in how living things change. If true, it would show the military at least considered building new kinds of beings.
former-dig-head-tells-congress-cia-spied: A filmmaker named Jeremy Corbell, on Jesse Michels's podcast in 2026, relays what a man he calls John, a former head of a government investigative group, told Congress. Corbell says the finding was that the CIA had been spying on UFO whistleblowers, people who came forward with inside claims. He mentions figures including intelligence chief Tulsi Gabbard, former Pentagon official Lou Elizondo, and journalist George Knapp. If true, it would mean the spy agency was watching the very people trying to talk.
former-dni-discusses-ufo-tracking-progra: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that a former director of national intelligence, the official who oversees all American spy agencies, has now spoken openly about a programme for tracking UFOs. He raises it as a sign that UFOs are being discussed at the very top of American intelligence.
former-employee-was-a-havana-syndrome-vi: Eric Hazeline, introduced on a podcast as a former director of the NSA (the US National Security Agency, which handles electronic spying and codebreaking), talked with podcast host Jesse Michels about Havana syndrome. That is the name for a set of unexplained health problems reported by US diplomats and intelligence staff. Hazeline says one of the people affected used to work for him and that he knows that person extremely well, which would put the problem very close to the top of American intelligence.
former-fortune-50-chairman-threatened-af: Steven Greer, a UFO researcher and activist, told podcast host Jesse Michels that in 2024 a retired chairman of one of America's fifty largest companies approached his group, apparently ready to speak about secret knowledge. Greer says that as soon as the man did this, an assassination team threatened to kill him, his whole family and his grandchildren. If true, it would mean someone is willing to use violence to keep powerful insiders quiet.
former-hells-angels-president-frozen-for: Brandon Fugal, the owner of a property called Skinwalker Ranch where he says strange things happen, tells of an October night sometime in the last decade behind a building on the ranch called Homestead 3. He says a man who had once led a large chapter of the Hells Angels motorcycle club was there working security, and that this man was frozen in place for about 10 minutes, which would mean something on the ranch can affect people's bodies.
former-ic-inspector-general-chuck-mccull: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, points out that Chuck McCullough, a man involved in the recent push for the US government to reveal what it knows about UFOs, used to be the Intelligence Community Inspector General, the official watchdog who investigates wrongdoing across America's spy agencies. Michels raises it to stress that people at the very top of the intelligence world are taking part, which would give the claims real weight if they hold up.
former-lockheed-cia-contractor-eg-g-scie: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in 2001 a man who had worked as a contractor for Lockheed, a major American aerospace and weapons company, and for the CIA, the US spy agency, went public. According to Michels, the man said Lockheed was working on UFO technology and that scientists hired through EG&G, a defense contractor, were running the work in private laboratories in Utah. If true, it would mean private companies, not just the government, hold and study such technology.
former-mayor-admits-the-event-city-build: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells of Varginha, a city in Brazil where people say a strange being was seen and captured in 1996. He says local farmers were among the witnesses, that the city's former mayor admits it happened, and that the city built a large model UFO statue to mark the event. He tells it to show that the town itself treats the story as real.
former-nsa-aaro-director-and-crowdsource: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, notes that the current head of AARO, the Pentagon office set up to investigate unidentified objects, is a former NSA man, the NSA being the US agency that intercepts communications. Michels uses this to float an idea: that releasing information about UFOs bit by bit may be a way to get the public to gather intelligence for the government, which would mean the slow disclosure is a deliberate tactic.
former-nsa-research-director-never-saw-a: Eric Haseltine used to be a senior research director in the US intelligence world. That includes the NSA, the National Security Agency, which collects electronic intelligence, and the Office of the Director of National Intelligence, which oversees all the spy agencies. Speaking with podcast host Jesse Michels, Haseltine says he had access to a great deal and never saw anything like that. He makes the point twice in the same interview. The second time he describes being made a "super user", someone cleared to see all of the Pentagon's walled-off secret programs. He says it was like the film Clockwork Orange, with his eyelids clamped open while he stared at the material for a whole day. He says he remembers none of it, but there was nothing about UFOs in there. It matters because if such a program existed, someone with his access might be expected to have come across it.
former-police-chief-pedro-aguiar-says-he: A documentary filmmaker named James Fox, on Jesse Michels' podcast, talks about Varginha, a town in Brazil where, people say, a strange living creature was captured in 1996. Fox says that a former police chief, Pedro Aguiar, eventually told his film team that he had taken part and was a witness, having seen the creature, perhaps its lower half, under a tarp. former-politico-journalist-asks-brent-ab: A man named Brent Friedman says that last November a journalist named Ben Schreckinger, who used to write for the news outlet Politico, asked him about a denial made by a man named John Harrington. former-soldier-sees-triangle-take-off-at: A UFO researcher who goes by the online name UAPGerb said on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels that he once talked with a former Army man who served in the mid 2010s. According to that man, he saw a triangle-shaped craft shoot off an airstrip at Area 51, a secretive US military test site in the Nevada desert. formula-given-to-brent-and-bryce-lost-fo: A writer named Brent Friedman tells this story on the show of a podcast host, Jesse Michels. He adds that his daughter found it around 2023 or 2024 in his garage in Washington. Brent is the only person telling it, and he tells it twice in the same interview, adding the detail about his daughter and the garage the second time. If it is what he believes, it would mean a strange gift from long ago has survived and can now be looked at again.
forrestal-flown-to-hobe-sound-reported-b: A UFO historian named Richard Dolan, speaking with a podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells about James Forrestal, the first US Secretary of Defense, in 1949. Dolan tells it as part of his argument that Forrestal's downfall was linked to UFO secrets.
forrestal-on-majestic-12-1947: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that James Forrestal, the first US Secretary of Defense in the late 1940s, was supposedly a member of Majestic 12. Majestic 12 is said by some to be a secret group of top officials and scientists set up to handle UFO matters. If true, it would mean UFOs were managed at the highest level of the US government.
forrestal-s-death-at-bethesda-1949: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, talks about the death of James Forrestal, the first US Secretary of Defense, in 1949. Michels says Forrestal ended up at the Navy's hospital in Bethesda, Maryland, and was "killed by gravity," putting the phrase in quotation marks. forrestal-s-limo-ride-with-symington-and: A UFO historian named Richard Dolan, speaking with a podcast host, Jesse Michels, describes James Forrestal, the first US Secretary of Defense, in 1949 after he was pushed out under President Harry Truman. forrestal-s-published-diaries-never-ment: Richard Dolan, a researcher who writes about UFO history, points out that James Forrestal, a US Defense Secretary of the 1940s, left diaries that were published in two volumes after his death. Dolan says those published diaries never mention UFOs. He raises it on Jesse Michels's podcast in an episode about claims that Forrestal's death was tied to the subject, where the silence matters because it would suggest that part of his record was left out.
forrestal-s-trips-to-paris-with-question: Harold Malmgren, a former advisor to US presidents, says on Jesse Michels's podcast that he found several records about James Forrestal, a top US defense official of the 1940s. According to Malmgren, these records show Forrestal going to Paris with questions and coming back with answers, which hints that a senior American official was quietly seeking knowledge abroad on secret matters.
forrestal-truman-meeting-dates-match-mj-: This story is about the Majestic 12 papers, a set of documents said to describe a secret group set up in 1947 to deal with UFOs. He points in particular to a paper known as the Eisenhower briefing document. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells it too, in his own words, and is more specific. He describes a memo from Truman to Forrestal dated 24 September 1947, and brings in the scientist Vannevar Bush, the first meeting of the National Security Council (the president's top security advisers), and the researcher Stanton Friedman. If the dates really match, believers say, it would suggest the papers were written by someone with real inside knowledge of 1947 Washington.
forrestal-unravels-says-he-is-followed-b: A UFO historian named Richard Dolan, speaking with a podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells how James Forrestal, the first US Secretary of Defense, seemed to come apart in Washington in 1948 and 1949. Dolan says Forrestal developed strange nervous tics and said he was being followed by "strange foreign looking men," with figures such as the newspaper columnist Drew Pearson and Air Force secretary Stuart Symington part of the story. Dolan tells it as part of his argument that Forrestal's end was tied to UFO secrets.
fort-worth-general-orders-blanchard-it-s: In 1947, near Roswell, New Mexico, the local Army air base said it had recovered something from a crash, and the story was soon changed to a weather balloon. If true, the balloon explanation was imposed from above rather than being what the base actually found.
fortune-10-scientist-with-free-energy-an: Steven Greer, a UFO researcher and activist, told podcast host Jesse Michels that in 2025 a scientist linked to one of America's ten largest companies flew in to meet him in Los Angeles. Greer calls the man a super genius and says he can build 'free energy' plasma devices, meaning machines said to produce power without fuel, and can do teleportation. If true, it would mean world-changing technology already exists out of public view.
fouche-and-the-tr3b-1970: This story is about Edgar Fouché, who calls himself a whistleblower about secret aircraft, and the TR-3B, said to be a flying triangle built by copying alien technology. Michels tells it differently: he says Fouché claimed to have been at Area 51, a secret US military base in Nevada, and knew about TR-3A and TR-3B craft from the defence company Northrop Grumman, powered by spinning mercury. fouche-saw-the-tr3b-twice-1990: An online researcher who goes by UAPGerb, on Jesse Michels' podcast, relays a claim by Edgar Fouche, a man who spoke at a 1998 UFO conference about secret aircraft. fouche-the-tr3b-uses-internal-mass-reduc: An online researcher who goes by UAPGerb, on Jesse Michels's podcast in 2026, passes on the claims of Edgar Fouche, a man who said he worked on secret aircraft. Fouche said a secret triangle-shaped craft called the TR3B does not use anti-gravity but "internal mass reduction", a way of cutting the craft's weight by about 89 percent. fouche-tr3b-program-led-by-nro-cia-and-n: An online researcher who goes by UAPGerb, on Jesse Michels's podcast in 2026, relays what Edgar Fouche, a man who said he worked on secret aircraft, claimed. fouche-tr3b-propulsion-reverse-engineere: An online researcher who goes by UAPGerb, on Jesse Michels's podcast in 2026, passes on a claim from Edgar Fouche, a man who said he worked on secret aircraft. founders-of-washington-copied-egypt-with: Chris Bledsoe, a man who says he draws UFOs to him, says a man named Robert Gilbert explained to him that the people who laid out Washington, DC copied ancient Egypt by raising obelisks, tall four-sided stone pillars. founding-myths-of-star-people-teaching-a: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, speaking with a Harvard astronomer, Avi Loeb, says that nearly every culture's founding myth talks about people from the stars teaching humans how to farm. He offers it as a hint that visitors from elsewhere may have shaped early human civilisation.
founding-of-nasa-s-electrostatics-lab-by: Charles Buer, introduced as a NASA scientist on Jesse Michels's podcast, describes the start of NASA's electrostatics lab at Kennedy Space Center in Florida, a lab that studies static electricity and electric charge. founding-of-the-pear-lab-by-bob-jahn-197: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that the PEAR lab, a research group at Princeton University that studied psychic effects and mind over matter, was started in 1979 by Bob Jahn. Michels tells it to show that serious scientists once took these questions on.
four-et-craft-appear-near-pensacola-1990: Steven Greer, a UFO researcher and activist, told podcast host Jesse Michels that in the early 1990s four craft from beings not from Earth suddenly appeared in the air near Pensacola, a city in Florida. In one telling he places it in 1992 on a beach, with a group of about 60 people gathered for a weekend to try to make contact. Greer says that after this, all kinds of insiders started coming to him, because to him it showed contact could be invited on purpose.
four-gliding-beings-in-uniforms-beside-t: Mario Woods, who says he was an Air Force guard at nuclear missile sites, tells of a night in 1977 at a missile launch site called November-5 near Nisland, South Dakota. four-hours-of-missing-time-and-crohn-s-d: Chris Bledsoe, a man from North Carolina, says that in January 2007, by a river there, he lost four hours he cannot account for and walked back to find his son missing. four-plus-four-tubes-descending-beneath-: Filippo Biondi, a researcher who has been scanning the ground beneath the pyramids at Giza in Egypt, told podcast host Jesse Michels in 2026 about what his work in the 2020s has found. He says his team counts four plus four tube-like shapes running downward under a pyramid, linking its base to something located far below. four-psychic-groups-of-ets-friends-enemi: Lyn Buchanan, a former US Army sergeant who worked in a military program on psychic abilities in the 1980s, says he took part in a study that compared the psychic ability of humans with that of extraterrestrials, meaning beings from other worlds. He says the friends who are as psychic as us, or less, come here to trade, which would mean Earth is part of some kind of exchange with other beings.
four-rabbis-attempt-celestial-ascent: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, retells an old Jewish parable, which he calls the parable of "the parties," in which four rabbis tried to rise up into the heavens and only one came back alive with his mind intact. He uses it to suggest that reaching for higher realms of reality is dangerous for whoever tries.
four-star-general-from-the-clinton-admin: A physicist named Eric Davis, who has advised the Pentagon, says on Jesse Michels's podcast in 2026 that he knows a four-star general from President Clinton's time in the 1990s. Davis says the general used his rank and authority to visit and get inside a hidden program said to hold recovered crashed craft. If true, it would mean even top generals had to push their way into a program kept secret from them.
four-star-general-says-mj-12-is-real: An online UFO researcher who goes by UAPGerb, speaking with podcast host Jesse Michels, tells of the Majestic 12 documents: papers said to describe a secret US group called Majestic 12 that dealt with UFOs. He says an unnamed four-star general was asked about the papers and said they are real, or that Majestic 12 itself is real. If true, it would mean a top US officer vouched for a secret UFO group at the highest level.
four-years-of-secret-funding-before-hist: The owner of Skinwalker Ranch, a property in Utah known for reports of strange happenings, told podcast host Jesse Michels that from about 2016 he paid for a scientific investigation of the ranch himself and kept it completely secret for four years. It matters to him because it would show the research began as a private, serious effort, not as a TV show.
fox-breaks-the-fife-symington-phoenix-li: James Fox, a documentary filmmaker who investigates UFOs, says he broke the story of Fife Symington, the governor of Arizona, about the Phoenix Lights, a huge formation of lights that many people say they saw over Phoenix in 1997. According to Fox, Symington later admitted, about ten years on, that he too had seen it, and that as a former Air Force pilot he said the thing could not have been from here. Coming from a sitting governor, that would be a powerful witness to something unexplained.
fox-concludes-there-were-more-beings-tha: James Fox, a documentary filmmaker who has spent years on the 1996 creature case in Varginha, Brazil, says there were more sightings later on. He says he is now coming to the conclusion that there were a lot more beings in the area than were first reported, which would make the event much bigger than the original story.
fox-finds-marco-chereze-s-sister-marta: James Fox, a documentary filmmaker who investigates UFOs, tells of searching in Varginha, a town in Brazil, for the family of a man named Marco Chereze, who figures in a local story about a captured creature. Fox says that after hours of knocking on doors, one finally opened and there stood Marco's sister, Marta. For Fox, finding her meant reaching someone close to the heart of the case.
fox-interviewed-all-three-rendlesham-wit: James Fox, a documentary filmmaker who investigates UFOs, says he is the only person to have interviewed all three main witnesses of the Rendlesham Forest incident. That is a reported 1980 encounter with a strange craft in woods beside RAF Woodbridge, a British air base used by the US military in Suffolk, England. He names the three as Cabansag, John Burroughs and Jim Penniston, which would make his account the fullest record of what they say they saw.
fox-s-interview-with-edgar-mitchell-at-h: James Fox, a documentary filmmaker who investigates UFOs, says he interviewed Edgar Mitchell, a former astronaut, at Mitchell's home in Florida. According to Fox, Mitchell told him plainly that yes, there have been visits by beings from other worlds, a striking claim from someone who had been to space.
fox-s-investigation-of-the-varginha-cras: James Fox, a filmmaker who investigates UFOs, says he looked into a case from 1996 in Varginha, a town in Brazil, where a UFO is said to have crashed and a being was reportedly captured. Fox says he travelled there five times over twelve years, and the work went into his film Moment of Contact. The journalist Michael Shellenberger later wrote about the case in a two-page spread in the New York Post newspaper, and the host Jesse Michels points to Fox's work there too, since if true it would be a crash with living non-human beings.
fox-s-vision-of-tim-coleman-keying-his-c: James Fox, a documentary filmmaker who investigates UFOs, says that while editing his film Out of the Blue, around the late 1990s or early 2000s, he suddenly got a picture in his head, clear as day, of a man named Tim Coleman holding a key. He tells it as a vision that Coleman was scratching his car with that key, a kind of knowing he could not explain.
fox-sends-out-of-the-blue-to-all-535-mem: James Fox, a UFO investigator and filmmaker, says that around 2000 he went around Washington, D.C., handing out copies of his UFO documentary Out of the Blue to every member of the House and Senate, all 535 of them. He tells it as his attempt to get the US Congress to take the subject seriously.
fracking-oil-with-nuclear-weapons-in-the: John Herrington, a former US Secretary of Energy, mentioned on Jesse Michels's podcast that in the 1950s, in the time of President Dwight Eisenhower, nuclear weapons were used for fracking, which means cracking rock deep underground to free up oil. He brings it up as an example of how far the government of that era was willing to go with secret, experimental projects.
fractals-in-jackson-pollock-s-paintings-: A philosopher named Jason Jorjani, on Jesse Michels' podcast, points listeners to a Scientific American article called "Order in Pollock's Chaos" by the scientist Richard Taylor. Jorjani says it shows that the painter Jackson Pollock's famous drip paintings contain fractals, patterns that repeat at every scale, suggesting hidden order inside what looks like random splatter.
francis-crick-s-1973-directed-panspermia: This story is about Francis Crick, the scientist who helped discover the double helix shape of DNA. According to a podcast host, Jesse Michels, Crick wrote a paper in 1973 on "directed panspermia," the idea that life on Earth was deliberately seeded from space by another intelligence. A writer on ancient history, Graham Hancock, describes the idea vividly: a spaceship carrying bacteria hit the early Earth and spilled out its contents. Hancock points to Crick's later book, Life Itself. Michels returns to it on several episodes, once mentioning a second date, 1981, and noting that Crick was a former associate of his guest, the scientist Rupert Sheldrake. In another episode he simply says Crick proposed the idea, with no date or paper. Michels and Hancock tell it in their own words. If the idea were right, life on Earth would have been planted on purpose by someone else.
franco-and-skorzeny-launch-saucer-shaped: A researcher named Jason Jorjani, speaking with podcast host Jesse Michels, says Spanish newspapers in 1946 reported that Otto Skorzeny, a German commando officer of the Nazi era, was with General Francisco Franco, Spain's ruler, on the Mediterranean coast of Spain, launching saucer-shaped rockets toward America. He draws on the work of a writer named Joseph Farrell. If true, it would mean flying saucer technology was in the hands of Nazi-linked figures right after the war.
frank-critzer-nazi-agent-killed-at-giant: Giant Rock is a huge boulder in the California desert, and a man named George Van Tassel later lived in a structure dug out beneath it. If it were true, a famous desert site would have a hidden wartime spy story behind it.
frank-drake-s-project-ozma-1961: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in 1961 the famous astronomer Frank Drake started Project Ozma, which Michels calls the first organized search for radio signals from other star systems. He tells it as the starting point of science's serious hunt for intelligent life beyond Earth.
frank-tipler-s-rotating-disc-time-machin: A researcher named Mike Masters, who argues that the beings behind UFOs (unidentified flying objects) may be humans from the future, traces a line of time travel ideas through physics. He says that after work by Albert Einstein and later models by the physicists van Stockum and Kurt Gödel, a physicist named Frank Tipler in the 1970s shrank the required machine down to a finite size: a rapidly rotating ring, sphere or disc. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, repeats the idea, calling Tipler a contemporary of the physicist Wheeler and saying the so-called Tipler disc is basically a flying saucer. If they are right, the classic saucer shape could be the shape of a time machine.
fravor-and-dietrich-disagree-on-how-long: In 2004, off Southern California, two Navy fighter pilots, David Fravor and Alex Dietrich, say they saw a white oval object, shaped like a Tic Tac mint, over the Pacific. Mick West, a researcher known for skeptical analysis of UFO cases, points out on Jesse Michels's podcast that Dietrich says her whole experience, from first meeting the object to it flying away, lasted only 8 to 10 seconds. He raises this because it differs from Fravor's account, and the gap matters for how much the pilots could really have seen.
fravor-and-dietrich-saw-appendages-on-un: In 2004, off the coast of Southern California near the aircraft carrier USS Nimitz, Navy pilots reported meeting a strange flying object, and a pilot named Chad Underwood filmed it with his jet's infrared camera (FLIR, short for forward-looking infrared). A man named Merrick, speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast, says that two other pilots from that day, Commander David Fravor and Lieutenant Commander Alex Dietrich, have stated that when they watched Underwood's footage afterwards they saw little appendages, small bits sticking out of the object. If true, the object had a shape and features you cannot easily make out in the footage most people have seen.
fravor-s-2004-nimitz-sighting-of-an-obje: In 2004, off the coast of San Diego, a Navy fighter pilot named Commander David Fravor says he saw a white oval object shaped like a Tic Tac mint. Michels often repeats Fravor's sense that the thing seemed aware of him, "conscious and almost breathing". Fravor was flying from the aircraft carrier USS Nimitz, and he describes it himself: it was "moving very abruptly over the water like a ping pong ball", then "rapidly accelerated in front of us and disappeared". Michels adds more details across many episodes: it hovered just above the water and seemed to go in and out of it, it climbed to 80,000 feet, and it was already waiting at the meeting point the pilots were heading to next. Other tellers bring in more crew and instruments. A guest named Merrick von Renenamp, retelling the crews' accounts, names other airmen and officers, including Alex Dietrich, Chad Underwood and Kevin Day. Michels mentions radar on the ship USS Princeton. Eric Haseltine, a former official at the National Security Agency (the US eavesdropping agency), says there were too many "independent parallel sensors" on it, and too many people "who didn't want to see it but saw it anyhow". The UFO researcher Jacques Vallee asks why such an object would let "11 f-18s" (Navy fighter jets) chase it "all over the Pacific". Michels notes that the case became widely known through a 2017 New York Times article by the journalist Leslie Kean. If true, it would be a craft far beyond known technology that seemed to notice who was watching it.
fravor-s-joe-rogan-interview-draws-merri: A man named Merrick von Renenamp, talking on Jesse Michels's podcast, says it was late 2019 when he got pulled into the subject of unexplained flying objects. What drew him in, he says, was an interview that a Navy commander named David Fravor gave on Joe Rogan's show, a very popular long-form talk podcast. He tells it to explain how one widely heard interview started his own involvement.
fred-crisman-and-hunt-as-the-dallas-tram: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that after President John F. Kennedy was shot in Dallas, Texas, in 1963, three men who looked like hobos were arrested, and that some people think one of them was a man named Fred Crisman. Michels adds that Crisman was also involved in the Maury Island incident of 1947, a reported UFO episode from around the time a man named Kenneth Arnold said he saw his UFO. A researcher and author, Peter Levenda, says he can back this up and suggests another man, E. Howard Hunt, may have been one of the three as well. If true, it would tie early UFO history directly to the Kennedy assassination.
fred-darwin-s-list-of-a-high-level-flyin: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, describes a list of names attributed to a man called Fred Darwin, as passed on by a researcher, William Steinman. According to Michels, Darwin named these people as members of a special top level committee on flying saucers inside the US defence research establishment around 1949 to 1954, among them the government science chief Vannevar Bush, the mathematician John von Neumann, and the scientists Lloyd Berkner, Karl Compton, Eric Walker and Robert Reinhardt. If true, it would mean some of the country's leading scientists quietly worked on the UFO question.
fred-maywald-confirms-the-story-in-recor: Robert Salas, a former US Air Force officer, says that in 1967, while he was on duty at a nuclear missile site in Montana called Oscar Flight, a UFO appeared and ten nuclear missiles shut down. Salas says that in 1996 he finally reached his old commander, Fred Maywald, who confirmed the essentials of the story on a recorded call now posted on the website spiralgalaxy.org, and that the call showed Salas had been at Oscar Flight, not a nearby site called Echo Flight. If true, it would mean something unknown could switch off America's nuclear weapons.
fred-reed-s-letter-on-relandscaping-the-: A researcher named Scott Ramsay, who studies a reported 1948 UFO crash at Hart Canyon near Aztec, New Mexico, tells podcast host Jesse Michels about a letter from a man named Fred Reed, dated March 27, 1999. According to Ramsay, Reed's letter says people came to the site to relandscape the mesa, the flat-topped hill where the crash is said to have happened. If true, it would mean someone reshaped the land to hide traces of a crash.
frederick-myers-and-the-society-for-psyc: A writer named Eric Wargo, speaking with a podcast host, Jesse Michels, talks about how strange mental experiences such as knowing things at a distance were explained in the past. Wargo says these were presumed to be telepathy, mind-to-mind communication, a model introduced in 1882 by Frederick Myers of the Society for Psychical Research, an English group that studied such claims. He raises it because he thinks the same experiences may have a different explanation, such as information coming from the future.
frederick-valentich-disappearance-1978: An Australian journalist, Ross Coulthart, recalls the case of Frederick Valentich, a young pilot who vanished while flying a small Cessna plane over Bass Strait, the stretch of sea south of mainland Australia, in 1978. Coulthart mentions it as a story that was fresh in people's minds a few months before other sightings he was discussing, part of why unexplained things in the sky felt so real in Australia at the time.
frederick-wolfe-german-pow-shot-at-fort-: A former CIA officer named Rolf Mowatt-Larssen, speaking on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, tells of a man called Frederick Wolfe. According to Mowatt-Larssen, Wolfe was a German soldier who was sent to Fort Knox, a US Army base in Kentucky, as a prisoner of war, and the story as it is filed says he was shot there around 1944. Mowatt-Larssen gives no source for the account.
free-edgar-mitchell-experiencer-study-hu: Podcast host Jesse Michels often mentions a study by FREE, a research group named after former astronaut Edgar Mitchell, which surveyed people who say they have had contact with beings not from Earth. Michels says that 52 percent of those who answered, elsewhere he says over half, reported meeting humanlike creatures, and that the survey now holds more than 5,000 people. If true, it would suggest many contact reports describe beings that look much like us.
free-energy-device-in-stan-meyer-s-archi: A UFO researcher named Steven Greer, on Jesse Michels' podcast, says his science adviser, Dr. Ted Loder, visited a warehouse in Michigan holding the archive of the late inventor Stan Meyer, full of floppy disks and devices. Greer says one item there was of great interest, a free-energy device, meaning a machine said to give out more energy than it takes in, and he points to a photo online. If true, it would mean world-changing energy technology is sitting unused.
freeman-dyson-on-ida-advisory-board: Bob Maguire, who says he worked as a contractor for the CIA, the US spy agency, told podcast host Jesse Michels that he once worked at the Institute for Defense Analysis's Center for Communications Research in New Jersey, a research group that does work for the US government. He says the famous physicist Freeman Dyson sat on that center's advisory board. He tells it to show the kind of top-level scientific company his workplace kept.
freemasonry-descends-from-cathedral-buil: Randall Carlson, a researcher of ancient history, says that Freemasonry, a fraternal society with secret rituals, grew out of several older traditions that merged together. According to him, two of these were the lodges of skilled builders who built Europe's medieval cathedrals and the Templar knights, a medieval Christian military order, which would tie the society to very old hidden knowledge.
freescale-semiconductor-engineers-aboard: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that among the passengers on MH370, a passenger flight that went missing in 2014, were 20 engineers from Freescale Semiconductor, a computer chip company. He brings it up in an episode about American scientists going missing, as a hint that the loss of these specialists may not have been chance.
freezing-at-the-communion-cover-in-a-bar: John Blitch, a scientist who worked with DARPA, the Pentagon's research agency for advanced technology, says he was once taken by an alien. He tells of walking through a Barnes & Noble bookstore in a mall in the 1990s, around the time of an incident on his mountain bike, and spotting the cover of Communion, a book by the writer Whitley Strieber about his own alien encounters, with its large-eyed face. He says he froze in his tracks, as if he recognised that face.
freikorps-stahlhelm-militias-wearing-swa: Peter Levenda, an author who writes about secret societies and history, says that in Germany just after World War I, around 1918 and 1919, armed volunteer militias called the Freikorps sprang up. He says one of them was the Stahlhelm, meaning steel helmet, and that its members had swastikas painted on their helmets, years before the Nazis made the symbol their own.
french-1999-cometa-report-conclusions: In 1999 a French committee, known as COMETA, put out a report on unexplained flying objects. A scientist named Kevin Knuth, speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast, says the report concluded that these things could be alien spacecraft, that there might be a base somewhere in our solar system, and that the United States is probably hiding information. If true, it would mean a serious group in another country reached that conclusion on paper.
french-bombing-of-the-greenpeace-boat-in: An Australian journalist, Ross Coulthart, recalls how a boat belonging to Greenpeace, the environmental campaign group, was blown up in Auckland Harbour, New Zealand, in 1985. He says it was done by the DGSE, France's foreign intelligence service, as a covert operation right in the middle of the harbour. He tells it as an example of what governments and their spy agencies are willing to do in secret.
french-demonstrations-escalating-up-to-a: A researcher named Jan Lundquist tells this story on an episode of Jesse Michels's podcast. The episode is about Townsend Brown, an American inventor it calls a CIA scientist who built flying craft. Lundquist says that around 1956, people in France were writing to a man named Jacques Cornillon to invite guests to demonstrations of the work. Each demonstration was for a higher-ranking audience, until they reached officials of France's atomic energy agency. If that is right, the work had caught serious government attention in France.
french-farmer-meets-an-nhi-holding-a-tra: A journalist named Michael Shellenberger, speaking on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, retells a case he credits to Jacques Vallee, a longtime researcher of UFO reports. According to Shellenberger, a trusted and respected farmer in France found a spaceship on his land, walked up to it, and found a non-human intelligence, meaning a being that is not human, standing there holding a tray full of soil samples. If true, it would suggest visitors who are quietly studying the Earth itself.
frequent-ufo-sightings-in-alamogordo: Lyn Buchanan, a former Army sergeant, told podcast host Jesse Michels that he has seen a lot of UFOs. He lives in Alamogordo, a town in New Mexico, and says people there see them all the time, which would make it a place where strange things in the sky are common.
fresh-yellow-curb-lines-marking-the-kill: In November 1963 President John F. Kennedy was shot in Dealey Plaza in Dallas, on Elm Street, an event also captured in a famous home movie called the Zapruder film. Dan Sheehan, speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast, says three yellow lines had been painted on the curb right where the shots happened, and that they were painted the night before, because a witness named Beverly Oliver was standing on one. If true, it would suggest the spot was marked out in advance.
freud-s-1895-dream-foreshadowing-his-ora: Eric Wargo, a writer who studies dreams that seem to predict the future, talks about a famous dream that Sigmund Freud, the founder of psychoanalysis, had in Vienna in 1895. Freud spent about 14 pages on it in his landmark book The Interpretation of Dreams. Wargo reads it as a glimpse of the mouth cancer Freud was found to have decades later, which would mean dreams can reach ahead in time.
friedman-and-the-woods-authenticate-mj-1: An online UFO researcher who goes by UAPGerb tells podcast host Jesse Michels that he follows the work of Stanton Friedman, a UFO researcher, who spent years with two other researchers, Ryan and Robert Wood, checking whether two papers were genuine. The papers are a Special Operations Manual, said to give instructions for handling crashed UFOs, and the Eisenhower briefing document, said to brief President Eisenhower on a secret UFO group called Majestic 12. If the papers are real, the US government secretly handled UFOs from the late 1940s on.
friend-abducted-by-grays-shows-delta-pat: Tim Alberino, a guest on Jesse Michels' podcast, says that last spring a friend at his house suddenly told him, "I forgot to tell you. They came and got me." According to Alberino, the friend meant he had been taken by grays, the small gray-skinned beings common in alien abduction stories, and showed marks on his body laid out in a triangle-like pattern. If true, the marks would be physical traces left by such a visit.
friend-dying-on-the-moon: Ross Coulthart, a journalist who reports on UFO claims, says that someone he trusts became very emotional while telling him about a friend who died on the moon. He told this on Jesse Michels's podcast in an episode about a hidden space programme. If true, it would mean people have been secretly sent to the moon, and some did not come back.
friend-mike-secretly-watched-buer-and-dr: Charles Buer, a man who says he worked on a propulsion project, tells this on a 2026 episode of a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels. He says that sometime before 2016, in Florida, he and another man, Drew, had each been working on the same kind of work separately for years, and a friend of theirs named Mike knew about both of them the whole time but never told either one. Buer tells it as a strange twist in how the work came together.
friend-s-family-sees-the-same-beach-ligh: A witness named Charles, speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast, describes strange lights seen near Cocoa Beach in Florida around 2020 or 2021. He says a friend told him that he and his family were at the beach late at night and saw the same thing, which Charles thought was very cool. He tells it because it means he was not the only one to see the lights.
friend-s-government-contact-warns-him-of: There is a story that US soldiers near Kandahar, Afghanistan, in the early 2000s came across a giant about 12 feet tall. Tim Alberino, a guest on Jesse Michels's podcast who looks into the story, says a friend of his asked a contact with government ties about the Kandahar giant, and the contact's whole manner suddenly changed and he warned the friend off. To Alberino, that reaction suggests there is something real being kept quiet.
friend-s-medium-reading-channels-his-lat: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells the parapsychologist Jeffrey Mishlove about a friend whose sister had died. According to Michels, the friend went to a medium, a person who claims to speak with the dead, and the medium straight away began teasing him in exactly the way his sister used to. Michels shares it as a hint that something of a person may survive death.
friend-sees-a-black-pyramid-in-antarctic: Jesse Michels, a podcast host, says a friend of his went to Antarctica, he thinks to make a documentary, and saw a kind of black pyramid there. He mentioned it while talking about Richard Byrd, the American polar explorer. If true, it would hint at some unknown structure hidden in the ice.
friend-sees-a-portal-open-in-the-sky-and: Tim Alberino, a guest on Jesse Michels's podcast, says a friend of his actually saw a portal, a kind of opening, appear in the sky, with saucer-shaped craft flying out of it. No time or place is given. If true, it would mean these craft come through doorways from somewhere else rather than flying in from space.
friend-spoke-to-amy-eskridge-hours-befor: Amy Eskridge was a woman in Alabama whose death in 2022 was treated as a suicide, and a podcast episode by Jesse Michels about scientists going missing included a friend of hers who did not give a name. The friend says they spoke with her four hours before she died, and that she had said again and again that she would never kill herself. So the friend does not believe she took her own life, which would mean something else happened to her.
friend-with-the-same-slit-in-his-eye-is-: Whitley Strieber, a writer, says on Jesse Michels's podcast that he has a friend in Marin County, California, who has the same kind of slit in his eye that Strieber has. He says this friend is one of the world's leading experts on Konstantin Raudive, a man known for studying mysterious voices on tape recordings. Strieber tells it as if the shared mark were a link between people drawn to unusual subjects.
friends-lab-work-becomes-a-weapon-in-mon: Dave Rossi, a man who says aliens taught him advanced physics, says he has mutual friends privately working on this kind of science in their own labs. According to him, after only six or seven months of lab work, what they were building turned into a weapon. If true, it would mean this physics is dangerous and easy to turn to harm.
friends-turned-away-from-area-51: Kiran Ilum Xenov, a former president of one of Russia's regional republics who says he was taken by aliens in 1997, says friends of his recently visited the United States and tried to drive up to Area 51, a secretive military test site in Nevada. He says the military would not let them through. To him, it shows how closely the site is guarded.
friends-who-fought-the-cia-and-dni-inter: Dylan Borland, a guest on Jesse Michels' podcast who says a top government official told him aliens run everything, says he has friends who took on the CIA, the US spy agency, and the DNI, the office that oversees all US spy agencies, from the inside during the 2020s. According to him, they told those agencies they could prove the agencies were lying, and then did. If true, it would mean insiders had caught the intelligence world hiding something.
friends-working-on-antigravity-received-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, puts a question to Kevin Knuth, a physicist and former NASA scientist. Michels recalls Knuth saying on another podcast, hosted by Danny Jones, that several of his friends worked on antigravity, technology meant to cancel or push against gravity, and got a backlash for it. The suggestion is that research in this area is being discouraged or kept quiet.
friendship-with-robert-anton-wilson-and-: Jeffrey Mishlove, a researcher with a doctorate who studies the mind and psychic claims, says that in the 1970s in Berkeley, California, he was friends with Robert Anton Wilson, a writer on strange ideas and consciousness. Mishlove says that Wilson's beautiful 15-year-old daughter was tragically murdered in Berkeley, and he mentions Wilson's book Reality Is What You Can Get Away With and his ties to the psychedelics figure Timothy Leary.
fritz-haber-reverse-engineered-the-red-p: A researcher named Geoffrey Drumm, who argues the pyramids were machines, tells podcast host Jesse Michels his idea about Fritz Haber, a German chemist who, with Carl Bosch, worked out a way to make ammonia in the early 1900s. Drumm says Haber studied the Red Pyramid in Egypt, which has three inner chambers, and copied how it worked, pointing to a book that mentions an Egyptian banker funding Haber's project and to postcards Haber dated from Egypt. He sets a picture of Haber's original apparatus beside the pyramid's three chambers to show they match. If true, the pyramid would have been an ancient chemical plant.
fugal-has-seen-ufos-in-the-air-himself: Brandon Fugal, the owner of Skinwalker Ranch, a property in Utah known for reports of strange happenings, told podcast host Jesse Michels that he has seen UFOs flying in the sky with his own eyes. He does not say where or when. He tells it to make clear that he is not just repeating other people's reports.
fulgurites-in-giza-iron-veins-as-evidenc: On Jesse Michels's podcast, a researcher called Jeffrey says that iron ore veins at the Giza Plateau in Egypt, where the great pyramids stand, contain fulgurites. These are glassy traces left when lightning or another strong electric current melts rock. He says they show that high-voltage electricity once ran through those veins, which would mean the site carried some kind of electrical energy.
fungi-growing-on-the-iss-and-mir: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that fungi have been found growing on the International Space Station, the orbiting laboratory shared by several countries, and on Mir, an earlier Russian space station. He mentions it in an episode about mushrooms with a guest named Tero Isokauppila, as a sign of how hardy fungi are, even off Earth.
fungi-on-the-iss-and-crick-s-directed-pa: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says fungi have been found on the International Space Station, the crewed laboratory orbiting Earth, and links this to Francis Crick, the scientist who helped discover the double helix shape of DNA. In another episode, Michels says Crick believed DNA could not have formed on Earth in 100 million years, which led Crick, in his book Life Itself, to the idea that life was seeded here from elsewhere, and he mentions the astronomer Carl Sagan alongside him. Michels tells it because, if true, life on Earth may have come from space.
fused-silica-microspheres-from-fulgurite: Geoffrey Drumm, a man with his own theory about the true purpose of the pyramids, showed podcast host Jesse Michels a picture of himself down inside one of the boat pits, the stone pits beside the Great Pyramid of Giza in Egypt where ancient boats were buried. He talks about finding fused silica there, tiny glassy beads like those in fulgurites, the glass tubes that form when lightning hits sand. To him, this would mean powerful electrical activity once happened at the site.
fusion-scientist-nuno-loureiro-shot-dead: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, in a debate with a well known skeptic, brings up Nuno Loureiro, a scientist he calls a leader in magnetic reconnection, a process in charged gas that Michels says is key to making nuclear fusion power work. Michels says Loureiro was shot dead at his own front door in 2025 and objects to treating it as a non-story, mentioning another scientist, Carl Grillmair, in the same breath. He raises it because some people suggest the deaths of scientists in sensitive fields may be connected.
fyodorov-s-russian-cosmism-and-resurrect: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, traces a line of ideas back to Russia, to a librarian and philosopher named Nikolai Fyodorov, the founder of a school of thought called Russian Cosmism. Michels says Fyodorov believed the true task of humanity and of Christianity was not to wait for the dead to be raised, but to make it happen. Michels tells it as the starting point of an episode about the space agency NASA and UFOs, as if this old dream of beating death sits underneath later space science.
gabinetto-rs33-and-its-nine-step-protoco: The podcast host Jesse Michels says that in 1933 Italy, under its dictator Benito Mussolini, set up a secret research group called Gabinetto RS33, the RS33 cabinet, which reportedly wrote a nine-step plan for handling a crashed craft at Magenta and any future ones, with the radio pioneer Guglielmo Marconi said to be its head. In other versions Michels relays what Marconi's grandson, a prince, told him: the scientist Enrico Fermi was vice-president and the group studied UFO sightings in 1953 near Varese in northern Italy. Michels has also called it Italy's version of Majestic 12, a supposed secret US group on UFOs, and stressed that Marconi's part is rumoured and that the grandson knew it through family talk, not documents.
gaffney-blocked-lockheed-to-bigelow-ufo-: This story is about Glenn Gaffney, a senior CIA official. The podcast host Jesse Michels says that George Knapp, a journalist who has long covered UFOs, told Congress under oath that Gaffney personally blocked a transfer of UFO material in 2008. As Michels tells it, the material was to move from Lockheed Martin, a large defence company, to Bigelow Aerospace, a private space company. If true, it would mean the CIA was guarding physical UFO material held by a private firm. In a later episode, a guest named Dylan Borland simply names "Glenn Gaffney, CIA" when talking about the congressional hearing. He gives no date and no details of the transfer.
galileo-project-instruments-on-harvard-c: A Harvard scientist named Avi Loeb said in early 2022 that his new research effort, the Galileo Project, which studies unexplained objects in the sky, had drawn thousands of excited emails and more than a hundred scientists. He said they were buying instruments to put on the roof of the Harvard College Observatory in the coming months, which would mean a major university looking at the question directly. Another researcher, Eric Weinstein, mentioned it in passing a few weeks later, saying only that Loeb was setting something up at Harvard.
galileo-project-monthly-meetings-2021: A researcher named Michael Shurmer says he has been part of the Galileo Project, a scientific effort led by Harvard scientist Avi Loeb to study unexplained objects, since its very first week in 2021. He says the team meets on Zoom on the first Friday of every month and that he has never missed a meeting, which he offers as proof of how closely he knows the work.
gallaudet-briefs-the-japanese-diet-s-uap: Tim Gallaudet, a retired Navy admiral, says that around 2024 or 2025 he gave an online presentation to a group of lawmakers in Japan's parliament, called the Diet, who had formed a caucus on UAP, the official term for unidentified objects in the sky and sea. He tells it to show that interest in the subject reaches lawmakers outside the United States.
gallaudet-co-writes-the-bluegill-triple-: Tim Gallaudet, a retired US Navy admiral, says he helped a man named Jeff Krookchank write a report on Bluegill Triple Prime, a US nuclear test carried out in 1962 near Johnston Atoll, a small island in the Pacific. He mentions it as part of his own first-hand work, in a conversation about unexplained objects in and over the ocean.
gallaudet-sees-the-go-fast-video-on-the-: Tim Gallaudet, who was then a one-star admiral in the US Navy, says that around 2015 he saw the Go Fast video, Navy footage of a small unknown object filmed by fighter jets off the US East Coast, on the Navy Secret Network, the Navy's classified computer system. He tells it because, if true, it means the Navy was passing around evidence of unexplained objects internally well before the public saw it.
gallaudet-visits-skinwalker-ranch-with-b: Tim Gallaudet, a retired Navy admiral, says he went out to Skinwalker Ranch, a property in Utah with its own lore of strange happenings, together with a man named Brandon Fugal. He describes it simply as a great day spent there together.
gallimore-and-strassman-s-2015-extended-: A neuroscientist named Andrew Gallimore says that in 2015 he and a colleague, Rick Strassman, put forward a model and paper for what they called extended-state DMT, or DMTx: a way to keep a person in the experience of DMT, a powerful psychedelic drug, for much longer than usual. He says the work did not end there and is still going on, and he tells it because longer visits could let people explore what he describes as a realm of other beings.
gallimore-s-laser-speckle-explanation-fo: A man named Danny claims that by shining a laser while on DMT, a powerful psychedelic drug, he could see a kind of code behind reality. Andrew Gallimore, a neuroscientist, offers another explanation on Jesse Michels's podcast: laser light makes a grainy speckle pattern on the retina, the light-sensing layer at the back of the eye. He says that under DMT the brain uses this pattern like a scaffold and builds complex forms around it, so the code would come from the eye and brain, not from reality itself.
games-resume-after-the-dtra-contract-end: Dylan Borland, a man who says a top government official told him aliens run everything, says that after his contract with DTRA, the Defense Threat Reduction Agency that deals with weapons of mass destruction, ended in 2024 or 2025, the strange "games" around him started again. He says a request to fill in an SF86, the US government form used for security clearances, left his clearance listed as "undefined". He ties this to a contact experience he had in the desert while using that clearance the previous June.
garrett-graff-s-ufo-debunking-book-after: A journalist named Michael Shellenberger says the Aspen Institute, a US policy think tank, held an exercise around 2020 to prepare the public in advance against UFO claims, which he calls pre-bunking, and he names Vivian Schiller in connection with it. He says that in 2024 the writer Garrett Graff published a book simply titled UFO that, in Shellenberger's words, is basically a debunking of the famous cases, suggesting, if he is right, a planned effort to shape opinion on the subject.
garry-nolan-debunking-atacama-mummy: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, mentions a man named Garry Nolan and a small mummified body from the Atacama region that some had claimed was not human. As Michels tells it, Nolan's work showing the mummy was not what it was claimed to be is how he first got drawn into the UFO field. It is told as the origin of someone Michels presents as holding a great deal of UFO evidence.
garry-nolan-has-seen-little-people-and-a: Jesse Michels, a podcast host, says that Garry Nolan, a scientist at Stanford University, has seen some little people, and a craft too. Michels gives no time or place for it. If true, it would mean a well-known scientist had a direct encounter with non-human beings and their vehicle.
garry-nolan-s-childhood-bedside-visitors: The podcast host Jesse Michels says that Garry Nolan, a professor at Stanford University, has claimed that as a child of about six or seven, in Windsor, he saw aliens standing at the foot of his bed. Michels is careful to say Nolan does not describe it as an abduction. If true, a respected scientist would have his own early encounter story.
garry-nolan-s-magnesium-bismuth-sample-f: Jesse Michels, a podcast host, says that Garry Nolan, a scientist at Stanford University, keeps a piece of metal made of magnesium and bismuth in his lab. The piece is said to come from Ubatuba, a coastal town in Brazil, linked to a reported UFO event in the 1950s or 1960s. If it came from such a craft, it would be physical material from something not made by people.
gary-mckinnon-finds-a-list-of-off-planet: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, retells the story of Gary McKinnon, a man in Britain who broke into US military computer systems around 2001 and 2002. According to Michels, McKinnon came across a page listing officers described as off-planet or non-terrestrial, which would point to a hidden space program. In one telling Michels puts the list at 11 or 12 names, and in a later one at 40.
gary-mckinnon-s-hack-and-the-tic-tac-ima: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells how a British computer hacker named Gary McKinnon, around 2001 or 2002, broke into computers at NASA's Johnson Space Center in Houston after hearing a former NASA worker, Donna Hare, claim UFOs were being hidden. Michels says McKinnon saw an image pop up on his screen of a white oval craft shaped like a Tic Tac mint that seemed to be orbiting Earth, which would mean NASA holds evidence of unknown craft in space.
gary-nolan-presents-his-injury-research-: Diana Pasulka, a scholar who studies religion and UFO beliefs, told podcast host Jesse Michels about a 2016 trip to a site in New Mexico. She says that the night before the group went to the site, while everyone was having a beer, the scientist Garry Nolan decided to share his research and photos of injuries suffered by people who reported strange encounters. She tells it as a first look at the serious science some researchers were quietly doing on the subject.
gary-nolan-s-caudate-putamen-theories: The podcast host Jesse Michels says that Garry Nolan, a Stanford scientist who studies the immune system, has been looking into the brains of people who report UFOs, and has working theories that are not final. As Michels tells it, Nolan says people with more densely packed brain cells in the caudate and putamen, two parts of a deep brain region called the basal ganglia, are more likely both to see UFOs and to be, in Michels's words, more psychic. Michels adds that this trait runs in families, which would give some people a built-in reason for seeing what others don't.
gary-nolan-s-cia-file-on-ufo-experiencer: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that a scientist named Garry Nolan told him the CIA, the US spy agency, once handed him a file and asked him to look into it. As the story goes, the file was about people who report UFO encounters and about Havana syndrome, a set of unexplained symptoms reported by US officials, sometime in the 2010s. If true, it would mean the agency quietly asked an outside scientist for help with these cases.
gary-nolan-s-crash-retrieval-parts-from-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Garry Nolan, a scientist at Stanford, has pieces said to come from crashed unknown craft, given to him by his friend Jacques Vallée, whom Michels calls the godfather of UFO research. Michels says he has seen the parts himself in Nolan's lab, and that Nolan suggested the materials might one day be used as tiny channels for guiding energy here on Earth.
gary-nolan-s-strontium-ufo-metamaterial-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says he believes that Garry Nolan, a scientist at Stanford University, keeps pieces of material in his lab that Nolan thinks could be UFO "metamaterials". These are specially engineered materials that Nolan suspects come from crashed craft. Michels says, with some hesitation, that one of the pieces contains strontium, a metallic chemical element.
gary-s-biefeld-brown-ccto-experiments-in: Gary McKinnon, a British computer hacker who says he found signs of a secret NASA space program, told podcast host Jesse Michels that he now runs his own experiments in a small garden shed, about ten feet by ten, in the UK. He says the work is based on the Biefeld-Brown effect, an old claim that devices charged with high voltage can produce a push on their own. He mentions the tiny shed to show how humble his setup is.
gary-stearman-s-cessna-escorted-by-a-wal: Tim Alberino, a guest on Jesse Michels' podcast, passes on a story he heard from a man named Gary Stearman about a flight in a Cessna, a small private plane, from Lubbock, Texas to Dallas. According to Alberino, a voice came over the radio saying "If you look to your left, you'll see a UFO," and Stearman's plane was then escorted by an object shaped like a walnut. If true, it would mean someone on the ground knew about the craft and was openly pointing it out to pilots.
gary-webb-and-cia-cocaine-in-the-inner-c: Kurt Metzger, a guest on Jesse Michels' podcast, brings up a man named Gary Webb, whom he calls "the guy that knew the CIA brought Coke into the hood."
