The CIA is America's foreign spy agency, and Metzger's point is that Webb found it had let cocaine flow into poor American neighborhoods, in a story running from the 1980s to 2004. He tells it as an example of the government hiding dark secrets from the public.
garyaev-healing-people-in-wooden-pyramid: Dave Rossi, a guest on Jesse Michels' podcast, describes the work of a Russian researcher named Peter Garyaev, drawing on a website about Garyaev's idea he calls "linguistic wave genetics." Rossi says Garyaev was healing people by placing them inside wooden pyramids. If true, it would suggest that shape alone can carry some kind of healing power.
gate-crashing-bobby-kennedy-s-funeral-at: Peter Levenda, an author who writes about secret history and the CIA, says that in June 1968 he and a friend slipped into the funeral of Robert Kennedy, the US senator, at St. Patrick's Cathedral in New York City. He says an official asked if they were Russian Orthodox representatives and he answered that they were Slavonic Orthodox representatives, and they were let in. He says a still photograph of the funeral procession captures the moment, near figures like Rose Kennedy and Jackie Onassis.
gate-started-by-sidney-marland-in-1972-p: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says he thinks GATE, an American school programme for gifted and talented children, was started in 1972 by an official named Sidney Marland. In an episode where a guest says he was taken into a secret UFO programme as a child, Michels raises the idea that GATE may have worked as a funnel, a way to spot and steer bright children. If so, it would mean an ordinary school programme fed young people into hidden projects.
gate-testing-and-grooming-by-outside-psy: Jordan Jose, a man who says a secret UFO programme took him as a child, says that around 2004 or 2005 in Springville, New York, he was tested for GATE, a gifted and talented education programme for bright schoolchildren, using a standard school exam called the Woodcock test of achievement. He says outside psychologists then worked with him and groomed him over the following years, which he links to claims that such testing is used to pick out children for hidden programmes.
gauge-theory-economics-and-dale-jorgenso: A researcher named Eric Weinstein says that in the 1990s, he and a colleague, Pia Malaney, worked on applying gauge theory, a branch of mathematics from physics, to economics. He says the idea was badly received by Harvard's economics department, especially by its chairman, Dale Jorgenson, and he tells it as an example of how established institutions push back against new ideas.
gauntlet-like-object-with-moving-hierogl: Randy Anderson told podcast host Jesse Michels that in 2014, at Naval Surface Warfare Center Crane, a US Navy research base in Indiana, he saw an object that looked like a gauntlet, an armored glove. He says it had a display screen with a shimmering, mirage-like effect, and above it symbols like hieroglyphs began to appear and move. If true, it would mean the military holds technology that is not human-made.
gec-marconi-scientist-deaths-during-star: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that between 1982 and 1990, 25 engineers and computer scientists working for GEC Marconi, a British defence company, on some of Britain's most classified defence projects died one after another. He places this in the era of Star Wars, the nickname for the American plan of the 1980s to defend against missiles from space. Michels tells it in an episode about top scientists going missing, as a sign that something more than chance may lie behind such deaths.
geller-2019-radio-interview-puharich-dru: Uri Geller is a performer known for claimed psychic feats, and in the 1970s he worked with a researcher named Andrija Puharich. A researcher called Greg says on Jesse Michels's podcast that Geller went on a radio show around 2019 and said Puharich had experimented on him with mushrooms and with hypnosis. If true, it would cast Geller's experiences with Puharich in a very different light.
geller-bends-a-spoon-during-the-film-int: A researcher named Greg, who worked on a documentary film, says that when his team interviewed a man named Uri Geller, Geller bent a spoon for them on the spot. Greg says he does not know how Geller did it.
geller-boards-a-landed-ufo-in-the-sinai-: A researcher called Greg, drawing on a book that the researcher Andrija Puharich wrote about the performer Uri Geller, tells on Jesse Michels's podcast of an event around 1971 or 1972 in the Sinai Desert. As Greg tells it, a UFO landed, Geller went into a kind of trance, boarded the craft, and came back carrying a pen. If true, Geller would have physically been inside a landed craft and brought something back.
geller-teleported-from-new-york-city-to-: A researcher called Greg, speaking on Jesse Michels' podcast, tells a story about Uri Geller, a man who worked with the researcher Andrija Puharich. Greg says that around 1973, as he remembers it, Geller was walking down a street in New York City and was suddenly teleported to Puharich's home in Ossining, a town north of the city. He links the story to a Super 8 home movie Puharich shot of a screened porch, and if it were true it would mean a person was moved across miles in an instant.
gemini-11-object-flyover-and-battery-dra: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that during Gemini 11, a 1966 NASA mission that orbited Earth with astronauts Pete Conrad and Richard Gordon, the radio transcripts describe an object passing by and the spacecraft's batteries draining one after another. In a later episode he says that researchers Kevin Knuth and Chris Ramsay told him it looks like a real unknown object caused an electrical outage, and he points to a photo from a NASA archive, which would mean something interfered with an American spacecraft.
gemini-7-frank-borman-s-bogey-at-10-o-cl: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, points to audio from Gemini 7, a 1965 NASA spaceflight in which astronauts orbited the Earth, and says that astronaut Frank Borman can be heard reporting a "bogey," pilot slang for an unknown object. Michels says Borman clearly separates the rocket booster, which he places at two o'clock, from a second, real object, and in a later episode he ties the audio to a release of government files on UAP, the official term for unidentified objects. If true, it would mean astronauts saw something in orbit they could not explain.
gemini-ufo-audio-and-airbrushed-ufo-in-n: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, talks about the 1960s Gemini missions, NASA's early two-man spaceflights, and says there is audio of a UFO from them. He also points to a book he calls the Simpkinson textbook, which the story says shows a UFO that was airbrushed out, and credits his friend Chris Ramsay, host of a show called Area 52, for finding it. If true, it would mean NASA saw something in orbit and edited it out of the record.
gene-cernan-s-flashes-and-blinking-objec: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Gene Cernan, an astronaut and the last man to walk on the Moon in 1972, saw strange flashes and distant blinking objects in space, and was even hit by blinding flashes of light in the dark while he slept. Michels links this to a release of UFO files from the US Department of War, the defence department. He tells it because, if true, even astronauts on the Moon met things they could not explain.
gene-roddenberry-channeling-session-with: A researcher called Greg, on Jesse Michels' podcast, describes a session held in Ossining, New York, in the mid-1970s. He says the television producer Gene Roddenberry sat with the researcher Andrija Puharich while a woman named Phyllis Schlemmer acted as the channel, a person who says she speaks messages from other beings. Greg points to a tape of the session kept in Puharich's archive, and the story matters to him because it would put a famous storyteller in the room with people who believed they were talking to non-human minds.
general-exon-held-a-roswell-body-like-a-: The writer Whitley Strieber, on Jesse Michels' podcast, passes on what he says an Air Force general named Arthur Exon told him. According to Strieber, when wreckage and bodies from a 1947 crash near Roswell, New Mexico, were brought to the military's equipment command at Wright Field, Exon held one of the bodies himself, and it felt like a big insect. If true, it would mean the military recovered non-human bodies in 1947.
general-moelner-the-secret-craft-filled-: Nick Cook, a writer interviewed on Jesse Michels' podcast about secret flying craft, passes on what he was told by a man he calls General Moelner. According to Cook, the general said a secret American craft was built to fill a gap in spying from the air, and once it had done that job, the military went back to using spy satellites. Taken at face value, it would mean an advanced secret aircraft was used and then quietly set aside.
general-muellner-s-retirement-day-interv: Nick Cook, a writer on military aviation who made a documentary called Billion Dollar Secret, says he interviewed General George Muellner, the US Air Force's head of research and development, on the day he retired in 1998. Cook says he asked him about Aurora, a rumoured secret American aircraft, hoping a general on his last day might speak more freely about what the military was really flying.
general-neil-mccasland-goes-missing-2020: Neil McCasland is a retired US Air Force general who, according to a podcast host, Jesse Michels, was extremely high up. Michels says McCasland ran the Air Force Research Laboratory at Wright-Patterson, an Air Force base, and sat on a committee overseeing special access programs, the military's most secret projects. He also says McCasland was a source for Tom DeLonge, who wrote a set of books called Secret Machines that are labelled fiction. Michels says that in the 2020s McCasland went very mysteriously missing from his home in New Mexico. A journalist, Jeremy Corbell, says it too, pointing out that this man was charged with protecting national security and is now missing. So the story comes mainly from the host, told across several episodes, plus a journalist guest. Why it matters to them: if true, a man said to hold deep secrets has simply vanished.
general-roya-makes-him-a-warrant-officer: Joe McMoneagle, a guest on Jesse Michels' podcast, says that in the late 1970s at US Army headquarters a general he calls General Roya told him he would make him a warrant officer, a specialist rank that sits between enlisted soldiers and commissioned officers. According to McMoneagle, he was later raised to chief warrant officer. He tells it to show how much the Army valued the work he was doing.
general-starbird-leaves-johnston-island-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, describes Operation Dominic, a 1962 series of US nuclear tests in the Pacific, and one test in it called Bluegill Triple Prime. He says a man named William Ogle wrote that General Alfred Starbird, a senior Army officer, left Johnston Island, the small island used for the tests, at 4 a.m. that night, and he credits the logs of a Navy ship, the USS Summit County. Michels tells it because, if true, a sudden departure that night might hint something unusual happened during the test.
general-stubblebine-recruits-buchanan-in: Lyn Buchanan, a former US Army sergeant, says that in the 1980s General Albert Stubblebine, an Army general looking for people with the power to move things with the mind, brought him into a remote viewing unit at Fort Meade, Maryland, an Army program that trained people to describe distant places using only the mind. Buchanan says that after computers broke down around him, the general got up in his face and asked, "Did you kill my computers with your mind?" He links the story to The Men Who Stare at Goats, a book and film about the US military's psychic programs.
general-stubblebine-s-2-billion-offer-19: This story is about an offer that Steven Greer, a UFO researcher, says he received from a US Army general named Albert Stubblebine. Greer says on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels that in 1992 Stubblebine offered him two billion dollars. He tells it while mentioning another host, Patrick Bet-David. Michels tells it again in a later episode, without the money or the date. In his version, Stubblebine was the first on the scene around Greer, apparently trying to recruit him into some kind of government program. It is told because, if true, it would mean a senior military figure tried to bring a leading UFO activist inside with an enormous offer.
general-tells-varginha-driver-what-he-sa: An unnamed military man, called only "military X," says he was a driver in the 1996 operation in Varginha, Brazil, where a strange creature is said to have been captured after a UFO crash. He says that afterwards a general told him that what he had witnessed was something supernatural. If true, it would mean senior officers knew they were dealing with something not human.
generals-without-clearance-turned-away-a: Greg Rogers, introduced as a doctor who worked with NASA, the US space agency, says that sometime around 1989 to the 1990s he worked at Cape Canaveral Air Force Station, a military rocket launch site in Florida. He says high-ranking officers, even three-star generals on vacation in Florida, would drive up to the gate hoping to look around and be turned away because they lacked the right security clearance. He tells it to show how tightly some things there were guarded, if true, even from senior military people.
genesis-two-lights-matched-to-the-cosmic: Greg Rogers, described as a NASA doctor and a guest on Jesse Michels' podcast, reads the opening of Genesis, the first book of the Bible, against modern science. He says the two separate lights in Genesis match the history of the early universe, from the faint glow left over from the Big Bang, which scientists call the cosmic microwave background, to the moment "light returned to the universe," which he calls "the light of the second day" when the first stars formed. If he is right, the ancient text would be describing the universe's beginnings accurately.
geomagnetic-anomalies-at-ufo-hotspots: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that places famous for strange sightings, like Skinwalker Ranch, a property known for reports of odd events, or Mount Sangun Mori in Japan near the Fukushima area and its civilian nuclear power network, always seem to have geomagnetic anomalies, meaning spots where the Earth's magnetic field behaves oddly. If true, it would hint that whatever is seen at these places is drawn to, or tied to, those magnetic quirks.
george-ball-s-vietnam-memos-with-dismiss: Harold Malmgren, who says he advised several US presidents, recalls going through the papers handed over when Richard Nixon took office in 1968 and 1969. He says he found letters from George Ball, a senior State Department official, pleading with the president to scale back the Vietnam War before it blew up, with dismissive cover notes from Dean Rusk, the secretary of state. He tells it to show the kind of secret, high-level papers he says he handled directly.
george-ellery-hale-s-inspiring-elf-or-sp: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that George Ellery Hale, a scientist tied to Pasadena, California, claimed he got creative inspiration from a being he described as an elf or a spirit. Michels tells it in an episode about NASA and UFOs, as a sign that some of modern science's founders drew on something beyond the ordinary.
george-h-w-bush-as-cia-director-told-of-: Eric Davis, a scientist who has worked on Pentagon studies, says that George H.W. Bush, in his first briefing as head of the CIA, the US foreign intelligence agency, in 1976, heard a briefer describe a major event involving unexplained objects from the early 1960s, and asked what on earth they were talking about, having never heard of it. In one telling Davis names the event as a landing at Holloman Air Force Base in New Mexico in April 1964, and in the story's earliest form Bush also refused to look at film of it, while the podcast host Jesse Michels later retells it as Bush learning of the event by accident. If true, it would mean even the CIA's own director had been kept in the dark.
george-h-w-bush-briefed-into-the-uap-rea: Lue Elizondo, a former Pentagon official who worked on unexplained aerial reports, says that George H.W. Bush, who once ran the CIA and later became US president, was briefed on what he calls the UAP reality. UAP stands for unidentified anomalous phenomena, the government's term for UFOs. He says this on podcast host Jesse Michels' show, and if true it would mean the subject reached the very top of American government.
george-h-w-bush-george-w-bush-and-cheney: Kurt McConnell, a former US Senate staffer speaking on Jesse Michels' podcast, repeats a claim linked to David Grusch, a witness who has spoken out about hidden government UFO work. According to McConnell, George H.W. Bush was allegedly told about a secret "legacy program" holding UFO material while he ran the CIA, America's foreign spy agency, around 1976, and later passed what he knew to his son George W. Bush, with Dick Cheney also playing a part. If true, it would mean the secret was handed down among the country's most powerful leaders for decades.
george-h-w-bush-says-public-not-ready-fo: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that around 2015 or 2016, at a campaign event for Jeb Bush, the former US president George H.W. Bush started talking about how the American public was not ready for the truth about UFOs. Michels stresses that this was well off script for him. If meant seriously, it would suggest a former president knew there was a truth being held back.
george-hunt-williamson-as-adamski-s-hand: A philosopher named Jason Jorjani, speaking on a podcast, says that George Hunt Williamson, a man linked to George Adamski, who claimed in the 1950s to have met visitors from space, was using a false name. Jorjani presents Williamson as Adamski's handler and ties him to the Silver Shirts, an American far-right group led by William Dudley Pelley, as an editor of a publication called Valor, and he also points to a book called Closer Encounters. If true, it would mean someone was steering early alien contact stories from behind the scenes.
george-knapp-brings-back-russian-ufo-fil: This story is about a journalist, George Knapp, who is said to have travelled to Russia in the 1990s and come back with files on Soviet UFO activity. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells it briefly. A physicist, Eric Davis, adds more. He says that when the Soviet Union fell, the KGB, its secret police and spy agency, opened up its files. According to Davis, Knapp and others went there and found a set of papers called the Thread Three documents, which he says show Russia had its own crash retrievals. If true, it would mean another superpower was also recovering unknown craft.
george-knapp-footage-off-baja-and-the-ta: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that a journalist named George Knapp has interesting footage of unexplained things filmed around Baja, on Mexico's Pacific side. Michels adds that across the country, on the other coast, the city of Tampico seems to be a hotspot for such sightings, which would make Mexico a place where these things keep turning up.
george-knapp-says-harry-reid-read-hastin: A researcher named Robert Hastings, who wrote a book called UFOs and Nukes about UFO sightings at nuclear weapons sites, says a journalist, George Knapp, told him something in late 2023. According to Hastings, Knapp asked whether he knew that Harry Reid, a US senator, had read the book, and that it was one reason Reid sought funding for AAWSAP, a Pentagon-funded programme that studied unexplained aerial reports. If true, it would mean a book about nuclear sites helped launch official government UFO research.
george-knapp-urges-lazar-to-go-public-19: Bob Lazar, a man who says he did secret work in Nevada, says that in 1989 in Las Vegas a man named George Knapp told him he had to get his information out publicly. According to Lazar, Knapp said going public was the only way, which Lazar presents as the reason he told his story to the world.
george-smith-deciphers-the-tablets-start: A guest named Matt, speaking on Jesse Michels' podcast, tells how a man named George Smith got hold of ancient clay tablets with writing on them and brought them to the British Museum in London. Matt says Smith spent the next ten years, through the 1870s, studying and decoding them, beginning with the Epic of Gilgamesh, a very old poem from the ancient Middle East. He tells it as the starting point for reading old records that may hold memories of a lost past.
george-trimble-s-1956-claim-on-cancellin: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in a 1956 article in Jane's Defense Weekly, a defence industry publication, George Trimble of the Martin Corporation, an American aircraft maker, said: we're already working on nuclear fuels and equipment to cancel out gravity. Michels raises it because, if true, major aircraft companies were openly chasing anti-gravity technology in the 1950s.
george-w-bush-considered-ufo-disclosure-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says it is now public knowledge, through a physicist named Hal Puthoff, that President George W. Bush thought about telling the public what the government knows about UFOs. According to Michels, Bush weighed this with his national security adviser, Stephen Hadley, at the White House during the 2000s, which would mean a sitting president took the idea of disclosure seriously.
george-w-bush-s-disclosure-net-assessmen: According to the podcast host Jesse Michels, a physicist named Hal Puthoff says President George W. Bush and his vice president, Dick Cheney, were very interested in disclosure, meaning telling the public what the government knows about UFOs. Puthoff says Bush's national security adviser, Stephen Hadley, ran a review of what disclosure would look like, and another researcher says Puthoff himself was asked to take part. In one telling the panel decided disclosure was not worth it. If true, it would mean a US president seriously weighed revealing the secret and chose not to.
georges-st-pierre-s-ce5-sessions-bring-o: Jesse Michels, a podcast host, says he was recently on the phone with Georges St-Pierre, a famous fighter in the UFC, a mixed martial arts league. According to Michels, St-Pierre has been doing CE5, a practice where people meditate in groups to try to call UFOs, and told him "they show up a lot" in the form of glowing orbs in the sky. If true, it would mean anyone could invite these lights to appear.
georgetown-pub-source-it-s-all-about-con: The journalist Ross Coulthart, on Jesse Michels' podcast, says that around 2018 he met a source in a pub in Georgetown, a neighbourhood of Washington, D.C. According to Coulthart, one of the first things this source told him about the secret world of non-human intelligence was that it is all about consciousness, which would mean the mystery is about the mind as much as about machines.
georgia-power-only-his-house-lost-a-leg-: A former guard at a nuclear site named Mario Woods, who says he was abducted, tells podcast host Jesse Michels that in December 2017 his home in Georgia lost one leg of its electric power. He says a supervisor at Georgia Power, the local electric company, told him only his house was affected and that it "lit up our board downtown like the Fourth of July," and he has photos of the transformer. If true, something unusual struck his home's power that night.
gerchsheimer-tricks-schauberger-into-sig: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells how in 1957 a man named Carl Gerchsheimer tricked Viktor Schauberger, an Austrian inventor, into signing over all his intellectual property, meaning the rights to his ideas and inventions, to the United States, with the story moving from Austria to Texas. Michels says that work was then relabelled as atomic energy research. He tells it, drawing on the writer Nick Cook, in a documentary about early secret flying-craft research, as a sign that unusual inventions were quietly taken into American programmes.
german-group-reproducing-the-effect-2020: A witness named Charles, talking on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels in an episode about a claimed antigravity propulsion device, says he is working with another group in Germany that is reproducing the same effect sometime in the 2020s. He gives no more detail than that. If true, it would mean the claimed effect can be repeated by people other than its first builders.
german-nuclear-tests-seen-over-the-balti: A researcher named Jason Jorjani, speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast, says there are eyewitness reports of two German nuclear weapons tests in late 1944 and early 1945, in the Baltic Sea area between Sweden and Finland. If true, Nazi Germany would have tested atomic weapons before the war ended.
german-perforated-metal-found-at-roswell: A researcher named Jason Jorjani, on Jesse Michels's podcast, says German engineers of the 1940s developed a kind of perforated metal, meaning metal full of tiny holes. He says this same material was later found at Roswell, New Mexico, the site of a famous 1947 crash that some say was an alien craft. He points to Philip J. Corso, a US Army officer who wrote about Roswell, and if true the claim would tie the Roswell wreckage to German technology.
german-saucer-airframe-with-boundary-lay: A researcher named Jason Jorjani, on Jesse Michels's podcast, says German engineers of the 1930s and 1940s came up with a saucer-shaped aircraft with suction vents all around its edge. The vents would pull in the thin layer of air that clings to a craft's surface, called the boundary layer. If true, it would mean Germany was designing flying saucers during the Second World War.
german-silver-sighting-balloons-explain-: During World War II, around 1944, aircrews over Germany reported strange spheres in the sky. Mick West, a researcher known for skeptical analysis of UFO cases, says on Jesse Michels's podcast that Germany was using shiny metallic silver balloons at the time to help aim its guns. He offers this as an ordinary explanation for what the crews saw.
german-submarine-carrying-uranium-to-jap: A researcher and author named Peter Levenda, speaking on Jesse Michels' podcast, tells of a German submarine that was stopped around 1945 while heading to Japan. He says it carried uranium, the fuel for atomic bombs, along with parts and engineers, and that Robert Oppenheimer, the physicist who led the American atomic bomb effort, supposedly visited it at a key moment because he could not work out how to make the bomb function. If true, it would mean the first American bomb leaned on captured German material.
german-windhund-bomber-tracking-technolo: An aviation writer named Nick Cook, on Jesse Michels's podcast, recalls a German technology from the Second World War that was used to track enemy bombers. He says he seems to remember that its German name was Windhund, which means greyhound.
gertrude-schmeidler-sheep-goat-studies-1: A researcher named Herb Metts, on an episode of Jesse Michels's podcast about the CIA's psychic spying programme, mentions Gertrude Schmeidler. He says she was a parapsychologist, someone who studies claimed psychic abilities, active in the 1950s, 60s and 70s. Her best-known work was the "sheep-goat" studies, which compared how believers in psychic ability (the sheep) and doubters (the goats) scored on psychic tests.
getting-angry-fries-50-million-of-comput: Lyn Buchanan, an Army sergeant who later joined a military unit that trained people in remote viewing, meaning the claimed ability to sense faraway places with the mind, tells a story from the 1980s at an Army field station in Augsburg, Germany. He says that when he got angry, the entire field station went down, and as he tells it about 50 million dollars of computers were ruined, with Soviet computers in East Germany also part of the story. If true, it would mean a person's mind can knock out machines.
getting-bob-lazar-onto-joe-rogan-s-show-: Jeremy Corbell, speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast, says that around 2019 he helped get Bob Lazar, a man who says he once worked on alien craft at a secret site in Nevada, onto the show of Joe Rogan, a hugely popular podcast host. Corbell says it started with a speakerphone call, when he told Lazar that he and his colleague George Knapp were coming out for a film screening in Michigan. He tells it as the inside story of how Lazar's account reached a huge new audience.
ghislaine-maxwell-s-swedish-male-aides-a: A philosopher named Jason Jorjani, speaking on a podcast, says that Ghislaine Maxwell, a British socialite, had live-in male aides from Sweden at her townhouse on Manhattan's Upper East Side. He bases this on an article by one former aide, which he discussed in a piece on his own newsletter, and the story as told says these aides collected hair, though no date is given. Told this way, it hints at some hidden purpose behind her household.
ghislaine-maxwell-s-terramar-project-as-: Jay Anderson, a guest on Jesse Michels' podcast, talks about the TerraMar Project, an ocean group run in the 2010s by Ghislaine Maxwell, a British socialite tied to the financier Jeffrey Epstein. Anderson says it was really an elite network of trading routes and shipping containers moving around remote places like the waters near Antarctica, off the grid, with links to the businessman Richard Branson's island. If true, it would mean the very rich were running a hidden trade beyond anyone's oversight.
ghost-murmur-quantum-sensor-detects-a-so: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, describes a device called Ghost Murmur, a quantum sensor, meaning an instrument that uses the strange physics of tiny particles to pick up extremely faint signals, linked to the defence company Lockheed Martin. He says that in the 2020s a soldier in the Middle East, in Iran or Afghanistan, needed rescuing, and the sensor found him by detecting his heartbeat. Michels raises it in an episode with a whistleblower, as a hint of how far hidden technology may have advanced.
giant-flown-to-a-base-in-qatar-2005: Tim Alberino, a guest on Jesse Michels' podcast who says US troops captured a 12 foot giant in Afghanistan, passes on what he was told about what happened next. According to Alberino, in 2005 the giant was moved to a military base in Qatar, a small country in the Persian Gulf. If true, it would mean the military took custody of a giant and kept it hidden.
giant-found-dead-at-a-table-with-oysters: Tim Alberino, a guest on Jesse Michels' podcast, relays a story he was told from Santa Anastasia, on the Italian island of Sardinia, around 1978 to 1981. According to Alberino, when a sealed stone tower was opened, a giant was found inside, seated dead at a table with oysters. If true, it would mean giants once lived there and were later hidden away.
giant-kills-a-recon-team-in-a-cave-and-i: This story is about a giant said to have been found in a cave in the Kandahar region of Afghanistan in 2005. A guest named Tim Alberino says a team of American scouts was killed there, and that soldiers found a huge human-like creature eating one of them before they shot it down. The podcast host, Jesse Michels, repeats it more briefly, saying a soldier claims his unit fought the giant in the caves, without mentioning a date, a place or the scouts being eaten. People tell it because, if true, it would mean giant beings have been met by the US military.
giant-progenitor-comet-behind-the-taurid: A researcher named Randall Carlson, on Jesse Michels' podcast, says that 25,000 to 30,000 years ago a gigantic comet, its core perhaps 50 to 60 miles across or more, was captured into an orbit inside Jupiter's. He draws on the work of Victor Clube, William Napier and William Asher, and presents this comet as the parent of the Taurids, a stream of meteors Earth passes through every year. If true, it would mean the debris of one huge comet still circles near our planet.
giant-raccoons-and-the-toe-implant: Steve Coburn, a scientist who studies objects that people believe were implanted in their bodies, says he once had a strange experience at his house in Fillmore, California. Alone one night, he says, he saw giant raccoons in his backyard, and the story ties that night to a small implant found in his toe, with a man named Roger Leer part of the account. If true, it would mean he himself became one of the people he studies.
giant-skeletons-dug-up-in-excavations-of: Randall Carlson, a researcher, says that 19th-century accounts of digging into huge ancient earthen mounds in the United States report giant skeletons over and over again, some seven, eight, even nine feet tall. He points to old records such as early papers of the Smithsonian, the US national museum, the Bureau of American Ethnology, a government office that studied Native American peoples, and 19th-century archives at Emory's library. If true, it would change how we picture the people who lived in ancient America.
giant-skull-carried-by-an-excavator-and-: Tim Alberino, a guest on Jesse Michels' podcast, passes on another story from Santa Anastasia in Sardinia, an Italian island, from around 1978 to 1981. According to Alberino, a man digging at the site found a giant skull so large that he and his wife had to carry it together, and they brought it into the church. If true, it would be physical evidence that giant people once lived there.
giants-driven-out-by-joshua-settle-on-sa: A researcher named Tim Alberino, speaking on the show of a podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells a story drawn from the Old Testament. He says that Joshua, the leader who in the Bible leads the conquest of the land of Canaan, drove out many of the giants there who were not killed in the fighting, and that these giants went on to settle on the island of Sardinia. If true, it would mean the Bible's giants survived and left a trace far from the Holy Land.
gibbons-calls-in-pandolfi-to-brief-on-th: A researcher named Grant Cameron, on Jesse Michels's podcast, says that in the 1990s John Gibbons, President Clinton's science adviser, called in a CIA scientist named Ron Pandolfi to give a briefing. The briefing was for the Rockefeller Initiative, a push by the wealthy philanthropist Laurance Rockefeller to get the White House to release what it knew about UFOs. Cameron says it is established that Pandolfi was the one chosen, which would mean UFO questions reached the president's own advisers.
gifted-and-talented-programs-as-a-funnel: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, suggests that US school programmes for gifted and talented children may have worked, in past decades, as a funnel for finding children with supposed psychic abilities. If so, ordinary education programmes would have doubled as a quiet way to spot recruits for that kind of research.
gifted-education-advisor-assigns-esp-cro: Deep Prasad, a researcher in technology, says that as a child in a school program for gifted students, his advisor kept assigning him topics like ESP, short for extrasensory perception, meaning psychic abilities. He says the assignments later moved on to crop circles, patterns that appear flattened into fields, and then to stories of people being abducted by aliens. He tells it as an early, unusual push toward these subjects.
gifted-kids-program-with-esp-training-fr: Deep Prasad, a technology researcher, says that around age 10 to 12, near Vancouver in Canada, he was in a program for gifted children run by a teacher he calls Miss Kaur. He says she got him to look into ESP, meaning psychic perception, and pointed him toward writers on hidden history such as an author named Jim Marrs. He tells it as the start of his interest in these questions.
gillibrand-and-rubio-s-push-for-accounta: A researcher named Matthew Pines, speaking on Jesse Michels' podcast in 2024, says that US senators such as Kirsten Gillibrand and Marco Rubio have spent the last several years chasing accountability more than disclosure. According to Pines, what drives them is learning that rogue secret programs they never knew existed were holding world-shaking information. If true, it would mean parts of the government kept such knowledge even from Congress.
gimbal-j-hook-path-matches-aircrew-radar: In 2015, off the coast of Florida, Navy jet crews filmed an object in what became known as the Gimbal video, named for the way the object seems to rotate on screen. The story here is an argument about its flight path. A researcher named Merrick von Rennenkampf, speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast in a debate with a skeptic, says the path in the video is a vertical U-turn, which he calls a J-hook. He says this matches exactly what the aircrew said the object tracked on radar did. He makes the point twice in the same debate. The second time, he describes it as a striking match with what the eyewitnesses said: the object reversed direction without making any turning curve at all. If his reading is right, the video would back up the crews' accounts of something moving in a way normal aircraft cannot.
gimbal-object-flying-with-a-v-shaped-fle: Gimbal is a 2015 Navy video, filmed off the US East Coast by fighter jets from the aircraft carrier Roosevelt, showing an object that seems to turn in the air. Marik von Rennenkampf, a guest on Jesse Michels' podcast, says that according to the Navy pilot Ryan Graves the object may have been flying with a whole fleet of other objects in a V shape, which would mean it was part of an organised group rather than a lone thing.
gimbal-object-is-a-distant-jet-2015: Mick West, a well-known UFO skeptic, debated the Gimbal video on Jesse Michels' podcast, a 2015 Navy cockpit video filmed off Florida that shows an object which seems to turn in the air. West says his hypothesis is that the object is simply a distant jet, seen far away by the camera, which would mean nothing unknown was there.
gimbal-object-wobbles-after-video-cuts-o: Gimbal is a 2015 Navy video, filmed off Florida, of an object that seems to turn in the air. A guest named Merrick says on Jesse Michels' podcast that according to the air crew, including the pilot Ryan Graves, the object kept wobbling after the recording stopped, which would mean the moving part of the story goes beyond what the video shows.
gimbal-pilot-confirms-the-lns-radar-targ: In the Gimbal video, a 2015 Navy cockpit recording made off the US East Coast of an object that seems to turn, the pilots can be heard talking. Marik von Rennenkampf, a guest on Jesse Michels' podcast, explains that when they mention the LNS they mean the launch and steering target, the one the radar has locked on to, which he says shows the object was a real radar target and not only a picture on the camera.
gimbal-radar-returns-as-interference-or-: Mick West, a UFO skeptic, discussed on Jesse Michels' podcast the radar readings that Navy aircrew describe around the Gimbal video, a 2015 recording off the US East Coast of an object that seems to turn. West says someone suggested to him that there may have been a distant jet and the radar got confused, making false returns or echoes, which would mean the strange radar picture came from the equipment, not from an unknown craft.
gimbal-recorded-by-ryan-graves-squadron-: A guest named Merrick says on Jesse Michels' podcast that the Gimbal video, a 2015 Navy cockpit recording made off Florida of an object that seems to turn in the air, came from the squadron of the Navy pilot Ryan Graves. He names it as VFA-11, a Navy fighter squadron nicknamed the Red Rippers, which ties the video to pilots who have spoken publicly about what they saw.
gimbal-rotation-is-a-camera-artifact-201: Mick West, a UFO skeptic, says on Jesse Michels' podcast that the turning seen in the Gimbal video, a 2015 Navy cockpit recording made off Florida, is probably a camera artifact. He says a mechanism inside the camera that keeps the image upright makes a blurry glare spin, and at one point he applies the same idea to the object's shape too. If he is right, the object's famous rotation would not be the object moving at all.
gimbal-ufo-video-argument-between-marik-: A journalist named Michael Shellenberger mentions a running argument about the Gimbal video, a military video of an unidentified flying object. He says a writer named Marik von Rennenkampff has been debating it with a man named Mick West, a dispute over whether the video really shows something unexplained.
gimbal-video-audio-a-whole-fleet-of-them: The Gimbal video is cockpit footage that Navy aircrew recorded around 2015 off the US East Coast, showing an unknown object that seems to rotate in the air. On the recording, one of the crew can be heard saying "there's a whole fleet of them" and telling another to look at the radar screen. If taken at face value, it means the crew saw not one strange object but a group of them.
girls-creature-and-hospital-being-were-t: A researcher named James Fox, on Jesse Michels' podcast, discusses events in the Brazilian town of Varginha in January 1996, where girls said they saw a strange creature and a being was reportedly captured and taken to a hospital. Fox, citing a witness named Italo Venturelli, says the creature the girls saw and the being at the hospital had to be one and the same. If true, it would tie the sighting directly to a capture of a living non-human creature.
girls-on-horseback-turned-back-on-her-bi: Scott Ramsay, who researches a flying saucer said to have crashed near Aztec, New Mexico in 1948, tells what a woman told him. She said that she and other girls riding horses were turned back on the road to Hart Canyon, where the crash is said to have happened. When he asked how she knew the date was March 25, 1948, she answered that it was her birthday, which if true pins the crash to that day.
giza-mapped-to-orion-s-belt-around-10-60: The podcast host Jesse Michels says in 2025 that the three great pyramids at Giza in Egypt line up exactly with Orion's Belt, the row of three bright stars in the constellation Orion. He says that perfect match happened around 10,600 BC, when the sky shifted into that position. Graham Hancock, an author who writes about lost ancient civilisations, also talks about the pyramids lining up with Orion's Belt, but he gives no date. He says instead that in many cultures Orion's Belt was seen as the place where souls rise to after death. If true, the alignment would point either to a much older plan for the pyramids or to a spiritual purpose.
giza-pink-granite-hauled-500-miles-from-: A researcher named Matt LaCroix, on Jesse Michels's podcast, says all the pink granite found across the Giza Plateau in Egypt, where the great pyramids stand, came from the Aswan quarry about 500 miles to the south. He tells it to show the huge effort the ancient builders would have needed to move such heavy stone so far.
giza-pyramid-stones-may-have-been-mixed-: Joe McMoneagle, a researcher who also wrote a book called The Ultimate Time Machine, suggests that the stones of the pyramids at Giza in Egypt may not have been cut and hauled. He says the builders might have mixed the stone material and poured it into shape, which if true would change how we think the pyramids were built.
giza-wide-model-presented-at-the-malta-c: A researcher called Jeffrey, on Jesse Michels's podcast, describes a model shown at the end of a conference in Malta in 2024 by a team including a man named Filippo. According to Jeffrey, the model covers the whole Giza Plateau in Egypt, including the Menkaure pyramid and the Sphinx. He says it shows vertical structures underground that connect to cube-shaped features, which if true would point to a large hidden network beneath the pyramids.
glasnost-era-russian-crashed-craft-us-as: A journalist named Ross Coulthart, speaking on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, passes on a story someone told him. He says that during glasnost, the period around the late 1980s when the Soviet Union opened up and it was friendlier with America, Russia told the United States it had a crashed craft, and an American astronaut was reportedly sent to help recover it. If true, it would mean the two rival powers once quietly worked together on something not of human make.
glenn-gaffney-allegedly-blocked-ufo-mate: Podcast host Jesse Michels says a couple of people, one of them under oath before the US Congress, have said that a man named Glenn Gaffney blocked a transfer of UFO material from Lockheed Martin, a large American defense company, to Bigelow Aerospace, a private space company. If true, it would mean private companies hold UFO material and someone stopped it changing hands.
glenn-gaffney-blocked-transfer-of-nhi-ma: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says there is congressional testimony that a man named Glenn Gaffney blocked a plan in 2008 to move exotic technology of non-human origin, held under lock and key, to Bigelow Aerospace, a private space company. He credits a report he calls the historical report, volume one. Michels tells it because, if true, it would mean such material exists and someone inside the government chose to keep it hidden.
glenn-gaffney-head-of-the-crash-retrieva: Eric Davis, a scientist who worked on a Pentagon-funded study of unexplained aerial phenomena around 2008 to 2012, says his team wanted to talk to Glenn Gaffney, who he says ran a program to recover crashed craft of unknown origin inside the CIA's science and technology branch. Davis says Gaffney refused to talk to them. If true, it would mean such a recovery program existed inside the CIA, the US spy agency.
glenn-gaffney-named-as-a-leader-of-the-l: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that many people name Glenn Gaffney, who headed science and technology at the CIA, the American foreign spy agency, in the 2000s, as one of the last leaders of the legacy program. That is the name used for a long-running secret effort said to hold recovered craft of non-human origin. If true, it would place that effort inside the CIA's own research branch.
glenn-gaffney-on-aaro-s-board-2020: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says he believes that Glenn Gaffney, whom he describes as the CIA's director of science and technology, sat on the board of AARO, a Pentagon office set up in the 2020s to look into unexplained aerial reports. If so, a senior CIA science official would have had a hand in the government's own UFO office.
glenn-gaffney-said-to-have-run-the-crash: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says there was a man rumoured to run the whole legacy crash retrieval program, a secret effort said to recover and study crashed craft not made by humans. He names him as Glenn Gaffney, who was the director of science and technology at the CIA, the American foreign spy agency. If true, it would mean one senior intelligence official oversaw the whole hidden effort.
glenn-martin-company-employs-louis-witte: In the 1950s, the story goes, an American aircraft maker called the Glenn Martin Company hired a physicist named Louis Witten, father of Edward Witten, to do research on anti-gravity, meaning ways to cancel or control gravity. A researcher, Eric Weinstein, says he believes the work was somehow linked to Wright-Patterson, an Air Force base in Ohio, and to Johns Hopkins University in Baltimore. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, states it more firmly: Witten worked in an anti-gravity unit inside Martin's research arm, which they call RIAS, the Research Institute for Advanced Study, and also did gravity contract work for Wright-Patterson. Weinstein likens RIAS to a hidden version of a famous corporate lab and lists well-known scientists who worked there, while Michels adds that a Martin vice-president, George Trimble, drove it and may have worked with the inventor Townsend Brown. If true, it would mean serious money and talent went into anti-gravity research in the 1950s.
glimpsed-classified-uap-photos-via-colle: Bob McGwier, described as a former contractor for the CIA, the US foreign intelligence agency, says that through colleagues in secret government settings he got to see classified material. He says this included photos and other records indicating that UAP, the government's term for unidentified objects in the sky, are really here. If true, it would mean the government holds hidden proof of such objects.
global-crash-recovery-and-reverse-engine: Jake Barber, who says he once flew a helicopter to retrieve a UFO, said on Jesse Michels's podcast that the US is not the only country doing this kind of work. He says there are programmes around the world that recover crashed craft and try to reverse engineer them, meaning take them apart to learn how to copy the technology. If true, the race to understand such craft would be global.
global-ufo-nuclear-link-from-roswell-to-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, draws a line linking UFOs and nuclear sites around the world. He starts at Roswell, New Mexico, in 1947, a place famous for a reported crash of a strange craft, which he calls the site of the largest nuclear weapons stockpile of its day, and runs it through Fukushima in Japan and Chernobyl in Ukraine, both tied to nuclear power. If true, it would suggest whatever is behind UFOs takes a special interest in nuclear power and weapons.
glomar-explorer-possibly-dual-use-1974: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, wonders aloud whether the Glomar Explorer, a big ship working in the Pacific Ocean around 1974 and tied to a huge corporation, might have served a second, hidden purpose. He raises it in a talk about unexplained things in the ocean, hinting that the ship's work might have touched on that subject too.
glomar-explorer-recovers-a-sunken-soviet: On a show hosted by a podcaster named Jesse Michels, a researcher and author named Richard Dolan describes how, in the 1970s, a huge corporation pulled a sunken Soviet submarine up from the floor of the Pacific Ocean using a ship called the Glomar Explorer. He names the businessman Howard Hughes and a company called Global Marine Corporation as part of it, and calls the recovery an incredible feat. He tells it as an example of how much secret retrieval work the government could pull off out of sight.
glowing-disc-photographed-over-property-: The owner of Skinwalker Ranch, a property in Utah's Uinta Basin known for reports of strange happenings, says that in June 2016 a glowing object was photographed over the land. He says the first image looked almost like the Millennium Falcon, the spaceship from Star Wars: a glowing, disc-shaped thing. He tells it as one of the sightings that, if real, point to something unexplained at the ranch.
glowing-hole-in-bedroom-wall-and-electri: Mario Woods, described as a former guard at a nuclear site, says that on December 17, 2017, at his home in Georgia, a glowing hole about four and a half to five feet across appeared in the north wall of his bedroom, and the electricity failed. He mentions a person named Jake in the account. He tells it as part of what he describes as an abduction experience.
glowing-orb-ufos-at-pyramid-kuromanta-sh: Geoffrey Drumm, a researcher who studies pyramids, talks about Kuromanta, a hill in Akita, Japan that some call a pyramid. He says glowing balls of light appear there, and that old Japanese paintings show these same glowing balls, which if true would mean the lights have been seen at the site for centuries.
glowing-red-metal-found-in-a-yard-under-: Chris Bledsoe, a man who says he has many encounters with UFOs, retells what another man told him in the 1990s in Zanesville, Ohio. According to that man, he saw something hovering over his house, it went away as he drove up, and a piece of glowing red metal was left in his yard. If true, it would be a physical piece left behind by an unknown craft.
go-fast-email-deleted-under-the-spillage: Tim Gallaudet, a retired US Navy admiral, says that a Navy official named Jay Stratton told him about an email carrying the Go Fast video, a Navy clip of a small object speeding low over the ocean, around 2015. According to Stratton's account, the email was deleted from Navy networks under the spillage protocol, the rule for wiping secret material sent to the wrong place, at a time when officials still were not sure whether the object was a rival nation's technology or something from off-world. If true, it would mean evidence was erased while the question was still open.
go-fast-is-a-wind-blown-balloon-2015: Mick West, a skeptic who studies UFO videos, talks about "Go Fast", a 2015 Navy video filmed off Jacksonville, Florida, that seems to show a small object racing low over the ocean. On Jesse Michels's podcast he says his best guess is that it is just something carried by the wind, like a balloon, and only looks fast because of how the camera views it. If he is right, the video shows nothing unusual.
go-fast-object-one-of-four-in-line-abrea: Go Fast is a video from 2015, recorded off the coast of Jacksonville, Florida, showing a small object moving fast over the ocean. On the podcast of a host, Jesse Michels, a debater named Merrick says, passing on what a Navy pilot named Ryan Graves has said, that the object was one of four flying side by side in a line. If true, it would mean the object was not alone but part of a group flying in formation. A retired Navy admiral, Tim Gallaudet, tells it too and goes further. He says it was a round object with no wings, flaps or visible engine, moving in an intelligently controlled way, and again that there were four of them. He rejects the idea that the speed is just an illusion caused by the camera's angle.
go-fast-video-recorded-off-jacksonville-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that the Go Fast video, a short Navy cockpit camera clip of an unexplained object, was recorded in January 2015 about 300 miles off the coast of Jacksonville, Florida, by aircraft from the USS Roosevelt, an aircraft carrier. He sets this out as the starting point for discussing the clip, because if the object is what it seems, Navy pilots filmed something they could not identify.
gobekli-tepe-as-a-possible-origin-of-civ: This story is about Göbekli Tepe, a very old stone site in Turkey. The talk show host Joe Rogan says many people think it may be where civilization began, rather than Egypt. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, goes further. Leaning on the writer Graham Hancock, author of the book Fingerprints of the Gods, and on National Geographic, he dates it to about 11,000 years ago. Michels says it rewrites the map of how old human civilization is, where Rogan only calls it a possible origin. If true, it would mean advanced human culture is far older than usually told.
gobekli-tepe-as-an-astronomical-calendar: Göbekli Tepe is a very old site in Turkey with huge carved stone pillars. On a show hosted by a podcaster named Jesse Michels, a researcher called Matt says the carvings on those pillars are basically star constellations, so the site worked as a calendar tracking the Great Year, the slow cycle of about 26,000 years in which the stars seem to shift across the sky. If so, the people who built it watched the sky far more closely than is usually thought.
gobekli-tepe-built-and-buried-by-survivo: On a show hosted by a podcaster named Jesse Michels, a researcher named Jay Anderson talks about Göbekli Tepe, a site in Turkey that he calls the oldest temple of huge standing stones. He says experts thought only simple hunter-gatherers lived in that area, and then this remarkable temple came up out of the ground, which he takes as a sign it was built, and later buried, by people who survived some ancient disaster.
gobekli-tepe-chalices-and-burial-rituals: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, points to Brian Muraresku, author of a book called The Immortality Key, who mentions drinking cups dug up at Göbekli Tepe, an ancient site about 12,000 years old. Michels says this dates to just before people began farming, and ties the cups to burial rituals. He brings it up in an episode about mushrooms, hinting that people may have used mind-altering drinks in ritual from very early on.
gobekli-tepe-datable-because-it-was-buri: On a show hosted by a podcaster named Jesse Michels, a researcher named Matt LaCroix talks about Göbekli Tepe, an ancient site of big carved stone pillars in Turkey, dated to around 9600 BC. He says the only reason anyone could put a date on it is that the site was believed to have been buried, which matters because it suggests other old stone sites that were never buried may be older than anyone can show.
gobekli-tepe-pillar-43-as-a-sky-map-of-1: Göbekli Tepe is an ancient site in Turkey of carved stone pillars, and one of them, known as Pillar 43, stands in a ring of stones called Enclosure D, which is dated to about 11,600 years ago. On a show hosted by a podcaster named Jesse Michels, a writer named Graham Hancock says the carvings on that pillar are, very persuasively, a picture of the sky at the summer solstice about 12,500 years ago. If true, the builders were recording the heavens, and perhaps a memorable event, with real skill.
god-s-divine-council-in-genesis-behold-m: Luke Caverns, a researcher, points to a passage in Genesis, the first book of the Bible, set in the Garden of Eden. He says God turns to a divine council, a mysterious gathering of other beings in heaven, and says "Behold, man has become like us." Caverns says this detail is often overlooked, and to him it suggests God was not alone but among other heavenly beings.
goethe-s-merging-with-strasbourg-cathedr: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells how the German writer Goethe once felt himself merge with Strasbourg Cathedral, drawing on the philosopher Rudolf Steiner and on Goethe's ideas about how we come to know things. Michels uses it as an example of a mind joining with what it looks at, a way of knowing beyond the ordinary senses.
going-back-in-time-in-dreams-with-the-mo: Rolf Mowatt-Larssen, a former senior officer at the CIA, the US intelligence agency, says that in dreams he visited a mountain with a group of monks he calls the Monotones and kept going back in time. He says a man named Harry Heller told him time is an illusion, and that his dream experiences proved it to him, an idea he links to Albert Einstein. If true, it would mean the mind can move through time.
going-public-with-the-find-through-expre: A Swedish treasure hunter named Dennis Asberg says that he found something on the seafloor that he describes as looking like a UFO. He tells podcast host Jesse Michels that around 2011 he went public with it by talking to a journalist at Expressen, a big newspaper in Stockholm. If his account is right, that newspaper story is how the find first reached a wider audience.
gold-flown-to-geneva-and-gold-certificat: Dan Sheehan, a lawyer and researcher, tells Jesse Michels' podcast that in the late 1940s huge amounts of gold were flown out of Europe on US military transport planes and deposited at the International Credit Bank in Geneva, Switzerland. He says gold certificates, paper notes backed by that gold, were then issued, and he links the scheme to Allen Dulles, a US intelligence official, as a way of funding secret operations against communism. If true, it would mean early covert operations ran on a hidden fortune outside normal oversight.
golden-calcite-alabaster-altar-of-unknow: On a show hosted by a podcaster named Jesse Michels, a researcher called Matt describes an ancient altar in the region around Lake Van in Turkey. He says it is made of golden calcite alabaster, a soft, glowing kind of stone, and that nobody even knows where the stone came from, which he offers as a hint of a lost history.
golden-orb-escorted-by-helicopters-risin: Ross Coulthart, a journalist, says he was told that if you watched one spot over Secret Mountain in Arizona, you would see a big orb rise from behind the mountain with helicopters escorting it. He says that at 1:30 in the morning, sure enough, up came a gigantic, beautiful golden orb that pulsed and looked like glowing plasma; in one telling he calls the helicopters Black Hawks, a type of military helicopter, dates it to 2025 and credits a woman named Melinda Leslie, and in another he leaves out the pulsing. If true, it would suggest the military is flying or guarding something unknown there.
golf-ball-bounces-off-the-reactor-s-fiel: Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked on alien craft in the late 1980s at S4, a secret site in the Nevada desert, says a colleague once showed him the invisible field around one craft's reactor. According to Lazar, the colleague said "Check this out" and threw a golf ball at the reactor, but it bounced off the field and hit a ceiling tile. If true, it would mean the craft's power source made something like a force field.
golf-ball-lands-on-frederick-wolfe-s-gra: Rolf Mowatt-Larssen, a former senior CIA officer, says that in 1976 he was playing golf at Fort Knox, an Army base in Kentucky whose course has a small cemetery on it. He says his ball landed on a grave whose marker read Frederick Wolfe, a German soldier who had died there. He tells it as a striking coincidence that seemed to mean something to him.
gorard-and-wolfram-hypergraph-physics-pr: Matthew Pines, an analyst speaking on a podcast, says that the physicist Jonathan Gorard, working with the scientist Stephen Wolfram and a researcher named Xerxes Arsiwalla, reached a breakthrough in 2020 and 2021. According to Pines, their project, which pictures the universe as a vast web of connected points called a hypergraph and grows out of Wolfram's book A New Kind of Science, recovered both general relativity, Einstein's theory of gravity, and quantum mechanics, the physics of the very small. He calls the result really suggestive, since it would hint that both theories come from one simpler foundation.
gorbachev-says-various-civilizations-hav: Kiran Ilum Xenov, a Russian politician presented on a podcast as a former president of a Russian republic who says he was taken by aliens in 1997, recalls a conversation from the 1990s. He says that Mikhail Gorbachev, the former president of the Soviet Union, told them that various civilizations have made contact with people on Earth. If true, it would mean a former Soviet leader believed contact had already happened.
gordon-cooper-mercury-astronaut-among-pi: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, names Gordon Cooper among the pilots who have seen UFOs. Cooper was one of the first American astronauts, part of Mercury, the first US programme to send people into space, and Michels says he spent more time in space than the others. He brings Cooper up because, if true, it would mean some of the most trusted flyers in the country have seen these things.
gordon-cooper-s-1957-craft-landing-on-ba: Gordon Cooper was an American astronaut and test pilot, and a man named Charlie Foltz says Cooper told him that in 1957 a craft physically landed on the air base where Cooper was working. In a clip of Cooper himself, shown on Jesse Michels's podcast, Cooper says a saucer flew right over a film crew, put down three small landing legs, and landed on a dry lake bed. If true, it would be a craft of unknown origin landing in full view on a military base.
gordon-cooper-s-book-von-braun-worked-on: Robert Salas, a former US Air Force officer, says that Gordon Cooper, an American astronaut, wrote a book describing a talk with Wernher von Braun, the German rocket scientist. According to Salas, Cooper writes that von Braun told him they had actually worked on UFO craft in Nazi Germany in the 1940s. If true, it would mean UFO-like craft were being built by humans during the Second World War.
gordon-cooper-s-saucer-shaped-craft-flyi: Gordon Cooper, an American astronaut who was earlier a military pilot, says that in the 1950s he saw craft flying in formation. He says it turned out they had no wings and were shaped like saucers. If true, it would mean a trained pilot saw flying machines unlike any known aircraft.
gordon-cooper-visits-puharich-s-ossining: In the 1970s, according to this story, the American astronaut Gordon Cooper visited a lab in Ossining, New York, run by a researcher named Andrija Puharich. A researcher named Greg, a guest on Jesse Michels's podcast, says Cooper went there many times. Greg says Cooper writes in his own book about watching experiments with a Faraday cage, a metal enclosure that blocks electrical signals, and about meeting the young people the group called the space kids. Another guest on the same episode adds that a woman named Valerie Ransone brought Cooper there, and places the visits in the late 1970s. It matters to the tellers because, if true, a famous astronaut took part firsthand in Puharich's unusual experiments.
gordon-creighton-and-prince-philip-s-int: Steven Greer, a man who collects witness accounts about UFOs, says he interviewed a British man named Gordon Creighton, who had worked in military intelligence and published Flying Saucer Review, a magazine of UFO reports. According to Greer, copies of this material used to go to the royal palace in the United Kingdom, and Prince Philip, of the British royal family, was very keen on all of it. If true, it would mean interest in UFOs reached the British royal household.
gordon-gray-named-in-the-mj12-documents-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that the government official Gordon Gray is named in the Majestic 12 papers, leaked documents that describe a top secret research group said to have been set up by President Truman in the late 1940s. According to Michels, Gray appears there as one of the group's advisers. He tells it to tie real officials to a hidden effort to deal with UFOs.
gordon-macdonald-said-the-moon-only-make: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Gordon MacDonald, whom he describes as a space adviser to President Eisenhower, possibly linked to NASA, the US space agency, claimed the Moon only makes sense if it is hollow. Michels says he has read MacDonald's work, and in a later episode calls him Eisenhower's chief space adviser. If true, a serious government scientist would have doubted that the Moon is an ordinary solid body.
gordon-novel-prosecuted-for-burning-down: Dan Sheehan, a lawyer and researcher, tells Jesse Michels' podcast about a man named Gordon Novel. Sheehan says Novel was arrested and prosecuted by Jim Garrison, the New Orleans prosecutor who investigated the killing of President Kennedy, for burning down 555 Camp Street, an office building that Sheehan connects to Lee Harvey Oswald, the man accused of shooting Kennedy, and to Guy Banister. If true, it would suggest someone wanted evidence at that office destroyed.
gordon-novel-shows-ufo-propulsion-drawin: Dan Sheehan, a lawyer who says he was representing a doctor named John Mack, says that in 1994 he was giving a presentation at the International UFO Congress, a gathering of UFO researchers. He says a man named Gordon Novel walked up out of the crowd and told him he had drawings showing how UFOs are propelled. If true, it would mean someone was offering inside knowledge of how such craft fly.
gordon-novel-threatens-sheehan-and-is-la: Dan Sheehan, a lawyer, says that sometime in the 1980s or 1990s in Washington, a man named Gordon Novel threatened him. He says Novel was later hired by John Alexander as one of the investigators for NIDS, a private group that looked into UFOs and other strange events. He tells it to suggest unsettling links between the people around this subject.
gorilla-masks-for-u-2-and-sr-71-test-pil: A philosopher named Jason Jorjani, drawing on the journalist Annie Jacobsen's book Area 51, about a secret US base in Nevada, says that test pilots of the U-2 and SR-71, high-flying American spy planes of the 1950s and 60s, were handed gorilla masks. According to the story, they were told that if they ever got close enough to a passenger airliner for its pilot to make eye contact, they should put the mask on first. Told this way, it suggests secret flights were made to look absurd so that any sighting would not be believed.
gotthard-tunnel-proof-of-concept-scan-20: The Gotthard Tunnel is a very long railway tunnel through the Alps in Switzerland. On a show hosted by a podcaster named Jesse Michels, a researcher called Jeffrey says a scan of the tunnel in 2024, credited to a colleague named Filippo, was the final proof that their scanning method works, meaning it can see what is really underground. He brings it up to back their claim that the same method has found a huge hidden structure beneath the pyramids of Egypt.
government-air-to-air-flir-expert-s-emai: Gimbal is a video filmed off the US East Coast around 2015 by an infrared camera on a Navy jet, the kind of camera called FLIR, which sees heat. It shows an object that seems to rotate, and people argue over whether the object really turns or whether the camera makes it look that way. During a debate on the podcast of a host, Jesse Michels, an analyst named Marik von Rennenkampf reads an email from a government expert in this kind of camera footage, who writes that the object is definitely maneuvering, causing the look of rotation. If so, the turning would be the object's own movement, not a camera trick. A second debater, Merrick, says he and others were on a call with the same expert, who called the video bizarre and said he had never seen anything like it. They make the point to a well-known skeptic, Mick West.
government-background-check-on-harringto: Brent Friedman, who grew up near a man named John Harrington in Walnut Creek, California, says that around 1980 his family was approached by people from a government agency, something like the NSA or the CIA, both US intelligence services. He says they came in and asked a lot of questions, which he took as a background check on Harrington's neighbours. If true, it would mean Harrington was being vetted for some kind of secret government work.
government-contracts-that-were-really-fo: James Valor, from Skywatcher, a startup that tries to call up and record UFOs, says that between about 2021 and 2025 his group got contracts from the US government to collect data on these unexplained objects. As the story goes, the contracts were presented as war games but were really about gathering this data. If true, it would mean the government quietly paid private groups to study UFOs.
government-crash-photos-that-faded-to-bl: Scott Ramsay, who researches a flying saucer said to have crashed near Aztec, New Mexico in 1948, refers back to the original story about it by a writer, Frank Scully. He says there were two sets of photographs of the crash, and that the set the government took did not last long, fading to blank. If true, it would explain why official pictures of the crash never surfaced.
government-documents-describe-metallic-r: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that US government papers from 1947 to 1952 describe the objects people saw as metallic, reflective and flat-bottomed. He names a 1947 Air Force letter called the Twining memo, a 1948 analysis by Project Sign, an early Air Force UFO study, a CIA analysis of UFOs seen over Washington, D.C. in 1952, and the work of Captain Edward J. Ruppelt, who led the Air Force's later UFO study. He tells it to show that officials themselves wrote of solid, built-looking craft.
government-gives-a-craft-to-industry-con: Eric Davis, a scientist who has worked with the Pentagon, says on Jesse Michels's podcast that two unnamed sources in the aerospace industry told him how it works: the government hands a company a craft and says "we want to know how it works." He adds that the company gets a sole-source contract, one given to a single firm without competition, with the job already set: take the craft apart piece by piece, put it back together, and see if they can make it fly. If true, private defence companies would be holding and studying non-human craft.
government-group-working-on-quantum-vacu: Dave Rossi, a guest who says aliens taught him advanced physics, talks about a kind of surveillance that draws on the quantum vacuum, the energy physicists say fills even empty space. He says he knows a group inside the government that has worked on this since the 1990s. He adds that they have had massive success and that the technology is established, not a prototype, which if true would mean a hidden spying ability already in use.
government-holds-close-range-cell-phone-: A man named Dylan Borland, talking to the podcast host Jesse Michels, says he knows for a fact that the US government holds mobile phone videos of the triangles, the large triangle-shaped craft people report seeing in the sky. He calls the footage undeniable and says it would settle the question once and for all. In another part of the talk he calls the videos classified but doesn't say who holds them or how close they were filmed. If he is right, there would be hard proof sitting in official hands.
government-knowledge-that-scalar-waves-a: A scientist named Steve, who studies objects he says are alien implants in human bodies, cites the books of a writer, Tom Bearden. He says the government has known for years that certain scalar electromagnetic waves, an unusual kind of wave Bearden wrote about, can change how fast radioactive materials decay. If true, it would mean a secret way to control radioactivity.
government-people-pushed-an-alien-narrat: A man named Chris Bledsoe, who says he has had many encounters with UFOs since 2007, told the podcast host Jesse Michels that government people tried from the start to steer what he believed. He says they kept pushing him to believe in flying saucers and little green men. His point is that someone wanted to shape how he explained his own experiences.
government-psychic-programs-prompted-by-: On a show hosted by a podcaster named Jesse Michels, a former US Senate staff member named Kirk McConnell talks about the government programmes, from the 1950s on, that studied psychic abilities. He says he suspects one of the main reasons the government ran them was what it was learning about UFOs and beings from other worlds, which would mean UFO knowledge was shaping secret research for decades.
government-published-propaganda-books-as: Brent Friedman, a guest on a podcast, retells what he says John Harrington, presented as a former US Secretary of Energy, told him around 1981. According to Friedman, Harrington said bookstore shelves hold many books with lots of truth about UFOs, but right next to them are books the government publishes full of propaganda. He called it a multi-billion dollar campaign to cover up the truth.
government-recruited-psi-capable-childre: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says the US government spent decades quietly finding children across the country who seemed able to affect things with their minds, and ran psychic experiments on them. In different episodes he says the children were found through gifted-children programmes and taken to national laboratories, naming the Atomic Energy Commission, a former US nuclear agency, and Battelle, a research institute, and elsewhere he links it to the psychic research of the physicists Hal Puthoff and Russell Targ. If true, it would mean psychic ability was treated as real enough to study in children for years.
government-underfunding-meant-no-helicop: Skywatcher, a startup that tries to call up and record UFOs, says the government paid for some of its observation events in the western United States between about 2020 and 2025, in a story that also mentions a man named Jake Barber. The group says it was disappointed because the money was too little, so it could not afford a helicopter for the events. If true, it would mean the government funded UFO watching, just not very generously.
government-wanted-as-many-crashes-as-pos: John Brandenburg, a scientist, says he has heard accounts about the US government during the Cold War. According to those accounts, the government wanted as many unknown craft to crash as possible so it could harvest as much of their technology as it could.
government-whistleblowers-claim-ufo-retr: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that government whistleblowers have come forward claiming the US has recovered UFOs. He notes that one of them has been on his show and that he finds it hard to poke holes in that man's story, which, if true, would mean the government holds crashed or captured craft.
governments-hide-the-bodies-for-cold-war: On a show hosted by a podcaster named Jesse Michels, a man named David Ruiz, speaking about strange three-fingered bodies said to come from Peru, says the governments most eager to hide such things are the ones that do the most reverse engineering, meaning taking apart an object to learn how to build it. He ties this to what went on during the Cold War, the long standoff between the US and the Soviet Union, implying the bodies are kept hidden to stay ahead in that race.
governor-richardson-on-looking-into-the-: James Fox, a UFO researcher, says that Bill Richardson, a former governor of New Mexico, once told him that one of the few things he did in his political career was look into UFOs, especially the Roswell crash. Roswell is the town in New Mexico where, many say, something crashed in 1947 and was taken away by the military. Fox tells it because it suggests a senior politician took that story seriously.
gps-lost-over-the-object-on-the-stockhol: A Swedish treasure hunter named Dennis Asberg says his team found a strange object on the floor of the Baltic Sea, between Sweden and Finland. He told the podcast host Jesse Michels that in June 2025 he went back out on a research ship from Stockholm University. He says that when the ship passed over the object, a man on board named Tomas told him their GPS, the satellite system that fixes a ship's position, had started acting up. He tells it as a sign that something odd is down there.
graham-hancock-on-joe-rogan-the-sarcopha: A pyramid researcher named Luke Caverns tells podcast host Jesse Michels that Graham Hancock, a writer on lost ancient civilizations, has said on Joe Rogan's popular podcast that the stone box in Egypt's Great Pyramid, usually called a sarcophagus or stone coffin, may not be one. According to Caverns, Hancock now suggests it was a place where a person lay down inside, to raise their consciousness. If true, the pyramid would have been built for a spiritual purpose rather than a burial.
graham-hancock-s-first-article-on-the-ar: Jesse Michels, a podcast host, recalls that the writer Graham Hancock told him his very first piece of writing was a magazine article about the Ark of the Covenant, the sacred chest from the Bible said to hold the Ten Commandments. Michels mentions it as an early sign of Hancock's lifelong pull toward ancient mysteries.
graham-hancock-s-lost-ice-age-civilizati: Michael Shermer, a well-known skeptic, describes on Jesse Michels's podcast the idea of the writer Graham Hancock, set out in books like "Fingerprints of the Gods". According to Shermer, Hancock thinks very old sites such as Göbekli Tepe, an ancient stone site in Turkey, were built by a lost advanced people from before the end of the Ice Age, "the Atlanteans or whoever." If true, human history would be much older and stranger than the textbooks say.
graham-hancock-s-text-doubting-the-giza-: In 2025 a researcher named Filippo Biondi was putting forward radar scans of the Giza pyramids in Egypt. The scans used SAR, short for synthetic aperture radar, a way of building pictures from radar signals. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says he texted Graham Hancock, a writer on lost ancient civilisations, to ask about it.
