According to Michels, Hancock wrote back that he had "no reason to believe that the source here is being honest", which matters because the scans would point to hidden structures under the pyramids if they hold up.
graham-hancock-s-yage-experience-of-a-co: A writer named Graham Hancock, who is known for his books about lost ancient civilisations, told the podcast host Jesse Michels about drinking yage, a plant brew from South America that causes visions. He says that during the experience he sensed a presence, and that this presence was communicating with him. To him, it suggests there may be other minds out there that we can reach this way.
graham-hancock-ties-cydonia-s-monoliths-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that the writer Graham Hancock, in his 1998 book The Mars Mystery, suggests a link between worn-down stone shapes in Cydonia, a region of Mars, and the symbols of ancient civilizations on Earth. If true, it would mean Mars and early Earth cultures share some kind of common story.
grail-finds-large-lunar-caverns-and-lava: An unnamed researcher on Jesse Michels' podcast says that in the 2010s NASA used a probe called GRAIL to see beneath the surface of the Moon. According to the guest, it found large caverns and lava tubes, long tunnels left behind by ancient lava flows. If true, it would mean the Moon has big hollow spaces under its surface.
grandfather-s-name-carved-atop-the-great: An author named Graham Hancock says that when he climbed the Great Pyramid in Egypt, he and Santha Faiia, who was with him, found a carving near the top that read "P Hancock, 5th of April 1916." He tells podcast host Jesse Michels that this was his grandfather, Philip Hancock, whose diaries back up the visit. In one telling he puts the name at the top, and in another one step down from the top on the south side. For Hancock, it is a personal link between his family and the ancient monument he has spent years writing about.
grandfather-s-radio-plays-on-wedding-day: A researcher named Michael Shermer, known for doubting such claims, says that on his wedding day in 2014, at his house near Los Angeles, he heard music coming from a desk. He says he opened the drawer and found a grandfather's old radio switched on, perfectly tuned to a station playing beautiful romantic music, a story he tied to his wife Jennifer and wrote about in his column for the magazine Scientific American. He tells it because, if taken at face value, it would look like a sign from beyond ordinary explanation.
grant-files-47-foias-at-midnight-on-janu: A longtime UFO researcher named Grant Cameron says that one second after midnight on January 20, he filed 47 requests under FOIA, a US law that lets anyone ask for government records, all at once. He tells podcast host Jesse Michels that the requests were aimed at records about whether Reince Priebus, a White House official, was briefed on UFOs. If such records exist, they would show UFOs being discussed at the top of government.
graves-s-congressional-uap-testimony-202: A former Navy fighter pilot named Ryan Graves, who flew F-18 jets for ten years, testified before the US Congress in Washington in 2023. In his own words he introduced himself as someone who had seen advanced UAP, the official term for unidentified objects in the sky, firsthand. He told the story again to the podcast host Jesse Michels and mentioned two other men who spoke at that hearing, a fellow Navy pilot named David Fravor and a former intelligence officer named David Grusch. If what they said is true, military pilots are running into craft that nobody can explain.
graves-s-space-situational-awareness-cam: Ryan Graves, a former Navy fighter pilot who says he has seen unidentified objects in the sky, told the podcast host Jesse Michels that he has started a small company. He says it builds what his team believes will be the next generation of space situational awareness cameras, meaning cameras that watch and track things moving in orbit around Earth.
graves-speaks-out-because-colleagues-rep: Ryan Graves, a former Navy fighter pilot, started speaking in public about unidentified objects around 2019. He told the podcast host Jesse Michels that he did it only because other pilots he worked with kept reporting these objects and getting no answers. In his telling, he spoke up because the military was leaving a safety problem unsolved.
gravitec-vacuum-chamber-tests: Gary McKinnon, a computer hacker who says he found signs of a secret NASA space programme, passes on something a man named Henrik told him. According to McKinnon, a company called Gravitec has tested its technology in a vacuum chamber, a sealed room with the air pumped out, and once did contract work for NASA, the US space agency. If true, it would mean some unusual propulsion idea had worked outside normal air.
gravity-a-and-gravity-b-in-barry-s-lab-n: Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked on alien craft at a secret site called S4 in Nevada in the late 1980s, says a colleague named Barry Castilio had other lab notes. According to Lazar, the notes described two kinds of gravity, gravity A and gravity B, and showed a direction the research had taken at one time, though he is not sure where the notes came from. If true, it would give a glimpse of how the craft's propulsion was studied.
gravity-researchers-went-dark-1950: On a show hosted by a podcaster named Jesse Michels, a man named Bob Maguire, described as a CIA contractor, says that scientists working on gravity in the 1950s suddenly went quiet. He says the physicist Louis Witten did nothing more on gravity, and the inventor T. Townsend Brown went to work for the military and the companies that supply it and never published about his work again. The point he draws is that gravity research may have gone secret because it was getting somewhere.
gravity-weakening-experiments-with-pulse: A physicist named John Brandenburg told the podcast host Jesse Michels about experiments he connects to a meeting of the American Physical Society, a professional body for physicists. He says that by sending pulses of electromagnetic energy, the kind behind magnets and radio waves, they got gravity to weaken in a small area, by about one part in a thousand, and that it was easy to measure. If true, it would mean gravity can be controlled in the lab.
gray-encounter-in-catskills-cabin-with-m: A philosopher named Jason Jorjani says that the writer Whitley Strieber, author of Communion, a book about his encounters with strange beings, met a Gray, the small grey-skinned figure of many alien accounts, at his cabin in the Catskills in New York in the 1980s. As Jorjani retells it, Strieber saw military and intelligence people, including CIA officers, standing around watching. If true, it would mean the government knew about such encounters and observed them.
gray-pilot-explains-implants-as-broken-i: Lyn Buchanan, an Army sergeant who later worked in a military unit that trained people to sense faraway places with the mind, says that around 1963 to 1965, somewhere off Earth, a Gray, the short grey-skinned alien of many abduction stories, explained the small implants people find in their bodies. According to Buchanan, the being said they are instrument tips carrying one or two cells of the aliens' own diseased tissue, placed in a human so the person makes antibodies the aliens can collect. If true, it would mean people are being used to make medicine for another species.
gray-types-aboard-craft-and-coburn-s-han: A man named Steve Coburn told the podcast host Jesse Michels that he remembers being on board a craft. He says he mostly saw different types of grays there. Grays are the small, grey-skinned beings with large heads and eyes that people often describe in these accounts. The story also has to do with one being he describes as his handler.
grays-as-biological-drones-1990: A YouTuber named Chris Ramsay tells podcast host Jesse Michels about an anonymous poster on 4chan, an anonymous online message board, who in early 2023 claimed to be a whistleblower. Ramsay says the poster described the grays, the small gray-skinned beings of many alien reports, as biological drones. If true, the grays would be built tools rather than the beings in charge.
grays-moon-base: A man named Charles Hall, who says he spent three years in the Nevada desert at a military base among tall, pale beings he calls the tall whites, told the podcast host Jesse Michels about another group, the grays, the small grey-skinned beings common in these accounts. He says the grays have a base on the Moon and come and go whenever they want.
grays-rescued-orphaned-chinese-children-: Charles Hall says that in the 1960s, while he was stationed in Indian Springs Valley in Nevada, he spent time among beings he calls the tall whites. He told the podcast host Jesse Michels that he saw young Chinese people there who had been rescued by the grays, the small grey-skinned beings, after being orphaned. He insists they weren't abducted, and he says the grays want to return them to human society.
grays-tall-whites-and-norwegians-arrived: Charles Hall, who says he lived alongside beings he calls the tall whites in the Nevada desert, told the podcast host Jesse Michels the order in which he believes different beings reached Earth. He is certain the grays, the small grey-skinned beings, came first, before the last ice age. He says the tall whites came second, and a third group he calls the Norwegians came at another point.
grays-that-handled-travis-walton-were-ro: Travis Walton is a logging worker who says he was taken aboard a UFO in Arizona in 1975 and handled by small grey beings, often called Grays. On a show hosted by a podcaster named Jesse Michels, a writer and philosopher named Jason Jorjani says one group of Grays are really robots built by the Nordics, tall human-looking beings in UFO lore, and that those robots are the ones that handled Walton, which would mean the Grays are not always the ones in charge.
grays-turning-into-owls-in-close-encount: Jason Jorjani, a researcher, says there are cases where people report seeing "grays", the small grey-skinned beings often described in alien encounter stories, turn into owls. He credits the idea to a writer named Mike Cleland and a work called Closer Encounters. If true, it would suggest these beings can change how they appear to the people who meet them.
greada-treaty-eisenhower-agreement-1950: Tim Alberino, a researcher, says that the Greada treaty, a supposed agreement made in the 1950s between the US government under President Dwight Eisenhower and non-human beings, was real and actually happened. He does not name his source. If true, it would mean the US government struck a formal deal with non-human visitors decades ago.
great-falls-tribune-reports-of-strange-l: Robert Salas, a former US Air Force officer, says that in March 1967, near Great Falls, Montana, the local newspaper, the Great Falls Tribune, ran accounts of strange lights in the sky that same week. He points to those newspaper reports as backing for his own account of unexplained events at the time, which would mean ordinary people saw something too.
great-figures-he-met-said-we-are-not-alo: An official who led a republic within Russia, speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast, says that the greatest minds he met all told him we are not alone in the universe. He names people such as Pope John Paul II, the Dalai Lama, the Bulgarian seer Baba Vanga, the Indian guru Sai Baba, the American statesman Henry Kissinger and the Russian physicist Zhores Alferov. He tells it because, if true, some of the world's most respected figures privately believed other intelligences exist.
great-pyramid-as-a-device-for-balancing-: On a show hosted by a podcaster named Jesse Michels, a researcher called Matt says he believes part of the purpose of the Great Pyramid of Giza in Egypt, and other ancient buildings, was to balance the Earth's energy. He points to the engineer Christopher Dunn, who has argued the pyramid was a kind of machine, which would make it far more than a tomb.
great-pyramid-as-a-giant-power-plant: Joe Rogan, a well-known podcast host, mentions on Jesse Michels' show the ideas of Christopher Dunn, a writer who thinks the Great Pyramid of Giza in Egypt was not a tomb but a gigantic power plant. If true, it would mean the ancient builders had technology far beyond what is usually credited to them.
great-pyramid-as-a-transmitter: A researcher named Joe McMoneagle, speaking in 2025 on the show of podcast host Jesse Michels, suggests that the Great Pyramid at Giza in Egypt worked as a transmitter. As he puts it, its users could send a signal of whatever they wanted to whoever they wanted to talk to. If true, it would mean the ancient Egyptians had a way to send messages over great distances.
great-pyramid-built-over-hundreds-of-yea: A writer on ancient history named Graham Hancock, talking in 2024 with podcast host Jesse Michels, says the Great Pyramid at Giza was most likely a project that took hundreds of years to finish. That goes against the usual view that it was built during the 23-year reign of Khufu, the Egyptian king it is credited to, and Hancock draws on the work of another author, Robert Bauval. If true, the pyramid's beginnings would reach back far earlier than the standard story allows.
great-pyramid-chambers-aligned-to-sirius: A researcher named Matt LaCroix, speaking in 2024 with podcast host Jesse Michels, says the two main rooms inside the Great Pyramid, known as the King's Chamber and the Queen's Chamber, face different parts of the sky. According to him, the Queen's Chamber faces Sirius, a bright star, and the alignments with Sirius and the Orion constellation fit the sky of about 10,500 BC. If true, it would suggest the pyramid was planned around a date thousands of years older than usually thought.
great-pyramid-sulfuric-acid-and-central-: A researcher named Geoffrey Drumm, on a 2026 episode of Jesse Michels's podcast titled with his claim that an alien gave him the true purpose of the pyramids, says the Great Pyramid at Giza was producing sulfuric acid. He says that acid was carried into the central pyramid of the Giza group, where it reacted with salt to make hydrochloric acid. If true, the pyramids would have been a kind of chemical factory rather than simple monuments.
greek-inventor-s-steam-sphere: A man named Greg Rogers, introduced on Jesse Michels's podcast in 2025 as a NASA doctor, mentions in passing a Greek inventor from ancient times who made a round, sphere-like device driven by steam. He brings it up as an example of surprisingly advanced ancient invention, which, if taken at face value, would mean people in antiquity were working with ideas of steam power long ago.
greek-professor-says-the-delphic-women-w: Luke Caverns, a researcher, says he has heard Greek history professors describe the women at Delphi, the ancient Greek shrine where priestesses gave prophecies. According to these professors, as he tells it, vapours rose from under the ground there and the women became possessed by the spirit of Zeus, the king of the Greek gods. If true, it would mean the ancient oracles were literally taken over by an outside intelligence.
green-fireballs-as-mothership-hypothesis: In the late 1940s, people reported glowing green fireballs, a bit like green meteors, along with UFOs near US nuclear sites. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, offers his own idea about them during a debate challenge with a UFO skeptic named Mick West, drawing on a work called UFOs and Nukes. Michels suggests that a large mother ship sat outside the atmosphere and that the green fireballs were connected to it, which, if true, would tie the fireballs and the nuclear-site sightings to a single watching craft.
green-object-over-savannah-river-site-en: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells how on July 19, 1952, an engineer named John Anderson and his colleagues at the Savannah River Site, a US nuclear facility in South Carolina, were overtaken by a glowing green object. According to the account, it was angular, darted back and forth at high speed and altitude, and moved with phenomenal agility, the kind of story told to suggest such objects watch nuclear sites.
green-orb-over-the-nevada-test-range-dur: Randy Anderson, a former military man who says he saw alien technology at a base, says that during training at the Nevada test range a green, ball-shaped object flew over and a buddy of his saw it. green-triangles-near-lax-are-airliner-bo: Michael Shermer, a well-known skeptic who debated UFOs on Jesse Michels' podcast, says that the green triangular objects shown on many UFO shows near LAX, Los Angeles International Airport, are not mysterious craft at all. In his view they are bokeh, the blurry shapes a camera makes when it films bright lights out of focus, here the lights of airliners. If he is right, a famous set of sightings would be an effect of camera lenses.
greenbrier-bunker-revealed-by-washington: This story is about a secret underground bunker at the Greenbrier, a place in West Virginia. He tells it to make a point: the government can keep large hidden facilities secret for decades, so other hidden places might exist too. The same words also appear credited to a journalist, Brent Friedman, on a later episode of the same podcast, so the two tellings disagree only about who said it.
greenstreet-of-the-new-york-post-dispute: Brandon Fugal, the owner of Skinwalker Ranch, a Utah property known for reports of strange happenings, says that a reporter at the New York Post named Steven Greenstreet disputed his account of a briefing and made him out to be a liar. greenwald-foia-finds-ufo-references-in-o: A researcher named Jason Simosa says on Jesse Michels's podcast that John Greenwald, a researcher who digs up government files, used FOIA, a US law that lets anyone request government records, to ask about President Obama's years in office, 2009 to 2017. Simosa recalls the answer showed perhaps 3,000 or 30,000 mentions of UFOs, UAP (the government's term for unidentified objects), and AATIP, a small Pentagon office that studied unexplained aerial reports. greenwald-s-foia-request-on-fast-walkers: FOIA is a US law that lets anyone ask for government records. greer-assistant-and-congressman-develop-: Steven Greer, a campaigner who pushes for the government to release what it knows about UFOs, says that he, his best friend who was also his assistant at the time, and a member of Congress all got aggressive cancers that had spread. greer-briefed-clinton-s-cia-director-199: Steven Greer, a doctor who has long campaigned for governments to reveal what they know about UFOs, told the podcast host Jesse Michels in 2025 that he briefed the head of the CIA, America's main spy agency, under President Bill Clinton. greer-briefs-admiral-wilson-j2-1997: Steven Greer, a man who collects witness accounts about UFOs, says that in 1997 he briefed Admiral Thomas Wilson, then the J2, meaning the head of intelligence for the Joint Staff, the group of top officers who advise the US military's leaders. greer-calls-uapgerb-an-intelligence-asse: An online UFO commentator who goes by the name UAPGerb says that in late 2024 someone told him that Steven Greer, a well-known campaigner for UFO disclosure, had called him an intelligence asset, meaning someone secretly working for spy agencies. greer-contacted-by-a-cosmic-intelligence: An online UFO commentator who goes by UAPGerb tells podcast host Jesse Michels about a claim from Steven Greer, an activist who campaigns for UFO disclosure. greer-gave-grusch-and-luna-an-unredacted: Steven Greer, a longtime campaigner for UFO disclosure, told the podcast host Jesse Michels in 2025 that he met David Grusch, a former intelligence officer who has testified that the government hides UFO material, and Anna Paulina Luna, a member of the US Congress. greer-passes-along-an-insider-s-contact-: Michael Herrera, a former Marine who says he saw a 300 foot UFO in the Indonesian jungle, says that around 2023 Steven Greer, a well-known UFO activist, gave him a man's contact details. greer-s-1993-95-recommendations-to-the-c: Steven Greer, a man who collects witness accounts about UFOs, says that between 1993 and 1995 he wrote a set of recommendations to President Bill Clinton's administration in Washington. greer-s-2001-national-press-club-whistle: A researcher who goes by UAPGerb says that in 2001 Steven Greer, a UFO activist, hosted a panel of whistleblowers at the National Press Club, a venue in Washington DC where news conferences are held. greer-s-ce5-coherent-thought-sequencing: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, describes the idea of Steven Greer, a man who promotes a practice he calls CE5, in which people try to contact unknown craft using their thoughts. greer-s-claim-that-nimitz-objects-were-l: Jesse Michels, a podcast host, says that Steven Greer, a UFO activist, claims the objects Navy pilots reported in 2004 near the aircraft carrier Nimitz off San Diego, including the "Tic Tac", a white oval object shaped like the mint, were secret projects of Lockheed Martin, a big aerospace company. greer-s-groups-call-up-lights-on-a-nearb: A man named Charles, who describes his own sighting on Jesse Michels's podcast, says that Steven Greer, a UFO activist, takes his groups to almost the same beach, about 40 minutes south of Cocoa Beach, Florida. greer-s-iphone-hacked-and-threats-1991: Steven Greer, a longtime campaigner for UFO disclosure, told the podcast host Jesse Michels in 2025 that only the week before, his iPhone had been hacked and he had been threatened. greer-s-joe-rogan-episode-removed-for-sp: Steven Greer, a campaigner who calls for UFO disclosure, tells Jesse Michels' podcast that his episode on Joe Rogan's show, one of the biggest podcasts, was taken down around 2020. greer-s-near-death-experience-at-17-1972: Steven Greer, a longtime campaigner for UFO disclosure, told the podcast host Jesse Michels in 2025 that at 17, around 1972 or 1973 in Charlotte, North Carolina, he became very sick and had a near-death experience. greer-says-the-octagon-craft-is-made-by-: On a 2025 episode of Jesse Michels's podcast with Michael Herrera, a man who says he saw a 300-foot UFO in the Indonesian jungle, an online UFO commentator called UAPGerb passes on a claim from the disclosure activist Steven Greer. greer-tells-fravor-the-tic-tac-was-a-sku: This story is about the Tic Tac, a white oval object shaped like the mint, which a Navy fighter pilot named David Fravor says he saw in 2004 off the coast of California while flying from the aircraft carrier Nimitz. greer-tells-rfk-jr-about-the-letter-at-s: Steven Greer, a longtime campaigner for UFO disclosure, told the podcast host Jesse Michels in 2025 that he once met Robert F. greer-warns-joe-firmage-at-mars-cafe-199: Steven Greer, a longtime campaigner for UFO disclosure, told the podcast host Jesse Michels in 2025 that in the 1990s he met Joe Firmage, a wealthy man, at the Mars Cafe in San Francisco's South of Market area. greg-eghigian-researching-his-ufo-histor: Clas Svahn, a researcher who keeps a large UFO archive in Sweden, says that the historian Greg Eghigian came and spent a couple of weeks there while researching his book on the history of UFOs. grey-four-fingered-beings-with-a-wand-te: A man named Charlie Foltz says that in August 1976, on a trip to the Allagash Waterway, a remote river area in Maine, he was taken by grey beings with four fingers who carried a wand. grinberg-and-puharich-meet-during-puhari: An unnamed researcher on Jesse Michels' podcast says that two scientists of the strange met in Mexico in the 1980s: Jacobo Grinberg, a Mexican brain researcher, and Andrija Puharich, a scientist the episode links to the CIA and to contact with an alien council. grof-s-book-discarnate-aliens-would-show: Andrew Gallimore, a neuroscientist who studies the psychedelic drug DMT, tells Jesse Michels' podcast about an idea from a book by Stanislav Grof, a psychiatrist who studied altered states of mind. ground-penetrating-radar-finds-50-ft-rei: Ross Coulthart, a journalist who reports on UFOs, told the podcast host Jesse Michels in 2025 and again in 2026 that a man named Paul scanned the road around Bradshaw Ranch, a property near Sedona, Arizona, with ground-penetrating radar, a tool that sees beneath the surface. ground-penetrating-radar-finds-cut-voids: Matt LaCroix, a writer on ancient civilisations, says he talked over dinner with a researcher named Robert Schoch about work in the 1990s at the Sphinx in Giza, Egypt. ground-radar-finds-debris-field-and-void: The owner of Skinwalker Ranch, a Utah property known for reports of strange happenings, says that ground-scanning radar run over a mesa on the ranch found hollow spaces underground and a field of debris. grusch-and-the-legacy-reverse-engineerin: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, talks about what a whistleblower named David Grusch may or may not have stumbled upon: a long-running secret programme, which Grusch's supporters call a legacy programme, said to study recovered craft and try to copy their technology. grusch-approaches-knapp-and-corbell-at-a: Jeremy Corbell, a guest on Jesse Michels's podcast, says that around 2022 or 2023, at an event in Huntsville, Alabama, known as Rocket City, a man named David Grusch came up to him and his colleague George Knapp at a bar. grusch-asks-brent-to-help-bring-john-har: A man named Brent Friedman, speaking on a podcast episode about Hollywood, the CIA and UFOs, says that David Grusch, a whistleblower who spoke publicly about secret UFO programmes in the 2020s, asked him for help bringing a man named John Harrington forward. grusch-assigned-to-the-uap-task-force-20: David Grusch, a former intelligence officer, told the podcast host Jesse Michels in 2023 that he was brought into the UAP Task Force, a Pentagon group set up to study UAP, the official term for UFOs, with its director routing the request through an operations centre. grusch-blows-whistle-on-crash-retrieval-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells how David Grusch, who served on the UAPTF, a Pentagon task force that looked into unexplained objects in the sky, followed up on what that group had found. grusch-colleague-finds-radar-data-on-big: Jesse Michels, a podcast host, says someone told him that David Grusch, who served on a government UFO task force, knew of a film of the 1964 Big Sur incident, when an object is said to have flown alongside a test missile warhead off the California coast. grusch-dick-cheney-headed-the-ufo-progra: Jesse Michels, a podcast host, says that David Grusch, a former intelligence official who went public with UFO claims, has said that Dick Cheney, the former US vice president who had just died, was head of the secret UFO programme. grusch-disgruntled-insiders-inside-the-l: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that a whistleblower named David Grusch told him in an interview that people inside a secret, long-running programme said to handle recovered craft wanted the story to come out. grusch-dodges-the-question-about-agreeme: This story is about David Grusch, a former intelligence official turned whistleblower, who testified before the US Congress in 2023 about hidden UFO programmes. grusch-files-ig-complaint-and-names-witn: David Grusch, a former intelligence official who came forward as a witness, says that in 2022 he filed a complaint with an Inspector General, a government internal watchdog, told them whom to interview, and that they concluded his claims were credible. grusch-gave-congress-locations-of-spacec: A journalist named Ross Coulthart says that David Grusch, a former US intelligence officer who went public as a whistleblower in 2023, gave the US Congress firsthand information from his sources about exactly where to look for recovered spacecraft. grusch-gave-hundreds-of-pages-to-the-ici: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that around 2022 a witness named David Grusch handed hundreds of pages of documents to the Intelligence Community Inspector General, the watchdog for US spy agencies, then led by Thomas Monheim. grusch-harassed-and-his-medical-file-lea: A physicist, Eric Davis, says that after David Grusch, a former intelligence officer, filed a whistleblower complaint about secret UFO programs, Grusch and his wife were harassed and intimidated by someone in the National Reconnaissance Office, the US agency that runs spy satellites. grusch-harrington-holds-oral-history-of-: This story is about a man named John Harrington and a gap in the government's records. grusch-has-no-information-on-lazar-1989: David Grusch, a former intelligence officer who says the government hides UFO material, told the podcast host Jesse Michels in 2023 that he has no information on Bob Lazar. grusch-hospitalization-and-retained-clea: Mick West, a well-known UFO skeptic, said in a 2025 podcast debate that David Grusch, a former US intelligence officer who later told Congress about UFOs, had a psychotic episode sometime in the 2010s and checked himself into a hospital. grusch-named-sarbacher-as-the-key-to-the: A man named Omar Candal, speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast, recalls asking David Grusch, a former US intelligence officer who has said the government hides crashed alien craft, which single person would help you understand how the secret program is built. grusch-on-a-multi-decade-cold-war-with-a: A researcher who goes by UAPGerb points to a 2023 interview on NewsNation, a US television news channel, with David Grusch, a former intelligence officer turned whistleblower. grusch-on-asking-sarbacher-and-oppenheim: David Grusch, a former US intelligence officer who says he uncovered secret government programs dealing with recovered craft, said on Jesse Michels's podcast what he would ask two scientists from the 1940s and 50s if he could. grusch-on-disclosing-the-biologic-side-2: David Grusch, a former US intelligence official who testified to Congress in 2023 that the government holds craft not made by humans, says he wanted to put enough out there to touch on all the most sensitive parts. grusch-on-jre-cia-psi-programs-as-a-key-: An online researcher who goes by UAPGerb recalls something David Grusch, a former intelligence officer turned whistleblower, said in 2024 on Joe Rogan's podcast. grusch-on-sarbacher-s-role-in-standing-u: David Grusch, a former US intelligence officer who says he uncovered secret government programs dealing with recovered craft, told the podcast host Jesse Michels that Robert Sarbacher, a scientist who advised the government in the 1940s and 50s, is reported to have helped set up the programs Grusch found. grusch-on-sentient-plasmoid-life-2020: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that David Grusch, a former US intelligence officer who became a whistleblower on UFO matters, spoke at a press event in Washington DC in the 2020s about the idea of sentient plasmoid life. grusch-oppenheimer-helped-set-up-ufo-sec: David Grusch, a former US intelligence officer who says he uncovered secret government programs dealing with recovered craft, told the podcast host Jesse Michels that Robert Oppenheimer, the physicist who led the building of the atomic bomb, is reported to have been involved in setting up those programs in the 1940s. grusch-oppenheimer-set-up-ufo-secrecy-19: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that if you believe David Grusch, a former intelligence officer turned whistleblower, then men such as Robert Oppenheimer, the physicist who led the US atomic bomb project, and a scientist named Robert Sarbacher literally set up the secrecy around UFOs in the 1940s and 1950s. grusch-reprisals-at-the-nga-2020: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that David Grusch, a former intelligence official turned whistleblower on UFO matters, suffered serious reprisals and was "dragged through the mud" while working at the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency, a US spy agency that deals with satellite imagery and maps. grusch-s-40-witnesses-are-firsthand-and-: Eric Davis, a physicist who has worked on Pentagon studies of unexplained craft, talks about the roughly 40 witnesses that David Grusch, a former intelligence officer turned whistleblower, said he interviewed in 2023. grusch-s-alternative-timeline-view-of-th: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, recalls what David Grusch, a former US intelligence officer who spoke to Congress in 2023 about UFOs, told him in an interview after that hearing. grusch-s-claims-of-reverse-engineering-p: This story is about David Grusch, a US intelligence whistleblower who spoke out in 2023. grusch-s-ig-complaint-and-aoc-exchange-a: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that David Grusch, a former intelligence officer who came forward as a witness in 2022 and 2023, gave hundreds of pages to Thomas Monheim, the inspector general of the intelligence agencies, meaning their internal watchdog. grusch-s-irad-fraud-allegation-2023: On Jesse Michels's podcast, a host named Jack raises what he calls David Grusch's IRAD fraud allegations. grusch-s-public-testimony-cleared-by-dop: Eric Davis, a physicist who has worked on Pentagon studies of unexplained craft, says that what David Grusch, a former intelligence officer, told Congress in public in 2023 had first been approved by the Department of Defense through its office that reviews material before it is released. grusch-s-secondhand-spaceship-testimony-: Michael Shermer, a writer often called America's top skeptic, talks about David Grusch, a former US intelligence officer who testified to Congress in 2023. grusch-s-terms-came-from-crash-retrieval: Eric Davis, a physicist who has worked on Pentagon studies of unexplained craft, says the special terms used by David Grusch, a former intelligence officer turned whistleblower, came from briefings Grusch was given about a secret program that recovers crashed craft. grusch-s-testimony-prompts-rogers-to-com: Greg Rogers, a doctor who has worked with NASA, the US space agency, and who says he saw a UFO in a secret hangar, explains why he decided to speak up. He says the real push came in 2023 when David Grusch, a former intelligence officer, testified before the US Congress about hidden UFO programmes. If true, it would show one public testimony drawing other witnesses out.
grusch-s-witness-and-the-300-ft-triangle: A podcast host named Jesse Michels passes on something he heard from David Grusch, a man who has spoken out about secret UFO programmes. grusch-says-cheney-was-the-last-at-the-t: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that David Grusch, a man who has spoken out about secret UFO programmes, told him something about Dick Cheney, the former US vice president. grusch-says-he-knows-john-harrington-202: Bryce Zable, a man who says he hosted David Grusch, a whistleblower who spoke in 2023 about secret government UFO programmes, at his house in Los Angeles, says he asked Grusch whether he had heard of a man named John Harrington. grusch-says-the-peruvian-skeletons-resem: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says he saw strange skeletons in Peru, and that David Grusch, a former US intelligence officer turned whistleblower, told him they looked like things Grusch had seen in classified settings. grusch-sends-someone-to-interview-mccasl: Eric Burlison, a US congressman, told the podcast host Jesse Michels in 2026 that David Grusch, a former intelligence officer who says the government hides UFO material, had sent someone to interview Neil McCasland, a retired Air Force general. Burlison says the interviewer could not get much out of the general, which matters because people suspect McCasland knows more.
grusch-speaks-of-interdimensional-beings: Eric Weinstein, a researcher and commentator, recalls that David Grusch, a former US intelligence officer, used the phrase "interdimensional beings" during a 2023 congressional hearing on UFOs in Washington. Weinstein says holography, the idea of images or realities built from projected light or information, also came up. If taken seriously, it would suggest officials are thinking about visitors in stranger terms than ships from other planets.
grusch-testifies-before-congress-2023: This story is about David Grusch, a former US intelligence officer, testifying before Congress about UFOs. The podcast host Jesse Michels says Grusch testified in Washington, D.C., in late July 2023, and in another episode gives the exact date as July 26, 2023. Michels stresses that Grusch spoke under oath and that he was describing what he had found, which, as told elsewhere, is that the government holds craft not made by humans. James Fox, a UFO investigator, also tells it on the same podcast. He says he watched the testimony live on his phone and describes Grusch speaking under oath to a group of lawmakers from both parties. If true, it would mean a former official was willing to tell Congress, at risk to himself, that such secrets exist.
grusch-testimony-some-craft-were-gifted-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says one interesting thing to come out of the 2023 testimony of David Grusch, a former US intelligence officer turned whistleblower, is that some of the unknown craft seem to have been gifted rather than crashed or captured. As Michels puts it, that would give humanity a kind of head start, handed over on purpose by whoever made them.
grusch-testimony-under-oath-and-inspecto: In 2023, a whistleblower named David Grusch came forward to the US government. A guest named Merrick von Rennenkampf says Grusch had people with firsthand knowledge go to the inspector general, an internal government watchdog, to file a complaint, and that, in his telling, a man named Lou Elizondo said under oath that the US has programmes to recover crashed craft. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says Grusch brought 40 firsthand whistleblowers to the inspector general for the intelligence agencies, Thomas Monheim, who called the claims urgent and credible. If true, it would mean the US government secretly holds craft that are not of human making.
grusch-the-symbol-rate-is-too-slow: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in an interview with David Grusch, a former US intelligence officer turned whistleblower, Grusch remarked that it is almost as if the symbol rate is too slow. Symbol rate means how fast information is passed along, and the remark, as Michels frames it, suggests our way of communicating may be too slow to connect with whatever intelligence lies behind these encounters.
grusch-uses-the-data-to-find-40-witnesse: Eric Davis, a physicist who has worked on Pentagon studies of unexplained craft, says that David Grusch, a former intelligence officer turned whistleblower, took the collection of data Davis and fellow physicist Hal Puthoff had gathered and ran with it. According to Davis, Grusch used it to track everything down and find 40 witnesses, which would make that data the starting point for Grusch's claims.
grush-tells-moskowitz-he-would-answer-on: An online researcher who goes by UAPGerb describes a moment in the 2023 congressional hearing where David Grusch, a former US intelligence officer, was questioned by Jared Moskowitz, a member of Congress. According to UAPGerb, Moskowitz asked whether Grusch had seen overhead collection, meaning satellite or aerial imagery, of UFO crashes, and Grusch said he would have to answer that only in a closed, classified session. The point is that, if true, such imagery would exist but is being kept secret.
guarded-portal-facility-under-forest-ser: Ross Coulthart, a journalist who reports on UFO claims, says on a podcast that there is a portal in the United States, which the story places at Bradshaw Ranch in Arizona. As the story goes, it is a guarded site hidden behind the cover of the US Forest Service, the agency that runs national forests. If true, the government would be protecting a doorway to somewhere else.
guardians-of-the-ark-sicken-and-die: Graham Hancock, a writer on lost ancient civilisations, says that in Aksum, Ethiopia, the monks chosen to guard the Ark of the Covenant, the sacred chest from the Bible that local tradition says is kept there, get sick and die very quickly. In one telling he passes this on from what others told him, and in a later one he says he learned it from his own interviews, adding that the guardians develop cataracts and live only about three years after being appointed. He tells it because, if true, the object would seem to have some real and dangerous power.
gudea-of-sumer-given-temple-plans-in-a-d: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, points to an ancient text about Gudea, a king of Sumer, one of the earliest civilisations in what is now Iraq. Michels says Gudea wrote that in a dream he was given something made of lapis lazuli, a deep blue stone, tied to the plans for a temple, and he mentions other ancient rulers, Thutmose and Nebuchadnezzar, in the same breath. He tells it as a hint that ancient builders may have received their designs from some outside source.
guest-contacts-hal-puthoff-as-a-high-sch: A researcher appearing on Jesse Michels's podcast in 2026 said that around 2002, while still a high-school student, they got in touch with Dr. Hal Puthoff, a physicist known for work on unusual science. The guest tells it as an early step into that field.
guest-interns-at-the-pear-lab-2003: A researcher appearing on Jesse Michels's podcast in 2026 said that around 2003 they got in contact with the PEAR lab, the Princeton Engineering Anomalies Research lab in New Jersey, linked to Robert Jahn and Brenda Dunne. The guest says they interned there, and presents it as a formative step into research on unexplained things.
guest-s-attempt-to-show-aldrin-uap-image: A researcher named Maaneli Derakhshani says he found UAP, the government's term for UFOs, in photos from Apollo 11 and Apollo 17, two of NASA's missions to the Moon. He says that in the 2020s he tried to show these images to Buzz Aldrin, the Apollo 11 astronaut, by writing to one of his assistants at Aldrin's company, Buzz Aldrin Ventures, and got a polite reply. He tells it because, if his finds are real, a man who walked on the Moon might have something to say about them.
guest-s-statistical-analysis-of-ganzfeld: A guest on a 2026 podcast, speaking as a researcher, describes the Ganzfeld trials, telepathy experiments begun in the 1970s in which a person in mild sensory isolation tries to pick out an image someone else is looking at, work associated with a researcher named Charles Honorton. The guest says that across the best quality studies the hit rate seems to be around 30 to 35 percent. If that holds up, it would suggest people can pick up information beyond chance, which would point to some kind of mind-to-mind connection.
guest-saw-no-ufo-trace-among-stony-brook: A researcher named Maaneli Derakhshani says that from 2004 to 2008, as a student at Stony Brook University in New York, he spent a lot of time with the leading theoretical physicists at its Yang Institute for Theoretical Physics and with the math department, where he ran the math club. He says he never saw any hint that any of them were interested in UFOs, which he offers against the idea that the place was quietly tied to such research.
guest-shadowbanned-after-posting-photo-w: An unnamed researcher on Jesse Michels's podcast says that after posting a photo of himself with a man named Robert Malone, taken at a gathering called Heretic-con, he was instantly shadowbanned on X, the site once called Twitter, meaning his posts were quietly hidden from others. He tells it as a sign, if true, that being linked to certain people gets you silenced online.
guide-s-son-claims-his-father-led-armstr: Jesse Michels, a podcast host, says he is in touch with the son of a guide who took Neil Armstrong, the first man on the Moon, into the Tayos Cave, a cave system in Ecuador, around 1975, when the expedition was looking for something hidden there and did not find it. Michels says the son, whom he names in a later episode as Luis Felipe San Salvador, claims his father deliberately sent Armstrong the wrong way, and that the family still knows the real location. If true, whatever was being sought in the cave would still be there, kept secret on purpose.
gus-grissom-s-lemon-and-cia-on-the-launc: Gus Grissom was an American astronaut who died in 1967 on an Apollo launch pad at Cape Kennedy in Florida. A podcast host, Joe Rogan, citing a man named Bart Sibrel and Grissom's wife, says Grissom hung a lemon on a coat hanger outside his spacecraft, complaining that they could not even talk to the control tower, so how would they talk from space. Rogan's version also places the CIA, the US spy agency, on the launch pad. Another host, Jesse Michels, mentions the lemon too and says Grissom died the next day. The story is told as a hint that his death may hide more than an accident.
guthrie-law-article-finds-no-prosecution: Kurt McConnell, a former US Senate staffer, mentions an article by a young lawyer named Dylan Guthrie, which he believes appeared in the Harvard Law Review, a well-known law journal. According to McConnell, the article finds that nobody has been prosecuted for passing secret information to Congress through proper secure channels. The point, if true, is that insiders with knowledge of hidden UFO programmes could speak to Congress without fear of being charged.
guy-banister-544-camp-street-and-the-fbi: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that before the 1963 killing of President Kennedy, Lee Harvey Oswald, the man accused of the shooting, was operating out of a building at 544 Camp Street in New Orleans. According to Michels, the building belonged to Guy Banister, a prominent FBI man who ran the bureau's UFO collection at the time, the real X-Files on which the television show was based. If true, it would link the Kennedy killing to the government's secret UFO files.
guy-banister-reports-ufo-sightings-to-ho: Peter Levenda, an author who writes about secret history, says that in 1947 in the Pacific Northwest of the United States, a man named Guy Banister had the job of reporting UFO sightings back to J. Edgar Hoover, the head of the FBI, under what is described as a special mission. If true, it would mean the FBI was quietly tracking UFO reports from the very start of the modern sightings.
gwynne-shotwell-s-special-launch-shoes-a: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells a small story about Gwynne Shotwell, the chief operating officer of the rocket company SpaceX, who he says basically runs the company now. According to Michels, Shotwell says she wears her special shoes for launches. He tells it to show that even the people at the top of hard engineering keep little rituals, and he credits it to a work called Countdown to Launch.
h-g-wells-the-world-set-free-predicts-th: Robert Salas, a former US Air Force officer, points out that in 1914 the writer H.G. Wells published a novel called The World Set Free. Salas says that in it Wells describes building an atomic bomb, long before one existed, which he raises as a sign that such ideas can appear ahead of their time.
hahn-splits-the-atom-in-1938: Robert Salas, a former US Air Force officer who tells of UFOs at nuclear missile sites, mentions in passing that a German scientist he names as Hahn, whom he calls a Nazi scientist, did an experiment in 1938 and was the first to split the atom. Salas brings it up as the start of the nuclear age, which in his account is what drew UFO interest to nuclear weapons.
haim-eshed-and-the-galactic-federation-2: This story is about Haim Eshed, an Israeli official described as the head of Israel's version of a space force, and what he is said to have claimed around 2020. A UFO researcher named James Fox, speaking with Michels, does not name Eshed or the Federation but stresses that the position of head of Israel's space force equivalent is an extremely important one. Michels tells it several times across his podcast, while Fox adds only the weight of the job. People tell it because, if true, a senior defence official would be saying openly that humans are in contact with an organised group of non-human beings.
haim-eshed-claims-us-astronauts-and-alie: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells how in 2020 Haim Eshed, the former head of the space department in Israel's defence ministry and, in Michels's words, essentially the father of Israel's space programme, made a public claim. According to Michels, Eshed said American astronauts and representatives of aliens were working together at underground bases on Mars. If true, it would mean a hidden space effort with non-human partners is already under way.
haim-eshed-s-galactic-federation-and-mar: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells of an Israeli figure named Haim Eshed. If true, it would mean contact with other civilisations is already happening out of public view.
haitian-traditions-of-beings-among-us: Diana Pasulka, a scholar who studies religion and UFO beliefs, says someone emailed her about traditions in Haiti of strange beings living among people. If true, it would suggest these encounters are an everyday part of life in some cultures.
hal-povenmire-s-visits-from-2008-and-his: Chris Bledsoe, a man from Fayetteville, North Carolina, who says he has had many UFO encounters, tells of visits from a man named Hal Povenmire starting in 2008. Bledsoe says that before Povenmire died in 2019, he had come to believe the phenomenon Bledsoe was experiencing was angelic. If true, it would cast these encounters as spiritual rather than as visits from space.
hal-puthoff-contacts-grant-cameron-about: A longtime UFO researcher named Grant Cameron says that Hal Puthoff, a physicist long involved in government research into unusual phenomena, suddenly got in touch with him. Cameron sees the contact as a sign that those papers mattered to people on the inside.
hal-puthoff-on-rogan-us-holds-15-crashed: Jesse Michels, a podcast host, says that Hal Puthoff, a physicist long tied to government studies of unexplained phenomena, went on Joe Rogan's podcast in 2025 and said the US has 15 crashed craft in its possession. hal-puthoff-ordered-copies-of-ufos-and-n: Robert Hastings, author of a book called UFOs and Nukes about UFOs seen at nuclear weapons sites, says that when its first edition came out, a scientist named Hal Puthoff suddenly wrote asking for four copies shipped overnight to hand out in Washington. hal-puthoff-s-2004-white-house-conversat: Lou Elizondo, a former Pentagon official who ran a small office studying unexplained aerial reports, refers to a conversation that physicist Hal Puthoff has described publicly. hal-puthoff-s-medieval-levitating-secret: Jesse Michels, a podcast host, recalls a conversation with Hal Puthoff, a physicist who has long studied UFOs. If true, UFOs would be the work of a hidden human group rather than visitors from elsewhere.
hal-puthoff-starts-the-government-s-psyc: Hal Puthoff is a laser physicist. hal-saflieni-hypogeum-oracle-room-tuned-: Jay Anderson, a man who says he visited the Hal Saflieni Hypogeum, a very old underground chamber complex in Malta, says that a space in it called the Oracle Room is precisely tuned to sound at 111 hertz, a particular low pitch. He tells it because, if true, the ancient builders shaped the room for sound on purpose, with knowledge we would not expect them to have.
hal-warns-of-33-million-volts-2007: Chris Bledsoe, a North Carolina man who says he has had many UFO encounters, recalls what a man he calls Hal told him sometime after 2007. If true, it would mean someone had measured the enormous power of these craft.
haldi-as-celestial-intelligence-rather-t: A researcher named Matt, talking in 2024 with podcast host Jesse Michels, discusses Haldi, a god worshipped in ancient times around Lake Van in eastern Turkey. If true, it would mean the old gods were memories of a contact with something in the heavens.
haldi-relief-read-as-a-spearhead-sites-c: A researcher named Matt, on Jesse Michels's podcast in 2024, describes a carved image of the god Haldi from the Lake Van area of Turkey, made by the ancient people known as the Urartians, in which an object is being passed from a hand. He says archaeologists firmly believe the object is a spearhead and see the culture as warlike, calling its sites kalesi, a Turkish word for fortresses. He suggests that reading may be mistaken, which would change what these ancient sites were for.
half-of-a-ready-room-says-they-saw-the-c: A Navy fighter pilot named Ryan Graves says that his squadron saw strange objects, which he calls "cubes and spheres," while flying off the US East Coast around 2014 and 2015. He tells podcast host Jesse Michels that after a New York Times article about these sightings came out, he asked pilots in a ready room, the briefing room where pilots gather, in a different area, and about half raised their hands to say they had seen them too. If true, it would mean the sightings were far more common than one squadron.
hall-confirms-tall-white-restroom-visits: Charles Hall, a man who says he worked as an Air Force weather observer in Nevada in the 1960s, says that someone told him tall pale beings he calls the Tall Whites came into the restroom at the weather station in the base operations building at Nellis Air Force Base. Hall says he later knew from firsthand experience that this was true, because one day his own work put him there. If true, it would mean non-human beings moved about inside a US military base.
hall-photon-theory-copyrighted-1997-and-: Charles Hall says he spent three years in Nevada, near Indian Springs, around tall, white-skinned beings he calls the Tall Whites, and watched their craft move in ways he believes were faster than light. He says this inspired his own physics idea, which he calls whole photon theory, and that he first copyrighted it in 1997, writing it up in books such as Beyond Relativity and Mirage Galaxies and Edges in Space. If true, his theory would be a human attempt to explain how those craft travel.
hall-s-books-presented-to-pope-benedict-: Charles Hall is a man who says he spent years with tall white aliens at Area 51, a secret US Air Force base in Nevada, and he wrote books about it. His wife says that around 2005 or 2006 she took his first three books to Rome as a gift for Pope Benedict. She tells podcast host Jesse Michels that the Pope sent a thank-you note, which is reproduced in Hall's fourth book.
hall-s-orders-said-he-could-never-be-bri: Charles Hall, a man who says he served as an Air Force weather observer at Indian Springs and Nellis Air Force Base in Nevada from 1965 to 1967, says his orders stated he could never be briefed or debriefed, meaning he could never be formally told about, or formally released from, the secret work he was part of. He says the reason was simple and ties it to a figure he calls the Teacher. If true, it would mean his time with what he describes as non-human beings was kept off the official record.
halloween-s-origins-linked-to-the-fall-t: Randall Carlson, a researcher of ancient catastrophes, talks about a link between the ancient origins of Halloween and the Taurid meteor shower, a yearly display of shooting stars in late October and early November. His idea is that the holiday may preserve an old memory of danger from the sky.
halls-of-amenti-ancient-library-under-th: This is a story about a hidden library said to lie under the Great Sphinx, the giant stone statue with a lion's body that sits at Giza in Egypt. A researcher named Matt LaCroix, talking to podcast host Jesse Michels, says we are told by Edgar Cayce, a man known for his visions, and by others that an ancient library was meant to be buried beneath the Sphinx. Another researcher, Luke Caverns, tells it on the same show as Cayce's own vision, which he dates to the 1940s. He says Cayce saw a chamber under the Sphinx holding a "hall of records" that tells the story of Atlantis, a legendary lost civilisation. If it were true, the oldest chapter of human history would be sitting in a room under the statue, waiting to be found.
halt-hears-radio-reports-of-beams-into-w: Robert Hastings, a researcher who collects accounts of UFOs at nuclear bases, tells what Charles Halt, a US Air Force officer, told him in a 2005 interview about December 1980 at RAF Bentwaters, a British air base used by the US Air Force. Hastings says Halt heard on his radio that security police at the base's weapons storage area were reporting an object hovering overhead and sending down beams of light. If true, it would mean something was taking an interest in stored weapons.
halt-memo-on-rendlesham-lights-1980: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, describes a memo written by a military officer, Lieutenant Colonel Charles Halt, about events in December 1980 near RAF Bentwaters, a Royal Air Force base in England. According to Michels, Halt wrote to the UK Ministry of Defence, Britain's defence department, saying a security patrol saw strange lights coming down into the nearby Rendlesham Forest, which would mean an officer put an unexplained sighting on the official record.
halton-arp-s-interacting-galaxies-with-d: An astronomer named Beatriz Villarroel, speaking with podcast host Jesse Michels in 2025, tells of Halton Arp, a famous astronomer working from about the 1960s to the 1980s. She says Arp found pairs of galaxies that looked like they were exchanging gas, yet had completely different redshifts, the stretching of light that astronomers use as a sign of distance. If true, it would mean the standard way of measuring how far away things are in space could be wrong.
hameroff-s-view-of-microtubules-and-anes: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, describes the idea of an anesthesiologist named Stuart Hameroff, who worked with the physicist Roger Penrose, author of the book The Emperor's New Mind. Microtubules are tiny tube-shaped structures inside our cells, and Michels says Hameroff found that when anesthesia shuts them off, the rest of the brain and body keep working normally but the person loses consciousness. If true, it would mean these tiny structures are the switch for consciousness itself.
hamlet-s-mill-on-ancient-knowledge-of-pr: Graham Hancock, a writer about lost ancient civilisations, points to Hamlet's Mill, a 1960s book by Giorgio de Santillana of MIT, a US university, and Hertha von Dechend of Frankfurt University. Hancock says the book argues that ancient myths carry very early knowledge of precession, the slow wobble of the Earth that shifts the stars' positions over thousands of years. If true, people in the distant past knew far more astronomy than is usually thought.
hancock-s-ayahuasca-alien-abduction-visi: Graham Hancock, a writer on lost ancient civilisations, says that around 2003, while taking ayahuasca, a strong psychedelic brew used by shamans in the Amazon, he had a vision outside a shaman's hut. He says he saw several flying saucers above him and the familiar alien face, heart-shaped with large dark eyes, much like accounts of alien abduction. He tells it because, if true, such encounters might be reached through altered states of mind.
hancock-the-great-pyramid-was-not-a-tomb: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Graham Hancock, a writer on lost ancient civilisations, told him the Great Pyramid at Giza in Egypt was not a tomb. When Michels asked him point blank what it was for, he says Hancock almost implied it was a kind of stargate, a portal to somewhere else, and in a later retelling Michels ties this to the pyramids lining up with the stars of Orion's belt. If true, it would mean ancient builders knew things we have since forgotten.
hancockdibble-debate-and-the-shipwreck-d: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, talks about a 2024 debate between Graham Hancock, a writer who argues for a lost ancient civilisation, and Flint Dibble, an archaeologist who disagrees with him. Michels says that if you fact-check Dibble afterwards, you find he got his figures about ancient shipwrecks completely wrong. He tells it to suggest that the experts' case against Hancock is weaker than it looked on stage.
handoff-to-the-next-contact-by-a-call-on: Dan Sherman, a former US Air Force sergeant, says that in the early 1990s he was trained to receive messages from aliens for the National Security Agency, the US spy agency that handles communications. He says that at his first base after training, the phone in his dorm rang, and it was his first contact officer, a Captain White, who gave him the name of the next person he would report to and told him that man would be waiting at a set time with his arms folded. In one version Sherman places this base overseas in a warm climate and says he was briefed there, and he tells it as the moment a secret programme quietly passed him from one handler to the next.
hannah-mcroberts-flying-saucer-photo-198: A UFO researcher and archivist named Clas Svahn tells podcast host Jesse Michels about a woman named Hannah McRoberts, who on October 8, 1981, was driving with her husband on Vancouver Island in Canada and stopped to photograph a well-known mountain. According to Svahn, her photo appears to show a flying saucer, and the case was featured in a publication called Files of the Unexplained. If true, a solid object was caught on camera by ordinary travellers.
hans-kammler-comes-to-the-us-1945: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says Hans Kammler, the Nazi official in charge of the most secret of Germany's "wonder weapon" projects, made his way to the United States around the end of the Second World War in 1945. Michels says "we now know" this. If true, it would mean the Nazis' most hidden weapons work was carried on quietly in America.
hans-kammler-s-skoda-works-saucer-projec: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says there is real documented evidence that Hans Kammler, a senior official in Nazi Germany, ran secret projects at the Skoda Works, a large industrial complex, between 1942 and 1945, with sites tied to Breslau and Pilsen. hapgood-s-earth-crustal-displacement: A researcher named Jason Jorjani, on Jesse Michels's podcast in 2025, brings up the idea of Charles Hapgood, a writer who proposed that the Earth's outer crust can slide as a whole over the layers beneath it. Jorjani says that, according to Hapgood, the North Pole was once where Hudson Bay in northern Canada is today, with the shift tied to the end of the last ice age and to Antarctica. harassment-of-ufo-whistleblowers-2010: A scholar named Diana Pasulka says that in the United States, sometime in the 2010s or 2020s, she saw with her own eyes people she calls whistleblowers, insiders who came forward with claims about UFOs, being harassed. hard-drives-recovered-from-a-glacier-lak: A helicopter pilot named Jake Barber, who says he flew missions to recover UFOs, says his team found a person who led them to a glacier lake high in the Sierra Nevada mountains of California. In one telling he says they came from Toughbooks, a kind of rugged laptop, and credits a man named Don Paul Bales, and he tells it as a piece of hidden evidence his team says it brought back.
hard-object-found-in-nostril-during-2001: A man named Richard, a former guard at a nuclear missile site who says aliens abducted him, says that in 2001 he had trouble breathing because of a crooked wall inside his nose and finally had surgery for it. According to Richard, a hard object turned up in his nostril during the operation, and he tells it as a sign that something may have been put inside his body.
harold-malmgren-nhi-track-the-frontier-o: Jesse Michels, a podcast host, says he spoke with Harold Malmgren, a presidential adviser who worked with Presidents Kennedy, Johnson, Nixon and Ford and who was briefed on UFOs. harold-malmgren-s-cia-connections-and-id: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Harold Malmgren, a man he interviewed in 2024, told him he had been best friends with Tom Farmer, the top lawyer of the CIA, the US spy agency, and Michels suggests that Malmgren's work with IDA, the Institute for Defense Analyses, a defense research group, served as cover for CIA ties going back to the 1960s. Michels adds that during the interview he held a walking stick that once belonged to the wealthy Paul Mellon, and he cites Malmgren's diary, which, if his reading is right, would mean Malmgren was close to the inner circle of US intelligence.
harold-malmgren-s-deathbed-account-of-na: Jesse Michels, a podcast host, recounts what Harold Malmgren, a former presidential adviser, told him late in his life. harold-malmgren-tweets-about-bissell-bri: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Harold Malmgren, an adviser to Presidents Kennedy, Johnson, Nixon and Ford, has been posting on social media about what he learned in that role, including briefings from a senior official named Richard Bissell. harrington-aliens-are-real-and-he-has-se: This story is about a private conversation in 1981 with a man named John Harrington. In a later telling Friedman puts the talk on the veranda, places the home near Washington DC rather than in Virginia, and links it to a briefing in West Virginia. People tell it because, if true, it would mean someone with inside knowledge had confirmed alien visitors firsthand.
harrington-briefed-for-months-in-undergr: Brent Friedman, a Hollywood figure, retells what a man named John Harrington told him. harrington-denies-brent-friedman-s-accou: John Harrington, who says he served as US Secretary of Energy, talks about a story told by a man named Brent Friedman, set around 1981 in Walnut Creek, California and Washington. harrington-has-seen-lasers-that-could-br: John Harrington, who says he served as US Secretary of Energy, says that he has seen laser technology in the United States that could bring down almost anything. harrington-s-buck-slip-congratulating-br: A writer named Brent Friedman tells this on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels. harrington-s-contact-with-david-grusch-a: A man named John Harrington, speaking on podcast host Jesse Michels's show, says he was in touch with David Grusch, a former intelligence official who gave testimony to the US Congress in Washington in 2023 claiming the government holds UFO secrets. harrington-s-fukushima-delegation-visit-: John Harrington, who says he served as US Secretary of Energy, says that after the 2011 disaster at Japan's Fukushima nuclear power plant he went there with a delegation. harrington-s-global-economy-reason-for-s: Brent Friedman, a guest on Jesse Michels's podcast, says a man named John Harrington, presented in the episode's title as a former US Secretary of Energy, told him why the government keeps contact with non-human intelligence secret, in a conversation set around 1981. harrington-tours-the-greenbrier-bunker-1: John Harrington, who says he served as US Secretary of Energy, says that around 1986 or 1987 he was at Greenbrier in West Virginia playing golf. harry-reid-s-plan-for-a-billion-dollar-a: A physicist named Eric Davis says that Harry Reid, a US senator, meant for AAWSAP, a Pentagon-funded study of unexplained aerial events that began in 2008, to be only a starting point. harry-reid-s-request-for-sap-status-deni: Eric Davis, who says he worked on a Pentagon-funded study of unexplained phenomena around 2009, says that Senator Harry Reid asked the deputy secretary of defense, William Lynn, to make their work a special access program, a tightly restricted category of secret project. harry-reid-s-special-access-program-requ: Eric Davis, a scientist who has worked on Pentagon research, says that around 2009 US Senator Harry Reid tried to set up a special access program, which is a tightly restricted secret government project, apparently for UFO research. harry-reid-the-ufo-information-is-alread: Peter Levenda, an author who writes about secret history, tells how Harry Reid, a longtime US senator, was asked by a journalist where a study of UFOs should even begin. harry-rositzke-pulled-out-of-retirement-: A writer on UFO history named Greg Bishop, talking with podcast host Jesse Michels in 2025, tells of Harry Rositzke, a retired American intelligence officer. harry-turner-investigates-uap-sightings-: Ross Coulthart, an Australian journalist, says that a man named Harry Turner was invited to investigate several sightings of UAP, short for unidentified anomalous phenomena, the official term for UFOs, at Maralinga, an Australian site used for British nuclear weapons tests in the 1950s and 60s, near the Woomera rocket range. harry-turner-s-1971-australian-intellige: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, often points to a document from 1971 written by Harry Turner, who he says headed the nuclear section of Australia's Joint Intelligence Organisation, the country's defence intelligence agency. harry-turner-ufo-obsessed-intelligence-c: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, brings up Woomera, a weapons test range in Australia used for nuclear tests in the 1950s. harvard-neuroscientist-s-telepathic-kids: Jesse Michels, a podcast host who interviews people about UFOs and strange experiences, says he recently interviewed a Harvard neuroscientist, someone who studies the brain, who is studying children said to be telepathic, meaning they can read minds. harvard-tried-to-get-rid-of-john-mack-wh: John Mack was a psychiatrist and professor at Harvard University who took the UFO subject seriously. haseltine-s-novel-out-of-time-hiding-tru: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, talks about Eric Haseltine, a former director of research at the NSA, the US National Security Agency that handles intelligence from communications, and a past guest on his show. hastings-confessions-his-own-abduction-e: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Robert Hastings, a researcher known for his 2008 book UFOs and Nukes about UFOs seen near nuclear weapons sites, later wrote a book called Confessions. hastings-did-not-systematically-ask-witn: Jesse Michels, a podcast host, says he once asked Robert Hastings, a researcher who collected accounts of strange craft seen near US nuclear weapons sites, whether he had asked every witness who saw a craft if they had also seen beings. hastings-s-nuclear-site-ufo-whistleblowe: A podcast host named Jesse Michels says he has information on more than 167 whistleblowers, people who worked at nuclear weapons sites across the United States and came forward about UFOs. hastings-s-phone-calls-followed-by-heavy: A researcher named Robert Hastings, who collects accounts of UFOs seen at nuclear weapons bases, says that mostly in February 1982 he phoned people for his research. hatshepsut-s-obelisk-inscription-dedicat: Luke Caverns, a researcher of ancient Egypt, says he has read translations of the carvings on an obelisk, a tall stone pillar, put up by Hatshepsut, an Egyptian ruler, at Karnak in Egypt. haughton-mars-project-simulation-and-chr: John Blitch, a former scientist at DARPA, the US military's research agency, who says he was abducted by an alien, says that in 2001 he took part in the Haughton Mars Project, a practice mission at Haughton Crater on Devon Island in the far north of Canada where a team pretended to be astronauts on Mars. havana-syndrome-as-pulsed-rf-directed-en: Havana syndrome is the name for a mysterious illness that a podcast host, Jesse Michels, places in Havana, Cuba, starting in 2016. Michels, speaking on another episode, describes the same idea more bluntly, saying the victims are being wholly destabilized by microwaves. havana-syndrome-as-russian-attacks-since: Eric Haseltine, a former senior official at the National Security Agency, the US spy agency for electronic communications, talked with podcast host Jesse Michels about "Havana syndrome." have-blue-prototype-owned-by-lockheed-sk: Greg Rogers, a doctor who has worked with NASA, says that in the 1970s an experimental aircraft project called Have Blue was not actually owned by the US Air Force, even though the plane carried Air Force markings. hawara-labyrinth-and-the-2008-mataha-exp: A researcher named Geoffrey Drumm talks about Hawara, an ancient site in Egypt said to hold a great labyrinth. hawass-1992-speech-on-subterranean-labyr: A researcher named Jay Anderson says that in 1992 Zahi Hawass, a well-known Egyptian archaeologist, gave a speech at a university in Cairo. hawkeye-360-searching-for-1-6-ghz-at-int: A researcher named Bob Maguire says he is certain that something called Hawkeye 360, which he describes as able to watch for radio signals, has looked for signals at 1.6 gigahertz, a particular radio frequency, at what he calls interesting places. hawksbill-creek-agreement-and-devco-1950: A guest who goes by Jason says that something happened in the Bahamas in the 1950s or 1960s, when a group of people made what was called the Hawksbill Creek agreement. headmaster-bans-louis-braille-s-books-at: Ky Dickens, a documentary maker who made a film about children said to read minds, tells a story from the history of Louis Braille, the man behind the raised-dot reading system for blind people. heat-exchanger-and-extraction-shaft-hypo: A researcher named Jeffrey, drawing on someone named Filippo, describes the Great Pyramid of Giza in Egypt as a kind of machine. heavyweight-champion-on-cia-operations-i: An author named Peter Levenda says that in the late 1960s, at the Brotherhood Synagogue in Greenwich Village, New York, a heavyweight boxing champion he names as Andre Pinacio spoke to him and others about running operations in Lebanon for the CIA, America's foreign spy agency. hedge-fund-recruits-memory-champion-nels: Chris Ramsay, a guest on Jesse Michels's podcast, passes on a story from Nelson Dellis, a memory champion, set around 2022 or 2023. If true, it would mean serious money is being bet on psychic abilities.
hegel-s-philosophy-of-mind-on-the-parano: A philosopher named Jason Jorjani says that Hegel, the German philosopher of the early 1800s, wrote a book called Philosophy of Mind, about the psyche, that has long passages on the paranormal. heifer-found-dead-with-ufo-shaped-object: Skinwalker Ranch is a property in Utah known for stories of strange events, and podcast host Jesse Michels says that one of the most disturbing things there was when a healthy two-year-old young cow was found dead with no injuries on the outside, an event he credits to a TV series about the ranch. The ranch's owner, Brandon Fugal, tells it firsthand, saying it happened in a field near a building called Homestead 1 and that cameras captured an object above the animal, crediting two of his team, Thomas Winterton and Caleb Benches. If true, it would tie the cow's death to an unknown craft.
heim-droscher-and-hauser-s-two-forms-of-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, describes a line of German physics running from Burkhard Heim, a physicist, to two later researchers, Dröscher and Hauser. According to Michels, they all believed there are two forms of gravity, not just the one we know. If true, it could offer a theory for how strange craft might fly.
heisenberg-s-heavy-water-program-and-deu: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, connects the 1940s German nuclear programme of physicist Werner Heisenberg, which relied on heavy water, a form of water made with a heavier kind of hydrogen called deuterium, to rumours about how UFOs fly. Michels says many of those rumours describe a deuterium reactor, a heavy water engine, sitting in the middle of the craft, which would hint that the secret of their flight has roots in wartime physics.
heisenberg-s-team-calculates-the-fissile: Jason Jorjani, a researcher who writes about secret Nazi programmes, says that in 1945 German atomic scientists led by the physicist Werner Heisenberg were held in the English countryside and secretly listened in on. He tells it as a sign that the Germans knew more about building such a bomb than was admitted.
heisenberg-s-uranium-program-as-decoy-fo: Jason Jorjani, a researcher who writes about secret Nazi programmes, says that in 1940s Germany the uranium project run by the physicist Werner Heisenberg was a red herring, a decoy. If true, it would mean Nazi Germany's atomic efforts went much further than history records.
heiser-affirms-the-watchers-and-their-gi: A filmmaker who researches giants, Tim Alberino, tells podcast host Jesse Michels that Michael Heiser, a Bible scholar and author of books such as The Unseen Realm and Reversing Hermon, accepted the ancient story of the Watchers, heavenly beings said to have come down and fathered giants. Alberino says Heiser affirmed the tale of the Anakim, a race of giants named in the Bible. If true, giants born of non-human beings once walked the earth.
helen-mccall-s-sol-foundation-white-pape: On a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, a researcher named Matthew Pines says that a writer named Helen McCall wrote a white paper, a short policy report, for an organisation called the Sol Foundation. The point of telling it is that serious people are asking what news of non-human craft might do to markets and the economy.
helicopter-chases-of-about-15-uap-in-60-: James Valor, a member of Skywatcher, a startup that says it can call up UFOs, says that in 2025 the team would spot objects and then jump into a helicopter to chase them. helicopter-freezes-mid-air-while-trying-: The team at Skywatcher, a startup that says it can call up UFOs, says that around February 2025 they sent a helicopter after a tic tac, a white oval object shaped like the mint, about 7 kilometres northwest of their site. helicopter-harassment-after-aaro-testimo: Michael Herrera, a man who says he saw a huge UFO in the Indonesian jungle, says that in April 2023 he gave testimony to AARO, the Pentagon office that looks into unexplained objects in the sky. helicopter-recovery-of-the-20-foot-egg-2: A helicopter pilot named Jake Barber says that around 2014 he flew a mission off a test range in the California desert to carry away a 20-foot object shaped like an egg, which his team simply called the egg. helicopters-escorting-ufos-into-mountain: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says there are reports of helicopters escorting UFOs, or UAPs (unidentified anomalous phenomena, the newer official term), into mountains. helicopters-vanish-into-a-pixelating-mou: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, retells a scene from a book called Sentinels of Ether, in an episode about why the Pentagon, the US military's headquarters, tried to censor it, and he cites a man named Jake Barber. hell-s-angels-chief-zapped-at-skinwalker: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, passes on a story from Brandon Fugal, owner of Skinwalker Ranch, a property in Utah famous for reports of strange events. hells-angels-member-hospitalized-for-wee: Brandon Fugal, the owner of Skinwalker Ranch, a property known for reports of strange events, says a man named Eric Bard, a member of the Hells Angels motorcycle club, visited the ranch at some point in the last decade. helms-club-secret-consciousness-study-gr: A scientist named Donald Hoffman, who studies how the mind sees the world, says he spent a lot of time with Francis Crick, one of the men who found the structure of DNA. hemi-sync-paper-from-the-mid-1980s-1983: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, talking with a researcher of psychic matters, Jeffrey Mishlove, mentions a paper from the mid-1980s about Hemi-Sync, a sound-based technique linked to Robert Monroe and the Monroe Institute in Virginia. hennessy-claims-cheney-visited-s4-1993: A researcher who goes by UAPGerb says that a man named Derek Hennessy claimed to have worked at S4, a site in Nevada. henri-coanda-s-1936-saucer-patent-and-pr: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, speaking with a writer named Peter Levenda, says that an inventor named Henri Coanda had basically the first patent on a flying saucer, in 1936.
