henri-coanda-s-patent-and-project-y-at-w: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells of Henri Coanda, a Romanian scientist who he says held a patent from 1936 on a flight technology and was living in Vichy France, the French state under Nazi influence during the war. According to Michels, Coanda was forced to work for the Nazis and was later taken to Wright-Patterson, a US Air Force base in Ohio, to work on Project Y. Michels says Project Y grew out of the Avro car project, an effort to make flying saucers actually fly, which would mean the US was quietly building saucer craft after the war.
henry-azadehdel-s-fraudulent-south-afric: A UFO researcher named Clas Svahn talks about a man named Henry Azadehdel, who he says published documents about South Africa. Svahn mentions something he calls "silver diamonds" in connection with them, and he treats the documents as fraudulent. He tells it as a warning about false papers circulating in the UFO world.
henry-wallace-astors-and-duponts-fund-pu: A researcher named Andrija Puharich, who studied telepathy, the idea of minds talking without words, says that in 1948 in Maine he was unexpectedly put in touch with Henry A. Wallace, a former US vice president under Franklin Roosevelt. According to the story, Wallace and the wealthy Astor and DuPont families went on to fund his telepathy research, which would mean powerful people were backing such work early on.
hereticon-talk-flood-myths-rooted-in-rea: Randall Carlson, a researcher of ancient catastrophes, describes a talk he gave at Hereticon, a gathering for unconventional ideas. His argument is that the flood myths found all over the world come from real floods, enormous ones that he says could be called biblical in scale, likely from ice melting at the end of the last Ice Age. If so, ancient legends would be memories of actual events.
hermann-oberth-on-non-human-intelligence: Hermann Oberth was a German rocket scientist and the mentor of Wernher von Braun, a famous rocket engineer. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says Oberth is on record saying that non-human intelligence helped them build rockets to go to space, and he points to a book called Secret Machines. In another episode Michels says there is even an audio recording of Oberth talking about UFOs, in which he says they were aided and had help. A guest, Jason Samosa, puts it more loosely: "the German guy, the Nazi guy," he says, claimed they had a relationship, without saying it was about rockets. So the story comes from the host repeating it in two episodes and from a guest who remembers it vaguely. If true, it would mean early space rockets owed something to beings from somewhere else.
hermann-oberth-on-video-about-ufos: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Hermann Oberth, one of the founding pioneers of rocket science, was recorded on video speculating about UFOs. According to Michels, Oberth said that the existence of UFOs should make anybody question reality, a striking thing to hear from a serious scientist.
hermann-oberth-s-1954-ufo-lecture-notes: A researcher named Kevin Knuth says he has the notes from a 1954 lecture in Germany by Hermann Oberth, an early rocket scientist who is named alongside his fellow rocket man Wernher von Braun. According to Knuth, Oberth wrote that he had seen many radar readings of unknown objects moving at up to 19 kilometres per second. If that is true, a founder of rocketry took UFO speeds seriously, and they were far beyond anything humans could build at the time.
herodotus-records-a-king-s-tomb-on-an-is: Luke Caverns, a researcher of ancient Egypt, says that Herodotus, an ancient Greek historian writing in the 5th century BC, recorded that a great king's tomb lay on an island surrounded by a lake of water underground at Giza. Caverns ties this to the Osiris shaft, a deep underground shaft near the pyramids that, he says, was dug out in the 1980s and 1990s, with the Egyptian archaeologist Zahi Hawass involved. If true, it would mean an ancient account described the site long before it was explored.
herodotus-takes-part-in-the-egyptian-mys: A researcher named Luke Caverns says that Herodotus, the ancient Greek historian of the 5th century BC, wrote about secret religious groups in Egypt known as mystery cults and wondered what went on inside them. According to Caverns, Herodotus was then allowed to take part in them while in Egypt and afterward never wrote about them again. He tells it to suggest the Egyptians held secrets so serious that even a famous writer kept quiet.
herrera-attends-greer-s-ce5-sessions: Michael Herrera, a man who says he saw a huge UFO in the Indonesian jungle, says he has personally attended a few CE5 sessions run by Dr. Steven Greer, a UFO campaigner. CE5 is Greer's practice of groups trying to invite contact with beings from elsewhere, and Herrera brings it up while saying this is what that effort is all about.
herrera-spoke-to-kirk-mcconnell-in-a-sci: Michael Herrera, a man who says he saw a huge UFO in the Indonesian jungle, says he spoke with a man named Kirk McConnell in a SCIF, a specially secured room where secret government information can be discussed, in Washington. He mentions it to show that his account was heard in an official, classified setting.
herrera-testifies-at-greer-s-2023-nation: Michael Herrera says he saw a huge UFO in the jungle of Indonesia. He says that in 2023 he gave public testimony at the National Press Club, a well-known venue for journalists in Washington DC, at an event run by Steven Greer, a campaigner who pushes for the government to reveal what it knows about UFOs. He brings it up to show that he has put his account on the record in public.
hess-s-flight-to-britain-and-lifelong-qu: A researcher named Jason Jorjani tells of Rudolf Hess, a top official in Nazi Germany, who in 1941 took a secret, unauthorised flight out of Germany and landed in a field in Britain. Jorjani links this to Winston Churchill, Britain's wartime leader, and to Hess being kept shut away for the rest of his life, until 1987. He tells it as part of a case that Hess knew secrets, including about a Nazi UFO programme, that could never be allowed out.
hessdalen-expedition-in-the-early-1980s: Clas Svahn, a Swedish UFO researcher, talks about Hessdalen, a valley in Norway where people report strange things in the sky. He says that in the early 1980s, Swedish and Norwegian researchers ran a big expedition there and managed to photograph the things they were looking for, and once even caught them on radar. If true, it would mean the sightings there could be recorded by cameras and instruments, not just by people's eyes.
hidden-evaluation-run-during-the-q-cours: Randy Anderson, a former soldier who says he saw alien technology at a military base, talks about the Q course, the US Army's demanding course for becoming a Special Forces soldier. He says that while he was going through it, a secret evaluation was quietly being run on the candidates for another military unit ranked above those units. He tells it to explain how he may have been picked out for work beyond ordinary Special Forces.
hidden-eye-patterns-on-product-packaging: A researcher named Don Hoffman, introduced on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels as an MIT scientist, says he has worked with companies to hide eye-like patterns in their product designs. In his words, you can make something that looks like eyes, but not obviously. He tells it as an example of how our brains pick up on things we don't consciously notice, which fits his wider claim that we may be built to miss what is really around us.
hidden-f-117-stealth-fighter-line-in-the: John Harrington, presented as a former senior official of the US Department of Energy, says that in the 1980s money for the F-117, America's first fighter plane meant to be invisible to radar, was tucked away in the Energy Department's budget. He says the plane was developed on Energy Department land in the Nevada desert. He tells it as an example of how secret military projects can be hidden inside budgets that seem to have nothing to do with them.
hidden-ufo-side-of-operation-paperclip: A former US intelligence officer named David Grusch tells podcast host Jesse Michels about Operation Paperclip, the American programme that brought German scientists such as the rocket engineers Wernher von Braun and Arthur Rudolph to the United States after the Second World War. Grusch says that there was another, hidden side to the programme, and that much of it dealt with UFOs in earnest. If true, it would mean the US government's interest in UFOs goes back to the end of the war.
hidden-weapons-bunker-under-a-fake-gener: A former US Army sergeant named Lyn Buchanan tells of a private facility belonging to Saddam Hussein, the former ruler of Iraq, around the time of the Gulf War. He says a generator there turned out to be hollow and would tilt back, and that underneath it steps led down into a weapons bunker "that you wouldn't believe." He tells it on Jesse Michels's podcast as something he says he took part in finding, and if it is true it shows how well such places could be hidden.
hieroglyphics-reported-at-historical-ufo: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, lists several famous American UFO cases: the 1947 crash at Roswell, New Mexico, a 1964 sighting by a police officer, Lonnie Zamora, in Socorro, New Mexico, and a 1965 event at Kecksburg, Pennsylvania. He says there are rumours that strange symbols like hieroglyphics were seen on the objects in these cases, including Kecksburg. If true, the shared markings would tie the cases together as the work of the same makers.
high-altitude-nuclear-tests-burned-holes: Jesse Michels, a podcast host who talks with guests about UFOs and hidden science, says that the nuclear bombs set off high in the sky in the 1950s and 60s would "burn holes" in the Van Allen belt. That belt is a zone of charged particles held around the Earth by its magnetic field, far above the planet. In his telling, these tests did real damage to a natural shield around our world.
high-definition-helicopter-video-of-orbs: A journalist named Michael Shellenberger says a report he obtained, about a secret program called Immaculate Constellation, describes a very high quality video filmed from a helicopter about 20 miles off the coast of Kuwait. According to that report, the video shows a glowing orb rising out of the ocean and then being joined by a second orb, which, if true, would mean the military holds clear footage of unknown objects coming from the sea.
high-level-unnamed-source-corroborates-t: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that a high-level source, whom he does not name, backed up many details of Dan Sherman's story. Sherman is a man who tells of secret US government work in the 1990s connected to UFOs. If the source is right, it would lend weight to Sherman's account of hidden programmes.
high-ranking-nasa-official-tells-chris-h: Chris Bledsoe, a man who says UFOs appear around him and who says NASA has taken an interest in him, describes an evening in 2025 at the Capitol Hill Club, a private club close to the US Congress in Washington. He says a high-ranking NASA official walked up, gave him a big hug and told him, "Chris, I'm a huge fan." He tells it as a sign that people inside the US space agency take his experiences seriously.
high-school-seti-home-club-crunching-are: Martin Shkreli, a former drug-industry businessman, says that as a teenager in the late 1990s he and two friends formed a high school club for SETI@home, a project that let ordinary home computers help search for radio signals from alien civilisations. He says they let their computers crunch data from the giant Arecibo radio telescope whenever the screen saver was on. He tells it to show his interest in the search for alien life goes back a long way.
high-vacuum-dual-thruster-spinner-test-a: Charles Buer, a guest on Jesse Michels's podcast, says a video shows a test in a vacuum chamber in Florida, where a pack of two thrusters mounted on a vertical spinner moved with no air around it. He puts the push at about 2.5 millinewtons, a very tiny force, and if true it would mean a new kind of propulsion that does not rely on ordinary rocket exhaust.
hike-up-stone-mountain-with-houston-2023: Ky Dickens, a filmmaker who made a documentary series called The Telepathy Tapes about people she says can read minds, recalls a hike from around 2023. She says that while in Atlanta she, Houston, one of the people in her project, and Dr Diane Powell, a doctor who studies these abilities, all hiked up Stone Mountain in Georgia together. She tells it as a warm memory of time spent with the people at the heart of her film.
hikers-on-public-land-threatened-by-arme: A journalist, Ross Coulthart, says several people told him privately that while walking on public parkland near Secret Mountain in Sedona, Arizona, they were stopped by men in uniform carrying automatic weapons. He says the men moved like highly trained elite soldiers. The podcast host Jesse Michels repeats such reports, placing them in the Coconino National Forest and describing black uniforms with no badges and M-16 rifles. Coulthart tells it as a sign that a hidden base may sit there.
hikers-photograph-diamond-shaped-craft-m: A documentary filmmaker named James Fox relays a story about two people out hiking who saw a large diamond-shaped craft hovering and took photographs of it. According to the story, they were then followed by "men in black", mysterious men in dark suits said to turn up after UFO sightings. Fox tells it as a sign that someone works to keep such sightings quiet.
hikers-who-vanish-near-the-alien-bases-a: Lyn Buchanan, a former US Army sergeant, says there are alien bases near two mountains: Mount Nyangani in Zimbabwe and Mount Zeil in Australia. According to him, hikers who go missing near these places have been killed or kept as workers, and he sums it up as "You see too much. You disappear." If true, it would mean the disappearances people report around these mountains have a hidden, non-human cause.
hill-at-hatshepsut-s-mortuary-temple-5-3: A researcher named Geoffrey Drumm says that near the mortuary temple of Hatshepsut, a temple built for an ancient Egyptian queen near Luxor, there is another of what he calls "white horse hills." He says it lies exactly 5,300 metres from the obelisks, tall stone pillars, at the Karnak Temple. He tells it to suggest the ancient sites were laid out on purpose, by precise measurement, as one connected plan.
hillary-clinton-tells-kimmel-she-ll-get-: A UFO researcher named Grant Cameron recalls that in 2016, Hillary Clinton, then running for US president, appeared on Jimmy Kimmel Live, a late-night TV talk show in Los Angeles. According to Cameron, Kimmel asked her about UFOs and she answered, "I'm going to get to the bottom of this." He tells it as a sign that UFO secrecy had reached the highest levels of politics.
hillary-s-presidential-run-timed-with-th: Jake Barber, a former helicopter pilot speaking with podcast host Jesse Michels, says the timing is probably no coincidence: according to him, when Hillary Clinton was running for US president, the setting up of AATIP, a small Pentagon office that studied unexplained aerial reports, lined up with the events that led to a New York Times article about that office. If he is right, the UFO story's move into public view was tied to presidential politics.
hillenkoetter-frustrated-at-being-kept-i: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says he thinks Roscoe Hillenkoetter, a former head of the CIA (the US spy agency), was frustrated that he never got the full story about Roswell. Roswell is the town in New Mexico where, by many accounts, something crashed in 1947 and was recovered by the military. Michels brings this up alongside Donald Keyhoe, a writer and UFO campaigner, and the point is that if even a spy chief was kept in the dark, the secret was held very tightly.
hillenkoetter-leaves-nicap-as-hearings-l: A UFO historian named Richard Dolan tells of Roscoe Hillenkoetter, a former head of the CIA, the US spy agency, who sat on the board of NICAP, a private civilian group that pushed for openness about UFOs. Dolan says Hillenkoetter resigned suddenly in 1962, just as his friend Donald Keyhoe, who led the group, was trying to get the US Congress to hold hearings on UFOs. He tells it to suggest pressure was applied to stop those hearings.
himmler-s-ahnenerbe-replacing-christiani: Peter Levenda, an author who writes about secret history, says the Ahnenerbe, which translates as Ancestral Heritage, was a real organisation in 1930s Germany under Heinrich Himmler, a top Nazi leader who ran the SS. According to Levenda, it worked to replace Christianity with old Nordic rites, which he tells as a sign of how deep the Nazi interest in the occult went.
historical-briefings-cut-off-in-the-earl: An online researcher who goes by the name UAPGerb tells podcast host Jesse Michels that, in the early 2010s, there was an effort inside the US government to stop giving historical briefings to people newly put in charge of secret programmes. He passes this on from someone he spoke with. If true, it would mean new officials were kept from learning the background of what they were running.
hitchhiker-effect-at-fugal-s-home-dog-gr: Brandon Fugal, a businessman who owns Skinwalker Ranch, a property famous for reports of strange events, talks about the "hitchhiker effect", the idea that something from the ranch can follow people home. He says that around 2024 his dog would get up at about 3 in the morning and growl and bark at something unseen in his house. If true, it would mean whatever is at the ranch does not stay there.
hitchhiker-effect-at-thomas-winterton-s-: Brandon Fugal, the owner of Skinwalker Ranch, a property known for reports of strange events, says that a man named Thomas Winterton has had strange things happen in his own home after coming back from the ranch. This is what people call the hitchhiker effect: the idea that whatever is at the ranch can follow visitors home. If true, it would mean the strange activity is not tied to one place.
hitler-and-the-magenta-crash-nazi-saucer: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, mentions reports that Adolf Hitler knew about the Magenta crash, a craft said to have come down near Magenta in northern Italy in 1933. He also points to rumors that Nazi Germany tested flying saucers in what is now the Czech Republic and Slovakia. If true, it would mean governments were studying such craft well before the famous American cases.
hitler-orders-arrest-of-occultists-and-a: An author named Peter Levenda, who wrote a book called Unholy Alliance about the Nazis and the occult, says that in 1941, after Hitler's deputy Rudolf Hess flew to Britain on his own, Hitler ordered every occultist and astrologer in Germany to be arrested and sent to the camps. Levenda tells it to show how deeply occult ideas ran in the Nazi leadership, and how much Hitler feared them.
hitler-regime-support-for-zionist-revolu: On the podcast of a host named Jesse Michels, a researcher named Matthew Brown says that Hitler's government in Germany gave some support, in the 1930s and 1940s, to the Zionist movement, the movement working toward a Jewish homeland in what was then British-ruled Palestine. He gives it as a summary and names no source. He raises it as part of a wider argument that hidden powers back unlikely allies to steer history.
hitler-s-world-war-i-poems-to-odin-and-t: An author named Peter Levenda agrees with podcast host Jesse Michels that Adolf Hitler, while a soldier in the First World War, wrote poems to the old Norse gods such as Odin and Thor. Levenda says the poems are reprinted in a biography of Hitler, which he believes is the one by the historian John Toland. He tells it to show that Hitler was drawn to pagan, mystical ideas from early on.
hittite-remains-in-underground-cities-sh: Derinkuyu, in Turkey, is a city carved deep underground out of soft rock. A researcher called Matt, speaking on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, says that evidence of the Hittites, an ancient people of the region, and of other cultures that are "not Ancient Ancient" has been found there. As he tells it, this means later peoples moved into these tunnels and reused them, which would make the cities older than the people found living in them.
hively-and-woodside-paper-on-extended-el: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, in an episode featuring the thinker Eric Weinstein and a Pentagon scientist, points to a paper on extended electrodynamics, a broader version of the physics of electricity and magnetism. Michels says it was written by a man named Lee Hively in Colorado Springs and a colleague named Woodside who, he believes, is in Australia, and he raises it as physics worth a look in the UFO debate.
hjalmar-schacht-advises-sukarno-on-a-rev: Peter Levenda, an author who writes about secret history and the occult, says on Jesse Michels's podcast that Hjalmar Schacht, a German financier from the Nazi era, went to Indonesia after the war. Levenda says Schacht had been through denazification, the Allied process of clearing former Nazis, and then visited Sukarno, Indonesia's leader. According to Levenda, Schacht told Sukarno to build an "Islamic crescent" of nations to hold back Chinese communism, a story told to suggest that old Nazi networks went on shaping world politics after the war.
hmnzs-southland-followed-by-an-800-foot-: Kevin Knuth, a physicist who once worked at NASA, the US space agency, says on Jesse Michels's podcast that in the 1980s a New Zealand navy ship, the HMNZS Southland, was followed by an underwater object about 800 feet long. He calls it a USO, short for "unidentified submerged object", the undersea version of a UFO. He tells it as one of many cases suggesting that unknown craft move through the oceans as well as the sky.
hms-blonde-orange-sphere-rises-from-the-: Richard Dolan, a researcher who writes histories of UFO reports, tells of a diary kept by Andrew Bloxom aboard HMS Blonde, a British navy ship, near the Cook Islands in the South Pacific. According to the diary as Dolan reads it, at 3:30 in the morning on 12 August 1825 the night watch saw an orange, ball-shaped object rise out of the ocean. Dolan tells it to show that such sightings go back some 200 years.
ho-chi-minh-s-letter-to-the-us-president: Joe McMoneagle, a former US Army remote viewer (someone trained in a government programme to describe faraway places using only the mind), tells podcast host Jesse Michels that Ho Chi Minh, the Vietnamese independence leader, sent a heartfelt letter to the US president in the late 1940s. McMoneagle says the letter included a copy of Vietnam's national constitution, which was identical to the American one. If true, Vietnam once looked to the United States as its model.
hoagland-and-flynn-hold-joint-conference: A researcher and filmmaker named Tim Alberino, a guest on Jesse Michels's podcast, says that two writers worked together in the 1990s and early 2000s: Richard Hoagland, known for claiming there are ruins on Mars, and David Flynn. According to Alberino, the two put on a series of joint conferences in the United States about those supposed Martian ruins, a sign of how far the idea that someone once built on Mars had spread.
hockey-puck-devices-on-the-shins-1976: Jim Weiner, one of several men who say they were taken aboard an alien craft in 1976 while in the Allagash wilderness of Maine, describes a moment on board. He says a being with long, thin, jointed arms came for him holding a device that looked like a flattened hockey puck, and put one on the outside of each of his shins, after which he could not move his legs. He tells it in almost the same words more than once, as part of his account of being abducted.
hoffman-at-mit-studying-under-marvin-min: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells his guest, a scientist named Hoffman who studies how the mind perceives the world, that he was at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology just as artificial intelligence was getting started. Michels says Hoffman studied under Marvin Minsky, one of the founders of the field, which frames Hoffman's ideas about perception and unseen intelligence as coming from the heart of that work.
hoffman-s-dmt-research-collaboration-wit: Donald Hoffman, a researcher who studies perception and consciousness, says that in 2026 he is working with a neuroscientist named Andrew Gallimore on research into DMT, a powerful psychedelic drug. He mentions it on Jesse Michels's podcast, and it matters to his story because some people believe DMT lets users see other realms or beings.
hoffman-s-team-of-mathematicians-working: Donald Hoffman, a researcher who studies perception and consciousness, says that in 2026 he is putting together a team of mathematicians. He says his group has published a number of open mathematical ideas, which he calls conjectures, from a framework known as trace logic, and the team will try to work them out. If his ideas hold up, they would give a mathematical basis to his view that reality is quite different from what we perceive.
hofmann-grof-and-ruck-s-reported-plan-fo: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Albert Hofmann, the chemist who discovered LSD, the psychiatrist Stanislav Grof and the classics scholar Carl Ruck may have wanted to create a new Eleusis, a modern version of the secret religious rite of ancient Greece that some believe used a mind-altering drink. Michels himself says this may be only a rumour, but if true it would show leading figures hoping to revive a ritual for reaching other realms.
holloman-afb-landing-footage-that-allan-: This story is about a film said to show flying saucers landing at Holloman Air Force Base, a US military base in New Mexico, in 1964. A UFO researcher named James Fox, speaking on the podcast of a host named Jesse Michels, says that a man named Allan Sandler told him he had seen this footage. According to Fox, the film showed three saucers coming in over the base, two peeling away and one coming down to land. Sandler, as Fox tells it, said it might have been a training video but that the saucers in it were real, and Fox says of it, "No question about it." Fox ties the story to other people, including Robert Emenegger, Paul Shartle and a Colonel Coleman, to a documentary called UFOs Past, Present and Future, and to articles by a UFO writer named Coral Lorenzen. A second teller, a scientist named Eric Davis, tells it on the same podcast without naming a source and puts it in April 1964. He adds that the landing craft set down on the tarmac near a hangar, and that a walkway came down and a very tall humanoid being stepped out, a non-human intelligence who looked Northern European. If true, it would mean the US military met and filmed visitors from elsewhere openly on one of its own bases.
holloman-footage-debunked-as-an-f-4-1970: This story is about film said to show a UFO landing at Holloman Air Force Base in New Mexico, from the 1970s. The footage appeared in a documentary called UFOs: Past, Present and Future. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that little bit of footage has since been shown to be just an F-4, a military jet. An unnamed documentary narrator, speaking on a later episode, tells how a sharper HD DVD release of the documentary changed things. Fast-forwarding to the landing scene, the narrator says the extra detail was stunning and showed the object was a plane, without saying an F-4. Both are speaking in their own words. The story matters because the footage had been offered as a filmed alien landing at a military base.
homeless-man-says-look-up-and-corbell-se: A filmmaker who makes UFO documentaries, Jeremy Corbell, says a homeless man once came up to him and said only "Look up." He says it happened in 2013, and that when he looked up he saw a globe-shaped object in the sky. He tells it on Jesse Michels's podcast as a personal moment that most people don't know about.
homestead-3-that-people-refuse-to-enter-: Brandon Fugal, the owner of Skinwalker Ranch, a property known for reports of strange events, talks about a building there called Homestead 3. He says it is the oldest structure on the property and that some people who visit refuse to go inside it. He tells it as one of the places on the ranch where people feel something is wrong.
honeymoon-photos-labelled-grand-central-: Chris Bledsoe, a man who says UFOs appear around him, says that his old honeymoon photos from New York in the early 1980s are labelled Grand Central Station, but that today the place is called Grand Central Terminal. He offers it as an example of the Mandela effect, the idea that many people clearly remember something differently from how the record now shows it, which some take as a sign that reality itself can shift.
hooded-figures-spraying-plague-from-land: A philosopher named Jason Jorjani cites a writer named William Bramley, author of a book called The Gods of Eden. Jorjani says Bramley found that the plague in medieval Europe broke out only after strange objects landed in fields and hooded figures came out carrying what looked like spray cans. According to this account, those figures became the source of the image of the Grim Reaper with his scythe, which would mean non-human beings spread the plague on purpose.
hooked-on-ufos-by-chariots-of-the-gods-1: A doctor named Greg Rogers, who says he worked with NASA and saw a UFO in a secret hangar, tells podcast host Jesse Michels how his interest began. He says that around 1969 he read Chariots of the Gods, a popular book by Erich von Däniken about ancient visitors from space, and was hooked. It is the start of the path that, by his account, led to what he later saw.
hoover-handwritten-note-army-grabbed-rec: James Fox, a UFO documentary filmmaker, describes an FBI memo from July 1947 that carries a handwritten note by J. Edgar Hoover, then head of the FBI, the US federal police bureau. As Fox reads it, Hoover wrote that the bureau must insist on full access to recovered discs, and complained that the Army grabbed one and wouldn't let the FBI have it even for a quick look. If true, it would mean the military had a recovered disc in 1947 and kept it from the FBI.
hoover-letter-calling-condon-a-russian-s: Robert Salas, a former US Air Force officer, told podcast host Jesse Michels about a letter from 1949 in Washington, D.C. He says he believes J. Edgar Hoover, the head of the FBI, wrote to Congress calling a scientist named Edward Condon a Russian spy. Salas raises it because it would cast doubt on Condon's standing, a man whose name comes up in the history of how the government handled UFOs.
hoover-letters-deny-fbi-jurisdiction-ove: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, drawing on a film called Out of the Blue by the filmmaker James Fox, says that J. Edgar Hoover, the longtime head of the FBI, the US federal police agency, wrote several letters in the 1940s and 1950s. According to Michels, the letters stated that investigating unidentified flying objects is not and never has been within the FBI's jurisdiction, which would show the agency officially keeping its distance from the subject.
hopi-ant-people-as-a-global-subterranean: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, passes on an idea from a Chilean researcher named David Velasco: that a race of beings might live underground all around the world. As an example, Michels points to the Hopi, a Native American people of Arizona, whose legends tell of the "ant people", who are said to live beneath the earth. If this were true, it would mean stories from very different cultures are describing the same hidden species.
hopi-ant-people-emerging-from-undergroun: Jay Anderson, a guest on podcast host Jesse Michels' show, passes on a story he credits to the Hopi, a Native American people of the North American Southwest. He says the Hopi tell of "ant people" who came up from under the ground to help humans in times of great trouble and strife. Anderson raises it as one of several old stories that, if taken literally, would point to helpful non-human beings living beneath the earth.
hornig-guards-the-trinity-bomb-the-night: A researcher named Kevin Knuth passes on a story from a scientist named Donald Hornig about Trinity, the first atomic bomb test, held in New Mexico in 1945. According to Hornig, the night before the test, Robert Oppenheimer, who led the bomb project, handed him a gun and had him guard the bomb up in its tower during a storm. Knuth tells it to show how close Hornig was to the heart of America's most secret work.
hospital-reprimands-italo-for-filming-th: Italo Venturelli, a surgeon in Varginha, Brazil, says his hospital once operated on an alien. He says that around 2023 he took the documentary filmmaker James Fox into the hospital's maternity ward and filmed the room where it had been, and that afterwards the hospital banned him from filming inside. He says he thinks the ban was fair.
hospital-staff-now-say-the-room-was-lock: Italo Venturelli, a surgeon at the regional hospital in Varginha, Brazil, talks about 1996, when, according to a number of stories, a strange creature was said to have been seen in the town and taken away. hospital-wing-closed-because-of-the-crea: A documentary filmmaker named James Fox relays what a witness told him about Varginha, a town in Brazil where people say a strange creature was captured in 1996. host-attended-the-congressional-uap-hear: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says he was in the room in 2023 when the US Congress in Washington held a hearing on UAP, the government's term for UFOs. host-discussed-precognition-hypothesis-w: A podcast host named Jesse Michels, who interviews people about UFOs and strange experiences, says he once spoke with Hal Puthoff, whom he describes as the man who ran Stargate, a CIA programme that tried to use psychics for spying. host-has-seen-jacobs-dd214-1964: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says he has personally seen the DD214 of a man named Bob Jacobs. host-s-dream-of-flea-texting-him: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that out of nowhere he had a dream in which Flea, the famous bass player, was texting him. He tells it as a strange personal moment, the kind of odd coincidence he finds meaningful.
host-s-father-dreamed-of-an-earthquake-o: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says his father wrote about a recurring dream in a book called The Tools, around the early 1990s in Los Angeles. host-s-frightening-month-after-visiting-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that after he visited Skinwalker Ranch, a property known for reports of strange lights and odd happenings, he had a strange month. host-s-mars-ufo-photo-tweet-turns-out-to: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says he once posted a small picture online that seemed to show a UFO on Mars. As he tells it, the object turned out to be a rock. He shares it as an example of how easy it is to see something strange in a blurry photo.
host-s-own-ayahuasca-experience: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says he once took ayahuasca, a psychedelic brew from the Amazon, but has never taken DMT, the strong psychedelic drug found in it. host-s-own-two-ufo-sightings-2020: A podcast host named Jesse Michels, who interviews people about UFOs, says he saw two UFOs himself in 2020. He says that after those sightings he became obsessed with the subject, and he gives this as the reason he started looking into it so closely.
host-s-reading-of-majestic-as-a-continui: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, suggests that "Majestic 12", a supposed secret group said to oversee UFO matters since the 1950s, may really be one of the high-level committees that have gone by names like 5412, the 303 Committee and the Committee of 40, and he raises this in an episode with a former presidential adviser named Harald Malmgren. host-s-talk-with-former-skunk-works-head: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in 2024 he spoke with a man who had been head of revolutionary technology at Skunk Works, the secretive advanced aircraft division of the company Lockheed. host-s-trifield-meter-drained-at-skinwal: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says he visited Skinwalker Ranch, a property in Utah's Uintah Basin famous for paranormal reports. host-sees-two-metallic-orbs-during-holot: A podcast host named Jesse Michels says he saw two metallic orbs while doing holotropic breathwork, a practice of deep, rapid breathing meant to bring on altered states, with a friend in Silver Lake, a neighbourhood of Los Angeles, California. host-smelled-sulfur-at-skinwalker-ranch-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that around 2022 he went to Skinwalker Ranch, a property in Utah famous for paranormal reports, and smelled sulfur there. hostile-telepaths-encountered-on-mars: Jeffrey Mishlove, a psychologist who studies psychic abilities, says on Jesse Michels's podcast that if you travel to Mars with your mind alone, using telepathy, the first thing you will meet is a group of five telepaths. hosting-the-mind-s-ear-on-kpfa-radio-197: A researcher of the paranormal, Jeffrey Mishlove, says that in the 1970s the KPFA radio station in Berkeley, California, part of the listener-funded Pacifica network, offered him a regular slot every Tuesday and Thursday at noon. houdin-s-theory-that-the-great-pyramid-w: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, has talked several times about the ideas of Jean-Pierre Houdin, a French architect he calls a leading researcher on how the Great Pyramid of Giza in Egypt was built. house-sized-tall-white-deep-spacecraft-s: A man named Charles Hall, who says he spent three years in the 1960s living alongside tall, white-skinned aliens near Area 51, a secret US military test site in Nevada, says he saw one of their deep space craft up close in Indian Springs Valley, Nevada. houston-answers-a-question-his-mother-as: A mother in Atlanta, Georgia, named Katie says that her son Houston answered a question she had only asked silently in her head, without speaking. houston-finds-crystal-dice-hidden-for-a-: Ky Dickens, a filmmaker behind a documentary about non-speaking children said to read minds, tells a story about a young non-speaker named Houston in Atlanta, Georgia, sometime in the 2020s. houston-finds-hidden-stones-and-senses-t: A mother in Atlanta, Georgia, named Katie says that her son Houston found stones that had been hidden from him and could sense their energy. houston-says-mama-i-love-you-the-day-bef: A mother in Atlanta, Georgia, named Katie says that the day before Thanksgiving, her son Houston, then about 17, said "Mama, I love you." houston-sends-ky-images-at-night-about-t: A filmmaker named Ky Dickens, who made a documentary called the Telepathy Tapes about children said to read minds, says she began getting images at night about her film in 2024. how-roger-leer-began-removing-alien-impl: Steve Coburn, a scientist who studies what are called alien implants (small objects some people believe were put into their bodies by non-human beings), tells how a foot doctor named Roger Leer got into the field. how-the-atlantis-story-passed-from-solon: Randall Carlson, a researcher of ancient catastrophes, explains on Jesse Michels's podcast how the story of Atlantis, the legendary lost island civilisation, reached the ancient Greek philosopher Plato. howard-hughes-and-the-mormon-mafia-1950: Matthew Pines, a security analyst, says on Jesse Michels's podcast that Howard Hughes, the rich American aviator and businessman, was closely tied to the Mormon church from the 1950s to the 1970s. howard-hughes-brought-to-the-bahamas: A guest who goes by the name JASON says on Jesse Michels's podcast that Howard Hughes, the rich American aviator and businessman, was suddenly brought to an island in the Bahamas. howard-hughes-s-undisclosed-sensitive-pr: Danny Sheehan, a lawyer known for big public-interest cases, says on Jesse Michels's podcast that Howard Hughes, the rich American aviator and businessman, was working on "a couple other extraordinarily sensitive programs." howard-hughes-visiting-george-van-tassel: In the 1950s a man named George Van Tassel lived at Giant Rock, a huge boulder in the California desert, where he kept a private airstrip. howard-morland-reconstructs-the-teller-u: Eric Weinstein, a mathematician and commentator, tells of Howard Morland, a writer for a magazine called The Progressive, who around 1979 was given an odd assignment: with no physics training, work out the Teller-Ulam design, the closely guarded secret of how a hydrogen bomb works, which US laws called the Atomic Energy Acts kept classified. huge-glowing-craft-over-the-november-5-m: A US Air Force veteran named Mario Woods says that in November 1977 a huge glowing craft appeared over a nuclear missile site called November 5, which belonged to Ellsworth Air Force Base in South Dakota. huge-unidentified-underwater-craft-promp: The president of a Russian republic, speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast, read from an account saying that very large unidentified craft were found moving underwater in the Pacific Ocean, and the story also places such sightings in the Baltic Sea, the North Sea and the Atlantic. hugh-angleton-in-italy-during-the-1933-m: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Hugh Angleton, father of the longtime CIA spy-catcher James Jesus Angleton, was stationed in Italy in 1933, when a craft is said to have crashed near Magenta in northern Italy. hugh-everett-s-multiverse-theory-and-his: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells of a physicist named Hugh Everett, who came up with the "many worlds" theory, the idea that every possible outcome plays out in its own branch of reality. hughes-aircraft-builds-the-glomar-explor: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, points to the Glomar Explorer, a ship built for recovering things from the deep ocean floor, which he says was built by Hughes Aircraft, an American aerospace company, in the 1970s. human-abduction-squads-made-to-look-like: Steven Greer, a man who gathers testimony from people claiming inside knowledge of secret programmes, says that from the 1990s people came forward telling him they had flown these craft, and others said they had served on human abduction squads dressed up to look like aliens. human-bottleneck-reset-event-70-000-year: A podcast co-host named Jack says that some people firmly believe human history has been "reset" more than once, with civilization wiped out and starting over. humans-as-slave-workers-in-eden: Jason Jorjani, a philosopher, offers a reading of Eden, the garden in the Bible's book of Genesis where the first humans lived. hundredth-monkey-effect-on-japanese-isla: Randy Anderson, a guest who says he saw alien technology at a military base, brings up what is known as the hundredth monkey effect, the idea that once enough members of a group learn something, others who were never taught seem to pick it up too. hunt-s-deathbed-confession-of-a-conspira: Peter Levenda, an author who writes about secret history, says on Jesse Michels's podcast that E. hybrid-woman-with-skateboard-in-the-groc: Whitley Strieber, a writer known for describing his own encounters with beings he believes are not human, told a podcast host, Jesse Michels, about a moment in a grocery store near Santa Monica, California, around 2024. hypnosis-with-dr-michael-o-connell-train: A man named Chris Bledsoe, who says he has had repeated UFO experiences in the Carolinas since 2007, says he later recovered memories of them through hypnosis. He raises it to suggest sightings cluster around military sites.
i-beams-with-hieroglyphics-told-at-the-r: John Brandenburg, a physicist, tells of a conference called Reminiscences of Roswell, about Roswell, New Mexico, where something is said to have crashed in 1947. He says officers who were there at the time, and daughters of the local sheriff, told him that all the material was flown out, including metal beams covered in markings like hieroglyphics and various plates. If true, it would mean the wreckage was something with writing no one recognised.
ian-fleming-s-mi6-mission-to-evacuate-ma: A researcher and author named Jason Jorjani says that Ian Fleming, who later wrote the James Bond novels, worked for MI6, Britain's foreign intelligence service, during the Second World War. According to Jorjani, Fleming's specific job at the end of the war in 1945 was to help Martin Bormann, one of Hitler's top aides, escape from Germany to Argentina, which would mean British intelligence quietly saved a senior Nazi.
ian-stevenson-s-reincarnation-cases-at-t: Jason Jorjani, a philosopher, says on Jesse Michels's podcast that Dr. Ian Stevenson, a researcher at the University of Virginia, gathered hundreds and hundreds of cases of young children who suddenly remembered past lives. He places this work from the 1960s through the 1980s. He tells it as evidence that the mind may outlive the body, which would change how we think about death.
iarpa-request-to-study-crispr-cas9-dna-d: Bob Maguire, who describes himself as a contractor for the CIA, the US foreign intelligence agency, told podcast host Jesse Michels that around 2013 or 2014 he was asked to look into storing information inside DNA using CRISPR-Cas9, a tool for editing genes. He says the request came through IARPA, a US government agency that funds research for the intelligence services, and his work was tied to the Hume Center, a research center at Virginia Tech university. He says it happened when Stacy Dixon, later deputy to the Director of National Intelligence (the head of all US spy agencies), was running IARPA, which would suggest the intelligence world was quietly exploring DNA as a way to hold data.
iblis-refuses-to-bow-to-adam: A researcher named Jason Jorjani retells an old religious story from Islam: Iblis, also called Shaytan, the figure known as Satan, refused to bow down before Adam, the first man God created. In Jorjani's telling this refusal is a key moment in the story of how humans and other kinds of beings came to stand against each other.
ice-age-crustal-rebound-as-the-cause-of-: A pole shift is the idea that Earth's outer shell can slide, moving lands to new places relative to the poles, a notion linked to the writer Charles Hapgood. Randall Carlson, a researcher, says that during the last great ice age and its melting, over places like North America, Hudson Bay and northwestern Europe, the rapid piling up and loss of ice could make the crust unstable enough to move faster than usual. If true, the planet's surface could shift suddenly enough to reshape the world humans lived in.
ice-age-gray-farm-and-granary-with-13-tu: Charles Hall, a man who says he spent three years with tall white aliens at Area 51, a secret US Air Force test site in Nevada, told podcast host Jesse Michels about an L-shaped valley in the desert of central Nevada. He says that during the last ice age, gray aliens (small gray-skinned beings) ran a farm there and cut 13 tunnels into the mountain on the valley's west side to use as a granary. If true, it would mean aliens were growing food on Earth long before recorded history.
ice-age-sahara-as-origin-of-egyptian-civ: A writer on ancient history named Graham Hancock says that to find where ancient Egyptian civilization really began, we need to look at the Sahara Desert during the Ice Age, many thousands of years ago, when it was not the desert it is today. If he is right, Egypt would have grown out of an older, forgotten culture that once lived in what is now the Sahara.
icecube-as-a-two-way-device-earthquake-g: This story is about IceCube, a large science station at the South Pole in Antarctica that is built to detect neutrinos, tiny particles that pass through almost everything. A man named Eric Hecker says it can also send energy out, not just take it in. Jay Anderson, a guest on Jesse Michels' podcast, says Hecker found documents suggesting it is a two-way device that can emit energy, and the story calls it an "earthquake gun." Michels himself retells it simply as Hecker's claim that there are neutrino detectors and emitters at the South Pole. If true, a science station would really be hiding a weapon.
icig-hinted-to-brown-that-humans-are-not: Matthew Brown, described as a Pentagon whistleblower, told a podcast host, Jesse Michels, about his dealings with the Intelligence Community Inspector General, the official watchdog that investigates wrongdoing inside US spy agencies. Brown says that office hinted to him personally that humans are not the ones in charge, adding that he wants to be respectful toward them but that they did it. If true, it would mean people inside the government's own oversight system are signalling that some other intelligence holds power.
icig-hints-that-humans-are-not-in-charge: Dylan Borland, interviewed by podcast host Jesse Michels in 2026, says the office of the Inspector General of the Intelligence Community, the internal watchdog that oversees US spy agencies, hinted to him that humans are not really in charge. He first says they "extremely hinted" at it, then stresses that they did it with him personally, while saying he wants to respect them. If true, it would mean an official watchdog privately suggests that something other than humans runs things.
idea-for-directed-energy-ufo-shootdowns-: Jesse Michels, a podcast host, says that Harald Malmgren, a former presidential adviser, told Pippa Malmgren privately, on his deathbed, a remarkable story about the reported 1947 crash of a strange object near Roswell, New Mexico. According to that account, the CIA, the US spy agency, and the Atomic Energy Commission, the US agency over nuclear work, got the very idea of shooting down UFOs with directed energy, meaning beams such as lasers or microwaves, from an alien who survived that crash. If true, a non-human being would have taught the US how to bring down its own kind's craft.
ignored-idea-to-carry-the-space-shuttle-: A former NASA doctor named Greg Rogers, speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast, recalls that in 1972, when NASA, the US space agency, was first planning the Space Shuttle, some ideas were good and some were bad. He tells of an idea to carry the Shuttle on the back of a Boeing 747 jumbo jet that was at first ignored, as an example of how good ideas can be passed over inside large organizations.
igy-listening-posts-for-u-2-overflights-: A researcher named Jan Lundquist, appearing in a documentary about the inventor Thomas Townsend Brown, says that the International Geophysical Year, a worldwide science effort in 1957, gave Brown a reason to travel the globe. According to Lundquist, Brown used those trips to set up listening posts for the U-2, an American spy plane flying over the Soviet Union, which would mean this science project also hid secret intelligence work.
illuminati-poster-in-the-dupont-circle-h: Peter Levenda, an author and researcher described as a historian of the CIA, told a podcast host, Jesse Michels, about a trip to Washington, DC, in the 1970s to research in the National Archives, where the US government keeps its historical records. He says that when he carried his suitcase into his hotel room near Dupont Circle, someone had left a huge poster on the wall of the eye in the pyramid, a symbol often tied to the Illuminati, a secret society of legend. He tells it as one of a string of strange coincidences around that trip, as if someone were watching or sending him a message.
immaculate-constellation-answers-to-the-: Matthew Brown, described as a Pentagon whistleblower, told a podcast host, Jesse Michels, about a secret program he calls Immaculate Constellation, which he links to the study of unexplained flying objects. Brown says it appears that the final authority over it, where the buck stops, is the National Security Council, the White House group that advises the president on defence and foreign affairs. If true, it would put responsibility for the program at the very top of government.
immaculate-constellation-as-quarantine-o: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, offers his own idea about something called Immaculate Constellation. He says that you would need something like it to quarantine, or wall off, some of the communications about the subject, both for physical reasons if there are crashed UFOs and otherwise. If he is right, it would be a way of keeping knowledge of such crashes sealed inside the government.
immaculate-constellation-hub-at-schrieve: Matthew Brown, a man who calls himself a Pentagon whistleblower, told podcast host Jesse Michels about "Immaculate Constellation," his name for a secret government programme that he says gathers data on UAP, the government's newer term for UFOs. Brown says a briefing on the programme's capabilities, from around 2018, pointed to Schriever Air Force Base in Colorado as at least one hub of the programme. If true, it would place a hidden UFO effort at a specific military base.
immaculate-constellation-report-describe: A journalist named Michael Shellenberger says that in 2024 he received a report about a secret US program called Immaculate Constellation. According to Shellenberger, the report reveals a very large strategic intelligence project set up to gather and evaluate information on UAP, the official term for UFOs, which would mean the government studies the subject far more seriously than it says in public.
immaculate-constellation-rotating-triang: A researcher who goes by the online name UAPGerb points to a document called Immaculate Constellation, which he links to a man named Matthew Brown. He says it describes slowly rotating triangles seen in 2017 over the area of Indo-Pacific Command, the US military command covering the Pacific and Indian Ocean region. If true, the military would have recorded strange triangular craft in its own operating areas.
immaculate-constellation-search-spike-an: Immaculate Constellation is the name of an alleged secret US programme on unexplained craft, raised by a journalist, Michael Shellenberger, in testimony at a November 2024 congressional hearing. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says the name had a spike in searches on Google Trends, Google's tool showing how often terms are searched, around August or September 2023, when a whistleblower named David Grusch went public, and that this data was later deleted. If true, it would suggest people knew the name long before it was public, and that someone wanted that trace gone.
immaculate-constellation-usap-managed-by: Immaculate Constellation is the name of what is said to be a secret US government program about UFOs. It is described as a USAP, an unacknowledged special access program, meaning a secret project whose existence the government does not admit. In 2024 a journalist, Michael Shellenberger, published a report about it. He says that after he published, he was told the program was managed by the Department of Defense, the Pentagon, but held at the White House. A man who describes himself as a Pentagon whistleblower, Matthew Brown, tells it differently. He says the program is run and owned by the National Security Council, the President's own security advisers in the White House, and that it is an old mission from before 2017. If true, it would mean UFO secrets are kept at the very top of the US government.
immaculate-constellation-usap-set-up-in-: A researcher who goes by UAPGerb says on Jesse Michels's podcast that a secret programme called Immaculate Constellation was set up in 2017 as a USAP, short for "unacknowledged special access program", a Pentagon project so secret its existence is not admitted. He says it was created in reaction to events, unlike older long-running programmes, and that it cuts out sensor and satellite data showing things like UFOs and hides it away in other secret programmes. If true, it would mean the government is quietly hiding its best UFO evidence.
imminent-names-bae-systems-as-an-inherit: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, points to Imminent, a book by Lou Elizondo, a former Pentagon official who worked on UFO questions. Michels says the book names BAE Systems, a large defence company, as one of the firms that inherited UFO technology. If true, it would mean private defence contractors hold recovered non-human technology.
immune-collapse-and-treatment-at-brooke-: Whitley Strieber, a writer who says he has met beings that are not human, says that in 1952, as a child in Texas, his immune system collapsed and he ended up at Brooke General Hospital in San Antonio. He mentions a school report card from the time as part of his account of his early life, which he links to the strange experiences he describes.
imperial-college-extended-the-dmt-state-: A researcher named Andrew Gallimore, speaking in 2025 on the show of podcast host Jesse Michels, says that some time after 2015 Imperial College, a university in London, took up research on DMT, a powerful psychedelic substance, and built a much better way of giving it, so that the experience could be stretched to about 30 minutes. He credits earlier work by a man named Chris Timberman, and adds that all the volunteers at Imperial got through the trials with no serious harm. If true, it would mean people could stay in the DMT state long enough to study it properly.
implant-from-a-va-surgeon-moving-under-t: Lou Elizondo, a former Pentagon official who has spoken publicly about unexplained flying objects, told a podcast host, Jesse Michels, about a small object taken out of a US military veteran's body. He says a surgeon from the Department of Veterans Affairs, the government department that provides care to former service members, removed it from a veteran who claimed a close encounter with a UAP, the official term for an unidentified flying object, and that a pathologist said it moved under the microscope on its own, as if alive. If true, it would suggest something non-human had placed a living device inside a person.
implant-indications-and-alien-dyes-found: Steve Coburn, a scientist who studies objects he believes are alien implants in human bodies, told podcast host Jesse Michels that he saw signs of implants in a man named Eric Mitchell. He says that recently they also found dyes on them, which he links to aliens. If true, it would be physical evidence that someone had been marked or tagged by non-human beings.
implant-paper-rejected-by-journal-of-sci: A scientist named Steve Coburn, who studies objects that people say are alien implants in their bodies, says that he and a colleague, Roger Leer, wrote a paper on their work. He tells podcast host Jesse Michels that they tried to publish it in the Journal of Scientific Exploration, a journal for research on unusual topics, and it was rejected. Coburn tells it to show how hard it is to get this research taken seriously.
implant-purpose-and-bloodline-hybrid-pro: Steve Coburn, a scientist who studies objects he believes are alien implants in human bodies, told podcast host Jesse Michels what he thinks such an implant is for. His understanding is that it was a medical monitoring device, tracking things like blood sugar and body temperature, and the story ties this to the idea of a program watching certain family bloodlines for breeding human-alien hybrids. If true, it would mean some people are being medically monitored by non-humans.
implant-starts-working-after-anne-s-deat: Whitley Strieber, a writer known for describing his own encounters with beings he believes are not human, told a podcast host, Jesse Michels, about something that happened after the death of Anne Strieber, around 2015. He says an implant, a tiny object he believes was put in his body during his encounters, began working, and that words came through it, slowing down until they clearly said "it's me." He tells it as a sign that Anne was reaching him after her death.
implant-tracking-patent: An engineer named Bob McGwier, who appears on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels in an episode that calls him a CIA contractor (the CIA is the US spy agency), talks about a patent he says he wrote. He says he never believed the stories about aliens putting small implants in people and tracking them, until he wrote a patent that explains how that tracking could work. In another part of the same interview he names it as a patent linked to Hawkeye 360, and says it describes how aliens would find these beacons all over the planet. McGwier is the only teller, and he comes back to it twice, the second time giving the patent a name. If true, it would mean the method behind those abduction stories is set out in an ordinary patent.
implants-emitted-radio-signals-during-ja: Steve Coburn, a scientist who studies objects he believes are alien implants in human bodies, told podcast host Jesse Michels that some implants started giving off radio signals. He says this happened while he was filming for a Japanese TV show. If true, it would mean the implants are active devices that send out signals.
implants-from-roger-leir-s-surgeries-one: Whitley Strieber, a writer known for describing his own encounters with beings he believes are not human, told a podcast host, Jesse Michels, about the 1990s work of Roger Leir, a surgeon who removed small objects people believed were alien implants. Strieber says that among the objects from those surgeries, one was remarkable: while it sat in a person's neck, near the second vertebra, it was giving off a radio signal. If true, it would mean the objects were working devices, not just stray fragments.
implants-modulating-gene-expression-thro: A researcher named Allan Ezarus talks about small bodies found near Nazca, Peru, said to be over a thousand years old and to have three fingers, and about metal implants said to be inside them. He suggests that these implants might work through the body's own electrical signals to switch genes on and off, shaping the beings into what they are, which would mean they were deliberately engineered.
in-air-scale-test-at-480-volts-showing-a: Charles Buer, who works at a Florida company called Exodus Propulsion, says his team put a device on a weighing scale in open air and ran 480 volts through it. He says the scale moved by about a tenth of a gram, which he works out to roughly one millinewton of thrust, a very small push, and he points to a 42-minute video of the test. He told this to a podcast host, Jesse Michels, in an episode about building propulsion that would work like antigravity, which is what it would hint at if true.
in-secure-meetings-officials-call-anothe: James Valor, a witness connected with Skywatcher, a startup that says it tries to call up unexplained flying objects, told a podcast host, Jesse Michels, about meetings in secure government buildings around 2024 and 2025. He says officials would hear what his team had, then say they would call another program that holds all the knowledge and data on the subject to see if anything matched, and the answer always came back "no." He tells it as a sign that a hidden program exists and is keeping its knowledge to itself.
in-the-aircraft-about-200-meters-from-a-: James Valor, a witness connected with Skywatcher, a startup that says it tries to call up unexplained flying objects, told a podcast host, Jesse Michels, about a flight near El Paso, Texas, in 2025. He says he was about 200 meters from what he calls an "8th class" object, a category in the team's own way of ranking what they see, and yet the people around him in the aircraft did not see it. If true, it would mean some of these objects can be right beside people without being noticed.
incident-at-nellis-area-2-weapon-storage: A researcher named Robert Hastings, who collects accounts of UFOs around nuclear weapons sites, said on podcast host Jesse Michels's show in 2024 that another incident took place at the weapons storage area known as Area 2 at Nellis Air Force Base in Nevada. He gives no date in this telling. He tells it as one more case in a pattern that, if true, would suggest something is watching nuclear weapons.
incorporating-a-church-to-avoid-the-viet: Peter Levenda, an author and researcher described as a historian of the CIA, told a podcast host, Jesse Michels, about his youth in the Bronx, New York, around 1968. He says he and others legally set up a church, which he names as the Ottophilis Savonic Orthodox Church of North and South America, as a way to avoid the draft, the compulsory call-up of young men to fight in the Vietnam War. He tells it as part of his own unusual path into the world of hidden religion and secret history.
incursions-in-the-city-of-nauta-2023: A researcher and filmmaker named Tim Alberino says that around 2023, strange beings made incursions, that is, appeared and attacked or intruded, among people in the Peruvian Amazon. According to Alberino, these events happened not only out in the jungle but also in the town of Nauta, which would mean the encounters reached a populated place and not just remote villages.
independence-day-script-came-from-the-ci: A researcher and disclosure campaigner named Steven Greer says on podcast host Jesse Michels's show in 2025 that the script of Independence Day, the 1996 Hollywood alien film starring Will Smith, came straight out of the CIA, the US spy agency. In his words, it was like the work of the agency's own scripting and casting department. If true, it would mean the government shapes how the public pictures aliens.
independent-brackish-aquifer-below-the-o: The Osiris Shaft is a deep shaft cut into the rock of the Giza Plateau in Egypt, the high ground where the great pyramids stand. A researcher named Jeffrey Drum, speaking on the podcast of host Jesse Michels, says that right below this shaft sits a body of underground water that is completely separate from the Nile River. If true, the water under the shaft would come from somewhere other than the river, which matters to people who think the site was built around water for a reason.
index-cards-with-records-of-the-et-inter: Dan Sheehan, a lawyer, passes on what he says a man named Oscar Wolf told him: at S4, a site said to be linked to Area 51, a secret US military base in Nevada, military men showed Wolf a set of index cards recording interviews with extraterrestrials. If true, it would mean the government has written records of talking with beings from elsewhere.
indigenous-initiation-ceremonies-for-con: A researcher named Diana Pasulka, who studies UFOs and religion, told podcast host Jesse Michels that contact with other kinds of beings is nothing new to many Indigenous peoples. She says that Native American tribes and Aboriginal Australian tribes have long known about such contact, and even have their own initiation ceremonies for it. If so, what modern people call UFO encounters would have a much older place in human spiritual life.
indonesia-herrera-s-unit-stumbles-on-a-p: This story is about a man named Michael Herrera, who says that while serving with a military unit in a disaster zone in Indonesia he saw a non-human craft. A guest named Matthew Pines offers a possible explanation: a 'psionic asset' team, people said to have mind powers, was there with the craft, and Herrera stumbled on it, an idea he links to another man, Jake Barber. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, credits the idea to Herrera himself: maybe it was a human trafficking operation moving these psychic people, or a secret programme trying to get out after an earthquake hit. If true, it would mean secret programmes use both craft and gifted people overseas.
indopacom-large-disc-using-clouds-as-con: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, interviewing Matthew Brown, described as a Pentagon whistleblower, someone who goes public about what happens inside government, reads from a document called the Immaculate Constellation report. One entry describes a large disc using clouds to hide, seen in the area covered by INDOPACOM, the US military command for the Indian and Pacific Ocean region, which would mean the military logged a craft deliberately concealing itself.
indus-valley-civilization-found-by-railw: The Indus Valley Civilization was an ancient culture whose ruined cities, Mohenjo-daro and Harappa, lie along the Indus River in what is now Pakistan. A writer on lost ancient civilizations, Graham Hancock, told podcast host Jesse Michels that it was found in the 1920s by accident, when railway workers laying a line came across the remains. He tells it to show how whole civilizations can stay hidden until luck turns them up.
industry-physicist-reads-the-propulsion-: A physicist from industry named James Valor spoke with podcast host Jesse Michels about Skywatcher, a startup that says it tries to call UFOs into view and record them. Valor says that while they were watching the skies in February and March 2025, they were shown technology that is in use, and that he could work out how it moves from footage that has not been released. If true, it would mean the way these objects fly can be studied from real recordings.
infiltrator-removed-before-the-1997-cong: Steven Greer, who campaigns for the government to release what it knows about UFOs, told podcast host Jesse Michels about private briefings his group gave members of the US Congress in 1997 at a hotel in Washington, D.C. Greer says that someone working against them got very far into the planning before being removed. If true, it would mean someone was trying from the inside to disrupt efforts to tell Congress about UFOs.
ingo-swann-affects-a-thermistor-in-a-far: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in early 1970s California, researchers Hal Puthoff and Russell Targ put a thermistor, a small sensor that reacts to temperature, inside a Faraday cage, a metal enclosure that blocks outside electrical signals. According to Michels, the psychic Ingo Swann was able to affect the sensor with his mind. If true, it would mean the mind can act on objects with no physical contact.
ingo-swann-affects-shielded-quark-detect: Physicist Hal Puthoff told podcast host Jesse Michels about tests he ran in the early 1970s at Stanford Research Institute, a research lab in California, with a man named Ingo Swann who was being tested for psychic ability. Puthoff says they had an extremely sensitive detector sealed inside layers of magnetic, electrical and superconducting shielding so that nothing outside could affect it, and that Swann affected it anyway, "unequivocally, 100 percent." If true, it would suggest the mind can act on matter with no physical contact.
ingo-swann-remote-viewing-alien-bases-on: This story is about Ingo Swann, a man known for remote viewing, the practice of trying to see faraway places with the mind alone, starting around 1972. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says Swann claimed to remote view alien bases on the Moon, and points to Swann's book Penetration. A philosopher, Jason Jorjani, tells a fuller version. He says Swann saw tall, statuesque Nordic-looking people who gave him a look that said he did not belong and should leave. According to Jorjani, Swann saw these same beings ruling over armies of naked slave laborers, and he credits a man named Axelrod who was involved. If true, it would mean someone is living on the Moon, hidden from us.
ingo-swann-remote-views-aliens-on-the-mo: Ingo Swann was a man known for "remote viewing", the idea that a person can see distant places using only the mind. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, and his guest, a researcher with a doctorate named Jeffrey Mishlove, both say Swann claimed he used it to travel to the Moon, where he believed aliens were present and forced him away. Mishlove places this in the 1970s. If true, it would mean someone is already on the Moon, and does not want visitors.
ingo-swann-remote-views-ruined-cities-on: Ingo Swann was a remote viewer, someone said to describe faraway places using only the mind. A philosopher, Jason Jorjani, says that Swann viewed Mars this way in the early 1980s and reported that the same beings he had earlier seen on the Moon had built a civilization there, whose ruins he saw. If true, a non-human people would have lived on both the Moon and Mars.
ingo-swann-s-book-penetration-says-the-m: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, talks about a psychic named Ingo Swann, who he says was part of Stargate, a CIA program that tried to use psychics as spies, and who wrote a book called Penetration. In one episode Michels ties the book to the idea that the Moon is a hollow spaceship, while in another he says it is about remote viewing, trying to see distant places with the mind, the dark side of the Moon, and links it to a man named Axelrod. If true, it would mean someone or something is active on the Moon, out of sight.
ingo-swann-s-reports-to-scientology-on-t: A lawyer named Dan Sheehan says that in the 1970s Ingo Swann, a well-known psychic, was secretly sending reports to the main Guardian's Office of the Church of Scientology in the UK. According to Sheehan, those reports described the inner workings of a remote viewing program, an effort to use the mind to see distant places, run by the Office of Naval Intelligence, the US Navy's spy service. If true, it would mean a church was quietly watching a secret military psychic project from the inside.
ingo-swann-s-thermistor-experiments-at-c: Hal Puthoff, a scientist described as a CIA UFO expert, says that in the early 1970s the psychic Ingo Swann took part in experiments at City College in New York under a professor named Gertrude Schmeidler. According to Puthoff, she set up thermistors, small temperature sensors, and Swann could make their readings go up and down from across the room. If true, a human mind could affect physical objects at a distance.
ingo-swann-sees-a-non-human-woman-at-a-s: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, talks about Penetration, a book by Ingo Swann, a famous remote viewer, meaning someone who claimed to see distant places with the mind, and who was there at the start of the US government's psychic spying programme. Michels says that halfway through the book Swann describes being at a supermarket and seeing one of them, a being who looked like a woman but was not human. If true, it would mean non-humans walk among us in ordinary places.
inisfada-school-for-gifted-children-did-: Jay Anderson, a guest on podcast host Jesse Michels' show, passes on what a man named Eric Hecker told him about his childhood. According to Anderson, Hecker went to a school called Inisfada on Long Island, New York, a strange school for gifted children where they practised remote viewing, the attempt to see distant places or things using only the mind. If true, it would mean children were being trained in psychic skills.
initiates-at-eleusis-came-away-believing: Eleusis is an ancient religious site in Greece, where people in antiquity went through secret rites. A speaker in a clip on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, passing on what someone else told them, says that people arrived at Eleusis as ordinary human beings and walked away thinking they were immortal. Told this way, it suggests that something at those ancient rites changed how people saw death itself.
inman-denies-retrieved-ufos-in-jay-ander: Bobby Ray Inman, a retired admiral who once held some of the top jobs in US intelligence, was asked in an interview with a researcher named Jay Anderson whether the government had ever recovered crashed unidentified craft. He says the answer is no, there were absolutely no retrieved UFOs, and that he has high confidence in that. The clip was played on Jesse Michels's podcast more than once, and it matters because it is a flat denial from someone who would likely have known.
inman-no-other-life-in-our-galaxy-2020: Bobby Ray Inman, a retired admiral who once held some of the top jobs in US intelligence, said in an interview shown on Jesse Michels's podcast that he has a high level of confidence there is no other living life anywhere in our galaxy. Coming from him, it would mean there are no visitors from nearby worlds to explain.
insider-adviser-s-email-pointing-to-gree: Peter Levenda, a researcher and writer, says that around 2015, while working with the musician Tom DeLonge, they got a long email from one of DeLonge's most trusted advisers asking how much they really knew about Greek mythology. The hint, as the story is framed, pointed toward Prometheus, the Greek figure who stole fire from the gods for humans. If true, insiders would be suggesting that ancient myths hold clues about contact with non-human beings.
insider-describes-place-where-bodies-are: A UFO researcher who goes by UAPGerb, speaking on Jesse Michels' podcast, says that he has heard from unnamed former military and intelligence insiders. According to him, one of them has talked about a place where bodies are stored, by which he means bodies of non-human beings, though he does not say where it is. If true, it would mean the government holds physical remains of non-human beings.
insider-says-10-people-have-the-bigger-p: James Fox, who makes films about UFOs, says that an insider told him only about 10 people have the bigger picture of what is going on, and that the intent behind it is a little scary. insiders-report-sources-afraid-to-come-f: Kirk McConnell, a staffer in the US Senate in Washington, says that in the 2020s his office wanted people with inside knowledge of UFOs to come forward. jacobs-and-hopkins-conclude-abductions-b: Tim Alberino, a filmmaker and researcher, says on Jesse Michels' podcast that David Jacobs and Budd Hopkins, two well-known researchers of people who report being taken by aliens, reached a conclusion about when it started.
