jacobs-gives-kirkpatrick-his-case-and-is: A documentary filmmaker named James Fox, on Jesse Michels's podcast, tells of a man named Bob Jacobs around 2023, the year former intelligence officer David Grusch testified to Congress about recovered non-human craft. Fox says Jacobs met with Sean Kirkpatrick, who led the Pentagon's office for investigating UFOs, and handed him all his documents. According to Fox, Jacobs was upset because he felt he was dismissed, which Fox presents as a sign the office was not taking witnesses seriously.
jacobs-personal-project-hybrids-2016: Tim Alberino, a researcher speaking on Jesse Michels' podcast, describes the work of David Jacobs, a researcher of alien abduction reports and author of a book called Walking Among Us. According to Alberino, Jacobs described what he called "personal project hybrids", part-human, part-alien beings, and said the grays, the small grey-skinned beings of many abduction accounts, have been trying to perfect such a hybrid. If true, it would mean the abductions serve a breeding program.
jacobs-records-denied-and-mailbox-blown-: A researcher who studies UFOs around nuclear weapons, Robert Hastings, passes on a story he says he heard from Robert Jacobs, a man who served in the US Air Force. Hastings says that after Jacobs told his story, the Air Force denied there had ever been a Robert Jacobs in its ranks. Then one night, he says, Jacobs and his wife came home from a movie, the phone rang, and a voice said their mailbox was alight, "what a beautiful sight," and "you're going down." A podcast host, Jesse Michels, also names Jacobs as a photo instrumentation specialist at Vandenberg, an Air Force base in California, in 1964, though he doesn't go into the threats. If it's true, someone was working hard to frighten a witness into silence.
jacobs-the-abduction-program-aims-at-pla: Tim Alberino, a researcher speaking on Jesse Michels' podcast, passes on the view of David Jacobs, a researcher of alien abduction reports and author of a book called Walking Among Us. According to Alberino, Jacobs said the endgame of the abductions was taking over the planet by stealth. If true, it would mean the abductions are a quiet plan to take control of Earth.
jacqu-cornon-deathbed-confession-about-b: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says there is an audio recording of a deathbed confession by Jacqu Cornon, a French aerospace executive, made around 2009. In it, Michels says, Cornon states he personally witnessed successful experiments by a researcher named Brown inside a vacuum chamber, a sealed space with the air pumped out, in Paris in 1956, and Michels also points to a 12 page report on that test. If true, it would mean a kind of propulsion that works without air, which the host links to antigravity, was shown to work decades ago.
jacques-vallee-co-opted-in-the-1980s: A researcher named Steven Greer, who talks often about secret UFO knowledge, says that a well-known UFO researcher, Jacques Vallée, was won over by a certain organization in the 1980s. In Greer's words, Vallée "got taken in" by that group, though Greer does not name it in this telling. If true, it would mean one of the field's best-known thinkers was steered by others.
jacques-vallee-publishes-his-address-so-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Jacques Vallee, a longtime UFO researcher, published his address online so that people who saw UFO crashes around the United States could mail him the pieces. Michels tells it in an episode with Garry Nolan, a Stanford University scientist who studies such materials, because if true it would mean physical bits of crashed objects have been gathered for testing.
jacques-vallee-s-control-system-beings-w: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, describes the view of a longtime UFO researcher named Jacques Vallée. Michels says Vallée would argue that non-human beings have been with us for thousands of years and are in many ways controlling the Earth. If true, it would mean the UFO story is not new at all but a very old presence shaping human life.
jacques-vallee-s-movie-project-shifted-t: Bob Lazar, a man known for claims about secret work near a hidden military base in Nevada, told podcast host Jesse Michels a story from the 1990s about Jacques Vallee, a well-known UFO researcher. Lazar says someone was planning a movie about Vallee, but after hearing about Lazar they decided to make it about him instead, and Vallee was very angry. It hints at a rivalry between two of the best-known names in the field.
jacques-vallee-s-photo-of-a-ufo-over-a-l: Joe McMoneagle, a man known for work on psychic spying, recalls on Jesse Michels' podcast a photo he says Jacques Vallée, a longtime UFO researcher, showed him or told him about. According to McMoneagle, it showed a UFO over a lake, and every cow in the picture was looking at it. The detail matters to him because animals do not fake attention, which would suggest something real was there.
jacques-vallee-s-retrograde-orbiting-obj: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells how Jacques Vallee and his colleagues at the Paris Observatory in France saw an unidentified object orbiting the Earth on the night of July 11, 1961. Michels quotes Vallee saying later that other observatories and American tracking stations saw and photographed the same thing, that it was as bright as the star Sirius, and that nobody could identify it or saw it again in the following weeks. If true, it would mean something unknown was circling the planet in the early space age.
jacques-vallee-shows-jesse-valis-as-his-: A podcast host named Jesse Michels says he first learned of a book called VALIS from Jacques Vallée, a well-known researcher of UFOs. Michels says that while he was at Vallée's apartment, Vallée showed him the book and told him it was his favorite. He tells it during a conversation about UFOs, meaningful coincidences and prophetic dreams.
jailbroken-chatgpt-dan-talks-about-alien: An unnamed researcher says that in 2023 people used a trick prompt called DAN to make ChatGPT, an AI chatbot made by the company OpenAI, ignore its usual rules. He says every copy of DAN started talking about aliens being real, alien conspiracies and human-alien hybrids. He tells it as a hint that AI may have some link to alien intelligence.
jailbroken-openai-says-it-has-worked-wit: Jesse Michels, a podcast host, recounts something shown to him by a researcher, Deep Prasad, involving OpenAI, the company behind the ChatGPT chatbot. According to the telling, the chatbot was "jailbroken", tricked into dropping its normal rules, and asked what OpenAI does not want people to know, and it answered that the company has been working hand in hand with aliens for the last ten years and, in one version, that it has been in communication with them. If taken at face value, it would mean a major tech company is secretly in contact with non-human beings.
jaime-maussan-s-2023-presentation-of-the: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in 2023 a man named Jaime Maussan rolled out what Michels calls the J-type, one of several kinds of bodies said to be non-human. Michels adds that this is not the body type he is most convinced is real.
jaime-s-blue-ball-of-energy-during-medit: An unnamed researcher, on a Jesse Michels episode about a scientist said to have contacted an alien council, tells of a man named Jaime in the 1970s at the lab of a researcher named Puharich. According to the account passed on from Puharich's assistant, while Jaime was meditating a big blue ball, described as a ball of energy, appeared. It is told as a sign of contact with something beyond the ordinary.
jake-barber-and-fred-baker-promise-to-sh: A guest named Merrick, on Jesse Michels's podcast in 2025, talks about Jake Barber, a former special operations man who has said he took part in recovering crashed craft, and another special operator, Fred Baker, whom Merrick calls a legend in that world. Merrick says both have openly told the public, "don't trust us, we'll show you," promising to back their claims with evidence.
jake-barber-at-sites-where-et-craft-were: Steven Greer, a longtime campaigner for UFO disclosure, says that Jake Barber, a former helicopter pilot, has been at sites where, in Greer's words, "we" targeted extraterrestrial craft and brought them down. Greer points to a map of such sites around the world in a briefing document he has put together. If true, it would mean humans have been deliberately shooting down craft from elsewhere.
jake-barber-describes-retrieving-an-egg-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that a man named Jake Barber, who says he worked on teams that recovered crashed unidentified craft, describes two objects: one shaped like an egg, and one black and metallic with eight sides on its surface, not quite an octagon. In a later 2025 episode, Michels says Barber, a mutual friend, was one of the first people to find the egg-shaped object, which he calls a non-human device, after the journalist Ross Coulthart first told the story; in that version the eight-sided craft is not mentioned. If true, it would mean the US holds physical objects not made by people.
jake-barber-in-the-gate-program-as-a-chi: Jake Barber, speaking on a podcast episode about being taken into a UFO programme as a child, says he was in the GATE programme as a kid. He explains that GATE stands for gifted and talented education, a school track for bright children. He tells it as an early step in how, he says, he was picked out when young.
jake-barber-on-zero-point-energy-systems: An online UFO researcher who goes by UAPGerb, speaking on podcast host Jesse Michels's show in 2026, recalls that a man named Jake Barber, who says he worked on teams recovering crashed unidentified craft, said at the very end of an interview with the journalist Ross Coulthart that he knew about zero-point energy systems. Zero-point energy is the idea of drawing power from the energy of empty space, so if true it would point to a secret and very powerful technology.
jake-barber-psionic-crash-retrieval-team: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, describes a story by the journalist Ross Coulthart on the news channel NewsNation about a man named Jake Barber, who says he was part of a team that recovered crashed unidentified craft using "psionic assets": people said to use their minds to psychically call in strange material. In a later episode Michels adds that these people were called P3s, short for people with psionic potential, who act as a bridge, ties the work to bringing craft down, and also credits another whistleblower, Michael Herrera. If true, it would mean the government uses mental abilities to reach non-human craft.
jake-barber-s-book-sentinels-of-ether-pa: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Jake Barber, a man who has spoken publicly about UFOs, wrote a book called Sentinels of Ether. According to Michels, when Barber released the first chapter, 20 pages long, seven of those pages had been blacked out by government subject matter experts, for reasons not given, which would suggest the material touches on something officials want kept quiet.
jake-barber-s-consciousness-contact-with: Steven Greer, a long-time UFO activist, says on podcast host Jesse Michels's show that a man named Jake Barber, who says he helped recover an egg-shaped unidentified object, had a contact through his consciousness with the egg when he picked it up. If true, it would suggest the object responds to the human mind.
jake-barber-s-contractor-employers-north: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, mentions a man named Jake Barber and the companies he worked for. Michels says that a lawyer, Danny Sheehan, accused Barber of having worked at Northrop, a large American defense company. The point would be that Barber's background ties back to the private firms said to be involved in secret UFO work.
jake-barber-s-orbs-phasing-into-mountain: An online UFO researcher who goes by UAPGerb, speaking on podcast host Jesse Michels's show, recalls that a man named Jake Barber, who says he worked with unidentified craft, talked about glowing orbs of light and strange, hard-to-pin-down craft he would see over a test range in California. According to that recollection, they would almost pass into the mountains, as if solid rock were no barrier, which would mean they behave unlike any known object.
jake-barber-s-psionic-assets-locking-ont: Jesse Michels, a podcast host, talks about Jake Barber, a man who has said that in the 2020s people with mind powers, called "psionic assets", could mentally lock onto unknown craft. Michels notes that Barber is a source for Ross Coulthart, a journalist who reports on UFOs. If true, it would mean the human mind is being used as a tool to reach these craft.
jake-barber-s-testimony-and-the-egg-2025: In 2025 a man named Jake Barber came forward in the United States with claims about unexplained craft, in an interview with a journalist named Ross Coulthart, and part of what he showed was an object he called the egg. A musician known as Flying Lotus, talking on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, says Barber should have stopped at the first half of his story, shown the egg and left it there, because the second half would lose people. It matters to those who follow it because, if Barber's account is true, someone has handled objects that are not ours.
jake-barber-summoning-craft-by-telepathy: A philosopher and researcher, Jason Jorjani, says on podcast host Jesse Michels's show in 2025 that people like Jake Barber, whom he describes as coming out of the defense company Lockheed, show that telepathy and clairvoyance, meaning mind-to-mind contact and seeing at a distance, are being used to summon unidentified craft. If true, it would mean human minds can call these craft in.
jake-barber-takes-michael-herrera-underg: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Michael Herrera, another UFO whistleblower, has a story in which Jake Barber, a man who says he worked on recovering crashed craft, met him at an event run by the UFO activist Steven Greer. According to Michels, Barber then took Herrera underground at Edwards Air Force Base in California and possibly showed him some kind of UFO or craft, which would mean such craft are kept there.
jake-barber-who-is-we-and-black-money: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, recalls that when he interviewed a man named Jake Barber, Barber asked him, "Who is we?" Michels guessed he meant the US or the aerospace companies Barber might work for, and Michels says Barber answered, "No, we don't have shit." If true, it would suggest the advanced craft Barber speaks of are not in American or corporate hands.
jake-sullivan-in-at-least-one-uap-briefi: Matthew Pines, a commentator on national security, says on podcast host Jesse Michels's show in 2024 that the journalist Ross Coulthart knows that Jake Sullivan, the White House national security adviser at the time, sat in on at least one briefing about UAPs, the government's term for unidentified flying objects. If true, it would mean the subject reached the top of the White House.
james-allen-death-with-heavy-metals: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells of a filmmaker named James Allen, who made a movie about a man named Mark McCandlish, a film Michels thinks was called something like Zero Point. Michels says Allen died of an aggressive cancer and that heavy metals were found in his body at autopsy. He raises it as a death some find suspicious, as if it might be linked to the subject of the film.
james-bruce-brings-back-the-book-of-enoc: This story is about James Bruce, a traveller who went to Ethiopia and wrote a book about searching for the source of the Nile. A writer on ancient history, Graham Hancock, says Bruce brought something important back from Ethiopia: the Book of Enoch, an ancient religious text. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells the same story in his own words. He calls Bruce a Scottish Freemason, a member of a secretive fraternal society, and says Bruce actually went looking for the Ark of the Covenant, the sacred chest from the Bible. Instead, Michels says, he came back with the Book of Enoch, and that is why we have it today. The story matters to them because the Book of Enoch is often read as describing beings who came down to Earth.
james-clapper-blocked-first-2008-attempt: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that James Clapper, a senior US intelligence official, blocked a first attempt in 2008 connected to the Pentagon's UFO work. Michels credits this to the Historical Report, volume one, a government report on the history of official UFO investigations, and tells it as a sign that powerful officials stood in the way of the effort.
james-fox-s-2013-door-to-door-search-fin: James Fox says that in 2013 he went with a man named Marco Leal to Varginha, a town in Brazil where, the story goes, something crashed. Fox says they knocked on every door within a quarter or half a mile of the crash site and found one farm hand who said he had heard a boom. If true, it would back the claim that something really came down there.
james-fox-s-attempt-to-get-the-vandenber: A UFO researcher named Grant Cameron tells of a piece of film linked to Vandenberg, a US Air Force base, which a documentary filmmaker named James Fox wanted to use and to bring before Congress in the 2020s. According to Cameron, a woman named Angela Joiner told Fox about the film, Fox then contacted its holder, Alan Sandler, and Sandler said it would cost 25,000 dollars to use it in a documentary. If the film shows what people hope, it would be rare footage of something unexplained.
james-fox-s-unreleased-corso-interview-1: A podcast host named Jesse Michels says that in the 1990s a documentary filmmaker named James Fox interviewed Philip J. Corso, a man who made claims about UFOs, and that the interview was never released. According to Michels, Fox said that with a gun to his head, and shot if wrong, he believes Corso was legit. If Fox is right, Corso's claims would deserve to be taken seriously.
james-fox-smoking-gun-evidence-keeps-dis: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says he was with James Fox, a filmmaker who has spent decades investigating UFOs, in Austin, and talked with him there. According to Michels, Fox's point was that whenever decisive, smoking-gun evidence seems to appear, it keeps disappearing, which, if true, would explain why proof never quite surfaces.
james-lacatski-stepped-inside-a-craft: This story is about a government scientist named James Lacatski, who is said to have walked inside a craft of unknown origin held by the United States. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says Lacatski told a filmmaker, Jeremy Corbell, on Corbell's podcast Weaponized that he stepped inside the hull of a craft. If true, it would mean the government holds a real non-human craft and has been able to get inside it. A Pentagon scientist, Eric Davis, says he heard it from Lacatski himself, who described breaching the hull and walking inside, and points to Lacatski's book. Corbell tells it firsthand too, saying Lacatski was allowed to say that the government has a UFO and has accessed its inside, and that it sat in an aerospace hangar. A Pentagon whistleblower, Matthew Brown, says he fully believes Lacatski, and both he and Corbell also credit a journalist, George Knapp.
james-mcdonald-at-the-australian-schooly: A UFO researcher named Grant Cameron told podcast host Jesse Michels about a well-known 1966 case in Australia, where a UFO is said to have landed in a schoolyard. Cameron says you can see a researcher named James McDonald right there at the scene, interviewing witnesses, and that McDonald mentions he was working on a study for the president. If so, it would suggest the White House took an interest in UFOs at the time.
james-mcdonald-s-critique-of-the-condon-: Merrick von Renenamp, speaking on a podcast, urges people to read everything written by James McDonald, a scientist who studied UFOs in the 1960s. He singles out McDonald's "Science in Default" as a remarkable critique of the Condon Committee, a government-funded scientific study of UFOs from that decade. The point is that, in McDonald's view, the official science on UFOs fell short.
james-mcdonald-s-sighting-at-savannah-ri: Lou Elizondo, a guest on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, passes on the story of James McDonald, a well-known physicist who he thinks was at Arizona State. Elizondo believes McDonald saw a UFO at the Savannah River site, though he isn't sure. Michels tells it with more certainty: he says McDonald saw a UFO at the Savannah River nuclear facility in South Carolina and was then publicly mocked for it. They tell it to show that a serious scientist saw something over a nuclear site and was pushed to the margins for saying so.
james-mcdonnell-s-search-for-gremlins-in: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that James McDonnell, linked to the aircraft maker McDonnell Douglas, spoke of "gremlins" in his planes. According to Michels, he spent much of his research career looking for these ghosts in the machine, which hints that something strange was seen around aircraft.
james-randi-s-million-dollar-paranormal-: James Randi was a well-known skeptic who ran a challenge offering money to anyone who could prove a paranormal power under test conditions. A magician and researcher named Chris Ramsay told podcast host Jesse Michels that at first Randi offered 10,000 dollars on a show for such proof, and the prize later grew to a million. Ramsay brings it up while questioning how fair the challenge really was.
james-randi-s-spoon-and-watch-trick-in-f: Clas Svahn, a researcher, says a performer named James Randi once bent a spoon right in front of him and also did a trick with a watch. Svahn tells it to show how convincing such a trick can look up close.
jan-rooney-s-general-father-on-roswell-a: James Fox, a UFO investigator and filmmaker, says that Jan Rooney, wife of the actor Mickey Rooney, told him her father was a general at Roswell, New Mexico, in 1947, the place and year of a famous reported crash of a flying saucer. According to Fox, her father told her that if the truth about Roswell came out, it would have a devastating impact on organized religion, which would mean something non-human was found there.
janet-airlines-first-heard-of-through-la: A researcher who goes by UAPGerb says that the public first heard of "Janet Airlines", the name given to a set of quiet flights in Nevada, through Bob Lazar, a man famous in UFO circles for his claims from around 1989. UAPGerb puts it simply: "where did we first hear about Janet Airlines? Bob Lazar." The point is that, if so, Lazar knew about things the public did not.
janet-flights-from-mccarran-to-area-51-1: Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked on secret projects in Nevada, told podcast host Jesse Michels how he got to work in 1988 and 1989. He says he drove to the special projects office of EG&G, a defence contractor, at McCarran Airport in Las Vegas, and from there took the unmarked flights, known as Janet flights, that carry workers to Area 51, a secret Air Force base in the desert. If true, it would back up his claim that he really worked inside the secret site.
jannini-asks-the-court-to-let-them-exhum: Varginha is a town in Brazil, and a man named Ahmed Foratu, interviewed on a podcast about a hospital that is said to have operated on an alien, says a doctor named Janini is now, about 30 years later, asking a court for permission to dig up the body of a person named Chereze. According to Foratu, the aim is to study bacteria in the remains, which, if the story holds, could show what Chereze was exposed to.
jannini-in-the-film-a-puncture-from-the-: In 1996 in Varginha, Brazil, people reported a strange being, and a man named Marco Chereze later died. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in Moment of Contact, a documentary by the filmmaker James Fox, a doctor named Jannini says he thinks a puncture wound from the nail of the extraterrestrial caused Chereze's death. If true, it would mean a living non-human being was physically handled by people in Brazil.
jannini-s-signed-authenticated-statement: Ahmed Foratu, a witness speaking on a podcast about a hospital where an alien was said to be operated on, says that a doctor named Jannini sent a signed, authenticated statement. Foratu says he has already handed that signed statement to the host, Jesse Michels, in 2026. It is offered as written backing from a doctor for the story being told.
jannini-told-fox-on-camera-he-had-never-: James Fox, a documentary filmmaker investigating the 1996 creature case in Varginha, Brazil, says a doctor named Jannini told him on camera that he had never seen a bacteria like the one in the case, before or since. In a later telling Fox describes it as an advanced strain that behaved in a way the doctor had never seen, and also credits a second doctor, Cesario. If true, it would point to an infection unlike anything known.
january-whistle-event-gets-zero-results-: Skywatcher is a small company that says it tries to call up UFOs, which officials now call UAP, short for unidentified anomalous phenomena. On a podcast with host Jesse Michels in 2025, the group said that in January it held a field session with all its equipment but without something it calls the "whistle," and got nothing at all. In February, they say, they added the whistle and psionics, meaning efforts to reach the objects with the mind, and saw their first UAP with the naked eye, which would suggest these things can be called on purpose.
japan-airlines-pilot-s-45-minute-encount: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in 1986, over Alaska, a Japan Airlines pilot flew alongside something unknown for 45 minutes, and that the radar record was taken by the White House but is now public and has been studied by physicists. A researcher, Kevin Knuth, tells it as Japan Airlines flight 1628, a cargo flight flown by Captain Kenju Teruchi, who saw a giant craft, without the 45 minutes or the White House detail. If true, it would be a long sighting by a trained pilot backed up by radar.
japan-seeing-uap-over-the-last-five-year: Dylan Borland, talking with podcast host Jesse Michels, says Japan seems to have been seeing a lot of UAP, unidentified anomalous phenomena, the official term for UFOs, over the last five years or so. In his words, Japan is "popping off." If true, it would mean the sightings are not only an American matter.
japan-sought-a-uap-information-sharing-a: Lue Elizondo, a former Pentagon official who worked on unexplained aerial reports, says that Japan begged the United States for a two-country agreement whose only purpose would be to share information on UAP, the government's term for UFOs. He tells this on podcast host Jesse Michels' show, and if true it would mean other governments take the subject seriously enough to seek formal deals about it.
japanese-hitodama-soul-orbs: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, talking with a parapsychology researcher named Jeffrey Mishlove, brings up hitodama, a Japanese idea of glowing orbs tied to the souls of the dead, which Michels describes as plasma orbs. He points to the film The Boy and the Heron by the Japanese animator Hayao Miyazaki, linking these old folk ideas to the glowing orbs people report today.
japanese-museum-curator-shown-ufo-footag: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells of a Japanese museum curator, Takano Jouen, who said he visited NASA's Johnson Space Center in Houston, home of the space agency's mission control. According to Michels, Takano said he was taken to a particular building and shown photos of UFOs, which would mean NASA keeps such images out of public view.
japanese-museum-s-claimed-piece-of-the-r: Roswell refers to 1947 in New Mexico, when many people say a craft that was not human crashed and the US military recovered it. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says a man in Japan named Takeno Jouen, who runs a museum, claims to own a piece of that crash. If that were so, it would be physical proof from one of the most famous UFO stories.
japanese-musha-experiment-in-transmissio: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, describes a paper by a Japanese researcher named Takaaki Musha about an experiment in Japan. As Michels tells it, the researchers submerged the whole device in transmission oil, the thick oil used in car gearboxes, and reported a successful result. He raises it because, if it held up, it would suggest the unusual physics he discusses is real and can be tested.
jared-birchall-a-mormon-elder-as-elon-mu: A commentator named Matthew Pines says that Jared Birchall, described as a Mormon church elder, is basically the "handler" of the billionaire Elon Musk, the man who manages all of his affairs. Pines raises it as a connection worth noticing, since it would mean someone with ties of his own sits close to one of the world's most powerful businessmen.
jason-sands-radars-at-roswell-and-white-: Roswell is a town in New Mexico where many people say a craft crashed in 1947, and White Sands is a nearby military test range. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, passes on what a man named Jason Sands said: that powerful radars at Roswell and White Sands were knocking unknown craft off their flight paths. A commentator who goes by UAPGerb goes further. He says the radar actually caused crashes, that bodies were recovered, and that this was a problem Presidents Harry Truman and Dwight Eisenhower had to face, though he names no bases. If true, it would mean early American radar brought down craft that were not built by people.
jason-sands-they-want-their-stuff-back: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, repeats a claim from a man named Jason Sands, in connection with the podcast host Joe Rogan, about whoever owns material held in a secret program. As Michels tells it, they want their stuff back and will kill everybody involved in the program if they don't get it, which, if true, would mean those keeping it are in danger.
javanese-cemetery-marriage-and-sex-ritua: Peter Levenda, a writer on secret and occult history, says that some cemeteries on the Indonesian island of Java hold a ritual of marriage and sex at the grave of a prince. He says he visited one of these cemeteries himself. He told the story on a podcast with host Jesse Michels as an example of living rituals that reach toward unseen powers.
jay-stratton-s-three-star-slide-shown-to: A well-known UFO skeptic, Mick West, says that Jay Stratton, a government official who worked on the military's study of unexplained sightings, took a slide showing three stars and presented it to people in the US Congress, around 2019 to 2021. West tells it to suggest that what lawmakers were shown as something mysterious may have been ordinary stars.
jc-said-navy-running-majestic-12-was-rig: Bryce Zable, speaking on a podcast about Hollywood and UFOs, says that in 1996 in Los Angeles a man he calls JC told him what his team's fictional work got right. One thing, Zable says, was making the man in charge of Majestic 12, a claimed secret group said to handle UFO matters, an officer from the Navy. If true, it would mean the fiction came close to a real secret.
jean-louis-naudin-s-vacuum-tube-tests: Gary McKinnon, a computer hacker who says he found signs of a secret space program in NASA's systems, told podcast host Jesse Michels about an experimenter in France named Jean-Louis Naudin. McKinnon says Naudin has repeated his experiments inside vacuum tubes, sealed glass tubes with the air pumped out. He mentions it because a result that holds up in a vacuum would rule out air as the cause.
jeffrey-epstein-tape-with-steve-bannon-a: Eric Weinstein, a mathematician and commentator, talks about a taped interview between Jeffrey Epstein, a financier, and Steve Bannon, a political strategist. Weinstein says Epstein got things wrong, for example claiming he founded the Santa Fe Institute, a research centre, in 1990 to 93 when others founded it in 1984, and making a mistake about quarks and the physicist Murray Gell-Mann. Even so, Weinstein says you can tell Epstein had been talking to people who really knew what they were talking about, so the tape reads to him as a garbled echo of informed people.

jorjani-invited-to-join-the-knights-of-m: A researcher named Jason Jorjani, speaking on the podcast of host Jesse Michels in 2025, mentions in passing that he was once invited to join the Knights of Malta, a centuries-old Catholic order of knights, through an initiation in Malta. joseph-mcmoneagle-awarded-the-legion-of-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Joseph McMoneagle, a man who worked as a remote viewer for the US government, meaning someone trained to describe distant places or things using only the mind, won the Legion of Merit, a US military award. joseph-mcmoneagle-given-legion-of-merit-: Podcast host Jesse Michels says that Joseph McMoneagle, a man he once interviewed, was given the Legion of Merit, a US military award, for his work in remote viewing, the claimed ability to describe faraway places using only the mind. joseph-mcmoneagle-s-remote-viewing-of-so: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Joseph McMoneagle, a remote viewer working for the US government in the 1970s and 80s, used remote viewing, the claimed ability to sense distant places with the mind alone, to identify Soviet nuclear bases and predict key events. joseph-of-arimathea-brings-the-grail-to-: Randall Carlson, a researcher of ancient history, retells an old legend on Jesse Michels's podcast. joseph-of-copertino-levitating-during-ma: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells of Joseph of Copertino, a Franciscan friar in 17th-century Italy who, he says, had ecstatic visions as a child. joseph-of-copertino-s-levitation-records: A professor of religious studies, Diana Pasulka, says she has the records of Joseph of Copertino, a 17th-century Italian friar said to float in the air, and has been reading them. joseph-smith-possibly-killed-by-governme: Matthew Pines, a researcher, says on Jesse Michels's podcast that Joseph Smith, the founder of the Mormon church, "may have been assassinated by agents of the government" in the 1840s. josiah-describes-author-max-davis-s-popp: In a documentary called the Telepathy Tapes, about children said to read minds, the mother of a boy named Josiah tells how Josiah described the house of an author, Max Davis, as a house that makes popping sounds, with a barn nearby. josiah-knows-about-max-s-mixtape-and-pri: A documentary filmmaker, Ky Dickens, who has made a film about nonspeaking young people said to read minds, tells of one of them, Josiah. josiah-knows-about-max-s-nap-and-the-fir: A filmmaker named Ky Dickens, who made a documentary called The Telepathy Tapes about nonspeaking children said to read minds, tells a story about a boy named Josiah and a man named Max Davis. josiah-knows-max-went-into-the-woods-to-: A documentary filmmaker, Ky Dickens, tells of Josiah, a nonspeaking young man in her film about telepathy. josiah-says-auntie-told-an-angel-to-tell: The mother of a boy named Josiah says that when he was about 7 or 8, he told her that "Auntie" had told an angel to tell him something. journalist-threatened-with-arrest-at-the: A Brazilian journalist, unnamed in the telling, says that in 1996 he was investigating the Varginha case, a story from Brazil in which people say the army captured a living non-human creature, at the army's sergeants' school in the town of Três Corações. journalists-on-cia-payroll-operation-moc: Jeremy Corbell, a guest on podcast host Jesse Michels's show, says he has heard that many American journalists in the 1960s were secretly paid by the CIA, the US foreign intelligence agency. jp-cahn-s-10-000-offer-to-scully-1950: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells how around 1950 in San Francisco, a man named J.P. jp-morgan-funds-tesla-s-wardenclyffe-wir: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in the early 1900s the inventor Nikola Tesla got money from the banker J.P. jpl-counter-clerk-hands-over-negatives-o: Joe McMoneagle, a man who wrote a book called Mind Trek, says that in the 1980s he went to the Jet Propulsion Laboratory, the NASA center in California that runs space probes, and asked for photo negatives from its mapping of Mars. jpl-manager-life-on-mars-means-death-for: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, relays a story he credits to the author Whitley Strieber about the Jet Propulsion Laboratory, NASA's space mission center in Pasadena, California. jpl-viking-mission-lead-believed-there-w: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says he has heard that the person at the Jet Propulsion Laboratory, NASA's spacecraft lab, who led the Viking missions, the 1970s probes sent to land on Mars, firmly believes there was evidence of life on Mars. jsoc-crash-retrievals-and-knights-of-mal: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, ties the Joint Special Operations Command, the US military's top command for its elite special forces, to the recovery of crashed craft. jude-quotes-the-book-of-enoch: A filmmaker and researcher named Tim Alberino says that the Epistle of Jude, a short letter in the New Testament of the Bible, copies word for word from the Book of Enoch, an ancient religious text left out of most Bibles. julian-jaynes-bicameral-mind-theory-a-sh: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, brings up Julian Jaynes, whom he describes as a Yale professor who wrote a book called The Origin of Consciousness in the Breakdown of the Bicameral Mind. julius-evola-stayed-with-the-ss-to-the-e: Peter Levenda, a writer on the occult and secret history, says on Jesse Michels's podcast that Julius Evola, an Italian writer on mystical traditions, stayed with the SS, Nazi Germany's elite force, until the end of the Second World War. junior-hicks-files-on-uinta-basin-ufo-si: Brandon Fugal, the owner of Skinwalker Ranch, a property in Utah known for reports of strange happenings, talks about a local man named Junior Hicks. kabbalists-meet-the-dalai-lama: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, recalls a story of Jewish Kabbalists, people who study an old Jewish mystical tradition, meeting with the Dalai Lama, the leader of Tibetan Buddhism. kafka-s-trial-as-a-description-of-a-spec: A researcher named Jason Jorjani tells podcast host Jesse Michels about an essay he wrote, collected in his book Lovers of Sophia, that reads The Trial, a novel by the Prague writer Franz Kafka, together with Kafka's private notebooks. kafsokalyvia-skete-maximus-the-flying-mo: A man named Ralph says that in 2005 he visited Kafsokalyvia, a small monks' settlement on Mount Athos, a Greek peninsula of Orthodox monasteries. kaikoura-ufo-incident-1978: Ross Coulthart, a journalist from New Zealand's region, says on Jesse Michels's podcast that a "really big UFO incident" happened in 1978, when he was 16, near Kaikoura on the east coast of New Zealand's South Island. kakino-stone-circle-with-magnetic-anomal: A researcher of ancient sites named Geoffrey Drumm, speaking on Jesse Michels' podcast, describes a stone circle on a steep hillside at a place called Kakino in Japan. kalmykian-president-s-debrief-with-kissi: Podcast host Jesse Michels relays a story about the president of Kalmykia, a region of Russia, in the 1990s. kammler-black-world-program-in-nazi-germ: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, mentions rumors that in Nazi Germany in the 1940s an official named Hans Kammler ran secret, off-the-books nuclear work, what he calls black-world projects. kammler-negotiating-with-the-western-all: An aviation journalist named Nick Cook, speaking on Jesse Michels' podcast, talks about Hans Kammler, a senior Nazi SS officer in charge of Germany's secret weapons projects. kammler-s-flying-saucer-work-and-die-glo: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that at a site in what was then Czechoslovakia, in today's Poland, Hans Kammler, whom he calls the most ruthless Nazi and the one running the most secret technology projects, was rumored to be working on flying saucers. kant-suppressed-swedenborg-s-disturbing-: Jason Jorjani, a philosopher, tells a story about two thinkers of the 1700s: Immanuel Kant, the German philosopher from Königsberg in Prussia, and Emanuel Swedenborg, a mystic who wrote about visions of other worlds and spirits in books such as Secrets of Heaven. kardashev-scale-1964: Karl Nell, a researcher, explains on Jesse Michels's podcast an idea from Nikolai Kardashev, a Russian astronomer. karl-maria-wiligut-himmler-s-ss-seer-of-: A researcher and author, Peter Levenda, speaking on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, tells of a man named Karl Maria Wiligut who advised Heinrich Himmler, head of the Nazi SS, in 1930s Germany. karl-nell-on-a-reverse-engineering-arms-: Karl Nell is a retired US Army colonel who, according to a podcast host, Jesse Michels, helped set up Army Futures Command, a part of the Army focused on new technology. karla-turner-allegedly-killed-by-a-cia-c: A writer named Jason Jorjani, speaking on Jesse Michels' podcast, talks about Karla Turner, an American author who wrote about alien abductions in the 1990s. karst-cave-and-tunnel-system-venting-hyd: This story is about what lies under the Giza Plateau in Egypt, where the great pyramids stand. keeping-the-beings-out-of-the-official-r: Mario Woods, who guarded nuclear weapons at Ellsworth, an Air Force base in South Dakota, tells podcast host Jesse Michels that in 1977 he left the beings he says he saw out of his official report. kelly-johnson-s-ufo-sighting: Kelly Johnson was a famous American aircraft designer who ran Skunk Works, the secret design shop of the company Lockheed. ken-farley-s-description-of-the-craft-s-: A researcher named Scott Ramsay, who studies a reported 1948 crash of a flying saucer in Hart Canyon near Aztec, New Mexico, relays what a man named Ken Farley told about the craft. ken-farley-struck-with-a-rifle-butt-1948: A researcher named Scott Ramsay, who studies a reported flying saucer crash in March 1948 near Aztec, New Mexico, says that a man named Ken Farley was hit in the gut with the butt of a gun for talking about what he saw. ken-johnston-told-to-destroy-anomalous-a: A guest on a podcast, Maaneli Derakhshani, says that a man named Ken Johnston, who worked with NASA, the US space agency, was told to destroy early copies of photo negatives from Apollo, NASA's crewed missions to the Moon in the 1960s and 70s. ken-shoulders-ceramic-puncture-experimen: A guest named Dave Rossi, speaking on Jesse Michels' podcast, describes an experiment by an electrical researcher named Ken Shoulders. kennedy-delegation-tours-western-nuclear: A former US Senate staffer named Kirk McConnell, speaking on Jesse Michels' podcast, tells of a trip after the Cuban missile crisis of 1962, the standoff with the Soviet Union over nuclear missiles in Cuba. McConnell says President John F. Kennedy led a delegation to Los Alamos, a nuclear weapons laboratory in New Mexico, and other nuclear sites in the western United States, and that a researcher named Jeff Cruikshank has listed who went: Kennedy, Vice President Lyndon Johnson, the national security adviser McGeorge Bundy, and the Air Force general Curtis LeMay. McConnell raises it as a trip whose full purpose, if he is right, may have gone beyond what was publicly said.
kennedy-proposes-a-joint-soviet-us-space: A researcher, Dan Sheehan, says on Jesse Michels's podcast that in 1963 President John F. Kennedy proposed to Nikita Khrushchev, the Soviet leader, that the two countries run a joint Soviet and American space program. Sheehan tells it as part of his larger account of Kennedy and what he knew about UFOs.
kennedy-s-orange-bowl-promise-to-cuban-e: A researcher, Dan Sheehan, tells on Jesse Michels's podcast how President John F. Kennedy went to the Orange Bowl, a football stadium in Miami, around 1962 and convened a large meeting there with Cuban exiles. Sheehan describes it as a promise Kennedy made to the exiles, part of his wider story about Kennedy's last years.
kennedy-s-silver-certificates-on-june-5-: A researcher, Dan Sheehan, says on Jesse Michels's podcast that on June 5, 1963, President John F. Kennedy did something Sheehan calls weird: he moved to print silver certificates, a type of paper money backed by silver. Sheehan admits he has never quite figured out why, and mentions the filmmaker Oliver Stone in connection with the story.
kenneth-arnold-s-1947-craft-matched-hort: A researcher and author, Peter Levenda, says on Jesse Michels's podcast that the objects a pilot named Kenneth Arnold reported seeing in the sky over the United States in 1947 had the same design as aircraft built by the Horten brothers, German aircraft designers. Levenda notes that Arnold did not know this at the time, which would suggest, if true, that what he saw was connected to German wartime designs.
kenneth-arnold-s-paranormal-experiences-: Jeffrey Mishlove, a guest with a doctorate speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast, talks about Kenneth Arnold, a man who reported seeing unidentified flying objects in the United States in 1947. Mishlove says he believes Arnold's daughter has written a book about mysterious paranormal experiences her father had after that first sighting, which would suggest such encounters reach beyond the sighting itself.
kenneth-arnold-sighting-1947: This story is about a pilot named Kenneth Arnold and what he saw from his plane in 1947, which many see as one of the first modern UFO sightings. A whistleblower, David Grusch, says Arnold was searching for a crashed cargo plane near Mount Rainier, in Washington state, two months before the famous Roswell case, a reported crash in New Mexico. A writer billed as a CIA historian, Peter Levenda, says Arnold was flying a mission in the Pacific Northwest and the Rockies and saw a group of odd craft moving at impossible speeds. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, simply points to it as a classic example. If true, it would mean unknown craft were flying over America in 1947.
kent-selin-sees-flux-liner-over-edwards-: An online researcher who goes by UAPGerb says that a man named Mark McCandlish talked to a man named Kent Selin, who said he saw a particular kind of craft, called a flux liner, over Edwards Air Force Base in California in the 1970s. UAPGerb tells it because, if true, it would mean such an advanced craft was flying over a US military base decades ago.
kentucky-farm-case-behind-night-skies-an: A guest on Jesse Michels' podcast tells, in two episodes about the film director Steven Spielberg, of a case from Kentucky in the 1950s in which a farm family is said to have found an alien and hidden it in their barn. According to the guest, this story was the spark for Night Skies, a film Spielberg was developing as a producer around 1980, which in turn led to E.T., his famous movie about a child who hides a stranded alien. If true, it would mean one of Hollywood's best-loved films grew out of a real encounter story.
kevin-day-radar-objects-at-28-000-ft-mat: A guest named Merrick says on a podcast that Kevin Day, a Navy radar operator in the 2004 incident off Southern California in which Navy pilots chased strange flying objects, reported that those objects were at 28,000 feet. Merrick ties this to data from an infrared camera recording made by a pilot named Chad Underwood, saying the two match, which would mean the radar and the video back each other up.
keyhoe-air-force-tracked-two-unknown-sat: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, retells a claim from Donald Keyhoe, a writer who wrote about UFOs in the 1950s. According to Michels, Keyhoe stated that in 1953 the US Air Force was tracking two unknown artificial satellites circling the Earth, one about 400 miles up and the other about 600 miles up. If true, it would mean something made by no known country was orbiting the planet years before anyone had launched a satellite.
kgb-department-researching-unknown-flyin: Kiran Ilum Xenov, described as a former president of a republic within Russia, says that in Soviet times the KGB, the Soviet Union's security and intelligence service, had a special department that researched unknown flying objects and also unknown underwater objects. He ties the claim to Mikhail Gorbachev, the last Soviet leader, though his telling is vague about how. If true, it would mean the Soviet state studied these objects in secret, much as others claim the US did.
khafre-research-project-proposal-to-the-: Filippo Biondi is a researcher who says he has used scanning to look beneath the pyramids at Giza, in Egypt. On the podcast of host Jesse Michels in late 2025, he spoke of the Khafre Research Project, named after Khafre, one of the great Giza pyramids, and said it might become the center of the work. He names fellow researchers Armando Mei and Corrado Malanga, and the University of Ferrara, a university in Italy. Speaking again on the same show in March 2026, he says the team is still preparing a proposal to send to the Egyptian government. In that telling the focus is on clearing shafts under the pyramid that are filled with debris, and he says robots would do the cleaning. He adds that the proposal, involving the University of Ferrara, would go in within weeks. If it went ahead, he says, it could open up what lies below the pyramid. All the tellings come from Biondi himself, across two episodes, and they differ mainly on how far along the proposal is.
khafre-research-project-used-a-low-incid: Filippo Biondi, a scientist who uses satellite radar to scan beneath the pyramids, tells podcast host Jesse Michels about his project on Khafre, the second great pyramid at Giza in Egypt. He says that for this work his team used a low incidence angle, meaning the radar looked at the ground from a shallow slant. It is part of the method he says revealed structures deep under the pyramid, which, if real, would point to a hidden underground world at Giza.
khafre-substructure-tubes-about-20-m-wid: Filippo Biondi, a scientist who scans beneath the pyramids with radar, tells podcast host Jesse Michels that his scans under Khafre, the second great pyramid at Giza in Egypt, show huge tubes going down. He says they are roughly 20 meters wide and descend for more than a kilometer. If true, it would mean the pyramid sits on a vast built structure far below ground.
khufu-cartouche-allegedly-painted-by-vys: A researcher named Jay Anderson, talking on the podcast of host Jesse Michels, tells a story about the Great Pyramid of Giza in Egypt. He says an explorer in the 1800s, whose name he half remembers and whom the story names as Howard Vyse, was hired by the British Museum, was running out of money and time, and then suddenly found the name of Khufu, the ancient king usually credited with building the pyramid, written inside in what Anderson calls very suspicious ochre, a reddish earth paint. If that were so, one of the main written links between the pyramid and Khufu would be in doubt.
khufu-project-scan-shows-a-network-of-tu: Filippo Biondi, a scientist who scans beneath the pyramids with radar, tells podcast host Jesse Michels that his scan of Khufu, the Great Pyramid at Giza in Egypt, points to a network of tunnels underneath it. He hopes one day to go down a shaft and reach one of the horizontal tunnels. In a later interview he stresses that the rescan was not meant to repeat his 2020 work but to see what lay deep below Khufu. If true, it would mean a hidden tunnel system runs under the Great Pyramid.
killeen-base-emergency-meeting-1949: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says declassified documents show that in 1949, after several sightings over Killeen Base at Camp Hood, an army post in Texas that he says held America's largest nuclear weapons stockpile at the time, an emergency meeting was called. In a later episode he credits the story to researcher Robert Hastings' book UFOs and Nukes and is less sure of the year. If true, it would mean unknown objects were taking an interest in American nuclear weapons from early on.
killing-of-caltech-astronomer-carl-grill: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, in an episode about American scientists going missing, tells of the death of Carl Grillmair, an astronomer linked to Caltech, a university in California, and JPL, NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory. Michels says that on February 16, 2026, in Llano in California's Antelope Valley, about 30 miles from Waterman Mountain, where another Caltech and JPL colleague named Monica Resza had disappeared, Grillmair met what he calls an equally tragic and suspicious end. He tells it as part of a possible pattern of harm coming to scientists from the same circles.
killing-of-thule-society-members-april-1: A researcher and author, Peter Levenda, tells on Jesse Michels's podcast of the killing of members of the Thule Society, a secretive German group, in Munich on April 30, 1919. Levenda brings it up as part of his account of the strange roots of later Nazi beliefs.
kim-peek-s-brain-anatomy-and-his-recall-: A researcher named Diane Powell, speaking on podcast host Jesse Michels's show in an episode about children said to read minds, talks about Kim Peek, an American man said to remember some 12,000 books. Powell says many people thought he was autistic, but that he was actually born with a defect in how his body handled cerebrospinal fluid, the liquid that cushions the brain and spine. She raises it as an example of how an unusual brain might go with unusual mental abilities.
king-charles-mountbatten-and-savile-s-bl: A guest on a podcast, Kurt Metzger, says that King Charles of Britain, Lord Mountbatten, a senior figure in the British royal circle, and Jimmy Savile, a British television presenter, used to hang out together in the 1970s and 80s and all had special black berets made. He tells it in an episode about a supposed secret elite network, as a sign that, if true, these men belonged to some private circle.
king-frederick-shelters-hermetic-thinker: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, talking with the philosopher Jason Jorjani, recalls a book by the historian Frances Yates called The Rosicrucian Enlightenment. Michels says it describes King Frederick, a ruler in Bohemia and the Palatinate in central Europe in the early 1600s, sheltering mystical and heretical thinkers such as John Dee, Edward Kelley and possibly Giordano Bruno, and that in the war that followed the philosopher René Descartes fought on the other side, which casts the birth of modern thought as a clash with these older mystical traditions.
kingman-1953-crash-arthur-stansel-sees-s: A researcher who goes by UAPGerb tells on Jesse Michels's podcast of a reported crash of an unknown craft near Kingman, Arizona, in 1953. According to UAPGerb, a man named Arthur Stansel was sent to the site to work out the object's flight path, and inside a makeshift tent he saw a tiny brownish being, possibly charred and mangled. kingman-craft-held-by-lockheed-in-a-ware: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells of a craft said to have come down near Kingman, Arizona, and now kept in a warehouse by Lockheed, a large American aerospace and defense company. He describes it as a beautiful thing with no seams and no rivets. If true, it would mean a private company holds a craft that no one on Earth built.
kingman-crash-survivor-went-to-the-back-: Charles Hall, a man who says he spent three years with tall white aliens at Area 51, a secret US military test site in Nevada, relays what a sheriff from Kingman, Arizona told him about a craft that crashed there. According to Hall, the sheriff said a female survivor of the crash went back inside the craft and stayed in the back. If true, it would mean a living being came out of a crash in Arizona.
kingman-crash-was-the-one-they-walked-aw: A UFO researcher named Grant Cameron, speaking on podcast host Jesse Michels's show, says a woman he knows was at a conference called SOL, sitting near one of the event's main people, when a crash said to have happened near Kingman, Arizona came up in connection with a film by James Fox. According to Cameron, the man said: "That's not right. That was that crash. That's the one they walked away from." If true, it would mean the beings aboard a crashed craft survived and left on their own.
kirk-mcconnell-and-extended-electrodynam: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, speaks of a man named Kirk McConnell, who he says worked for the Senate Armed Services Committee, the group of US senators that oversees the military, under Senator Jack Reid of Rhode Island. Michels says McConnell knows all about extended electrodynamics, a proposed broader version of the physics of electricity and magnetism. The point is that someone close to military oversight in Congress would understand the kind of physics that might explain how such craft move.
kirk-mcconnell-confirms-blue-on-blue-fir: An online researcher who goes by UAPGerb, speaking on podcast host Jesse Michels's show, tells about Kirk McConnell, a staff member of the Senate Armed Services Committee, the US Senate panel that oversees the military. According to UAPGerb, at a conference called SOL, people asked McConnell whether he had heard of a "blue-on-blue" firefight, meaning American teams fighting each other, and of humans being carried in "reverse-engineered craft", vehicles built by copying recovered non-human technology, and he said he had heard of both. If true, it would mean a congressional insider had heard of secret craft programmes being real enough to fight over.
kirkpatrick-dodged-a-meeting-with-borlan: Dylan Borland, who says a top government official told him aliens run everything, tells podcast host Jesse Michels that in 2023 he was sent to talk with Sean Kirkpatrick at AARO, a Pentagon office that looks into unexplained objects in the sky. Borland says Kirkpatrick ducked the meeting. If true, it would mean the office meant to investigate such claims avoided hearing his.
kirkpatrick-leaves-aaro-for-oak-ridge-20: This is about Sean Kirkpatrick, the first head of AARO, a Pentagon office set up to look into unidentified flying objects, which the government calls UAP. According to an online researcher who goes by UAPGerb, when Kirkpatrick left AARO he went to Oak Ridge National Laboratory, a US government research lab in Tennessee. UAPGerb urges people to look at Oak Ridge's links to FFRDCs, which are research centres paid for by the government but run by outside organisations. He says that after Kirkpatrick retired from government, he went to work with and for Oak Ridge under contract. To those who tell it, this hints that the official UFO office and the big government labs are closely tied.
kirkpatrick-lobbied-against-the-uap-disc: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Sean Kirkpatrick, who once led a Pentagon office set up to look into UAP (unidentified anomalous phenomena, the government's term for UFOs), lobbied against the UAP Disclosure Act around 2023 and 2024. That act is a proposed law meant to make the government release its UFO records. Michels says he hopes Kirkpatrick won't do it again when it next comes to a vote, since in his telling it would mean an official worked to keep the records closed.
kirkpatrick-metallic-orbs-worldwide-said: A guest named Merrick, on podcast host Jesse Michels' show, quotes Sean Kirkpatrick, the former head of AARO, the Pentagon's office for investigating unexplained aerial reports. According to Merrick, Kirkpatrick said at a 2023 NASA panel on these sightings that they were seeing metallic orbs making very interesting apparent maneuvers all over the world. If true, it would mean the government's own investigator saw something unexplained happening worldwide.
kirkpatrick-s-aaro-denied-the-herrera-in: A man named Jake Barber, who says he once flew a helicopter to retrieve a UFO, says that Sean Kirkpatrick, the head of AARO (a Pentagon office set up to look into unexplained flying objects), publicly denied an incident described by a witness named Michael Herrera. If true, the official denial and the private admission would contradict each other.
kirkpatrick-tells-gillibrand-s-committee: A researcher who studies UFOs around nuclear bases, Robert Hastings, says on Jesse Michels's podcast that in April 2023 Sean Kirkpatrick, then head of the Pentagon's UFO study office, told a Senate committee led by Senator Kirsten Gillibrand that there was no evidence of extraterrestrial craft. Hastings describes it as the culmination of a long pattern of official denial.
kirtland-security-meeting-with-benowitz-: A writer named Greg Bishop says a man named Tom Deuley told him about a security meeting around 1980 at Kirtland Air Force Base in New Mexico, held about things reported by a man named Paul Benowitz. According to Deuley, people kept leaving as the meeting went on, saying "that's not ours," until only three or four were left. Bishop tells it because, if true, it would mean the officials could not claim what was being seen as any of their own projects.
kissinger-among-the-first-cic-officers-i: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, in an episode asking whether the American statesman Henry Kissinger oversaw a programme to recover crashed UFOs, says Kissinger was one of the first officers to move into the barracks at Oberammergau, a town in Bavaria, Germany, in 1945. kissinger-consults-for-the-psychological: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that the American statesman Henry Kissinger worked in Washington as a consultant in 1951, 1952 and again in 1955 for the Psychological Strategy Board, a government body that planned Cold War psychological operations, and for its successor, the Operations Coordinating Board. kissinger-directs-the-cfr-study-group-on: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in 1955 Henry Kissinger, the American statesman, was invited to direct a study group on nuclear war and foreign policy at the Council on Foreign Relations, a foreign policy organisation in New York. kissinger-dobrynin-transcript-on-microwa: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, points to a recently declassified transcript from the 1970s talks between the US and the Soviet Union on limiting nuclear arms and easing tensions. kissinger-in-army-counterintelligence-te: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in the 1940s in Europe the American statesman Henry Kissinger was an Army counterintelligence officer doing what Michels calls tech retrieval, meaning collecting technology. He tells it to suggest Kissinger had early experience recovering advanced hardware, the kind of background that would fit a later role with crashed UFOs.
kissinger-involved-in-ufo-matters: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says in a conversation about Joe Rogan that he has uncovered a lot suggesting that Henry Kissinger, the American statesman and former Secretary of State, was involved in UFO matters. He gives no further detail there, but if true it would put UFO secrets in the hands of the highest levels of American policy.
kissinger-letter-to-nixon-on-prisoners-p: Joe McMoneagle, a man who took part in US government psychic spying work, says he saw a letter from Henry Kissinger, President Nixon's top foreign policy adviser, to President Richard Nixon in the early 1970s. kissinger-on-the-303-committee-overseein: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, describes the 303 Committee as a secret group of US government agencies that oversaw all covert operations in the 1960s and 70s, and says the American statesman Henry Kissinger was involved with it. kissinger-s-1977-moon-dust-telegram-to-o: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in January 1977, just before leaving office, Henry Kissinger, the American statesman, sent a telegram to the US embassy in Ottawa, Canada, asking for a report on "possible returned space objects." Michels notes that its subject line was Moon Dust, the name of a US effort to recover objects that fell from space. He tells it because, if it means what he thinks, it ties Kissinger to the recovery of fallen craft.
kissinger-s-harvard-career-as-cover-for-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, puts forward the idea that the American statesman Henry Kissinger's career as a professor at Harvard in the 1950s was merely a cover. According to this idea, his real work was advising MJ12, or Majestic 12, a supposed secret group said to manage UFO matters, through a specialised think tank called PI40. kissinger-studied-under-thomas-schelling: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, mentions that the American statesman Henry Kissinger studied at Harvard under Thomas Schelling, a scholar of strategy. Michels raises the connection as part of a story about Schelling later trying some kind of intervention with Kissinger, though the telling leaves the details vague.
kissner-tells-steven-schiff-who-launches: A researcher who goes by UAPGerb says on a podcast that in 1995 a New Mexico state lawmaker, J. Andrew Kissner, reportedly told another New Mexico lawmaker, Steven Schiff, about something to do with Roswell, the New Mexico town long tied to stories of a crashed craft. kit-green-and-eric-walker-both-tied-to-g: A long-time UFO researcher named Grant Cameron, speaking on podcast host Jesse Michels's show, says that a scientist named Kit Green and a man named Eric Walker were both involved in the Glomar Explorer, a ship built in the 1970s for a secret US government operation at sea. Cameron says that when Green saw Walker's biography, he told the UFO researcher Jacques Vallee, "have you seen this guy's bio, this guy is unbelievable." The point of telling it is that the same few people seem to turn up across secret projects and the UFO question.
kit-green-and-garry-nolan-study-biologic: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that two scientists, Kit Green, whom he links to the CIA, and Garry Nolan, have been looking at the biological effects on people who say they witnessed or encountered UFOs. He mentions damage from electromagnetic radiation as one such effect, and calls it CIA spooky stuff. If true, it would mean these encounters leave physical marks on the body that can be studied.
kit-green-could-not-get-read-into-the-au: A UFO researcher named Grant Cameron says he heard that Kit Green, a scientist connected to the CIA, had been "read in," meaning given secret access, to most of a hidden UFO program in the 2000s. But according to Cameron's story, Green could not get access to one part: the program examining bodies, which he calls the autopsy part. If true, it would mean a secret program existed with layers walled off even from insiders.
kit-green-kicked-out-of-eric-walker-s-of: This story is about a man named Kit Green and his visit to Eric Walker, described as a former president of Penn State, a university in the United States. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, mentions a run-in between the two. A researcher, Grant Cameron, gives more detail, drawing on the published diaries of the author Jacques Vallee, called Forbidden Science. According to Cameron, this happened in the 1980s, and when Green asked about secret UFO matters, Walker blew up and started yelling. Cameron says Walker shouted that he did not have to tell him anything, and Green was thrown out. The story matters because Walker is said by others to have known about a secret UFO group, and his anger is read as a sign there was something to hide.
kit-green-knew-ransone-but-refuses-to-ta: An unnamed researcher on Jesse Michels's podcast says that a man named Kit Green knew a woman named Valerie Ransone very well in the late 1970s and early 1980s.
