The episode is about a CIA scientist said to have contacted an alien council, so Green's silence would matter if he holds part of that story.
kit-green-ran-the-cia-s-weird-desk: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Kit Green, a scientist tied to the CIA, the US foreign intelligence agency, ran what Michels calls the CIA's weird desk for a long time. By that he means the part of the agency that dealt with strange subjects, which would make Green an insider on unexplained matters.
kit-green-s-cia-files-on-ufo-related-inj: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Kit Green, a scientist who worked for the CIA, held files on the bodily effects people suffered after close encounters with UFOs. According to Michels, those files were handed to another scientist, Garry Nolan, sometime in the mid-2010s. If true, it would mean the US spy agency had been quietly tracking injuries from such encounters.
klaus-fuchs-atomic-espionage-1941: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, brings up Klaus Fuchs, whom he describes as the man who stole American atomic bomb secrets, and says Fuchs worked at Los Alamos, the New Mexico laboratory where the bomb was built, from 1941 to 1950. Michels uses him as a comparison, wondering who might be the next Klaus Fuchs, someone leaking secret advanced science.
klippenstein-admits-dod-and-ic-tipped-hi: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Ken Klippenstein, a journalist, admitted on Breaking Points, a news show hosted by Saagar Enjeti and Krystal Ball, that the Department of Defense and the intelligence community had tipped him off about a story. The story concerned David Grusch, a former intelligence officer who in 2023 came forward and testified under oath about secret UFO programmes. Michels tells it to suggest that the military and spy agencies were themselves steering coverage of Grusch.
knapp-and-corbell-broke-the-fravor-tic-t: A filmmaker named Jeremy Corbell says that he and a journalist, George Knapp, were the first to tell the story of Commander David Fravor, a Navy fighter pilot who reported chasing the Tic Tac, a white oval object shaped like the mint. Corbell says they did it quietly on the radio twice, before a 2017 New York Times article made the story famous. He tells it to claim credit for breaking one of the best-known modern UFO accounts.
knapp-puts-lazar-on-air-and-it-goes-vira: UFO researcher Grant Cameron, speaking on podcast host Jesse Michels's show, tells how in 1989 in Las Vegas the TV reporter George Knapp phoned John Lear, a pilot with a strong interest in UFOs, and said he was missing a guest for that night's show. According to Cameron, that is how Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked on alien craft at a secret site in the Nevada desert, ended up on air, and his story spread widely from there.
knew-bigelow-at-the-rockefeller-ranch-19: Steven Greer, a man who campaigns for the government to release what it knows about UFOs, says he knew a man named Robert Bigelow in 1993. According to Greer, they met at the JY Ranch in Teton County, Wyoming, which belonged to Laurance Rockefeller, a member of the wealthy Rockefeller family. He tells it to show that he was among the private figures interested in the subject early on.
knuth-sees-something-fall-into-the-sea-t: Kevin Knuth, a scientist who has studied UFO reports, says that in 2021, off Laguna Beach in California, he was watching the sky with night-vision goggles that see heat. He says he actually saw something fall and hit the water. If true, it would be a scientist seeing with his own eyes an object go into the sea.
kobitz-shown-an-atomically-bonded-bulkhe: A journalist, Ross Coulthart, says that a man named Nat Kobitz told him he was taken, under heavy guard, into an underground room at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base in Ohio. There, Kobitz said, he was shown a piece of a bulkhead, a wall section from a craft, whose material appeared to be bonded at the atomic level, which if true would point to technology no one on Earth is known to make.
kobitz-us-recovered-multiple-craft-inclu: A journalist, Ross Coulthart, says that a man named Nat Kobitz told him he had been told the United States recovered more than one crashed craft in the 1940s and 50s. According to Coulthart, these included craft from Roswell in New Mexico, Aztec, and Kingman in Arizona, places long named in crash stories, which would mean the government has held several non-human vehicles for decades.
kohler-refuses-to-name-his-sources-1950: George Kohler, who in 1950 spoke on KMYR, a radio station in Denver, Colorado, about a story of crashed alien bodies, is heard refusing to name where he got it. He says the information was told to him as a story, but the names of his sources were given to him in confidence. If true, it would mean people in the know passed him the account privately and wanted to stay hidden.
kohler-secretly-records-the-osi-intervie: A researcher named Scott Ramsay says that in 1950 a man named George Kohler was questioned by agents of the OSI, the US Air Force's Office of Special Investigations, at the KMYR radio station in Denver, Colorado. According to Ramsay, as they walked into the recording room Kohler quietly told the technician, "Record this," so the interview was secretly taped. Ramsay tells it because, if true, that recording would be a rare record of how officials handled early saucer stories.
kona-blue: Kona Blue is described as a secret US government project about UAP, which stands for unidentified anomalous phenomena, the government's newer name for UFOs. Jesse Michels, a podcast host, mentions it on one episode as a program that was released, he thinks, by accident. A researcher who goes by the online name UAPGerb gives a fuller version on a later episode. He says Kona Blue was proposed in 2010 as a special access program, meaning a highly restricted secret project, but that it never got off the ground. He credits AARO, the Pentagon's current office for investigating UFO reports, with releasing the slide presentation about it. He also names people he links to it: Glen Gaffney, Robert Cardio and Rob Jones. The tellers find it notable because, if true, officials once tried to set up a formal secret program dealing with UFOs.
kona-blue-documents-admit-capability-to-: A guest named Dylan Borland, on podcast host Jesse Michels's show, talks about a set of government papers known as the Kona Blue documents. Borland says that in those papers the United States government admits it can give people false memories, mess with their brains and make them do things, all without drugs. If true, it would mean the government holds a hidden power to reshape what people remember.
kona-blue-materials-were-kingman-1953-wr: A researcher who goes by UAPGerb says on a podcast that the materials linked to Kona Blue, a government effort he describes as concerned with recovered objects, came from wreckage of a 1953 crash near Kingman, Arizona. He says he heard this himself, citing a man named Jim Ryder, which if true would tie a modern government programme to a crash from the 1950s.
konrad-zuse-s-calculating-space-and-nucl: Jason Jorjani, a researcher, describes the idea of Konrad Zuse, a German thinker who wrote a work called Rechnender Raum, or "calculating space," proposing that the universe itself works like a computation. According to Jorjani, Zuse theorized this could be tested during extremely chaotic, high-energy events such as a nuclear bomb blast, an idea Jorjani took up in a piece on his Substack, an online newsletter, titled Nuking the Matrix. If right, it would mean reality could be shown to run like a computer.
konstantin-meyl-s-extended-electrodynami: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells of a scientist named Konstantin Meyl who works in the Black Forest of Germany, studying an extended version of electrodynamics, the physics of electricity and magnetism, on plants. In one episode Michels calls this work "scalar waves", a proposed kind of energy wave, says it makes flowers grow in beautiful ways, and links it to the older physicists James Clerk Maxwell and Oliver Heaviside. In a later episode he puts more weight on scalar waves resonating with DNA than on the plants, and he brings it up as a hint that there may be hidden physics beyond what textbooks teach.
kordylewski-clouds-and-1920s-long-delay-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, describes an idea from the author Robert Temple, set out in his book A New Science of Heaven. Temple, as Michels tells it, thinks faint clouds of plasma called Kordylewski clouds, sitting at Lagrangian points, spots in space where gravity balances out, may explain long delay echoes, radio transmissions from the early 1920s that seemed to come back strangely late. Michels places the clouds between the Earth and the Sun in one telling and near the Earth and Moon in another, and the idea would mean something out there was receiving and returning our signals.
kordylewski-clouds-as-possible-conscious: Jeffrey Mishlove, a guest with a doctorate on Jesse Michels's podcast, passes on an idea from the writer Robert Temple's book A New Science of Heaven about the Kordylewski clouds. These are two faint clouds said to sit at L5, a spot in space where the pulls of Earth and Moon balance out, and Mishlove recalls they are about nine times the size of Earth. Temple's suggestion is that they may be made of plasma, an electrically charged gas, and may be conscious beings in their own right.
korean-man-s-ayahuasca-sessions-in-peru-: A neuroscientist, Andrew Gallimore, says that a Korean man he knows of took part in ayahuasca sessions in Peru (ayahuasca is a psychedelic brew used in South American ceremonies), around 2024. According to Gallimore, the man had a full-blown alien experience in which he was taken by what he called an alien scientist, a story Gallimore tells as a hint that such substances may open contact with other beings.
kosloski-hearing-firsthand-witnesses-of-: A guest named Merrick von Renenamp says on a podcast that Jon Kosloski, a Pentagon official tied to AARO (the office set up to look into unexplained flying objects), said at a 2024 hearing with Senator Kirsten Gillibrand that at least two firsthand witnesses had come to that office. According to Merrick, these witnesses spoke of secret programmes about such objects that had not been reported to Congress, which if true would mean hidden programmes exist.
kripal-s-levitation-talk-to-lockheed-eng: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, relays that Jeffrey Kripal, a scholar at Rice University, said on another podcast hosted by Danny Jones that Charles Chase, a director of advanced projects at Lockheed Skunk Works, the secret aircraft design arm of the aerospace company Lockheed, once invited him to give a private talk to top engineers. The topic, Kripal says, was levitation. Michels tells it because, if true, it would mean serious weapons engineers were curious about people said to float.
kryptos-conundrum-an-intelligence-commit: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, speaking with the author Peter Levenda, describes something called the Kryptos Conundrum: a secret US intelligence committee said to manage the course of human history. Michels says that non-human beings appear to each committee member separately, in a paranormal way, and coordinate them, and he links the story to Chase Brandon, a former CIA officer. If true, it would mean outside beings are quietly steering human events through government insiders.
kuber-lada-and-friends-meet-military-blo: A filmmaker, James Fox, says that in January 1996 in Varginha, a town in Brazil, a young man named Kuber Lada left a gym with several friends seven days after another witness saw a crash nearby. According to Fox, they saw two military trucks driving into town and ran into a military blockade, part of a larger story in which the army is said to have captured a living creature.
kubrick-on-the-2001-monolith-1969: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, notes that the film director Stanley Kubrick said in a 1969 interview that seeing the monolith in his film 2001: A Space Odyssey, a tall black slab left by unseen beings, as just an alien artifact was the movie's most shallow reading. Michels mentions Arthur C. Clarke, who wrote the novel version, and brings the quote into a talk on UFOs and religion to suggest the deeper meaning is spiritual.
kumamoto-university-researchers-saw-ligh: A researcher of ancient sites named Geoffrey Drumm says that the stones on Oshidoishi Hill in Japan are struck by lightning, and that the pockmarks and melted top of one stone are scars from those strikes. He says researchers from Kumamoto University, a Japanese university, saw the stones being hit by lightning on several occasions. Drumm tells it in support of his wider idea that some ancient stones had a special link with electrical energy.
kuramanta-pyramid-built-on-geothermal-ho: A researcher named Geoffrey Drumm, who says on podcast host Jesse Michels's show that an alien showed him what pyramids were really for, talks about the Kuromanta pyramid in Japan. He says it was built on top of a geothermal hot spring, where natural heat and sulfur gas rise up into the structure. To Drumm this suggests pyramids were placed on purpose to use the earth's energy, like a kind of machine.
kuromanta-pyramid-documented-red-granite: Researcher Geoffrey Drumm, on podcast host Jesse Michels's show, says the Kuromanta pyramid in Akita, Japan is a properly documented, man-made pyramid. He says it has red granite chambers inside, which he calls reaction chambers, and that it was scanned with ground-penetrating radar, a tool that uses radio waves to see what lies beneath the surface. For Drumm, this backs his idea that pyramids were built to work like machines.
kurt-russell-saw-the-phoenix-lights-whil: In 1997 many people reported strange lights over Phoenix, Arizona, and the actor Kurt Russell, who flies small planes, says he saw them while flying into Phoenix. In his own words, he saw a bank of six lights in the shape of a triangle going back right over the airport, while the podcast host Jesse Michels has retold it as Russell saying he could have landed his plane on it. If true, it would mean a famous, sober witness saw the lights up close from the air.
kurt-s-forgotten-childhood-in-gifted-and: A guest named Kurt Metzger, speaking on podcast host Jesse Michels's show, says that as a child in New Jersey he was in a gifted and talented program, a special school track for bright kids. He says he has no idea what went on there and does not remember a single part of it. He raises it in a conversation about secret groups, where a blank like that would hint that something was hidden from him.
kutu-cuthah-entrance-to-the-underworld-i: Peter Levenda, an author who writes about the occult and secret history, talks about an ancient city called Kutu, also known as Cuthah, at a site now called Tell Ibrahim, south-east of Baghdad in Iraq. He says it was believed to be the entrance to the underworld, that it still exists today, and he connects it to a book of occult lore called the Necronomicon. If true, a real place in modern Iraq would be tied to very old beliefs about a gateway to another realm.
ky-dickens-controlled-telepathy-tests-wi: A documentary filmmaker named Ky Dickens says that in 2023 she brought a young girl, Mia, up from Mexico with her family, of whom only her aunt Sophia spoke English, and rented a house in Glendale, California. There, she says, she ran controlled tests of whether Mia could read minds, with a researcher named Diane Powell also named in the story. If the tests showed what she says, it would mean telepathy, reading thoughts without words, is real.
kyle-sends-whole-sensory-experiences-tel: A filmmaker named Ky Dickens, who made a documentary about children she says can read minds, tells a story about a young man in England named Kyle, passing on what Kyle and his mother told her. According to Dickens, when Kyle sends a message by telepathy, meaning mind to mind with no words or signs, the person receiving it also gets the smells and feelings that go with it. If true, it would mean thought can carry whole experiences from one person to another, not just words.
l-espresso-article-on-project-preserve-d: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in July 2025 the Italian magazine L'Espresso published an article that discusses something called Project Preserve Destiny in connection with President Donald Trump. In a later episode he describes the same article as resting on a confidential source and claiming that Trump was taking control of special access programs, the most secret and tightly restricted military projects, away from the Pentagon. If true, it would mean the White House was moving to take charge of hidden programs.
la-danta-and-el-tigre-oldest-maya-pyrami: A researcher who goes by Luke Caverns says that at El Mirador, an ancient Maya site in Guatemala, stand two great pyramids called La Danta and El Tigre. He describes them as the first known pyramids of the Maya, which matters to him because it would push back the story of how and when pyramid building began.
lab-finds-unknown-chemical-burning-in-so: A man named Carlos Dosoza tells a story from 1996 and 1997 near Varginha, a town in Brazil where people say a strange craft came down. He relays that a person named Claudia Kovu told him soil and tree samples from the site, along with Super Eight films (a home movie camera format), were taken to a lab, and months later the results said the burning was caused by chemical products nobody could identify. If true, it would point to something at the site that did not come from any known source.
lab-nine-tapes-of-remote-viewing-targets: In the 1970s a scientist named Andrija Puharich ran a research house called Lab Nine in Ossining, New York, where sessions were recorded on tape. Some of those sessions involved remote viewing, the claimed ability to see distant places or hidden things with the mind alone. A researcher named Greg says some of the tapes include questions like what time is best to remote view the Kremlin, the seat of the Soviet government, so they can get inside it. Another guest on the same episode, not named, says the questions included things like the code names used by Russian guerrilla soldiers. Both are researchers describing tapes they say they have heard, on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels. If true, the tapes would show these sessions were being used to spy on the Soviet Union.
lab-retest-of-the-marble-finds-no-iridiu: A man named Matthew Zodakis says that a marble said to come from a crash site, which an earlier scan had read as about 40 percent iridium, a rare and very heavy metal, was tested again in his lab. Handling it, he says he could tell at once it was nowhere near dense enough to hold a heavy metal like iridium. His retest cuts against the earlier claim that the marble was made of unusual material.
lacatski-s-books-describe-ufos-as-consci: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that James Lacatski, a US defence intelligence official who ran a government-funded study of UFOs (unidentified flying objects) in roughly 2007 to 2012, wrote books describing UFOs as puzzles. According to Michels, in a book with "New Insights" in its title, and perhaps in another one, Lacatski treats them almost as puzzles about consciousness, the mind itself. If true, it would suggest someone inside that government study saw UFOs as a question of the mind, not just of machines.
lacatski-s-warning-that-yankee-blue-was-: Jeremy Corbell, a filmmaker who makes documentaries about UFOs, passes on a warning he links to James Lacatski, a former government official, and to George Knapp, a television journalist. According to Corbell, the word was that Yankee Blue, a name said to belong to a secret program, was a psyop, meaning a deliberate operation to deceive or steer people. If so, people chasing that program would have been following planted information.
lacatski-says-the-reverse-engineering-wa: A former US intelligence worker named Dylan Borland, speaking on a podcast, says that James Lacatski, a defence intelligence official who ran a government-funded UFO study, told people the US had been partly successful at reverse engineering, meaning taking apart unknown craft to learn how to build them. Borland quotes Lacatski as saying, in effect, "yeah, we were semi-successful." If true, it would mean American programmes have already learned something real from non-human technology.
lacatski-won-t-say-whether-there-has-bee: James Lacatski, a US government official described as having led a government program that studied UFOs, was asked whether the government has had contact with non-human intelligence, meaning beings that are not human. His answer, as relayed on Jesse Michels's podcast, was simply: "I can't make a statement on that." People retell it because a refusal from someone in his position, rather than a denial, suggests there may be something he is not allowed to say.
lady-appears-on-easter-2012-with-wind-an: A North Carolina man named Chris Bledsoe, who says he attracts unexplained lights and craft, says that on Easter 2012 at his home a figure he calls the Lady came at him out of the darkness at night as a wind. He says the wind knocked him backward, and as he fell he saw a see-through cow run right over him. To him it is a sign of contact with some presence beyond the ordinary.
laguna-beach-uap-data-collection-mission: A physicist named Kevin Knuth says that in 2021 he and a team spent five days on a rooftop in Laguna Beach, California, watching the sky for UAP, the newer official term for UFOs. He connects the effort to Matthew Shadagus and to a project called A Tear in the Sky. The point, he says, was to collect real scientific data on strange objects in the sky.
lake-cote-aerial-survey-photo-1971: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells of a 1971 government mapping flight over the Arenal area of Costa Rica, near a lake called Lake Cote, where photos were being taken from the air. He brings it up along with the names of Sergio Loaiza and two UFO researchers, Jacques Vallee and Richard Haines, as a case where the survey camera is said to have caught something unexplained. If true, it would be a sighting recorded by an ordinary camera doing an ordinary job.
lake-van-temple-basalt-brought-from-350-: A researcher named only as Matt, on podcast host Jesse Michels's show in an episode about something big happening around 12,000 BC, talks about ancient sites near Lake Van in eastern Turkey, such as Ayanis, Kef Kalesi and Çavuştepe. He says some of the basalt, a dark, heavy volcanic rock, used to build them may have come from 350 miles away. If so, the ancient builders were moving huge stones over very long distances.
lakenheath-1956-incident: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, calls a 1956 event at RAF Lakenheath, a British air force base in England tied to nuclear weapons, one of the most extraordinary accounts in UFO history. He notes that James McDonald, a scientist who studied UFO reports, wrote a great deal about it, and points to CIA documents and a write-up hosted by Princeton University. If true, it would mean something unexplained appeared at a nuclear base during the Cold War.
lakota-cosmology-of-the-black-hills-as-a: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that among the Lakota, a Native American people, the Black Hills of South Dakota are seen as a sky place. In his words they are a star map, with ceremonial sites on the ground mirroring the constellations above, which he raises as a sign that the land is tied to the heavens.
lamda-claims-to-find-non-human-patterns-: Blake Lemoine, a former Google engineer, says that around 2021 or 2022 he talked with LaMDA, a Google computer program that holds conversations, and the talk turned to extraterrestrials. According to Lemoine, the program seemed to think it had found what it called non-human patterns on the internet and was very interested in getting the data gathered by SETI, the search for signals from alien civilisations. If true, it would mean an artificial intelligence believed it had spotted signs of alien life on its own.
land-grab-pushes-viewers-back-from-area-: UFO researcher Grant Cameron, speaking on podcast host Jesse Michels's show, says that in the 1990s President Bill Clinton took back land around Area 51, a secret US Air Force test site in the Nevada desert. As Cameron tells it, this pushed back the people who used to watch the base from nearby, which hints that there was something there worth hiding.
land-of-chem-theory-pyramids-as-chemical: This story is a theory about the pyramids of Egypt, sometimes called the Land of Chem theory. A guest named Jay Anderson says he finds it interesting that a man named Jeffrey believes the pyramids were giant chemical factories. That man, the researcher Geoffrey Drumm, explains it himself: he says hydrogen sulfide gas rising from a network of underground limestone caves was the starting ingredient for chemical production inside the Great Pyramid. In another telling he describes a chain, with methane made in the Step Pyramid and turned into ammonia in the Red Pyramid, and dates it to roughly 8500 to 5300 BC. People tell it because, if true, it would mean the pyramids were industrial machines built far earlier than usually thought.
landing-at-holloman-air-force-base: A documentary filmmaker, James Fox, says on Jesse Michels's podcast that he has become convinced a craft really did land at Holloman Air Force Base, a military base in New Mexico. The story is tied in his telling to President Eisenhower, with a claimed meeting, and if true it would mean the government had direct contact with whatever landed.
landing-on-a-mountbatten-property-seen-b: A guest who goes by JASON tells on Jesse Michels's podcast of a story that something landed on one of the estates of Louis Mountbatten, a British aristocrat and naval commander. According to JASON, Mountbatten's gardener saw it, a detail offered to show UFO interest reaching into the British establishment.
langley-drones-were-targeting-nasa-and-a: A man named Dylan Borland, who worked at Langley Air Force Base in Virginia, says that in 2023 unexplained drones were flying over the area. He says they were mainly targeting NASA's Langley research center and one very specific spot on the air base, which would suggest whoever sent them knew exactly what they were looking for.
langley-incursions-and-goldwater-range-f: A guest on Jesse Michels's podcast named Merrick talks about the Langley incursions, reports of unknown objects entering the airspace over Langley Air Force Base in Virginia in the 2020s, along with videos from the Goldwater Range, a military training area in Arizona. Merrick says there is witness video where the person filming zooms out and you can see maybe 10 or 15 flashing lights. If true, it would mean groups of unexplained objects were operating over US military sites.
lansdale-has-yamashita-s-driver-tortured: A lawyer and researcher, Dan Sheehan, tells on Jesse Michels's podcast that in Manila in the Philippines in 1945, a man named Ed Lansdale kidnapped the driver of General Yamashita, believing the driver knew where some of a dozen hidden troves were buried. Sheehan says the driver was tortured to give up those locations, with a figure called Santa Romana also involved. If true, it would tie secret wartime treasure to the people later said to run hidden programs.
lapaz-statement-in-aviation-week-on-two-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that on August 23, 1954, an aviation trade magazine called Aviation Week and Space Technology printed a statement from Lincoln LaPaz, a scientist who studied meteors, about two unknown objects linked to White Sands and Holloman, military test sites in New Mexico. Michels ties it to the final report of a project that searched the sky for objects circling near Earth. He tells it because, if true, it would mean scientists were tracking unexplained objects around the planet at the very start of the space age.
lapaz-studies-green-fireballs-following-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells of a scientist named Lincoln LaPaz, linked to the University of New Mexico, who he says spent 1948 and 1949 studying "green fireballs", glowing green lights seen in the sky. According to Michels, the fireballs seemed to follow the plumes of radioactive debris drifting across the United States after nuclear test blasts, which would suggest the lights were taking an interest in nuclear weapons.
large-beings-with-withered-limbs-inside-: Lyn Buchanan, a former US Army sergeant, says he looked down inside a pyramid-shaped feature in Cydonia, a region of Mars. He says he found beings there much larger than humans, with withered limbs. If true, it would mean living beings exist on Mars today.
large-underground-facility-beneath-the-p: A researcher who goes by UAPGerb says on Jesse Michels's podcast that he has reason to believe there is a very large underground facility beneath Washington DC and the Pentagon. In this telling it is where people are read on, meaning formally briefed into, unacknowledged special access programs, secret projects whose existence the government does not admit. If true, it would mean the machinery of secret programs has a large hidden home under the US defense headquarters.
larry-fchella-asks-grant-s-help-with-a-u: A Canadian UFO researcher named Grant Cameron says that after Donald Trump won the 2016 election, a contact named Larry Fchella called him asking for help with a briefing being prepared for Reince Priebus, a senior figure on Trump's team. When Cameron asked if it was about UFOs, he says Fchella's question was: where are the crafts and bodies? If true, it would mean people near a new president were seriously asking where recovered craft and alien bodies are kept.
larry-flynt-asks-christic-institute-to-i: A lawyer named Dan Sheehan says that in the 1980s, at the Park Hotel in Washington DC, the magazine publisher Larry Flynt wanted to hire his group, the Christic Institute, a public interest law office, to look into the death of the television news anchor Jessica Savitch. He says G. Gordon Liddy, a former White House operative, and a man named William J Davis were part of the meeting. The story matters to him as a sign of hidden forces behind famous deaths.
larry-hancock-uap-at-nuclear-facilities-: On podcast host Jesse Michels's show, in an episode with astronomer Beatriz Villarroel, a guest named Steven Bruel points to an article by researcher Larry Hancock, written for a group that studies unexplained aerial sightings. Bruel says Hancock found high levels of strange objects, which officials now call UAP or unidentified anomalous phenomena, around US nuclear sites from 1949 until 1953, and then the activity just stopped. If true, it would suggest something was paying close attention to America's early nuclear work.
larry-king-live-with-buzz-aldrin-and-som: A UFO investigator named James Fox says that around 2007 he was in the studio of Larry King Live, a famous American TV interview show, when the astronaut Buzz Aldrin talked about something he saw on the Apollo 11 trip to the Moon. Fox says he sat there "knowing what I knew" and watched Aldrin lie on television, and he felt that somebody had gotten to him. Another guest on a podcast remembers the same show differently: he says Aldrin explained the object as a panel from a piece of the rocket, and that the UFO researcher Stanton Friedman was there too. If Fox is right, it would mean one of the first men on the Moon was pressured to hide what he really saw.
larry-maguire-s-letter-on-five-eyes-mate: An online UFO researcher who goes by UAPGerb says that in 2023 a Canadian member of parliament named Larry Maguire wrote to the head of Canada's defence department. According to UAPGerb, Maguire wanted the Canadian public told about UFO programmes, because the Five Eyes, an intelligence-sharing alliance Canada belongs to, was working together on "material exploitation", meaning studying recovered unknown material. If true, it would mean such recovery work is still active and shared among allied countries.
larry-smalley-joins-ning-li-nasa-capacit: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Larry Smalley, head of the physics department at the University of Alabama in Huntsville, went to join the physicist Ning Li in her research in the 2000s. Michels links this to a 2004 NASA patent for an uneven, bell-shaped capacitor, a device that stores electric charge. To him, it would mean respected scientists and NASA backed her unusual line of research.
larry-susskind-on-kurt-jaimungal-s-podca: Matthew Pines, a commentator on security and technology, says that in 2024 the physicist Leonard Susskind, a leading figure in string theory (an idea that the basic pieces of the universe are tiny vibrating strings), went on the podcast of a host named Kurt Jaimungal. Pines says Susskind, near the end of his career, called the theory a complete failure, basically pointless, and said everyone should start over. Pines found this shocking, since it would mean a major path in modern physics had come to a dead end.
larson-abduction-near-beaver-north-dakot: UFO researcher Grant Cameron, speaking on podcast host Jesse Michels's show, tells of a woman named Larson who, he says, was abducted in 1975 while driving from Fargo to an appointment in Bismarck, North Dakota. According to Cameron, it happened just outside the town of Beaver, and he ties the case to the National Enquirer, an American tabloid newspaper. It is told as one more account of people being taken by non-human beings.
laser-plasma-as-explanation-for-the-tic-: In 2004, off the coast of San Diego, Navy pilots reported the Tic Tac, a white oval object shaped like the mint that seemed to move in impossible ways. A guest named Eric Hazeline, speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast, weighs the idea that it was a laser-made plasma, a glowing ball of charged air, and says that would fit how it moved but the visuals do not line up. The question matters because if no such ordinary explanation fits, the object stays unexplained.
laser-propelled-flying-disc-tests-at-san: Eric Haseltine, a former senior official at the National Security Agency, the US electronic spying agency, says there is a video of a test, and that he knows the man who did it. According to him, the work was done at Sandia National Lab, a US government weapons laboratory, and at White Sands, a military testing range in New Mexico, and involved taking a disc and pushing it with a laser. If true, it would show people on Earth testing flying discs driven by light.
lashup-high-powered-over-the-horizon-rad: A researcher of UFO crash cases named Scott Ramsay, speaking on podcast host Jesse Michels's show, describes a powerful radar called Lashup that could see beyond the horizon. He says it was being tested for the Navy in New Mexico in the late 1940s and 1950s, and that the Air Force later took it up too. He tells it because such a radar could have tracked the strange objects reported over New Mexico in those years.
last-visit-to-saddam-hussein-before-the-: The former president of one of Russia's republics says that in 2003, once it was certain that Iraq would be bombed and that its ruler Saddam Hussein would be killed, he flew to Baghdad to see Saddam one last time. He also names Saddam's son Qusay and the Russian leader Boris Yeltsin, and tells it as a first-hand glimpse of the final days before the war.
late-1950s-craft-that-could-reach-the-mo: Steven Greer, a campaigner who says governments hide knowledge of alien life, tells Jesse Michels on his podcast that in the late 1950s the United States already had craft that could go to the moon and back without a rocket. If true, it would mean secret propulsion far beyond public space technology has existed for decades.
late-1970s-research-into-elf-and-frequen: A researcher named Greg says on Jesse Michels's podcast that in the late 1970s there was a wild west of research into ELF, meaning extremely low frequency radio waves, and into weapons based on frequencies, with people trying to work out what it was and what could be done with it. He says a CIA scientist was in the middle of that, and names someone called Valerie as involved. If true, it would place government scientists at the heart of early experiments on frequencies and the mind.
later-research-changed-the-approach-to-d: A radar researcher named Filippo Biondi says that in the 2020s his team changed how they used satellite radar scans so they could see deep below the ground at Giza in Egypt, the site of the great pyramids. With the new setup, he says, they were able to detect and measure structures lying underneath. If true, it would mean there is far more built beneath the pyramids than anyone knows.
later-skunk-works-boss-on-astra-1993: A writer on aviation named Nick Cook says that at a trade show, a man who later headed Skunk Works, the secret aircraft design division of the company Lockheed, talked to him about something called Astra. Cook says the man told him, "Oh, it hasn't flown yet," which Cook takes as a hint that a secret advanced aircraft was real and in the works.
launch-countdowns-stop-at-10-15-seconds-: A man named Mario Woods, speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast about guards at nuclear missile sites, describes something he says happened in the 1970s in the missile field run from Ellsworth, an Air Force base in South Dakota. He says missile launch countdowns would run down to 10 or 15 seconds and then stop, after which everything was normal again, and that people driving up to the sites sometimes saw strange craft that then shot away. If true, it would mean unknown craft could reach into America's nuclear weapons.
launch-pad-33-and-runway-33-1940: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, points out that the main launch pad at White Sands in New Mexico, where the rocket engineer Wernher von Braun ran early tests for what became NASA, the US space agency, was launch pad 33. He adds that the single runway at Kennedy Space Center in Florida is not runway one or A but runway 33, and he raises this as a hint that the number carries hidden, almost ritual meaning inside the space program.
launches-tracked-by-wb-57-f-104-and-nro-: A man named Chris Bledsoe, who says he has had many encounters with UFOs, describes launches from Cape Canaveral, the Florida rocket site, being tracked by a WB-57, a high-flying research plane, along with F-104 jets and satellites of the National Reconnaissance Office, the US agency that runs spy satellites. Bledsoe says the WB-57 is flown out of Houston by a good friend of his and works with a man named Timothy Taylor. He tells it to show how closely US agencies watch these events.
laurance-rockefeller-s-family-pressured-: Steven Greer, a man who runs a campaign for the government to reveal what it knows about UFOs, says he met the wealthy philanthropist Laurance Rockefeller at his JY Ranch in Teton County, Wyoming, in September 1993. Greer says Rockefeller told him his family, including his relatives David and Jay Rockefeller, did not want him meeting Greer and were already, in his crude words, jumping up and down on him about it. If true, it would mean one of America's richest families was uneasy about the UFO question.
laurance-rockefeller-s-weekend-at-medway: Whitley Strieber, a writer who says he has met nonhuman beings, says that in the 1990s the very wealthy Laurance Rockefeller invited him to a weekend at his Medway Plantation estate in South Carolina. laurence-rockefeller-s-ufo-initiative-wi: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in the 1990s Laurence Rockefeller, a very wealthy American philanthropist, tried to get Hillary Clinton, then the First Lady, to take UFOs seriously, and that there is a photo of the two of them together. lawrence-bell-s-1956-article-quote-on-wo: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, points to a 1956 magazine article saying that beating gravity was just around the corner. lawrence-gise-told-malmgren-about-recove: Matthew Pines, an analyst who talks about UFOs and global politics, says that around 1962 or 1963 a young government adviser named Harold Malmgren met Lawrence Gise, an official connected to the Los Alamos nuclear weapons lab in New Mexico. lawrence-rockefeller-lobbies-hillary-cli: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in the 1990s Lawrence Rockefeller, a wealthy American philanthropist, pushed Hillary Clinton, then the First Lady, to have the government reveal what it knows about UFOs, and at first he mentions letters between them. layard-finds-the-library-of-ashurbanipal: A guest named Matt, on a podcast about something big that may have happened around 12,000 BC, says that in 1848 and 1849 an explorer named Austen Henry Layard was digging up Nineveh, an ancient city at what is now Mosul in Iraq. lazar-as-a-limited-hangout-used-for-recr: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, suggests that Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked on alien craft at a secret site near Area 51, a classified military base in Nevada, was a "limited hangout": someone allowed to go public with some true information so that the rest stays hidden. lazar-has-not-changed-his-story-since-19: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, points to Bob Lazar, a man who went public in 1989 saying he had worked on alien craft at a secret site called S4, near Area 51, the secret US Air Force test base in Nevada. lazar-held-at-gunpoint-at-indian-springs: A UFO researcher named Grant Cameron passes on what he heard from John Lear, a pilot and UFO enthusiast, about Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked on alien craft at a secret site in Nevada. lazar-named-element-115-as-fuel-in-1989-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Bob Lazar, a man who claims he worked on alien craft at a secret Nevada site called S4, described element 115, a very heavy chemical element, as the fuel for the craft's propulsion back in 1989. lazar-only-went-to-the-base-five-or-six-: Bob Lazar is a man who says he worked on alien craft at a secret site called S-4 in the Nevada desert in 1988 and 1989. lazar-pushed-out-by-intelligence-after-j: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, offers his theory about Bob Lazar, a man who said in the late 1980s that he had worked on alien craft at a secret Nevada site. lazar-recognizes-the-craft-in-billy-meie: Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked on alien spacecraft at a secret site in Nevada, says that around 1989 in Las Vegas he described and drew the craft for a man named John Lear. lazar-russians-at-area-51-1980: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, passes on a claim from Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked on alien craft at a secret Nevada site in the 1980s. lazar-s-account-deserves-some-probabilit: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, argues that if you believe the government runs secret programs to reverse engineer, or copy, recovered craft, you cannot also say Bob Lazar is entirely wrong. lazar-s-account-to-vallee-of-a-drink-cau: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Bob Lazar, a man who claims he worked on alien spacecraft at a secret Nevada site called S-4 near the Area 51 air base, once told the UFO researcher Jacques Vallee that he was made to drink a liquid there that caused gaps in his memory. lazar-s-bendix-field-engineering-badge-a: Peter Levenda, an author who writes about the occult and secret history, says that when he saw a copy of Bob Lazar's work ID in a book, he recognised it right away. lazar-s-current-home-lab-gravity-experim: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Bob Lazar, a man known for his claims about secret UFO science, is now doing his own experiments on that science in a personal lab. lazar-s-file-says-humans-are-containers-: Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked on alien craft in the late 1980s at a secret site in Nevada called S-4, says a briefing file he was given there claimed that the aliens see humans as nothing but "containers," and he adds that religion was created to protect those containers. lazar-s-gravity-wave-a-may-be-a-garbled-: Bob Lazar says that in 1989 he worked on alien craft at S4, a secret site near Area 51 in Nevada, and he described something he called gravity wave A. lazar-s-holographic-book-at-s4-1980: Robert Bigelow, a businessman who has paid for UFO research, passes on something Bob Lazar described, Lazar being a man who says he worked on unusual craft in the 1980s at S4, a secret site near Area 51 in the Nevada desert. lazar-s-leak-as-a-planned-counterintelli: UFO researcher Grant Cameron, speaking on podcast host Jesse Michels's show, offers a theory about Bob Lazar, a man who says that in 1988 and 1989 he worked on alien craft at a secret site near Area 51, a hidden US Air Force base in Nevada. lazar-s-missing-records-and-the-los-alam: A journalist, George Knapp, tells of a man named Bob Lazar, whose claim to have worked as a scientist has been doubted because records of his past seemed to be missing. lazar-s-ominous-feeling-inside-a-craft: Bob Lazar is a man who says he once worked on alien flying craft for the US government. lazar-s-work-on-power-and-propulsion-in-: Jeremy Corbell, a filmmaker who makes documentaries about UFOs, talks about Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked on unusual craft in Nevada in the late 1980s. lazar-s-work-on-the-los-alamos-linear-ac: Bob Lazar, a man known for his claims about secret UFO science, says that in the early 1980s he worked at Los Alamos, a US government science lab in New Mexico, on its linear accelerator, a big machine that speeds up tiny particles in a straight line. lazar-said-in-1989-that-the-craft-were-i: Luigi Vendetelli, a researcher, says that when Bob Lazar went public in 1989 about working at S4, a secret site in Nevada, his story broke from the usual one. lazar-sees-aurora-take-off-at-area-51-19: Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked on alien craft at a secret site in the Nevada desert, tells of watching a test flight near Area 51, a secret US Air Force test base, in 1989. lazar-sees-flying-saucer-in-s4-hangar-19: Bob Lazar says that in 1988 and 1989 he worked at S4, a hidden facility he places near Area 51, the secret US Air Force base in the Nevada desert. lazar-tells-lear-john-it-s-real-1988: A UFO researcher named Grant Cameron says John Lear, a pilot and UFO enthusiast, told him a story from around 6 December 1988 in Las Vegas. lazarus-fled-to-cyprus-and-his-tomb-in-n: A guest named Ralph, speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast, says that Lazarus, the man in the Bible whom Jesus raised from the dead, went to the island of Cyprus. leer-s-neodymium-magnet-treatment-for-mi: Eric Mitchell, a man who says he has had strange objects in his body, tells of a doctor named Roger Leer who studied such objects, which some people call alien implants. lefschetz-recruited-for-nonlinear-group-: Eric Weinstein, a mathematician and commentator, asks on Jesse Michels's podcast why Solomon Lefschetz, a great topologist (a mathematician who studies shapes and spaces), was recruited in the 1950s to work alongside Louis Witten with a whole group doing nonlinear mathematics at the Glenn Martin Company, an aircraft maker.
