left-alone-at-11-figure-on-the-roof-and-: Whitley Strieber, a writer who says he has met nonhuman beings, says that around 1956, when he was 11 and left alone at home in Terrell Hills in San Antonio, Texas, there was a figure on the roof. He says a policeman came and went up to look, and seconds later came running down yelling "There's no one there. There's no one there." He tells it as one of the strange early events of his life.
legacy-crash-retrieval-program-should-ou: David Grusch, a former US intelligence officer, says there is a decades-old secret programme, which he calls a legacy programme, that collects crashed craft of non-human origin. Speaking with podcast host Jesse Michels, he says the programme should want to reveal itself, and he describes losing a lot of sleep after he uncovered it by interviewing witnesses he found genuine. Michels retells it in his own words, saying Grusch exposed a multi-decade effort to recover and reverse engineer crashed UFOs paid for by American taxpayers. A filmmaker and UFO investigator, James Fox, also repeats Grusch's claim and says the programme has been running since at least World War II. If true, it would mean the US government has been hiding recovered craft for generations.
legacy-crash-retrievals-luring-craft-wit: A guest named Jordan, who says he was taken into a secret UFO programme as a child, passes on what he says a journalist named Ross Colart told him. The story is about a supposed hidden effort to recover crashed craft that are not of human making. According to it, people used psionics, meaning claimed powers of the mind, to lure the craft in, "almost creating this like honeypot of like hey we love you come see us," and then brought them down in the desert with energy weapons. If true, it would mean these crashes were caused on purpose, not by accident.
legacy-program-as-a-dummy-program-that-k: Eric Weinstein, a mathematician and commentator, suggests on Jesse Michels's podcast that the so-called legacy program, the long-running secret effort said to study recovered craft at an established aerospace company, might be a dummy program hiding something else. Pointing to the experience of a scientist named Bernie Haisch, he argues that the last thing such a decoy would want is a real physicist on board. If true, the program people talk about would be a cover for the real work.
legacy-program-insider-the-answers-are-i: An online researcher who goes by UAPGerb says a friend of his, a firsthand insider from a "legacy program", meaning a long-running secret government effort said to study non-human craft, once gave him a tip. According to UAPGerb, the friend said the answer to most of what he was looking for is in Crystal City, Virginia. If true, it would point to where that secret work is run.
legacy-program-insiders-on-ufo-materials: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, refers to people inside what he calls the UFO legacy program, a secret, long-running government effort said to hold materials from UFOs. He says there is a particular way these insiders talk about such materials. If true, it would mean such a program exists and its members share their own way of speaking.
legacy-program-insiders-tell-corbell-and: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that a filmmaker, Jeremy Corbell, and a journalist, Ross Coulthart, hear unnerving stories from people they say work on "legacy programs", long-running secret government efforts said to study non-human craft. According to Michels, those insiders all say the same thing at a certain point: "If you knew what I know," you would not be pushing for disclosure. If true, it would mean insiders believe the full truth is too troubling to release.
legacy-program-money-routed-through-ffrd: A researcher who goes by the online name UAPGerb, talking on podcast host Jesse Michels' show in 2025, says the money behind a so-called legacy program, a secret effort said to handle craft that are not human-made, moves through hidden channels. In this telling it goes through federally funded research centers (privately run labs paid for by the government), Defense Department labs and military test ranges, and offices in Crystal City and Arlington, near the Pentagon in Virginia. UAPGerb says he has talked to witnesses who saw physical bales of cash taken to locations, which, if true, would mean nobody could really track how much is spent.
legacy-program-oral-tradition-of-agreeme: A man who presents himself as a Pentagon whistleblower, Matthew Brown, says he has learned of an oral tradition inside the "legacy program", a long-running secret government effort said to deal with non-human intelligence. According to Brown, the story passed down there is that the United States struck agreements with a "third party", meaning a non-human power. If true, it would mean the government made secret deals with non-humans.
legacy-program-recruits-psionic-assets-f: A psychologist with a doctorate, Jeffrey Mishlove, says a so-called "legacy program", a secret government effort, works with "psionic assets", people with psychic abilities used to draw UFOs in. According to Mishlove, the program has been reaching out to people from native cultures around the world, especially young children who were never taught that such things are impossible. If true, it would mean children's minds are being used to make contact with non-human craft.
legacy-program-rumored-to-lure-ufos-with: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says there are rumors that the "legacy" UFO program, a long-running secret government effort some people say exists, uses protocols to draw UFOs in. The idea is that people with psychic or mind-based abilities are used to attract the craft, which would mean the government can call them on purpose.
legacy-program-secrecy-kept-through-trus: Matthew Brown, who calls himself a Pentagon whistleblower, says there is a "legacy program," a long-running secret effort dealing with UFOs that goes back to the 1940s. He says he has come to learn that its secrecy is kept partly through trusted families, with the knowledge passed down inside them over generations. If true, it would explain how such a secret could last so long without leaking.
legacy-program-staff-take-on-dual-roles-: An online researcher who goes by UAPGerb says he has been told how staff in a "legacy program", a long-running secret government effort said to study non-human craft, keep it small. According to what he was told, a scientist there might also do some accounting or personnel work so that fewer new people need to be "read in", formally cleared into the secret. If true, it would explain how such a program could stay hidden for decades.
legacy-programs-bait-ufos-with-nuclear-m: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that older secret US government UFO programs used nuclear material, or sometimes fake nuclear material, as bait to make UFOs show up. He credits the claim to Garry Nolan, a Stanford microbiologist, and in that version it also covers Russia, from the middle of the last century into the 1990s. If true, it would mean these objects are drawn to nuclear material and that governments have known this and used it on purpose.
legacy-uap-program-rotten-and-breaking-a: Matthew Pines, an analyst, tells Jesse Michels on his podcast that the push for disclosure in the 2020s is a recognition that the legacy program, a long-running secret effort on UAP (unidentified anomalous phenomena, the official term for UFOs), is rotten in more ways than one. He says it may be rotten as an institution and also morally, and that it seems to be breaking as everyone defects from it. If true, it would explain why insiders are now coming forward.
legacy-ufo-program-secrecy-rooted-in-the: Someone who goes by the online name UAPGerb, speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast, draws on what a witness named David Grusch said in an interview with podcaster Joe Rogan. The claim is that long-running secret government UFO programs, called legacy programs, were built on the same secrecy rules as the Manhattan Project, the US wartime effort to build the atomic bomb, and on the 1954 Atomic Energy Act, a US law controlling nuclear secrets. If so, the rules that hid nuclear weapons work would also be what keeps UFO programs hidden.
legacy-ufo-program-tests-psionic-ability: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, relays what a man named Michael Herrera says: that after seeing something disturbing in Indonesia around 2009, he was quietly contacted by someone claiming to be from the "Legacy" programme, a supposed secret government effort to deal with craft not made by humans. According to that contact, the programme was gathering people from disaster zones like Indonesia and testing their psionic ability, meaning claimed powers of the mind. Herrera tells it a little differently himself, naming his source as a man called Jake Barber, calling the programme "P3" (not its real name), and saying people with these mind abilities were carried in the shipping containers he saw.
legend-of-range-four-harry-the-glowing-r: Charles Hall, a man who says he worked on the Air Force gunnery ranges near Indian Springs, Nevada, in the mid 1960s, tells of a legend the men there passed around. According to Hall, the story on Range Four was of a giant white horse, glowing and radioactive, nicknamed Harry. He tells it as part of his wider account of tall white beings he says he met on those ranges, hinting that the legend may have grown out of them.
legend-of-the-virgin-mary-landing-on-ath: A guest named Ralph, interviewed on a podcast that billed him as a former spy chief, says that while travelling in Greece in the mid-2000s a monk told him an old legend about Mount Athos, a Greek peninsula full of monasteries. According to the monk, the Virgin Mary was blown off course by the wind and came ashore there, and a monastery called Iveron now stands on the spot where she is said to have landed.
leibniz-s-monadology-of-observing-entiti: A researcher, Don Hoffman, says on a podcast that the philosopher Leibniz already suggested his idea back in 1700, in a work called the Monadology, which pictures the world as made up of observing entities. Hoffman brings it up to show that his own view of reality has a very old ancestor.
lemay-s-unauthorized-u-2-overflight-of-r: Dan Sheehan, a lawyer and researcher, says on Jesse Michels's podcast that in 1962 the Air Force general Curtis LeMay ordered a U-2, a high-flying American spy plane, to fly over Russia without permission to do final retargeting. If true, it would mean a military commander acted on his own over the head of the president at a dangerous moment.
lennon-s-and-rfk-s-assassins-as-mk-ultra: Steve Coburn, who speaks as a witness on a podcast, suggests that the men who killed the senator Robert F. Kennedy in 1968 and the musician John Lennon in 1980 were subjects of MK Ultra, a secret CIA program that experimented with controlling people's minds. If true, it would mean both killings were shaped by a hidden government program.
leo-sprinkle-finds-benowitz-armed-and-sa: A writer, Greg Bishop, passes on a story from a psychologist named Leo Sprinkle about a visit to the Albuquerque home of a man named Paul Bennewitz in the late 1970s. Sprinkle said Bennewitz met him holding a rifle and a pistol and told him, "they're coming, you have to come in the house right now." Bishop tells it to show how frightened Bennewitz had become, in a story about a man he says was driven to madness by what he believed were aliens.
leonardo-da-vinci-given-information-by-a: A guest on podcast host Jesse Michels' show, Kiran Ilum Xenov, introduced in the 2025 episode title as the president of a Russian republic who says he was taken by aliens in 1997, says that Leonardo da Vinci, the Italian Renaissance artist and inventor, "was given information" by beings from elsewhere. He names him alongside the Talmud, the body of Jewish religious writings, as an example. If true, some of humanity's great ideas would have come from outside humanity.
leonidas-consults-the-oracle-of-delphi-b: A researcher of ancient sites, Luke Caverns, speaking on podcast host Jesse Michels' show in 2025, retells how Leonidas, a king of ancient Sparta, went to the Oracle of Delphi, a temple in Greece where a priestess gave prophecies, to ask whether his people should fight the invading Persians, around 480 BC. He brings it up while talking about ancient sites that people once trusted as sources of real knowledge.
leslie-kean-publishes-the-grusch-article: Podcast host Jesse Michels says that in 2023 the journalist Leslie Kean published the first article about David Grusch, a witness whose claims of secret government UFO programs set off a wave of public attention. Michels says Kean had to publish it in The Debrief, a smaller online news outlet, because the New York Times passed on it, and he connects that decision to a Times reporter named Julian Barnes.
leslie-kean-s-2017-new-york-times-ufo-st: In December 2017 the New York Times newspaper ran an article about UFOs written with a journalist named Leslie Kean. A UFO documentary filmmaker, James Fox, says it was her biggest story and one of the most popular the paper ever published. A skeptic, Mick West, says the article was co-written with Ralph Blumenthal and came with Navy videos called Gimbal and FLIR1, with another, Go Fast, released a little later. Why it matters, as told, is that it brought the subject out of the fringe. An analyst, Matthew Pines, describes the articles as the start of a slow, semi-official acceptance of a topic that had been an outsider culture. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says a former official named Lue Elizondo helped get the article published through Kean while he was in charge of AATIP, a small Pentagon office that studied unexplained aerial reports. So it is told by the host, a filmmaker, an analyst and a skeptic alike, each stressing a different side.
leslie-kean-s-list-of-ordinary-explanati: A researcher known as a skeptic, Michael Shermer, reads out a list of ordinary explanations for UFO sightings during a debate on a podcast. He says the list comes from a 2010 book by Leslie Kean called UFOs: Generals, Pilots, and Government Officials Go on the Record. He uses it to point out that even a book that takes UFOs seriously admits that most sightings have everyday causes.
letter-from-senator-cohen-thanking-the-r: Joe McMoneagle, a remote viewer, meaning someone in a US government programme that tried to describe distant places using only the mind, says he has a letter in his personnel file from a US senator named Cohen. According to McMoneagle, the letter thanked the remote viewers for saving $100 billion sometime in the 1980s, and he says a colleague, Dr May, has one in his file too. He tells it as proof that the government valued the psychic work.
letter-on-sullivan-s-death-sent-to-the-f: Eric Burlison, a US congressman, says that he and his team took information about the death of a man named Sullivan, linked to the UFO whistleblower David Grusch, and wrote a letter about it to the FBI through the House Oversight Committee, the part of Congress that investigates the government. He says they were told the letter had been sent, but later found out the FBI never got it. He tells it to suggest that inquiries on this subject get quietly blocked.
letter-to-the-pope-the-night-john-paul-i: Rolf Mowatt-Larssen, a former senior officer at the CIA, the US foreign intelligence agency, says the Virgin Mary told him to write a letter to Pope John Paul II. He says it took him a long time to write, which he regrets, and that he finally sent it to the Vatican and got a reply. The story ties this to the night the Pope died in 2005, when he was at the Hotel Crillon in Paris, and he reproduces the letter in his book. If true, it would mean a message from a religious vision reached the head of the Catholic Church.
letter-to-william-shockley-recommending-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in the 1950s Claude Shannon, the mathematician who founded information theory, wrote a letter to William Shockley, a physicist who helped invent the transistor, recommending someone to him. According to Michels, the person turns out to be L. Ron Hubbard, the founder of Scientology. He tells it to show how close fringe figures were to top scientists of the time.
letters-from-the-vatican-and-the-orthodo: A man identified only as Ralph, who has written a book, says on Jesse Michels's podcast that he sent copies of it to religious leaders. He says he got letters back from the Vatican, the headquarters of the Catholic Church, and from the leadership of the Orthodox Church in Istanbul, Turkey. He tells it to show that his ideas reached, and drew replies from, the highest levels of two great churches.
letters-to-mitre-rand-and-mit-lincoln-la: Eric Burlison, a US congressman, says that in 2026 he has been sending letters to MITRE, RAND and MIT Lincoln Laboratory, private research groups that do science and defense work for the US government. He mentions this while talking about the government's release of UFO files, and he means that he is pressing these groups for whatever they know about the subject.
levenda-as-the-model-for-johnny-depp-s-c: Peter Levenda, an author presented on Jesse Michels's podcast as a historian of the CIA, says he was the model for Johnny Depp's character in The Ninth Gate, a late 1990s film made by Roman Polanski. He links it to things he says happened to him in New York in the 1970s, and says people around Depp were saying the film's story actually happened.
levenda-s-archival-assessment-of-mj-12-a: A researcher, Peter Levenda, talks about the MJ-12 documents, a set of papers said to date from the 1940s and 1950s that describe a secret group called Majestic 12. He says that after looking at them against records in Washington, at the National Archives and the Library of Congress, the documents look real to him, and he says he discussed them with a man named Stanton Friedman at a gathering called Contact in the Desert. If the papers are genuine, a secret group of officials would have been handling UFO matters at the highest level.
levenda-s-unholy-alliance-on-nazis-and-t: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, describes Unholy Alliance, a book by the author Peter Levenda about Nazi Germany in the 1930s and 1940s. According to Michels, Levenda writes that the Nazis aligned themselves with the "tall whites" or "Nordics," tall, pale, human-looking beings described in some UFO stories, and that some kind of secret technology was involved. If true, it would mean non-human beings shaped one of history's darkest regimes.
levin-s-decapitated-flatworms-keep-their: A biologist known for unusual ideas, Rupert Sheldrake, speaking on podcast host Jesse Michels' show in 2024, describes experiments by Michael Levin, a biologist at Tufts University in Massachusetts. Sheldrake says Levin trained flatworms to respond to certain stimuli, then cut their heads off, and that the worms kept what they had learned after regrowing. If true, memory would not be stored only in the brain.
levin-s-flatworm-experiments-read-as-mor: A biologist known for unusual ideas, Rupert Sheldrake, speaking on podcast host Jesse Michels' show in 2024, offers his own explanation for flatworm experiments by Michael Levin, a biologist at Tufts University, in which worms seem to keep learned memories after losing their heads. Sheldrake says it is "morphic resonance", his idea that living things tune in to similar forms from the past, so the regrown worms are resonating with their own earlier, intact selves. If true, nature would carry a kind of memory outside the body.
levitating-metallic-sphere-above-a-podiu: Randy Anderson, a man who says he worked at Naval Surface Warfare Center Crane, a Navy research base in Indiana, says that around 2014 he was shown a metal sphere about the size of a basketball. He says it simply floated above a podium with nothing holding it up. In another telling he places it in an area he calls Off-World Technology and dates it only to the 2010s; if true, it would mean the military holds objects that defy ordinary physics.
lewis-black-at-epstein-s-mansion-and-the: A comedian, Kurt Metzger, retells a story he says comes from another comedian, Lewis Black, by way of a third, Bobby Slayton, about a visit to the New York mansion of the financier Jeffrey Epstein. In Metzger's telling, Black walked in and saw a marker board covered in what looked like football plays, and the story goes on to involve Israel's defence minister. Metzger tells it as a hint of what was really going on behind Epstein's doors.
lewis-chase-reports-to-air-force-headqua: Robert Salas, a former US Air Force officer, says that in March 1967 at Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana, a base that held nuclear missiles, an officer named Lewis Chase decided he had to report what had happened there during the UFO events Salas describes. According to Salas, Chase sent a telegram to Air Force headquarters and also reported to Edward Condon, the scientist who led an Air Force funded study of UFOs. If so, it would mean the incident was officially passed up the chain at the time.
liberation-times-piece-on-the-legacy-pro: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, points to an article by the reporter Christopher Sharp in Liberation Times, an online news outlet, describing what Michels calls the network of secret long-running UFO programs, involving the US Department of Energy and the CIA's work on stopping the spread of weapons. Michels says the article lays out the chain of command for this UFO effort and names Glenn Gaffney, the CIA's director of science and technology, as a key figure, which would mean the programme reaches into senior intelligence posts.
liberman-s-goldfish-centrifuge-and-freez: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells of a Soviet scientist, Efim Liberman, who he says did an experiment with four goldfish, spinning them in a centrifuge, a fast-spinning machine, and freezing them. Michels brings it up while talking about the idea that the brain may work in quantum ways, even in ways linked to time, with much of Liberman's thinking centered on that experiment.
lidar-detected-pyramid-in-the-amazon-202: A writer on lost ancient civilisations, Graham Hancock, said on a 2022 podcast that an archaeologist from the University of Exeter, in England, told him about a find in the Colombian Amazon. Using lidar, a laser scan from the air that can map the ground beneath the trees, the team is said to be sure it has found an enormous pyramid in the middle of the rainforest. If true, it would mean a large building culture once lived where people thought there was only jungle.
lidar-reveals-lost-amazon-cities-and-geo: A writer on lost ancient civilisations, Graham Hancock, says that lidar, a laser scan from the air that can see the ground through treetops, is turning up big surprises in the Amazon rainforest, as shown in the second season of his TV series Ancient Apocalypse. He says the Amazon was once home to tens of millions of people who fed themselves, with huge permanent cities and vast, very precise geometric earthworks that can only be seen whole from above. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, later repeated a shorter version, mentioning only the shapes popping out of the scans, and it matters because it would mean the jungle once held a great civilisation.
light-flashes-answered-by-a-stationary-l: Mario Woods, a guard at a nuclear missile control post called November-1 in the missile field of Ellsworth Air Force Base in South Dakota, says that in 1977 he saw a light hanging still over the prairie. He says he flicked his own lights off and on three times, and after a minute or so the distant light blinked back the same way, which sent shivers up his spine because it meant, as he put it, they could see him. He tells it as the lead-up to the abduction he says he and fellow airmen went through.
light-over-the-mesa-green-light-missing-: An unnamed camper, out with a group on a mesa near Aztec, New Mexico, where some say a craft once crashed, says he and a friend watched a light make a sharp 90 degree turn. He says that as they walked back to the group it was suddenly right above them, followed by a green light, a stretch of time none of them could account for, and then Apache military helicopters. If true, it would suggest both something unknown and the military were taking an interest in the site.
lights-around-ellsworth-nuclear-sites-be: Michael Johnson, an airman in the missile field of Ellsworth Air Force Base in South Dakota, says that in 1977 he kept seeing lights out around the nuclear missile sites. He tells it as what came just before the abduction he says he and other airmen went through, which would mean something was watching the nuclear weapons.
lights-filmed-near-brunswick-nuclear-pla: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells of lights filmed in November 2024 right near the Brunswick nuclear power plant, run by the power company Duke Energy, in Southport, North Carolina. In a later episode with Mick West, a well-known UFO skeptic, he calls it unexplained aerial activity near a Duke Energy nuclear site, with the facility named only as Duke Energy. The story matters because it would add to claims that unknown objects take an interest in nuclear sites.
lights-on-a-road-stretch-at-mattibu-gotl: Clas Svahn, a Swedish researcher who collects UFO reports, says there is a place called Mattibu on Gotland, an island in Sweden, where people go to a certain stretch of road at night. According to Svahn, they go there to watch for lights that come wandering along the road, which makes it a local spot where the strange lights are said to keep returning.
lilli-hornig-s-los-alamos-typing-intervi: A researcher, Kevin Knuth, passes on a story from a woman named Lilli Hornig about the 1940s, when she arrived at Los Alamos, the New Mexico laboratory where the atomic bomb was built. According to the story, during her job interview they asked her how fast she could type, and she answered, "They don't teach typing at Harvard."
limestone-cube-erosion-study-on-the-smit: A researcher named Randall Carlson, speaking on the podcast of host Jesse Michels, describes an experiment at the Smithsonian Institution, the big national museum and research body in Washington, D.C. He says scientists put a freshly cut cube of limestone on the Smithsonian's roof and watched how it wore away over many decades. He tells it as a way of showing how fast stone actually erodes, which matters if you are trying to judge how old weathered stonework is.
lincoln-lapaz-studies-green-fireballs-19: Podcast host Jesse Michels says that in 1948 Lincoln LaPaz, a well-known meteor expert at the University of New Mexico, began studying "green fireballs", bright green lights seen in the sky. According to Michels, these fireballs often showed up near nuclear sites and nuclear test explosions. If that is true, it would suggest something was taking an interest in America's early atomic work.
lincoln-s-niagara-speech-on-the-giants-w: A researcher, Tim Alberino, points to a speech about Niagara Falls written by Abraham Lincoln, the American president. He quotes Lincoln as saying that "that ancient species of giants whose bones fill the mounds of America" once gazed on Niagara as we do now, meaning the old earth mounds found across the country. Alberino offers it as a sign that giants were once openly talked about in America.
linda-bradshaw-saw-and-photographed-port: Ross Coulthart, a journalist speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast, says there is allegedly a portal, a kind of doorway to somewhere else, at Bradshaw Ranch near Sedona, Arizona. He says the ranch's former owner, Linda Bradshaw, saw it and took photographs of it, which would make the ranch a place where something comes and goes.
linda-brown-s-2014-review-of-tim-taylor-: Podcast host Jesse Michels tells this story about Townsend Brown, a scientist he describes as building flying-saucer-like devices for the government long ago. Michels says a man named Tim Taylor wrote an autobiography, Launch Fever, in 2003, and that Brown's daughter Linda wrote a review of it, in 2014 by one account and on Amazon, before anyone knew who Taylor was. He tells it as a sign of a hidden link between Taylor and the Brown family.
linda-brown-sees-a-100-000-check-from-th: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, in a film about an inventor named Townsend Brown, who he says built flying-saucer-like devices, relays a memory from Brown's daughter, Linda. She remembers that in the 1970s, while visiting her father in Atherton, California, she saw a check for $100,000 from his foundation made out to Stanford, the nearby university and research institute. It is told as a sign that Brown's work was quietly tied to serious research.
linda-jones-and-grass-growing-rapidly-wh: Mike Masters, a researcher who argues that so-called aliens might be humans from the future, tells of a woman named Linda Jones in Manchester, England. He says she was running with her children to get away from a UFO, and the grass grew quickly under her feet as she ran. He uses it as a hint that time itself might behave strangely around these objects.
linda-tripp-placed-beside-monica-lewinsk: A researcher, Steven Greer, says that in the 1990s a woman named Linda Tripp, whom he describes as an army intelligence and NSA person (the NSA is the US National Security Agency, which handles electronic spying), was placed on purpose right beside Monica Lewinsky, the young White House staffer linked to President Bill Clinton. In Greer's telling it was a setup: when Clinton was asked about the affair he lied under oath, and that led to his impeachment. If true, it would mean hidden forces inside the intelligence world arranged the fall of a sitting president.
little-a-le-inn-we-made-a-digital-copy-2: A documentary filmmaker named James Fox says he went to the Little A'Le'Inn, a small diner and motel in Rachel, Nevada, asking about a VHS tape made by a man named Chuck Clark. According to Fox, the woman there scoffed and asked if he really thought they were stupid enough not to have made a digital copy. The story suggests the footage on that tape has been kept safe.
little-glowing-glass-like-being-with-a-t: Chris Bledsoe, a man from North Carolina who says he draws UFOs to him, says that in 2007 he met a small glowing being in the woods near his house. He describes it as looking like it was made of glass, and he ties a triangle to the encounter. If true, it would be a direct meeting with a being that is not human.
little-progress-reverse-engineering-reco: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, gives his own view on the idea that the United States has recovered crafts not made by humans, starting around 1947. He says he doesn't think much has been done with what was recovered, and compares it to a caveman holding a USB drive: owning the thing without any idea how to use it. If true, it would mean the technology is beyond what our scientists can understand.
little-sophia-doll-used-to-map-children-: A comedian, Kurt Metzger, talks about a talking doll called Little Sophia, which he says was sold as a way to get children thinking about science and technology. In his telling, the doll was used in Africa to map children's brains, which would mean children were being studied without knowing it.
livelsberger-email-gives-area-51-coordin: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, describes what he calls a very strange email sent in 2025 by a man named Matthew Livelsberger. According to Michels, the email gives the map coordinates of "America's gravitic propulsion operations center", meaning a base for craft that move by controlling gravity, and those coordinates point to Area 51, a secret military test site in Nevada. If true, it would mean such a programme exists and is run from there.
livermore-s-nuclear-pumped-space-laser-l: John Harrington, who says he was a senior official at the US Department of Energy, describes a 1980s weapons project at Lawrence Livermore Laboratory, a government weapons lab. He says the plan was to set off a nuclear explosion in space and focus its energy through a lens about the size of a thumbnail, and that the physicist Edward Teller sat on his couch one afternoon, showed him the lens and called the program Excalibur. He tells it to show how far secret weapons work went in those years.
living-at-arthur-young-s-institute-for-t: Jeffrey Mishlove, a researcher of psychic experience who earned a PhD on the subject, says that in the 1970s the inventor and thinker Arthur Young came into his life and invited him to live with him. He says he moved into the Institute for the Study of Consciousness, a center Young had set up in Berkeley, California, and he tells it as a turning point in his path into studying the mind.
living-crystal-orb-shown-in-psychologist: Jordan Jose, who says he was taken into a secret UFO program as a child, says that around 2008 he was shown a crystal orb in a local psychologist's office in western New York. He says it had a clear outer shell, but the inside, for lack of a better word, was alive. If true, it would mean something living and unknown was being shown to a child in an ordinary office.
living-reptilians-from-a-crash-were-shot: In a clip shown on a podcast episode about a former US energy secretary, an unnamed speaker is asked what happened to living reptile-like beings said to have survived the crash of a craft. He answers that they died, that they were killed. If true, it would mean living non-human beings were captured and deliberately put to death.
lizard-dna-sequences-pulled-for-the-hill: Martin Shkreli, a former drug company executive, says that in 2017 he offered a reward for a strand of the politician Hillary Clinton's hair as a joke, playing on the idea spread by the writer David Icke that some leaders are secretly lizard people. Shkreli says he went to BLAST, a genetic database run by the NIH, the US government's health research agency, and pulled out lizard DNA sequences to go with the stunt.
lk-99-room-temperature-superconductor-pa: In 2023, a research team linked to South Korea put out papers about a material called LK-99, which they said was a superconductor at room temperature. That means a material that carries electricity with no loss at all without being chilled to extreme cold, which would change technology if true. A podcast host named Jack says the team was so sure of their results that they published one paper with six authors and then a second with only three, because a Nobel Prize can only be shared by three people.
local-name-of-the-nazca-region-meaning-a: This story is about a place name in the Nazca area of Peru. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says the local name of the region translates to "laboratory for insemination and hybridization," meaning the mixing of different kinds of beings. He credits a book from 2006, without naming it. A researcher, Thierry Jamin, who has worked in Peru, tells it a bit differently. He says the source is a small book from 2004 by a local Nazca author describing sites in the area, and he adds "cloning" to the meaning. The story matters to them because it seems to hint that the region was long linked to the making of hybrid beings.
local-tribal-people-told-not-to-look-tow: Brandon Fugal, the owner of a ranch in Utah known for strange reports, says local tribal people have a warning about it. According to what he was told by people from the nearby Ute Ouray reservation, which is Native American land, their people have been told for generations not even to look toward the property. He tells it as a sign that the place has been feared as unusual long before anyone studied it.
locked-car-found-open-repeatedly-fear-of: This story is set in Las Vegas in 1989 and 1990 and comes from Bob Lazar, a man known for claims about secret work he says he did in the Nevada desert. Lazar says that his car, which he and others locked and checked, was found open again and again. He says they would lock it and test the door because it had happened before, and still it would be open. The fear, as told, was that someone had planted a bomb in the car. A guest named Luigi, on the same podcast episode hosted by Jesse Michels, retells it from a man named Mario, who he says was with Lazar all the time. According to Luigi, Mario said they were scared something would blow up, but he was going through such hard times that he did not care, so he told Lazar to stay back while he started the car himself. If true, it would suggest Lazar was being harassed or threatened over what he knew.
lockheed-divests-a-craft-which-may-end-u: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says his friend Rob Jones, a researcher, has found that Lockheed, the big American aerospace company, eventually handed off a craft it held, he thinks to an investment firm called Veritas Capital. Jones himself says the material is now held by a defense company he names as Peraton (heard on air as 'Paritin' or 'Peritin'), which has offices at Picatinny Arsenal, a US Army research base in New Jersey, and in one telling he dates this from 2008 to the present. If true, it would mean a mysterious craft has quietly passed between private companies.
lockheed-engineer-this-is-what-you-learn: Peter Levenda, an author speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast, relays a story from a book by a man named John Alexander about an engineer at Lockheed, a large American aerospace and defense company. Unlike Ben Rich, a Lockheed figure Levenda describes as open to the subject, this engineer pushed back and said, "you're not supposed to learn about this. This is what you learn about when you die," a remark suggesting the secret goes beyond technology into questions of life and death.
lockheed-executive-admitted-to-fravor-th: A researcher, Steven Greer, says that very recently an executive at Lockheed, a big American aerospace and weapons company, admitted to a Navy fighter pilot named David Fravor that the Tic Tac was theirs. The Tic Tac is the white oval object, shaped like the mint, that Fravor reported meeting. If true, the famous object would be a secret human-made aircraft and not something from elsewhere.
lockheed-martin-coherent-matter-wave-bea: Dave Rossi, a guest on a podcast about advanced physics, says the aerospace and defense company Lockheed Martin holds a patent called a coherent matter wave beam. He says it makes use of the Aharonov-Bohm effect, a quantum physics effect in which particles are influenced by electromagnetic fields in places they never pass through. He brings it up as a sign that a big defense firm is working on exotic physics.
lockheed-martin-divesting-ufo-material-t: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says the journalist George Knapp has said publicly, including before Congress, that in 2008 the defence company Lockheed Martin tried to hand off UFO material to Bigelow Aerospace, a private space company owned by Robert Bigelow. Knapp himself says he confirmed that Bigelow and a colleague from a Pentagon-funded programme studying unexplained phenomena negotiated a deal with senior Lockheed executives for unusual material stored at a facility in California. According to Knapp, that material was not made here, meaning not made by humans, which would be a huge revelation if true.
lockheed-martin-vp-tried-to-bring-the-cr: Jeremy Corbell, a guest on a podcast, says that around 2008 to 2010 a vice president of Lockheed Martin, a major American aerospace and weapons company, tried to get craft and hardware the company had obtained long ago "out the back door." He credits the account to Jim Ryder, Colm Kelleher and James Lacatski. If true, it would mean a private defense company has long been holding recovered craft and that someone inside wanted them out.
lockheed-s-quantum-magnetometer-modelled: A young researcher in quantum physics, Deep Prasad, speaking on podcast host Jesse Michels' show in 2022, says robins sense the Earth's magnetic field through a protein called cry4. He says Lockheed, the big American defense company, studied the physics of these birds and, about six years earlier, built a quantum sensor that copies the trick, which he calls the "dark ice magnetometer", a device for measuring magnetic fields. If true, it would show defense firms quietly turning nature's quantum effects into working technology.
lockheed-skunk-works-and-the-ufo-topic-b: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Ben Rich, a former president of Skunk Works, the most secretive division of the defence company Lockheed Martin, used to call UFOs "unfunded opportunities." Michels connects this to emails from 2016 and 2017, published by WikiLeaks, a site that releases leaked documents, which involve a Skunk Works figure named Rob Weiss and the musician and UFO advocate Tom DeLonge. He tells it because it would suggest the company has a real, quiet interest in UFOs.
lockheed-skunk-works-response-to-grusch-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, talks about how Lockheed Martin, a big defense company, and its secret advanced projects division, known as Skunk Works, answered 2023 testimony to Congress by David Grusch, a former intelligence officer who said the government holds non-human craft. Michels says the company replied only that questions about unexplained aerial phenomena are best answered by the federal government. He finds that answer telling, as if the company were not denying it.
lockheed-ttsa-and-killing-the-schumer-bi: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, suggests a link between Lockheed, a large American defense company, and To The Stars Academy, a UFO research company set up in 2017 by Tom DeLonge. He points to Robert Weiss, director of Skunk Works, Lockheed's secret aircraft design division, and his ties to DeLonge's group, and frames it as part of a wider story about efforts to kill a bill from Senator Chuck Schumer on UFO records. If true, it would mean defense industry insiders were shaping the push for UFO disclosure from behind the scenes.
lockheed-vp-jim-ryder-the-veil-thinning-: A crew member on a podcast says that Jim Ryder, described as a vice president of space systems at the aerospace company Lockheed Martin, talked about "the veil thinning." According to this account, Ryder meant it literally: the veil is the magnetosphere, the magnetic shield around the Earth, which he said is weakening right now. If true, it would tie an old spiritual phrase to a real physical change around the planet.
loeb-s-artificial-light-sail-theory-of-o: A Harvard scientist, Avi Loeb, talks about 'Oumuamua, an odd object that passed through our solar system in 2017 after coming from between the stars. He says every natural explanation offered for its strange behavior needed a kind of rock nobody has ever seen, and in his book Extraterrestrial he argues it may instead be an artificial light sail, a thin sheet pushed along by sunlight. If he is right, it would be a piece of technology built by someone else.
logan-paul-offers-chuck-clark-100-000-fo: James Fox, a UFO investigator and filmmaker, says that around 2022 the internet celebrity Logan Paul offered a man named Chuck Clark, who lives in remote Arizona, $100,000 for a VHS videotape Clark owns. According to Fox, Clark refused to sell, which tells you how much the tape is said to matter to him.
logger-saw-the-same-craft-in-the-area-19: Charlie Foltz, a man who says he saw a strange craft near the Allagash Waterway in Maine in the 1970s, says he was not the only one. According to Foltz, a logger working in that same area also saw the same craft. He tells it as backing from an outside witness for what he and his companions say happened there.
london-bridge-at-lake-havasu-has-childre: Kurt Metzger, a guest on a podcast, repeats a claim he credits to a man named Nathan Reynolds about London Bridge, the old bridge that was moved to Lake Havasu, Arizona, in the 1960s. According to the claim, the Knights of Columbus, a Catholic men's group, held the controlling interest, and the bridge was brought over because there are children walled up inside it. It is told as a sign of dark secrets hidden by powerful groups.
london-drought-and-mishlove-s-first-meet: A researcher of psychic claims named Jeffrey Mishlove says that during a drought in London in the summer of 1976, someone contacted Ted Owens, a man who claimed psychic powers, to end it. Mishlove says Owens was then invited to a conference at the University of London, where Mishlove met him and became his friend, and he names the researchers Hal Puthoff and Russell Targ in the same account. If true, it would be an example of a man said to influence the weather with his mind.
long-delay-echoes-behind-sagan-s-contact: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that the astronomer Carl Sagan's novel Contact, about humans receiving a message from aliens, may be drawing on long delay echoes. These, Michels says, were strange radio signals heard coming back seconds after they were sent, reported in the 1920s and 30s when radio was new. If true, some have taken them as a hint that something out in space was answering.
long-delay-echoes-rise-when-earth-moon-l: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, talks about long delay echoes, radio signals that seem to come back seconds after they are sent, first noticed in 1927. He says one study found a statistically significant rise in these echoes when the Earth-Moon L5 point, a stable spot in space where an object can sit balanced between the pull of Earth and the Moon, was above the horizon. If true, it would hint that something parked at that spot might be bouncing the signals back.
long-delay-radio-echoes-heard-by-norwegi: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says the story begins in 1927, when Norwegian shortwave radio operators started to notice something odd: their signals seemed to come back as echoes long after they were sent. He links the story to Karl Stormer, a Norwegian scientist of the time. If the echoes came from something out in space, it could mean an unknown object was near Earth.
long-distance-healing-in-australia-over-: A man named Chris Bledsoe, who says strange things happen around him, told podcast host Jesse Michels that he has seen healing happen at a distance. He says he has seen it many times, including once in Australia, over the phone. If true, it would mean someone could be healed without anyone being in the room with them.
long-island-crash-near-moriches-bay-1989: A UFO historian, Richard Dolan, speaking on podcast host Jesse Michels' show in 2025, mentions a story of a crash on Long Island, New York, near Moriches Bay, which he says was "supposed to be" in 1989. He connects it with the names John Ford and Elaine Douglas. If true, a craft of unknown origin would have come down near New York.
lonnie-zamora-never-the-same-after-socor: James Fox, a guest on a podcast, recalls speaking with the wife of Lonnie Zamora, a man who reported an encounter near Socorro, New Mexico, in 1964. Fox says she told him, "I don't know what happened when he looked at that creature, but he was never the same." In this telling the encounter left a lasting mark on the man who saw it.
lonnie-zamora-s-socorro-landing-1964: On April 24th, 1964, in Socorro, New Mexico, a police officer named Lonnie Zamora says he saw a craft land. A UFO investigator and filmmaker, James Fox, has looked into the case. He draws on the researcher Ray Stanford, on a work titled Socorro Saucer in a Pentagon Pantry, and on J. Allen Hynek, a scientist. According to a podcast host, Jesse Michels, Zamora saw an egg-shaped craft come down, said to have little legs, and later found burnt plants where it had been. Fox adds that Zamora came face to face with one of the beings and locked eyes with it. So the story comes from Fox, an investigator going through the record, and from the host repeating it in several episodes. If true, it would be a close sighting of a landed craft and its crew by a police officer.
lonnie-zamora-sighting-near-nuclear-site: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, brings up Lonnie Zamora, a police officer who reported seeing a strange craft near Socorro, New Mexico, in 1964. Michels says the sighting happened a couple of miles from nuclear sites. He raises it as part of a pattern linking such sightings to nuclear places.
looking-for-city-lights-on-proxima-b-202: A Harvard scientist, Avi Loeb, says that in 2021 he wrote a paper with a Stanford undergraduate arguing that the James Webb Space Telescope, a large new space telescope, could search for city lights on the dark side of Proxima b, a planet that circles a nearby star called Proxima Centauri. If such lights were found, they would be a sign of a civilization there.
lookout-mountain-cia-facility-in-laurel-: Eric Weinstein, a researcher, agrees with podcast host Jesse Michels that Lookout Mountain, in the Laurel Canyon area of Los Angeles, was a facility of the CIA, America's foreign intelligence agency. Weinstein links the place to a wider 1960s history of drugs, the government, the Vietnam War and spying. It comes up as an example of secret government work hidden in plain sight.
lookout-mountain-laboratory-as-manhattan: A writer named Paul Schatzkin, who wrote about the inventor Townsend Brown, says on podcast host Jesse Michels' show in 2024 that Lookout Mountain Laboratory, a secret site in the Laurel Canyon hills of Los Angeles, was more than it seemed. He says newly released information shows it served as the film labs for the Manhattan Project, the American effort to build the atomic bomb during the Second World War, around 1942 to 1945. If true, the site's secret history would reach back to the bomb itself.
loose-stone-samples-tested-in-israel-tur: Dennis Asberg, a treasure hunter, led a team that found an odd shape on the floor of the Baltic Sea between Sweden and Finland, which some have compared to a sunken craft. He says that loose stones taken from the site, starting around 2012, were tested in Israel and found to be basalt, a volcanic rock. He tells it as one of the puzzles about what the object really is.
looting-at-eridu-and-the-campaign-to-sav: A guest named Matt, speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast, talks about Eridu, an ancient city site in Iraq. He says he found many photographs from the last ten years showing locals going into the site and plundering it, and that this pushed a campaign to save it. He tells it because, as he sees it, the site's history could be lost before anyone studies it.
lore-of-lockheed-and-northrop-crash-retr: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, describes a body of stories in UFO circles claiming that defense companies such as Lockheed and Northrop have recovered crashed craft. According to this lore, they did it without proper government supervision or oversight. If true, it would mean private firms hold such secrets beyond the reach of elected officials.
lorentz-regauging-of-maxwell-s-quaternio: A guest named Dave Rossi, on a 2025 episode of podcast host Jesse Michels' show titled "Aliens Taught Me Advanced Physics!", says that in the early 1900s the physicist Lorentz (Hendrik Lorentz, whom he calls Heinrich) did something called "symmetrical regauging" of the equations of James Clerk Maxwell, the 19th-century scientist who described electricity and magnetism. Rossi says Maxwell first wrote them using quaternions, a four-part kind of number, and he tells it as a turning point in how that physics came to be written down.
lorie-barnes-visited-by-blue-dwarfs-whil: A writer, Whitley Strieber, passes on the story of a woman named Lorie Barnes, who he says was visited by small blue beings in 1954 while she was pregnant. According to the story, they told her, "We're interested in the girl child you're carrying." If true, it would suggest these beings take a special interest in certain people even before they are born.
los-alamos-disinformation-as-a-model-for: Eric Weinstein, a researcher, points to Los Alamos, the New Mexico lab where the US built the atomic bomb in the 1940s, and cites the scientist Harold Urey. He says the project used misleading paperwork so that outsiders would not learn that plutonium and uranium were the two radioactive elements it cared about most. He offers it as a model for how a secret programme today, including one about UFOs, might hide what it is really doing.
los-alamos-hiring-during-a-nuclear-arms-: Greg Bishop, a writer on UFO topics, relays what a woman connected to Los Alamos told him; Los Alamos is the US government lab in New Mexico where nuclear weapons are designed. According to her, there is a huge nuclear arms race going on right now in the 2020s, and they are building bombs like mad, which is why the lab is hiring.
los-alamos-insider-surfaces-that-solid-o: Mario Woods, an Air Force veteran who says he was abducted by non-human beings, relays what someone connected to Los Alamos, the US government weapons lab in New Mexico, told him. According to that person, there are metal surfaces that can be manipulated so that solid things pass through them, in or out. If true, it would point to technology far beyond anything known.
los-alamos-insider-their-propulsion-syst: Mario Woods, an Air Force veteran who says he was abducted by non-human beings, says a man connected to Los Alamos, the US government weapons lab in New Mexico, told him something striking. According to that man, the propulsion systems of these non-human craft are not built, they are grown. If true, it would mean the craft are something closer to living things than machines.
los-alamos-tiger-team-security-test-fail: A man named Bob Lazar, talking with podcast host Jesse Michels, passes on something he says he was told about Los Alamos, the government laboratory in New Mexico, around 1990 or 1991. According to Lazar, a "tiger team", a group brought in to test a site's security by trying to get past it, came to check security there, and the place failed very badly. He tells it as a sign of how weak security was at one of the country's most sensitive sites.
los-alamos-working-group-concludes-ufos-: A guest named Jay Anderson, on podcast host Jesse Michels's show, says a man named Oke Shannon told him about a working group at Los Alamos National Laboratory, a US government research lab in New Mexico, sometime in the 2000s. According to Anderson, the group concluded that UFOs are interdimensional objects coming down into a lower dimensional plane, an idea he links to Flatland, a story about beings who live in only two dimensions. If true, it would mean government scientists believed the objects come from beyond our ordinary space.
los-alamosbattelle-nitinol-contract-of-1: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that some of the most interesting evidence he has found for Roswell, the 1947 claim that a crashed craft was recovered in New Mexico, is a 1949 contract between Los Alamos, the New Mexico nuclear weapons lab, and the Battelle Memorial Institute, a research organisation. He links the contract to Nitinol, a nickel and titanium metal that returns to its original shape. To Michels, it would suggest that strange material from a crash was being studied.
loss-of-the-marine-sulphur-queen-1963: Mario Woods, a former guard at a nuclear site, told podcast host Jesse Michels about the Marine Sulphur Queen, a ship that he says sank at sea in 1963 after leaving port in Port Arthur, Texas. He says it was the first ship he ever went on, as a five-year-old child, which ties his own life to the ship's loss.
lost-hiker-meets-a-woman-who-went-missin: A researcher named Jason Jorjani, on podcast host Jesse Michels's show, relays a story he credits to a man he calls David Pitus and to Missing 411, a series of books about strange disappearances in the wild. As Jorjani tells it, a hiker lost in a US forest met a woman whose description fit someone who had gone missing in that same place a decade or more earlier. If true, it would hint that missing people can turn up somewhere outside normal time.
lost-submarines-like-the-uss-connecticut: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, mentions in passing that there are lost or troubled submarines, like the USS Connecticut, a US Navy submarine, where, in his words, we don't really know what happened. He raises it in a talk about strange things under the ocean, implying that something unknown might be down there.
lot-s-angelic-visitors-extract-him-befor: This story comes from Genesis, the first book of the Bible. A researcher, Tim Alberino, retells it: Lot, the nephew of Abraham, meets angelic beings who come to get him and his family out before the city of Sodom is destroyed. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells it in his own way. In his version, two angels walk into Sodom the night before fire falls on the city, and he does not mention them leading Lot's family away. Both retell the scripture rather than citing a witness. They raise it because they read the angels as possible non-human visitors at work in ancient times.
lou-baldin-s-day-aboard-a-ship-with-milt: A UFO historian named Richard Dolan, on podcast host Jesse Michels's show, retells the story of Lou Baldin from Baldin's book A Day with an Extraterrestrial. Dolan says that in a park near where he lived, sometime in the 2000s, Baldin was paralyzed and floated up into a ship, where he spent a day with a being called Milton. If true, it would be a direct, long meeting with a non-human visitor.
lou-baldin-s-in-league-with-a-ufo-1947: Richard Dolan, a historian who writes about UFOs, talks about a man named Lou Baldin. Dolan says that in the mid 1990s Baldin wrote a book called In League with a UFO, telling of his own claimed experiences, with a story that reaches back as far as 1947.
lou-elizondo-told-kirkpatrick-where-the-: This story is about a film said to show a UFO shooting down a dummy nuclear warhead during a missile test over Big Sur, on the California coast, in the 1960s. A researcher of UFOs and nuclear weapons, Robert Hastings, says a man named Kurt McConnell emailed him about it. According to Hastings, McConnell drove Lou Elizondo, a former Pentagon official, to an interview with the Pentagon's current UFO office. On the way back, Elizondo told McConnell that he had told Sean Kirkpatrick, an official there, that he had seen the Big Sur film. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, also says that Elizondo saw the footage, though he leaves out Kirkpatrick and McConnell. Hastings also names Bob Jacobs, a man linked to the film. If true, it would mean the film still exists inside the government and officials have been told where it is.
low-s-handwritten-note-hippler-blames-em: This story is about a handwritten note from 1967 and the Condon Committee, a scientific study of UFOs carried out for the US Air Force in the late 1960s. A former Air Force officer, Robert Salas, says a note written by Robert Low, an organiser of that study, records a talk with an Air Force colonel named Robert Hippler. According to Salas, Hippler told Low that the missile shutdowns of that time came from an EMP, a burst of electromagnetic energy, released by nuclear testing. Salas also names Roy Craig, another person on the study. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells the same thing, but he gets it from a 2025 Wall Street Journal article and not from the note itself. He says the colonel blamed EMP fallout from a nuclear blast. The story matters to its tellers because, if true, an Air Force officer was offering an ordinary cause for an event that the witnesses link to UFOs.
luc-montagnier-on-electromagnetic-inform: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, points to Luc Montagnier, a French scientist who won the Nobel Prize. Michels says that at the end of his life Montagnier argued that electromagnetism, the force behind light and radio, is important for passing information within DNA, the molecule that carries our genes. Michels uses this to suggest that life may communicate in ways science does not yet accept.
lucille-ball-hears-the-radio-through-a-t: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, retells a story about Lucille Ball, the American TV comedian, linked to a source called The Telepathy Tapes. According to Michels, after she got a tooth filling she was driving one day and began hearing the radio playing inside her head. He tells it as a sign that the human body can pick up signals directly.
luckman-book-s-alien-drawing-matches-a-b: A UFO researcher named Grant Cameron, on podcast host Jesse Michels's show, relays a claim from Michael Luckman about a 1970s book called UFOs: Past, Present and Future, which was tied to Bob Emenegger and Alan Sandler. According to Cameron, a drawing of an alien in that book is exactly the same being as one shown in an image held at the British Museum in London, and he says he sent the host the photo. If true, it would suggest the same beings have been pictured since long ago.
lue-elizondo-s-book-on-anti-gravity-bubb: Eric Burlison, a US congressman, told podcast host Jesse Michels about a book by Lue Elizondo, a former Pentagon official. Burlison says the book explains that the odd shapes of reported craft make sense if they carry some kind of anti-gravity device that wraps them in a bubble. If true, it would mean the shapes are a clue to how these craft fly.
lue-elizondo-s-superiors-who-saw-the-phe: Mario Woods, a former guard at a nuclear site who says he was abducted, tells podcast host Jesse Michels about a book by Lue Elizondo, who once worked in a small Pentagon office that studied unexplained aerial reports. Woods says he found the part where Elizondo describes some of his superiors seeing the phenomenon as demonic. If true, it would mean some officials treated UFOs as a spiritual threat, not just a technical one.
luigi-s-company-attacked-court-demand-fo: A businessman known as Luigi, based in Montreal, says that in the 2020s his company was attacked ferociously for more than a year and a half, nearly dropping to zero. He says nobody knows this, and he points to a court document demanding his communications with Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked on alien spacecraft. He tells it as a sign of the pressure that came from being linked to Lazar.
luis-alvarez-muon-scan-of-khafre-pyramid: A researcher who goes by Luke Caverns says that Luis Alvarez, a physicist who worked on the Manhattan Project, the US wartime effort to build the atomic bomb, took a team to Egypt in the 1960s. He says they scanned the Khafre pyramid at Giza, using muons, tiny particles from space that pass through rock and can reveal hidden chambers. The podcast host Jesse Michels tells it twice, once saying Alvarez x-rayed the pyramids in the 1950s and once placing it in the 1970s, and neither time does he name the pyramid. People tell it because, if true, it shows a top nuclear scientist was searching the pyramids for hidden spaces.
luke-s-theory-old-kingdom-pharaohs-were-: A researcher of ancient sites, Luke Caverns, speaking on podcast host Jesse Michels' show in 2025, says the pharaohs of Egypt's Old Kingdom, the early age when the great pyramids were built, were never buried in their pyramids. He says their real tombs lie to the south, near Abydos, and suggests a later pharaoh, Amenemhat III, knew this. If true, the pyramids would not be the tombs they are usually taken to be.
luke-s-visit-down-the-osiris-shaft: A researcher named Luke Caverns told podcast host Jesse Michels that he went down the Osiris shaft, a deep shaft under the causeway, the old stone road, at Giza in Egypt. He says someone known as Land of Kem took him there and showed him how you go down and the shaft drops further. He tells it as part of his case that the pyramids are not what most people think.
lunar-dust-prevented-a-fourth-eva-for-ap: Charles Buer, speaking as a witness on Jesse Michels's podcast, passes on what he says he was told about the Apollo Moon landings of 1969 to 1972. According to Buer, the Moon's dust caused the astronauts so much trouble that they could not do a fourth EVA, meaning a fourth trip outside the lander to work on the surface. He brings it up as an example of how hard the Moon's surface is to work on.
lunar-laser-reflectors-1969: James Fox, speaking as a witness on Jesse Michels's podcast, repeats what he says a man named Ben told him about the Apollo Moon missions of 1969 to 1972. According to Fox, Ben said that we can shine a laser onto some of the equipment the astronauts left on the Moon's surface. He tells it as a way of showing that people really did go there and left things behind that can still be found.
lunar-layers-are-inverted-like-an-excava: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that on the Moon the lower layers of material are actually newer than the layers above them, the reverse of what you would normally expect. He says this pattern matches an excavation site, where dug-up material gets piled on top. If true, it would hint that someone once dug into the Moon.
lunar-mascons-forced-apollo-orbit-correc: A guest on Jesse Michels's podcast, in an episode about secrets of the Moon, talks about "mascons", patches of the Moon where its gravity is unevenly strong. The guest says the Apollo spacecraft, NASA's crewed Moon missions of the 1960s and 70s, ran into trouble with their orbits and landings because of this. It is told as a sign that the Moon's inside is stranger than it looks.
lunar-transient-phenomena-outgassing-and: Lunar transient phenomena are short-lived flashes, glows, clouds or changes that people say they have seen on the surface of the Moon. A researcher named Randall Carlson, on Jesse Michels's podcast, says there are hundreds of recorded examples. According to him, they include the Moon giving off gases such as carbon dioxide and water vapor. A different guest on a later episode tells it another way. lunch-with-stubblebine-about-buchanan-s-: A former Army sergeant named Lyn Buchanan tells a podcast host, Jesse Michels, about a lunch in the 1980s with an Army general, Albert Stubblebine, whom he calls Bert. lunch-with-von-daniken-attended-by-joe-r: Podcast host Jesse Michels says he once organized a lunch with Erich von Däniken, a writer known for saying that beings from elsewhere visited ancient people. He says Joe Rogan, a famous podcast host, came to that lunch.
lundahl-s-cuban-missile-crisis-briefing-: A UFO researcher, Grant Cameron, speaking on podcast host Jesse Michels' show, says that during the 1962 Cuban missile crisis, the standoff over Soviet missiles in Cuba, a man named Arthur Lundahl briefed President John F. Kennedy. Cameron says Lundahl got an award from Kennedy for that work, and he brings it up because Lundahl is a figure in his account of who knew about UFOs inside government.
lyn-buchanan-army-psychic-spy-behind-the: Podcast host Jesse Michels says the character Cassidy in The Men Who Stare at Goats, a film about US Army soldiers trained in psychic powers, is based on a real man named Lyn Buchanan. Michels describes Buchanan as a well-known army psychic spy and remote viewer, someone said to see distant places with the mind alone, and says he recently interviewed him, which would mean the film's odd premise has a real army program behind it.
lyn-buchanan-brought-to-an-underground-s: A researcher and philosopher named Jason Jorjani, on Jesse Michels's podcast, passes on a story he says came from a man named Lyn Buchanan. According to Jorjani, Buchanan was taken to a facility deep underground in California, at a time the story does not give. lyn-buchanan-met-by-three-nordic-men-at-: Jason Jorjani, a researcher, relays a story he credits to a man named Lyn Buchanan.
