lyn-buchanan-met-with-an-alien-as-a-remo: A writer named Greg Bishop, speaking on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, says that Lyn Buchanan told him something striking around 2016. Buchanan is described as an Army remote viewer, meaning someone trained by the military to try to see distant places or hidden things with the mind alone. Bishop says Buchanan told him he had once met with an alien, probably at a military base, which would mean the Army's mind-spying work touched on contact with beings from elsewhere.
lynda-bird-johnson-says-lbj-valued-georg: Harold Malmgren, who presents himself as a former advisor to US presidents, says on Jesse Michels's podcast that he heard something from President Lyndon Johnson's daughter, Lynda Bird Johnson. According to Malmgren, she told him that her father really valued a man named George Ball during the 1960s in Washington. He tells it to show how close he was to the people at the top of the government.
macarthur-s-1955-west-point-interplaneta: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in 1955 the American general Douglas MacArthur gave a speech at West Point, the US Army's officer academy in New York. According to Michels, MacArthur told the cadets that "the next war will be an interplanetary war." Michels raises it because, if MacArthur meant it, a top military leader was openly picturing conflict beyond Earth decades ago.
machine-based-and-person-based-uap-summo: A former helicopter pilot named Jake Barber, who says he once flew a recovered UFO, told a podcast host, Jesse Michels, that there are two ways to summon unidentified craft: one using machines and one using people. Barber says both have been proven to work and that his group is still working with them. If true, it would mean people can call these craft on purpose.
mack-and-sheehan-s-plan-to-train-repeat-: A lawyer named Dan Sheehan tells a podcast host, Jesse Michels, that before 2004 he and a Harvard psychiatrist, John Mack, who studied people reporting alien abductions, planned to train people who had repeated encounters with non-human beings. Sheehan says the training was to use holotropic breathing, a deep, fast breathing method meant to bring on altered states of mind. The idea, as he tells it, was to help these people handle and perhaps guide their encounters.
mack-s-mother-sends-him-to-bud-hopkins-1: Dan Sheehan, a guest on Jesse Michels's podcast, recounts how a man named John Mack came to meet a man named Budd Hopkins, sometime in the 1980s or 1990s. According to Sheehan, it was Mack's mother who sent him, and that is how Mack ended up talking with Hopkins. He tells it as the origin of how Mack got drawn into the subject of UFOs.
mack-used-grof-s-holotropic-breathwork-t: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in the 1990s John Mack, a researcher who worked with people who said aliens had taken them, borrowed a method from Stanislav Grof called holotropic breathwork, a deep, fast breathing practice meant to bring on altered states of mind. According to Michels, Mack used it with these so-called abductees to help them recall their experiences, which would matter because it suggests a way of reaching memories people could not otherwise reach.
madden-s-turn-to-ufos-2017-openness-and-: A philosopher named James Madden tells a podcast host, Jesse Michels, that like many people he got pulled into the UFO subject around 2017, when it suddenly felt acceptable to talk about it. He says that in the summer of 2021 he was watching The X-Files, a TV show about government UFO secrets, with his kids right when the Pentagon held its first big press event on the topic. He tells it as the turning point that made him take the subject seriously.
maeterlinck-s-the-cloud-that-lifted-fore: A researcher and author named Peter Levenda, speaking on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, points to a play called The Cloud That Lifted by Maurice Maeterlinck, a Belgian writer who also wrote The Blue Bird. Levenda says the play seems to foretell the 1963 killing of President John F. Kennedy in Dallas, Texas, and he brings up Lee Harvey Oswald, the man accused of the shooting, alongside it. If true, it would suggest that some writers somehow glimpse future events.
mafia-enforcement-in-malmgren-s-rhode-is: A former advisor to US presidents named Harold Malmgren tells a podcast host, Jesse Michels, about growing up in Rhode Island in the 1940s, around Providence and Narragansett Bay. He says that mafia enforcers would come in, grab a man, take him outside and beat him badly, and he laughs as he recalls it. He tells it as a picture of the rough world he came from.
magellan-radar-finds-metallic-snow-on-ve: A physicist named Kevin Knuth, who worked at NASA, the US space agency, tells a podcast host, Jesse Michels, that he was at NASA in the 1990s when the Magellan probe was mapping the planet Venus with radar. He says the radar found what looked like metallic snow on the Venusian mountains. He brings it up to show that strange findings turn up in space data.
magenta-case-mussolini-s-rs33-investigat: A researcher who goes by the online name UAPGerb, speaking on podcast host Jesse Michels' show in 2025, tells of a craft said to have crashed in 1933 near Magenta, in northern Italy. He says Benito Mussolini, Italy's dictator, at first thought it was an advanced Nazi, British or American aircraft, but his special investigation group, called RS33, was keen on the idea that it was not human technology and likely later worked with the Nazis. If true, a government would have been studying a non-human craft years before the Second World War.
magenta-craft-as-a-trigger-for-the-axis-: Harald Malmgren, a former adviser to US presidents, talks about the "Magenta craft", an unexplained craft that the tellers link to Italy in the 1930s. He wonders aloud whether it helped push Italy and Germany into forming the Axis, the alliance they led in the Second World War. If so, it would mean a UFO helped shape the road to that war.
magenta-craft-taken-to-nazi-germany-1930: Robert Salas, a former US Air Force officer, talks about the "Magenta craft", an unexplained craft the tellers link to Italy in the 1930s. He says it is reasonable to think the craft was taken to Nazi Germany, where studies were done on it. If true, it would mean Hitler's scientists had their hands on non-human technology.
magonia-people-arrested-at-lyon-agobard-: Jason Jorjani, a philosopher, recalls a story that the researcher Jacques Vallee writes about, set around the 800s in Lyon, France. He says people were said to have arrived from a mysterious place called Magonia, some of them were arrested, and a bishop named Agobard, an early rational thinker, argued that it could not possibly be real. Jorjani tells it as an old example of a strange visitation being explained away by authorities.
maguire-saw-a-ufo: Bob Maguire, who worked as a contractor for the CIA, the US spy agency, told podcast host Jesse Michels that he once saw a UFO, an unidentified flying object. He says that after seeing it he could never go back to how he thought before.
maison-rouge-meeting-1944: A guest named Jason, citing the author Peter Levenda, describes a 1944 meeting in Paris called the Maison Rouge meeting. He says Martin Bormann, one of Hitler's top officials, secretly gathered the leaders of German industry there, and the rooms were swept so no one could listen in. He raises it while tracing where today's UFO secrecy might lead back to, suggesting a hidden network that outlived the war.
majestic-12-as-a-cover-for-continuity-of: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that a man named John Alexander once admitted something to him about Majestic 12, which is said to be a secret group of US officials formed in the 1940s to handle UFO matters. According to Michels, Alexander said Majestic 12 was basically just a cover for continuity of government programs, the secret plans for keeping the US government running through a catastrophe. If true, the famous UFO group would be a front for something else entirely.
majestic-12-briefing-document-1952: Majestic 12 is said to be a secret group of officials formed to handle crashed flying saucers, and the story centres on a document about it. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, calls it the most controversial document in UFO circles: a briefing supposedly written in 1952 for Dwight Eisenhower, who had just been elected president, with Harry Truman also named. Michels, drawing on a UFO researcher named Stanton Friedman, says that if the document is real it proves a flying saucer crashed and the wreckage was recovered. In that telling the story runs from 1947 onward, and a scientist named Donald Menzel is said to have been a member. A researcher who goes by the online name UAPGerb says he is particularly fond of the Eisenhower briefing. He dates the documents from 1947 to 1952 and names other officials in them, James Forrestal and Walter B. Smith.
majestic-12-committee: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, mentions a rumored secret committee in the United States known as Majestic 12. As he puts it, it is talked about in UFO circles as a group connected to the subject, though he gives no dates or details. If such a group existed, it would mean someone in government was quietly overseeing the UFO question.
majestic-12-maji-named-in-an-nro-documen: A researcher named Steven Greer, on Jesse Michels's podcast, talks about the secret group he says controls the UFO secrets. According to Greer, it used to be called Majestic 12, and the latest name he can point to is something like "Magic" (MAJI), which he says he saw on a 1990s document from the NRO, the National Reconnaissance Office, the US agency that runs spy satellites. If true, it would mean the group was still active and still had a name decades later.
majestic-documents-curated-by-ryan-and-b: A researcher named Richard Dolan, speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast, talks about the Majestic documents, a set of papers said to describe a secret US government group that handled UFO matters from the 1940s to the 1960s. Dolan says these papers were gathered and put in order by Ryan Wood and Bob Wood, and that there are page after page of them. He calls them highly sophisticated, extremely so, which he presents as a reason to take them seriously.
major-murphy-tells-vallee-about-1943-sau: A researcher identified as Jason, on Jesse Michels's podcast, points to Messengers of Deception, a book by Jacques Vallée, a well-known investigator of UFO reports. According to that telling, a man called Major Murphy told Vallée to look at 1943 and asked what if someone was already experimenting with flying-saucer technology then, adding that its real advantage was not how it flew but its "psychotronic" effect, meaning its power to affect the human mind. If true, it would mean saucers were valued as tools for influencing people rather than as aircraft.
malign-swarm-like-nhi-in-delonge-s-books: A researcher named Matthew Pines, talking with podcast host Jesse Michels, says that several sources share one idea: some NHI, short for non-human intelligence, may be hostile, and may act like a swarm. He says this idea runs through books by Tom DeLonge, who has written about UFOs, through hints from Lou Elizondo, a former Pentagon official who speaks about UFOs, and through a book called the Cryptoterrestrial Conundrum. If true, it would mean that not everything behind these encounters means humans well.
malmgren-at-the-ida-interviewed-by-the-h: Podcast host Jesse Michels says that Eric Walker was chairman of the Institute for Defense Analyses, a US research group that advises the military, and that a man named Malmgren was part of that institute early on. Michels says he had the chance to interview Malmgren himself. He raises it to tie these figures to the story of a secret government UFO program.
malmgren-diaries-record-meetings-with-ri: A journalist named Ross Coulthart says he has seen the diaries of a man named Harold Malmgren, which he says are now kept somewhere safe and backed up. According to Coulthart, the diaries record many meetings between Malmgren and a man named Richard Bissell, and he raises them as written support for Malmgren's account.
malmgren-goes-public-that-nhi-are-real-2: Matthew Pines, a commentator on Jesse Michels's podcast in late 2024, talks about Harold Malmgren, a man described as a former presidential advisor. According to Pines, Malmgren went public that year saying that NHI, short for non-human intelligence, are real, and that "we have their stuff." It is told because, if true, it would be a senior former insider saying the government holds alien material.
malmgren-helped-shoichiro-toyoda-set-up-: Podcast host Jesse Michels recalls what Harold Malmgren, described as a former presidential advisor, told him about his career. According to Michels, Malmgren said he helped Shoichiro Toyoda, of the Toyota car company, set up Toyota's headquarters in Kentucky in the 1980s. It is told to show how well connected Malmgren was.
malmgren-introduced-to-putin-at-an-arran: A former advisor to US presidents named Harold Malmgren tells a podcast host, Jesse Michels, that someone found him in a crowd and introduced him to Vladimir Putin, later Russia's leader. In one telling he names the introducer as Yevgeny Primakov, a senior Russian official, places it in St. Petersburg in 1992, and says Primakov told him Putin was rising and would soon matter greatly to Russia. malmgren-investigates-for-kennedy-admini: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells of Harold Malmgren, who he says was looking into matters for President Kennedy's administration around 1962. malmgren-links-his-life-and-his-knowledg: A former advisor to US presidents named Harold Malmgren tells a podcast host, Jesse Michels, that after thinking about it many times, he believes time travel is the answer to something in his own life. He points to the 1950s at MIT, a leading science university in Cambridge, Massachusetts, when he says he spoke to a professor with no hesitation at all about things he seemed to already know. malmgren-on-his-deathbed-cia-and-the-maj: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that a former presidential advisor named Harold Malmgren told him from a hospital bed near the end of his life that the CIA, the US spy agency, began tracking him in the 1950s. If true, it would mean a hidden UFO body was watching him for decades.
malmgren-on-office-of-naval-intelligence: Podcast host Jesse Michels says that Harold Malmgren, described as a former presidential advisor, kept stressing one thing about the 1960s and 1970s: the Office of Naval Intelligence, the US Navy's intelligence service, knew far more about UFOs than it let on. malmgren-on-the-secret-committee-1940: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that a man named Harold Malmgren, before he died, spoke about a secret committee said to have run UFO secrecy in the United States from the 1940s and 1950s onward. malmgren-ran-sub-four-minute-miles-after: Podcast host Jesse Michels recalls a story Harold Malmgren, described as a former presidential advisor, told him about the 1950s. malmgren-read-into-legacy-uap-retrieval-: A journalist named Ross Coulthart, on Jesse Michels' podcast, says the diaries of a man named Harold Malmgren record that he was told about a long-running secret effort to recover crashed UAP, the government's term for unidentified flying objects. malmgren-s-ida-job-as-cover-for-nsc-work: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, repeats a claim by Harald Malmgren, a former advisor to US presidents, about his work in the 1960s and 70s. malmgren-s-ida-work-a-cover-for-the-nsc-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Harold Malmgren, a government economist and adviser, claimed in a 2024 interview that his 1960s job at the Institute for Defense Analyses, a research group that works for the Pentagon, was really a cover. malmgren-s-research-on-thomas-townsend-b: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Harald Malmgren, a former adviser to American presidents, told him he had done deep research on Thomas Townsend Brown, an inventor of the mid-1900s who worked on anti-gravity, meaning machines meant to cancel out the pull of gravity. malmgren-s-two-unherd-essays-on-putin-20: Harald Malmgren, a former adviser to US presidents, says he wrote two essays about Russian president Vladimir Putin for UnHerd, an online magazine, around 2022. malmgren-saw-video-of-the-roswell-being-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Harald Malmgren, a former adviser to American presidents, told his daughter Pippa that later in his career he saw a video of a creature being interviewed. In one retelling Michels places this confession on Malmgren's deathbed. If true, it would mean the government not only recovered a living being but recorded talking with it.
malmgren-sent-into-the-tank-to-stall-cur: An analyst named Matthew Pines tells a podcast host, Jesse Michels, that during the 1962 Cuban missile crisis a young advisor, Harold Malmgren, was sent by President John F. Kennedy into the tank, a secure Pentagon meeting room for top commanders, to stall Air Force General Curtis LeMay and keep him from possibly using nuclear weapons. Malmgren himself tells it firsthand, saying he argued that striking Moscow would be madness because it would leave no one to negotiate with, and he names defense officials Robert McNamara and McGeorge Bundy as present. Told this way, it would mean Malmgren helped hold back a nuclear war.
malmgren-tracked-by-majestic-12-guardian: Harald Malmgren, an economist who advised several US presidents, tells podcast host Jesse Michels that from the 1950s on he was being watched by the CIA and by Majestic 12, which he describes as guardians who protect the world, a secret group said to oversee UFO matters. He says his name went into the important books of talent the day he met the president of MIT, the Massachusetts Institute of Technology. If true, it would mean a hidden group was quietly tracking promising young people for this work.
malmgren-tracked-by-majestic-guardians: Harold Malmgren, speaking to podcast host Jesse Michels, says he was watched not only by the CIA, the US spy agency, but also by people tied to "Majestic", a name some give to a secret group said to handle UFO matters. He calls them guardians who see themselves as protecting the world. If true, it would mean such a hidden group exists and keeps track of people.
malmgren-tweet-on-bluegill-tests-and-jfk: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, reads out a post on social media by Harold Malmgren, a former government adviser. In it, Michels says, Malmgren wrote that he was piecing together his own dealings with Los Alamos, the US nuclear weapons lab, during the 1961 and 1962 Bluegill tests, which he called tests of intercepting long-range nuclear missiles, and President John F. Kennedy's visit there in November 1962. Michels raises it in a talk about UFOs being seen around nuclear sites.
malmstrom-afb-disc-wobbling-on-edge: In a debate on Jesse Michels's podcast, a speaker named Merrick describes a sighting at Malmstrom Air Force Base, a US base that holds nuclear missiles. He says a border patrol officer saw a metal disc about 30 feet wide, roughly 100 feet away, "wobbling on its edge." It is told because it would mean a strange craft came close to America's nuclear weapons.
malmstrom-missiles-disabled-by-red-glowi: Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana held some of America's nuclear missiles, the long-range kind called ICBMs, or intercontinental ballistic missiles. Robert Salas, a former Air Force officer, says that on March 24, 1967 he was on duty underground at a launch control center called Oscar when guards reported a red glowing object hovering above. He says that before he could even pass on the phone calls, an alarm horn went off and the first missile went from green to red, and soon the missiles were in a "no-go" condition, meaning they could not be launched. If true, it would mean something unknown could switch off nuclear weapons at will, or as filmmaker James Fox puts it, take matches out of a baby's hands. The details shift between tellings: most say all ten missiles went down, while podcast host Jesse Michels once says nine of ten. Michels, who met Salas, repeats the story across many episodes, and another Air Force man, Bob Jamison, says a whole flight of ten missiles showed red on the control wall. Researcher Robert Hastings gathered Salas and other Air Force witnesses at a 2010 press conference, a former official named Karl Nell says missiles there were taken offline in the 1960s, and a guest named Danny Sheehan says the base commander, Arie Arnoldson, filed a UFO report with NORAD, the military command that watches North American airspace.
malta-foundation-with-a-solar-power-stat: A man named Filippo told podcast host Jesse Michels that his foundation is setting up in Malta in the 2020s. He says they rented a place and installed a solar power station there, and plan to add a data center of GPUs, powerful computer chips used for heavy calculation.
maltese-legend-of-giants-building-the-te: A man named Jay Anderson, speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast, describes a legend from Malta, the small island nation in the Mediterranean that is home to very old stone temples. He says the local legends hold that giants once lived on these islands and helped build the temples, a story that would point to someone other than ordinary people raising them.
man-abducted-off-a-downtown-street-in-co: A researcher of psychic and unexplained events, Jeffrey Mishlove, says that in 1976 a man walking through downtown Concord, California, at four in the morning claimed he had been abducted, taken by beings, right off the street. Mishlove says the man had no interest in UFOs, and that he and his colleagues interviewed him, and he links the case to a police report and to a man named Ted Owens. He tells it as one of several such cases he looked into himself.
man-in-a-black-duster-carrying-the-mothm: A man named Bryce, who worked in Hollywood with a partner named Brent, says that early in their partnership the two of them met a stranger in a long black coat in a movie theater parking lot in Los Angeles. According to Bryce, the man was holding a copy of The Mothman Prophecies, a book about strange sightings and odd events. He tells it as one of the uncanny coincidences that seemed to follow their work.
man-made-craft-rising-from-desert-openin: A UFO disclosure campaigner named Steven Greer tells a podcast host, Jesse Michels, that he has flown over desert sites where man-made craft rise up out of the ground. In one telling he names the site as Lockheed Skunk Works, the secret aircraft design arm of the company Lockheed, and says he flew over it by helicopter in 2023 and took video and photos on his iPhone. If true, it would mean humans secretly build and fly such craft.
man-made-ufo-down-in-russia: Steven Greer, a campaigner who pushes for governments to reveal what they know about UFOs, says a man-made UFO, meaning a craft of that kind built by humans, went down in Russia. He says his group recently got this confirmed by a special operations team, a unit of elite soldiers. If true, it would mean humans are already building and flying such craft.
man-who-says-he-was-in-the-gate-program: A researcher named Greg says he spoke with a young man who claimed to have been part of the GATE program, which in the United States is a school track for gifted and talented children. Greg will not give the young man's name. He brings it up as part of a wider story about hidden government work that touches on contact with other beings.
managed-disclosure-campaign-that-began-i: An online researcher who goes by UAPGerb says there is a carefully managed disclosure campaign, a slow, planned effort to let the public learn about UFOs, which he says began in 2017. A man named Karl Nell has said this campaign is now more or less dead, and UAPGerb says he strongly disagrees. If true, it would mean that what the public has heard since 2017 was released on purpose, step by step.
manchester-airport-orb-2024: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, points to a sighting labelled as having happened at Manchester Airport in England in June 2024, described as an orb, a round glowing object in the sky. He gives few details beyond the place and date, raising it as one more example of unexplained things seen near airports.
manchester-orb-sized-at-24-inches-at-mos: Mick West, a researcher known for skeptical looks at UFO videos, talks about a round glowing object, an "orb", filmed near Manchester Airport in England in June 2024. He says his team rebuilt the scene in 3D from the exact viewpoints and found the object was at most 24 inches across. He offers this to show the object was small, not a large craft.
mandela-effect-remembered-death-of-nelso: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, explains the Mandela effect, named because a big group of people say they remember Nelson Mandela, the South African leader, dying in prison in the 1980s, though he later walked free. Michels brings it up in a talk about the idea that we live in a kind of hologram, where shared false memories might be signs that reality itself can shift.
manhattan-project-as-original-ufo-legacy: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, mentions rumors that the Manhattan Project, the secret US effort of the 1940s to build the atomic bomb, was the original UFO legacy program, meaning the first hidden government effort to study crashed alien craft. If true, it would mean the secret handling of UFOs grew out of the same machinery that built the bomb.
manhattan-project-as-the-first-blue-book: David Grusch, a former US intelligence official who went public with claims about hidden UFO programmes, says some of his colleagues had grandparents who handled UFO reports for the Manhattan Project, the secret American effort to build the atomic bomb in the 1940s. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says Grusch told him during a car ride in Washington that the Manhattan Project was basically the original UFO programme, a forerunner of Blue Book, the US Air Force's UFO study of the 1950s and 60s. If true, it would mean the government was studying UFOs even before the famous sightings of the late 1940s.
manipulated-ellsworth-document-traced-to: This story is about a supposed Air Force document describing an incident in November 1977 at Ellsworth Air Force Base in South Dakota. A historian of UFOs, Richard Dolan, says the Ellsworth document has been tampered with, and that this has been traced back to Richard Doty, a man well known in UFO circles. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, describes the document itself: it claims that on November 16, 1977, at a site called L9, something attacked with a beam, and he mentions a researcher, Brad Sparks, in connection with it. Michels then goes further than Dolan. He says that according to a physicist and UFO researcher, Bruce Maccabee, another researcher, Bill Moore, said Doty confessed to forging the whole document. So the tellers differ on whether it was altered or made up outright. The story matters because, if genuine, the document would record an alien attack at a nuclear-era Air Force base.
mansmann-letters-describe-domed-disc-on-: A researcher named Robert Hastings, who studies reports of UFOs near nuclear bases, tells of a 1964 film taken at Vandenberg Air Force Base in California. manson-modeled-his-life-on-heinlein-s-st: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Charles Manson, the California cult leader of the 1960s, carried around a copy of Stranger in a Strange Land, a science fiction novel by the writer Robert Heinlein, and shaped his life around it. mantell-s-plane-disintegrated-by-magneti: In 1948, near Fort Knox in Kentucky, a pilot named Thomas Mantell lost his plane, and a man named Silus Newton offers his own account of what happened. mantis-being-at-the-bedside-tears-flesh-: John Blitch, a scientist who worked on military research, told podcast host Jesse Michels that in 1995, at his home near Denver, Colorado, a being shaped like a praying mantis stood by his bed. manuel-caceres-knockoff-figure-confused-: In Peru, small three-fingered mummified figures known as the Nazca bodies are claimed by some to be non-human, and a podcast host, Jesse Michels, says one figure got mixed up with them. map-of-key-black-sites-in-greer-s-brief: Steven Greer heads a group that pushes for governments to reveal what they know about non-human visitors. marble-from-crash-site-tests-about-40-ir: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says a small marble found at the Aztec crash site in New Mexico, a place where a UFO is said to have come down, was tested with XRF, a machine that reads which elements a material contains using X-rays. marcel-s-son-handled-the-roswell-materia: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Jesse Marcel, an Army intelligence officer at Roswell, New Mexico, in 1947, brought home debris from what many say was a crashed craft. marcker-s-general-electric-experiment-te: On the podcast of a host named Jesse Michels, a researcher named Eric Davis says that a scientist he calls Marcker ran an experiment at General Electric, the big American engineering company, to test whether spacetime has "torsion", a kind of twist in the fabric of space and time. marco-chereze-dies-after-handling-the-va: In 1996, in the town of Varginha in Brazil, several people said they saw a strange creature, and some said it was captured. marco-leal-re-interviews-carlos-about-25: Carlos Dosoza, a man in Sao Paulo, Brazil, tied to a claim that a hospital operated on a non-human being, told podcast host Jesse Michels that a researcher named Marco Leal interviewed him again around 2021, about 25 years after his first account. marco-rubio-s-attempt-to-approach-harrin: A man named Brent Freriedman, speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast, relays something he says came from David Grusch, a man cited as a witness on secret UFO matters. marco-rubio-s-ssci-staff-seek-whistleblo: A researcher who goes by the online name UAPGerb says on Jesse Michels's podcast that Marco Rubio, a US senator, has been interested in UFOs since 2017. marconi-believed-the-magenta-craft-non-h: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells of a craft said to have been recovered in Italy in the 1930s, known as the Magenta craft. marconi-radar-and-the-italian-crash: John Blitch, a researcher who says he has had his own encounters, talked about it with podcast host Jesse Michels in 2025. marconi-s-grandson-tells-oggi-about-the-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that a grandson of Guglielmo Marconi, the Italian inventor of radio, gave a filmed interview to Oggi, an Italian celebrity magazine. marconi-s-transatlantic-radio-experiment: This story is about Guglielmo Marconi, the radio pioneer, who in the early 1900s sent a radio signal across the Atlantic from Cornwall in England to Newfoundland in Canada. marcos-obtains-two-troves-through-tortur: A researcher named Dan Sheehan says on Jesse Michels's podcast that Ferdinand Marcos, who ruled the Philippines in the 1970s and 1980s, got hold of two troves of something, obtained through torture, with a Colonel Ver also named in the story. marcus-vinicius-s-chain-smoking-after-th: Italo Venturelli, a witness from Varginha, Brazil, told podcast host Jesse Michels about a man named Marcus Vinicius. marcus-vinicius-s-video-of-the-being-sho: Italo Venturelli, a surgeon connected to the regional hospital in Varginha, Brazil, says a colleague of his, Marcus Vinicius, had a video of a strange being, which Venturelli ties to his hospital's story of operating on an alien in 1996. maria-farmer-mural-showing-epstein-in-a-: A guest named Jay Anderson, on podcast host Jesse Michels's show, describes a mural called The Elite by the artist Maria Farmer. maria-s-finger-bones-tested-in-sri-lanka: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, discusses strange three-fingered bodies said to come from Peru, one of which is known as Maria. maria-wang-says-her-husband-reported-dir: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells of a woman named Maria Wang, whose husband Eric Wang is said to have worked in the 1950s at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base in Ohio, a base long linked in UFO stories to recovered crashed craft. marilyn-monroe-rumor-that-jfk-spilled-uf: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, brings up a rumor from the 1960s that President John F. Kennedy told the actress Marilyn Monroe some secrets about UFOs. marine-claims-he-was-on-the-usaf-flight-: A UFO investigator named James Fox, on Jesse Michels' podcast, says he got an email from an anonymous US Marine about events in Brazil in 1996. marine-squadron-commander-saw-the-churni: In 2004, off the coast of Southern California, Navy pilots said they saw a patch of churning white water in the sea near a strange white flying object. mariner-4-photographs-a-barren-mars-1965: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, recounts that in 1965 Mariner 4, an American space probe, flew past Mars and took the first close-up photos of the planet. mariner-9-s-inca-city-ruins-near-the-mar: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in 1972 Mariner 9, an American space probe orbiting Mars, sent back pictures from near the planet's south pole that looked like ancient ruins. mario-finds-his-right-b-52-pilot-glove-m: An Air Force veteran named Mario Woods says that in 1977, while serving at Ellsworth, an Air Force base near Rapid City, South Dakota, he went through his bag back home and found something wrong. mario-keeps-the-beings-out-of-his-debrie: Air Force veteran Mario Woods says that in November 1977, after a strange night in the nuclear missile field at Ellsworth Air Force Base in South Dakota, he left out of his official debriefing that he had seen beings. mario-s-childhood-sightings-of-craft: Air Force veteran Mario Woods, who says he was taken by beings as a young man, tells podcast host Jesse Michels that he has seen their craft many times, going back to when he was a boy. mario-s-doe-clearance-delays-and-repress: Air Force veteran Mario Woods says that after 1978 he went to work for the US Department of Energy, at sites such as Los Alamos in New Mexico and Oak Ridge, and that his first security clearance there took more than eight months to come through. mario-s-earlier-hypnotic-regression-trig: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells of Mario Woods, one of a group of Air Force veterans who say they were taken by aliens decades ago. mario-s-glove-seen-on-the-shiny-floor-of: An Air Force veteran named Michael Johnson says that in November 1977, during a night he and fellow airman Mario Woods spent in the nuclear missile field at Ellsworth Air Force Base in South Dakota, he found himself lying down somewhere and saw a glove on a very shiny floor, nothing like the inside of their truck. mario-s-regression-a-device-pushed-into-: Air Force veteran Mario Woods says that under regression, a kind of guided session meant to recover buried memories, he recalled being aboard a craft in November 1977. mario-s-regression-because-he-s-here-197: Air Force veteran Mario Woods says that in a regression session, meant to bring back buried memories, he recalled being aboard a craft in November 1977 with beings around him. mario-woods-abduction-at-ellsworth-afb: Podcast host Jesse Michels tells, again and again on his show, how Mario Woods and his partner Michael Johnson were on duty at Ellsworth Air Force Base in South Dakota in 1977 and were, according to Woods's memories recovered under hypnosis, abducted. mario-woods-becomes-obsessed-with-pyrami: In 1977, at Ellsworth Air Force Base, a US military base in South Dakota, a group of airmen say they had an encounter they describe as an alien abduction. mario-woods-debriefed-and-found-with-cir: Robert Hastings, a researcher who studies UFO reports at nuclear weapons bases, tells of a man named Mario Woods at Ellsworth Air Force Base in South Dakota in the 1960s. mario-woods-reports-the-incident-to-aaro: A military veteran named Mario Woods tells a podcast host, Jesse Michels, that around March 2023 he reported an incident he was part of to AARO, the Pentagon office set up to look into reports of unidentified objects. mark-felt-pushes-to-investigate-the-mexi: Dan Sheehan, a lawyer and researcher, told podcast host Jesse Michels in 2024 about something that happened at the FBI in 1972. mark-felt-s-biography-nixon-shown-covert: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that the biography of Mark Felt, a senior FBI official in the 1970s, describes President Richard Nixon being shown secret technology. mark-mccandlish-s-alien-reproduction-veh: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, mentions the claims of a man named Mark McCandlish about alien reproduction vehicles, meaning craft that humans built by copying technology from other beings. mark-twain-predicts-his-death-with-halle: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells how the great American novelist Mark Twain was born on November 30, 1835, just as Halley's Comet, a comet that returns about every 76 years, was passing Earth. mars-destroyed-by-a-cme-and-plasma-event: Matt LaCroix, a researcher of ancient history, told podcast host Jesse Michels in 2024 that Mars was ruined long ago by a huge blast from the Sun. mars-global-surveyor-image-of-a-square-s: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in 2001 the Mars Global Surveyor, a spacecraft that photographed Mars from orbit, captured an image of a square structure that looks artificial. mars-global-surveyor-images-of-possible-: A researcher named Maaneli Derakhshani says on Jesse Michels's podcast that several pictures taken by Mars Global Surveyor, a NASA spacecraft that orbited and photographed Mars from the late 1990s to the mid 2000s, show shapes that look like they could be the skeletons of large fossilized creatures. mars-investigation-at-sri-just-down-the-: A physicist named John Brandenburg, who argues that Mars once had life, says that in the 1980s a study of Mars was run out of SRI, the Stanford Research Institute in California. martial-arts-programs-that-train-people-: Rupert Sheldrake, a biologist known for unusual ideas about the mind, told podcast host Jesse Michels in 2024 that some martial arts programmes train people to know when they are being looked at from behind. martian-meteorite-alh84001-with-possible: This story is about a rock from Mars that landed on Earth. martian-scout-ship-finds-a-volatile-prim: A philosopher named Jason Jorjani relays a story he credits to a man named Joe McMoneagle: in the far distant past, millions of years ago, beings living on Mars sent a group out in a craft to scout a new world they might settle. martian-survivors-fled-and-some-may-have: Joe McMoneagle, who worked as a remote viewer, someone trained to describe distant places using the mind alone, told podcast host Jesse Michels in 2025 about people on Mars in the very distant past. martians-attacked-from-space: John Brandenburg, a physicist who studies Mars, told podcast host Jesse Michels in 2025 that something happened on Mars long ago. martians-built-the-moon-as-a-transport-a: A philosopher named Jason Jorjani, speaking on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, says that people living on Mars long ago probably built Earth's moon for two purposes: as a way to travel and as a tool for making Earth livable. martin-cannon-s-the-controllers-and-john: There is a book called The Controllers by a writer named Martin Cannon. martin-gardner-finds-his-own-lost-book: Michael Shermer, a researcher known as a skeptic, tells on Jesse Michels's podcast a story about the writer Martin Gardner. mary-k-sturdivant-as-lockheed-insider-wh: A researcher who goes by UAPGerb suggests on Jesse Michels's podcast that a proposed government UFO programme called Kona Blue may have been stopped because of a conflict of interest inside Lockheed Martin, a large American defence contractor. mary-magdalene-lands-at-marseille-merovi: A researcher named Randall Carlson says on Jesse Michels's podcast that, according to some traditions, Mary Magdalene, a follower of Jesus, travelled with Joseph of Arimathea, another figure from the Gospels, and came ashore at the place that is now Marseille in France. mary-s-mosaic-mary-pinchot-meyer-and-jfk: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, points to a book he thinks is called Mary's Mosaic, which deals with a woman named Mary Pinchot Meyer and President John F. masonic-and-zodiac-symbolism-in-nasa: Some people say the US space agency NASA is full of hidden symbols. mass-of-online-prophecies-of-9-11-2001: Eric Wargo, a writer on dreams and the ability to sense the future, told podcast host Jesse Michels in 2024 about the attacks on New York on September 11, 2001. mass-sighting-near-hometown-explained-as: A Swedish UFO researcher named Clas Svahn says that when he was 16 there was a huge sighting near his hometown of Mariestad, with many people watching something in the sky. massive-cme-event-during-the-older-dryas: Matt LaCroix, a researcher of ancient history, told podcast host Jesse Michels in 2024 that about 14,500 years ago, during a cold spell called the Older Dryas near the end of the last ice age, a massive blast of charged gas from the Sun hit the Earth. masters-childhood-precognition-of-a-gray: A man named Mike Masters, who argues that the beings people call aliens may be humans from the future, told a podcast host, Jesse Michels, in 2023 how his interest began. masters-face-to-face-contact-with-future: Mike Masters, a man who argues that the visitors may be humans from the future, told a podcast host, Jesse Michels, about a meeting at a conference hotel in Phoenix, Arizona, around Halloween 2022. matching-puncture-marks-examined-by-dr-m: A man named Mario Woods, a former guard at a nuclear site who says he was abducted, describes marks on the body that a doctor he calls Dr Margo examined, up to 2019 on St. Simons Island in Georgia. material-found-buried-deep-in-rocks-at-t: A religion scholar named Diana Pasulka says that in 2016 she went with others to a place in New Mexico said to be a crash site of an unknown craft. materials-scientist-the-metal-acts-like-: A man named Chris Bledsoe, who says he attracts UFOs, recounts what a materials scientist told him in the 2020s about an unusual metal, with the setting given as Silicon Valley and NASA, the US space agency. Bledsoe says the words he heard were that this metal acts much like an animal, always seeking energy and seeking to connect, which would make it something closer to alive than any ordinary material.
mathematician-sees-dmt-entities-solving-: A neuroscientist named Andrew Gallimore says on Jesse Michels's podcast that a mathematician he calls Andress took DMT, a powerful drug that causes intense visions. According to Gallimore, Andress saw beings in that vision solving the four color theorem, a famously hard maths problem about colouring maps, in under a second and over and over again. If true, it would suggest that the beings people meet on DMT have minds far beyond ours.
matt-bell-funds-robots-to-drill-the-quee: A researcher named Jeffrey told podcast host Jesse Michels in 2026 that Matt Bell, from a show called the Limitless podcast, is helping pay for robots to explore the Great Pyramid in Egypt. The robots would go up the narrow shafts leading from the Queen's Chamber, a room inside the pyramid, and drill through a small door in the northern shaft, following earlier robot work by an engineer named Gantenbrink. If it happens, people could finally see what lies behind that door.
matt-gaetz-constituent-describes-similar: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Matt Gaetz, a US congressman, once told an online audio chat that a voter from his district came into his office with a story. Michels says the voter described something very similar to another account about humans with mind powers being carried as cargo. If true, it would mean more than one person has brought this kind of claim to a member of Congress.
matthew-bevan-s-1990s-hacks: A British computer hacker named Gary McKinnon, who says he found signs of a secret space programme while breaking into NASA computers, mentions another hacker named Matthew Bevan. McKinnon says Bevan came earlier, doing his own hacking in the 1990s, with the story tied to the UK and the US Department of Energy, the government agency that runs America's nuclear and energy work.
matthew-brown-amentum-hangars-at-pax-riv: An online UAP researcher known as UAPGerb told podcast host Jesse Michels that Matthew Brown, a man who calls himself a Pentagon whistleblower, has said that hangars run by a defense contractor called Amentum at Naval Air Station Patuxent River, a Navy base in Maryland, hold "anomalous stuff." Brown, speaking on the same podcast later, put it a little differently. He points to his own public post to the tech billionaire Elon Musk, suggesting Musk should easily be able to get a tour of Amentum's "special project hangars," without saying outright what is inside. If true, it would mean unexplained material sits at a working Navy base.
matthew-brown-discovers-immaculate-const: A UFO investigator named Jeremy Corbell, speaking with podcast host Jesse Michels, says that a government official named Matthew Brown came across something called Immaculate Constellation in the 2020s. According to Corbell, it had been wrongly uploaded to IntelLink, a shared computer network used by US intelligence agencies, and he also brings up Lou Elizondo, a former Pentagon official. If true, it would mean evidence of a hidden UFO effort leaked onto an official network by mistake.
matthew-brown-prison-planet-humans-captu: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, passes on what a man named Matthew Brown told him in 2025. According to Michels, Brown said that there is a god, but that Earth is a kind of prison planet and that humans are, in a sense, held captive by certain beings. If true, it would mean our world is not free but run by others who keep us here.
matthew-brown-s-view-of-humans-as-a-reso: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, recalls an interview that the UFO filmmaker Jeremy Corbell did with a man named Matthew Brown in the 2020s. Michels says that at the end of that interview Brown suggested that people might be a resource for NHI, short for non-human intelligence, which would mean humans are being used rather than simply watched.
matthew-brown-s-wmd-corruption-whistlebl: A filmmaker named Jeremy Corbell says on Jesse Michels's podcast that Matthew Brown, a whistleblower who worked inside the US government, also reported corruption at the State Department, the US foreign affairs agency, in the 2020s. According to Corbell, this corruption had to do with weapons of mass destruction, such as nuclear or chemical arms, which he says was Brown's speciality. Corbell tells it to show that Brown has spoken up about wrongdoing before.
matthew-brown-snuck-into-secret-congress: A man named Jeremy Corbell, speaking with a podcast host, Jesse Michels, in 2026, says he quietly brought a man named Matthew Brown into a secret briefing in Washington, DC, sometime between 2024 and 2026. According to Corbell, three members of Congress had agreed to meet, and he snuck Brown in so Brown could speak to them privately, which would mean lawmakers were hearing UFO claims behind closed doors.
matthew-brown-uncovers-immaculate-conste: Podcast host Jesse Michels says that in 2024 a man named Matthew Brown told him he had figured out Immaculate Constellation, said to be a hidden US government program about UFOs, and that the name of Lue Elizondo, a former official from a small Pentagon office that studied unexplained aerial reports, was tied to it. According to Michels, Elizondo then testified alongside the journalist Michael Shellenberger and said he could not confirm or deny whether he had been given access to it. If true, it would mean a secret program exists that even its public figures will not openly discuss.
matthew-brown-white-house-ai-timeline-ma: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Matthew Brown, a former government official turned whistleblower, has talked about a computer system run by artificial intelligence that the White House supposedly has for managing timelines. In a later episode, Michels describes it as a special AI that can accurately predict a range of future events. If true, it would mean the US government can see some of the future before it happens.
matthew-sullivan-s-death-and-his-legacy-: This story is about a man named Matthew Sullivan, who is said to have worked inside a so-called legacy program, meaning a long-running secret government effort that people claim holds crashed craft not made by humans. A US congressman, Eric Burlison, says on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels that Sullivan was in that program and had firsthand experience with craft. Burlison connects this to David Grusch, a former intelligence officer who has publicly said such programs exist, and to another man named Jake Barber. The story is told around 2023. Jeremy Corbell, a guest on the same podcast, also tells it and says Sullivan had direct, hands-on contact with the craft. Corbell adds that Sullivan was due to testify behind closed doors about two weeks before he died, and that people, including the FBI (the US federal police), are looking into whether his death was suspicious. In one of his tellings Corbell places it in 2025 to 2026 rather than 2023, and mentions the ICIG (the official watchdog that takes complaints about US spy agencies) and a letter from members of Congress. If true, it would mean a firsthand witness to secret craft died just before he could speak to lawmakers.
maurice-hill-s-jellyfish-shaped-ufo-1973: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that a groundskeeper named Maurice Hill told of an up close encounter with a UFO shaped like a jellyfish. Hill places this around 1973 or 1974 in Washington DC. Michels tells it as part of a documentary about Lou Elizondo, a former Pentagon official who has spoken publicly about UFOs.
maurice-hill-witnessed-the-1952-washingt: Lou Elizondo, a former Pentagon official who has spoken publicly about UFOs, says that a man named Maurice Hill was living in Washington DC in 1952. That was the year of a well known event when strange lights were reported flying over the US capital, near the Capitol building. Elizondo tells it to show that Hill was a living witness to that famous night.
maury-island-incident-slag-rains-onto-a-: A researcher named Peter Levenda describes on Jesse Michels's podcast a 1947 story in which a man sitting in a boat in Puget Sound, in Washington state, saw what seemed to be several UFOs flying overhead. According to Levenda, one of them appeared to be in trouble and showered shards of metal or slag over the boat, with a man named Fred Crisman linked to the tale. If true, it would mean physical debris fell from an unknown craft.
maussan-sues-the-peruvian-government-for: Jaime Maussan, a man who promotes small three-fingered bodies from Peru as possibly not human, says that around 2024 or 2025 he filed a lawsuit against the Peruvian government for 300 million dollars. A journalist named Pavel says the lawsuit pushed Peru's Ministry of Culture and the government to take the bodies more seriously, though he gives no dollar figure.
max-davis-s-first-skeptical-reaction-to-: A man named Max Davis appears in a documentary about children said to read minds, including a boy named Josiah. He says that when the messages from Josiah first began, he was a skeptic, and his doubt made a woman involved cry. That, he says, is how his part in the story began.
maxwell-and-epstein-meet-castro-for-perm: A philosopher named Jason Jorjani says on Jesse Michels's podcast that, sometime in the 2010s, a person he names as Maxwell went to Cuba together with a man named Epstein. According to Jorjani, they met with Fidel Castro, Cuba's longtime leader, to get permission to dive on an underwater site that had dropped out of the news. He tells it as a sign that powerful people took a strong interest in that site.
maxwell-sells-promis-software-to-sandia-: A speaker identified as JASON says on Jesse Michels's podcast that Robert Maxwell, a British media businessman, sold a piece of software called Promis to Sandia Labs, a US government research laboratory in New Mexico, in the 1980s. The telling is brief and does not say much more about the deal.
mayan-flood-legend-of-atlan-and-tulan: Jason Jorjani, a philosopher and researcher, told podcast host Jesse Michels in 2025 about a flood legend from the ancient Maya of Central America. He says they used two words for the place their ancestors came from, Atlan and Tulan, a point he credits to the writer Graham Hancock, and the sound of Atlan hints at a link to the lost land of Atlantis.
mayor-earl-cabell-brother-charles-cabell: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, points out that in the early 1960s the mayor of Dallas, Texas, was a man named Earl Cabell. He says Earl's brother, Charles Cabell, held a senior role at the CIA, the US spy agency, tied to the Bay of Pigs, the failed 1961 US-backed invasion of Cuba. Michels raises it in connection with the route of President Kennedy's motorcade through Dallas in 1963, suggesting a link between the city's leadership and the agency.
mccasland-and-monica-reza-cases-possibly: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, made an episode about American scientists who he says have gone missing, and in it he looks at the case of a retired Air Force general named Neil McCasland and the case of a woman named Monica Reza. Michels says the two cases seem "eerily possibly connected," though he doesn't say how. If he's right, it would point to a pattern behind the disappearances rather than unrelated events.
mccasland-as-pentagon-director-of-specia: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, in an episode about missing American scientists, says that from June 2009 to May 2011 a man named Neil McCasland served as director of special programs at the Pentagon, in the office that handles buying weapons, technology and supplies. Citing McCasland's official Air Force biography and Pentagon training papers, Michels frames this as a post overseeing special access programmes, the most tightly guarded secret projects, which would put McCasland close to any hidden UFO work if such work exists.
mccasland-buys-a-medical-kit-at-rei-befo: Eric Burlison, a US congressman, talks with podcast host Jesse Michels about Neil McCasland, a retired senior Air Force officer who went missing in New Mexico in 2026. Burlison says the latest information is that McCasland went to REI, an outdoor gear store, and bought a medical kit before he vanished, a detail that matters to those who link his disappearance to the UFO subject.
mccasland-delonge-contacts-as-a-disclosu: A filmmaker and journalist named Jeremy Corbell, speaking with a podcast host, Jesse Michels, describes contacts in 2015 and 2016 between Neil McCasland, a retired Air Force general, and Tom DeLonge, a rock musician who started a public effort to reveal UFO secrets, all of it surfacing in emails published by WikiLeaks, a website that posts leaked documents. Corbell says these contacts were an "operation", which he says was not a bad thing: people on the inside trying to get information out, meant to prepare the ground for a Hillary Clinton presidency. He cites the journalist George Knapp, and if he is right, insiders were quietly working toward official disclosure.
mccasland-s-elephant-remark-to-delonge-2: A researcher named Jason Simosa says on Jesse Michels's podcast that, around 2015 or 2016, Tom DeLonge, a rock musician who began looking into UFOs, spoke by phone with Neil McCasland, a senior military figure. According to Simosa, McCasland warned DeLonge that he might find a group of people stumbling around an elephant, meaning people circling something huge without seeing it whole. Simosa tells it as a hint that insiders knew of a big secret that outsiders only glimpse in pieces.
mccasland-s-wife-tweets-about-alien-abdu: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells of a man named McCasland who vanished in New Mexico in 2026. According to Michels, McCasland's wife later wrote on Twitter that perhaps the best explanation was that aliens had taken him up to a mother ship, a large spacecraft, though she added that no mother ship had been found in the area.
mcconnell-invites-kirkpatrick-to-senate-: Kirk McConnell, a staff member for the US Senate, says that between about 2017 and 2022 he regularly invited a man named Sean Kirkpatrick to sit in on interviews his team held with Navy pilots and some scientists. He says these took place in the hearing room of the Senate Armed Services Committee, the Senate committee that oversees the military, and he also tells of a briefing connected to a man named Brandon Fugal. He tells it as an insider showing how seriously Congress was gathering first-hand accounts of unexplained sightings.
mccord-s-letter-to-judge-sirica-1973: Dan Sheehan, a lawyer, tells of a 1973 letter that James McCord, one of the men arrested in the Watergate break-in (the scandal that brought down President Nixon), wrote to John Sirica, the judge hearing the case in Washington DC. Sheehan says McCord, connected to his own office, got angry because he believed the defendants were all being sold down the river, and that this is what led him to write. If true, it would place Sheehan's circle close to a turning point of the scandal.
mcculloch-letters-urging-cia-and-navy-to: A researcher named Greg Malatzi says on Jesse Michels's podcast that the papers of Warren McCulloch, a scientist, kept at Northwestern University, hold letters from the late 1940s and early 1950s. According to Malatzi, in those letters McCulloch urged the CIA, the US spy agency, and the Navy to check out a researcher named Andrija Puharich, a lead he also credits to the writer Annie Jacobsen. He tells it to show that government agencies were steered toward Puharich, who later claimed contact with an alien council.
mccullough-on-the-phone-they-did-it-not-: Dylan Borland is a man who has come forward with claims about secret US government UFO programmes. He says that in 2025 a man named Chuck McCullough told him on the phone, "Well, they did it. The whistleblowers didn't," and the story is linked to the journalist Jeremy Corbell. As Borland tells it, the remark means that something blamed on the whistleblowers, the insiders who speak out, was really done by someone else.
mcdonald-confronts-hynek-over-the-swamp-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells how a physicist named James McDonald confronted J. Allen Hynek, a scientist who explained UFO sightings for the US government, sometime in the 1960s. The trigger was a wave of sightings in Michigan that had been explained away as swamp gas. According to Michels, McDonald told Hynek he was taking part in a cover-up and that what people saw in Michigan was not swamp gas, which would mean the official explanations were hiding something real.
mcdonnell-douglas-parapsychology-lab-197: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says the big aerospace company McDonnell Douglas ran a parapsychology program, meaning research into things like telepathy and other mind powers, tied to Washington University in St. Louis, Missouri. In one telling he says the company's founder, James McDonnell, set up the institute in the 1960s and was close to Bob Jahn, Princeton's dean of engineering, who went on to start a lab at Princeton that studied anomalies. If true, it would mean serious aerospace money was quietly backing research into the mind.
mcdonnell-instructs-staff-to-study-ufos: A researcher and writer on aircraft secrets, Nick Cook, says there are declassified papers, meaning once-secret records now released, showing James McDonnell, the head of the aircraft maker McDonnell Douglas, telling his company to study UFOs. If so, it would mean a major aircraft builder took the subject seriously behind closed doors.
mckenna-brothers-weeks-long-mushroom-tri: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells of the brothers Terence and Dennis McKenna, known for their writing on psychedelic drugs, and their time in the Amazon rainforest in the 1970s. He says they went on mushroom trips lasting several weeks in which they would "download and channel things," meaning they felt they were receiving information from somewhere outside themselves.
mckenna-stone-ape-theory-consciousness-f: Jeffrey Mishlove, a psychologist and interviewer, says on Jesse Michels's podcast that the writer Terence McKenna had an idea known as the stone ape theory. According to this idea, human consciousness first developed when our ape-like ancestors found and ate mushrooms that cause visions. If true, the human mind would owe its start to a plant-like drug.
mckinnon-on-why-he-scanned-us-military-n: Gary McKinnon is a British man who, around 2002 and 2003, searched through US military computer networks from the UK. On a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, he says he did it after reading a book from the Disclosure Project. That is a group led by Steven Greer that collects testimony from people who say the government hides what it knows about UFOs. As McKinnon tells it, he was looking for proof that such secrets were sitting on military computers.
mckinnon-s-hard-drives-seized-by-office-: Gary McKinnon, a British computer hacker, says that when he was arrested around 2002, all his data was taken to the Office of Naval Intelligence, the US Navy's intelligence service. He says they still have his hard drives, and that for years he has tried to get them back, only to be told it is still an ongoing investigation. He tells it because, if true, it suggests the US government still cares about what he found inside its computers.
mckinnon-s-left-heel-puncture-experience: Gary McKinnon, a British computer hacker, says that one night in 2006 at his home he was woken by a sudden sharp pain in his left heel. He says that when he pulled off his sock he found two perfectly circular holes, each about five millimetres across. In another telling he dates it to 2005, places it in a small first-floor rented room, and adds that bumps later appeared that he suspected were an implant, the sort of mark people link to alien abduction.
mcminnville-photo-string-revealed-at-fre: Clas Svahn, a longtime UFO researcher and record keeper, told podcast host Jesse Michels in 2026 about two famous photos of a disc-shaped object taken in 1950 in McMinnville, Oregon. He says that at a conference in France a couple of years ago, someone showed that a string could be seen in the photos, which would mean the object was hanging rather than flying.
mcminnville-trent-photos-1950: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, talks about photos that a farming couple, Paul and Evelyn Trent, are said to have taken of something in the sky near their home in McMinnville, Oregon, around 1950. Michels calls the Trents "hapless farmers" and says the case can't be finally proved or disproved either way, and on another show he groups it with a case at Lake Cote as one where there is a visual record. Supporters bring it up because, if the pictures show what they seem to, they would be early photographic evidence of an unknown craft.
mcmoneagle-remote-views-a-submarine-bein: Joseph McMoneagle was part of a US programme that trained people in remote viewing, the claimed skill of describing distant places with the mind alone. According to the podcast host Jesse Michels, in 1979 McMoneagle was asked to view a sealed building at a shipyard on the White Sea in Russia, and he described a huge nuclear submarine being built inside. If true, it would mean the mind can gather real spy information from far away. Michels tells it twice, once in his own framing and once passing on what McMoneagle told him in an interview, where he puts the date at 1978 or 1979. McMoneagle also tells it himself, first-hand, on the same show. He says what he got was a very unusual submarine, which he calls TK-089, north of the Arctic Circle. He says his report went to the National Security Council, the White House body that advises on security, that Robert Gates was involved, and that the submarine was confirmed 114 days later.
mcmoneagle-s-cia-mars-remote-viewing-mar: Remote viewing is the claimed practice of describing a far-off or hidden place using only the mind. A researcher and philosopher named Jason Jorjani, speaking on Jesse Michels' podcast, says that in 1984 a remote viewer named Joseph McMoneagle, working at the Monroe Institute in Virginia, did a session for the CIA in which he viewed Mars. Jorjani links this to a document known as "Mars 1 Million BC." Michels, the host, mentions it himself on a later episode with a former Army remote viewer. He says McMoneagle was tasked with viewing Mars as it was a million years ago, though he gives no date and does not mention the CIA or the institute. They tell it because, if true, a US intelligence agency was trying to use the mind to look at ancient life or activity on another planet.
mcmoneagle-s-cia-remote-viewing-of-mars-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says the CIA gave a man named Joe McMoneagle the job of remote viewing Mars as it was a million years ago. Remote viewing means trying to see faraway places or times using only the mind. Michels says McMoneagle described giant beings there, which would mean intelligent life once lived on Mars.
mcmoneagle-s-jpl-correspondence-and-life: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says he has been in contact with Joseph McMoneagle, a man who took part in a US government psychic spy programme. According to Michels, McMoneagle implied that at the Jet Propulsion Laboratory, NASA's space probe centre in Pasadena, California, it is an open secret that there was once life on Mars. If true, scientists there would quietly know something the public has not been told.
mcmoneagle-s-legion-of-merit-for-remote-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says a man named Joseph McMoneagle was given the Legion of Merit, a US military award, for remote viewing, which means trying to see distant places or hidden things using only the mind. According to Michels, McMoneagle used it more than 200 times to help gather intelligence, working on hostage cases and drawing nuclear sites. If true, it would mean the military found mind-based spying useful enough to reward it.
mcmoneagle-s-pentagon-remote-viewing-of-: A researcher of UFO reports at nuclear weapons sites, Robert Hastings, says on Jesse Michels's podcast that Joseph McMoneagle did a session for the Pentagon. McMoneagle was trained in remote viewing, the claimed ability to see distant places using only the mind. According to the story Hastings tells, McMoneagle saw a UFO hovering over a nuclear missile, which would mean UFOs take an interest in nuclear weapons.
mcmoneagle-tasked-to-remote-view-mars-a-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Joseph McMoneagle, a member of a US psychic spy programme in the 1980s, was given map coordinates and asked to "remote view" Mars, that is, to see it with his mind alone, as it was a million years ago. Michels says this tasking is now public and declassified. If so, it would mean the government was curious enough about ancient Mars to point its psychics at it.
mcmoneagle-tells-jesse-that-humans-may-b: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says he once spoke by phone with Joseph McMoneagle, a man known as a remote viewer, meaning someone who tries to describe distant places or things using the mind alone. According to Michels, sometime in the 2020s McMoneagle told him that humans might be turning into the ETs, the extraterrestrials, or that the visitors might be nudging us to become like them. If true, it would mean the beings people report are, in some sense, our own future.
mechanical-watch-stopped-by-the-emitter-: A researcher, Luigi Vendetelli, passes on a detail from Bob Lazar, a man who says that in the late 1980s he worked at S4, a secret site in Nevada. As Vendetelli tells it, Lazar describes a device called the emitter that made a mechanical watch simply stop. If true, it would point to a strange technology whose effects reached ordinary objects nearby.
medications-and-diagnoses-cleared-within: A man named Jordan, who says he was taken into a secret UFO programme as a child, says that around 2010 to 2011 in Springville, New York, he came off his medications. He says that within a year he was released from every psychological diagnosis he had been given. He tells it as part of his larger story, where it would mean his troubles came from what happened to him rather than from illness.
medieval-angel-hierarchy-guiding-stars-a: Rupert Sheldrake, a biologist known for unusual ideas about the mind, told podcast host Jesse Michels in 2024 about an old Christian view of the heavens, going back to a 6th-century Syrian writer known as Dionysius the Areopagite and carried on by the medieval thinker Thomas Aquinas, with roots in the earlier philosopher Iamblichus. He says they believed each star and planet was alive and intelligent and had its own guiding angel, a view that would make the whole sky a place full of minds.
medieval-paintings-with-ufo-like-objects: Michael Shermer, a researcher known as a skeptic, mentions on Jesse Michels's podcast the medieval paintings that show something in the sky that looks a bit like a UFO. He brings this up in connection with writers such as Jacques Vallee and Jeffrey Kripal, who look at old art and stories as possible records of the same kind of phenomenon people report today.
medvedev-april-fool-s-interview-on-russi: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells of an interview with Dmitry Medvedev, a senior Russian political leader, that took place on April Fool's Day. According to Michels, the interviewer asked about UFOs expecting a joke, and Medvedev answered that Russia keeps an extensive file on the subject. If he meant it, it would suggest the Russian government takes the topic seriously behind closed doors.
meeting-a-real-recluse-on-the-second-ath: A man named Ralph says that on his second trip to Mount Athos in Greece, around 2005, he met a real hermit living apart from the world. He says the hermit gave him a book and that the two had a remarkable conversation about the apocalypse, the end of the world. He tells it as one of the encounters that shaped his unusual spiritual and personal story.
meeting-archbishop-marcinkus-at-the-vati: Harold Malmgren, a man described as a former adviser to US presidents, told a podcast host, Jesse Michels, about a visit to the Vatican Bank, the Catholic Church's own bank in Vatican City, in 1973, in a story that also involves a man named Pete Peterson. Malmgren says he met Archbishop Marcinkus, a senior churchman there, who looked up and told him they knew about him from his boyhood, through many of their associates in the Mafia. He tells it as a sign of how far hidden networks of power reached.
meeting-bob-lazar-and-george-knapp-at-th: Peter Levenda, a writer presented on the show as a historian of the CIA, told a podcast host, Jesse Michels, that he met Bob Lazar for the first time at the start of a project in the late 2010s. Lazar is a man who says he once worked on alien craft for the government, and George Knapp, a journalist who has long reported his story, was there too. Levenda says the three of them came together as that project began.
meeting-edward-teller-before-his-los-ala: Bob Lazar, a man who says he later worked on alien craft at a secret Nevada site, told a podcast host, Jesse Michels, that in 1982 he was working at Los Alamos National Laboratory, a US government nuclear research lab in New Mexico. He says the local paper ran a front-page story that day on a jet-powered car he had built, and by coincidence the famous physicist Edward Teller was giving a speech there the same day, and Lazar met him beforehand. The story matters to his telling because Lazar says Teller later helped him get the job at that secret site.
meeting-eric-davis-hal-puthoff-and-sonny: A man named Jack says that while he was a graduate student researching fusion, the process of making energy by forcing atoms together, he went to a conference to present his work. He says that there he was introduced to three men named Eric Davis, Hal Puthoff and Sonny White. He tells it to show how he first came into contact with people tied to research on unusual advanced technology.
meeting-jeffrey-epstein-a-constructed-pe: Eric Weinstein, a researcher, told a podcast host, Jesse Michels, that he met the financier Jeffrey Epstein only once, for about an hour. Weinstein says Epstein was an absolutely terrifying person to encounter, and that he struck him as a 'constructed' person, someone built up by others rather than who he appeared to be.
meeting-john-lear-through-gene-huff-s-ap: Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked on alien craft at a secret Nevada site, told a podcast host, Jesse Michels, how he met a man named John Lear in Las Vegas in the 1980s. Lazar says his friend Gene Huff, a property appraiser, was hired to appraise Lear's house, and Lazar tagged along. He tells it as the chance meeting that pulled him into the circle where his story would later come out.
meeting-lab-partner-barry-earlier-teams-: Bob Lazar told a podcast host, Jesse Michels, about his time in 1988 and 1989 at S-4, a secret site in the Nevada desert where he says he worked on recovered alien craft. He says he was paired with a lab partner named Barry, and that the teams who had been there before him had reached the point where working with the craft was nonchalant. If true, it would mean the government had been studying such craft long enough for it to feel routine.
meeting-spielberg-about-a-video-game-in-: Bryce Zabel, a Hollywood television writer and producer, says that in 1996, in the middle of a dispute, he went to Amblin, the Los Angeles film company of the famous director Steven Spielberg, to meet about a video game. He says he waited in Spielberg's office until Spielberg came in, shook his hand and said, "Great to see you again." He tells it as part of his story about how Hollywood and UFO stories have crossed paths.
meeting-steven-greer-at-a-boulder-book-s: Michael Herrera, a man who says he saw a huge UFO in the Indonesian jungle, says that in 2018 he went to a book signing in Boulder, Colorado, held by an author named Steven Greer. He says that after he shared his story, Greer stood up, handed him his card and told him, "Don't tell anybody this information." He tells it because, if true, it shows his account was taken seriously and treated as sensitive.
meeting-the-bali-bombing-leader-who-beli: Peter Levenda is a writer and researcher of hidden history. On a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, he says he once met, in Indonesia, the man who led the 2002 bombings on the island of Bali. michael-sees-football-field-sized-octago: A person who posts about UFOs online as UAPGerb tells of a witness named Michael who saw a huge eight-sided craft about the size of a football field. According to UAPGerb, such a craft would be used for moving humans from one place to another, which would mean someone is planning to relocate people on a large scale.
michael-shermer-on-the-white-house-uap-s: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, speaking with Michael Shermer, a researcher well known as a skeptic, mentions a White House science advisory committee on UAP, which stands for unidentified anomalous phenomena, the government's newer word for UFOs. Michels speaks of it in 2026, loosely tying it to people with connections inside government, though he gives few details. If such a committee exists, it would mean the subject has reached the highest level of the US government.
michael-talbot-dies-of-the-leukemia-he-w: Jeffrey Mishlove, a researcher of the mind and psychic experience, says he visited his friend Michael Talbot, author of a book called The Holographic Universe, in the hospital before Talbot died in 1992. He points to an irony: Talbot had written a vampire novel in which vampirism was a rare form of leukemia, a blood cancer, and then Talbot died of a rare form of leukemia himself.
michael-wonders-who-built-the-pyramids-a: Michael, a man who says he was abducted by aliens, speaks on a podcast about ancient monuments. He wonders aloud who built the pyramids of Egypt and how the great standing stones of England got where they are. He asks it as a hint that someone other than ordinary people of the time may have been involved.
michele-sindona-s-money-laundering-opera: On a 2026 episode of Jesse Michels's podcast, a speaker named Jason describes a money laundering operation tied to a financier named Michele Sindona, starting around 1964. Citing the author Paul Williams, he says it was the biggest money laundering operation ever, about 200 billion dollars, and he links it to other names including James Jesus Angleton and Charles Hambro. He tells it as part of an argument that secret money and secret networks sit behind the hiding of UFO knowledge.
michels-s-own-sighting-at-the-start-of-h: Jesse Michels, a podcast host who interviews people about UFOs, says he has seen strange things in the sky himself. He brought it up while talking with a treasure hunter, Dennis Asberg, and says it happened right when he was starting his show. He does not give a place or describe what he saw, but if true it would mean the host has his own sighting behind his interest.
michelson-morley-ether-experiments-1890: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, brings up the Michelson-Morley experiments, which he places in the 1890s. He describes them as a set of light-based measurements by two scientists, Michelson and Morley, meant to detect the ether, a substance once thought to fill all of space. He uses them as an example of how science tests, and sometimes throws out, big ideas about how the world works.
michigan-swamp-gas-case: A guest named Merrick, on a 2025 episode of Jesse Michels's podcast framed as a challenge to the UFO skeptic Mick West, brings up the Michigan 'swamp gas' case, a sighting in Michigan that was put down to gas rising from marshland. He lists it among cases where, he says, people also reported large disc-shaped objects.
mick-s-2017-metabunk-post-calls-the-diet: Merrick von Renenamp, speaking on a podcast, confronts Mick West, a skeptic who analyses UFO videos, with something West wrote on Metabunk, an online forum, on December 30, 2017. That post was a reaction to an interview released by To the Stars Academy, a company that put out UFO material, with Alex Dietrich, a Navy pilot who says she saw an unexplained object. Merrick says West called her account laughable, and he raises it to question how the skeptic treated a witness.
mick-s-analysis-flir1-object-is-a-distan: A skeptic, Mick West, discusses a 2004 Navy video known as FLIR1, filmed with an infrared camera off Southern California, which many found amazing because the object seems to zip off the screen. West argues the object is most likely a distant airliner and that the sudden zip is caused by the camera moving, not the object. Merrick von Renenamp, debating him, recalls West saying the plane was probably 50 to 100 miles away, though he does not mention the camera point.
mick-west-sees-a-wingless-plane-fuselage: Mick West, a well-known UFO skeptic, says that once while flying down to Los Angeles he saw what looked like the body of a plane with no wings. He mentions it as something he has seen with his own eyes, in a talk about how strange things look in the sky.
mick-west-tic-tac-video-zoom-change-2004: A researcher, Michael Shurmer, passes on a point from Mick West, a skeptic who analyses UFO videos, about the Tic Tac video, footage of a white oval object shaped like the mint, filmed by Navy jets from the aircraft carrier USS Nimitz off San Diego in 2004.
