According to Shurmer, West noted that the screen shows a reading of zoom 1.0, suggesting the camera's zoom changed during the clip. The point matters because a zoom change could explain how the object seems to move.
mickelsen-safeguard-abm-site-and-the-197: A researcher named Grant Cameron, on Jesse Michels's podcast, says that in February 1975 a base opened near Nekoma, North Dakota, called the Mickelsen Safeguard site. He describes it as the only working anti-ballistic missile unit in the United States, a base built to shoot down incoming nuclear missiles. Cameron ties its opening to a wave of UFO sightings that year, which, if true, would mean UFOs were taking an interest in America's nuclear defenses.
microwave-cannons-used-to-bring-down-cra: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, points to a man named Jake Barber, who has been tied to psionics (using the mind to affect the world) and to Northrop Grumman, a large US defense company. Michels says the people in that circle have a lot of microwave cannons, and suggests these are used to bring down unknown craft. If true, it would mean someone has a working way to knock such craft out of the sky.
mid-1950s-aerospace-propulsion-breakthro: A philosopher, Jason Jorjani, says on a 2025 episode of Jesse Michels's podcast that in the mid-1950s there was a breakthrough in aircraft propulsion at Martin Aircraft, an American plane maker, and possibly at other companies too. According to him, people at the time said they could roll these new craft off an assembly line within three years, which, if true, would mean exotic flight technology was within reach decades ago.
mike-masters-abductees-sanitize-before-b: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, cites Mike Masters, a researcher who explores the idea that the beings behind UFOs could be time travellers. Michels says that in many of the cases Masters studied, people who say they were abducted had to clean themselves first, by showering or with chemical rinses, before being taken aboard the craft. Michels raises it because such care about germs could hint that the visitors are biologically close to us.
mike-masters-theory-that-ufos-are-time-t: Podcast host Jesse Michels describes the idea of Mike Masters, an evolutionary biologist at Montana Tech, a university in Montana. Michels says Masters has written books, including Identified Flying Objects and Extempore, arguing that UFOs may be humans from the future travelling back in time. If true, it would mean the visitors are not aliens but our own descendants.
mike-mcconnell-as-dan-burisch-s-godfathe: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, mentions in passing that there are strange stories around a man named Dan Burisch. Michels says he thinks that Burisch's godfather was a man named Mike McConnell, and he links the story to another person, Brian Jackson. He brings it up as one more odd personal tie in the web of people around secret UFO programmes.
mike-mcconnell-linked-to-s4-area-51-via-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, speaking with Bob Lazar, a man who tells his own story about working at S4, said to be a secret site near Area 51, the closely guarded US military base in Nevada, suggests that a person Lazar mentioned may have been Mike McConnell, who later became director of the NSA, the US National Security Agency that handles electronic spying. Michels says McConnell was involved in S4 matters connected to Dan Burisch, another man with an S4 story set in the 1980s and 1990s, though Michels thinks Burisch's account holds up far less well than Lazar's. If true, it would tie a future intelligence chief to the alleged secret work at the site.
mike-turner-and-aerospace-donors-removed: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, gives his own guess at what happened behind the scenes in 2023, when a proposed law about UFOs lost a clause that would have let the government take UFO technology and materials away from private companies. He says his understanding is that a congressman, Mike Turner, whose region includes Wright-Patterson Air Force Base in Dayton, Ohio, worked with aerospace donors and with House leader Mike Johnson to get the clause removed. If true, it would mean defense companies used political influence to keep control of any such materials.
mike-turner-wright-patterson-donors-and-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, points to a congressman named Mike Turner, who represents the Ohio district that contains Wright-Patterson Air Force Base. Michels calls that base the center of UFO lore and of claims about taking apart and copying recovered craft, going back to Roswell, the 1947 New Mexico incident where a craft is said to have crashed. He says that around 2023, while Congress was dealing with a bill that had an eminent domain clause (a provision about the government's power to take private property), Turner's top donors included big defense companies such as Boeing and Lockheed. If that is true, it would suggest that defense industry money shapes how Congress handles UFO secrets.
milab-abductee-meets-a-nordic-on-a-milit: A researcher, Tim Alberino, retells a story from a book called Taken by the abduction researcher Karla Turner. In it, a woman who says she was taken by the military, not only by aliens, met a "Nordic", a tall, human-looking being, on a military base, and asked whether the Nordics were involved with the Greys, the small grey beings of many abduction stories. According to the story, the Nordic replied "by degrees", which would mean the different beings, and maybe the military, work together in some way.
military-abductions-of-abductees-after-g: Tim Alberino, a researcher speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast and drawing on the work of abduction researcher Karla Turner, says some people were taken by gray aliens, small grey-skinned beings, and then returned home. He says the military would then show up and take these same people again, to Air Force bases and underground bases. If true, the military knows about the abductions and is following up on the people involved.
military-base-calls-a-witness-after-the-: James Fox, a documentary filmmaker who investigates UFO cases, says that around 2021 or 2022 in Brazil he filmed an interview with a local witness. Right after that, according to Fox, a military base phoned the man they had just met on camera. He tells it as a sign that the military was keeping close watch on who was talking to him.
military-convoy-cordons-the-crash-site-a: Carlos de Souza is a Brazilian man who says he saw a craft crash near the town of Varginha, Brazil, in January 1996. He says the site was near an army sergeants' school. On the podcast of host Jesse Michels, he says that as he was there, a military convoy came toward his car and soldiers closed off the area. In a later episode of the same show, about famous Brazilian cases, he goes further. He says a soldier stepped back, raised his gun, cocked it, and pointed it at his head. If true, it would mean the army moved fast to seal off the crash and keep witnesses away. Both tellings are Carlos's own, given on two different episodes, and the second adds the threat with the gun.
military-driver-sees-non-human-creature-: In 1996, people in Varginha, a town in Brazil, said a strange craft had crashed and a living creature had been caught. A military man, named only as "X", says he drove for the military at the time and saw a non-human creature at the town's Humanitas Hospital. He describes its skin as very oily, with a texture like silicone. He tells this on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels and in a film called Moment of Contact, and if true it would mean a real non-human being was held in that hospital.
military-helicopters-following-researche: Scott Ramsay, a researcher of a UFO crash said to have happened near Aztec, New Mexico, says an earlier researcher of that case, Bill Steinman, claimed he was followed by military helicopters a couple of times as he left the crash site in Hart Canyon. Ramsay says the same thing happened to his own group once, when they were putting up a plaque at the site. To him it suggests the military was still watching the place decades later.
military-members-saw-football-field-size: A man named David Grusch says that, at some point around 2019 to 2021, he interviewed military members in the United States who told him they had seen something remarkable. According to Grusch, they described large triangular craft, as big as a football field, hovering right above them. He tells it as an example of the kind of first-hand accounts he heard, which if true would mean huge unknown craft are flying over American service members.
military-officer-briefs-gaetz-on-hybrid-: A man named Eric Burles says that a US congressman, Matt Gaetz, told him about a visit to his office in Washington in the 2020s. According to Burles, Gaetz said a senior military officer, whose rank was not given, came in and told him about hybrids, meaning programmes said to breed beings that are part human and part something else. If true, it would mean members of Congress are being briefed on such programmes in private.
military-officers-who-reported-ufos-were: A man named Dan Sheehan says that in the 1980s and 1990s, a number of high-ranking military people who had reported UFOs were sent for psychiatric exams to John Mack, who headed clinical psychiatry at Harvard University in Cambridge, Massachusetts. As Sheehan tells it, hearing these officers' accounts is what led Mack to start investigating the subject himself, which would mean the military's own people pulled a respected psychiatrist into UFO research.
military-officials-approach-sandler-and-: This story is about two filmmakers, Allan Sandler and Robert Emenegger. A researcher who goes by UAPGerb says that in the early 1970s two US military officials came to them and asked them to make a documentary. The officials said they could include film from Holloman Air Force Base, and a man named Weinbrenner is mentioned. The podcast host Jesse Michels tells it as well: he says Emenegger was in contact with Norton Air Force Base, where everyone talked to him about UFOs, and that this led to a film called UFOs: Past, Present and Future, with J. Allen Hynek and Rod Serling also named. A third teller, the researcher Grant Cameron, relays what he says Emenegger told him. He places it at Norton around 1973 and names Paul Shartle, H.R. Haldeman and a Colonel Coleman, and he says the officials asked for the UFO film to be hidden among eight other documentaries. If true, it would mean the military itself quietly wanted the public to see UFO material.
military-trying-to-contact-ufos-with-fig: A researcher named Grant Cameron, on Jesse Michels's podcast, says there was a story from the 1950s that the American military used lights on fighter jets to try to signal to UFOs. If true, the military was secretly trying to talk to whatever was flying in its skies.
military-video-of-instantaneous-accelera: A filmmaker and journalist, Jeremy Corbell, says that he and fellow journalist George Knapp got hold of a military video and released it to the public. As Corbell tells it, the video shows an object accelerating instantly while a military weapons system held a firm targeting lock on it, and analysis of the footage followed its release. If true, it would mean the military had recorded something moving in ways no known aircraft can.
military-x-everything-started-at-my-farm: James Fox, a documentary filmmaker who made a film called Moment of Contact about events in the Brazilian town of Varginha in 1996, where people say a strange creature was seen and captured by the military, says he met a source he calls "military X". According to Fox, when he asked a question, the man told him that everything that happened in Varginha started at his farm. If true, it would pin down where the whole affair began.
minas-gerais-as-the-centre-of-brazil-s-u: On an episode of Jesse Michels' podcast about famous Brazilian UFO cases, an unnamed researcher talks about Minas Gerais, a state in Brazil known for its mining. The speaker says that, for their group, there is a close link between UFO sightings and the rare elements and minerals found across the state. If that were so, it would suggest the visitors are drawn to places for what lies in the ground.
mind-lamp-turns-green-during-the-episode: On a 2021 episode about a CIA program that used psychics as spies, podcast host Jesse Michels tells of a "mind lamp" in Princeton, New Jersey. The lamp is a device said to respond to people's intentions, and he connects it to a researcher named Herb Metts. Michels says the lamp turned green on the first try, within the first 30 seconds, and by his math the odds of that were about 2%. If that is true, it would hint that the mind can affect a machine.
minister-joe-s-special-needs-youth-group: Ky Dickens, a filmmaker who made a documentary about non-speaking children she says can read minds, tells this on podcast host Jesse Michels' show. She says a minister named Joe, who ran a youth group for children with special needs at a large church, told her around 2023 that some of the kids in his group were talking about "the Hill", a place she says came up among the children. If true, it would mean children who had never met were describing the same shared place.
ministry-of-culture-raids-a-press-confer: Podcast host Jesse Michels talks about a set of three-fingered mummified bodies from Peru that some people say are not human. He says that during one of the press conferences about the bodies, Peru's Ministry of Culture, the government department in charge of national heritage, came down on a woman named Joyce Mantilla, and he describes it as a raid. In his telling, this shows the authorities trying to shut the subject down.
minot-afb-all-ten-missiles-down-after-uf: A former US Air Force officer, Robert Salas, says that in September 1966 at Minot Air Force Base in North Dakota, all ten nuclear missiles at a site went out of action after a UFO appeared. Salas says he learned this from another witness who came forward, a man named David Shindell. If true, it would mean an unknown object was able to switch off American nuclear weapons.
minot-afb-radar-reviewed-by-kevin-knuth-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, points to a 1968 incident at Minot Air Force Base in North Dakota, where something unexplained is said to have been seen. Michels says that, unusually, there is radar data from the event, and that physicists, including one named Kevin Knuth, have looked it over. He brings it up because radar backing would make the sighting harder to put down to people's eyes playing tricks.
minot-launch-signal-stopped-by-inhibit-s: Podcast host Jesse Michels, in a 2024 episode with Robert Hastings, a researcher who collects accounts of UFOs at nuclear bases, recounts a 1966 incident at Minot Air Force Base in North Dakota, a base with nuclear missiles. He says Hastings interviewed by phone a Captain David Sher, who received a launch indicator, a signal that a missile was starting to launch, at his post, and that it was stopped by an inhibit switch, a safety control. It is told as part of the claim that UFOs have been watching and interfering with nuclear weapons.
minuteman-silos-on-black-hills-land-guar: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that 150 underground launch sites for Minuteman nuclear missiles were dug into land in South Dakota's Black Hills region. He points out that this land had been promised to the Great Sioux Nation, a group of Native American peoples, by the 1868 Fort Laramie Treaty, an agreement with the US government, and he raises it as backdrop to stories of strange events around those missile bases.
miracle-of-fatima-mass-sighting-1917: In 1917, in the town of Fatima in Portugal, a huge crowd gathered and reported a strange sight in the sky, an event known as the Miracle of Fatima. A well-known skeptic, Michael Shermer, mentions it as a case seen by 50,000 or 70,000 people. Another guest on the same podcast, Jason Samosa, says the clouds parted and something appeared in the sky, which lawyers, doctors and other serious witnesses described as a silvery disc. If taken at face value, it would be one of the largest group sightings of an unexplained object ever recorded.
misawa-disc-flips-on-its-edge-1952: A guest named Merrick, on a 2025 episode of Jesse Michels's podcast, describes a 1952 training exercise at Misawa, Japan, where military pilots were practising intercepts, meaning flying up to meet a target. According to him, one pilot saw a disc come right up to his plane and flip on its edge, which, if true, would be a close look at a disc-shaped craft by a trained flier.
mishlove-s-accredited-doctorate-in-parap: Jeffrey Mishlove, a researcher and interviewer, says that in the 1970s he earned a doctorate from the University of California, Berkeley, with the word "parapsychology" printed on the diploma. Parapsychology is the study of claimed mind powers such as telepathy. He says he thinks he is the only person in the world ever to get an accredited doctoral diploma with that word on it.
mishlove-s-eleven-year-study-of-ted-owen: Jeffrey Mishlove is a researcher with a doctorate who studies psychic claims. On a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, he says he worked with a man named Ted Owens for eleven years, from 1976 until Owens died in 1987, and kept an archive of that work. Mishlove links the study to Hal Puthoff and Russell Targ, two other researchers of psychic abilities, and tells it because he says Owens's abilities deserve serious study.
mishlove-s-prize-winning-bigelow-essay-o: Jeffrey Mishlove is a researcher with a doctorate who studies psychic claims. He says that in 2021 a wealthy businessman, Robert Bigelow, ran an essay contest asking for the strongest evidence that the human mind survives the death of the body. On a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, Mishlove says he wrote one of the winning essays, which, if its case holds, would mean consciousness goes on after death.
mishlove-s-remote-viewing-trial-at-sri-1: Jeffrey Mishlove, a researcher and interviewer, says that in February 1976 he was invited to SRI, the Stanford Research Institute, a research lab in California, by the researchers Hal Puthoff and Russell Targ to try remote viewing. Remote viewing is the claimed ability to describe a faraway place or object using only the mind. Mishlove says his trial there was very successful.
missile-fields-as-the-obvious-place-for-: Podcast host Jesse Michels argues that if non-human visitors have been watching humanity since the start of the nuclear age in 1945, then the nuclear missile fields of South Dakota and Montana would not be a strange place to find them. He calls them "the obvious place." If he is right, it would mean these visitors take a special interest in our nuclear weapons.
missing-411-national-park-disappearances: A writer and researcher, Jason Jorjani, relays the work of a man he names as David Pitus, who wrote a book series called Missing 411 about people who vanished in US national parks. According to Jorjani, Pitus found that in the same areas where people went missing, people also reported seeing UFOs, a link explored in a related work called Closer Encounters. If true, it would tie unexplained disappearances to UFO activity.
missing-and-dead-scientists-loureiro-gil: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, mentions cases people are talking about in which scientists have gone missing or died, naming Nuno Loureiro, who Michels says basically ran the plasma fusion lab at MIT, the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, along with Carl Gilmore and Neil McCasland, with links to Caltech, the California Institute of Technology, and Wright-Patterson Air Force Base in Ohio. Michels presents these as cases being discussed together, suggesting some people suspect a connection to sensitive research.
missing-fetus-syndrome-grays-take-back-h: Tim Alberino, a researcher speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast, describes what he calls missing fetus syndrome. He says that when some abducted women are pregnant with part-human, part-alien babies, the pregnancy vanishes because the grays, small grey-skinned aliens, come and take the fetus. If true, aliens would be breeding hybrids using human mothers.
missing-time-on-drive-home-from-college: Bob Maguire, described as a former contractor for the CIA, the US foreign intelligence agency, says that in his first month of college he was driving home with others. About two and a half hours into the trip, he says, they suddenly found themselves in the middle of nowhere with no idea how they got there, and their watches showed an hour and a half had gone by. He calls it a classic case of "missing time", lost hours that some people link to encounters with beings from elsewhere.
missing-time-waking-up-by-a-reservoir-da: Podcast host Jesse Michels tells of two US Air Force men, Mario Woods and Michael Johnson, who were on duty in South Dakota in November 1977. He says they had an experience of "missing time," a gap in memory that people who say they were taken by aliens often describe. In his account, their truck ended up parked behind the wall of a reservoir dam near a town called Newell, more than 8 miles from their post, which in his telling points to an abduction.
mission-control-split-between-nasa-and-t: Chris Bledsoe, a man who says UFOs appear around him and that NASA, the US space agency, has studied him, describes visiting mission control at Cape Canaveral, Florida, with a contact named Timothy Taylor. He says that on one side sat people at the consoles, and on the left was an identical setup staffed entirely by Air Force people. To him it suggests the military runs a hidden twin of the civilian space operation.
mission-to-recover-panasonic-toughbooks-: Jake Barber is a former helicopter pilot. On a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, he says he took part in a mission to recover sensitive information thought to be stored on Toughbooks, which are rugged laptop computers made by Panasonic. Barber says the laptops held evidence about recovering crashed craft that were not made by humans, and that they were brought back to a facility in the California desert.
misty-echo-test-portal-and-dan-burisch-s: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, describes a patch, a cloth badge, made for Misty Echo, a 1988 underground test at the government's test site in Nevada, and says its design looks like it shows a portal underground. Michels says this would fit the story told by Dan Burisch, a man who claims to know of secret work at S4, a site said to be near Area 51, the closely guarded military base in Nevada. If so, the patch would hint that something like a doorway was part of that secret work.
mit-dream-implantation-technology: On the show of a podcast host, Jesse Michels, a guest named Matthew Brown, introduced as a Pentagon whistleblower, says there are recent public technical applications from MIT, the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, about putting dreams into a person's mind, even from a distance. He names no specific source beyond MIT itself. If true, it would mean technology to shape what people dream already exists and is on the public record.
mit-ion-plane-credits-obscure-1920s-scie: Jan Lundquist, a researcher speaking in a documentary on Jesse Michels's channel about the scientist Townsend Brown, says that in 2018 the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) showed a plane with no moving parts, flown by electrically charged air, which it called an ion plane. Lundquist says this work owes a debt to a little-known scientist from the 1920s, which would mean ideas long dismissed as fringe actually worked.
mitchell-and-uri-geller-svahn-meets-gell: Clas Svahn, a longtime UFO researcher who keeps a large archive, says he spoke at length with Edgar Mitchell, an astronaut who walked on the Moon, about Mitchell's meeting with Uri Geller, a performer famous for claiming psychic powers such as bending spoons. Svahn says he met Geller himself too. The story matters to those who think an astronaut took psychic abilities seriously.
mitchell-confessed-blue-orbs-to-the-spac: A guest named Maaneli Derakhshani, on Jesse Michels' podcast, points to a book called In Plain Sight by journalist Ross Coulthart. He says the book quotes an anonymous close friend of astronaut Edgar Mitchell, nicknamed the Spaceman, who says Mitchell confessed that on the 1971 Apollo 14 moon mission the crew saw blue, orb-like lights following them or seen from the moon's surface. If true, it would mean astronauts met something unexplained on the moon.
mitchellhoagland-debate-on-coast-to-coas: A guest, Maaneli Derakhshani, says on a 2026 episode of Jesse Michels's podcast about the Moon that in the 1990s the astronaut Edgar Mitchell and a writer named Richard Hoagland had a long debate on Coast to Coast AM, a late-night American radio show hosted by Art Bell. He brings it up in a conversation about what NASA, the US space agency, may know about the Moon.
mithras-liturgy-ascent-through-seven-hea: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, describes the Mithras Liturgy, an ancient text found in a collection of Greek magic spells written on papyrus. He says that in it, a person being initiated uses breathing, visualisation, chanting and ritual to rise up through seven heavens. He brings it up as an ancient example of people trying to reach other levels of reality.
mitre-as-the-place-to-look-for-the-legac: A man called Jordan, who says he was taken into a secret UFO programme as a child, says that anyone looking for the "legacy program", a supposed decades-old secret effort to study recovered non-human craft, should look at MITRE. MITRE is a US nonprofit that runs research centres for the government. If true, it would point to where such a hidden programme sits.
mitre-funded-papers-detecting-gravitons-: Dave Rossi, a researcher who says he learned advanced physics in unusual ways, says on podcast host Jesse Michels' show that the MITRE Corporation, an American research company that does work for the government, funded scientific papers going back 20 to 25 years. According to Rossi, those papers show that gravitons, the tiny particles some physicists think carry the force of gravity, could be detected near Earth's atmosphere at both very high and very low frequencies. If so, it would mean gravity was being studied in secret ways long before the public knew.
mj-12-burned-memo-on-lancer-1963: A UFO historian named Richard Dolan describes a so-called burned memo, a partly burned paper among the Majestic documents, which are papers said to come from a secret group of officials who handled the UFO question. According to Dolan, the memo mentions Lancer, the code name for President John F. Kennedy, in 1963. If real, it would tie that secret UFO group to Kennedy in the year he died.
mj-12-document-cardinal-spellman-given-a: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, talks about the Majestic 12 documents, papers said to describe a secret group set up to handle UFO matters. He says one of them describes Francis Spellman, a Catholic cardinal, being given access to the materials from Roswell, New Mexico, where something is said to have crashed in 1947. If true, it would mean a senior church leader was let in on the secret.
mj-12-documents-surface-in-1984-sent-fro: Richard Dolan, a researcher who writes histories of UFOs, says on podcast host Jesse Michels' show that the MJ-12 documents, papers describing a supposed secret committee called Majestic 12 that handled crashed UFOs for the US government, first appeared in 1984. He says they were probably sent from somewhere near Kirtland Air Force Base, a US military base in Albuquerque, New Mexico, and he discusses them alongside people such as the Air Force agent Richard Doty and the UFO researcher Bill Moore. Where they came from matters because, if real, they would show a hidden top-level group, and if planted, someone inside the system wanted them out.
mj-12-papers-judged-compelling-but-not-c: Greg Bishop, a writer on UFO history, recalls that the MJ-12 papers surfaced in the 1980s: documents, including a supposed briefing memo for President Eisenhower, describing a secret group of officials said to handle crashed UFOs. Bishop says that when researcher Bill Moore first released a report on them, in a book called The MJ12 Papers, it judged them "compelling but not conclusive". If real, the papers would show a top-level government group managing the UFO question.
mj-12-scientists-really-were-involved-19: A writer named Whitley Strieber talks about Majestic 12, a name found in documents that describe a secret group of scientists and officials said to have handled UFO matters in the late 1940s and 1950s. Some people say a researcher named Stanton Friedman made the whole thing up, but Strieber says that is not true and that the scientists named, including a mathematician named John von Neumann, really were involved, even if the group's name was not real. If so, top American scientists would have been working on UFOs in secret from the start.
mj12-document-jfk-asks-dulles-for-a-revi: MJ12, or Majestic 12, is a set of papers said to describe a secret group that handled UFO matters for the US government. The podcast host Jesse Michels points to one of these papers, leaked in 1995. He says it records a top secret request from President John F. Kennedy to Allen Dulles, then head of the CIA, dated 28 June 1961. He notes that journalist Ross Coulthart discussed it on the TV channel NewsNation with Jeff Krushank, a former Australian intelligence officer. As they tell it, a diary of Dulles's released in 2022 shows the same date, which would suggest the paper is real. Coulthart tells it himself on the same episode, stressing that the MJ12 files are heavily disputed.
mj12-memos-reference-cic-involvement-at-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that leaked memos from the 1940s, known as the MJ12 papers and said to come from a secret group handling UFO matters, mention the CIC, a US Army counterintelligence unit, taking part in UFO investigations. He says this includes Roswell, New Mexico, where a crashed object is said to have been recovered in 1947, which would tie military intelligence directly to that case if the memos are real.
mk-monarch-acknowledged: Kurt Metzger, a comedian, says on podcast host Jesse Michels' show that his friend Emma made a YouTube show called Imagination Podcast about MK Monarch, a name he uses for an alleged secret mind-control programme. Metzger says that MK Monarch has been acknowledged, and he says he sent the host a link about it. If so, it would mean a programme many dismiss had been officially admitted.
mk-ultra-bluebird-artichoke-and-occult-r: An author introduced as a CIA historian, Peter Levenda, tells podcast host Jesse Michels in 2025 that during MK Ultra, Bluebird and Artichoke, secret American programmes of the 1950s and 60s that researched control of the human mind, and another operation he names, government researchers were looking at occult systems, meaning magic and hidden spiritual traditions. If true, it would mean intelligence agencies took the occult seriously as a tool.
mk-ultra-born-of-mind-control-race-fears: A well-known skeptic, Michael Shermer, in a 2026 debate with podcast host Jesse Michels, says that MK Ultra, a secret US government programme of the 1950s to 1970s that experimented with mind control, came out of fear that America was losing a race with the Russians on mind control. He offers it as an example of how secret programmes grew out of Cold War worries.
mk-ultra-lsd-dosing-death-at-new-york-ho: Dan Sheehan, a lawyer who has worked on many high-profile government cases, tells of a man who went to a New York City hospital in the 1950s for counselling. Sheehan says the hospital was running MK Ultra experiments, a secret CIA mind-control research programme, and after about two days staff gave him a huge dose of the drug LSD without telling him, and the man died. Sheehan says the death was covered up with help from politician Jacob Javits and judge Warren Burger, which would mean powerful officials hid the programme's harms.
mk-ultra-purpose-lsd-as-interrogation-tr: Dan Sheehan, speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast, talks about MK Ultra, a secret program of the CIA, the US spy agency, that tested mind-altering drugs in the 1950s and 60s. Sheehan says its aim was to use LSD, a powerful psychedelic drug, as a truth serum for questioning people, because a dose dissolves the boundaries of how a person organizes their thoughts. If true, the drug tests were really about breaking down people under interrogation.
mk-ultra-remote-viewing-and-ufos-under-o: Dylan Borland, a researcher, says on podcast host Jesse Michels' show that MK Ultra, the CIA's mind-control experiments that began in the 1950s, remote viewing, which is the attempt to see distant places using only the mind, and UFO study all sit under one umbrella. He ties in James Lacatski, a government scientist who led a Pentagon study of strange events, and Skinwalkers at the Pentagon, a book about that study. If true, it would mean the same hidden part of government has run all these efforts for decades.
mlk-essay-on-mystery-religions-and-chris: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says the civil rights leader Martin Luther King wrote a little-known essay called 'The Influence of the Mystery Religions on Christianity', about the secret initiation cults of the ancient Mediterranean. He links it to the work of Dennis MacDonald, a scholar of early Christian writings, and to the Gospel of John. He tells it to suggest that Christianity borrowed from older hidden religious traditions.
modern-4602d-personnel-attend-ramsay-lec: Scott Ramsay, a researcher of an alleged UFO crash in New Mexico, says people from today's version of the 4602D, an Air Force intelligence unit tied to investigating UFO reports, came to one of his lectures. He says this happened in Denver, Colorado. If true, it would suggest the military still quietly follows UFO research.
moment-of-contact-the-varginha-witnesses: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, praises Moment of Contact, a documentary by the filmmaker James Fox about events in 1996 in Varginha, a town in Brazil, where residents say strange beings were seen and captured. Michels says these local witnesses are not part of any US government story and are not lying, and he notes that the beings were described with three fingers, which he links to three-fingered bodies reported in Peru.
monk-timotheus-says-other-monks-have-see: A man named Ralph, speaking on podcast host Jesse Michels' show, says that in 1991 he met a monk named Timotheus at Dionysiou, a monastery on Mount Athos, a mountain in Greece full of Orthodox Christian monasteries. According to Ralph, the monk told him that other monks had seen a light they called the light of the Virgin Mary coming down, and suggested Ralph might have seen it too. Ralph tells it because it hints that the strange lights he saw may be the same thing holy men have long described.
monsanto-chemicals-sprayed-in-vietnam-ca: Brigham Buhler, a guest on podcast host Jesse Michels' show about drug companies and human experiments, says that Monsanto, a large American chemical company, shipped its chemicals to Vietnam and to poorer countries that had few safety rules. According to Buhler, the chemicals were sprayed on crops there and then began causing birth defects. He tells it as an example of companies harming people where no one was watching.
monsanto-pays-agent-orange-veterans-comp: On an episode about UFOs and past human experiments by drug and chemical companies, made with a guest named Brigham Buhler, podcast host Jesse Michels says that in the mid-1980s the chemical company Monsanto was required to pay millions in compensation to war veterans. These veterans had been exposed to Agent Orange, a highly toxic chemical. He uses it as an example of big companies harming people and being held to account only later.
montagnier-dna-water-teleportation-confi: Dave Rossi, a man who says aliens taught him advanced physics, refers to a paper by a French scientist, Luc Montagnier, claiming that the signal of DNA can be passed into water at a distance, which he calls teleportation. Rossi says he has personally witnessed lab experiments in private laboratories that confirm it. If true, it would mean biology and water behave in ways mainstream science does not accept.
montauk-experiments-1950: Podcast host Jesse Michels mentions the Montauk experiments, secret experiments said to have been carried out in Montauk, New York, in the 1950s and 1960s. He says he believes some kind of machinery was found there, and he points to a book by an author he remembers as "Preston something," Preston Nichols. If that is true, it would mean the government ran hidden experiments there that the public never heard about.
montauk-experiments-behind-stranger-thin: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that even the makers of Stranger Things, a popular TV series about secret government experiments, say it is based on the Montauk experiments. Michels says it is pretty well established that some experiments took place at Montauk, on Long Island, New York, though he doesn't say what they were. People tell the story because it suggests strange secret research really happened there.
months-of-swarms-over-navy-ships-off-sou: A commentator, Marik von Rennenkampf, passing on what journalists Jeremy Corbell and George Knapp have reported, says that in 2019 US Navy ships off the Channel Islands and the Southern California coast faced five or six months of incursions by unexplained objects. Corbell tells it a little differently: he speaks of about 100 UAP, short for unidentified anomalous phenomena, the official term for UFOs, in swarms, and says some were shaped like pyramids, without naming the place. If true, it would mean unknown craft repeatedly moved around Navy warships for months.
montserrat-scanned-and-found-to-carry-a-: Jesse Michels, a podcast host, says that while visiting Peru in the 2020s he was shown footage of scans of "Montserrat", one of several small mummified bodies with three fingers on each hand found there. He says the footage captured the exact moment the scanners discovered she was carrying a fetus, live as it happened. If true, it would mean these three-fingered beings could reproduce, like a real species.
moon-dust-document-fireball-and-silent-a: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, cites a declassified document from Moon Dust, a US government effort to recover objects that fell from the sky. He says it describes a fireball in Bolivia followed by sightings of silent aircraft near the crash site, which he raises as a sign that the government quietly tracked and retrieved unknown crashed objects.
moon-dust-document-spherical-objects-rec: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, cites a declassified document from Moon Dust, a US government effort to recover objects that fell from the sky. He says it describes spherical objects being recovered from farmland in New Zealand, which he offers as evidence that the government ran a quiet worldwide crash retrieval effort.
moon-ruins-at-33-in-the-disney-von-braun: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, describes a 1950s space film made by Walt Disney with the rocket engineer Wernher von Braun. He says that in one long scene astronauts reach the far side of the Moon for the first time and a radar engineer shouts that their sensors are picking up radiation at 33 degrees, a scene Michels reads as a hint that the filmmakers knew of ruins there.
moon-s-two-moments-of-inertia-suggest-it: A researcher, Randall Carlson, says on a 2025 episode of Jesse Michels's podcast that he is willing to consider that the Moon was geoengineered, meaning deliberately shaped by someone, in the remote past. His reason, as the story is summarised, is that the Moon seems to have two moments of inertia, a measure of how its mass is spread out, which he finds odd for a natural body. If true, it would mean someone built or reshaped our Moon.
moore-benowitz-operation-as-a-24-hour-st: Greg Bishop, a writer who has researched UFO deception, says on podcast host Jesse Michels' show that the UFO researcher Bill Moore described the Benowitz operation, an effort around the late 1970s and early 1980s near Kirtland Air Force Base in New Mexico aimed at a man who believed he was picking up alien signals, as a 24-hour stage play. Moore drew on the writing of Harry Rositzke, a former CIA officer. If that is right, it would mean the whole affair was a staged performance put on by government agents.
moore-hands-aquarius-document-to-benowit: A writer named Greg Bishop retells a story from 1981 in Albuquerque, New Mexico, about a UFO researcher named Bill Moore and a local businessman named Paul Bennewitz. Bishop says the two went into a supply closet at Bennewitz's office, turned the radio up, and Moore handed him the Aquarius document, a paper said to describe a secret government UFO project, saying he had been told to pass it on and to take it with a grain of salt. Told this way, it would mean someone was deliberately feeding Bennewitz material.
moore-photographs-documents-in-an-upstat: Greg Bishop, a writer who has researched UFO deception, says on podcast host Jesse Michels' show that the UFO researcher Bill Moore told of being sent, in the early 1980s, to a hotel room in upstate New York. According to the story, Moore was told to go there partway through his dealings with government contacts, and he photographed documents in that room. It matters because it would show insiders were feeding him secret papers in a carefully controlled way.
more-crash-retrievals-in-the-ocean-than-: A retired US Navy admiral, Tim Gallaudet, passes on a claim from a man named Eric Davis. According to Gallaudet, Davis has said that more crash retrievals, meaning operations to recover crashed unknown craft, have happened in the ocean than anywhere else. If true, it would mean the sea is where most such secret recoveries take place.
more-detailed-image-based-communications: Dan Sherman, a former Air Force sergeant who says the NSA, the US signals intelligence agency, trained him to talk to aliens with his mind, describes his work at a site he calls Base 2 in the early 1990s. He says the messages became much more colourful there, coming as pictures and images with emotion, showing things like rockets and troop movements. If true, it would mean the government ran a telepathic line to non-human beings.
more-than-one-non-human-species-not-all-: Richard Barth, a former guard at a US nuclear missile site, tells podcast host Jesse Michels about being taken by non-human beings around September 1964 at Vandenberg, an Air Force base in California. He says he learned that more than one non-human species was involved, and that not all of them were as kind as the ones he met. If true, it would mean that whatever is visiting us is not one friendly group but several, with different aims.
morgan-and-townsend-brown-s-conversation: In a documentary about Townsend Brown, a scientist he presents as having worked for the CIA and having built UFO-like craft, podcast host Jesse Michels tells of a conversation in the office of a man named Morgan. According to Michels, Brown asked Morgan, "What if we had the ability to time travel?" and said he believed they would be able to do it in their lifetime. In his telling, this shows how far Brown thought his research could go.
morgan-robertson-s-wreck-of-the-titan-fo: A novel written in 1898, years before the Titanic sank, seems to tell its story ahead of time. In Morgan Robertson's Futility, or the Wreck of the Titan, the Titan is the largest and most luxurious ocean liner ever built, and it hits an iceberg in the North Atlantic on an April night and sinks. Michels tells it several times as something he knows from his reading. Once he dates the book only vaguely, to the early twentieth century, about ten years before the Titanic, and another time he says "like 12 years before". The writer Eric Wargo also tells it, drawing on his own book Time Loops, which is about dreams and hunches that seem to foresee the future. If it is more than coincidence, it would suggest that people can glimpse what is still to come.
morgan-says-brown-was-cia-research-1950: Jan Lundquist, who appears in a documentary about the inventor Townsend Brown, an American who built devices some say were early flying saucer technology, speaks on podcast host Jesse Michels' show. Lundquist says that a man named Morgan told Paul Schatzkin, a writer who studied Brown's life, that Brown's work was basically CIA research. If true, it would mean the US spy agency was quietly behind Brown's work from the 1950s on.
mork-mindy-white-egg-as-a-hint-of-hidden: A man named Jake Barber, who says he helped retrieve a UFO with his helicopter, brings up Mork & Mindy, a 1970s American TV comedy where Robin Williams played an alien. Barber points out that in every episode the alien flies to Earth in a white egg, and he suggests this may hint that someone knew about real egg-shaped craft. If true, it would mean hidden knowledge was slipped into popular television.
mormonism-as-a-ufo-religion-joseph-smith: A commentator, Matthew Pines, tells podcast host Jesse Michels in 2024 that if you look into Mormonism, the religion founded by Joseph Smith in the United States between the 1820s and 1840s, it is 'kind of a UFO religion'. He points to Smith's reported contacts with otherworldly beings and the messages he says Smith received, which, read that way, would put UFO-like encounters at the root of a major faith.
morphologies-of-the-peruvian-mummies: Podcast host Jesse Michels talks about a set of mummified bodies from Peru that some people say are not human. He says they come in different body types, which he calls the J types, the S types and the M types. The idea is that more than one kind of being is represented.
moses-burning-bush-as-a-plasmoid: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, suggests that the Bible story of Moses speaking to a burning bush on Mount Sinai could have been a plasmoid, a glowing ball of electrically charged gas, and so a kind of modern UFO encounter. He draws on a book by the author Robert Temple called A New Science of Heaven, and the idea would mean some ancient religious visions were the same thing people now report as UFOs.
most-hessdalen-residents-report-experien: Jesse Michels, a podcast host, says he visited Hessdalen, a valley in Norway known for strange lights, and talked with the people who live there. He says it was easy to see that a very high share of residents, upwards of 80 to 90 percent by his estimate, had experienced something odd themselves. If true, it would make Hessdalen a place where these experiences are ordinary local life, not rare events.
mosul-dam-turbine-proof-of-concept-scan-: A researcher named Jeffrey, on Jesse Michels's podcast about a supposed energy grid under the pyramids of Egypt, says that in 2024 a team, which he links to someone named Filippo, scanned the Mosul Dam in Iraq. He calls it a proof of concept, a test showing their scanning method could see inside a big structure like the dam and its turbines. If it works, the same method could reveal what lies hidden beneath the pyramids.
mother-ayahuasca-gives-hancock-a-novel-s: Graham Hancock, a writer known for books on lost ancient civilizations, says that in 2006 in Brazil he drank ayahuasca, a psychedelic brew from the Amazon, over five sessions. He says that during them he was given, literally, the entire plot of a novel, which became his book Entangled. He credits the plot to the spirit people call Mother Ayahuasca, which would mean the brew can pass on ideas from outside the mind.
mother-faking-telepathy-on-danny-jones-s: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, talks about The Telepathy Tapes, a series about children said to communicate by reading minds. He says a mother of one of the children who went on the show of another podcast host, Danny Jones, was in his view faking it, and was clearly peeking past her blindfold. Michels calls this unfortunate, since he thinks such cases hurt the more serious claims.
mother-s-apparition-in-the-kitchen: Mario Woods, a former guard at a US nuclear weapons site, tells podcast host Jesse Michels that a couple of days after his mother died, at home in Tampa, Florida, he and his family saw her standing in the kitchen during a lightning storm. He says the family talked about it among themselves afterwards. If true, it would suggest that the dead can somehow appear to the living.
mother-s-earlier-sightings-in-rocky-moun: Mario Woods, a former guard at a nuclear site who says he was abducted, tells on podcast host Jesse Michels' show that his mother once told him she had seen things before. He says she saw them as a child growing up in Rocky Mount, North Carolina, but she never explained further. He tells it because it suggests strange encounters may run in his family.
mothership-at-langley-incursion-per-chri: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, relays what Chris Mellon, a former senior Pentagon intelligence official under Presidents Clinton and Bush, has said about unknown objects flying over Langley Air Force Base in Hampton, Virginia, in 2023. According to Michels, Mellon said there was a mothership pattern, with small saucers flying out of a larger craft. If true, it would mean a coordinated group of unknown craft entered a US military base's airspace.
motion-sciences-anti-gravity-effort-debu: The owner of Skinwalker Ranch, a Utah property famous for reports of strange events, tells podcast host Jesse Michels about an effort called Motion Sciences, run around 2010 out of a hangar at the Provo Airport in Utah, that aimed to build anti-gravity technology, a way of lifting things without pushing against air or ground. He says two scientists, Dr. Hal Puthoff and Dr. Kit Green, sat on its science advisory board, alongside a businessman named Joe Firmage, and that he was there when the effort's claims were shown not to hold up.
mount-athos-dedicated-to-mary-and-closed: A guest on Jesse Michels's podcast, a man named Ralph who speaks as a witness, says that to this day women cannot set foot on Mount Athos, a mountain in Greece. He says this is because the mountain is dedicated entirely to Mary, the mother of Jesus, and women are excluded. He brings it up as part of a wider discussion of sacred and ancient oracle sites in Greece.
mount-kailash-as-an-energy-vortex-where-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, describes a mountain called Mount Kailash as an "energy vortex", a place where some special force is said to gather. As proof, he passes on what a man he calls Sod Guru said: that his fingernails grew faster while he was on the mountain. If true, it would mean the place itself changes the human body in some way.
mount-nemrut-near-lake-van-erupted-at-en: Matt LaCroix, a researcher speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast, talks about Mount Nemrut, a volcano southwest of Lake Van in Turkey. He says it last erupted at the end of the last ice age, around the sudden cold periods known as the Older and Younger Dryas. If true, it adds to his picture of a great catastrophe striking the world around 12,000 BC.
mount-nyangani-as-a-ufo-repair-facility: A former Army sergeant named Lyn Buchanan says that he looked into Mount Nyangani, a mountain in Zimbabwe, and found that it seems to be a repair facility for UFOs. If true, it would mean craft that are not human are being fixed inside a mountain on Earth.
mount-shasta-portal-opening-and-the-10-f: Grant Cameron, a researcher who writes about UFOs, tells a story set on Mount Shasta, a mountain in northern California, around 2014 and 2015. He says a group of people opened a "portal" there in 2014, a kind of doorway to somewhere else, and that in 2015 he interviewed almost everyone who was present. According to Cameron, what they described seeing was a being about ten feet tall who wore boots. If true, it would mean people met a giant non-human being on a California mountain.
mount-st-helens-observers-killed-by-heat: Matt LaCroix, a guest on Jesse Michels' podcast who talks about ancient catastrophes, points to the 1980 eruption of Mount St Helens, a volcano in Washington State. According to LaCroix, documentaries show that people watching from five to ten miles away were killed by the heat. He tells it to show how far the force of a natural disaster can reach, which would matter for his ideas about a great catastrophe long ago.
mount-wilson-cover-up-buried-fried-serve: The owner of Skinwalker Ranch, a Utah property famous for reports of strange events, tells podcast host Jesse Michels about a site on Mount Wilson, said to be property of the businessman Robert Bigelow. He says that from around 1996 onward his team found evidence of earlier activity there and a cover-up, including buried, burned-out computer servers and a buried rail system. If true, it would mean someone did secret work at the site and tried to hide it.
mount-zeil-as-an-alien-port-of-entry-to-: A former Army sergeant named Lyn Buchanan says that Mount Zeil, a mountain in Australia, is a kind of port of entry to Earth, a place where friendly beings from elsewhere arrive. He links the idea to another man, Pat Price. If true, it would mean visitors who are not human have a regular doorway onto our planet.
mountain-bike-ride-with-missing-time-at-: John Blitch, a scientist who worked with DARPA, the Pentagon's advanced research agency, tells podcast host Jesse Michels that in 1995 he went on a mountain bike ride at Daniels Park, a site south of Denver, Colorado, said to hold an old burial ground. He says he lost at least five hours he cannot account for, something his wife Cindy is part of the story of, and that before this ride he had been a skeptic. He presents it as the event that changed his mind about contact with non-human beings.
mountain-bike-sabotage-after-senate-brie: Steven Greer, a campaigner who has long pushed for the government to reveal what it knows about UFOs, says that in 2023 he gave a briefing to people at the US Senate. About three weeks later, he says, someone sawed through the bolt that holds the seat on his mountain bike. He tells it as a sign that someone wanted to hurt or frighten him for speaking out.
mountains-as-possible-non-human-no-go-zo: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, talks about mountains such as Secret Mountain in Arizona, Mount Shasta in California and Mount Inyangani in Zimbabwe as places where, he says, people see glowing orbs and craft going into the mountain. He raises the idea that these spots could be areas held by non-human beings, places humans are kept away from.
mountains-worldwide-as-possible-alien-ba: On an episode with the owner of Skinwalker Ranch, a ranch famous in UFO circles for reports of strange events, podcast host Jesse Michels suggests that mountains around the world could be bases for aliens. He lists Mount Zeil in Australia, Mount Hayes in Alaska, Mount Perdido and Mount Shasta. If he is right, it would mean non-human beings are hidden inside or under mountains on several continents.
moving-boulders-of-the-mojave-racetrack: Michael Shermer, a researcher known as a skeptic, brings up the story of the moving boulders in the Mojave Desert in California: big rocks that seem to have shifted across the desert floor with no one moving them. He mentions it on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, in a debate about UFOs, as an example of a strange story told about a place.
moving-the-sine-wave-by-mentally-humming: Dan Sherman, a former Air Force sergeant who says the NSA, the US agency that intercepts communications, hired him to talk to aliens with his mind, tells of training in the early 1990s at a facility near the NSA complex in Maryland. He says he had to mentally hum a tone while watching a wavy line, a sine wave, on a box, and that when he saw the line move it all came into focus. He tells the story in his book Above Black, and if true it would mean the government trained people in telepathic communication.
mr-d-s-signal-discovery-for-locating-uap: James Valor, from Skywatcher, a startup that says it tries to call up and track UFOs, says a colleague known only as Mr. D worked out how to pick up signals from these objects, which officials now call UAP, short for unidentified anomalous phenomena, so the team could tell where they were in the sky. Valor also says that, sometime between 2021 and 2025, government radar saw the same objects but did not tell Skywatcher. If true, it would mean these objects can be found on purpose, and that the government knew more than it shared.
mr-x-s-work-on-exotic-vacuum-objects-and: Jay Anderson, a guest on Jesse Michels' podcast, talks about a man he will only call Mr. X, who he says is not a government man but a true savant. Anderson says that around 2020 and 2021 Mr. X did a great deal of work on what are called exotic vacuum objects, or EVOs, and on self-organizing plasma, meaning electrically charged gas that arranges itself into shapes. If true, it would mean a private outsider had made real progress on strange forms of energy.
mris-of-ufo-contact-dod-and-intelligence: Garry Nolan, a scientist at Stanford University, says that in the 2010s he was shown MRIs, which are detailed brain scans, of people from the Department of Defense (the US military) and intelligence agencies, most of whom had had run-ins with UFOs, and that they showed a larger than usual caudate-putamen, a pair of structures deep in the brain. If true, it could mean some people are wired in a way that makes these encounters more likely. The podcast host Jesse Michels later raised it as a question, wondering whether fighter pilots who see UFOs might more often have this brain feature.
muldoon-americans-wanted-kaikoura-shut-d: A journalist, Ross Coulthart, says he interviewed a man named Robert Muldoon in New Zealand in the early 1980s and asked about Kaikoura, a 1978 New Zealand case that the story ties to UFOs. Coulthart says Muldoon chuckled and let slip something like, "Yeah, the Americans wanted that one shut down pretty quickly." If true, it would mean the United States pushed to close down the case.
multi-billion-dollar-propaganda-book-cam: Brent Friedman, a guest on Jesse Michels' podcast talking about Hollywood, the CIA and UFOs, passes on what a man named John Harrington said around 1981. According to Friedman, Harrington said that next to the honest books on the shelves sit books "we publish full of propaganda", part of a multi-billion dollar campaign to cover up the truth. If true, it would mean someone was spending vast sums to steer what the public reads about UFOs.
mummified-pharaohs-in-the-cairo-museum-w: On an episode about the pyramids with a guest named Luke Caverns, podcast host Jesse Michels says that some of the mummified pharaohs (ancient Egyptian kings) in the national museum in Cairo look very short. He says they clearly reshaped their skulls on purpose to look like the gods. To him they resemble gray aliens, the small, big-headed beings described in many alien encounter stories, and if that is true it would suggest the ancient Egyptians were imitating beings like that.
muon-detected-big-void-to-be-excavated-i: A researcher named Jeffrey, speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast, talks about the "Big Void": a large empty space inside the Great Pyramid of Giza in Egypt. It was found by the ScanPyramids team, a group that looks inside pyramids using muons, tiny particles from space that pass through stone. Jeffrey says that in 2026, with approval from Egypt's Ministry of Antiquities, the government office in charge of ancient sites, workers will dig into the pyramid to investigate the void, which could reveal what the space was built for.
muon-team-may-have-mistaken-the-grand-ga: Inside the Great Pyramid of Giza in Egypt is a long, tall sloping passage called the Grand Gallery, and in the 2020s a research team called ScanPyramids used muon detectors, which read tiny particles from space that pass through stone, to report a large hidden space they named the Big Void. A researcher named Filippo, speaking on Jesse Michels' podcast, says the team may have been confused, and that what they saw could be the floor or roof of the Grand Gallery itself, though at another point he describes the void as running parallel to the gallery. If he is right, the famous hidden chamber might not be a new room at all.
musgrave-saw-snake-like-things-writhing-: Kevin Knuth, a guest on a podcast episode about NASA (the US space agency) and hidden UFO data, passes on the story of Musgrave, a pilot on the Space Shuttle, the American spacecraft that carried crews into orbit. Knuth says Musgrave spoke of seeing things like snakes out in space. The podcast host, Jesse Michels, repeats the story in nearly the same words. If true, it would mean something moving, maybe even alive, is out there around the Earth.
musha-s-ex-honda-team-and-capacitors-in-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, mentions a team in Japan that he believes came out of the carmaker Honda, led by a scientist he thinks is named Musha. According to Michels, their work involves capacitors, devices that store electric charge, placed in transmission oil, and he brings it up while talking about efforts to build propulsion that works against gravity. If it worked, it would be a step toward the kind of flight people link to UFOs.
mushrooms-tell-mckenna-about-hyperlight-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, has told several times how the writer Terence McKenna said magic mushrooms spoke to him, pointing to McKenna's book True Hallucinations. In Michels' retelling, the mushrooms said that within their memory lay the blueprints for hyperlight drives, engines that would carry ships faster than light, and in one version this happened on a two-week trip in the Amazon. If taken at face value, it would mean the mushrooms carry knowledge from somewhere far beyond us.
musk-and-mike-griffin-go-to-russia-for-r: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells a story from the early days of the businessman Elon Musk's rocket ambitions, around the early 2000s. According to Michels, Musk and a space engineer named Mike Griffin travelled to Russia looking for rocket engines, and they actually found them. He tells it as part of the backstory of how private spaceflight got started.
mussolini-asks-hitler-about-the-magenta-: A podcast host named Jesse Michels, talking with a former presidential advisor, says that an object crashed in Italy around 1933, and that it is known as the Magenta object. According to Michels, the story goes that Italy's dictator Benito Mussolini then went to Adolf Hitler in Germany and the two formed a partnership over it. If true, it would mean that a crashed craft was being studied by governments well before the Second World War.
myles-standish-recalculates-and-dismisse: This story is about a hidden planet far out in the solar system that was talked about and then dropped. Matt LaCroix, a researcher, says on Jesse Michels' podcast that in the 1990s NASA, the US space agency, spoke of something like a "Planet 10." Then, he says, an astronomer named Myles Standish redid the maths and said, in effect, we made a mistake, forget about it. LaCroix tells it to suggest that the idea of a hidden planet was dismissed too quickly.
myrna-hansen-hypnotic-regression-and-und: Greg Bishop, a researcher and author, tells of a woman named Myrna Hansen who, in the 1980s, kept visiting the house of a man named Paul Bennewitz in Albuquerque, New Mexico. Bishop says she talked about being abducted and taken to an underground facility. The title links her story to hypnotic regression, where a hypnotist tries to recover hidden memories, and Bishop names a counselor called Leo Sprinkle, along with Sandia National Laboratories, a US government research lab near the city. If true, it would point to a secret underground base tied to abductions.
mysterious-death-of-pat-price-1975: A former US Army sergeant, Lyn Buchanan, talks about the death of a man named Pat Price in 1975, in a story that also involves a man named Hal Puthoff. Buchanan says he has heard from people who were there a different account from the published one, and in one telling he adds that it happened in Washington DC, that an unmarked ambulance was involved, and that a head of security later said that Price died "and we haven't heard from him since." The remark suggests, as Buchanan tells it, that Price's death may not have been what it seemed.
mysterious-jungle-sickness-and-deafness-: Luke Caverns, a researcher who studies ancient pyramids, tells podcast host Jesse Michels that on a 2024 trip to Tikal, the ruins of an ancient Maya city in the Guatemalan jungle, he came down with a mysterious illness. He says that by the end of the trip he had lost about 75 percent of the hearing in each ear.
mysterious-man-plays-ransone-a-metallic-: An unnamed researcher, on Jesse Michels' podcast, retells a story from a YouTube interview given by a woman named Valerie Ransone. According to the telling, in Houston in the early 1970s a mysterious man put a cassette tape into his car stereo, and it played a metallic voice that was presented as coming from an alien. If true, it would mean someone had recordings of non-human voices and was sharing them quietly.
mystery-airship-phenomenon-1807: Tim Alberino, a researcher and filmmaker, mentions the "mystery airship phenomenon": reports in the 1800s, in the United States and Europe, of strange flying craft seen in the sky at a time when nobody was supposed to have such machines. He brings it up as something that happened "at the same time" as other strange events he describes, and credits the idea to a UFO historian named Richard Dolan. If true, it would mean unknown craft were flying long before modern aircraft existed.
mystery-schools-aim-to-recover-the-lost-: Tim Alberino, a guest on Jesse Michels' podcast, says that one of the main goals of the mystery schools, secret groups that pass down hidden teachings, is to recover the lost knowledge of the gods from Mars. He links this to the work of a writer named David Flynn and to Cydonia, a region of Mars that some people believe holds artificial structures. If true, it would mean these secret traditions believe gods once lived on Mars.
name-dennis-mariani-confirmed-by-someone: Jesse Michels, a podcast host, spent time with Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked on alien craft at a hidden site in the Nevada desert in the late 1980s. Michels says he knows of one case where a name from Lazar's story, Dennis Mariani, was confirmed by someone at the Nevada Test Site, a large government area in the desert used for weapons testing. If true, it would back up a piece of Lazar's account with a voice from inside.
nanosims-analysis-finds-anomalous-magnes: A Stanford University scientist named Garry Nolan says he tested some small metal fragments, known as the Ubatuba fragments, that are claimed to be pieces of a UFO. He says that sometime between the 2010s and 2021 he used a NanoSIMS, a machine that measures the exact mix of slightly different forms (isotopes) of an element in a tiny sample, and that one fragment was anomalous: its magnesium ratios were "way off" from what is normally found. If true, it would suggest the metal was made in an unusual way or came from somewhere unusual.
narmer-palette-shows-egypt-existed-befor: Geoffrey Drumm, a guest on Jesse Michels' podcast who has his own theory about the pyramids, points to the Narmer Palette, an ancient carved stone slab from Egypt. He says the start of the age of the pharaohs is marked by the "reunification" of Upper and Lower Egypt shown on the palette, and that the word means a united Egypt must have existed before. If true, it would push Egyptian civilization further back than the usual story.
narrator-clip-the-channeler-s-second-tra: In a clip played on Jesse Michels's podcast, an unnamed narrator describes a scene in Washington, D.C., in 1959. A channeler, someone who claims to pass along messages from other beings while in a trance, is said to have gone into trance a second time in front of a man named Friend. According to the narrator, the man sat for several minutes and then seemed to fall into a deep trance, his Adam's apple moving rapidly up and down, which would suggest contact with non-human beings was being tested in front of government witnesses.
nasa-3i-atlas-press-conference-2025: In 2025 NASA, the US space agency, held a press conference about 3I/ATLAS, an object passing through our solar system from somewhere outside it. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, calls it an idiotic press conference about manipulation, and he points to the views of an astronomer, Avi Loeb. In Michels's framing, it is a sign that NASA is not being open about what such objects might be.
nasa-administrator-isaacman-says-some-ca: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Jared Isaacman, the current head of NASA, the US space agency, has admitted that some UFO cases are unresolved. In a later episode Michels says this came after the Department of War, the name now used for the Defense Department, released a first batch of files on space exploration and astronaut encounters. As Michels tells it, Isaacman said this was not about reverse engineering UFOs or confirmed alien bodies, but that the sightings were unexplained, which Michels calls a huge update.
nasa-announcement-of-planet-x-planet-10-: Matt LaCroix, a writer on ancient history, says that NASA, the US space agency, once made an announcement about an unknown planet in the far outer solar system. He believes it was a real announcement and says they called it Planet X or Planet 10. If true, it would mean a large hidden world sits beyond the known planets, which some link to stories about ancient catastrophes.
nasa-announcement-of-possible-life-on-ma: Dan Sherman, a former Air Force sergeant who says the NSA, the US spy agency that listens in on communications, hired him to talk with aliens, mentions a recent news item in 2025. He says that NASA, the US space agency, had just announced it found some sort of life on Mars. If true, it would be official word that life exists beyond Earth.
nasa-assessor-baron-killed-by-train-500-: Joe Rogan, a well-known podcast host, tells of a man named Thomas Baron who, he says, was hired by NASA, the US space agency, around 1967 to assess how likely its programme was to succeed. According to Rogan, Baron wrote a 500-page report, was then killed by a train, and the report vanished. Rogan tells it as a sign that someone may have wanted Baron's findings buried.
nasa-attempt-to-read-the-ramey-memo-with: Kevin Knuth is a physicist who once worked at NASA, the US space agency. On a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, he says that in the early 2000s, while at NASA's Intelligent Systems Division, he and his colleagues wrote computer programs to try to read the Ramey memo. That is an old memo, barely readable, that people have long tried to make out, hoping it says something about a UFO crash. Knuth tells it as an example of serious scientists looking at UFO evidence.
nasa-dart-mission-hits-dimorphos-2022: In 2022 NASA, the US space agency, flew a spacecraft called DART into a small space rock named Dimorphos, which circles a larger one. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, brings it up in an episode about the idea that the Moon is an alien spaceship, saying he looked into the mission and that the craft was knocking into the rock. He raises it as a clue to how bodies in space really behave.
nasa-department-of-war-special-investiga: A guest named Maaneli Derakhshani told podcast host Jesse Michels about an image of lights from Apollo 17, a 1970s US Moon mission. He says NASA released the image in 2026 as part of the first batch of its files on UAP, the government's newer term for UFOs, and that the description next to it states that NASA and the Department of War, the name now used for the Pentagon, have opened a special investigation into that image. If true, it would mean officials still see something unexplained in a picture from the Moon.
nasa-didn-t-want-to-talk-after-news-call: Chris Bledsoe, a man who says he draws UFOs to him and that NASA, the US space agency, has studied him, tells what he heard from a friend at the CIA in Washington around 2024 or 2025. According to Bledsoe, something he said caught the attention of the news, reporters called NASA, and NASA's reaction was that it did not want to talk about it. He tells it as a sign that the agency knows more than it says.
nasa-director-wrote-psychic-spy-manual-f: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says he thinks there is a director at NASA, the US space agency, named Steven Hubbard, as he believes, who wrote a psychic spy manual for the CIA, America's foreign spy agency. If true, it would tie the space agency to government work on using the mind to gather secrets.
nasa-eagle-works-engineer-s-casimir-effe: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells of an engineer from NASA Eagle Works, a small lab at the US space agency that looked at far-out ideas for moving through space. Michels says the engineer claims to have produced 1.5 kilovolts and powered a little microchip using the Casimir effect, a tiny force that appears between objects held very close together in empty space. If true, it would mean energy can be drawn from empty space itself.
nasa-electrostatics-lab-measures-thrust-: A man named Charles Bueller, who works in an electrostatics lab at NASA's Kennedy Space Center in Florida, says his team has been testing devices for thrust inside a high vacuum since 2020, almost every day or every other day. He links the work to the ideas of an earlier inventor, Townsend Brown, and to a colleague called Drew. If the thrust is real, it would point to a way of moving craft without ordinary fuel or propellant.
nasa-electrostatics-scientist-charles-bu: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, describes a scientist named Charles Buehler, who he says worked on electrostatics (the study of static electric charge) at NASA, the US space agency. Michels says Buehler insists that the effect they are discussing is real and that it works even in a vacuum, the empty conditions of space. If true, it would mean a kind of electrical push that could work beyond the air, where many critics say it should not.
nasa-employee-wrote-a-cia-remote-viewing: Kevin Knuth, a scientist who once worked at NASA, the US space agency, says he was told that one of his NASA colleagues wrote a training manual for the CIA, the US foreign intelligence agency. The manual, he says, was for remote viewing: the claimed skill of seeing distant places or hidden things with the mind alone. If true, it would tie a government science agency to psychic spying work.
nasa-experiment-tardigrades-survive-18-m: A guest named Dr. Gilbert says that NASA, the US space agency, ran an experiment outside the International Space Station in which tardigrades, tiny eight-legged animals, survived 18 months in the vacuum of space. He tells it on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels as a point about how tough some life can be, which matters to the question of whether life can survive beyond Earth.
nasa-flight-surgeon-on-apollo-astronauts: John Blitch, a former scientist at DARPA, the Pentagon's research agency, says that in the summer of 2008 he was diving at Aquarius, an underwater research base off Key Largo in Florida, with a NASA flight surgeon, a doctor who looks after astronauts, whom he won't name. According to Blitch, the doctor told him that the Apollo astronauts, the men from the moon missions, shunned their fellow astronaut Edgar Mitchell. He tells it because it suggests that speaking openly about strange experiences can cost even an astronaut his standing.
nasa-langley-staff-tag-puzzles-and-hiero: Dylan Borland, a guest on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, says that people who work at buildings at NASA Langley, a NASA research center beside Langley Air Force Base in Virginia, tag puzzles, hieroglyphs, rocks and formations on Google Maps. He says he took screenshots a few years ago, including labels of labyrinths and pyramids at the hypersonic facilities complex, and that they were later scrubbed. He presents it as hidden messages left by insiders.
nasa-mission-controller-tells-of-space-p: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, passes on a story from Diana Pasulka, a writer on beliefs about UFOs, who spoke with a NASA mission controller named Tim Taylor. According to Michels, Taylor spoke of people in a so-called secret space program, a hidden effort said to run alongside the public one, who honour their "sponsors" in second-century Latin. If true, it would mean the space program quietly answers to some unnamed patrons.
nasa-mission-controller-tim-taylor-s-adv: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says a NASA mission controller named Tim Taylor told him, on a FaceTime call, that to make a rocket venture succeed you have to think about what "they" want, and Michels understood "they" to mean non-human intelligence. He links this to American Cosmic, a book by Diana Pasulka, a scholar of religion, about people in tech and science who say they get ideas from such beings. If true, it would mean some space work is shaped by an outside intelligence.
nasa-mission-controller-tim-taylor-says-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that a NASA mission controller, the person on the ground who helps run space flights, named Tim Taylor has said that astronauts see things in space. Michels links the name to the book American Cosmic and says Taylor has now been named publicly. If true, it would mean astronauts have encounters that the public does not hear about.
nasa-moon-pigeons-report-1970: A podcast guest, Maaneli Derakhshani, says that NASA, the US space agency, published a report in the early 1970s called "Moon Pigeons." He mentions it while discussing what NASA may know about the Moon, as a sign that the agency once put out a report on something odd seen there.
nasa-moon-program-development-at-langley: Dylan Borland, a former Air Force member who talks about UFO secrets, says that in the 1960s much of the work NASA, the US space agency, did to reach space, including the work on pressurization, keeping air pressure safe for astronauts, took place at Langley Air Force Base in Virginia. He tells it as background about the base and what went on there, as part of a larger story he tells on Jesse Michels's podcast.
nasa-operator-disconnects-gary-during-ha: Gary McKinnon, a British computer hacker, tells podcast host Jesse Michels that around 2001 and 2002 he broke into computers belonging to NASA, the US space agency, from his home in the UK over a British Telecom line. He says that at one point someone on the other end noticed him, right clicked the network icon on screen and cut him off, and that this was NASA itself. He tells it as part of his claim that he found signs of a secret space program.
nasa-people-invite-him-to-lunch-during-a: Kiran Ilum Xenov, who later became president of a republic within Russia, tells podcast host Jesse Michels that in the late 1990s, while visiting the US Congress as a member of the Russian parliament, he got a phone call. He says the callers said they were from NASA, the US space agency, had heard about his public statement of being taken by aliens, and wanted to meet him over lunch. If true, it would mean the US space agency took a quiet interest in his account.
nasa-people-study-the-phenomenon-and-tra: Chris Bledsoe, a man who says strange lights and craft appear around him, tells podcast host Jesse Michels that since about 2007 people from NASA, the US space agency, have studied what happens around him and travelled with him.
