He names some of them and says there are many other NASA people he is talking with now. If true, it would mean people inside a major government agency are quietly looking into these experiences.
nasa-program-with-psychic-kids-in-florid: A researcher named Greg says he has heard a lot about a programme somewhere in Florida in the late 1960s. According to what he heard, it was a NASA project, NASA being the US space agency, that worked with children, which the story takes to mean children thought to have psychic abilities. If true, it would mean the space agency was quietly studying such abilities.
nasa-representative-4-000-recorded-cases: Kiran Ilum Xenov, introduced as the former president of a republic within Russia, says he was taken by aliens in 1997. He says that around then a representative of NASA, the US space agency, told him that they officially record about 4,000 cases a year of people seeing unidentified objects like saucers. If true, it would mean the agency quietly keeps a large count of such sightings.
nasa-s-higher-resolution-mars-images-rel: Tim Alberino, a researcher and filmmaker, talks about Cydonia, a region of Mars where some see a "face" and other shapes that look built. He says that in the 1990s and 2000s NASA, the US space agency, released a second set of sharper images of the area to calm the uproar that had broken out over those shapes. In his telling, the new pictures were meant to settle the argument over whether anything artificial is on Mars.
nasa-s-innovative-propulsion-program-fun: Eric Haseltine, a former senior official at the National Security Agency, the US government's electronic spying agency, spoke on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels about a NASA programme for new and unusual ways of moving spacecraft. According to him, this programme, which he calls fantastic, has funded research into warp drive, an idea for travelling faster than light by bending space itself. He points to a document called The Shadow of Time, and if he is right, it would mean the US space agency takes seriously ideas that sound like science fiction.
nasa-space-force-track-uncorrelated-targ: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says he has been in touch with a person who currently works at NASA, the US space agency. According to Michels, this person told him that NASA tracks what it calls "uncorrelated targets" all the time. These are objects picked up by tracking systems that don't match anything known, so if this is true, unexplained objects in space are a routine sight for the agency.
nasa-telepathy-experiments-and-remote-vi: A researcher called Greg says that in the 1960s a man named Andrija Puharich held contracts with NASA, the US space agency, for telepathy experiments, pointing to newspaper articles about them. According to Greg, Puharich claimed that NASA sent remote viewers, people said to see faraway places with the mind alone, to look at the moon. If true, the space agency was testing psychic methods alongside its rockets.
nasa-tries-to-replicate-podkletnov-s-wei: Nick Cook, a journalist who writes about aviation and secret aircraft, says NASA, the US space agency, oddly took an interest in anti-gravity, meaning technology that cancels or reduces gravity, in the mid-1990s. According to Cook, this followed reports from a Russian scientist named Yevgeny Podkletnov, working at the University of Tampere in Finland, that objects seemed to lose weight in his experiments, and NASA tried to repeat the effect. If true, it would mean a government agency took a real way to beat gravity seriously.
nasp-as-cover-program-for-aurora-1980: Nick Cook, an aviation journalist, passes on a suspicion held by a fellow aviation writer, Bill Sweetman, about secret American aircraft in the 1980s and 1990s. According to Cook, Sweetman came to believe that NASP, a public US government project to build a plane that could fly into space, was really a cover for Aurora, a rumoured secret high-speed aircraft. If so, a project the public could see would have been hiding a far more advanced one they couldn't.
nat-kobitz-as-coulthart-s-original-navy-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, mentions a man named Nat Kobitz, whom he describes as a senior scientist for the US Navy. Michels says Kobitz was the original source for an Australian journalist, Ross Coulthart, who reports on UFOs, and that it was Kobitz who first drew Coulthart deep into the subject. It matters to the story because it would place the start of Coulthart's reporting with someone on the inside of the military.
nat-kobitz-confirms-being-read-into-a-ua: Ross Coulthart, an Australian journalist who investigates UFO claims, says that sometime around 2018 to 2020 he put a direct question to a man named Nat Kobitz. He asked whether Kobitz had ever been "read in", meaning given secret clearance and briefed, on any programme involving unidentified aerial phenomena (the government's term for UFOs) or alien technology. Coulthart says Kobitz confirmed that he had, which would mean such a secret programme exists.
nathan-twining-reference-in-disclosure-d: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, points to a reference in a film called Disclosure Day to Nathan Twining, the general who in 1947 headed Air Materiel Command, the military's aircraft equipment and research branch. Michels says Twining wrote the Twining memo, a 1947 letter about flying disc reports, and was rumoured to belong to Majestic 12, a supposed secret group of twelve officials said in disputed documents to manage the UFO matter, and he adds that in the film twelve people are missing. He reads it as the film nodding to that history, which would mean the filmmakers are hinting at real events.
national-archives-extends-the-deadline-f: A man named Dan Sheehan, speaking on a podcast in 2025, says the National Archives, the US government agency that keeps official records, gave an extension until the end of September 2025 for records about UAP, the government's term for UFOs. He mentions it as a date to watch, since it would be when more government UFO records are due.
national-archives-photos-of-eg-g-sandia-: An online UFO researcher who goes by UAPGerb says the US National Archives, the government's official records store, holds a series of photographs taken from 1972 to 1992. According to him, they show underground work at the Nevada Test Site, a government nuclear testing ground, carried out by EG&G, a defence contractor, and Sandia, a US nuclear weapons laboratory, before the aerospace company Martin Marietta took over Sandia in 1993. He raises it because it would point to hidden underground operations in the same desert as the secret base known as Area 51.
national-geographic-double-blind-remote-: Joe McMoneagle, a man known for remote viewing, which is the practice of trying to describe a faraway place using only the mind, tells podcast host Jesse Michels about a test filmed for National Geographic in the San Francisco Bay Area. He says it was set up so that neither he nor the people with him knew the target, and that he described the end of the Dumbarton Bridge, which turned out to be where a man named Ed had gone. If true, it would suggest the mind can perceive distant places.
national-security-act-passed-weeks-after: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, points out that the National Security Act, the 1947 US law that reorganised the country's military and intelligence agencies, was passed in September 1947. That was only weeks after Roswell, the July 1947 report of a crashed object near Roswell, New Mexico. He raises the timing because, if the two were connected, it would mean the government's new secrecy machinery was shaped partly by the crash.
national-underwater-reconnaissance-offic: A researcher who goes by the online name UAPGerb says there is a National Underwater Reconnaissance Office, which he calls the NURO, a secret US agency for spying under the sea. According to him it was set up in 1969 and has still not been officially acknowledged. He tells it on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, because if true it would mean a whole government agency has stayed hidden for over fifty years.
nato-warships-around-the-expedition-2011: Dennis Asberg, a Swedish treasure hunter, tells podcast host Jesse Michels about his diving expeditions from 2011 onward to a strange object his team found on the floor of the Baltic Sea, between Sweden and Finland. He says warships from NATO, the Western military alliance, gathered around his boat, including French, German, American and British ships. If true, it would suggest that powerful militaries were closely watching what he had found.
navair-high-energy-electromagnetic-field: A Navy scientist named Salvatore Pais, who holds patents some call UFO patents, says he worked on an experiment at NAVAIR, the Navy's air systems command, that used a high-energy electromagnetic field generator. He says the team could only build up a tiny electric charge, far short of the amount needed to prove what he calls the Pais effect, his own proposed physical effect. If it had worked, he suggests, it would have shown his theory was correct.
navajo-curse-legend-of-skinwalker-ranch: Skinwalker Ranch is a piece of land in Utah's Uinta Basin known for strange happenings, named after skinwalkers, shape-shifting beings from Native American lore. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says the legend is that the Ute tribe, who worked with the US government, fought the Navajo, and the unhappy Navajo cursed the spot with skinwalkers. In a later telling he leaves out the Navajo and says the Ute call it cursed ground and will not talk about it, adding that drones, helicopters and equipment fail there.
navajo-skinwalker-lore-matches-ranch-act: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, talks about the Navajo tradition of the skinwalker, a shapeshifting figure in the stories of the Navajo people, and Skinwalker Ranch, a property in the American West known for reports of strange events. Michels says that while searching online he found that the old lore talks about luminous, glowing objects, which he links to what is reported at the ranch. If the link holds, it would suggest the strange activity there is much older than modern reports.
naval-intelligence-as-a-major-funder-of-: A researcher named Greg says that Naval Intelligence, the US Navy's spy service, was at one point a big funder of Andrija Puharich, a man whose work is the subject of the episode. Greg says this funding ran from the 1950s into the early 1980s. He tells it on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, since it would tie the Navy to Puharich's work over decades.
naval-intelligence-commander-s-email-uap: Tim Gallaudet, a retired US Navy admiral, told podcast host Jesse Michels about an email he says came from a Navy intelligence commander on a restricted, secret network. According to Gallaudet, the email said these unidentified objects are seen in the ocean more than anywhere else, going in and out of the water, in five to seven areas of the world. Elsewhere in the same talk he calls those locations possible undersea bases, which would mean something is living or working beneath the sea.
naval-intelligence-sphere-program-for-vi: An online UFO researcher who goes by UAPGerb says someone told him they had served in naval intelligence, the US Navy's spying arm. According to UAPGerb, this person said they took part in a programme that used a sphere, much like one described by a man named Randy Anderson, as a remote viewing tool, a way of trying to see distant places or events with the mind. The story is told as a programme for glimpsing other possible timelines, and if true, it would mean the Navy has worked with technology far stranger than anything known to the public.
navy-astronomer-measures-wobbling-disc-1: A UFO researcher named Merrick points to a famous 1947 article in Life magazine, a popular American picture magazine. He says the article reports that one of the US Navy's top astronomers, in New Mexico, saw and measured a disc that wobbled as it flew. He raises it because it would mean a trained scientist recorded a flying disc in the very first year of the modern UFO story.
navy-aviators-privately-report-regular-s: A man called Dr. Gilbert says that on a visit to a US Navy base, Navy pilots told him and others privately that they were seeing things in the sky they couldn't understand on a very regular basis, including close calls, but that they were not talking about it openly. If true, it would mean strange sightings were common among military pilots and kept quiet.
navy-cia-tug-of-war-over-the-nuro-1969: A researcher who goes by UAPGerb says that from 1969 until 1972 there was a big fight between the US Navy and the CIA, the US foreign intelligence agency, specifically its science and technology branch, over who would control the NURO, a secret office for underwater spying. He cites a man named Bobby Rayanman for this and tells it on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, as a sign of how much the agencies cared about that office.
navy-commander-george-hoover-on-roswell-: In 1947 something crashed near Roswell, New Mexico, and many people say it was a craft carrying beings that were not human. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that a Navy commander named George Hoover, who held top secret clearance for most of his life, admitted that the beings in the crash were simply humans travelling back from the future. If true, the visitors would be our own descendants, not aliens.
navy-gave-pais-crash-material-for-his-pa: Bob Maguire, described as a former CIA contractor, talks about Salvatore Pais, a US Navy scientist who filed patents in the 2010s for strange, advanced craft and devices. Maguire guesses that the Navy gave Pais material from a crashed unknown craft, and that Pais worked out the equations behind it and wrote them into his patents. If true, the patents would be a public trace of studying a recovered craft to learn how it works.
navy-gun-camera-videos-off-san-diego: John Harrington, who appears as a former US Secretary of Energy, recalls seeing Navy videos on television, filmed by the cameras mounted on fighter jets off San Diego, California. He says they showed an object moving at enormous speed and diving into the ocean. To him, it suggested craft with abilities far beyond known aircraft.
navy-has-no-original-flir1-tape-only-the: Mick West, a well-known sceptic who analyses UFO videos, talks about a Navy fighter jet video known as FLIR1, named after the jet's heat-sensing infrared camera. He says the US military does not have the original recording. According to West, the version the Navy officially released is the very same copy that had earlier turned up on a German file-sharing server online, which matters because it would mean nobody can check the footage against a cleaner original.
navy-intelligence-visits-frances-swan-19: Grant Cameron, a researcher of UFO history, tells of a woman named Frances Swan who lived in Eliot, Maine, in the 1950s. He says Navy intelligence took notice of her and visited her in 1954, a story he links to an FBI and Navy intelligence document and to a man named Wilbert Smith. If true, it would show the military taking a private citizen's UFO-related claims seriously enough to check on her.
navy-misidentifications-a-jet-called-a-d: Mick West, a researcher known for doubting UFO claims, says that in 2019 a team of trained lookouts on a US Navy ship, called the Snoopy team, mistook stars for drones, and that a jet was also called a drone. He tells it on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels to argue that even trained military observers can get things wrong.
navy-overcharging-for-parts-1980: A researcher who goes by UAPGerb says there is a really interesting example from the 1980s and 1990s of the US Navy overcharging for parts. He tells it on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels while explaining how money can move through military budgets in ways that are hard to see.
navy-patent-for-laser-drawn-plasma-decoy: Eric Haseltine, a former senior official at the National Security Agency, the US electronic spying agency, says he once wondered whether lasers could create glowing shapes in the air. He says it turned out the US Navy holds a patent for exactly that: using lasers to make plasma, a glowing electrically charged gas, in the shape of an airplane to fool incoming missiles. If so, some strange lights in the sky could be fake targets made by the military itself.
navy-pilots-interviewed-including-fravor: A former US Senate staffer named Kirk McConnell says that while looking into strange reports, including ones tied to Skinwalker Ranch, a ranch famous for tales of odd happenings, his team interviewed a series of Navy pilots. Among them, he says, were David Fravor and Alex Dietrich, two pilots from the 2004 Tic Tac episode, when Navy fliers off the US coast reported a white oval object shaped like the mint. Their accounts matter to him because trained military pilots are hard witnesses to dismiss.
navy-recovering-non-human-craft-from-the: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that craft not made by humans are being recovered by the US Navy from the bottom of oceans all over the world. If true, it would mean the Navy is quietly collecting such craft on a wide scale.
navy-says-brown-s-work-still-classified: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, talks about a scientist named Townsend Brown who did work for the US Navy. Michels says that when Brown's daughter, Linda Brown, and his biographer, Paul Schatzkin, asked the Navy for his records, the Navy was at first very uncooperative, and in a later episode he says he believes Brown's work is likely still classified today. If so, it would suggest the Navy still sees his research as too important to share.
navy-seal-finds-a-black-octagonal-struct: Jason Jorjani, a researcher and writer, passes on an account he credits to Linda Moulton Howe, a journalist who covers UFO stories. As he tells it, a Navy SEAL, a member of the US Navy's special forces, came across a highly polished black stone structure with eight sides, sticking about 18 feet out of the ice near McMurdo, the main US research station in Antarctica. If true, it would mean something built and unexplained is buried under the Antarctic ice.
navy-secretary-kimball-and-admiral-radfo: Richard Dolan, a historian of UFO reports, relays an account linked to the writer Donald Keyhoe about a flight from California to Hawaii around 1950. He says the planes carrying Dan Kimball, then Secretary of the Navy, and Admiral Arthur Radford, a senior Navy commander, were both approached by an unknown object that circled around them. If true, some of the highest Navy leaders would have seen a UFO up close themselves.
nazca-and-paracas-cranial-elongation-rit: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, discusses two ancient peoples of Peru, the Nazca and the Paracas. He says that one of the things they practised was skull elongation, rituals that reshaped the head to make it long. He raises it in an episode about strange three-fingered bodies found in Peru, as part of the background for weighing what those bodies might be.
nazca-lines-made-to-be-seen-from-the-sky: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, talks about the Nazca Lines, huge figures and lines drawn into the desert ground in Peru. He says they only make sense when seen from 150 to 500 metres up in the air, far higher than any nearby spot on the ground. If so, it raises the question of who the makers expected to be looking at them from above.
nazi-aneutronic-fusion-bomb-traded-away-: Jason Jorjani, a philosopher and author, suggests that Nazi Germany may have developed an aneutronic fusion bomb in 1944 and 1945, a weapon that fuses atoms together without giving off the usual neutron radiation. He says that if they had, atom bombs "would be like matches" by comparison, and the story's title says the weapon was traded away in exchange for amnesty, meaning a pardon, which would mean the secret ended up in someone else's hands after the war.
nazi-antarctica-expedition-1938: Around 1938 and 1939, Nazi Germany sent an expedition to Antarctica. Talking with a writer, Peter Levenda, a podcast host named Jesse Michels says that this Antarctica expedition was very real. It comes up because, in stories like these, the trip is linked to secret Nazi interest in the far south.
nazi-bell-propulsion-research-at-the-sko: A researcher named Jason Jorjani says that in the 1940s Nazi Germany ran advanced propulsion research, including a device called the Bell, at the Skoda Works, a large industrial site just outside Prague, under SS General Hans Kammler. He draws on writers such as Nick Cook, author of The Hunt for Zero Point, Igor Witkowski and Joseph Farrell. If true, it would mean the Nazis were chasing exotic flight technology during the war.
nazi-bell-scientists-killed-1940: This story is about the Bell, said to be a secret device built in Nazi Germany or occupied Czechoslovakia in the 1940s. A researcher of UFO secrecy named Richard Dolan tells it on a podcast with the host Jesse Michels. He draws on a writer named Nick Cook and his book The Hunt for Zero Point. According to Dolan, about sixty scientists worked on it, a number of them died from its effects, and the rest were executed at the end of the war so they would not talk. A second researcher, Jason Jorjani, tells it on a later episode. He speaks of a first team and says that plants placed around the device would turn to mulch, though he does not give the figure of sixty or mention the killings. If true, it would mean the Nazis built something exotic and deadly that was hidden by killing the people who knew.
nazi-disc-shaped-craft-projects-miethe-s: A researcher who goes by the name JASON says that in 1940s Nazi Germany several men, among them Richard Miethe, Rudolf Schriever and someone named Lutzow, along with four or five others, claimed to have worked on different attempts to build disc-shaped flying craft. He tells it on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, since it would mean people were trying to build flying saucers decades ago.
nazi-discs-brought-to-us-via-operation-p: Michael Herrera, a man who says he saw a huge UFO in the Indonesian jungle, mentions what he has heard about the 1940s. He says material was recovered from Nazi Germany and sent to the United States through Operation Paperclip, the American programme that brought German scientists and technology over after the Second World War. In this story, that included disc-shaped craft, which would mean the US inherited early saucer technology from the Nazis.
nazi-enriched-uranium-sent-to-the-us-by-: Jason Jorjani, a researcher and writer, draws on a book called Critical Mass by Carter Plimpton Hydrick. He says that in 1945 a deal was struck with the SS, Nazi Germany's elite paramilitary organisation, to ship by submarine to the United States the nuclear material that went into the atomic bombs dropped on Hiroshima and Nagasaki in Japan. If true, the first atomic bombs would partly rest on Nazi work.
nazi-expeditions-searching-for-atlantis-: Jay Anderson, a podcast host who talks about hidden history, says that in the 1930s and 1940s members of the SS, the Nazi party's elite force, went on expeditions through Peru, Nepal and Tibet looking for Atlantis, a legendary lost civilization. He says there are photos of them with high lamas, senior Buddhist monks, with swastikas in the background, which in his telling shows how seriously the Nazis took ancient myths.
nazi-expeditions-to-the-himalayas-in-sea: Kirk McConnell, a former US Senate staffer, recalls that a Polish writer named Igor Witkowski described Nazi expeditions to the Himalayas in the 1930s and 1940s. According to McConnell, the Nazis went there searching for evidence of their "Aryan" myths, legends about the ancient origins of a supposed master race, which in his telling ties Nazi research to ancient lore.
nazi-flying-saucers-attempted-but-not-ac: A researcher named Lue Elizondo says the Nazis in World War II certainly tried to build flying saucers, pointing to experiments and to the foo fighters, strange lights that pilots reported, over Bavaria in southern Germany. But in his view they did not actually have the technology. He says it on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, to argue that German wartime projects do not explain UFOs.
nazi-memorabilia-at-paperclip-facilities: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, talks about the late 1940s, when the United States brought German scientists to work for it after the Second World War, an effort known as Operation Paperclip. He says that swastikas and other Nazi items were reportedly on open display at some of the facilities where they worked, such as Fort Bliss and White Sands, military sites in Texas and New Mexico. He tells it to show how openly these men's past was tolerated in the early American rocket and space work.
nazi-missions-to-antarctica: A researcher named Lue Elizondo says the Nazis were fascinated by Antarctica and sent several missions there. He mentions it on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, as part of a talk about what Germany was exploring in that era.
nazi-occult-documents-found-in-a-cave-19: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in 1945, near the end of the Second World War, American forces found a hidden stash of Nazi documents in a cave in southern Germany. According to him, these included records of real occult projects, meaning work on magic and the supernatural, paid for by the Nazi state. If true, it would mean a modern government took such things seriously enough to fund them.
nazi-submarine-traffic-intercepted-near-: Jason Jorjani, a philosopher and author, says that around 1946, after World War II had ended, Nazi submarine traffic was intercepted heading to Argentina, near Patagonia, the country's far southern region. If true, it would mean Nazis and their secrets kept moving to South America after Germany's defeat.
nct-s-darpa-contract-and-military-ties-a: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, speaking with a former Army sergeant named Dan Sherman, who says the NSA (the US electronic spying agency) hired him to communicate with aliens, points to a June 1991 Washington Post report. According to Michels, the report says a company called Noise Cancellation Technologies in Linthicum, Maryland, near the military base Fort Meade, won a $210,000 research contract from DARPA, the Pentagon's advanced research agency. He offers this and the company's other military ties as support for parts of Sherman's account.
near-death-experience-after-poisoning-ou: Joe McMoneagle, a guest on Jesse Michels's podcast, says that in 1970 he was poisoned in Austria and arrived dead at a clinic in Passau, Germany, with no heartbeat for almost 40 minutes. He says that during that time he left his body and saw a white light. To him it suggests the mind can go on outside the body.
near-death-experiencers-describe-living-: A researcher named Grant Cameron, speaking on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, says that people who have had near-death experiences, meaning they nearly died and later described what they saw, report buildings that seem alive, with doors that open like molten metal. Cameron says he has gathered a list of maybe 20 such accounts so far. He tells it because, if true, many people would be describing the same strange place on the edge of death.
nearly-2-000-experimental-variations-tra: A man named Charles Buer, working with a colleague named Drew at a Florida company called Exodus Propulsion Technologies, says the two of them have kept a record of their experiments and have now tested close to 2,000 variations. The work is aimed at a new kind of propulsion that the podcast calls antigravity, and he names another person, Andrew Arjima, in connection with it.
neighbor-moved-to-roswell-to-see-ufos: At a live podcast event with Jesse Michels, an audience member told a story about a neighbour. According to the audience member, this neighbour moved to Roswell, New Mexico, a small town famous for UFO stories, because he wanted to be close to the action. The neighbour claimed he did see something there.
neighbor-saw-backyard-lit-up-like-a-holl: Mario Woods, a former guard at a nuclear site who says he was abducted by aliens, describes a night in December 2017 at his home in Georgia. He says a neighbour later told him his backyard had been lit up like a Hollywood film set. For Woods, it is outside support that something strange happened at his house that night.
neighboring-farmer-s-house-shook-at-5-a-: In January 1996, in Varginha, a town in Brazil where people say a strange craft came down and creatures were captured, a farmer living near the site reportedly said his whole house shook at 5 a.m. and soldiers told his family to stay inside. A man named Carlos Dosoza relays this from film recordings made by Claudia Kovu. If true, it would point to a real crash and a military operation that morning.
neil-armstrong-discusses-a-ufo-research-: The son of J. Allen Hynek, an astronomer known for studying UFOs, says that in the early 1970s Neil Armstrong, the first man to walk on the Moon, asked to sit with his father and the family. According to the son, the two men talked seriously about starting a new group to research UFOs. If true, it would mean one of the most famous astronauts took the subject to heart.
neil-armstrong-s-1975-tayos-cave-expedit: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Neil Armstrong, the first man to walk on the Moon, later went to the Tayos cave at the edge of the Amazon in Ecuador, bringing a BBC film crew to explore what he thought might be an alien cave. Michels ties this to Chariots of the Gods, a book by the writer Erich von Däniken about visitors from space in ancient times, and dates the trip to 1975 in one episode and 1976 in another. It matters to him because it would show a famous astronaut taking the idea of ancient alien sites seriously.
neil-armstrong-s-truth-s-protective-laye: Neil Armstrong, the astronaut who walked on the Moon, once gave a speech that some read as a coded hint about hidden knowledge. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, quotes it: "There are great ideas undiscovered. Breakthroughs available to those who can remove one of truth's protective layers." Michels first remembered it as a 1980s speech at a medal ceremony, but in a later episode he places it at the White House in 1994. Another podcast host, Joe Rogan, says it was given 25 years after the moon landing, to the brightest high school students. Those who tell it hear Armstrong hinting that important truths are still being kept from the public.
neil-armstrong-seemed-scared-at-his-spee: Neil Armstrong was the American astronaut who first walked on the Moon in 1969. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that when Armstrong gave a speech about three weeks after coming home, calling it a big step for mankind, he looked scared and sheepish. Michels raises it in an episode about the idea that the Moon is an alien spaceship, as a hint that Armstrong may have seen more than he said.
neil-armstrong-we-were-told-not-to-come-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, mentions stories, which he himself calls apocryphal (passed around without a firm source), about Neil Armstrong, the first person to walk on the Moon. According to these stories, Armstrong said in Washington DC sometime in the 1970s, "We were told not to come back to the moon." If true, it would suggest someone or something on the Moon warned the astronauts away.
nellis-object-as-balloons-drifting-in-th: Mick West, a researcher known for doubting UFO claims, looks at a 1994 video of an object filmed over the Nellis and Tonopah military range in Nevada. He says he thinks it is just a balloon, or a bunch of balloons, floating in the wind. He says this on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels to offer an ordinary explanation for the footage.
nellis-range-face-to-face-encounter-1994: James Fox, a documentary filmmaker, says that in August 1994 a man named Jason Sands had a face-to-face meeting with a being at the Nellis testing range, a military area in Nevada, and that Sands tells this in Fox's film The Program. In one telling Fox says the being wore a military outfit but did not look human, and the podcast host Jesse Michels, retelling it, describes it as a blue alien being. If true, it would mean non-human beings were present on a US military base.
nematode-revived-after-46-000-years-in-s: A guest named Dr. Gilbert says that in 2023 it was reported that nematodes, tiny worms, were brought back to life after 46,000 years frozen in the Siberian permafrost, the ground in Siberia that stays frozen all year. He tells it on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels as a point about how long life can survive in harsh conditions.
network-of-underground-tunnels-beneath-t: A scientist named Filippo Biondi, who says he scanned beneath the pyramids of Giza in Egypt, reports that in 2025 his team found a tangle of signals in their underground images, the kind of pictures built up from waves bounced off hidden layers. He says it looks like a network of underground tunnels under the plateau, work he did alongside Armando Mei. If true, it would mean far more lies under the pyramids than anyone has mapped.
neuralink-implant-immune-reaction-2024: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, talks about Neuralink, a company started by the businessman Elon Musk that puts electronic implants into people's brains. Michels says he believes the first patient, whom he calls Nolan Arba, may need some adjustment, because after the first success the body had a kind of immune reaction to the implant. He brings it up in an episode about a scientist who studies objects said to be alien implants in human bodies.
neurologist-steers-jim-toward-john-mack-: Jim Weiner, one of the men in what is called the Allagash case, a 1976 account of men who say they were taken by beings, says that years later a neurologist in the Boston area pointed him toward help. He says the doctor told him about Raymond Fowler, a UFO investigator who was coming to a conference at a hotel, and also toward John Mack of Harvard. This, he says, is how his story first reached serious investigators.
neurotypical-woman-with-a-head-injury-re: A documentary filmmaker named Ky Dickens says that her series The Telepathy Tapes, about non-speaking people said to share thoughts, includes a neurotypical woman, meaning someone whose brain works in the usual way, who after a head injury can reach the same mental space that non-speakers reach. If true, it would suggest that this shared space is open to anyone under the right conditions.
nevada-test-fallout-theory-dismissed-as-: Brandon Fugal, the owner of Skinwalker Ranch, a property famous for reports of strange events, speaks about the idea that the oddities there could come from weapons testing in Nevada. He allows that some Nevada testing could have played a part, though the story is framed as him rejecting the idea as having no basis.
never-before-seen-footage-of-a-ufo-at-ar: Area 51 is a secret US military base in the Nevada desert, long linked to stories about UFOs, or unidentified flying objects. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, promises what he calls legendary, never-before-seen footage of a UFO at the base. If real, it would be a direct image of such a craft at the place most tied to these stories.
new-data-show-the-object-separated-from-: A Swedish treasure hunter named Dennis Asberg, whose team found a strange shape on the floor of the Baltic Sea between Sweden and Finland, says new data from June 2025 show the object sits apart from the seabed. "That's what I can say," he says. If so, it would mean the object is not just part of the sea floor.
new-hoffmanlevin-collaboration-on-recurs: A scientist named Donald Hoffman says that in 2026 he is just starting a collaboration with another researcher, Mike Levin, built around a mathematical idea he calls recursive trace logic. He says they plan to bring on a postdoctoral researcher to work on it together. It ties into Hoffman's broader view that our senses hide much of what is really out there.
new-jersey-and-uk-base-drone-sightings-2: In late 2024, according to the podcast host Jesse Michels, strange objects were seen hovering near military bases in the UK and sensitive sites in New Jersey. He names places such as Picatinny Arsenal, an Army site in New Jersey, the Lakenheath air base in England, and the Salem nuclear power plant, and he credits the researcher Robert Hastings, who links such objects to nuclear sites. A witness named Merrick says the FBI and the FAA, the agency that runs US air traffic, got involved, drone flights were restricted and the governor took part. The researcher Michael Shermer calls it the New Jersey swarm, and a former presidential advisor, Harald Malmgren, says objects were flying all over the United States. Michels frames it as proof that unknown objects are still watching nuclear sites.
new-jersey-drone-flap-and-objects-emergi: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, talks about the wave of mystery drone sightings over New Jersey in 2024, citing a Rolling Stone article, a man named Greg Scaduto, and comments from President Donald Trump. Michels says the remarks seemed to imply the objects were coming from underwater, and that around that time there were sightings off the coast where UAPs, the government's term for unidentified objects, seemed to be coming up out of the water. If true, it would point to something hiding in the ocean.
new-jersey-drone-flap-and-the-disclosure: Jesse Michels, a podcast host, links two things that happened in New Jersey. In late 2024, many people across the state reported mysterious drones and lights in the sky, and around the same time Steven Spielberg's alien film Disclosure Day was being made there. Michels credits the idea to his friend Chris Ramsey, who hosts a show called Area 52, and floats that the sightings and the film might be connected. In a later episode he says filming began in February 2025, a few months after the sightings, and mentions Morris County and Picatinny Arsenal, a military base in the state.
new-nautics-and-university-of-florida-pr: A neuroscientist named Andrew Gallimore says that a company called New Nautics has contracted a team at the University of Florida to develop ways to "hack" the brain's own DMT system. DMT is a powerful psychedelic substance that the brain is thought to make by itself, and the project is said to be ongoing in 2025. Gallimore's interest is that, if this works, people could reach the strange realm DMT users describe in a more controlled way.
new-parapsychology-degree-program-at-the: A researcher with a doctorate, Jeffrey Mishlove, says he has just helped create a doctoral and a master's degree programme at the California Institute for Human Science that includes a specialization in parapsychology, the study of claimed psychic abilities. He presents it as a sign that the subject is getting a formal place in higher education.
new-start-treaty-to-reduce-nuclear-weapo: Robert Salas, a former US Air Force officer who looked after nuclear missiles, describes the New START treaty, an agreement signed by President Barack Obama with Russia around 2010. Salas says the treaty cut the number of nuclear weapons each side keeps ready to use. He brings it up as background to his account of UFOs interfering with nuclear missiles, where the fate of these weapons is the heart of the story.
new-tall-white-arrivals-come-too-close-a: Charles Hall, who says he spent three years with tall white beings while serving at an air force range in Nevada, tells of a night in 1965 at a spot called Range Three in Indian Springs Valley. He says that about a week after the full moon a group of newly arrived tall whites came too close to him. If true, it would mean the military was quietly sharing ground with visitors from elsewhere.
new-zealand-archives-reveal-kaikoura-cov: Ross Coulthart, an Australian journalist who investigates UFO claims, says he discovered that New Zealand released government archives around 2011 about the 1978 sightings of strange lights off Kaikoura, a stretch of the New Zealand coast. According to Coulthart, the files show a cover-up and how officials settled on explaining the lights as squid fishing boats, which use bright lamps at night. If he is right, the official explanation was a convenient story rather than a real answer.
newgrange-curbstone-with-perplexing-symb: A researcher named Geoffrey Drumm, speaking on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, describes Newgrange, a very old stone mound tomb in Ireland. He says that a curbstone, one of the large stones set around the outside of the mound, is carved with many puzzling symbols. He raises it as a sign that the ancient builders were recording something we do not yet understand.
newly-found-mysterious-sites-in-eastern-: A researcher of ancient history called Matt says he came across very mysterious sites in eastern Turkey, in the region of Mount Ararat that was once part of Armenia, found in 2001 and 2017. He says the sites were brand new to research. To him they point to something big that happened around 12,000 BC.
news-clip-victory-learning-center-employ: A news clip played on a podcast episode about a man who says he was taken into a UFO program as a child reports that three employees at the Victory Learning Center, a school in Lackawanna, New York, were put on leave. According to the reporter, the organisation that runs it, OLV Human Services, said this was over allegations that they physically mistreated students.
news-report-of-the-oklahoma-city-bombing: A news report from 1995, played on a podcast episode about a scientist who studies objects said to be alien implants in people's bodies, describes the Oklahoma City bombing. The reporter says a huge car bomb went off outside a large federal building downtown, shattering it and killing children, federal workers, military members and civilians.
news-report-survivors-of-the-plane-crash: A news report, played on a podcast episode about a supposed secret Nazi UFO program, says that Jamaica Hospital in New York had received 14 survivors from a plane crash. The clip gives no more detail about when or which crash it was.
newsnation-finds-nothing-in-the-vatican-: A well-known skeptic and writer, Michael Shermer, brings up a claim tied to the Vatican, the headquarters of the Catholic Church, and to the year 1933. He says that NewsNation, an American TV news channel, went to the Vatican and searched its files itself, and reported that it could not find anything. He tells it because if the claim were true, the Church's own records would be expected to show it.
newsnation-slide-showing-a-doe-gravity-p: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, describes a slide from a report by NewsNation, an American cable news channel. He says the slide shows a patient with what he calls a kind of white matter syndrome, an injury to the brain's connecting tissue, and the story ties this patient to secret gravity-propulsion work at the Department of Energy, the US government agency that runs nuclear and energy research. Michels connects it to the journalist Ross Coulthart and the researcher Eric Weinstein. If true, it would mean people near that hidden work were physically harmed by it.
newton-and-gebauer-framed-in-fraud-trial: A researcher who goes by the online name UAPGerb says that in the 1950s two men, Silas Newton and Leo GeBauer, were put on trial for fraud in Colorado over a "doodlebug" device, a gadget said to find things like oil underground. UAPGerb says the author William Steinman went through the Colorado court records for his book Aztec and found the two men were unfairly attacked in the case. The point of the story is that, if true, the men were set up to discredit them.
newton-diaries-sarbacher-tells-wilbur-sm: A UFO researcher who goes by the online name UAPGerb talks about the diaries of a man named Silas Newton, from around 1950. According to UAPGerb, the diaries describe Wilbur B. Smith, a Canadian radio engineer who led Canada's first government project on UFOs, being told by a man named Robert Sarbacher that UFOs were a top-secret subject, and the name of Vannevar Bush also comes up. If true, it would mean that by 1950 the subject was already being kept highly secret at senior levels.
newton-saucer-settled-gently-within-500-: A man named Silas Newton said in 1950 that in 1948 a round object, already identified as a flying saucer, settled gently to Earth within 500 miles of Denver. If true, it would mean a craft from elsewhere came down whole and was recovered.
next-30-years-a-danger-time-in-the-tauri: Graham Hancock, an author who writes about lost ancient civilisations, passes on a warning from Allen West and the Comet Research Group, a team of scientists who study ancient comet impacts. He says they believe the next 30 years will be a dangerous time as Earth passes through the Taurid stream, a band of comet debris the planet crosses every year. If true, a major impact like those they think struck in the past could happen again soon.
nhi-communication-ci-wizards-are-messing: Matthew Pines, a guest on podcast host Jesse Michels' show, passes on a story someone else told him about contact with an NHI, short for non-human intelligence, meaning beings that are not human. He says the NHI was asked something like why it was here, and the answer was that "CI wizards" were messing with the timeline. When he tells it a second time the phrase comes out as "CIA wizards", the CIA being the US spy agency. If true, it would suggest someone is tampering with time itself.
nhi-component-to-the-new-jersey-drone-fl: A helicopter pilot named Jake Barber, who says he once helped retrieve a UFO, talks about the wave of mysterious drone sightings over New Jersey in 2024. He says he thinks there was a non-human intelligence part to it, mixed in with other things. If so, some of those lights in the sky would not have been made by people.
nhi-testing-us-at-missile-fields: A Navy scientist named Salvatore Pais, speaking on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, talks about non-human intelligence, meaning beings that are not human, showing up at nuclear missile fields, the places where nuclear missiles are kept ready to launch. "Of course, they're testing us," Pais says. If true, it would mean someone else is watching how humanity handles its most dangerous weapons.
nhtcu-meets-oni-doj-extradition-threat-o: A British computer hacker named Gary McKinnon, who says he found signs of a secret space programme while breaking into US government computers, tells of what followed in 2002. He says the UK's National Hi-Tech Crime Unit, a British police cybercrime team, met with the Office of Naval Intelligence and the US Department of Justice. He says they then threatened to send him to the US for trial, where on paper he faced 70 years in jail.
nicap-s-founding-as-a-possible-link-to-t: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, talks with an astronomer, Beatriz Villarroel, about a change around 1956 that they are discussing. Michels points out that this is when NICAP, which he calls the first civilian UFO research group in the United States, was formed. He suggests the timing could be connected, which would mean public UFO research and the change happened together for a reason.
nick-cook-rebuffed-by-a-scared-george-tr: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that an aviation journalist named Nick Cook tried to meet George Trimble, a long-retired aerospace man then in his eighties, through a friend at Lockheed Martin, a large American aerospace and defence company. According to Michels, Trimble seemed scared and turned Cook away. The story is told because it would suggest that secret work in the aerospace industry still frightened the old men who knew about it.
nick-cook-s-search-for-1950s-gravity-res: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells how Nick Cook, an aviation journalist at Jane's Defence Weekly, a British military trade magazine, stumbled onto a lot of research from the 1950s into controlling gravity. According to Michels, Cook then saw that all of this research suddenly vanished and went nowhere, and he wrote about it in his book The Hunt for Zero Point. If true, it would suggest the work did not stop but went secret.
nick-pope-s-death-from-cancer-2020: Michael Shermer, a researcher known for questioning these claims, said this on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels. He says that a man named Nick Pope, the husband of a woman named Elizabeth Weiss, died of cancer in the United Kingdom sometime in the 2020s. He mentions it in passing and names no source.
nids-study-correlating-triangle-sighting: Matthew Brown, described as a Pentagon whistleblower, mentions a study by NIDS, the National Institute for Discovery Science, a private group that researched unexplained phenomena. He says that in the late 1990s or early 2000s, as far as he remembers, the study matched reports of triangle-shaped flying objects to the locations of US naval bases. If true, it would hint at a link between these craft and the Navy.
night-aircraft-spotting-with-lear-outsid: A man named Bob Lazar says that in the 1980s he went out with another man, John Lear, into the desert outside Tonopah, a small town in Nevada, in the middle of the night with binoculars. He tells it as a time they spent watching for secret aircraft flying in that area.
night-intrusion-at-the-cabin-when-the-im: A writer named Whitley Strieber says that one night in May 1989, at his cabin in upstate New York, he turned in bed and saw a woman standing near the foot of the bed with a man beside her, already in the room, while a male voice in the backyard said "Condition red." He links that night to a small implant he says was put into his body, and he mentions his wife, Anne Strieber, in the story. If true, it would mean unknown visitors entered his home and placed something in him.
night-meeting-with-military-x-about-the-: A filmmaker who investigates UFOs, James Fox, says he drove about four hours into the night, deep into Brazil north of the town of Varginha, to meet a military source he calls "military X." The meeting was about a 1996 military operation in Varginha, where people say a strange creature was found and taken away. If the source is right, it would mean the Brazilian military handled something non-human.
night-meeting-with-puthoff-and-hameroff-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in 2026 he spent an evening in a room with a man named Hal Puthoff and with Stuart Hameroff, a researcher known for a theory that consciousness comes from quantum effects in microtubules, tiny tube structures inside our cells. Michels tells it as something he was there for, and to him it means serious thinkers are linking the mind, physics and the UFO question.
night-of-shifting-timelines-in-an-la-air: A man named Brent Friedman, speaking on a podcast about Hollywood and UFOs, says that one night around 2024 or 2025, while staying at a rented Airbnb home in Los Angeles, he was trying to calm himself down with a mantra. He says he got in the shower to wind down and heard a voice say one word: "Timelines." He tells it as a strange night when reality itself seemed to shift around him.
night-scarb-s-measurements-of-the-osiris: A researcher named Jeffrey, speaking on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, points to work by an online channel called Night Scarb about the Osiris shaft, a deep shaft beneath the ground at Giza in Egypt that was scanned around 2024. According to Jeffrey, Night Scarb's measurements show that the scan's signals are off and do not match the shaft's known layout. If so, it would suggest there is more down there than the known structure.
night-sky-suddenly-bright-in-the-brookha: An unnamed witness, heard in a clip on a podcast, says that one November evening in 1992 in Brookhaven, on Long Island in New York, it was about seven o'clock and fully dark. Then, the witness says, all of a sudden it became lighter outside than daytime. It is told as part of a wider event in that area, a sign that something unexplained lit up the sky.
night-visitors-in-the-twins-childhood-ho: A man named Jim Weiner says that in the 1950s, when he and his twin brother Jack were boys sharing a bedroom near Allentown, Pennsylvania, strange things happened at night. He says they would wake up to find something pulling the covers off their beds. He tells it as an early sign of the contact experiences he believes the brothers have had all their lives.
nightly-3-a-m-wake-ups-and-communing-201: Whitley Strieber is a writer who says he has been in contact with non-human beings for many years. On a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, he says that from 2015 to 2020 these beings woke him at his home every single night around 3 a.m., and that he spent that time in contact with them. He writes about this in his book The Hidden Garden, and tells it as proof that the contact is ongoing and personal.
nile-freshwater-mussels-found-120150-ft-: A researcher named Randall Carlson told podcast host Jesse Michels that freshwater mussels and the remains of other animals that live in the Nile, the great river of Egypt, have been found 120 to 150 feet above the river's present-day floodplain. If that is true, he takes it to mean the Nile once ran far higher than it does today, perhaps as the Ice Age ended.
nimitz-encounter-as-multisensory-evidenc: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in 2004, off the coast of San Diego, the Nimitz carrier strike group (the aircraft carrier USS Nimitz and its escort ships) ran into unexplained objects over three days, with 11 or 12 witnesses including the Navy pilot David Fravor. He stresses that it was seen by several means at once: radar, people's own eyes, and a released video from FLIR, a forward-looking infrared camera that films heat. To Michels this is why the case matters: it is hard to dismiss something many people and many machines caught together.
nimitz-tic-tac-acceleration-and-power-es: In 2004, off Southern California, Navy pilots from the aircraft carrier USS Nimitz say they saw the Tic Tac, a white oval object shaped like the mint. A researcher named Kevin Knuth told podcast host Jesse Michels that his group estimated how fast the object accelerated when it reportedly dropped from 28,000 feet to sea level in a matter of seconds. If the figures hold, that would be a speed and power far beyond any known aircraft.
nimitz-tic-tac-incident-2004: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, calls the 2004 Tic Tac incident one of the holy grail events of the UFO subject. In that story, Navy pilots flying from the aircraft carrier Nimitz, off San Diego, including a fighter pilot named David Fravor, are said to have met a white oval object shaped like the mint. Michels says many people rest their belief in UFOs on this case, and in a second telling adds that the film director Steven Spielberg cites it as the reason his own interest in UFOs came back.
nina-kulagina-stops-the-hearts-of-animal: Lyn Buchanan, a former US Army sergeant, told podcast host Jesse Michels about the Soviet Union's work on mind powers. He says the Russians had a woman named Nina Kulagina who could stop the hearts of rats, rabbits and other animals, apparently with her mind alone. If true, it would mean the mind can directly harm a living body.
nine-craft-seen-through-the-open-hangar-: Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked at a secret site in the Nevada desert called S-4 around 1988 and 1989, says that one day he looked down a row of hangars and saw other craft parked there, nine of them. When pressed, he says it was "nine for sure" and that he can only speak to what he saw himself. If true, it would mean the government was keeping a whole fleet of unusual craft hidden in the desert.
nine-dr-g-scientists-traced-to-bush-s-os: Scott Ramsay, a researcher of a claimed crash of a craft with alien bodies, talks about a 1950 book called Behind the Flying Saucers, which credited its secret information to a mysterious scientist called Dr. G. Ramsay says his team identified nine scientists behind that name and traced them to the wartime research network of Vannevar Bush, who ran the OSRD, the US office that organised scientific work during the Second World War. He links them to names such as the founders of Texas Instruments, and if true, the crash story would trace back to the core of America's wartime science establishment.
nine-page-pentagon-uap-report-2021: In 2021 the Pentagon, the headquarters of the US military, put out a short report on UAP, the official term for unidentified aerial phenomena, or what most people call UFOs. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says it came out on June 25th, 2021, and that it admitted there are objects in our sky that nobody can explain. A researcher named Eric Weinstein says the report was nine pages long, with only six that mattered, and that it was written to be as dull as possible about the most exciting thing imaginable. He says it leaves two choices: either the Pentagon is running a huge psychological operation, or some people inside it believe almost for certain that aliens are visiting and watching Earth. In a later conversation Weinstein credits it to the ODNI, the office that oversees America's spy agencies, and he hears something different in it: two authors fighting, one who wanted to reveal more and one who said "over my dead body." So the story comes from Weinstein reading the document himself and from Michels describing it in his own words as host. Why it matters to them: if they read it right, the government quietly admitted the sky holds things it cannot account for.
nine-vanishing-transients-on-1950s-plate: Beatriz Villarroel, an astronomer, says that on old 1950s photographs of the night sky from the Palomar Sky Survey, a big photographic map of the sky made in California, she found nine points of light that were there and then vanished. She says a friend later pointed the Gran Telescopio Canarias, the world's largest optical telescope, 10.4 meters across, in the Canary Islands, at those spots and found nothing left. She tells it because, if real, these brief flashes may point to unknown objects in the sky in the 1950s.
ning-li-and-podkletnov-rotating-supercon: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, talks about two scientists, Ning Li and Eugene Podkletnov, who he says each worked with spinning superconductors, materials that carry electricity with no resistance when very cold. He mentions Ning Li's work with a spinning disc made of a superconducting material called YBCO. He raises it among claims that such devices might produce unusual effects on gravity, which would matter greatly for flight if true.
ning-li-and-smalley-took-400-000-in-army: On Jesse Michels's podcast, a scientist named Eric Davis, introduced as a Pentagon scientist, says that two researchers at the University of Alabama in Huntsville, Ning Li and Larry Smalley, took $400,000 from the Army Research Lab, a US Army research agency, sometime between the 1990s and 2000s. According to Davis, they delivered nothing for the money, and he mentions another researcher, Travis Taylor, as part of the story. He tells it as a warning about funded fringe research that produced no results.
ning-li-email-intercepted-by-west-point-: Dave Rossi, a guest on Jesse Michels's podcast, passes on a story about a woman named Ning Li from the early 2000s. He says her emails were intercepted by a computer address traced to West Point, the US Army's military academy in New York, and that after that no one ever heard from her again. Told this way, it hints that someone in the military was watching her work closely.
ning-li-last-seen-at-mitre-anti-gravity-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells of a scientist named Ning Li, who he says worked on anti-gravity, meaning ways to cancel or weaken the pull of gravity. According to Michels, the last time she spoke publicly and on the record about that work was at a conference about anti-gravity held by MITRE, a research company, near Washington DC around 2003. He tells it because, as he frames it, someone working on gravity-defying technology seems to have stepped out of public view after that.
ning-li-s-disappearance-after-breakthrou: Matthew Pines, a researcher and commentator, told podcast host Jesse Michels about a scientist named Ning Li. He says she was one of several people doing breakthrough research on the edges of strange subjects in the United States in the 1990s and 2000s, and then simply vanished from view. He offers her as an example of how such work may disappear into secrecy.
ning-li-s-gravito-magnetic-research-move: Podcast host Jesse Michels tells of a scientist named Ning Li who, in the 1990s, studied a possible link between gravity and magnetism at the University of Alabama in Huntsville. He says she left the university to work full-time at Redstone Arsenal, a US Army base nearby, on research so sensitive that it effectively vanished from public view. If true, it would suggest the government took her gravity work seriously enough to hide it.
ning-li-s-last-talk-was-at-a-mitre-confe: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, talks about a physicist named Ning Li. He says her last public talk was at a conference held by MITRE, a US research organisation that does work for the government, and that after that she went into the black, meaning she seemed to vanish into secret, classified work. He tells it as a sign that her research may have been taken out of public view.
ning-li-s-spinning-superconductors-nasa-: A guest named Charles, on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, talks about scientist Ning Li's experiments with spinning superconductors, special materials that carry electricity without resistance when very cold, which she claimed could affect gravity. He says that someone, he thinks NASA, the US space agency, tried to repeat her work and did not see the effect.
ning-li-s-superconductor-antigravity-wor: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in the 1990s and 2000s at the University of Alabama in Huntsville, a scientist named Ning Li worked under a man named Larry Smalley. Michels says she was studying something like weight reduction using superconductors, materials that carry electricity with no resistance when very cold. If true, it would mean serious researchers were trying to make objects lighter, a step toward machines that defy gravity.
ning-li-superconductor-gravity-shielding: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells of a scientist named Ning Li at the University of Alabama in Huntsville in the 1990s and 2000s, who he calls a really interesting case. Michels says she spun solid superconductors, materials that carry electricity with no resistance when very cold, very fast, and said they gave off gravitons, the tiny particles some physicists think carry gravity, which shielded things from gravity. He links her to a company called Anti-gravity LLC, and tells it as a possible human attempt to copy the kind of flight people attribute to UFOs.
nitinol-developed-from-the-roswell-crash: A researcher named Grant Cameron, speaking on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, says he thinks a metal called nitinol was developed from the Roswell crash, the reported 1947 crash of an unknown craft near Roswell, New Mexico. If true, it would mean a material in use today came from studying a craft that was not made by people.
nixon-calls-hughes-to-set-up-a-castro-as: A lawyer named Danny Sheehan says that Santos Trafficante, an organized crime figure, told him and his team directly how a plot came about around 1960. As Sheehan tells it, Richard Nixon called the billionaire Howard Hughes to set up the killing of Fidel Castro, the leader of Cuba, with Hughes's aide Bob Maheu, the mobsters Johnny Roselli and Sam Giancana, and Nelson Rockefeller also part of the account. If true, it would tie top US politicians and the mob together in secret operations.
nixon-ended-the-apollo-program-and-scrap: Researcher Randall Carlson, talking with podcast host Jesse Michels, discusses why the Apollo moon landings stopped between 1969 and 1972. He says the more ordinary explanation is that President Richard Nixon pulled the plug because the Vietnam War was costing so much money, which implies he weighs other, less ordinary reasons too.
nixon-haldeman-smoking-gun-tape-1972: Dan Sheehan, a lawyer and researcher speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast, points to a 1972 recording made secretly in the White House, known as the "Smoking Gun" conversation. He says that on the tape, dated by him to June 21, Richard Nixon's close aide H.R. Haldeman walks into the president's office and says, "Mr President, I think we've got a problem here." Sheehan treats the tape as a key piece of evidence for the larger hidden story he tells about the people around Nixon.
nixon-headed-the-5412-committee-under-ei: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says he believes that Richard Nixon, who served under President Dwight Eisenhower in the 1950s, also headed something called the 5412 commission. Michels describes it as a continuity of government initiative, meaning a plan to keep the government running through a catastrophe. He raises it while talking about secret programs of that era, and if true it would mean Nixon sat close to the government's most hidden decisions.
nixon-on-whether-the-cia-conspired-to-re: Richard Nixon, the US president who left office in 1974 over the Watergate scandal, which began with a break-in at his opponents' offices in Washington, was asked whether the CIA, America's foreign intelligence agency, plotted to bring him down. In the clip, Nixon says he does not know, that many people think so, and that he found it hard to understand why the CIA, which apparently knew about the break-in in advance, did not tell him. If true, it would mean the intelligence agency had a hand in the fall of a president.
nixon-s-1960-assassination-team-killed-j: Dan Sheehan, a lawyer and researcher, says on Jesse Michels's podcast that he was told about a secret assassination team that Richard Nixon set up in 1960. According to Sheehan, the same team later killed President John F. Kennedy in Dallas in 1963. He links the claim to people including Santo Trafficante, Andy Toney and William Johnstone Taylor, and if true it would mean the killing grew out of an earlier government plan.
nixon-s-filing-cabinet-folder-of-alien-b: Grant Cameron, a longtime researcher of UFO stories, passes on a tale about Richard Nixon from his years as president, 1969 to 1974. Cameron says Nixon was said to keep a folder in his filing cabinet holding photographs of dead alien bodies, and that these pictures were shown to people. If true, it would mean a sitting president personally held proof of beings from elsewhere.
nixon-sets-up-operation-40-after-castro-: Dan Sheehan, a researcher, told podcast host Jesse Michels that around 1959 and 1960, after Fidel Castro, Cuba's new leader, refused Richard Nixon's terms, Nixon set up a secret operation first called Operation 40. Sheehan tells it as part of a wider story linking hidden government operations to the killing of President John F. Kennedy and to UFO secrecy.
nixon-shows-brezhnev-a-folder-moon-fligh: This story is set at a meeting between the American and Soviet leaders in the early 1970s. A man named Kiran Ilum Xenov, introduced on a podcast as the president of a Russian republic, tells it to the host, Jesse Michels. Xenov passes on what he says he was told, and among the names he cites is the later Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev. According to Xenov, once the others had left the room, US President Richard Nixon opened a small folder and showed it to the Soviet leader Leonid Brezhnev, with a senior Soviet figure named Yuri Andropov present. The story, as titled, links that moment to the end of the American flights to the moon. Michels repeats it in his own words in the same conversation, saying Nixon gave the Soviet Union information about what the CIA, the American spy agency, and the White House knew about UFOs and aliens, though he leaves out the folder and the moon flights. If true, it would mean the two rival powers privately shared secrets about aliens.
nixon-takes-jackie-gleason-to-homestead-: This story is about US President Richard Nixon and his friend, the comedian Jackie Gleason. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, calls it a famous story. He says that in 1973 Nixon came to Gleason's home, told him the government had secret UFO technology, and took him to Homestead Air Force Base in Florida. The talk show host Joe Rogan tells a fuller version he credits to a magazine article. In Rogan's telling, Gleason saw a recovered crashed UFO and alien bodies in freezers, and was so shaken that he became obsessed with UFOs for good. If true, it would mean a sitting president personally showed proof of alien visitors to a celebrity.
nixon-used-malmgren-to-check-kissinger-1: Researcher Matthew Pines told podcast host Jesse Michels that President Richard Nixon used a trade official named Harold Malmgren to keep an eye on Henry Kissinger, his top foreign policy aide, in many negotiations. According to Pines, Malmgren's job was to confirm that Kissinger was not going rogue, which would make Malmgren a trusted insider worth listening to.
nixonford-era-decision-to-privatize-the-: Matthew Brown, described as a Pentagon whistleblower, passes on what he calls "legacy program lore", meaning stories about a long-running secret US effort tied to non-human craft. He says the story goes that a decision was made during the Nixon administration and carried into the Ford administration, between 1969 and 1977, to essentially hand the program over to private companies. If true, it would explain why such a program might sit outside normal government oversight.
nnsa-officials-attend-sol-foundation-ufo: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that at a gathering of the Sol Foundation, a group at Stanford University devoted to UFO research, people from the National Nuclear Security Administration showed up. That agency is the part of the US government that looks after the country's nuclear weapons. Michels tells it as a sign that nuclear officials quietly take the UFO subject seriously.
nnsa-reply-to-foia-request-on-starfish-p: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells of a request made under FOIA, a US law that lets anyone ask for government records. The request went to the National Nuclear Security Administration, the US agency that looks after nuclear weapons, and asked for every record under any UFO-related term linked to Starfish Prime, a series of US nuclear tests. Michels says the agency wrote back in June 2022 that the case needed extra review by an expert with authority over the matching records. He mentions it as a hint that such records may exist, though in some tellings he gives no date and calls the requester anonymous.
no-american-flag-on-the-sport-model-1988: Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked at a secret Nevada site called S-4 around 1988 and 1989, tells of a craft he calls the "sport model". He says he noticed on his very first day there that it carried no American flag. If true, it would hint that the craft was not built by the United States.
no-column-supports-the-craft-s-53-ft-flo: Bob Lazar is a man who says he worked on alien craft in 1988 and 1989 at a secret site in Nevada called S-4. A researcher named Luigi Vendetelli told podcast host Jesse Michels that when Lazar peeked into one craft's bottom level, he saw no supporting column holding up its 53-foot-wide floor. If true, the craft would be built in a way ordinary engineering would not allow.
no-footage-until-the-lady-allowed-filmin: A North Carolina man named Chris Bledsoe, who says he has long had UFO encounters behind his house, says that from 2007 to 2012 he went out every night with a camera and captured nothing at all. He says he was desperate for pictures to clear his name with neighbours who doubted him, and that footage only came once a being he calls the Lady allowed it. If true, it would mean whatever he meets decides when it can be seen.
no-loose-nuke-nest-and-fbi-wmd-staff-sta: Jake Barber, a man who says he once carried a UFO with his helicopter, talks about the mysterious events in New Jersey in December 2024. He says it was not a lost nuclear weapon, because people he knows on NEST, the US government's nuclear emergency team, and FBI staff who deal with weapons of mass destruction stayed in New Jersey with their families. If they had believed there was a loose nuke, he reasons, they would have moved their families away.
no-physicists-on-nasa-s-follow-up-uap-st: A man named Charles, described as a former senior NASA figure, says that around 2023 and 2024 he and his wife were asked to help when NASA, the US space agency, was running its own study of UAP, the official term for unidentified objects in the sky. As the story is framed, that follow-up study had no physicists on it, which, if true, would suggest the agency was not taking the hard science seriously.
no-physicists-on-the-claimed-crash-retri: Eric Weinstein, a researcher, put a question to a Pentagon scientist on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels. He asks whether two things are connected: physics has not moved past its two main theories, the standard model of particles and Einstein's theory of gravity, since about the 1970s, and, he says, no physicists work on the claimed crash retrieval program, a supposed secret effort to recover crashed craft. If they are linked, it would mean secrecy itself has stalled science.
no-real-physicists-on-the-program: Eric Davis, a physicist who has worked on government-funded research into UFOs, speaks about a government program connected to the subject. He says there was not a real physicist there, nobody at the PhD level in applied or theoretical physics. If true, it would mean the people looking at the hardest questions lacked the scientific training to answer them.
no-reverse-engineering-success-after-eig: Eric Davis, a physicist who has worked on Pentagon-linked UFO research, says he spent years interviewing a senior vice president at one of the big American aerospace companies, before and after the man retired. According to Davis, this man confirmed that a program trying to reverse engineer recovered craft, meaning to take them apart and learn how they work, had no success over eight decades from the 1940s on. If true, it would mean such craft exist but have stayed beyond human understanding.
no-transient-nuclear-test-matches-after-: A researcher named Steven Bruel, speaking on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels alongside the astronomer Beatriz Villarroel, discusses transients, brief points of light that appear on old photographs of the sky taken at Palomar Observatory in California. Bruel says these flashes sometimes lined up in time with nuclear tests, but that the last such match was on 17 March 1956. He tells it because the timing of the matches could say something about what those lights were.
no-writings-in-the-great-pyramid: A researcher named Matt, speaking on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, says that inside the Great Pyramid of Giza in Egypt there are no writings anywhere. He raises it as a puzzle, since it would leave open who built the pyramid and why.
noah-rodek-s-foia-on-project-preserve-de: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells of an independent researcher named Noah Rodek who used FOIA, a US law that lets anyone request government records, to ask the Air Force about Project Preserve Destiny. That is a secret programme described by Dan Sherman, a former Air Force man, in his book Above Black. According to Michels, the Air Force passed the request on to the NSA, the US spy agency that handles communications intelligence, which he takes as a sign that the project may be real and tied to that agency.
non-disclosure-agreement-incident-made-c: Mario Woods, a former guard of nuclear weapons, told podcast host Jesse Michels about something that he says happened to him in 1977 at Ellsworth Air Force Base in South Dakota, an event he describes as a UFO abduction. Woods says that afterwards, while his own paperwork was being put down, a man named Jack Reed walked over and handed another person a non-disclosure agreement, a document that legally binds someone to keep quiet, and that the incident was made classified. He also names a Colonel Spraker. If true, it would mean the military worked to keep a UFO encounter at a nuclear base secret.
non-human-biologics-recovered-with-crash: This story is about "non-human biologics", meaning bodies or remains of beings that are not human, said to have come with crashed craft that the US recovered in secret. A former intelligence officer turned whistleblower, David Grusch, says, as he said in an earlier TV interview, that biologics came with some of these recoveries. He bases this on what others told him, and names a congresswoman, Nancy Mace, and a journalist, Ross Coulthart. If true, it would mean the government holds the remains of non-human beings. A man named Jake Barber, who says he helped retrieve a UFO with his helicopter, says there are reports of biologics in storage that no one understands, without tying them to particular crashes. A filmmaker, Jeremy Corbell, says he has heard the same, mostly through autopsy reports. All three tell it on the podcast of a host, Jesse Michels.
non-human-biologics-stored-at-institutio: Brigham Buhler, a guest on Jesse Michels's podcast, recalls hearing in a documentary, though he can't remember which one or who said it, that "non-human biologics" are kept at various institutions. By that he means bodies or tissue from beings that are not human, and he says they are stored at different places, which he connects to healthcare. If true, it would mean such material is quietly being held and studied.
non-operational-emp-testing-at-samso-and: Robert Salas, a former Air Force officer who says a UFO shut down nuclear missiles under his watch, talks about tests of EMP, short for electromagnetic pulse, a burst of energy that can knock out electronics. He says the testing on equipment like his was done not at working missile sites but at places like the Space and Missile Systems Organization in San Bernardino, California, and Hill Air Force Base in Utah, in the 1960s and 70s, drawing on a book called The Faded Giant by James Klotz. He raises it because EMP tests have been offered as an explanation for the missile shutdowns, and the location matters for whether that holds.
non-verbal-amazon-tribes-and-their-ancie: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says there are apparently tribes in the Amazon rainforest who communicate without speaking. In a later episode he goes further and says these tribes call it the ancient language and send information to each other by telepathy, meaning mind to mind. He brings it up as a sign that people might share thoughts directly.
nordic-alien-on-orcas-island: Brent Friedman is a Hollywood writer. On the podcast of host Jesse Michels, he says he once saw a Nordic alien on Orcas Island, in Washington state. A Nordic alien is a term for a being said to look like a tall, fair human. He gives no date. In a fuller telling on the same episode, he says it happened on a friend's 20-acre property. All of a sudden, he says, there was a person who looked just like a Scandinavian male model. He says the being spoke to him without moving its mouth. If true, it would mean beings that pass for human can show up and talk by thought. Both tellings are Brent's own, from one conversation, the second adding the details.
nordics-from-mars-caused-the-extinction-: A philosopher named Jason Jorjani, drawing on a work called Closer Encounters, describes the "Nordics", tall human-looking beings that appear in UFO stories. He says that Nordics who came to Earth from Mars were responsible for wiping out the dinosaurs. If true, it would mean non-human beings shaped the whole history of life on Earth.
