norseen-report-under-nasa-weather-contra: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, points to a report from around 2000 by a researcher named John Norseen, titled Biofusion, Reflexive Control and Neuro-ergonomic Integration in Adaptive Cockpits, which is about fitting aircraft cockpits to the pilot's brain. Michels says that, by Norseen's own citation, the report was paid for under contract N66001, a contract the story links to NASA weather work and to the Navy's SPAWAR Systems Center in San Diego, a Navy research center for communications and electronics. If true, it would show brain-related research being funded under a contract with an unrelated label.
norseen-s-not-heard-nor-seen-email-and-d: Duncan Laurie, a researcher, tells of a man named John Norseen, linked to the Naval War College, a US Navy school in Newport, Rhode Island, who sent him an email in the early 2000s using the phrase "not heard nor seen". Laurie says that just about two weeks later Norseen was found dead in a motel room. If the two are connected, it would suggest Norseen knew something dangerous.
norsine-at-allagash-in-august-1976-runni: Charlie Foltz, a man who says he had a strange experience at the Allagash Waterway, a wilderness river route in Maine, in August 1976, relays what a man named John Norsine told him. According to Foltz, Norsine said he had been running a "tag, trace, retrieve" exercise there that summer, using a small device placed under the skin. If true, it would put a hidden human operation in the same place and time as the experience Foltz describes.
norsine-denies-a-government-cover-story-: Jim Weiner, a man who says he was part of an abduction experience, describes asking John Norsine in Newport, Rhode Island whether a government cover story lay behind it. Weiner says Norsine simply answered "No," and that Norsine believed what he was saying. Weiner tells it because it would mean the event was not a staged government operation.
norsine-s-bioenergetics-work-with-duncan: Jim Weiner, a man who says he was part of an abduction experience, mentions that John Norsine worked with a man named Duncan Luri in Jamestown, Rhode Island. The work was in bioenergetics, a loose term for the study of energy in living bodies, though Weiner's description of exactly what they did trails off. He brings it up as part of the background of the people around his story.
north-american-indian-legends-of-six-fin: A researcher named Tim Alberino, speaking on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, says that Native American peoples had legends of giants with red hair and six fingers. At another point in the same conversation he mentions only the red-haired giants, without the six fingers. He tells it because, if true, these stories would point to a lost race of giants in North America.
north-sea-oil-rig-engineer-sighting-in-j: A British defence journalist, Nick Cook, says that around 1989 an engineer working on an oil rig in the North Sea, a man he names as Chris Gibson, looked up and saw a black, dart-like craft shaped like an arrowhead. Cook credits the account to another aviation writer, Bill Sweetman, and says the story ran in Jane's Defence Weekly, a respected military trade magazine. It is told as a possible glimpse of a secret aircraft that officially did not exist.
north-sentinel-island-analogy-for-hidden: A researcher named Eric Weinstein, speaking on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, compares our situation to North Sentinel Island, a remote island that India governs but whose people it leaves alone and never visits. He says the islanders could wonder why nobody out there ever shows up, which is the same puzzle we face when we ask why we see no sign of other intelligent life. His point is that non-human observers could be watching us while deliberately choosing not to land.
northcom-jellyfish-uap-crosses-us-mexico: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, speaking with Matthew Brown, described as a Pentagon whistleblower, reads a line from a document called the Immaculate Constellation report. The line describes a jellyfish-shaped UAP, the government's term for an unidentified flying object, crossing the US-Mexico border, in a case the story attributes to NORTHCOM, the US military command that defends North America. If true, it would mean the military tracks strange objects over American borders without telling the public.
northern-lights-seen-as-far-south-as-lon: Rupert Sheldrake, a British scientist, mentions on Jesse Michels's podcast that in 2024 the northern lights, the glowing coloured skies usually seen near the Arctic, were spotted as far south as London. He says he didn't see them himself because it was cloudy. He brings it up as an example of unusual things happening in the sky.
northern-sweden-police-investigator-of-t: A researcher named Clas Svahn, speaking on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, talks about the ghost rockets, a wave of unexplained objects people reported over Sweden in the 1940s. Svahn says one of the people looking into them was a policeman far up in the north of the country. He mentions it as part of the record of how those sightings were investigated at the time.
northrop-grumman-area-51-arv-story-calle: Eric Davis, a physicist who has worked on Pentagon-linked UFO research, says he asked an insider about stories that the aerospace company Northrop Grumman, or someone at Area 51, a secret US air base in Nevada, had an ARV, meaning a human-built copy of a non-human craft. According to Davis, the man answered that it was all myth. This bears on claims like those of Bob Lazar, a man who has said he worked on alien craft near Area 51.
northrop-grumman-s-corporate-security-as: Matthew Brown, a man presented as a Pentagon whistleblower, says that Northrop Grumman, a large American defence company, has for some time been given the authority to enforce secrecy on certain classified programmes through its own corporate security staff. If true, it would mean a private company is policing government secrets on the government's behalf.
northrop-paper-vanishes-b-2-electrostati: Jesse Michels, a podcast host, tells of a 1968 paper by Northrop, a big American aircraft maker, about using electric charge to help move or lift aircraft, an idea tied to the inventor Townsend Brown, and links it to talk of electric charging on the wings of the B-2, a stealth bomber. He says that when a researcher named Dan Marcas went looking for the paper in an aerospace journal, it had completely vanished. The writer Nick Cook also recalls such Northrop papers but places them, unsure, in the early 1960s, and the vanishing matters to the tellers because it would suggest the work was pulled into secrecy.
northwest-airlines-pilot-s-telepathic-en: James Fox, a UFO investigator, says he once interviewed a man he believes was a former pilot for Northwest Airlines, an American passenger airline. As the story goes, the pilot described an encounter in Arizona in which he felt he was communicated with by mind alone, which, if true, would point to beings that can reach people telepathically.
norwegian-farmer-sees-a-craft-hovering-b: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that while he was in Norway he talked with a farmer who told him he had seen a craft hovering right around his house. Michels brings it up as an example of ordinary people having close sightings.
norwegians-with-24-teeth-want-to-build-c: A man named Charles Hall, who says he spent three years around tall white aliens at Area 51, a secret US Air Force base in Nevada, tells of another group of beings he calls the Norwegians, who he says have 24 teeth. He says that around 1965 they could only repair their craft once they got to Earth, and wanted to work with the American government to build craft here. If true, it would mean the US was in talks with more than one kind of visitor.
nova-scotia-navy-divers-see-occupants-be: Tim Gallaudet, a retired US Navy admiral, relays an account he credits to Chris Styles and Brian Fitzpatrick about navy divers off Nova Scotia, Canada, around 1960, during an operation called Sweep Clear Five. According to the account, the divers said they saw two saucer-shaped craft on the seabed with occupants outside them, and even filmed it. If true, it would mean unknown craft and their crews were operating under the sea.
november-1975-helicopter-near-miss-with-: A Swedish UFO researcher, Clas Svahn, says he recently got clearance to see files from a Swedish military, customs and police operation of the 1970s, papers meant to stay sealed until 2040. Among them, he says, is the case of a helicopter pilot near the Swedish and Norwegian border on November 7, 1975, flying 20 meters over the treetops on a moonlit, snowy night, who nearly collided with a "ghost rocket," the name for rocket-like objects people reported in Scandinavian skies. He tells it because the files would show the state took these objects seriously.
nrl-s-1952-appraisal-of-brown-s-device-m: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in 1952 the Naval Research Laboratory, the US Navy's research centre, wrote an assessment of experiments by Thomas Townsend Brown, an inventor who worked on electrogravity, the idea that electricity could push against gravity. The paper was called "TT Brown electrogravity device." Michels says that when Tom Valone, of a research group called the Integrity Research Institute, tried to find a copy, the laboratory no longer had it, which suggests records of this work went missing.
nro-corona-satellites-immediately-imagin: A researcher who goes by UAPGerb, talking with podcast host Jesse Michels, suggests that in the late 1950s and 1960s, under President Eisenhower, the National Reconnaissance Office, the US agency that runs spy satellites, took over Corona, the country's first spy satellite programme, and later launched more spy satellites known as Keyhole. He says one could build a theory that these satellites almost at once began picking up photos and radio signals of many UFOs. If so, the US government would have held hard evidence of UFOs since the early space age.
nro-founded-for-reconnaissance-in-denied: A researcher who goes by UAPGerb tells podcast host Jesse Michels that the National Reconnaissance Office, the US agency behind spy satellites, was created to gather intelligence over places American planes could not safely fly, such as the Soviet Union. He says this mattered because everyone knew a nuclear war with the Soviets would destroy both sides, so seeing what the other side was doing was vital.
nro-neutrino-detectors-used-to-target-an: Steven Greer, a man who has long campaigned for the government to reveal what it knows about aliens, says on a podcast that the NRO, the US agency that runs spy satellites, had detectors for neutrinos, tiny particles that pass through almost anything, on its satellites. According to Greer, those detectors picked up the signature of alien craft so they could be targeted and knocked out of the sky, without other people knowing. If true, it would mean the US secretly hunts and downs visiting craft.
nro-nga-senate-and-gao-audit-over-carryo: A researcher who goes by UAPGerb tells podcast host Jesse Michels that in 1994 and 1995 two US spy agencies, the National Reconnaissance Office, which runs spy satellites, and the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency, which studies satellite images and maps, were audited by the Senate and by the Government Accountability Office, Congress's watchdog for spending. He says the audit was over roughly 3.2 billion dollars in misused carryover funds, meaning money left unspent and rolled into later years. He raises it as a sign that large sums could have quietly gone to hidden work.
nro-program-b-ground-element-at-pine-gap: A researcher who goes by UAPGerb tells podcast host Jesse Michels that the ground part of Program B, a branch of the National Reconnaissance Office, the US spy satellite agency, was set up at Pine Gap, a secretive satellite station in Australia. He places this in the 1980s, as part of a wider picture of how hidden US intelligence programmes are spread out and run.
nro-sentient-program-integrated-with-imm: Matthew Brown, introduced on Jesse Michels's podcast as a Pentagon whistleblower, says the National Reconnaissance Office, the US agency that runs spy satellites, has a program called Sentient. As he understands it, Sentient came online after another secret program he calls Immaculate Constellation already existed, and the two were linked together. If true, it would mean secret programs are joined up across agencies.
nrol-16-on-walpurgisnacht-matching-a-nec: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that a US spy satellite launch called NROL-16 lifted off at 12:50 a.m. on April 30, 2005. He notes that this is Walpurgisnacht, a European folk night linked with witches, and, drawing on a man named John Ramirez, says the timing matches a rite in the Necronomicon, a book of supposed magic rituals. If true, it would hint that ritual timing plays a part in secret space launches.
nsa-certificate-for-ea280-electronics-in: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, interviews Dan Sherman, a former military sergeant who says the NSA, the National Security Agency that handles US electronic spying, hired him to communicate with aliens. Michels shows a certificate he says the NSA gave Sherman in the early 1990s, at its complex in Maryland, for finishing a course called EA280 on collecting and analysing electronic intelligence. It is offered as proof that Sherman really was trained by the agency, which would lend weight to his story.
nsa-glomar-response-cites-executive-orde: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in 2023 a person named Noah Hradek used a US law that lets anyone request government records to ask the NSA, America's electronic spying agency, for certain material. Michels says the agency gave what is called a Glomar response, a reply that will neither confirm nor deny that records exist, saying that even whether the material exists is a classified matter, citing Executive Order 13526, the presidential order that sets the rules for government secrets. He tells it because it would suggest the agency is guarding something it will not even admit to having.
nsa-may-have-tracked-sherman-since-child: Dan Sherman is a former military sergeant who says the NSA, the US agency that intercepts communications, hired him to communicate with aliens. According to podcast host Jesse Michels, Sherman believes the NSA may have been tracking him since childhood, through his young adulthood and into his military service. If that were true, it would mean he was picked out for the role long before he knew about it.
nsa-personnel-attend-ramsay-lecture: A researcher named Scott Ramsay, who studies a story about a crashed craft with alien bodies, says that people from the National Security Agency, the US spy agency that handles communications intelligence, came to one of his talks in Baltimore, Maryland. He says something similar had happened at another of his talks too. He tells it as a sign that intelligence people keep an eye on his research.
nsa-purges-borland-s-jwics-document-data: Dylan Borland, a man who says he worked with classified US systems, says that in 2024 he had saved a large collection of documents, briefings and private messages on JWICS, a top-secret US government computer network for intelligence. He says the NSA, the US National Security Agency that handles electronic intelligence, wiped that collection out. He tells it as a sign that someone wanted the UFO-related material he had gathered erased.
nsa-source-at-collusion-meetings-with-a-: Steven Greer, a campaigner for UFO disclosure, says that he knows a man at the NSA, the National Security Agency, the US spy agency that intercepts communications. Greer says this man sat in meetings with top executives of a major tech and telecommunications company, and that the two sides were, in his words, sort of colluding. Greer told this to podcast host Jesse Michels as part of his claim that UFO secrets are kept by a hidden alliance of government and private business.
nsa-treat-men-in-black-unit: An online UFO researcher who goes by UAPGerb describes a supposed men in black unit, the kind of mysterious agents said to visit UFO witnesses, inside the NSA, the US agency that handles electronic spying. He says it was called the Tactical Reconnaissance Engineering Assessment Team, created by an Army general named Albert Stubblebine, and he links it to Edgar Fouche, Prince Hans-Adam II of Liechtenstein and a set of archived emails. If true, it would mean a spy agency keeps a team for handling UFO matters.
nsa-utah-data-center-code-named-bumblehi: A researcher named Matthew Pines tells podcast host Jesse Michels that the National Security Agency, the US agency that intercepts communications, built what was then its largest single data centre in Utah, around the mid 2000s. He says its code name, now made public, was Bumblehive, a detail he brings up while talking about secrecy and hidden government programmes.
nsc-study-on-disclosure-of-recovered-cra: A former US Senate staffer, Kirk McConnell, says there was a report that the National Security Council, the White House's group of top security advisers, under President George W. Bush commissioned a study, through a Pentagon planning office called the Office of Net Assessment, on whether the time had come for disclosure, meaning telling the public about recovered craft. He connects this to Sean Kirkpatrick, a former head of the Pentagon's UFO office. If true, it would mean the White House seriously weighed going public in the 2000s.
nsf-and-nasa-co-sponsor-extended-electro: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that around late 2024 the National Science Foundation, a US government agency that funds research, and NASA, the US space agency, co-sponsored a podcast. According to Michels, it featured well-credentialed scientists and engineers looking into extended electrodynamics, an expanded version of the physics of electricity and magnetism that some link to unusual propulsion. He presents it as a sign that serious institutions are taking the idea seriously.
nsf-gulfstream-v-surveys-over-the-triang: The owner of Skinwalker Ranch, a property in Utah famous for reports of strange happenings, says that a part of the ranch called the triangle has been surveyed from the air. He says the plane was the National Science Foundation's 50 million dollar Gulfstream V jet, the NSF being a US government agency that funds science. He tells it as proof that serious scientific resources are being pointed at the ranch's mysteries.
nttr-retrieval-insider-describes-a-crack: A researcher who goes by the online name UAPGerb says an insider told him about a mission to recover a crashed craft on the Nevada Test and Training Range, a huge US military testing area in the desert. If true, it would mean the US military has picked up crashed craft that were not built by people.
nuclear-assets-of-the-29th-guards-missil: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says the 29th Guards Missile Division, a Russian military unit, is and long has been a live nuclear force near Irkutsk, a city in Siberia. He says it operates mobile ICBMs, which are long-range nuclear missiles that can cross continents, and he raises this as background to an account from around 2011 linked to a man named Stephen Pearson. The point, as he frames it, is that strange events seem to happen near nuclear weapons.
nuclear-posture-review-and-the-motive-to: Robert Salas, a former US Air Force officer, told podcast host Jesse Michels that the Nuclear Posture Review, a Pentagon document setting out US nuclear weapons policy, calls nuclear deterrence "the backbone" of national security. Salas offers this as the reason, going back to the 1950s, why the military would want to discredit people who report UFOs near nuclear weapons: admitting that something could interfere with them would undercut the country's main defense.
nuclear-powered-airplane-in-an-idaho-fal: John Herrington, a former US Secretary of Energy, which is the cabinet member who runs the government's energy and nuclear work, spoke with the podcast host Jesse Michels. If true, it would mean a secret aircraft of that kind was built and then hidden away. He makes the point twice in the same conversation. The second time he links it to Howard Hughes, the famous American aviator and businessman, and does not say how long ago it was.
nuclear-silo-shutdowns-and-anti-nuclear-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, drawing on the work of researcher Robert Hastings, says many UFO accounts tied to nuclear weapons involve missile silos, the underground launch sites, being shut down. He adds that the messages people say they receive often warn that humanity will destroy itself in a nuclear holocaust. If true, it would suggest whatever is behind these events cares about our nuclear weapons.
nuclear-systems-kept-archaic-so-they-can: A man named Michael Herrera, who says he once saw a 300 foot UFO in the Indonesian jungle, says he found out personally that around 2017 the systems at NORAD, the military command that watches North American skies, and at secret military facilities were kept deliberately old fashioned. He says this is because outdated systems are harder to hack. He tells it as part of what he learned about how hidden military sites really run.
nuclear-test-sites-with-marines-dug-in-n: A man named Randy Anderson, who says he saw alien technology at a military base, says that in the 1950s at the Nevada Test Site, the desert area where the US tested nuclear bombs, the military set off nuclear blasts with Marines dug in right next to them. He tells it as part of the hidden history of that secret region of Nevada, near Area 51, a secret Air Force base.
nuclear-weapons-aboard-the-nimitz-group-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that during the 2004 sightings by the Nimitz carrier strike group, a Navy aircraft carrier and its escort ships off San Diego, the ships likely had tactical nuclear weapons, smaller battlefield nukes, on board. He ties this to the writer Robert Hastings and his work UFOs and Nukes, which links UFO sightings to nuclear weapons. If true, it would suggest the objects showed up where nuclear arms were.
number-137-in-the-proportions-of-the-sec: A researcher named Armando Mei, speaking on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, says that the number 137 shows up in the proportions of the second pyramid of Giza in Egypt. He links it to the same number as discussed by the physicists Richard Feynman and Leon Lederman. If true, it would suggest the pyramid's builders knew something about the deep workings of nature.
numbers-spoken-from-television-sets-1960: A philosopher named Jason Jorjani, speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast, says that John Keel, a writer who investigated strange phenomena in the 1960s, reported cases of people hearing numbers spoken at them out of their television sets. He tells it as part of a wider picture in which some unknown intelligence reaches into ordinary people's lives in odd ways.
nuraghe-towers-buried-as-if-by-a-tidal-w: A researcher named Tim Alberino, speaking on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, describes the nuraghe, ancient stone towers on the Italian island of Sardinia. He says they were suddenly covered in earth, almost as if a tidal wave had swept across the island. If true, it would point to a sudden disaster in the ancient past.
nuro-finding-things-on-the-seafloor: John Harrington, a former US Secretary of Energy, was asked on Jesse Michels's podcast about NURO, a little-known secret office said to handle underwater reconnaissance. When it was put to him that they might be finding things on the seafloor, he answered, "Yep. They are." If true, it would mean a hidden government effort is recovering unexplained objects from the ocean floor.
nurse-says-she-was-there-1996: James Fox, a documentary filmmaker, tells of meeting a nurse while looking into events in Varginha, Brazil, in 1996, when people say a strange creature was captured and taken to a hospital. When Fox and his team asked how she could know what happened, he says she began shaking and answered, "Because I was there." If true, she would be a firsthand witness to a non-human being in the hospital.
nurse-says-the-wright-patterson-craft-ca: Scott Ramsay, a researcher of a claimed crash near Aztec, a small town in New Mexico, passes on what a nurse told about a craft held at Wright-Patterson, an Air Force base near Dayton, Ohio. According to Ramsay, the nurse said the craft there had come from Aztec, and that this is how the link was made. If true, it would tie the Aztec crash story to the military holding the wreck.
nurse-speaks-for-first-time-in-virginia: A podcast host named Jesse Michels interviewed a surgeon whose hospital, the episode says, operated on an alien being. Michels says that a nurse who had once worked under this surgeon has, for the first time, begun to speak about the being. If true, it would add another voice from inside the hospital to the claim that a non-human creature was treated there.
nurses-and-radiology-technician-also-wit: In January 1996, in the Brazilian town of Varginha, a strange creature is said to have been brought to the town's Regional Hospital. A surgeon named Italo Venturelli, speaking on the podcast of host Jesse Michels, says that many people there say they saw it, including nurses, and that the radiology technician, the person who runs the X-ray machines, says he saw a closed box. If true, it would mean hospital staff quietly witnessed the handling of a non-human body.
o-reilly-brown-inventions-handed-to-cons: Townsend Brown was an American inventor of the mid-1900s, described in a documentary by podcast host Jesse Michels as a scientist who built flying-saucer-like devices for the government. Michels relays that a source named O'Reilly says a couple of Brown's other inventions were handed over to outside organisations, and that a group he calls a consortium seems to have something to do with it. If true, it would mean Brown's work was quietly passed to private hands rather than vanishing.
oak-ridge-magnesium-bismuth-technical-do: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, speaking in an episode about a US Secretary of Energy and UFOs, says that among documents on UFOs there is a 1950s technical paper from Oak Ridge National Laboratory, a government nuclear research lab in Tennessee. He says the paper talks about the metals magnesium and bismuth. He mentions it because, if true, it would tie a government lab to materials he connects with UFOs.
oak-ridge-visit-arranged-by-howard-baker: Harold Malmgren, a former advisor to US presidents, says that sometime in the 1970s or 1980s a political figure named Howard Baker arranged for him to visit Oak Ridge, a US government nuclear research site in Tennessee, where he spent time with the people working there. He tells it as part of his account of handling UFO-related material, which, if true, would tie that material to top-level government science.
obama-at-a-campfire-tells-eddie-vedder-t: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells a story about Eddie Vedder, the lead singer of the band Pearl Jam, sitting drunk around a campfire with former President Barack Obama. According to Michels, Vedder asked Obama what was really going on, and Obama told him to read The Three-Body Problem, a science fiction novel about contact with an alien civilisation. Told this way, it would hint that a president knows something about aliens that he could only point to sideways.
obama-on-james-corden-about-unidentified: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, recalls that in 2021 former US President Barack Obama went on the late-night talk show of James Corden. According to Michels, Obama said there are things in our sky that we cannot identify and do not know what they are. Michels tells it as a sign that even a former president openly admits the mystery is real.
obama-on-jimmy-kimmel-says-the-aliens-wo: Kurt Metzger, a guest on podcast host Jesse Michels' show, recalls a moment when Barack Obama, the former US president, appeared on Jimmy Kimmel Live, an American late-night TV talk show. Metzger says Obama joked, with a smile, that the aliens won't let it happen, meaning that they won't let the government reveal what it knows about them, and Metzger asks what Obama was really saying underneath the joke.
obama-s-area-51-remark-later-walked-back: The podcast host Jesse Michels says that in 2026 Barack Obama, the former US president, spoke about Area 51, a secret US military test base in the Nevada desert long linked to UFO stories, and about alien beings kept underground there. Michels says Obama then walked his statement back. A guest named Bryce says the walk-back came the very next day, and that Donald Trump took the bait. If true, it would mean a former president briefly hinted at something he then had to take back.
obama-s-betty-and-barney-hill-documentar: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that former US President Barack Obama has been involved with a documentary about Betty and Barney Hill, an American couple known for saying they were taken aboard a UFO, and that Obama visited the set of Disclosure Day, a film by the director Steven Spielberg. Michels tells it both as Obama thinking about producing the documentary and, another time, as Obama actually producing it. He sees it as a sign that Obama is quietly interested in the subject.
obama-says-on-a-podcast-that-aliens-are-: A researcher and well known skeptic, Michael Shermer, says that former US President Barack Obama went on a podcast in the 2020s, was asked by the host whether he thought aliens were real, and answered, "Yeah, I think aliens are real." Shermer says this remark is what set off a large public release of government UFO files. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells the same story but frames Obama's comment as a way of provoking President Donald Trump. If so, a single offhand remark would have pushed the government to open its files.
obama-shuts-down-a-putin-back-channel-th: Podcast host Jesse Michels says that Harald Malmgren, a former advisor to US presidents, told him that in 2009 Vladimir Putin, the Russian leader, wanted to set up a private diplomatic line of contact with Washington through Malmgren. According to Michels, President Barack Obama shut the idea down. Michels raises it to show how close Malmgren, who says he handled UFO material, was to the centre of power.
obamatrump-exchange-over-ufos-2026: Aldo Rebelo, a former Brazilian defense minister, mentions that the UFO question recently became a public controversy in the United States. He says it came up through what he calls a dialogue between former President Barack Obama and current President Donald Trump. He tells it to show that the subject has reached the highest levels of American politics.
oberth-and-von-braun-s-neopagan-rituals-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in the 1930s and 1940s in Germany, Hermann Oberth, a rocket pioneer, and his student Wernher von Braun, who later led rocket work in America, went through strange neopagan rituals, meaning ceremonies drawn from old pre-Christian religions, as part of the Nazi space programme. In some tellings Michels mentions only von Braun, and once adds that von Braun was believed to be a Freemason, a member of a secretive fraternal society. He tells it to suggest that early space science had a hidden mystical side.
object-abroad-too-large-to-move: Eric Burles, a US congressman, says he has heard that there is an object held outside the United States that is so big it cannot be moved. He gives this as a reported claim, without saying where it is or who told him. If true, it would point to a recovered craft too large to bring home.
object-appears-beside-the-atlas-8f-reent: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, describes film from an Atlas missile test, flight 8F, launched from Cape Canaveral in Florida over the Atlantic in September 1962. He says that 4 minutes and 40 seconds into the video, an object seems to phase into existence beside the reentry vehicle, the part of the missile that falls back through the atmosphere, while it was moving at 20,000 feet per second, or Mach 18, and he credits a US Air Force and NASA report written after the flight. If true, it would mean something kept pace with one of the fastest machines of its day.
object-came-out-of-the-water-and-zapped-: Matthew Pines, a guest on Jesse Michels's podcast, says that in late 2024 he met people working in intelligence at the Department of Defense, the US military's parent department. He says they told him that one of the unexplained objects rose out of the water and hit, or in one version zapped, a person. If true, it would mean these objects can come from the sea and harm people.
object-inside-the-mesa-at-skinwalker-ran: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, speaks of an object said to lie inside the mesa, a flat-topped hill, at Skinwalker Ranch, a property in Utah known for strange reports and the subject of the TV series Secrets of Skinwalker Ranch. He says such objects have been located but are hard to dig out, because it is as if they have a life of their own. If true, it would mean something alive or self-willed is buried there.
object-shot-down-over-alaska-said-to-hav: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, talks about an object shot down over Alaska in 2023. He says he heard claims that it had put itself back together and was later seen flying over Canada. If true, it would mean the object was not anything ordinary, but something able to repair itself.
objects-on-radar-and-seen-by-airmen-over: Robert Salas, a former US Air Force officer, says that on 24 March 1967 there were reports at Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana of objects showing up on radar and being seen by airmen at the base, a detail he links to a man named Lewis Chase. Salas tells it as part of his larger account of a UFO that, he says, shut down ten nuclear missiles that same period.
objects-over-ellsworth-runway-weapons-st: Mario Woods, an Air Force veteran, says that from the late 1950s on he heard of four or five cases of unknown objects at Ellsworth Air Force Base in South Dakota and in its nearby nuclear missile fields. According to him, objects came down the runway and appeared over the weapons storage area and the pad where B-52 bombers sat on alert, ready to fly. If true, it would mean unknown craft were showing interest in America's nuclear forces.
occult-minded-nazis-brought-in-through-p: A YouTube host named Chris Ramsay says that from 1945 on, Nazis with an interest in the occult were brought to the United States through Operation Paperclip and Operation Overcast, post-war programmes that brought German scientists over, and ended up running the American space programme. If true, it would mean Nazi thinking shaped how America went to space.
ocean-shells-on-the-eridu-ziggurat-summi: A researcher named Matt, speaking on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, says that at Eridu, an ancient city in southern Iraq, he found ocean shells still lying on top of its ziggurat, a stepped temple tower. He says this fits a flood coming in from the sea, the Persian Gulf, rather than from rivers. He tells it as possible evidence of a great ancient flood.
oceanographer-says-the-objects-are-under: Harald Malmgren, a former advisor to US presidents, says that in 2025 an unnamed oceanographer, a scientist who studies the sea, came out and said the mysterious objects are neither Chinese nor American. Malmgren presents this as a revelation pointing to the objects living under the sea or underground, which would mean something non-human sharing the planet with us.
odlum-investment-guidance-technologies-s: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells how an inventor named Townsend Brown, who worked on using electric charge to push or lift craft, ran a company in Santa Monica, California, called Guidance Technologies, and that in the fall of 1967 he shut it down with no explanation, saying he got no results. Michels says that soon after, in 1968, the aircraft maker Northrop, linked to the wealthy investor Floyd Odlum, wrote a paper saying it was investing in this kind of electric propulsion, and he connects it to the Air Force general Curtis LeMay, the jet maker Bill Lear, and an Aviation Week magazine report on the B-2 stealth bomber. The suggestion is that Brown's work quietly went into secret aerospace projects.
odlum-s-open-ended-payments-to-the-brown: A woman named Linda Brown, speaking on a podcast episode about claims of antigravity craft, says that a man named Floyd Odlum made her family sign an open-ended contract with her father, starting in the 1960s. She tells it as part of the story of how her father's work came to be tied up with powerful backers, which matters to those who believe that work touched on secret flying technology.
odni-claim-that-dylan-borland-drew-a-sen: Jeremy Corbell, a filmmaker who reports on UFO claims, says that word came directly from the ODNI, the office that oversees all US spy agencies, that a man named Dylan Borland had made a fourth drawing, this one of a sensor system. Corbell ties it to claims, around 2025 and 2026, about a craft said to be slowly heading toward Earth, and if true it would mean intelligence officials were shaping what witnesses and the public were told.
odni-duplicated-borland-s-phone-2025: A man named Dylan Borland, who has come forward with claims about secret government knowledge of non-human beings, told a podcast host, Jesse Michels, that he believes he is being watched. Borland says that around 2025 the Office of the Director of National Intelligence, the US office that oversees the country's spy agencies, made a duplicate of his phone. He says, "I know I'm tapped." If true, it would mean the government was keeping close tabs on him because of what he knows.
odni-interested-in-how-borland-tracked-s: Dylan Borland, a man who came forward with claims about unexplained craft, told the podcast host Jesse Michels that between about 2023 and 2025 officials from the Office of the Director of National Intelligence, the office that oversees US spy agencies, and its internal watchdog wanted to know how he had kept track of search-and-rescue assignments. Borland says he knows such an assignment when he sees one, backed by images and intercepted electronic signals, and he can tell which ones involve "our guys" and which do not. If true, it would suggest some of those missions were about recovering things that were not human-made.
odni-nine-month-operation-against-whistl: Jeremy Corbell, a filmmaker who reports on UFO claims, says that the ODNI, the office that oversees all US spy agencies, ran a nine-month operation around 2025 and 2026. He links it to whistleblowers and journalists such as George Knapp, Dylan Borland and Matthew Brown, and to the office's head, Tulsi Gabbard. If true, it would mean the intelligence world was actively working against the people speaking out about UFOs.
odni-tells-corbell-that-borland-told-the: Jeremy Corbell, a documentary filmmaker, says that a leader in the Director's Initiatives Group, a unit inside the Office of the Director of National Intelligence (the office that oversees all US spy agencies), told him something directly. According to Corbell, he was told that a man named Dylan Borland had told the Intelligence Community Inspector General, the watchdog that takes complaints from inside the spy agencies, about a programme called Project Rubik's Cube, which the telling does not describe. Corbell raises it to show that officials have taken Borland's claims seriously.
odyssey-systems-data-management-platform: A man who goes by Jordan, who told the podcast host Jesse Michels that a secret UFO program took him in as a child, says that around 2008 to 2010 some of the computer systems the program used to manage its data came from a company called Odyssey Systems. He also mentions MITRE, a nonprofit that does research for the US government. If true, it would tie ordinary government contractors to a hidden UFO effort.
oechsler-on-the-news-inman-convinced-him: Bob Oechsler, a man who researched UFOs in the late 1980s and 1990s, said in a news interview that Admiral Bobby Ray Inman, a retired senior Navy officer and intelligence official, had convinced him that certain craft were not made with human technology. Oechsler said that was conclusive for him, which, if true, would mean a top insider privately confirmed non-human vehicles.
oedipus-fulfills-the-prophecy-by-fleeing: On the show of a podcast host, Jesse Michels, a researcher of dreams and prophecy named Eric Wargo retells the ancient Greek myth of Oedipus, a young prince of the city of Thebes. As Wargo tells it, a prophecy says the prince will grow up to kill his father and marry his mother, and he ends up doing exactly that while trying to escape it. Wargo brings up Sigmund Freud, the founder of psychoanalysis, and uses the story to talk about how foretelling the future might shape it.
off-base-doctor-asks-had-they-let-you-se: John Blitch, a scientist who once worked for DARPA, the Pentagon's advanced research agency, told the podcast host Jesse Michels about a time he was posted to Wright-Patterson Air Force Base in Ohio. He says a doctor he saw off the base leaned in and asked him, "had they let you see the alien bodies yet?" The story matters because it suggests that, around that base, the idea of stored alien bodies was something even locals talked about.
off-planet-pin-given-at-cape-canaveral-2: Chris Bledsoe, a man who says he attracts UFOs and whom NASA has taken an interest in, told the podcast host Jesse Michels about a pin with an "off-planet" theme. He says that sometime around 2007 to 2010 it was handed to him at Cape Canaveral, the Florida rocket launch site, by someone "everybody has read about," though he would not say who. If true, it would mean someone well known in the space world quietly reached out to him.
off-record-source-the-sun-as-a-portal-to: Podcast host Jesse Michels says that a source who spoke to him off the record compared the sun to a kind of portal leading to other star systems. If true, it would suggest that visitors could travel between stars through the sun rather than across empty space.
office-of-naval-intelligence-man-offers-: Brent Friedman, a Hollywood writer who helped create Dark Skies, a 1990s TV series about a hidden alien presence, told the podcast host Jesse Michels that in the mid-1990s in Los Angeles a man from the Office of Naval Intelligence, the US Navy's spy service, offered him and his co-creator Bryce Zabel a deal. Friedman says the man was abusive to them in a conference room, and they feared he would end up as their boss, so they turned the deal down. If true, it would show military intelligence trying to shape a UFO story on television.
office-of-naval-intelligence-reports-tim: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, mentions reports written by the Office of Naval Intelligence, the US Navy's intelligence branch. He says Tim Gallaudet, a former senior Navy officer, talks a lot about USOs, objects seen moving underwater that no one can identify. If true, it would mean the Navy has been tracking unexplained things in the sea as well as in the sky.
officer-points-to-his-phone-when-giants-: Tim Alberino, who claims US troops captured a 12-foot giant in Afghanistan, told the podcast host Jesse Michels about talking with military officers. He says that when he raised the subject of giants, one of them said nothing and simply pointed at his phone. Alberino tells it as a sign the topic was too sensitive to discuss where it might be heard.
officers-keep-saying-don-t-worry-about-m: Mario Woods, who guarded nuclear weapons at Ellsworth Air Force Base in South Dakota, told the podcast host Jesse Michels about an event in 1977 that he links to a UFO abduction. He says that afterward, every time he asked about a fellow airman named Michael Johnson, officers kept telling him not to worry, that Johnson was fine. If true, it would suggest the military was keeping quiet about what happened to both men.
officials-asked-whether-he-had-a-mental-: Dylan Borland, a man who came forward with claims about unexplained craft, told the podcast host Jesse Michels that when he went to the government, officials were very interested in whether he had a mental connection to something he calls "the triangle." If true, it would mean officials took seriously the idea that a person could be linked to such an object by the mind.
officials-deny-such-a-craft-in-inventory: Greg Rogers, a doctor who has worked with NASA, says he once saw an unusual craft in a secret hangar. He told the podcast host Jesse Michels that between about 2023 and 2025 some government officials said publicly they had never had a craft like that, and he remembers thinking, "What are you talking about? I saw it." If true, it would mean officials denied something a witness says he saw with his own eyes.
officials-endorse-a-multi-generational-c: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that past directors of the CIA, the US spy agency, along with members of Congress and whistleblowers from several agencies, have backed the existence of a secret programme. According to Michels, this programme has run for decades and across generations, collecting crashed UFOs and trying to work out how they function so the technology can be copied. If true, it would mean the US government has held alien craft for a very long time.
officials-evasive-on-crash-materials-of-: Peter Levenda, an author billed on the podcast as a CIA historian, says that when he asked whether the US has materials of unknown origin in its possession, the answer came by omission. He says the response was wishy-washy rather than a clear no. To him, that dodge hints the government may be holding such materials.
officials-say-the-lady-s-dates-and-symbo: Chris Bledsoe is a man who says he attracts UFOs and is visited by a being he calls the Lady, who gives him dates and symbols. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says some officials imply that those dates and symbols line up with things they already monitor and have seen from other trusted sources. If so, it would mean Bledsoe's experiences match what the government is tracking on its own.
offworld-technology-sign-on-the-wall-at-: Randy Anderson, a man who says he saw alien technology at a military site, told the podcast host Jesse Michels that in 2014 he was at Naval Surface Warfare Center Crane, a Navy research and testing base in Indiana. He says he entered an area with a marking on the wall that read "offworld technology." If true, it would mean the Navy openly labeled a space at the base for technology not made on Earth.
oil-and-gas-company-drills-beside-the-me: The owner of Skinwalker Ranch, a Utah property linked to UFO claims where he says something lies underground, told the podcast host Jesse Michels about a strange turn of events. He says that last year an oil and gas company suddenly showed up, rushed its permits through, and began drilling on the ranch's northern border, right beside the spot where his own team had been drilling on a mesa. He tells it because the timing seemed too close to be chance.
oke-shannon-discussed-on-classified-serv: A man named Dylan Borland, speaking on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, says that sometime before 2024 a subject he calls Oke Shannon was "a massive conversation" on JWICS, a top secret computer network the US government uses for intelligence. He says he saw this himself, and he tells it because, if true, it would mean the subject was being discussed seriously inside the intelligence world.
oke-shannon-s-1985-bdm-physics-working-g: A researcher who goes by UAPGerb says that notes from 1985 by a man named Oke Shannon, from an advanced theoretical physics working group at BDM, a defence contracting company in McLean, Virginia, include a line saying to ask Don Kerr for funding. According to UAPGerb, the line comes up where the notes discuss programmes to take apart and copy UFO technology, and the same documents mention figures such as John Alexander and Stubblebine. If true, it would show such work was being planned and funded in the 1980s.
oki-shannon-on-building-an-anti-gravity-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says a figure connected to Los Alamos, the US nuclear weapons laboratory in New Mexico, named Oki Shannon, is on record about a theory by a man named Ferris Williams. According to Michels, Shannon said that if anyone were to build an anti-gravity device, a machine that cancels the pull of gravity, it would be based on Williams' theory. Michels tells it as a sign that such ideas were taken seriously by insiders.
old-agreement-with-non-human-beings-from: Matthew Brown, who describes himself as a Pentagon whistleblower, says he has been told of at least one very old agreement between the US and non-human beings, made sometime in the era of Presidents Truman and Eisenhower, between 1945 and 1961. If true, it would mean the US government has had a secret pact with non-human beings for decades.
old-maps-show-antarctica-as-two-islands: Jason Jorjani, a researcher who appeared on Jesse Michels' podcast, talks about old maps from the 1500s, including ones known as the Piri Reis map and the Oronteus Finaeus map. He says one of them shows Antarctica as two islands sitting very close together. Told this way, the maps would suggest that someone mapped Antarctica's land long before anyone is thought to have seen it.
older-bae-archives-colleague-with-ts-sci: Dylan Borland, speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast, says that when he worked at BAE, a large defence company, an older colleague in the archives warned him about something. Borland says this man held a TS/SCI clearance, one of the highest levels of US security clearance, and later moved into the intelligence community as a government employee, which is why Borland treats the warning as coming from someone who would know.
older-pilots-private-ufo-stories: Ryan Graves, a US Navy fighter pilot who later spoke publicly about strange objects seen by his squadron, says that before he spoke out, older pilots who had been flying a long time all seemed to have a cool story of their own. According to Graves, they would only tell it once they had a few drinks in them, which suggests such sightings were common but kept private.
oliver-reiser-s-tone-theory-and-letters-: A researcher on a podcast says that Oliver Reiser, a thinker at the University of Pittsburgh, wrote dozens and dozens of letters to Andrija Puharich, a man known for research into psychic matters, in the 1960s and 1970s. Reiser, he says, had a theory about tones, set out in his book Cosmic Humanism, and the researcher connects it to Albert Einstein. It is told as part of the background to Puharich's ideas about contact with other minds.
oliver-sacks-autistic-twins-who-traded-s: Diane Powell, a guest on Jesse Michels' podcast, recalls a case report by the writer Oliver Sacks, author of the book Awakenings. She says it described autistic twins living in an institution who played a game of saying prime numbers back and forth to each other, numbers six digits long. She tells it as a hint that some minds may reach information in ways we don't understand, even mind to mind.
one-in-four-ellsworth-missile-security-p: Mario Woods, a former guard of nuclear missiles at Ellsworth Air Force Base in South Dakota, spoke on a podcast about his time there. He says that among the security police guarding the missiles, about one in every four has probably seen something strange in the night sky. If true, it would mean such sightings were common among the people protecting the weapons.
one-of-grusch-s-40-witnesses-died-at-a-c: Jake Barber, a man who says he flew a helicopter to recover a UFO, talks about the roughly 40 witnesses that whistleblower David Grusch, a former intelligence officer, says backed his claims. Barber says one of those witnesses has since died, and that the death came at a very convenient time for whoever might want him silenced. He tells it to suggest that the people involved face real danger.
one-to-two-craft-brought-down-per-year-a: An online researcher who goes by UAPGerb says that Steven Greer, a well-known UFO activist, and others claim that one to two unknown craft are brought down each year at certain black sites, meaning secret military facilities that do not officially exist. If true, it would mean the government is regularly capturing non-human vehicles.
ongoing-arrangement-with-pilots-of-the-b: Matthew Brown, introduced on Jesse Michels's podcast as a Pentagon whistleblower, says the United States has some kind of exchange or arrangement with whatever pilots the black triangles, large dark triangle-shaped craft that people report seeing in the sky. He also suggests there is a US-built version derived from them. If true, it would mean the government is in an ongoing deal with whoever flies these craft.
ongoing-hybrid-program-semen-extraction-: Jeffrey Mishlove, a researcher of psychic phenomena, was talking with a podcast host, Jesse Michels. He mentioned that the writer Whitley Strieber talks about semen being taken from people during alien abductions. The idea behind it is that if this happens, abductions would be part of an ongoing programme to breed human and alien hybrids.
ongoing-psionic-operation-in-the-pentago: Ross Coulthart, a journalist, told a podcast host, Jesse Michels, that he has spoken to people who confirmed a psionic operation is still running inside the Pentagon, the headquarters of the US Defense Department in Arlington, Virginia. "Psionic" here means work that uses the mind's claimed psychic powers. If true, it would mean the military still takes psychic abilities seriously today.
onion-effect-gray-project-hidden-inside-: A former US Air Force sergeant, Dan Sherman, says that in the early 1990s he was briefed about what he calls a "gray project" hidden inside a "black project", meaning a secret programme tucked inside another secret programme so only a few people in it knew. He says an officer named Captain White told him this, connected to the NSA, the US spy agency that intercepts communications, and that his own job was to communicate with non-human beings. On Jesse Michels's podcast he places the briefing at NSA headquarters in Maryland in one telling and in a communications van at an overseas post in another.
online-whistleblower-nhi-live-and-build-: Tim Gallaudet, a retired US Navy admiral, told a podcast host, Jesse Michels, about statements from an online whistleblower who goes by the name Condor Man. According to those statements, there are five to seven places in the world's oceans where UAP, the government's term for UFOs, are seen going in and out of the water, and these are where NHI, meaning non-human intelligences, live and build their own craft. If true, it would mean something non-human has bases on Earth, under the sea.
only-about-150-of-40-000-ashurbanipal-ta: The Library of Ashurbanipal was a collection gathered by an ancient king at the city of Nineveh, in what is now Iraq, written on clay tablets in cuneiform, the wedge-shaped script of the ancient Middle East. A researcher named Matt says that of the roughly 40,000 tablets, only about 150 have been translated. If so, most of what those ancient writers recorded would still be unread.
only-minuteman-launched-from-a-silo-at-n: Mario Woods, a former nuclear missile guard in South Dakota, says the site where he was posted, a launch facility called November 2, has a special history. According to Woods, it was the only place a Minuteman, the US land-based nuclear missile, ever actually flew out of its underground silo, back in the 1960s, before his time. He believes it flew for about five seconds.
onr-studies-of-a-sixth-sense-2011: A UFO researcher who goes by the online name UAPGerb says, on podcast host Jesse Michels's show, that in 2011 and 2012 the Office of Naval Research, the US Navy's science research office, published studies on a "sixth sense" in humans. He brings it up as a sign that the military has taken unusual human perception seriously.
operation-40-becomes-operation-mongoose-: A researcher named Dan Sheehan tells podcast host Jesse Michels that in the early 1960s, in the time of President Kennedy and Soviet leader Khrushchev, a secret anti-Castro group called Operation 40 was turned into Operation Mongoose, a covert US campaign against Cuba. He says it was run from a large operation called JM WAVE on the campus of the University of Miami. He tells it as background to his claim that Kennedy's death ties into the world of secret programmes, including UFO secrets.
operation-bluebird-as-the-first-mkultra-: On a podcast, the host Jesse Michels and his guest agree that Operation Bluebird, a CIA project of the early 1950s, came before MKUltra, the CIA's later programme of mind-control experiments, and was in effect the first MKUltra. They tell it as part of a story in which UFO research and research into the human mind grew up together inside US intelligence.
operation-castle-sailors-see-discs-over-: A researcher named Robert Hastings, who gathers accounts of UFOs near nuclear sites, tells podcast host Jesse Michels about Operation Castle, a series of US nuclear bomb tests in the Marshall Islands in the Pacific in 1954. He says he found sailors on several ships who described brief but clear sightings of disc shaped or round objects hovering over their vessels. If true, it would suggest UFOs were taking an interest in nuclear weapons tests.
operation-highjump-1946: A researcher and writer named Jason Jorjani, speaking with podcast host Jesse Michels, recalls Operation Highjump, a large US Navy expedition of ships sent to Antarctica in 1946 and 1947. Jorjani names the polar explorer Richard Byrd in connection with it and says the Navy sent it "for whatever reason", framing its true purpose as an open question.
operation-highjump-and-byrd-s-statement-: This story is about Operation Highjump, a US Navy expedition to Antarctica in 1946 and 1947, and something Admiral Richard Byrd said afterwards. A researcher, Jason Jorjani, says that when Byrd reached a port in Chile he told the Chilean press that America needed to prepare for a third world war, in which aircraft could fly from pole to pole at tremendous speed. Some people read that as a hint that Byrd met strange flying craft in Antarctica, and a related version even speaks of discs shooting lasers. Another researcher, Richard Dolan, tells it differently. He says he read Byrd's full statement and does not think Byrd was really talking about flying saucers. So the two agree there was a statement but disagree on what it meant.
operation-highjump-laser-shooting-discs: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells of Operation Highjump, a US Navy expedition led by Admiral Richard Byrd that went down the coast of Argentina toward Antarctica. In one telling Michels describes it as roughly 70 ships, 33 aircraft and almost 5,000 men around 1946 and 1947, and links it to James Forrestal, a top US defence official. According to Michels, the fleet reportedly met flying saucers that shot at them with lasers, which, if true, would mean an early armed clash with unknown craft.
operation-moonwatch-and-its-36-ufo-repor: Beatriz Villarroel, an astronomer, describes Operation Moonwatch, a 1950s sky-watching program run from Harvard by the astronomer Fred Whipple with tracking stations around the world. She says the astronomer J. Allen Hynek helped Whipple, and that the program gathered 36 UFO reports, which she thinks were found by the researcher Jacques Vallée and which her team is now going through. If true, it would mean trained observers logged unexplained objects decades ago in records that are only now being studied.
operation-overlord-with-bodyguard-and-fo: A researcher named Eric Weinstein, speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast, uses the Second World War as an example: Operation Overlord, the real D-Day invasion of Normandy in 1944, was hidden behind fake plans called Bodyguard and Fortitude, which claimed the Allies would invade Norway. He says the invasion of Norway never happened, and he offers this to show how real secrets can be covered by deliberate false stories, which he suggests may also apply to UFO secrecy.
operation-paperclip-scientists-in-the-ch: Whitley Strieber, a writer known for describing his own encounters with beings, says that when he was a boy in the 1950s in Terrell Hills, a neighbourhood of San Antonio, Texas, people from Operation Paperclip apparently lived nearby. Operation Paperclip was the US programme that brought German scientists to America after the Second World War, and if true, it would place his childhood right next to secret government science.
operation-prato-as-an-official-armed-for: Aldo Rebello, presented on Jesse Michels's podcast as a former defence minister of Brazil, talks about Operation Prato, a military effort in 1977 in Pará, a state in northern Brazil. Reading from the operation's official report, he says it really took place and was an official armed forces operation set up to monitor strange phenomena in the state. If so, it would mean Brazil's military formally investigated these sightings.
operation-snow-white-scientology-infiltr: A guest named Jay Anderson, speaking on podcast host Jesse Michels's show, recalls Operation Snow White, which he describes as a 1970s effort by Scientology, a religious movement, to infiltrate several US agencies. According to Anderson, these included the IRS, the US tax agency, and the CIA, the US foreign intelligence agency. He raises it as an example of how deeply outside groups could get inside the government.
oppenheimer-created-the-classification-c: David Grusch, a former US intelligence officer turned whistleblower, told a podcast host, Jesse Michels, that Robert Oppenheimer, the physicist who led the wartime effort to build the atomic bomb, created the secrecy category that also covered UFO material, and he linked this to a scientist named Robert Sarbacher. Michels later repeated it a little differently, saying Oppenheimer helped set up the original UFO secrecy rules with the Atomic Energy Commission, the US agency that ran nuclear matters after the war. If true, UFO secrecy would date back to the very birth of nuclear secrecy in the 1940s and 50s.
oppenheimer-first-nuclear-weapon-in-mode: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, repeats what he calls an apocryphal story about Robert Oppenheimer, the physicist who led the building of the first atomic bomb in 1945. As Michels tells it, a student asked how it felt to be the first person to create a nuclear weapon, and Oppenheimer answered that he was the first in modern history, a remark the story links to the Bhagavad Gita, an ancient Hindu scripture. If true, it would hint that nuclear weapons existed in the ancient past.
oppenheimer-on-the-aztec-crash-retrieval: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, cites a book by William Steinman, UFO Crash at Aztec, about a craft said to have crashed near Aztec, New Mexico, in 1948 and been recovered. Michels says the book claims Robert Oppenheimer, the physicist who led the building of the atomic bomb, was part of the team that recovered it. If true, it would place one of America's top scientists at a recovered craft.
oppenheimer-recalls-the-trinity-test-and: Robert Oppenheimer, the physicist who led the American effort to build the atomic bomb, is heard in an episode of Jesse Michels's podcast remembering Trinity, the first atomic bomb test, in New Mexico in 1945. He recalls that on seeing the blast he thought of a line from the Bhagavad Gita, a Hindu scripture: "Now I am become death, the destroyer of worlds." The episode uses his words to mark the start of the nuclear age.
oppenheimer-s-gita-quote-originally-i-am: Dave Rossi, a guest on Jesse Michels' podcast, talks about the famous line the physicist Robert Oppenheimer quoted in 1945 from the Bhagavad Gita, an ancient Hindu scripture: "I am become death, the destroyer of worlds." Rossi says he read that the original translation said not death but "I am time, the destroyer of worlds," which would give the famous quote a quite different meaning.
oppenheimer-s-late-speech-on-abolishing-: Robert Salas, a former US Air Force officer, told a podcast host, Jesse Michels, about one of the last speeches given by Robert Oppenheimer, the physicist who led the building of the first atomic bomb. According to Salas, Oppenheimer told his scientists that we cannot afford to think we can't get rid of all nuclear weapons. Salas brings it up because he links UFOs with nuclear weapons and sees a warning in it.
oppenheimer-set-up-ufo-secrecy-1940: The podcast host Jesse Michels says in 2024 that some people claim Robert Oppenheimer, the physicist who led the US atomic bomb project during the Second World War, set up the secrecy around UFOs, and that a man named Rush said so on record in an interview with him. A researcher named Bob Maguire says on the same podcast later that year that he personally believes Oppenheimer and others from that bomb project, called the Manhattan Project, were the original secret keepers. If true, it would mean the hiding of UFO knowledge began with the people who built the bomb in the 1940s and 1950s.
oracle-at-delphi-as-a-burning-methane-se: The Oracle at Delphi was an ancient Greek shrine where a priestess gave prophecies. A researcher named Geoffrey Drumm, speaking with podcast host Jesse Michels, says the oracle was really a burning methane seep, a spot where natural gas leaked out of the ground and burned. If so, the shrine's power would have come from the earth itself.
orang-pendek-and-surviving-flores-homini: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, speculates about the Orang Pendek, a short, human-like creature some people say lives in the forests of Indonesia. He raises it alongside the idea that small ancient human relatives once known from the island of Flores might have survived. If so, it would mean other human-like beings still share the planet with us.
orange-moved-by-psychokinesis-in-a-vivid: A researcher named Deep Prasad says that when he was about 12, in a vivid dream set in his family's drawing room, he moved an orange with his mind, a power called psychokinesis. He says it suddenly slid eight or ten inches "as if something had pushed it", and he mentions a person called Miss Kaur in the story, which he tells on Jesse Michels's podcast as an early hint of unusual abilities.
orange-orb-lands-near-an-open-minot-miss: James Fox, a documentary filmmaker, told a podcast host, Jesse Michels, about an incident at Minot Air Force Base in North Dakota, in 1966 or 1968, that he covered in his film The Phenomenon. He says that one morning a UFO, an orange glowing ball, came over the base and hovered near an open nuclear missile silo while a man screamed that it was landing. It is told as one more sign that UFOs take an interest in nuclear weapons.
orange-reddish-wobbling-ufos-around-area: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that since the 1980s and 1990s, orange-reddish UFOs have been flying around Area 51, a secret US military test site in the Nevada desert. orb-and-tall-glowing-figure-filmed-at-a-: Chris Bledsoe, a North Carolina man who says he has seen glowing balls of light called orbs for years, says that sometime between 2013 and 2015 he was filmed at his home during a healing for a cancer patient. orb-as-ancient-relic-compared-with-salva: Jordan Jose, who told podcast host Jesse Michels that he was taken into a UFO programme as a child, talks about an orb and the word "relic" that he says was used to describe it. orb-flies-figure-eights-over-the-capitol: Chris Bledsoe, a man who says glowing balls of light called orbs appear around him, says that in 2025, after a congressional hearing in Washington tied to Anna Paulina Luna and others, a group went up on a platform at the Library of Congress to watch the sky. orb-photo-showing-chris-s-lost-child: Chris Bledsoe, a North Carolina man who says he often sees glowing balls of light called orbs, says that he and his wife lost one of their children. orbs-appearing-inside-bledsoe-s-house-20: Chris Bledsoe, a North Carolina man, says that since 2007 glowing balls of light called orbs have appeared to him almost every day. orbs-rise-out-of-the-sea-for-danny-jones: Chris Bledsoe, a man who says glowing balls of light called orbs appear when he asks, says that in 2025 at Indian Rocks Beach in Florida he asked for one to show up for a man named Danny Jones. orbs-seen-during-sky-observing-at-bledso: Bob McGwier, described on Jesse Michels's podcast as a former CIA contractor, says he watched the sky at the North Carolina home of Chris Bledsoe, a man known for reports of glowing balls of light called orbs, with Ryan Bledsoe and Richard Dolan. orbs-seen-with-unmarked-black-helicopter: Skinwalker Ranch is a property in Utah known for reports of strange events. orbs-summoned-to-hover-over-jay-anderson: A man named Jay Anderson says that in recent years he went into a meditative state and asked for something to appear and float down over his house. origin-of-adjustment-team-philip-k-dick-: A researcher named Riz Virk says that Tessa Dick, wife of the science fiction writer Philip K. origins-of-the-us-remote-viewing-program: A former Army sergeant named Lyn Buchanan tells podcast host Jesse Michels how the US government's remote viewing programme began, remote viewing being the claimed ability to describe distant places or things using only the mind. orion-and-osiris-symbolism-in-the-apollo: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says the patch for Apollo, NASA's 1960s programme to send people to the Moon, hides an ancient symbol. orion-correlation-theory-1994: This story is about an idea called the Orion correlation theory, about the pyramids at Giza in Egypt. osap-at-skinwalker-ranch-and-the-hitchhi: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that a government study programme called OSAP ran from 2007 to 2012 with the backing of the politician Harry Reid. oscar-wolf-s-project-blue-book-special-u: Dan Sheehan, a lawyer, says a man named Oscar Wolf told him he worked directly with Project Blue Book, the US Air Force's UFO study of the 1950s and 60s. oscar-wolfe-deathbed-interview-about-s4-: Jeremy Corbell is a filmmaker who makes documentaries about UFOs. osireion-built-to-tap-the-water-table: The Osireion is an ancient stone structure at Abydos in Egypt. osiris-myth-as-preserving-antediluvian-k: Tim Alberino, a guest on podcast host Jesse Michels' show, reads the ancient Egyptian myth of the god Osiris, whose story links Egypt with Byblos, an old port city on the Phoenician coast, as a hidden record. osiris-shaft-water-samples-tested-with-t: A researcher named Jeffrey Drum says that sometime in the 2020s he took samples of the water in the Osiris Shaft, a deep water-filled shaft under the Giza plateau in Egypt, near the pyramids. oslo-peace-process-dinner-clinton-presse: Rolf Mowatt-Larssen, a former officer of the CIA, the US foreign intelligence agency, says he was at a dinner at the royal castle in Oslo, Norway, around 1998, held as part of the Middle East peace talks. osmium-and-cadmium-implants-in-the-m-typ: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, describes a set of small three-fingered bodies said to come from Nazca, Peru, and said to be more than a thousand years old. oss-project-mcgregor-moves-italian-ufo-t: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that near the end of World War Two, agents of the OSS, America's wartime spy agency, ran a secret effort called Project McGregor to go after advanced technology in northern Italy, including a crashed UFO that was rumored to be there. oswald-at-atsugi-u-2-base-1950: A researcher named Dan Sheehan tells podcast host Jesse Michels that Lee Harvey Oswald, the man accused of killing President Kennedy, worked in the 1950s at Atsugi, a base in Japan. oswald-could-not-have-fired-all-the-shot: In 1963 President John F. Kennedy was shot in Dallas, Texas, and a man named Lee Harvey Oswald was accused of the killing. oswald-infiltrates-free-cuba-group-and-i: A lawyer and researcher named Dan Sheehan, talking with a podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells a story about Lee Harvey Oswald, the man accused of shooting President John F. oswald-s-attempted-call-to-nags-head-196: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Lee Harvey Oswald, the man accused of shooting President John F. Kennedy in Dallas in 1963, tried to place a phone call to a place called Nags Head. oswald-s-fair-play-for-cuba-leaflets-car: Peter Levenda, an author who writes about secret history, told a podcast host, Jesse Michels, about leaflets handed out in New Orleans in 1963 by Lee Harvey Oswald, the man accused of killing President Kennedy. oswald-s-planned-role-and-the-killing-of: A lawyer named Dan Sheehan, speaking with podcast host Jesse Michels, passes on what he says he was told about the 1963 killing of President Kennedy in Dallas. oswald-trained-by-oni-part-of-private-fi: Dan Sheehan, a lawyer and researcher, tells a podcast host, Jesse Michels, that Lee Harvey Oswald, the man accused of shooting President Kennedy, was trained by the Office of Naval Intelligence, the US Navy's spy service, and not by the CIA, the country's main foreign spy agency. other-remote-viewing-teams-trained-by-pa: Remote viewing is the claimed ability to describe distant places or objects using only the mind, and the US government funded research into it from the 1970s to the 1990s. other-ufo-nuclear-witnesses: Robert Salas, a former US Air Force officer who says UFOs interfered with nuclear missiles, told a podcast host, Jesse Michels, that he is not the only witness to such events. otto-skorzeny-in-the-same-building-as-ru: A researcher who goes by JASON, speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast, points to a detail from Spain in the years after the Second World War. otto-skorzeny-s-ratline-used-knights-of-: Dan Sheehan, a lawyer, told a podcast host, Jesse Michels, about Otto Skorzeny, a Nazi commando officer who he says ran a "ratline", a secret escape route smuggling Nazis out of Europe after World War Two. otto-skorzeny-working-with-the-mossad-19: Otto Skorzeny was a commando officer in Nazi Germany during the Second World War. ouija-board-warning-of-an-aboriginal-upr: Peter Levenda, an author who writes about secret history, says that in the mid-1960s in New York, a Ouija board, a lettered board people use to try to receive messages from spirits, gave him and others a very specific warning of an uprising by Aboriginal Australians outside Perth. outer-limits-episode-premiered-before-th: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, cites American Cosmic, a book by the religion scholar Diana Pasulka, which discusses The Outer Limits, a CBS science fiction TV show. oval-office-briefing-on-zarqawi-camp-bef: Rolf Mowatt-Larssen, a former officer of the CIA, the US foreign intelligence agency, says that in 2003, before the US invaded Iraq, he briefed President George W. over-30-000-nuraghe-towers-on-sardinia: Nuraghe are ancient round stone towers found on Sardinia, an island in the Mediterranean. over-a-hundred-crash-retrieval-cases-in-: An online researcher who goes by UAPGerb told podcast host Jesse Michels to look at Majic Eyes Only, a book by researcher Ryan S. Wood. overseas-prospecting-for-psionic-assets: A former helicopter pilot named Jake Barber, who says he helped retrieve a UFO, states that there are operations outside the continental United States where people search for "psionic assets," meaning people said to have psychic abilities, and that such people are highly prized. overwhelming-evidence-of-subsidence-on-t: Randall Carlson, a researcher of ancient catastrophes, told a podcast host, Jesse Michels, that there is overwhelming evidence the floor of the Atlantic Ocean sank in a big way, mostly along the Mid-Atlantic Ridge, an underwater mountain chain running down the middle of the ocean. owens-168-demonstrations-over-20-years-1: Jeffrey Mishlove, a researcher of psychic phenomena, told a podcast host, Jesse Michels, about a man named Ted Owens, who said in advance that certain events would happen as demonstrations of his powers. owens-approaches-puthoff-and-targ-at-sri: Jeffrey Mishlove, a researcher of psychic phenomena, told a podcast host, Jesse Michels, about the 1970s, when two physicists, Hal Puthoff and Russell Targ, were testing the famous psychic performer Uri Geller at the Stanford Research Institute, a research lab in California. owens-brain-operated-on-beside-a-circle-: Jeffrey Mishlove, a researcher with a doctorate who studies psychic claims, told podcast host Jesse Michels a story he got from Ted Owens, a man who said he had psychic powers. owens-declares-war-on-the-us-government-: Jeffrey Mishlove, a researcher with a doctorate who studies psychic claims, told podcast host Jesse Michels that in the early 1980s Ted Owens, a man who said he had psychic powers, announced, "I'm declaring war against the United States government." owens-extorts-sports-team-owners-and-a-s: Jeffrey Mishlove, a researcher of psychic phenomena, tells a podcast host, Jesse Michels, about a man named Ted Owens, who claimed to have unusual powers. owens-predicts-end-of-california-drought: Jeffrey Mishlove, a researcher with a doctorate who studies psychic claims, told podcast host Jesse Michels that in 1976, while California was in a bad drought, Ted Owens, a man who said he had psychic powers, promised to end it within a couple of days. owens-space-intelligences-mantid-like-be: Jeffrey Mishlove, a researcher with a doctorate who studies psychic claims, told podcast host Jesse Michels what Ted Owens, a man who said he had psychic powers, claimed was the source of his abilities. owens-summons-lightning-near-the-camden-: Jeffrey Mishlove, a researcher of psychic phenomena, tells a story about Ted Owens, a man who claimed he could control weather and events with his mind, and who was the subject of a book called The PK Man (PK means psychokinesis, moving things with the mind). owens-takes-an-eagles-fullback-out-of-a-: Jeffrey Mishlove, a researcher of psychic phenomena, tells of Ted Owens, a man who claimed psychic powers, at a game played by the Philadelphia Eagles, an American football team. owens-three-ufo-sighting-experiment-arou: Jeffrey Mishlove, a researcher with a doctorate who studies psychic claims, says that in 1976 a man named Ted Owens announced he would create three UFO sightings within 90 days and within 100 miles of San Francisco, with San Diego used as a comparison area. owens-tries-to-sway-football-games-while: Jeffrey Mishlove, a researcher with a doctorate who studies psychic claims, told podcast host Jesse Michels about the habits of Ted Owens, a man who said he had psychic powers. owner-s-own-physical-impact-hitchhiker-e: The owner of Skinwalker Ranch, a Utah property known for reports of strange events, says on a podcast that whatever happens there has had a very real physical effect on people's lives, his own included. p3-operators-as-interfaces-to-et-vehicle: Steven Greer, a campaigner who says UFO secrets are held by a hidden global group, told podcast host Jesse Michels about something a man named Jake Barber described. pablo-amaringo-on-flying-saucers-as-spir: Graham Hancock, a writer on lost ancient civilizations, says that a Peruvian painter from the Amazon named Pablo Amaringo once told him, matter-of-factly, that the flying saucers in his paintings were "vehicles for entering and leaving the spirit world." pacaccini-says-he-saw-35-second-video-of: Vitorio Pacaccini, a UFO researcher in Brazil, says that around 1996 he saw a 35-second military video.
