pacaccini-shot-at-and-disappears-for-20-: James Fox, speaking on podcast host Jesse Michels' show about a 1996 case in Brazil where the army is said to have captured a live alien, talked about a man named Vitorio Pacaccini who had looked into it. pais-agrees-his-devices-facilitate-vacuu: Dave Rossi, a guest on a podcast who says aliens taught him advanced physics, says he raised an idea with Salvatore Pais, a Navy scientist known for patents on unusual craft and energy devices, and that Pais agreed with him. pais-inspired-by-steven-greer-documentar: Salvatore Pais, a US Navy scientist known for patents on unusual craft designs, says much of what inspired him came from the work of Steven Greer, a UFO researcher and filmmaker. pais-on-theory-of-everything-plasma-as-d: A man named Dave Rossi, talking with podcast host Jesse Michels, points to something an engineer named Salvatore Pais said on Theory of Everything, a podcast hosted by Curt Jaimungal. pais-patent-test-at-pax-river-had-no-def: A US congressman, Eric Burlison, says that around 2025 he learned about tests at Naval Air Station Patuxent River, a Navy air base in Maryland where aircraft are tested. pais-s-career-at-navy-programs-and-space: Salvatore Pais, a Navy scientist known for patents on unusual craft, says he was fortunate to work for Strategic Systems Programs, a Navy office at the Washington Navy Yard in Washington, D.C., and then went on to work for the Space Force, the US military branch for space. pais-stops-jesse-s-questions-in-motel-in: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says he once interviewed a scientist named Salvatore Pais in a motel near Pax River, a Navy base in Maryland, sometime in the 2020s. pais-told-ashton-forbes-that-the-mh370-o: Salvatore Pais, a Navy scientist who holds patents on unusual propulsion ideas, told podcast host Jesse Michels about videos said to show orbs around MH370, a passenger plane that went missing. pakistani-gunsmith-who-hammers-out-aks-f: Joe McMoneagle, a former army psychic spy who says he used remote viewing, a claimed ability to describe faraway places with the mind alone, told podcast host Jesse Michels a story he had heard. palermo-stone-shows-pre-dynastic-egyptia: A researcher named Geoffrey Drumm, who studies the Egyptian pyramids, told podcast host Jesse Michels about the Palermo Stone, an ancient carved slab that lists early Egyptian rulers. Drumm says he believes the stone shows Egyptian civilization going back long before the age of the pharaohs. If so, Egypt's history would be far older than usually told.
palomar-transients-missing-in-earth-s-sh: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, talks about the VASCO project, studies of old sky photographs taken at Palomar Observatory in California between 1949 and 1957, and a researcher he names as Beatrice Valale. The studies found brief points of light, called transients, in those photos, and the story says they go missing in the part of the sky inside Earth's shadow, where sunlight cannot reach. If true, it would suggest the lights were sunlight bouncing off real objects high above Earth.
pamela-fails-her-trust-test-while-about-: Charles Hall, who says he spent three years in the 1960s working alongside tall white aliens at a Nevada air base, tells of one night in Indian Springs Valley, on the ranges near an ammunition bunker. He says a being he calls Pamela failed a test of trust that night while about 70 small scout craft watched. He tells it as part of his account of living close to these beings and learning how they behave.
pan-starrs-discovers-oumuamua-2017: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in 2017 a telescope in Hawaii called Pan-STARRS found a fast-moving object travelling through space, which was named Oumuamua. He tells it while introducing a Harvard scientist, Avi Loeb, as a starting point for the question of whether an object passing through from the space between the stars could be something more than a natural rock.
pandolfi-email-senators-let-him-carry-th: A UFO researcher named Grant Cameron told podcast host Jesse Michels about an email he says he has from Ron Pandolfi, a man Cameron describes as a senior figure in the government's handling of UFOs. According to Cameron, Pandolfi wrote that senators and congressmen keep asking about the material, not realising the real issue is who can get access to it, that asking can get you in trouble, and that the senators simply let him carry the keys. If true, it would mean one insider quietly controls who reaches the secrets.
pandolfi-going-to-los-alamos-to-talk-to-: A UFO researcher named Grant Cameron told podcast host Jesse Michels a story about Ron Pandolfi, a man Cameron describes as a senior figure in the government's handling of UFOs. Cameron says that around 1991, at a meeting that also involved Dan Smith and John Alexander, Pandolfi said he was going that week to Los Alamos, a government science lab in New Mexico, to talk to a live alien. If true, it would mean the government held a living being from elsewhere.
pandolfi-s-teenage-metallurgical-analysi: A UFO researcher named Grant Cameron told podcast host Jesse Michels a story about Ron Pandolfi, a man Cameron describes as a senior figure in the government's handling of UFOs. According to Cameron, when Pandolfi was a teenager his father, who was involved with a secret ship called the Glomar Explorer, gave him a piece of metal from that work to analyse. Cameron tells it as an early sign of Pandolfi's ties to hidden government projects.
pandolfi-s-uncle-a-founding-member-of-th: Jason Simosa, a researcher, told podcast host Jesse Michels that when someone tried to get certain UFO information, the request was shut down by a man he calls Dr. Pandolfi. Simosa adds that Pandolfi's uncle, Louis Pandolfi, was a founding member of the OSS, the American wartime spy service that came before the CIA. He tells it to suggest the secrecy runs in families with deep ties to intelligence work.
pandolfi-steers-clinton-toward-a-maccabe: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in the 1990s Ron Pandolfi, a man at the CIA (America's foreign intelligence agency), told President Bill Clinton he should get a briefing from Bruce Maccabee. Maccabee, Michels explains, had written a book about UFOs and the FBI, America's federal police agency. If true, it would mean a sitting president was being pointed toward someone who studied UFOs.
panelists-claiming-trade-agreements-with: An author, Peter Levenda, says that he once sat on a conference panel with people who insisted that humans already have trade agreements with other planets. According to Levenda, they claimed goods were being traded back and forth. He tells it as an example of the claims he has heard first-hand, which would mean open contact with other worlds if true.
pantex-diamond-shaped-ufo-in-2015: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says a release of government records he connects to something called the PURSUE act describes a diamond-shaped UFO in 2015 at Pantex, the facility in Texas where the US assembles its nuclear weapons. If true, it would mean an unknown craft was seen over one of the country's most sensitive nuclear sites.
paper-great-pyramid-concentrates-electri: A researcher named Geoffrey Drumm, who studies the Egyptian pyramids, told podcast host Jesse Michels about a scientific paper that came out a while back. He says it described how the Great Pyramid of Giza can store and concentrate electric fields right around the King's Chamber, a room deep inside it. Drumm tells it because, if true, it would support his idea that the pyramid was built as a kind of machine.
paper-on-the-moon-s-effect-on-lightning: A researcher named Geoffrey Drumm, who studies the Egyptian pyramids, showed podcast host Jesse Michels a scientific paper called "The moon effect on lightning." He uses it to suggest that the moon has an influence on lightning, which he connects to his ideas about how the pyramids worked.
paper-on-why-ufos-appear-near-nuclear-si: Lyn Buchanan, a former US Army sergeant, talks about the idea that UFOs tend to appear near nuclear sites such as Chernobyl, the Soviet nuclear plant. He says he has written a paper on it, and that if his idea is right, their appearances there have nothing to do with the usual explanation, but rather with disturbances in space and time.
paperclip-and-the-gehlen-network-as-a-ho: After the Second World War, the US brought German scientists to America in a programme called Paperclip, and took over a German spy network run by an intelligence officer named Reinhard Gehlen. A researcher named Jason Jorjani tells podcast host Jesse Michels that both were really a "homecoming", and that it is almost as if Nazi Germany had been set up as a field laboratory to do highly unethical things. If true, it would mean the Nazi research was tied to American interests from the start.
paperclip-scientists-confirm-german-ufo-: Robert Salas, a former US Air Force officer, told podcast host Jesse Michels that in the 1960s some of the Paperclip scientists, Germans brought to America after the Second World War under a government programme of that name, confirmed to astronauts that Nazi Germany had worked on UFOs. He says this came out during weekend meetings between the scientists and some of the astronauts. If true, it would mean UFO research reached back to the war and was quietly known inside the space programme.
paperclip-scientists-in-new-mexico-mail-: Peter Levenda, an author who writes about secret history, tells a podcast host, Jesse Michels, about Operation Paperclip, the US programme that brought German scientists to America after the Second World War. He says that in the late 1940s scientists living in New Mexico would go into the local towns and mail letters back to Germany, and a courier then carried those letters to colleagues being held in the Soviet Union. If true, it would mean secrets were quietly passing between the two rival powers.
paperclip-scientists-split-between-redst: Matthew Brown, described as a former Pentagon insider, tells a podcast host, Jesse Michels, how the German scientists brought to America after 1945 were divided up. He says those who were Nazis in name only settled around Redstone Arsenal, an Army base in Huntsville, Alabama, while the true believers went to Los Alamos, the weapons laboratory in New Mexico. Brown links this split to later contact with non-human beings, which would mean committed Nazis were close to the most secret work.
paperclip-scientists-work-on-the-magenta: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that after World War Two, many top Nazi scientists were brought out of Germany by the Allies under Operation Paperclip, a program that put German scientists to work for the United States. He says some of them went to Wright-Patterson Air Force Base in Ohio to work on what he calls the Magenta craft, a UFO said to have crashed in Italy. If true, it would mean captured German experts helped study a crashed craft.
papoose-lake-map-altered-eight-days-afte: Luigi Vendetelli, a researcher, told podcast host Jesse Michels that government geological maps of Papoose Lake and Groom Lake, dry lake beds in the Nevada desert on secret military land, were changed in 1989. He says the change is stamped May 23rd, 1989, exactly eight days after Bob Lazar, a man who went public with claims about secret work at the site, first spoke out. If true, it would suggest the government moved quickly to hide the place Lazar described.
paralysis-a-shimmering-object-golden-sym: Deep Prasad is a researcher who appears on the podcast of host Jesse Michels. He says that one night he suddenly could no longer move. He noticed a shimmering object and moved his eyes left and right, hoping it would go away. When he looked back, it had fully appeared, with beautiful golden symbols dancing at its center. As soon as it touched him, he says, he got a true download, a sudden rush of knowledge. In other tellings on the same episode, he places it in 2019 in a 30th-floor apartment in Toronto. There he describes a visor that turned out to belong to a whole face, suit and helmet, and says that when the beings were unmasked they looked like the Peruvian mummies, small mummified bodies from Peru that some say are not human. If true, it would mean beings visited him and passed knowledge straight into his mind. All the tellings are his own, and they differ on whether he saw golden symbols or a being in a suit.
paranormal-activity-in-towns-after-nucle: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in the New Mexico towns near the first nuclear explosions, starting in 1945, people reported devils chasing them and all sorts of other strange, ghostly happenings. He raises it while talking with the UFO researcher Jacques Vallee, as a hint that nuclear blasts and strange phenomena may be linked.
parapsychology-master-s-program-at-john-: A psychologist and interviewer, Jeffrey Mishlove, says that around 1980 he taught at John F. Kennedy University in California, back when it offered a master's degree in parapsychology, the study of claimed psychic abilities. He mentions it to show that the field was once taught as a serious university subject.
parapsychology-programs-at-elite-us-univ: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that several top American universities once ran research programmes in parapsychology, the study of claimed mind abilities such as telepathy and sensing the future. He names a research centre linked to Duke University, a lab at Princeton, and work at a research institute tied to Stanford. In a later episode he adds that these programmes came out saying the present moment seems to be 'constricted', which he raises as a hint that the mind may reach beyond the here and now.
parents-see-a-hooded-being-in-their-bedr: A man named Jim Weiner, who tells of his own strange experiences, told podcast host Jesse Michels that in the 1950s, near Allentown, Pennsylvania, his parents saw a hooded being in their bedroom one night. He says he never knew about it until Ray Fowler, a UFO investigator, interviewed his mother. If true, it would mean such visits ran in his family before his own.
parsons-and-hubbard-s-babylon-working-19: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells of the Babylon Working, a magic ritual that Jack Parsons, a Pasadena rocket scientist, and L. Ron Hubbard, the man who later founded Scientology, are said to have performed in Pasadena in 1946. According to Michels, they were trying to summon a divine feminine figure called Babylon, following ideas from Aleister Crowley, an English occultist, and his novel Moonchild. He tells it because it would tie the birth of American rocketry to the occult.
parsons-crater-and-jack-parsons-laborato: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, talks about Jack Parsons, an early American rocket pioneer. Michels says a crater on the Moon now carries Parsons' name, and that some insiders at JPL, a NASA rocket and space laboratory in Pasadena, California, still jokingly call it the Jack Parsons Laboratory. He tells it to show how central Parsons is said to be to the lab's story.
parsons-death-in-a-home-lab-explosion-19: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Jack Parsons, an early American rocket pioneer, died in 1952 in an explosion in his home laboratory in Pasadena, California. According to Michels, it was officially ruled an accident with volatile chemicals, but some people found the circumstances suspicious, which would mean his death may not have been as simple as the record says.
parsons-invokes-bartzabel-against-hubbar: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells a story from 1946 about Jack Parsons, an early American rocket pioneer who also practised ritual magic, and L. Ron Hubbard, later the founder of Scientology. Michels says that Parsons, furious with Hubbard, tried a magical counterattack in a Miami hotel room by calling on Bartzabel, which Michels describes as the spirit of Mars. He tells it to show how closely early rocketry and the occult were tangled together.
parsons-past-life-regression-as-simon-th: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Jack Parsons, an early American rocket scientist, underwent a past-life regression, a practice where someone is guided to "remember" lives they supposedly lived before. According to Michels, Parsons came to believe he had once been Simon the Sorcerer, a magician figure from early Christian times. He tells it to show the mystical side of a man tied to early rocketry.
part-of-a-program-shut-down-as-demonic-t: A physicist, Hal Puthoff, who has worked on government research into unusual phenomena, says that people inside the US government once shut down part of a research program. According to Puthoff, they argued that American taxpayer money should not be spent pursuing what they called demonic technology. He tells it in a debate with a podcast guest, Eric Weinstein, to show that religious belief has shaped how such research is handled.
parthian-feudal-houses-rule-iran-for-ove: The Parthians were an ancient ruling people of Iran. A researcher named Jason Jorjani tells podcast host Jesse Michels that they ruled Iran directly for 400 years, and the story as told holds that their noble family houses kept power there for more than a thousand years in all. He offers it as a sign of how long hidden lines of power can last.
party-crasher-jc-knows-the-unaired-dark-: Bryce Zabel is a television writer who co-created Dark Skies, a 1996 TV series about a secret government cover-up of aliens. On the podcast of host Jesse Michels, he says that in 1996 a man crashed a party at his house in Los Angeles. The man introduced himself as JC, congratulated him on the show, and said, "You guys got a lot right." According to Zabel, JC said he had seen the pilot, the show's first episode, which had not yet aired. His writing partner, Brent Friedman, tells the story too on the same episode, and adds more. Brent says JC claimed to be from the Office of Naval Intelligence, the US Navy's spy agency. He says JC offered a deal: they would get access to information, and in return help with a slow drip disclosure program, a gradual release of the truth to the public. If true, it would mean a military agency was trying to use a TV show to prepare the public.
parviz-jafari-s-1976-tehran-ufo-encounte: James Fox, a documentary filmmaker, says he met Parviz Jafari, an Iranian pilot who, he says, had a dramatic UFO encounter over Tehran in the mid-1970s while flying an F-4 Phantom fighter jet. Fox points to an assessment of the incident by the DIA, the US Defense Intelligence Agency, as backing for the account. If true, it is a military jet meeting an unknown object, with US intelligence taking note.
pascagoula-abduction-near-a-nuclear-sub-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in 1973 two men, Charles Hixon and Calvin Parker, claimed they were taken aboard a craft by aliens, examined and then released while they were fishing near Pascagoula, Mississippi. He points out that Pascagoula was where the Navy built nuclear submarines, which fits his idea that UFOs are drawn to nuclear sites. In other episodes he places the town in Missouri, dates it to 1974, and credits a researcher, Luigi Vendetelli, with the nuclear link.
passing-massive-body-rearranged-the-plan: On the show of a podcast host named Jesse Michels, a researcher named Joe McMoneagle says that long ago some big object passed through our solar system, and its gravity rearranged the planets and stripped Mars of its atmosphere. He gives no source for the idea. If true, it would mean Mars was once a very different world, one the episode suggests could have held life.
past-experimental-interbreeding-between-: Dan Sherman, a former US Air Force sergeant, says that in the early 1990s the NSA, the US agency that intercepts communications, hired him to communicate with aliens. He says that through this contact he got the impression that they had interbred with humans in the past, as an experiment. If true, it would mean aliens had a hand in human ancestry.
past-extraterrestrial-presence-on-the-mo: A guest named Max, speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast about the Moon, says that the best way to explain a growing pile of data is that beings from elsewhere were once present on the Moon and on Mars. He does not say when, only that it was in the past and perhaps across the solar system more broadly. If true, it would mean humans are not the first intelligence to have visited our neighbouring worlds.
pastor-apologizes-for-misattributing-the: A US congressman, Eric Burlison, says that around 2026 a group of pastors was told he believed that all such unexplained beings are demons. According to Burlison, one of the pastors later came out publicly, apologized, and said Burlison had never said this. He tells it to set the record straight about his own views.
pasulka-and-the-vatican-archives: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, mentions Diana Pasulka, a professor of religious studies, while listing people who might know more about UFOs. He says she has visited the Vatican archives, the Catholic Church's private records, and speaks with conviction that the Church knows more about UFOs than it lets on. If so, it would mean one of the world's oldest institutions is holding back knowledge on the subject.
pasulka-and-vallee-aliens-as-the-modern-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, points to two thinkers: Diana Pasulka, a professor of religious studies, and Jacques Vallee, a French researcher of UFOs. Michels says both believe that what people now call aliens are a modern version of what earlier ages called angels and demons, which would mean the same kind of presence has been with us all along under different names.
pasulka-finds-space-program-records-clas: Diana Pasulka, a professor who studies religion and belief in UFOs, says that when she began her study in 2012 she did the normal academic search for records about the space program. She says she immediately saw how much of it was classified, meaning kept secret by the government. She tells it as an early sign that her subject touched on hidden material.
pasulka-meets-garry-nolan-and-sees-his-i: A professor of religious studies, Diana Pasulka, says she met a scientist, Garry Nolan, early on, around 2014. According to Pasulka, Nolan shared his own research with her, work on injuries in people tied to unexplained encounters, and he had been recruited into this world of study just as she was being recruited. She tells it to show how a quiet circle of serious scientists was forming at the time.
pasulka-meets-tyler-and-begins-an-emerge: Diana Pasulka, a professor who studies religion and belief in UFOs, says that over the 2010s and up to 2023 she met a man she calls Tyler, who she says belongs to a secret tradition of people working on these matters inside closed circles. She says this led to a collaboration and an openness between the secret world and outsiders like her that had never been seen before. If true, it would mean insiders are starting to share what they know.
pasulka-s-encounters-source-daughter-of-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that one source in Encounters, a 2023 book by the religion professor Diana Pasulka, was the daughter of a man Pasulka believed worked in a secret space programme. According to the daughter, her father kept using the word "simulacra," meaning copies or imitations, at lunch with his colleagues, a detail Michels says gives him chills. If true, it would hint that insiders think our reality may be some kind of copy or simulation.
pasulka-s-research-on-historical-angelic: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Diana Pasulka, a religious studies professor at the University of North Carolina Wilmington, was researching a 2014 book on Purgatory called Heaven Can Wait when she began recording dozens of historical cases of nuns, priests, brothers and saints who reported direct contact with God or angels. In another episode he describes these accounts as resembling alien abductions and brings up Saint Francis of Assisi. He tells it because it would suggest modern UFO encounters echo much older religious experiences.
pat-price-remote-views-a-file-inside-a-c: Dan Sheehan, an American lawyer, tells of Pat Price, a man who took part in remote viewing, the claimed practice of seeing distant places with the mind alone. Sheehan says that in the 1970s Price used this to view a file kept inside a top security facility of the CIA, the US foreign intelligence agency, and he links the story to Russell Targ and Ingo Swann, two other figures in that work, and to reports Swann wrote. If true, it would mean the mind could reach past the tightest government security.
pat-price-remote-views-denied-soviet-sit: Joe McMoneagle, a former army psychic spy, told podcast host Jesse Michels about Pat Price, a fellow practitioner of remote viewing, the claimed ability to describe faraway places with the mind alone. McMoneagle says that in the early 1970s Price described closed-off Soviet sites accurately, down to machinery, a big tower and steel spheres. If true, it would mean the mind can spy on places no one is allowed to go.
pat-price-remote-views-underground-base-: Remote viewing is the idea that a trained person can use the mind alone to see faraway places, and the US government is said to have tested it for spying. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in 1973, in a remote viewing programme of the CIA (the US spy agency), a psychic spy named Pat Price described a huge underground base inside Mount Hayes in Alaska, with advanced technology, control consoles and staff who looked military. Price is said to have named three more: Mount Perdido in Spain, Mount Inyangani in Zimbabwe and Mount Ziel in Australia. Lyn Buchanan, a former Army sergeant who later joined the remote viewing unit, calls them alien bases and says the work, called Project 8200, happened before his time, while Michels elsewhere credits the programme to a man named Skip Atwater. If true, hidden bases sit inside mountains around the world.
pat-price-remotely-reads-a-file-inside-a: Pat Price was one of the people tested in the 1970s for remote viewing, the claimed ability to see distant places with the mind. A guest on Jesse Michels's podcast, Dan Sheehan, says Price became so good at it that he was given the exact map coordinates of a top-security CIA site. As Sheehan tells it, Price was able to read a file inside. He names the researchers Russell Targ and Ingo Swann as part of the story. If true, it would mean secrets behind locked doors could be read by the mind. Joseph McMoneagle, himself a remote viewer, tells it differently on the same show. In his version, passed on from others, Price was meant to describe an old cabin in the woods and instead described a hidden government site nearby.
pat-price-s-death-linked-to-psychokinesi: Jason Jorjani, a philosopher and researcher, told podcast host Jesse Michels his view on why Pat Price, a man who worked in psychic research in the 1970s, ended up dead. Jorjani thinks Price was recruited into a secret programme using psychokinesis, the claimed power to move or affect things with the mind, was given certain operations, and developed serious moral doubts about them. If true, it would mean the programme was willing to silence its own people.
patents-for-a-memory-erasing-neuralizer-: Chris Bledsoe, a man who says he attracts UFOs, told podcast host Jesse Michels that he learned about a technology that erases memories, nicknamed a "neuralizer" after the device in the movies. He says he has seen US patents for it. If true, it would mean such a tool exists on paper in official records.
path-of-souls-the-soul-s-leap-to-orion-a: A writer on ancient civilisations, Graham Hancock, told a podcast host, Jesse Michels, in 2024 about an old belief he calls the path of souls. In this belief, a dead person's soul leaps up to the star pattern Orion and then travels along the Milky Way, and Hancock says the idea is found in North, Central and South America, a theme he links to his television series Ancient Apocalypse. He tells it because a shared star map of the afterlife across distant peoples would suggest a common ancient source.
pathologist-attributes-infection-to-the-: A pathologist, a doctor who studies causes of illness and death, known as Dr. Armando, speaks about a case in Varginha, Brazil, in 1996. Looking at the autopsy report of a man named Marco Chereze, he says there was a very distinct and deliberate scratch on his skin, and he links the infection that followed to the claw of a strange being. If true, it would mean contact with a non-human creature could injure and infect a person.
patient-17-s-implant-cut-from-his-leg-an: A filmmaker, Jeremy Corbell, says that in the 2010s he watched an object being cut out of the leg of a man known as patient 17, one of the people who believe something was implanted in their bodies during encounters. According to Corbell, the man only told him his terrifying story afterward, and the object was tested for zinc-64, a particular form of zinc; he links the case to a surgeon who removed such objects, Roger Leir, and a researcher, Jacques Vallee. If true, it would mean physical objects of unknown origin are being found inside people.
patrick-afb-helicopter-flies-out-to-the-: A witness named Charles says that around 2013, off Cocoa Beach in Florida, he and others watched a strange light. According to Charles, they saw a helicopter from the nearby Patrick Air Force Base, a US Air Force base on that coast, fly out toward it. He tells it because it suggests the military saw the light too and went to check.
patrick-jackson-s-theory-of-spheres-as-a: Ross Coulthart, a journalist who reports on UFOs, told podcast host Jesse Michels about the idea of a man named Patrick Jackson. According to Coulthart, Jackson believes the mysterious spheres people report seeing in the sky are part of a worldwide defence system set up by an alien civilisation to keep bad actors away from Earth. If true, it would mean someone out there is guarding our planet.
patton-s-army-rushes-to-pilsen-before-be: A researcher who goes by JASON, speaking with a podcast host, Jesse Michels, points to the end of the Second World War in 1945. He says the army of General Patton, a leading American commander, raced to Pilsen, a city in Czechoslovakia, before heading for Berlin, which he finds very interesting. JASON suggests the rush means there was something at Pilsen the Americans badly wanted to reach first.
paul-eluard-s-mantis-collection-and-cail: A researcher named Jason Jorjani, speaking with a podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Paul Éluard, one of the founders of surrealism (an early 20th century art movement), kept an extraordinary collection of praying mantises in his home in France. He links this to a writer, Roger Caillois, who studied the folklore surrounding the mantis. Jorjani tells it to show how strongly this insect gripped the imagination of that circle of thinkers.
paul-feyerabend-s-astrology-chart-and-hi: Jeffrey Mishlove, a researcher of psychic phenomena, says that the philosopher of science Paul Feyerabend put an astrology chart on the back page of his 1970s book Against Method. According to Mishlove, Feyerabend also publicly scolded a group of scientists who had signed a statement against astrology. Mishlove tells it to show a respected thinker pushing back on how science dismisses such subjects.
paul-hellyer-briefed-by-greer-press-conf: Steven Greer, a campaigner for government openness about UFOs, says he was one of the reasons Paul Hellyer, a former Canadian minister of defence, began speaking publicly about the subject in the 2000s. Greer says he briefed Hellyer and that the two held a press conference together in Toronto, and he mentions The Day After Roswell, a book by Philip J. Corso. It matters because it would mean a senior former official was persuaded to speak out.
paul-hellyer-dying-canadian-emergency-ma: A researcher, Grant Cameron, told the podcast host Jesse Michels a story he credits to a man named Paul Hellyer, about a dying man who had headed emergency management in Canada. According to the story, this man said he was taken to Langley, Virginia, home of the CIA, the US spy agency, where he "signed my life away," and was then flown to Area 51, a secret US military base in Nevada, where he sat inside a craft. If true, it would mean the US holds a flying craft that someone from Canada's government was allowed to see.
paul-mccartney-s-flaming-pie-dream-and-t: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, mentions in passing that he thinks Paul McCartney, one of the Beatles, once had a dream about a flaming pie, a story tied to how the band got its name in 1960s England. He raises it as an example of strange visions shaping real events.
paul-mellon-brought-back-a-nazi-flying-d: A UFO activist, Steven Greer, says that a man named John Warner IV heard Paul Mellon, a very rich American, admit to going over at the end of World War Two and bringing back a flying disc built by the Nazis. The podcast host Jesse Michels tells it with more detail: over his third martini, Mellon said he and Allen Dulles, an American spy chief, were on a mission to recover technology, and that he stood on top of a saucer in Pilsen, in Czechoslovakia, not Germany. If true, it would mean flying-disc technology reached America from the Nazis in 1945.
paul-mellon-s-family-and-support-for-fas: On the podcast of a host named Jesse Michels, a guest named Steven Greer, who talks about hidden UFO secrets, passes on what a man he names told him about a figure called Paul Mellon and his family in the United States, roughly from the 1930s to 1945. According to Greer, this man said Mellon was a huge supporter of Adolf Hitler and fascism, and so were the carmaker Henry Ford and Watson of the computing company IBM. Greer tells it to suggest that powerful American families have a long history of hidden loyalties.
paul-mellon-s-walking-stick: A former presidential advisor named Harold Malmgren, speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast about the UFO material he says he handled, mentions a walking stick in Virginia. Malmgren says he was told it belonged to a man named Paul Mellon. He does not say much more, but it comes up as one of the objects and links in his account.
paul-muller-confiscates-and-destroys-val: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells a story from the early 1960s about Jacques Vallee, then a young worker at a French observatory who later became a well-known UFO researcher. According to Michels, Vallee had recorded tracking data of something in the sky on tape, and his boss, Paul Muller, whom Michels says acted like a petty army officer, took the tape the next morning and destroyed it. If true, it would mean early evidence of unknown objects was thrown away by the scientists themselves.
paul-s-ascent-to-the-third-heaven: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says some scholars believe the Apostle Paul, an early Christian leader, may have known about ancient practices of rising up through the heavens. Michels points out that Paul describes his own ascent to "the third heaven" in Second Corinthians, one of his letters in the Bible. photos-of-kirkpatrick-meeting-with-brand: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, discussing the Pentagon's work on UFOs, says there are pictures of a man named Sean Kirkpatrick in a meeting with another man, Brandon Fugal. photos-of-tim-taylor-at-bledsoe-children: A guest who goes by the online name UAPGerb asks on Jesse Michels' podcast whether there aren't photos of a man named Tim Taylor at the football games of the children of Chris Bledsoe, a man who has spoken publicly about UFO encounters. He raises it as a question, hinting that Taylor may have been quietly keeping an eye on Bledsoe's family.
phyllis-schlemmer-channels-the-nine-eart: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, describes a woman named Phyllis Schlemmer, who wrote a book called The Only Planet of Choice. phyllis-schlemmer-says-puharich-used-the: On a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, an unnamed researcher passes on what a woman named Phyllis Schlemmer said about the 1970s, when she worked with a man named Andrija Puharich. According to the researcher, Schlemmer said Puharich used a device called the TD 100 machine on her all the time, and that she never knew what it did and never asked. physicist-friend-sees-boulder-pushed-int: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says he visited the Roswell site in New Mexico, where many people believe a craft crashed in 1947. He says he saw a boulder that had clearly been pushed into what was probably a young tree back then. He offers it as a physical trace that, if he is right, would suggest something struck the ground there with force.
pictures-mailed-to-sagan-never-arrived-1: John Brandenburg, a scientist, says that sometime in the 1980s he mailed some pictures to Carl Sagan, the famous astronomer at Cornell University. He says that when he later asked Sagan what he thought of them, Sagan told him, "I never got them," which Brandenburg presents as a sign that someone was intercepting what he sent.
pills-handed-out-during-intuitive-commun: Dan Sherman, a former sergeant, says the NSA, the US spy agency that intercepts communications, hired him to talk to aliens. He says that in the early 1990s he trained in "intuitive communication," meaning receiving messages with his mind, at an unnamed site near the NSA's headquarters in Maryland. He says an officer he calls Captain White told him he would also be given some pills to take as part of the training.
pilot-compatibility-with-different-class: A man who goes only by Jordan says a secret UFO program took him as a child, around 2008 to 2010, at a place in New York called Baker Victory Services. He says the program was testing which craft each person could work with. UAP is the government's term for unidentified anomalous phenomena, or UFOs. In his words, "I might work very well with object A but I can't work with object B or C," which would mean these craft somehow match up with particular pilots.
pilot-photo-of-arv-over-provo-1960: A researcher who goes by the name UAPGerb says that an artist, Mark McCandlish, has a photo taken in the 1960s by a pilot whose first name was Harvey. According to UAPGerb, the photo was taken over Provo, Utah, near Dugway Proving Ground, a military testing site, and it shows an ARV, short for "alien reproduction vehicle", a craft said to be built by humans copying alien technology. If true, it would suggest such craft were flying over Utah decades ago.
pilot-vouches-for-marzulli-s-source-usin: A filmmaker, Tim Alberino, tells of a source who came forward to an author named L.A. Marzulli some time after 2005, and of a pilot who checked that source's story. According to Alberino, the pilot had kept certain details of his own account secret so he could test anyone who later claimed to know more, and the pilot said this man was telling the truth. Alberino tells it because it would mean the source's claims were confirmed by someone who knew details only a real witness would know.
pilot-who-flew-the-gold-out-is-still-ali: Dan Sheehan, a lawyer and researcher, says on Jesse Michels' podcast that the commander and pilot who flew a load of gold out at the end of the Second World War, around 1945, is still alive. piloting-uap-orbs-by-moving-consciousnes: A man who goes only by Jordan says a secret UFO program took him as a child, around 2008 to 2010, at a place in New York called Baker Victory Services. He says that in a lab there he was asked to fly glowing orbs and other unexplained objects by moving his mind into them. If true, it would mean these craft are steered by thought, not by controls.
pilots-mistaking-u-2-and-sr-71-for-ufos-: Michael Shermer, a well-known skeptic, argues on Jesse Michels' podcast that in the 1950s and 60s airline pilots flying at 35,000 feet saw things streaking above them at two or three times their height and several times their speed and called them UFOs. He says they were really seeing the U-2 and the SR-71 Blackbird, secret American spy planes that flew very high and very fast, which the pilots could not have known about. In his telling, this explains many sightings of that era without anything unearthly.
pilots-report-uaps-emerging-from-the-dip: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that a former Navy pilot named Ryan Graves, whom he calls careful about his claims, has said that pilots reported UAPs, meaning unidentified anomalous phenomena or unexplained objects, coming out of something called the Dipper. According to Michels, the pilots also described these objects dogfighting near it in orbit, in the 2010s. If true, it would mean unknown craft were active high above the Earth and seen by military pilots.
pilots-seeing-uap-at-lemoore-fallon-and-: A former Navy fighter pilot, Ryan Graves, says that pilots are seeing UAP, meaning unexplained objects in the sky, not just off the coasts of Virginia and California but also further inland. He names Lemoore and Fallon, which he describes as big Navy training ranges, and Pax River, where the Navy trains its test pilots, saying they are having incidents there too. If true, it would mean these objects are showing up across many military training areas, not just one place.
pines-judges-barber-credible-as-a-delive: In 2025, on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, a commentator named Matthew Pines spoke about a man named Jake Barber. Barber describes having worked in a crash retrieval program, a secret effort said to recover crashed craft that are not of human making. Pines says he finds Barber extremely credible and truthful, but sees him as essentially a delivery man, a helicopter pilot who knows what he saw without knowing the whole picture. If Pines is right, Barber's account would be a real first-hand glimpse of such a program, though only from the edges.
pines-speculates-the-psionic-programs-us: Matthew Pines, a researcher who writes about national security, guesses on Jesse Michels' podcast how secret government programs might train people in psionics, meaning abilities of the mind such as sensing things at a distance. He imagines they find people who are naturally gifted, maybe from certain family lines, give them mixes of drugs as part of training when they are young, and then bring them into the programs. If true, it would mean governments are deliberately growing mind powers in people.
pioneer-mission-tenth-planet-covered-up-: Podcast host Jesse Michels passes on a claim from a man named Matt LaCroix about the Pioneer missions, space probes sent out to the far edge of the solar system. According to Michels, LaCroix says that in the 1990s the probes found a tenth planet beyond the Kuiper Belt, the band of icy bodies past the known planets, four to five times larger than Earth, and that its presence was covered up. If true, it would mean a major discovery about our own solar system was hidden from the public.
piri-reis-map-showing-antarctica: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, drawing on the writer Graham Hancock, points to the Piri Reis map, a map dated 1513, and to a similar one called the Oronteus Finaeus map. Michels says the Piri Reis map seems to show parts of Antarctica as tropical, near the top of the map. The story is told because, if true, it would mean someone mapped Antarctica long before anyone is thought to have seen it, when it was not covered in ice.
pla-rocket-force-purges-and-a-possible-h: Matthew Pines, a researcher who writes about national security, notes on Jesse Michels' podcast that in recent years China's leader Xi Jinping has removed many officers from the Rocket Force, the branch of China's military that runs its missiles. Pines raises the idea that these purges might be connected to a hidden Chinese program, which would mean China has its own secret effort of the kind the podcast discusses.
pla-s-ufo-report-tracking-system: A historian and researcher named Richard Dolan, speaking with a podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that the People's Liberation Army, the Chinese military, is very sophisticated at tracking UFO reports. He gives no source. If true, it would mean China takes the subject seriously as a military matter.
plains-of-san-agustin-saucer-crash-with-: This story says that in 1947 a flying saucer crashed on the Plains of San Agustin, a wide, flat stretch of New Mexico. According to the story's title, dead aliens and one live alien were found. A researcher named John Brandenburg tells it on a podcast. He says that around the morning of the 4th of July an object came down on the plains about 100 miles away. A second man, Charles Hall, who says he spent three years among tall white aliens at Area 51, a secret US military site in Nevada, mentions the same crash. Hall describes it as a craft in deep trouble over the plains in 1947. He does not talk about any dead or living beings. If true, it would mean an alien craft fell to Earth and was found in the American desert.
plan-for-oswald-to-fire-a-deliberate-mis: Dan Sheehan, a lawyer and researcher, says on Jesse Michels' podcast that the plan in Dallas in 1963 was to coax Lee Harvey Oswald, the man accused of killing President Kennedy, into firing at the president's motorcade on purpose without hitting anyone. According to Sheehan, the shot was meant to be blamed on Cuba, which would have given a reason to move against that country, and he ties the story to J. D. Tippit, a Dallas police officer killed that same day.
plan-to-move-the-program-to-kwajalein-so: Bob Lazar, who says he worked in the late 1980s at S4, a secret site in the Nevada desert where he says alien craft were studied, says the people running the programme told him they would have liked to move it to the South Pacific, maybe to Kwajalein Island. According to Lazar, they said the cost would have been so great that it was impossible, a detail that, if true, shows how seriously they guarded the work.
planck-joked-planck-length-would-be-best: David Grusch, a witness in the debate over government UFO secrets, said on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels that the German physicist Max Planck had an idea about aliens. According to Grusch, after Planck worked out the Planck length, the shortest length that makes sense in physics, he thought it would be the best way to communicate with aliens, since it is a measure any advanced mind would share. Grusch tells it to suggest that physics itself might be a common language with other intelligences.
plane-carrying-maury-island-slag-explode: Peter Levenda, an author who writes about secret history, tells on Jesse Michels' podcast part of a 1947 story from Maury Island in Washington State, where men including one named Fred Crisman said they had pieces of slag, a rocky metal leftover, from a strange craft. Levenda says two military officers came to collect the material, and on the flight back to their base their plane exploded in midair, killing them. In the story, this makes the debris seem dangerous or worth hiding.
planned-double-blind-dna-test-of-the-per: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in 2025 a man named Michael Mazzola, connected to a documentary called This Is Not a Hoax, was arranging DNA tests on strange bodies from Peru that some people present as possibly non-human. Michels says the tests would be run with independent aerospace contractors and done "double blind," meaning the testers would not know which sample was which, so that no one could cheat.
planned-film-tests-of-telepathy-and-of-c: A documentary maker named Ky Dickens, who made a film series called The Telepathy Tapes about children said to read minds, says that from 2025 she planned filmed tests with a researcher, Diane Powell. According to Dickens, the plan was to put two or three non-speaking people in different places and have them talk to each other through "the Hill", which she describes as a shared meeting place in the mind. If it worked as she hopes, it would suggest that people can communicate by thought alone.
planned-live-demo-at-electrostatic-socie: Charles Buer, a scientist presented on Jesse Michels's podcast as a former NASA figure who claims to have built an antigravity drive, says he planned a live demonstration of it at a conference of the Electrostatic Society of America, a group of scientists who study static electricity. He says his lab is in Cocoa Beach, Florida, and that he will show the device working in public, which would matter because it would put the claim in front of other experts.
planned-move-to-a-boarding-facility-in-e: A man who gives only the name Jordan says that as a child he was taken into a secret government UFO program. He says that around 2010 he was told he would move to a facility in eastern New York and live there full-time. If true, it would mean a hidden program was gathering and housing children.
planned-public-uap-summoning-demonstrati: Jake Barber, a helicopter pilot who says he helped carry a recovered UFO, told the podcast host Jesse Michels in early 2025 that his group hoped to stage a public demonstration within the first half of that year. The idea was to call in UAP, short for unidentified anomalous phenomena, the official term for UFOs, in front of witnesses, which would be striking proof if it worked. Michels later said, looking back in 2026, that Barber apparently did not land another egg, his word for the egg-shaped craft, as he had predicted.
planned-wrightsville-beach-skywatch-broa: Chris Bledsoe, a man who says UFOs appear around him and that NASA has studied him, describes a plan for 2025. He says about 40 people would gather on the beach at Wrightsville Beach, North Carolina, to watch the sky together, and that the event would be broadcast through a group he calls the World Forum. plaque-at-hospital-regional-marking-the-: James Fox, a filmmaker who studies UFOs, told podcast host Jesse Michels about Hospital Regional in Varginha, a town in Brazil where people say strange beings were seen and captured in 1996. plasma-balls-turning-into-solid-objects-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that people who claim to have worked in a secret government effort, which he calls the UFO legacy program, describe balls of glowing plasma that seem to pull together, go still and turn into solid objects. plasma-compression-fusion-device-paper-c: Salvatore Pais, a US Navy scientist with patents on unusual craft designs, says one of his papers, on a plasma compression fusion device, a machine meant to make energy by squeezing superhot gas until atoms fuse, is being cited by important research teams in China. plasma-orbs-seen-around-the-nasa-space-s: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, raises the plasma orbs, glowing balls of light, that he says people in and around NASA's space shuttle have described during the shuttle years of 1981 to 2011. He asks about them as a puzzle worth explaining, since it would mean something unknown was seen in Earth orbit.
plato-s-atlantis-date-matches-the-end-of: This story is about Atlantis, the lost island civilisation described by the ancient Greek philosopher Plato in two of his dialogues, the Timaeus and the Critias. plato-s-atlantis-located-in-antarctica: Jason Jorjani, a researcher on Jesse Michels' podcast, talks about Atlantis, the lost island civilisation described by the ancient Greek philosopher Plato in his works Timaeus and Critias. Jorjani says Plato's "world ocean" is the place where the Pacific, Atlantic and Indian oceans meet, off the coast of Antarctica, and so places Atlantis there, about 9600 BC. plato-s-cave-someone-outside-the-cave-pu: In The Republic, the ancient Greek philosopher Plato has his teacher Socrates describe prisoners in a cave who see only shadows on a wall until one is freed and led out into the light. plato-s-myth-of-er: Plato, the ancient Greek philosopher, tells a story in his book The Republic called the Myth of Er. A guest named James Madden tells it a little differently. He says Er was a virtuous man who died fighting for his city, and he doesn't call it a near-death experience. Both are drawing on Plato's text directly, on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels. Why they bring it up: if it is a real account, people have been describing journeys beyond death for thousands of years.
plato-took-ergot-at-eleusis: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that the ancient Greek philosopher Plato went to Eleusis, a Greek site of secret religious rites, and was tripping on ergot, a fungus that grows on grain and can cause visions. plutarch-names-sonchis-priest-at-sais: This story is about Atlantis, the legendary lost island first described by the ancient Greek writer Plato. He says Sonchis was the source of the Atlantis story told to Solon, a Greek statesman who visited Egypt, and that the story passed from Solon down to Plato. He raises it more than once in the same podcast episode, the second time more firmly. It matters to him because a named priest would give the Atlantis tale a real person at its root.
podcast-with-doty-where-mario-confronts-: Mario Woods, an Air Force veteran who says he and fellow airmen were taken by aliens decades ago, says he later went on a podcast with Richard Doty, a man who has told his own version of what happened to Woods. podesta-emails-and-the-delongemccaslandw: A researcher named Jason Simosa, speaking on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, describes emails of a Washington political figure, John Podesta, that were hacked and made public around 2015 and 2016. podesta-emails-hillary-clinton-s-seven-y: A researcher, Grant Cameron, describes the Podesta emails, private emails of John Podesta, a political adviser to Hillary Clinton, that later became public. podesta-staffer-mentions-the-ufo-project: A researcher named Jason Simosa, on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, points to the hacked emails of a Washington political figure, John Podesta, from around 2015. According to Simosa, one staffer wrote to Podesta suggesting a certain person be considered for "the UFO project." If true, it would mean a project about UFOs was being discussed inside a political circle in Washington.
podkletnov-rumored-to-work-for-an-americ: A Navy scientist, Salvatore Pais, who holds patents on unusual technology, says he was once told that a researcher named Eugene Podkletnov was working for an American contractor, meaning a private company that does work for the government. podkletnov-s-father-a-soviet-agent-retri: Podcast host Jesse Michels passes on a story linked to journalist Nick Cook and his book The Hunt for Zero Point. According to Michels, a scientist named Eugene Podkletnov said his father was a Soviet counterintelligence agent who, in the 1940s, was sent to collect many of the files of Viktor Schauberger, an inventor working in Germany. Told this way, Schauberger's work would have ended up in Soviet hands.
podkletnov-s-father-retrieved-schauberge: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells a story about a scientist named Eugene Podkletnov. If true, it would mean Podkletnov's own work came partly from Schauberger's ideas, passed down through Soviet hands.
podkletnov-s-gravity-shielding-and-a-sch: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells of a researcher named Eugene Podkletnov at the University of Tampere in Finland who, in the 1990s, claimed that objects weighed less when placed above spinning superconductors, materials that carry electricity with no resistance. If true, it would mean people have found a way to partly block gravity.
podkletnov-s-impulse-gravitational-gener: A Navy scientist named Salvatore Pais, who holds patents on unusual propulsion ideas, tells a podcast host, Jesse Michels, about a Russian scientist named Eugene Podkletnov. Pais says that if it is true Podkletnov has built an "impulse gravitational generator," a device said to fire off a pulse of gravity-like force, then Podkletnov may already have hit on something real, which would point toward new ways to move through space.
point-dume-alien-base-erased-from-maps: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, mentions in passing an alien base said to be at Point Dume, a headland in Malibu, California. He says it was erased, apparently meaning from maps, though he gives no further details. He brings it up as an example of a place said to have been hidden from view.
point-mugu-missile-base-near-oxnard: A guest named Steve, on an episode of the podcast host Jesse Michels's show about a scientist who studies objects said to be alien implants in human bodies, mentions a military base near Oxnard, California. He says this base, Point Mugu, a missile site, was very important at one time, and he brings it up as a landmark near the area his story concerns.
police-explain-the-attacks-as-river-mine: A filmmaker, Tim Alberino, talks about attacks on villagers in San Antonio de Pintoyaku, a village in Peru, in 2023, which some people linked to strange beings. Passing on what a woman named Talia told him, Alberino says the police concluded the villagers were being attacked by river miners using jetpacks. He tells it because the official explanation itself sounds strange, which leaves open what was really going on.
polish-magical-working-animating-a-golem: A writer named Whitley Strieber says on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels that at a party in New York in the 1970s, a woman told him she had done a magical working, a ritual, in Poland in the 1930s.
