If true, it would mean ritual magic had a hand in the events leading into the Second World War.
polished-marble-found-at-the-crash-site-: Some people say a flying saucer crashed in Hart Canyon, near the town of Aztec, New Mexico, in 1948. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in 1999 a couple who searched the site, Scott and Suzanne Ramsay, found what looked like a small polished marble that seemed out of place there. If true, it would be a physical leftover from the crash.
polygraph-question-about-loyalty-to-a-no: A commentator named Matthew Pines, on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, says he was told that around 2020 to 2022, people being screened for the UAP Task Force, a Pentagon group looking into unidentified objects in the sky, faced an unusual lie-detector question. According to what Pines was told, one or two questions were added asking whether the person had any undisclosed relationships with, or loyalty to, any non-human faction. If true, it would mean officials took seriously the idea that people might be in contact with non-human beings.
polygraph-with-flashing-images-and-air-h: Dylan Borland, a man who says a top government official told him aliens run everything, describes being given a lie detector test sometime in the 2010s or 2020s. He says he was hooked to the machine while a computer flashed images at him and air horns went off. He tells it as part of how he was treated after coming forward, which, if true, would mean people with UFO stories are tested and pressured in unusual ways.
polymeropoulos-feels-betrayed-by-the-cia: Eric Hazeline, talking on Jesse Michels's podcast, repeats something said by Marc Polymeropoulos, a man who appeared on 60 Minutes, an American TV news programme, in a segment about Havana syndrome, a set of unexplained illnesses reported among US officials. Hazeline says Polymeropoulos put it well: he loves the CIA, America's foreign spy agency, but feels it betrayed him. As told, it suggests the agency failed its own people.
pompeo-i-saw-the-ufo-files-too: This story is about a strange remark by Mike Pompeo, a former head of the CIA, the main US spy agency. The podcast host Jesse Michels says that when Pompeo was asked why thousands of government files about the killing of President John F. Kennedy still had not been released, he changed the subject in an odd way. According to the telling, Pompeo said he had also seen the UFO files. A journalist, Michael Shellenberger, tells the same story on the same podcast. He says the interviewer was a TV host known as Judge Napolitano, and that Pompeo first said the Kennedy files could not be released because some of the people involved are still alive. Then, Shellenberger says, Pompeo added that he had seen the UAP files as well, UAP being the government's newer word for UFOs. It is told because, if taken at face value, it suggests a former spy chief has seen secret UFO records.
pons-and-fleischmann-cold-fusion-rumor-1: Stanley Pons and Martin Fleischmann are two scientists whose names are tied to cold fusion, the idea of getting nuclear energy at room temperature. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, mentions a rumor that someone did have a real cold fusion breakthrough in the 1990s or 2000s, in the spirit of their work. If true, it would mean a huge energy discovery was made and kept quiet.
pope-francis-message-and-vatican-paintin: Chris Bledsoe, a man who says he has had many encounters with UFOs and glowing orbs, tells of a message he says came to him through Diana Pasulka, an academic. According to Bledsoe, she told him that Pope Francis wanted him to know that the Vatican, the headquarters of the Catholic Church, knows these beings are angels, a story he connects to Vatican paintings showing orbs with angels. If true, it would mean the Church sees these encounters as religious rather than alien.
pope-john-paul-ii-we-are-not-alone-1994: Kiran Ilum Xenov, described as a president of a Russian republic who says he was taken by aliens in 1997, says he met Pope John Paul II, then head of the Catholic Church, at the Vatican in 1994. He says the Pope conveyed that "we are not alone," and that he only understood what that meant later. If true, it would mean the Church's leader hinted at life beyond Earth.
pope-john-xxiii-to-broker-the-warhead-de: A man named Dan Sheehan says on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels that in 1963 the United States and the Soviet Union were working toward taking apart and destroying their nuclear warheads. According to Sheehan, the Soviet leader Nikita Khrushchev proposed that Pope John XXIII, head of the Catholic Church, broker the whole deal so each side could check the other was keeping its word. If true, it would mean the two superpowers came close to a secret disarmament pact run through the Vatican.
pope-pius-xii-informs-allies-of-the-craf: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that around the 1930s and 1940s a crashed craft, which he calls the Magenta crash, was held in Italy, possibly by the Vatican, perhaps at the Soratte bunker outside Rome. According to Michels, Pope Pius XII, head of the Catholic Church at the time, quietly passed word of the craft and where it was stored to the Allies, in one telling to US President Franklin D. Roosevelt. If true, it would mean the Church knew of a recovered craft before the famous American cases.
porch-insight-the-big-bang-as-a-ripple-i: Rolf Mowatt-Larssen, a former CIA chief who says he is a time traveler, describes sitting on his screened porch and picturing the Big Bang, the birth of the universe, for the first time. He says it came to him as a ripple inside a larger universe at rest, drawing on thinkers like Thomas Aquinas, Leibniz and Einstein, and that this could explain where the Virgin Mary came from. To him it ties science and faith together in one picture.
portage-county-police-chase: A guest named Merrick says on Jesse Michels' podcast that police officers in Portage County, Ohio, chased a large, metal, disc-shaped object for 90 minutes over 86 miles. He offers it as a case where trained law officers followed something they could not explain for a long time.
portal-or-wormhole-theory-for-the-ranch-: Brandon Fugal, the owner of Skinwalker Ranch, a property in Utah known for reports of strange happenings, talks about an idea put forward by a scientist he calls Dr. Taylor and others. According to Fugal, they speculate that there may be a portal or a wormhole, a kind of shortcut through space, on the ranch. If true, it would explain the odd events people report there as things coming and going from somewhere else.
portland-police-see-nine-discs-1947: A researcher named Merrick, debating on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, points to raw reports from Project Sign, the US Air Force's first study of UFOs in the late 1940s. According to those reports as he describes them, in July 1947 in Portland, Oregon, five police officers saw a total of nine discs flying in different directions. He cites it as a case of several trained witnesses seeing the same thing at once.
poseidon-temple-on-little-st-james-and-a: Jason Jorjani, a philosopher, says, relaying a commentator known as Dark Journalist, that a temple on a property called Little St. James was built to Poseidon, the Greek sea god, as a patron deity. He adds that on another property, Zorro Ranch, where he says a breeding programme took place, the owner built a labyrinth laid out like the plan of Atlantis, the lost island Plato describes in his ancient dialogues Timaeus and Critias, which Jorjani takes as a sign of hidden beliefs at work.
possible-mixing-of-us-secret-technology-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, wonders aloud about a widely read 2017 New York Times article on UFOs and the US government. He asks whether part of what came out in that article was really secret American technology mixed in with the UFO material, which would mean some of what looked unexplained was actually made by the US.
post-assassination-letters-telling-ruth-: An author named Peter Levenda, on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, describes letters written after President Kennedy was shot in 1963 between Ruth Forbes Paine Young, wife of a man named Arthur Young, and her daughter-in-law Ruth Paine, who knew Lee Harvey Oswald, the man accused of the killing. Levenda says the older woman was telling Ruth Paine, in effect, to keep quiet about Oswald. If true, it would suggest people close to Oswald were being steered on what to say.
post-malone-s-security-detail-sees-a-spe: Brandon Fugal, the owner of Skinwalker Ranch, a property in Utah known for reports of strange happenings, says the well-known musician Post Malone once visited with a heavily armed security team. According to Fugal, the security team saw a ghostly figure dart through a ranch building called Homestead 2 and up through the roof. He tells it because even tough, trained guards say they saw something they could not explain.
post-war-nazi-network-die-spinne-in-the-: A writer and researcher named Jason Jorjani, talking with podcast host Jesse Michels, says that after the Second World War there was an international network of former Nazis, which some people call Die Spinne, German for "the spider", and that it reached into the Arab world. He says he builds on the work of another researcher, Joseph Farrell, and sets it out in his book. If true, it would mean Nazi remnants kept organising across borders long after the war ended.
postwar-secrecy-shaped-by-war-of-the-wor: This is an idea about why the US government kept UFOs secret after the Second World War. In 1938 the actor Orson Welles broadcast War of the Worlds, a radio drama about an invasion from space. Kirk McConnell, who worked as a staff member in the US Senate, says that in the late 1940s the country was barely ten years past that broadcast. John Harrington, speaking in an official role, puts it more bluntly: Welles broadcast War of the Worlds and the country went nuts. The point both make is that officials may have feared a similar panic if they admitted something real was in the skies, so they chose secrecy.
potassium-chloride-suicide-plan-2008: Gary McKinnon, a British computer hacker who says he broke into NASA systems and found signs of a secret space program, describes a dark time in the UK around 2008. He says he bought potassium chloride, one of the chemicals used in lethal injections, planning to end his life. He tells it to show how heavy the consequences of his hacking were for him.
ppd-shut-down-and-possibly-reborn-as-oth: Dan Sherman, a former Air Force sergeant who says the NSA, the US spy agency that intercepts communications, hired him to talk with aliens by thought, says the secret program he worked in, known as PPD, was shut down in the early 1990s. He says he is pretty sure it ended, though he suggests its work may have carried on under other programs, mentioning a man named Scott Andrews. If true, contact work would have continued under new names.
prayer-breakfasts-and-doug-coe: A researcher and author, Peter Levenda, says that a powerful group in Washington, DC held prayer breakfasts where its members would meet and talk, and he links this to a man named Doug Coe. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, adds that Coe was one of the leaders of this group, which he calls the Family, in the 1980s. Michels says Coe hosted a prayer breakfast that every US president had to attend. It is told to suggest a quiet religious network with access to the very top of government.
prayer-to-reach-rock-musicians-answered-: Chris Bledsoe, a man who says UFOs appear around him and that NASA has studied him, says he prayed to reach rock musicians such as Sammy Hagar, Kirk Hammett, Robert Plant and Fred Durst. He says the prayer was answered: on his birthday last year he got a phone call from Sammy Hagar's wife. He tells it as a sign that his prayers are heard and acted on.
pre-adamic-cosmic-war-wipes-out-the-civi: Tim Alberino, a guest on Jesse Michels' podcast, describes a war in the cosmos that he says happened in pre-Adamic times, meaning before Adam, the first man in the Bible. He says that in this conflict a civilisation living on Mars was wiped out, drawing on the writer David Flynn and works named Cydonia and Birthright. If true, Mars once held life that was destroyed.
pre-dynastic-maadi-lion-cult-around-the-: A researcher named Luke Caverns, speaking with a podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that an early people known as the Maadi culture lived around Giza in Egypt before the first kings, perhaps 5,000 to 7,000 years before Christ. Drawing on the work of Robert Schoch, he says he has always thought the Sphinx, the giant lion-bodied statue at Giza, could have been their god. If true, the Sphinx would be far older than the pharaohs.
pre-war-ig-farbenstandard-oil-monopoly-a: A guest who goes by the name JASON says on Jesse Michels' podcast that in the 1930s, before the Second World War, the big German chemical company IG Farben and the American oil company Standard Oil, owned by the Rockefeller family, agreed to give each other monopolies, each staying out of the other's field. He mentions the Schroeder banking family in the same breath, and tells it as a sign that powerful business circles on both sides were tied together.
preacher-solon-brown-sees-beings-in-the-: Some people say a flying saucer crashed in Hart Canyon, near Aztec, New Mexico, around March 25, 1948. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that a preacher named Solon Brown was there, and years later said he saw a few beings, maybe three, slumped over a kind of table or panel inside the craft. If true, it would be an eyewitness account of dead crew from a crashed craft.
precognitive-dream-of-the-focus-magazine: Jeffrey Mishlove, a researcher of psychic phenomena, says that in 1972, while living in married student housing in Berkeley, California, he dreamed of a magazine lying on his living room floor. He says that afterwards he found a magazine there in the middle of the floor, just as he had dreamt, called Focus, put out by KQED, a local public broadcaster. If true, it would be a dream that showed the future.
predecessor-killed-when-a-running-reacto: Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked on alien craft at a secret site in the Nevada desert in the late 1980s, tells podcast host Jesse Michels what he says he was told about the man who had his job before him. According to Lazar, that man was killed when a team took one of the craft's power reactors to the Nevada Test Site, the government's nuclear testing ground, and cut into it while it was running under load, and it exploded. If true, it would show how dangerous and poorly understood that technology was to the people handling it.
predicted-extraction-shaft-beneath-the-r: A researcher named Geoffrey Drumm, on the podcast of a host named Jesse Michels, says he has a theory of the true purpose of the pyramids, one he says came to him from an alien. He predicts there should be an extraction shaft running down from below what he calls the final synthesis chamber of the Red Pyramid, an ancient pyramid at Dahshur in Egypt. If true, it would suggest the pyramid was a place where something was made and then drawn out.
predicted-hidden-anticamera-linking-the-: A researcher named Filippo, speaking on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels in 2026, describes a hidden small room, an "anticamera" or antechamber, that he predicts lies inside the Great Pyramid of Giza in Egypt. He says this room connects a corridor on the pyramid's north side to the Grand Gallery, the pyramid's tall sloping inner passage, and to the Big Void, a large empty space found inside the pyramid by earlier scans. In his words, "that chamber goes directly to the Grand Gallery," which, if true, would mean the pyramid's known spaces are linked by rooms no one has yet entered.
predicted-ufo-hovers-over-puharich-famil: A researcher named Greg, speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast, passes on an account from the family of Andy Puharich, a scientist the episode links to contact with an alien council. Greg says that at a family gathering in North Carolina in the late 1980s, a UFO had been predicted in advance, and Puharich's son and two or three cousins all saw a huge thing hover silently over them. He mentions a family video connected to the event, and if true, it would mean the sighting was foretold.
predicting-three-orange-orbs-at-9-45-at-: Chris Bledsoe, a man who says UFOs appear around him and that NASA has studied him, describes a 2025 night at Contact in the Desert, a UFO gathering near Palm Springs, California. He says he told the whole group in advance that at 9:45 three orange balls of light would appear under the clouds. He tells it because, if it happened as he says, it would mean he can predict or call these lights.
premonition-dream-of-friends-2-a-m-arres: Randall Carlson, a researcher of ancient history and catastrophes, says that when he was 18 or 19 he was home asleep while his best friend from high school and the friend's older brother were out. He says he had an intense dream that they were in trouble and got busted, and that they were in fact arrested around 2 a.m., which he tells as a sign that the mind can sense things at a distance.
premonition-of-the-dc-metro-red-line-fir: Lou Elizondo, a well-known figure in the push for UFO disclosure, says he had a premonition linked to a count of days that he connects with the physicist Hal Puthoff. He says that on the 89th day there was a fatal fire on the red line of the Washington, DC metro, which he tells as a sign that such foresight can be real.
preparata-and-del-giudice-worked-with-fl: Filippo Biondi, a researcher who scans beneath the Egyptian pyramids, told podcast host Jesse Michels that two Italian physicists from the University of Milan, Giuliano Preparata and Emilio Del Giudice, worked alongside Martin Fleischmann and Stanley Pons. Fleischmann and Pons are the two chemists linked to cold fusion, the idea of getting nuclear energy from a tabletop experiment at room temperature. Biondi brings it up to place his own scientific roots in that line of work.
presidency-cut-out-of-the-loop-under-eis: On the podcast of host Jesse Michels, a researcher named Steven Greer says that in the 1950s, while Dwight Eisenhower was US president, the presidency was "decapitated": cut out of the loop on UFO secrets, with no source named for this. In a second telling he adds that Richard Nixon, then Eisenhower's vice president and, as Greer puts it, chairman of the space council, was part of the team that betrayed Eisenhower. If true, it would mean that since then the people holding these secrets have answered to no elected leader.
president-of-kalmykia-abducted-by-aliens: Podcast host Jesse Michels, speaking with fellow podcaster Joe Rogan, says he once interviewed the president of Kalmykia, a Buddhist republic inside Russia near Dagestan. According to Michels, the man says he was abducted by aliens in the 1990s while he was the sitting president. If true, it would mean the leader of a whole region claimed a direct encounter while in office.
presidential-advisor-held-ufo-material-f: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says he interviewed Harold Malmgren, a top advisor to US presidents, near the end of his life. According to Michels, Malmgren said he held pieces of a UFO that came down after a high-altitude nuclear test in the Marshall Islands, Pacific islands where the US tested bombs; Michels places it in late 1963 in one telling and names the 1962 test called Bluegill Triple Prime in others, crediting a man named Lawrence Preston Gise. If true, it would mean a senior official handled material from an unknown craft.
presidential-ufo-briefings-nixon-to-bush: A researcher named Jason Simosa, speaking with podcast host Jesse Michels, says that US presidents from 1969 to 1993, Nixon, Carter, Reagan and the first Bush, all seem to have been given private briefings about UFOs. He says it is pretty clear that Bill Clinton, who came next, was not, which if true would mean the briefings stopped at some point and presidents were left outside.
presidents-look-into-ufos-and-find-nothi: On the podcast of host Jesse Michels, in a debate where he takes the skeptic's side, a researcher named Michael Shurmer says that every new president, Clinton, Obama and Trump among them, arrives promising to find out what is going on with UFOs. His point, as he tells it, is that they look and come away with nothing, which he takes to mean there may be no hidden secret to find.
presidents-not-told-unless-like-bush-41-: David Grusch, a former US intelligence officer who has gone public with claims about hidden UFO programmes, tells podcast host Jesse Michels that American presidents are probably not told about these secrets. He says the exception would be someone like George H.W. Bush, the 41st president, who had earlier been director of the CIA, the country's foreign intelligence agency. If true, it would mean the secret is kept even from the elected head of government.
presocratic-cave-rituals: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that ancient Greeks before the time of Socrates practised rituals in caves, citing a writer named Peter Kingsley. In one telling Michels describes them as sensory deprivation rituals older even than the Eleusinian mysteries, the famous secret rites of ancient Greece, and also credits the philosopher Martin Heidegger. He brings them up as an old route to strange inner experiences.
price-and-mcmoneagle-find-aliens-and-hum: Lyn Buchanan, a former Army sergeant who served in a military unit of "remote viewers", people trained to try to see distant places using only the mind, tells podcast host Jesse Michels what he heard about work done before he joined. He says two of the unit's viewers, Pat Price and Joe McMoneagle, had found aliens and humans working side by side inside Mount Hayes in Alaska, at what seemed to be an intelligence gathering post. If true, it would mean aliens and people were secretly cooperating on American soil.
priest-tells-vallee-to-burn-an-ibm-circu: Jacques Vallee, a French-born UFO researcher and computer scientist, says that in France, sometime in the 1950s or 60s, a priest was shown an IBM circuit card, a piece of early computer hardware. According to Vallee, the priest looked at it and said, "My son, burn it, it is from the Devil," a story he tells about how new and strange technology can frighten people.
primakov-proposes-that-the-svr-keep-araf: A former senior officer of the CIA, the US foreign intelligence agency, named Rolf Mowatt-Larssen, recalls a meeting in Moscow around 1993 with a senior Russian official, Yevgeny Primakov. According to Mowatt-Larssen, Primakov proposed a deal: the SVR, Russia's foreign intelligence service, would work to keep Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat alive, while the CIA would work to keep Israeli prime minister Yitzhak Rabin alive. If true, it shows the two rival spy services quietly cooperating to protect the Middle East peace effort.
prince-hans-adam-expects-jesus-on-a-flyi: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Hans-Adam, the reigning prince of Liechtenstein, a small country in Europe, believes Jesus will arrive on a flying saucer. Michels mentions it as part of a wider talk about secret groups and a coming final event.
prince-hans-adam-gathered-the-roswell-wi: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Hans-Adam, the prince of Liechtenstein, a small European country, once brought together all the witnesses to the Roswell event, the 1947 New Mexico case many believe was a crashed craft. In one telling Michels says he heard this from a man he interviewed, John Brandenburg, and places it around the 1970s or 1980s; in another he links it to a writer, Whitley Strieber, and gives no date. If true, it would show a European royal taking a private, serious interest in the case.
prince-hans-adam-of-liechtenstein-s-lett: Hans-Adam II is the prince who rules Liechtenstein, a small country in Europe. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says the prince wrote a thoughtful letter back to a man named Max who had written to him, a story tied to the physicist Hal Puthoff, in which the prince said that proof about UFOs always slipped through his fingers. If true, it would mean even a head of state looked for answers and could not get them.
princeton-anomalies-research-lab: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, mentions a research lab at Princeton University in New Jersey that studied anomalies, meaning strange things science cannot easily explain. He brings it up as an example of serious places that looked into such questions.
princeton-parapsychology-lab-studied-uri: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in the 1970s a lab at Princeton that studied psychic powers looked at Uri Geller, a man famous for claiming he could bend spoons with his mind. According to Michels, Geller was brought there by Andrija Puharich, a researcher of the paranormal. If true, it would mean a top university took claimed psychic powers seriously enough to test them.
princeton-pear-lab-and-the-global-consci: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, talks about a Princeton University lab tied to a scientist named Bob Jahn and a related effort that ran machines making random numbers around the world, to see if human feelings could affect them. Michels says the machines showed their biggest spike ever on September 11, 2001, the day of the terror attacks, and another when Jahn died. If true, it would suggest that human minds together can touch the physical world.
princeton-pear-lab-random-event-generato: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says a close friend and mentor of his worked at a lab at Princeton University, which he calls the PEAR lab, that studied all sorts of unexplained things. There, according to Michels, his mentor ran experiments with machines that produce random results, and described something he called the rebound effect. Michels mentions it as a sign that the mind might affect such machines in odd ways.
princeton-random-event-generators-affect: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, passes on something an unnamed friend told him about a lab at Princeton University in New Jersey that studied the mind's possible effect on machines. The lab used random event generators, devices that churn out random results like an electronic coin toss, and his friend says it is an open secret in that field that the more "heart-centered" a person is, the more they can nudge the machine's output. If true, it would mean feelings, not just thoughts, can reach out and change the physical world.
princeton-studies-of-geller: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that a man named Geller was studied at Princeton, the university in New Jersey, and that there are papers written about those studies. He mentions a friend at the Princeton lab that studied psychic abilities, and he raises it as a sign that serious scientists took Geller's claimed powers seriously enough to test them.
priscilla-mcmillan-revealed-as-cia-asset: A researcher named Jeremy Riss, on a Jesse Michels podcast episode about UFOs and the killing of President Kennedy, says that Priscilla McMillan, a writer who interviewed Lee Harvey Oswald, the man accused of shooting Kennedy, when he went to Russia, and who later befriended his wife Marina and wrote her life story, was a willing asset of the CIA, the US foreign intelligence agency. He ties this to the government's released Kennedy assassination files. If true, it would mean the CIA was closer to Oswald and his family than it let on.
private-contractor-and-jsoc-team-exchang: A story goes around about two teams who showed up at the same crash site and fought over it. A podcast host named Jack, speaking on an episode of Jesse Michels' show, says a private military contractor working for the defense company Lockheed Martin was sent to recover a crashed craft. He says a team from JSOC, the US military's Joint Special Operations Command, which runs elite special forces units, was sent to the same site. Michels himself repeats it later as a rumor of a firefight between a Lockheed retrieval team and a JSOC retrieval team. He dates it to 2004 and places it at Coyame, in Mexico. He ties it to a man named Jake Barber and a project called Sentinels of Ether. They tell it because, if true, rival government and private groups are competing, even with gunfire, to recover crashed craft.
private-jsoc-veteran-team-behind-herrera: A researcher known online as UAPGerb told podcast host Jesse Michels that two men, Michael Herrera and Jake Barber, each of whom has described dealing with recoveries of unknown craft, seem to have been dealing with the same private team. He suggests the team is made up of veterans of JSOC, the US military command that runs its most elite special forces units, and that it has been active since around 2009. If true, it would mean such recoveries are carried out by a private outfit rather than an ordinary government unit.
private-lab-effects-verified-by-others: Dave Rossi, a man who says aliens taught him advanced physics, says he has seen things in private laboratories that are undeniable. He says other people working in those facilities verified them too, not just him. If true, it would mean the physics he describes produces real, checkable effects.
private-sector-companies-with-wet-works-: Eric Burlison, a US congressman, tells podcast host Jesse Michels that the people who have come to him with UFO claims, including former intelligence officer David Grusch and a man named Jake Barber, all warn about the same thing. He says they claim certain private companies tied to the secret have bad actors who will carry out "kinetic activity", meaning physical violence, sometimes called wet works. If true, it would mean those who speak out could be in real danger.
prodigy-spotted-at-age-12-or-13-and-recr: A researcher named Matthew Pines, talking with podcast host Jesse Michels, tells of a gifted young man he calls Harold Mgrren, who he says was spotted at about 12 or 13 years old and recruited by the president of MIT, the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, a leading American science university. Pines offers it as an example of how very bright young people are found early and brought into science, which if true would point to a quiet system for picking talent for sensitive work.
professor-s-friends-at-malmstrom-ufos-di: Kevin Knuth, a scientist and former NASA researcher, tells podcast host Jesse Michels about something a professor told him in 1988. According to Knuth, the professor said he had friends at Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana, a base that runs nuclear missiles, who had problems with UFOs flying over the missile sites and disabling the missiles. If true, it would mean unknown craft could switch off nuclear weapons.
program-reported-by-shellenberger-that-u: A commentator, Matthew Pines, speaking in 2024, refers to a secret programme that the journalist Michael Shellenberger wrote about and might testify to Congress about. Pines says the programme apparently uses artificial intelligence to identify UAP, short for unidentified anomalous phenomena, the official term for UFOs, and maybe even ARVs, a term for human-built craft said to be copied from non-human ones. If true, it would mean the government is quietly running a hidden system to track these objects.
program-traced-to-dachau-vanished-childr: Whitley Strieber, speaking as a researcher on the podcast of host Jesse Michels, says he believes a secret programme had its roots in the 1940s in Dachau and the other Nazi prison camps of the Second World War, a story the episode ties to children who vanished in the gas chambers. "I think it started in the camps," he says, which if true would mean the programme began with the Nazis' crimes.
programs-call-psionic-operators-pink-ass: Michael Herrera, a man who says he saw a huge UFO in the Indonesian jungle, says a man named Jake Barber told him something about secret long-running programs said to deal with non-human craft. According to Herrera, some of these programs use the nickname "pink assets" for psionic operators, people said to use the power of their minds on their work. If true, it would mean hidden programs have their own code words for people with psychic abilities.
programs-for-summoning-ufos-such-as-skyw: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says there are efforts to summon UFOs, naming a modern one called Skywatchers. He says it seems the US government has been doing this kind of thing for a while inside special access programs, which are highly restricted secret projects. If true, it would mean contact with these craft has been sought on purpose and kept hidden.
project-a119-to-set-off-a-nuclear-blast-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says the astronomer Carl Sagan was a secret consultant on Project A119, a top-secret US Air Force plan run out of Kirtland Air Force Base to set off a nuclear bomb on the Moon. In later episodes Michels dates it to 1958 and says the point was a show of force against the Soviet Union. He tells it because, as he sees it, it puts a famous public scientist inside a hidden military project.
project-aquarius-document-said-to-be-rea: Eric Davis, a scientist who has worked with the Pentagon, told Jesse Michels's podcast that he has seen the Aquarius document, a paper said to describe a secret US government UFO project from around 1977. People have said for years that two men, Bill Moore and Rick Doty, made it up. Davis says a man named Alonzo McDonald told him the document is real and those two had nothing to do with it, which would mean the secret project was real too.
project-atom-in-serpo-matches-ttsa-s-ato: A researcher, Deep Prasad, points to Project Serpo, a set of leaked papers that claim the US swapped people with an alien planet, and its mention of something called Project Atom. He describes Project Atom as a secret program at Los Alamos, the US nuclear laboratory in New Mexico, that studies the radiation of materials taken from alien spacecraft, and he links it to a project of the same name in the mid-2010s at To The Stars Academy, a private UFO research company tied to Tom DeLonge and a physicist named Hal Puthoff. If the match holds, it would suggest the leaked papers and the later company drew on the same hidden source.
project-blue-beam-conspiracy-theory: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, brings up an idea called Project Blue Beam while interviewing Jake Barber, a man who says he helped retrieve a UFO with his helicopter. Michels himself calls it a conspiracy theory, but in the episode he gives no details about what it claims.
project-blue-book-and-the-condon-study-1: Project Blue Book was the US Air Force's UFO study of the 1950s and 60s. Near its end, the Air Force paid the University of Colorado for an outside study, led by a physicist named Edward Condon who had worked on the Manhattan Project, the wartime effort to build the atomic bomb. A guest named Karl Nell, citing the record, says Condon wrote the study's conclusion before the study was finished and bragged about it. If so, it would mean the official verdict on UFOs was decided ahead of time. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells it in nearly the same words on his own, leaving out the bragging. So it reaches listeners both from a guest and from the host himself.
project-blue-book-and-the-pentagon-repor: Eric Weinstein, a researcher debating on Jesse Michels's podcast, compares two government records: Project Blue Book, the US Air Force's UFO study of the 1950s and 60s, and a 2021 Pentagon report on unidentified objects in the sky. He says the two do not seem to fit together. In his view, either the government was lying back then when it said there was nothing to see, or it is telling the truth now, and it cannot be both.
project-galileo-briefing-and-its-two-dir: Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked around 1988 and 1989 at S-4, a secret site in the Nevada desert where he says alien craft were studied, describes the briefing papers he read there. He says one project, called Galileo, dealt with how the craft were propelled, and another briefing was called Looking Glass; if true, it would mean the US government held and studied non-human craft.
project-orion-nuclear-propulsion-1950: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, describes Project Orion, a US plan in the 1950s and 60s to push spacecraft using nuclear power. He says Air Force general Curtis LeMay wanted it and the physicist Freeman Dyson worked on it, but President John F. Kennedy was strongly against it, so it was dropped. He tells it as an example of bold space ideas that were stopped.
project-pandora-and-soviet-radio-frequen: A researcher called Greg, speaking with podcast host Jesse Michels, mentions Project Pandora, a US government project he says started in the 1960s and which the story links to Soviet weapons that used radio waves. He gives it as background to other secret research of that time, which if true would mean both sides of the Cold War were testing radio signals as weapons.
project-preserve-destiny-code-name-staun: A former Army sergeant named Dan Sherman says that around 1991, at a training site in Maryland run by the National Security Agency (the NSA, the US government's code-breaking and communications spy agency), he was part of a project called Preserve Destiny. On a podcast with host Jesse Michels, he gives its code name as Staunch 118. If true, it would mean the government ran a secret named programme he says he was hired into, one he links to speaking with aliens.
project-preserve-destiny-mother-abducted: Podcast host Jesse Michels relays the story of Dan Sherman, author of a book called Above Black. As Michels tells it, Sherman was told in the 1990s that he was part of something called Project Preserve Destiny, and that while his mother was pregnant with him she was abducted by aliens and the baby was genetically altered. If true, a secret programme would have been working with alien changes to people from before birth.
project-serpo-book-built-on-puthoff-s-sp: A researcher, Deep Prasad, says that when he read the Project Serpo book around 2019 or 2020, one thing stood out. The book, based on papers leaked from 2005 onward that claim the US swapped people with an alien planet, fully weaves in the ideas of a physicist named Hal Puthoff about "spacetime metric engineering," the notion of reshaping space and time itself to travel. To Prasad, that overlap would mean the story is tied to serious physics thinking rather than standing alone.
project-serpo-exchange-program-1947: An unnamed researcher on Jesse Michels' podcast describes Project Serpo, which he calls an alien exchange programme. purple-lady-seen-on-first-dmt-trip: A comedian named Kurt Metzger tells podcast host Jesse Michels that the first time he took DMT, a powerful psychedelic drug, he saw a figure he calls the Purple Lady. He raises it in a conversation about other beings and hidden powers. To him, it suggests such drugs can open contact with something beyond ordinary experience.
pursue-file-law-enforcement-officers-rep: A retired US Navy admiral, Tim Gallaudet, told podcast host Jesse Michels about a report he says is in a set of government records called the PURSUE files. According to Gallaudet, the report describes law enforcement agents at a national security site somewhere in the western US who had many encounters with glowing orbs, including one big "mother ship" of orbs that launched smaller orbs from itself. If true, it would mean strange objects are showing up at sensitive US sites and the government has written it down.
push-for-the-uap-disclosure-act-in-the-n: A US congressman named Eric Burlison says that between 2023 and 2025 he took part in a push to add wording from the UAP Disclosure Act into the National Defense Authorization Act, the big yearly law that sets the US military's budget and rules. UAP stands for unidentified anomalous phenomena, the government's term for UFOs, and the Disclosure Act was a bill meant to force the release of government records about them. He names fellow members of Congress Tim Burchett and Anna Paulina Luna as part of the effort, which, if it worked, would put legal pressure on the government to reveal what it knows.
puthoff-and-davis-describe-how-the-legac: A researcher who appeared as a guest on Jesse Michels's podcast passes on what two physicists, Hal Puthoff and Eric Davis, told them about the "legacy program", a claimed hidden, long-running US effort to study UFOs. According to the guest, Puthoff and Davis said the way in is to first apply to one of the major aerospace companies said to be part of that program. If true, that would make private defence firms the front door to a secret project.
puthoff-and-davis-never-shown-aaro-notes: Kirk McConnell, a former US Senate staffer, says that two physicists, Hal Puthoff and Eric Davis, met with AARO, the Pentagon office set up in 2022 to look into UFO reports. According to McConnell, to this day neither man has been shown the notes the office took of those meetings. If true, it would mean the office's record of what they said cannot be checked by the people who said it.
puthoff-and-green-introduce-owner-to-big: The owner of Skinwalker Ranch, a Utah property famous for reports of strange events, tells podcast host Jesse Michels that around 2016 two men, Hal Puthoff and Kit Green, reached out to him. He says they offered him the chance to meet Robert Bigelow, and that he is thankful they trusted him. It is part of his story of how he came to the ranch and its claimed secrets.
puthoff-floats-a-joint-space-program-202: An online researcher who goes by UAPGerb says he asked a physicist, Hal Puthoff, whether a hidden space effort belonged to "them," a non-human intelligence, or to us. He says Puthoff answered by asking, "what if it's a joint space program?" If true, it would mean humans and non-humans are working on space together in secret.
puthoff-green-davis-email-chain-on-alien: An online researcher who goes by UAPGerb describes a chain of emails from around 2001 and 2002 between a physicist named Hal Puthoff, a man named Kit Green and another physicist, Eric Davis. In it, he says, they discuss the Santilli alien autopsy film, a 1990s film said to show doctors cutting open an alien body, and Green says he had seen different pictures of an alien autopsy. If true, it would mean other images of alien bodies exist beyond the famous film.
puthoff-head-of-stargate-and-leader-on-u: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, describes Hal Puthoff as the head of Stargate, which Michels calls the CIA's psychic spy program, and as a leading thinker on how UFOs might fly. Michels finds it telling that the same man links government psychic research with ideas about UFO propulsion.
puthoff-later-briefs-grusch-s-group: Eric Davis, a physicist, said on Jesse Michels's podcast that the group around David Grusch, a whistleblower who has gone public with claims about hidden UFO programs, eventually got to meet Hal Puthoff, a physicist long involved in this research. Davis says Puthoff then briefed them with his own set of information. He gives no date or place, but the story would mean that Puthoff's knowledge helped shape what Grusch's group came to believe.
puthoff-met-townsend-brown: Chris Bledsoe, a man who says he has had repeated encounters with UFOs, told a podcast host, Jesse Michels, about something Hal Puthoff, a physicist, once told him. According to Bledsoe, Puthoff said he had met Townsend Brown, an inventor known for experiments he thought could move objects in new ways. If true, it would link two people from different generations who both chased unusual ideas about flight.
puthoff-mk-ultra-and-the-remote-viewing-: A researcher named Matthew Pines, talking with podcast host Jesse Michels, says a scientist named Hal Puthoff worked on both UFOs and research into the human mind. Pines puts it this way: MK Ultra, a secret US programme of mind experiments, was the more weaponised side of that mind research, and remote viewing programmes, which tried to use the mind to see distant places, were the practical spy-craft side, running roughly from the 1950s to the 1990s. If he is right, the same people were studying UFOs and the powers of the mind at once.
puthoff-s-article-on-the-stargate-and-sc: A guest on Jesse Michels's podcast shows an article he wrote about remote viewing, the attempt to see faraway places using only the mind. He says it covers two 1970s government programmes, Stargate and Scanate, run with the DIA, the US military's intelligence agency, and the CIA, America's foreign spy agency, with work done by the physicists Hal Puthoff and Russell Targ at the Stanford Research Institute in California. As told, it shows the government took psychic spying seriously enough to pay for it.
puthoff-s-cia-psychic-spy-program-and-re: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says a man named Hal Puthoff ran a psychic spying programme for the CIA, the US Central Intelligence Agency, between roughly the 1970s and 1990s. The programme used remote viewing, the practice of trying to see distant places with the mind alone. Michels says many of these remote viewers, such as a man named Ingo Swann, reported seeing beings in various places, including the far side of the Moon. A researcher and author, Peter Levenda, describes the same work differently, stressing that the tests at SRI, the research institute where they were done, showed statistical improvements, and praising Swann's work. If true, it would mean the government took psychic spying seriously and that its spies glimpsed beings off Earth.
puthoff-s-earthtech-papers-as-a-guide: Dave Rossi, a researcher who says aliens taught him advanced physics, told a podcast host, Jesse Michels, that he finds the work of a physicist named Hal Puthoff fascinating. Rossi says the full set of papers on the website of EarthTech, Puthoff's research outfit, has served him as a kind of mentor, guiding his own thinking.
puthoff-s-extended-electrodynamics-model: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says the physicist Hal Puthoff has a model he calls extended electrodynamics, an expanded version of the physics of electricity and magnetism built on quantities called vector and scalar potentials. In a later episode Michels says Puthoff talked about it openly on Anna Brady-Estevez's podcast, mentioned work with Josephson junctions, which are tiny superconducting electronic devices, and also credited Lewis Darro and Larry Forsley. Michels raises it because he thinks it might help explain how alien intelligences could communicate.
puthoff-s-paper-on-ultraterrestrials-sur: Jesse Michels, a podcast host, says that the physicist Hal Puthoff has written a paper on "ultraterrestrials", meaning intelligent beings native to Earth rather than from space. As Michels puts it, these are beings that could have died off in a cataclysm, and the story places them, or what remains of them, in bases under the sea and on the Moon. If true, the beings behind UFOs might be an older Earth civilisation rather than visitors from other worlds.
puthoff-s-polarizable-vacuum-approach-to: A physicist named Hal Puthoff, described on the show as a CIA-linked UFO expert, says he published a paper in a physics journal describing what he calls a polarizable vacuum approach to gravity. The idea treats empty space as something that can be stretched or polarized, a bit like a material, and Puthoff says it reproduces all the standard tests of general relativity, Einstein's theory of gravity. If he is right, it would give a different way of understanding how gravity works.
puthoff-s-silurian-hypothesis-paper: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, mentions a researcher named Hal Puthoff, who he says lives in Austin, Texas. According to Michels, Puthoff wrote an interesting paper on the Silurian hypothesis, the idea that an advanced civilisation could have lived on Earth long before humans and left few traces.
puthoff-s-vector-scalar-potential-commun: A researcher named Dave Rossi says on Jesse Michels's podcast in 2025 that Hal Puthoff, a physicist, invented a way to communicate using what are called vector and scalar potentials, deeper quantities in the physics of electricity and magnetism that sit beneath ordinary electric and magnetic fields. Michels tells it again in 2026, saying Puthoff is now working on a quantum communications company built on those same potentials. If true, it would mean a kind of signalling that works outside ordinary radio.
puthoff-says-he-consulted-on-the-net-ass: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that a physicist named Harold Puthoff is on record saying he consulted on a government "net assessment", a big-picture strategic study, in Washington in the 2000s. Michels adds that Stephen Hadley, the US national security adviser, was involved. If true, it would mean people at the top of US national security were looking into unexplained phenomena.
puthoff-skeptical-of-lazar-after-a-clear: A physicist named Hal Puthoff, introduced on Jesse Michels's podcast as a CIA UFO expert, talks about a man named Bob Lazar. Puthoff says that, as far as he could check behind the scenes on Lazar's security clearances, he has reason to be skeptical of him. It matters because it casts doubt on whether Lazar worked where he says he did.
puthoff-the-1950s-anti-gravity-craze-eit: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in the 1950s the United States had a craze for anti-gravity, the idea of craft that could cancel out gravity, and that by the 1960s it seemed to just vanish. Michels, who also points to the researcher Eric Weinstein, says the physicist Hal Puthoff told him that either the work went nowhere or it "went black", meaning it moved into secret, classified programmes. If it went black, the research would have kept going out of public view.
puthoff-visited-ossining-and-heard-about: A researcher called Greg, speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast, says the physicist Hal Puthoff told them he went to the house of the researcher Andrija Puharich in Ossining, New York, in the 1970s. There, Greg says, Puthoff heard all about "the Nine", a council of non-human beings that Puharich's circle claimed to be in contact with, and the story also involves Puthoff's research partner Russell Targ. If true, it would link serious government-funded scientists to that circle's contact claims.
putin-asks-for-the-full-account-1997: Kiran Ilum Xenov, described as a former president of one of Russia's republics who says he was taken by aliens in 1997, tells podcast host Jesse Michels that Vladimir Putin, Russia's leader, later asked him about it. Xenov says Putin told him, "Please tell me exactly how everything transpired, how it all unfolded." If true, it would mean the head of Russia took a personal interest in an alien abduction account.
putin-s-post-9-11-proposal-to-unite-agai: Kiran Ilum Xenov, a man who once led a republic inside Russia and says he was taken by aliens in 1997, told a podcast host, Jesse Michels, about an idea from Russia's president, Vladimir Putin. He says that after the September 11, 2001 attacks on the United States, Putin proposed that nations unite against shared threats, including ones from space, since there are good and not so good extraterrestrials and some "might even want to enslave our earth." If true, it would mean a world leader was openly weighing threats from beyond Earth.
pyramid-sarcophagi-too-big-for-the-entra: A researcher named Luke Caverns told podcast host Jesse Michels that the stone coffins, or sarcophagi, inside the pyramids are too big to fit through the entrances. So, he says, they were not brought in later but were set in place while the rooms around them were being built. He uses this to argue the pyramids are not what most people think they are.
pyramid-texts-as-initiation-rite: Karl Nell, who speaks on these subjects as a researcher, argues that the Pyramid Texts, ancient Egyptian religious writings from around 2500 BC found inside pyramids, were part of an initiation experience. He says they draw on the Sed festival, a known Egyptian kingship ritual, so that the pyramid and its texts worked as an "initiatic engine" that transformed the person going through it. The podcast host Jesse Michels later repeats the idea and adds the Egyptian magical papyri, ancient spell books, and secret brotherhoods in Egypt.
pyramids-as-generators-of-plasma-energy: A researcher named Randall Carlson, speaking with podcast host Jesse Michels, says he thinks the pyramids at Giza in Egypt were built to generate some kind of energy. If he had to pick one, he says, it would be plasma, an electrically charged gas, and he draws on the work of a man named Bob Greener. If true, it would mean the pyramids were machines and not only tombs.
pyramids-built-during-the-saharan-humid-: A researcher named Jeffrey Drum told podcast host Jesse Michels that he thinks the pyramids of Egypt were built by a civilization living there during the Saharan Humid Period, a time when the region was much wetter, which he dates from about 8,500 BC to about 5,300 BC. If true, it would make the pyramids thousands of years older than usually believed.
pyramids-in-the-elysium-region: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that space probes photographed huge pyramids in a region of Mars called Elysium. According to him, some stand about 500 meters high and some have four sides, just like the Great Pyramids of Giza in Egypt. If true, it would suggest someone once built things on Mars.
quantum-gravity-appears-out-of-nowhere-a: Eric Weinstein, a mathematician and commentator, said on Jesse Michels's podcast that a Google Ngram search, a tool that counts how often a phrase appears in books over time, shows almost no use of "quantum gravity" until around 1972. He takes this as a sign that the field appeared suddenly and acted as a blocking mechanism, a way to steer physicists away from more fruitful work. If he is right, the direction of modern physics was deliberately managed.
quantum-gravity-pushed-as-the-holy-grail: A researcher named Eric Weinstein, on podcast host Jesse Michels's show, says that from 1984 to 1987 quantum gravity, the effort to join the theory of gravity with the physics of the very small, was forced on physicists as the field's holy grail. By 1987, he says, everybody had accepted it, which would mean the direction of physics was pushed on the field rather than chosen by it.
queen-s-chamber-sarcophagus-as-healing-d: A man named Steve Coburn, speaking on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, talks about the Great Pyramid at Giza in Egypt. He says the stone box in the room called the Queen's chamber, the thing people call a sarcophagus, or stone coffin, was "probably a healing device." If he is right, the pyramid was built for more than burial.
queen-s-chamber-shaft-points-at-orion: A writer named Graham Hancock told podcast host Jesse Michels that one of the narrow shafts leading out of the Queen's Chamber, one of the rooms inside the Great Pyramid of Giza, points at the star pattern Orion. He notes that not every chamber points at Orion, but this shaft does, which fits his wider idea that the pyramid was aligned to the stars on purpose.
questionable-groups-targeting-women-via-: Matthew Brown, described as a Pentagon whistleblower, said on Jesse Michels's podcast that some questionable groups use UFO "call-down" events, gatherings meant to summon craft through meditation, as a cover. Based on what people he knows experienced with these groups, Brown says the groups seem more interested in women. If true, some groups in the UFO world would be using the subject to target women.
quigley-s-anglo-american-establishment: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, points to a book called The Anglo-American Establishment by a writer named Carroll Quigley, which deals with figures such as Cecil Rhodes and Alfred Milner. Michels says the book describes how American spy agencies grew out of a culture of "round table" groups and secret societies linking the United States and Britain, which would mean those agencies have older, hidden roots.
quranic-verses-calling-the-world-a-game: Rizwan Virk, a scientist who argues that we may live in a kind of computer simulation or hologram, told a podcast host, Jesse Michels, that Islamic tradition has verses saying, "We have set up this world for you as a game, as a pastime, as a sport." He credits these to the Quran, Islam's holy book, and offers them as an ancient echo of the idea that our reality is a built game.
rabbi-ariel-zadok-s-chant-causes-a-sudde: Brandon Fugal owns Skinwalker Ranch, a ranch in Utah known for reports of strange events. He told podcast host Jesse Michels that sometime in the 2020s a rabbi named Ariel Zadok chanted at Homestead 2, a site on the ranch, and that he was there. Fugal says the temperature dropped sharply around the building and right in the doorway, which would suggest the place reacts to what people do there.
radar-from-wright-patterson-brought-down: A former government scientist named John Blitch, who says he was taken by an alien, told podcast host Jesse Michels his idea about a craft said to have crashed near a place called Cape Girardeau before the Second World War. He suggests that if something fast was interfered with, perhaps by radar, near Wright-Patterson, an Air Force base in Ohio, it could have come down right there. He draws on the work of UFO writers Philip J. Corso, Stanton Friedman and Don Schmitt.
radar-incursions-over-northern-us-missil: On Jesse Michels's podcast, a guest named Karl Nell says that in the 1970s, radars in the northern US ballistic missile warning system, the network that watches for incoming nuclear missiles, picked up UFOs crossing into its airspace. If true, it would mean unknown objects were flying near some of the country's most sensitive defenses.
radar-sites-built-1946-plus-mori-arti-an: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that a researcher named Scott Ramsay, looking into a claimed crash of a craft carrying alien bodies in New Mexico, found that a nearby radar site was first built in 1946 and then moved in 1950. Michels says Ramsay also found two other bases close by, called Mori Arti and Continental, though they were not active until around 1950 or 1951. The point is that radar in the area could have tracked a crash there.
radcliffe-says-uap-show-technology-we-ca: Merrick von Renenamp, appearing as a witness in a debate with a UFO skeptic on Jesse Michels's podcast, cites John Ratcliffe, a former top US intelligence official. He says Ratcliffe has stated that UAP, the official term for UFOs (unidentified anomalous phenomena), show technologies the US does not have and cannot defend against. If true, it would mean a senior official has admitted these objects outmatch the American military.
radiation-like-sickness-after-a-mystery-: Jake Barber, a former military helicopter pilot, says that sometime in the 1990s he flew on a mission escorting a mysterious box aboard an aircraft. He says he became very sick afterwards, lost every hair on his body, and had skin peel off his arms, symptoms like radiation sickness. He mentions a scientist named Garry Nolan in connection with it, and tells it as a sign that whatever was in the box was something out of the ordinary.
radio-station-calls-lead-moore-to-meet-d: This story is about Bill Moore, a writer who in 1980 was touring to promote his book The Roswell Incident, about a claimed UFO crash in New Mexico. A researcher, Greg Bishop, relays what Moore said: at radio stations on the tour, a mysterious voice kept calling him. When he reached Albuquerque and went into the radio station, the same voice called again. Bishop says this led Moore to meet a man named Rick Doty and an insider known only as Falcon, and he also names Harry Rositzke. Another researcher, Grant Cameron, says the first call came seven days into the tour and was probably from Doty in Albuquerque. It is linked to another story about a security meeting at Kirtland Air Force Base. If true, it would mean people inside the government were reaching out to steer UFO researchers.
radioactive-decay-tracks-seen-coming-off: Charles Hall says that around 1965 he was stationed in Indian Springs Valley in the Nevada desert, where he met tall, pale beings he calls the Tall Whites. Speaking to podcast host Jesse Michels, he says he saw the tracks left by radioactive decay coming off their suits, and he knew exactly what they were. If true, it would mean the beings' suits gave off radiation.
raf-pilots-encounter-aurora-over-the-nor: Nick Cook, a writer on secret aircraft and anti-gravity, told a podcast host, Jesse Michels, about a man who had spoken with pilots from the RAF, Britain's Royal Air Force. According to Cook, those pilots said they had run into the Aurora, a rumoured secret high-speed aircraft, over the North Sea sometime in the late 1980s or 1990s. If true, it would mean such a craft was really flying.
rahab-an-exploded-planet-that-became-the: Tim Alberino, a researcher speaking with podcast host Jesse Michels, describes an idea he credits to a writer named David Flynn. The idea is that the asteroid belt, the band of rocks between Mars and Jupiter, is what remains of a planet that exploded, and that this planet was the Rahab named in the Bible's book of Psalms. He links it to works called Cydonia and Birthright, and if true it would mean the old texts describe real events in the solar system.
raiju-thunder-beast-of-japanese-folklore: A researcher named Geoffrey Drumm, who says an alien told him the true purpose of the pyramids, mentions to podcast host Jesse Michels a creature from Japanese folklore he calls the Rayu, or Raiju. He describes it as a thunder beast that comes alive during thunderstorms, and brings it up as part of his ideas about ancient stories linked to electricity and energy.
ralph-mote-larsson-says-he-knows-nothing: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, speaking with a former director of the NSA, the US agency that intercepts communications, mentions a man named Ralph Mote Larsson whom he has interviewed. Michels says Larsson and other people he respects from government circles tell him they know nothing about UFOs, and the story's framing is that Larsson says he would make it public if he did.
ramsays-14-000-retrieval-reenactment: Suzanne Ramsay, speaking on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, talks about Hart Canyon near Aztec, New Mexico, where some people say a craft carrying alien bodies crashed. She says she and her family staged a reenactment of the recovery of that craft, and that it cost them more than $14,000 in one week.
ramsays-bolt-a-plaque-to-the-mesa-2007: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in 2007 a couple named Scott and Suzanne Ramsay, who researched a claimed crash of a craft with alien bodies at Hart Canyon near Aztec, New Mexico, bolted a signed and dated plaque to the mesa there. According to Michels, they did it to "fix the record" themselves, marking the spot where they believe the crash happened.
rand-paul-confronts-fauci-over-the-gain-: In 2021, at a hearing in the US Senate in Washington, Senator Rand Paul confronted Anthony Fauci, the government's top infectious disease official, about gain-of-function research, work that makes viruses more contagious or dangerous. Paul says Fauci was defining gain of function away, claiming it did not exist simply because the definition had been changed on the website of the NIH, the main US medical research agency. If true, it would mean officials reworded the rules to avoid admitting to risky research, and the story is retold as an example of how government can hide things by changing words.
randi-s-million-dollar-challenge-was-rea: Joe McMoneagle, a man known for remote viewing, the practice of trying to describe faraway places with the mind alone, told a podcast host, Jesse Michels, about James Randi, a stage magician who offered a million dollars to anyone who could prove a paranormal power. McMoneagle says the prize was not a million dollars in hand but an investment that would pay out over about 30 years, and that Randi judged the tests himself. If so, the famous challenge would be less fair than it sounds.
randolph-afb-accelerated-learning-skinne: Whitley Strieber, an author known for describing his own encounters with non-human beings, says that in 1952 children were taken into a program at Randolph Air Force Base in San Antonio, Texas, that involved Skinner boxes, closed chambers used in conditioning experiments. According to what he was told, parents were told it was an accelerated learning program for children with very high IQs. If true, the military was running experiments on gifted children under a false label.
random-event-generator-research-at-elite: Jesse Michels, a podcast host, says scientists at elite US universities studied random event generators, machines that produce random numbers, to test whether the human mind can influence them. In different episodes he points to the statistician Jessica Utts, to SRI (a California research institute), and to Princeton's Engineering Anomalies Research lab, which he says was started by Robert Jahn, dean of the engineering school there. If such effects were real, they would show the mind can affect the physical world directly.
randy-anderson-saw-triangles-taking-off-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, mentions a man named Randy Anderson. Michels says Anderson claimed he saw triangle-shaped craft taking off from Area 51, a secretive US military test site in the Nevada desert. Michels brings this up with his guest, a researcher who goes by the name UAPGerb and who first made Anderson's account public, because if true it would mean unknown craft were flying out of one of America's most secret bases.
randy-anderson-taken-to-an-underground-f: Randy Anderson, a man who worked around a Navy site called Naval Surface Warfare Center Crane in Indiana, a weapons and technology base, says he was taken deep underground there by elevator and saw strange things: an object like a glove, or gauntlet, showing glowing symbols with a shimmering, mirage-like effect, and, in the host's retelling, a floating orb. Podcast host Jesse Michels repeats the story across several episodes and links it to a possible hidden division studying technology not made by humans, which he says an online researcher called UAP Gerb helped bring to light. If true, it would suggest the government keeps such objects in a secret facility.
range-four-harry-on-scout-craft-and-the-: Charles Hall, a man who says he spent three years in the mid 1960s on Air Force ranges near Indian Springs Valley, Nevada, living alongside tall white aliens, told a podcast host, Jesse Michels, about a man he calls Range Four Harry, whom he says he was close to "like brothers." Hall says he once asked Harry whether one of the egg-shaped scout craft there could go faster than light, and Harry firmly said it could, though no one in their right mind would ever take it that fast. If true, it would mean these craft could break what we think is the universe's speed limit.
range-four-harry-s-high-speed-horse-form: Charles Hall says that between 1965 and 1967, in Indian Springs Valley, Nevada, he watched pale beings he calls the Tall Whites. He told podcast host Jesse Michels that one of them, whom he calls Range Four Harry, flew craft in what Hall calls a "high-speed horse formation," and that the craft merged their fields to form a single larger craft. If true, it would mean these craft could join together in flight.
ransone-predicts-a-rocket-launch-failure: An unnamed researcher, speaking on podcast host Jesse Michels's show in an episode about a government scientist said to have contacted aliens, tells of a woman named Valerie Ransone who worked around important scientists. According to the guest, she predicted that a rocket launch in the late 1970s would fail, and it did. If true, it would suggest she could foresee events.
ransone-s-college-ufo-sighting-in-the-ey: This story is about Valerie Ransone, who tells of seeing a UFO when she was young, in a video interview on a YouTube channel called Eyes on Cinema. An unnamed researcher, speaking on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, says that in the video she describes a strange experience from her college years, and that a friend of hers saw it too. The story places it in the 1960s in northern Illinois. The host, Jesse Michels, tells it again on a later episode, reading her account. In his version it happened at Northern Illinois University in October 1971, at about 11 in the morning, when she noticed a strange object above the student union building. So the two tellings differ on the date. It is told because, if true, it would add one more ordinary person's sighting to the record, backed by a second witness.
rare-book-stripping-monks-above-a-strip-: Peter Levenda, an author who writes about the occult and secret history, says that in the early 1970s he visited a group of monks in Jamaica, Queens, in New York City. He says their chapel sat above a strip club, and that these monks were involved in stripping and taking rare books. He tells it as one of the odd underground worlds he moved through as a young man.
rare-book-theft-ring-and-the-burning-of-: Peter Levenda, an author who writes about the occult and secret history, says that in the early to mid 1970s a group he knew was arrested for what he calls the largest rare book theft in American history. The story, as he frames it, also involves stolen books being burned. He tells it as part of a strange circle he was drawn into in New York.
rat-brain-neurons-fly-an-f-22-simulator-: A researcher named Grant Cameron, speaking with podcast host Jesse Michels, describes an experiment from around 2004 at a university in Florida. He says a scientist took about 20,000 nerve cells from a rat's brain and used them to fly a computer simulation of the F-22, an American fighter jet, and he tells listeners to search for it themselves. He brings it up as an example of how far living brain tissue might be pushed to control machines.
rat-learning-experiments-as-evidence-for: A biologist and author named Rupert Sheldrake has an idea he calls morphic resonance: once some members of a species learn something, others of the same species elsewhere find it easier to learn, as if nature has a kind of memory. Speaking with podcast host Jesse Michels, he says a long series of experiments with rats, in cities from London to Melbourne to Beijing, gives actual evidence that this happens. If true, it would mean learning can spread between animals with no ordinary contact.
ray-fowler-s-sylvania-contractors-report: Robert Salas, a former US Air Force officer, tells a story about a man named Ray Fowler, a manager at Sylvania, a company doing contract work for the military. According to Salas, in 1967 Fowler's contract workers at Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana reported UFOs to Roy Craig, an investigator for the Condon study, a university study of UFOs paid for by the Air Force in the late 1960s. If true, it would mean civilian workers backed up reports of UFOs at a military base and passed them to the official investigators.
ray-hernandez-pulled-out-of-his-car-in-a: Grant Cameron, a researcher who studies UFOs, told a podcast host, Jesse Michels, a story about a man named Rey Hernandez, which he connects to Edgar Mitchell, an astronaut who walked on the Moon. Cameron says that two days after an earlier event, Hernandez was sitting in a completely stalled traffic jam in Miami, Florida, when he was pulled out of his car. He tells it as a sign of something strange reaching into ordinary life.
raymond-lavos-claims-esoteric-math-for-b: Jan Lundquist, speaking in a documentary by a podcast host, Jesse Michels, about the inventor Townsend Brown, tells of a man named Raymond Lavos. According to Lundquist, Lavos swears he worked on some very unusual mathematics in the 1980s for the B-2, the US Air Force's stealth bomber. If true, it would hint that strange science went into that plane.
raymond-moody-s-psychomanteum-and-the-un: Jeffrey Mishlove, a researcher with a doctorate who studies psychic experiences, talks about a man named Raymond Moody and something Moody developed called a psychomanteum, a modern setup for seeking visions. Mishlove says Moody based it on the discovery of underground temples in ancient Greece, places where people went to consult oracles. He tells it as a sign that an ancient way of reaching beyond ordinary experience has been brought back into use today.
raytheon-distances-itself-from-what-its-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in 2004 a new FLIR system, a camera that sees heat, made by the defense company Raytheon, had just been installed with a US Navy aircraft carrier group off San Diego before it recorded an unexplained object. According to the story, Raytheon then kept its distance from what its camera had picked up, which Michels raises in a debate with a skeptic.
raytheon-man-made-triangle-at-fort-irwin: Steven Greer, author of a book called Disclosure: An Illustrated History, shows on Jesse Michels's podcast what he calls the Raytheon triangle, a triangle-shaped craft he says was built by Raytheon, a US weapons maker, and seen at Fort Irwin, an Army base in California, based on what a witness told him. In a later episode he adds that the craft could make holograms and might be used to fake an alien invasion. He also says the witness and his wife were later abducted by the craft.
razor-sharp-stone-cuts-at-kef-kalesi: A researcher identified only as Matt, speaking with podcast host Jesse Michels, talks about Kef Kalesi, an ancient stone site in Turkey. He says some of the cuts in the stone there are so sharp you can still cut your finger on them. He offers this as a sign that the ancient builders had more advanced tools or methods than people usually credit them with.
reaction-to-communion-cover-at-beth-isra: Jim Weiner, a man who tells of being abducted by aliens, told podcast host Jesse Michels about seeing the cover of Communion, a book by the writer Whitley Strieber about his own encounters, in the late 1980s at Beth Israel Hospital in Boston. Weiner says that when he saw the face on the cover he "flipped out." He tells it because the face seemed to match what he had experienced.
reactor-theorized-as-a-cyclotron-hitting: Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked on alien craft at a secret site called S4 in the Nevada desert in the late 1980s, talks about the reactor that he says powered those craft. Lazar says a colleague named Barry Castilio and another lab partner thought part of it was a cyclotron, a kind of particle accelerator, firing at element 115, a very heavy chemical element. If true, it would offer a physical explanation for how the craft got their power.
reactors-in-all-the-craft-are-identical-: Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked on alien craft at a secret site called S4 in the Nevada desert in the late 1980s, says the reactors that powered the craft were apparently exactly the same in every one of them. If true, it would suggest the craft were built to one standard design, like a production line.
read-in-personnel-dig-into-the-program-s: Dylan Borland, a man who says a top government official told him that aliens run everything, told a podcast host, Jesse Michels, about people in a secret programme in the 2010s. He says that once some people were "read in", meaning formally given access to the secret, they began digging into the programme's backlog of older history, and that is when they got into trouble. If true, it would mean the programme's past is guarded even from its own members.
readers-of-the-sacred-mushroom-find-mush: Jeffrey Mishlove, a researcher with a doctorate who studies the paranormal, tells Jesse Michels's podcast what he heard from Andrija Puharich, a scientist who wrote a book called The Sacred Mushroom about a mind-altering mushroom. Mishlove says Puharich told him that people who read the book in the 1960s and 70s found those same mushrooms growing in their backyards within days. As told, it is a strange coincidence that hints at some hidden link between mind and world.
reading-a-book-aloud-at-age-three: Bob Maguire, a man who says he did contract work for the CIA, the US spy agency, told a podcast host, Jesse Michels, about his early childhood. He says that at age three, before he had spent a day in school, he walked in on his mother and a friend having coffee, pulled a book off the shelf, and read it aloud to them. He tells it as an early sign of an unusual gift.
reading-corso-s-the-day-after-roswell-19: John Blitch, a scientist who worked with DARPA, the Pentagon's research agency for advanced technology, told podcast host Jesse Michels that around 1997 he read The Day After Roswell. That is a book by Philip J. Corso, a former Army officer, about the claimed 1947 crash of a UFO near Roswell, New Mexico. Blitch says it was then that he really started digging into the subject.
reading-raw-project-blue-book-case-files: Merrick von Renenamp, a researcher, says he has read the raw case files of Project Blue Book, the US Air Force's UFO study of the 1950s and 60s. He describes them as the straight reports, with no analysis added. He raises this on a podcast episode about a debate with a UFO skeptic named Mick West, to make the point that the original reports, read on their own, tell a different story than the official conclusions.
reagan-and-bill-paynter-s-1974-sighting-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells how Ronald Reagan, while governor of California, was flying in a small Cessna plane near Bakersfield with his pilot, a man named Bill Paynter. The story, set in 1974, is that the two saw something unexplained in the sky. It matters to people because the witness later became president of the United States.
reagan-asks-gorbachev-for-help-against-a: Pippa Malmgren, speaking on a podcast episode featuring the presidential advisor Harald Malmgren, recounts a moment from a 1980s summit between the US and the Soviet Union. She says that President Ronald Reagan asked Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev, "If the United States were attacked by someone from outer space, would you help us?", and she links the story to the TV interviewer Charlie Rose. It is told as a hint that a US president took the idea of visitors from space seriously.
reagan-diary-on-the-capacity-to-put-300-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that diary entries written by Ronald Reagan, the US president in the 1980s, record him meeting top astronomers from NASA, the US space agency. As the story is told, the entries mention a capacity to put 300 people in orbit, which would mean the country could do far more in space than the public was told.
reagan-era-release-of-falcon-and-condor-: A UFO researcher named Grant Cameron, talking with podcast host Jesse Michels, describes a story from around 1988 and 1989. He says Ronald Reagan, the US president of the 1980s, allowed material to come out about two insiders known as the Falcon and the Condor, and about an alien said to be held at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base, a US Air Force base in Ohio. Cameron ties this to a television program called UFO Cover-Up Live and gives no other source; if true, it would mean a president quietly let secrets about aliens reach the public.
reagan-family-feud-over-lost-spanish-gol: A researcher named Luke Caverns, talking with podcast host Jesse Michels, passes along a story he heard about Reagan Canyon, a canyon in the Big Bend region of West Texas. He says there is a huge old tale, set around the 1890s, of a family feud over lost Spanish gold, with mystery and strange deaths reaching from West Texas all the way to San Antonio.
