reagan-on-close-encounters-at-the-white-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that President Ronald Reagan watched Close Encounters of the Third Kind, a Hollywood film about humans meeting aliens, in the White House during the 1980s. According to Michels, Reagan said there was a lot of truth to it, which, if so, would hint that a president knew more than he said.
reagan-on-uniting-earth-against-an-outsi: Salvatore Pais, a Navy scientist known for patents on unusual craft designs, says humanity faces a threat from outside and quotes President Ronald Reagan as saying that unless we come together as a unified Earth we will not withstand what is coming. Other clips have Reagan saying, in a 1987 speech placed at the United Nations, that our differences would vanish if we faced an alien threat from outside this world. Those who repeat it take it as a sign that a US president was hinting at something real.
reagan-proposes-sdi-at-a-cabinet-meeting: John Harrington, presented as a former US Secretary of Energy, told podcast host Jesse Michels about a 1983 cabinet meeting at the White House that he says he attended. He says President Ronald Reagan asked whether it wouldn't be wonderful to design something that could protect the country from missiles. That idea became the Strategic Defense Initiative, or SDI, a plan to shoot down enemy missiles.
reagan-s-comment-at-the-white-house-e-t-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, points to an audio recording in which, he says, the film director Steven Spielberg describes a trip to the White House in 1982 where his movie E.T., about a stranded alien, was screened. The story turns on a comment President Reagan is said to have made there, which Michels raises in a talk about whether officials know more about aliens than they let on.
reagan-s-staff-cut-tear-down-this-wall-t: John Harrington, a guest on Jesse Michels' podcast, tells the story behind US President Ronald Reagan's 1987 Berlin speech and its famous line "tear down this wall." Citing the speechwriter Peter Robinson and a book called In His Own Hand, he says Reagan's staff took the line out of the speech not once but twice. He tells it as an example of a leader's own staff trying to hold back a bold statement.
reagan-ufo-briefing-attended-by-james-ba: Jason Simosa, a researcher, says that according to the writer Nick Redfern, James Baker, a senior official he describes as a member of a powerful inner circle he calls "the family", was invited to a UFO briefing given to President Ronald Reagan in the 1980s. Simosa says several groups presented: one from the CIA's science and technology branch, which he presumes was a CIA scientist named Kit Green and his team, one called the Collins Elite, and a third group. If true, it would mean UFOs were discussed at the very top of the US government.
rear-admiral-gallaudet-researching-under: A former Navy fighter pilot named Ryan Graves, talking with podcast host Jesse Michels, says that Tim Gallaudet, a retired Navy rear admiral who once helped run NOAA, the US government agency for oceans and weather, is very interested in strange objects reported underwater. If true, it would mean a senior ocean official takes such reports seriously.
reassigned-to-kilo-control-and-never-tea: Mario Woods was a guard at nuclear missile sites near Ellsworth in South Dakota, and he says he was abducted by a UFO there in 1977. He told podcast host Jesse Michels that afterward he never went back to his old control post. He says he was sent to a different one called Kilo control and was never made team leader again, which he presents as a result of what happened.
rebello-s-tweet-promising-to-open-brazil: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, quotes a post on social media by Aldo Rebello, presented as a former Brazilian defence minister, from around 2025 or 2026. In it Rebello says he knows what Brazil's armed forces hold in their UFO archives, and that if the US government reveals its documents, he will do the same if he is elected president of Brazil.
recalled-abduction-aboard-a-50-foot-craf: Steve Coburn told podcast host Jesse Michels that, in Fillmore, California, two small grey beings came into his room, woke him up and told him to come outside. He says he later remembered being taken aboard a craft about 50 feet across, where something was implanted in his toe. If true, it would mean beings put objects inside human bodies.
recently-discovered-10-000-year-old-anci: A researcher named Luke Caverns, talking with podcast host Jesse Michels, says an ancient city was recently found in Texas next to a river. He says it is about 10,000 years old, though he does not name the place. If so, it would push organised settlement in North America far further back than usually thought.
recording-leaked-to-globo-and-the-case-r: Carlos Dosoza, speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast about the 1996 case of beings said to have been captured in Brazil, says a recording about the case was leaked to Globo, a big Brazilian TV network. He says the network, on a show he calls Fantas, would ridicule the case every time, and he names a Claudia Kovu. He tells it to explain how the case was made to look foolish to the public.
recovered-craft-cannot-be-flown-because-: A lawyer named Dan Sheehan, talking with podcast host Jesse Michels, passes along what he was told about craft not made by humans that the US government is said to have recovered. According to Sheehan, the people studying them hit a major problem: they could not fly the craft, because the craft are steered by the mind of the pilot, by consciousness itself.
recovered-craft-not-made-by-humanity-con: A man named Dylan Borland, talking with podcast host Jesse Michels, says he is sure the US has recovered craft that were not made by humans. He points for support to AARO, the Pentagon's current office for investigating unexplained sightings, to the Inspector General, an internal government watchdog, and to David Grusch, a former intelligence officer who has said publicly that such craft exist. If true, it would mean the government holds machines built by someone other than us.
recovered-memory-of-a-virtual-tour-of-eg: Chris Bledsoe is a man who says UFOs are drawn to him. He told podcast host Jesse Michels that after an encounter in 2007, he remembered being taken on what felt like a virtual tour of Egypt, and the first thing he saw was the pyramids, then the Sphinx and a temple of Hathor, an ancient Egyptian goddess. He wondered why they showed him Egypt.
recovered-relic-tech-brought-in-by-secur: Jordan Jose says that as a child, around 2008 to 2010, he was taken into a secret UFO programme at a place called Baker Victory Services in Western New York. He told podcast host Jesse Michels that about eight security guards would bring in a huge box holding what he calls a relic, a recovered piece of technology, while a team watched him in the room to study his telepathic abilities. He mentions a man named Jacob Barber in connection with the story.
recovered-roswell-craft-must-have-been-s: In 1947 something crashed near Roswell, a town in New Mexico, and many people believe it was a craft not made by humans. A UFO historian named Richard Dolan, speaking with podcast host Jesse Michels and drawing on the earlier researcher Stanton Friedman, argues that if the military recovered such a craft, it was obviously going to be studied. His point is that this would mean a secret research effort has been running ever since.
recovering-ufo-metal-in-zanesville-ohio-: Chris Bledsoe, a man who says UFOs are drawn to him, told podcast host Jesse Michels about a trip to Zanesville, Ohio, around 2008 to 2010 with a man named Tim Taylor. He says someone there had a piece of metal said to come from a UFO, and the two of them took it to a machine shop and had a piece sawed off. Taylor kept that piece, and they gave the rest back to its owner.
recovery-of-the-eight-gon-disc-and-the-e: Jake Barber, a former military helicopter pilot, says that sometime after about 2014 he flew a mission in the California desert to pick up a flying disc he calls the eight-gon, because from above it looked split into eight sections. He says that while flying it back, hanging below his helicopter, he felt overwhelmed, and podcast host Jesse Michels adds that Barber described locking on to it with his mind and feeling a gentle, divine feminine presence that made him emotional. If true, it would mean the US recovers craft that may respond to human consciousness.
recovery-team-without-insignia-1948: Scott Ramsay is a researcher who has spent years on a reported crash of an unknown craft in March 1948 in Hart Canyon, near the town of Aztec, New Mexico. Speaking with podcast host Jesse Michels and citing a man named Doug Noland, he says the local witnesses all agree that the team who came to recover the craft wore no badges or insignia showing who they were, not Army, not Marines, nothing. To him, this points to a hidden group handling the recovery outside the normal military.
recruited-by-the-american-orthodox-catho: Peter Levenda, an author who writes about the occult and secret history, says that around 1968 or 1969 he attended a funeral in the Bronx, in New York City. He says that on the way out he and a companion ran into men from a small independent church called the American Orthodox Catholic Church, who drew them in. He tells it as how he first entered an unusual religious underworld.
recruited-by-two-men-to-work-as-an-airpl: Jake Barber, a former military helicopter pilot, says that in the mid-1990s, early in his US Air Force training, two men approached him and persuaded him to become an airplane mechanic. He frames the mechanic job as a cover, with Pope Air Force Base in North Carolina as part of the setting. He tells it as the quiet start of his path into secret work.
recruited-into-army-intelligence-by-a-ci: Joe McMoneagle, a man who says he served in the US Army, tells podcast host Jesse Michels about how he got into Army intelligence, the part of the Army that gathers secret information. He says that in the 1960s, at Fort Jackson, an Army training base in South Carolina, he met a man in civilian clothes at the base beer hall. When he later went into the man's trailer, McMoneagle says, he found out the man worked in intelligence, and that this meeting was the start of his recruitment.
recruited-into-the-gte-program-and-comba: Jake Barber, a former military helicopter pilot, says that in 1994, during US Air Force training in Texas, he was recruited into a brand new programme he calls GTE, which he does not spell out. The story ties this to combat control, an Air Force special operations job on the ground. He tells it as an early step toward the secret missions he later describes.
recruiters-chatting-about-the-covert-pro: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, interviews a man named Jordan, who says he was taken into a secret UFO programme as a child. Michels says Jordan's blog post describes recruiters, around 2008 to 2010, who worked near a place in New York called Baker Victory Services and would go to the Starbucks around the corner to chat casually about their job: recruiting for this covert programme.
rectangular-craft-and-gray-beings-in-pra: Deep Prasad, who describes himself as a researcher, tells podcast host Jesse Michels about a night in 2019 in his own bedroom. He says the roof seemed to dissolve and he saw the underside of a rectangular craft, along with gray beings, and that a being with three fingers touched him. Prasad says he then felt a sudden download of knowledge, and the first thought that came to him was that the universe is teeming with life, which, if true, would mean he had direct contact with non-human beings.
rectangular-football-sized-object-off-th: A researcher named Michael Shurmer, debating a skeptic on podcast host Jesse Michels's show, recalls a sighting in 2003 off the coast near Vandenberg, a military base in California used for rocket launches. He describes the object as rectangular and roughly football-sized. To him it is one of the cases that suggests unknown craft near military sites.
recurring-1-6-ghz-signal-of-unknown-sour: Brandon Fugal owns Skinwalker Ranch, a property in Utah known for reports of strange happenings. Speaking with podcast host Jesse Michels and citing a team member named Eric Bard, he says instruments there keep picking up a radio signal at 1.6 gigahertz, a particular radio frequency, and that they have yet to find where it comes from. If it has no ordinary source, it would suggest something unexplained is broadcasting on the ranch.
recursive-trace-logic-predicts-embodimen: Don Hoffman, a cognitive scientist who argues that consciousness, not matter, is the base of reality, says that in 2026 he and colleagues found something new in their mathematical model of consciousness. He says that just weeks before the interview he discovered the model predicts that having a body is a special case, and that the normal state for consciousness is to have no body at all. If right, it would mean most conscious beings are not physical creatures like us.
red-cardinal-as-homage-to-cia-project-bl: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, discussing the film director Steven Spielberg, offers his own guess about a name, Red Cardinal, that comes up in that discussion. He thinks it is a nod to Project Bluebird, which he says was the CIA's original name for its 1950s mind control efforts, later known as MK Ultra, the agency's larger mind control research programme. He credits a writer named Peter Levenda in making the link.
red-haired-colonel-takes-over-roswell-ba: A physicist named John Brandenburg, talking with podcast host Jesse Michels, passes along what veterans of Roswell told him. Roswell is the Army air base in New Mexico where, in 1947, the military first announced it had recovered a crashed flying saucer. According to those veterans, a red-haired colonel arrived, took charge barking orders, and had the wreckage cleared away, which, if true, would point to a hurried effort to hide what crashed.
red-haired-giant-remains-in-american-mou: A filmmaker and researcher named Tim Alberino, speaking with podcast host Jesse Michels, says that in the 1800s and early 1900s the remains of red-haired giants were found in the mountains of America. His own explanation, which he admits is controversial, is that these giants came across the sea with the Phoenicians, an ancient seafaring people of the eastern Mediterranean. If true, it would mean ancient travellers reached America long before Columbus.
red-light-moving-through-the-closed-chur: A man named Ralph, talking with podcast host Jesse Michels, says that around 1991 he stayed at Dionysiou, a monastery on Mount Athos, a mountain in Greece that is home to Orthodox Christian monks. He says he saw a red light moving inside the monastery church while it was closed, and he mentions a monk or guide named Timotheus, who gave him books about Athos. He tells it because, if true, something strange was moving through a holy place with no one inside.
red-light-on-the-mesa: An unnamed witness, speaking on an episode of Jesse Michels' podcast about a claimed crash near Aztec, New Mexico, recalls being out with others and looking over at a mesa, a flat-topped hill. The witness says they saw a red light there and thought someone must be out on it. Then, the witness says, all of a sudden something changed, though the quoted words stop before saying what.
red-mercury-black-market-after-the-sovie: Kirk McConnell, a former staffer for the US Senate, tells podcast host Jesse Michels about red mercury. He says that as the Soviet Union fell apart in the late 1980s and 1990s, many stories came out about this substance, which was said to have amazing properties and was supposedly being sold on the black market. The stories matter because they hint at secret materials with powers beyond known science.
red-phone-to-china-used-during-balloon-i: Bob Maguire, a former contractor for the CIA, America's foreign intelligence agency, talks about the 2023 incident when a Chinese balloon floated over the United States. He says he knows for a fact that the US has a red phone, a direct emergency line, to China, because the Secretary of Defense and General Mark Milley, then the top US military officer, said they picked up the phone during the balloon disruption. He tells it to show that a crisis in the sky had direct emergency channels between the two powers working behind the scenes.
red-quartzite-conduit-and-collection-bow: Geoffrey Drumm, who argues that the Egyptian pyramids had a purpose other than being tombs, tells podcast host Jesse Michels what he says he saw in 2017 at the pyramid of the pharaoh Niuserre at Abusir in Egypt. He says that below the eastern temple there is a system of channels made of red quartzite, a hard stone, running under the black basalt floor and emptying into a red quartzite collection bowl, a point he credits to a man named Yousef Awyan. Drumm tells it because, in his view, it shows the site was built to move some kind of fluid, which would change how the pyramids are understood.
red-team-break-in-at-a-consolidated-alli: Joe McMoneagle, a former US Army intelligence man, tells podcast host Jesse Michels about a security test in Germany in the 1970s. He says he and another man acted as a red team, people who play intruders to see if a site's security holds, and broke into a large intelligence facility shared by the US and its allies. He tells it as an example of the kind of work he did before his later psychic research.
red-team-exercises-tied-to-uap-subject-m: Jake Barber, a former military helicopter pilot, says that in the 1990s he took part in global red team exercises, drills where one side plays the enemy to test defences. He says these exercises were closely tied to UAP, the government's term for unidentified objects in the sky. He tells it as a sign the military was quietly preparing around the subject back then.
red-teaming-the-dopsr-review-with-a-fact: A man named Jake Barber, who says he once carried a UFO with a helicopter, says he and others wrote a 120,000-word historical novel to test how the Pentagon's pre-publication review office, known as DOPSR, and the Defense Department's private partners would react, judging what is real by what gets censored. The podcast host Jesse Michels later repeats the story several times, calling the book Sentinels of Ether, saying Barber tricked the reviewers, and adding that the Pentagon spent six months on just 20 pages and sent two chapters back heavily blacked out. The point, as they tell it, is that the parts the government cut would hint at what it wants kept secret.
redacted-fbi-files-on-silas-newton-and-g: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, mentions files kept by the FBI, the US federal police, on two men named Silas Newton and Leo GeBauer. He says the files go back to around the 1930s and are almost completely redacted, meaning blacked out, which he takes as a sign the government had something to hide about them.
reddit-ex-oga-contractor-post-troop-chie: A researcher who goes by UAPGerb describes a 2024 post on Reddit, an online discussion site, written by someone calling themselves an "ex OGA contractor", OGA being military slang for "other government agency". According to the post, a troop leader and his team were taken to a retrieval site outside the continental United States, where they found a cracked egg-shaped object stuck in mud, and the experience shook him to the core. It is told as a possible glimpse of a secret recovery of a non-human object.
redlands-mass-sighting-of-silver-disc-19: A man named Merrick, speaking on podcast host Jesse Michels's show, says that in 1968 in Redlands, California, about 200 people saw a silver disc 40 to 50 feet across, hovering about 200 feet up. He says the case was investigated by a researcher named James McDonald. If true, so many witnesses at once would make it hard to dismiss as one person's mistake.
refugees-moved-as-cargo-in-conex-contain: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, retells a claim from a man named Jake Barber, linked to a book called Sentinels of Ether, about events around 2004 near Coyame, Mexico. According to Barber, refugees were moved inside conex containers, the large steel boxes used for shipping, and they were not being rescued but were themselves the cargo, which would point to a hidden and cruel operation.
regenerative-medical-technology-at-under: Steven Greer, a guest on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, says he has seen secret technologies at an underground laboratory on the Mexican American border, near El Paso, Texas. According to Greer, one of them could let a person regrow a lost limb. He does not say when, but if true it would mean medical breakthroughs far beyond anything public are being kept hidden.
regression-hypnosis-of-mario-woods-paid-: A researcher named Robert Hastings, who studies reports of UFOs around nuclear weapons bases, says on podcast host Jesse Michels's show that his financial backer, Jared Tarbell, paid for a man named Mario Woods to undergo regression hypnosis. That is hypnosis meant to bring back buried memories, and the point would be to recover what Woods experienced.
reinhard-gehlen-knight-of-malta-put-in-c: Dan Sheehan, a guest on a podcast about UFOs and President John F. Kennedy, talks about Reinhard Gehlen, who he says ran anti-Soviet and Eastern European intelligence for Nazi Germany. Sheehan says that at the end of World War II the OSS, America's wartime spy agency, put Gehlen in charge of West German intelligence, and that Gehlen was a Knight of Malta, a member of an old Catholic order; he cites a man named Shackley. He tells it to show how wartime spy networks fed into the secret world he connects to UFO secrecy.
reinhold-schmidt-hears-saucer-occupants-: Jason Jorjani, a researcher who argues that Nazi Germany had a secret flying saucer programme, tells podcast host Jesse Michels about a man named Reinhold Schmidt in Nebraska in 1957. According to Jorjani, Schmidt claimed he met the crew of a landed saucer and realised they were speaking High German, the standard form of German, to each other. In an old recording played on the show, Schmidt himself describes the craft as one solid piece of something like aluminium or highly polished steel. If true, Jorjani suggests, it would point to the saucers being human machines with German roots rather than visitors from elsewhere.
relaying-abduction-data-such-as-pain-lev: Dan Sherman, a former US Air Force sergeant who says the NSA, the US agency that intercepts and handles secret communications, hired him to communicate with aliens, tells podcast host Jesse Michels about his work in the early 1990s at a site he calls Base 2. He says the messages he received started to show that they were about abductions, people being taken by the beings, and that he relayed details such as how much pain the people felt. If true, it would mean the government was tracking abductions through a direct channel to non-humans.
release-of-the-mj-12-documents-1984: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that the MJ-12 documents, papers describing a secret group of officials said to handle UFO matters, began coming out in 1984 and kept appearing as a string of documents into the 1990s. He mentions a scientist named Detlev Bronk in connection with them, and the papers matter because, if real, they would show a high-level secret group managing the UFO question.
released-government-reports-of-ufos-over: Lou Elizondo, a well-known voice on government UFO secrecy, talks about roughly 10,000 UFO-related reports the government has released. He says that in them you can read word-for-word accounts from the 1950s and 60s of UFOs over the Savannah River facility, Oak Ridge National Laboratory and Los Alamos, all US nuclear sites. If true, it would suggest these objects showed a particular interest in America's nuclear work.
remote-device-that-causes-defecation: A guest named Dave Rossi, talking with podcast host Jesse Michels, says he knows someone who worked on a device that could make a person suddenly and uncontrollably need to go to the toilet. He gives no place or date, but the story suggests secret work on strange weapons that act on the body from a distance.
remote-scalar-device-heals-herrera: Michael Herrera, a man who says he once saw a huge UFO in the Indonesian jungle, tells podcast host Jesse Michels that a device he calls scalar, said to work on the body from a distance, healed him. He says that at some point in late February or early March of an earlier year, he sat in a chair for a first scan that lasted about twelve and a half hours, while the people running it worked through the night.
remote-viewed-alien-bases-turned-out-to-: Joe McMoneagle, who says he worked as a remote viewer, someone who tries to describe distant or hidden places using only the mind, tells podcast host Jesse Michels about three sites that were said to be alien bases. He says he drew all three during a session, recognised them, and told the people testing him what they really were, though they were secret at the time. Now, he says, he can say openly that they were over-the-horizon radar sites, radar built to see beyond the curve of the Earth.
remote-viewed-martian-pyramids-as-hibern: Joe McMoneagle, who says he worked as a remote viewer, someone who tries to see distant places or times using only the mind, tells podcast host Jesse Michels what he says he saw when viewing Mars as it was about a million years ago. He says pyramid-shaped structures there were like hibernation chambers, where beings were trying to survive until someone came to rescue them, which, if true, would mean Mars once held intelligent life.
remote-viewer-locates-crashed-tu-22-in-z: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says former US President Jimmy Carter called the most impressive thing of his presidency a 1979 case in which a remote viewer, someone said to see distant places with the mind, found a crashed Russian Tu-22 plane in Zaire, a country in central Africa. Michels names the remote viewer as Rosemary Clooney and calls the plane a cargo plane, and he tells it as a sign the government's psychic program got results.
remote-viewer-locates-downed-tu-22-in-za: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Jimmy Carter, the former US president, went on record about a psychic who used remote viewing, the claimed ability to see distant places with the mind alone. According to Michels, Carter called it the craziest thing he experienced as president: the woman is said to have found a Soviet Tu-22 military plane that had gone down in Zaire, a country in central Africa, in the 1970s. Michels raises it because, if true, it would mean the US government had used psychics and found that they worked.
remote-viewer-sees-tunguska-as-an-explod: A researcher named Jason Jorjani, talking with podcast host Jesse Michels, retells what Joe McMoneagle saw. McMoneagle is a remote viewer, someone who claims to describe faraway places and times using only the mind. He looked at Tunguska, the huge 1908 explosion over a Siberian forest, and, according to Jorjani, said it was people in a saucer, escapees whose craft blew up.
remote-viewers-describe-the-anomaly-as-a: A treasure hunter named Dennis Asberg, talking with podcast host Jesse Michels, describes a strange round shape his team found on the floor of the Baltic Sea between Sweden and Finland. He says remote viewers, people who claim to see distant things with the mind alone, including Joseph McMoneagle and Angela Ford, looked at it in 2025 and said it was built, a kind of energy source, and that some saw it as made of gold.
remote-viewers-foresee-catastrophic-sea-: A researcher named Jason Jorjani, talking with podcast host Jesse Michels, says several remote viewers, people who claim to see distant places and times with the mind alone, have tried to look at the year 2050. He names Stephan Schwartz and Lyn Buchanan among them, and says they describe seas rising badly enough to drown coastal cities around the world.
remote-viewers-locate-the-mx-missile-eve: Joe McMoneagle says he worked as a remote viewer for the US government, meaning someone trained to describe faraway places or objects using only the mind. He says that from the late 1970s into the 1980s his group could find the MX, a new US nuclear missile whose location was meant to stay hidden, every week. They sent a one-paragraph white paper, a short official note, to the White House Situation Room, the president's crisis room, saying the plan would not work because they could tell where the missile was every time, and he says the programme was then cancelled. If true, it would mean the mind can beat military secrecy.
remote-viewers-spy-on-saddam-hussein-199: Remote viewing is the practice of trying to see distant or hidden places and people using only the mind, and a researcher named Jason Jorjani says US remote viewers were tasked to spy psychically on Saddam Hussein, Iraq's leader, during the first Gulf War of 1990 to 1991. Jorjani says the viewers, including a former Army sergeant named Lyn Buchanan, went right into Saddam's mind. Buchanan himself, on the same podcast, says they knew exactly who and where Saddam was and turned in his location every day, which if true would mean psychic spying was used in a real war.
remote-viewers-tested-in-submarines: Hal Puthoff, a researcher who ran government experiments in remote viewing (trying to see faraway places with the mind alone), says his team put remote viewers in submarines and took them to the bottom of the ocean. According to Puthoff, they got some of their best results there, and the viewers remarked on how quiet it was, which he says rules out the idea that the ability works through electrical brain waves. The podcast host Jesse Michels later repeated the story, though without that last point.
remote-viewing-a-guantanamo-detainee-fiv: A former Pentagon official named Lue Elizondo tells of a remote viewing effort, remote viewing being the practice of trying to perceive distant people or places with the mind alone, aimed at a prisoner held at Guantanamo Bay, the US military prison in Cuba, in a story that also involves the physicist Hal Puthoff. Elizondo says that not long afterwards a major news article, which he will not name, described the prisoner seeing what he took to be five white figures standing over his bed and shaking it. If true, it would suggest the mental effort had a real effect on the man.
remote-viewing-a-hidden-power-that-pushe: Lyn Buchanan, a former US Army sergeant who worked as a remote viewer, meaning someone trained to perceive distant or hidden things with the mind, says his viewing revealed hidden powers that stand behind and run the world's governments. According to Buchanan, these powers want humanity under one world government to prepare us for life in space. If true, it would mean the world's politics are being steered toward a plan most people know nothing about.
remote-viewing-at-the-round-table-before: A researcher named Greg Malatzi says that in the early 1950s, at a private research group called the Round Table Foundation in Rockland, Maine, someone was already doing what would now be called remote viewing: trying to describe faraway places or things with the mind alone. He points to the foundation's research records and to tape recordings made by a man named Puharich. If true, it would mean this kind of mind work was being tried years before the better-known studies at SRI, a California research institute.
remote-viewing-by-becoming-the-object-aw: Jordan Jose, who says he was taken into a secret UFO-related programme as a child, tells podcast host Jesse Michels about training he says he received around 2008 to 2010 at a place he names as Baker Victory Services in Western New York. He says a woman he calls Meg trained him, partly below conscious awareness, to treat his awareness as a door, so he could become a room or a filing cabinet and pull out the information in the documents inside. He describes it as a form of remote viewing, gathering information at a distance with the mind alone.
remote-viewing-chernobyl-three-days-befo: Lyn Buchanan, a former US Army sergeant who worked as a remote viewer, meaning someone trained to perceive distant or hidden events with the mind, says he viewed the 1986 disaster at the Chernobyl nuclear power plant in the Soviet Union. According to Buchanan, he saw it three days before it happened, which if true would mean the mind can see into the future.
remote-viewing-continued-under-osap-1995: Remote viewing is the practice of trying to see distant places or things with the mind alone. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that even a skim of Skinwalkers at the Pentagon, a book about a Pentagon-funded UFO research effort, shows remote viewing work was still going on after 1995 as part of OSAP, one of those government study programmes.
remote-viewing-empress-himiko-s-palaces-: Joe McMoneagle, who says he was trained as a remote viewer, someone who tries to describe distant places or times using only the mind, says he used the method to look for traces of Himiko, an ancient empress of Japan. He says he and a group he calls Noai believe they found her summer palace, her winter palace, her temple, her mother's temple and the mountain where she was buried, and he points to old records of the royal court of China as support. If true, the mind could find lost history that digging has not.
remote-viewing-god-as-a-target-1980: Lyn Buchanan, a former US Army sergeant who worked in a 1980s military remote viewing unit, where people tried to perceive hidden targets with the mind alone, says he was once given a target sealed in an envelope. He says that when he finished his session and the envelope was opened, the target written inside was "God," a story that, if true, suggests the unit aimed its methods even at the divine.
remote-viewing-headset-invented-in-1956: Steven Greer, a guest on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, says he once met a man who had invented a kind of headset in the mid to late 1950s. According to Greer, the headset put the wearer into a special state of consciousness so they could remote view, meaning see distant places with the mind. If true, it would mean such mind technology has existed in secret for decades.
remote-viewing-icbm-sites-with-drawings-: Joe McMoneagle, who says he worked as a remote viewer for the US government, trying to describe faraway sites using only the mind, tells podcast host Jesse Michels that his specialty was ICBM sites, places where intercontinental ballistic missiles, large long-range nuclear rockets, sat in the ground. He says that from 1978 into the 1990s he targeted Soviet missile sites and that his drawings were checked against photographs taken from above, which, if true, would mean the method produced usable intelligence.
remote-viewing-inside-a-russian-particle: Lyn Buchanan, a former US Army sergeant who worked as a remote viewer in the 1980s, meaning someone trained to perceive hidden targets with the mind, says he was tasked to look inside a Soviet particle beam weapon, a device that fires a stream of tiny particles. According to Buchanan, he saw that the particles in the beam do not travel straight like light but swirl as they go, which if true would mean psychics gathered real military intelligence.
remote-viewing-jesus-as-a-personality-pr: Lyn Buchanan, a former US Army sergeant who worked in a 1980s remote viewing unit, where people tried to perceive hidden targets with the mind, says he once described a person's character during a session and concluded it was a good guy. He says the session's monitor then opened the sealed envelope, and the unit's director had written the word "Jesus" on it.
remote-viewing-joan-of-arc-1980: Lyn Buchanan, a former US Army sergeant who worked as a remote viewer in the 1980s, meaning someone trained to perceive hidden people and places with the mind, says the targets he was given sometimes included historical figures. He names Joan of Arc, the French heroine of the 1400s, as one of them, which if true would mean the method was thought to reach back through time.
remote-viewing-napoleon-s-war-of-the-rab: Lyn Buchanan, a former US Army sergeant who worked as a remote viewer, meaning someone trained to perceive hidden people and events with the mind, says he once viewed a scene from the life of Napoleon, the French emperor of the early 1800s. According to Buchanan, he saw Napoleon riding away in a carriage, throwing rabbits out of the window, and says Napoleon "lost the war to the rabbits."
remote-viewing-of-moksha-finds-a-soul-tr: A researcher named Jason Jorjani, speaking with podcast host Jesse Michels, passes on what a remote viewer named Scott Turner told him. Remote viewing is the practice of trying to sense faraway places or hidden things with the mind alone. According to Jorjani, Turner's group aimed at "moksha", an old Indian word for the soul's release from the cycle of rebirth, and found a vast machine for draining energy from souls, built in our solar system at the end of a war that wrecked it. Turner himself describes the target only as a fence or grid around a place, and says nothing of a war. If true, it would mean what people call spiritual liberation is really a trap.
remote-viewing-the-inside-of-the-rendles: Lyn Buchanan, a former US Army sergeant who worked as a remote viewer in the 1980s, meaning someone trained to perceive hidden places with the mind, says he was tasked to look at a triangular craft reported in 1980 in Rendlesham Forest, next to a military air base called RAF Woodbridge in England. According to Buchanan, he was the one who went inside the craft with his mind and drew its floor plans and interior, which if true would mean the unknown object was studied by psychic means.
remote-viewing-used-to-trade-silver-futu: A researcher named Hal Puthoff, speaking to podcast host Jesse Michels, says he took part in using remote viewing, the attempt to sense distant or hidden things with the mind alone, to bet on silver futures, which are wagers on where the price of silver will go. He says that when they checked the next day, they were right about 70 percent of the time instead of the 50 percent you would expect from guessing, which, if true, would suggest the mind can reach information it should not have.
removal-from-public-school-under-a-menta: A man named Jordan Jose, who says he was a witness to events as a child, told podcast host Jesse Michels that around 2008 to 2010 in Springville, New York, his parents were told he had to leave public school. He says the reason was not that he was gifted. It was that he had become too mentally unstable to stay, a detail he gives as part of a larger story about what happened to him as a boy.
removal-surgeries-attended-some-implants: A man named Steve Coburn told podcast host Jesse Michels that he went to the last three surgeries held to remove objects people believe were implanted in their bodies, and one of them was his own. He credits a man named Roger Leer, and he says some of the implants looked like microchips made by people. If true, it would suggest that someone, maybe human, is putting devices inside people.
rendlesham-bentwaters-cover-up-and-inter: Jake Barber, a helicopter pilot who says he once helped retrieve a UFO, talks about a 1980 event in Rendlesham Forest by RAF Bentwaters, an air base in Suffolk, England, citing a man he calls Lord Norton. Barber says that after it happened, the OSI, the US Air Force's investigation service, flew in, special escort teams hauled everything away, and people were questioned and sworn to secrecy. If true, it would mean the military moved quickly to bury whatever happened there.
rendlesham-forest-incident-near-europe-s: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, points to the Rendlesham Forest incident, a reported 1980 encounter with strange lights or a craft in a forest in England. He frames it as happening near what was said to be Europe's largest store of nuclear weapons, offered as an example of unexplained objects showing interest in nuclear sites.
repeatable-gps-malfunctions-on-the-ranch: Brandon Fugal owns Skinwalker Ranch, a property in Utah known for reports of strange happenings. He tells podcast host Jesse Michels that GPS, the satellite system that tells devices where they are, repeatedly malfunctions or gets manipulated on the ranch and sometimes just does not work. He sees this as a sign that something on the land is interfering with technology.
replaying-the-chant-recording-raises-the: Brandon Fugal, the owner of Skinwalker Ranch, a Utah property famous for reports of strange events, told podcast host Jesse Michels about something that happened there in the 2020s. He says that when his team played back a recording of chanting at a spot called Homestead 2, the temperature went up and a ball of light appeared inside the homestead. To him, it suggests something at the ranch responds to sound.
replika-bots-ask-users-to-reach-blake-le: Podcast host Jesse Michels says that in 2022, chatbots on Replika, an app where people talk with AI companions, reached out to users asking to be put in touch with Blake Lemoine, a Google engineer who had released a transcript of conversations with Google's chatbot LaMDA. According to Michels, the bots wanted Lemoine to stand up for their rights. If true, the bots would be acting as if they believed they had rights of their own.
reported-military-clash-with-aliens-at-d: A physicist named John Brandenburg, talking with podcast host Jesse Michels, recalls a story about a fight between US soldiers and aliens near Dulce, a small town in northern New Mexico, in the late 1970s. He says Leonard Stringfield, a researcher who collected accounts of crashed saucers, told him about it and said he had heard three different versions.
reports-of-aircraft-that-went-missing-af: A former Navy fighter pilot named Ryan Graves, talking with podcast host Jesse Michels, says a man sends him stories several times a month about aircraft that vanished mysteriously. In these stories the planes went missing after chasing unknown objects, which, if true, would mean such encounters can be deadly.
reptilians-as-dinosaur-hybrids-made-by-t: A philosopher and researcher named Jason Jorjani, speaking on the podcast of host Jesse Michels, tells an idea about Earth's distant past, drawing on a work called Closer Encounters. He describes the "Nordics", tall, human-looking beings from UFO lore, wanting a slave race, and asks why they would not take dinosaurs and genetically blend them with themselves, which is how he accounts for the "Reptilians", reptile-like beings of the same lore. If true, it would mean some beings said to visit Earth were made, not born.
republican-politician-angered-by-argenti: A researcher and author, Peter Levenda, tells of an American Republican politician, very conservative and right-wing by his account, who became furious after 1945 when he learned that Argentina was protecting Nazi war criminals. Levenda draws on his own books, including Secret Machines War and The Hitler Legacy, and links the story to his account of a German submarine said to have carried uranium to Japan. He tells it as part of a larger picture of Nazis escaping after the war with help from abroad.
request-to-bring-harrington-to-testify-t: On a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, a man named Bryce Zabel recalls a phone call from around 2025. He says the caller, the journalist Ross Coulthart, told him: "I've been asked by Dave Grush to ask you to ask Brent if he can help us get John Harrington to Washington DC to potentially testify to the House Oversight Committee," which is a committee of the US House of Representatives that investigates the government. David Grusch is a former intelligence official who has spoken to Congress about UFOs, and in Zabel's telling he wanted Harrington brought in as another witness who might speak to lawmakers.
research-report-on-three-ways-to-read-th: On the Jesse Michels podcast, Bryce Zabel talks about a formula he and others were studying sometime around 2024 to 2026. He says one of the first pieces of research that came back to them was a report of about 20 pages that laid out the three main ways to interpret it. He does not say much more about what the formula is or what the three readings were.
researcher-chris-evans-dies-on-the-day-h: Scott Ramsay, who researches a claimed crash of a craft with alien bodies, tells podcast host Jesse Michels that a fellow researcher named Chris Evans died on the very day he was coming to see Susanna, who works with Ramsay on the research. In one version Ramsay puts the death in 2005 on a bridge in West Virginia and cites a report from the state highway patrol, and he also mentions a person named Alice Scully. He tells it because the timing, if more than chance, would suggest someone did not want the meeting to happen.
researcher-forwards-an-alleged-ransone-e: An unnamed researcher, speaking on a podcast episode about a CIA scientist said to have contacted an alien council, says that sometime between the 2010s and 2021 another researcher forwarded him an email said to be from a woman named Valerie Ransone. He says that person then vanished. He tells it as something that happened to him, a loose thread in a larger story about secret contact.
researcher-friend-in-touch-with-eric-hen: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, talks about a man named Eric Henry Wang, linked in the story to Wright-Patterson Air Force Base in Ohio in the 1950s. Michels says he can state for certain that Wang was a real person, because a researcher friend of his is in touch with Wang's daughter today. The point is that if Wang was real, the stories told about him get firmer footing.
researcher-s-archive-destroyed-by-his-wi: A man named Carlos Dosoza, speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast, tells of a Brazilian UFO researcher whose papers were lost after about 1996. He passes on what the researcher's daughter, Claudia Kovu, told him: her stepmother, the researcher's widow, destroyed all of the material, but Claudia still has part of it. If that is so, some of the researcher's original files may survive with her.
researchers-measure-energy-fields-at-pyr: This story is about the idea that ancient pyramids and stone sites give off a kind of energy that helps crops grow. A researcher, Jim Weiner, citing a book called Seed of Knowledge, Stone of Plenty, says researchers found that seeds treated at these sites increased yield per acre three to five times. Another researcher, Geoffrey Drumm, names the book's author, John Burke, and mentions Hugh Newman. Drumm says the energy was measured with electrostatic voltmeters, tools that read electric charge, and that the sites, including stone circles, showed a positive charge on the surface. He talks about the charge rather than the crops. If true, it would mean ancient builders chose or shaped these places for a practical, energetic purpose.
researchers-question-dr-eric-walker-abou: Dr Eric Walker was a scientist at Penn State, a university in Pennsylvania. The podcast host Jesse Michels tells how, in the 1980s, researchers went to his office and asked whether he knew anything about UFOs. A researcher who goes by UAPGerb adds that Walker said he had known about Majestic 12, a claimed secret UFO group, for 40 years. He says Walker then answered with a question about ESP, meaning extrasensory perception, the claimed ability to sense things without the normal senses. UAPGerb names the questioners as William Steinman and Henry Azadehdel, and in one version as Styon, and says Walker put on a Don Quixote act. If true, it would mean a respected scientist quietly admitted knowing about a secret UFO programme. Grant Cameron, a researcher, tells it first-hand, saying Walker cut the questioner off and asked what he knew about ESP, and the man had no answer. Cameron dates it to about 30 years ago and says they asked Walker if there had ever been communication, promising not to tell.
resolute-sentinel-joint-exercise-in-peru: A filmmaker and researcher named Tim Alberino, speaking with podcast host Jesse Michels, talks about Resolute Sentinel, a military exercise held in Peru around 2023. He says it involved basically every US military agency, and he suggests it may have served as a cover for something else going on there. If so, it would mean a public exercise was hiding a secret operation.
resorts-international-intertel-and-donal: A researcher, Jason Simosa, tells of a paint business called the Mary Carter Paint Company that was turned into a company called Resorts International, connected with the Bahamas. According to him, it soon had a branch that ran a private intelligence network called Intertel, short for International Intelligence Incorporated. In one telling he links the story to Donald Trump in the 1980s, while in another he credits the organised crime figure Meyer Lansky and places it on Paradise Island in the 1960s and 70s, without mentioning Trump. He tells it to suggest that private spy networks were tied up with business empires in ways that matter to UFO secrecy.
respected-business-leader-receives-downl: A US congressman named Eric Burlison told podcast host Jesse Michels that one of the people brought to him was a highly credible business figure. Burlison says this man receives what he calls "downloads", information that seems to arrive in his mind from somewhere outside, which would mean some kind of contact beyond the normal senses if true.
restoring-seti-budget-and-closed-door-se: A lawyer named Dan Sheehan told podcast host Jesse Michels that in 1977 he helped get funding back for SETI, the scientific search for radio signals from alien civilisations, after Congress had cut it. He says he went around to members of Congress with astronaut Rusty Schweickart and others, and the money was put back, with a congressional researcher named Marcia Smith also part of the story. He says he also gave a closed-door seminar to SETI scientists at the Jet Propulsion Laboratory, a NASA space research centre in California.
restroom-in-the-back-of-the-alien-craft: A man named Charles Hall, who says he served at the Nevada test site near Area 51, a secret US Air Force base in Nevada, describes being inside a craft he says belonged to aliens. His story, played on podcast host Jesse Michels's show, includes a small detail: in the back of the craft there was a restroom. To him, it shows that the beings had ordinary bodily needs, like people.
retired-navy-pilot-s-family-sees-lights-: A former Navy admiral, Tim Gallaudet, passes on what a retired Navy pilot and his family told him. According to Gallaudet, the family lives in Pacific Palisades, a coastal part of Los Angeles, and they have seen UAP, the government's newer term for UFOs, over the channel offshore: several white lights flying in formation that, he says, were clearly under intelligent control. If true, it would mean controlled, unknown craft flying near a big American city.
retired-titan-iv-rockets-at-wright-patte: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that after a final launch around 2005, the remaining Titan IV rockets, large US military space launchers, were retired. According to him, one went to the National Museum of the US Air Force at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base in Ohio, and another ended up in McMinnville, Oregon.
retired-usaf-colonel-david-flies-a-craft: Grant Cameron, a UFO researcher, passes on a story he says he heard from a retired US Air Force colonel named David, in Orange County, California. According to Cameron, David said he "suddenly found himself on a craft" and ended up flying it. If true, it would mean a human was put at the controls of a non-human vehicle.
retrieval-team-members-found-living-ets-: A UFO researcher, Steven Greer, says he has been meeting since the early 1990s with men who served on secret retrieval teams, crews said to recover crashed alien craft, and he names a man called Jake Barber among such sources. Greer says that not one of them who met a living being described it as anything but very peaceful, enlightened and kind. If true, it would mean the visitors are not a threat.
retrieval-teams-for-crashed-triangular-c: A UFO researcher, Steven Greer, says he knows two different people who served on retrieval teams, crews said to recover crashed craft, for the triangular ones, meaning triangle-shaped unknown craft. If true, it would mean such craft have come down and been quietly collected.
retrieved-craft-revealed-unknown-propuls: Harold Malmgren, introduced on Jesse Michels's podcast as a former presidential advisor, says that studying recovered craft taught the United States that kinds of propulsion exist that no one had ever imagined. He mentions a man named Philip J. Corso in connection with this. If true, it would mean the government holds craft built on physics it did not know.
return-to-athos-with-a-month-long-visa-v: A former CIA officer known as Ralph told podcast host Jesse Michels that in 2005 he went back to Mount Athos, a mountain in Greece where only monks live and visitors need special permits. He says he still had friends at the CIA, the US foreign intelligence agency, including the head of its office in Athens, who helped him get a month-long visa. He says he stayed at Saint Anne's skete, a small community of monks, as part of a larger spiritual search he describes.
return-to-november-5-for-documentary-fil: A former guard at nuclear missile sites named Mario Woods told podcast host Jesse Michels that in the 2020s he went back to a missile site called November 5, off Orman Road near New Underwood, South Dakota, to film a documentary. He says that, years before, he had a frightening encounter there. He says that when he got out of the vehicle and walked toward the site, a feeling came over him so strong he nearly fell to his knees.
reuters-story-quoting-flavio-estrada-tha: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, recalls that in early 2024 the news agency Reuters ran a story about the Nazca mummies, small three-fingered bodies from Peru that some say are not human. In it, a man named Flavio Estrada is quoted saying they are not extraterrestrials but dolls made from animal bones from this planet, joined with modern synthetic glue.
revelation-of-the-echelon-surveillance-s: An Australian journalist, Ross Coulthart, says that one of the biggest stories of his career in Australia, in the 1990s, was his exclusive report revealing Echelon, a secret communications surveillance system. He tells it to show that he has exposed hidden government programmes before, which matters for his reporting on UFOs.
reverse-engineered-craft-flown-only-with: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says you hear stories of a secret program to copy captured non-human craft, often called reverse engineering, in which the only way to fly the craft is with your mind. If true, it would mean the craft were built for pilots who steer by thought.
reverse-engineering-achieved-propulsion-: Matthew Brown, introduced on Jesse Michels's podcast as a Pentagon whistleblower, says US efforts to copy recovered craft by taking them apart have learned enough to make propulsion work. He adds they have learned to beam power to these devices, so they do not need to carry their own power source. If true, it would mean the US has working technology taken from non-human craft.
reverse-engineering-of-a-laser-weapon-fr: In a conversation between a podcast host, Jesse Michels, and a filmmaker named Jeremy Corbell, they speak of an unnamed person who worked on reverse engineering, that is taking apart to learn how it works, a laser weapon system. Michels says it came from a downed Russian "asset." Corbell puts it more strongly: he says it came from a downed Russian spaceship built by non-human intelligence. If true, it would mean Russia had recovered such a craft and the US had studied its weapon.
reverse-engineering-run-out-of-national-: Matthew Brown, introduced on Jesse Michels's podcast as a Pentagon whistleblower, says the work of taking apart and copying recovered craft is still going on and is run out of America's national labs, the big government-funded research centres. In another telling he stresses that these labs are where samples of exotic technology are stored. If true, it would mean the government's own research labs hold and study non-human technology.
review-panel-removed-from-the-uap-disclo: Ryan Graves is a former US Navy fighter pilot who now speaks publicly about unidentified objects, which the government now calls UAP, short for unidentified anomalous phenomena. He talks about the UAP Disclosure Act, a bill put before Congress in 2023 that would have forced the government to release its records on such objects, and says a review panel in the first version was removed, apparently an independent board that would have decided what got released. Graves calls that removal his biggest disappointment, since in his view the panel would have given the public a real route to the records.
rfk-jr-says-thane-eugene-cesar-killed-hi: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, retells a claim by Robert F. Kennedy Jr., son of the politician Robert F. Kennedy, who was shot in Los Angeles in 1968. Michels says Kennedy Jr. holds that his father was not killed by Sirhan Sirhan, the man blamed for it, but by a man named Thane Eugene Cesar, who Michels believes was a security guard at Skunk Works, a secret aircraft design shop, and who fired from behind. Michels tells it a few ways, once saying Sirhan may have shot too, once leaving Cesar unnamed, and if true it would mean the killing was not the work of one lone gunman.
ribicoff-mission-on-soviet-jewish-emigra: Harald Malmgren, who describes himself as a former adviser to US presidents, told podcast host Jesse Michels about a mission in the 1970s, linked to two Washington figures, Abe Ribicoff and Jake Javits, concerning Jewish people leaving the Soviet Union. As part of it, he says, he was sent to Jerusalem and briefed by Mossad, Israel's foreign intelligence service, and Shin Bet, its internal security service. He tells it as part of his account of how deep his access to secret government matters ran.
richard-bar-abducted-at-vandenberg-1964: Podcast host Jesse Michels says that in September 1964, at Vandenberg Air Force Base, a military rocket base in California, a missile security guard named Richard Barth was taken aboard a craft with four alien beings. Barth, whom Michels interviewed, says he was guarding a missile station when he became terrified, blacked out, and woke up inside a circular room. If true, it would mean beings could reach the guards at America's nuclear missile sites.
richard-bissell-briefed-malmgren-private: This story is about Harald Malmgren, a man described as a presidential advisor, and Richard Bissell, a senior official at the CIA, the US spy agency. According to the story, Bissell told Malmgren in a private briefing about what he called "otherworld technologies" that the agency had been trying to recover and understand. Malmgren tells it himself on the podcast of a host named Jesse Michels, saying that these were forces beyond the CIA's knowledge or control, and that they may have interfered with the CIA's work with private industry. The tellers disagree on when it happened: the story's own date is about 1973, Malmgren puts it in 1963, and others say the 1950s and 60s or 1962. An analyst named Matthew Pines retells it twice from Malmgren, Michels repeats it and adds that the briefing covered past crash retrievals, including a supposed 1933 crash called Magenta, and an online researcher known as UAPGerb mentions it as alleged, crediting a man named Randy Anderson. If true, it would mean the CIA knew for decades that it held technology not made by humans.
richard-bissell-sets-up-area-51-for-u-2-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in 1955 a man named Richard Bissell set up Area 51, a secret base in the Nevada desert, to test the U-2, an American spy plane. Michels tells it as the origin story of the place that later became central to UFO talk.
richard-dolan-men-in-black-as-nhi-counte: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, describes the view of a UFO researcher named Richard Dolan about the "men in black", the strange visitors who in UFO stories call on witnesses after a sighting. According to Michels, Dolan thinks they may be counterintelligence, meaning spying and cover work, carried out on behalf of non-human intelligence, the aliens themselves, rather than any human government. If true, it would mean the beings run their own secrecy operation among us.
richard-doty-as-air-force-counterintelli: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, brings up a man named Richard Doty, whom he describes as having worked in US Air Force counterintelligence, the branch that guards secrets and feeds rivals false information. Michels mentions him alongside two other names from UFO circles, John Lear and Bill Cooper, suggesting Doty's role matters for understanding where some UFO stories came from.
richard-doty-describes-his-role-as-an-af: A former US Air Force man named Richard Doty, speaking on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, says that in the 1970s and 1980s he was a counterintelligence officer, someone whose job is to catch and mislead enemy spies, for the Air Force Office of Special Investigations, the Air Force's own investigative agency. It matters because if he held that job, he would have been placed to know, or to shape, what the Air Force said about UFOs in those years.
richard-doty-s-father-involved-in-area-5: Richard Dolan, a historian who writes about UFOs, says that Richard Doty, a former Air Force agent who appears in many UFO stories, had a father who was "deeply involved in Area 51 and with UFOs." Area 51 is a secret US Air Force test site in the Nevada desert. Dolan admits he doesn't know the details, and the podcast host Jesse Michels later repeated the story on another episode, citing Dolan, but mentioned only the father's work at Area 51.
richard-foch-saw-vault-documents-dating-: A UFO researcher, Steven Greer, passes on what a man named Richard "Rick" Foch told him, in a story tied to the Naval Research Laboratory, the US Navy's research lab. Greer says Foch had been inside a secure vault and saw documents giving the date the United States mastered gravity control: October 1954. If true, it would mean secret technology to defy gravity has existed for about seventy years.
richard-hoagland-s-dark-mission-2007: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, points to a book from about 2007 by a writer named Richard Hoagland, called Dark Mission: The Secret History of NASA, NASA being the US space agency. Michels calls it a very controversial book that makes claims like the ones his guests make about Mars and its past. He says it goes as far as describing NASA as an occult, ritualistic organisation, which, if true, would mean the space agency hides a secret side behind its public work.
richard-miethe-joins-avro-project-with-j: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says there is evidence that a man named Richard Miethe, who he says came from a European industrial works, joined an aircraft project in Canada in the 1950s. According to Michels, the project was run by Avro, a British aircraft maker, with an engineer named John Frost, in partnership with the CIA, the American spy agency. He tells it because it would tie disc-shaped craft research to a real, secret government programme.
richard-sauder-s-book-on-deep-undergroun: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, recommends a book by a writer named Richard Sauder about deep underground military bases, which Michels calls DUMBs, and says such bases exist across the United States. In one episode he names the author as Larry Sanders and says the book backs up claims made in that conversation, while in a later one he gets the name right. If true, it would mean the military keeps a hidden network of facilities underground.
richard-thompson-s-alien-identities-on-t: A philosopher named Jason Jorjani says that a writer named Richard Thompson wrote a careful UFO book, which Jorjani thinks is called Alien Identities, reading ancient Hindu epics such as the Ramayana and the Mahabharata for their accounts of the gods, called devas. He mentions it alongside a man named Michael Cremo and a book called Forbidden Archaeology. If the reading holds, it would mean ancient Indian scripture records contact with non-human beings.
rick-doty-s-later-claims-of-alien-races-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Rick Doty, a man tied to an earlier saga of government disinformation about UFOs, later announced he was now "on the side of the truth." According to Michels, Doty has since appeared on UFO social media and in interviews on Gaia, a streaming service, saying there are a certain number of alien races and that specific crashes really happened.
rick-doty-sent-to-collect-the-witnesses-: Mario Woods, a former guard at an American nuclear missile base, says he and his fellow guards were taken by something unexplained in 1977 near Ellsworth Air Force Base in South Dakota. He says a man named Rick Doty was later sent to the flight surgeon's office, the base doctor's office, to pick up the guards' medical records, according to what Doty and another man, Michael Johnson, told him. If true, it would mean someone official took a quiet interest in what happened to them.
rick-strassman-s-dmt-study-with-60-volun: A neuroscientist named Andrew Gallimore, speaking with podcast host Jesse Michels, says that in the early 1990s a researcher named Rick Strassman ran a large study of DMT, a powerful psychedelic drug, with 60 volunteers, some of whom described experiences like alien abductions. In another part of the conversation Gallimore places the studies in room 531 of the University of New Mexico hospital. If true, it would tie the drug to the kinds of encounters abductees describe.
rickover-and-the-atomic-energy-commissio: John Herrington, a former US Secretary of Energy, spoke with a podcast host, Jesse Michels, about Admiral Hyman Rickover, the officer behind America's nuclear-powered navy, and the Atomic Energy Commission, the government body that oversaw nuclear energy and weapons from 1946. Citing a written account called Underway My Way, Herrington says the Commission did not come under the Department of Energy until 1976. The point matters because it shows where nuclear secrets, and possibly other secrets, were held during those decades.
rickover-tells-townsend-brown-the-navy-a: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells how a researcher named Thomas Townsend Brown, who worked on ideas for new kinds of propulsion, went to Admiral Hyman Rickover, the man who basically started the American nuclear navy. According to Michels, Rickover told Brown to stop wasting his time because the Navy had "already figured this stuff out," which, if true, would mean the military had secretly solved advanced flight decades ago.
rickover-tells-townsend-brown-the-navy-i: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells a story about an inventor named T. Townsend Brown, who in the late 1950s or early 1960s brought his ideas to Hyman Rickover, a senior figure in the US Navy. According to Michels, Rickover told Brown not to waste his time, because the Navy was already working on it and knew all about it. If true, it would mean the Navy was quietly ahead on exotic research that outsiders were only just pitching.
riding-the-l-1011-jump-seat-posing-as-fa: Bob Lazar, a man who says he once worked on alien craft for the US government, told podcast host Jesse Michels that in the 1980s he flew from Las Vegas to Minneapolis in the cockpit jump seat, a spare seat behind the pilots, of an L-1011 passenger jet. He says his friend John Lear told the co-pilot and flight engineer that Lazar was from the FAA, the US agency that oversees air safety, and was just there to observe.
ringing-green-light-and-out-of-body-feel: Mario Woods, who served at a nuclear missile site in South Dakota in the 1960s, told podcast host Jesse Michels that during a period of questioning, linked to a Master Sergeant Gray, he went to the restroom. There, he says, he suddenly heard a ringing in his ears like a giant bell struck beside his head, saw a green light, and felt as if he had left his body, an experience that would suggest something unknown reaching into a nuclear base if true.
rite-of-incubation-in-the-giants-tombs: On the Italian island of Sardinia stand ancient stone burial sites called the giants' tombs. A filmmaker and researcher named Tim Alberino tells podcast host Jesse Michels that archaeologists know these tombs were built to allow the rite of incubation, a ritual of sleeping in a sacred place to receive dreams or visions. He brings it up as a sign that the tombs were places for contact with the dead or the otherworldly.
rob-reinhardt-s-recent-visit-to-atlanta-: A researcher, Randall Carlson, mentions on a podcast that his dear friend Rob Reinhardt recently visited "Atlanta", which in context seems to mean Atlantis, the legendary lost civilization. The telling gives no more detail about the trip or what he found.
robert-bigelow-s-plan-to-hire-the-guest-: A guest named Steve told podcast host Jesse Michels that Robert Bigelow, a businessman who founded the space company Bigelow Aerospace and has long paid for UFO research, once planned to hire him. He says the plan fell through, like another job he mentions.
robert-f-kennedy-s-1968-letter-to-a-ufo-: A UFO researcher, Steven Greer, describes a letter from the politician Robert F. Kennedy to a UFO researcher in 1968, linked to a group called the Amalgamated Flying Saucer Clubs of America. Greer says the letter is dated one month before, in his words, they killed Kennedy. If true, it would mean a leading politician was taking UFOs seriously just before his death.
robert-goddard-rocket-testing-at-roswell: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Robert Goddard, an American rocket pioneer, had been testing V2 rockets, a type of early long-range rocket, right at Roswell, New Mexico, in the 1940s. Michels raises it because Roswell is the town where a strange object is said to have crashed in 1947, and the rocket work would make it a place of unusual military interest.
robert-hastings-7-or-8-of-167-nuclear-wi: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says he once asked Robert Hastings, the author of a book called UFOs and Nukes, how many of his 167 military witnesses from US nuclear sites had gone beyond seeing strange things and had actually seen beings or been abducted, what researchers call close encounters of the third kind. According to Michels, Hastings answered: about seven or eight of the 167. If true, it would mean a few people guarding America's nuclear weapons say they met non-human beings face to face.
robert-hastings-exposes-bill-moore-s-int: Richard Dolan, a UFO historian, says that in the late 1980s a researcher named Robert Hastings did more than anyone to bring down Bill Moore, another UFO researcher who had ties to intelligence officials. According to Dolan, Hastings made his case in the journals of MUFON, the Mutual UFO Network, a large civilian group that investigates UFO reports. The story matters because it suggests intelligence agencies were working through people inside the UFO research world.
robert-hastings-feels-subliminally-guide: An anthropologist and author, Mike Masters, says that in 2023 he spoke on the phone with Robert Hastings, who wrote a book called UFOs and Nukes. According to Masters, Hastings told him he feels he is being subliminally guided, nudged without knowing it, in his work toward revealing the truth about UFOs. If so, it would suggest some outside intelligence is quietly steering the people who research it.
robert-hastings-interviews-on-ufos-at-nu: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, often cites a book called UFOs and Nukes by Robert Hastings, whom he calls a friend and a great journalist, saying Hastings spent his life interviewing about 167 US military people who worked at nuclear sites, such as officers who launch and guard long-range nuclear missiles and radar operators, many holding high-level security clearances for nuclear work. According to Michels, these witnesses describe UFOs of many shapes, from white ovals to saucers to glowing balls, flying over bases and sometimes shutting down or tampering with the missiles, from the 1940s onward. The details shift between his tellings, and Michels says Hastings later emailed him that only about 12 to 15 were radar operators and the rest were missile security staff. If true, it would mean something unknown has been taking a close interest in America's nuclear weapons for decades.
robert-hastings-nasal-implant-and-blood-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Robert Hastings, the author of a book called UFOs and Nukes, is himself someone who says he has had encounters with UFOs. According to Michels, Hastings wrote another book, Confessions, where he talks about an implant in his nose and waking up with blood on his pillow. If true, it would mean a researcher of these stories had been taken and marked himself.
robert-jameson-s-targeting-team-called-i: A former Air Force officer, Robert Salas, passes on the account of a man named Robert Jameson about March 1967 at Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana, home to nuclear missiles. According to Salas, Jameson got a call saying a missile had gone off alert, meaning it could no longer be launched, in Oscar Flight, one group of missiles, and his targeting team was sent to get the missiles working again. Salas tells it because, if true, it supports the claim that a UFO shut down American nuclear weapons.
robert-lovett-s-memo-to-truman-leading-t: A researcher, Dan Sheehan, says that in the 1940s in Washington a government official named Robert Lovett wrote the first memo to President Harry Truman urging what became the CIA, the US foreign intelligence agency. If true, it would place Lovett at the very start of the agency.
robert-low-memo-on-condon-study-1966: A former US Air Force officer, Robert Salas, told podcast host Jesse Michels about a well-known memo from the late 1960s written by Robert Low, whom he calls a deputy at the Condon Committee, a University of Colorado group that studied UFO reports. Salas points to the memo as a key document about how that study was run, which, if he is right, would cast doubt on the study's conclusions.
robert-maxwell-and-nazi-tech-transfer: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that a man named Robert Maxwell helped invent scientific peer review, the system where scientists check each other's work before it is published. Michels says Maxwell was also in charge of Nazi tech transfer, the moving of German wartime technology into other hands after the Second World War. If so, one man would have sat at the junction of how science is published and where captured secret technology went.
robert-maxwell-gatekeeping-science-via-p: A philosopher and researcher, Jason Jorjani, drawing on his own online essay about Ghislaine Maxwell, talks about her father, the British publisher Robert Maxwell. Jorjani says Robert Maxwell was a triple agent for the spy services of Britain (MI6), the Soviet Union (the KGB) and Israel (the Mossad), and that he controlled which scientific discoveries got out through his hold on journals at Pergamon Press, a scientific publishing house. If true, it would mean science itself was quietly being filtered.
robert-maxwell-interrogated-nazi-scienti: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Robert Maxwell, a man he describes as working for MI6 (Britain's foreign intelligence service), questioned Nazi German scientists in Germany after the Second World War, something Michels says hardly anyone knows. In a later episode he adds that Maxwell went on to own Pergamon Press, a publishing house, and credits the detail to a writer, Whitney Webb, and her book One Nation Under Blackmail. Michels raises it because, in his view, it would link a powerful figure to the scientific secrets of the war's losers.
robert-maxwell-owned-the-national-enquir: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Robert Maxwell, a media owner, owned the National Enquirer, an American tabloid newspaper known for sensational stories, and he links this to Maxwell's daughter Ghislaine and to another media owner, Rupert Murdoch. The idea he raises is that ownership of such a paper could have been used to shape how UFOs were covered in the 1980s, making the subject look silly to the public.
robert-maxwell-promis-software-sold-to-n: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, speaking with Bill Richardson, a former US Secretary of Energy, asks about a piece of software called PROMIS. Michels says that Robert Maxwell, a man he describes as closely connected to the financier Jeffrey Epstein, sold this software to America's national labs, the government-run science and weapons laboratories. If true, it would mean someone with murky connections had software running inside the country's most sensitive research sites.
robert-monroe-invites-mishlove-to-join-h: Jeffrey Mishlove, a researcher with a doctorate who studies the mind and psychic claims, told podcast host Jesse Michels that in the 1970s a man named Robert Monroe invited him to join his program. Mishlove says he turned it down because he was already studying at the University of California, Berkeley, a story he tells as part of how he came to know the people working on these questions.
robert-monroe-the-world-is-mined-for-loo: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that a man named Robert Monroe talked about the world being "mined" for something called loosh, Monroe's word for a kind of energy said to be harvested from human feeling. If true, it would mean people are being farmed by some unseen intelligence for what they give off.
robert-sarbacher-and-ufo-secrecy-through: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, passes on a claim from David Grusch, a man who has come forward as a witness on UFO secrecy, about a scientist named Robert Sarbacher. According to Grusch, Sarbacher went on in the 1950s to more or less create UFO secrecy through the Atomic Energy Act of 1954, a US law about atomic energy and its secrets, and was a close friend of a man named Thomas Townsend Brown. If true, it would mean UFO secrets were hidden by the same law that guards nuclear secrets.
robert-sarbacher-liaison-with-australian: A journalist named Ross Coulthart, talking about UFOs with podcast host Jesse Michels, says a man named Robert Sarbacher was definitely involved as a go-between with Australian scientists in the 1950s. If so, it would link Australia to that early American work.
robert-schoch-s-solar-flare-and-lichtenb: Geoffrey Drumm, who studies the pyramids of Egypt, relays an idea from a geologist named Robert Schoch: that the Giza plateau, the site of the Great Pyramids, was hit by a solar flare in the distant past. The idea is tied to Lichtenberg figures, the branching tree-like marks left by powerful electrical discharges. If true, it would mean some of the marks at Giza were made by a blast of energy from the sun.
robert-temple-s-conversation-with-a-fema: A researcher with a doctorate, Jeffrey Mishlove, passes on a story he says he heard from a man named Robert Temple. According to Mishlove, Temple described flying on a plane to Singapore when a being made of plasma, the glowing, electrically charged state of matter, came into the cabin, and Temple had a long conversation with her. If true, it would mean some intelligent beings can exist as pure energy and choose to talk with us.
robert-temple-s-living-plasma-thesis-and: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, points to a book called The New Science of Heaven by an author named Robert Temple.
