According to Michels, Temple argues that plasma, the electrically charged gas found in things like lightning and stars, is the basic stuff of the universe and is itself alive. If that were so, Michels suggests, intelligence could exist in forms we hardly think to look for.
roberto-pinotti-s-book-and-the-1933-blac: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, points to a book by an Italian researcher, Roberto Pinotti, about telegrams said to come from Italy's Fascist government in 1933. Pinotti quotes one as saying that, by personal order of Mussolini, Italy's dictator, nothing at all may be said about the reported landing of an unknown aircraft on Italian soil, and he links the telegrams to the Stefani agency, the country's news agency of that era. If true, it would mean a government was hiding a strange landing well before UFOs became a public topic.
robertson-panel-adopts-a-policy-of-ridic: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that the Robertson panel, a 1953 group named for a scientist, H.P. Robertson, that reviewed UFO reports for the US government, deliberately adopted a policy of ridiculing the subject. He cites the panel's report as the source. If true, it would mean the stigma around UFOs in America was partly built on purpose.
robertson-panel-aim-to-debunk-sightings-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, points to papers from the Robertson Panel, a 1953 government panel whose report was classified at the time. He says the documents show that Project Blue Book, the US Air Force's UFO study of the 1950s and 60s, had the explicit aim of throwing the public off and downplaying, suppressing and explaining away UFO sightings. Elsewhere, citing the physicist Hal Puthoff, he puts the reason differently: a fear that the subject would set off mass hysteria.
robertson-panel-directive-to-watch-and-i: A former US Air Force officer, Robert Salas, told podcast host Jesse Michels that the Robertson Panel, a 1953 government panel that reviewed UFO reports, directed officials to keep an eye on civilian UFO groups. If true, it would mean the government was watching ordinary people who were interested in UFOs, not just studying the sightings.
robertson-panel-recommends-downplaying-u: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that around 1952 and 1953 a physicist from Caltech, a California university, named H.P. Robertson led a panel of academics on UFOs for the US government. According to Michels, the panel concluded that the government should systematically downplay the subject through the media, films and other means, and in one telling he adds that it feared the truth would set off mass hysteria. He tells it as the start of a long official effort to make UFOs seem unworthy of serious attention.
rock-formation-like-a-second-sphinx-head: A researcher named Luke Caverns told podcast host Jesse Michels about a spot on the southeast side of the Giza plateau in Egypt, near the tombs of the pyramid workers and the tomb of an ancient queen named Khentkawes. He says that down in there, a piece of limestone has worn away in such a strange way that, when you walk up to it, it looks like the back of the head of a second Sphinx. To him, it hints that the site may hold more than people think.
rockefeller-files-correspondence-routed-: Grant Cameron, a UFO researcher, says that among the Rockefeller files, papers tied to the wealthy philanthropist Laurance Rockefeller, who pressed the 1990s White House on UFO secrecy, he found two documents he couldn't work out at first. One said that all the letters between Rockefeller and the president's science adviser were going through the mailbox of Hillary Clinton, then the First Lady. If so, it would put her at the center of a White House inquiry into UFOs.
rockefeller-funding-intercepted-by-cia-n: Steven Greer, a campaigner who pushes for governments to reveal what they know about UFOs, told podcast host Jesse Michels that in the 1990s the wealthy Laurence Rockefeller tried early on to fund the effort. Greer says the money was intercepted by people on Rockefeller's own team who were secretly CIA officers working under non-official cover, meaning posing as private citizens, which if true would mean the spy agency was quietly steering the push for disclosure.
rockefeller-pressure-leads-the-clinton-a: A documentary filmmaker, James Fox, says that in the 1990s the wealthy philanthropist Lawrence Rockefeller pressed President Bill Clinton's White House to look into Roswell, the 1947 New Mexico event often said to involve a crashed UFO. According to Fox, John Podesta, a senior Clinton aide, told him Clinton was unhappy with the answers he got and felt he was being given the runaround. If true, it would mean even a sitting president could not get straight answers about UFOs from his own government.
rockefeller-s-panel-meets-at-quantico-19: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in 1955 a group led by Nelson Rockefeller, a powerful political figure, first met at Quantico, a military base in Virginia, to draft reports for President Eisenhower. Michels tells it in an episode asking whether Henry Kissinger oversaw a programme to recover crashed unidentified craft, so the meeting would be an early link in that chain if true.
rockefeller-serves-breakfast-and-vows-to: Grant Cameron, a UFO researcher, passes on a story he heard from Budd Hopkins, a man who studied people who said aliens had taken them. Hopkins said that in the 1990s he and two fellow researchers, David Jacobs and John Mack, went to the house of the billionaire Laurence Rockefeller, who served them breakfast like a butler and told them, "I'm going to get disclosure," meaning an official release of what the government knows about UFOs. If true, it would show a very rich and well-connected man personally pushing for that release.
rockefellers-fund-greer-mack-and-the-pri: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that the wealthy Rockefeller family, and Laurance Rockefeller in particular, quietly paid for a lot of UFO research in the 1990s. According to Michels, the money went to Steven Greer, a disclosure campaigner, to John Mack, a Harvard psychiatrist who studied people reporting alien abductions, to the writer Whitley Strieber, and to a lab at Princeton University that studied whether the mind can affect matter. He tells it because it would mean one of America's richest families was backing the subject behind the scenes.
rod-serling-s-film-and-the-footage-edwar: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Rod Serling, a writer he describes as his own father's godfather, made a film called UFOs Past, Present and Future around 1974. Michels says he thinks Edwards Air Force Base, a US military base in California, reached out to Serling and promised him footage of a UFO, which would mean the military was ready to show the public real evidence.
roddenberry-s-script-the-nine-1970: A researcher named Greg, speaking on a podcast, says that in the 1970s the television writer Gene Roddenberry wrote a script called The Nine. He tells it as part of a larger story about a scientist said to have been in contact with a council of non-human beings, suggesting those claims reached Hollywood at the time.
rodent-microdialysis-studies-show-dmt-le: A neuroscientist named Andrew Gallimore says on podcast host Jesse Michels's show that in recent lab studies, researchers measured DMT, a powerful psychedelic the body itself can make, in the brains of rodents. According to him, as the animals died, their DMT levels spiked. If true, it would hint that the drug plays a part in what happens at death.
rodri-castle-sees-a-giant-triangle-and-b: A researcher known online as UAPGerb relays the account of Rodri Castle, who in 1997 was a technician on the Harrier, a military jump jet, during Hunter Warrior, a military exercise testing new ways of fighting. According to UAPGerb, Castle was sent to check on unauthorised flares, came upon a huge triangular craft guarded by a "black team", meaning an unmarked security crew, and was held at gunpoint. In another retelling UAPGerb calls him Roger Castle, places it in Nevada, and says he stood about 150 feet from a rotating triangle much like the TR-3B, a secret triangular aircraft rumoured to exist.
rodriguez-paper-proposing-to-test-dmt-en: A neuroscientist named Andrew Gallimore says on podcast host Jesse Michels's show that in the early 2000s a man named Rodriguez published a paper proposing a test for the beings people say they meet on DMT, a powerful psychedelic drug. The idea was to ask them to break a large number into its prime factors, a hard maths problem, to see whether they know things the person taking the drug could not.
rogan-backlash-over-malone-and-mcculloug: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that around 2022 the well-known podcaster Joe Rogan faced a backlash, and that it was because he had two guests on his show, Robert Malone and Peter McCullough. Michels brings it up while talking about how public figures get punished for airing views outside the mainstream.
rogan-s-first-5-meo-dmt-experience: Joe Rogan, a podcast host, told fellow host Jesse Michels about the first time he took 5-MeO-DMT, a very strong psychedelic drug. He says it was so overwhelming that he was sure it had killed him and could not believe it was real.
rogan-s-offline-explanation-of-lazar-s-d: Jesse Michels, a podcast host, says that the popular podcast host Joe Rogan has a habit whenever Bob Lazar comes up. Lazar says he worked on alien craft at a secret site in Nevada in the 1980s, and critics point out that no records show he studied at MIT, the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, as he claims. According to Michels, Rogan always says he'll tell you something off the air that would make the missing MIT records make sense.
rogan-s-possible-childhood-sighting: Joe Rogan, a podcast host, told fellow host Jesse Michels that he wishes he had seen a UFO and thought maybe he did as a child. He adds that he now thinks it was probably just a fighter jet.
rogan-s-reading-on-project-blue-book-hyn: A well-known podcast host, Joe Rogan, says he once got deeply into reading about Project Blue Book, the US Air Force's UFO study of the 1950s and 60s, and about J. Allen Hynek, the astronomer who worked on it. He also says he read the claims of Philip Corso, an Army officer who wrote about crashed alien technology, and material about Roswell, the 1947 New Mexico event said by some to involve a crashed saucer. He tells it to explain how his own interest in the subject began.
rogan-s-vivid-dream-of-slender-pinkish-h: Joe Rogan, a podcast host, told fellow host Jesse Michels about a vivid dream he had at home in 2025, a few weeks before they spoke. He says very slender, tall, humanlike beings were talking to him, and they were not grey but pinkish, like us. He mentions discussing it with Brett Weinstein and returns to the dream more than once in the conversation. He says the feeling he came away with was that someone was trying to get him used to this kind of contact, which would mean beings preparing people for meeting them if taken at face value.
roger-leir-s-implant-extractions: Tim Alberino, a filmmaker, talks about Roger Leir, a surgeon who removed small objects from people that some believed were alien implants. Alberino says his colleague and friend Ellie Marculli worked with Leir and was there when some of these implants were taken out. If true, it would be physical evidence of something put inside people's bodies by non-humans.
roger-leir-s-licence-targeted: Whitley Strieber, a writer known for describing his own encounters with beings, told podcast host Jesse Michels that a man in California named Roger Leir had the same thing happen to him that happened to Strieber. He says they went after Leir and his professional licence, which he presents as a sign that people working on these topics get pushed back against.
roger-leir-s-tapes-and-book-doctors-tele: James Fox, a filmmaker who investigates UFO cases, told podcast host Jesse Michels about a 1996 case in Varginha, a town in Brazil, where some say a live alien creature was captured. Fox points to tapes and a book by a researcher named Roger Leir, who, he says, describes meeting two doctors at a hospital. According to Fox, the doctors talked about a creature there and about communicating with it by telepathy, mind to mind, which would mean doctors had direct contact with a living alien if true. In a later conversation he names the place as Humanitas Hospital and says this part is in Leir's book but not on the tapes.
roger-leir-s-video-of-a-craft-with-grays: Tim Alberino, a filmmaker, describes a video he says came from Roger Leir, a surgeon known for removing what he believed were alien implants. According to Alberino, it was filmed over the ocean near Lebanon or Turkey and shows what looks like a craft, with grays, the small grey-skinned beings of many abduction stories, visible inside. If real, it would be a rare image of the beings themselves.
rogers-book-we-got-it-from-them-2025: Greg Rogers, a doctor who says he worked with NASA and once saw a UFO inside a secret hangar, tells podcast host Jesse Michels that in 2025 he wrote a book and, joking about how clever he was, named it We Got It From Them. He links it to Contact in the Desert, a UFO gathering where he spoke. The title states his point: that some human technology came from non-human craft.
rogers-craft-as-human-built-but-aerodyna: A doctor who worked with NASA, Greg Rogers, told podcast host Jesse Michels that around 2000 he saw a strange craft inside a secret hangar. He says he thinks it was built by humans, even though its shape made no sense for flying through air. If so, it would point to a hidden human technology that does not depend on normal flight.
rogers-egg-craft-resembles-lazar-s-sport: Greg Rogers, introduced on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels as a NASA doctor, says he once saw an egg-shaped craft in a secret hangar, somewhere around the Nevada test site and Area 51, a secret US Air Force base in the Nevada desert, sometime between 1989 and about 2000. Rogers says the egg, as he describes it, would be very much like the "sport model", a craft described by Bob Lazar, a man who has claimed he worked on flying saucers at a hidden site near Area 51 called S-4. If true, it would mean two separate people saw the same kind of craft.
rogue-elements-of-us-government-managing: An analyst, Matthew Pines, says that his reading of a whistleblower named David Grusch is that some parts of the US government have, since about the 1970s, effectively gone rogue in running secret programs about UAP, the official term for UFOs, standing for unidentified anomalous phenomena. The big aerospace company Lockheed comes up as part of the picture. If true, it would mean these programs have slipped out of normal government control.
roman-gods-on-mission-patches-for-our-sp: A researcher who is not named says, on the podcast of host Jesse Michels, that the US space program puts images of Roman gods and old Latin phrases on its mission patches, the cloth badges made for each space mission. He says he asked a man involved why they did this, since no one up in space would read Latin, and the man answered, "Our sponsors." The story gets told because it hints that someone beyond Earth is the intended audience.
romans-say-phoenicians-sacrificed-childr: Tim Alberino, a researcher who talks about ancient giants and lost peoples, tells a podcast host, Jesse Michels, about the Phoenicians, an ancient seafaring people who also settled on the island of Sardinia. Alberino says that according to the Romans, the Phoenicians sacrificed their children to Molech, a god named in ancient writings. He raises it as part of a darker picture of these ancient people.
ron-evans-and-bae-s-project-greenglow-an: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that a scientist named Dr. Ron Evans, at the British defence company BAE Systems, spoke about something called Project Greenglow, a research effort into anti-gravity. Michels adds that Evans wrote a public book about it, which would mean a major arms maker openly looked into ways of beating gravity.
ron-hell-maria-is-a-natural-asian-africa: David Ron Hell, a researcher speaking on a podcast with host Jesse Michels about small three-fingered mummified bodies said to come from Peru, gives his view on one of them, called Maria. He says his hypothesis is that Maria is a hybrid, but a natural one, a mix of Asian and African lineages rather than something made. If true, it would mean these strange bodies have an earthly, if unusual, origin.
ron-johnson-sees-his-lost-dog-s-fate-in-: Grant Cameron, a UFO researcher, tells a story about a man named Ron Johnson whose dog went missing around 1972 and who never knew what happened to it. Cameron says that, years later, Johnson watched the dog's life play out in a crystal and saw a neighbor come by, shoot the dog, throw it in the back of a pickup and dump it at the town dump. In his telling, the crystal could show real past events.
ron-johnson-sees-the-milky-way-from-a-di: A UFO researcher named Grant Cameron, speaking on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, passes on a story he says he heard from a man named Ron Johnson. According to Cameron, someone asked Ron where he would like to go, and Ron said he would like to see the Milky Way, our home galaxy, from a distance. If true, it would mean a person was offered a trip far beyond Earth by whoever was asking.
ron-pandolfi-breakthrough-into-the-next-: Grant Cameron, a researcher, tells podcast host Jesse Michels about Ron Pandolfi, who he says has worked at the CIA, the US foreign intelligence agency, since 1984 and is rumored to brief presidents. According to Cameron, Pandolfi said on a tape that there had been a "breakthrough" in going "into the next world," and that the next time a man called John went to the desert, several of them would go there and come back. Cameron says he found the tape on the internet, that Pandolfi never expected it to become public, and that Pandolfi was clearly talking about portals, doorways to somewhere else.
ron-pandolfi-links-the-jasons-and-the-uf: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, points to a man named Ron Pandolfi, who he says seems to be part of JASON, a group of top scientists who advise the US government. According to Michels, Pandolfi also keeps turning up in the UFO world, which suggests a link between elite government science and the UFO question.
ron-s-visits-to-the-spirit-world-with-el: A UFO researcher named Grant Cameron, speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast, relays a story from a man he calls Ron, linked to Utah. Cameron says a being or guide named Elby took Ron to the spirit world three times, and the story involves a crystal table there. If true, it would suggest contact with something that can lead a living person into a realm beyond death.
ronald-moultrie-scrubbed-battelle-board-: A researcher known online as UAPGerb says that Ronald Moultrie, a senior Pentagon official, set up the offices under which AARO was created, AARO being the Pentagon's office for looking into UFO reports. UAPGerb says Moultrie also sat on the board of the Battelle Memorial Institute, a large private research organisation, and later deleted that role from his LinkedIn page, a professional networking website. He raises it as a sign of quiet links between the people overseeing UFO inquiries and private contractors.
ronald-richter-s-fusion-project-in-baril: Jason Jorjani, a researcher who studies claims of a secret Nazi flying-saucer program, tells podcast host Jesse Michels about Ronald Richter, a German scientist who, he says, set up a project to make power from nuclear fusion in Bariloche, a town in Argentina, in the late 1940s and up to 1951. Jorjani adds that Richter was promising nuclear weapons to Juan Perón, then Argentina's leader, and that this is why an intelligence agency went down there. He tells it as a sign that German wartime science carried on in hiding after the war.
rongorongo-and-nazca-lines-as-depictions: Matt LaCroix, a writer about lost ancient civilizations, passes on what a researcher named Robert Schoch told him about a trip to Easter Island with his wife Katie. They looked at rongorongo, carved markings there long thought to be a form of writing, and the idea he relays is that these symbols, like the Nazca lines, giant drawings scratched into the ground in Peru, show plasma discharges, huge glowing electrical shapes in the sky. If so, ancient people may have been recording something dramatic they saw overhead.
room-of-antiques-with-a-singer-sewing-ma: Mario Woods, who says he was a guard at a US nuclear weapons site, tells podcast host Jesse Michels that in 1977 near South Dakota he was taken aboard a craft and shown a room full of old things, including a Singer sewing machine on its table, with a round window, and he has made drawings of it. In a later telling he adds that a small being led him there and let him look around, and that the objects looked like the ones in his childhood home in Port Arthur, Texas. If true, his takers knew his own past closely.
rosemary-smith-remote-views-a-downed-tu-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that former US president Jimmy Carter is on record calling one event the craziest thing of his presidency, 1976 to 1980 as Michels puts it. According to Michels, a woman named Rosemary Smith used remote viewing, the claimed ability to see far-off places with the mind, to find a Soviet Tu-22 plane that had gone down in Zaire, a country in central Africa. If true, it would mean psychic methods actually helped the US government.
ross-coulthart-gets-brent-to-name-harrin: Brent Friedman, who speaks as a witness, tells podcast host Jesse Michels that around 2019 or 2020 a man named Ross Coulthart got him on camera and kept pushing him. Friedman says this pressure led him to name a person called Harrington on camera, a name tied to the secret story he was telling.
ross-coulthart-s-investigation-at-bradsh: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that an investigative journalist, Ross Coulthart, has been researching Bradshaw Ranch near Sedona, Arizona. According to Michels, there is a place there called Secret Mountain where UFOs are said to fly into the mountain itself. If true, it would suggest these craft have hidden bases inside the earth.
ross-coulthart-says-on-need-to-know-that: A writer and producer, Bryce Zabel, says that around 2025 on a show they did together called Need to Know, a journalist named Ross Coulthart told him he could now state categorically that the Tic Tac, a white oval object shaped like the mint that Navy pilots reported, is technology made by Lockheed Martin, a big American aerospace and weapons company. A clip of Coulthart has him saying it slightly differently: that he now knows it categorically. If true, it would mean the famous object was a human-built craft, not something from elsewhere.
rossi-devices-and-ring-superconductor-ex: Dave Rossi tells podcast host Jesse Michels that between about 2021 and 2024 he built a handful of devices, including experiments with rings of superconductor, a material that carries electricity with no resistance. He says they produced interesting effects that seemed to back up theories discussed by researchers Hal Puthoff, Eric Davis and others, which would matter because it would mean those unusual physics ideas work in practice.
roswell-as-home-of-the-509th-atomic-bomb: A man named Marik von Rennenkampf, speaking on podcast host Jesse Michels's show, points out that in 1947 Roswell, New Mexico, was home to the 509th, which he calls the first atomic bomber squadron in the US. He raises it because, if UFOs came to Roswell, it would tie them to the place where the country's nuclear bombers were based.
roswell-bodies-kept-on-ice-at-wright-pat: In 1947, near the town of Roswell in New Mexico, something is said to have crashed, and many people believe it was a craft from somewhere else. A researcher who goes by UAPGerb, speaking on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, says that bodies from that crash were flown to Wright-Patterson, an Air Force base in Ohio, and kept there on ice. If true, it would mean the military had held non-human bodies since the 1940s.
roswell-boulder-split-and-memory-metal-1: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says the 1947 Roswell incident, when something is said to have crashed near Roswell, New Mexico, deserves more investigation, including reports of a split boulder and of a "memory metal" in the debris that sprang back to its shape. He says he believes the accounts of Jesse Marcel, an Army officer involved in the recovery, and Walter Haut, from the local base, which would mean the wreckage was something unknown.
roswell-corona-crash-confirmed-via-ed-mi: A scientist who has worked with the Pentagon, Eric Davis, says that at a science advisory meeting he heard from Ed Mitchell, an astronaut, about briefings the Pentagon got from Steven Greer, who ran the Disclosure Project, a campaign to get officials to speak about UFOs. According to Davis, a Navy admiral, Thomas Wilson, then came back and confirmed that the 1947 crash near Corona, New Mexico, usually called Roswell, really happened and was not a secret high-altitude spy balloon, as the official explanation says. If true, it would mean a senior officer confirmed a real crash of something unknown.
roswell-craft-said-to-have-been-brought-: Bob Lazar, a well-known figure in UFO circles, recalls earlier stories that the craft said to have crashed near Roswell, New Mexico, in 1947 was struck by lightning and went down. The story offers a simple reason why an advanced craft might have crashed at all.
roswell-crash-and-stringfield-s-marcel-i: Richard Dolan, a historian of UFO claims, talks on Jesse Michels's podcast about Roswell, a town in New Mexico where something is said to have crashed in 1947. Dolan says Leonard Stringfield, a researcher who gathered stories of crashed flying saucers, was one of the first people to interview and publish an interview with Jesse Marcel Senior, a military officer who handled the Roswell debris, in the late 1970s. He tells it as part of how the Roswell story came back into public view.
roswell-crash-as-exotic-human-technology: A writer and historian, Peter Levenda, says he thinks it possible that whatever crashed near Roswell, New Mexico, in 1947 was human technology rather than something from elsewhere, and he points to a book called Secret Machines. If true, it would mean people were building strange, advanced craft far earlier than anyone admits.
roswell-crash-caused-by-radio-signatures: In 1947, something is said to have crashed near Roswell, New Mexico, and people have argued ever since about what it was. An online commentator who goes by UAPGerb, speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast, points to a man named Philip J. Corso, who he says claimed the crash happened because clashing radio signals confused the craft's navigation. If true, it would mean ordinary human radio could bring down a craft that was not ours.
roswell-crash-debris-retrieved-by-mac-br: In 1947, near Roswell, New Mexico, a rancher named Mac Brazel is said to have found the debris of a crashed craft scattered across his land. Michels tells it "as the story goes". The physicist John Brandenburg, repeating what Roswell veterans said, adds that Brazel brought the wreckage into town and showed it to the sheriff, who told him to take it to the nearby military base. A guest named Luigi adds a second site about two miles away, where hikers with children found a crashed pod with beings inside. The journalist Michael Shellenberger asks whether one craft came down or two, and whether radar brought them down. The researcher Robert Hastings notes that Roswell was then the world's only nuclear bomber base. Michels says he himself thinks what happened there "was otherworldly", which is why the story matters: it would be the first known recovery of a craft not made by people.
roswell-crash-test-dummy-and-project-mog: In 1947 something came down near Roswell, a town in New Mexico, and many people believe it was a crashed craft that was not from Earth. Over the years officials offered other explanations: a secret balloon project called Project Mogul, and bluish crash-test dummies that people might have mistaken for bodies. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, waves both away, saying the dummies and Project Mogul both came later than the crash, so neither could explain it, which would leave the event without an ordinary answer.
roswell-date-of-july-7-1947-in-the-brief: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, points to a book, A State of Mind: Faith and the CIA, that gives July 7, 1947 as a date tied to Roswell, New Mexico, where a strange object is said to have crashed that summer. His guest, Ralph Moat Larson, says he once had a dream in which a string of numbers was "downloaded" into his head, including 747, and Michels asks whether that number points to the date 7/4/7 or 7/7, linking the dream to Roswell. If the link holds, the guest's dream would be pointing at that crash.
roswell-debris-swapped-for-the-ramey-pho: In 1947 the military near Roswell, New Mexico, collected wreckage from a crash, and a general named Ramey later showed reporters debris for a photograph. A researcher named Kevin Knuth, on Jesse Michels's podcast, says he thinks the wreckage was switched, so the photographed debris was not what was really found, and he points to Jesse Marcel, an officer who handled the original material. If true, it would mean the public was shown a substitute to hide the real crash.
roswell-flying-disc-announcement-then-re: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in July 1947 a flying disc came down near Roswell, New Mexico. According to Michels, the Roswell Army Airfield, the local military base, put out a press release saying it had a flying disc and then took the statement back in a panic. He tells it because the official announcement and its quick reversal would suggest something real was being hidden.
roswell-held-the-most-us-nukes-in-1947: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in 1947, when something is said to have crashed near the town of Roswell, New Mexico, Roswell was the site holding more nuclear weapons than anywhere else in the United States. If true, it would mean the famous crash happened right beside the country's most sensitive military site.
roswell-ignored-until-berlitz-s-1980-boo: A well-known skeptic, Michael Shermer, says the 1947 Roswell incident, a reported crash in New Mexico, did not become a big story until 1980, when the writer Charles Berlitz published a book about it called The Roswell Incident. According to Shermer, the researcher Stanton Friedman and others only took it up after that, which in his view shows the legend was built decades later.
roswell-material-as-seed-for-an-exotic-a: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, describes a theory that whatever was recovered from the 1947 crash near Roswell, New Mexico, became the seed of a secret research programme. According to the theory, the material ended up at the Air Force Research Lab at Wright-Patterson, an Air Force base in Ohio, where it fed long-running work on exotic metals. If true, it would mean the recovered material shaped secret technology research for decades.
roswell-operators-part-of-the-craft-s-gu: An online UFO commentator who goes by UAPGerb tells podcast host Jesse Michels about the 1947 crash at Roswell, New Mexico. He says that Philip Corso, a former US Army officer, said in interviews that the operators of the Roswell craft were themselves part of its guidance system. If true, it would mean the beings and the machine worked as one.
roswell-s-shifting-official-stories-incl: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, talks about the 1947 incident near Roswell, New Mexico, where something is said to have crashed and been recovered by the military. He says the official explanation has changed so many times that it is laughable, and the story's title points to one version in which bodies seen there were explained as children with progeria, a rare disease that makes the body age fast. For Michels, the shifting accounts suggest the real story is being hidden.
roswell-style-seeding-of-our-internet-te: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, offers an idea tied to Roswell, the New Mexico town where many believe a craft from elsewhere crashed in 1947. He suggests that, as some say happened at Roswell, much of our internet technology was handed to us by these other beings. In his telling the purpose was to keep people constantly distracted.
roswell-technologies-per-corso-were-germ: Jason Jorjani, a researcher, talks about Philip Corso, an Army officer whose book The Day After Roswell says many modern technologies came from a craft that crashed near Roswell, New Mexico, in 1947. Jorjani says another researcher, Joseph Farrell, found documents showing the Germans had invented every one of those technologies in the 1940s. If true, it would mean the Roswell technology was human and German, not alien.
roswell-the-world-s-only-nuclear-bomber-: In 1947, near the town of Roswell, New Mexico, something came down in the desert, and the story is often told as a crashed flying saucer that the military later called a weather balloon. A researcher named Bryce points out that the people at Roswell were running the only nuclear bomber base in the world at the time, so it seems odd to him that they could mistake a saucer for a balloon. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, makes a similar point in his own words: Roswell was not just a random desert, he says, but the largest concentration of nuclear weapons in the world at that moment. The two tell it a little differently, one stressing the bomber base and the other the weapons, but both use it to suggest that the people on the ground knew what they were looking at, and that a crash there would have mattered a great deal.
roswell-was-a-nazi-staged-event-1947: Jason Jorjani, a researcher who studies claims of a secret Nazi flying-saucer program, tells podcast host Jesse Michels his view of the 1947 crash at Roswell, New Mexico. He says the Nazis created the crisis at Roswell and staged the event, drawing on the account of Philip Corso, a former US Army officer. If true, it would mean the most famous UFO crash was a human scheme, not a visit from elsewhere.
roswell-witnesses-describe-non-human-bei: In 1947 something crashed near Roswell, New Mexico, and many believe it was a craft that was not human-made. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says people at Roswell described a strange being with three or four fingers and toes coming out of the craft. According to those witnesses it was clearly not human, which would mean someone other than us was flying it.
roswell-witnesses-describe-threats-made-: Roswell is a town in New Mexico where, in 1947, people say something crashed and the military came to collect it. A UFO investigator named James Fox says that while he interviewed local witnesses around the fiftieth anniversary in 1997, several men told him they had been threatened at the time, with words like "they'll be picking your bones out of the desert." If true, it would mean people were scared into silence about what they saw.
roswell-wreckage-in-the-hangar-had-the-b: Charles Hall, who says he spent three years with tall white aliens at Area 51, a secret US Air Force site in Nevada, talks with podcast host Jesse Michels about the wreckage from Roswell, New Mexico, where a crashed craft is said to have been recovered in 1947. Asked what it was like being near that wreckage in a hangar, Hall says simply that it sat in the hangar with the bathroom on the other side, as if it were an everyday part of the building.
roswell-wreckage-rumoured-at-wright-patt: Many people believe that wreckage from a 1947 crash near Roswell, New Mexico, came from a craft that was not from Earth, and that it was taken to Wright-Patterson, an Air Force base in Ohio. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, points out that an Air Force general named Neil McCasland once ran the lab at Wright-Patterson where, as the rumour goes, the wreckage ended up. If so, McCasland may have been close to the material.
round-table-foundation-elf-research-pene: A researcher named Greg, on Jesse Michels's podcast, tells of work at the Round Table Foundation, a private research group linked to a scientist named Andrija Puharich, in the 1950s and again in the late 1970s and 1980s. According to Greg, they studied ELF, very low frequency radio waves, and found a frequency that could get through the walls of a Faraday cage, a metal enclosure built to block electrical signals. If true, it would suggest signals, or minds, could reach places thought to be sealed off.
round-table-foundation-funded-by-army-na: A researcher, Greg Malatzi, says that around 1949 and 1950 the US Army, the Navy and the CIA, America's spy agency, flocked to the Round Table Foundation, a research group in Rockland, Maine, and gave the man running it money for his research. He bases this on letters from the agencies to the foundation, and tells it to show that the military took this unusual research seriously very early on.
rov-camera-and-lights-fail-at-the-object: Dennis Asberg, a Swedish treasure hunter, says his team found a strange object on the floor of the Baltic Sea between Sweden and Finland in 2011, known as the Baltic Sea anomaly. He tells podcast host Jesse Michels that whenever they dive on it, the camera and the lights stop working, including on their remote-controlled underwater robot. That would suggest the object itself interferes with equipment.
rov-image-shows-a-straight-wall-on-the-a: Dennis Asberg, a treasure hunter, says that in 2025 an image from a remote-controlled underwater robot showed a straight wall on the Baltic Sea anomaly, a strange object his team found on the seafloor between Sweden and Finland. He tells podcast host Jesse Michels the wall must be at least 30 meters long and the whole object about 60 meters, which would make a straight edge that size hard to explain as natural rock.
roy-craig-interview-with-lewis-chase-who: A former US Air Force officer, Robert Salas, played podcast host Jesse Michels a recorded interview from 1967 in which an investigator named Roy Craig questions Lieutenant Colonel Lewis Chase, head of operations at Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana, a base that ran nuclear missiles. According to Salas, Chase says in the interview that he knows nothing about the incident being asked about, which Salas presents as part of a pattern of officials keeping quiet about UFO events at the base.
royal-raymond-rife-s-microscope-and-freq: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells of an inventor in California named Royal Raymond Rife, who in the 1930s claimed to have built a microscope so powerful it could watch live viruses. The story, told in an episode about the dark history of the drug industry, holds that Rife's microscope and a machine he built that worked with frequencies were suppressed. If true, it would mean a promising medical invention was buried.
royal-tomb-theory-and-the-lack-of-mummie: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, notes that most experts on ancient Egypt believe the Great Pyramid at Giza was built around 2500 BC as a tomb for the king Khufu, and the next pyramid as a tomb for his son Khafre. But Michels points out that no confirmed mummies or burial chambers of either king have ever been found inside. He raises this in an episode about a claimed energy grid under the pyramids, as a hint that they may have served some other purpose.
rubik-and-jabs-reanalyse-the-michelson-m: In the 1890s, the scientists Michelson and Morley ran a famous experiment looking for the ether, a substance once thought to fill all of space. A researcher named Diane Powell, on Jesse Michels's podcast, says a biophysicist named Beverly Rubik and a physicist named Harry Jabs later looked at that data again and wrote a paper saying there actually was an effect. If true, it would reopen a question most of physics considers closed.
rubio-credible-witnesses-with-high-clear: Merrick von Renenamp, a guest on a podcast, says the politician Marco Rubio has stated again and again, on camera, that people who have come forward about UFOs are credible, hold high security clearances, meaning permission to see secret information, and sit in high positions, yet fear for their lives. He also mentions other lawmakers, Kirsten Gillibrand among them. If true, it would mean insiders believe speaking out is truly dangerous.
rubio-s-2020-intelligence-committee-prov: Speaking on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, a man named Merrick von Renenamp says that in 2020 a US senator, Marco Rubio, quietly slipped a provision into the written report of the Senate Intelligence Committee, the Senate panel that oversees the spy agencies. He brings it up while arguing with Mick West, a well-known UFO skeptic, and the story is also tied to something West tweeted. If it happened as described, it would mean UFO questions were being pushed into official intelligence business through the back door.
rubio-things-flying-over-nuclear-sites: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Marco Rubio, the US Secretary of State, was once asked what conspiracy he believed in most. According to Michels, Rubio answered that there are things flying with impunity around America's nuclear sites. If true, it would mean a top official is acknowledging unknown craft moving freely over the country's most guarded places.
rudolf-hess-s-telepathy-experiments-and-: Rudolf Hess was a senior Nazi leader who flew to Britain in 1941 and was then held prisoner. An author named Peter Levenda, on Jesse Michels's podcast, says Hess's flight was timed by astrology, that Hess believed he was in telepathic contact with his wife from prison, and that telepathy experiments were run with him. If true, it would show occult beliefs shaping events at the top of wartime Germany.
rudolf-hess-sent-to-antarctica-1938: A researcher named Jason Jorjani, speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast, says that around 1938 and 1939 Nazi Germany sent people to Antarctica, and that one of the main figures involved was Rudolf Hess, a senior Nazi leader. He credits a document or work called Hess and the Penguins. If true, it would tie the Nazi leadership directly to a secret interest in the frozen continent.
ruins-of-an-ancient-civilization-at-cydo: Tim Alberino, a guest on Jesse Michels's podcast, says there are ruins of an ancient civilization on Mars, in a region called Cydonia, an idea made popular in the 1990s by writers such as Richard Hoagland, David Flynn and Michael Heiser. He goes further and predicts that within our lifetime it will be revealed that an ancient alien civilization really did live on Mars. If true, it would mean we were not the first builders in our solar system.
rumored-crash-in-chinese-territory: Peter Levenda, a writer who spent years doing business with the Chinese government, says that while he was there he heard many rumors that something unexplained had crashed on Chinese soil. He adds that he thinks the Russians ended up getting it. If true, it would mean other countries besides the United States have recovered strange crashed craft.
rumored-dod-hybrid-program-using-non-hum: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says rumours have reached Congress about a secret project inside the Department of Defense, the US military's headquarters department. According to those rumours, the project mixes human genetics with what is described as non-human genetic material. If true, it would mean the military has both non-human biology and a programme working to blend it with ours.
rumored-tunnels-and-cave-system-under-me: The owner of Skinwalker Ranch, a property in Utah long known for reports of strange happenings, said on Jesse Michels's podcast that there have long been rumours of tunnels and a cave system under a mesa, a flat-topped hill, on the land. The owner says these rumours go back to an earlier owner's time and, as the story goes, even back to the Mayans. If true, it would mean something hidden lies underground beneath the ranch.
rumors-about-area-51-at-the-energy-depar: John Harrington, introduced on Jesse Michels's podcast as a former US Secretary of Energy, the cabinet member who runs the department in charge of nuclear weapons work, says that in the 1980s his department heard plenty of rumors about Area 51. He describes it as a highly classified site in Nevada full of secret projects. If true, it means even people that senior were left wondering what went on there.
rumors-of-elites-having-out-of-body-expe: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, asks a guest whether he has heard rumours that elite people today spend time inside the granite chambers of some pyramids. The rumour, as the story frames it, is that they go there to have out-of-body experiences, which would mean the chambers still hold some special power that the powerful quietly use.
rumour-that-the-giant-ended-up-at-wright: A man named Tim Alberino, on Jesse Michels's podcast, talks about a story that US forces captured a twelve-foot giant in Afghanistan. rumoured-2027-arrival-clock: Matthew Pines, a commentator on national security, says that word has gone around that non-human visitors are going to show up openly in 2027. rumoured-badlands-incident-in-which-two-: A former guard at a US nuclear missile site named Mario Woods, speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast, recalls a rumour from before he arrived in South Dakota around 1977. rumoured-deep-underground-military-bases: A podcast host named Jesse Michels mentions rumours of deep underground military bases hidden beneath several American sites: Edwards and Nellis, two Air Force bases in California and Nevada, Peterson in Colorado, and Cheyenne Mountain, the dug-in Colorado mountain complex that houses NORAD, the joint US and Canadian air defence command. rumoured-jfk-joint-space-program-with-th: In the early 1960s, John F. Kennedy was US president, and the Soviet Union, led by Nikita Khrushchev, was America's great rival. rumoured-mormon-connection-to-the-ufo-le: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says there are rumours that Mormons are connected to what he calls the UFO legacy program, meaning a supposed long-running secret government effort to study crashed or recovered craft. rumsfeld-admits-trillions-missing-in-aud: An Australian journalist, Ross Coulthart, says that while writing his book he tracked down a speech by Donald Rumsfeld, then the US Secretary of Defense, given on 10 September 2001, the day before the September 11 attacks. ruppelt-in-look-magazine-on-sightings-at: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, cites a 1952 article in Look, a popular American magazine, titled "The Hunt for the Flying Saucer." ruppelt-pressured-to-debunk-his-own-book: A UFO historian named Richard Dolan, on Jesse Michels's podcast, talks about Edward Ruppelt, who wrote a 1950s book called The Report on Unidentified Flying Objects. ruppelt-s-account-of-early-ufo-hypothese: A researcher named Jason Simosa points to a book by Edward Ruppelt, who ran the US Air Force's UFO study of the 1950s, describing how investigators back then worked through possible explanations. ruppelt-s-book-reports-metallic-spheres-: A man named Merrick points to a 1956 book, The Report on Unidentified Flying Objects, written by Captain Ed Ruppelt, whom he calls the first director of Blue Book, the US Air Force's UFO study of the 1950s and 60s. ruppelt-s-serious-cases-cluster-near-nuc: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, points to The Report on Unidentified Flying Objects, a book by Edward J. ruppelt-s-study-of-sightings-near-nuclea: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, points to an early study of UFO sightings by a man named Edward J. Ruppelt, carried out between 1947 and 1952. russell-targ-coming-around-to-remote-vie: Eric Wargo, a writer on dreams and seeing the future, tells podcast host Jesse Michels that remote viewing, the claimed ability to describe faraway places with the mind alone, may really be precognition, knowing things before they happen. russell-targ-saw-real-miracles-while-wor: A magician and video host named Chris Ramsay, on Jesse Michels's podcast, says a man named Russell Targ told of working as a stage magician in his younger days. russia-and-china-retrieval-teams-and-the: A former US Marine named Michael Herrera, speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast, says Russia and China have their own teams for recovering craft made by non-human intelligence, meaning beings that are not us. russia-used-nuclear-material-to-bait-ufo: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in Russia nuclear material was apparently used as bait to draw UFOs in. He gives no date or details. If true, it would mean the Russians believed UFOs were drawn to nuclear material and tried to use that.
russian-admiral-the-phenomenon-s-reality: A UFO investigator named James Fox says that in Russia, sometime in the 1990s, he sat down with a Russian admiral to ask about UFOs. russian-deception-as-source-of-some-uap: A guest named Eric Hazeline, introduced on Jesse Michels's podcast as a former director at the NSA, the US agency for electronic spying and codebreaking, says some UAP, the official term for unidentified objects in the sky, come from deliberate deception. russian-dna-phantom-experiments-1990: A podcast host named Jesse Michels says that in the 1990s Russian scientists described something he calls even more bizarre than what came before, in what were known as the DNA phantom experiments. russian-earthquake-weapons-could-set-off: Lyn Buchanan, a former US Army sergeant, says on Jesse Michels's podcast that the Russians have earthquake weapons. russian-general-alexeyev-in-german-magaz: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in 2000 a Russian general named Vasily Alexeyev spoke publicly in a German magazine about UFOs. russian-high-school-taught-moon-landing-: Podcast host Jesse Michels says a friend of his who grew up in Russia told him that in high school they were taught the American moon landing was faked. He shares it as an example of how countries can shape what their people believe about space.
russian-intelligence-sends-an-armed-team: Rolf Mowatt-Larssen, a former officer of the CIA, the US foreign intelligence agency, tells podcast host Jesse Michels about 1993, when people tried to overthrow Russia's president Boris Yeltsin. russian-officials-studying-ufos: Robert Salas, a former US Air Force officer, says that several Russian officials have publicly said they have people studying UFOs. He gives no names or dates. If true, it would mean Russia, like the United States, treats the subject as worth official attention.
russian-snow-alien-body-found-in-siberia: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells of two Russian men who, he says, came upon an alien body lying in the snowy woods of the Irkutsk region in Siberia around 2011, about a month after something else strange happened in the same area. russian-triangle-event-as-pre-arranged-m: Matthew Brown, introduced on Jesse Michels's podcast as a Pentagon whistleblower, talks about an event around 2018 in the Pacific off Kamchatka in eastern Russia involving a triangle-shaped craft. russians-beaming-negative-mental-energy-: Eric Haseltine, introduced on Jesse Michels's podcast as a former senior official at the NSA, the US agency that intercepts electronic communications, says the Russians used mind power in chess. ruth-paine-and-marina-find-the-walker-no: Dan Sheehan, a lawyer and researcher, talks about the events after President John F. Kennedy was shot in 1963. ruth-paine-at-naushon-island-retreat-wit: Dan Sheehan, a researcher who talks about the 1963 killing of President John F. ruth-paine-houses-lee-harvey-oswald-and-: A researcher and author, Peter Levenda, says that in 1963 Lee Harvey Oswald, the man accused of shooting President John F. ruth-paine-s-sister-works-for-the-cia-pa: Dan Sheehan, a researcher on the Kennedy assassination, says on Jesse Michels's podcast that Ruth Paine, a woman who helped Lee Harvey Oswald, the man accused of killing President Kennedy, and his wife Marina, turned out to have a sister working for the CIA, the US spy agency. ryan-graves-says-go-fast-was-recorded-by: Podcast host Jesse Michels says he interviewed Ryan Graves, a Navy fighter pilot who testified under oath before Congress, about the Go Fast video, a 2015 Navy clip of a small fast-looking object filmed off Jacksonville, Florida. s-4-facility-hand-scanner-corridor-and-n: Bob Lazar is a man who says that in 1988 and 1989 he worked at S-4, which he describes as a secret site near Papoose Lake in the Nevada desert. s-force-triangular-fire-team-trained-on-: Dan Sheehan, a researcher on the Kennedy assassination, says on Jesse Michels's podcast that between 1960 and 1963 a group he calls S force, tied to Fort Huachuca, an Army base in Arizona, set up a training base on a Mexican ranch owned by Texas businessman Clint Murchison Jr. There, he says, a team practised shooting a moving target from three different spots at once, and he links the effort to Carl Jenkins and the mobster Santos Trafficante. s4-imagery-covered-up-on-google-earth-pr: S4 is a site in the Nevada desert that a man named Bob Lazar has long talked about as a place where secret work on flying craft took place. s4-project-directives-duplicate-propulsi: Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked at a secret Nevada site called S-4 in 1988 and 1989, says the project there had two orders. sac-telegram-on-echo-flight-demands-boei: A former US Air Force officer, Robert Salas, told podcast host Jesse Michels about a 1967 telegram the Air Force released to him from Strategic Air Command, the branch that ran America's nuclear bombers and missiles. sagan-and-shklovskii-s-intelligent-life-: Jason Jorjani, a philosopher, mentions a 1960s book called Intelligent Life in the Universe, which he says the American scientist Carl Sagan co-wrote with Iosif Shklovsky, a Soviet scientist. sagan-bumped-up-against-the-ufo-program: Bob Maguire, introduced as a former CIA contractor, talks with podcast host Jesse Michels about Carl Sagan, a famous astronomer and science popularizer. sagan-in-venus-anomaly-meeting-with-whit: Podcast host Jesse Michels relays a story, connected to the scientist Carl Sagan and to people named John Brandenburg and Bob Maguire, about a meeting over something unexplained concerning Venus. sagan-s-1963-paper-estimating-et-visitat: Maaneli Derakhshani, a researcher speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast, says the famous astronomer Carl Sagan wrote a technical paper in 1963 using the Drake equation, a formula for guessing how many advanced civilizations exist in our galaxy. sagan-s-1975-paper-on-detecting-artifici: Maaneli Derakhshani, a researcher on Jesse Michels's podcast, says the astronomer Carl Sagan wrote a paper in 1975 about how to look for signs of advanced life on other planets. sagan-s-early-diaries-about-ufos-1950: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Carl Sagan, a famous American astronomer later known as a sceptic, wrote about UFOs all the time in his early diaries. sagan-s-nsa-contractor-green-badge: Bob Maguire, described as a contractor who worked for the CIA, the US foreign intelligence agency, tells podcast host Jesse Michels that the well-known scientist Carl Sagan carried a green contractor badge with his photo for the NSA, the US agency that intercepts communications. sagan-whispers-keep-up-the-great-work-to: Maaneli Derakhshani passes on a story about Richard Hoagland, a man known for claims about strange features on other worlds, and the famous scientist Carl Sagan. sagancarlotto-correspondence-on-the-face: The Face on Mars is a hill in a region of Mars called Cydonia that looked like a human face in photos taken by a NASA probe. sages-helped-by-the-gods-founded-a-new-c: A guest named Matt, speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast about a great change around 12,000 BC, tells a story set at Lake Van in eastern Turkey after an ancient flood. saic-as-contractor-for-psionic-testing-n: A podcast host named Jesse Michels says that a person called Sammy believes SAIC, a large American defence contracting company, was the contractor doing psionic testing, meaning tests of supposed mind powers, in the 1980s. saic-connection-to-crane: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that an online researcher who goes by UAP Gerb has dug up a lot of material about the work of SAIC, a large American defence contracting company, with Crane, a Navy weapons research base in Indiana. saic-exotic-science-and-stargate-links: A podcast host named Jesse Michels says that SAIC, a large American defence contractor based in Reston, Virginia, has openly studied exotic propulsion, anti-gravity, directed energy weapons and other unusual science, and seems to have worked hand in hand with Stargate, the CIA's psychic spy programme. sal-pais-applauds-rossi-s-panel-example-: Dave Rossi tells podcast host Jesse Michels that about two summers before, around 2023, he spoke on a panel with Salvatore Pais and several others. salas-rebuts-the-emp-explanation-1967: In 1967, according to accounts, nuclear missiles at Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana went offline, and a Wall Street Journal article suggested the cause was the Air Force testing an EMP, a burst of energy that can knock out electronics. salas-s-14-point-wsj-rebuttal-2025: Robert Salas, a former US Air Force officer who says a UFO shut down the nuclear missiles he was guarding, says that in 2025 the Wall Street Journal ran an article claiming the shutdown was really a test of an electromagnetic pulse, a burst of energy that can knock out electronics. salas-s-2-5-hour-aaro-interview: Robert Salas is a former US Air Force officer who says a UFO once shut down nuclear missiles he was responsible for. salty-liquid-water-on-the-martian-surfac: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, recalls that in 2015 researchers stunned the world by claiming they had finally found definitive evidence of salty liquid water flowing on the surface of Mars. salvatore-pais-filed-patents-at-pax-rive: The story concerns Salvatore Pais, a man who filed patents, the legal claims that protect an invention, on behalf of the US Navy in the 2010s. salvatore-pais-inertial-mass-reduction-p: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in 2016 the US Navy filed a patent, with an inventor named Salvatore Pais, for a craft using what it called an inertial mass reduction device, meaning something that would make a vehicle act as if it had less mass and so move far more easily. same-distances-encoded-at-roman-sites: Geoffrey Drumm, a researcher who says an alien told him the true purpose of the pyramids, tells podcast host Jesse Michels that he finds the same distances, 5,300 meters and 2,300 meters, built into Roman sites. same-words-do-not-fear-recalled-by-both-: A podcast host named Jesse Michels tells of two Air Force men, Mario Woods and Michael Johnson, who say they were abducted near Ellsworth Air Force Base in South Dakota in November 1977. sami-shaman-s-amanita-muscaria-winter-so: Tero Isokauppila, a Finnish mushroom entrepreneur, tells podcast host Jesse Michels about an old winter-solstice custom of the Sami, the reindeer-herding people of Lapland in the far north of Europe. sammaciccia-s-guess-about-ss-eugenics-pr: A philosopher named Jason Jorjani, talking on a podcast with host Jesse Michels and discussing a man named Bruno Sammaciccia, says it struck him that the SS, the Nazi party's elite military and police force, ran eugenics programmes, meaning efforts to breed people for chosen traits. sammy-hagar-s-love-walks-in-lyrics-came-: Chris Bledsoe, a man who says he has had many encounters with strange lights, tells a podcast host, Jesse Michels, about a conversation with the singer Sammy Hagar. samples-from-the-baltic-sea-anomaly-test: Dennis Asberg, a treasure hunter, says his team took samples around 2011 and 2012 from the Baltic Sea anomaly, a strange object on the seafloor between Sweden and Finland. san-jose-woman-s-disc-that-was-bigger-in: Jacques Vallee, a longtime UFO researcher, tells of a woman in San Jose, California, who saw a big disc over her house. sandia-history-lists-kissinger-as-a-semi: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that a redacted history of Sandia Laboratories, a US government weapons laboratory in Albuquerque, New Mexico, describes a man named Don Carter organizing seminars with noted experts around 1961. santa-anastasia-excavation-yields-giant-: A researcher named Tim Alberino tells a podcast host, Jesse Michels, about a dig at the Church of Santa Anastasia on the Italian island of Sardinia, around 1978 to 1981. santa-claus-tradition-traced-back-to-the: A Finnish mushroom entrepreneur named Tero Isokauppila, talking on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, traces the Santa Claus story back through history to the Sami, the reindeer-herding people of Lapland in the far north of Europe.
