sar-doppler-tomography-paper-on-vesuvius: Filippo Biondi, an Italian scientist who works with satellite radar, tells podcast host Jesse Michels that before 2019 he wrote a paper with the National Research Council of Italy, the country's main public science body. He says it used radar images from satellites, together with readings from seismographs, instruments that record ground vibrations, to see what lies under the volcano Mount Vesuvius near Naples. He tells it to show that his method of looking deep underground worked before he turned it on the pyramids.
sar-doppler-tomography-research-started-: A researcher named Filippo, part of a team claiming to have found a huge energy grid beneath the pyramids of Egypt, tells podcast host Jesse Michels that their work began in 2018. He says they used SAR Doppler tomography, a way of using radar from satellites to picture what lies underground, and that they had been at it for six or seven years, starting two years before they published their papers.
sar-scan-shows-shaft-system-coming-out-o: A researcher called Jeffrey, speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast, describes a 2020 scientific paper by researchers he names as Filippo and Corrado. The paper used a satellite radar method that reads tiny vibrations inside solid structures to look into the Great Pyramid of Giza in Egypt. Jeffrey says the images show a system of shafts running down from the bottom of the Queen's Chamber, one of the pyramid's inner rooms, which would point to hidden structures beneath the pyramid.
sar-team-detects-the-big-void-in-a-trans: A researcher named Filippo says that his team scanned the Great Pyramid at Giza in Egypt using SAR, a radar method that builds images from radar echoes, during work he dates to about 2018 to 2020. He says they picked up the Grand Gallery, the pyramid's long inner passage, and also what is called the Big Void, a large hidden space inside the pyramid, lying east to west, and he stresses that these were real readings, not simulated ones. He tells it, on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels and crediting a colleague named Corrado, because if true it would mean radar can see hidden structures inside the pyramids.
sar-tomography-detects-king-s-chamber-re: A researcher called Jeffrey, on Jesse Michels's podcast, describes a 2020 paper, credited to a scientist named Filippo, that used satellite radar to read vibrations inside the Great Pyramid of Giza. He says the scan picks up the King's Chamber, the main inner room, along with the stone beams above it and the stone box known as the sarcophagus, with red areas showing a very strong vibration signal from inside. If the method works as described, it could map hidden spaces inside the pyramid without digging.
sar-tomography-mapping-of-the-gran-sasso: A researcher named Jay Anderson, speaking on Jesse Michels' podcast, says a team linked to a scientist named Filippo Biondi used a radar technique to map the Gran Sasso Laboratory in Italy, a research site about 1.4 kilometres inside a mountain. The technique, called SAR tomography, uses radar signals, often from satellites, to build up pictures of what lies beneath the surface. Anderson tells it because, if it works, the same method could reveal hidden spaces deep underground elsewhere.
sarbacher-craft-at-wright-patterson-take: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that a government scientist named Robert Sarbacher claimed a craft was being held at Wright-Patterson, an Air Force base in Ohio, sometime between the 1940s and 1960s. According to Michels, Sarbacher said the craft was taken over by a group called the Anderson trust, with a link to Karl Compton, a leading scientist at MIT, the Massachusetts Institute of Technology. If true, it would mean a recovered craft passed out of plain military hands into a private circle of scientists.
sarbacher-involved-in-standing-up-the-pr: David Grusch, a former US intelligence officer who became a whistleblower about hidden UFO programmes, says that a scientist named Robert Sarbacher was reportedly involved in setting up the secret effort Grusch says he uncovered, sometime in the 1940s or 1950s. The podcast host Jesse Michels, relaying Grusch, puts this setup of UFO secrecy in 1954 and links it to Robert Oppenheimer, the physicist who led the atomic bomb work, and the inventor Townsend Brown. If true, it would trace the start of government UFO secrecy to a handful of named scientists.
sarbacher-karl-compton-briefed-on-ufo-te: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells of a scientist named Robert Sarbacher, who spoke to Stanton Friedman, a nuclear engineer and UFO researcher. Michels says Sarbacher told Friedman that Karl Compton, president of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT), was briefed on UFO technology in 1950 at Wright Field, an Air Force airfield in Ohio. If true, it would mean top American scientists were brought in to study the technology.
sarbacher-known-to-australian-nuclear-en: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Ross Coulthart, a journalist, has found interesting information about some nuclear engineers in Australia who knew the scientist Robert Sarbacher. The story links to Woomera, a weapons testing site in Australia, in the 1950s. Michels presents it as a sign that Sarbacher's claims about secret UFO work were known about overseas.
sarbacher-picks-up-townsend-brown-after-: A podcast host named Jesse Michels says that in 1956 an inventor, Thomas Townsend Brown, ran an experiment in Paris showing that the Biefeld-Brown effect, a push produced by high electric voltage, works even in a vacuum, hinting at a link between electricity and gravity. Michels says that when Brown came back to the US he was picked up in a black Cadillac by Robert Sarbacher, a government scientist. If true, it would suggest officials quietly took an interest in work that could lead to anti-gravity.
sarbacher-put-cameras-on-modified-v2-roc: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says the son of a scientist named Robert Sarbacher has now gone on record about his father's work. According to the son, his father told him he used to put cameras on modified V2 rockets, German rockets from the Second World War, so he could chase UFOs. If true, it would mean the US was actively trying to film these objects in the late 1940s and 1950s.
sarbacher-s-letter-to-william-steinman-1: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, talks about a letter that a scientist, Robert Sarbacher, wrote in the 1980s to William Steinman, another UFO researcher. Michels brings it up while discussing famous American scientists of the mid-century, John von Neumann, Vannevar Bush and Robert Oppenheimer. He tells it as a paper trail suggesting that respected insiders knew about the UFO question.
sarbacher-s-secret-atomic-lab-in-washing: A researcher named Jan Lundquist, on Jesse Michels' podcast, says that in the 1950s a man named Robert Sarbacher ran atomic research out of a house in a residential part of Washington DC. According to Lundquist, a newspaper reported that Sarbacher had asked to renew a permit to do atomic research at that home address. She tells it as a sign that secret, serious scientific work was going on in unexpected places in that era.
sarbacher-said-von-neumann-was-directly-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that an American scientist named Robert Sarbacher once claimed the famous mathematician John von Neumann was directly involved in secret government work on UFOs in the 1950s. If true, it would mean one of the great minds of the century was brought in to study whatever the government had found.
sarbacher-tells-strieber-about-battelle-: Whitley Strieber, an author, says that in the 1980s a man named Sam gave him the phone number of Robert Sarbacher, a scientist, and told him Sarbacher was eager to talk. Strieber says that when he called, Sarbacher told him in detail about materials he had been working on at the Battelle Memorial Institute, a research institute. Strieber tells it because, as he presents it, it would mean a scientist spoke first-hand about studying unusual materials.
sardinian-elders-dug-up-giant-bones-with: Tim Alberino, a guest on Jesse Michels's podcast, says he interviewed dozens of older people on Sardinia, an Italian island, who told him they had dug up the bones of giants with their own hands, along with jewellery, sometime between the 1930s and 1960s. He credits a researcher named Steve Quayle in connection with the story. If true, it would mean very tall humans once lived there.
sardinians-said-to-descend-from-giants: A researcher named Tim Alberino tells a podcast host, Jesse Michels, about a belief on the Italian island of Sardinia. According to Alberino, some Sardinians say they are descended from giants, which would tie the local people to an ancient race of very large humans.
sarfatti-s-claimed-non-human-intelligenc: Bob Maguire, described as a former contractor for the CIA, the US spy agency, talks on Jesse Michels's podcast about a man named Jack Sarfatti. Maguire says Sarfatti has been working on the question of alien contact for about 50 years, ever since he first claimed, in the 1970s, to have had an experience with a UFO or some non-human intelligence.
sarfatti-s-navy-friend-and-the-living-cr: A researcher named Grant Cameron tells Jesse Michels a story he says came from Jack Sarfatti, about a friend of Sarfatti's in the US Navy on the East Coast. According to the story, the Navy could not break into a craft it held, because the craft is alive, conscious, and has an attitude: unless you vibrate at the right level, you cannot get in. If true, it would mean some recovered craft are living things rather than machines.
sars-spike-protein-modification-proposal: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in 2017 a research group called EcoHealth Alliance submitted a proposal to DARPA, the Pentagon's agency for advanced research, to modify a SARS virus so its spike protein could latch onto ACE2, the doorway the virus uses to enter human cells. According to the story's framing, DARPA turned it down and the work moved to the Wuhan Institute of Virology in China. He tells it in an episode about human experiments, because if true it would mean risky virus work went ahead abroad after being refused at home.
satan-and-his-angels-cast-down-to-earth-: A researcher named Tim Alberino, speaking on Jesse Michels' podcast, describes a belief that Satan and his angels came to Earth, or were thrown down to it, long ago after a great battle in the heavens. In his telling this happened before Adam, the first man in the Bible. If true, it would mean other beings were on Earth before humanity.
satellite-mistaken-for-object-near-jupit: A researcher named Michael Shurmer, speaking in a debate with a skeptic, says that about a year earlier he saw people on X, the social media site, excited about a strange object apparently moving around Jupiter or Saturn. According to Shurmer, it was really a satellite going around the Earth. He tells it as an example of how easily people mistake ordinary things in the sky for something strange.
satellites-shake-over-roraima-s-rare-ear: Aldo Rebelo, a former defence minister of Brazil, tells Jesse Michels about a belief concerning Roraima, a state in the far north of Brazil. He says it is believed that American satellites scanning the planet for minerals shake violently, almost to the point of falling, when they pass over Roraima, because the signal from its rare earths, valuable metals used in electronics, is so strong.
saucer-as-contractor-owned-prototype-wit: Greg Rogers, who describes himself as a NASA doctor, says that in 1992 he saw a saucer-shaped craft in a secret hangar at Cape Canaveral Air Force Station in Florida, hooked up to cables and hoses. He says he believes it was probably owned by a defense contractor, a private company building for the military, and was not part of the US Air Force's own fleet. If true, it would mean private companies hold saucer-shaped craft out of public view.
saucers-fly-on-magnetic-lines-of-force-1: A man named Silus Newton, speaking around 1950 at the University of Denver in Colorado, said that the flying saucer he described, and the others flying, travel along magnetic lines of force, the invisible paths of a magnetic field. He presented this as something he knew first-hand, and if true it would mean saucers use a form of propulsion unknown to ordinary science.
saudi-pilots-filmed-orbs-2024: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in 2024 two pilots flying over Saudi Arabia saw, and filmed, what he calls some crazy orb action: glowing round objects in the sky. He brings it up as a sign that pilots around the world keep running into things they can't explain.
saul-on-the-road-to-damascus-blinded-by-: Chris Bledsoe, a man who says he has seen many strange lights himself, gives his reading of a Bible story from the Book of Acts, where a man named Saul is struck blind by a light on the road to Damascus. Bledsoe says simply that it was an orb, a glowing ball of light, which would link that ancient religious moment to the lights people report today.
saw-sharper-uap-video-on-the-inside-than: Matthew Brown, who presents himself as a Pentagon whistleblower, says that from around 2018 he was shown videos of UAP, the government's newer term for unidentified flying objects. He says the footage he saw on the inside varied in quality, some of it much sharper and clearer about what the object was than anything released to the public. If true, it would mean the government holds better evidence than it has shown.
scalar-treatment-cures-herrera-s-dog-s-b: Michael Herrera, a man who says he saw a huge UFO while serving in Indonesia, says that his dog was diagnosed with a bladder mass that vets thought was cancer. He says the dog was treated with what he calls a scalar treatment, a kind of energy-based healing, and that it cleared the mass. If true, it would mean such treatments can heal disease.
scandinavian-ghost-rockets-that-hit-wate: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells of the "ghost rockets" of the 1940s, a wave of strange flying objects seen over Norway and Sweden. He says there were at least 1,400 documented sightings of rocket and cigar-shaped objects, and that they never landed or crashed on land but always plunged into water, so many that the Swedish government formed a special military unit. He brings it up because, if true, it would suggest these objects had some particular link to the sea.
scandinavian-ufos-come-down-only-in-wate: A Swedish UFO researcher named Clas Svahn says on Jesse Michels' podcast that, since 1946, the unexplained objects reported coming down in Sweden and Norway have all come down in water. He stresses that not a single one has crashed on land in either country. He sees this as an important pattern, since it would suggest the objects choose, or need, water.
scanpyramids-project-uses-muons-to-find-: This story is about ScanPyramids, a project that began around 2015 to look for hidden empty spaces inside the pyramids of Giza in Egypt. A scientist named Filippo Biondi, who has worked on scanning beneath the pyramids, describes it on a podcast with the host Jesse Michels. He says the project uses muons, tiny particles that rain down on Earth from space and can pass through stone. A pyramid researcher named Geoffrey Drumm also talks about it on a later episode. He says a Japanese team has been paying for the work, alongside Egypt's Ministry of Antiquities, the government office in charge of ancient sites. He also points to the project's published paper on muons. If its findings hold, it would mean the pyramids still hold rooms or passages no one has entered.
scans-show-a-second-grand-gallery-inside: A writer on ancient civilisations named Graham Hancock says on Jesse Michels' podcast that scans of the Great Pyramid of Giza in Egypt seem to show a second Grand Gallery. The Grand Gallery is the tall, sloping passage already known inside the pyramid, and Hancock says the scanning shows what looks like another one above it. If so, the pyramid would hold large hidden spaces nobody has entered.
schauberger-devices-that-reportedly-took: A writer named Nick Cook, speaking on Jesse Michels' podcast, mentions old and obscure stories about an Austrian inventor named Viktor Schauberger. According to these stories, in the 1940s, around Austria and Czechoslovakia, Schauberger built machines that reportedly lifted off the ground. If true, it would mean someone built flying devices of an unusual kind decades ago.
schauberger-s-propulsion-work-taken-to-b: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that a man named Viktor Schauberger, who worked on unusual ways of propelling craft, was tricked by the Army Counter Intelligence Corps, a US Army intelligence unit, into handing over his work. Michels says that work ended up at Brookhaven National Laboratory, a US government research lab, and points listeners to the writer Nick Cook for more, which if true would mean the US quietly took over this exotic research.
schauberger-s-wartime-diary-matches-the-: Nick Cook, a writer on aviation, tells podcast host Jesse Michels that he visited the family of Viktor Schauberger, an Austrian inventor, who opened their family files to him, including Schauberger's diary from 1942 to 1945. Cook says the diary matches places, such as Jablonec in what was then Czechoslovakia, tied to Hans Kammler, a Nazi officer who ran secret weapons projects. If true, it would mean Nazi Germany was working on unusual flying technology, possibly antigravity, at those sites.
schauberger-taken-by-ss-to-secret-work-1: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in 1941 an officer of the SS, the Nazi regime's elite force, approached an Austrian man named Viktor Schauberger, and that a period of complete silence in Schauberger's life followed. Michels points to a letter Schauberger wrote to his son, and the story suggests he was taken to do secret work for the Nazis in Austria and Czechoslovakia.
schindele-red-glowing-object-over-minot-: The podcast host Jesse Michels relays the memory of a retired US Air Force captain, David Schindele, who says that in 1966, as he started his shift at Minot Air Force Base in North Dakota, a base holding nuclear missiles, he heard reports of a bright red glowing object hovering over the base. It is told as one of many accounts suggesting UFOs take an interest in nuclear weapons.
schliemann-finds-troy: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells how Heinrich Schliemann, a 19th century German treasure hunter and amateur archaeologist, took the old Greek poet Homer and the historian Herodotus seriously when they wrote about the city of Troy, and found it in Anatolia, in modern Turkey. Michels uses it to make a point: stories people write off as myth can turn out to point at something real.
schriever-disc-test-flight-in-prague-194: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says a man named Hans Kammler recruited Rudolf Schriever, a German technician who claimed to have worked on a disc-shaped flying craft in Prague. According to Schriever's claim as Michels retells it, the disc made its first test flight in February 1945 and climbed to 40,000 feet in three minutes, which if true would mean wartime Germany had built a working flying saucer.
schriever-s-1944-disc-flight: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says a German engineer named Rudolf Schriever claimed that in 1944, in Nazi Germany, his team finally flew a disc-shaped craft and it rose to 40,000 feet in a few minutes. If true, it would mean flying saucers were being built by humans before the first big UFO reports.
schrodinger-s-1944-what-is-life-lectures: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that the physicist Erwin Schrödinger, in his 1944 lecture series called What is Life?, theorized that life is drawn toward order. Michels links this to the work of a biologist at Tufts University, Michael Levin, who he says is finding that living cells have clear goals and intentions, which would mean purpose is built into life itself.
schrodinger-s-what-is-life-and-aperiodic: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, has said more than once that the physicist Erwin Schrödinger, in his 1944 work What is Life?, wrote about "aperiodic crystals" in our genetic material, meaning irregular, non-repeating structures. Michels says Schrödinger saw these as important stores of information, an idea he brings up in talks about strange experiences and how information might reach living things.
schumer-amendment-to-ndaa-gutted-mike-tu: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in 2023 a proposed addition to the yearly US defence law, the National Defense Authorization Act, put forward by Senator Chuck Schumer and aimed at releasing UFO information, was entirely gutted. Michels points to a congressman named Mike Turner as part of that story, which he offers as a sign that some in Congress worked to block disclosure.
schumer-s-64-page-uap-amendment-2023: In 2023, US Senator Chuck Schumer put forward a long amendment, a proposed addition to a law, about UAP, the official term for unexplained objects in the sky. It is often called the UAP Disclosure Act. David Grusch, a man who speaks publicly about secret UFO programs, says Schumer was pushed into writing the 64-page text, and that it openly talks about non-human technology and its recovery. If true, senior senators believe the government holds things that were not made by people. Others name the senators who joined him, including Mike Rounds, Kirsten Gillibrand, Martin Heinrich, Todd Young and Marco Rubio. A man named Karl Nell, speaking from official experience, says the bill basically says Congress is not being told the truth. A commentator, Merrick von Rennenkampff, says the bill mentions non-human intelligence 22 times and also mentions biological evidence. The tellings agree on Schumer and differ in which details they stress.
scientific-breakthroughs-as-divine-inspi: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, suggests that some of the great leaps in physics came to scientists almost like messages from outside. He points to Albert Einstein working out the photoelectric effect while bored at a Swiss patent office desk, Wolfgang Pauli dreaming up the structure of the hydrogen atom, Werner Heisenberg "downloading" his new mathematics on the island of Helgoland, and Paul Dirac staring into a fire in Cambridge before arriving at his famous equation. In a later episode, drawing on the writer Jimena Canales, he adds Niels Bohr and René Descartes and stretches the pattern back to the 1600s, framing it as a sign that inspiration might come from some other intelligence.
scientific-engineering-institute-passes-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says the Scientific Engineering Institute, a research outfit belonging to the CIA (the US spy agency), was quietly moved into private hands in the late 1970s. As he tells it, it passed to the drug company Searle and then to the company Monsanto by 1985, and he ties the story to Donald Rumsfeld, which if true would mean secret government research carried on inside private industry.
scientist-x-lecture-at-university-of-den: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells how on March 8, 1950, a man named Silas Newton took the stage at the University of Denver in Colorado as a mysterious speaker called "Scientist X." Michels tells it in an episode about crashed craft and alien bodies, linking it to names such as George Koehler, Francis Broman and John Torrance Tate, as an early public claim that such crashes had happened.
scientists-find-traces-of-underground-dw: An official described as the president of a republic within Russia tells Jesse Michels that he knows scientists who study caves and rocks. He says that in the Caucasus mountains, in India, in Tibet and in the Altai mountains of Central Asia, they found traces of beings living underground, which would suggest hidden peoples dwelling inside the mountains.
scientists-limited-to-20-minutes-inside-: This story belongs to a reported 1948 crash of a flying saucer in Hart Canyon, near the town of Aztec, New Mexico. Podcast host Jesse Michels says the scientists who went into the craft could not stay inside more than 20 minutes at a time because some negative energy overcame them. Scott Ramsay, who has researched the case for years, tells it secondhand: he says a man told him that a woman told him the scientists would come out sick if they stayed in any longer. If true, the craft itself would have given off something harmful to people.
scientology-belief-in-a-pleiadian-zeta-r: A lawyer and researcher named Dan Sheehan says on a podcast that followers of Scientology, a religious movement, believe a great conflict is under way. In his telling, it pits humanlike beings from the Pleiades, a cluster of stars, against reptilian beings from Zeta Reticuli, another star system, with Earth caught up in it.
scientology-flies-sheehan-to-florida-to-: Dan Sheehan, a lawyer, says that in the 1970s the Church of Scientology tried to recruit him to work for its leader, L. Ron Hubbard. He says they flew him down to Clearwater, Florida, to their big blue building, which he calls the big blue cube. He tells it as part of his story of the powerful groups that tried to win him over.
scientology-s-claim-to-sovereign-status-: Dan Sheehan, a lawyer who says he dealt with the Church of Scientology, says the church believed it deserved to be treated as a sovereign entity, like its own country, because the Catholic Church was. He also speaks of a church programme called Fair Game. He tells it to explain how the organisation saw itself and how it operated.
scientology-s-surveillance-file-on-sheeh: A lawyer named Danny Sheehan says that in the 1970s, around Clearwater, Florida, the Church of Scientology, a religious organisation, kept a file on him that included photographs of him. He tells it in connection with a man named Mark Lane, as an example of being watched by a powerful group while working on sensitive cases.
scif-meeting-with-aaro-head-jon-kosloski: A documentary filmmaker named James Fox, who made a film called The Phenomenon, says that in the 2020s he met Jon Kosloski, head of AARO, the Pentagon office that now investigates UFO reports, inside a SCIF, a sealed room near the Pentagon used for classified conversations. Fox says Kosloski told him, "You know, James, I can't part my hair without the approval of the DoD," meaning the Department of Defense. Fox tells it as a sign of how little freedom the office's head had to speak.
scif-meeting-with-congressional-staffers: Dylan Borland, a man who has come forward with claims about UFOs, says that people helping him put him in touch with the US Congress in 2023. He says he spoke with Congress a few days earlier and then, on March 3, sat in a SCIF, a secure room for discussing classified information, with congressional staffers. He tells it because, as he presents it, it would mean lawmakers' staff took his account seriously enough to hear it in secret, around the same time other whistleblowers were going to Congress.
scif-world-map-briefing-on-borderless-co: Steven Greer, a campaigner who says UFO secrets are held by a hidden global group, says he was once inside a SCIF, a secure sealed room where classified information is discussed. He says there was a map of the world on the wall, used to brief him on a secret organisation that works across national borders. If true, it would mean the secrecy is run by a group answering to no single country.
scott-andrews-taken-to-space-command-as-: Podcast host Jesse Michels, talking with a former Army sergeant named Dan Sherman, passes on a story about a man named Scott Andrews. According to Michels, Andrews was taken as a child to an Air Force base with a space command center, a military hub for watching space, where he did intuitive, mind-based communication with aliens. If true, it would mean the military used gifted children to try to talk with non-humans.
scott-crane-meets-eric-walker-of-majesti: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells of a man named Scott Crane who met a man named Eric Walker, who Crane believed belonged to Majestic 12, a secret group said to control what the US government knows about UFOs. According to Michels, Crane then became a devout Christian and dropped the whole matter, a story that hints at how unsettling such a meeting might be.
scott-kelly-s-tomcat-ufo-was-a-bart-simp: Scott Kelly, who flew the Tomcat, a Navy fighter jet, says that one time in the 1990s, flying off Virginia Beach in a military training area, the officer in his back seat who runs the radar was sure they had flown past a UFO. According to Kelly, it turned out to be a Bart Simpson balloon. He tells it to show how trained crews can mistake everyday things for something strange.
scott-overhears-navajo-men-talk-of-the-o: Scott Ramsay, a researcher, says that around 1988 near Farmington, New Mexico, he overheard some Navajo men talking about a crash site. He says that when he asked, they told him it was an old wives' tale that a UFO had crashed out there in the late 1940s or early 1950s. If true, it would mean local people had long remembered a UFO crash in the area.
scout-craft-powering-up-and-accelerating: Charles Hall, a former Air Force weather observer, says that between 1965 and 1967, in Indian Springs Valley in Nevada, he watched small scout craft belonging to tall white beings power up and race off at 8,000 to 12,000 miles per hour. He says he watched from a distance because getting too close meant the craft's fields would burn you like a microwave. If true, it would mean non-human beings were operating craft near a US military range.
scu-study-of-ufos-at-nuclear-sites-1940: Kevin Knuth, a physicist who researches UFO reports, says that SCU, a group of researchers who study unexplained aerial sightings, did a study on UFOs appearing to monitor US nuclear sites, going back to the 1940s. If true, it would point to a long pattern of these objects watching nuclear weapons.
scully-meets-a-scientist-in-the-mojave-1: A researcher named Scott Ramsay tells Jesse Michels how a writer, Frank Scully, came to write Behind the Flying Saucers, an early book about a crashed saucer. Ramsay says that around 1949 or 1950, Scully met in the Mojave Desert of California with one of two men, named as Silas Newton and Leo GeBauer, who told him an amazing story about recovering a flying saucer. The story matters because it is said to be one of the first accounts of a crashed craft being retrieved.
scully-says-dr-g-is-no-longer-available-: A researcher named Scott Ramsay tells on Jesse Michels' podcast of a 1950 moment at a Chicago radio station involving Frank Scully, a writer who claimed knowledge of crashed flying saucers, and a man named John Torrance Tate. Ramsay says that when Scully was asked to bring forward his scientist source, known as Dr. G, Scully replied that it would not be possible because Dr. G was "no longer available." The moment matters to Ramsay because it bears on whether Scully's source could ever be checked.
sdi-as-a-back-door-to-fund-uap-programs-: A researcher who goes by UAPGerb, speaking with podcast host Jesse Michels, talks about SDI, the Strategic Defense Initiative, which was President Ronald Reagan's 1983 plan for a space-based missile shield. UAPGerb says it likely had a hidden back door to fund secret programmes on UAP, the government's term for unidentified objects in the sky, and even to act offensively against them. He gives it once as his own view and once as something unnamed sources told him. If true, it would mean a famous defence project secretly paid for work on, and against, unknown craft.
sdi-brilliant-pebbles-as-a-black-budget-: A UFO researcher named Steven Greer says that the Strategic Defense Initiative, a 1980s US plan to shoot down nuclear missiles from space, nicknamed Star Wars, and its Brilliant Pebbles scheme of small space-based interceptors, were just a front. He says most of the money went instead into black projects, secret programmes whose budgets are hidden from public view, which would mean a famous defence effort was cover for something else.
sea-supply-corporation-heroin-profits-fu: A lawyer and researcher named Dan Sheehan says that in the 1950s a company called the Sea Supply Corporation was set up with offices in Havana and Miami. In his account, profits from heroin flowed through it to buy weapons for the Kuomintang, the Chinese Nationalist party, and he links it to figures including Paul Helliwell, the mobster Santos Trafficante, William Pawley and Clare Boothe Luce. If true, it would tie secret drug money to Cold War arms deals.
seal-beach-weapons-station-sightings-200: A researcher and writer named Robert Hastings, who studies reports of UFOs near nuclear sites, says local news outlets reported several sightings in March 2009 near the Seal Beach Naval Weapons Station in Orange County, California. According to him, the sightings were close to bunkers that held nuclear weapons, and he tells it as part of a pattern of unknown objects watching nuclear arms.
sealed-needle-in-tube-device-moves-3-4-f: A researcher named Charles Buer says that around 2016, in his lab, he sealed a needle inside a tube, turned up his power supply, and the device moved three to four feet into the air. He mentions a man named Andrew Arjima and says videos are posted on a website called Exodus. If true, it would point to a way of moving things without ordinary thrust, the kind of propulsion the episode calls antigravity.
sean-kirkpatrick-s-aaro-as-a-debunking-e: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that AARO, a Pentagon office set up to investigate unexplained aerial reports, was under Sean Kirkpatrick probably just a "fake hit job on UFOs." sean-kirkpatrick-s-background-at-brookha: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, points out that Sean Kirkpatrick, a US government scientist who has spoken officially about UFOs, once worked at Oak Ridge National Laboratory in Tennessee, a major atomic research site, and at Brookhaven Lab in New York. sean-ryan-threatened-after-the-herrera-i: A UFO researcher named Steven Greer says that Sean Ryan, a podcast host, had a guest named Michael Herrera on his show around 2023, and that shortly afterwards Ryan was threatened. search-for-a-metal-tablet-given-to-a-boy: A Swedish UFO researcher, Clas Svahn, told podcast host Jesse Michels about a search in the north of Sweden. search-for-the-missing-team-brought-in-s: Mario Woods, a former guard at an American nuclear missile base, says his security team went missing for a time in 1977 in the missile fields around Ellsworth Air Force Base, South Dakota, during what he describes as an abduction. search-of-marcus-vinicius-s-house-and-co: Italo Venturelli, a surgeon in Brazil, tells of a man named Marcus Vinicius, who is said to have had a video tape tied to a reported alien case in the town of Varginha. searching-for-a-ufo-that-landed-and-sank: Jesse Michels, a podcast host, says that he and a guest once went to Norway to look for a UFO that witnesses said had landed and then sunk into the water. He mentions it in passing, and if true it would mean a craft might still lie hidden there.
second-alien-communicator-nicknamed-bone: Dan Sherman, a former Air Force sergeant, says that the NSA, the US spy agency that intercepts communications, trained him in the early 1990s to receive messages from aliens by thought. second-century-latin-inscribed-on-rocket: The podcast host Jesse Michels says that Diana Pasulka, a professor who studies religion and belief in UFOs, has said that second-century Latin was written or inscribed on some NASA missions, such as on the rockets. second-craft-near-skinwalker-ranch-shoot: The podcast host Jesse Michels relays an account from the businessman Robert Bigelow about a craft seen near Skinwalker Ranch, a Utah property known for reports of strange happenings. second-face-found-in-utopia-1980: John Brandenburg, a physicist, says that in the 1980s he studied pictures of Utopia, a region of Mars that he says once lay on the shore of an ancient ocean. second-giza-scan-paper-under-peer-review: Filippo Biondi, an Italian scientist who uses satellite radar to look underground, tells podcast host Jesse Michels that in 2025 his team is working on a second scientific paper about their scan beneath the Khafre pyramid at Giza in Egypt. second-marine-squadmate-reaches-out-via-: Michael Herrera, a former US Marine who says he saw a huge craft, about 300 feet across, in the Indonesian jungle, tells podcast host Jesse Michels that in 2024 a second man from his old squad contacted him on LinkedIn, a website for work contacts. second-meeting-implants-not-ganglion-199: Bryce Zable, a television writer, says that in 1996, at the offices of Dark Skies, a TV series about aliens he worked on, he had a second meeting with visitors he refers to as JC and the captain. second-night-at-carman-ping-pong-ball-ob: A Canadian UFO researcher named Grant Cameron says that around May 1975, near the small town of Carman in Manitoba, Canada, he went out a second night and watched an object people called the "ping pong ball" jumping around the sky, and that it was photographed. second-regression-michael-lying-opposite: A former US Air Force man named Mario Woods says he was taken aboard a craft in 1977 while serving in South Dakota. second-silent-object-seen-by-three-witne: The owner of Skinwalker Ranch, a Utah property famous for reports of strange events, says that around 2016 a second unknown object appeared there a few weeks after a first one. second-voice-download-you-have-everythin: A witness named Brent says he has received messages he calls "downloads", which come to him like a voice in his mind. He says the second one he got told him: "you have everything you need." He gives no time or place for it.
secrecy-briefing-at-kilo-control-and-ost: A former US Air Force man named Mario Woods says that in November 1977, after a strange incident in the nuclear missile fields around Ellsworth Air Force Base in South Dakota, he was sent to Kilo control, one of the posts that oversee those missiles. secret-electrogravitic-propulsion-progra: Matthew Brown, introduced on Jesse Michels's podcast as a Pentagon whistleblower, says the United States has secret programs on electromagnetic and electrogravitic propulsion, meaning ways to move craft by using electricity to work against gravity. secret-kennedy-khrushchev-letters-on-des: Dan Sheehan, a lawyer who has worked on UFO disclosure, says that in 1963 President John F. Kennedy began secretly exchanging letters with Nikita Khrushchev, the Soviet leader, passed through the American editor Norman Cousins. secret-machines-adviser-genocides-may-be: Jason Samosa, a UFO researcher, points to Sekret Machines, a series of non-fiction books written by the musician Tom DeLonge and the author Peter Levenda with input from military and intelligence advisers. secret-pentagon-program-to-build-weapons: A man named Dan Sheehan says on Jesse Michels' podcast that from about 2007 to 2017 the Pentagon, the headquarters of the US military, ran a secret program classified above top secret. secret-radiation-testing-of-animals-afte: An Australian journalist, Ross Coulthart, says that one of the first things he found in the Australian national archives was evidence of secret tests on animals. secret-service-guarded-the-dying-von-neu: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that when the famous mathematician John von Neumann lay dying in a naval hospital in 1957, the Secret Service was posted outside his room because they were afraid of what he might say. secret-space-program-friend-s-father-s-s: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that a writer named Diana Pasulka, in her book Encounters, interviews a friend who was allegedly part of one of the secret American space programmes. secret-ufo-briefings-of-the-trump-camp-b: Ross Coulthart, an Australian journalist who reports on UFOs, says that in 2024, before Donald Trump's team took office, there were several secret briefings about UFOs given to the Trump camp. secret-us-air-force-plane-landed-without: James Fox, speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast, recounts what he was told about Varginha, a town in Brazil where people say a strange creature was captured in 1996. secret-us-fundamental-physics-research-a: This story is the idea that the US government has secretly been doing research into the basic laws of physics since around the end of the Second World War, and has kept the results hidden. secretive-spy-vs-spy-meetings-with-gary-: James Valor, connected to a startup called Skywatcher that says it tries to call UFOs down, says that between 2021 and 2024 he took part in secretive, spy-versus-spy style meetings with a man named Garry Nolan and with staff from the US Congress. security-guard-george-frozen-and-later-h: A businessman named Brandon Fugal, who owns Skinwalker Ranch, a property in Utah famous for reports of strange happenings, says that around October 2016 a security guard named George had a frightening experience on a raised flat area of the ranch called the mesa. seeing-a-tag-along-object: In a clip played on a podcast episode about a NASA doctor, an unnamed witness says he saw an object that he calls a "tag along", meaning something that seemed to follow along. He gives no place or time for the sighting.
seeing-a-ufo-while-remote-viewing-mount-: A former US Army sergeant named Lyn Buchanan says he once trained in remote viewing, the practice of trying to describe a distant place using only the mind. seeing-tall-white-children-in-the-indian: A man named Charles Hall, who says he spent three years in the 1960s among tall, pale beings he calls the Tall Whites while stationed at Indian Springs, a military site in the Nevada desert, says these beings would come into his barracks there. selective-service-chief-russians-moving-: A writer named Peter Levenda says that around 1968 the head of the Selective Service in New York, the US office that ran the military draft, told him the Russians were sneaking spies into the United States through Orthodox churches. selectively-visible-lights-over-valley-o: A man named Steve says that once, while driving with his son on Highway 40 through a remote stretch toward their old vacation spot in Bullhead City, Arizona, he saw a bright white light hovering over a valley about 5 to 10 miles away. self-designed-doctorate-in-parapsycholog: A researcher named Jeffrey Mishlove says that in the 1970s he designed his own doctoral program at the University of California, Berkeley. semivan-and-kit-green-question-tom-delon: A UFO researcher named Grant Cameron says on Jesse Michels' podcast that around 2015 two advisers, Jim Semivan and Kit Green, met a musician named Tom DeLonge in a hotel room in the United States. semivan-on-a-non-state-intelligence-netw: On a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, a narrator relays a claim from Jim Semivan, a former CIA officer. senate-armed-services-staff-on-admiral-w: This story is about a Navy admiral named Thomas Wilson and claims about wreckage from UFOs that has been taken apart and copied, which people call reverse engineering. senate-findings-that-uap-records-were-wr: Matthew Pines, a security analyst, says that the US Senate, in findings attached to its 2023 and 2024 legislation on UAP, the government's term for UFOs, stated that credible evidence indicates UAP records were wrongly kept secret. senate-intelligence-scif-meeting-and-bla: This story is about a meeting around 2022 with the Senate Intelligence Committee, the part of the US Senate that oversees spy agencies, held in a SCIF, a sealed room built for discussing classified secrets. senate-language-on-historical-exotic-tec: Matthew Pines, a security analyst, points to wording in US Senate legislation from 2023 and 2024 on UAP, the government's term for UFOs. senate-staff-meet-mellon-puthoff-davis-t: A former US Senate staff member, Kurt McConnell, says that around 2017 and 2018 he and other Senate staff in Washington met a string of people tied to the UFO subject: Chris Mellon, Lou Elizondo, Dr. Harold Puthoff and Dr. Eric Davis. senate-to-pass-the-64-page-uap-disclosur: A lawyer named Danny Sheehan says that in 2025 or 2026 the US Senate is going to pass again the 64-page UAP Disclosure Act, a bill meant to force the government to release its records on UFOs, which it calls unidentified anomalous phenomena. senator-claiborne-pell-part-of-the-cabal: A UFO researcher named Steven Greer says that Claiborne Pell, a US senator, was part of a cabal, a small secret group he believes controls UFO secrets. Greer says he only found this out after Pell died.
senator-cussed-out-by-curtis-lemay-over-: The story is that a US senator once phoned Curtis LeMay, a top Air Force general, and said he knew there was a room at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base in Ohio where all the secret material was kept, and asked to go in. senator-gillibrand-s-uap-legislation-gil: Matthew Pines, a security analyst, notes that Senator Kirsten Gillibrand of New York was involved both in early UAP laws, UAP being the government's term for UFOs, through amendments with Senator Marco Rubio, and in cryptocurrency legislation through a bill with Senator Cynthia Lummis, all in the early 2020s. senator-inouye-on-a-shadow-government-du: A UFO researcher named Steven Greer recalls that Daniel Inouye, a US senator, spoke during the Iran-Contra affair, a 1980s scandal over secret US arms sales to Iran. senator-reid-they-re-shutting-down-our-n: A filmmaker named James Fox says that around 2019 or 2020 he asked Harry Reid, a former US Senate leader, about UFOs. senator-ted-stevens-foo-fighter-encounte: Ted Stevens flew as a pilot in World War II and later became a US senator for Alaska. senior-ge-scalar-physicist-at-greer-s-20: Steven Greer, a man who runs a group pushing for the government to reveal UFO secrets, says that at a 2023 conference he held in Washington, just before an event at the National Press Club, a speaker was a senior physicist from GE, the big American engineering company. senior-intelligence-official-and-his-wif: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says he knows of one very senior US intelligence official who, together with his wife, had a frightening experience of being abducted, taken away by some non-human presence. senior-navy-sources-say-the-greys-geneti: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says he has heard from some senior and impressive people in the US Navy that the greys may be real. senior-nsa-official-blocks-a-finding-fro: Eric Haseltine, a former senior official at the NSA, the US agency that intercepts and studies communications, says that in the 2000s his team found something they planned to tell President George W. Bush. He says a senior official above him, a woman, refused and said she would not let them do it. If true, it would show that findings can be stopped before they ever reach the president.
senior-vp-material-scientist-no-physicis: Eric Davis, a physicist who has worked on Pentagon studies, says that in the 2010s a senior vice president and materials scientist at an old, established aerospace company told him about the company's program to study crashed craft of unknown origin. sensory-deprivation-training-as-sac-s-ba: An author named Peter Levenda, who writes about secret history, says that Strategic Air Command, the US Air Force branch that ran nuclear bombers, used sensory deprivation training, cutting people off from sight and sound, between the 1950s and 1970s. sent-to-sri-to-assess-the-gondola-wish-p: A former US Army soldier named Joe McMoneagle says that in 1978 a General Roya learned of a secret Army project called Gondola Wish starting at Fort Meade, an Army base, and was nervous about it. sentinels-of-ether-reverse-engineered-cr: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, citing a work called Sentinels of Ether and a man named Jake Barber, says that craft copied from recovered non-human technology need "psionic assets" to fly. september-1993-meeting-with-wright-patte: Steven Greer, a man who campaigns for the government to reveal UFO secrets, says that in September 1993 he met a colonel he calls Colonel Canola at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base in Ohio. serapeum-granite-boxes-found-blown-apart: A researcher named Matt, speaking on Jesse Michels' podcast, talks about the Serapeum, a set of underground chambers at Saqqara in Egypt that hold huge granite boxes. sergeant-larson-s-onion-speech-on-secrec: Dan Sherman, a former US Air Force sergeant who says the National Security Agency, the US spy agency for intercepted signals, had him communicate with aliens, tells podcast host Jesse Michels about a moment in the early 1990s at a base overseas. serpo-alien-language-decoded-from-a-live: Deep Prasad, a guest on Jesse Michels's podcast, talks about Roswell, New Mexico, where some say a craft crashed in 1947 and bodies were recovered. sethite-theory-adopted-by-jews-and-by-th: Tim Alberino, a guest on Jesse Michels's podcast, talks about a passage in Genesis 6, the part of the Bible where the 'sons of God' have children with human women. seven-government-attempts-to-seize-the-b: A witness named Martin Alacrone, speaking about strange three-fingered bodies kept at the University of Ica in Peru, says that in the 2020s the authorities came to take them on seven separate occasions. several-such-sites-around-the-world: Michael Herrera, a man who says he saw a huge craft in the Indonesian jungle, told podcast host Jesse Michels that such sites are not unique. shaft-and-chamber-system-found-under-the: A man named Jeffrey, speaking on a podcast about a hidden energy system under the pyramids of Egypt, says early excavation reports on the Great Pyramid of Giza, from the late 1800s or early 1900s, describe a pit in the Queen's Chamber, a room inside the pyramid, that was filled with rubble and dirt. shafts-below-the-sphinx-admitted-by-zahi: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says there definitely are shafts running beneath the Great Sphinx at Giza in Egypt. shah-bought-laser-isotope-enrichment-tec: A writer named Jason Jorjani says on Jesse Michels' podcast that in 1970 the Shah, the king who then ruled Iran, bought laser isotope enrichment technology from Switzerland. shallow-lunar-craters-with-a-hard-convex: A philosopher named Jason Jorjani says on a podcast that craters on the Moon are all only a few miles deep, never more than five or six. He takes this to mean the Moon has a hard floor beneath its surface, a hint that it may not be what it seems.
shamans-accounts-of-little-men-out-of-a-: A researcher and writer named Jacques Vallee, author of a book called Passport to Magonia that compares old folklore with modern UFO reports, tells of a shaman, a traditional spiritual healer, from the Pacific or Siberia region. Vallee says the shaman told him that, fifty years before, little men had come out of a big light. He tells it because, if such accounts are real, the beings in today's UFO stories would have been showing up in traditional cultures for a long time.
shane-freaks-shown-a-sphere: Podcast host Jesse Michels mentions a man named Shane Freaks, an old military veteran who posts on Twitter. According to Michels, Freaks says he was once shown a sphere, apparently some kind of unexplained object. If true, it would add one more person claiming to have seen such hidden objects up close.
shard-thousands-of-feet-tall-beside-a-ma: Joe McMoneagle, who says he was trained as a remote viewer, someone who tries to see distant places using only the mind, tells podcast host Jesse Michels about photo negatives from the mapping of Mars by JPL, NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory. He says that beside an impact crater on Mars there is an object he says is not a pyramid but a shard, thousands of feet tall. He tells it because, if true, Mars once held life that built things.
sheehan-as-counsel-to-disclosure-project: A lawyer named Dan Sheehan says that for about 20 years he was legal counsel for the Disclosure Project, a group pushing the government to reveal what it knows about UFOs. He says he also represented a doctor named John Mack and took part in a peer group, and that a man named Lou Elizondo knew all of this, which he offers as proof of his long place at the center of the subject.
sheehan-gets-access-to-every-internal-sc: A man named Dan Sheehan, speaking with podcast host Jesse Michels, says that in the 1970s he dealt with the Church of Scientology, a religious movement founded by L. Ron Hubbard, at its headquarters in Florida. Sheehan says he refused even to meet Hubbard unless he was first given access to every internal document the church held anywhere in the world, including the files of its Guardian's Office, the church's internal security and legal branch. He tells it to show how deep his inside view of the organisation went.
sheehan-gets-an-injunction-against-the-s: A lawyer named Dan Sheehan, speaking with podcast host Jesse Michels, says that in the 1970s he went to New York to fight subpoenas, court orders forcing people to testify, that a grand jury had aimed at the Church of Scientology. Sheehan says he was licensed to practise in the federal court for southern New York, and that he got an injunction there, a court order that shut the subpoenas down. He tells it as part of his story of a career spent in the middle of big, contested legal fights.
sheehan-represented-john-mack-and-vetted: A lawyer named Dan Sheehan tells podcast host Jesse Michels that from the 1990s until about 2004 he was the legal representative of John Mack, a man at Harvard who worked with people who say they have had contact with non-human beings, often called experiencers. Sheehan says that over those ten years he met dozens of the people Mack had worked with. If his account holds, it means a lawyer saw these witnesses up close and took their stories seriously.
sheehan-s-account-of-james-mccord-and-th: A lawyer named Dan Sheehan says that in 1972 President Richard Nixon wanted to know whether Larry O'Brien, a Democratic party leader, knew about a secret matter tied to the billionaire Howard Hughes and might use it, so he had O'Brien's phone tapped and office bugged, the break-in at the Watergate building in Washington that became a national scandal. Podcast host Jesse Michels repeats the story, adding that James McCord, one of the burglars, was ordered to do it without being told why, though in one retelling Michels calls O'Brien the head of George McGovern's campaign and the bugged line his cell phone. If true, it would mean the scandal that brought down a president began with a hidden secret.
sheehan-visits-ingo-swann-at-his-new-yor: A lawyer named Dan Sheehan says that in the 1970s he went to see Ingo Swann, a man known for psychic work, at his apartment in New York City. Sheehan says Swann led him all the way upstairs and out onto the roof. He tells it as part of his own path into the world of psychics and UFOs, a meeting that, if true, put him in contact with a key figure in that world.
sheffield-edwards-gives-the-green-light-: A guest named Dan Sheehan, speaking on a podcast episode about UFOs and President John F. Kennedy, tells of a 1960 meeting at the Fontainebleau Hotel in Miami. Sheehan says another man joined the meeting under the cover name "Mr. Ed", and that this man was Sheffield Edwards, who gave the go-ahead for what was being planned there. He names others linked to the meeting as Santos Trafficante, Johnny Roselli, Bob Maheu and Sam Giancana, and tells it because, if true, it ties secret government dealings to the story he goes on to tell about Kennedy.
sheldrake-s-crystals-growing-faster-afte: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, describes an idea from a biologist named Rupert Sheldrake: when you grow a new kind of crystal in a lab dish, it takes a long time the first time, then grows much faster after that. If true, it would suggest nature has a kind of memory, with things getting easier once they have happened somewhere before.
sheldrake-s-paper-is-the-sun-conscious: A guest on a podcast about consciousness and UFOs, James Madden, mentions a paper by the writer Rupert Sheldrake titled "Is the Sun Conscious?". Madden calls it really interesting, and raises it because, if the Sun could have a mind of its own, consciousness might be far more widespread in the universe than we usually assume.
sheldrake-s-plant-research-at-an-agricul: A scientist named Rupert Sheldrake tells podcast host Jesse Michels that he spent years in India working at an agricultural research institute. He says his job there was breeding better chickpeas and pigeon peas, two food crops. He brings it up as part of his background as a working plant scientist, before the ideas that made him controversial.
sheldrake-s-ted-talk-censored-and-taken-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in 2013 a talk given by the scientist Rupert Sheldrake for TED, a well-known series of short public lectures, was censored and taken off YouTube. He tells it to suggest that mainstream science pushes out ideas it finds uncomfortable.
sherman-accounts-of-orbs-and-giant-wolf-: Brandon Fugal, the owner of Skinwalker Ranch in Utah, a property known for reports of strange events, says the stories go back to the Shermans, the family who lived there in the 1990s. According to those accounts, glowing balls of light and even giant wolf-like creatures were seen heading toward Dry Gulch Creek, a part of the ranch, and then vanishing. He tells it because it suggests that one spot on the ranch has long drawn something unusual.
sherman-family-haunted-off-the-ranch-199: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in the 1990s a family called the Shermans took over Skinwalker Ranch in Utah, a property famous for strange happenings, and were basically haunted off it. According to his telling, they saw glowing orbs, UFOs and skinwalkers, shape-shifting creatures from Native American legend, and were even rushed by an oversized wolf walking on two legs that they said survived a close-range shotgun blast, which if true would make the ranch a hotspot for things science cannot explain.
sherman-on-affecting-the-sine-wave-at-wi: A man named Dan Sherman, who says he was drawn into a secret UFO programme as a child, tells podcast host Jesse Michels about tests in the 1990s at a complex of the NSA, the US government's signals intelligence agency, in Maryland. Sherman says he was shown a sine wave, a smooth repeating wave line, and that he could change its motion with his mind, just at will. If true, it would mean a person's mind can directly affect a machine's signal.
sherman-s-base-photo-identified-as-san-v: A podcast host named Jesse Michels says that a man named Dan Sherman included a photo of the base where he worked in his book Above Black. Michels says he and his researcher ran the photo through a reverse image search and found it was San Vito dei Normanni, a base in southern Italy, from the 1990s. He tells it as a way of checking where Sherman's story took place.
sherman-s-mother-abducted-and-fetus-gene: Dan Sherman, a former Air Force sergeant who says the NSA, the US agency that intercepts communications, hired him to talk with aliens, tells a story about his own birth. He says a Captain White told him that his mother had been abducted before, and that in 1963, while she was pregnant with him, she was taken again and the baby was 'genetically managed'. If true, it would mean he was shaped from before birth for that contact work.
sherman-s-sine-wave-tone-training-1990: A former intelligence worker named Dan Sherman says that in the early 1990s he was put through an unusual training. He says a trainer played a pure, steady tone and told him to hum it in his mind. If true, it would be part of an effort to train people to receive messages by thought alone.
shermans-direwolf-survives-a-12-gauge-sh: Brandon Fugal, the owner of Skinwalker Ranch, a Utah property famous for strange reports, tells of the Sherman family, who lived there in the mid 1990s. According to Fugal, citing a Deseret News newspaper report by Zack Van Eyk, a huge wolf-like animal attacked their prized cattle and was shot with a 12-gauge shotgun yet seemed unharmed, which would suggest something far from an ordinary animal.
shermer-s-1983-alien-abduction-experienc: A well-known skeptic and writer named Michael Shermer says that in 1983, while riding in the Race Across America, a bicycle race across the country, he had what he calls an alien abduction experience on a lonely rural highway near Haigler, Nebraska. He mentions the cyclist Eric Heiden and says he described the episode in an interview on ABC's Wide World of Sports, a television sports show. He tells it as something he lived through himself.
shirley-maclaine-s-going-within-meeting-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that the actress and writer Shirley MacLaine wrote in her book Going Within about being in a government office in Washington, DC with Claiborne Pell, a US senator. Michels links the scene to Budd Hopkins, a researcher of alien abduction accounts, and to a prince, Hans-Adam. He tells it because it would place powerful officials in quiet conversations about these subjects.
shoemaker-levy-9-breaks-apart-and-strike: A researcher named Randall Carlson says that a comet called Shoemaker-Levy 9 broke apart into 21 pieces. He says those pieces struck the planet Jupiter in about the second week of July 1994, which he offers as proof that such impacts really happen in our solar system.
short-strange-looking-police-officer-esc: A former truck driver, known only as Michael, tells podcast host Jesse Michels that around 1977, after a UFO sighting and a stretch of time he cannot account for, he ended up on restricted government land in Nevada. He says a police officer escorted him off, and that the man looked strange: short, with a puffy face and a hat like the one worn by the cartoon character Deputy Dawg. He tells it because the officer seemed not quite like an ordinary person, which would hint that something unusual was guarding that land.
shroud-of-turin-dating-tested-later-repa: A researcher named Randall Carlson talks about the Shroud of Turin, a linen cloth kept in Turin, Italy, that many believe wrapped the body of Jesus. Carlson says the cloth was repaired several times over the centuries, so some of its pieces are much younger than the original, and that the scientific dating done in the 1980s may have tested those later patches. If he is right, the original cloth could be far older than the tests suggested.
shurmer-and-avi-loeb-s-alien-bet-with-th: Michael Shermer, a well-known skeptic, says he and Avi Loeb, a Harvard astronomer who searches for signs of aliens, have a $1,000 bet about whether proof of aliens will turn up by 2030. He says the bet is held by the Long Now Foundation, a group that keeps long-term wagers. It shows two scientists disagreeing openly, with money on the line, over whether alien contact will be confirmed soon.
shuruppak-excavation-finds-a-flood-layer: A researcher named Matt, on Jesse Michels's podcast, talks about Shuruppak, an ancient city in what is now Iraq. Citing a 1931 dig report from the Penn Museum, the University of Pennsylvania's archaeology museum, he says a layer of flood mud about four feet thick sits right on top of the city, which he calls one of the oldest on Earth, sealed and buried by the flood. He tells it as evidence that a great flood of the kind in ancient stories really struck.
sidney-sheldon-s-novel-about-a-crashed-s: A lawyer and activist, Dan Sheehan, says the best-selling novelist Sidney Sheldon knew something about UFOs that he would never dare say in public, so he wrote a novel, The Doomsday Project, about a crashed saucer in Italy seen by people on a tour bus. Sheehan links the story to the television producers Bill Todman Sr. and Jr. He tells it to suggest that fiction was used to hint at real secrets.
sighting-map-clusters-around-trinity-sit: James Fox, a documentary filmmaker known for a film called The Phenomenon, says that when UFO sightings from the 1940s and 1950s were plotted on a map, they bunched up around Trinity Site, the spot in the New Mexico desert where the first atomic bomb was tested. Drawing on the work of researchers Lance Mungia and Robert Hastings, he says "the proximity to Trinity site was unbelievable." If true, it would suggest that whatever people were seeing was drawn to the birthplace of nuclear weapons.
signals-beamed-into-benowitz-s-computer-: Greg Bishop, a writer on UFO history, told Jesse Michels about a man named Benowitz in Albuquerque, New Mexico, in the early 1980s, near Sandia National Laboratories, a government research lab. Bishop says UFO researcher Bill Moore told him that signals were beamed into Benowitz's computer from across the street. If true, it would mean someone was deliberately feeding Benowitz information, and Bishop allows that maybe it happened.
signed-copy-of-alien-conspiracy-2004: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says he came across a copy of a work called Alien Conspiracy, and when he opened it the first page was signed by a man named Chris Evans and dated December 1st, 2004. Michels tells it as a find that links Evans to the material, which he presents as part of his search for proof of crashed alien bodies.
silas-newton-speech-beings-interested-in: In 1950 a man named Silas Newton gave a speech in the United States about visitors from elsewhere, and his words are replayed in an episode of Jesse Michels' podcast. Newton says that these beings were, without question, interested in human atomic research. If true, it would mean non-human visitors were watching our work on nuclear power and weapons.
silent-black-triangles-over-aboriginal-c: An Australian journalist, Ross Coulthart, says that Aboriginal people, the first peoples of Australia, living in the remote Outback have told of black triangles flying over their communities. According to them, these triangle-shaped craft make no sound at all, which, if true, would point to some unknown aircraft operating over the Outback.
silent-triangle-ufo-in-florida-2019: A writer named Peter Levenda says that in December 2019, shortly before the COVID pandemic, he saw a silent, triangle-shaped object with lights in the sky over Florida. He says he was with someone named Tom at the time. If true, it would be a firsthand sighting of a strange craft that made no sound.
silver-bridge-collapse-drowning-victims-: A philosopher named Jason Jorjani, talking on the podcast of host Jesse Michels, retells a story he credits to John Keel, a writer on strange events. Jorjani says that around Christmas 1967, when the Silver Bridge at Point Pleasant (which he places in Pennsylvania) fell into the river, some people who were drowning suddenly heard voices calling out numbers, like 3004 and 3,486, and saying "wake up, wake up", and then they came back to life. If true, it would suggest some unseen intelligence stepping in at the moment of death.
silver-disc-above-the-mesa-darts-away-20: Brandon Fugal is the owner of Skinwalker Ranch, a property in Utah known for reports of strange events. On the podcast of host Jesse Michels in 2022, he says that on 14 October 2016 he looked straight ahead above the mesa, a flat-topped hill on the ranch. He says a silver-gray disc was hanging in the air about a hundred feet above it, and then it darted away. In a 2026 episode of the same show, he calls it his first sighting, the one that turned him from a skeptic into an experiencer within minutes. There he credits Eric Bard, who was with him. He also describes it as a physical craft, a flying saucer in broad daylight right in front of them, without saying it darted off. If true, it would mean a solid craft showed itself openly over the ranch. All the tellings are Fugal's own, years apart, with a fellow witness named.
silver-sky-memo-given-to-moore-as-a-test: A writer named Greg Bishop tells of a document called the Silver Sky memo, which seemed to describe a secret government project named Silver Sky from around the late 1940s or early 1950s in New Mexico. According to Bishop, the memo was handed to a UFO researcher named Bill Moore around 1980 as a kind of test, and Moore says he checked it out and found it was made up too. The story matters because, had the memo been real, it would have pointed to a hidden project tied to UFOs.
silver-snake-comes-out-of-the-burnt-tree: A man named Chris Bledsoe, who says UFOs show up around him, tells podcast host Jesse Michels about something he saw in his backyard in North Carolina, some time after a trip to Zanesville. He says that all of a sudden a silver snake came out of a burnt tree. He tells it as one more strange event in a life he says is full of them.
silver-surfer-video-bill-nye-s-brine-shr: Jeremy Corbell, a guest on Jesse Michels' podcast, says that around 2008 in Santa Monica, California, he saw something in the sky he could not identify, filmed it, posted the video online and nicknamed the object the Silver Surfer. As the story is told, the TV science presenter Bill Nye suggested the thing was brine shrimp, and another explanation said it was a Red Bull skydiver. Corbell rejects both, and he tells it because to him it shows an unknown object being explained away.
similar-incursions-at-norfolk-naval-base: A former Navy fighter pilot named Ryan Graves, speaking on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, passes on what someone told him: unknown objects had made similar incursions, meaning they entered protected airspace without permission, at Norfolk Naval Base in Virginia and over Washington, DC. He gives no date. If true, it would mean unexplained objects were moving freely over a major military base and the nation's capital.
similar-structures-under-menkaure-2-2-an: A scientist named Filippo Biondi, who says he used radar scans to look beneath the pyramids of Giza in Egypt, tells podcast host Jesse Michels that in 2025 he found structures under the pyramid of Khafre. He says he found the same kind of thing under the pyramid of Menkaure, two pairs of them, and one under the Sphinx, the great carved lion statue nearby. If true, it would mean there is a hidden, planned system underground across the whole site.
simon-magus-levitating-and-peter-and-pau: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, retells an early Christian legend about Simon Magus, a sorcerer who uses black magic to levitate, and then comes up against the apostles Peter and Paul. He brings it up as an old story of strange powers in the air and a clash between rival forces.
simone-s-belief-that-ai-is-the-current-r: A researcher named Diana Pasulka, who studies religion and beliefs about UFOs, says that a woman called Simone, the subject of a chapter in her book Encounters, believes we are living through a literal revelation in the 2020s. According to Pasulka, Simone thinks the thing being revealed is AI, meaning artificial intelligence. If true, it would recast today's technology as something closer to a religious event.
simons-engineered-stony-brook-joint-mana: A researcher named Matthew Pines, speaking on podcast host Jesse Michels's show, says that Stony Brook University teamed up with the Battelle Memorial Institute, a private research organisation, to run Brookhaven National Laboratory, a US government science lab on Long Island, New York. Pines says this partnership was personally arranged by Jim Simons, a mathematician and wealthy investor, which he presents as a sign that powerful private figures quietly shape where serious physics gets done.
simons-foundation-head-david-spergel-cha: In 2022 the US space agency NASA set up an independent panel to study UAP, which stands for unidentified anomalous phenomena, the newer name for UFOs. A researcher named Matthew Pines, speaking on Jesse Michels' podcast, says the panel was chaired by Dr. David Spergel, the head of the Simons Foundation, a science foundation linked to Jim Simons. Michels, the host, returns to this on several later episodes. Once he poses it as a question, asking whether the panel's leader had ties to Simons. Another time he adds that Simons started a company called Renaissance Technologies, and another time he calls Spergel Simons' principal scientific adviser. Michels credits the researcher Eric Weinstein for drawing attention to the link. They raise it because, if it means what they suggest, the same small circle of wealthy patrons may shape how official UFO science is done.
simons-if-you-knew-how-he-actually-made-: Eric Weinstein, a researcher, says he once met a man named Jim Simons. In this telling, Simons took a drag on his cigarette, paused for a long time, and said, "Eric, if you knew how he actually made money, you'd be so disappointed." A podcast host, Jesse Michels, later repeated the story secondhand without the cigarette, and he tells it as a hint that the real source of some famous success is hidden.
simosa-s-conversion-to-and-departure-fro: Jason Simosa, a researcher from England, says he became a Christian at 19, "kind of out of nowhere," and that he left the faith again by about 25. He mentions someone named Viv Whitten as part of that story, which he tells to explain how his own religious journey shapes his view of the subject.
simpkinson-gemini-11-ufo-lithograph-like: A physicist and UFO researcher, Kevin Knuth, talks about a printed picture from Gemini 11, a 1966 NASA spaceflight, that seems to show a UFO and is tied to a NASA man named Scott Simpkinson. Knuth says a colleague, Ed Wilson, found the original photograph in the University of Arizona archives, showing Earth with the same cloud pattern but no UFO. That, as Knuth tells it, means the UFO in the printed version was likely added as a mock-up.
simpkinson-s-nasa-files-auctioned-and-bo: A scientist named Kevin Knuth, speaking on a podcast about NASA, the US space agency, tells how a set of NASA files belonging to a man named Scott Simpkinson came to light. Knuth says that after Simpkinson and a woman named Emily Erdle had both died, the files went up for auction, a man named Ed Wilson bought them, and among them he found a lithograph, a kind of printed image. The story matters to Knuth because, as he tells it, the files held material NASA had never shared.
sir-peter-horsley-approached-by-nordics-: A philosopher named Jason Jorjani tells of Sir Peter Horsley, a senior British figure, who in the 1950s was reportedly approached by "Nordics", the tall, fair, human-looking beings described in some UFO stories. According to the account, which Jorjani credits to a book called Closer Encounters, two of them, calling themselves Miss Markham and Mr. Janus, invited Horsley to a quiet fireside talk. If true, it would mean non-human visitors sought out people close to power in Britain.
sirhan-sirhan-as-an-mk-ultra-subject-lin: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Sirhan Sirhan, the man convicted of shooting Robert F. Kennedy in 1968, was himself a patient of MK Ultra, a secret CIA programme that experimented with mind control. Michels bases this on Sirhan having spent time with a man named William Joseph Bryan, with the story tied to the Santa Anita racetrack in California, which if true would mean the killing was shaped by government mind experiments.
sirhan-sirhan-s-diary-before-the-rfk-sho: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, mentions the diary of Sirhan Sirhan, the man who shot the politician Robert F. Kennedy in Los Angeles in 1968. Michels points to what Sirhan wrote in that diary just before the shooting, raising it as a possible sign that more lay behind the killing than one man acting alone.
sirius-program: A man described as a Pentagon whistleblower, Matthew Brown, told podcast host Jesse Michels about something called Sirius, which comes up in a message he posted publicly to the tech billionaire Elon Musk. Asked about it, Brown said only that "Sirius is a star," and left what the name points to unclear.
sister-maria-s-flame-in-the-convent-cell: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells of a young nun, Sister Maria, who in the late 1800s was sleeping in her small cell in a Catholic convent. He says she was woken by a shining object like a flame that seemed to come out of the wall and hover above her, a story he tells in an episode about how religious visions and UFO encounters might be linked.
site-in-texas-that-teaches-blindfolded-s: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says he thinks there is a site in Texas that teaches people to develop unusual senses, such as sensing things while blindfolded. He mentions it in a conversation about the edges of science, as a hint that people may have abilities that can be trained.
sitting-beside-arthur-c-clarke-at-the-20: Whitley Strieber, a writer known for describing his own encounters with strange beings, says that in London in 1968 he went to see 2001: A Space Odyssey, Stanley Kubrick's film based on a story called The Sentinel, and ended up sitting right beside its co-writer, Arthur C. Clarke. He tells it as a memorable chance meeting from his early life.
six-fingered-diorite-hand-found-at-shuru: A researcher named Matt, speaking on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, says that in 1931 diggers at Shuruppak, an ancient city site in Iraq now called Tell Fara, found a carved hand with six fingers. He says it was made of diorite, one of the hardest stones on Earth, and points to the Penn Museum's excavation report on the site. He tells it as a sign that ancient people may have known of, or carved, beings unlike ordinary humans.
six-of-knapp-s-corroborating-witnesses-w: A researcher named Luigi Vendetelli relays what George Knapp, a Las Vegas journalist, told him about Bob Lazar, a man who said in 1989 that he had worked on alien craft at a secret site in Nevada. According to Knapp, six other people who could have backed up Lazar's story all got phone calls, were threatened, and never went public, which, if true, would mean someone worked to keep the story from being confirmed.
six-tons-of-missing-fissionable-material: A former US Army sergeant, Lyn Buchanan, says that after the 1986 disaster at the Chernobyl nuclear plant in the Soviet Union, six tons of fissionable material, meaning fuel that can sustain a nuclear chain reaction, went missing. According to him, this material was kept elsewhere at the plant, not in the reactors. He says he was personally involved in the matter, and if he is right, a large amount of dangerous nuclear material vanished without the public hearing about it.
size-of-the-pyramid-at-el-mirador-2024: A researcher named Luke Caverns tells podcast host Jesse Michels about visiting El Mirador, an ancient site in the jungle of Guatemala, in 2024. He says the pyramid there is so huge that he had been walking straight on it for five minutes before he realised it. He tells it to show how much bigger and older these ancient builders' work may be than people imagine.
skeptic-carl-pflock-s-only-visit-to-the-: A man named Scott Ramsay, who has long studied a reported UFO crash at Hart Canyon near Aztec, New Mexico, tells podcast host Jesse Michels that only one skeptic has ever visited the site. He says that was Carl Pflock, a doubter of the story, and that Pflock only came because Ramsay drove him out and walked him around, even though Pflock lived just two hours away. Ramsay tells it to say that those who dismiss the crash have barely looked at the place.
skeptical-cinematographer-michael-convin: A film cameraman named Michael, who worked on a documentary by filmmaker Ky Dickens about children said to read minds, tells podcast host Jesse Michels about filming tests with a girl named Mia in Glendale, California, around 2023. He says he has been a skeptic about most things in his life, but after seeing these tests it is hard for him not to believe.
