If the tests are what he says, it would mean telepathy, reading thoughts without words, is real.
skeptical-finnish-rov-team-calls-it-man-: A Swedish treasure hunter named Dennis Asberg says that in 2019 a skeptical Finnish team sent an ROV, a remotely operated underwater robot, down to the Baltic Sea anomaly, a strange shape his team found on the seafloor between Sweden and Finland. According to Asberg, the Finnish operator concluded, "This must be man-made. This is constructed," and compared part of it to a power line. If true, it would mean even doubters saw the object as built rather than natural.
skiers-in-antarctica-evacuated-by-black-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that skiers who went to Antarctica for sport have had black helicopters come down on them and take them away. He gives no names or dates. He tells it as a hint that someone may be guarding something on the frozen continent.
skinny-bob-video-dismissed-as-cgi-2020: A musician known as Flying Lotus, talking with podcast host Jesse Michels about his interest in UFOs, discusses the Skinny Bob video, a clip passed around online that some people share as footage of an alien. He says it is clearly CGI, meaning computer-generated imagery, and brushes it off, showing that even fans of the subject reject some of what circulates.
skinwalker-ranch-camera-dismantled-betwe: A philosopher named Jason Jorjani, on podcast host Jesse Michels's show, retells a story he credits to John Alexander, a researcher of strange phenomena, about Skinwalker Ranch, a Utah property known for reports of odd happenings. According to Jorjani, a camera was taped to a pole, and in the short gap between its pictures someone or something cut its wires and pulled all the duct tape off the pole. If true, it would point to an unseen presence able to act faster than the camera could catch.
skinwalker-ranch-cattle-mutilations-and-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells of Skinwalker Ranch in Utah, where he says the family who once lived there found many mutilated cattle and went through all sorts of paranormal events. According to him, a businessman named Robert Bigelow, very interested in UFOs, bought the land in the 1990s, and it became a place for experiments, with strange electromagnetic effects on the grounds.
skinwalker-ranch-freaky-stories: A journalist, Michael Shellenberger, mentions Skinwalker Ranch, a property in Utah. He says it is a very freaky place and that many strange stories come out of it. It is talked about because, if those stories are true, the ranch would be a hotspot for unexplained events.
skinwalkers-at-the-pentagon-on-aatip-and: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says he was reading Skinwalkers at the Pentagon, a book about AATIP, a small Pentagon office that studied unexplained aerial reports from around 2007, along with a related programme. According to Michels, the book suggests that remote viewing, the claimed ability to perceive distant places with the mind alone, was taken up again within that work. If so, it would mean the government was still quietly exploring psychic research.
skip-atwater-s-contact-in-australia-sees: A former Army sergeant, Lyn Buchanan, relays a story from a man named Skip Atwater about a contact of his who worked near Mount Zeil, a mountain in central Australia. Buchanan says the contact called it the most boring job he ever had, except for all the UFOs going in and out of the mountain, which, if true, would suggest something hidden inside it.
skorzeny-shown-a-demonstration-of-the-be: A researcher named Jason Jorjani, speaking on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, tells of a secret Nazi flying craft known as the Bell. He says that around 1944 Otto Skorzeny, whom he calls Germany's master of psychological warfare and special operations at the time, turned up at the Skoda Works, a big industrial plant, and was supposedly given a demonstration of the craft. If true, it would mean the wartime Nazis had built something unusual enough to show off to one of their top special operations men.
skunk-works-advisors-to-secret-machines-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that senior figures from Skunk Works, the secret aircraft design division of the defence company Lockheed, named Robert Weiss, Steve Justice and Eric Schrock, advised a project called Secret Machines from around 2016. He says Neil McCaslin, a commander at the Air Force Research Laboratory, also advised it, and that the project was run by the musician Tom DeLonge and the writer Peter Levenda, which would mean insiders from secret aerospace work backed a public UFO effort.
sky-elements-drones-fall-from-the-sky-ov: A businessman named Brandon Fugal, who owns Skinwalker Ranch, a property known for reports of strange events, tells podcast host Jesse Michels about a drone flight there between about 2023 and 2025. He says a fleet of drones from a company called Sky Elements flew over a part of the ranch called the East Field, then all started acting strangely and dropped like bricks from the sky. He tells it as a sign that something on the ranch interferes with machines.
sky-ship-with-glowing-sails-snags-a-lond: A man named Chris Bledsoe, who says he has had many UFO encounters, says he once read an old story set in London in the early 1800s. According to that story, a sailing ship with glowing sails flew over the city, dropped an anchor that caught on a chimney, and broke the top off. He tells it as an example of strange flying craft being reported long before modern aircraft.
sky-watcher-operators-differ-from-legacy: A man named Michael Herrera, who says he saw a 300 foot UFO in the Indonesian jungle, talks about Sky Watcher, a team led by a man named Jake Barber. Herrera says Barber's operators do completely different work from the "legacy programs", the long-running secret government efforts said to deal with UFOs. The point is that this new group should not be confused with the older hidden ones.
skywatcher-s-government-funded-uap-obser: A witness from Skywatcher, a startup that says it tries to call up UFOs, describes about four and a half years, around 2020 to 2025, of field events in the western United States, funded by the government, for watching UAP, a term for unexplained objects in the sky. According to this witness, for that whole stretch they used no psionics, meaning mind-based methods for making contact, and the group says it runs eight classes on this. If true, it would mean the government paid for organized efforts to watch these objects.
skywatcher-s-jordan-psionic-mind-meld-wi: An analyst named Matthew Pines relays what a man called Jordan, from a group named Skywatcher, has said about flying unknown craft with the mind. According to Pines, Jordan describes this "psionic" ability, meaning mental power, as a mind meld with a craft that is itself conscious, with control parts that a person can essentially take over. If true, it would mean these craft are steered by thought rather than by hand.
skywatcher-s-mechanical-and-human-dog-wh: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, describes the work of Skywatcher, a private group in the United States in the 2020s, drawing on a man named Jake Barber. As Michels puts it, the group had "a mechanical dog whistle" and "a human dog whistle," which he frames as one way of calling something using a machine and another using a person. If true, it would mean people have found ways to draw unknown craft toward them on purpose.
skywatcher-sees-orange-orbs-over-picatin: Jake Barber, who says he once flew a helicopter to recover a UFO, says that in 2024, while there was a wave of reported drone sightings over New Jersey, his team from the startup Skywatcher went to Picatinny Arsenal, a US military site there. He says that on their first night, within 30 minutes, many orange orbs appeared right over the base. If true, it would tie the mystery lights directly to a military site.
skywatcher-sessions-psionic-calls-brough: A man named Jordan, interviewed by podcast host Jesse Michels, says he took part in field sessions run by a group called Skywatcher at sites in the United States around 2024 and 2025, where people tried to draw out UAP, meaning unidentified anomalous phenomena, the official term for unexplained things in the sky. According to Jordan, when they called out with the mind alone, which he calls psionic calls, whatever answered was always gentle, but when they used a mechanical device he likens to a dog whistle, the things that came were aggressive. If true, it would suggest these phenomena respond differently depending on how they are summoned.
slime-mold-out-designs-the-japanese-subw: A mushroom enthusiast and guest on a podcast, Tero Isokauppila, passes on a story about slime mold, a simple brainless organism that spreads across surfaces looking for food. He says that when food was laid out in the shape of the Japanese subway map, the slime mold found a more efficient network of routes than the real subway system. He tells it to suggest that intelligence can exist in living things without brains.
slow-acceptance-of-gobekli-tepe-1960: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, talks about Göbekli Tepe, an ancient stone site in Turkey. He says an archaeologist named Klaus Schmidt began digging there in 1994, and that mainstream archaeology took 15 years to accept the site. He uses it to suggest that experts can be slow to accept finds that upset what they already believe.
small-ancient-cities-in-the-united-state: A researcher named Luke Caverns, speaking with podcast host Jesse Michels, says there are small ancient cities in the United States that have never been discovered, in places like Florida, Georgia, South Carolina, Alabama and West Texas, dating from roughly 1,000 to 6,000 years ago. He points to the work of Ed Barnhart, and if he is right, it would mean a large part of the continent's deep past is still hidden in plain sight.
small-grays-and-a-tall-gray-during-mario: A man named Mario Woods says that in the 1960s in South Dakota he was taken on board a craft. He describes beings that looked like "Grays", the familiar small, gray-skinned aliens with large heads and eyes, and behind them a taller one, which he compares to the beings in Communion, a well-known book by the writer Whitley Strieber about his own encounters. If true, it would be a first-hand account of being abducted by non-human beings.
small-helicopter-circles-the-crash-site-: A researcher named Scott Ramsay, who studies a craft said to have crashed in Hart Canyon near Aztec, New Mexico, on March 25, 1948, passes on what local people told him. He says a man named Ken Farley was the first to describe how a very small helicopter suddenly appeared, circled the crash site, and flew off to the northeast. If true, it would mean someone with aircraft was watching the site right after the crash.
smith-propulsion-paper-sent-to-vannevar-: A UFO researcher named Grant Cameron says that the personal files of Wilbert Smith, a Canadian who studied UFOs in the 1950s, contain a document about a way of propelling craft. According to Cameron, Smith wrote that UFO writer Donald Keyhoe had taken the paper to Vannevar Bush, a senior American government scientist, and that they were waiting for his opinion. If true, it would mean UFO-linked propulsion ideas reached the top of US science in that decade.
smith-s-memo-to-the-psb-on-1-500-ufo-rep: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in 1952 Walter B. Smith, then head of the CIA, the US spy agency, sent a memo to the director of the Psychological Strategy Board, a government body that planned propaganda and psychological warfare. According to Michels, the memo noted that over 1,500 UFO reports had been logged, a sign of how seriously officials took the sightings.
smithsonian-digs-up-giant-bones-in-ameri: A researcher named Tim Alberino says that the Smithsonian Institution, America's national museum and research body, once dug up the remains of giants in the mountains of America. In another telling he puts it a bit differently, saying the Smithsonian's own annual reports describe very unusual skeletons, many of them very large, without mentioning mountains. If true, it would mean a race of giant people once lived in North America.
smoke-but-no-flame-at-darpa-and-afrl-wri: John Blitch, a scientist who worked at DARPA, the Pentagon's advanced research agency, and who says he was once taken by aliens, tells podcast host Jesse Michels about his time there and at the Air Force Research Laboratory at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base in Ohio, where he was posted for three years. He says there was a lot of smoke but no flame: hints of something unusual, but nothing he saw with his own eyes that confirmed it.
smyslov-s-alien-chess-vision-before-the-: This story is about a famous chess player, Vasily Smyslov, in a hotel room in Germany in the 1970s, in 1972 or 1974. Kiran Ilum Xenov, a man introduced on a podcast as the president of a Russian republic, tells it to the host, Jesse Michels, passing on what he says he heard. He names Smyslov's wife, Nadezhda Smyslova, and the opponent Smyslov was about to face, a player named Robert Hübner. According to Xenov, as Smyslov worked through his moves before the match, you could say an alien appeared right in front of him, and Xenov mentions Smyslov's own records of the game. Months later, Michels retells the story on another episode, crediting Xenov. In the host's version the player goes unnamed, the moves seemed to make themselves during a practice game, and the player put it down to some kind of alien help. If true, it would suggest that something non-human took a hand in a top chess game.
snow-would-not-settle-on-the-saucer-airm: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells of a disc-shaped craft said to have crashed in Hart Canyon near Aztec, New Mexico, in March 1948. According to a young airman on guard duty around the site, Donald Bass, snow blew across the area and piled up on the ground and rocks, but vanished as it hit the craft and never built up on it. If true, it would suggest the craft gave off heat or energy unlike any ordinary aircraft.
snowden-s-revelations-about-bullrun-and-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, recalls that in 2013 Edward Snowden, a former US intelligence contractor, revealed Bullrun and PRISM, secret government programmes that he says gave spies back doors into technology. Michels says he doesn't believe this happened without Google and Apple knowing, and he uses it to argue that big companies can quietly keep government secrets.
society-for-psychical-research-and-the-h: A documentary maker named Ky Dickens, talking on Jesse Michels' podcast about her project on telepathy, meaning reading minds, says that serious study of such abilities goes back to the 1870s. She points to the Society for Psychical Research, a group formed to investigate claims of the mind reaching beyond the senses, and names thinkers Frederick Myers and William James as part of that history. Her point is that, if she is right, this is a long scientific tradition and not a new fad.
socorro-footprints-and-hynek-s-conversio: John Blitch, a scientist who once worked for DARPA, the Pentagon's advanced research agency, and who says he was abducted by an alien himself, tells this one on Jesse Michels' podcast. He says that in 1964 at Socorro, New Mexico, where a craft was reported to have landed, footprints were left on the ground. According to Blitch, J. Allen Hynek, an astronomer who advised the Air Force on UFO reports, saw those marks and that is what turned him from doubter into believer, which, if true, makes Socorro the moment a key skeptic changed his mind.
solar-camera-aimed-at-the-portal-spot-on: Ross Coulthart, a guest who says he found a UFO base in Arizona, says that in 2025 he saw a solar-powered camera on the fenced-off Bradshaw Ranch near Sedona. According to him, it was pointed exactly at the spot where a woman named Linda Bradshaw says she saw a portal, a kind of doorway to somewhere else. He takes it as a sign that someone is still watching that spot closely.
soldiers-and-officers-confirm-the-giant-: A researcher named Tim Alberino, who tells of a 12 foot giant said to have been captured in Afghanistan, says a handful of soldiers and officers have told him that the story is true. According to Alberino, they also said there are even wilder stories and more giants out there than just one. If true, it would mean the military knows of living giants.
solon-brown-weeps-telling-deacon-bruce-s: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells of a man named Solon Brown who, on March 25, 1948, near Aztec, New Mexico, broke down and cried while talking to a church deacon, Bruce Seer, in a story tied to a reported saucer crash there. Sixty years later, Seer's son told a researcher, Scott Ramsay, that he never forgot that night because it was the first time he had seen a grown man cry. Michels tells it as a sign that whatever Brown saw shook him deeply.
solon-told-the-atlantis-story-by-priests: This is the ancient source of the Atlantis legend, a story of a great island civilisation that was destroyed. A writer on lost ancient civilisations, Graham Hancock, says that Solon, a lawmaker of ancient Athens, travelled to Egypt and visited a temple of the goddess Neith at a city called Sais, in the Nile Delta. Hancock says the Egyptian priests there read the picture writing on the temple walls to Solon and translated it for him. He says this is why the Greek philosopher Plato, writing in his works Timaeus and Critias, gives such an early date for Atlantis, around 9600 BC, with Solon's visit around 600 BC. Hancock tells this on two different podcast episodes. Another guest, Tim Alberino, also refers to the priest of Sais teaching Solon. Alberino focuses on the priest's lesson that the world goes through repeated great disasters, and ties it to our own time. If the account is true, an advanced civilisation was lost long before written history.
something-above-the-ranch-defies-rockets: Brandon Fugal, the owner of Skinwalker Ranch, a property in Utah known for reports of strange happenings, tells podcast host Jesse Michels that since about 2016 his team has documented something in the space above the ranch that throws off rockets and interferes with drones, along with odd readings below the ground. He cites a Dr. Taylor, and if true, it would mean some unknown thing is physically present at the site and acting on machines.
something-showed-up-in-the-mid-2000s-tha: A man named Dylan Borland, who says a senior government official told him that aliens run everything, tells podcast host Jesse Michels that he believes something happened in the mid 2000s that changed the game. In his view, something showed up that the government was not tracking, which, if true, would mean a new and unexpected presence appeared around that time.
son-of-man-title-taken-from-the-parables: Tim Alberino, a researcher, tells podcast host Jesse Michels that the title "son of man," used for Jesus of Nazareth, comes from 1 Enoch, an ancient Jewish religious text, and specifically from its second section, known as the Parables. He also mentions the Book of Daniel, and his point is that the roots of a key Christian title lie in this Enoch writing.
sonny-white-at-nasa-eagleworks-claims-ca: A podcast host named Jesse Michels says that an engineer named Sonny White, who worked at NASA Eagleworks, a small NASA lab that explored far-out propulsion ideas, claims he can power a microchip at 1.5 kilovolts using the Casimir effect. The Casimir effect is a tiny force that appears between objects placed very close together, said to come from the energy of empty space itself. Michels raises it because, if true, it would mean energy could be drawn from empty space, an idea often linked to how UFOs might be powered.
sonny-white-harnessing-the-casimir-force: A podcast host named Jesse Michels says that an engineer named Sonny White appears to be harnessing the Casimir force, a tiny force between very close objects said to arise from empty space, at small scales. Michels brings it up during a debate with a skeptic as a sign that this kind of exotic physics, if real, may be within human reach.
sonny-white-s-casimir-effect-chip: A podcast host named Jesse Michels says that an engineer named Sonny White can engineer the Casimir effect, a tiny force between objects placed very close together that is said to come from the energy of empty space. Michels mentions it as an example of people building with physics that, if it works as described, could point toward the kind of technology some link to UFOs.
sonny-white-s-nasa-eagleworks-warp-drive: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that a scientist named Sonny White worked at Eagleworks, a small lab inside NASA, the US space agency, trying to build toward a warp drive, a way of moving faster than light. Michels says he thinks White is now funded by DARPA, the Pentagon's agency for advanced research, through a company called "Limitless or something like that." If true, it would mean the military is backing serious work on exotic travel.
sound-light-and-frequency-formula-writte: A writer named Brent Friedman tells this on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels. He says that in 1996, in the backyard of his writing partner Bryce Zabel in Los Angeles, a man he calls JC spent about 30 seconds writing on a piece of paper, which was a bank cash machine deposit envelope. JC folded it up and handed it over, Brent says, and told him to put it in a safety deposit box for 10 to 15 years, so that if they never made a deal, he would know JC had been for real. Brent says it looked like an incomprehensible formula, and when he asked what it was, JC told him it was sound, light and frequency, the secrets of the universe. Brent is the only teller, telling it twice in one interview, and the second time he gives the exact date, September 21, 1996, and says Bryce was there. If true, it would mean someone passed them hidden knowledge on a scrap of paper.
sound-light-and-frequency-turns-up-in-a-: A guest named Brent Friedman, speaking on a podcast about Hollywood, the CIA and UFOs, says he once searched for the exact phrase 'sound, light and frequency' and got a match in 2012, roughly 15 years after he first came across it. He says it turned up in a white paper from CERN, the big European physics laboratory, about turning the discovery of the 'God particle', a nickname for the Higgs boson, into sound. He tells it as a striking coincidence that hints the phrase meant more than it seemed.
source-visibly-shaking-while-briefing-se: Kurt McConnell, a former staff member for the US Senate, says that between about 2017 and 2024 people came to Capitol Hill in Washington to tell senators and staff what they knew about unexplained phenomena. He recalls one source who was visibly shaking as they began to explain, and in a second conversation with podcast host Jesse Michels he describes such sources more generally as earnest people with credible backgrounds who were nervous and trembling, which he takes as a sign of how serious they were.
source-who-has-been-inside-s4: An online UFO researcher who goes by the name UAPGerb says he has spoken with one person who has been to S4, a secret site said to lie near Papoose Lake in Nevada, close to the military base known as Area 51. He does not name the source. The claim matters because S4 is said to be where the government keeps and studies craft that are not of human origin.
sources-tell-senators-of-recovered-and-r: Kurt McConnell, a former US Senate staff member, tells podcast host Jesse Michels that between about 2017 and 2024 people found their way to Capitol Hill and met with senators. He says they claimed that craft of unknown origin had been recovered and taken apart to learn how they work, which, if true, would mean such objects are held in secret.
southcom-tic-tac-detected-by-space-asset: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, reads from what he calls the Immaculate Constellation report, a document tied to a Pentagon whistleblower named Matthew Brown. According to the entry he reads, in the area of Southern Command, the US military command covering the seas and lands south of the United States, a Tic Tac, a white oval object shaped like the mint, was detected by a sensor in space near a naval ship. If true, it would mean the military tracks such objects from orbit and keeps records of them.
southwest-research-analysis-of-the-impla: A writer named Whitley Strieber, who says he has been in contact with non-human beings, tells of a small sliver he believed was an implant placed in his body. Strieber says that in the mid-1990s a man named Bill, William Malow, studied a piece of it at the Southwest Research Institute, a research lab in San Antonio, Texas, and told him it had a metal base with tiny moving hair-like strands coming off it. If true, it would suggest the object was something no ordinary source would produce.
soviet-divers-meet-tall-humanoids-at-lak: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, brings up a story from 1982 about Soviet divers at Lake Baikal, a huge deep lake in Siberia. As he tells it, the divers went down looking for something and met very tall human-like beings under the water. If true, it would mean something not human was living or working beneath the lake.
soviet-horten-based-flying-saucer-progra: A researcher and author named Peter Levenda, speaking on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, says that after the Second World War the Soviet Union ran a secret project to build a kind of flying saucer. According to Levenda, the design was based on the work of the Horten brothers, two German aircraft designers, and the story came out when some Soviet documents became available after the Soviet Union fell in 1991. If true, it would mean the Soviets were also trying to build saucer-shaped craft from captured German ideas.
soviet-microwave-beaming-of-the-us-embas: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that around 1976, during the SALT talks, arms-limitation negotiations between the United States and the Soviet Union, the US diplomat Henry Kissinger told the Soviet official Anatoly Dobrynin to stop beaming the American embassy in Moscow with microwaves. Michels connects this to the US ambassador of the time, Walter Stoessel, and credits reporting by the German magazine Der Spiegel and the American TV news show 60 Minutes. He tells it because it would show that governments were already aiming energy at people in secret decades ago.
soviet-military-exercise-drew-ufos-once-: A researcher named Robert Hastings, who studies reports of UFOs around nuclear weapons sites, tells podcast host Jesse Michels about a retired Soviet army colonel who appears in a video online. Hastings says the colonel described taking part, during the Soviet era, in a military exercise deliberately designed to attract UFOs, and that they showed up once nuclear weapons were brought in. If true, it would suggest whatever is behind UFOs takes a particular interest in nuclear weapons.
soviet-missiles-brought-online-1960: Karl Nell, a guest speaking from a government background, told podcast host Jesse Michels that in the Soviet Union in the 1960s there were cases where nuclear missiles were switched on by themselves, like the American cases where missiles were said to be switched off. He says records released under FOIA, a US law that lets anyone ask for government records, along with witness testimony, back this up, which would mean UFOs were meddling with nuclear weapons on both sides of the Cold War.
soviet-paleocontact-theories: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in the Soviet Union, figures named Alexander Kazantsev and Felix Zigel put forward the idea that alien visitors may have shaped early human development. This idea is often called paleocontact, meaning contact with outsiders in the ancient past. If true, it would mean human history was nudged along by beings from elsewhere.
soviet-phobos-probe-s-last-image-before-: A podcast host named Jesse Michels says that in 1989 a Soviet space probe sent to Phobos, a small moon of Mars, took a final picture before it stopped working. According to Michels, that last image shows an object shaped like the fin on the tail of a plane. He tells it because, if true, it would suggest something unexplained near Mars was caught on camera just as the probe went silent.
soviet-psychics-tasked-against-us-congre: Joe McMoneagle, a man known for his work as a psychic, says the Soviet Union trained its own psychics to spy with their minds on American congressmen, senators, members of the president's cabinet and the president himself. He says he learned this from a box of material that came from a Soviet psychic unit. If true, it would mean both sides of the Cold War took mind-spying seriously enough to aim it at the top of government.
soviet-psychokinesis-experiments-on-mice: A philosopher named Jason Jorjani, speaking with podcast host Jesse Michels, says that in the 1970s Soviet researchers took mice down in submarines and tried to stop their hearts using psychokinesis, the supposed power of the mind to affect physical things. Jorjani says the Soviets figured out this power could be used to kill a person, which, if true, would make the mind a possible weapon.
soviet-spy-at-1950-pearl-harbor-demo-wou: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, drawing on The Man Who Mastered Gravity, a book by Paul Schatzkin about the scientist Townsend Brown, says that in 1950, during a demonstration of Brown's work at Pearl Harbor in Hawaii, a Soviet spy posing as a janitor compromised it. The story ties this to a ruse called the "wounded prairie chicken" routine, and suggests Brown's gravity research was valuable enough for the Soviets to steal.
soviet-target-mice-psi-experiment-in-the: Joe McMoneagle, a guest who speaks about psychic research, says he received a box of material from a Soviet psychic research unit, obtained after the Soviet Union opened up. He says it described an experiment in Russia's Ural Mountains where people tried to affect mice with their minds, and that when the results were sorted, the top 12 were all the target mice and the bottom 12 all the untouched control mice, a perfect match. If true, it would suggest the Soviets found evidence that the mind can act on living things at a distance.
soviet-ukraine-missiles-enter-countdown-: A researcher and author, Robert Hastings, says that in 1982 a huge disc-shaped object was seen hovering over a missile base in Soviet Ukraine, and that down in one of the launch rooms the nuclear missiles suddenly went into countdown on their own. He says this came from classified Soviet UFO documents, passed on by a journalist named George Knapp and a man named Vladimir Platonoff. If true, it would mean something unknown could take control of nuclear weapons.
soviet-version-of-operation-paperclip-19: A researcher named Peter Levenda tells podcast host Jesse Michels that the Russians had their own version of Operation Paperclip, the American programme that brought German scientists to the United States after the Second World War. Levenda says the Russians brought more than 3,000 scientists and their families into Russia, drawing on a book called Secret Machines. If true, it would mean much of Germany's wartime science went east as well as west.
space-act-of-1958-ties-nasa-to-dod-and-a: A researcher named Maaneli Derakhshani, speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast, points to the Space Act of 1958, the law passed by Congress that created NASA, the US space agency. He says that law has always tied NASA closely to the Department of Defense, the US military's parent department, and the story holds that it lets the agency withhold information. If true, it would mean what NASA shares with the public can be shaped by military secrecy.
space-force-people-ask-about-hawkeye-360: Bob Maguire, who says he worked as a contractor for the CIA, tells podcast host Jesse Michels that in 2022 he went to a meeting of the Scientific Coalition for UAP Studies, a group that studies unexplained aerial phenomena, in Huntsville, Alabama. He says people tied to the Space Force, the US military branch for space, and to intelligence agencies approached him about using the signal-detecting abilities of a company called Hawkeye 360 to look for signals from unexplained objects on the ground.
space-intelligences-chose-owens-for-the-: A parapsychology researcher named Jeffrey Mishlove tells podcast host Jesse Michels about a man named Ted Owens. According to Mishlove, Owens claimed that intelligences from space had picked him because they found he had the most powerful nervous system of anyone they had met since Moses. If true, it would mean these beings choose certain humans as special contacts.
space-kid-channels-an-egyptian-god-insid: An unnamed guest on podcast host Jesse Michels's show says that in 1976 Andrija Puharich, a researcher of psychic phenomena, ran experiments inside the Great Pyramid in Egypt with one of the so-called "space kids", children said to have psychic gifts. According to the guest, information came through during these sessions, apparently from an Egyptian god being channelled, meaning speaking through the child, which would suggest contact with a non-human mind.
space-kid-shows-copper-bracelet-worn-in-: Greg Malatzi, a researcher, says that a few years ago he filmed an interview with a woman who, as a child in the 1970s, took part in channeling sessions, attempts to receive messages from non-human beings, with a CIA scientist. He says she pulled out a bracelet with a small copper plate, and told him all the children had to wear one during the sessions. He tells it as physical proof that the sessions he describes really took place.
space-kids-channeling-tapes-name-israeli: A researcher named Greg, on Jesse Michels's podcast, describes tapes made in the 1970s in Ossining, New York, by Andrija Puharich, a scientist linked to the CIA, with a group of young people called the space kids who channeled, meaning they spoke messages said to come from beings beyond Earth. Greg says that on many of these tapes Puharich refers by name to Israeli generals, such as Aharon Yariv. If true, it would tie these channeling sessions to military and intelligence figures.
space-program-insiders-learn-their-missi: Diana Pasulka, a scholar who studies beliefs about UFOs, says she spent time with people in the US space program who had to work out their missions on their own, without anyone telling them what they were. According to her, it was hard for them, and they only learned they had got it right when they got an award, sometimes two years later. She tells it as a sign that some knowledge in these circles is passed on unspoken, like an oral tradition.
space-program-latin-symbols-as-homage-to: A religious studies professor named Diana Pasulka tells podcast host Jesse Michels that people in the space world told her the Latin symbols on their mission patches, the cloth badges made for each launch, were a way to pay homage to beings they call the sponsors. She says that when she asked whether the sponsors read Latin, they said absolutely, though elsewhere in the same talk she places the patches in today's Space Force without the sponsors claim. If true, it would mean some people in the space programme believe they answer to non-human patrons.
space-scientist-david-w-webb-and-governm: Whitley Strieber, a writer who says he has met non-human beings, says that in the mid-1980s, around the time of experiences at his cabin in upstate New York, he met a space scientist named David W. Webb. According to Strieber, this showed him there were people inside the government who already had some contact with these beings, and he also mentions a researcher named Stanton Friedman. If true, it would mean officials knew about abductions, people being taken by non-humans, well before the public did.
spacecraft-momentum-anomalies-in-the-van: A guest named Charles, speaking on podcast host Jesse Michels's show, says that spacecraft circling the Earth show odd changes in their motion when they reach the Van Allen belts, zones of charged particles that surround the planet. He says they either speed up or slow down for no clear reason, which he offers as a hint of physics we do not yet understand.
spacecraft-recovered-from-aztec-kingman-: A journalist named Ross Coulthart, speaking with podcast host Jesse Michels, relays a remark linked to David Grusch, a former intelligence officer turned whistleblower, that a spacecraft was recovered from Aztec, New Mexico. The story ties this to supposed crash recoveries between 1948 and 1953, including one at Kingman, Arizona, which, if true, would mean the US government has held non-human craft for decades.
spaceship-reportedly-landed-and-was-hush: Barry Goldwater, a well-known US senator, is heard in a clip played on Jesse Michels's podcast saying that, reportedly, a spaceship landed and the whole thing was hushed up and kept quiet. The story is tied to Wright-Patterson Air Force Base in Ohio, and no date is given. If true, it would mean the US military had a landed craft and kept it secret.
special-forces-guys-play-hunter-skinwalk: Skinwalker Ranch is a property in Utah known for reports of strange happenings. On a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, a guest named Grant Cameron passed on a story he says came from a man named Brandon Fugal: three armed men, described as special forces soldiers, went onto the ranch planning to play what he calls "Hunter Skinwalker", meaning they meant to hunt down whatever was there. The story is told because it would suggest the place is serious enough to draw trained soldiers.
special-programs-bring-secret-technology: James Valor, a witness connected to the startup Skywatcher, says that in the 2020s he took part in projects with the US military. According to him, secret special programs brought their own hidden technology to the group's sky-watching events without telling them, and the participants were afterward asked to sign NDAs, non-disclosure agreements that forbid talking about what they saw. If true, some of what was seen at those events may have been secret human-made technology.
special-ufo-briefing-for-maintenance-tea: A former Air Force officer named Robert Salas, who served at Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana, a base that controlled nuclear missiles, tells podcast host Jesse Michels about March 1967. Passing on what a man named Robert Jameson told him, Salas says the maintenance teams were called into a special briefing and told there were UFOs out in the area. If true, it would mean the military knew of UFOs near its nuclear missiles and warned its own crews.
spectre-modeled-on-odessa-1945: SPECTRE is the secret criminal organisation that James Bond fights in the spy novels of the British writer Ian Fleming. A researcher named Jason Jorjani says on a podcast that SPECTRE is "very obviously" Fleming's version of ODESSA, which he presents as a real network that carried on after the end of the Second World War in 1945, and he links it to the Nazi figures Martin Bormann and Otto Skorzeny. If he is right, a famous piece of fiction would be hiding a real story about Nazis organising across borders after the war.
speculation-that-kirkpatrick-was-read-in: Sean Kirkpatrick was the first head of AARO, a Pentagon office set up around 2022 to look into unexplained objects in the sky. A former US Senate staffer, Kurt McConnell, says on a podcast that some people suspect Kirkpatrick was "read into", meaning secretly briefed on, a so-called legacy program, a hidden effort that people claim holds craft that were not made by humans. If true, the official in charge of investigating would have known more than he said.
sperm-sampling-and-insect-like-faces-197: Jim Weiner, one of a group of men on a camping trip on the Allagash Waterway in Maine in August 1976, tells podcast host Jesse Michels that he was taken aboard a craft where beings took samples of his sperm. He says that in a second session of recalling the event, their faces finally came back to him and he remembers screaming that they looked like bugs.
sphere-crash-south-of-the-border-that-ki: On a podcast episode about a scientist who studies objects said to be alien implants in people's bodies, a guest named Steve tells a story from a man named Massan. Steve says Massan bought a crashed sphere from a farmer whose land is about 100 miles south of the US border near Brownsville, Texas, on Mexico's east coast, and that the farmer said the crash set off an explosion that killed a cow 100 meters away. The story matters to the tellers because it would mean a physical object from such a crash is in private hands.
sphere-described-as-a-control-mechanism-: Randy Anderson tells podcast host Jesse Michels that in 2014, at Naval Surface Warfare Center Crane, a Navy research site in Indiana, he saw a sphere he believes was alien technology. He remembers people there saying it might be part of a control system that responded to human consciousness, which, if true, would mean a machine driven by the mind.
sphere-holds-15-ft-from-a-friend-s-cockp: Ryan Graves, a US Navy fighter pilot, tells a podcast about a case involving one of his good friends at Patuxent River, a naval air base in Maryland usually called Pax River. According to Graves, while his friend was flying and turning hard, a sphere pulled up about 15 feet from his cockpit and stayed there with him for a while. If true, it would mean something unknown can keep pace with a fighter jet at close range.
sphere-inside-a-cube-near-miss-at-oceana: This story is about a near collision between a Navy fighter jet and a strange object around 2014 or 2015, off the US East Coast. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, relays what a Navy pilot named Ryan Graves has described: an object that almost hit a pilot and looked like a sphere inside a cube. Michels places it around Naval Air Station Oceana, a Navy airbase in Virginia. A retired Navy admiral, Tim Gallaudet, tells it as happening during a training exercise with the aircraft carrier Roosevelt and a fighter squadron called VFA-11, and says the cube-and-sphere object flew right between two jets flying together. If true, it would mean unknown objects were putting military pilots in danger.
sphere-leaves-in-eight-seconds-1976: Charlie Foltz, one of a group of campers at Eagle Lake on the Allagash Waterway in Maine in 1976, tells podcast host Jesse Michels that they saw a glowing sphere over the water. He says that when it took off, only eight seconds passed from the moment he noticed it moving until it was a pinpoint of light in the night sky, a speed far beyond any ordinary aircraft.
sphere-recovered-from-a-crashed-craft-20: A man named Randy Anderson, speaking to a podcast host, Jesse Michels, says he saw alien technology at Naval Surface Warfare Center Crane, a US Navy research base in Indiana, around 2014. According to Anderson, the people there talked about a sphere and said it had been recovered from a craft that crashed. If true, it would mean the military holds pieces of a non-human vehicle.
spheres-entering-the-water-at-guadalupe-: A UFO writer, Marik von Rennenkampf, says that Lou Elizondo, a former Pentagon official who worked on UFO reports, and Sean Cahill, a former Navy sailor, went to Guadalupe Island off Mexico for a National Geographic television series called Unidentified. They went, he says, because there had been reports of glowing spheres going in and out of the water there. If true, it would suggest these objects move between sky and sea.
sphinx-enclosure-filled-in-and-excavated: A researcher of ancient Egypt, Luke Caverns, says on Jesse Michels' podcast that the Sphinx is older than the usual story allows. He says that roughly a thousand years after it was supposedly carved, the pharaoh Thutmose IV recorded that the pit around the Sphinx had filled in with sand and that he had to dig it all out and clean it before he could become pharaoh. For Caverns, that long burial is a sign the monument had already been there a very long time.
sphinx-enclosure-opening-said-to-connect: Geoffrey Drumm, a man who has his own theory about what the Egyptian pyramids were for, says there are three openings at the back of the sunken area that surrounds the Sphinx at Giza. He says a friend who works in Egypt's Ministry of Antiquities, the government body that runs the country's ancient sites, has confirmed that one of these openings leads into the Queen's Chamber, a room inside the Great Pyramid. If so, it would mean hidden passages link the two monuments.
sphinx-originally-had-a-lion-s-head: This story is about the Great Sphinx, the huge stone statue at Giza in Egypt with a lion's body and a human head. The writer Graham Hancock says on Jesse Michels' podcast that the Sphinx was first carved entirely as a lion, and that the pharaohs, Egypt's ancient kings, later recut the head. He credits the researchers Robert Schoch, John Anthony West and Manu Seyfzadeh. Matt LaCroix, another researcher, points out that the head is too small for the body, which he says shows it was recarved by later Egyptians. Michels adds that a lion would have lined up with the constellation Leo at the spring equinox around 10,500 BC. If true, the Sphinx would be far older than the pharaohs, made by an earlier, forgotten people.
sphinx-outcrop-was-always-visible-from-t: Luke Caverns, a researcher of ancient Egypt, says on Jesse Michels' podcast that the Sphinx was carved from a huge outcrop of limestone rock. He argues that the people of the region must always have known that rock was there, which, as he frames it, bears on how early it could have been shaped.
spider-bite-leads-fox-to-one-of-the-girl: James Fox, who presents himself as a witness to his own investigation, says that around 2012 in Varginha, a town in Brazil, a spider bite led him to meet a man who told him, "Oh my gosh, I dated one of the girls." The girls were central to a reported incident in Varginha in which, as it is told, the army captured a live alien. Fox tells it as the lucky break that brought him closer to the original witnesses.
spielberg-approached-by-naval-intelligen: This story is about the film director Steven Spielberg. Brent Friedman, a guest on a podcast episode about Hollywood and UFOs, says that a man named Tobe Hooper told him, around 1995 in Newhall, California, that after Spielberg became a big name with the shark film Jaws, some men from Naval Intelligence, the Navy's spy branch, approached him and offered him a deal. In one telling Spielberg took the deal, and another version credits Hooper but does not say whether he did. People tell it because, if true, it would suggest the government helped shape Spielberg's later films about aliens.
spielberg-based-the-close-encounters-sci: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that when the film director Steven Spielberg made Close Encounters of the Third Kind, his 1977 movie about people meeting visitors from space, he based its eccentric but brilliant UFO scientist on Jacques Vallée, a real-life UFO researcher. In the film that character is played by François Truffaut. If so, one of the best-known UFO films took its hero from a real investigator.
spielberg-binge-watched-the-secret-of-sk: Brandon Fugal, a businessman who owns Skinwalker Ranch, a property famous for reports of strange happenings, says the film director Steven Spielberg told him something in the 2020s. According to Fugal, Spielberg said that between the hearings in the US Congress and the government starting to admit the reality of the subject, he had just binge-watched all 72 episodes of The Secret of Skinwalker Ranch, a TV series about the ranch, before his project Disclosure Day. Fugal tells it as a sign that one of Hollywood's biggest names is taking the topic seriously.
spielberg-s-ea-game-lmno-about-a-woman-w: A writer named Brent Friedman says that around 2004 he worked at Electronic Arts, a big video game company in Los Angeles, on a game with the famous film director Steven Spielberg. Friedman says the game was code-named LMNO and was about a woman who is human but has alien abilities, using the power of empathy to disarm people while the government chases her. He tells it on a podcast about Hollywood, the CIA and UFOs, as a sign of how long Spielberg has been drawn to these themes.
spielberg-s-letter-to-james-fox-about-i-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that James Fox, a well-known maker of UFO documentaries, revealed a letter sent to him by the film director Steven Spielberg. The letter was about Fox's 2009 documentary, I Know What I Saw. Michels tells it because it would suggest one of the world's most famous filmmakers takes the subject seriously.
spielberg-s-live-imax-interview-for-disc: A writer and producer named Bryce Zabel says that in 2026 he and a podcast host, Jesse Michels, watched a live interview with the film director Steven Spielberg at an IMAX theater, a cinema with an extra-large screen. The interview was tied to something called Disclosure Day, and Zabel brings up what Spielberg said there the night before as a hint about Spielberg's views on the subject of non-human intelligence.
spielberg-s-tip-about-the-ariel-school-l: A documentary filmmaker named James Fox tells podcast host Jesse Michels that the film director Steven Spielberg, through a producer named Janet Yang, pointed him to a reported landing at the Ariel School in Ruwa, Zimbabwe, in the 1990s. Fox says the tip was that anyone serious about UFOs should look into this landing, which, if true, would mean even Spielberg considered it an important case.
spielberg-tells-robert-liefeld-ufos-may-: Podcast host Jesse Michels says that, according to Robert Liefeld, the comic book artist who created the character Deadpool, the film director Steven Spielberg asked him in 1993 what was easier to believe: that we are being watched by aliens from another world, or that we are studying ourselves from the future. In another episode Michels tells it without a date, as future versions of ourselves guarding us in the present. If true, it would mean one of the best known UFO filmmakers privately suspected UFOs are humans from the future.
spielberg-ufos-as-future-humans-2020: Steven Spielberg, the film director, once wondered aloud to the TV host Stephen Colbert whether UFOs might not come from a distant advanced civilisation at all. In the clip, played on a podcast episode with a musician, Spielberg asks: what if "it's us 500,000 years into the future?" The idea is that the visitors would be our own descendants coming back in time.
spillage-reported-up-the-chain-told-to-g: Matthew Brown, who says he worked inside the Pentagon, says that around 2018 he came across "spillage", meaning secret material turning up where it shouldn't, tied to a briefing on a hidden programme he calls Immaculate Constellation. He says he reported it up the chain, including to the office that oversees the Pentagon's most secret programmes, and that a superior advised him to "delete that and pretend he never saw it" and then walked out of the room. If true, it would mean officials were actively burying records about unexplained craft.
spinning-mercury-in-the-vimanas: A podcast host named Jesse Michels says that the vimanas, flying machines described in ancient Indian texts, involved spinning mercury. He mentions it because, if those old accounts describe something real, they would echo modern claims about how UFOs might fly.
spiritualism-wave-seances-as-common-as-c: Tim Alberino, a filmmaker and researcher, describes a craze in the late 1800s and early 1900s for spiritualism, the practice of trying to contact the dead. He says magazine and newspaper articles from that time, which he gathered for a project called Birthright, claimed that at its height an American was as likely to go to a seance, a gathering to speak with spirits, on Sunday morning as to go to church. He tells it to show how common contact with the unseen once seemed to ordinary people.
spock-s-reverence-for-the-sun-1990: Dan Sherman, a former US Air Force sergeant who says the NSA, the US electronic spy agency, hired him to communicate with aliens, tells of the early 1990s at an overseas base where he served. He says a being or contact he calls Spock talked to him about how humans do not really understand the value of our sun. He tells it, as in his book Above Black, as a glimpse of the outlook of those he says he spoke with.
spock-says-you-can-go-around-time-1990: Dan Sherman, a former Air Force sergeant who says the NSA, the US government's code-breaking and eavesdropping agency, hired him to communicate with aliens, tells a podcast host about his time at an overseas base in the early 1990s, connected to a secret program he refers to by the letters PPD. Sherman says a figure he calls Spock told him that you can go around time, and that he did not really understand it then. If true, it would hint that whoever he was talking to treated time in a way we do not.
sport-model-came-from-an-underwater-arch: Bob Lazar is a man who says that in 1989 he worked on taking apart alien craft at a secret site called S4, near the Nevada military base known as Area 51. Lazar says a colleague named Barry Castilio told him that the craft he studied, which he calls the "sport model," came from an archaeological dig, and that the dig was in the water, not the desert. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, later repeats it as Lazar correcting himself: not an archaeological dig, but something the Navy found on the seafloor. If true, it would mean the craft came out of the ocean and the Navy handed it over.
spotting-the-nsa-by-where-number-theory-: A mathematician named Eric Weinstein, on podcast host Jesse Michels's show, describes a way to find hidden government work. He says you could look at people with doctorates in number theory, a branch of mathematics used in code-making, who never got a visible university job, and check where they live. He says they turn out to cluster around Fort Meade, Maryland, home of the NSA, the US code-breaking agency, which he offers as a way secret programmes give themselves away.
squadron-safety-survey-turns-up-four-mor: Ryan Graves, a US Navy fighter pilot whose squadron flew from the Virginia Beach area, says that after a near collision in the air, his squadron did a safety survey and filed a hazard report, the Navy's formal safety warning. According to Graves, the survey showed about four other near-midair collisions over the past few months with the same issue, none of them reported. If true, it would mean pilots were nearly hitting unknown objects and keeping quiet about it.
squanto-unites-three-rival-tribes: A researcher, Luke Caverns, speaking on a podcast with host Jesse Michels, tells of Squanto, a Native American man in Massachusetts. Caverns says Squanto brought together three tribes that had been rivals and formed them into a single alliance. He tells it as part of a wider look at hidden or overlooked history.
squared-off-object-tumbles-into-the-back: Whitley Strieber, a writer known for his books about meeting strange beings, told a podcast host, Jesse Michels, about something from his childhood in Texas in the 1950s. He says that at his family's country house, an object with squared-off edges came tumbling across the sky and fell into the back pasture behind the house, and he names a relative, Karl Strieber, in the story. If true, it would mean his strange experiences began with a crash he saw as a boy.
sr-71-pilot-encourages-sherman-to-join-t: Dan Sherman, a former US Air Force sergeant who says he was later hired to communicate with aliens, says that before he enlisted he met a pilot of the SR-71, a very fast American spy plane. He says that pilot strongly encouraged him to join the Air Force, which he tells, as in his book Above Black, as an early step on the path that led to his later claimed work.
sri-and-at-t-chairman-meeting-on-unackno: Steven Greer, a doctor who campaigns for governments to reveal what they know about UFOs, told the podcast host Jesse Michels that in the 1990s he was once at a meeting with a chairman connected to SRI, a large American research institute, and to AT&T, the big US telephone company. He says the talk was about secret projects that officially do not exist. If true, it would mean leaders of major private companies know about hidden UFO-related work.
sri-pay-stub-to-puharich-s-lab-nine-1973: A researcher named Greg says there is a pay stub in the archives of Andrija Puharich, a researcher of psychic phenomena, showing a 1973 payment from SRI, the Stanford Research Institute, a California research organisation, to Puharich's own lab, called Lab Nine, in Ossining, New York. Greg brings it up to push back on the idea that Puharich had simply disappeared from that world, since it would mean SRI was still paying him.
sri-psi-research-1960: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, mentions SRI, the Stanford Research Institute, a research lab in Menlo Park, California. He points to its work in the late 1960s and early 1970s on psi, meaning abilities of the mind such as sensing things far away or ahead of time. He raises it as a sign that serious institutions once looked into such powers.
ss-officers-freemasons-and-occultists-ru: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that by the mid-1960s the real power structure of NASA, the US space agency, was "a strange cocktail" of former SS officers, meaning members of Nazi Germany's elite force, along with Freemasons, a fraternal society with private rituals, and people drawn to the occult. He names figures such as John Glenn, Buzz Aldrin, James Webb, Kenneth Kleinknecht, Edgar Mitchell and James Irwin. If true, it would mean the space program was steered by hidden beliefs and loyalties.
ss-tibet-expedition-of-1938: A writer and researcher named Peter Levenda says he was going through captured German documents on microfilm and looking at the 1938 Tibet expedition run by the SS, Nazi Germany's elite organisation under Heinrich Himmler. He tells it because it would show the Nazi leadership sending people to Tibet in search of something hidden or ancient.
ssris-that-made-him-suicidal-his-psychia: Dylan Borland, a military veteran who says a top government official told him aliens run everything, describes his treatment in 2016 and 2017 through the VA, the US government health system for veterans. He says doctors put him on SSRIs, a common type of antidepressant, that made him suicidal, and that this is why his first psychiatrist quit, pointing to his medical records as backing his account of how he was treated.
st-andrews-study-finds-magnetic-signatur: Geoffrey Drumm, who has his own theory about the purpose of ancient monuments, points to a study by the University of St Andrews in Scotland that measured the ground around the Callanish stone circle, a ring of ancient standing stones in Scotland. According to Drumm, the study found a magnetic trace left by lightning striking the site again and again. For him, this would hint that such monuments were tied to electricity in some way.
st-francis-of-assisi-s-stigmata-as-ufo-r: Saint Francis of Assisi, the medieval Christian saint, is said to have received the stigmata, wounds like those of Christ, on a mountain in Italy, and a religion scholar named Diana Pasulka retells it from the old sources: his young companion Brother Leo, about 15, watched a being described as a seraph, a kind of fiery angel, deal harshly with Francis and leave him injured. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, crediting Pasulka and her book American Cosmic, describes it as a spinning disk, atmospheric sparks and telepathic talk, says the original wording is closer to a flaming torch than Christ or an angel, and suggests the wounds were electromagnetic burns. If so, one of the most famous saints' visions would have been an encounter with a craft.
st-francis-s-final-tau: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Saint Francis of Assisi, the Italian holy man, saw a seraph, a fiery angel from the Bible, which Michels suggests was probably a craft or a glowing orb. He says the last thing Francis wrote in his diary was the Greek letter Tau, which Michels says means conversion. If that reading is right, an old religious vision could be seen as an encounter with something not human.
st-mary-s-chapel-at-glastonbury-abbey-ke: A researcher of ancient sites named Randall Carlson, on podcast host Jesse Michels's show, talks about St Mary's Chapel at Glastonbury Abbey, a ruined medieval church in England. He says its width of 39.6 feet is said to preserve the size of the very first chapel built there, which would mean an ancient measurement was carefully carried down through the centuries.
st-patrick-s-day-argument-darpa-as-corso: John Blitch, a scientist who worked at DARPA, the Pentagon's advanced research agency, says that around 2001, on a St Patrick's Day, he argued a case in a DARPA office. He says he made the case that DARPA grew out of the section run by General Trudeau where Philip Corso served, Corso being an Army officer whose book The Day After Roswell says he helped pass on technology from a craft said to have crashed near Roswell, New Mexico, in 1947. In Blitch's telling, DARPA became the channel that broke that technology into parts and handed them out, which would mean crash material quietly shaped modern American inventions.
stack-five-ceremonial-magic-program-at-w: A podcast host named Jesse Michels says he believes there was a program at Wright Field, a US military airfield, called Stack Five, or ST5. According to Michels, the people in it were carrying out strange magical rituals, what is called ceremonial magic. He tells it because, if true, it would mean the military explored the occult alongside its study of unexplained craft.
staff-found-the-kalmykian-president-miss: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in the 1990s the president of Kalmykia, a small republic inside Russia, vanished from his room, and that he has the president's staff on record saying they went in, found his clothes missing, and could not find him anywhere. Michels also cites the chess champion Garry Kasparov in connection with it, and tells it because it would back up the president's own account of being taken.
stan-marcus-tells-nick-cook-the-bell-slo: In a documentary about an American inventor named Townsend Brown, the podcast host Jesse Michels retells a claim about "the Bell", a device said to have been built in secret in Nazi Germany in the 1940s. Michels says that a source named Stan Marcus told the writer Nick Cook that the Germans had managed to slow down time inside a twisting energy field around the Bell. If true, it would mean wartime Germany had touched physics far beyond anything known.
stan-meyer-collection-group-killed: Steven Greer, a man who campaigns for the government to reveal what it knows about UFOs, talks about Stan Meyer, an inventor who worked on energy from water. Greer says that the men who got hold of Meyer's collection of work, including a ring-shaped device called a toroid, were all killed except one, which he says he heard from an unnamed British lord. He tells it as a sign that someone is willing to kill to keep such inventions buried.
stan-meyer-poisoned-per-his-twin-steve-1: Steven Greer, a campaigner for UFO disclosure, says that the twin brother of the inventor Stan Meyer, Steve Meyer, is completely convinced Stan was poisoned and killed, in 1998. If true, it would mean an inventor of a new energy source was murdered for his work.
stan-meyer-water-dissociation-and-zero-p: Steven Greer, a campaigner for UFO disclosure, says an inventor named Stan Meyer saw that at certain frequencies, water would split into hydrogen and oxygen using less energy than standard chemistry allows, a limit set by a figure called the Faraday constant. Greer links this to "zero point energy," the idea of drawing power from empty space, and to a work called The Lost Century, because it would mean a cheap new energy source was found and lost.
stan-romanek-contactee-and-hybrid-photog: A Canadian UFO researcher named Grant Cameron tells a podcast host about Stan Romanek, a man living north of Denver, Colorado, in the 2000s, who described himself as being in contact with beings. Cameron says Romanek was a major contactee, someone who reports repeated visits, and that there was a photograph his wife took of one of the hybrids, meaning a being said to be part human and part alien.
stanford-team-finds-two-cavities-under-k: Luke Caverns, a researcher of ancient Egypt, says on Jesse Michels' podcast that scans have found hollow spaces beneath the pyramid of Khafre at Giza, the second of the great pyramids. He says that in the 1970s a team from Stanford University came in, ran another scan, and confirmed these cavities, which, if true, would mean there are hidden rooms under the pyramid.
stanley-mcdaniel-s-book-on-nasa-s-failur: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Stanley McDaniel, a retired professor at Sonoma State University, wrote a 200-page book in the 1990s about how NASA, the US space agency, failed to properly study what he called structures on Mars. Michels raises it to suggest the agency looked away from possible signs of past life there.
starfish-prime-bluegill-triple-prime-emp: A podcast host named Jesse Michels talks about Starfish Prime and Bluegill Triple Prime, American nuclear tests set off high above the Pacific in 1962. He says that in the Starfish Prime series the US accidentally created an EMP, an electromagnetic pulse, a burst of energy that can knock out electronics. He raises it in a debate with a skeptic, tying these tests to the wider story of unexplained events around nuclear weapons.
stargate-as-a-vestibule-for-a-deeper-bla: A podcast host named Jesse Michels says that Stargate, a US government program run partly at the Stanford Research Institute, a California research lab, that tried to use the mind to see distant places, was shut down in 1995 but was really just a front room for a darker, deeply secret project that still exists. He says a man named Pat Price, who took part in that work, was recruited into the deeper project and was killed over it. If true, it would mean the government's mind research never really ended.
stargate-ends-in-1995-and-puharich-is-si: A researcher on a podcast says that Stargate, a US government programme that studied using psychics to spy, officially ended in 1995, and that the government then put out newspaper stories everywhere saying there was nothing to it and it was all bunk. He ties this to the silencing of Andrija Puharich, a researcher of psychic phenomena, and cites the journalist Annie Jacobsen, suggesting the public dismissal was a cover.
stargate-files-declassified-2017: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Stargate, a US government program that used psychics to spy, was declassified in 2017. He says all of its files are now online, which would mean anyone can read how the government tried to gather intelligence with the mind.
stargate-inscriptions-at-dendera: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Ben Van Kerkwyk, a researcher of ancient Egypt, explained on Joe Rogan's show that literal translations of inscriptions at Dendera, an ancient Egyptian temple site, come out as "stargate," meaning a gateway to other places. If so, the ancient Egyptians would have been writing about such gateways.
stargate-psychic-spy-program-1972-1995: From 1972 to 1995, according to Jesse Michels, the US government ran a psychic spy program called Stargate. It tested "remote viewing", the claimed ability to describe distant or hidden places with the mind alone. Michels comes back to it in many episodes. He says it was founded by the physicists Hal Puthoff and Russell Targ, backed first by the CIA and then by the Defense Intelligence Agency (the Pentagon's military intelligence service), and aimed at targets such as Russian nuclear bases and American hostages. He adds that its files became public in 2017 under a US law that lets anyone request government records. Puthoff, who took part, says the work grew from viewing "super secret facilities and project titles hidden in safes" into "a 20-year 20 million dollar program". Joe McMoneagle, who also took part, says it was "super supported by five presidents" and by senators such as John Glenn, and that stigma ended it, not failure. The tellers disagree about whether it worked. Michels notes that many later said it "wasn't all that effective", and that the stated reason for closing it was "only offense, there was no defense". David Grusch, a former intelligence official, passes on what Puthoff told him: that in many cases the viewers' information was confirmed by ordinary intelligence methods. Others mention it too: the former Pentagon official Lue Elizondo calls Puthoff "the Godfather" of the program, and Matthew Brown, a Pentagon whistleblower, talks about the problems of putting psychics on the official payroll. If it worked as its supporters say, the government spent over twenty years using the mind as a spying tool.
stargate-psychic-spy-program-made-public: A podcast host named Jesse Michels mentions Stargate, which he describes as a US government psychic spy program, meaning an effort to use people who claimed mental powers to gather intelligence. He says the program was more or less pried out of the government's hands and made public, which he places around 2017. He tells it as part of a wider point: if true, the government has been pushed into revealing strange programs it once kept secret.
stargate-recruitment-6-of-600-people-tes: A magician and YouTuber, Chris Ramsay, tells on Jesse Michels' podcast about Stargate, a US government programme that ran from the 1970s to 1995 and tried to use remote viewing, meaning seeing distant places or things with the mind alone. He says the programme reached out to 600 people to find viewers, that only 6 showed real talent, and that all 6 had synesthesia, a condition where the senses blend, such as seeing colours when hearing sounds. If true, it would hint that this kind of ability is tied to how a person's brain is wired.
stargate-staff-came-from-sidney-gottlieb: A podcast host named Jesse Michels says that many of the original people on Stargate, a US government program at the Stanford Research Institute in California that tried to use the mind to see distant places, came from the technical services staff of Sidney Gottlieb, a CIA scientist. He tells it because, if true, it would tie the psychic research to the CIA's own secret experiments.
stargate-within-the-mesa: On a podcast episode with the owner of Skinwalker Ranch, a property in Utah known for reports of strange happenings, a speaker invites listeners to imagine that there is a stargate, a kind of doorway to somewhere else, inside the mesa on the ranch. It is offered as a possible explanation for what people say goes on there.
staring-app-citizen-science-project-2024: Rupert Sheldrake, a British biologist known for unusual ideas about the mind, tells a podcast host in 2024 that he is releasing a phone app about the feeling of being stared at. According to Sheldrake, people can use the app to train themselves to get better at sensing a stare, which, if it works, would suggest the mind reaches beyond the body.
starlink-trains-seen-from-shurmer-s-hous: Michael Shermer, a researcher known as a leading skeptic, told the podcast host Jesse Michels about the night sky over his home in the 2020s. He says he lives in the dark mountains above Santa Barbara, California, about 90 miles from Vandenberg, a base where rockets launch every week, and that he sees the launches and hears the sound about six minutes later, along with lines of Starlink satellites, a company's internet satellites that can look like a train of moving lights. He tells it to show how ordinary things in the sky can look mysterious.
state-inspection-blocked-for-five-months: A man named Jordan, who says he was taken into a UFO-related government program as a child, tells a podcast host about records from around 2010 at Baker Victory Services, an organization in Springville, New York, where he was staying. Jordan says that, according to the records, the place refused to let state officials in to inspect his situation for five months, and that he was then sent home in a hurry. He mentions a man named Ross Colart in telling it, and to him it points to something being hidden.
station-wagon-woman-reappears-at-changi-: Peter Levenda, an author who writes about secret history and was billed as a CIA historian, told the podcast host Jesse Michels about a strange moment around 1990. He says he was at Changi Airport in Singapore when a woman he connects with an earlier encounter involving a station wagon appeared again there. He tells it as a sign that something was arranging or watching his path.
stationary-objects-over-montana-written-: A man named Robert Hastings tells a podcast that a controller once told him about objects seen over Montana that were basically stationary in the sky. Hastings says the rumor at the time was that they were Soviet spy planes, but he doubts the Soviets were flying hovering aircraft over Montana, which would leave the objects unexplained.
stealth-bomber-over-altadena-on-new-year: Michael Shermer, a researcher known as a leading skeptic, told the podcast host Jesse Michels that when he lived in Altadena, California, he once saw a stealth bomber, a US military plane with an odd flat, wing-shaped body, fly over his house on New Year's Day. He uses it as an example of how a real but unusual aircraft could be mistaken for something otherworldly.
stealth-fighter-panels-rumored-to-be-ant: Greg Bishop, a writer about UFO stories, tells a podcast what someone told him about the stealth fighter, a US Air Force jet built to be hard to see on radar. According to that person, people would come in, pull panels off the plane, put them in briefcases and leave, and the rumour was that some of those panels were anti-gravity parts to help it fly in a different way. If true, it would mean secret anti-gravity technology was already flying in military aircraft.
stefan-hogeborn-s-2012-dive-dark-black-s: Dennis Asberg, a Swedish treasure hunter, leads a team that found a strange shape on the floor of the Baltic Sea between Sweden and Finland, often called the Baltic Sea anomaly. He says that in 2012 one of the divers, Stefan Hogeborn, went down in near-freezing water, brushed the mud off the object and found its surface was dark black. The detail matters to the tellers because it would say something about what the object is actually made of.
steinman-fired-by-lockheed-after-his-boo: Scott Ramsay, a researcher of a reported UFO crash, tells a podcast about a man named Bill Steinman who worked for Lockheed, a large American aircraft company, and wrote a book about flying saucers. Ramsay says Steinman was warned that the company did not like employees writing such books, and that a couple of days after it came out in 1986, he was fired. The story is told as a sign of how much pressure there was to keep quiet on the subject.
steinman-s-ufo-crash-book-aztec-1948-eri: Jesse Michels, a podcast host, says he read a book by a UFO researcher, William Steinman, about a flying saucer said to have crashed near Aztec, New Mexico, in 1948, and that it describes Eric Henry Wang, a scientist brought to the US after World War Two under Operation Paperclip, a program that recruited German experts, who ran special projects at Wright-Patterson, an Air Force base in Ohio. Michels says Steinman figured out that Wang reported to someone called "HAK", meaning Henry Kissinger, later a top US diplomat, and in another telling he puts the claim in the mouth of Wang's wife, Maria, who said her husband worked on UFOs and his boss was Kissinger. If true, it would tie one of America's most famous statesmen to secret work on crashed saucers.
step-pyramid-as-methane-fracking-system: Geoffrey Drumm, who says an alien told him what the pyramids were really for, explains on Jesse Michels' podcast his idea about the Step Pyramid at Saqqara in Egypt. He says it was a machine for drawing methane gas out of the ground by fracking, cracking rock with pressure, and that an outside water reservoir was used to raise and lower the water inside the pyramid to push pressure up and down in its tunnels. If true, the pyramid would be an industrial plant rather than a tomb.
step-pyramid-design-at-angkor-thom: A guest named Matt, on Jesse Michels' podcast about a possible great event around 12,000 BC, says he has seen the same step pyramid design, a pyramid built in stacked tiers, at Angkor Thom, an ancient temple city in Cambodia. The point of noting it is that matching designs far apart might, to him, suggest a shared lost source.
stephen-braude-s-first-person-plural-on-: A philosopher named Jason Jorjani says that another philosopher, Stephen Braude of the University of Maryland, Baltimore, wrote a first book called First Person Plural that included a chapter on cases of multiple personality disorder. Jorjani raises it because, as he frames it, some of those cases might be better explained as possession by an outside intelligence.
stephen-dick-paper-on-ufos-as-cellular-a: A podcast host named Jesse Michels says that Stephen Dick, an adviser to NASA, wrote a paper suggesting that UFOs might be part of some kind of computing system, something like cellular automata, which are simple rule-following patterns that can grow into complex behavior. If that idea were right, UFOs would be less like visiting ships and more like parts of a vast calculating machine.
stephen-dick-s-early-suggestion-that-the: Diana Pasulka, a professor who writes about religion and UFO belief, said on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels that a scholar named Stephen Dick had an unusual idea more than twenty years ago. According to Pasulka, Dick suggested that the unexplained phenomena people report are a form of artificial intelligence, or that if we ever met whoever is behind them, they would turn out to be AI. If he is right, the visitors would be machines rather than living beings. She brought it up next to the ideas of another researcher, Jacques Vallee.
stephen-hawking-s-submarine-trip-to-poss: A comedian named Kurt Metzger says that a man called Fog Daniel told him the famous physicist Stephen Hawking went down in a submarine to look at underwater ruins that some think could be Atlantis, the legendary sunken city. Metzger links the story to National Geographic. If true, it would mean one of the world's best-known scientists took a personal interest in a lost-civilization site.
stephen-miller-s-ufo-task-force-2026: A US congressman named Eric Burlison, speaking on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels in 2026, says that Stephen Miller, an official in the White House, has put together a task force, a small working group, dealing with UFOs. Burlison mentions it alongside President Donald Trump, and if it is as he says, the White House itself would be running its own effort on the subject.
sterilizing-world-physics-so-others-can-: A mathematician named Eric Weinstein, on podcast host Jesse Michels's show, offers a possibility about why Americans were pushed out of US physics and science programmes in recent decades. He suggests the goal may have been to "sterilize" the world's physics so that no one else could catch up to what the US had already secretly achieved, which would mean breakthroughs are being hidden on purpose.
steve-justice-at-to-the-stars-wanted-to-: Peter Levenda, an author who writes about secret history, told the podcast host Jesse Michels about meeting Steve Justice at To the Stars Academy, a company set up in the late 2010s to research UFOs.
