Levenda says Justice was the kind of man who would know where the secrets were buried, yet told him he did not know how the saucers flew and really wanted to find out. He tells it to suggest that even well-placed insiders lack the answers.
steven-dick-s-ai-protective-layer-of-ear: A podcast host named Jesse Michels says that Steven Dick, a former NASA figure who is part of the Galileo Project, an effort led by the researcher Avi Loeb to search the skies for unexplained objects, talks about UFOs as some sort of artificial intelligence layer protecting Earth. If true, it would mean something intelligent and non-human is quietly watching over the planet.
steven-greenstreet-s-one-night-visit-201: Brandon Fugal, the owner of Skinwalker Ranch, a Utah property known for reports of strange happenings, talks to a podcast host about a visit by a reporter named Steven Greenstreet. Fugal says Greenstreet spent only one night on the ranch and arrived already expecting to find nothing, which Fugal offers as a reason not to trust his account.
steven-greer-cut-the-four-fingered-arm-f: An online researcher who goes by UAPGerb says that Steven Greer, who in 2000 recorded witness interviews for a UFO disclosure campaign, cut a detail out of his interview with a witness named Jonathan Weygandt: a four-fingered arm. UAPGerb says this shows up in the raw files from Greer's archive and mentions the filmmaker James Fox in connection with it, and tells it because it would mean a key piece of testimony about a non-human body was left out.
steven-greer-laurence-rockefeller-defect: A podcast host named Jesse Michels passes on something he heard from Steven Greer, a man who campaigns for governments to reveal what they know about UFOs. According to Michels, Greer claimed that Laurence Rockefeller, a member of the wealthy Rockefeller family who was involved with UFO questions in the 1990s, was a kind of defector from his own family. If true, it would mean one powerful family member broke ranks with the rest over the subject.
steven-greer-s-benevolent-alien-theory: A podcast host named Jesse Michels says that Steven Greer, a well-known campaigner for UFO disclosure, holds the view that the visitors are all love and light and good. Michels brings it up in a debate with a skeptic as one of the competing ideas about what these beings want, which, if Greer is right, would be nothing to fear.
steven-greer-s-practice-of-calling-ufos-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, talks about a UFO researcher named Steven Greer, whose work he calls a mixed bag but says is now being vindicated in many ways. According to Michels, Greer believes ordinary people can try to "call in" UFOs, summoning them on purpose. If that were true, contact would be open to anyone, not just governments.
steven-lovekin-eisenhower-doodled-ufos-a: A UFO researcher named Grant Cameron says he spoke with Steven Lovekin, a man who says he was inside Mount Weather, a government site in Virginia, with President Dwight Eisenhower in the 1950s. According to Cameron, Lovekin said Eisenhower used to doodle UFO drawings there, and that Mount Weather was where the UFO matter was headquartered. If true, it would put the president personally close to the subject.
steven-lovkin-eisenhower-said-he-no-long: Steven Greer, a doctor who collects testimony from people he calls UFO whistleblowers, told podcast host Jesse Michels about one of them: Steven Lovkin, a young Army man in the signal corps, the unit that handles communications, who worked at the White House around 1959 and 1960. Greer says Lovkin saw President Dwight Eisenhower doodle pictures of alien craft, and that when Lovkin raised the subject, Eisenhower told him, "I don't have control of this anymore." If true, it would mean that even a sitting president had lost his grip on the UFO secret.
stigmata-man-at-a-ufo-conference: Dan Sherman, a former Air Force sergeant who says the NSA, the US government's code-breaking and eavesdropping agency, hired him to communicate with aliens, tells a podcast host about people he met at a UFO conference. Sherman says one man there had the stigmata, wounds like those of the crucified Jesus, which he mentions as one of the stranger things he saw on that circuit.
stigmatization-campaign-since-the-robert: A retired US Navy admiral, Tim Gallaudet, told podcast host Jesse Michels that the shame and ridicule around UFOs comes from a deliberate, well-funded campaign that has run for about 80 years. He says it began after the Robertson Panel, a 1953 government panel that reviewed UFO reports, and that it has worked very well, which would explain why so few people take the subject seriously.
stonehenge-altar-stone-as-a-lightning-ro: Geoffrey Drumm, who says an alien revealed to him the true purpose of ancient monuments, says on Jesse Michels' podcast that the Altar Stone at Stonehenge, the ancient stone circle in England, was a lightning rod. He calls it an obelisk, a tall standing stone, and treats it, if he is right, as part of an energy system rather than a place of worship.
stones-floated-in-on-reed-boats-and-the-: Joe McMoneagle, a man known for remote viewing, a claimed ability to see distant places or times with the mind, offers his own account of how the pyramids at Giza in Egypt were built. He says the builders made reed boats, cut the stone up the Nile, floated it downriver, and that the pyramid site was flooded so the boats could bring the stone in. He links the idea to his book The Ultimate Time Machine, and if true it would explain how such huge blocks were moved.
strange-deaths-of-abduction-researchers-: Tim Alberino, a filmmaker who tells stories of giants and the unexplained, speaks on Jesse Michels' podcast about a string of strange deaths among people who studied alien abductions, naming researchers such as John Mack, Karla Turner, Budd Hopkins and Barbara Bartholic. He says that, if he recalls rightly, when the abduction researcher John Mack was hit by a car in England, another man also named John Mack was hit by a car the same day. He tells it as an eerie coincidence hanging over the field.
strange-explosions-caught-on-home-camera: Whitley Strieber, a writer known for his books about meeting strange beings, told the podcast host Jesse Michels that around 2022 the beings he deals with got angry at him. He says that afterward the cameras at his home picked up a series of strange explosions. If true, it would mean these visitors can act on the physical world in ways cameras can record.
strange-lights-over-the-san-juan-coal-mi: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says he spoke to a local man from Aztec, a town in New Mexico, who had seen strange lights darting above the San Juan coal mine, right by where the man worked. Michels brings it up while looking into claims of a crashed craft in that area. If true, it would suggest odd things are still being seen in the sky there.
stranger-in-long-john-silver-s-says-read: Rolf Mowatt-Larssen, a former senior CIA officer, says that in 1976 he was in a Long John Silver's fast food restaurant near Fort Knox, a US Army post, when a stranger walked straight up to him. He says the man told him to read Ezekiel, Daniel and Revelation, three books of the Bible, then walked away. He describes it in his book A State of Mind: Faith in the CIA as a moment that seemed to carry a message meant for him.
stranger-with-air-force-ties-at-hart-can: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in 2026, while visiting Hart Canyon near Aztec, New Mexico, a remote spot where some say a craft crashed with alien bodies aboard, a stranger showed up at the same time as his crew. Michels says the man had curious ties to the Air Force, and that it seemed odd for anyone to turn up at such an obscure and hard-to-reach place right when they did.
strassman-s-repeat-dose-dmt-tests-showin: A neuroscientist named Andrew Gallimore, on podcast host Jesse Michels's show, refers to studies in the 1990s by Rick Strassman, a doctor who gave volunteers DMT, a powerful psychedelic drug, by injection. According to Gallimore, Strassman gave people repeated doses and found their bodies did not build up tolerance to it, which Gallimore treats as a clue that DMT plays some special role in the brain.
strassman-s-spirit-molecule-hypothesis-d: A neuroscientist named Andrew Gallimore, speaking on a podcast, explains where the nickname "the spirit molecule" comes from for DMT, a powerful psychedelic chemical. He says it came from the idea of a researcher named Rick Strassman, set out in his work titled DMT: The Spirit Molecule, that the brain releases DMT at the moment of death. If true, it would tie the experiences people report near death to a chemical in the body.
strategic-air-command-letter-congratulat: Peter Levenda, an author who writes about the occult and secret history, helped publish a book of spells in the late 1970s called the Necronomicon, named after a fictional book of dark magic from horror stories. He says that, along with other letters, the publishers received a friendly note on the stationery of Strategic Air Command, the US Air Force branch that ran the nation's nuclear bombers and missiles, simply congratulating them on the new publication. If true, it would hint that people in the nuclear military were paying attention to occult material.
stratton-and-lacatski-built-osap-togethe: Eric Davis, a physicist who has worked on Pentagon research, told the podcast host Jesse Michels about the start of OSAP, a secret study program run in 2008 through the Defense Intelligence Agency, the Pentagon's military intelligence service, that looked into unexplained aircraft. He tells it to set the record straight on who created the program.
stratton-forms-the-uap-task-force-2020: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that a man named Jay Stratton, who he thinks may have been in the Navy, formed the UAP Task Force around 2020. UAP stands for unidentified anomalous phenomena, the government's term for UFOs, and Michels describes the task force as a group set up to review all the government's data on them internally. He tells it as a step in the US government taking these reports seriously.
streak-left-on-the-cliff-by-the-craft-19: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, talks about a mesa, a flat-topped hill, near the Archuleta ranch in New Mexico, where some say a craft came down in 1948. Drawing on a man named Scott Ramsay, Michels says the streak the craft left on the cliff as it crashed can still be seen there today. If true, it would be physical trace evidence of the crash still sitting on the land.
stress-iq-test-during-air-force-recruitm: Jake Barber, a former helicopter pilot who says he once carried a UFO with his aircraft, told the podcast host Jesse Michels about being screened for the Air Force around 1994 near UCLA, a university in Los Angeles. He says he took an intelligence test once normally and then again wearing an oxygen mask sealed to his face with no air coming in. He tells it to show the unusual testing he says marked him for special work.
strieber-helps-fund-the-first-scientific: Whitley Strieber, a writer known for his books about strange beings, told the podcast host Jesse Michels that in 1978 he helped pay for the first scientific studies of the Shroud of Turin, an old linen cloth in Italy that many believe shows the image of Jesus. He says he and his family gave a few thousand dollars and followed the work, though he only spoke with the researchers, named Jackson and Jumper, in a fundraising setting and never became friends with them. He tells it to show his long interest in mysteries science struggles to explain.
strieber-s-career-destroyed-which-he-tie: Whitley Strieber, a writer famous for describing his own encounters with non-human beings, says his career and life were wrecked from the late 1980s on. He points to the third episode of Beyond, a series made by the studio MGM, as showing what happened to him, and says he is convinced it had to do with the Collins Elite, a group said to exist inside the government. If true, it would mean someone in power set out to ruin a man for speaking about his experiences.
strieber-s-childhood-mind-control-camp-a: A philosopher named Jason Jorjani, speaking on a podcast, relays a claim made by Whitley Strieber, a writer known for describing encounters with strange beings. According to Jorjani, Strieber says that as a child in the 1950s he was sent to a summer camp at Randolph Air Force Base, a US military base near his family's home in Texas, where he alleges he suffered physical torture and mind control experiments. If true, it would mean the military experimented on children.
strieber-s-meeting-with-james-jesus-angl: A podcast host named Jesse Michels says that Whitley Strieber, a writer known for describing encounters with strange beings, told him on the show that he once met James Jesus Angleton, a senior figure in the CIA, the US spy agency. No time or place is given, but if true it would link Strieber's story to the highest levels of American intelligence.
strieber-s-written-account-to-sarbacher-: Whitley Strieber, a writer known for his book Communion about his own encounters, says that in 1986 a scientist named Robert Sarbacher asked him to write out his whole experience. Strieber says he wrote it up at his cabin in upstate New York and shipped it to Sarbacher in Florida, and the next morning the delivery driver called to say "The recipient has expired": Sarbacher had died that night. Strieber tells the story twice in the same interview, and once he only stresses Sarbacher's request, without mentioning the death.
strieber-taken-to-a-school-for-special-c: A philosopher named Jason Jorjani, speaking on a podcast, relays another part of the childhood story told by Whitley Strieber, a writer known for describing encounters with strange beings. According to Jorjani, Strieber says that in the 1950s he was at one point taken from Randolph Air Force Base, a US military base in Texas, to a school for special children in Baja California, Mexico. If true, it would suggest the program he describes reached beyond the base and across the border.
strieber-writes-to-warn-against-the-oxfo: Whitley Strieber, a writer known for his books about strange beings, told the podcast host Jesse Michels that in 1988 he wrote to a churchman, Father Raldi, warning him not to let a lab in Oxford test the Shroud of Turin, an old cloth believed by many to show Jesus, with carbon dating, a method that estimates age. He says he warned that scientists would defend their existing beliefs and lie without knowing it, and that in the end they declared the shroud to be from the Middle Ages and destroyed the earlier research. He tells it as an example of science burying evidence it cannot fit.
string-theory-as-an-intentional-dead-end: Podcast host Jesse Michels has asked whether string theory, a popular idea in physics that Ed Witten, a leading physicist, worked on, might be a deliberate "bridge to nowhere". The mathematician Eric Weinstein makes the same claim his own, saying it may have been a blocking mechanism to keep people from doing dangerous physics work, and he links it to an account of hidden physics from the tech investors Andreessen and Horowitz, naming Witten and the physicist Brian Greene. If true, it would mean mainstream physics was steered away from secret discoveries on purpose.
stringfield-files-on-headband-transceive: A researcher who goes by the name UAPGerb (UAP is the newer official term for UFOs) says he went through the files of Leonard Stringfield, a UFO researcher based in Cincinnati, Ohio, who wrote a series of seven reports in the 1970s and 80s about crashed craft said to have been recovered. According to UAPGerb, the files mention many witnesses who saw recovered UFOs, along with cutaway diagrams, and in some cases a headband or headband transceiver, a device for sending and receiving signals, worn by the craft's operators. If true, it would hint at how the crews controlled their craft. He also draws on the work of another researcher, Michael Schratt.
stringfield-s-investigations-into-crash-: A journalist, Michael Shellenberger, says that a man named Stringfield carried out a large number of investigations into crash retrievals, meaning claims that the US government recovered crashed craft of unknown origin. Shellenberger brings him up as an earlier researcher whose work, if sound, would add weight to the idea that such recoveries happened.
sts-124-bolt-in-the-payload-bay-was-the-: A former NASA astronaut named Scott Kelly passes on a story from his brother Mark Kelly, also a former astronaut and now a US senator, about the time Mark commanded STS-124, a Space Shuttle mission in 2008. As the story is framed, something that looked like a bolt floating near the shuttle's open cargo bay turned out to be the International Space Station, the large orbiting laboratory. It is told as an example of how a puzzling sight in space can turn out to be something familiar.
sts-48-and-sts-80-shuttle-uap-videos-199: Two space shuttle missions, known by their NASA flight codes STS-48 in 1991 and STS-80 in 1996, are said to have filmed unexplained objects in orbit around Earth. NASA is the US space agency, and these objects are what officials now call UAP, unidentified anomalous phenomena. A guest named Maaneli Derakhshani brings up both videos as key cases, and another guest, Max, refers back to them in passing. They are told as evidence that strange objects may have been caught on camera in space.
stubblebine-s-effort-to-cognitively-enha: A researcher who goes by UAPGerb says on Jesse Michels' podcast that in the 1980s General Albert Stubblebine, who headed INSCOM, the US Army's intelligence and security command, wanted to cognitively enhance soldiers, meaning boost their mental powers. If true, it shows the Army's top intelligence leadership taking an interest in pushing the limits of the human mind.
student-vanishes-on-mountain-excursion-i: Aldo Rebelo, a former Brazilian defense minister, tells of a well-known event in the mountains of Minas Gerais, a state in Brazil, that was reported in the local press. He says a group of students was on a trip there when one girl walked away from the group for a while and simply vanished. He tells it as one of the strange, unexplained cases from his country.
sturgis-led-raid-sinks-a-russian-ship-ma: A guest named Danny Sheehan, on podcast host Jesse Michels's show, says that in 1962 a man named Frank Sturgis led a group of Cubans from a base on No Name Key, a small island in Florida, in an attack on Cuba that sank a Russian ship. According to Sheehan, US marshals, federal law officers, then burned down the No Name Key base, with Robert Kennedy, brother of the president, in the story, which he ties to hidden fights inside the government of the time.
sub-bottom-profiling-shows-the-layers-un: A Swedish treasure hunter named Dennis Asberg says his team found a strange object on the floor of the Baltic Sea, between Sweden and Finland. Speaking with a podcast host, Jesse Michels, in 2025, he says they have also done sub-bottom profiling, a sonar method that looks at the layers of mud and rock beneath the seabed, to see what lies under the object. If the scans show what he suggests, it would help say whether the object is a natural formation or something else.
submarine-crew-showed-the-doctor-the-son: A doctor who worked with NASA, the US space agency, named Greg Rogers says that while he was aboard a US Navy submarine, the crew took him into the sonar room, where the boat listens for sounds under the water. He told this to a podcast host, Jesse Michels, as part of a longer account of what he says he saw during his career.
submarines-take-evasive-action-from-fast: A retired US Navy admiral named Tim Gallaudet says several submarine officers, plus one enlisted sailor, came to him with reports of sudden encounters with objects under the water that were closing on their submarines very fast, forcing them to take evasive action. He gives no time or place. If true, it would mean unknown craft are moving through the oceans at speeds the Navy cannot explain.
substack-article-on-the-boxer-upsets-the: Peter Levenda, an author who writes about the occult and secret history, says he wrote an article on his Substack, an online newsletter he admits he has barely used in a year, about an event involving a boxer. He says the piece upset people in the wrestling world.
subterranean-chamber-as-giza-s-original-: A researcher and writer on ancient history, Graham Hancock, told a podcast host, Jesse Michels, in 2022 that a rock-cut room about 100 feet straight down beneath the base of the Great Pyramid in Giza, Egypt, is, in his view, the original sacred site there, older in meaning than the pyramid above it. Another researcher, Luke Caverns, later passed the idea along on the same show, saying Hancock had told it on another podcast: most of the pyramid was built under the ancient king Khufu, and the underground level may have been there already. If true, it would mean the pyramid was built on top of an even older holy place.
sudden-mastery-of-morse-code-under-threa: A former US Army intelligence soldier named Joe McMoneagle says that in the 1960s, while training at an Army intelligence school, he was told he would be sent to the Vietnam War if he failed his Morse code tests. He says that in about two hours on one day he passed test after test at faster and faster speeds, because something just "popped" in his head. He tells it as an early sign of unusual mental abilities.
sufi-imam-jinn-change-physical-scripture: Rizwan Virk, a computer scientist and author who argues that our world may be a kind of simulation, tells of a Sufi imam, a religious teacher from the mystical branch of Islam. According to Virk, the imam said the Quran, Islam's holy book, is still memorized word for word because jinn, spirit beings that live outside normal space and time, can go back and change physical objects like written pages but are not allowed to change human memory. Virk shares it as an old idea that echoes his own view that reality can be edited.
suicide-stand-down-in-the-drone-program-: A man named Dylan Borland says that in 2013 people working in the US Air Force drone program called him with troubling news. According to Borland, they told him they had just had a "suicide stand-down," meaning work was paused so everyone could deal with suicides among the crews. He tells it to show how heavy the strain inside that program was.
suited-beings-on-a-scrap-metal-train-car: Clas Svahn, a Swedish UFO researcher who has gathered a huge archive of reports, says a woman recently wrote to him and then spoke with him. sumer-over-12-000-years-old-based-on-geo: A researcher named Matt told a podcast host, Jesse Michels, in 2024 that Sumer, the ancient civilisation of southern Iraq, goes back well over 12,000 years, judging by how its sites line up with measurements of the Earth's shape and position, a field called geodesy. sumerian-accounts-of-civilizations-from-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that the Sumerians, one of the earliest known civilizations of the ancient Middle East, spoke of civilizations that existed before there was a moon. sumerian-anunnaki-engineered-a-slave-rac: The Sumerians were an ancient people of Mesopotamia who left some of the oldest written texts. sumerian-astronomical-knowledge: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that the buildings of the Sumerians, one of the earliest known civilizations of the ancient Middle East, show a surprisingly advanced knowledge of astronomy. sumerian-flood-story-as-the-source-of-no: A researcher named Matt says on Jesse Michels's podcast that if you read the Epic of Gilgamesh and the Atrahasis, two ancient poems from Mesopotamia, the land of today's Iraq, their flood stories are almost identical to the one in Genesis, the first book of the Bible. sumerian-god-who-emerged-from-the-water-: A writer named Peter Levenda, on podcast host Jesse Michels's show, points to the myths of Sumer, one of the earliest civilisations, in what is now Iraq. sumerian-king-list-with-kings-ruling-ten: Joe Rogan, a comedian and podcast host, spoke with podcast host Jesse Michels about the Sumerian King List, an ancient text from Sumer in Mesopotamia, modern Iraq, that names its early rulers. summoning-and-piloting-uap-through-medit: Jake Barber, a helicopter pilot who says he worked on secret UFO retrieval missions, told the podcast host Jesse Michels that people can call up UFOs with their minds. summoning-demonstrations-for-the-aaro-di: Jake Barber, a helicopter pilot who says he once flew a recovered UFO under his helicopter, told the podcast host Jesse Michels that his team was showing off its skill at calling up UFOs. summoning-team-present-the-night-of-the-: Jake Barber, a helicopter pilot, says that around 2014 he flew a mission in the California desert to pick up a large egg-shaped object he believes was not made by humans. summoning-the-egg-in-daylight-after-leav: Jake Barber, a helicopter pilot who says he once helped recover an egg-shaped craft, told the podcast host Jesse Michels that in August 2024, after leaving that secret program, he saw the egg again in the desert, in daylight. sun-angle-3d-reconstruction-of-the-flir1: In 2004, off Southern California, a Navy jet's heat-sensing camera filmed a strange object, and that video is known as FLIR1. sun-is-400-times-larger-and-400-times-fa: A researcher named Randall Carlson, on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, points to an odd coincidence: he says the sun is 400 times larger than the moon and also 400 times farther away. suppressed-childhood-memories-resurface-: Jordan Jose is a man who says he was taken into a secret UFO program as a child. surgical-animal-mutilation-with-no-blood: Around Aztec, New Mexico, a small town where a famous crash story is told, locals speak of animal mutilations. surrealist-founders-occult-seances-and-b: A researcher and writer, Jason Jorjani, told a podcast host, Jesse Michels, in 2025 that the founders of Surrealism, an art movement born in 1920s France, including André Breton, Max Ernst and Paul Éluard, were taking part in occult rituals and long séances, sessions meant to contact spirits, from the very start, even before the movement had its name. survey-finding-only-about-30-of-physicis: A researcher with a PhD, Jeffrey Mishlove, who studies psychic claims, says on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels that a recent survey found only about 30 percent of physicists stick with the standard model, the mainstream theory in physics. susan-clancy-s-harvard-study-of-abductee: A well-known skeptic named Michael Shermer, debating on a podcast, brings up the work of Susan Clancy, a psychology researcher at Harvard University. susan-gough-by-kirkpatrick-s-side-at-geo: A witness named Merrick told the podcast host Jesse Michels that he met Sean Kirkpatrick, then head of the Pentagon's UFO office, in person at an event at George Mason University in Virginia in November 2023. susan-gough-refuses-to-amend-statement-t: An online researcher who goes by UAPGerb tells, on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, of a moment in the 2020s involving Susan Gough, a Pentagon spokesperson. susan-gough-s-psychological-operations-r: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says one of the main sources for a 2025 Wall Street Journal article on UFOs was a woman named Susan Gough. susan-gough-says-gimbal-is-not-a-trainin: Mick West, a skeptic who studies UFO videos, told podcast host Jesse Michels that he asked Susan Gough, a Pentagon spokesperson, about the Gimbal video, a 2015 clip filmed by a Navy jet's camera off Florida that shows a strange object turning in the sky. susan-mccasland-accepted-a-calendar-invi: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, points to a document from the Podesta emails, a batch of private emails belonging to the political adviser John Podesta that the website WikiLeaks made public. susan-mccasland-s-911-call-about-her-hus: Susan McCasland, whose husband went missing in Albuquerque, New Mexico, in 2026, made a call to 911, the US emergency phone line. susan-mccasland-s-facebook-statement-on-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, reads from what he presents as a 2026 Facebook post by Susan McCasland, a senior US Air Force officer. susi-temples-no-longer-face-east-west-im: On a 2024 episode of a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, about something big that happened around 12,000 BC, a researcher named Matt LaCroix talks about a kind of ancient temple in eastern Turkey that he calls a Susi temple. suspected-spook-at-the-hotel-during-the-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that while he and a companion were in Washington, DC, for congressional hearings on UFOs in 2024, a man he describes as "straight up" a spook, slang for an intelligence agent, came up to them. suzanne-s-mother-moves-the-family-to-azt: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells of a woman named Suzanne, born in South Dakota to a mother obsessed with UFOs. swedenborg-s-visits-to-other-planets: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, mentions Emanuel Swedenborg, a Swedish mystic he places in the 17th century, who said he travelled to other planets and came back. swedish-ghost-rockets-and-doolittle-s-in: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in 1946 and 1947 people in Sweden reported over a thousand sightings of what were called ghost rockets, which looked like modified V2s, the rockets Germany built in the Second World War. sweep-and-the-1964-money-funnel-in-sekre: A speaker identified only as JASON, on a podcast, describes part of Sekret Machines, a series of books linked to a man named Tom DeLonge that tells of hidden UFO programs. switching-astronaut-chem-lights-from-red: A doctor named Greg Rogers, who worked with NASA, the US space agency, at Kennedy Space Center in Florida around 1989 to 1991, says he spent a year and a half persuading NASA to switch the glow sticks used by astronauts from red to green. sycamore-knoll-undersea-base-claim-rejec: This story is about Sycamore Knoll, an undersea hill off Point Dume near Malibu in Southern California, which some have said hides an alien base under the sea. synesthete-watson-who-saw-and-felt-taste: A cognitive scientist named Don Hoffman, on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, tells of a man he thinks was named Watson who had synesthesia, a condition where the senses blend. szydagis-tests-alleged-crash-debris-with: A physicist and former NASA scientist, Kevin Knuth, says on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels that his colleague Matthew Szydagis, at the University at Albany, has been studying debris said to come from UFO crashes. t-pillar-at-cavustepe-visited-with-rober: A man named Matt, speaking on a podcast with a host, Jesse Michels, about ancient history, says he recently visited Çavuştepe in Turkey with a researcher named Robert Schoch. t-pillar-design-on-the-gate-of-the-sun: A researcher named Matt told a podcast host, Jesse Michels, in 2024 that the back of the Gate of the Sun, a carved stone gateway at Tiwanaku, an ancient site in Bolivia, shows a T-shaped pillar design with the same idea of three doorways that he sees elsewhere. t-t-brown-apparatus-left-in-the-eureka-g: Clas Svahn, a researcher who collects UFO records, says that a group called the Borderland Society, based in Eureka, California, had ties to Townsend Brown, an inventor who patented a device he called an electrokinetic generator and is the subject of a book called The Man Who Mastered Gravity. tactical-plan-to-stand-down-the-covert-o: Steven Greer, a doctor who has long campaigned for the government to reveal what it knows about UFOs, told the podcast host Jesse Michels that a plan already exists to shut down the secret group he says controls UFO secrets. tae-technologiestrump-media-merger-annou: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, points out that a merger deal between a company called TAE Technologies and Trump Media was announced on December 18, 2025, and that a man named Loureiro died two days earlier, on December 16. tag-17-dead-end-corridor-behind-the-nort: A researcher named Jeffrey told a podcast host, Jesse Michels, in 2026 that a scan of the Great Pyramid in Egypt made in 2020, by a team that included a man named Filippo, picked up a dead-end corridor, labelled Tag 17, behind the large angled stone blocks on the pyramid's north face. talbert-newspaper-series-on-1950s-aerosp: This story is about a set of newspaper articles from the 1950s saying that big American aircraft companies had suddenly become interested in anti-gravity, meaning ways to fly by cancelling or controlling gravity instead of using engines or wings. tall-white-deep-spacecraft-schedules-and: Charles Hall, a man who says he spent three years among tall, pale beings he calls the Tall Whites near Area 51, a secret Air Force base in Nevada, says he saw their flight schedules while stationed in Indian Springs Valley between 1965 and 1967. tall-whites-gated-compound-on-orcas-reac: A guest named Brent says a friend on Orcas Island told him that the Tall Whites, tall pale beings some people say live among us, have a gated compound on the island. tall-whites-in-suits-forming-a-high-spee: Charles Hall, a man who says he spent 1965 to 1967 on the Indian Springs ranges in the Nevada desert alongside tall, pale beings he calls the Tall Whites, says they wore suits that gave off a kind of force field. tall-whites-mistaken-for-ancient-egyptia: Charles Hall, a man who says he worked on the Indian Springs ranges in the Nevada desert in the 1960s alongside tall, pale beings he calls the Tall Whites, says not everyone there knew what they were. tall-whites-playing-airplanes-on-the-ind: Charles Hall, a man who says he spent 1965 to 1967 at Indian Springs in Nevada alongside tall, pale beings he calls the Tall Whites, says he used to watch them play on the runways of Indian Springs Air Base on summer nights. tall-whites-posing-as-charlie-hall-and-h: Charles Hall, a man who says he lived alongside tall, pale beings he calls the Tall Whites in the Nevada desert in the 1960s, says some of them passed themselves off as humans. tall-whites-say-dominant-species-kill-of: A guest named Kurt Metzger retells what Charles Hall, a man who says he lived and worked near tall pale beings called the Tall Whites in Indian Springs, Nevada, in the 1960s, says they told him. tall-whites-two-month-trip-to-a-star-nea: Charles Hall, a man who says he worked at Range Three near Indian Springs, Nevada, alongside tall, pale beings he calls the Tall Whites, says that in late summer 1965 some of them were gone for about six weeks to two months. tapes-mention-coupling-to-the-computer-d: An unnamed researcher on a podcast describes recordings of 1970s sessions run by a scientist named Puharich, in which people said they were in contact with non-human intelligences. If taken at face value, it would suggest the voices described some kind of link to a vast store of information.
tapes-of-puharich-meditating-in-the-king: This story is about audio recordings of a researcher named Andrija Puharich meditating inside the King's Chamber, the main stone room deep inside the Great Pyramid in Egypt. tara-swart-s-husband-s-death-and-doves: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, mentions a woman named Tara Swart whose husband died under unfortunate circumstances. targ-and-puthoff-publish-in-nature-and-w: Joe McMoneagle, a man who appeared on podcast host Jesse Michels's show in 2025, says that around 1972 two scientists, Russell Targ and Dr. Hal Puthoff, wrote an article in what he thinks was Nature, a well-known science journal, and then a book called Mind-Reach. tate-s-post-trip-talk-on-solved-energy-1: A researcher named Scott Ramsay, speaking on the podcast of host Jesse Michels, describes the archived papers of a man named John Torrance Tate, which also mention a figure named Vannevar Bush. tate-s-sealed-archive-at-university-of-m: Scott Ramsay, a researcher appearing on Jesse Michels's podcast, says he and others flew to Minneapolis and got a meeting in the archives of the University of Minnesota to see the records of a man named John Torrance Tate, dating from about 1948 to 1950. taylor-flying-cargo-jets-between-florida: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, talks about Timothy Taylor, a man he describes as being studied by NASA, the US space agency, because UFOs are said to show up around him. taylor-hospitalized-with-injuries-from-r: The owner of Skinwalker Ranch, a property in Utah known for reports of strange events, says on Jesse Michels's podcast that a man named Travis Taylor, who has worked there, had to go to the hospital because of injuries. taylor-next-rocket-science-advance-will-: Podcast host Jesse Michels retells a moment from American Cosmic, a book by Diana Pasulka, a scholar of religion. taylor-says-bledsoe-may-need-to-hide-out: Chris Bledsoe, a man who says he attracts UFOs, tells podcast host Jesse Michels that around 2008 a man named Timothy Taylor told him he might have to go hide out for a while in Nassau, in the Bahamas. taylor-secretly-chief-scientist-of-uap-t: The owner of Skinwalker Ranch, a property known for reports of strange events, says that around 2020 a scientist on the ranch team, Travis Taylor, was quietly called into meetings in Washington, D.C. taylor-warned-off-driving-up-the-road-at: The wife of Charles Hall, a man who says he spent three years with tall white aliens while stationed in the Nevada desert, tells on Jesse Michels's podcast about a visit by a man named Timothy Taylor to Creech Air Force Base in Indian Springs, Nevada. tayos-cave-metallic-library-of-alien-art: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, talks about Tayos Cave in Ecuador, which he says supposedly holds ancient metallic artifacts that look alien, arranged like a library of metal books. td-100-experiment-on-a-woman-on-film-196: A researcher named Greg Malatzi says there is silent film from the early 1960s, shot at Intelectron, a company in New York City, showing an experiment on a woman sitting behind a wall in another room. team-statement-that-limestone-absorbs-th: A man named Jeffrey, speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast, relays a 2025 statement posted on Facebook by a research team, including men named Armando and Filippo, who scanned the Khafre pyramid at Giza in Egypt. teardrop-shaped-transmedium-uap-video-sh: Tim Gallaudet, a retired Navy admiral, told podcast host Jesse Michels about an email that a naval intelligence commander sent with a video attached. tech-sergeant-warns-borland-never-to-spe: Dylan Borland, a man who served in the US Air Force, says that in 2012 at Langley Air Force Base in Virginia he saw a triangle-shaped craft. technicians-at-a-book-signing-say-the-si: A writer named Whitley Strieber, known for describing encounters with strange beings, says that at a book signing in San Antonio, Texas, in the 2010s, some technicians came up to him. technology-transfer-with-aliens-who-deve: A former Army sergeant named Lyn Buchanan, speaking with a podcast host, Jesse Michels, says he has a friend who was in charge of technology transfer with one group of aliens, meaning the passing of their know-how to humans. ted-owens-book-how-to-contact-space-peop: A researcher with a doctorate, Jeffrey Mishlove, tells podcast host Jesse Michels that a man named Ted Owens published a book in the United States in 1969 called How to Contact Space People. ted-owens-mr-pk-claimed-to-be-a-biologic: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, recalls that the researcher Jeffrey Mishlove wrote about an American man named Ted Owens, nicknamed Mr PK, for psychokinesis, the supposed power to move things with the mind. ted-owens-warns-of-challenger-shuttle-lo: Jeffrey Mishlove, a researcher with a PhD who studies psychic claims, told the podcast host Jesse Michels that on Christmas Eve 1985 he got a call from Ted Owens, a man who claimed he could command UFOs. ted-owens-wills-an-airliner-to-crash: A researcher and writer, Jason Jorjani, told a podcast host, Jesse Michels, in 2025 about a man named Ted Owens who, according to the story, used the power of his mind to make a passenger plane flying ahead of him and his companions crash, and it did. ted-rice-s-story-in-masquerade-of-angels: Tim Alberino, a filmmaker and researcher, mentions on Jesse Michels's podcast a book called Masquerade of Angels, linked to the writer Karla Turner. ted-serios-thoughtographs-studied-by-jul: Jeffrey Mishlove, a researcher with a PhD who studies psychic claims, tells on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels of Ted Serios, a Chicago hotel bellhop in the 1960s. tedesco-brothers-data-on-orbs-entering-t: A retired Navy admiral named Tim Gallaudet tells podcast host Jesse Michels that two brothers, Jerry and John Tedesco, have serious data on glowing balls of light, called orbs, seen offshore near Long Island, New York. teenage-alberino-finds-the-book-of-enoch: A researcher named Tim Alberino, speaking on podcast host Jesse Michels's show, remembers driving to a Borders bookstore at about 16 and browsing the shelves. teenage-robert-temple-helps-arthur-young: Jeffrey Mishlove, a researcher and interviewer who studies psychic phenomena, told podcast host Jesse Michels that the writer Robert Temple, as a teenager in 1960s Philadelphia, worked with the inventor and philosopher Arthur Young. telepathic-contact-with-the-orb-sylvia-2: A man named Jordan Jose, speaking on the podcast of host Jesse Michels, says that between about 2008 and 2010, at a place called Baker Victory Services in Western New York, he had mind-to-mind contact with a glowing ball of light, which he calls an orb. telepathic-escape-plan-with-cousin-ian: James Fox, a filmmaker who makes documentaries about UFOs, told the podcast host Jesse Michels about a moment in downtown San Francisco when he was about 13. telepathic-friend-meets-an-unvoiced-tele: A writer named Whitley Strieber, who says he has met beings from elsewhere, tells podcast host Jesse Michels that a friend of his who is telepathic, able to share thoughts without speaking, recently had contact with an "unvoiced person". telepathic-interview-with-a-live-et-at-s: A guest named Danny Sheehan tells podcast host Jesse Michels what a man named Oscar Wolf told him about S4, said to be a secret site near Area 51, a guarded military base in the Nevada desert. telepathic-projection-from-a-canadian-fa: Dan Sheehan, a lawyer, says that reports by Ingo Swann, a psychic who worked with the US government along with another psychic, Pat Price, describe a 1970s experiment from a facility in south central Canada. telepathic-projection-test-makes-people-: Dan Sheehan, a guest on the podcast of host Jesse Michels, describes a test from the 1970s that he says he was part of. telepathy-tapes-experiments-with-nonverb: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, describes The Telepathy Tapes, a 2024 project linked to people he names as Ky Dickens and Diane Powell, which tests whether autistic children who cannot speak can pick up their parents' thoughts. telepathy-tapes-nonverbal-autistic-child: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, speaking in an interview that also involves a man named Kai Dickens, brings up The Telepathy Tapes, a podcast about autistic children who cannot speak. telepathy-tapes-you-don-t-get-my-powers-: Podcast host Jesse Michels mentioned The Telepathy Tapes, a 2024 podcast by filmmaker Ky Dickens about children who are said to communicate by telepathy. telephone-telepathy-experiments: A biologist named Rupert Sheldrake tells podcast host Jesse Michels about experiments he says he ran on telephone telepathy, the idea that people can sometimes sense who is calling before they answer. If he is right, minds would be linked in ways science does not yet explain.
televised-remote-viewing-by-japanese-sch: Joe McMoneagle, who practises remote viewing, the attempt to describe a hidden or faraway target using only the mind, tells podcast host Jesse Michels about a remote viewing session shown on Japanese television. teller-and-sakharov-meet-sakharov-says-t: Physicist John Brandenburg tells Jesse Michels that Edward Teller, a scientist linked to the American hydrogen bomb, later met Andrei Sakharov, whom he calls the father of the Russian hydrogen bomb. Brandenburg tells it in support of his larger argument about nuclear science and its hidden history.
teller-letter-commending-john-alexander: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says there is a letter from Edward Teller, the physicist behind the American hydrogen bomb, praising a man named John Alexander. teller-refuses-on-camera-to-discuss-laza: A man named Bob Lazar, interviewed by podcast host Jesse Michels, tells of a moment around 1989 when a scientist, Edward Teller, was asked about Lazar on camera and refused to talk about him. teller-s-name-on-a-project-sign-grudge-u: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that a document from Project Sign or Project Grudge, the US Air Force's first UFO studies in the late 1940s, before its better-known study called Blue Book, has the name of Edward Teller on it. teller-shown-townsend-brown-s-demo-floyd: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that the physicist Edward Teller was friendly with Thomas Townsend Brown, an inventor of unusual electrical propulsion devices, and was shown a demonstration of one of Brown's experiments. templars-and-the-secrets-of-time-travel: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, mentions the Knights Templar, a religious order of knights from the Middle Ages. It is told as one more thread in old stories of hidden knowledge.
templars-as-keepers-of-advanced-knowledg: A researcher named Randall Carlson, on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, says he believes the Knights Templar, a medieval order of knights in France whose leader Jacques de Molay was brought down around 1307, guarded advanced knowledge. templars-lalibela-and-the-ark-in-ethiopi: Author Graham Hancock tells Jesse Michels about an idea from his book The Sign and the Seal. templars-persecuted-by-philip-the-fair-a: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells of the Knights Templar, a medieval order of Christian knights, who were accused of rituals such as spitting on the cross. temple-of-sais-as-a-record-keeping-site-: Researcher Matthew LaCroix tells Jesse Michels that, drawing on the ancient writer Plutarch and a figure named Sonchis, the Temple of Sais in ancient Egypt existed to keep records of history. LaCroix says the temple was destroyed sometime within 500 to 1,000 years after the Greek visitor Solon heard its stories, so those records were lost, which would mean a key archive of very ancient history vanished.
temporary-duty-at-the-pentagon-handling-: Joe McMoneagle, a former US Army man later known for remote viewing, tells podcast host Jesse Michels that during the Vietnam War, in the late 1960s, he was sent on temporary duty, what the military calls TDY, to the Pentagon, the headquarters of the US military in Washington, DC. He says this was because protesters against the war were throwing balloons full of blood. He tells it as part of his own story of how he came to serve close to the centre of military power.
tens-of-thousands-of-alien-satellites-st: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, presents the work of an astronomer named Beatriz Villarroel, who has looked at old photos of the night sky. He frames it as the possibility that tens of thousands of alien satellites were studying Earth before humans launched their first one, Sputnik, in 1957. tentacle-shape-analysis-says-the-jellyfi: Skywatcher, a startup company that says it can summon UFOs, told the podcast host Jesse Michels about objects it calls the "7th class," shaped like jellyfish with dangling tentacles, which it says it filmed at its field site between about 2023 and 2025. The team says its published images show the tentacles sometimes held straight, which they argue means these are not balloons drifting in the wind, and they compare them with jellyfish-like footage released by Jeremy Corbell, a UFO filmmaker. If true, it would mean these objects move under their own control.
teotihuacan-as-a-gold-and-silver-ore-pro: A researcher named Geoffrey Drumm, who says an alien showed him the true purpose of the pyramids, told a podcast host, Jesse Michels, in 2026 that Teotihuacan, an ancient city in Mexico known for its great pyramids, was a plant for processing gold and silver ore. terence-mckenna-s-overdosing-girlfriend-: Writer Jason Jorjani tells Jesse Michels a story about Terence McKenna, a well known speaker on psychedelic drugs. terence-mckenna-staying-with-the-sheldra: The biologist Rupert Sheldrake tells podcast host Jesse Michels that the writer Terence McKenna was one of his very good friends. He says that whenever McKenna was in London, he stayed with the Sheldrake family at their home. He shares it to show how close he was to McKenna and his ideas.
tero-s-remark-to-merlin-sheldrake-on-mus: Tero Isokauppila, a mushroom specialist, tells podcast host Jesse Michels about a remark he says he made around 2020 to Merlin Sheldrake, a researcher of fungi. If he is right, these special foods would have a particular role at the turning points of nature.
terra-exploration-group-survey-finds-tun: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that underground surveys by a company called Terra Exploration Group, using magnetic sensing, showed a straight man-made tunnel about 50 feet wide in Arizona. terraforming-the-sahara-with-thunderstor: A researcher named Geoffrey Drumm told a podcast host, Jesse Michels, in 2026 that during the African Humid Period, a time roughly 14,000 to 5300 BC when the Sahara was green and wet, ancient builders in the upper eastern Sahara used fertilisers together with machines that made big thunderstorm clouds to reshape the land. terry-and-linda-jamison-one-person-split: A philosopher named Jason Jorjani tells podcast host Jesse Michels about Terry and Linda Jamison, identical twin sisters who are also psychics. terry-lovelace-and-partner-toby-never-re: Mario Woods, a former guard at a nuclear site who says he was abducted, tells Jesse Michels about a man named Terry Lovelace and his friend Toby. terry-lovelace-hears-a-being-s-voice-tel: A guest named Mike Masters, on a podcast with host Jesse Michels, recalls a man named Terry Lovelace describing his meeting with a non-human being he called Betty Rubble. terry-lovelace-s-dr-bug-abduction-told-a: John Blitch, introduced on a podcast as a scientist from DARPA, the US military's advanced research agency, tells the podcast host Jesse Michels about a talk he heard at a conference in 2018. terry-lovelace-s-phone-health-data-shows: John Blitch, a scientist and podcast guest, tells about the health data on Terry Lovelace's mobile phone, Lovelace being a man who says he was abducted by non-human beings. tesla-and-marconi-claimed-alien-communic: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Nikola Tesla and Guglielmo Marconi, two famous early inventors who worked on electricity and radio, both claimed to have picked up communication from aliens. tesla-and-thomas-townsend-brown-discover: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says he thinks the inventor Nikola Tesla and a later researcher named Thomas Townsend Brown both discovered the same thing. tesla-and-townsend-brown-collaboration-l: This story is about two inventors, Nikola Tesla, a famous electrical pioneer, and Townsend Brown, a researcher, and the claim that they secretly worked together sometime between the 1920s and 1940s. tesla-at-wardenclyffe-tapping-the-ether-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that the inventor Nikola Tesla used high voltages across short distances in the early 1900s at Wardenclyffe, his work site in New York. tesla-causes-an-earthquake-in-manhattan-: A researcher and writer, Jason Jorjani, told a podcast host, Jesse Michels, in 2025 that the inventor Nikola Tesla described using what Jorjani calls earthquake weaponry in his laboratory in the 1890s, and that he caused an earthquake in Manhattan, New York. tesla-killed-in-1943: Steven Greer, a doctor who campaigns for governments to reveal what they know about UFOs, says on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels that the inventor Nikola Tesla was killed in 1943. tesla-offers-his-work-to-soviet-and-germ: A former US Senate staffer, Kurt McConnell, told a podcast host, Jesse Michels, in 2025 that there are stories of the inventor Nikola Tesla offering his work and ideas to Russian or Soviet contacts and to the Germans. tesla-reportedly-flew-scalar-powered-veh: A guest named Steve says that, as rumor has it, the inventor Nikola Tesla actually flew craft powered by scalar energy, a proposed exotic form of power. tesla-s-alien-contact-at-colorado-spring: The inventor Nikola Tesla said that in Colorado Springs, around 1899, he communicated with beings from beyond Earth. tesla-s-wireless-power-and-claimed-over-: A former US Senate staffer, Kurt McConnell, told a podcast host, Jesse Michels, in 2025 that, alongside his work on sending electricity without wires, the inventor Nikola Tesla believed, according to some accounts, that he had reached over-unity, meaning a machine that gives out more energy than is put in. tesla-s-work-on-electron-movement-and-tr: Harald Malmgren, a former advisor to US presidents, says on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels that the inventor Nikola Tesla was working on how moving electrons could let you rearrange almost anything. tesla-s-world-wireless-drawings-show-win: Jason Jorjani, a researcher and writer, says that the drawings the inventor Nikola Tesla made for his "World Wireless" system, Tesla's plan to send power and messages through the air without wires, are "full of UFOs". tesla-seeing-the-future-in-high-voltage-: Jesse Michels, a podcast host, passes on something he says comes from a biographer of the inventor Nikola Tesla. tesla-travels-to-europe-to-persuade-hert: A former US Senate staffer, Kurt McConnell, told a podcast host, Jesse Michels, in 2025 that, from what he has read, the inventor Nikola Tesla travelled to Europe, sometime around the late 1880s or 1890s, to convince the German physicist Heinrich Hertz that Hertz was wrong about how electrical waves work. tessa-dick-says-philip-k-dick-believed-t: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says his friend Rizwan Virk, an author of books on the idea that our world is a kind of computer simulation, is friends with Tessa Dick, the wife of the science fiction writer Philip K. test-flight-of-the-sport-model-with-a-vh: Bob Lazar is a man who says he worked on alien flying craft in 1988 and 1989 at S-4, a secret site in the Nevada desert. testimony-to-ross-coulthart-in-washingto: A man named Jordan, who says he was taken into a secret UFO programme as a child, tells podcast host Jesse Michels that in 2024 he got in touch with a journalist named Ross Coulthart. tethys-sea-seabed-and-hydrothermal-vents: A researcher, Geoffrey Drumm (also listed as Jeffrey), says on Jesse Michels's podcast in 2026 that the Giza Plateau, the high ground in Egypt where the great pyramids stand, was once the bottom of an ancient ocean from millions of years ago called the Tethys Sea. texas-death-row-convictions-partly-based: Jesse Michels, a podcast host, passes on what his guest John Blitch, a scientist, told him: that two men are on death row in Texas right now whose convictions rested partly on hypnotic regression. texas-instruments-worker-given-unknown-m: A commentator who goes by UAPGerb, who talks online about UAP, the official term for UFOs, points to an anonymous whistleblower who appeared on a popular online video channel called The Infographics Show. thane-heins-coil-reverses-generator-drag: Gary McKinnon, a British computer hacker, tells podcast host Jesse Michels that he repeated a test based on the work of an inventor in Canada named Thane Heins. the-1943-philadelphia-experiment: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, retells a legend that in 1943 the US Navy tried to teleport a ship in Philadelphia, in what is now called the Philadelphia Experiment. the-1952-hottel-memo-on-a-crashed-ufo-wi: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, talks about the Hottel memo, a note to an official of the FBI, the US federal police agency, named Guy Hottel. the-1958-western-trackdown-and-a-wall-bu: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, speaking with a guest about the idea that the mind can glimpse the future, brings up Trackdown, a Western on American television in 1958. the-1995-96-official-statement-that-the-: In the United States there was a government program on remote viewing, the claimed ability to describe faraway places or hidden things using only the mind. the-2020-scan-detects-the-queen-s-chambe: Jeffrey Drum, a researcher, discusses a 2020 study that used a kind of satellite radar imaging to look inside the Great Pyramid of Giza in Egypt. the-2020-scan-misses-the-king-s-chamber: Jeffrey Drum, a researcher, looks at a 2020 study that used a kind of satellite radar imaging to see inside the Great Pyramid of Giza in Egypt. the-angel-of-the-lord-in-the-assyrian-ca: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, in an episode about Air Force veterans who say they were taken by aliens, recalls a story from the Bible. the-angels-who-visited-abraham-and-lot-i: In the Bible, angels visit the patriarch Abraham and then his nephew Lot in the city of Sodom. the-association-of-24-retired-officials-: Dan Sheehan, a guest on a podcast, passes on what a man named Michael Phillip told him: that an "insurgency" has formed, a group of about 24 retired officials who once held very high positions in the US Defense Department, the CIA (America's foreign intelligence agency) and big aerospace companies. the-astronaut-photo-behind-elizabeth: Clas Svahn, a researcher who keeps a large archive of UFO material, talks on podcast host Jesse Michels's show about a very famous photograph taken on a moor in England. the-audrey-phone-messages-2000: Grant Cameron, a long-time researcher of UFO claims, says that over the 2000s and 2010s more than 80 phone calls came from a mysterious caller known as "Audrey" to all sorts of people in the United States. the-aviary-and-bill-moore-s-mufon-speech: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, describes the Aviary as a long-rumoured group in the 1980s whose members, all given bird code names, were said to spread false information about UFOs. the-being-was-nearly-taken-to-the-zoo-be: Italo Venturelli, a surgeon connected to a hospital in Varginha, a town in Brazil, talks about the story that a strange living being was captured there in 1996 after a craft came down. the-bell-levitated-and-had-to-be-chained: Jason Jorjani, a researcher speaking on podcast host Jesse Michels's show about what he calls Hitler's secret UFO program, describes a device known as the Bell that he places in the 1940s. the-bell-s-alternate-name-the-beehive-19: Jason Jorjani, a researcher speaking on podcast host Jesse Michels's show about what he calls Hitler's secret UFO program, discusses a 1940s device known as the Bell, which he ties to the Skoda Works, a large industrial and arms works. the-big-void-as-a-heat-exchanger-for-rea: Inside the Great Pyramid at Giza in Egypt there is a large empty space called the Big Void, sitting above the Grand Gallery, a tall sloping corridor. the-black-mailbox-began-as-a-vague-landm: Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked on alien craft at a secret Nevada site around 1989, tells podcast host Jesse Michels how a desert spot became famous. the-blue-book-briefing-folders-of-160-re: Joe McMoneagle says he worked in a US military programme on "remote viewing", the idea that a person can describe a distant place or target using only the mind. the-boat-pits-as-acid-filled-circuit-bre: Geoffrey Drumm, who studies the pyramids of Egypt, tells podcast host Jesse Michels that the boat pits, long trenches cut into the rock beside the Great Pyramid at Giza, contain more sulfate compounds, chemicals linked to acid. the-breathing-hole-on-the-object-2012: Dennis Asberg, a treasure hunter, helped find a strange object on the floor of the Baltic Sea between Sweden and Finland. the-bubble-energy-field-mapped-over-the-: The owner of Skinwalker Ranch, a property in Utah known for strange events, tells podcast host Jesse Michels that there is a kind of bubble of energy over the land. the-business-plot-against-fdr-1930: A podcast guest who goes by the name JASON tells Jesse Michels about the so-called Business Plot of the 1930s. the-cia-as-the-brainchild-of-brown-broth: Dan Sheehan, a researcher speaking on podcast host Jesse Michels's show, says that the CIA, the US Central Intelligence Agency set up after the Second World War, was the brainchild of people at Brown Brothers Harriman, a private banking firm. the-cia-convenes-the-robertson-panel-195: Bryce Zabel, a writer and researcher speaking on podcast host Jesse Michels's show about Hollywood, the CIA and UFOs, points to 1953 as a turning point. the-cia-showed-elizondo-mris-of-uap-witn: Lue Elizondo is a former Pentagon official who says he worked in a programme that studied UFOs. the-city-of-london-s-remembrancer-sits-i: Jay Anderson, a researcher and podcaster, says the City of London, the old financial district with its own separate government, has an official called the Remembrancer. the-collins-elite-as-a-fundamentalist-fa: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, describes something called the Collins Elite, which he says, drawing on Lou Elizondo and a private UFO group called To The Stars Academy, is a faction of deeply fundamentalist Christians embedded in the US government. the-dirt-road-leads-straight-to-the-army: In 1996, people in the Brazilian town of Varginha say a strange creature, an alien being, was seen and taken away. the-dogon-s-knowledge-of-the-sirius-bina: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, citing Robert Temple's book The Sirius Mystery, says the Dogon people of Mali somehow knew, through their own traditions, that Sirius, a bright point in the night sky, is really two bodies, which he calls Sirius A and Sirius B. the-drones-were-orbs-from-the-sea-now-ov: Chris Bledsoe, a man who says he attracts UFOs, tells podcast host Jesse Michels about the so-called drones that people reported seeing in the skies over the United States in 2024 and later over Europe. the-electromagnetic-black-project-at-the: Dan Sherman, a former sergeant who says the National Security Agency, the US spy agency for communications, hired him to speak with aliens, tells podcast host Jesse Michels about a black project, meaning a secret programme hidden from public view. the-endless-frontier-read-as-working-bac: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, points to Science, The Endless Frontier, a 1945 report by Vannevar Bush, the scientist who led American war research, which set out how the US government should fund science after the war. the-et-s-account-galactic-monitors-of-li: Danny Sheehan, a lawyer active in UFO disclosure circles, told podcast host Jesse Michels about records of an interview with an extraterrestrial, written on index cards and tied to a man named Oscar Wolf, connected to S4, a reported secret site near Area 51, the classified Air Force base in Nevada. the-face-peeler-legend-of-the-peruvian-a: Tim Alberino, a filmmaker and researcher speaking on podcast host Jesse Michels's show, talks about a local legend in the Peruvian Amazon about a so-called face peeler. the-fake-l9-incident-document-1977: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells of a document about something called the L9 incident at Ellsworth Air Force Base in South Dakota, dated a day before an experience he says two men, Michael and Mario, had there in 1977. the-family-the-fellowship-network-in-gov: A researcher, Jason Simosa, speaking on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, describes a quiet network in Washington, DC known as The Family, or The Fellowship. the-fenced-vacant-lot-where-the-beings-a: In 1996, people in the Brazilian town of Varginha say strange beings, thought to be aliens, were seen in town. the-flying-house-of-loreto-1800: A researcher, Diana Pasulka, tells the old story of the Flying House of Loreto, from the town of Loreto in Italy. the-g-engines-are-coming-article-arrives: This is about an old magazine article from 1956 titled "The G Engines Are Coming", meaning engines that would work by controlling gravity. the-gadarene-demoniac-and-the-appointed-: On the show of a podcast host, Jesse Michels, a researcher named Tim Alberino retells an old story from the New Testament gospels, the accounts of Jesus' life in the Christian Bible. the-golden-age-of-general-relativity-bah: A researcher, Eric Weinstein, talks about what he calls the golden age of general relativity, a burst of work on Einstein's theory of gravity in the United States in the 1950s and 60s. the-gran-sasso-laboratory-and-the-gerda-: A researcher named Filippo Biondi, speaking with podcast host Jesse Michels, talks about a science laboratory under the Gran Sasso mountains in Italy. the-great-year-documentary-proposes-a-bi: This story is about a documentary film called The Great Year. It deals with a long, slow cycle in the sky known by that name. the-holy-grail-as-a-technology-of-regene: Randall Carlson, a researcher into ancient history and lost knowledge, told podcast host Jesse Michels that the Holy Grail of medieval European legend, described in tales by writers such as Chrétien de Troyes, Robert de Boron and Wolfram von Eschenbach in his poem Parzival, was not just a cup or a symbol. the-host-s-own-rectangular-craft-sightin: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, mentions in passing during an interview that he has seen a rectangular flying craft himself. He gives no time, place or details. If true, it would mean the host is a witness himself, not only an interviewer.
the-hosts-saw-a-green-orb-with-elizondo-: Jesse Michels, a podcast host, says that a couple of years before 2024 he and his team were at the Wyoming home of Lue Elizondo, a former Pentagon official who ran a small office studying unexplained aerial reports and wrote a book called Imminent. the-hughes-group-s-cia-covert-actions-th: A researcher, Matthew Pines, says that a group around the businessman Howard Hughes did covert work for the CIA, the US spy agency, in the 1960s and 70s, including the project involving a ship called the Glomar Explorer. He adds that this same group may even have carried out killings, which the story links to the Kennedy assassinations. If true, it would mean a private group close to these secrets was also doing the government's darkest work.
the-jailer-s-file-submariners-on-lsd-200: Gary McKinnon, a computer hacker who says he got into US military and space agency computers around 2000 to 2002, says that on one military site he found what he calls the jailer's file. He explains that every military base has a jailer, and says the file showed men who worked on submarines taking LSD, a powerful hallucinogenic drug. He tells it as an example of the strange things he says he saw inside those systems.
the-jasons-solve-dod-problems-in-summer-: A scientist who has worked for the Pentagon, Eric Davis, describes a group called the JASONs, a panel of scientists who advise the US Department of Defense. According to Davis, they meet in summer studies and are supposed to solve problems the Defense Department hands them, which would mean outside experts are quietly brought in on hard military questions.
the-kandahar-giant-seen-on-a-cargo-palle: Tim Alberino, a filmmaker and researcher, says an unnamed cargo pilot told him that during the war in Afghanistan in the 2000s he saw the body of a giant on a cargo pallet. According to the pilot, the first thing that hit him was a smell of body odor and death, and the being had red hair, pale skin, and six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot. In another version Alberino credits the author Steve Quayle and a source called True Legends and puts the loading at Bagram Airfield in 2005; if true, it would mean the US military recovered an actual giant.
the-kgb-gives-the-tsar-s-box-seat-to-mal: Harald Malmgren, a former adviser to US presidents, tells podcast host Jesse Michels about a night in Moscow around 1982. He says that at an event there, men from the KGB, the Soviet secret police, told former US secretary of state Henry Kissinger that the old Tsar's box seat was not for him that night but for "Dr. Mal." He tells it to show how much standing he says he had with the Soviets.
the-king-s-chamber-as-an-acoustic-cataly: Geoffrey Drumm, a researcher speaking on podcast host Jesse Michels's show, says that the King's Chamber and the small room before it inside the Great Pyramid in Egypt were acoustic catalyst chambers, rooms that used sound to speed up a chemical reaction. According to him, they turned sulfur dioxide and oxygen into sulfur trioxide to make sulfuric acid. If true, the pyramid would have been a chemical plant rather than a tomb.
the-king-s-chamber-shafts-end-horizontal: Inside the Great Pyramid at Giza in Egypt, a room called the King's Chamber has narrow shafts running out from it through the stone. A researcher named Geoffrey Drumm tells podcast host Jesse Michels that the original archaeological records show these shafts turn flat, running level, at their far ends. He brings it up as a clue in his own idea about what the pyramid was really built to do.
the-lacerta-files-swedish-documents-abou: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, talking with a video maker named Chris Ramsay, praises a piece Ramsay made on the Lacerta files. Michels describes them as documents from Sweden about reptilians, meaning lizard-like beings said to live among or beneath humans. He mentions them as one of the stranger corners of the subject that Ramsay has explored.
the-lone-stars-group-after-aawsap-2010: A researcher called Jason says that after AAWSAP, a Pentagon-funded programme that studied unexplained phenomena, came to an end around 2010, some of the people involved kept going on their own. He says they formed an informal group called the Lone Stars, and he names the researchers Jacques Vallee, Eric Davis and Hal Puthoff. If so, the study of these mysteries carried on quietly after the official money stopped.
the-luxor-temple-back-chamber-reserved-f: Luke Caverns, a researcher of ancient sites, talks on a podcast about Luxor Temple, a large ancient temple in Egypt. He says that a huge chamber at the back was, as far as anyone knows, reserved only for the pharaoh Amenhotep, an ancient Egyptian king, to connect with his divine father, the god Amun-Ra. For Caverns it suggests the temple was built as a place of contact with the gods.
the-man-in-the-red-plaid-shirt-was-a-man: John Blitch, introduced as a scientist from the Pentagon's advanced research agency, says that in 1995 at Daniels Park in Colorado he had what he remembered as a strange bug dream and a separate mountain biking episode involving a man in a red plaid shirt. He says that later, under hypnotic regression, a hypnosis technique meant to bring back buried memories, done with a man named Leo Sprinkle and dated in one telling to 2018, he realized the two were one event and the man was really a mantis-like being in a red uniform. If true, it would mean he was taken by a non-human creature.
the-man-in-the-shroud-of-turin-was-alive: Randall Carlson, a researcher into ancient history, told podcast host Jesse Michels his view of the Shroud of Turin, a linen cloth kept in Turin, Italy, that bears the image of a man and is said to be the burial cloth of Jesus. Drawing on the cloth and the Gospels, Carlson says, "The man in the shroud was living." If true, it would change the story of what happened in the tomb.
the-microbiologist-leak-experts-judge-th: Around 2023, an anonymous person who said they were a microbiologist, a scientist who studies tiny living things like bacteria, posted claims online about non-human intelligence. A man named Chris Ramsay tells podcast host Jesse Michels that people who looked closely at the writing think the author really does have doctorate-level knowledge of microbiology. That would make the leak harder to wave off as the work of an amateur.
the-military-police-commander-s-witch-hu: A doctor named Ahmed Foratu, speaking about events in Varginha, Brazil, in 1996, when people say a strange creature was captured and a soldier who handled it fell ill and died, criticizes the commander of the local military police barracks. He says that a medical complication there deserved investigation, but that the commander pursued a fellow doctor who worked at the barracks with what he calls a witch hunt. According to Foratu, that doctor spent years having to explain himself to the courts, which he presents as a sign of how hard the authorities pressed anyone close to the case.
the-monte-carlo-group-at-the-top-of-the-: Danny Sheehan, a lawyer, tells podcast host Jesse Michels about what he calls the Monte Carlo group. He says it sits at the very top of the Knights of Malta, an old Catholic religious order, and names former US secretary of state Henry Kissinger and former president George Bush Senior in connection with it. If true, it would mean a small, hidden circle of powerful men sits above that order.
the-moon-as-a-logical-refuge-for-a-space: A researcher, Randall Carlson, says that if a civilization able to travel in space faced a catastrophe on Earth, the Moon would be the obvious place to take refuge. He comes back to this several times on Jesse Michels's podcast, linking it to the Younger Dryas, a time of sudden cold about 12,000 years ago that he ties to a comet, and he notes that NASA, the US space agency, has floated similar ideas for people today. If true, it would mean the Moon might hold traces of an earlier civilization that fled there.
the-moon-as-an-anomalous-alien-spacecraf: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, recalls an interview, recorded around 2023 near Decatur outside Atlanta and never released, with a researcher named Randall Carlson. Michels says much of that talk was about the idea that the Moon may be an anomalous alien spacecraft rather than a natural body. If true, it would mean something built has been hanging in our sky all along.
the-moon-rang-like-a-bell-during-the-apo: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that during the Apollo missions to the Moon in 1969, when Apollo 10 left the Moon, the Moon "rang like a bell," and NASA, the US space agency, was baffled. A researcher, Randall Carlson, says NASA collected three or four years of data from instruments on the Moon showing it kept vibrating for a long time. A philosopher, Jason Jorjani, says the test was then repeated on purpose, he thinks on Apollo 13, and Michels later says seismometers (quake-measuring instruments) were set up and a rocket stage was crashed into the Moon deliberately, crediting a scientist named Gordon MacDonald. Those who tell it take it as a sign the Moon may be hollow, or even something built, as one episode puts it, an alien spaceship.
the-moon-s-low-density-old-material-and-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says the Moon is strange: it is far less dense than the Earth, and its material is older than the Earth, even though it is supposed to have formed from the Earth after a huge collision. His guest, a researcher named Randall Carlson, makes a related argument, saying it is extremely hard to get from a ring of debris around the Earth to the Moon we see today. Carlson also doubts the other idea, that the Earth simply captured the Moon. Both tell it on an episode asking whether the Moon could be something other than natural, which is what it would mean if neither explanation works.
the-moon-was-placed-or-towed-into-positi: A man named Chris Bledsoe, speaking with podcast host Jesse Michels, wonders aloud whether the Moon is quite what it seems. He says a man named Timothy Taylor hinted that the Moon did not end up where it is by accident, but was put there on purpose, which would mean someone placed it.
the-nine-as-a-psychological-warfare-expe: A researcher, Greg Malatzi, talks about The Nine, a group of beings that people in 1950s Maine said they contacted through a group called the Round Table Foundation. Drawing on the writer Peter Levenda, he says one idea is that this was a side operation, an early psychological warfare experiment. If so, the contact story would have been a test of how people could be influenced rather than a message from beyond.
the-nine-identified-as-a-ufo-in-low-eart: A writer, Peter Levenda, says that The Nine, a group of beings first contacted through seances in the 1950s, were later described as living on a UFO in low Earth orbit. He says this was the same craft later contacted by Uri Geller, a performer known for claimed psychic powers, with the researcher Andrija Puharich linking the two. If true, it would tie decades of contact claims to a single source in the sky.
the-nine-instruct-building-a-copper-fara: A researcher named Greg Malatzi says that in the 1950s a research group in Maine, the Round Table Foundation, made tape recordings of messages from a council of beings called the Nine, received through a psychic. According to Malatzi, the Nine told them that for a clearer transmission they had to put the psychic inside a copper Faraday cage, a metal enclosure that blocks electrical signals, which, if true, would mean the beings were giving practical instructions for talking with them.
the-nine-s-message-surveillance-of-earth: A researcher named Greg Malatzi, speaking on a podcast, describes messages from "The Nine", a group said to be a council of non-human beings who spoke through people in recorded sessions held from the 1950s at the Round Table Foundation, a small research group in Maine. According to Malatzi, The Nine said they had been watching Earth and seeing the bad things happening here, especially wars and nuclear weapons. He draws on the transcripts of those sessions, and the story matters to those who tell it because it would mean someone out there is monitoring humanity's capacity to destroy itself.
the-nine-say-they-are-behind-nuclear-bas: On a podcast, an unnamed researcher describes messages said to come from "The Nine", a supposed council of non-human beings contacted through recorded sessions in the 1970s. According to this researcher, The Nine claimed that they were behind many of the sightings of strange objects reported at nuclear weapons bases. If true, it would tie those sightings to a single group with a purpose.
the-nine-seance-in-maine-new-year-s-eve-: A writer, Peter Levenda, says that a seance, a gathering meant to contact unseen beings, was held in Maine around New Year's Eve of 1952 to 1953, with nine people taking part, among them Andrija Puharich, Arthur Young and Ruth Forbes Paine Young. The podcast host Jesse Michels repeats the story, citing Levenda, and adds that the nine were members of the elite. It matters to tellers because this is said to be where contact with a group called The Nine began.
the-nine-send-puharich-and-schlemmer-to-: An unnamed researcher on a podcast says that in the mid-1970s Andrija Puharich, a scientist described in the episode as tied to the CIA, and his collaborator Phyllis Schlemmer, along with a man named John Whitmore, received messages from "The Nine", a supposed council of non-human beings. According to the researcher, the session tapes show The Nine telling them they needed to travel to Egypt, the Middle East and Russia. Those who tell it see it as a sign that the messages were steering real people on real missions.
the-non-terrestrial-officers-spreadsheet: Gary McKinnon, a computer hacker who worked from London, says that around 2000 to 2002 he got into a US Navy computer system and found a spreadsheet titled "non-terrestrial officers". He says it also listed transfers of unusual chemicals such as molybdenum, along with transfers between ships and between whole fleets.
