travis-walton-abduction-as-shown-in-fire: In 1975, in Arizona, a young forestry worker named Travis Walton says he was taken aboard a UFO, and his story was later made into a Hollywood film called Fire in the Sky. A guest on a podcast, Chris Ramsay, says the film played the events very differently from Walton's own account. In the film, he says, the beings doing a procedure on Walton ignored his screams. A second person, Bryce, passes on what he heard from Tracy Tormé, who was involved with the film. According to Bryce, the filmmakers told Tormé that Walton's real story was not good enough and that they needed a better abduction. Both tellers are relaying others, and together they suggest the frightening film version was Hollywood's invention, not what Walton describes.
travis-walton-abduction-two-weeks-after-: A researcher named Bryce, on Jesse Michels's podcast about Hollywood and UFOs, points to timing in 1975. He says that NBC aired The UFO Incident, a TV film starring James Earl Jones based on The Interrupted Journey, a book about a couple who said they were abducted, and that two weeks later a man named Travis Walton said he was abducted himself. Bryce raises it to suggest a link between what appears on screen and what people then report.
travis-walton-case-dismissed-as-fabricat: A well-known skeptic, Michael Shermer, debating podcast host Jesse Michels, gives his view of Travis Walton, a man who says he was abducted by a UFO in 1975. Shermer suggests Walton made it up because he was late getting a job done, and says Walton did not pass a lie detector test, adding that he was once on a show with him.
travis-walton-case-fire-tower-debunk-dis: In 1975 in Arizona, a man named Travis Walton became the centre of a well-known story about an encounter with something unexplained, and some people have tried to explain it away by pointing to a nearby fire tower, a lookout used to spot forest fires. A researcher named Greg Bishop, speaking with podcast host Jesse Michels, says that this explanation gets the place wrong: it claims the tower was right next to the road, but he says it is actually over a hill. If he is right, that ordinary explanation of the case would be weaker.
travis-walton-handed-over-from-greys-to-: A philosopher named Jason Jorjani, on a podcast, retells the story of Travis Walton, a man who says he was taken aboard a strange craft in Arizona in 1975. Jorjani says Walton was first with greys, the small grey beings common in such accounts, then wandered down a hallway, ran into tall human-looking beings often called Nordics, and was handled by them from then on. In Walton's own words, played on the same show, he simply says a human-looking man came in while he was looking for a way out, with no mention of a handover; the story matters to those who tell it because it would suggest different kinds of beings working together.
travis-walton-is-struck-by-a-craft-s-ene: Joe Rogan, a comedian and podcast host, appearing on Jesse Michels' show, spoke about Travis Walton, a man who says he was taken aboard a UFO in Arizona in 1975. Rogan says the beings did not pick Walton: he ran up to the craft and got blasted by it. If true, it would mean Walton's encounter was an accident, not a planned abduction.
travis-walton-wakes-with-a-full-beard-19: A researcher, Mike Masters, who argues that aliens may be humans from the future, tells podcast host Jesse Michels about Travis Walton, a man who says he was abducted by a UFO in Arizona in 1975. Masters says Walton had shaved right before the experience but woke up afterwards with a full beard. If true, it would suggest far more time passed for Walton than for the world around him.
travis-walton-was-dead-and-revived-1975: A man named Steve Coburn, speaking on podcast host Jesse Michels's show, passes on the view of a doctor named Roger Leer about Travis Walton, the man at the center of a 1975 encounter case in Arizona. According to Coburn, Leer thinks Walton actually died and was brought back to life by whoever had him. If true, it would make Walton's experience far more extreme than a simple sighting.
treat-team-under-albert-stubblebine-per-: An online researcher who goes by UAPGerb said on Jesse Michels's podcast that a 1990s email between Hans-Adam II, the prince of Liechtenstein, and Steven Greer, a campaigner for UFO disclosure, mentions a team called TREAT. According to that email, the team sat under Albert Stubblebine, who ran INSCOM, the US Army's intelligence and security command. The telling never spells out what TREAT did, but it points to a hidden UFO-related group working inside Army intelligence.
tree-in-the-backyard-bursts-into-flame: Chris Bledsoe, a North Carolina man who says strange things happen around him, says that after a trip to Zanesville a tree in his backyard just burst into flames by itself. He adds that it had rained for two days before. He tells it on Jesse Michels's podcast as one of the odd events in his life that he can't explain.
trees-knocked-flat-to-the-northeast-1948: A researcher named Scott Ramsay told podcast host Jesse Michels about Hart Canyon near Aztec, New Mexico, where a craft is said to have crashed in 1948. Ramsay says a man named Bill Steinman showed him trees at the site and explained that the craft was dragged over soft trees up to a "dragon wagon," a big heavy hauling vehicle, and that the trees all lay flattened toward the northeast. If true, the trees would be physical marks left by the recovery of a crashed craft.
tres-coracoes-army-battalion-supports-th: Aldo Rebelo, a former Brazilian Defense Minister speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast, says that in 1996 an army unit based in Três Corações, a town near Varginha in Brazil, sent at least part of its troops to support an operation there. trevor-grassi-s-corridor-of-rooms-leadin: A scientist named Filippo Biondi, who has scanned beneath the pyramids of Egypt, told podcast host Jesse Michels about work by a man named Trevor Grassi on the Giza Plateau. trevor-paglen-s-book-on-black-project-pa: A former Pentagon official turned whistleblower, Matthew Brown, mentions to podcast host Jesse Michels a book by Trevor Paglen. triangle-and-gravity-control-patents-tha: A guest named Dylan Borland told podcast host Jesse Michels that if you look through patents for triangle-shaped craft and for gravity control, using Google Patents, a public search site for patents, the trail of power sources and gravity work leads back to the US Air Force and NASA, the US space agency, in the 1950s. triangle-appears-above-russian-naval-ves: A man described as a Pentagon whistleblower, Matthew Brown, says that around 2018 a US surveillance asset in the Pacific off Kamchatka, in far eastern Russia, was watching Russian navy ships when a large black triangle appeared above them, and that this is in a briefing for what he calls Immaculate Constellation, a secret government UFO program. triangle-of-orbs-follow-him-home-and-app: Bob McGwier, an engineer who says he did contract work for the CIA, the US spy agency, says a triangle of glowing balls of light followed him home to Blacksburg, Virginia, and showed up in his yard. triangle-with-a-round-hole-caught-on-fil: Dennis Asberg, a Swedish treasure hunter, says that from 2011 onward his team filmed a strange object on the floor of the Baltic Sea, between Sweden and Finland. triangles-seen-on-launch-pads-at-groom-l: A researcher who goes by the name UAPGerb, speaking with a podcast host named Jesse Michels, says he knows many people who have seen triangle-shaped craft sitting on launch pads at Groom Lake, a secret test site in Nevada often called Area 51. triangles-stored-on-doe-land-across-the-: An online UFO researcher who goes by UAPGerb tells podcast host Jesse Michels that triangle-shaped craft are stored on land owned by the Department of Energy, the US agency that runs nuclear and weapons labs. tridactyl-beings-of-peru-from-the-nazca-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, talks about "tridactyl beings", meaning three-fingered bodies, from Peru, which he says date from the Nazca period, an ancient era in a region full of cave art. trinity-and-roswell-crashes-1940: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, speaks of 'known crashes' of UFOs at Trinity, the New Mexico site where the first atomic bomb was tested, and at Roswell, a New Mexico town linked to a famous 1947 crash story. trinity-flash-explained-away-as-an-ammo-: In 1945 the United States set off the world's first atomic bomb at a desert test site in New Mexico called Trinity. trinity-plutonium-fallout-plume-over-ros: A scientist, Dr. John Brandenburg, speaking on Jesse Michels' podcast, says he was told that after the 1945 Trinity test, the first atomic bomb explosion, in the New Mexico desert, a cloud full of unburned plutonium drifted over the town of Roswell. trinity-test-warning-1945: A former US Secretary of Energy, John Herrington, speaking on Jesse Michels' podcast, recalls what he says Robert Oppenheimer, the scientist who led the building of the first atomic bomb, told people before the 1945 Trinity test in the New Mexico desert. trip-to-russia-to-save-kgb-files: Clas Svahn, a researcher who collects UFO records, says he once travelled to Russia to try to save files of the KGB, the Soviet Union's spy and security agency. He tells it as an effort to keep those records, which may hold UFO reports, from being lost.
trojan-war-the-bronze-age-collapse-and-t: A researcher named Luke Caverns, talking with podcast host Jesse Michels, offers a view of ancient Greek history. trucker-s-ufo-sighting-and-missing-time-: A former truck driver who gives only his first name, Michael, says that sometime after 1977 he saw an unidentified flying object while driving on the I-20 highway near El Paso, Texas, and then lost track of time. truman-interview-ufos-discussed-at-every: Harry Truman, the US president, is heard in an interview played on Jesse Michels's podcast saying that UFOs came up at every conference he had with the military. truman-meeting-and-the-secret-anderson-t: A researcher, Dan Sheehan, tells podcast host Jesse Michels that in 1945 President Harry Truman met with a circle of senior officials and generals, naming figures such as Douglas MacArthur, Henry Stimson and John J. McCloy. He says they agreed to set up a secret fund called the Anderson Trust, based in Houston, Texas. trump-administration-attributes-new-jers: A Senate staffer named Kurt McConnell, speaking as a guest on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, talks about mysterious drone sightings over New Jersey around 2024 and 2025. trump-briefed-on-legacy-uap-programs-201: A researcher named Matthew Pines says he believes Donald Trump has been briefed on parts of "legacy programs," meaning long-running secret efforts said to deal with unexplained craft, and that Trump knows at least the broad outline that the subject is real. trump-briefed-on-nordic-aliens: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, asks on his show whether Donald Trump, the US president, was once briefed about 'Nordics', aliens said to look like tall, fair-haired humans. trump-cancels-bedminster-trip-over-drone: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in December 2024 Donald Trump, then about to become president again, had to skip a trip to his summer home in Bedminster, New Jersey. trump-executive-order-making-nasa-an-int: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in 2025 Donald Trump, the US president, described NASA, the US space agency, as something like an intelligence agency. trump-hints-at-knowledge-about-roswell-1: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, repeats something he says Donald Trump said about Roswell, New Mexico, the town linked to a reported crash of a strange object in 1947. trump-on-rogan-links-jfk-records-to-peop: A researcher named Matthew Pines describes a 2024 moment on The Joe Rogan Experience, a popular podcast hosted by Joe Rogan, when Donald Trump was a guest. trump-on-the-new-jersey-drones-2024: In 2024, during a wave of reports of mysterious drones flying over New Jersey, Donald Trump said the military knows where they took off from, and that if it was a garage, they could go right into that garage. trump-pilots-say-spheres-outfly-f-22s: A guest named Merrick, on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, quotes Donald Trump as saying that Air Force pilots, including one he called a very good guy, better than Tom Cruise, told him they had seen spherical, circular objects outfly the F-22, a top US Air Force fighter jet. trump-says-aliens-are-classified-materia: A researcher named Grant Cameron, speaking with podcast host Jesse Michels, describes a 2026 moment involving Donald Trump, the US president. trump-says-the-ufo-issue-is-being-looked: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in 2026, after a strange public back-and-forth with former president Barack Obama, US president Donald Trump said his government was 'looking into the UFO issue'. trump-told-of-hybrids-living-among-us-du: A congressman, Eric Burlison, tells a podcast host, Jesse Michels, that during a briefing Donald Trump was told there are hybrids, part human and part something else, that may be living among us. trusted-colleagues-report-firsthand-enco: A helicopter pilot named Jake Barber, who says he once carried a UFO with his helicopter, tells podcast host Jesse Michels that the most trusted people he has worked with speak of having firsthand encounters with beings. trw-and-skunk-works-crates-in-close-enco: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, points out that in Close Encounters of the Third Kind, Steven Spielberg's 1977 film about humans meeting aliens, some crates are marked TRW and Skunk Works. tsiolkovsky-in-touch-with-angelic-beings: Konstantin Tsiolkovsky was a Russian thinker often called the father of Russian rocketry, and podcast host Jesse Michels says he believed he was in touch with angelic beings and wrote about it, at first crediting the religion scholar Diana Pasulka. tuatha-de-danann-weather-control-magic: Geoffrey Drumm, a man who talks about the purpose of ancient monuments, tells podcast host Jesse Michels about the Tuatha Dé Danann, whom he describes as the mythological gods of Ireland. tulsi-gabbard-mentions-uaps-in-her-dni-c: A researcher named Matthew Pines says that in 2025 Tulsi Gabbard, chosen as Director of National Intelligence (the official who oversees all US spy agencies), spoke openly about UAPs, the government's term for UFOs, during her testimony before the US Senate. tumbling-dipper-shaped-lights-near-mansf: A man named Jim Weiner says that in spring 1973, near Mansfield State College in Pennsylvania, he looked up above the trees and saw a group of lights shaped like the Little Dipper, a small pattern of stars. tunguska-air-burst-as-part-of-the-taurid: A researcher named Randall Carlson talks about the Tunguska event, a huge explosion over the Siberian forest on 30 June 1908, which he calls an air burst, meaning something blew up in the sky before it hit the ground. tunisian-column-inscription-of-the-canaa: Tim Alberino, a man who talks about ancient giants, tells podcast host Jesse Michels about an old column in Tunisia, in North Africa. tunnel-linking-derinkuyu-and-kaymakli: A researcher called Matt, speaking with podcast host Jesse Michels, talks about Derinkuyu and Kaymakli, two ancient underground sites in Turkey. tunnels-under-saqsaywaman-known-months-b: A researcher who goes by Luke Caverns says he was inside tunnels under Saqsaywaman, an ancient stone site above Cusco in Peru, in September, months before they were officially announced. turing-s-paper-treats-esp-as-an-objectio: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, points out that Alan Turing, the British mathematician, wrote a 1950 paper proposing the Turing test, a way to judge whether a machine can think by seeing whether it can pass as human in conversation. turner-s-virtual-reality-scenarios-in-ab: Tim Alberino, speaking with podcast host Jesse Michels about alien abduction stories, mentions a woman named Karla Turner. tutankhamun-s-tomb-stays-hidden-under-ru: A researcher named Luke Caverns, talking with podcast host Jesse Michels, tells of the tomb of Tutankhamun, an ancient Egyptian king, in Egypt's Valley of the Kings. tv-clip-of-a-ufo-turning-away-from-a-bea: Lyn Buchanan, a former Army sergeant, tells the podcast host Jesse Michels about a clip he says is shown on TV now and then. tv-globo-reporter-asks-venturelli-if-he-: A Brazilian surgeon named Italo Venturelli says that in January 1996, at the regional hospital in Varginha, Brazil, a reporter from TV Globo, a huge Brazilian TV network, asked him outright, "Did you operate on the ET?", meaning an extraterrestrial. tv-producer-s-master-tape-lost-on-his-de: A UFO investigator named James Fox tells of a video recording kept on a Beta SP master tape, a professional TV tape format, that a man named Chuck Clark got from a television producer in Los Angeles. tweet-the-murder-of-the-first-public-sen: A man described as a Pentagon whistleblower, Matthew Brown, read out on a podcast a message he posted to the tech billionaire Elon Musk. twelve-town-square-witnesses-including-u: A documentary maker, James Fox, says that while looking into the 1996 events in Varginha, a town in Brazil where people say a strange creature was seen, he spoke to about 12 different people in the town square, each saying different things. twin-knocked-out-when-brother-is-sedated: A man named Jim Weiner says that in the late 1950s, near Allentown, Pennsylvania, a doctor gave him a shot to knock him out, and a minute later his twin brother Jack went out cold too. twining-best-brains-in-the-air-force-195: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, cites a 1971 Australian intelligence document. twining-memo-and-its-postscript-on-indep: In 1947, after many UFO sightings across the United States, a senior Air Force general named Nathan Twining wrote a letter that is now known as the Twining memo. twins-matching-nightmares-in-two-states-: Charlie Foltz, who says he himself was part of a strange experience, tells on Jesse Michels' podcast about twin brothers, Jim and Jack Weiner. two-air-force-generals-at-the-pentagon-k: Chris Bledsoe, a man who says UFOs are drawn to him, tells on Jesse Michels' podcast what a man named Tim, Timothy Taylor, told him. two-craft-scanning-low-for-plutonium-in-: Roswell is a New Mexico town where, in 1947, many people say a strange craft crashed. two-del-rio-crashes-willingham-and-the-m: An online researcher who goes by UAPGerb says that two different crashes of unknown craft near Del Rio, Texas often get mixed up. two-flaming-balls-of-fire-over-the-field: Chris Bledsoe, a North Carolina man, says that in January 2007 he climbed a hill near the Cape Fear River and saw two huge glowing red and orange balls of fire, about 40 feet across, over a field. two-guards-found-nearly-naked-in-the-ech: Mario Woods, a former Air Force man who says he and fellow airmen were taken by aliens, tells on Jesse Michels' podcast about an earlier case he heard of. two-incomprehensible-beings-in-a-cave-on: Lyn Buchanan, a former Army sergeant who worked in remote viewing, the practice of trying to perceive distant places with the mind, tells the podcast host Jesse Michels that he once found two beings in a cave on Titan, the largest moon of Saturn. two-lights-over-the-uss-holland-off-spai: A man named Charlie Foltz says that in May 1970, aboard the USS Holland, a US Navy ship off the coast of Spain, he looked back and saw two lights coming toward the ship. two-men-at-the-door-explain-the-implant-: Whitley Strieber, a writer known for describing his own encounters with unknown beings, told the podcast host Jesse Michels that a few years ago two men came to the door of his apartment in California. two-men-in-el-paso-say-they-are-escaped-: An Army sergeant named Lyn Buchanan, speaking with podcast host Jesse Michels, passes on a story he credits to a person named Linda Molton How about two men in El Paso, Texas. two-saucers-at-roswell-left-melted-fiber: Charles Hall, a man who says he spent years in contact with aliens while serving at a US air base and who wrote a book called The Valley of the Grays, talks about Roswell, the 1947 crash in New Mexico that many say involved an alien craft. two-sets-of-orders-real-ones-to-san-ange: Charles Hall, a man who says he spent three years living alongside tall white aliens while serving in the US Air Force, describes how his assignment began around 1965 at Lackland Air Force Base in Texas. two-star-general-furious-at-doctor-s-ali: John Blitch, a scientist who worked for DARPA, the Pentagon's advanced research agency, and who says he was taken by an alien, tells on Jesse Michels' podcast about a visit to a doctor near Wright-Patterson Air Force Base in Ohio, a base long rumoured to hold alien bodies. two-years-packaging-the-thruster-into-gr: Charles Buer, whom a podcast title calls a NASA chief, says that after he and a colleague named Andrew Arjima ran experiments in Florida in 2016 on a thruster, a device meant to push something along, they spent about two years fitting it into electrically grounded boxes. tyler-as-secret-space-program-mission-co: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, speaking with a researcher named Diana Pasulka, describes a man known as Tyler as someone tied to a "secret space program", a hidden space effort beyond the public one. Michels says Tyler is a mission controller who has worked on all these missions since the Challenger space shuttle era of the 1980s, and that Pasulka collaborating with him is "wild", since it would mean an insider to a hidden program is talking to a researcher.
tyler-from-american-cosmic-identified-as: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that a man called Tyler in American Cosmic, a book by Diana Pasulka, is really a NASA mission controller named Timothy Taylor. NASA is the US space agency. If true, it puts a real name and a real job to one of the book's anonymous sources.
tyler-on-several-1940s-crashes-in-new-me: Diana Pasulka, a scholar who writes about religion and UFOs, tells on Jesse Michels' podcast what a source she calls Tyler told her. According to Tyler, there was a secret place on government land in New Mexico, not Roswell, where crashed craft were recovered, and there were a few such crashes in the 1940s. If true, it would mean the famous 1947 Roswell crash was not the only one.
tyler-reverse-engineering-ufo-crash-debr: A scholar named Diana Pasulka, who wrote a book called American Cosmic, says a man she calls Tyler, who worked in the US space program, told her that his group had gotten hold of debris from UFO crash sites. According to her, Tyler said he was studying those pieces to learn how they worked and copy them, and that this was producing game-changing technology, which would mean human inventions are being built from crashed craft.
tyler-s-claimed-time-travel-group-with-t: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says a man known only as Tyler told a family named Bledsoe, including Chris and Ryan Bledsoe, that he had been part of a group based at NASA, the US space agency, and in the Bahamas. According to Tyler, a man named Townsend Brown was president of the group, and its work involved time travel technology. If true, it would mean a hidden group once worked on time travel.
tyler-s-constant-interest-in-time-travel: A religious studies professor named Diana Pasulka says that in the 2010s she knew a man she calls Tyler, who was always talking about time travel. She told this on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, as part of a wider talk about UFOs and angels. If true, it hints that the people she studied were thinking about time as well as space.
tyler-s-conversion-at-the-vatican-archiv: A religious studies professor, Diana Pasulka, says that in the 2010s she watched a man she calls Tyler go through a deep personal conversion. According to her, it began at the Vatican, where they read old church records about Joseph of Copertino, a saint said to float in the air, and Maria de Agreda, a nun said to appear in two places at once. She tells it as a striking thing to witness, one that ties modern UFO interest to old religious marvels.
tyler-s-machine-room-and-ideas-for-biome: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, speaking with Diana Pasulka about her book American Cosmic, retells what a man called Tyler says in it. According to Michels, Tyler says he goes to a room with a machine he doesn't fully understand, connected in the telling to a secret US space programme, and comes away with ideas for biomedical inventions, meaning new medical technology. Michels says Tyler then started companies that became very successful, which, if true, would mean real businesses grew out of that strange room.
tyler-s-protocols-and-the-incoming-signa: Diana Pasulka, a scholar who writes about religion and UFOs, tells on Jesse Michels' podcast what a source she calls Tyler described to her in the 2010s. According to her, Tyler said that using certain methods he would feel something like a signal coming in, and then receive the information he needed to build new technologies or start businesses. If true, it would suggest ideas can arrive from some outside intelligence.
uap-activity-at-nuclear-sites: Karl Nell, speaking on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels in 2024, says there is a strong link between UFO sightings, which officials now call UAP or unidentified anomalous phenomena, and nuclear sites. He names Pantex, a nuclear weapons plant in Texas, and Hanford, a plutonium production site in Washington state, as places with many sightings, and says the pattern reaches overseas, even to the Fukushima nuclear disaster in Japan. If true, it would suggest that whatever is behind the sightings has a particular interest in nuclear power and weapons.
uap-class-objects-coming-down-from-the-o: A former military helicopter pilot named Jake Barber says that in December 2024 he saw objects south of Picatinny Arsenal, a US Army research site in New Jersey, that he calls UAP, the government's term for unexplained flying objects. He says they came down from the outer atmosphere, hovered in place, and then went back into space. If true, something was moving freely between space and the sky over New Jersey.
uap-craft-manipulate-a-subquantum-inform: Eric Davis, a physicist described as a Pentagon scientist, says he thinks UAP craft (unidentified anomalous phenomena, the government's term for UFOs) work by manipulating information at a level deeper than quantum physics. He bases this on the work of Roy Frieden of the University of Arizona, who wrote two books on Fisher information, a mathematical way of measuring how much information something carries. If he's right, these craft would be bending the basic rules of reality, not just flying with better engines.
uap-data-withheld-to-protect-classified-: Eric Hazeline, described as a former director of the NSA, the US agency that gathers intelligence from communications and signals, says he has no doubt about one reason UFO material stays secret. According to him, some of it was captured by collection systems, meaning spy sensors, that the government does not want anyone to know it has, so the data is held back to protect the sensors rather than to hide the objects.
uap-disclosure-act-controlled-disclosure: A researcher named Matthew Pines describes the UAP Disclosure Act, a bill put before the US Congress in 2023 and 2024 about releasing government records on UAP, meaning unidentified anomalous phenomena, the official term for UFOs. He says its plan for a controlled release of information, which he links to a man named Karl Nell, would create a UAP records review board with the standing of a government agency, the power to force testimony and records, and the power to declassify secrets on its own, with the president able to overrule it. Pines tells it to show how seriously the bill's authors took the idea of hidden records.
uap-disclosure-act-eminent-domain-over-p: A researcher named Matthew Pines says the UAP Disclosure Act, a 2023 bill in the US Congress about releasing records on UAP, the official term for UFOs, included eminent domain, the government's power to take private property. He says the bill aimed this power at material held in private hands, such as by companies. To Pines, this suggests the bill's authors believed such material exists outside government control.
uap-fly-around-government-teams-at-event: James Valor, from a startup called Skywatcher that says it can call in UFOs, says that at government test events in the early 2020s, unexplained flying objects flew around the government teams on the very first day. According to him, the teams had no idea it was happening. If true, the objects were right there and trained people were missing them.
uap-gerb-ties-elizondo-to-isa-gray-fox-a: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that an online researcher who goes by UAP Gerb links Lou Elizondo, a former Pentagon official who speaks publicly about UFOs, to the Intelligence Support Activity, also called Gray Fox. Michels describes that as a secret unit that scouts very sensitive places before other forces go in, part of Joint Special Operations Command, the military's command for its most secret special forces. The idea is that this background would tie Elizondo to a long-running secret program said to handle unexplained craft.
uap-hedge-tweet-responding-to-ft-alphavi: Matthew Pines, a guest on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, says that around 2020 or 2021 he posted a half-joking tweet asking "What's your UAP hedge?" with the tag Bitcoin. UAP stands for unidentified anomalous phenomena, the government's newer word for UFOs. He says he was answering an article on FT Alphaville, a finance blog of the Financial Times newspaper, about the risk that official disclosure of UFOs could shake the financial system.
uap-hit-by-hellfire-missile-video-shown-: Dan Sherman, a former Air Force sergeant who says the NSA, the US signals-intelligence agency, hired him to communicate with aliens, mentions on Jesse Michels' podcast a video a man named Eric Brent told him about. According to Sherman, the video, shown before the US Congress in 2025, shows a UAP, the government's term for a UFO, being hit by a Hellfire, a missile fired from military aircraft and drones. If true, it would mean the military has fired on one of these objects on camera.
uap-incidents-routinely-in-counter-wmd-i: A former Pentagon official turned whistleblower, Matthew Brown, says that from around 2018 reports of UAP, the government's term for unexplained flying objects, turned up very often in the intelligence he handled. He worked on stopping weapons of mass destruction, such as nuclear or chemical arms. If true, these sightings were a routine part of national security work rather than a rare oddity.
uap-moving-at-mach-40-explained-as-large: A scientist named Donald Hoffman, who argues that what we see is not reality as it really is, turns to UAPs, the government's term for UFOs, said to move at around Mach 40, forty times the speed of sound. He explains such objects through his idea that reality is made of networks of conscious observers, which he calls observer matrices, and suggests the objects could be larger versions of those networks showing up in our world. If he is right, these objects would be less like machines and more like something outside our normal picture of space.
uap-near-plants-ages-them-10-years: Dave Rossi, a man who says aliens taught him advanced physics, tells on Jesse Michels' podcast about a case he heard of, which he places in a 1970s study. According to him, a UAP, a UFO, was hovering near some plants and shot off when a person came close, and when the plants were tested they had aged ten years, he says within a matter of hours. He tells it as a sign that these objects may bend time itself.
uap-over-the-triangle-followed-by-hoveri: Brandon Fugal, the owner of Skinwalker Ranch, a Utah property known for reports of strange events, says his team was once launching rockets over an area of the ranch called the triangle when an unexplained flying object appeared. He says that within minutes a Black Hawk military helicopter came over the mesa, dropped down and hovered over the ranch's south field. If true, someone in the military was watching closely and responding fast.
uap-science-advisory-committee-s-first-z: A researcher named Michael Shurmer says that in 2026 he sat on a White House science advisory committee about unexplained flying objects. He says that at its first Zoom meeting the members worried the government might mislead them, for example by handing a researcher named Avi Loeb some material just to keep him busy analyzing it for weeks. If true, even the official advisers doubted they would be shown the real evidence.
uap-secrecy-justified-under-a-law-enforc: A journalist named Michael Shellenberger, speaking on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, passes on something a researcher named John Greenwald noticed. Greenwald collects government records. According to Shellenberger, Greenwald saw that the US government was keeping its files on UAP (the official term for UFOs, unidentified anomalous phenomena) secret under a rule meant for law enforcement, not just under the usual national security grounds. If that is right, the secrecy may rest on a different legal footing than people would expect.
uap-task-force-members-confirm-the-egg-w: A helicopter pilot named Jake Barber tells podcast host Jesse Michels about an egg-shaped object he says he encountered one night. He says senior members of the UAP Task Force, a Pentagon group set up to study unidentified aerial objects, later confirmed to him that what he ran into was NHI, meaning non-human intelligence. If true, it would mean officials privately agreed that the object was not made by people.
uap-task-force-the-grusch-inquiry-and-co: A commentator named Matthew Pines says things really got moving in 2019 and 2020, when the UAP Task Force, a Pentagon group set up to look into unexplained aerial sightings, began its work. He says the group came about because Congress heard things after news stories in 2017 and 2018 and through quiet back-channel talks, and decided a formal team was needed to dig in, including hunting for long-hidden programs. Congress backed this with requirements in the National Defense Authorization Act, the yearly US defense law, and Pines says David Grusch, a former intelligence officer, and Karl Nell, a retired Army officer, worked out much of what was going on.
uapx-becomes-project-x-at-university-at-: Kevin Knuth, a physicist and former NASA scientist, says that UAPx, a private group he helped run that studied unexplained flying objects, has been dissolved. He says its work has moved to the University at Albany in New York, where it is now called Project X. If true, the study of these objects has found a home in a regular university.
uas-activity-over-wright-patterson-2024: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, plays audio that he says comes from the control tower at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base in Ohio in 2024. On it, the tower warns a medical flight to use extreme caution because of heavy UAS movement on the base. UAS means unmanned aircraft, such as drones. He tells it as a sign that unknown craft were moving over a major military base.
uc-provost-unaware-of-laws-secretly-bene: A mathematician named Eric Weinstein says he once spoke with the provost, a top academic officer, of a major University of California research school. According to Weinstein, the provost had no idea that laws had been changed to quietly reward universities for doing certain kinds of work. He tells it to suggest that hidden research arrangements exist that even university leaders do not know about.
udo-wartena-s-tour-of-a-craft-with-count: Mike Masters, a researcher who argues that aliens may be humans from the future, tells about a miner named Udo Wartena, who he says was given a tour of a craft. According to Masters, Wartena knew nothing about UFOs or electromagnetism, yet the beings told him the craft worked using flywheels spinning in opposite directions, which would offer a rare look at how such a craft is said to fly.
uffington-white-horse-and-st-george-s-dr: Geoffrey Drumm, a man who talks about the purpose of ancient monuments, tells podcast host Jesse Michels about Uffington in England, where a huge figure of a horse is cut into a hillside. He says a mound right next to it is known as St. George and the Dragon's Mound, the spot where, in legend, St. George killed the dragon. He raises it because it would tie the old dragon legend to that ancient site.
uffington-white-horse-hill-as-a-thunders: Geoffrey Drumm, a man who talks about the purpose of ancient monuments, shows podcast host Jesse Michels a picture of the Uffington White Horse Hill, an English hillside with a giant horse figure cut into it. He says hills like this were used to create towering thunderstorm clouds, and the story links this to Avebury, a nearby prehistoric stone circle. If true, it would mean ancient people built landscapes to make weather on purpose.
ufo-and-consciousness-stories-intertwine: A researcher named Matthew Pines says the history of UFOs and the history of studying the mind are closely tied together inside US intelligence. He points to the early 1950s, when he says LSD was discovered, the US probably had some craft, and the country tested the Teller-Ulam device, the design behind the hydrogen bomb. For Pines, so much happening at once suggests the two stories cannot be told apart.
ufo-claims-raised-on-the-floor-of-congre: A guest named James Madden, talking with podcast host Jesse Michels about consciousness and UFOs, points out that UFO claims have been raised on the floor of the US Congress. He says that fact has to make the claims seem a bit more likely to be true.
ufo-enters-east-field-below-helicopter-a: A podcast host named Jesse Michels passes on a story from Brandon Fugal, the owner of Skinwalker Ranch, a property in Utah known for reports of strange happenings. According to Michels, Fugal described a UFO that dropped out of the sky, flew into the ranch's east field below a helicopter, and then left by way of a mesa, a flat-topped hill. If true, it would mean an unknown craft moving in and out of the land itself, right under an aircraft.
ufo-flying-figure-eights-shoots-into-mou: Robert Bigelow, a businessman who once owned Skinwalker Ranch, a Utah property known for reports of strange happenings, passes on what witnesses there told him. He says they stood watching a UFO fly figure eights until it suddenly changed course, shot off at low altitude and went straight into the mountain. According to Bigelow there was no explosion, it was simply gone, which if true would mean an object that can pass into solid rock.
ufo-history-hidden-in-tom-delonge-s-fict: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says a lot of real UFO history is hidden in plain sight inside a series of fiction books. The series was written by Tom DeLonge, the lead singer of the rock band Blink-182, together with the writers Peter Levenda and AJ Hartley. If true, it would mean true secrets were slipped to the public dressed up as novels.
ufo-looking-ancient-cave-art-in-australi: Joe Rogan, a well-known podcast host, says that Australia has a lot of strange cave art, some of it looking like UFOs and thousands of years old. He tells it as a hint that people long ago may have seen something like what people report today.
ufo-material-seemed-to-communicate-telep: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, passes on a story from Harald Malmgren, a former advisor to US presidents, and his daughter Pippa. According to Michels, in 1962 a man named Lawrence Gise handed Malmgren pieces said to come from a UFO, and as Malmgren held them he heard words in his head, as if the material were speaking to him by telepathy, meaning mind to mind. Michels places this at Los Alamos, the US weapons laboratory in New Mexico, in one telling and at the Sandia and Kirtland military sites in New Mexico in another; if true, it would mean the debris was not just strange metal but something able to communicate.
ufo-obsessed-japanese-town-near-fukushim: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, describes a story from Vice, a news outlet, about a small town in Japan next to Fukushima, where an earthquake set off a nuclear power plant meltdown in 2011, whose people are devoted to UFOs. He quotes the chief monk of a local temple saying so many UFOs came after the explosion that he was shocked, and in other tellings he mentions a UFO museum, a nearby mountain dedicated to UFOs, and a local belief that the UFOs helped clean up the spill. Michels tells it as one more sign that UFOs show up around nuclear sites.
ufo-over-a-big-game-in-italy-1950: A documentary filmmaker named James Fox mentions a UFO sighting in Italy in the 1950s, around 1957 as he remembers it, over some big game where many people were watching. He gives only a passing mention, as an example of a sighting seen by a large crowd.
ufo-over-sonoma-state-college-art-event-: Jeffrey Mishlove, a researcher of psychic phenomena, says a man named Ted Owens, who claimed he could make UFOs appear, predicted one would show up over an art department event at Sonoma State College in California. According to Mishlove, about a hundred people were outside with cameras and videotape in December 1976 when a UFO appeared roughly 3,000 feet above the campus. He says it made the front page of the Berkeley Gazette and the Channel 9 evening news, which would mean someone could summon these things on cue.
ufo-professor-privately-agrees-ufos-aren: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that around 2019 or 2020 he was at a conference, standing by the bar with a professor known for studying UFOs. Michels says he told him that, if you reason carefully from the evidence, these things are not from other planets, and the professor leaned in and whispered, "you're right." If true, it would suggest that some experts privately hold views they do not share in public.
ufo-programs-hidden-under-the-department: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says Chris Mellon, a former Pentagon intelligence official, told him that UFO programs are hidden inside the US Department of Energy. The reason, as Michels tells it, is the Atomic Energy Act of 1954, a law that makes anything nuclear a matter of national security, so putting the programs there keeps them locked away from outsiders.
ufo-said-to-hover-over-channeling-sessio: An unnamed researcher on a podcast describes sessions in the 1970s at the lab of Andrija Puharich, a scientist who studied psychic claims, where young people called the "space kids" would channel, meaning speak messages said to come from beings beyond Earth. According to the researcher, during one session it was announced that a UFO was hovering over them, and some people claim they saw it. If true, it would tie the messages to a real craft overhead.
ufo-shines-light-at-chernobyl-reactor-19: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that a writer with a Harvard doctorate, whom he calls Jensen Andreon, writes about a UFO seen at the height of the Chernobyl disaster in 1986, when a nuclear plant in Soviet Ukraine blew up. According to that account, many people nearby saw the object arrive, stay about three minutes, shine a light at the reactor and leave. Michels tells it as part of a pattern of UFOs said to watch over nuclear sites, and in a later episode he mentions the Chernobyl accounts again only in passing.
ufo-sightings-in-varese-1953: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, passes on what a grandson of Marconi, the Italian radio pioneer, told him: in 1953 people around Varese, a town in northern Italy, reported seeing so-called UFOs, meaning unidentified flying objects. The story comes up as part of a wider conversation, and if true it would place these sightings in Italy as early as the 1950s.
ufo-subreddit-growth-after-the-2017-arti: A researcher named Jason Simosa says that when a 2017 New York Times article about UFOs came out, the UFO forum on the website Reddit had about 70,000 members. By 2026, he says, it had about 4 million. He tells it to show how much public interest grew after that article.
ufo-targets-in-the-remote-viewing-unit-c: An Army sergeant named Lyn Buchanan says that in the 1980s he served in a unit doing remote viewing, the attempt to describe distant places or things using only the mind. He says much of the unit's UFO work came under the label of practice sessions, or as favors for generals, and he mentions a fellow member, Ed Dames. If true, the military was quietly pointing psychic spying at UFOs off the books.
ufo-that-came-down-through-redwood-trees: A scientist and author named Rizwan Virk says that Jacques Vallée, a well-known researcher of UFO cases, told him about a sighting somewhere in the tall redwood forests of northern California or Oregon. According to Vallée, the witnesses said an unidentified flying object came down at a 45-degree angle and left marks on the ground. Virk says the case got him thinking, because it would suggest something physical was there.
ufo-tracking-a-soviet-boomer-submarine-f: A podcast guest named Dan Sheehan tells of Pat Price, a man in 1970s research into remote viewing, the attempt to see distant places with the mind, alongside researchers Russell Targ and Ingo Swann. According to Sheehan, citing reports by Swann, Price located a Soviet "boomer," a submarine carrying nuclear missiles, somewhere at sea, and saw a huge UFO hovering over the water above it, tracking and watching it, which would mean something was keeping an eye on nuclear weapons.
ufo-trapped-in-canyon-near-belt-montana-: This story takes place in 1967 near Belt, a small town in Montana not far from an Air Force base. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, relays an account from a man named Bob Jameson that a UFO went down into a canyon near the town and was trapped there. A former Air Force officer, Robert Salas, tells it too, also citing Jameson, and adds that once daylight came the military sent helicopters, and the UFO shot right out between them and escaped. If true, it would mean the military tried and failed to capture a craft near its own bases.
ufo-waves-in-dalarna: Clas Svahn, a Swedish researcher who collects UFO reports, tells podcast host Jesse Michels about Dalarna, a region in the middle of Sweden. He says that Dalarna has had several waves of UFO sightings, meaning bursts of many reports at once. He mentions it because such clusters would suggest something keeps returning to the same area.
ufo-working-group-funded-by-stubblebine-: A researcher who goes by UAPGerb, on Jesse Michels's podcast, cites Philip Corso, an Army officer who wrote about UFO secrets, and his writings, including an unpublished manuscript. According to UAPGerb, Corso said that in 1986 a group called the UFO Working Group was formed with support from Albert Stubblebine, an Army general. In one version UAPGerb adds that this was really Majestic 12, a supposed secret panel of officials said to manage UFO matters, under a new name, with new members including people from the NSA, the US spy agency for electronic signals.
ufos-appear-at-the-time-of-the-manhattan: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, points out that in the 1940s, while physicists such as Robert Oppenheimer and Edward Teller were building the first atomic bomb in the Manhattan Project, the secret US wartime effort to make it, UFO sightings started to show up. Talking about the film Oppenheimer, he says "you have to wonder at that time because that's when all the UFOs pop up." If the timing means something, it would suggest the sightings are tied to humans getting the bomb.
ufos-appeared-the-day-after-the-fukushim: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that UFOs showed up the day after the Fukushima disaster, the 2011 nuclear accident at a power plant in Japan. In a later episode he puts it more loosely, saying only that UFOs were reported around the disaster. He tells it because, if true, it would suggest these objects take a special interest in nuclear sites and nuclear trouble.
ufos-appearing-around-high-voltage-exper: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that UFOs seem to show up, anecdotally, around high-voltage experiments and particle accelerators, the huge machines physicists use to smash tiny particles together. He doesn't name any particular lab or date. If true, it would hint that whatever is behind UFOs is drawn to our most powerful energy and physics work.
ufos-as-homeostasis-probes-showing-up-at: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, drawing on thinkers named Jacques Vallee and Steven Dick, floats the idea that UFOs might be part of the Earth's own "homeostasis kit", a self-balancing system that keeps the planet in check. In his telling they show up at turning points for civilization, such as nuclear sites, which would mean they act as a kind of planetary regulator rather than as visitors.
ufos-at-civilian-nuclear-sites-in-hastin: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Robert Hastings, a researcher who writes about UFOs and nuclear weapons, has an appendix in his book listing six to eight civilian nuclear power sites where UFOs were reported, including a famous case at Bariloche in Argentina. In another episode Michels mentions similar reports at Chernobyl and Bariloche without crediting Hastings, dating the Bariloche sighting to 1995. If true, it would mean the interest in nuclear sites reaches beyond military bases to ordinary power plants.
ufos-at-nuclear-facilities: Many people in this field say that UFOs tend to appear near nuclear sites, such as nuclear weapons bases and power plants, all over the world. A researcher, Eric Hazeline, talks about the idea with care. He says it could be true or it could not, and he points out that there are many more sensors around nuclear plants, so more sightings might simply get recorded there. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says it more directly: UFOs show up around nuclear sites everywhere. A man who describes himself as a Pentagon whistleblower, Matthew Brown, goes furthest. He says it is established beyond reasonable doubt, and that the interest covers not just nuclear sites but all weapons of mass destruction, crediting a former Air Force officer, Robert Salas, and his work on UFOs and nukes. If true, it would suggest that whatever is behind these sightings is paying attention to humanity's most dangerous weapons.
ufos-at-nuclear-facilities-as-future-hum: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, describes an idea that UFOs are humans from the future, and says they have shown up more often since our nuclear programmes began. According to him, they try to watch, shut down, or sometimes switch on nuclear facilities. If true, it would mean someone is steering our nuclear history to protect their own timeline.
ufos-come-from-whatever-direction-he-loo: Chris Bledsoe, a man who says he seems to attract UFOs, describes watching the night sky with others. He says they can turn in any direction, focus there, and that is where the objects will come from. If true, it would suggest the sightings respond to the watchers themselves.
ufos-denature-nuclear-weapons-putin-s-te: A guest on a podcast, Joe McMoneagle, says that ever since the first atomic bombs in 1945, UFOs have taken a huge interest in our nuclear weapons and have quietly disabled them so they will not go off. He adds that the last test missile Russia's president, Vladimir Putin, tried to launch blew up in its underground launch silo. If true, it would mean something non-human has been switching off the world's nuclear arsenals.
ufos-never-discussed-at-the-top-of-nsa-a: Eric Haseltine, a former senior official at the NSA, the US spy agency that intercepts communications, and at the ODNI, the office that oversees all US spy agencies, says UFOs never came up at the top of those agencies in the 2000s. In his words, nobody there spent a fifth of a second thinking about them. If true, any secret UFO work was kept away from even the most senior intelligence leaders, or did not exist there.
ufos-over-bariloche-nuclear-site-1995: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that UFOs have been seen buzzing around Bariloche, a city in Argentina that he says has its own civilian nuclear energy grid. He places a famous case there in 1995 and, in one telling, adds that it involved a commercial plane, though another time he gives no year. He raises it as one more example of UFOs appearing near nuclear sites.
ufos-over-nuclear-bases-every-night-of-t: A UFO researcher named Grant Cameron, speaking with podcast host Jesse Michels, tells a little-known side of the story of Travis Walton, a man who says he was taken by a UFO and was missing from November 5 to 10, 1975. Cameron says that on every one of those nights, a UFO was seen over a nuclear missile site or nuclear weapons store somewhere in the United States, and he names Air Force bases such as Loring, Wurtsmith, Minot and Malmstrom. If true, it would tie one man's abduction story to a wider pattern of interest in American nuclear weapons.
ufos-over-nuclear-icbms-as-a-message-not: An unnamed researcher, a guest on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, says that UFOs are seen over nuclear ICBMs, the long-range missiles that carry nuclear warheads. The guest suggests this might be a message, and in an episode about artificial intelligence the contrast is that they appear over nuclear weapons rather than over data centers, which would say something about what they care about.
ufos-past-present-and-future-and-the-hol: James Fox, a filmmaker who makes UFO documentaries, talks about UFOs Past, Present and Future, a 1970s documentary made by Robert Emenegger and Allan Sandler and narrated by Rod Serling, a well-known TV host. According to Fox, the film describes contact between beings and the military at Holloman Air Force Base in New Mexico in 1972 or 1974. If true, it would mean an actual meeting with non-human visitors on a US base.
ufos-seen-cleaning-up-radiation-at-fukus: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, citing a researcher named Jensine Andresen, talks about two nuclear disasters: Chernobyl in Ukraine in 1986 and Fukushima in Japan in 2011. He says that in both cases people saw UFOs come down and seemingly clean up the radiation, which would mean something out there is stepping in when our nuclear mistakes get dangerous.
ufos-seen-on-pine-ridge-reservation-1970: Michael Johnson, a US Air Force veteran who says he was once abducted by aliens, recalls seeing UFOs in the 1970s on the Pine Ridge Indian Reservation, a Native American reservation in South Dakota. In his words, he saw one, then two, there. He tells it as part of a wider history of strange encounters in his life.
ufos-showing-up-at-nuclear-sites-waiting: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, describes an idea that the beings behind UFOs follow a kind of rule against interfering, a "prime directive", and are waiting for humanity to become less violent. He says they keep an eye on us and show up at all of our nuclear sites. If true, it would mean we are being quietly watched until we grow up as a species.
ufos-shut-down-nuclear-missiles: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, speaks about the story that UFOs have shut down nuclear missiles at US missile sites. He says he has interviewed many of the men involved firsthand and thinks they are all legitimate, which, if they are right, would mean something unknown can switch off the country's nuclear weapons.
ugaritic-texts-summoning-dead-nephilim: A researcher named Tim Alberino says that ancient writings found at Ugarit, a city in the old land of Canaan, contain rites for summoning the dead Nephilim, the giants mentioned in the Bible. He offers these texts as proof that people back then believed the Nephilim were real beings, which would mean the giants were more than legend.
ukraine-peace-deal-of-april-2022: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says in passing that there was a peace deal for the war in Ukraine in April 2022, right after the war started. He mentions it during a talk with a former Air Force officer, without giving more detail.
ultrasound-brain-targeting-breakthrough-: A former military helicopter pilot named Jake Barber says that, shortly before 2025, a member of his team made a breakthrough with a non-invasive ultrasound system that can reach through the skull and target parts of the brain. He says it is meant to help a person shift from thinking into intuition, and in another telling adds that subjects were tested with random number generators and the work was done with a partner group. If true, it would be a tool for opening the mind, which his circle links to contact with unexplained phenomena.
uncle-matt-missiles-disabled-at-malmstro: Kevin Knuth, a physicist and former NASA scientist, passes on what his uncle Matt told him about Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana, a base that holds nuclear missiles, in the early 1970s. According to Knuth, his uncle said it happened all the time: these things would show up and disable the nuclear weapons. If true, it would mean something unknown could repeatedly switch off US nuclear missiles.
uncle-mickey-and-general-exon-at-air-mat: Whitley Strieber, an author known for writing about his own encounters with strange beings, says his uncle Mickey worked alongside General Arthur Exon at Air Materiel Command, the US Air Force's equipment and research command at Wright Field in Ohio, in 1947. He tells it as a family link to people working there in that year, which he treats as important to the UFO story.
underground-atomic-blast-for-natural-gas: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, in an episode about a claimed crash of a craft with alien bodies near Aztec, New Mexico, points to a local piece of history known as Gasbuggy. He describes it as the place where the government once set off an atomic bomb underground to blast open natural gas reserves, a detail he raises as part of what makes the area notable.
underground-cavern-on-mars-with-wiring-a: Joe McMoneagle, who says he did psychic "remote viewing" work for the US military, describes an underground cavern on Mars with wiring and a bright red light that later went out. He links it to photo negatives from Mars mapping by JPL, the NASA lab that runs space missions, saying the light was bright red when they first caught it. If true, it would point to working technology under the Martian surface.
underground-cities-built-before-the-youn: A researcher called Matt, talking with podcast host Jesse Michels, says he believes the underground cities of Cappadocia in Turkey, huge networks of rooms dug into the rock, were built well over 10,000 years ago. In his view they had to be built before the Younger Dryas, a time of sudden climate upheaval near the end of the last ice age, as shelters to survive its disasters. If so, it would mean an advanced people existed far earlier than history usually allows.
underground-cities-of-turkey: Graham Hancock, a writer on lost ancient civilisations, tells podcast host Jesse Michels about the famous underground cities of Turkey. He describes them as huge cities dug out beneath the earth, looking like ant farms on an enormous scale. He raises them as a sign that ancient people went to great lengths to live underground.
underground-infrastructure-at-the-nevada: An online researcher who goes by UAPGerb says that tunnels and buildings under the Nevada Test Site, a large government nuclear testing area in the desert near the secret base known as Area 51, are there to hold unexplained craft and the teams that recover them. He links this to craft he connects with a man named Alfred O'Donnell and to Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked on alien craft in that area. If true, it would mean the government keeps such craft hidden underground there.
underground-us-rapid-reaction-facility-a: An online researcher who goes by UAPGerb suggests, drawing on a man named Jake Barber and a source called Sentinels of Ether, that there may be an underground US facility near Coyame in northern Mexico. He describes it as a rapid reaction site, meaning a base for responding quickly, starting around 2004. If true, it would mean the US keeps a hidden base abroad for fast response to UFO events.
underwater-ufo-bases: A physicist named Kevin Knuth, speaking on a show about suppressed NASA data, talks about the idea that UFOs have bases under Earth's oceans. Asked where such objects might come from or stay, he says that is probably the best bet, which would mean whatever is behind them may be living right here on Earth.
underwater-ufo-cases-back-to-the-1800s: Kevin Knuth, a physicist and former NASA scientist, mentions a new book by Richard Dolan, a historian who writes about UFOs, about UFOs seen in and under the ocean. According to Knuth, Dolan's cases go back to the 1800s, which if true would mean such sightings in the water have been reported for well over a century.
underwood-says-the-flir-could-not-have-l: In 2004, off the coast of Southern California, Navy fliers say they ran into an unknown object, and one of them, a back-seat crew member named Chad Underwood, filmed it with the jet's FLIR, a heat-sensing camera that locks onto a target and follows it. On a podcast debate hosted by Jesse Michels, a guest named Merrick von Renenamp says Underwood told him there was no way the camera could have lost its lock on the object. Von Renenamp adds that an unnamed weapons systems officer (the crew member who runs a jet's sensors) now on active duty told him the opposite, that the system is finicky. The question matters because if the lock held, the object's sudden moves on the video would be real and not a camera glitch.
undisclosed-drugs-administered-for-exper: A man named Jordan Jose tells a podcast host, Jesse Michels, that as a child he was taken into what he calls a UFO program. He says that around 2008 to 2010, at a facility called Baker Victory Services in Western New York, he was given drugs that his parents knew nothing about. His medical records, he says, do not show what was really being given to him inside. In the same interview he says there were all sorts of substances and that he was essentially an experiment. Jordan is the only teller, returning to it twice in one conversation. If true, it would mean children were being secretly drugged as part of hidden research.
undisclosed-finding-at-the-signal-cutoff: A researcher named Filippo, part of a 2025 effort to look beneath the pyramid of Khafre, one of the great pyramids at Giza in Egypt, says their scans found something at the depth where their signal cuts off. He will not say what it is, only: "There is something." He tells it alongside claims of huge underground structures beneath the Giza pyramids, which, if true, would change what we think lies under them.
unexplained-10-minute-delay-on-rescue-fl: Greg Rogers, a doctor who worked with NASA, the US space agency, says that sometime between 1989 and 1993 he was on a rescue flight over the Atlantic, about 130 miles out from Cape Canaveral in Florida. He says they arrived 10 minutes later than expected, and no one could explain why. If true, it would point to time the crew could not account for.
unexplained-mass-caught-as-rockets-destr: The owner of Skinwalker Ranch, a property in Utah known for reports of strange events, says that during rocket launches above a part of the ranch called "the triangle," some rockets were destroyed. He says an unexplained mass was recorded by their instruments at the same moments. If true, it would suggest something unseen over that spot was interfering with the rockets.
unexplained-vertical-bedrock-shafts-besi: A researcher named Jeffrey tells podcast host Jesse Michels about vertical shafts cut into the bedrock beside the Khafre causeway, the ancient stone walkway leading to the pyramid of the pharaoh Khafre at Giza in Egypt. He says archaeologists and Egyptologists have no good explanation for them as part of royal burial practice. He brings them up as possible evidence of something hidden beneath the pyramids, which the episode frames as an energy system.
unexplored-martian-lava-tubes: A researcher named Chris Gilbert points out that Mars has many lava tubes, long caves left behind by ancient lava flows, and that no one has ever been inside them. He asks what might be in there, raising the idea that something could be hidden on Mars where we have never looked.
unidentified-hyperobjects: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells his listeners about a professor named James Madden, who he says wrote a book called Unidentified Hyperobjects. Michels calls him "a really cool professor" and brings up the book as a way to think about UFOs as something bigger and stranger than ordinary objects in the sky.
unidentified-objects-repeatedly-appearin: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that there are things in the sky we cannot identify that keep showing up around America's most sensitive nuclear sites. He offers it as a pattern, which, if true, would suggest that whatever these objects are, they take a particular interest in nuclear weapons.
union-bank-and-dulles-financing-the-nazi: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that an American bank called the Union Bank funded the Nazis in Germany before the Second World War. He adds that he thinks the American Allen Dulles also took part in financing them, and that Dulles was stationed somewhere like Norway. He brings it up as part of a wider story about powerful insiders and hidden history.
union-bank-and-dulles-in-nazi-financing: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says he thinks a banker named Prescott Bush was president of the Union Bank, and that the American Allen Dulles was helping with some Nazi financing. He links this to his larger story about a secret society behind the hiding of UFO knowledge, which, if true, would tie that secrecy to old wartime money networks.
unit-731-data-handed-to-the-us-in-exchan: Unit 731 was a secret Japanese army unit that did biological and chemical warfare research during the Second World War, led by a general named Shiro Ishii. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that after Japan's defeat in 1945, the unit's research data was not used to punish anyone. Instead, he says, it was stamped top secret and quietly handed to the United States, which was then occupying Japan. If true, it would mean the US took the results of wartime human experiments for itself in exchange for letting the people responsible go free.
unit-731-human-experiments-1930: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells of Unit 731, which he describes as a secret biological and chemical warfare research programme run by the Imperial Japanese Army. He says it was set up in Manchuria, in northeast China, under a general named Shiro Ishii, and ran from the 1930s until 1945. He brings it up in an episode about human experiments, as an example of how far governments have gone in testing on people.
united-nuclear-supplies-dhs-and-fbi-trai: Bob Lazar, whose company United Nuclear sells scientific supplies, told the podcast host Jesse Michels that the business has been involved with federal training since about 1999. He says the people they work with train the Department of Homeland Security, the US agency that protects the country at home, and the FBI, the US federal police. If true, it would mean his small supply business sits close to government security work.
university-of-cagliari-people-collect-th: A researcher named Tim Alberino says that around 1978 to 1981, certain people connected to the University of Cagliari, in the capital city of the Italian island of Sardinia, collected ancient artifacts along with the bodies of giants. If true, it would mean remains of giant humans were found and taken away by academics.
unlit-drones-hovering-over-400-ft-above-: A helicopter pilot named Jake Barber told the podcast host Jesse Michels that in December 2024 he saw drones with their lights off, sitting still more than 400 feet above Picatinny Arsenal, a US Army research base in New Jersey. He tells it as something he saw himself, which, if true, would mean unknown craft were hovering freely over a military site.
unmarked-black-helicopters-arrive-at-ell: Podcast host Jesse Michels, in an episode with a researcher named Robert Hastings about UFOs over nuclear bases, passes on what someone told him about Ellsworth Air Force Base in South Dakota in the 1960s. According to that account, over a few weeks a wave of shiny black helicopters with no markings at all suddenly showed up at the base. The story is told as a sign that some unexplained event there drew a quiet, secret response.
unmarked-blackhawks-during-notam-experim: The owner of Skinwalker Ranch, a property in Utah known for reports of strange events, says that during experiments run under a NOTAM, a formal notice warning pilots to keep out of a stretch of airspace, unmarked Black Hawk military helicopters showed up in the middle of the night. If true, it would suggest that someone in government was quietly watching what happened at the ranch.
unnamed-group-extended-low-dose-dmt-to-6: On a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, a neuroscientist named Andrew Gallimore says that a research group, which he does not name, has stretched the DMT experience to six hours by giving a very low dose. DMT is a powerful psychedelic drug that some users say takes them to a realm full of beings. If true, it would let people stay in that realm far longer than usual and study it more closely.
unnamed-insider-on-a-ufo-crash-retrieval: A researcher who goes by the online name UAPGerb says, on Jesse Michels' podcast, that one of his sources claims to have served on a team that recovers crashed UFOs, working out of the Nevada Test and Training Range, a huge military testing area in Nevada. According to UAPGerb, this person held a badge from the National Reconnaissance Office, the US agency that runs spy satellites, and a Q clearance, a top-level security clearance for nuclear secrets. If true, it would mean the US government has a working unit that retrieves non-human craft.
unnamed-law-enforcement-entity-investiga: Steven Greer, a longtime campaigner for the release of government UFO secrets, told the podcast host Jesse Michels in 2025 that he is passing information to a law enforcement body he cannot name. He says this body could go to people inside secret programs, get their information and question them. If true, it would mean officials were starting to investigate the insiders themselves.
unnamed-major-we-got-it-from-them-1992: Greg Rogers, a doctor who worked with NASA, the US space agency, says that in 1992 at Cape Canaveral Air Force Station, a military launch site in Florida, he spoke with an Air Force major whose name he does not give. According to Rogers, the major looked at him and said, "We got it from them." If true, it would mean the military had something it obtained from non-human visitors.
unnamed-president-and-wife-see-a-ship-wh: A guest on a podcast, Kiran Ilum Xenov, introduced as the president of a republic within Russia, says he was told that the president of a large country, one of the G7 group of wealthy nations, saw a strange craft. According to him, the president and his wife were on holiday fishing on the coast when a ship came descending toward them. If true, it would mean a sitting world leader has seen such a craft with his own eyes.
unnamed-raytheon-engineer-and-academic-e: Marik von Rennenkampf, arguing against a skeptic on Jesse Michels's podcast, says that around 2024 he and others consulted experts about the Gimbal video, a Navy cockpit video of an unidentified object filmed off the US East Coast around 2015. He says they spoke with a senior engineer at Raytheon, the defense company, who knew the camera system intimately, as well as academic experts. The point is that people who know the equipment best could say whether the video shows a real object or a camera effect.
unnamed-southern-california-facility-sto: The researcher UAPGerb says on Jesse Michels' podcast that an unnamed source told him non-human bodies are being stored at a place in California. He describes it as a site with no official name or designation of its own, and at one point says only "California" rather than Southern California. If true, it would mean the government is quietly holding the remains of beings that are not human.
unreleased-photo-of-massive-triangle-ove: Bob Maguire, a former contractor for the CIA, the US foreign intelligence agency, says that after joining a university research group he saw photos that have never been released. One, he says, shows a massive triangle-shaped object above the water, and he stresses that the thing is huge. If true, it would mean clear images of such craft exist but are being kept from the public.
unsuccessful-search-for-partner-michael-: Mario Woods, a former Air Force guard at a nuclear weapons site who says he was abducted by aliens in 1977, says he spent decades and real money trying to find his partner from that night, Michael Johnson, searching even in hospitals and knowing only that Johnson said he was from Chicago. According to podcast host Jesse Michels, Woods hired private investigators, went to the FBI, and was promised help by AARO, the Pentagon's official UFO office, while amateur sleuths online also searched, all with no luck. Michels says a tip from a fan finally found Johnson, letting the two men, whose shared story would back each other up, meet again about 50 years later.
unusual-rate-of-carcass-decay-on-the-ran: Brandon Fugal, the owner of Skinwalker Ranch, a property in Utah famous for reports of strange events, tells podcast host Jesse Michels that dead animals there rot in an unusual way. He says the rate of decay on the ranch is dramatically different from anything normally seen in nature, and he credits this partly to a man named Ben Woodruff. If true, it would suggest something on the land is changing ordinary biology.
upper-paleolithic-cave-art-showing-non-h: A neuroscientist named Andrew Gallimore, speaking on Jesse Michels' podcast in an episode about DMT, a powerful psychedelic drug, points to the writer Graham Hancock's book Supernatural. Gallimore says that, as Hancock describes, Stone Age paintings deep inside caves, made tens of thousands of years ago, clearly show beings that were neither human nor animal. He brings it up as a hint that people have been meeting such beings for a very long time, perhaps in altered states of mind.
uranium-at-skinwalker-ranch: Skinwalker Ranch is a property in Utah known for reports of strange lights, creatures and other odd events. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that people who look at the ranch today claim there is a lot of uranium, a radioactive metal, in the ground around it. He raises it as a possible link between the land itself and the strange things said to happen there.
urartians-as-a-later-culture-built-on-ol: A researcher called Matt tells podcast host Jesse Michels about the Urartians, an ancient people of the Lake Van region in eastern Turkey whom he dates to around 2000 BC, or about 3,000 years ago. He says mainstream archaeology credits them with the ruins, artefacts and symbols there because they carved cuneiform, the ancient wedge-shaped writing, into some temples. Matt suggests instead that they built on much older foundations left by an earlier culture.
uri-geller-abducted-as-a-child: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Uri Geller, a man famous for claiming psychic powers, has a story of being abducted as a young child. According to Michels, Geller says he gained his psychic abilities that way. If true, it would link alien encounters to unusual powers of the mind.
us-air-force-plane-lands-at-campinas-and: In 1996 the town of Varginha, Brazil, is said by many tellers to have seen a crash and the capture of a strange creature. A witness named Jose Fernandez, citing a man named Louzando and a documentary called Moment of Contact, says that a US Air Force plane landed at Campinas, a Brazilian city, and that helicopters collected something from Varginha, which would mean the United States took part in carrying the find away.
us-and-china-crash-retrieval-and-back-en: Joe Rogan, a popular podcast host, said on Jesse Michels's show that Dan Farah, who made a documentary called The Age of Disclosure, firmly believes both the United States and China have recovered crashed craft that are not human-made. According to Rogan, Farah believes both countries are also trying to take those craft apart and copy them, which would mean a quiet technology race between the two powers.
us-black-psychokinesis-unit-separate-fro: A philosopher named Jason Jorjani says on Jesse Michels' podcast that, based on what some of the country's top remote viewers have said (people trained by the government to describe distant places using only the mind), the US had a secret unit in the 1970s and 80s working on psychokinesis, the idea of moving or affecting things with the mind. He says this unit was separate from the remote viewing programmes that Congress eventually stopped funding. If true, it would mean the government took mind-over-matter powers seriously enough to study them in secret.
us-fitted-a-non-human-power-source-into-: Jeremy Corbell, a filmmaker who reports on UFOs, told the podcast host Jesse Michels that there is evidence the United States has fitted a power source that was not made by humans into a craft that humans built. He compares it to dropping a Ferrari engine into a Pinto, a cheap small car. If true, it would mean the US has not only recovered such technology but managed to use part of it.
us-in-possession-of-exotic-material: Lou Elizondo, a former Pentagon official who says he ran a small Pentagon office that studied unexplained aerial reports, is heard on Jesse Michels's podcast saying he believes the United States has exotic material in its possession. No time or place is given. If true, it would mean the government holds physical pieces of something not made by us.
us-pilot-testifies-about-scrubbed-cia-an: Podcast host Jesse Michels says a US pilot named Fred Clawson now states on the record that in 1996 there were flights linking the CIA, the US spy agency, and the Air Force to Varginha, the Brazilian town where many say a craft crashed and a creature was captured, and that those missions were later wiped from the record. Clawson himself explains that securing a cargo plane follows a set protocol, and points to Scott Air Force Base as where the paper trail came from. If true, it would tie the United States directly to what happened in Varginha.
us-racing-to-occupy-earth-moon-lagrangia: A US congressman, Eric Burlison, says on a 2026 podcast that the United States government is racing to occupy a Lagrangian point between the Earth and the Moon, a spot in space where the pull of the two bodies balances so that something can stay parked there. He says he knows this firsthand, and if true it would mean a quiet contest is under way for a strategic position in space.
us-scalar-weapons-rumor: A journalist named Ross Coulthart says on Jesse Michels' podcast that people have passed him second-hand information suggesting the United States has built what are called scalar weapons, a kind of exotic energy weapon whose workings he does not spell out. If true, it would mean the US has secret weapons beyond anything publicly known.
us-scientists-lose-clearances-while-nazi: On Jesse Michels's podcast, a writer and researcher named Peter Levenda says that in the late 1940s and 1950s, Americans who had worked for the United States during the Second World War lost their security clearances, the official permission to handle secret work.
