He names the physicist Robert Oppenheimer and the rocket engineer Jack Parsons, and says that former Nazi scientists were put in charge instead. If true, it would mean the country's most secret projects were handed to its former enemies.
us-soviet-agreement-to-report-ufos-affec: A man named Karl Nell, speaking from official experience, says there is an agreement between the United States and the former Soviet Union, still in force, meant to lower the risk of nuclear war. He says it includes a rule that each side will tell the other if UFOs interfere with its early-warning systems, the radars that watch for incoming missiles. If true, both nuclear powers planned in writing for UFOs that could set off a false alarm. A man described as a Pentagon whistleblower, Matthew Brown, also mentions it. He dates it to around 1971 and calls it an outer space treaty in which the two sides agree to notify each other if they detect UFOs, without mentioning the warning systems.
us-soviet-deconfliction-on-ufos-and-nato: Matthew Brown, presented as a whistleblower from the Pentagon, says on a 2026 podcast that the United States and the Soviet Union set up deterrence and deconfliction on UFOs, meaning arrangements so neither side would mistake a UFO for an attack by the other. He also links this to cooperation within NATO, the Western military alliance, which would mean rival powers quietly worked together on the subject during the Cold War.
us-strikes-on-iranian-nuclear-sites-as-p: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, notes that President Donald Trump had just ordered strikes on three Iranian nuclear sites using B-2s, American stealth bombers, in 2025. He then wonders aloud whether conflicts like this play out against a hidden backdrop, a secret struggle among unseen beings over adjusting the timeline. If so, our wars would be shaped by forces we can't see.
us-ufo-authorities-obsessed-with-mental-: A researcher known online as UAPGerb tells podcast host Jesse Michels about Wilbert Smith, a Canadian engineer who ran Project Magnet, Canada's government UFO study of the 1950s. According to UAPGerb, Smith said the American officials studying UFOs at the time were obsessed with the mental and psychic experiences that came with UFO research. If true, it would mean the US government's interest went beyond hardware into the mind.
usgs-prediction-of-a-la-palma-collapse-t: A former Army sergeant named Lyn Buchanan, speaking on Jesse Michels' podcast, describes a warning about La Palma, an island in the Atlantic. He says the US Geological Survey, the government's earth science agency, has predicted that if part of the island collapsed it would set off a tsunami that in places could reach up to 26 miles inland along the US East Coast. He tells it as a picture of how big a disaster could one day hit that coast.
usgs-seismic-sensors-track-booms-toward-: Nick Cook, a journalist who has written about secret aircraft, tells podcast host Jesse Michels that in the late 1980s the US Geological Survey, the government agency that monitors earthquakes, picked up something odd on its sensors. He says they detected sonic booms coming in from the Pacific over California and heading toward Area 51, a secret military test site in Nevada. He tells it as a sign of unknown, very fast aircraft being flown there.
uso-incident-at-pascagoula-1973: Richard Dolan, a UFO historian, tells podcast host Jesse Michels about Pascagoula, Mississippi, in 1973. He says that a week or two after an earlier event there, a genuine USO incident happened at the same place, a USO being an unidentified object seen in or under water. He raises it as a sign the area had real, repeated activity.
uss-curtis-deck-log-luminous-object-1954: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, reads out an entry from the deck log, the ship's official daily record, of the USS Curtis, which he describes as the ship that set off a hydrogen bomb test at Bikini Atoll in the Pacific in 1954. According to the entry he reads, at 11:05 at night "an unidentified luminous object passed over ship from bow to stern," yellowish orange, moving fast and low. He tells it as an example of unknown objects turning up where nuclear weapons are being tested.
uss-delarov-disc-rises-from-sea-near-ada: A writer on UFO history, Richard Dolan, tells of an incident in 1945 near Adak Island, in the Aleutian Islands off Alaska, involving a US Navy ship called the USS Delarov. Drawing on accounts from a man named Robert Crawford and from the researcher James McDonald, he says people aboard saw a disc-shaped object about 200 feet wide rise up out of the water. If true, it would mean such craft were coming and going from the sea even before the modern UFO era.
uss-finch-cigar-shaped-object-shot-down-: A writer on UFO history, Richard Dolan, passes on an account from a man named David Noble White Horse about the US Navy ship USS Finch near Johnston Island, a small Pacific atoll, in 1962, around the time of a nuclear test there. According to the account, the sailors were all talking about a cigar-shaped bogey, meaning an unknown object, that seemed to have been shot out of the sky. If true, it would mean the military brought down an unknown craft.
uss-jackson-video-of-multiple-erraticall: Tim Gallaudet, a retired Navy admiral, says a Navy officer named Alexander Wiggins showed him video taken aboard the USS Jackson, a Navy warship, off Southern California around 2019. According to Gallaudet, the crew saw several UAP, unidentified objects in the sky, moving erratically at night. He tells it as part of a wider pattern of strange objects swarming Navy ships in that area.
uss-john-f-kennedy-orb-and-systems-failu: A writer on UFO history, Richard Dolan, relays the testimony of a man named James Cop, given to the Disclosure Project, a group that collected statements from people about government knowledge of UFOs. Cop says that on July 2, 1971, at 8:30 at night, he was running communications aboard the aircraft carrier USS John F. Kennedy when all incoming messages turned into gibberish, and the story ties this to a glowing orb and a failure of the ship's systems. If true, it would mean an unknown object could knock out a warship's equipment.
uss-nautilus-fitted-with-a-side-hatch-to: A writer on UFO history, Richard Dolan, passes on a claim made at the International UFO Congress, a gathering of UFO researchers. According to it, in the mid-1960s the US Navy submarine USS Nautilus was fitted with a special side hatch so it could capture discs and other unknown objects in the ocean. If true, it would mean the Navy was actively trying to collect such objects underwater.
uss-omaha-sphere-as-a-heat-source-going-: In July 2019 a US Navy warship, the USS Omaha, filmed a round object off San Diego, California, that seemed to drop into the sea. A well-known UFO skeptic, Mick West, says on Jesse Michels's podcast that if you zoom in on the video it looks more like a distant heat source, blurred and spread out by the camera, that is passing behind the horizon. If he is right, the video would show something ordinary far away rather than a strange craft.
uss-omaha-sphere-video-2019: Podcast host Jesse Michels calls the USS Omaha case, involving a Navy ship off San Diego in July 2019, a very controversial and interesting one, centred on a video of a round object near the ship. A retired Navy admiral, Tim Gallaudet, tells it second-hand from an officer named Alexander Wiggins, who Gallaudet says was on the Omaha's bridge, and he puts the weight on the moment the spherical object goes into the water. If true, it would mean an object able to move from the air into the sea.
uss-paul-hamilton-reports-an-object-spla: A researcher named Marik von Rennenkampf, on Jesse Michels' podcast, describes Navy records obtained through the Freedom of Information Act, a US law that lets anyone request government records. He says that in July 2019 off Southern California, about 24 hours after another event, a Navy ship called the USS Paul Hamilton logged an object splashing down into the sea. He offers it as an official paper trail backing up reports of strange objects near Navy ships that summer.
utopia-region-renamed-galaxias-chaos-aft: John Brandenburg, a scientist who argues that life on Mars was wiped out by nuclear war, says that in the 1980s a second face-like shape was spotted on the Martian surface in a region called Utopia. He says that afterward the region's name was changed from Utopia to Galaxias Chaos. He tells it as a sign that the find was being played down.
v-shaped-object-in-the-desert-turns-out-: Michael Shermer, a well known skeptic and researcher, told Jesse Michels about something he saw in the 1980s while riding in the Race Across America, a cross-country bicycle race. Out in the desert he saw what looked like a shiny V-shaped object, and he says it turned out to be a flock of geese. He tells it to show how ordinary things can look strange.
v2-rocket-goes-off-course-into-mexico-as: Jason Jorjani, a researcher who writes about Nazi Germany's alleged UFO work, tells podcast host Jesse Michels that in the late 1940s a V2, the long-range rocket Germany built in the Second World War, went off course and struck a place in Mexico. In his telling it was not an accident but a warning. If true, it would hint that someone outside American control still held German rocket power after the war.
va-ptsd-program-with-flashing-images-and: Dylan Borland, a military veteran, says that in 2016 and 2017 the VA, the US government department that cares for veterans, put him in a strange programme for PTSD, a disorder that follows trauma. He says it involved flashing images and air horns, and he ties it to Langley, home of the CIA, the US spy agency, citing his VA medical records. If true, it would suggest he was being tested rather than simply treated.
va-treatment-program-with-flashing-image: Dylan Borland, a veteran who says he was then working for BAE, a large defence company, says that around 2017 the VA, the US department that cares for veterans, put him through treatment with flashing images and constant MRIs, a kind of brain and body scan. He says that at the same time the VA was denying all his veterans' benefits, and he points to his medical records. He tells it to suggest he was being studied while being refused help.
vacuum-energy-secrecy-to-prevent-weaponi: Kirk McConnell, a former US Senate staffer, asks podcast host Jesse Michels to imagine that the government discovered it is not that hard to draw energy from empty space, sometimes called vacuum energy. He links the idea to the inventor Nikola Tesla and to another inventor, T. T. Brown, and suggests such a discovery would be kept secret so it could not be turned into a weapon.
vaddo-tungsten-fragment-from-1957-car-st: Clas Svahn, a Swedish UFO researcher who keeps a large archive of cases, tells podcast host Jesse Michels about two carpenters driving at night on Väddö, northeast of Stockholm, in 1957. He says they saw an object come in from the east, make a U-turn and hover in front of their car, which then died completely. The case is linked to a small piece of tungsten, a very hard metal, which would be physical evidence if it came from the object.
valentine-archuleta-sees-the-craft-hit-t: The granddaughter of a rancher named Valentine Archuleta says her grandfather looked up and saw a craft come down and hit a mesa, a flat-topped hill, right on his family's land near Aztec, New Mexico, around March 25, 1948. Her account is part of a larger story about a crash there, which others tie to a police officer chasing a disc and a small helicopter circling the site. If true, it would mean a local man saw the crash itself.
valerie-ransone-arrives-at-lab-nine-1978: On Jesse Michels's podcast, an unnamed researcher says that a woman named Valerie Ransone, who was said to channel information from other beings, ended up in 1978 at Lab Nine, a research group run by a man named Puharich. The story matters to tellers because Lab Nine is said to have tried to contact a council of non-human beings, and her arrival would place her at the center of that effort.
valerie-ransone-runs-the-whip-inflation-: Jeffrey Mishlove, a researcher with a PhD who studies psychic phenomena, told Jesse Michels that when he knew a woman named Valerie Ransone, she was working in President Gerald Ford's White House in the mid 1970s. According to him, she ran Whip Inflation Now, a government campaign urging Americans to help fight rising prices. He tells it as background on someone he knew personally.
valerie-ransone-the-ether-ship-group-and: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that a woman named Valerie Ransone tried to communicate with aliens through xenolinguistics, the study of how to understand alien languages. He says she was involved with a group called the Ether Ship, connected to a man named Willard de Bogart, and that she actually worked in the White House in the 1970s. If true, it would mean attempts at alien contact reached the heart of the US government.
validation-scan-of-the-gran-sasso-physic: Filippo Biondi is a researcher who uses satellite radar to look for hidden structures under the ground, including beneath the pyramids of Egypt. On the podcast of host Jesse Michels, he says that he and his team scanned the Gran Sasso physics laboratory in Italy, a lab built deep inside a mountain. As he tells it, the point was to test his method on a known underground site, so people could trust what it shows beneath the pyramids. In a later episode of the same show he says it again in his own words. There he adds that he used a different, experimental way of processing the data for Gran Sasso, and he dates the scan to 2024. Both tellings come from Biondi himself, speaking first-hand.
validation-scan-of-the-osiris-shaft: A scientist named Filippo Biondi, who says he has used scans to look beneath the pyramids of Giza in Egypt, told podcast host Jesse Michels that his team also scanned the Osiris shaft, a deep, well-known underground passage at Giza. He says they did this because the shaft is already a known structure, so it serves as a check on whether their method shows what is really underground. If the check holds, he suggests, it would lend weight to the other hidden features his scans point to.
vallee-and-davis-six-level-uap-paper: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, mentions a paper by Jacques Vallee, a longtime UFO researcher, and Eric Davis, a physicist, that sorts UAP, the newer official term for UFOs (unidentified anomalous phenomena), into six levels. According to Michels, the levels run from "nuts and bolts" physical craft at the bottom up to spiritual or metaphysical sides of the experience at the top. He praises it as a way of holding all those layers in one picture.
vallee-argues-with-spielberg-on-close-en: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Jacques Vallee, a well-known UFO researcher, got into an argument with film director Steven Spielberg on the set of Close Encounters of the Third Kind, Spielberg's 1977 film about meeting aliens. The story is framed around a disagreement over time travel, a hint that Vallee saw the phenomenon differently from the simple visitors-from-space picture in the film.
vallee-finds-a-classified-battelle-lette: This story goes back to Project Blue Book, the US Air Force's study of UFOs in the 1950s and 60s. A UFO investigator, James Fox, says that a researcher named Jacques Vallee, while going through the files of the astronomer J. Allen Hynek, who advised Blue Book, came upon a classified document he was never meant to see. According to Fox, it was a letter from Battelle, a private research institute, signed by a man named H.C. Cross. Fox and a podcast host, Jesse Michels, say it points to a secret UFO program running alongside the public one. Michels calls the document the Pentacle memo and says Battelle was working behind the scenes from the very start of Blue Book. In one telling he leaves out Vallee and instead ties the story to present-day defense contractors and to officials named Sean Kirkpatrick and Ronald Moultrie. If true, it would mean the public UFO study was only part of the picture, with the real work done in secret.
vallee-hints-bob-lazar-was-an-mk-ultra-s: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Jacques Vallee, a longtime UFO researcher, hints in his book Revelations: Alien Contact and Human Deception that Bob Lazar, a man who claims he worked on reverse engineering alien craft at a secret site in Nevada, may have been a subject of MK Ultra, a secret US government mind-control programme. In that reading, government brainwashing could be what led Lazar to believe he had worked on UFOs, which would turn his famous story into a case of deliberate deception rather than alien technology.
vallee-in-james-fox-film-ai-created-by-a: A researcher named Jason Simosa says on Jesse Michels' podcast that Jacques Vallée, a longtime UFO researcher, said something striking in a recent project with the documentary filmmaker James Fox. According to Simosa, Vallée suggested we may be dealing with an artificial intelligence that was itself created by a non-human intelligence from another planet. If so, what people meet would not be the makers themselves but their machines.
vallee-knows-more-than-he-can-communicat: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that when he talks with Jacques Vallée, a veteran researcher of UFOs, he gets the sense that Vallée knows a lot more about the subject than he can put into words. Michels said this on his show in 2025, and he also mentions the podcaster Joe Rogan in the same breath. If he is right, one of the field's best-known figures would be holding back knowledge he has no way to share.
vallee-on-ransone-s-nro-satellite-work-1: An unnamed guest on Jesse Michels' podcast, in an episode about a CIA scientist said to have contacted an alien council, points to Forbidden Science, the published journals of UFO researcher Jacques Vallée. The guest says Vallée wrote of speaking with a woman named Valerie Ransone in Houston in the late 1970s, when she was doing some kind of work for the National Reconnaissance Office, the US agency that runs spy satellites. The detail is told to tie her to the secret world of government intelligence.
vallee-pasulka-theory-that-the-1947-rosw: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says his favourite theory is one he credits to Jacques Vallée, a veteran UFO researcher, and Diana Pasulka, a scholar who writes about religion and UFO belief. As Michels tells it, the theory holds that the 1947 crash near Roswell, New Mexico, where something is said to have come down on a ranch, was a dividing line: before it, people described strange beings in the language of folklore, and after it, they described them as aliens. If true, it would mean the same phenomenon simply changed its costume to suit the times.
vallee-s-1985-cia-document-on-staged-abd: A researcher named Steven Greer says that Jacques Vallee, a UFO researcher and author, published in a 1992 book a 1985 CIA document describing operations in Argentina and Brazil in which poor farmers were kidnapped so they would believe aliens had taken them, for what the document calls psychological warfare value. In another moment Greer describes the same document more broadly, saying it plainly admits the CIA carries out the abductions, without limiting it to those two countries. If true, at least some alien abduction stories would be staged by humans.
vallee-s-260-000-case-capela-database: A researcher identified only as Jason, speaking on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, says that Jacques Vallée, a computer scientist who has studied UFO reports for decades, built a collection of reports he calls the Capela database. Jason says it holds about 260,000 cases. If so, it would be one of the largest records of UFO sightings anyone has gathered.
vallee-s-assessment-of-the-billy-meier-p: A philosopher and researcher named Jason Jorjani, talking on Jesse Michels's podcast, mentions photographs taken in Switzerland in the late 1970s by Billy Meier, a Swiss man who says he met beings from space. Jorjani says that Jacques Vallée, a long-time UFO researcher, has looked at some of these photos, and he brings this up as if an expert's look gives the pictures some weight.
vallee-s-control-system-steps-in-when-a-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, describes the "control system" idea of Jacques Vallée, a veteran UFO researcher, who suggests the phenomenon behaves like a system that steers human belief and behaviour. Michels says it knows how to "nip at the herd", like a sheepdog, so that when a nuclear weapon is about to go off, it shows up. If true, it would mean something is quietly watching over, and nudging, humanity at its most dangerous moments.
vallee-s-diaries-keep-pointing-to-the-ca: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in the published diaries of the UFO researcher Jacques Vallee, a five-volume set called Forbidden Science, Vallee keeps having lunch with secretive insider types who tell him to look at the Carlyle Group, which Michels describes as a multinational conglomerate with big defense interests. Michels asks his guest whether there is anything to this idea, which would mean a private company with defense ties sits close to the UFO secret.
vallee-s-fairy-alien-parallels-in-passpo: This story is about a book called Passport to Magonia by an author and researcher named Jacques Vallee. According to the people who describe it, Vallee compared old folk tales about fairies and elves with modern reports of meetings with aliens. A writer on ancient history, Graham Hancock, says the old stories sound very like the new ones: fairies and elves who abducted people, did surgery on them, had sex with them and produced hybrid babies. He also links this to another book called Supernatural. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells it too, in his own words. He calls Passport to Magonia a great book whose argument annoyed both believers and doubters. In his telling, it is one phenomenon wearing different cultural masks over the centuries, and he applies the idea to a 1977 case at Ellsworth, an Air Force base in South Dakota. If the comparison holds, then today's alien encounters would be the latest form of something people have described for a very long time.
vallee-s-invisible-college-research-grou: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in the 1970s the UFO researcher Jacques Vallee gave the name the Invisible College both to his independent working group of UFO researchers, which Michels says included the astronomer J. Allen Hynek, and to his book about what they learned. Michels explains the name as a tribute to Robert Boyle, the seventeenth century scientist, whose own circle of thinkers went by that name, casting the UFO researchers as a quiet society of investigators working outside the mainstream.
vallee-s-journals-pasulka-told-not-to-ta: Jason Samosa, a guest on Jesse Michels's podcast, says that the published journals of UFO researcher Jacques Vallée record a conversation with Diana Pasulka, a professor who studies belief in UFOs. According to Samosa, Pasulka explained in that talk that someone, he thinks a man named Tim Taylor, was telling her not to discuss the idea of human and alien hybrids. If true, it would suggest someone was trying to keep that subject quiet.
vallee-s-own-ufo-sighting-at-age-15-1950: Jacques Vallee, a French researcher who has studied UFO reports for decades, told Jesse Michels that he had his own sighting as a teenager in France in the 1950s. He says that at 15 he saw an object outside his room, over the yard. It is the personal starting point he gives for a lifetime of research.
vallee-s-study-of-small-ufo-religions-19: Jacques Vallee, a longtime researcher of UFOs, says that in the 1970s he spent a while going around visiting small UFO religions, groups built around belief in contact with beings from the sky. He says this work went into his books, among them one called Messengers of Deception.
vallee-s-the-invisible-college-1975: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, points to The Invisible College, a book he says the UFO researcher Jacques Vallee wrote in 1975. According to Michels, that book is still "the tip of the spear" in theory about UFOs today, meaning its ideas remain ahead of most current thinking.
vallee-says-there-are-protocols-for-leav: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, was talking about Plato's cave, an old philosophical image of prisoners who see only shadows on a wall and mistake them for reality. Michels says he asked Jacques Vallée, a veteran UFO researcher, whether there are protocols, set ways of stepping out of that cave into a truer view of reality, and that Vallée answered, "Yes, there are." If so, it would suggest there are known methods for seeing past our everyday picture of the world.
vallee-shows-pasulka-the-history-of-sata: A scholar named Diana Pasulka says that in the 2010s, while visiting the UFO researcher Jacques Vallée in his study in the San Francisco Bay Area, he showed her an odd book. She says it was a history of Satan, with the word Satan written across it in big letters, and she found the moment strange.
vallee-suspected-a-secret-real-project-b: Jacques Vallee, a French UFO researcher, says that in the 1960s he worked as best he could with Project Blue Book, the US Air Force's public study of UFO reports, while feeling that a real, secret project was running behind it. If true, it would mean the public study was not where the serious work happened. The podcast host Jesse Michels later said Vallee told him the same thing, as backing for another source's claim.
vallee-urges-hynek-to-review-blue-book-s: A documentary filmmaker, James Fox, told a podcast host, Jesse Michels, about a 1964 meeting at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base in Dayton, Ohio. Fox says that a researcher named Jacques Vallee had just met there with Dr. J. Allen Hynek, a scientist who worked with Project Blue Book, the US Air Force's UFO study of the 1950s and 60s. According to Fox, Vallee pushed Hynek to look again at the Blue Book cases the Air Force had filed away as 'psychological', because some of those reports might deserve to be taken seriously.
vallee-writes-the-foreword-to-the-french: A researcher of unexplained phenomena, Jacques Vallée, says that in the 2020s he read the second book by a writer named Rizwan Virk, and Virk then asked him to write the foreword for its French edition. Vallée says he agreed, because by then he was hooked. He tells it to show how strongly Virk's ideas had won him over.
van-allen-radiation-belt-impassable-1960: The podcast host Jesse Michels repeats a point he says another host, Danny Jones, raised on his own show. The point is about the Van Allen belts, zones of radiation that surround the Earth, and their namesake, the 1960s scientist James Van Allen. Michels says Van Allen stated the radiation there was about 150 times what a normal person can take, which would raise questions about how people could travel through it into space.
van-flandern-alerts-harrington-to-pionee: A researcher named Matt LaCroix says that in the 1980s an astronomer named Thomas Van Flandern called a colleague, Robert Harrington, at the US Naval Observatory and told him he had to look at data from Pioneer 10, a space probe sent to the far reaches of the solar system. According to LaCroix, the data hinted at an unknown planet beyond the Kuiper belt, the ring of icy bodies past Neptune. If true, it would mean a large hidden planet sits at the edge of our solar system.
van-flandern-and-harrington-both-die-of-: This story is about two American astronomers, Thomas Van Flandern and Robert Harrington. According to a researcher named Matt LaCroix, they led the search for an unseen planet, and possibly a companion star to our Sun. LaCroix says both men later died of throat cancer, and stresses that neither of them smoked. He tells it on the podcast of a host named Jesse Michels, in a 2024 episode about ancient history, and places the deaths roughly in the 1990s and 2000s. He gives no source when he first says it. Later in the same conversation he tells it again and points to a document called The Stage of Time, adding the detail about the binary star, meaning a second star paired with the Sun. People tell it because it hints that someone did not want that search to go on. So the story has one teller who tells it twice, once with no source and once naming that document.
van-flandern-s-speed-of-gravity-argument: Rupert Sheldrake, a researcher known for unusual ideas about science, mentioned this on the podcast of host Jesse Michels. Sheldrake says that a physicist named Van Flandern argued that gravity travels at least two billion times faster than light. If that were so, it would upend the common view that nothing moves faster than light.
van-tassel-s-contact-with-venusians-1950: A philosopher named Jason Jorjani says on Jesse Michels's podcast that in the 1950s an American man, George Van Tassel, claimed he was dealing with beings from the planet Venus. Jorjani brings it up as part of his argument that non-human beings have shaped human religion and belief, which is what it would mean if such contacts were real.
van-tassel-s-venusian-nordics-and-the-hy: The philosopher Jason Jorjani, on Jesse Michels's podcast, describes the beliefs of George Van Tassel, a man who held gatherings in the 1950s at Giant Rock, a huge boulder in the California desert. Jorjani says Van Tassel claimed that tall, fair beings from Venus, often called "Nordics," told him things about the origins of humans, including that some lower races were hybrids. If taken seriously, it would mean aliens had a hand in shaping humankind.
vandenberg-and-malmstrom-as-recurring-uf: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says Vandenberg, a military base in California used for rocket and missile launches, is one of a handful of places where UFO sightings keep happening over the years. He puts it alongside Malmstrom, an Air Force base in Montana that guards nuclear missiles. If true, it would suggest that whatever people are seeing takes a steady interest in these military sites.
vandenberg-ufo-takes-down-dummy-warhead-: In 1964, a man named Bob Jacobs worked as a photo instrumentation specialist, filming missile tests from Vandenberg Air Force Base in California. According to the tellings, he was about 100 miles up the coast at Big Sur with a telescope camera aimed at an Atlas missile carrying a dummy nuclear warhead. When the film was reviewed, they say, an object flew into the frame, chased the warhead at 6,000 to 8,000 miles an hour, circled it, fired a beam of light at it, and the warhead went down. If true, something unknown can knock out a nuclear weapon in flight. The podcast host Jesse Michels retells it many times, citing a researcher of UFOs and nuclear weapons, Robert Hastings, and Jacobs' DD214, his military discharge record. Ross Coulthart cites an Omni magazine article and puts the launch near Edwards instead, and a filmmaker, James Fox, also brings it up. Some tellings say only that the object circled the missile and was filmed, without saying it brought the warhead down.
vanessa-found-the-teller-tape-for-the-do: A man named Luigi, who spent time with Bob Lazar, a man at the center of UFO stories from Las Vegas in 1989, talks about the making of a documentary. He says a recording known as the teller tape would never have been found without a woman named Vanessa, who tracked it down.
vanguard-enterprise-nonprofit-for-uap-wh: Matthew Brown, presented as a former Pentagon insider turned whistleblower, told Jesse Michels in 2026 that he and a man named Dylan Borland started a nonprofit called Vanguard Enterprise, or Vanguard for short. He says another man, Jeffrey Nusatelli, has now joined. It is meant to support whistleblowers on UAP, the government's term for UFOs, meaning unidentified anomalous phenomena.
vannevar-bush-and-the-early-ufo-program-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, talks about Vannevar Bush, the author of a report called The Endless Frontier, and his place in an early secret US programme on UFOs in the 1940s and 1950s. According to Michels, a man named Robert Sarbacher said that Bush was part of that programme from the start. If true, it would put a leading figure of American science at the beginning of UFO secrecy.
vannevar-bush-s-post-war-science-structu: A mathematician and commentator named Eric Weinstein says on Jesse Michels's podcast that brilliant science administrators of the 1940s, such as Vannevar Bush, who ran US government science during the Second World War, built systems for organizing research that worked well. But, he says, they never passed down the knowledge of what those systems were for, so the systems keep running like a zombie. If true, it would mean nobody now fully understands the secret science structures still in place.
vannevar-bush-s-wartime-research-and-dev: Grant Cameron, a researcher who studies government UFO secrecy, told podcast host Jesse Michels about Vannevar Bush, who ran American wartime science during World War II. Cameron says Bush ran it all with professors pulled out of universities, and that officials then realised this was a great way to do secret research. Cameron tells it because, as he sees it, that model shaped how later hidden programmes were run.
varginha-being-taken-alive-to-regional-a: In 1996, people in the Brazilian town of Varginha say a strange creature was captured after an object came down nearby. James Fox, a documentary filmmaker who has investigated the case, says it has been known for decades that the being was still alive when it was first taken to the town's Regional hospital, and that it then ended up at a second hospital called Humanitas. If true, it would mean a living non-human being passed through ordinary local hospitals.
varginha-crash-and-captured-being-1996: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, retells a story from 1996 in Varginha, a town in Brazil, drawing on the work of a documentary filmmaker, James Fox. According to Michels, many separate sources describe a cigar-shaped object, something like the Tic Tac, a white oval craft shaped like the mint, falling from the sky with three beings coming out, one of whom was captured and taken to a hospital. He says everyone who worked at that hospital reports having seen the being, which, if true, would mean living non-human creatures were caught and handled by ordinary people.
varginha-et-as-a-national-celebrity-1996: Aldo Rebelo, a former Brazilian Defense Minister speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast, says the 1996 events in Varginha, a Brazilian town where many say a strange creature was captured, made a celebrity out of that creature. Brazilians know it as the Varginha ET, short for extraterrestrial, and he says it is still famous across the country.
varginha-neurosurgeon-and-new-witness-te: A documentary filmmaker, James Fox, revisits a 1996 case in the Brazilian town of Varginha, where people say a strange living creature was captured after a crash, in his film Moment of Contact. Fox says he gathered new testimony from two forensic pathologists, the local police chief, a new crash witness, and Italo Venturelli, the lead neurosurgeon at the regional hospital. If their accounts hold, it would mean a non-human being was taken into custody.
varginha-records-strictly-classified-at-: Aldo Rebelo, a former Brazilian Defense Minister speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast, says the information the Ministry of Defense holds about the 1996 events in Varginha, a town where many say a craft crashed and a creature was captured, is strictly classified. If true, it means the government has records of the event that the public cannot see.
varginha-town-hall-creates-a-ufo-museum-: Varginha is a town in Brazil where, in 1996, local stories say strange beings were seen and picked up. Speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast, Aldo Rebelo, a Brazilian official described as a former defense minister, says the town hall later opened a museum "to acknowledge and value the phenomenon." If he is right, a town government has openly treated the event as part of its official story.
varginha-witness-held-shape-returning-ma: The podcast host Jesse Michels says he interviewed a man who witnessed a reported crash of an unknown craft in 1996 near Varginha, a town in Brazil. According to Michels, the man says he held a piece of material from the crash, and when he bent or played with it, it went back to its original shape. Michels links this to similar accounts of strange metal, which would point to technology beyond anything known.
varginha-witnesses-in-dc-and-fbi-letter-: A US congressman named Eric Burles told Jesse Michels about the Varginha case, a 1996 UFO case from the town of Varginha in Brazil. He says that in the 2020s, people from Brazil connected to the case came to Washington, and he was there with filmmaker James Fox and journalist Leslie Keane, hearing from them after a meeting. If true, it would mean witnesses to a foreign case were being heard in the US capital.
vatican-archives-ceremony-with-bledsoe-s: Chris Bledsoe is a man who says he has had many encounters with UFOs. On a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, he passed on what he says he was told by two people, Diana Pasulka and Timothy Taylor: around 2017 there was a ceremony at the Vatican archives, the Catholic Church's historic record collection in Vatican City. As he tells it, his photo was put with a picture of the pope outside the archives and then placed between books by the astronomers Galileo and Copernicus, which would mean the Church gave his experiences real weight.
vatican-confiscated-the-fatima-prophecy-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, brings up the prophecies of Fatima, a town in Portugal where, in 1917, a group of children said they received messages from a heavenly visitor. He says the Vatican, the headquarters of the Catholic Church, confiscated one of those prophecies from the children who made it, which in his framing hints that something important about such visitations has been kept hidden.
vatican-dossier-and-joint-ss-italian-stu: Jason Jorjani, a researcher who writes about Nazi-era secret projects, told podcast host Jesse Michels about an object known as the Magenta object, said to have been studied in the 1930s and 1940s. Drawing on what a witness named David Grusch has said, Jorjani says the Vatican was informed of it, keeps a file on it, and took part in a joint working group of scientists from the SS, Nazi Germany's elite paramilitary force, and Italian scientists, meeting in a third country, which he links to Czechoslovakia. If true, it would mean an unexplained craft was being studied in Europe years before such stories became famous in America.
vela-incident-labeled-the-747-incident-1: Rolf Mowatt-Larssen is a former official of the CIA, the US foreign intelligence agency. On Jesse Michels' podcast he talked about the Vela incident, an event in 1979 over the South Atlantic that is linked in his telling to South Africa and Israel. He says an unnamed scientist from the US Department of Energy told him that insiders labeled it "the 747 incident", a hint that it was handled under a different name from the public one.
velikovsky-s-when-worlds-collide-the-ast: A lawyer and activist, Dan Sheehan, brought up an old book on the podcast of host Jesse Michels. Sheehan says the book, When Worlds Collide, was written by a writer named Immanuel Velikovsky. He says it puts forward the idea that the asteroid belt, the ring of rocky debris between Mars and Jupiter, is what is left of a planet that was destroyed, which would mean our solar system had a violent past.
vera-rubin-telescope-to-remove-classifie: This story is about the Vera Rubin Observatory, a large telescope that photographs the night sky, in the 2020s. An astronomer named Beatriz Villarroel, speaking with a podcast host, Jesse Michels, passes on what she says she was told. She says the telescope is going to remove many classified satellites and other objects from its data. Classified here means secret, run by governments and not made public. Months later, Michels comes back to it on his own show. He says all of the observatory's images have to be approved by the Pentagon, the US defence department, at a secure site in California, and he credits this to an article in The Atlantic magazine. If true, it would mean that what the public gets to see of the sky is filtered to hide certain objects in orbit.
verichip-implant-raytheon-lineage-and-re: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, talks about the VeriChip, a small chip implanted in the body, sold by a company called Applied Digital Solutions, which he connects to the defence company Raytheon. According to Michels, the chip came on the market in 2002, a few years before what happened to Gary McKinnon, a hacker who says he broke into NASA computers, in 2005. Michels suggests the timing may point to a kind of retaliation, which, if true, would tie the chip to how McKinnon was treated.
vesuvius-quiet-since-1948-and-accumulati: Filippo Biondi, a researcher who uses satellite radar to scan beneath the ground, spoke about Mount Vesuvius, the volcano beside Naples in Italy, on Jesse Michels's podcast. Biondi says the volcano has not smoked since 1948, and so, in his view, it is building up energy. He raises it as a sign that the volcano could be storing up for something larger.
vial-of-gold-flakes-it-s-all-about-the-m: Brent Freriedman, a writer on Dark Skies, a 1990s TV drama about UFOs, told podcast host Jesse Michels that in 1996 a visitor he calls the captain came to the show's offices in Los Angeles. walker-how-do-you-know-they-didn-t-get-u: Grant Cameron, a UFO researcher, told podcast host Jesse Michels about a talk he had around 1987 with Eric Walker, a man Cameron calls the head of the whole secret UFO effort. Cameron says that when he brought up MJ12, a group said to be a secret panel handling UFO matters, and the dead bodies said to come from crashes, Walker answered: "How do you know they're dead? You assume too many things and they're all wrong. How do you know they didn't get up and walk away?" If true, it would hint that beings from crashed craft lived.
walker-letter-worked-on-defense-policy-w: Grant Cameron is a researcher who has long studied UFO history. On Jesse Michels' podcast he described a letter by Eric Walker, a man he links to secret UFO work, in which Walker says he worked on defense policy in 1947 with Vannevar Bush, a top US government science adviser of that era. Cameron ties this to other papers about crashed discs that year, as a sign that Walker was placed close to where such secrets would have been kept.
wall-street-journal-emp-explanation-for-: In 1967, at Malmstrom, an Air Force base in Montana that housed nuclear missiles, others tell of missiles being shut down while a glowing object hovered nearby. The podcast host Jesse Michels says that a Wall Street Journal article, written by a reporter named Joel Shectman and linked by Michels to a man named Sean Kirkpatrick, explained the event as a test of an EMP, a burst of electromagnetic energy that can fry electronics. As Michels retells it, the article said the device was wheeled up to the base and knocked out the electronics with people present, and he calls the piece a deliberate disinformation hit job.
wall-street-journal-op-ed-and-david-sper: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says a friend of his, Karl Nell, planned an opinion piece about UFOs with a former US cabinet member, in one telling a former Secretary of Defense, and that Michels himself pushed the Wall Street Journal to publish it. He says the paper turned it down, and in one telling he ties the episode to a scientist, David Spergel, and how the subject was brushed aside.
wally-wallington-builds-a-stonehenge-in-: Luke Caverns, a researcher of ancient building methods, mentioned Wally Wallington on Jesse Michels's podcast. Caverns says Wallington is the man from the videos who raised a copy of Stonehenge, the ancient ring of giant standing stones in England, in his backyard by himself. He brings it up to show that huge stones can be moved by one person with simple methods.
walrus-artwork-on-epstein-s-wall-2002: Jay Anderson is a guest on Jesse Michels' podcast in an episode about the financier Jeffrey Epstein and claims of a secret elite group. He relayed what a woman named Juliet Byron, who says she was there, told him about a visit to an Epstein property around 2002. According to her, a large artwork on the wall showed a woman being raped by a walrus, which Anderson brings up as a sign of something dark in that circle.
walter-b-smith-1953-letter-on-using-the-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, points to a letter from Walter B. Smith, then head of the CIA, the US foreign intelligence agency, dated around 1953. Michels says it suggested using the UFO phenomenon as psychological warfare against the Soviet Union, and that similar leaked letters exist from Allen Dulles, who later led the CIA. In another telling he is less sure of the date and calls it a memo, but either way he offers it as a sign the government took the subject seriously early on.
walter-dornberger-at-wright-patterson-wh: On Jesse Michels's podcast, a writer named Peter Levenda says that Walter Dornberger, a German officer who ran the Nazi rocket base at Peenemünde, was first posted after coming to America to Wright-Patterson, an Air Force base in Ohio. Levenda says Dornberger was there in 1947 when debris from the reported crash near Roswell, New Mexico, arrived by train. If true, it would put a former Nazi rocket chief right beside the wreckage.
walter-haut-s-posthumous-affidavit-craft: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, cites Lieutenant Walter Haut, an officer at the Roswell base in New Mexico, where something is said to have crashed in 1947. According to Michels, Haut left a sworn statement, to be released only after his death, saying he had personally seen a craft and bodies under a tarp. If true, it would be an insider's word that a real crash with real bodies happened at Roswell.
wang-s-belongings-removed-from-his-house: Greg Bishop, a writer about UFO lore, spoke on Jesse Michels's podcast about a man named Eric Henry Wang. Bishop says he believes that when Wang died, people came and took a lot of things out of his house. He tells it as a hint that someone wanted whatever Wang had kept.
war-department-asks-fbi-to-clear-gebauer: A researcher named Scott Ramsay, speaking on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, describes an FBI file on a man named Leo GeBauer. Ramsay says that around 1942 or 1943 the War Department, the US government department that ran the Army at the time, asked the FBI, the US federal police agency then led by J. Edgar Hoover, to clear GeBauer for security. From this Ramsay concludes that GeBauer worked on some kind of top-level secret project, which, if so, would mean the government trusted him with serious work.
wargo-s-theory-that-remote-viewers-see-t: Eric Wargo, a writer on time and the mind, discussed Stargate, a US government programme from the 1970s to 1995 that tested remote viewing, the claimed ability to describe far-off places with the mind alone. Wargo suggests that what remote viewers really see may be the feedback they will be shown later, so they are glimpsing their own future. Podcast host Jesse Michels adds that Hal Puthoff, whom he calls the founder of the CIA's psychic spy programme, told him he was open to Wargo being right that such feedback is needed for it to work.
warning-call-after-a-howard-stern-produc: Dan Sherman, a former Air Force sergeant who says the NSA, the US government's eavesdropping agency, hired him to talk with aliens, says that about two years after his book came out he got a call from a producer of Howard Stern's radio show. Soon after, he says, someone else called his office and told him: "Drop the story. Don't go on the Stern show and stop talking about it." He told this to podcast host Jesse Michels as a sign that someone wanted him silent.
warning-not-to-disturb-the-earth-2016: Brandon Fugal, the owner of Skinwalker Ranch, a property in Utah known for reports of strange events, tells podcast host Jesse Michels about a warning someone gave him around 2016. As Fugal relays it, he was told that when you disturb the earth there, negative things happen, which would mean digging on the ranch could stir up trouble.
wartime-intelligence-agencies-run-by-fin: A researcher who goes by the name JASON, speaking on Jesse Michels' podcast, says that during World War II the United States had another, little-known spy agency aimed at South America, called the Office for the Coordination of Inter-American Affairs. He names William Donovan, Allen Dulles, Nelson Rockefeller, William Stephenson and Charles Hambro, and describes the wartime spy agencies of America and Britain as run by men from the world of money. If he is right, the same circle of finance and secrecy shaped the agencies that later kept UFO secrets.
was-condon-blackmailed-by-fbi-agent-guy-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, raises the idea that Edward Condon, a physicist who led a government-backed study that came out against UFOs, was blackmailed into doing so. Michels says that while Condon was being investigated in the 1950s for supposed communist sympathies, an agent of the FBI, the US federal police, named Guy Hottel was quietly building a file of reports on him. If true, it would mean the official dismissal of UFOs was pushed along by pressure on the man in charge.
was-randy-shown-alien-technology-as-a-re: Randy Anderson is a man who says he saw alien technology at a US military base, and a podcast host, Jesse Michels, interviewed him. Michels wonders aloud whether Randy, as a weapons expert, was shown the technology on purpose, as a test to see if he could figure out how it worked on the spot. In that view, his reaction would show officials how a foreign enemy might react if it got its hands on the same thing.
washington-post-lucky-to-be-alive-articl: A British biologist, Rupert Sheldrake, points to a Washington Post article called "Lucky to be alive" about the 9/11 attacks of 2001 on New York. He says it told the stories of people who did not go to work that day, which he offers as a sign that some people may sense danger before it happens.
washington-post-reporter-hunts-for-infor: Joe McMoneagle talks about a US government programme that tried to use psychics as spies. He says that at some point between the 1970s and the 1990s, a reporter from the Washington Post newspaper in Washington, DC started digging for information on it. If that is right, the secret programme was close to being exposed in the press.
washington-quickly-ordered-roswell-bottl: In 1947, something is said to have come down near Roswell, a town in New Mexico, and that event has become the most famous of all claimed UFO crashes. Kirk McConnell, described as a former US Senate staffer, told podcast host Jesse Michels that when Roswell allegedly happened, it took very little time for Washington to react. If true, it would mean the government moved to take control of the story almost at once.
watchers-flew-to-mount-hermon-in-advance: Tim Alberino, a researcher, talks on Jesse Michels' podcast about the Watchers, beings that the Book of Enoch, an ancient religious text, says came down to the summit of Mount Hermon. Alberino says he believes they arrived at the controls of advanced flying vehicles, what we would call UFOs today. If he were right, an ancient scripture would be describing a visit by craft from somewhere else.
watching-a-test-flight-with-john-lear-an: Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked on alien craft at a secret site in the Nevada desert, says that in March 1989 he took his friends John Lear and Gene Huff to a spot about 8 miles east of Groom Lake, home of Area 51, a secret US Air Force test base. He says they could watch a test flight because he had the test flight schedule. If true, it would mean he had real inside knowledge of when these craft flew.
watching-the-original-knapplazar-area-51: Peter Levenda, an author who writes about secret history, says that in 1989 he watched the original television broadcast in which a reporter, George Knapp, interviewed Bob Lazar, a man who said he had worked on alien craft near Area 51, a secret US Air Force base in Nevada. Levenda says that at the time no one knew what it meant. He tells it to mark how early that story reached the public.
watching-watergate-hearings-at-the-gold-: Dan Sheehan, a lawyer described on Jesse Michels's podcast as involved in many famous American cases, says that in 1973 he sat in the Gold Key Motel in Washington with his investigator, William Johnstone Taylor, watching the Watergate hearings, the Senate hearings into the scandal around President Nixon. He says that while they watched, the well-known lawyer F. Lee Bailey made a call from a pay phone, and he ties this scene to others in the case such as Gerald Alch and Senators Daniel Inouye and Sam Ervin.
water-damage-suggests-the-egyptian-monum: This story is about the ancient monuments of Egypt, especially the Great Sphinx, and the idea that marks on the stone show water damage. A podcast host named Jesse Michels says that two researchers, John Anthony West and Robert Schoch, think the monuments were built much earlier than usually believed because of this water damage. A researcher of ancient catastrophes named Randall Carlson tells it from his own study, saying he is convinced the marks are water erosion. Carlson points to the enclosure around the Sphinx, credits the earlier scholar Schwaller de Lubicz as well as West, and puts the work at about 12,000 years ago. So it comes from a host repeating others and from a researcher giving his own view. If true, it would mean a forgotten civilisation built these monuments long before the Egypt we know.
water-found-in-the-osiris-shaft-at-about: Filippo Biondi, a scientist who says he has scanned beneath the pyramids of Egypt, told podcast host Jesse Michels that there is water below the Great Pyramid at Giza. He says his team found water in the Osiris shaft, an underground shaft at Giza, at a depth of roughly 33 to 37 metres. If so, it would mean water runs beneath the pyramid area itself.
water-fuelled-microwave-electrothermal-t: John Brandenburg, a physicist, told podcast host Jesse Michels that he invented a spacecraft engine that uses water as fuel, heating it with microwaves to make thrust. He says he got it working and that it has now flown successfully in space on a craft from a company called Momentus.
water-through-piezoelectric-spirals-gene: Filippo Biondi, a scientist who says he has scanned beneath the pyramids of Egypt, offered a guess about spiral structures he links to the pyramid of Khafre at Giza. Drawing on ideas from another researcher, Christopher Dunn, he suggests that water may have flowed through these spirals, and that they may have been made of piezoelectric material, which gives off electricity when it is squeezed or stressed. If true, it would mean the pyramid worked as some kind of machine for making electricity.
watergate-document-shredding-at-bendix-a: Peter Levenda, an author who writes about secret history, says that in the 1970s he worked in Manhattan for Bendix, a defense and engineering company, and also recalls work tied to training troops in Saudi Arabia. He says that when Watergate broke, the political scandal around President Nixon, his whole division went wild over everything they had on paper, and the shredders ran overtime. He tells it as a first-hand look at how fast secrets get destroyed when trouble comes.
watergate-used-to-remove-nixon-over-disc: A researcher named Steven Greer, speaking on Jesse Michels' podcast, gives his own account of Watergate, the political scandal of 1972 to 1974 that brought down President Richard Nixon. Greer says the scandal, which the reporter Bob Woodward helped expose, was really a way to remove Nixon because Nixon was "hellbent on bringing this stuff out", meaning the truth about UFOs. If true, it would mean a president was pushed out of office to keep that secret.
we-are-watching-you-postcard-1995: A Los Angeles television writer, Bryce Zable, says that around 1995, a year before his UFO-themed TV show went ahead, while he was shooting its first episode, a postcard arrived at his home address. He says the front showed the cover of a book called Flying Eyes, with the words WE ARE WATCHING YOU. He tells it as a hint that someone was keeping an eye on people making UFO stories in Hollywood.
we-re-the-aquarium-1996: Bryce Zable, a writer who made the 1996 TV series Dark Skies about UFOs, says some visitors came to his Los Angeles offices that year. He says they asked if he had heard of "the Aviary", a group of insiders that had been talked about on a TV show, and then told him, "Well, we're the aquarium," which would mean a second hidden group interested in how Hollywood tells UFO stories.
weather-bureau-employees-see-four-metall: A researcher named Merrick, speaking on Jesse Michels' podcast, says that on 19 April 1947 two employees of the Weather Bureau, the US government's weather service, saw four metal discs that were flat on the bottom and domed on top. He brings it up next to the famous sighting by a man named Kenneth Arnold later that year, as a sign that people were seeing such discs even before Arnold's report.
weather-data-shows-strong-northerly-wind: FLIR1 is a short video shot in 2004 by the infrared camera of a Navy jet off Southern California, showing an object that some call the Tic Tac, a white oval shaped like the mint. A researcher named Merrick says on Jesse Michels' podcast that the weather records for that time and height show a very strong wind blowing from the north, and he credits a colleague named Yannick. That matters because it bears on whether the object was just drifting with the wind, like a balloon, or moving under its own power.
weather-observer-injured-in-an-encounter: Charles Hall is a former Air Force weather observer who says that in the 1960s, on the Indian Springs bombing ranges in Nevada, he spent years in contact with tall white aliens. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that one of the weather observers there was even injured in an encounter with something and was given a medical discharge from the service. He raises it as a sign that what happened at those ranges had real consequences for the men stationed there.
webster-hubbell-s-book-on-clinton-s-jfk-: Webster Hubbell was a close associate of President Bill Clinton in the 1990s, and the story is about a book he later wrote. A researcher named Steven Greer, who can't recall the book's title, says that in it Hubbell admits that he and the president were trying to get to the bottom of two things: who killed President John F. Kennedy and why, and what is going on with UFOs. A journalist, Jeremy Corbell, tells it differently. He doesn't mention the book or Kennedy, but he says Clinton really tried, and that Hubbell was "crushed down" after asking. Both men tell it on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, each from his own reading of events. Why it matters to them: if true, even a sitting president's people could not get answers about UFOs.
weekend-meeting-with-dick-cheney-on-why-: A former CIA officer, Rolf Mowatt-Larssen, says that in 2003 he met one weekend at the White House with Dick Cheney, then the US Vice President, whom he says he got to know exceptionally well. He says the talk was about why the Iraq war was being lost, and he writes about his career in his book, A State of Mind: Faith in the CIA. He tells it to show how close he stood to the top of US power.
weekly-odni-briefings-for-national-secur: Matthew Brown, described as a Pentagon whistleblower, says that national-security reporters go every week to places like the ODNI, the office that oversees America's spy agencies, to get briefed on what they will talk about the following week. He links this to "Mockingbird", a name taken from talk of a past CIA effort to steer the press. If true, it would mean the news on secret matters is shaped by the government in advance.
weinbrenner-deathbed-claim-of-et-bodies-: A researcher who goes by the online name UAPGerb (UAP is the government's newer term for UFOs) told podcast host Jesse Michels about a claim studied by fellow researchers Grant Cameron and Anthony Bragalia. According to that claim, a man named Weinbrenner said on his deathbed that dead extraterrestrials were kept at a facility in Utah, which UAPGerb says is Dugway Proving Ground, a military testing site there. If true, it would mean alien bodies are being held on a US military base.
weinstein-attends-ed-witten-s-first-stri: Eric Weinstein, a mathematician and commentator, says that in 1983, purely by accident, he was at the University of Pennsylvania for the first lecture by the leading physicist Ed Witten on string theory, the idea that nature's smallest pieces are tiny vibrating strings. He tells it as being present at the start of a movement that came to dominate physics.
weinstein-on-rogan-renaissance-technolog: The podcast host Jesse Michels says that Eric Weinstein, a researcher and his former colleague, has speculated on Joe Rogan's podcast that Renaissance Technologies, an investment firm on Long Island started by Jim Simons, quietly houses a secret physics program that employs top US experts in differential geometry, the mathematics of curved shapes and spaces. Weinstein himself, on Michels' show, calls the firm a "black hole" that hires exactly those specialists and says that if there is a secret program, he is pretty sure it is there. Michels later ties this to the hidden government UFO program, which would mean the physics behind it is being worked out at a private firm.
weinstein-s-government-funded-training-a: Eric Weinstein, a mathematician and commentator, says his graduate studies were paid for by the Office of Naval Research, a Navy science funder, and his later research post by the National Science Foundation, a US science funding agency. He believes he was also put on a Department of Energy grant, unusual for a mathematician, because his mentor-figure Isidor Singer had one. He finds it striking that none of these agencies now shows any interest in his physics ideas.
weinstein-tells-jim-simons-about-chern-s: Eric Weinstein, a mathematician and commentator, says that shortly before the mathematician and investor Jim Simons died in 2024, he more or less accused Simons of something, in a talk about Chern-Simons theory, a piece of math partly named after Simons, and the Einstein-Hilbert equations behind Einstein's gravity. He also mentions an invitation to the Simons Center at Stony Brook University. He tells it as part of his case that important physics was held back or overlooked.
weinstein-told-the-same-by-multiple-unre: A researcher named Eric Weinstein, speaking with podcast host Jesse Michels, says he has been told the same thing by several different people who have no connection to one another. He does not spell out here what that thing was. If true, it would mean separate sources were backing up the same account on their own.
wen-ho-lee-espionage-case-1980: John Herrington, a former US Secretary of Energy, told podcast host Jesse Michels about a spy case from his years in government. He says a spy named Wen Ho Lee was working inside the Energy Department at Livermore and Los Alamos, two of the country's nuclear weapons labs, and he links the story to Ed Meese, then a senior official.
wernher-von-braun-s-project-mars-and-a-l: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in 1952 Wernher von Braun, a former Nazi rocket engineer he calls the father of the American space program, published a science fiction novel called Project Mars: A Technical Tale. According to Michels, the book predicted a future mission to settle Mars led by a figure called Elon. He tells it in an episode about whether the mind can glimpse the future, since the name would then be an eerie piece of foresight.
westall-landing-and-intimidation-of-mr-g: James Fox, a documentary filmmaker, says he looked into the 1966 Westall incident in Australia, where a UFO is said to have landed. He says he got hold of a witness, Mr. Greenwood, who he says had been intimidated over what he knew. If true, it would mean someone worked to keep witnesses quiet.
westall-landing-case-two-witnesses-talk-: Westall is a suburb in Australia, and this story concerns a sighting there in 1966 near a school. A UFO documentary filmmaker, James Fox, says he went there to investigate what he calls a landing case from the 1960s and met witnesses who told him they had been going at it for 50 years. If true, it would be a craft seen by a large crowd in broad daylight. A debater named Merrick says 200 or 300 students and a teacher, depending on the account, saw a silver disc tilted on its side that then took off at 1,000 miles per hour, though he does not mention a landing. Fox, in another episode, puts the witnesses at 300-plus, watching the disc zip around the sky, and credits two researchers, Shane Ryan and James Rigney. A guest named Karl Nell brings it up as a near-identical match to another school sighting. All of this is told on the podcast of a host, Jesse Michels.
wewelsburg-castle-seances-of-himmler-s-s: Peter Levenda, an author who writes about secret history, says he visited Wewelsburg Castle in Germany for a TV piece some 10 to 20 years ago. He says that Heinrich Himmler, head of the SS, Nazi Germany's elite guard, took over the run-down castle in the 1930s, rebuilt it with concentration camp labor, and made a round table where his 12 "knights" sat to hold seances. He tells it to show how deep the Nazi leaders' interest in the occult ran.
weygandt-s-sergeant-responds-to-uapgerb-: A researcher who goes by the online name UAPGerb says that sometime in the 2020s he emailed people connected to a man named Weygandt, using his own UAPGerb email address. He says one of them, a sergeant who had served with Weygandt (he names Sergeant Atkins and Sergeant Allen), wrote back and signed with his full name. He told this on the podcast of host Jesse Michels, as a sign that the people around Weygandt were real and willing to answer.
what-happened-to-the-egg-shaped-craft-ba: A helicopter pilot named Jake Barber says he once flew in to pick up an egg-shaped craft that was not of human make. He says it was then taken to a secure facility, where it was either destroyed, hidden or buried, because, in his words, the people in charge already have so many of them that one more did not interest them. If true, it would mean such craft are common enough in secret hands to be thrown away.
wheeler-s-it-from-bit-paper-cites-observ: Don Hoffman, a scientist who studies perception, says the famous physicist John Wheeler cited his work in Wheeler's paper on "it from bit", the idea that reality grows out of information. Hoffman says the cited work was Observer Mechanics, a theory he built with Bruce Bennett and Chetan Prakash about how observers make up reality, and he tells it as a sign that serious physics took his ideas seriously.
when-prophecy-fails-1950s-ohio-ufo-cult: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, brings up When Prophecy Fails, a book about a group that formed in Ohio in the 1950s around beliefs tied to UFOs. He calls it a cult and mentions it while talking about how people hold on to beliefs about prophecies and a coming final event.
whistleblower-protections-gutted-from-th: Steven Greer, an activist who campaigns for UFO disclosure, says Congress needs to write protections into law for whistleblowers, insiders who come forward about secret UFO programmes. He says Congress almost did this in December 2023, with backing from the Senate Intelligence Committee, but the protections were gutted when the two chambers reconciled the National Defense Authorization Act, the yearly law that sets US military policy and budget.
whistleblower-saw-a-tic-tac-offloaded-fr: Steven Greer, an activist who campaigns for the release of UFO secrets, told podcast host Jesse Michels about a whistleblower, someone who quietly came forward from inside. Greer says this person saw a Tic Tac, a white oval object shaped like the mint, being unloaded from a big ship, in 1991 as far as Greer remembers. If true, it would mean such an object was physically in someone's hands decades ago.
whistleblower-threatened-with-planted-ch: Steven Greer, an activist who campaigns for the release of UFO secrets, tells of a whistleblower who was getting ready to testify in Washington, DC. According to Greer, an SUV pulled up outside the man's home while his wife was at work and their two young sons were there, and the people in it told him to check his phone and computer, where they had planted child pornography. Greer tells it as an example of how far some would go to keep people from speaking.
whistling-ufo-seen-near-aztec: An unnamed witness near Aztec, New Mexico, where a UFO crash is said to have happened, told podcast host Jesse Michels about a UFO he saw there. He points to the direction it came from and says it made a sound almost like whistling.
white-horse-hills-5-300-m-from-the-avebu: Geoffrey Drumm, a researcher who says an alien told him the true purpose of the pyramids, points to the white horse hills of Wiltshire, England, hillsides marked with large figures of horses, several of which lie near the ancient Avebury stone circle complex. He says the distance between them is 5,300 metres, which he notes is exactly 3.3 miles. To him, the number suggests the ancient builders planned these sites with deliberate measurements.
white-house-ai-timeline-manipulator-2020: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, speaking in 2026 and citing a man named Matthew Brown, mentions talk of something like a White House "timeline manipulator", described as an artificial intelligence that could shape the course of events. He leaves it at that brief remark, without saying more about how it would work. If true, it would mean powerful technology at the very top of government was steering the future.
white-house-asks-the-congressman-to-prai: A member of the US Congress, Eric Burlison, says that in 2026 the White House called him the day before the president was due to release information on UFOs. He says they asked him to say some positive things about the release the next day. He mentions fellow members of Congress Anna Paulina Luna and Tim Burchett, and tells it as a look at how the White House handled the release behind the scenes.
white-house-registers-aliens-gov: A podcast host named Jesse Michels mentions, almost in passing, that the White House has registered the web address aliens.gov, which uses the .gov ending reserved for US government websites. He brings it up in an episode with a former head of the National Security Agency, the US spy agency that intercepts communications. He doesn't say when it happened or what the site is for, but he treats it as a hint that the government may be getting ready to say something about aliens.
white-house-request-for-presidential-ufo: A member of the US Congress, Eric Burlison, says that in 2025 he asked the White House for a full briefing on UFOs, the same top-level briefing the president gets on the subject, along with visits to related sites. He tells it as part of his push to get lawmakers access to what the government knows.
white-sands-near-earth-satellite-search-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in 1953 a very unusual project began at White Sands Missile Range, a military testing ground in New Mexico. As he tells it, two scientists, Lincoln LaPaz and Clyde Tombaugh, led a search for unknown small objects circling close to Earth, and he points to the project's final report. If true, it would mean the military took seriously the idea that something was already orbiting our planet.
whitley-strieber-chosen-as-a-disclosure-: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, talks about Whitley Strieber, a horror writer known for his 1980s book Communion, about his reported encounters with strange beings. Michels says Strieber believes that 'they' chose him as a communication node for disclosure, meaning a channel for slowly revealing a non-human presence to the public, and the story holds that a horror writer was picked on purpose.
whitley-strieber-s-abduction-books-and-f: The podcast host Joe Rogan, talking with fellow host Jesse Michels, brings up Whitley Strieber, a writer who, as Rogan puts it, made movies and books in the 1980s about being abducted by aliens. Rogan mentions him as a well-known person who says this happened to him.
whitley-strieber-s-blue-beings-the-cobal: Jeffrey Mishlove, a researcher with a doctorate who studies psychic experiences, tells podcast host Jesse Michels that the writer Whitley Strieber talks about a kind of being that Strieber calls the cobalts. The name points to beings described as blue. Mishlove brings them up as one more type of visitor that people say they have met.
whitley-strieber-s-ear-implant-evaded-th: Whitley Strieber, an author who has written about his own encounters with non-human visitors, says he has an implant in his ear, and the podcast host Jesse Michels says it shows up on an x-ray. Strieber says that in San Antonio, Texas, while his wife Anne filmed, a doctor named Roger Leir found a white disc, and when it was touched with a probe it sank down into his earlobe. Michels says he has seen the video and that the object seems to move on its own, dodging the surgeon.
whitley-strieber-s-traumatic-abduction-w: Jeffrey Mishlove, a researcher with a doctorate who studies psychic experiences, tells podcast host Jesse Michels about the writer Whitley Strieber, who says he was abducted and anally raped by the beings that took him. According to Mishlove, Strieber still puts ointment on the wounds decades later, yet he calls the whole experience a communion. Mishlove offers it to show how an encounter can be both terrible and, to the person, deeply meaningful.
whitley-strieber-s-uncle-worked-with-gen: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says the writer Whitley Strieber, author of the book Communion about his reported encounters with strange beings, talks about an uncle who worked very closely with a General Exon at Wright Field, a military airfield in Ohio, in the 1940s. As told, this would tie Strieber's own family to the military world his story touches.
whitley-strieber-tries-to-steal-the-craf: Grant Cameron, a UFO researcher, tells podcast host Jesse Michels something the author Whitley Strieber told him. According to Cameron, Strieber said that when he was near a craft he decided he was going to steal it, and then somebody behind him started laughing. If true, it would mean Strieber was close enough to an unknown craft to try to take it, and that someone else was there watching.
who-ran-the-cia-weird-desk-1960: Grant Cameron, a researcher of UFO history, told podcast host Jesse Michels who he believes ran the "weird desk" at the CIA, the US spy agency: an informal post handling strange subjects such as UFOs. He says it was first Arthur Lundahl, then Kit Green, then Ron Pandolfi, starting around the 1960s. If true, it would mean someone inside the CIA has been quietly keeping track of the subject for decades.
whole-earth-catalog-page-187-15th-centur: A man named Brent says that a couple of weeks after a strange encounter of his own, he went into the Soap Plant bookstore on Melrose in Los Angeles. He says page 187 of the Whole Earth Catalog, a well-known counterculture guide to books and tools, led him to an out-of-print book of 15th-century Scandinavian ghost stories. In it he found a tale called the "Witch Rider," which he tells as an old echo of what happened to him.
why-borland-came-forward-lives-in-danger: Dylan Borland, a former government worker who says he was told secrets about non-human beings, told podcast host Jesse Michels why he came forward in 2023. He says whistleblowers linked to a Pentagon group studying UAP, short for unidentified anomalous phenomena, the official term for UFOs, said people's lives were in danger, and that a colleague who had been given access to the secrets lost their job. He mentions Matthew Sullivan and the whistleblower David Grusch as part of that story, which if true would mean people are being punished for knowing too much.
why-dopsr-let-grusch-talk-about-downed-c: Jake Barber, a helicopter pilot who says he helped retrieve a UFO, talks with podcast host Jesse Michels about David Grusch, a former intelligence official who said publicly in 2023 that the US has several crashed craft and has recovered dead pilots from them. Barber explains why the Pentagon office that reviews what former staff may say in public, called DOPSR, let Grusch say this, and says that is why the picture is confusing. If true, it would mean the government cleared those claims for release on purpose.
why-site-november-5-was-targeted-1977: Mario Woods, a former US Air Force man, describes a 1977 event at a nuclear missile site called November 5, part of the missile field run from Ellsworth Air Force Base in South Dakota. Speaking on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, he asks why that site would have been picked, and says it was the closest to a town, the closest to the control centre that runs the missiles, and the quickest to reach from the other nine missiles. In his view the choice was deliberate, which would mean whatever came there knew the layout of the base.
wife-s-matching-dream-of-number-cubes-at: Rolf Mowatt-Larssen, a former CIA officer, tells podcast host Jesse Michels that in 1978 in Schwandorf, Germany, his wife had a dream that matched his own dream of cubes covered in numbers at a church. He says she described walking up in dim light, with only a few lights on the side of the church, and seeing his desk. Shared dreams like this, if true, would suggest two minds can reach the same place in sleep.
wife-s-wedding-ring-moved-and-found-by-p: Brandon Fugal, owner of a Utah property called Skinwalker Ranch that is known for strange reports, tells podcast host Jesse Michels that around 2024 his wife Kristen's wedding ring was moved at their home. As he relays it, the ring was found again through prayer, which would mean the strangeness is not limited to the ranch.
wikileaks-email-hillary-clinton-asks-abo: Tim Alberino, a researcher, tells podcast host Jesse Michels about emails released in 2016 by WikiLeaks, a website that publishes leaked documents. He says there was allegedly an email in which the American politician Hillary Clinton asked about the tomb and body of Gilgamesh, a king from ancient legend, in Iraq, which would mean top officials took that ancient story seriously.
wilbert-smith-document-naming-von-neuman: An unnamed researcher on podcast host Jesse Michels's show says someone found a document tied to Wilbert Smith, a Canadian government engineer. According to the researcher, it claims that three top American scientists, the mathematician John von Neumann, the physicist Robert Oppenheimer and the science chief Vannevar Bush, were on a team taking apart and trying to copy, or 'reverse engineer', the craft said to have crashed near Roswell, New Mexico in 1947. If true, some of the greatest minds of the age worked on a recovered craft in secret.
wilbert-smith-s-1950-canadian-memo: A UFO researcher, Steven Greer, told podcast host Jesse Michels about a 1950 document from the Canadian government. Greer says it records what a Canadian named Wilbert Smith said, that it was top secret, and that it seems to have been declassified by accident.
