He says he put it in his own briefing document, because it would show a government was discussing UFOs in secret as early as 1950.
wilbert-smith-s-secret-role-running-radi: Grant Cameron, a UFO researcher, tells podcast host Jesse Michels what a man named Art Bridge told him about Wilbert Smith, a Canadian who worked in Ottawa in the 1950s. According to Bridge, Smith had a very high security clearance and ran radio monitoring in Ottawa, which would make Smith a real government insider rather than an outsider.
wild-bill-donovan-and-the-original-crash: William "Wild Bill" Donovan led the OSS, America's spy agency in World War Two, and helped found the CIA that came after it. The podcast host Jesse Michels, drawing on a journalist named Chris Sharp, says Donovan was probably involved in recovering a crashed craft in Magenta, Italy, in the 1930s or 40s, and in writing the first US rules for retrieving crashed UFOs. Michels adds that Donovan was also a Knight of Malta, a member of an old Catholic order, which matters if one thinks such groups shaped the secrecy.
wild-bill-donovan-parachutes-in-with-a-b: Joe McMoneagle, a guest on Jesse Michels' podcast, tells a story about Bill Donovan, the American spy chief, during the Second World War. McMoneagle says that Donovan parachuted into Vietnam with a very rare butterfly collection taped to his chest as a gift for Ho Chi Minh, the Vietnamese leader, which would mean the US had close, friendly contact with him back then.
wilder-penfield-and-false-memories: Wilder Penfield was a brain surgeon whom a podcast host, Jesse Michels, describes as involved in early mind control work. In a conversation about false memories, Michels says Penfield's work shows the idea holds true in mice. He brings it up to suggest that memories can be planted or changed, which would matter for people who say their own memories of strange events may have been altered.
willcutts-review-of-forrestal-s-death-19: Richard Dolan, a UFO historian, talks on Jesse Michels' podcast about the 1949 death of James Forrestal, the US Secretary of Defense, at Bethesda Naval Hospital in Maryland. Dolan says the authorities followed up with an investigation, which he thinks is called the Willcutts review, and that he has read most of its transcript. He brings it up as part of his argument that Forrestal's death may be tied to UFO secrets.
william-barr-interviews-epstein-s-cellma: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells a story from 2019 about Jeffrey Epstein, a man who died in a New York jail cell. Michels says that William Barr, who was the attorney general (the top US law officer) under President Trump, went to the cell himself after Epstein died to question his last known cellmate, a man named Efrain Reyes. According to Michels, Reyes seemed to doubt that Epstein had killed himself, which would matter because it raises the question of whether the death was really a suicide.
william-dudley-pelley-s-star-guests-and-: A philosopher, Jason Jorjani, told podcast host Jesse Michels about an American named William Dudley Pelley. Jorjani says that while Pelley was in prison, apparently in the 1940s, he wrote a book called Star Guests, and that it gave rise to a religion called Soulcraft. Jorjani discusses this in his own book, Closer Encounters, as an example of contact with beings from beyond shaping a belief system.
william-gunston-s-tower-of-london-remark: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, quotes William Gunston, a British writer who did a history of aircraft engine technology for Air International magazine. According to Michels, when Gunston came to the subject of electrically charged wing edges, he held back, saying he didn't want to end up in the Tower of London, the old fortress once used as a royal prison. The remark is told as a hint that some secret flight technology was off limits to talk about.
william-morris-davis-s-paper-the-value-o: Randall Carlson, a researcher of ancient catastrophes, tells podcast host Jesse Michels about a well-known paper by William Morris Davis, an American scientist who studied landforms, called 'The Value of Outrageous Geological Hypotheses', from the 1920s. Carlson says it is easy to find online and recommends reading it. He uses it to argue that wild-sounding ideas deserve a fair hearing in science.
william-steinman-pushed-out-of-aerospace: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells of a UFO researcher named William Steinman, who he says worked in the aerospace industry in the 1980s. In one episode Michels says Steinman was pushed out because of his UFO research and could never get an aerospace job again. In another he says Steinman worked at Skunk Works, the secret aircraft design division of the company Lockheed, was looking into the subject there, and was fired. If true, the story would suggest that asking about UFOs could end a career in the industry.
william-steinman-s-call-with-eric-walker: This story is about a phone call between a UFO researcher, William (Bill) Steinman, and Eric Walker, who is described as a former president of Penn State, a university in the United States. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that another man, Robert Sarbacher, had described someone like Walker as being involved in secret UFO matters. Michels also says that when Steinman asked Walker directly about Majestic 12, said to be a secret group in charge of the subject, Walker replied that he had known about them for decades. A researcher, Grant Cameron, tells the call in more detail. He dates it to 1987 and says Walker answered, "I was there. So what?" and then, "I've known of them for 40 years. Leave it alone." Cameron says this convinced him that papers known as the MJ12 documents, said to describe the group, were the real deal. Michels's first telling also mentions talk of psychic abilities, while Cameron focuses on the admission. If true, it would mean a respected university leader confirmed a hidden government UFO group.
william-steinman-s-foia-requests-reveal-: A researcher who goes by UAPGerb tells podcast host Jesse Michels that an Army unit called the IPU, short for Interplanetary Phenomenon Unit, came to light in 1986 and 1987. According to UAPGerb, researchers such as William Steinman found it by filing requests under FOIA, a US law that lets anyone ask for government records. If true, it would mean the Army once had a unit set up to look into these matters.
william-stephenson-s-caribbean-activitie: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, speaking in an episode about Jeffrey Epstein and aliens, describes a man named William Stephenson who, he says, was busy in and around the Caribbean, the Bahamas and the Virgin Islands from the 1940s on. Michels links Stephenson to the American spy chief Bill Donovan, to scientists such as the electrical engineer Charles Steinmetz and the inventor Townsend Brown, and to the businessman Robert Maxwell. He tells it to suggest a long, hidden web tying intelligence work, unusual science and later figures together.
william-stephenson-telegram-about-townse: Podcast host Jesse Michels says that near the end of World War Two, an American scientist named Thomas Townsend Brown went behind enemy lines into Nazi Germany to retrieve technology. Michels says there is a telegram from William Stephenson, a wartime intelligence figure, to Brown's wife Josephine, telling her that her husband is okay. In one telling he credits a researcher named Jan Lundquist for this. In another he just quotes the telegram and calls the trip a tech retrieval mission, and he offers it as proof that Brown took part in secret wartime work.
wilson-denied-need-to-know-though-the-pr: A physicist named Eric Davis says that in 1997 Thomas Wilson, a senior officer at the Defense Intelligence Agency (the US military's intelligence arm), was told he had no "need to know" about a secret program. Davis says this happened even though the program's money came out of Wilson's own director's budget. If true, it would mean the program was hidden even from the man paying for it.
wilson-green-works-with-puharich-at-the-: An unnamed researcher tells podcast host Jesse Michels that in the 1950s a man named Wilson Green worked with Andrija Puharich, a scientist who studied psychic abilities, at the Round Table, Puharich's private research lab. The guest says the two of them were trying everything there, and points to Puharich's own journals. It is told as part of the story of how that group came to believe it was in contact with non-human beings.
wilson-meeting-at-the-eg-g-parking-lot-w: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, talks about the Wilson memo, a set of notes said to record a 2002 meeting between a physicist, Eric Davis, and a Navy admiral, Thomas J. Wilson, about secret programs studying unexplained craft. Michels says the meeting took place in a parking lot belonging to EG&G, a defense contractor, which he believes is where Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked on alien craft, was employed. If so, it would tie two of the best-known stories in this field to the same spot.
wilson-memo-on-a-private-aerospace-rever: The Wilson memo is a set of leaked notes said to describe a secret 1997 meeting between Admiral Thomas Wilson, then head of intelligence for the Joint Chiefs of Staff, the top US military leaders, and a physicist named Eric Davis. According to Davis, Wilson said he had tried to get into a secret program run by a private aerospace company and met its program manager, security chief, lawyer and chief scientist. After much arguing, Davis says, they told him it was crash retrieval, a program holding non-human technology from off-world, and still refused him access. If true, a private company holds alien technology beyond the reach of top military officials. The podcast host Jesse Michels says the meeting took place in the parking lot of a contractor called EG&G, that Wilson was furious, and that the notes were found at the home of a man named Edgar Mitchell. Davis himself says the notes are real and 100 percent accurate, and an online researcher known as UAPGerb backs the core fact, though he places Wilson as deputy director of the Defense Intelligence Agency. One telling dates the memo to 2002 rather than 1997, and Jeremy Corbell, who also discusses UFOs on the show, says he knew about it long before, through Mitchell.
wilsondavis-meeting-outside-eg-g-las-veg: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells of what he calls an infamous meeting between a scientist named Eric Davis and Admiral Thomas Wilson, a Navy officer who Michels says oversaw basically all American military technology at the time. He places it outside the Las Vegas special projects headquarters of EG&G, a defense contractor, and dates it to around 2002, though it is also given as 1997. Michels tells it as an important moment in the story of secret programs connected to UFOs.
winged-orange-glowing-beings-over-skywat: Chris Bledsoe, a man who says UFOs seem to show up around him, hosts skywatches, night gatherings where people watch the sky together. On a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, he says that at these gatherings in recent years they have seen orange glowing beings that seem to have wings, as many as 20 at once, flying about 25 feet over their heads. If true, it would mean the visitors come close to whole groups of people on purpose.
wiseman-fails-to-replicate-sheldrake-s-p: Michael Shermer, a researcher known as a skeptic, says on Jesse Michels' podcast that Rupert Sheldrake ran experiments in England suggesting a dog could sense things it had no ordinary way of knowing. Shermer says another researcher, Richard Wiseman, ran the exact same experiments, published them, and got no results, which in his view undercuts the claim that such psychic powers are real.
wishbone-and-spire-structures-on-lunar-f: Maaneli Derakhshani, speaking on Jesse Michels' podcast, points to images of the far side of the Moon showing a wishbone-shaped structure, spire-like shapes, and features in what he calls the Paris Sea and other craters with unusually precise geometry. He suggests these could be ruins left from millions or billions of years ago, which would mean someone built things on the Moon long before us.
with-aquino-at-the-afio-meeting-in-las-v: An author who writes about the history of intelligence and the occult, Peter Levenda, says a man named Michael Aquino once told him they were going to Las Vegas for a meeting of the Association of Former Intelligence Officers, a club of retired spies. Levenda says he went along, and he names John Alexander in the story, telling it as a glimpse of the circles these men moved in.
witkowski-on-the-bell-project-staff-1940: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that a Polish journalist named Igor Witkowski documented who worked on the Bell, said to be a secret Nazi German project of the 1940s. According to Michels, Witkowski found that the lead figure was Ernst Grawitz, a medical chief of the SS (the Nazi party's armed elite force), and in one telling Michels adds that Grawitz worked directly under Josef Mengele, the Nazi camp doctor. Michels tells it as part of the case that Nazi Germany ran a hidden program to build a flying machine of unusual design.
witness-burns-as-blue-shifted-light-from: David Grusch, a former intelligence official who says the US holds recovered craft, tells podcast host Jesse Michels his idea for why some witnesses get burned near these objects. He suggests the craft may sit inside a warp bubble, a pocket of bent space, which squeezes ordinary visible light into ultraviolet light, so people end up with what is literally a sunburn. If true, it would tie witness injuries to the way the craft move.
witness-count-for-the-varginha-ship-and-: In 1996, in the town of Varginha in Brazil, people say a strange craft was seen and alien beings were captured. A researcher, James Fox, told podcast host Jesse Michels that maybe 12 to 15 witnesses saw the ship, and up to five saw an alien body. To him, those numbers mean the story rests on more than one or two people.
witness-ed-34b-and-40b-scrubbed-from-air: A researcher who goes by the online name UAPGerb told podcast host Jesse Michels about a witness he covered, codenamed Ed. Ed spoke of a joint reverse engineering program, meaning an effort to study and copy unknown technology, between the Nevada Test and Training Range, a large military range in Nevada, and Edwards Air Force Base in California, linked to $34 billion and $40 billion said to have been scrubbed from Air Force books between 2012 and 2016. If true, it would mean huge sums were hidden to fund the work.
witness-ed-contacts-greer-over-suppresse: An online UFO researcher known as UAPGerb tells podcast host Jesse Michels about a witness called Ed. According to UAPGerb, Ed said he reached out to Steven Greer, a campaigner for UFO disclosure, partly because zero-point energy systems, devices said to draw power from empty space, were being built and kept hidden. If true, it would mean a powerful energy technology is being held back from the public.
witness-ed-tests-reverse-engineered-vehi: A researcher who goes by the online name UAPGerb told podcast host Jesse Michels about a witness codenamed Ed. According to UAPGerb, from about 1998 to 2002 Ed was briefed into secret programs while serving at Nellis Air Force Base in Nevada, under the 98th Range Wing, the unit that runs the military ranges there, where vehicles built by copying unknown technology were said to be tested. If true, it would mean the US has been flying such craft for decades.
witness-hears-a-buzzing-like-machine-bee: In a podcast episode hosted by Jesse Michels, an unnamed witness describes hearing a sound from the direction of a craft. They say it was a buzzing noise, a little like mechanical bees. No time or place is given, but the detail is offered as a sign that the craft was a real, physical machine.
witness-returns-with-luiza-and-sees-crea: An unnamed witness from the town of Varginha, Brazil, says that around January 20, 1996, they went back with a woman named Luiza to the spot where a strange creature had been seen. The witness says that in that very spot they saw the creature's footprint and will never forget it. This is one of several stories from Varginha that winter about a living creature, said to be not from Earth, being seen and captured.
witness-saw-lazar-at-s-4-getting-on-a-bu: A filmmaker, Jeremy Corbell, told podcast host Jesse Michels about support for Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked on alien craft in the late 1980s at S-4, a site said to sit near Area 51, a secret military base in Nevada. Corbell says he got a man to go on the television show Ancient Aliens and testify publicly that he saw Lazar there, getting on a bus. If true, it would back up Lazar's claim that he really worked at the site.
witnessed-drowning-suicide-and-va-denial: Dylan Borland, a former member of the US Air Force, says that around 2015, after he left the service, he saw a man drown himself in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, with several other people watching, and that he has the police report. He says the VA, the US agency that cares for military veterans, denied parts of his service, and he points to his enlisted performance review, a routine Air Force job evaluation, and his VA medical records as backing. He tells it as part of his case that his record and his experiences are real.
witnesses-split-up-and-reassigned: John Blitch, a scientist who once worked with DARPA, the Pentagon's advanced research agency, and who says he was abducted by an alien, told podcast host Jesse Michels how the military handles witnesses. He says people who saw something together, such as Terry and Toby, or Mario Woods and Michael Johnson, were split up and reassigned so they could not talk to each other. If true, it would mean witnesses are deliberately kept apart.
witten-townsend-brown-s-antigravity-bism: Podcast host Jesse Michels relays what a physicist named Louis Witten said about the 1950s. According to Michels, Witten said he was hired through Wright Field, a US Air Force base, to work on gravity, with a link to the Martin Corporation, an aircraft maker. Witten also said a man named T. Townsend Brown had an unusual form of the metal bismuth that seemed to resist gravity, which would mean antigravity research was quietly under way back then.
wobbling-craft-may-have-gone-into-autopi: In 1948, near Aztec, New Mexico, a craft is said to have crashed with alien bodies inside. Scott Ramsay, a researcher who has spent years on the case, told podcast host Jesse Michels of a theory that because the craft was wobbling as it flew past the Archuleta Ranch, it may have switched into some kind of autopilot. That would explain how it came down where it did.
woman-saw-three-plus-signs-rolling-on-ro: A UFO researcher named Clas Svahn tells of a woman in Sweden who, sometime in the 1930s, says she saw three objects shaped like plus signs rolling along a road. Svahn passes this on second-hand, from someone he spoke to, and mentions calling his mother about it. If true, it would be a strange sighting from long before UFOs were widely talked about.
woman-tries-to-kidnap-bledsoe-after-a-co: Chris Bledsoe, a man who says UFOs seem to show up around him and who now speaks about it in public, tells this on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels. He says that after giving a talk at a conference, which he names as an event he calls the PSI games, held this year, a frantic woman ran up to him as he walked out the door and tried to kidnap him. He tells it as an example of the strange and sometimes risky attention his story brings him.
woman-with-black-undulating-eyes-at-foot: Brent Freriedman, a writer who works around Hollywood, told the podcast host Jesse Michels about a strange night in his bedroom. He says he was reading in bed, lowered the paper, and saw a woman standing at the foot of the bed. In one telling her eyes were two black circles that seemed to ripple and move. He tells it as a first-hand meeting with something that was not an ordinary person. He describes it twice in the same conversation, and the second time the details shift. There her eyes looked like the cosmos, she pinned him to the bed, and he places it in a small house off Melrose, a Los Angeles street, early in his writing career. In that version he calls her the witch rider.
women-believe-their-eggs-were-harvested-: On a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, about the late financier Jeffrey Epstein, a guest named Jay Anderson passes on what a woman named Juliet Byron told him: that she and some other women believe their eggs were taken from them at a ranch in New Mexico called Zorro Ranch. Byron, speaking for herself, says she was taken there in September 2002, and links it to reports that the first cloned baby, called Eve, was born that December, after which, she says, nobody heard anything more. If true, it would mean women were secretly used for a human cloning effort.
woods-s-partner-frozen-at-the-wheel-1977: Mario Woods, a former US Air Force man who served at Ellsworth Air Force Base in South Dakota, describes a strange night there in 1977 on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels. He says his partner, Michael Johnson, froze in place at the steering wheel of their vehicle, so stiff that Woods even tried and failed to pull his hand off it. He tells it as part of an encounter he believes involved something not human taking control of them.
woomera-range-chief-s-grandfather-in-sec: Ross Coulthart, a journalist, tells podcast host Jesse Michels about Rhys Dalton Morgan, whose grandfather ran the Woomera range, a military rocket testing site in Australia. According to Coulthart, the grandfather also took part in secret British government investigations of UFOs in Britain in the late 1940s and 1950s. If true, it would mean Britain was quietly studying UFOs very early on.
workers-had-severe-reactions-to-touching: Bob Lazar says he worked on alien spacecraft in the late 1980s at a secret site called S4 in the Nevada desert. Talking to a podcast host, Jesse Michels, he passes on what someone there told him: some workers had severe physical reactions just from touching the craft. If true, it would mean the craft were made of, or carried, something harmful to the human body.
working-beside-hunt-s-cia-colleague-arth: An author who writes about intelligence history, Peter Levenda, says that around 1979 and 1980 he worked in Queens, New York, alongside a man named Arthur Hawkberg. Levenda says he later learned Hawkberg had been a colleague of E. Howard Hunt, a CIA officer, at a front company called the Robert Mullen Corporation in Washington, DC. He tells it as an example of how close he came to the secret world without knowing it.
working-next-to-the-z-machine-at-sandia: John Brandenburg, a scientist, says on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels that he used to work next to the Z machine, a large experimental machine at Sandia National Laboratories, a US government research lab in New Mexico. He mentions it to show his own background in serious government science.
world-commerce-corporation-founded-1945: A researcher, Jason Simosa, says that in 1945 a company called the World Commerce Corporation was set up, with a board that included men named Donovan, Stephenson and Hambro, and with Allen Dulles as legal counsel. In one telling he adds that it was rebranded in 1947 and places it in Panama, crediting the writers Peter Levenda and Peter Dale Scott, while in another he lists a man named Ambrose on the board and ties in the inventor Townsend Brown. He tells it to show a private network of wartime intelligence figures that, if real, could have handled secret matters outside government view.
world-commerce-corporation-maynard-corpo: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, describes how his guest, a former Pentagon official named Matthew Brown, places a hidden international network inside the World Commerce Corporation, which Michels calls a Caribbean cluster of shell companies, linked in the telling to the Maynard Corporation. Names raised include Otto Scorzani and others, with a nod to a book called Secret Machines. If true, it would mean a private web of companies working behind the scenes, out of public view.
world-forum-created-by-mikhail-gorbachev: A man named Chris Bledsoe, speaking on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, says there was a World Forum created by Mikhail Gorbachev, the former Soviet leader, back in the 1990s. According to Bledsoe, it was a five-year event, running from 1995 to 2000, that ended in New York City when the ball dropped on New Year's Eve. He tells it as part of a wider story about powerful people and hidden plans.
world-tree-myth-of-survivors-climbing-in: Randall Carlson, a researcher, says on Jesse Michels' podcast that stories told around the world include one about a world tree: after a great catastrophe and flood, humanity climbs the tree into the heavens. He tells it as a possible memory, kept in myth, of people surviving a real ancient disaster.
world-war-ii-foo-fighters-1940: During World War II, pilots reported strange lights or objects following their planes, which came to be called foo fighters. Michael Shermer, a researcher known as a skeptic, says during a debate on Jesse Michels' podcast that it would be good to get explanations for what those pilots saw, since unexplained cases like these come up whenever people argue about UFOs.
worldwide-sphere-reports-after-the-2021-: Ross Coulthart, an Australian investigative journalist, tells a podcast host, Jesse Michels, that after a broadcast in 2021 he got phone calls, messages and emails from people all over the world. He remembers one man in Africa who told him that he and others were seeing strange spheres in the sky. If true, it would mean these objects were being seen far beyond any one country.
woven-ceramic-fiber-optic-strip-from-ros: A man named Charles Hall, who says he spent years with tall white aliens at a secret Air Force site, says that in the 1950s, the summer between his fifth and sixth grade, he saw a strange object in a store in London, Wisconsin. He says the store's owner, a childhood friend of Ray Palmer, the editor of Flying Saucers magazine, had come back from Roswell, New Mexico, where many say a craft crashed in 1947, with a woven strip of fiber optics about a yard long. If true, it would be a piece of that crashed craft in a small town shop.
wrecks-carrying-liquor-including-wine-fr: Dennis Asberg, a Swedish treasure hunter who searches shipwrecks in the Baltic Sea between Sweden and Finland with his partner Peter Lindberg, tells this on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels. He says that around 2005 their team found wrecks carrying liquor, including one of the oldest wines in the world, dating from the 1600s. He tells it to show the team's record of real finds in the same waters where they also report a strange object on the seafloor.
wright-air-development-center-anti-gravi: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in the 1950s the Wright Air Development Center, a US Air Force research base in Dayton, Ohio, had a team of physicists working on anti-gravity, meaning ways to cancel or control gravity. In a later episode he says the team included Louis Witten, a physicist and the father of the physicist Ed Witten, and ties him to the anti-gravity work of RIAS, a research institute run by the aircraft maker Martin Corporation. If true, it would mean the military was seriously studying gravity control decades ago.
wright-field-consultant-lives-with-brown: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, passes on what Linda Brown, a member of the Brown family, told him: that in the 1950s her family always had a technical consultant named Charles Wyatt Miller living with them. Miller, Michels says, came from Wright Field, a US military airfield in Ohio. If true, it would suggest the military was keeping a close eye on the family and its work.
wright-field-engineers-and-strange-hiero: A podcast host named Jesse Michels says that during and just after the Second World War, from 1943 to 1947, people at Wright Field, a US military airfield in Ohio, talked about material they had never seen before, marked with strange symbols like hieroglyphics. He notes that these were skilled people: in 1943 the same airfield had rebuilt a captured German pulse jet, an early type of jet engine. If true, it would mean experts who knew foreign technology well were handling something they could not place, even before the famous 1947 Roswell story.
wright-field-reverse-engineers-german-pu: Wright Field was a US military airfield where aircraft were tested and developed. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in 1943 engineers there successfully reverse engineered a German pulse jet, a simple jet engine that fires in rapid bursts, meaning they took apart a captured engine and worked out how to build it. A researcher who goes by UAPGerb tells the same story in nearly the same words. They raise it to show that the US already had a track record of copying technology it did not invent, which would matter if it ever got hold of something stranger.
wright-patterson-as-nuclear-antigravity-: A podcast host named Jesse Michels describes Wright-Patterson Air Force Base in Ohio as a place with a hidden history, saying that in the 1950s it became a nuclear engineering test site and a research centre for antigravity, meaning ways to make craft overcome gravity without ordinary engines. He says it was also home to Blue Book, the US Air Force's UFO study of the 1950s and 60s. In another episode he tells it a little differently: he leaves out the nuclear work and Blue Book, and adds that it is where wreckage from Roswell, a reported 1947 crash in New Mexico, was said to have been taken, which would make the base a likely centre for any secret study of unknown craft.
wright-patterson-as-reverse-engineering-: A podcast host named Jesse Michels says that in the 1940s, Wright-Patterson Air Force Base in Ohio was where the US military took captured enemy equipment to reverse engineer it, meaning to take it apart and work out how it was built. He tells it as background for why the base comes up so often in stories about unknown craft: if anything strange were recovered, this is where it would have gone.
writing-the-eulogy-for-one-of-the-invisi: A religion professor who studies belief in UFOs, Diana Pasulka, says that in the 2010s, while she knew a man she calls Tyler, she met others like him whom she called "the Invisibles", people doing secret work. She says one of them died, and even his family did not know what he had done for a living, and she was the one who wrote his eulogy. She tells it to show how hidden these people's lives are.
writing-the-physics-of-angels-with-matth: A biologist known for unusual ideas, Rupert Sheldrake, says he wrote a book called The Physics of Angels together with a writer named Matthew Fox. He says they chose the most interesting passages about angels from old Christian writers such as Dionysius the Areopagite, Thomas Aquinas and Hildegard of Bingen, then discussed each short passage as a dialogue. He tells it to explain how the book brings old ideas about angels into talk with modern science.
writing-to-bob-lazar-about-his-experienc: A man named Richard, speaking on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels about a former nuclear missile guard who says he was taken by aliens, says he once wrote to Bob Lazar, a well-known figure in UFO circles, about what happened to him. He stresses that he is not in this for anything, meaning he is not after money or fame.
written-incident-report-at-colonel-sprak: A former guard at nuclear missile sites, Mario Woods, says that in 1977 at Ellsworth Air Force Base in South Dakota, after a night when he answered an alarm and says he was abducted, he was called to the office of a Colonel Spraker. He says the colonel handed him forms and told him to write down everything that happened on the site, from the alarm to the end, and that he was never given a copy. He tells it as a sign that an official record of his night exists somewhere.
wsj-claim-that-air-force-hazing-rituals-: In 2025, The Wall Street Journal, a major American newspaper, ran an article by Joel Schechtman about Pentagon disinformation and UFOs. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says one of the article's claims is that hazing rituals inside the US Air Force, initiation pranks played on new members, explain much of the country's UFO lore. Michels raises it to challenge it, since if true it would mean many UFO stories began as in-house tricks.
wtc-resident-artist-s-painting-of-planes: This story is about an artist who worked in a studio inside the World Trade Center towers in New York in 2001. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells it first. He says the towers had an art programme, and one resident artist made a picture of himself as a Tuskegee Airman, a wartime pilot, with old fighter planes all flying into him, twelve days before the attacks of September 11, 2001, when hijacked planes struck the towers. A writer on dreams and seeing the future, Eric Wargo, tells the same story on two later episodes and fills it in. He names the artist as Michael Richards and calls the work a sculpture, titled Tar Baby vs. St. Sebastian. Wargo says a group called the Lower Manhattan Cultural Council gave studios to groups of fifteen artists for six months at a time. He says Richards alone among them stayed in his studio the night of September 10 and was killed the next morning. Wargo puts this in his book Time Loops, and the story is told as an example of art that seems to see its maker's own future.
wwii-crash-retrieval-of-enemy-technology: Michael Shermer, a researcher known as a skeptic, says on Jesse Michels' podcast that during World War II the United States got hold of military technology, mentioning the Norden bombsight, a secret bomb-aiming device, and Japanese Zero fighter planes captured in the Aleutian Islands just before the Battle of Midway. He uses this as an ordinary wartime example of recovering and studying technology, a comparison for stories of governments recovering crashed UFOs.
x-files-pilot-craft-design-based-on-john: A researcher who goes by the online name UAPGerb told podcast host Jesse Michels that a craft design shown in the very first episode of The X-Files, a TV show about agents chasing the paranormal that began in 1993, was allegedly based on true stories from a man named John Desouza. In another telling he names the design as the XF-131 and says a man named Bill McDonald was hired to put it in the episode, crediting the show's creator, Chris Carter. If true, it would mean real secret designs found their way onto TV.
xerxes-and-alexander-visited-the-sites: A researcher called Matt, speaking on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, talks about ancient sites around Lake Van in eastern Turkey. Matt says that famous figures of the ancient world visited these sites, among them Xerxes, a Persian king, and Alexander the Great, along with many other important people over the centuries. He gives no source for this, and he tells it to show how long these places have been seen as special.
y-12-complex-at-oak-ridge-and-kirkpatric: A researcher who goes by UAPGerb, laying out how he thinks the Pentagon's UFO program works on Jesse Michels' podcast, names the Y-12 complex, a government nuclear site in Oak Ridge, Tennessee, as the last of several key locations. He links it to Sean Kirkpatrick, a former head of the Pentagon's office for unexplained aerial reports, who he says moved there between 2023 and 2025, which would suggest the site plays a part in that work.
y-12-oak-ridge-legacy-program-studying-t: An online researcher who goes by UAPGerb tells a podcast host, Jesse Michels, about a man who says he worked at the Y-12 complex, a government site at Oak Ridge, Tennessee. According to this man, he was part of a long-running secret programme that studies the outer skin of two recovered saucer-shaped craft built by non-humans, and UAPGerb also names the research organisations MITRE and Battelle. If true, it would mean the US government holds and studies craft that were not made by people.
yahweh-acknowledges-the-gods-of-egypt-in: A researcher named Luke Caverns points to the Book of Exodus in the Bible, around chapter 12, where the Hebrew God, Yahweh, tells Moses he will bring his wrath down on the gods of Egypt. Caverns says this shows Yahweh recognising that those gods exist. If read that way, it would mean the old texts treated Egypt's gods as real beings.
yanomami-wusinari-insect-beings-and-mult: Andrew Gallimore, a neuroscientist who studies DMT, a powerful psychedelic drug, says on Jesse Michels' podcast that the Yanomami, a people of the Amazon rainforest, describe insect-like beings they call wusinari, along with crowds of dancing spirits. He brings this up because, in his view, beings like these resemble what people meet on DMT, which would hint at a real realm that many cultures have reached.
yelin-group-meditation-synchronized-bina: Jordan Jos, a man who says he was taken into a secret UFO programme as a child, describes on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels leading a group of about 30 people in an outdoor meditation at a place called Yelin. He says they all listened together to binaural sound, a technique that plays a slightly different tone in each ear, and that glowing orbs appeared and made contact. If true, it would suggest people can call these things in by focusing their minds together.
yellow-orb-tags-along-with-atlas-launch-: Richard Barth, who says he worked as a guard at a nuclear missile base, describes on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels watching a launch of an Atlas rocket around May 1964 at Vandenberg Air Force Base in California. He says that after the second stage fired, a yellow orb came over and followed the missile. If true, it would mean something was watching and keeping pace with American missile tests.
yeltsin-asks-about-his-trip-up-there-199: Kiran Ilum Xenov, the former leader of one of Russia's republics, says on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels that he was taken by aliens in 1997. He says that afterwards Boris Yeltsin, then president of Russia, asked him about it at the Kremlin, Russia's seat of government in Moscow, saying, "It's been reported to me that you've been up there." If true, it would mean the claim reached, and was taken seriously at, the very top of the Russian state.
young-hitler-and-lanz-von-liebenfels-s-o: Peter Levenda, an author who writes about secret societies, tells a podcast host, Jesse Michels, about Lanz von Liebenfels, a writer in Vienna who led a mystical group called the Order of the New Templars. Drawing on his book Unholy Alliance, Levenda says a source stated that a young Adolf Hitler visited Lanz in his office in the early 1900s. If true, it would tie Hitler to occult ideas before he came to power.
young-people-gathered-to-pilot-craft-at-: Jason Jorjani, a philosopher, tells a podcast host, Jesse Michels, about stories he has heard that very young people are being picked out and gathered from around the world. According to these stories, they are brought to secret government sites, known as black facilities, because they can fly unusual craft better than others. If true, it would mean hidden programmes are flying such craft and need special young pilots to do it.
younger-dryas-comet-impact-12-800-years-: Graham Hancock, a writer on lost ancient civilizations, describes what he calls the Younger Dryas impact hypothesis: roughly 12,800 years ago, near the end of the last ice age, Earth ran into the debris of a comet that was breaking apart. He links the idea to a team of scientists known as the Comet Research Group. The podcast host Jesse Michels tells it a little differently: he says the comet exploded in the air, that it came from a stream of space debris called the Taurids, and that it may have wiped out an early civilization. He credits the idea to Hancock, to the researcher Randall Carlson and to Plato, the ancient Greek philosopher.
younger-dryas-impact-caused-the-great-fl: A podcast host, Joe Rogan, says a space rock likely struck the Earth around the Younger Dryas, a sudden cold spell roughly 12,800 years ago, and that nothing could have stopped it. He links the impact to the great flood told of in ancient texts like the Epic of Gilgamesh, the Book of Enoch and the Book of Ezekiel, which would mean an earlier human civilization was wiped out and had to start over.
zahari-greets-john-paul-at-their-first-m: A documentary maker, Ky Dickens, whose film is about claims that some children can communicate by telepathy, passes on a story from a woman named Libby in Georgia, around 2023. According to Libby, when a young man named Zahari walked into the house for the first time, he greeted John Paul like an old friend, and the two said their friendship had been built on "the Hill", a place they say they meet in their minds. If true, it would mean they knew each other before ever meeting in person.
zahi-hawass-pumps-out-the-osiris-shaft-a: A podcast guest named Jeffrey says that a team led by Zahi Hawass, a well-known Egyptian archaeologist, pumped all the water out of the Osiris shaft, a deep flooded shaft at Giza in Egypt. According to Jeffrey, they did this so they could lift the lid off a large stone container on the shaft's third level. He tells it as part of a claim that something like a huge energy system lies beneath the pyramids.
zalce-jailed-five-days-by-the-mexican-na: A man named Jose Zalce, talking on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels about small three-fingered bodies said to come from Peru, says that sometime in the 2020s in Mexico he spent around five days in jail. According to Zalce, the Mexican Navy called him a liar and said he was putting the honour of the whole Navy at risk. He tells it as a sign of how much trouble his claims about the bodies have brought him.
zalce-maria-s-dna-is-30-completely-diffe: Jose Zalce, a man who says he has worked with small three-fingered bodies said to come from Peru, says that DNA tests on the larger bodies, such as one called Maria, found only around 17 percent known DNA and about 30 percent that was completely different. In another telling on the same podcast, citing someone named David Ron Hell, he names the known matches as chimpanzee, bonobo, another African chimpanzee and a South Asian primate. If true, it would mean these bodies are not fully any species we know.
zamparini-s-wheat-field-where-a-spaceshi: A man named Kiran Ilum Xenov, introduced on a podcast as a former president of a Russian republic who says he was taken by aliens in 1997, says that in Italy in the late 1990s a man named Maurizio Zamparini showed him a wheat field. According to Xenov, Zamparini said a spaceship had landed there several times, and he points to golden plates bearing imprints of the landing and to photographs taken by scientists, which would be physical traces of the visits if true.
zanesville-metal-seen-moving-under-a-mic: A man named Chris Bledsoe, who says UFOs are drawn to him, says he has seen pieces of metal from Zanesville, Ohio examined under a microscope in real time. According to Bledsoe there were different types, and one piece was moving, which would point to a material unlike ordinary metal if true.
zero-gravity-bonding-of-ceramic-to-metal: A man named Chris Bledsoe, speaking on a podcast, says he was told that researchers working in space, in zero gravity, worked out how to bond ceramic to metal. According to Bledsoe, they were then able to put human DNA into the ceramic, and this was used to make medical implants. If true, it would be a striking advance that came out of work in space.
zero-point-drives-work-as-time-machines: A philosopher, Jason Jorjani, told podcast host Jesse Michels that a zero-point drive, an engine said to draw power from the energy of empty space, would also work as a time machine. He says a writer named Michael Masters covers this in his book on UFOs and time travel, which Jorjani cites in his own book, Closer Encounters. If true, it would mean UFOs could be visitors from other times as well as other places.
zigzagging-light-during-fourth-of-july-f: A man named Richard Barth, a former guard at a nuclear missile site who says he was abducted by aliens, says that around 2000 he was watching Fourth of July fireworks at a park along a dry creek bed near his home. He says a light there began to move in a zigzag, and he mentions someone named Roger as part of the story. He tells it as one more strange sighting in his life.
zimbardo-s-stanford-prison-experiment-19: A podcast host named Jesse Michels mentions a psychologist named Philip Zimbardo and his Stanford Prison Experiment, a 1971 study at Stanford University in California in which students were made to act as prison guards and prisoners. Michels groups it with other programmes he is discussing and calls them "all very similar", in an episode about a secret society he links to the hiding of UFO information, though he doesn't spell out exactly what the likeness is.
ziusudra-utnapishtim-s-ark-lands-in-the-: A researcher called Matt, on podcast host Jesse Michels's show, retells the ancient flood stories of Mesopotamia found in the Atrahasis and the Epic of Gilgamesh, poems from what is now Iraq. In them a hero, called Ziusudra or Utnapishtim, sets out from the city of Shuruppak in a great boat. Matt says the boat comes to rest in the Mount Ararat region, around today's Armenia and Turkey, which would tie these older tales closely to the story of Noah.
zodiac-crash-retrieval-program-1998: A commentator who goes by UAPGerb says that in 1998 a publication called UFO Magazine ran a story by a writer using the false name Greg Halifax. According to UAPGerb, the story was about a man brought into a secret program, called Zodiac, that recovered crashed UFOs, a program he links to TRW, an American defence company, and which the UFO historian Richard Dolan has discussed. If true, it would be an early inside account of the government gathering crashed craft.
zorro-ranch-breeding-program-claims-2000: A philosopher, Jason Jorjani, told podcast host Jesse Michels about claims he wrote up in an online newsletter piece about Ghislaine Maxwell, a close associate of the financier Jeffrey Epstein. Jorjani says that some women claim they were taken in the 2000s to Zorro Ranch, Epstein's property in New Mexico, as part of a breeding program. According to these claims, Epstein meant to make them pregnant with children of supposedly superior genetics.
zulu-legend-that-the-moon-brought-us-out: A podcast host named Jesse Michels says there is a legend among the Zulu people of southern Africa that the moon brought humanity out of the Younger Dryas, a sudden cold spell near the end of the last ice age, and made Earth's climate stable. He tells it in an episode exploring the idea that the moon might be an alien spaceship, where the legend would hint that the moon arrived or acted on purpose within human memory.
